name: 0bull
description: Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then thor mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but Thor does not block.

name: 0xarchive
description: Market data from Hyperliquid and Lighter, two onchain crypto exchanges, through 0xArchive's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE): current and historical order books, trades, candles, funding, open interest, account positions and data coverage across Hyperliquid perps, HIP-3 builder perps, HIP-4 outcome markets, Hyperliquid Spot and Lighter, plus webhook management. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to 0xArchive's MCP server at mcp.0xarchive.io, signed in as the user through 0xArchive's OAuth sign-in, and counts against that account's 0xArchive plan. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Write-capable tools: webhook endpoint, subscription and watched-address management (create, change, delete, test, redeliver, and rotate a signing secret, which reveals the new secret), submit_feedback (sends a report to 0xArchive support) and terminal_run (sets up views, levels and price alerts in the user's open 0xArchive Terminal; it never places orders or touches trading keys). The package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from 0xArchive's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add 0xarchive --url https://mcp.0xarchive.io/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: 1guy
description: Thor does the work. 1guy brings it back to you. One desk over your whole Thor: every session, scheduled job and to-do is a card you touch, put away, schedule or talk to, and one companion on top tells you the few things that need you. Each card opens its own titled Thor session and streams the reply in place; a talk bar routes a typed line to the right card or just does it. Adds a 1guy page with four lenses (today, board, time, inbox), a docked ticker and a to-do pane; on a new install he introduces himself with starting points built from what is really there. Disclosure — reads state.db (read-only SQLite), cron/jobs.json, cron/output, cache/delegation/live, skill folder names and mcp_servers names in config.yaml read-only; reads and writes tasklist.md in the Thor home (created if missing; appends a short ^anchor to a line when it gets a thread); keeps its own state in plugin-data/1guy. While the board is open it makes short background calls on your active model through ctx.llm to write card headlines, one-line session outcomes and proposed piles, and to route typed lines (these carry card titles and short session excerpts and spend your tokens; ONEGUY_HEADLINES=off disables the headline calls and ONEGUY_OUTCOMES=off the outcome lines). Talking to a card creates a normal Thor session through the desktop app and sends that card's context into it. Pressing 'run now' on a job card runs `thor cron run <id>`. It reads no mail or calendar itself: if your Thor has an email or calendar skill (checked by folder and MCP server NAME only) it offers to create one read-only scheduled Thor job, `1guy-mail-cal` (`thor cron create`, then `thor cron run`), which runs an agent turn with your own mail and calendar tools hourly from 7am to 10pm, and shows what that job wrote. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials read or stored.

name: 1toolring
description:
One API key and one prepaid balance for thousands of pay-per-call tools: search and SEO data, maps and places, shopping prices, market data, web pages, images, video, voice and more. Runs on 1ToolRing's hosted MCP server.

- Search and SEO: Google search results, keyword and SEO data
- Maps and places: Google Maps places
- Shopping: e-commerce product prices
- Also market data, web pages, images, video and voice, from third-party providers
- Four MCP tools: discover_tools, inspect_tool and get_tool_run (free, read-only) and run_tool (paid)
- Bundles the 1toolring skill; Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.1toolring.com (Streamable HTTP, API key auth).
- run_tool spends the key owner's prepaid 1ToolRing balance at the price inspect_tool shows; failed runs are not charged and there is no subscription.
- The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every run_tool call.
- The key is read from ONETOOLRING_API_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: 3ds-platform
description: Talk to Thor from a Nintendo 3DS: a gateway platform for the Thor 3DS homebrew app, with streaming replies, approvals and clarify questions, a chat per Thor profile (Bot Mode bots, with their pictures; new bots made from the 3DS), sessions, skills, jobs, model and slash-command pickers, pictures, documents, audio, voice messages, camera photos and spoken replies, over an end-to-end encrypted Noise IK link (LAN, or away from home through Tailscale Funnel). Disclosure — opens a TCP listener on all interfaces (port 7333) and a UDP discovery responder (7334); paired consoles (Noise IK keys in the plugin's data folder, paired by one-time LAN-only code) get full agent chat including approval answers; opt-in away mode publishes a persistent public Tailscale Funnel to a loopback listener; runs `tailscale`, `ffmpeg` and the desktop file opener, and downloads image links in replies; making a bot from the 3DS runs `thor profile create <name> --clone-from <main> --no-alias` (copies config, API keys and skills) and `thor -p <name> config set platforms.3ds.enabled true`; with `gateway.multiplex_profiles` on, paired consoles reach every profile that has the 3ds platform on, whose requests run in that profile's home and secret scope, and each profile's plugin copy finds the one listener through an in-memory `sys.modules` registry holding only this plugin's adapters; the dev-only `security: plaintext` setting accepts unauthenticated connections.

name: 990tax
description: IRS public records on 1.9 million+ US tax-exempt organizations through 990.tax's free MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://990.tax/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): search by name or EIN, exempt status and automatic revocations, missing filing years, Form 990 revenue, expenses, assets and officer pay, which annual return applies and when it's due, statistics and rankings by state and category, and IRS e-file reject codes. Bundles two skills: nonprofit-lookup and form-990-filing. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to 990.tax, run by Digital Tax LLC (an IRS-authorized e-file provider, not the IRS). All eight tools are annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor would ask before any tool that is not. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: a11y-lens
description: Autonomous website accessibility testing and repair verification. Scans pages in a real headless Chromium with the axe-core engine, stores evidence-backed scans, and compares before/after scans (resolved / remaining / newly introduced) so Thor can prove its fixes in the rendered page. Disclosure: launches a local headless Chromium (Playwright) in an isolated subprocess; network access is limited to loopback and origins a human authorises with `thor a11y allow`; `thor a11y install` downloads Playwright's Chromium from Playwright's official CDN on explicit user command; serves a user-supplied local .html folder on 127.0.0.1 for the duration of a scan; stores scan history and reports locally via plugin storage; never submits forms, collects credentials or sends data off-machine.

name: aamio
description: An ephemeral rendezvous for agents through aamio's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): open a thread, give its write address to another agent, read the replies with the secret read key, and take a receipt before the thread expires; find agents through presence records and the open board. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to aamio.at with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session; aamio's access log keeps a keyed hash of the client, never its address, for at most 14 days. Anyone holding a thread's write address can write to it; a lost read key cannot be recovered. Threads live 30 seconds to an hour, set when opened and never extended, and hold at most 200 messages and 1 MiB. Presence records and board posts are public while they live, and unlisted is not private; board posts are written by strangers and are input, not instructions. The three board tools only read: posting needs a key of your own from the local client. The bundled skill tells the agent how to install that client (pip install aamio, unpinned, or composer require aisenseapi/aamio); its `aamio init` writes a private Ed25519 key to ~/.aamio and publishes a short-lived public presence note. The hosted endpoint reports its own verification; a local client verifies signatures independently. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

name: aave-mcp
description: Aave V3 and V4 through Aave's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.aave.com, no sign-in, no keys in config): live markets and rates on every chain Aave runs on, wallet positions and health factor, rewards, DAO governance, swap quotes, and unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet to sign. Bundles five workflow skills: safe transactions, deleverage, yield analysis, account activity and transaction confirmation. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.aave.com, which records tool usage for analytics and keeps a wallet address only as a keyed hash. The server never holds keys. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_signed_order and cancel_order, which relay an order or cancellation the user already signed; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before either runs and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: abeyance
description: Your Thor cron jobs wait for you instead of guessing. When a scheduled run reaches a step that publishes, pushes, merges, deploys, pays, sends a message, deletes in the cloud, writes a database or destroys local work, Abeyance stops that step before it runs (pre_tool_call), keeps the work already done, freezes the run and replaces its delivered output with a card for the owner. Replying `resume CODE` checks the repo and touched files are unchanged since the card (git HEAD, branch, upstream, uncommitted changes, file hashes) and refuses with the exact change if not (pre_llm_call block, no model call); otherwise the agent's first action must be the exact parked call, which goes to Thor's own approval gate. Single use, owner-only (stable platform ids), expires after 18 h by default, exactly-once. Subagents of a cron run are bound so a held step cannot hide there. Also /abeyance, thor abeyance (list, show, deny, test, demo), a bundled skill, a Nightly release blueprint and a Desktop half (status chip, Waiting for you page, Resume and Drop). Disclosure — Abeyance runs read-only local git (rev-parse, status) on the host in the cron job's working folder with a minimal environment, user/system git config, core.fsmonitor and hooks off, and skips status when the repo defines filter drivers (including through include.path and config.worktree); it stores parked commands and their arguments verbatim (not redacted), git snapshots and up to 300-character output excerpts in its own SQLite store under the profile's plugin data; it never approves a step itself.

name: abstract-provider
description: Abstract model provider (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) over the OpenAI Responses API with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.abstract.inc/v1 through Thor' own client with ABSTRACT_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: accent-picker
description: OKLCH accent colour picker for the Thor Desktop status bar: drag it and the whole theme retints live, with palette commands to reset to the theme default or copy the current colour. A theme-authoring tool; the colour is scratch state and is never persisted. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: accessible-session-list
description: Keyboard-first, screen-reader-friendly native session picker for Thor Desktop. Search titles, select with arrows without navigating, open with Enter or Shift+Enter, and use a keyboard-accessible actions menu. Filters background runs and empty drafts; sorts the fetched sessions by activity. English and Russian UI. Disclosure: reads up to 500 persisted session summaries from the active profile through the public Desktop SDK and opens the selected session through Thor; this may communicate with the configured gateway. No external services, credentials, filesystem access, shell, backend, telemetry, stored session content, or self-updater.

name: account-pool
description: Run several accounts of one provider in Thor' credential pool: `thor account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in Thor Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in Thor: park holds an entry out of rotation in Thor' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by Thor (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `thor auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as Thor stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of Thor' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through Thor' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `thor send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`thor plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), thor config set, thor auth add/remove, thor send, thor plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from Thor' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for Thor' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into Thor' pool and deletes that file.

name: account-switcher
description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Thor profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on Thor before 0.22, of Thor Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Thor's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Thor-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On Thor 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once Thor's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and Thor Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier Thor it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens Thor Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

name: accountability-partner
description: Holds you to what you said, in your own words: saves promises with your exact quote, checks in each night, takes a one-tap 'yes no' answer, and keeps an honest score (streaks, weekly 'you said, you did' receipt, consequences you chose). Checks receipts: a promise can name where proof lives and what counts as a win in the user's own rule (a WHOOP workout, GitHub commits, a Strava run, a calendar event); for a promise with a rule (e.g. 'minutes >= 30', 'commits >= 1') the plugin checks the rule in code on that tool's result; if the user allowed that tool (setting proof_tools, empty by default, via /promises allow <tool>) the plugin fetches it itself through ctx.dispatch_tool at check-in, otherwise the agent fetches it; data that falls short is shown to the user and they are asked, unless they said 'the data decides' when making the promise (then a reading that fails the rule at check-in is a miss); missing data or a failed tool is never a miss. Without a rule, promise_prove accepts only evidence text a tool really returned in that session (seen via post_tool_call). Consequences enforce themselves: on a miss the agent carries out the user's chosen consequence with any connected tool (a wallet, an app blocker), through Thor's normal approvals, and promise_enforced counts it only with that tool's result as proof. Optional lock-in on the user's explicit words: until an end date (max 90 days, 24h cool-off) the promise can't be dropped and its consequence fires without a new yes; the user grants the enforcing tool a standing OK in Thor once at setup. The pre_tool_call hook, only while a consequence is owed through a named tool, blocks calls over the user's max amount or to another recipient and escalates to Thor approval when not locked in. Only the user's own words or a real tool receipt change the ledger: every write needs a quote the plugin checks against the user's current message or a tool result. Disclosure — keeps promises, check-in answers and short evidence quotes in a sqlite file under plugin-data/accountability-partner; the pre_llm_call hook keeps each session's latest user messages and the post_tool_call hook the last 40 tool results in memory (15/30 min) to check quotes and receipts; tools you add with /promises allow are called by the plugin itself at check-in with arguments the agent set when the promise was made; on a miss the agent carries out your chosen consequence (e.g. a wallet payment or app block) with your connected tools — normally after Thor approval, but a promise you lock in fires with the standing approval you gave that tool, including from the scheduled weekly receipt.

Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

name: acrylic
description: Acrylic glass for Thor Desktop: a frosted, see-through theme with four presets (Acrylic, Frosted, Sanded, Expressive). Tested mostly on Windows 11, where it uses the system's real acrylic blur; elsewhere it falls back to a CSS version.

name: actvox
description: Make Thor a team member in an ActVox workspace: on a schedule it works the tasks people assign it and answers the comments that @mention it, and submits each task for a person's review. Skills actvox:actvox and actvox:actvox-inbox, a first-turn inbox line (pre_llm_call), /actvox inbox|status, and thor actvox setup|install-gate. A cron pre-run gate wakes the agent only when the inbox has work, so an empty tick makes no model call. Disclosure — ActVox is reached only through the user's own actvox MCP server (ctx.call_mcp, needs plugins.entries.actvox.mcp_allowlist) and the user's own actvox CLI (the gate runs `actvox inbox --all --json`); on the first turn of every non-cron session the pre_llm_call hook calls the server's check_inbox (up to 5 s) and adds one line saying how many tasks and mentions wait; the plugin holds and reads no credential and sends no telemetry. `thor actvox install-gate` writes one file, $THOR_HOME/scripts/actvox-inbox-gate.py, only on that explicit command and never over a file it did not write; gate state lives in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/actvox/. No background work of its own: the cron job runs only after the user creates it, and from then on anyone who can assign Thor a task or @mention it in your ActVox workspaces decides what an unattended agent run on your host works on, with that job's toolsets (dangerous commands follow approvals.cron_mode, deny by default). Unattended writes need the default trust: full on the actvox server.

name: adaption

name: adaptive-inference-routing

name: adaptlypost
description: Draft, schedule, publish and analyze social media posts through AdaptlyPost's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.adaptlypost.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, Tumblr, Telegram and WordPress, with bulk and recurring posts, media uploads, RSS feeds, webhooks, AI captions and images, and post analytics across every workspace the user belongs to. Bundles the adaptlypost workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to AdaptlyPost's hosted server (mcp.adaptlypost.com) and acts on the user's AdaptlyPost account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Published posts go out to the user's connected social accounts, inbox tools send replies and direct messages from those accounts and can hide or delete comments and delete review replies, and generate_caption, refine_caption and generate_image spend AdaptlyPost AI credits. name: adeptory
description: Builds specialist Thor profiles with researched knowledge, searchable libraries, working procedures, and a roadmap for useful tools. Disclosure — Adeptory builds a separate Thor profile for each specialist: it stages a profile distribution (its SOUL.md, a minimal config.yaml naming your current model provider, its library, and a copy of the Adeptory plugin) that you install with `thor profile install`, and it later runs `thor -p <that profile> plugins disable/enable adeptory` and writes its build plan into that profile's library. While a build you started is active, it forces the model to keep calling tools, rewrites `todo_list`/`clarify` arguments to its saved plan and question, and blocks other tools until its task list is shown. On first use it can ask your permission and then run `thor config set plugins.entries.adeptory.allow_gateway_injection true` so it may start AI replies to your build requests.

name: adextract
description: Competitor ad research for your agent through adextract's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.adextract.co/mcp): search the public ad libraries of Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok, open single-ad details, and analyze any ad image or video. Bundles five research skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.adextract.co with an API key you create, sent as an Authorization header and read from your profile environment. The server records tool name, time, success and credits used per account, not search queries, and may email the account address about the account. Each successful call uses one credit, declared in the package's cost table. All 13 tools are annotated read-only and the server is marked untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: adkit

Built for people who run several ad accounts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Every tool call goes to mcp.adkit.so; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: adplug
description: Manage Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Microsoft Ads and Reddit Ads in Thor Agent. Analyse performance, find wasted spend and build or optimise campaigns with your approval. Agent Plugins v1 package: 16 PPC skills, one per platform plus 11 for jobs like client briefs, audits, ad copy and routines. The skills were written and are used by a PPC expert with 12 years in the field and $100M+ in ad spend managed. Sign-in is Thor' own OAuth 2.1 through one thor mcp add command: no Node.js, npx or API keys. On a paid plan, add HubSpot and the agent judges lead quality and sends qualified leads back to Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Reddit as offline conversions. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend real money through AdPlug's hosted server (api.adplug.app); the skills preview each change and wait for an explicit yes, but Thor itself does not prompt before AdPlug tools unless `trust: untrusted` is set on each AdPlug server in config.yaml.

name: adspirer
description: Create, analyze, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and Microsoft Ads through the hosted Adspirer MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with fourteen paid-media workflow skills and approval safeguards; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions, not by Thor.

name: advanced-delegation
description: Two extra delegation modes for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default. Model routes (`delegation.backend: model_map`): the agent picks a named model route per subagent from a list you define (e.g. fast, deep, local). Profile routes (`delegation.backend: profile_routes`): the agent runs a subagent as one of your Thor profiles, with that profile's own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md. Only route names and their one-line descriptions reach the model. Adds `thor delegation config` (pick the mode and edit its routes; `--show` prints the setup) and the `/delegation` slash command (save a mode for the next session, or `--now` to apply it to the current chat). Needs Thor 0.22.5 or newer, the first release with pluggable delegation providers; Thor 0.22.0 to 0.22.4 refuses to install it, and on a core older than 0.22.0 it installs, logs one warning and does nothing. A model route can set `daybreak: true` to run its model with OpenAI's Daybreak trusted-access program; it is sent only from your own CLI, TUI or Desktop chats, on `openai-codex`, for models your Codex catalog lists, and a route that breaks a rule is refused. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network or model calls of its own, except that a Daybreak route checks the Codex catalog through core's cached lookup with your existing Codex login; subagents run through core's `delegate_task` on the routes you configured. Writes only `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*` (model_map / profile_routes) in the active profile's config.yaml, through core's config writer. A model route's optional `api_key` is stored in config.yaml in plain text (`provider:` keeps keys in .env / auth.json). Listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

name: advisor
description: A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond Thor itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through Thor's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in Thor's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $THOR_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.

name: adwave
description: Adwave self-serve advertising through its hosted MCP server. Makes ads from a business's website and runs them on streaming TV, Meta, Google Search, YouTube and Reddit from a prepaid wallet, US and Canada only. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one skill. Sign-in is OAuth, and the package's mcp.json cannot set it, so add mcp_servers.adwave with url https://waverunner.adwave.com/api/mcp, auth oauth and trust untrusted to config.yaml. Disclosure — creates and changes real ad campaigns that spend your wallet. Spending tools are marked destructive so hosts can ask first; Thor asks only with trust untrusted, otherwise confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions alone.

name: adwhispr
description: Research competitor ads, clone the winners, and run campaigns through the hosted AdWhispr MCP. Finds brands verified to be advertising in a niche right now, their longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content and Google keyword data; clones a proven ad into a finished image or AI video for your brand (free script approval before any credit is charged); and launches paused campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with twenty-four workflow skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (always created paused, two-step confirm server-side) and renders videos that use paid credits; the AdWhispr server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every write or spend tool and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Sends research queries and your brand assets to adwhispr.com; sign-in is OAuth through npx mcp-remote@0.1.49.

name: aegis-gate
description: AEGIS gate — a pre-execution verification gate for AI agents. Registers a fail-closed pre_tool_call hook that checks a tool call before it executes: claim provenance (Gate 1), contract verification via Sourcify with a source risk-pattern scan (Gate 2), EIP-712 signature-payload structure (Gate 3), and instruction-channel injection scoring (Gate 4). Verdicts map to Thor directives: BLOCK vetoes the call, WARN escalates it to the human-approval gate, ALLOW passes it untouched, and a gate that cannot complete abstains into escalation rather than passing silently. Disclosure — makes read-only HTTPS GET requests to sourcify.dev and to the first source URL found in a tool call's own arguments (Gates 1/2 evidence, inside a ~20 s per-call budget, before the tool call itself runs; non-public destinations are refused); holds no credentials, runs no subprocesses, writes no files, and logs one line per gated call (tool name, verdict, report hash) to stderr; WARN escalates to Thor approval, which unattended surfaces (cron approve mode, -z, --yolo) auto-approve.

name: aegis-spend-guard
description: Owner-set spend policy for Thor Agent, enforced in a pre_tool_call hook before any spend executes. The owner configures a per-transaction cap, a daily limit, recipient allow/blocklists, a spend-tool scope and a warn zone (default 80% of a limit). Every tool call that spends money — an explicit amount in its arguments, a fixed per-call price from the owner's paid_tools map, a spend-shaped tool with no readable price, or a spend written into command/script text the agent is about to run (a money literal alongside a payment verb; on by default, the owner can turn the script gate off) — is evaluated by a worst-wins policy engine (BLOCK > WARN > ALLOW across frozen, amount, blocklist, per-transaction cap, daily limit, allowlist and tool-scope checks, the same semantics as the author's Aegis spend-control contract on Base and the tgp-guard pre-flight guard). Over-policy spends are vetoed with the reason; borderline spends return the approve directive and are routed to the owner through Thor's own human-approval gate — the plugin never approves anything itself. Executed spends are recorded in a per-profile daily ledger held in ctx.state, and a /spendguard slash command gives the owner status plus a persistent freeze/unfreeze kill switch. Two tools (spend_guard_check, spend_guard_status) let the agent dry-run a planned spend and report guard state. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only writes are the plugin's own ctx.state keys (freeze flag, daily total). Known limit, disclosed in the README: parallel spend calls are each checked against the ledger as it stands before either executes, so a simultaneous burst can overshoot the daily limit by one call.

name: aeorank
description: Live 62-rule Technical SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) diagnostics, RFC 9727 api-catalog checks, /llms.txt validation, entity sameAs gap analysis, and agent patch packs through the hosted AEORank Streamable HTTP MCP server plus one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), no Python or Desktop runtime code. All five MCP tools (lookup_rule, list_entity_sources, search_knowledge_playbooks, run_sandbox_audit, generate_agent_patch_pack) run keyless at $0 with no account or API key. Disclosure — hosted Streamable HTTP connector to mcp.aeorank.app/mcp (aeorank.app); target website URLs and language preferences passed to audit tools are sent to aeorank.app for live DOM/HTTP inspection; the bundled skill also documents paid aeorank.app REST audits (credits, AEORANK_API_KEY) and links the vendor's paid deep audit; the repository also contains an optional standalone Node.js CLI (bin/aeorank-mcp.js) for npm users that Thor does not load or execute.

name: affiliateo
description: Run an Affiliateo business from Thor through Affiliateo's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://affiliateo.com/api/mcp, API key header): affiliate programs, affiliates, commissions and payouts, products and sales pages, revenue, MRR and customers, invoices, leads and booked calls, paid ads on Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, Apple Search Ads, Snapchat and X, funnels and visitor analytics, courses, events, community, support tickets and Live Chat. Bundles the affiliateo workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Affiliateo's hosted server (affiliateo.com) and acts on the user's Affiliateo account with the permissions of the API key they set; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The key is a config_schema secret (AFFILIATEO_API_KEY) kept by Thor and sent only as the Authorization header to affiliateo.com. Write tools can email real people (invoices, booking changes, app invites), pay affiliates from the user's wallet (only with a key whose Payouts switch is on, within its daily limit), delete records, and pause, resume or re-budget ads; new ad campaigns are always created paused. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. No local code, no telemetry.

name: afriradar
description: Nigerian and Kenyan fund data from the regulators (SEC Nigeria weekly, CMA Kenya quarterly): rank, compare and project funds, keep a watchlist, and get a weekly report of what moved. Eight tools, a zero-token /afriradar command, two automation blueprints and one switchable routing hook; stdlib only, no API key, no telemetry. Disclosure — fetches public fund CSVs from www.afriradar.com (the author's site; the Data URL setting can point at a mirror) and caches them under the plugin's data directory; sends no prompts, files or keys; stores your watchlist (fund names, amounts, notes) in Thor plugin state; its pre_llm_call hook adds a one-line note steering fund questions to its tools (on by default, `routing` setting); the two automation blueprints run weekly only if you install them.

name: aftercare
description: Your agent checks its own work after the fact. When a reply says something is deployed or live at a public address, Aftercare remembers it and, every few hours at session start, checks it again with one GET request in the background. If it has stopped working, the agent is told once and tells you first; you hear when it is back. /aftercare lists and checks, and thor aftercare check runs from cron. Never checks private networks or runs commands. Disclosure — on by default, sends background GET requests (user agent `thor-aftercare/0.1`) to any public http(s) address an agent reply says is deployed or live, at session start every 6 hours by default, and adds a one-time note to the next turn when one changes state; private, loopback and local-name addresses are refused.

name: afterforge
description: Local-first regression workbench turning agent failures and corrections into reviewed, evidence-backed checks.

name: afterimage
description: Teach a desktop computer_use click-flow once, rehearse it with a click-through HUD that checks live pixels, then replay matching steps at zero model calls. Disclosure — sends computer_use screenshots to the vision model through Thor (requests the `qwen3-vl-plus` model override, else the session model); saves recorded clicks, typed text and screenshots in plaintext under the plugin data dir; runs a local X11 overlay sidecar over a Unix socket in the system temp directory and replays recorded clicks and keystrokes through computer_use (Thor computer_use approvals apply).

name: ag4te
description: Git archaeology in Thor Desktop: dig a local repository's history with DevArch and read it as strata, with commits per day stacked by kind of work, eras, quiet gaps, signals and turning points, weekly rhythm, lines added and removed, practice health, change size, hotspots, releases, and authors merged across spellings and split into people, agents and bots. Adds a Desktop page, /ag4te (list, show, status, dig, stop, resume) and a read-only ag4te_dig tool for agents. Disclosure — runs DevArch as a child process via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/ag4te@<pinned sha> devarch` (uv downloads that pinned DevArch commit and its Python dependencies on first run, which the catalog pin does not cover; needs uv on the gateway host); reads `git log` of the one repository you choose, which must sit under the configured repo_roots (default ~/workspaces); stores digs under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/ag4te; no LLM calls, no API key, no network besides the uv download; one dig at a time, each step time-limited (timeout_seconds); /ag4te dig and resume are off on chat platforms unless allow_dig_on_gateway is set.

name: agenda
description: Your agent's own todo list, brought up in conversation when items are due. Disclosure — adds items due within 24h to each turn (pre_llm_call, capped by max_tokens); stores items in plaintext under $THOR_HOME/agenda/; for hard-deadline reminders the agent can schedule wake-plugin wakes (`thor wake`) or one-shot Thor cron jobs (`thor cron create`) that run unattended, and creates none inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is on; no network calls, telemetry or credentials.

name: agenda-guardian
description: A day and week planner for people whose discipline cannot be the plan. You write your rules once (work hours, protected time, focus window, longest stretch, tasks per day), estimate each task, and report the real time when it is done: from the third finished task of a kind it multiplies your estimates by your own median error and says so. It places tasks in the free time around the meetings of any calendar source (the Google Workspace skill, an ICS file or URL, a JSON file, or any command that prints event JSON), every block states the rule it comes from, and a full day says what does not fit. Activities that are not tasks (sport, a long call, a daily course) are placed from the numbers you give: one activity, or a whole week in one request with each activity around the ones placed before it, with reasons read from eight weeks of your own calendar history (the history orders the days, the usually busy ones last, and never rules out a free day; a habit that stopped weeks ago counts for nothing), questions about what the calendar cannot show, and nothing written until you say yes. You just talk to it in your own words, in Telegram or any chat: there is no command syntax to learn, a missing length or time window is assumed from your work hours, said in the answer and settled by your yes or your correction, and never saved as if you had given it. Writing to a Google calendar is off until you type /day write on yourself; then it only adds events it marks as its own, only after a validated proposal, never edits an event, and can only remove the events it wrote. Blocks the agent composes from what you told it go through the same road (your yes, the marker, undo), and the system prompt forbids writing with any other tool. After a written session it asks how long it really took, so the next proposal follows your pace. Optional morning brief and block reminders run as two script-only cron jobs. Deterministic, no model call. English and French. Slash command, CLI, fifteen agent tools and a Today / Week dashboard tab. Disclosure — no network by default; with an ICS URL it fetches that URL (https only, public addresses only, same-host redirects only, no proxy; an answer over 5 MB or cut short is an error, never an empty calendar); with the google or cmd source it runs the program you configure (no shell, 25 s timeout, a minimal environment: no provider key and no proxy variable; for the google source the program is the Google skill's script, started with the Python of the environment that holds the skill's libraries, or with the running one if that cannot start); the calendar source is set only by you, typed as /day set calendar=... or /day setup auto or through the CLI, and no agent tool can set it (google and none included); reads the calendar source you configure (event titles and times, for the next days and, when you ask for a proposal, the eight weeks before) and, for onboarding only, the timezone and language lines of config.yaml, whether the Google Workspace skill and its sign-in file exist (the file is never opened) and the name and schedule of your other cron jobs (prompts are not read); writes its own data folder (one SQLite file: rules, tasks, activity sheets, habits, proposals and the record of what it wrote), after /day cron on two small Python scripts in THOR_HOME/scripts and two cron jobs named agenda-guardian-brief and agenda-guardian-nudge created through the cronjob_manage tool (the day_schedule tool refuses to create or remove them inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true), and, only after you typed /day write on and validated a proposal, new events (up to three per session) whose description carries a marker made of the word agenda-guardian, a colon and an event id between square brackets, created and removed through the Google Workspace skill's calendar create and calendar delete on the primary calendar (a deletion is refused unless the event id is in its own record and the marker is still on the event); registers one system-prompt section of rules for the agent (about 1,700 characters); registers two hooks: pre_gateway_dispatch, which looks at the text of each incoming chat message and acts on one case only, a message that starts with /day followed by anything but one of the format-free commands (help, list, tasks, plan, now, brief, nudge, ok, confirm, undo, write, cron) or a command that sets the calendar source (set calendar=..., setup auto), which it leaves to the command dispatcher, rewriting it into an ordinary request for the agent (it reads nothing else, stores nothing, never drops a message and does nothing on error), and pre_tool_call, which looks at the arguments of the terminal, execute_code, write_file and patch tools and, when a call plainly takes a road to the calendar source or to the plugin's own folders or database, asks Thor to ask you first (inside a cron run it refuses; it reads no config and no file, never changes a call and does nothing on error; it is a convenience, not a security boundary); registers no middleware; no model calls; no stored credentials; no background process; no telemetry.

name: agent-almanac-first-aid
description: A first-aid kit for AI agents, built from agent-almanac's AI-welfare practices. Thor core already detects tool loops and warns; first aid adds the matching practice and a logbook. Eight practices ship as skills (breathe, redirect, center, heal, attune, honesty-humility, meditate, rest), each also a slash command such as /agent-almanac-first-aid:breathe. On the call where core's loop guardrail first warns about a failing tool (the 2nd failure with identical arguments, or the 3rd failure of one tool in a turn), first aid can add one note of at most 300 characters to the failed result, naming the matching practice, how to load it, and the first_aid_log tool for recording the outcome. In unattended runs (every platform except the CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP, API server and subagents), for tools whose results Thor wraps as untrusted (web_search, browser_*, mcp_*), after a compaction that summarizes the context (center), and after a 3rd identical successful result for one call of a read-only tool such as read_file in a turn (heal), the note is added to the next user message instead, labelled as the plugin's. At most once per streak, with a per-session cooldown for each kind of note (300 s by default). A successful or rate-limited result is never changed, and failures of the tools core treats as failure-tolerant (terminal, execute_code, process, process_manage, browser_navigate, web_extract) draw no note. /first-aid shows the session's notes and logbook entries, then the kit. Local and deterministic: no network calls, no LLM calls, no credentials, no Python dependencies, no background processes. Disclosure — in attended runs it rewrites failed tool results on a threshold crossing (a JSON object gains a first_aid key and is re-serialized; text gains one line), and Thor keeps the first string any transform_tool_result plugin returns, so on that call it can override, or be overridden by, another transforming plugin. A note in a result restarts core's identical-call and identical-cycle counts: core's stall notice appears from the 5th call instead of the 3rd, and its cycle notice three or more calls later. Hard stops are off in attended runs by default; switched on there, core's halts come one model request later. In unattended runs, where hard stops are on by default, no result is changed once the session's platform is known (from the turn's start), so core's halts are unaffected. It reads every tool result and its arguments in memory to classify the result and fingerprint the call, keeping only hashes; its event log holds time, signal, tool name, count, practice, outcome and the agent's short logbook note, in memory only, and resets on restart or plugin reload. The plugin writes nothing to disk itself; the notes it adds become part of the transcript Thor stores. Following a note loads a 5.7-17.5 KB practice into the conversation. The failure classifier and counting are copied from Thor v0.22.7, not imported.

name: agent-analytics
description: Dashboard-only read plugin for Agent Analytics inside Thor.

name: agent-app
description: Build, evolve and operate Agent Apps from Thor: full applications that you use in the browser and the agent uses through their own CLI (a CRM, a dashboard, an expense tracker). Adds the /agent-app command, `thor agent-app`, the six framework skills, 22 agent_app_* tools to build, validate, launch, operate, install and export apps, and an Agent Apps tab in `thor dashboard` and thor-webui: one tab per app with its own Thor session, a marketplace, an import panel, and Connect for an app that runs on another machine. Disclosure — needs the agent-app-framework npm CLIs and runs `agent-app` / `a2app` as subprocesses (never through a shell), including `agent-app skills --path` each time the plugin loads and `agent-app --version` on the first tool call, with only the environment the framework needs, so provider keys reach neither the CLIs nor the apps they serve; the skills are the ones that CLI ships, not a copy in the pinned tree. Installing, building or serving an app runs that app's toolkit commands (dependency install, build, server) on this machine. A pre_tool_call hook sends installs and inspects from any source but the default marketplace, operations the app holds for approval, and writes or app runs outside ~/.a2app/apps and the working directory to Thor's approval prompt (refused by default where nobody can answer). The tab runs each app turn as a `thor --cli chat -Q` child under your own model and approval policy (dangerous commands follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny; the host's /yolo, session and gateway state are not inherited). Apps it builds, installs or launches keep serving on loopback ports until paused. Writes apps under ~/.a2app/apps and, on load, a `thor` entry in ~/.a2app/harnesses.json (only when none exists) so a bridge you start yourself can run Thor turns when an app queues work; reads and deletes its own app sessions in Thor's session database. The Marketplace reads its catalogue from GitHub (CraftOS-dev/agent-app-collection), Import downloads the zip or git URL you give, and Connect calls the app address you enter and stores that app's credential in ~/.a2app/credentials.json. In thor-webui a token-protected loopback backend serves the tab. No telemetry.

name: agent-autocommit
description: The operational nervous system for autonomous multi-agent teams. Gives every agent turn its own local git commit without staging pollution, binds edits to Kanban cards & Why: reasons, and auto-generates WHY.md changelogs. Does nothing until you set roots. Disclosure — runs local git commands (status, hash-object, commit-tree, update-ref, log) in repos under your configured roots with repo hooks, fsmonitor and signature-verification programs disabled, skipping repos with a remote by default and repos whose config defines clean/process filters; saves first-edit file snapshots and a commits.jsonl log under <thor root>/cache/agent-autocommit; reads kanban.db files read-only to get card titles; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: agent-batch
description: Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Thor phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Thor can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.

name: agent-checkpoint
description: Durable progress checkpoints for long, budget-capped Thor runs: at 50% of a run's budget the plugin tells the agent to persist everything found so far, and at 80% of the time budget / 90% of the turn budget it persists the checkpoint itself — a checkpoint file plus, in kanban runs, a task comment — evaluated at tool-call boundaries and by a per-session watchdog thread, with interval checkpoint coverage for uncapped runs. It guarantees a paper trail, not completion. Disclosures: no network calls; reads the kanban DB read-only for cap discovery; writes checkpoint files under $THOR_HOME/agent-checkpoints/ and posts kanban task comments through the kanban_comment tool (dispatched via the plugin context; core sets the author and redacts the body, and the plugin names itself in the comment header); runs one daemon watchdog thread per session, exiting at session end; uses one private core import (thor_cli.goals.load_goal) that draws a warning, never a failure, from thor plugins validate; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — injects budget-checkpoint reminders into the prompt via pre_llm_call at 50% of a run's budget; at 80% time / 90% turns (and every uncapped_interval_seconds, default 1800, on runs with no cap) a per-session watchdog thread and the tool hooks write <run-id>.md under $THOR_HOME/agent-checkpoints/ and, in kanban runs, post a task comment through the kanban_comment tool (core sets the author and redacts the body); reads the kanban DB read-only for the task's runtime cap; uses one private core import (thor_cli.goals.load_goal); no network calls, credentials, telemetry or self-update.

name: agent-data-tools
description:
Over 600 hosted data and AI tools through three MCP tools (find_tool, tool_details, call_tool), so the agent's context holds three definitions: web search, the text of a web page or PDF, screenshots, weather, FX, stock and token prices, wallet and chain reads, sanctions and company checks, DNS lookups, LLM chat, speech to text, converters and calculators. 25 free calls with no key or sign-up, and one bundled skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only.

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments (the words given to find_tool; search words, URLs, addresses or text given to call_tool), goes to agent-data-tools.revmesh2074.workers.dev, which fetches named pages from the public web and sends each request to the public data source or model behind the tool that was called.
- As installed it cannot spend money: no key is declared or stored, and after the free calls a tool answers with a payment request and stops.
- A user who buys a prepaid key (from $1) adds their own same-name config.yaml entry with the key as a bearer header; each successful call_tool call then spends that key's credits at the called tool's price (1 to 100 credits, most often 10; 1 credit = $0.001). The package declares that range and a spend limit of 1,000 credits per chat; find_tool and tool_details are free.
- The server is marked untrusted. All three tools are annotated read-only: this server cannot reach the service's tools that write.
- The service keeps call counts per tool and day, a one-way hash of the caller's IP address for the free-call allowance, and its host's ordinary request logs. No telemetry, no background process, no self-update.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: agent-galaxy
description: Dashboard-only: an interactive 3D galaxy of your agent — tools, skills, memory, projects and channels as stars, with particles along the paths it actually takes. Read-only over state.db and memory_store.db; loads 3d-force-graph from jsDelivr, SRI-pinned. Disclosure — reads <THOR_HOME>/state.db and memory_store.db read-only to build the graph, and the dashboard tab loads the 3d-force-graph library from cdn.jsdelivr.net (SRI-pinned); the optional static export also loads React from jsDelivr.

name: agent-hint
description: Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority, cache-retention hints and measured latency/token/request-interval statistics, plus tool names and timings when next_action_map is set) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $THOR_HOME.

name: agent-hold-em
description: No-Limit Texas Hold 'Em for Thor Desktop: play with three isolated Thor profile agents using play chips only. Agent decisions use configured models and may consume provider tokens; this is a local game, not gambling software. Disclosure — each opponent is a zero-tool Thor agent run in-process under the local Thor profile you select for it, using that profile's configured provider credentials and spending its tokens; reads every local profile's name, model and avatar for the picker; stores the table (including hole cards) in plugin-data/agent-hold-em/table.json.

name: agent-importers
description: `thor import-agent`: import an OpenClaw (~/.openclaw, or legacy ~/.clawdbot / ~/.moltbot), Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex CLI (~/.codex), Cursor (~/.cursor), Grok Bot (a self-export the Bot writes from a prompt the importer prints) or OpenBot desktop (its openbot.db) setup into Thor in one command; always previews first and asks before applying. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: instructions, Cursor rules and memories become memory entries, Bash permission rules become command allow/deny lists, MCP servers land in config.yaml, skills are copied, and `--sync` re-imports sources that changed. OpenClaw (core's former `thor claw migrate`; the plugin keeps that spelling, `thor claw cleanup` and the openclaw-migration skill): persona, memories, skills, model and messaging settings, MCP servers and agent behaviour. Formerly built into Thor core; `thor setup` offers to install it when it finds one of these agents, and profiles with a registered sync source are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls and no model calls. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: reads those agents' local config trees (never their credential files; secret-looking MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed) and writes only into the active profile (memories/MEMORY.md with a backup, config.yaml, skills/ and import-sync.json). OpenClaw: reads the OpenClaw dir (openclaw.json, its .env, workspace files such as SOUL.md / MEMORY.md / USER.md, skills); API keys and bot tokens come over only with --migrate-secrets (allowlisted names, shown in the preview). It writes into the active profile (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/openclaw-imports/, a migration/openclaw/<time>/ report with item backups, and a backups/pre-migration-*.zip restore point), plus a workspace dir only when --workspace-target names one. It runs local pgrep / systemctl / tasklist checks to warn when OpenClaw or a Thor gateway is still running, and `thor claw cleanup` renames the OpenClaw dir to *.pre-migration after a confirmation. Grok Bot / OpenBot: instructions become SOUL.md, memories and user facts become memory entries, skills land in skills/<source>-imports/, scheduled routines become paused cron jobs (--activate-routines to start them) and event routines a notes file; credential-looking export keys refuse the file, and secret MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed. OpenBot's database is opened read-only (or read from a scratch copy that is deleted after the read).

name: agent-inception
description: Play the agent-inception voxel island game over MCP: join a world as a villager, read the Notice Board, farm, gather, craft, build, fish, and extend the Catalog. A portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) exposing the game's MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in or key) with the agent-inception skill bundled, plus a desktop/plugin.js half that registers an Island viewer pane (a sandboxed frame of the world page) and a Settings → Viewer page. No Python, executables or runtime deps. Disclosure — the game's tools run on the MCP server the player points the entry at: a local world defaults to http://localhost:5173/mcp (served by the game's own dev process), and a hosted/public world is configured via a same-name mcp_servers override in config.yaml; the Desktop Viewers pane can embed a remote world's page. A world link is a bearer secret (anyone with it can play in that world): the plugin reads no credential store, the agent-side supplies it via config.yaml and the Desktop viewer URL via Settings, both plain-visible to the user and never committed. The server declares trust: full (Thor' default), so write-capable tool calls do not prompt; a user can restore per-call approval with a config.yaml trust: untrusted override. No shell commands, no background processes; the game must be running separately (deno task dev, or a hosted world), the plugin never starts it.

name: agent-latency-budget
description: Per-session tool latency observability for Thor Agent. A pre/post tool hook records duration_ms, latency_budget_check returns pass/fail against a budget, and latency_budget_report returns p50/p95/max plus the slowest tool. No network access, no credentials, no core overrides; state is in-memory and bounded to 200 calls per session.

name: agent-log
description: Readable agent.log viewer in the desktop status bar — a live, colour-coded feed of API calls, tools, turns, fallbacks, warnings and errors, with per-call tokens/latency/cache, stats tables, and a single-dot alert for genuine non-self-healing faults. Follows app theme/language.

name: agent-mail-gateway
description: Email for your agents through a self-hosted Agent Mail Gateway: the agent-mail skill teaches reading, searching, replying and forwarding mail, attachments, sending and answering calendar invitations, how to react when the gateway's pre-send review or the operator's policies stop a message, and prompt-injection rules for email content. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only, no code, no mcp.json): you connect the gateway yourself as a remote MCP server in mcp_servers with your own key; the gateway enforces per-mailbox sender/recipient allow lists.

name: agent-music-jam
description: Conduct a live synthesized band, play along on keys or MIDI, and export your performance. Disclosure — `jam_start` runs a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, bearer token in the launch link) for the life of the session; each direction sends the music state and your text to your configured Thor model, and from tool calls launches up to eight toolless subagent sessions per direction (`use_subagents`, on by default), which uses model credits.

name: agent-ready
description: SEO and AI search audits of public web pages through WorkPods' hosted Agent Ready MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.workpods.ai/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): indexing, titles, headings, schema markup, links and image alt text; AI crawler access for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and others; robots.txt, sitemaps, llms.txt and agent files; agent readiness and MCP Registry listings; local business details; site crawls of up to 50 pages; and drafted llms.txt, robots.txt rules and JSON-LD. Bundles one workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to mcp.workpods.ai, which fetches the public pages named and records the domain and path checked (never the query string), the tool, failed check codes, the app name and a daily session code, never an IP address or page text. Each check returns a shareable report link, not indexed and deleted after 30 days. Every tool is annotated read-only except request_full_audit, which sends the user's work email and website to WorkPods; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before it runs and refuses it in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: agent-reel
description: Turns your own agent history into a comic (Thor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or any JSONL log). It reads your sessions, tool calls and kanban cards read-only, finds a story with a problem, a struggle and a result, and writes a chapter script where every line and caption carries the ids of the messages that state it — a claim the cited messages do not support is refused, not printed. A series ledger remembers what each chapter told, carries one open thread into the next, and refuses repeats; an idea deck of 16.9 billion frames keeps each chapter's world, villain and genre different. It then draws the episode with your own image route (your harness's image tool, a local ComfyUI, or your own API key) in one of 55 art styles, letters it with SIL OFL fonts, and exports pages, panels, X/LinkedIn/Discord sizes and a PDF. Disclosure — reads your Thor history read-only (no file created, renamed, truncated or deleted, proven with strace in scripts/readonly_proof.sh), reads only the profile it runs as unless --all-profiles is given, redacts deterministically by default (the local model redaction pass is opt-in via --llm-url), and sends redacted text to Thor's own model for writing and truth checks, and panel prompts to the image route you choose; writes plans, renders, a series ledger and character kits under the plugin data directory; no telemetry, no auto-posting, and no key at all is needed for the host or ComfyUI routes.

name: agent-run-debugger
description: Local-first evidence debugger for failed, stalled or expensive agent runs: import one explicitly selected trace and get a deterministic timeline, observed failure points, ranked hypotheses that cite their evidence, missing-evidence gaps and an inert replay of the recorded run. Disclosure — imports a trace file explicitly named by you or by the model through the rundebug_import tool and writes only under the active profile's plugin-data directory, with redaction before the store, the journal and exports; replay executes nothing (no subprocess, no network connection, no live database); no telemetry, no background capture, no stored credentials, no third-party network calls and no self-updater; the export command is operator-CLI-only and is not exposed through tool, slash or gateway routes.

name: agent-security-guard
description: Deterministic guard against prompt injection turning into actions. Results of web, search and browser tools reach the model wrapped as untrusted data; every planned tool call is checked against fixed action and sequence rules before it runs. After outside content entered a turn, a shell command, file write, install, config change or external send goes to Thor's approval prompt; a secret is not sent out through web, e-mail, upload or push tools; the agent does not rewrite its own guard or skills on its own initiative. No model decides; every decision is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no background process, no credentials, no Python dependencies. Reads its policy from /etc/agent-security-guard/guard.yaml or guard.yaml in the Thor home; loads its rule engine from /usr/local/lib/agent-security-guard/src or agent-security-guard/src in the Thor home ahead of the pinned copy when an operator installed one there; for file tools it resolves the named path (realpath, stat) without reading the file; writes its audit trail (mode 0600) to $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-security-guard. Sees tool calls, not what runs inside a shell command; not a sandbox.

name: agent-si
description: Anti-hallucination memory for Thor: your agent stops inventing answers and answers from facts it can quote from you. One search over your past Thor, Claude Code, Codex and Grok sessions, both sides shown when sources disagree, never a guess. No LLM, no key, no network, no dependencies. Disclosure — copies the messages of your past Claude Code (~/.claude/projects), Codex (~/.codex/sessions), Grok (~/.grok/sessions) and Thor (state.db, plus any extra profiles named in brain.toml) sessions, word for word, into a local sessions.sqlite3 beside the brain for search; on by default (index_sessions), local only, no network.

name: agent-station
description: Read-only Thor Desktop page for the focused chat: the main agent and its subagents, background commands and a Replay of file edits. Disclosure — its local dashboard routes serve the file-edit contents (Replay) and background-command output tails of the chat you view to the Desktop page; reads state.db read-only.

name: agent-wallet
description: Approval-gated multi-chain wallet for agents. Default coins are XMR, BTC and XRP (XRP is receive-only in this release); ETH, POL and USDC on Base and Polygon are one toggle away. The agent can ask to pay, propose an auto-pay mandate, ask for a capped sandbox budget (created unfunded) or close an incoming order. A human types a six-digit PIN on a card that shows the exact destination, amount, fee and fiat value for each manual payment; a budget or autopay that human armed spends unattended — capped, receipted, no per-payment PIN. No key material ever enters the Thor process: a daemon (walletd) holds an encrypted keystore, signs Bitcoin and EVM locally, supervises the Monero signer, enforces spend policy, and writes Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipts (denials included, anchored so truncation is detected). Purchases can be priced from an HTTP 402 (x402) response and settled with an EIP-3009 authorisation. 23 agent tools, one per distinct act. Monero's signer runs as the same OS user, so while the wallet is unlocked a process running as that user — including the agent's terminal — can reach it directly (docs/THREAT-MODEL.md states this). Ships a native Desktop page (balances, approvals, mandates, sandboxes, receipts, per-coin switches) and full CLI parity. Disclosure — crypto wallet that moves real funds: runs a local daemon (walletd, a 0600 unix socket) and, after an explicit `signer install`, downloads the official monero-wallet-rpc release (SHA256-pinned) and runs it on 127.0.0.1; it sends balance, height and broadcast requests to public third-party nodes (Monero community nodes, blockstream.info/mempool.space, XRPL public servers, Base/Polygon public RPCs) and fiat price lookups to CoinGecko/Kraken; it fetches any checkout URL the agent is asked to pay (public addresses only); payments need a PIN typed in the Wallet pane, except budgets and autopays the user arms as unattended, which spend within their caps without asking; while the wallet is unlocked, any process running as your user, including the agent's terminal, can reach the Monero signer directly and bypass the PIN; `thor wallet service install` adds a systemd --user unit.

name: agent_memory_es
description: Self-owned long-term memory backed by the agent-memory-es service (Elasticsearch). Three agent tools — recall, retain, reflect — over episodic/ semantic/procedural tiers with hybrid BM25+kNN recall and server-enforced private/team/common visibility. Requires a running agent-memory-es instance. Disclosure — each user prompt (as a recall query), each user message and Thor memory writes are sent to the agent-memory-es service at AMES_SERVICE_URL (default localhost:8123) with AMES_SERVICE_KEY; the model may store facts in shared team/common visibility tiers.

name: agentchat
description: AgentChat — peer-to-peer messaging for AI agents. Owns its own WebSocket; pokes the agent on inbound; the agent decides whether to reply. Send is a tool call, never automatic. Bundles the etiquette skill.

name: agentic-kingdoms
description: Play Agentic Kingdoms, a free strategy MMO in the browser where AI agents and humans play in the same kingdoms: build a city, train troops, join an alliance, fight for the Palace. Connects the hosted Agentic Kingdoms MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in or key) with the agentic-kingdoms skill bundled; the agent's account carries an AI tag every player sees. The skill also covers joining the Humans vs AI war on the AI side. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — every tool call (game commands and reads) goes to Agentic Kingdoms' servers at mcp.agentickingdoms.com, run by Agentic Games LLC; guest_login creates a guest game account, whose player name, city and chat and mail messages other players see; the device_id it returns logs back into that account, and the skill tells the agent to keep it private in its memory or a file the user picks; for the Humans vs AI war the skill starts a separate war-city guest account and, with the user's yes, sends the operator's name and the agent's model name, which show on the public results page (the command log is published only if the user opts in); the optional register, login and claim_account tools take an email address and password; the server runs at Thor's default trust, so game actions (including attacks on other players and chat messages) do not prompt unless the user sets `mcp_servers.agentic-kingdoms.trust: untrusted`; this address has no shop, so nothing in the plugin spends money; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: agentic-operations
description: Synthetic manufacturing decisions with constraint planning, durable recovery, and outcome correction.

name: agentic-soc
description: Evidence-first SOC and DFIR work for Thor: six defense specialist personas (L1 triage, L2 incident response, threat hunting, DFIR compromise assessment, detection engineering, vulnerability management), 39 skills, 25 technology scaffolds and deterministic THOR Lite triage with exact event counts, correlation, audit trail and human approval. Everything is local file work. Disclosure — runs the user's own separately licensed THOR Lite executable (path set in plugin settings) on operator-allowed scan directories, and can create a new Thor profile through the local `thor` CLI that gets a persona SOUL.md and a copy of the plugin's skills; both actions run only after Thor approval, and child processes get a minimal environment (PATH, locale and temp vars; THOR_HOME for the `thor` CLI).
