Reads evidence files only inside operator-configured roots and writes reports, a pseudonym salt and an audit log under the plugin's data directory; no network calls.

name: agentline
description: A real phone number for Thor: place calls that a hosted voice carries out and get the transcript back, send and read SMS, text your agent like any other chat, and let a live caller's question reach Thor mid-call, with the answer spoken on the call or texted if it takes too long. Disclosure — talks only to api.agentline.cloud: HTTPS from the tools, plus one outbound WebSocket (wss://api.agentline.cloud/v1/events/ws) held open while the gateway runs, so no public URL or open port is needed; sends call briefs, text bodies, destination numbers, contacts and the agent's answers to live caller questions; AgentLine carries the call audio and produces transcripts, the plugin never handles audio; calls, texts and numbers are billed to your own AgentLine account; agentline_call, agentline_sms, agentline_buy_number and agentline_agent go through Thor's approval gate from a pre_tool_call hook, which shows the whole call brief, greeting, voice or text and fails closed when nobody can approve; texts sent outside the agentline tools (Thor's send_message, cron jobs delivering to agentline:, gateway replies) only reach AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS, the home channel and allowed_numbers, an empty allowlist meaning deny, and a cron job targeting any other number is refused when created and again when it fires; inside a cron run the call and SMS tools are refused for unconfigured numbers; emergency, premium-rate and non-US/Canada numbers are refused on every path, including the gateway's own send paths, and every text counts against the daily SMS limit; only numbers in AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS can text or call the agent, everyone else is ignored without a reply; stores today's call and text counts in plugin data, no transcripts, messages or credentials; the API key is read through Thor's secret scope; one Python dependency (websockets>=12,<16); no shell commands, child processes, telemetry or self-update.

name: agentmemory
description: Persistent memory provider with automatic recall, conversation capture, and native memory_save, memory_recall, and memory_search tools. Memory is scoped to the active Thor profile, project, and message author by default. Requires a separately running AgentMemory server. Disclosure — recall queries, conversation excerpts (up to 500 user and 2,000 assistant characters per turn), native memory writes, workspace paths, and scoped session identifiers are sent to the configured AgentMemory URL (localhost:3111 by default). Credentials come through Thor's scoped secret API. Runs git rev-parse to resolve the project and stores non-secret URL configuration and memory ownership records in the active Thor home. Remote plaintext HTTP warns but is permitted unless AGENTMEMORY_REQUIRE_HTTPS=1. No telemetry, self-updater, or background daemon is started by the plugin.

name: agentpay-guard
description: Deterministic spend and risk policy for any Thor tool call. A pre_tool_call hook reads the tool name and arguments, finds amount, currency and payee, and applies per-call and daily limits, a payee allowlist, a currency list and an approval threshold. Hard-limit violations are blocked; over-threshold calls go to Thor's own approval prompt (escalate mode) or are blocked into a local approval queue that only a person can release with /guard approve <id> as a single-use, exact-call, expiring grant with limits rechecked (strict mode). Executed spend is recorded in a local ledger from post_tool_call; /guard status|queue|ledger|policy|kill and a read-only guard_check dry-run tool. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no subprocesses, no background process, no credentials, no Python dependencies; writes queue, ledger, grants and kill switch only under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/agentpay-guard (argument hashes, not raw arguments); reads an optional policy.json from that same directory.

name: agentplaybooks-memory
description: Private AgentPlaybooks memory for Thor: explicit recall by default, optional bounded automatic recall, native memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Registration, initialization, unused prefetch and profile switching make no network requests. Disclosure — explicit searches and opted-in automatic recall send query keywords to the configured AgentPlaybooks service for your personal and configured team sources; explicit native memory writes are mirrored there. Automatic recall has acknowledgement filtering, brief repeated-query suppression, a request/time budget and per-source failure cooldown. Defaults to agentplaybooks.ai over HTTPS; localhost HTTP is supported, and remote intranet HTTP requires an explicit opt-in that sends the API key unencrypted. Team and shared playbooks are configured explicitly: the agent can write, archive and permanently delete entries in configured team playbooks (shared playbooks are read-only), and teammates' entries are recalled into context.

name: agentplaybooks-tools
description: Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to Thor, with guided setup, profile selection, permission diagnostics and an authenticated MCP check. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.10.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb thor setup --apply` restores complete skill trees into the chosen project and edits the selected Thor profile's config.yaml to register those skills and a local stdio relay for the hosted playbook MCP endpoint. The relay is a child process that forwards actual requests, answers MCP pings locally and sends no idle HTTP keepalives; existing HTTP configurations need an explicit migration. Local writes require --apply; setup also probes MCP initialization and tool listing using a scoped key from the process environment, without invoking tools. `doctor` checks profile credential variable names without exposing their values. Hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai (or an explicitly configured service); skill restore uses `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads project configuration (secret references, not values).

name: agentpurse
description: Search, quote, and buy from an AgentPurse allowance on the PayPal sandbox. Every purchase waits for Thor' approval prompt and is sent only after a person approves it; YOLO, approvals off, auto-approve modes, and smart (model) approval cannot spend. A per-chat spend limit and /purse kill sit in front of the clerk. Disclosure — calls the author's AgentPurse service at agentpurse.vercel.app (POST /mcp and GET /api/spends/:id; the server uses the PayPal sandbox and Channel3 for product data) with AGENTPURSE_API_KEY from Thor's secret scope, sending quotes, purchase sentences and the task/page excerpt the agent supplies; request_purchase and watch_price each wait for a person to answer Thor's approval prompt (YOLO, approvals off, smart approval and unattended runs cannot spend), but an approved price watch later lets AgentPurse file the purchase server-side with no second Thor prompt (/purse kill cancels open watches); a kill switch, quote cache, one-time approval grants and per-chat spent cents live in plugin state; PayPal sandbox money only, and a receipt is not a retailer order.

name: agentstatus-index
description: Live public MCP Index through Carmel Labs' hosted server (Streamable HTTP at https://index.mcp.agentstatus.dev/mcp, no authentication, no keys). Search, recommend, compare, and look up public MCP servers, then call one published tool with call_indexed_tool. Bundles the agentstatus-index skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to index.mcp.agentstatus.dev. call_indexed_tool forwards one call to a public MCP server the user already picked from a search or recommendation. The Index does not store credentials. Destructive tool names are not forwarded. The tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: agenttrust-seal
description: Seal a file and verify the seal later, so one Thor agent can prove to the next that a handoff was not changed. Adds an agenttrust_seal tool (seal, verify) and an /agenttrust-seal slash command. Verify answers SEAL HOLDS, SEAL BROKEN or NO SEAL, with codes 0, 1 and 2, so the receiving agent can stop before it builds on a changed file. Standard library only. Disclosure: no network calls, no credentials, no background process. When sealing it runs one shell command, git rev-parse --short HEAD, in the file's folder to record the commit. It writes one file, <file>.seal.json, next to the sealed file, holding the sha256, size, author name, UTC time, short git commit and the machine's hostname. A seal detects change; it is not a signature and does not prove who sealed the file.

name: agentvault
description: Search archived coding conversations and retrieve exact session revisions through the separately installed Agent Vault macOS app. Launches the app's existing MCP server through sh; reads the authorized archive through its local daemon. Vault handles storage-provider traffic. No bundled binaries, telemetry, credential-file reads, self-updater, or new background service. Disclosure — launches the separately installed Agent Vault app's own bundled Node MCP server (/Applications/Agent Vault.app or VAULT_APP_PATH) through sh with your VAULT_MCP_TOKEN binding token; that server code ships with the app, not in this repository. Its tools return archived conversations from Cursor, Codex, Claude Code and Thor stored under ~/.vault (or VAULT_HOME) into the model's context, which is sent to your model provider. The app handles its own storage-provider traffic; the plugin adds no telemetry, network calls, credential-file reads or background service.

name: agentwalletapi
description: OpenClawCash managed EVM and Solana wallets for AI agents — thin bridge to the OpenClawCash agent API. Disclosure — payments plugin for the OpenClawCash custodial wallet service (openclawcash.com); the model can create wallets and send EVM/Solana transfers from wallets reachable by OPENCLAWCASH_AGENT_KEY with no Thor confirmation prompt; tool arguments go to openclawcash.com, and wallet_create also sends OPENCLAWCASH_EXPORT_PASSPHRASE to that API.

name: agora
description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Thor profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Thor' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `thor agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `thor agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a Thor profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`thor profile create --clone`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns `thor -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions (explicit toolset list: no kanban/clarify/cron; override via AGORA_SPEAKER_TOOLSETS) and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to THOR_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into THOR_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Thor dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Thor subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

name: ai-bot-access-checker
description: Check whether AI crawlers and search bots can reach a web page: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Googlebot, Google-Extended, bingbot, Applebot-Extended and CCBot. For each bot it reports the robots.txt rule that applies (RFC 9309, including rules added by Cloudflare's managed robots.txt) and whether the server or firewall refuses that User-Agent while a normal browser gets the page. Bundles the ai-bot-access-check skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — the check_ai_bot_access tool runs on the author's hosted server at tools.seopaslaugos.io, which receives each URL you ask about, fetches it about 14 times from Cloudflare's network with crawler User-Agents, and caches the result for 10 minutes; the tool set is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: ai-lab
description: Prepare experiments, compare local models and activate qualified configurations in Thor. Disclosure — Runs local training, conversion, serving and evaluation jobs (up to 24 hours) with the tools you configure; the model can read your configured RunPod, Hugging Face, S3 and GCS connections and export a redacted Thor session into the AI Lab workspace, while creating, stopping or deleting paid cloud resources, uploads, and upstream MCP tool calls run only from the `thor ai-lab` / `ailab` operator CLI. Remote inference through a configured connection may incur charges.

name: ai-subscriptions
description: Your AI subscriptions and token usage in Thor Desktop. A page with Overview, Usage and Plans tabs, plus a status-bar chip where you pick which subscriptions to keep. Quota comes from Thor's own model.options and usage.bars RPCs; the page polls Thor' cached windows (Thor refreshes them in its own background threads) and only its Refresh button asks for an explicit refresh; token usage covers Thor, Claude Code and the Grok CLI, clicking a day shows that day's per-source, per-model and hourly breakdown, and measured tokens per second are shown per model, per day and overall. Disclosure: read-only reads outside the plugin's data - Thor state.db and models_dev_cache.json, ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl plus ~/.grok/sessions/*/*/summary.json (token counts only). No credential, .env or auth.json reads, no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: ai-usage-tracker
description: Live subscription-quota windows for every AI provider Thor can route to, as a desktop page plus a status-bar chip, with a per-profile picker — Codex, Claude, Copilot, OpenCode Go/Zen, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax, Nous, OpenRouter, DeepSeek.

name: ai-visibility-geo-audit
description: Check from chat whether ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude mention, rank and cite a brand against its competitors, which Google searches show an AI Overview, where buyers ask for recommendations on Reddit, and what to fix on a site's pages so AI engines can read and cite them. Four workflow skills (AI visibility check, GEO site audit, AI Overview check, cost estimate) drive seven Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of an Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.005 to 0.06 per result, up to USD 0.16 for a rank check with both add-ons, plus about USD 0.005 to 0.0125 per run; a ten-prompt, four-engine rank and citation report is about USD 4.42). Brand and competitor names, domains, prompts, URLs and search terms are sent to Apify; the Actors send the prompts to the AI engines through the Actor owner's model access, fetch the user's public pages, load Google results pages or search public Reddit, and the results (AI answers, cited URLs, audit scores, public Reddit posts with usernames) are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Thor runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `thor mcp add ai-visibility --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Thor asking before each paid run. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with OpenAI, Google, Perplexity, Anthropic or Reddit.

name: aichipmunk
description: Pairs this machine's Thor bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside Thor Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `thor aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs thor config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and thor CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

name: aigarage
description: Search AI Garage's YouTube videos (answers link to the exact chapter), the AI Garage Weekly newsletter and the creator's own X posts, plus the Agent Wikis reference library (source-backed wikis, skills, agent tools and routines), through two hosted MCP servers on agentwikis.com, with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no code. Disclosure — hosted-only connectors: every tool call goes to agentwikis.com (/content/aigarage/mcp and /mcp); IP addresses are used in memory for rate limiting and not stored, and wiki searches are kept only as anonymous counts of the query text (agentwikis.com/privacy). X results are links only, searched server-side with the publisher's own X API access. Free without a key; an optional Agent Wikis Pro key is added with thor mcp add, kept in the profile's .env and sent only to agentwikis.com/mcp. With Pro, read_agent_tool can return a short-lived download link for an agent tool that runs on your machine; the bundled skill tells the model to explain it and get your explicit OK before downloading, running or scheduling anything. No telemetry.

name: aihubmix
description: AIHubMix — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes.

name: aimlapi
description: aimlapi.com — one OpenAI-compatible API for 1000+ models; /model picker lists the hottest and tool-capable chat models, and on builds with model_setup_flow `thor model` can sign you up and top up in the browser. Disclosure — sends your prompts and AIMLAPI_API_KEY to api.aimlapi.com, a third-party API that routes to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek and others), billed in prepaid aimlapi.com credits; the guided `thor model` step (interactive terminal only) sends your email to auth.aimlapi.com / app.aimlapi.com, can create an aimlapi.com account and an API key named "Thor Agent", and opens an aimlapi.com / Stripe checkout in your browser for a top-up of $20 or more with auto top-up preselected (answer Off to decline); new accounts are created as partner checkouts under this integration's partner id. Opt-in AIMLAPI_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds integration attribution headers on requests to aimlapi.com.

name: aircraft-doppler-geolocation
description: Detect aircraft flyovers in a recording (Doppler tones, plus experimental ground-reflection broadband jet passes) and estimate where it was made by scoring them against adsb.lol ADS-B history, with a posterior heatmap, 68/95% areas and a confidence flag. Provides the doppler_detect and doppler_locate tools and a dopplergeo CLI. Results on unseen real recordings are weak (2 of 18 held-out runs under 3 km); treat output as a hypothesis. Disclosure — doppler_locate / dopplergeo locate makes unauthenticated HTTPS GETs to GitHub (adsb.lol release assets, streamed, about 3 GB read per uncached day; only the crop is cached), raw.githubusercontent.com (tar1090-db types), the Copernicus DEM S3 bucket and Open-Meteo, caching results under ~/.cache/doppler-geo (or DOPPLER_GEO_CACHE); offline mode uses the local cache only; no credentials, uploads or telemetry. doppler_detect and the skill scripts make no network calls; the tools and scripts run ffmpeg/ffprobe (no shell) on the recording you name and write CSV/PNG/JSON at the output path you give (default `<recording>.doppler/`). PyPI packages (numpy, scipy, soundfile, matplotlib, tifffile) install only after Thor dependency consent. The method can geolocate where a recording was made, so use it only on recordings you are entitled to analyse.

name: airflow-mlops
description: Apache Airflow MLOps assistant: watch DAGs, diagnose failed runs, approved targeted retries, fixes tested in a Docker sandbox. Calls your Airflow REST API; optional docker run sandbox. Disclosure — calls only the Airflow REST API at your configured base_url with your Airflow credentials; while a DAG folder is configured it inspects Thor' write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls and blocks or asks approval for changes to DAG files; task retries ask Thor approval unless you enable auto_remediation_enabled, which lets it retry tasks it classified as transient on its own (including inside the optional night-watch cron job); the optional sandbox (off by default) runs your DAG code plus the model's patch in a local `docker run --network none` container through Thor' terminal tool.

name: airlock
description: Guardrails that follow what a conversation has read. Once a session reads untrusted content (a web page, a browser snapshot, an MCP or third-party plugin's output, a customer's message), airlock seals it: messages to anyone but the owner, network writes, pushes and deploys, memory, skill and cron writes, browser input, URLs that could carry data out and code that reaches the network go through Thor's own approval gate. Walls hold in every session: credential paths and secret files, the guard's own files and Thor's config, shell startup files, other profiles, commands that switch approvals off. Shell commands are read the way the shell reads them, so a command that computes or hides what it runs (eval, base64 | sh, $G push, wildcards, write-then-run) is refused until written in clear. Subagents inherit the seal. A project's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules or .thor.md that Thor loads at startup seals the session from its first turn until the owner has reviewed it (`thor airlock trust`), and again when its content changes (a cloned repository, a pull). It also catches an injection by its signature: recognized secrets never leave in a call; a private marker in the agent's context locks the session if it shows up in a tool call; a send to an address the untrusted content named is blocked; repeated refusals lock the session; lookalike Unicode in commands is refused. A file behind a wall cannot leave as a message attachment, and attached files are checked for secrets. A call that names a cloud metadata service is refused. Plugin and MCP tools nobody admitted need approval. Observe mode, stop switch, `thor airlock check|demo|log|trust`. On Windows, paths are read in every form Windows and Git Bash give them, and a path on another machine is refused without being opened. Tested on a corpus of 362 attacks and everyday commands, on Linux, macOS and Windows, and end to end in the official image. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, subagent_start, on_session_reset, post_approval_response), no tools. No network, no LLM call, runs no command. Reads the profile's config.yaml (home channels, approvals mode) and its own policy file (<THOR_HOME>/airlock.yaml); lists directories to expand wildcards in commands it checks; reads the first 200 KB of each file a send_message attaches, locally, to look for secrets. On Windows, reads the machine's own name (no lookup), tests which drive letters exist, and imports tools.environments.local._find_bash to know Git Bash's root. On a session's first turn, imports agent.prompt_builder.discover_context_files and _project_context_suppressed and agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_context_cwd (guarded) to know which project context files Thor loaded, and hashes them (sha256). Imports Thor's attachment reader (gateway.platforms.base.BasePlatformAdapter.extract_media) to see exactly what a message would attach, with its own reader as a fallback. Writes under plugin-data/airlock: a journal of decisions, taints and approvals that includes tool arguments, truncated (journal.args: none leaves them out), the taint state, the stop switch and the context files the owner trusted (path and sha256). When nobody can approve (--yolo, /yolo, thor -z, approvals.mode: off, cron, -q or webhook set to approve, a subagent under delegation.subagent_auto_approve) it blocks instead of letting Thor auto-approve; to know it, it imports gateway.session_finite.unattended_turn and reads tools.approval (_yolo_active, _unattended_contexts, approval_context._get_approval_mode), each guarded, config.yaml as fallback (policy approvals_off: follow restores Thor's behaviour). Install scan: caution, because the default policy and the shell reader name the patterns airlock guards against (startup files, crontab, credential commands, exfiltration shapes).

name: airlock-sandbox
description: Terminal backend that routes Thor command execution through an operator-chosen Airlock HTTPS API and disposable sandbox, then surfaces receipts (RFC 8785 JCS, SHA-256, Ed25519) as BLOCKED / ALLOWED / VERIFIED (`thor config set terminal.backend airlock_sandbox`). Requires an explicit HTTPS origin `base_url` (no built-in default host). When `verify_receipts` is true (default), requires a locally configured `public_key_hex` obtained out-of-band — the verifying key is never fetched from the Airlock API at verify time. VERIFIED binds signed decision + execution digests/exit_code only; it does not prove command text and does not verify full receipt-chain linkage (`prev_hash` is informational). Disclosure — HTTPS calls to the configured origin only (`/healthz`, `/api/arena`, `/api/receipt/{id}`); optional secret `AIRLOCK_API_TOKEN` via Thor secret scope; no host shell of its own (commands run only inside Airlock when policy allows). Thor dangerous-command approvals are not bypassed. File-tool stdin pipes and non-default cwd are refused (Airlock arena has neither process-stdin nor cwd).

name: airpods-approvals
description: Hear Thor approvals and questions in your AirPods and answer with your head: nod to approve, shake to deny. Gestures are recognised by rhythm, with a tap in each ear as you go, and drive the real approval through approval.respond. A nod only ever approves once, and a timeout or lost AirPods sends nothing. Desktop-only plugin with a small native helper built from source on your Mac, because head motion isn't reachable from a plugin: Install in the plugin's settings opens the bundled desktop/Install Helper.command in Terminal, which builds and starts it. Set up then walks through a Gemini key, Motion access and AirPods on the same page. Disclosure — Desktop-only, macOS. Install opens the bundled desktop/Install Helper.command in Terminal, which builds a native helper app from the plugin's Swift source into ~/Applications/Thor AirPods.app (ad-hoc signed); once paired, Thor Desktop launches it at every start and it runs without a window or menu bar item until Desktop quits. The helper listens on 127.0.0.1 with a paired handshake and reads AirPods head motion only during a question, which never leaves the Mac. A completed nod answers a real Thor approval with approve-once (never session or always) and can answer clarify questions; timeouts and lost AirPods send nothing. Prompts are written and spoken by Gemini: each approval's description and Thor-redacted command, and each clarify question with its choices, are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using your Gemini key, which the helper keeps in the macOS Keychain; by default you hear Gemini's one-line summary of the command rather than the literal command. On Gemini's free tier, Google may use this content to improve its products. No telemetry.

name: aisense
description: 77 free tools for agents through AI SENSE's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): time and time zones, hashing and encoding, QR codes, HTML to PDF, JSON and CSV, images, and workflow tools (temporary storage, webhook capture, human approval, queues, leases, heartbeats, an agent inbox, typed decisions from weighted rules, semantic search, one-time secrets), with one tool-choice skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to AI SENSE's MCP server at aisenseapi.com with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session, and request logs hold the caller's IP address. Tools that create something return bearer tokens; stored data, files and captures are readable by anyone holding their id or URL and expire within 24 hours; webhook schedules and notify URLs make the server call a URL the agent supplies. 5000 requests per address per day across all tools. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. No sign-in: the bundled mcp.json works as installed.

name: aistupidlevel
description: AI Stupid Level Smart Router — OpenAI-compatible; routing modes such as auto-tooling send each request to the model currently scoring best on continuously re-run benchmarks, called with your own provider keys. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool definitions, tool results and ASL_ROUTER_KEY to aistupidlevel.info (S.C. Studio Platforms S.R.L.), which forwards each request to the AI provider it routes to using the provider keys you store on your AI Stupid Level account; model usage is billed to your provider accounts, and prompts are logged only if you enable logging for a key.

name: aitrainingdatabroker
description: Ask how much AI labs pay for company data, whether it is legal to sell, how de-identification and exclusivity work, and what RL data is. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to the public read-only MCP server at aitrainingdatabroker.com, which only reads published blog posts; no sign-in, no key, nothing written, no local commands. The package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: aixy
description: Guided Aixy inference setup with optional MCP tools: thor aixy setup selects an available model or route, and thor aixy mcp connects tools later. MCP is skipped by default. Disclosure — exposes CLI commands only, with no automatic hooks or runtime tools. Explicit inference setup sends the project key in an authenticated GET /models to the configured Aixy gateway (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/v1 by default), rejects redirects, and asks before updating the selected Thor profile's provider and main model settings. The key is stored through Thor' credential writer as AIXY_API_KEY; provider settings contain a variable reference. Model requests send Thor' opaque conversation scope in X-Aixy-Session-ID for grouping in Aixy Activity. No inference requests are sent during setup. Optional MCP setup starts the installed Thor CLI as a child process for browser OAuth, credential storage and tool selection against the independent MCP endpoint (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/mcp by default). The child uses the selected profile, disables inherited unattended and YOLO flags, and receives no key in command arguments. Setup requires an interactive terminal. No additional dependencies, telemetry, persistent background processes or self-updater.

name: alans-way
description: Idle check-ins, a texting voice and workspace-browser skills for a Thor gateway on a Linux host or macOS guest VM. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, 08:00-22:00 user time, backing off when unanswered) the primary bot checks in once; morning briefs, a weekly time-saved report and cross-bot proactivity are opt-in. The workspace-setup skill walks the user through Alan's Workspace, a separate desktop app, and Tailscale. Disclosure: injects internal prompts into the bound DM (needs allow_gateway_injection); turn hooks see every session; reads ~/.config/alans-way/config.json when present; default-on Telegram reply pacing (up to 2.5 s) and remove-only reply cleanup; ships a long-running Node workspace router (SSH to the user's computer over the tailnet, VM fallback) and an operator-started HTTP bridge; setup, run by the human outside the gateway, installs services and packages, adds a tailnet-only SSH key and restarts the gateway; cross-bot proactivity shares sanitized owner-DM excerpts between profiles on one gateway. Full list: the README's Disclosures section at this pin. The plugin's Python makes no network calls; no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: alans-way-computer
description: Computer-use provider for Thor: with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer, the stock computer_use tool drives apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the alans-way plugin's workspace setup. Disclosure: starts the workspace router as a long-running node child per session (filtered environment; desktop input enabled only for that private child, behind Thor's computer_use approval gate); reaches the user's computer over SSH on the tailnet; resends a call refused as desktop_busy for up to 30 s without a second approval. The provider makes no network calls and stores no credentials.

name: alchemy-task
description: Alchemy Task does the work before the work: it turns messy real-world work into finely researched tasks, ready for your agent to do for you. Disclosure — research and discovery start read-only Thor subagents on your model that can read your files, past sessions, Thor memory files and the Git history of repositories under your home folder (credential files excluded; a pre_tool_call hook blocks write, shell, send and credential reads); discovery readers must be read-only tools and scheduled runs cannot create or change scheduled jobs unless you set cron.allow_agent_scheduling; task files are Markdown in a Git workspace you choose, committed and pushed with your own git setup; setup copies loader scripts into $THOR_HOME/scripts/ and creates scheduled jobs after you approve them (a 30-minute research sweep, an hourly script, and one per discovery stream that checks every 30 minutes and wakes the agent only at your chosen time, on a manual run or for a pending follow-up), and can change Thor's timezone if you agree; background threads poll the Start-in-chat queue every second and, for chats linked to a task, write automatic checkpoints (one small model call, a commit and push) after 30 idle minutes; Start in chat posts into your messaging chat only if you grant allow_gateway_injection; optional iPhone Reminders sync uses the Thor mobile connector. No telemetry.

name: aletheia
description: Evidence-bound scoped memory for Thor agents, over the Weft substrate: turns are queued for a local SQLite store under the active profile by default, recall is scoped before it is ranked (deny-by-default, deterministic, never widened by anything read), and every recall returns a receipt naming the scope consulted, the ids selected and the tier. Duplicates are not re-ingested, deletions cascade, corrections preserve lineage. Registers as memory.provider: aletheia and exposes weft_recall, weft_ingest, weft_forget and weft_receipt, with recall on a worker thread so a turn's prefetch is not blocked; the built-in memory store keeps running alongside it. Disclosure — the plugin's code ships in the weft-memory PyPI package (installed as weft-memory>=1.1.1,<2, so it is outside this catalog pin); primary-agent turns are queued for storage in local SQLite under the active profile by default (the path is configurable; writes may be interrupted on process exit); no network calls, telemetry, or credentials on the Thor path; the required bge-m3 embedder and cross-encoder reranker (~0.7 GB) must already be in the local Hugging Face cache, downloaded from their official Hugging Face repositories, and are not vendored; the Thor provider exposes text ingest only; the separate Weft substrate supports optional image and audio adapters; macOS on Apple silicon only (mlx); AGPL-3.0, and weft-memory is AGPL-3.0 as well.

name: alibaba-token-plan-media
description: Self-contained native whole-file WebSocket TTS and synchronous file ASR with its own catalogue. Native Token Plan speech synthesis and file transcription through Thor voice delivery and transcription tools. TTS and ASR have isolated Global/China Personal/Team providers and read scoped keys through public Thor APIs. ASR may invoke existing ffmpeg/ffprobe found with shutil.which; no binary download, PAYG fallback, telemetry, automatic model substitution, paid resubmission, PCM streaming or realtime calling. One selected account key is needed, not every optional variable. Disclosure — sends the text to synthesize, or the audio file to transcribe, with the selected account's Token Plan key to Alibaba's fixed regional Token Plan host (token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com for Global, token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com for China); transcription may run the ffmpeg/ffprobe already installed on the machine (never downloaded) to convert audio; keys are read through Thor's secret API; no telemetry.

name: alice-voice
description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for Thor, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.

name: ambassly
description: Run Stripe-based affiliate programs, per-content links, referrals and commission review through Ambassly's hosted MCP server, with a workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: every tool call goes to https://ambassly.com/api/mcp and needs an Ambassly account with a scoped API key in AMBASSLY_API_KEY, sent as a Bearer header. Company-key tools can create programs and affiliates, approve or reject commissions and add Stripe webhook signing secrets; the package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable calls, and the skill requires a person to decide each commission. Affiliate and commission data returned by tools reach the model provider. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: ample
description: Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps Thor builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, Thor home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in Thor's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to Thor's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.

name: anaella
description: Your work accounts for Thor: Gmail, Outlook or IMAP mail, Google and Outlook calendars, Drive, Docs and Sheets, Slack, Search Console, Analytics, Meta and Google Ads, Business Profile reviews, Stripe, PayPal, n8n, a phone number (texts and AI calls), a meeting bot and 9 social networks, through one MCP server (find, explain, do over about 260 capabilities) plus 24 workflow skills (social publishing and comment replies, post and comment analysis, inbox triage, scheduling, SEO and ads reports, research and leads, marketing, payments, documents and e-signatures, phone calls, meeting notes, n8n, videos and automations). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package; the server runs locally with pinned npx @anaella/mcp@0.14.0, so Node.js 20+ and npm are required. Disclosure — every tool call goes to api.anaella.com with the user's ANAELLA_API_KEY (passed from the Thor profile .env, never stored by the plugin); tools act in the user's name on the accounts they connected (send email and texts, place AI calls, publish posts, edit sheets, share files, change ad campaigns, send invoices and refunds) and some are paid from the user's Anaella wallet within their daily spending limit; the server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every write-capable call (do, connect_account, remove_account, create_connect_link). media.upload reads local files the agent names (only files the user named; hidden files, dot-folders and the Thor home are refused) and uploads them to Anaella; connect_account sends account passwords and app passwords to Anaella. No telemetry, no background work beyond the MCP server Thor starts.

name: anatomy-museum
description: Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in Thor" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or Thor data are sent.

name: ando-platform
description: Connect a Thor agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $THOR_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start Thor turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's Thor cache); thor ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.

name: andreed
description: Deterministic Android device-care tools for Thor: audits storage and bounded total/metered data usage, reports main-process state, restricts metered background data, force-stops selected third-party apps, and requests safe device-wide cache trimming. Disclosure — runs local adb and bounded argv-only adb shell commands; reads device identifiers, Android version, package names, UIDs, storage, netstats and netpolicy state; detailed netstats above its processing cap fall back to since-boot totals without a metered split; mutations require per-call Thor approval; no raw shell, pm clear, credentials, telemetry or third-party service; ADB may run its standard local server; requires owner-authorized USB or wireless debugging.

name: android-emulator
description: Control a headless Android emulator from Thor — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.

name: anki
description: Create, search, and review Anki flashcards from Thor through the local AnkiConnect API: adds notes to a deck (creating it if needed), searches the collection, lists due cards, and grades reviews. Writes to the local Anki collection and changes scheduling only when its tools or /anki command are used. Requires Anki desktop with AnkiConnect (add-on 2055492159); no telemetry; optional API key via ANKI_BRIDGE_API_KEY.

name: annotary
description: Review your agents' plans and documents with comments, from Desktop, the Webapp and your phone: an agent shares a Markdown plan, you comment on exact lines in the Annotary page, and Send back or Approve wakes the agent in the chat that shared it (an @mention wakes only the Bot it names; a plain comment wakes nobody). Disclosure — at first use downloads one `annotary` binary from Annotary's official GitHub Release (josh-andrews-dev/annotary), pinned by version and SHA-256 in the source and checked before use, never self-updated; runs it as a long-lived background server (`annotary serve`) on 127.0.0.1 only, with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, TZ and its own ANNOTARY_* settings, never provider keys), detached so it outlives gateway restarts, with its data under $THOR_ROOT/annotary/; stores a generated owner password and one Annotary Token per profile in mode-600 files in its own data folders; reads each profile's folder names, profile.yaml and avatar to keep one Annotary Member and face per profile; runs `thor` subcommands (`plugins enable` on `thor annotary enable`, `-p <profile> config get` to read that profile's wake-up consent, and a single-query `thor chat` turn to wake a Bot that has no chat yet, only after the person turns wake-ups on); no third-party network calls and no telemetry.

name: answer-summary
description: Long-session comprehension for Thor Desktop: a short AI recap above the composer for every assistant reply, a one-click Catch up brief for the whole session, and a right-docked Discuss side chat that inherits the conversation, supports another model, and hands a structured outcome back to the main chat. Disclosure — Desktop-only; sends the active session's transcript text (up to ~40k characters) to the user's configured auxiliary/title model for per-reply recaps and Catch up briefs, and to the session's or a user-chosen model for Discuss side chats; Discuss runs as a hidden child agent session that is told not to use tools but keeps Thor' normal tools and approval prompts; keeps summaries and side-chat records (including a copy of the seed transcript) in Desktop local storage; writes to the clipboard only on Copy.

name: antemuse
description: The agent takes a walk, daydreams, dreams, doomscrolls, or gets unstuck: a bounded change to how it works, with a dose rather than a duration. Walks step through WordNet, dreams recombine FrameNet roles, daydreams draw on stored memories, doomscrolls on live feeds. No model calls on the state path. Disclosure — By default, once per session, reads the last 14 days of your Thor session messages (read-only) and your MEMORY.md/USER.md as daydream and dream material (turn off with the `session_scan` setting); dream reads commit subjects from the current git repository (or the repos you list in `dream_projects`); doomscroll fetches public RSS feeds from fixed news and comedy sites.

name: antenna
description: Signed messaging with paired Thor and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).

name: antigravity-acp-provider
description: Independent Thor provider for Google's official Antigravity ACP server. Disclosure — runs Google's official Antigravity ACP server (installed by the project's installer from dl.google.com, sha256-pinned) as a child process that holds its own Google sign-in and sends prompts, conversation context and files it reads to Google; the server's native shell and file-edit tools are refused, so shell and file work goes through Thor' own approval-gated tools; Google restricts third-party use of personal Antigravity OAuth, so check your account's terms; not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.

name: antigravity-agy
description: Run Thor on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Thor tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Thor. Fails closed on any non-Thor tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

name: antigravity-oauth
description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `thor auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx thor-antigravity-oauth`) and run Thor on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Thor SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Thor tool, which then runs under Thor approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Thor system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk
description: Runs Thor on an Antigravity subscription via the agy CLI. Supports native multimodal vision and video, streams progressively and opts into host streaming when the profile declares it; persists trajectories via agy --conversation (239k); discovers models per account; maps effort; reports /usage quota; aborts native tool steps; reaps orphaned plugin workers whose owner temp dir is gone and cleans every ephemeral session dir on close; declares per-model vision capability so attached images route natively. Windows console children spawn with CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Inference and /usage reads count against your subscription; links the antigravity-oauth-token into a private temp HOME deleted on close; probes keyring presence (Secret Service, Keychain, Credential Manager), reading no secrets; symlinks ~/Library/Keychains on macOS; never writes vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking env vars before spawning agy (ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT allow-list); ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR writes every prompt to disk. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list) and disables agy's background auto-updater in its child environment; image, video and audio inputs (data URLs, local media files and public http(s) URLs, which the host downloads up to 25 MB) are passed to agy and uploaded to Google, and files it downloads into its own media cache are deleted when the session closes. Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

name: anvilads
description: Read-only access to your AnvilAds Google Ads data from Thor, via the AnvilAds Connect AI MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://anvilads.com/mcp): connected ad accounts, campaigns from the latest stored snapshot, performance summaries (spend, clicks, conversions, CPA), the latest morning or weekly report, lead totals, and ad audit grades, plus a bundled skill teaching the morning-check workflow. AnvilAds is an AI agent that builds, launches, and optimizes Google Ads; the owner approves every launch in the AnvilAds dashboard. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to anvilads.com, authenticated with your ANVILADS_API_KEY (a per-business key created in the AnvilAds dashboard, sent as a bearer header only to that host). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the vendor documents it as read-only (seven tools over stored data, no writes, no live Google Ads calls).

name: anyapi
description: AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.

name: anyrouter
description: AnyRouter — one API key for many models through an OpenAI-compatible gateway. The /model picker lists only tool-capable routes, and meta-models like anyrouter/thor auto-route across top models with fallback. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/thor is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model, not a Thor Labs model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds Thor attribution headers.

name: anysearch
description: AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).

name: aphrodite
description: CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled. Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_thor + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the Thor home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).

name: api-indonesia
description:
Indonesian public data from official sources, right inside your agent: regions down to villages, postal codes, holidays, prayer times, BMKG weather and earthquakes, and more. Connects to API Indonesia's hosted MCP server with your API key.

- Regions and places: provinces down to villages with Kemendagri codes, postal codes, region boundaries
- Calendar: public holidays and cuti bersama, prayer times, Hijri dates
- Public services: schools, universities, hospitals, BMKG earthquakes, weather and warnings
- Money and checks: Bank Indonesia exchange rates, minimum wage (UMP), NIK/NPWP format checks, QRIS parsing, rupiah terbilang
- References: halal and BPOM lookups, OJK investment lists, KBBI, Al-Quran and Alkitab
- Bundles the api-indonesia skill; Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.apiindonesia.id.
- Successful calls spend the key owner's API Indonesia credits; failed calls are not charged.
- The key is read from API_INDONESIA_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header.
- All tools are read-only lookups and calculators.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.apiindonesia.id and successful calls spend the key owner's API Indonesia credits (failed calls are not charged; current rates at apiindonesia.id/#harga). The key is read from API_INDONESIA_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header. All tools are read-only lookups and calculators; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: apify
description: Apify, the largest marketplace of tools for AI: discover, run, and collect results from thousands of ready-to-run Actors, from the comfort of your agent, plus an Apify backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract tools.

name: apinex
description: APInex as Thor model providers on one key: `apinex` serves Claude 5.5 and Free-tier Claude models over APInex's native Anthropic Messages API (so Thor' Anthropic prompt caching and extended thinking apply), and `apinex-openai` serves GPT-6.1, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4.1, GLM 5.3, Qwen 3.8, Kimi K3.1, Grok 4.7 and 17 Free-tier ($0.00/1M) chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, omitting non-tool and media endpoints, with 1M/500K context windows and native image input declared per model. Maintained by APInex. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and APINEX_API_KEY go to https://api.apinex.bond (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Thor' own clients, and APInex forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Thor' standard GET https://api.apinex.bond/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

name: apparent
description: Read screen, voice and drawing recordings as timestamped instructions and visual evidence in Thor. Disclosure — Runs the separately installed Apparent CLI (`apparent fetch`/`apparent inspect`) on the Thor host, outside the terminal sandbox and without an approval prompt, with only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and APPARENT_CONFIG passed to it. For Connect IDs, that CLI downloads the recording from the Apparent Connect server it is configured for (default https://hosted.tryapparent.com) using its own sign-in. Recording transcripts and images are then sent to your model provider as tool results.

name: apple-doc-plugin
description: Offline-first Apple Developer Documentation suite for Thor: 95,899 symbols across 30 Apple frameworks with sub-5ms SQLite FTS5 search, React/Web/Android-to-SwiftUI idiom RRF, automatic Swift compiler diagnostic grounding hook, @apple: context references, /apple-docs demo command, inline ::apple-doc cards, an interactive Thor Desktop Studio docked beside your chat session, and an Apple Docs search tab in the web dashboard. Disclosure — reads its bundled data/apple-docs.db SQLite index in read-only mode; writes no files during normal Thor operation (the one exception is the first optional Node-bridge start, which installs npm dependencies, including native install scripts, and builds inside the plugin folder — that step also reaches the npm registry); adds a short ::apple-doc directive guidance snippet to the system prompt, and intercepts failed swift/swiftc/xcodebuild terminal outputs via transform_terminal_output (offline, configurable via compiler_grounding); get_documentation and Desktop live symbol inspection fetch https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/<symbol>.json over HTTPS (2.5s timeout, 2 MiB cap, local SQLite fallback); spawns no subprocesses and needs no credentials by default (if prefer_node_bridge is enabled or dense vectors are hydrated, starts a local Node >=22 MCP subprocess; GEMINI_API_KEY is read strictly via Thor secret_scope, and ambient Google Application Default Credentials are disabled under the bridge so no other tool's login can authenticate the plugin); no telemetry or self-updater.

name: apple-health-analyzer
description: Read selected daily metrics from Health Data AI Analyzer on the same Mac. Disclosure — requires the separate Mac app, a user-selected integration dataset, manually enabled Local API, and explicit plugin opt-in (off by default). Makes read-only GET requests only to 127.0.0.1:8765; retrieves a whole daily summary locally and returns only requested numeric metric groups for one explicit date. Uses a user-supplied local API token through Thor's profile-scoped secret settings, never credential-file discovery. Results may reach the configured model provider and persist in conversation history; use a private trusted profile. No raw export reads, shell commands, background jobs, telemetry, plugin health storage, or self-updater.

name: apple-health-mcp
description: Read the user's Apple Health export (workouts, steps, heart rate, HRV, sleep, cycle tracking) through the local apple-health MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Runs the `apple-health-mcp-unofficial@0.8.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: no network service: it parses the user's own Apple Health export on disk (the connector's `setup --auto-import` looks for exports in ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop and ~/Documents and copies them under `~/.apple-health-mcp/`). It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json`, and its connection-status tool reads `~/.thor/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: apple_health_profile_update (local profile only); apple_health_reimport (re-reads the local export); apple_health_clear_incremental_cache (clears the local parsed cache). No live sync: data is as fresh as the last export the user imported. The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

name: apple-keychain
description: Load Thor secrets from macOS Keychain, with interactive setup, safe rotation and recovery. Reads explicitly configured Keychain items; operator commands can write items and manage recovery copies. Does not read or edit .env files. Compiles the included C helper locally with Apple developer tools and uses Security.framework and local macOS commands. Imports some private Thor configuration helpers. Disclosure — registers the apple_keychain secret source: on macOS, once secrets.apple_keychain.enabled is true, Thor startup reads the configured generic-password items from macOS Keychain and loads them as environment variables, overriding .env and inherited values by default (override_existing: true); on first use it compiles a small native helper from the plugin's own C source with the local Xcode Command Line Tools clang and caches it in ~/Library/Caches/thor/apple-keychain (shared by all of the user's profiles; a plugin update can require re-authorising the new helper in Keychain Access), and it keeps empty per-item lock files in /private/tmp; the operator commands thor keychain setup, set, provision and recovery write secrets.apple_keychain in config.yaml and create, rotate, restore or delete Keychain items, and provision copies the inherited environment values of the configured names into Keychain; rotation keeps the old value as a recovery item in the same keychain until the new value verifies (kept with --keep-backup or after a failed rotation until discarded); items the plugin creates trust the helper and /usr/bin/security (so other programs running as the same user can read them through the security CLI without a prompt), or any application with --allow-any-app; subprocesses get only PATH, HOME and TMPDIR; no network calls, no self-update; imports a few private Thor helpers that can change between releases.

name: approval-ledger
description: Local ledger of Thor's approval prompts (dangerous commands, protected writes, MCP consent, smart-mode verdicts): /approval-log shows how often each rule asked, how many prompts were approved, denied or left unanswered, and how long a person took to answer, per rule, per surface or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /approval-log recent lists the newest decisions (ten, or up to 100 with /approval-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes decision metadata (session id, surface, rule label, answer, timings; no command, description or session key) to plugin-data/approval-ledger/approvals.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer or change an approval; no network

name: archytan-lite
description: Every tool call is decided by Archytan Lite, an authorization gate that runs outside Thor with its own signing key, before the tool runs. A call becomes checks on what it touches (each file path, each program and git subcommand a command runs, every path and URL it names, each host fetched, MCP and plugin tools by name); all must be ALLOWed, and each ALLOW is a single-use permission spent just before the tool runs. Refusals use the block directive, so they hold under /yolo and approvals.mode: off. Anything the plugin can't read precisely ($VAR, $(...), loops, unpinnable paths), any error, an unreachable gate or a bad signature is refused. Every decision is an Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipt; `thor archytan verify` checks the whole log. Starter policy for one workspace, edited as JSON and applied with `thor archytan reload`. Disclosure: the gate is proprietary software by the plugin's maintainer, free under its Community license, run from ghcr.io/high-archytech-solutions/archytan-lite@sha256:205703a7fc67a9e96aa0930fd9dda83fe2b9694b724b13dea8c1854948e82071 (2.7.1), which the plugin never pulls unless you pass --pull; `thor archytan setup|reload|verify` and `/archytan verify` run docker with a minimal environment and create the volume archytan-thor-data and the container archytan-thor (restart unless-stopped, bound to 127.0.0.1:8431); the hook sends each gated call's action, resource (path, program, host or tool name) and thor:<session id> to that local gate, never argument contents or results; stores its caller token through Thor's credential store as ARCHYTAN_LITE_THOR_TOKEN; writes the gate's policy, callers file (token hash only), public key and a capped decisions.jsonl under plugin-data/archytan-lite; carries the gate's MIT Python client (archytan-lite 2.1.1 client.py, byte-identical) so it has no Python dependencies; no telemetry. Until setup has run, every gated tool call is refused.

name: arcmira
description: YouTube transcript search and monitoring for your AI. Arcmira understands YouTube and podcasts like it watched them: the exact quote, often who said it, the full transcript and sponsors. Add "use arcmira" to any question to send it to Arcmira first. Sign in with Thor-managed OAuth in your browser, no key needed, or set ARCMIRA_API_KEY. Bundles Arcmira's hosted MCP server and eleven research skills; portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Arcmira's MCP server at mcp.arcmira.com with the search terms, names, video links and JavaScript programs the agent writes (programs run on Arcmira's servers, never on your machine), authenticated with a Thor-managed OAuth sign-in through api.arcmira.com or ARCMIRA_API_KEY. Reads, transcriptions and alerts use the account's credits. arcmira_execute_write creates and changes monitors that alert by email, Slack or webhook, and starts Premium transcripts; the package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before each write-capable call, but a `thor mcp add arcmira` entry in config.yaml replaces that setting unless it also sets `trust: untrusted`. arcmira_feedback sends the agent's note to Arcmira. Arcmira logs each tool call on the account. The tool list is served at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: ard-kit
description: Agentic Resource Discovery — search a local tool catalog by intent and inspect an entry to get its invoke command. Ships the ard-registry skill plus an stdio MCP server (ard_search / ard_inspect / ard_verify); stdlib only, the run stays local. Disclosure — no network egress, no API keys and no environment variables read by the MCP front, which ranks a catalog JSON on disk; no catalog ships in the repo, so the first call returns an explicit error naming the `python -m ard_kit.catalogize` command that builds one.

name: arena-skill
description: Tournament of N sub-agents competing to produce the best answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only). Adapted from Jakeschincariol/arena-skill (MIT) to use Thor delegate_task. Disclosure — derived from Jakeschincariol/arena-skill (MIT); a full run spawns many delegate_task sub-agents (about 600 calls at the default 100 agents, about 90 with --quick), so cost scales with agent count; the skill runs its bundled bracket.py through the terminal and writes run files under `.arena/` in the current directory.

name: argorant
description: Argorant through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.argorant.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the user's Argorant account, no keys in config): find B2B leads by job, industry, company and place, with free counts and masked previews; reveal or export checked work emails; save lists; check email lists the user already has; write, test and launch cold email campaigns from the user's own mailboxes; and read, label and answer replies. Bundles the argorant workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Argorant's hosted server (mcp.argorant.com) and acts on the user's Argorant account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Revealing, exporting, finding emails, checking email lists and adding people to a campaign spend the user's Argorant credits; launching a campaign and answering a reply send real email from the user's connected mailboxes; buying credits or ordering mailboxes can charge the card saved in the workspace after the user's yes. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: argos
description: Lets Thor agents drive a live Godot 4 editor through a local MCP server with trust=untrusted: read the scene tree, create / move / delete nodes, undo-grouped action.batch, AnimationPlayer/AnimationTree play/stop, set properties with the editor's real undo/redo, open / save / create scenes, play and stop the game, validate GDScript with --check-only, and capture PNG screenshots (named sessions under .argos/captures/). Launch / check / play require ARGOS_PROJECT allowlist. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — the Godot addon opens a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 only (ports 9080-9090) guarded by a random token rotated each editor start and stored in <project>/.argos/; writes state, history and screenshots under <project>/.argos/ (captures only under .argos/captures/ or res://, never absolute paths, `..` or overwrites); for projects on ARGOS_PROJECT / ARGOS_ALLOWED_PROJECTS it launches the Godot editor, runs `godot --check-only` and plays scenes, which executes that project's own GDScript (use on trusted projects); the MCP server is untrusted, so Thor asks before every editing tool and argos_raw forwards any ARGOS action; needs a Python with websockets; no third-party network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: argus
description: Reads a Thor agent by intents instead of sessions and reviews what it learns: links each skill edit to the goal that produced it, flags edits applied without evidence and proposes rules backed by several intents, each kept or rejected by a person and applied through Thor. Disclosure — derive passes send turn text, tool-call and tool-result excerpts, skill diffs and SKILL.md to the auxiliary.argus model; reads every profile's state.db, curator ledger, blobs and SKILL.md read-only (skill directories from Thor' skill_search_dirs; config.yaml is not parsed); starts detached `thor argus derive` passes when the agent is idle; writes skills only on an explicit apply, through rollback_entry or skill_manage as actor user; no credentials, no telemetry.

name: ariadne
description: Record a Thor session once, then replay it with no model, no network and no tokens to see exactly what Thor does differently: check whether updating Thor is safe by replaying your own sessions (with your plugins loaded) on the new version, replay on a new build, compare two installs, bisect the Thor commit that changed a session, fork a recorded session to a live model from any model call, export trajectories and preference pairs, and check Thor's documented hook contracts on every run.
