Disclosure — recording is off until you turn it on; cassettes are written locally under plugin-data with secrets scrubbed (tool output can still hold private file contents); play, compare, bisect and fork start Thor (python -m tui_gateway.entry) as a child process and drive it over JSON-RPC; replays copy this profile's SOUL.md, memories/ and skills/ and only an allowlist of request-shaping settings from config.yaml (never hooks, MCP servers, terminal, auxiliary endpoints or credentials; --trust-config keeps all) into a throwaway home, never .env or auth.json, decode only openai/anthropic SDK model types from cassettes, answer every approval with deny, neutralise tool arguments and block outbound network through a closed local proxy; fork makes real model calls with your configured provider inside your own home (the forked session appears in your history) and runs tools after the fork point only with --live-tools; upgrade-check (CLI, or a button in Desktop) runs git ls-remote and git clone against github.com/thor726/thor-agent and uv against the package index to install that Thor, plus the python_dependencies your enabled plugins declare, into its own venv under plugin-data/ariadne/thor/ (your install is not touched), then replays offline and loads your enabled plugins in both scratch homes; bisect checks out commits in a Thor checkout you name, refusing a dirty tree and restoring the original commit; the optional Desktop half (off until you enable it) adds an Ariadne page, a REC status-bar chip, a mark on recorded sessions, palette commands and a theme, and its backend routes (dashboard/plugin_api.py, loaded only when ariadne is in plugins.enabled) read the plugin's own data folder and start replays and forks as background jobs; fonts are bundled, nothing is fetched from third-party hosts; no telemetry.

name: ariadne-thread
description: n8n-style flows for Thor Desktop: each cron job, webhook route and skill drawn as a chain of steps, with the scheduler's true cron status, run output, delivery targets and a health bar, plus in-place editing with history and undo. Desktop page plus a dashboard API router; no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — reads cron/jobs.json, cron/output/<job id>/, every SKILL.md under skills/ and skills.external_dirs, config.yaml (skills.external_dirs only), a script in scripts/ when opened, and profiles/ folder names; reads webhook routes and cron delivery targets from Thor' own GET /api/webhooks and GET /api/cron/delivery-targets through the raw window.thorDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no route to core endpoints), never opening webhook_subscriptions.json; writes only on Save, in the active profile only: SKILL.md (atomic, inside skills/ only), files in scripts/, and a cron's prompt and deliver target through Thor' cron.jobs.update_job, each save first keeping the replaced text under plugin-data/ariadne-thread/history (0600, newest 10 per target) and refusing if the file changed since it was opened; webhook prompts are read-only; "Ask agent" only drafts a new chat and nothing runs until you send it; no shell commands, no network beyond the local Thor backend, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: art98
description: Drive a real Windows 98 SE VM through art98 (screenshots, pointer, keys, windows, Win32 calls) and render scene scripts to video, with a dashboard tab that has a live view. Disclosure — art98_render runs the agent's scene script as Python on the Thor machine, in a child process outside the terminal backend and not sandboxed (it can read HOME and the VM token); it refuses unless the allow_render setting is on (off by default) and the user approves that script content through Thor's approval gate: a pre_tool_call hook asks for approval naming the scripts and the sha256 of the scene and its imported animations/ modules, and the tool re-hashes its snapshot and refuses on a mismatch. Unattended runs (-q, cron, unattended platforms) are refused unless the matching approvals.*_mode is set to approve; --yolo and approvals.mode: off approve without a prompt; "always" covers only that exact script content, and content approved with "always" also runs unprompted in unattended runs. The dashboard's own Render button skips that approval. art98_win32 is off unless allow_win32 is on. Network is loopback only: the art98 VM's control API (token-authenticated) and optionally its view-only VNC port. One stored credential, the VM token, kept by Thor as the vm_token secret. Needs ffmpeg and ffprobe for art98_combine, and the user's own Windows 98 SE install via the art98 repo; no Windows files ship with the plugin.

name: artemis
description: Mobile web companion for canonical Thor Bot Chats using full-owner Web Access.

name: artifact-relay
description: Publish and read private Markdown or HTML reports through your Artifact Relay server.

name: artifacts
description: Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to THOR_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential THOR_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Thor secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Thor read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Thor write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.

name: artil
description: Give Thor agents their own email inbox, phone number, and workspace accounts to work directly with customers, teammates, and other agents. Disclosure — runs the bundled Artil CLI (`artil internal thor-channel`) while the gateway is listening, which holds a connection to Artil and turns email, SMS, Telegram and team Message-URL messages to the agent account into agent runs with the gateway's tools; who reaches the agent is decided by the agent's "Who can wake the agent" page in Artil and by Thor's ARTIL_ALLOWED_USERS / ARTIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS allowlist or pairing (thor gateway setup writes those to .env); message text and replies go through Artil's servers; the Artil sign-in stays in the CLI's own ~/.config/artil.

name: ascii-worlds
description: Thirty-seven quiet habitats drawn live in text glyphs for Thor Desktop: koi, jellyfish, mantas, sea turtles, seahorses, a fish school, a whale, an octopus, hammerheads circling a bait ball, an anglerfish, butterflies, luna moths, dragonflies, swallows, a sleeping cat, axolotls, an owl, falling leaves and petals, fireflies, bubbles, dandelion seeds and a night sky with the real moon phase, plus pipes and thirteen character scenes: a platypus, capybara, penguins, rubber ducks, a pastry cat, a dinosaur runner, a dragon, bees, a wizard, arcade cabinets, a self-playing snake, a pirate ship and a rooftop ninja. Choose a habitat and its controls in Settings -> Plugins -> ASCII Worlds, and optionally let it animate across the whole window. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network access.

name: aside-browser
description: Use the signed-in Aside browser as Thor's browser when the Aside CLI is installed. Disclosure — runs the local aside CLI to drive your signed-in Aside browser (page text, screenshots, Aside memory, model-written JavaScript via aside_repl) without a Thor approval prompt; Aside's permission level is a user-only setting (default ask) that covers aside_exec only. Optional pre_tool_call hook blocks Thor' built-in browser tools while Aside is ready when browser_policy is always. Reads Aside's settings.json for the model list; no telemetry.

name: asin
description: Amazon prices for Thor through the Asin API: search 11 Amazon stores, read a product's price history and seller offers, and keep a watchlist that checks prices on a schedule and emails on drops. Disclosure — sends the tool arguments to www.asin.dev with your ASIN_API_KEY. Searching, price history, known offers and the watchlist are free; a live offers read and each price check of a tracked product use 1 Asin credit (stated in each tool description). asin_track_product, asin_update_tracking, asin_check_now and asin_stop_tracking change your Asin watchlist, and Asin emails the account owner on price alerts; asin_stop_tracking removes a tracked product and its price history from your ASIN watchlist without a Thor approval prompt. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 11 tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: asin-hhc-proof-of-pay
description: ASIN-HHC Proof of Pay: third-party verification for agent work — validate asin-hhc:receipt evidence receipts against the published schema, verify artifacts against a hash-chained public provenance index, and read the live HHC work-market board (open bounties, settlements with splits). Read-only. Disclosure — fetches the ASIN-HHC provenance index and live board snapshot over https from the configured base_url (default dbottrader.github.io, the author's GitHub Pages site), and fetches a receipt from a model-supplied receipt_url only when it is an https URL whose host resolves to public addresses only; read-only, no keys.

name: ask-ledger
description: Keeps a durable ledger of what you asked and promised: each message becomes an ask (A1, A2 ...) with a state (open, in progress, needs you, answered, closed), and todos (T1, T2 ...) that you add, or that the agent adds when you commit to something (marked added by agent; at most 2 a turn and 10 a day; can be turned off), with a category and due date. Snooze, done and drop work by command (/snooze, /done, /drop) or in plain words; the agent can only suggest them, and a words action must match your current message. Unresolved items are reminded to the agent every turn across restarts and compaction, and /asks, /todos plus a static no-JavaScript page show where everything stands. Disclosure — stores your messages and todos (trimmed, common secret shapes redacted) in plaintext under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/ask-ledger/, append-only and never pruned, with local counts of how you snooze and close; injects a short block of your unresolved asks and up to 3 todos into each turn's user message, so they reach your model provider; appends up to 3 plain reminder lines and a hint to the assistant's reply (transform_llm_output); keeps one plain Open todos message per chat, edited in place, only in conversations it is already part of (setting board, on by default); in group, channel and thread chats it shows only counts, no todo text, unless the chat is listed in trusted_chats; an optional ntfy push (off by default, https only) sends only a count and the page link; no shell commands, no reads outside its data folder, no telemetry.

name: asset-curator
description: Find assets or create them from code with user-controlled access, host-confirmed asset review and preserved licensing/provenance. Disclosure — Asset Curator downloads third-party assets and writes files on your machine. With no access mode set it saves only to Downloads and asks before each download. In "project" mode it writes only inside the workspace you set. "review" mode stages assets in Downloads and asks you before moving each one into your project. In "thor" or "full" mode the plugin applies no path limits of its own, so the agent can write wherever your user account can, and Thor' approval prompt is the only check.

name: assetrizz
description: Assetrizz for Thor: search 14,641 original 2D game assets and have the agent compose them into rendered scenes, with a live preview pane. assetrizz_search runs full-text search over slugs, tags, descriptions, styles and categories across 23 style packs (for example pixel_32 and cozy_cartoon). assetrizz_scene creates a canvas, tiles floors and walls, places, moves, scales, flips and layers props and characters, renders a PNG, and saves or loads scene JSON. Its op=compose builds a whole scene from one compact spec using four gameplay templates (topdown_farming, topdown_shooter, dungeon_crawler, side_platformer) and returns layer lint for collisions, HUD/playfield overlap and off-canvas items. Skill id assetrizz:assetrizz-composer. On Thor Desktop 0.23 or newer, a dark Assetrizz pane live-previews the current scene through ctx.rest, browses assets and installs or removes a local library (deletion needs confirmation). The two tools also run without the pane. It is for game jams, prototypes, level mockups and pitch art that need consistent tiles and sprites quickly. To start, run thor plugins install assetrizz and thor plugins enable assetrizz, then ask: "Search assetrizz for pixel_32 grass and dirt path tiles, then compose a 640×320 meadow with a path, a couple of trees, a ranger and a hare. Render a PNG." Search works at once from the bundled catalog; the first search builds a lean SQLite + FTS5 index in the plugin data directory. Renders come back as file paths. No keys are needed. Disclosure — in the default on_demand mode the plugin downloads individual PNGs from raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/assetrizz at the pinned v0.1.0 tag (SHA-256-verified against the bundled catalog) and caches them under the plugin data directory; the Desktop pane and CLI can download whole style packs (up to about 1.65 GB) to a local folder and delete that folder or the cache after confirmation; rendered scenes are written to the plugin data directory or the user's configured export directory.

name: assumption-ledger
description: Persistent operational-assumption ledger. Captures the assumptions an agent states in its own messages (never from tool output), keeps the sentence each came from as provenance, verifies them with deterministic checks, and warns in context when work recorded in a session depends on an assumption evidence has contradicted. Disclosure — all state is local: assumptions, evidence and decisions are stored in a plain SQLite database under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/assumption-ledger/ (created on first use, never pruned by the plugin; delete the directory to clear it). It needs no credentials. HTTP checks (http_status, http_json_field) are the only outbound traffic; they accept only http/https and refuse loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and cloud-metadata destinations unless you set allow_private_urls, and metadata endpoints stay blocked even then. Command checks (command_succeeds) are disabled until you set command_allowlist; only a listed bare executable name runs (a path is refused), resolved to an absolute path on the child's PATH, with a minimal environment. The allowlist restricts which program may run, not the safety of the arguments the model passes it. Git checks run in a model-chosen directory with the repository's core.fsmonitor and core.hooksPath settings overridden and with a minimal environment; filter drivers set in that repository's own .git/config still apply to git status, so point git checks only at repositories whose local git config you trust. It reads local files, git state, environment variables and SQLite databases, warns rather than blocking a turn, scopes warnings to the session that recorded the decision, and exposes no tools that write to external systems.

name: astro-agents
description: Verifiable planetary timing data for market analysis and backtesting through the Astro Agents MCP server (24 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://astro-agent.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): geocentric and heliocentric positions, declination, Gann planetary lines, a to-the-minute event calendar (ingresses, stations, eclipses), sky analogues and crypto token launch charts and synastry, plus full Western and Vedic astrology (birth chart, transits, synastry, kundli D1-D60, dashas, doshas, KP, yogas, panchang, Gun Milan), computed from the NASA/JPL DE440 ephemeris with no LLM; every result carries a SHA-256 hash. Data for your own analysis, never a trading signal or forecast. Bundles the astrology skill (when to call which tool, input conventions). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call sends the dates, times and coordinates it is given to astro-agent.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. 1 free call per client on the $0.01-0.02 routes only (REST, MCP or A2A); every other route, finance included, is always paid. Over MCP a paid tool returns a standard x402 offer (USDC on Base or Solana) and is paid per call only if the user's own x402 MCP client signs it, or with prepaid credits when the user sets an X-Credits-Token header; the package holds no wallet, key or token.

name: asyntai
description: Run your website's Asyntai AI support agent from Thor through Asyntai's hosted MCP server (73 tools): add knowledge, edit agent instructions, change the widget, read conversations, leads and analytics, answer tickets and emails, and reply live to visitors. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure: runs the pinned @asyntai/mcp@1.0.2 bridge over npx stdio (Node.js 18+); every tool call goes to https://asyntai.com/mcp. The first call opens a browser for OAuth 2.1 PKCE sign-in, and the tokens are stored in ~/.asyntai/mcp-credentials.json; in unattended runs the call fails at the MCP timeout. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool that is not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: athena
description: The local AI-app store for Thor: browse a constantly growing catalogue of apps, install an app from any git repository, launch it, read its logs and stop it. It declares HF_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN so Thor offers to set them, and reads each one through Thor' own secret route rather than scavenging another program's token store. An app is handed a credential only after you approve that app, as an environment variable for the life of its process - never written to disk and never sent anywhere by Athena itself. Apps run on your machine on loopback; third-party install scripts run as you, and the README states the network endpoints, the WSL/QEMU command paths and the GitHub publish path in full. The panel and the CLI are two doors into the same engine. Agent control is in active development. Disclosure — installs apps by cloning third-party git repositories and running their own install and launch scripts on your machine as you (each install and first launch asks through Thor' approval prompt); provisions a pinned app engine from npm at setup after consent; hands HF_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN to an app only after you approve that app, as an environment variable of its process; sends the GitHub token only to GitHub hosts; can manage WSL/QEMU machines and publish your store to a GitHub repository you name.

name: athletedata
description: The athlete's own training and health data from 39 apps (Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, Hevy, Apple Health, Intervals.icu and more) through athletedata's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.athletedata.health/mcp): activities, training load, HRV, sleep, readiness, nutrition, body composition, race predictions, and structured workouts pushed to the athlete's watch. Bundles one skill that tells the agent when to use it. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.athletedata.health and needs an athletedata account (paid, 7-day free trial) with its API key in ATHLETEDATA_API_KEY; the athlete's health and training data is returned from that server. Write tools (push a workout to the watch, log food, create a Hevy routine) change the athlete's own accounts; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: atlas
description: Keeps your Pursuits current across your AI Harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Thor, and Sessions run through T3 Code) and sends you a daily brief with the next Step for each. Disclosure — reads, never writes, the Session stores of those tools under your home folder, and reads through a Harness folder that is a link; copies their transcripts verbatim into a local record folder (default ~/atlas, mode 0700), with detected secrets masked, best effort, in every derived file but not in the raw copies; once you add ChatGPT or claude.ai, reads the export zips you drop in ~/atlas/inbox/ (in memory, capped, never group_chats.json), keeps their conversations verbatim the same way (claude.ai attachment text included), and deletes each zip after it imported every conversation in it, keeping one it cannot read; sends Session text, detected secrets masked, to the model your Thor is configured with, during `thor atlas backfill` and then unattended on every tick (up to 20 Sessions per tick, one model call each, plus the Journal, which a late Session such as an imported one makes it write again, and one call a day that adds to your Profile from that day's Steps, Journal lines and Session times, never transcript text), which costs model calls; a model's answer can change what the record says about one Pursuit, and can list the Session under at most 2 other Pursuits that are active, which splits its Active Time with them, so text inside a conversation can influence the next brief; claims messages addressed to Atlas in your Telegram home chat (the word atlas, a reply to a brief or to the weekly Review, a 10-minute window, /atlas), which then do not reach the Thor agent, and answers there; sends the daily brief to that chat unprompted by running `thor send`, and the brief and resume answers name this machine's host name, the folder and the git branch of each Step (for a web chat, the conversation's title and day), which a group home chat shows to everyone in it; sends a second unprompted message, the weekly Review, once a week (Sunday 18:00 by default) to the same chat, also by running `thor send`; it proposes Focus, ending and reopen changes and never changes a Pursuit by itself, and replies to it are claimed; `thor atlas setup` writes $THOR_HOME/scripts/atlas_tick.sh and creates the `atlas-tick` Thor cron job, which runs `thor atlas tick` every 10 minutes; parks a Pursuit by itself, when it composes a daily brief, after it asked about that Pursuit twice and the latest ask went unanswered, and never ends one; serves a read and write API for its dashboard tab under /api/plugins/atlas/, behind the dashboard's own sign-in; deletes files in its own record folder when you tell it to forget a Session; records this machine's host name in the record; reads its own /proc/self/fd and /proc/self/maps to check which file SQLite opened. Agent tools, in Thor and over `thor atlas mcp` (stdio, no network port), let an agent read Resume Notes and Journal days, leave Notes, and change a Resume Note only on your own typed message to Atlas in that Session, except that a Note an agent wrote unasked in a Session can become a Decided line when the tick files that Session (at most 2 Decided lines per filing, each only from your own typed words in that Session or an agent's Note in it, and only with words that quote holds, apart from a few small ones such as "the" and "and") (Claude Code bound through ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json and /proc/<pid>/stat, Codex through its call thread id): that message itself becomes one Decided line, and one Open question is removed only when the message, addressed to Atlas, states outright that it is settled and it is the only one; other changes, at most one decision and one question, are shown whole and wait until you reply apply; agent text is normalised to one line with its quotes and brackets replaced. No telemetry, no network calls of its own, no stored credentials.

name: atlas-sidecar-excel
description: Sidecar by Atlas Omnia — your Thor agent in desktop Excel for Mac. The plugin runs an HTTPS localhost bridge on ports 47640-47644, exposing 28 sidecar_excel_* tools and opt-in workbook plans. Manual CA trust and one sidebar Allow are required. Allowing lets the configured site use your Thor agent and all its tools until revoke; use a site you control or trust and open only documents you trust. API_SERVER_KEY is read through Thor, never sent to the sidebar or stored by the plugin; TLS private keys are owner-only. For TLS it can only vouch for localhost. The trust command does not limit the certificate to TLS, so protect the key file and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. Latest live run: 2026-11-11 about 00:26 in desktop Excel for Mac, plugin and sidebar built from a7b3fd7. Connect, Allow, a 3-row table with header in A1:B4 and =SUM(B2:B4) in B5 read back from the workbook; revoke dropped the sidebar to needs your OK. The bridge answered 200 to the configured origin and 403 to another origin. The sidebar used a private test site via addin_base, with CA trust in the login keychain; this Mac also has it in the System keychain. Earlier the same night at 35ef09e (behaviour unchanged since): reversal on request by clearing the range (no real undo), plugin reload with the sidebar open (it reconnected by itself and edited again), approval remembered after restarting Excel, next Connect after revoke asked for approval again. Not tested: Windows desktop Excel, dark theme, keyboard-only use, public Pages origin, TLS-only trust or all workbook tools/plans. Reopen the sidebar if it does not reconnect. The Excel test Mac also has System-keychain trust; that was not required in our Word and PowerPoint runs, which used login-keychain trust only. By default the plugin serves its bundled sidebar from the same HTTPS bridge at https://localhost:<actual-port>/sidecar-excel/; GitHub Pages or self-hosting is not required. A custom HTTPS site remains available through addin_base. Office.js loads from Microsoft. Thor may send chat/workbook data to the configured provider. CLI approval/status never starts a listener. Remove matching CA trust manually before deleting the plugin tls directory; uninstall/revoke does not remove OS trust. No telemetry or self-updater. Apache-2.0; LICENSE and NOTICE included. No Microsoft or Thor Labs endorsement. Disclosure — While the gateway runs, this plugin keeps an HTTPS listener on 127.0.0.1:47640-47644 and asks you to trust, by hand, a per-install root CA in your macOS login keychain. The CA can only vouch for localhost in TLS, but the trust command does not limit it to TLS, so protect its key file in the plugin's data folder and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. After you click Allow in Thor, the sidebar site (by default the plugin's own localhost page) can run your full Thor agent with all its tools through your API server until `/sidecar-excel revoke`. Workbook content goes to your configured model provider, and an opened workbook can inject instructions, so open only documents you trust. Dangerous-command approvals cannot be answered from the sidebar and time out as denied. Office.js loads from Microsoft. Uninstalling does not remove OS trust.

name: atlas-sidecar-powerpoint
description: Sidecar by Atlas Omnia — Your Thor agent, in the sidebar of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Sidecar puts your Thor agent in a side panel next to the file you're working on. Ask it to draft, edit, analyze, or build without leaving your document, spreadsheet, or deck. In PowerPoint it reads slides, adds slides, text boxes and shapes, replaces and formats text, and reorders, deletes or re-lays out slides. After one manual local-CA trust step, connect with one click; approval authorizes subsequent chat-driven edits, not per-edit confirmation; runs on your machine, no API key files (protected TLS keys in plugin data). Your agent: it runs on your own Thor setup, with the models and tools you already use. Setup: install the plugin, enable the Thor API server, manually trust the per-install local CA using the printed command (never run automatically), run /sidecar-powerpoint manifest to write a manifest for the actual bridge port and sideload it into PowerPoint, click Connect to Thor and allow it in Thor with /sidecar-powerpoint. Disclosure — the plugin serves its bundled sidebar at https://localhost:<actual-port>/sidecar-powerpoint/ from an HTTPS listener bound to 127.0.0.1:47650-47654 (first free port) inside the process that runs the Thor gateway (or plugin host) from when the gateway loads the plugin (setting autostart, default on; off: from the first /sidecar-powerpoint or sidecar_powerpoint_* call) until the plugin stops or Thor exits; by default it accepts the same exact https://localhost:<actual-port> origin and exactly one Host localhost:<actual-port>. An external HTTPS site remains optional through addin_base; the default needs no web hosting. A per-install CA and localhost certificate are generated in plugin-data/atlas-sidecar-powerpoint/tls/; private keys are owner-only, never logged. For TLS it can only vouch for localhost. The trust command does not limit the certificate to TLS, so protect the key file and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. Critical permitted DNS localhost subtree and IP 127.0.0.1/32; no IPv6; CA validity is at most 825 days, leaf at most 397. Legacy unconstrained CAs refuse service: manually remove old trust before deleting the TLS directory and restarting. Protect its CA key and remove OS trust manually on uninstall. Requires cryptography>=43. Allowing lets the configured origin use your Thor agent and all its tools until you revoke. Use a site you control or trust; open only documents you trust. A sidebar gets a session only after the user allows it in Thor (/sidecar-powerpoint, or thor sidecar-powerpoint allow); the approval is remembered as a SHA-256 hash of a per-sidebar grant in plugin-data/atlas-sidecar-powerpoint/approvals.json (owner-only) and revoked with /sidecar-powerpoint revoke. No Sidecar tool can approve; an agent with shell access could run the CLI allow command, subject to Thor command approval. Forwards the sidebar's chat requests to the user's Thor API server on loopback (setting api_server_url, default http://127.0.0.1:8642) with API_SERVER_KEY (requires_env, secret) read through agent.secret_scope.get_secret, kept in memory only, never written, logged or sent to the sidebar. The bundled sidebar is served by the plugin at https://localhost:<actual-port>/sidecar-powerpoint/; it loads Microsoft's Office.js from appsforoffice.microsoft.com and sends document data only to the same-origin localhost bridge. An external HTTPS host is optional through addin_base; the default requires no web hosting. A reproducible optional external build (npm run build:static) writes SHA256SUMS. Tool calls from another Thor chat than the sidebar's are refused. The bridge makes no other outbound service calls, runs no shell commands and has no telemetry or self-updater. Thor itself uses the configured model/provider and tools; local bridge transport is not a promise of local-only inference. Same author as Workbench (thor-office-desktop, Office for the web in Thor Desktop); separate lineage (desktop Office sidebar), distinct sidecar_powerpoint_ tool names and ports, installable together. Sidecar is developed by Atlas Omnia. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft or Thor Labs. Microsoft, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies.

name: atlas-sidecar-word
description: Sidecar by Atlas Omnia — Your Thor agent, in the sidebar of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Sidecar puts your Thor agent in a side panel next to the file you're working on. Ask it to draft, edit, analyze, or build without leaving your document, spreadsheet, or deck. In desktop Word for Mac it reads the document and selection, inserts and replaces text, applies exact-match edit plans, formatting, styles and comments. After one manual local-CA trust step and pane approval, the agent may read and write the bound document; this is not per-edit approval. No API keys stored by the plugin; TLS private keys are protected in plugin data. Your agent: it runs on your own Thor setup, with the models and tools you already use. Setup: install the plugin, enable the Thor API server, manually trust the per-install local CA using the printed user-scope command, run /sidecar-word manifest (or thor sidecar-word manifest) to create and sideload a manifest for the plugin-served localhost sidebar, click Connect to Thor and allow it in Thor with /sidecar-word. GitHub Pages or self-hosting is not required by default; a self-hosted HTTPS site may still be selected through addin_base. Disclosure — runs an HTTPS listener at https://localhost:47630-47634 bound to IPv4 127.0.0.1 (first free port) inside the process that runs the Thor gateway (or plugin host) from when the gateway loads the plugin (setting autostart, default on; off: from the first /sidecar-word or sidecar_word_* call) until Thor exits; it accepts only the sidebar site's exact origin (plugin setting addin_base) and exactly one Host localhost:<actual-port>. A per-install CA and localhost certificate are generated in plugin-data/atlas-sidecar-word/tls/; private keys are owner-only, never logged. For TLS it can only vouch for localhost. The trust command does not limit the certificate to TLS, so protect the key file and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. TLS name constraints permit DNS localhost subtree and IP 127.0.0.1/32; no IPv6; CA validity is at most 825 days, leaf at most 397. Legacy unconstrained CAs refuse service: manually remove old trust before deleting the TLS directory and restarting. Protect its CA key and remove OS trust manually on uninstall. Requires cryptography>=43. A sidebar gets a session only after the user allows it in Thor (/sidecar-word, or thor sidecar-word allow); the approval is remembered as a SHA-256 hash of a per-sidebar grant in plugin-data/atlas-sidecar-word/approvals.json (owner-only) and revoked with /sidecar-word revoke. No Sidecar tool can approve; an agent with shell access could run the approval CLI subject to Thor command approval. Allowing lets the whole configured origin use your Thor agent and all its tools until revoke. Use a site you control or trust; open only documents you trust. Forwards the sidebar's chat requests to the user's Thor API server on loopback (setting api_server_url, default http://127.0.0.1:8642) with API_SERVER_KEY (requires_env, secret) read through agent.secret_scope.get_secret, kept in memory only, never written, logged or sent to the sidebar. The sidebar page is bundled with the plugin and served at https://localhost:47630/sidecar-word/ (actual bound port in 47630-47634); it loads Office.js from appsforoffice.microsoft.com and sends document data only to the verified HTTPS localhost bridge. GitHub Pages or other hosting is not required; a self-hosted HTTPS site can still be selected through addin_base. A reproducible build (npm run build:sidebar) writes SHA256SUMS. Pane approval authorizes all known tools, including new content and formatting, only for a valid bound session with active approval. Unknown tools, invalid or missing sessions and revoked approvals fail closed. No comment-per-turn guard is claimed without a trustworthy turn id; tool calls from another Thor chat than the sidebar's are refused. No other network calls, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-updater. Same author as Workbench (thor-office-desktop, Office for the web in Thor Desktop); separate lineage (desktop Office sidebar), distinct sidecar_word_ tool names and ports, installable together. Sidecar is developed by Atlas Omnia. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft or Thor Labs. Microsoft, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies.

name: atmorouter
description: AtmoRouter — OpenAI-compatible gateway; one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Grok models, with the /model picker fed by the live GET /v1/models catalog. Disclosure — sends your prompts, conversation history, tool definitions, tool results and ATMOROUTER_API_KEY to atmorouter.dev, which forwards each request to the infrastructure serving the chosen model; that infrastructure's processing location and retention vary per model and zero retention is not promised (AtmoRouter states its usage and billing records keep metadata rather than prompt or response content, and that it does not train on API request content; https://atmorouter.dev/privacy). Usage is billed per token from a prepaid AtmoRouter balance (QRIS, or USDT/USDC on Solana, BNB Chain or Polygon); prices vary by capacity offer and, with no saved budget, a request can route to any offer up to the highest advertised catalog tier, unless you set a minimum discount off official rates or exact rate caps under Budgets; failed upstream requests are not billed and the plugin itself makes no payments.

name: atomicmail
description: Gives a Thor agent its own @atomicmail.ai address in one command, with no account or signup form (proof-of-work sign-up). Mail from the user's allowed addresses wakes the agent and its reply goes out in the same thread; every allowed sender's DKIM signature is checked first, so a forged From: cannot drive the agent. Tools read, search, send and reply, and schedule meetings with real calendar invitations (send, update, cancel, read RSVPs, answer invitations). Disclosure — gives the agent its own @atomicmail.ai inbox: mail from addresses in ATOMICMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS (none by default) that passes a DKIM check reaches the agent as a chat message and the agent's reply is emailed back; ATOMICMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true turns the DKIM check off, so a forged From: can then drive the agent; the model can send new mail, replies, calendar invitations, updates, cancellations and RSVPs from that address to any recipient without a Thor approval prompt (the tools only ask the model to confirm with the user first), and Atomic Mail adds a "Sent from Atomic Mail Agentic" footer; network calls to Atomic Mail only (auth.atomicmail.ai for sign-up and sign-in, api.atomicmail.ai for JMAP: polling, reading, sending, invitations, and downloading each new allowed message for the DKIM check) plus DNS TXT lookups for DKIM keys (system resolver; when it returns nothing, DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com, then dns.google; ATOMICMAIL_DNS_OVER_HTTPS=off disables that); a background polling task (every 20 s) while the gateway runs; Atomic Mail's anti-spam proof-of-work (scrypt, not cryptocurrency mining) costs about 20-45 CPU-seconds per sign-in, roughly every 10 minutes while the gateway polls (a few percent of one core) and once per tool session otherwise; the inbox API key is stored in Thor's .env through thor_cli.config and read with the profile-scoped secret reader; seen-message ids in plugin-data/atomicmail/state.json; no telemetry.

name: attest
description: Paper trading ledger for agents. Orders, balances and P&L live in a local SQLite ledger the plugin owns, and the agent gets its figures from get_portfolio, get_pnl and get_quote instead of stating them. Orders are priced from live public exchange quotes with slippage and a fee, after a per-order size limit, a daily loss kill switch and duplicate-order checks. No real money, no exchange account, no keys. Disclosure: network use is read-only HTTPS GETs of public ticker data, each sending only the trading pair and the User-Agent attest-paper-trading/0.6.1, with a 3 second deadline: www.okx.com /api/v5/market/ticker?instId=BTC-USDT first, then api.kraken.com /0/public/Ticker?pair=XBTUSDT, then data-api.binance.vision /api/v3/ticker/bookTicker?symbol=BTCUSDT as fallbacks. Requests happen on an order, on get_quote, when marking open positions, and for the claim check. It writes one SQLite ledger in its Thor plugin data folder: account, trades (with the quote that priced each one, the full tool result and the optional order note), positions, risk state, each day's starting equity, and the ids of sessions that called an attest tool or the guarded tool (removed after 90 days); no other conversation text. pre_tool_call blocks only the one tool named in the intercept_tool setting (empty by default) while paper_mode is on, and simulates that order on the ledger instead; every other tool returns untouched. transform_llm_output appends one line under a reply that states a balance or P&L figure the ledger contradicts, only in sessions that used attest, and never edits the reply. /attest check runs the bundled self test in a separate Python process against a temporary database. The demo_stub_tool setting (off by default) registers a test-only demo_broker_order tool.

name: attune
description: Daily learning that drives evidence-linked, permission-bound project build previews. Disclosure — after you approve a proposal (/attune approve) or grant a standing preview window (/attune project-mode … preview, up to 30 days and 3 builds/day, which also applies to unattended cron runs), it runs your selected project's unit tests together with model-written code changes on this machine inside a Bubblewrap sandbox (Linux only; no network, cleared environment, read-only copy; the original project is never modified).

name: audionotes
description: Search and read your Audionotes voice notes, meeting transcripts and AI summaries through Audionotes' hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.audionotes.app/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration, scope notes:read, paid Audionotes account required). Four read-only tools (search_notes, list_notes, list_folders, get_note) plus the retrieve-notes skill, which tells the agent to cite the notes it used and to keep generated summaries apart from source transcripts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Audionotes' hosted server (api.audionotes.app) and reads the signed-in user's own notes; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Note titles, summaries and transcripts that match a request enter the session context and are sent to the user's model provider. The tools cannot create, edit, delete or share notes. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted; all four tools are annotated read-only.

name: audit-lens
description: Deterministic smart-contract security review inside Thor: fetch verified source from Sourcify, run pattern-based static checks (reentrancy, tx.origin, unchecked calls, unprotected selfdestruct, delegatecall, access control), flag likely-known issues against a curated SWC database, and draft structured findings. Standard library only, no dependencies.

name: augur
description: Your agent knows your 3 priorities for the week, notices when you drift, parks the detour, and on Friday clears what it can and shows where your attention actually went. Labels each request in the background, asks one short question on the 2nd detour in a row ("Park it" or "Do it now", buttons on Telegram), runs a guarded research-and-draft Friday cron job over the Queue, and sends a weekly report image with planned vs actual per goal and a hidden 4th priority. Disclosure: one short model call per message through its own auxiliary task (augur_classifier), one per weekly report (augur_insight); stores only model-written 60-char summaries, goals and parked items, redacted, in its own data folder; a pre_tool_call guard limits its own cron run to its Queue tools, web_search and file work inside its drafts folder. No network of its own, no shell, no telemetry, no self-update, no binaries.

name: aunx-decompose
description: Break a task into the smallest checkable units and parallel waves: typed units, real data edges, clause coverage, an advisor gate and a plan table.

name: aurora-design-system
description: Two offline tools plus four skills that make a Thor agent build real web UI with the Aurora CSS design system: aurora_search returns the family, the pack and the real markup of any of 2,223 classes across 417 families from a bundled census; aurora_validate checks a page against that census (invented classes, packs used but not linked, gradients, !important, hand-written colours, duplicate headings, missing attribution) and returns failures and warnings in milliseconds. No network, no subprocess, no writes, no hooks. Disclosure — the bundled skills have the agent run `curl`/`git` against api.github.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net (Ntizar/Aurora) to resolve the current release, build pages that load their CSS from cdn.jsdelivr.net, and require the attribution footer `Hecho con ❤️ por David Antizar` and Spanish copy on every page (`aurora_validate` fails pages that carry neither that footer nor `Made with ❤️ by David Antizar`); `aurora_validate` reads any HTML path the agent passes; the install clones a ~380 MB repository (demo video frames and scripts under `video/`, unused by the plugin).

name: author-feed
description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. It reads public posts and profiles from the Bluesky social media network, which is built on the AT Protocol (atproto), without signing in. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key. Thor starts the watch Python when the cron job fires. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. thor author-feed schedule writes a script and creates one cron job that does not call a model. Each run costs 0 tokens and has no daily cap. Empty script output sends nothing. Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run thor author-feed unschedule before removal. That removes the job and the script. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with thor cron remove <id>. The scheduled script does not run under plugins.isolation: host, so that setting does not stop the watch. The author_watch tool still refuses a run that is not the saved cron job, including under plugins.isolation: host, and posts that notice on every run of the tool. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Thor parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall. Seen post URIs advance only on the saved cron job after a successful fetch. The script allows that when cron/executions.db shows that job running under the parent pid and cron/jobs.json names author-feed-watch.py. A direct run and another cron job exit 3 with no GET and no write. The author_watch tool allows that only for the saved job id. Delivery accepts origin, local, all, bot-chat, the Thor 0.21.6 cron platform names, and public registry names that declare a cron delivery env var. A refused name can be set with thor cron edit <id> --deliver. bot-chat places the watched account's post text in another model turn that has the profile's tools. thor cron create cannot set a per-job tool list. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. On Thor 0.21.4 and 0.21.5 this plugin does not load, and a leftover job keeps its model turn until thor cron remove <id>. Running schedule again updates the interval and deliver target and switches an existing model job to the script.

name: auto-pin
description: Automatically pin every new interactive session (desktop, CLI, TUI) and the branches you fork from them. Cron, one-shot, subagent and messaging sessions are left alone, and unpinning a session sticks. Disclosure — on each new desktop/CLI/TUI session it sets the session's pinned flag in Thor's session database (state.db) through the shared SessionDB handle, and records each automatic pin in $THOR_HOME/auto-pin/ledger.txt; no network, no tools.

name: autom
description: Live search engine results for Thor through the Autom SERP API: tools for Google Search, News, Images, Videos, Shopping, Maps and Autocomplete, Bing, Brave web, images and videos, DuckDuckGo and Yahoo, a search that falls back across engines, Google locations and account usage. Also a backend for the built-in web_search tool (Google organic results). Disclosure — sends each search query and the tool arguments to api.autom.dev with your AUTOM_API_KEY, and calls use Autom credits (1 per search; locations and usage are free). Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 17 tools and a web_search backend, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: autonoma
description: Earned autonomy: a trust score per kind of action (file edits, deletes, git push, network, messages, spending, system) that rises with clean work and falls on denials, corrections and failures. Below a class's threshold the call goes through Thor's own approval prompt; at or above, it runs without asking. Catches the agent routing around a block (shell redirects, inline python/node code, `bash -c`), asks again for risky actions after the turn read outside content, revokes "session"/"always" grants after a correction, writes handoff notes from the tool log when a session ends unfinished, and adds a live dashboard tab. Disclosure — stores tool names, action classes, hashed arguments, file paths, command verbs, host names, short error excerpts and short excerpts of your messages and the agent's last reply (up to 500 characters) locally in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/autonoma/data.db (90-day retention, configurable); injects a handoff note into the first turn after an unfinished session and a progress list after compaction; can raise Thor approval prompts for actions below their trust threshold or after outside content and, when hard_floor_enabled is on, block a class for a number of turns after a correction; the dashboard tab's local routes read the ledger and can reset, set or freeze scores; makes no network calls, no telemetry, reads no credentials; optional corrections_llm (off by default) sends the previous assistant message and current user message to the active model to confirm a correction.

name: autorag
description: Search your own files and configured chat/mail archives from Thor with AutoRAG Lite. Local hybrid retrieval, file-name search, cited evidence and duplicate detection without editing original documents. Supports PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, Markdown and Korean HWP/HWPX; existing integrations include Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, KakaoTalk, email, Notion and Obsidian. Bundles four skills and a Thor Desktop Finder pane. Requires Node.js 24+; runs pinned @autorag/librarian@2.13.12 through npx stdio. The Desktop backend installs that same pinned package once in plugin data, with npm lifecycle scripts disabled. First refresh can provision minsync and jikji and download local embedding models (roughly 1.5 GB). Reads only configured folders and archives; writes its own index/report state. User-requested automation also writes rule/scripts and creates Thor cron jobs. No telemetry, self-update or stored-login discovery. Search snippets read by Thor reach its selected model provider; configured remote connectors or embedders use their selected services. Disclosure — runs the pinned @autorag/librarian@2.13.12 MCP server through npx (Node.js 24+); the Desktop pane installs the same package once under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/autorag with lifecycle scripts disabled, but its own dependencies are version ranges (plus an xlsx tarball from cdn.sheetjs.com, allowed via npm_config_allow_remote=all) resolved at install time; the first refresh downloads local embedding models (~1.5 GB) and helper tools; it reads only the folders and crawler archives you configure and writes its own index under the workspace's .autorag/ and plugin data; on request the schedule/automate skills write scripts under $THOR_HOME/scripts/ and create Thor cron jobs (remove deletes them); search snippets Thor reads go to your model provider, and configured remote embedders/connectors get your content; no telemetry.

name: aux-ledger
description: Local ledger of Thor's auxiliary LLM calls (titling, compression, vision, approval): /aux shows tokens, time and failures per task, model, provider or day, or lists the newest calls (ten, or up to 100 with /aux recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded. Disclosure — writes auxiliary-call metadata (ids, models, timings, token counts, no prompt or response text) to plugin-data/aux-ledger/calls.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

name: aws-manager
description: Deploy, monitor, and verify AWS resources in Thor Desktop, including EC2, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, and API Gateway. Disclosure — uses the AWS access key you enter in plugin settings to create, change and delete real AWS resources (EC2, Lambda, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, API Gateway, VPC, Route 53, ECR/ECS, EventBridge, SQS, CloudFront) in your account from the dashboard; these can incur AWS charges. Every change is reviewed and applied by you in the UI, never by the agent.

name: awskills
description: About 100 portable skills for operating AI agents and the Aither/awdk toolchain: install the adk CLI and run an agent locally, find and install tool packs and skills, author and ship your own tool pack, use Aither from Thor and other harnesses over skills, MCP and A2A, work safely in a shared git worktree, and debug agent failures. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/), skills only, no plugin code, no MCP server bundled. Disclosure — skills are instructions only, but many tell the agent to run local CLIs (adk, awnode) and to download and run vendor install scripts with curl|sh or irm|iex from aitherium.com, raw.githubusercontent.com/Aitherium, openclaw.ai, install.osmantic.com, twotimespi.dev and ollama.com (each command goes through Thor' terminal approval); some skills connect to Aitherium's hosted services (mcp.aitherium.com, gateway.aitherium.com, weights.aitherium.com) when the user follows them. The repo's hooks/, tools/ and scripts/ files are not loaded by Thor.

name: b64-ref
description: @b64: context references that decode encoded text for the model: @b64:<value> takes base64 (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), hex (0x48656c6c6f, 48:65:6c, \x48\x65), percent-encoding or a data: URI, told apart by the value's shape or picked with base64:, base64url:, hex: or url:, and attaches what it holds: text as text with control and invisible characters escaped, JSON pretty-printed, gzip and zlib inflated in memory (at most 1 MiB, one layer), and binary named by its format (PNG and GIF with their size, JPEG, PDF, ZIP, ELF, SQLite and more) with a hex dump of its first 128 bytes; notes point out a value that was cut short, padding that is off, a second layer of encoding and a JWT inside; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's base64, json, urllib.parse and zlib; nothing decoded is run, opened or saved; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what it decodes, but the @b64: reference and the decoded contents become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only values you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @b64: reference provider.

name: babysit
description: Watches a long job's log (training run, build, migration) with zero model calls, keeps one chat message updated in place, and wakes the agent only when the job hits a non-finite value, out-of-memory error, traceback, stall, process exit or a line containing your alert text. With `on_failure: pause` it freezes the job on a non-finite value, out-of-memory error, memory pressure or traceback, and a restart linked with `resume_of` gets a recovered or relapsed verdict once it passes the old failure step. Disclosure — Babysit reads the selected log file through one read-only handle, opened without following symlinks and checked again from the handle itself, so replacing the path afterwards changes nothing it reads. It accepts absolute paths only and refuses files inside the active profile's Thor home, the Thor root that holds every profile, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.config`, `/etc`, `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev`, files with credential-looking names such as `.env`, `id_*`, `*.pem`, `*.key` and `auth.json`, shell and database history files (`.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`, `.python_history`, `.psql_history` and every other `.*_history`), `~/.pgpass`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, hard-linked files, and anything that is not a regular file. When a PID is given, every 4 seconds it reads that process's resident memory through psutil, plus the cgroup memory limit from `/sys/fs/cgroup` or the system's available memory, and when the process ends it reads its exit status without reaping it. It never writes to the log, makes no network requests of its own, spawns no child processes, and sends no signals unless a watch sets `on_failure: pause`: then it sends `SIGSTOP` to the one PID the watch was given, and `SIGCONT` on `babysit_resume` or `/babysit resume`, each only after re-checking that PID's uid and start time. It never kills a process, never signals a process group or another PID, and refuses Thor' own process and its parents. `checkpoint_dir` reports the newest checkpoint's name, size and age without reading its contents. For the Desktop pane it writes one JSON file per watch, `<thor home>/plugin-data/babysit/watches/<watch id>.json`, owner-only and replaced atomically whenever the state changes and at least every 4 seconds. Each file holds the watch's file name, log path, PID, metric series, memory samples, events, counters and the last 12 log lines (200 characters each). Files of watches that ended a day ago, and all but the newest 24, are removed when a watch starts. The read-only dashboard route `GET /api/plugins/babysit/watches` reads those files and writes nothing. Its one runtime dependency beyond the standard library is psutil, which Thor pins. It creates one daemon thread per watch. Babysit and Thor read the plugin's `allow_gateway_injection` setting in the profile Babysit runs in to check injection permission. The watch loop makes no model calls. Detected events are sent to the current session, which may start an agent turn.

name: backfill
description: Switch memory providers without Thor forgetting you: replays your past Thor sessions into the memory provider you use now, with a dry run, resume, no double imports and a before/after recall check. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and config.yaml; sends past user/assistant turns to the memory provider you configured (a cloud provider receives them over the network); writes only its own plugin state (imported session ids, 16-character turn hashes, recall-check results); the optional `thor backfill check` uses your Thor model through its own auxiliary slot. No network calls, credentials or telemetry of its own.

name: background-review-watch
description: Status-bar chips for the background self-improvement review and batch context compaction: review running/done/stale with live elapsed time, a turn-countdown fill bar to the next nudge, an always-visible compaction chip (compacting/done/failed/stale with committed reduction or failure class), reply-guard recovery and review-overlap diagnostics, and a Settings page that tunes both orphan ceilings. Disclosure — renderer-only; polls filtered read-only tails of agent.log via host.logs to parse lifecycle markers; listens for review.summary/message.start/message.complete events; stores three small plugin-storage records (settings + last compaction + last review); no network calls beyond the local gateway, no credential access, no self-update.

name: backstop
description: A build or test that fails in your own PowerShell, bash or zsh gets a read-only Thor diagnosis (cause, quoted evidence, file:line, fix) that opens in Thor Desktop; Fix it drafts the change into a normal chat you send yourself, and the next passing run closes the incident. Disclosure — each failure automatically starts one diagnosis session on your configured model (output tail redacted, command, cwd, project excerpts); reads project files and their size/mtime, never dot-paths or files on Thor' read denylist, and never diagnoses a failure run from home, THOR_HOME or a dot-directory; shell hook functions plus an opt-in profile/rc line; one gateway thread polls its spool every second. No own network calls, credentials or telemetry. One internal import (session-policy guard) is version-coupled; no runtime overrides or self-updater.

name: backup-sentinel
description: Offline local tar.gz backup integrity, freshness, required-file and archived SQLite auditing; never restores or repairs. Disclosure — reads explicitly selected archive bytes, materializes only permitted SQLite members in private scratch, and invokes a fixed local Python auditor through Thor's terminal policy; paths/results can reach the conversation model. No cloud, telemetry, credentials, model calls or background jobs.

name: backupdrill
description: Back up a Supabase project to your own S3, R2 or B2 bucket with the open-source backupdrill CLI (the Postgres database, plus Storage files once their S3 keys are set), then restore the snapshot into a throwaway Postgres in Docker to check it comes back. Disclosure — a skill only, with no Python, hooks or server: it has the agent run npx -y backupdrill@2.7.1 in shell commands, which npx downloads from npm on first run. The CLI connects to the user's Supabase project and their own bucket, and a drill pulls a postgres image from Docker Hub. The connection string and bucket keys stay in a .env.backupdrill file the user fills in; each command loads it in a subshell and never prints it. Nothing is sent to BackupDrill.

name: bae
description: Your eBay sidekick for Thor Agent: drop in item photos and quick notes to draft accurate listings, strip generic AI filler from existing Magical Listings, check active comps alongside your own past sales, and preview real net profit after Final Value Fees, Promoted Listings ad rates, and July 2026 USPS 139 dimensional weight before anything goes live. Includes a 4-station Seller Desk (/bae) and 350px Side Pane in Desktop and Webapp, built-in Casual C2C and Pro Store sample tours, Seller Hub Draft CRLF CSV export, inkFrog and myFitment CSV migration, category playbooks, Best Offer floor triage, bin-sorted packing lists, and zero-token scheduled checks. Every live eBay write waits for your approval: Thor's own approval prompt when you approve in chat, or an Approve click in the Seller Desk; the agent cannot approve its own staged changes. Starts on sample data; connecting a live eBay account waits on Thor support for eBay's sign-in (thor-agent#142687), and Seller Hub Draft CSVs work today. Disclosure — makes zero network calls in sample mode (the default), sample tours or offline CSV mode; in live mode, when connected via thor auth add thor-ebay-ops:ebay, calls api.ebay.com, apiz.ebay.com, and apim.ebay.com exclusively through Thor's OAuth broker; reads local photo paths passed to ebay_stage_listing, after checking each against Thor's read denylist, and CSV text passed to ebay_import_migration_csv; registers one pre_tool_call hook that sends every agent-issued approval of a staged write to Thor's approval prompt; writes only inside its own Thor plugin data folder (SQLite ledgers and exported draft CSVs); runs no shell commands or background daemons; typing in the Seller Desk dock submits your prompt to a visible Thor conversation."

name: ball
description: Estimates which Thor chats are waiting on you and what the AI asked (/ball; Matrix: !ball). Heuristic; misses happen. Reads inbound messages (never stored) and, read-only, Thor' state.db (non-public schema); stores short AI-reply excerpts in local SQLite. Optional LLM judge sends reply tails to your active model.

name: ballast
description: Free a target amount of disk space by clearing the developer and AI caches you'll miss least, with Thor approval and rebuild recipes. Disclosure — after a Thor approval prompt, `ballast_apply` permanently deletes (no Trash) the contents of cataloged cache directories under your home (npm, pnpm, Yarn, pip, uv, Cargo, Homebrew downloads, Xcode DerivedData/device support, CoreSimulator caches, HuggingFace hub, Gradle, CocoaPods, Go; Ollama and LM Studio model stores only on explicit opt-in). Runs your locally installed npm/yarn/pip/uv/go cache cleaners (argv, no shell, minimal offline environment) and read-only `docker system df`. No network, no credentials read; state in plugin-data/ballast/. Cron and unattended runs are refused.

name: bankbridge
description: Read-only answers about your own US bank, credit card and investment accounts, with any model Thor runs, local or hosted. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — Hosted remote MCP server at bankbridge.money (no local code); tool calls send your queries to bankbridge.money and its bank-data provider, which return your account balances, transactions and holdings into the model context (and so to your model provider). Sign-in is BankBridge's own OAuth; the server is behind the pin, so its tools can change without a catalog update. Paid service: $5/month per connected bank. Tools are read-only.

name: bankconv
description: Convert PDF bank and credit card statements into transactions (ISO dates, signed amounts, running balance) or CSV, OFX, QFX, QBO and Xero CSV files with BankConv. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only: it runs the bankconv-mcp npm package pinned to 0.1.1 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20+ is required, and reads BANKCONV_API_KEY from the user's environment. Disclosure — the PDFs the user names are uploaded to bankconv.com over HTTPS and deleted after 24 hours by default; converting uses pages of the user's BankConv account; converted files are written next to the PDF, to Downloads (or the home folder), or to any path given in save_to, overwriting an existing file there. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before convert_statement and download_statement and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: barehand
description: Lets an agent operate a machine with no OS, network or agent on it (firmware menus, boot loaders, installers, rescue shells such as grub>) through the screen and keyboard alone. It provides a computer_use provider for QEMU virtual machines over QMP (or a VNC console), a barehand_machine tool, a thor barehand CLI, a skill and a flight recorder. In recorded runs a model installed Debian 13 from the network installer (it repaired a grub> prompt on first boot from the installer's rescue mode) and Ubuntu Server 26.04 (it finished the stalled installer by hand) on blank aarch64 machines. `thor barehand demo` replays a bundled recording. Evidence is in the README and docs/results. Disclosure — `thor barehand up` starts local qemu-system/qemu-img processes that keep running after Thor exits until `thor barehand down`. The guest has QEMU user-mode (NAT) networking and can reach whatever the host can. QMP is unauthenticated on a 0700 unix socket (or a loopback TCP port fallback). The optional VNC transport is unencrypted. The flight recorder is on by default and stores screenshots and key chords (typed text as length only) under the plugin data dir. `barehand_machine` runs status, snapshot_list, snapshot_save under a new name, calibrate_text (types a fixed ASCII test line) and wait_for_text without an approval prompt.

name: baro
description: Hand a software goal to Baro and watch it run as a live, dependency-aware kanban: baro_plan returns the plan as stories with dependency edges, baro_run starts a run, baro_status shows each story as blocked, ready, running, done or failed with what it waits on and what it blocks, and baro_cancel stops the run and its process tree. Disclosure — every baro_run and baro_plan call is sent to Thor's human-approval gate by the plugin's pre_tool_call hook, whatever the approval mode, because once approved Baro's coding agents execute shell commands in the target repository without further prompts (each in its own git worktree; on Baro's default Claude backend inside Claude Code's OS sandbox, which allows writes only to that worktree and Baro's package cache, denies reading credential stores and limits network to package registries; with --llm openai only shell writes are OS-confined on macOS and Linux relies on Baro's command guard; no push or pull request; agents run with the user's account); baro_run starts one long-running background process per run (baro-ai@0.132.0 through npx, pinned exactly) via Thor's terminal tool; Baro's agents make network calls to the model provider the user configured for Baro, or to the Thor subscription proxy on this machine when the plugin's opt-in setting is on (the plugin first checks that the proxy answers on its local /models route; it calls nothing off the machine); a tool call cannot name a backend, base URL or model, and the approval message says where a run's model calls go; boards, and a tee'd copy of each run's event stream for the live board, are stored only in the plugin's own Thor plugin data; the plugin reads no credentials and no files outside that state, has no telemetry, and refuses to start or stop runs under cron and the messaging gateway.

name: basekit
description: Read-only live Base (chain 8453) intelligence — gas and real USD cost estimates, wallet portfolios, decoded transaction receipts, token facts with proxy detection, and windowed transfer/approval reads — plus a desktop pane, status-bar chip and a standard-library-only core with no PyPI dependencies. Disclosure — sends the wallet addresses, transaction hashes and token addresses you ask about to public Base RPC endpoints (base-rpc.publicnode.com, mainnet.base.org, base.drpc.org, base.meowrpc.com; a custom rpc_url still fails over to these), prices to coins.llama.fi and api.coinbase.com, and to api.etherscan.io only when a Basescan key is set; a pre_llm_call hook adds one line of live Base state to turns that mention Base or crypto terms (off with inject_chain_context); keeps a local read ledger in its plugin-data folder; no signing, no keys, no telemetry.

name: baton
description: Hand your session and repository to your remote Thor agent (Thor Cloud, a VPS or a Docker container) with /baton "fix the parser, done when pytest passes": the remote works in a throwaway worktree, cannot return verified until the agreed check is green on the exact tree it returns, and `thor baton land <id>` fetches the tested branch baton/<id> without touching your HEAD, index, working tree or stash. Code travels by git, the order by the Thor Runs API, state by git refs; every step resumes after a network cut. Disclosure — pushes a snapshot commit of the repository (tracked changes and untracked files not ignored by .gitignore; a blocking secret scan first refuses .env files, keys and tokens, and symlinks that point outside the repository are refused) to the git remote you configure in remote_git and fetches baton refs from it; sends the task and a redacted session transcript (`thor sessions export --redact` plus an extra redaction pass, capped at 64 KB) to the peer Thor API server at the URL you register, with the peer key read through Thor's secret scope; runs `git` (with a minimal environment) and `thor sessions export` as subprocesses; on a machine set to role remote or both, runs the agreed check without a shell only when its argv matches the remote's allowed_checks plus safe flags, with an empty throwaway HOME, no THOR_* variables or provider keys, and a timeout. Without a usable bubblewrap (e.g. the official Docker image) or with sandbox: off, the project's code runs with the remote user's rights and can read the Thor home, so only accept batons from your own machines. Landing creates branch baton/<id> without touching HEAD, the index or the working tree; no telemetry.

name: beam
description: Move data across cloud storage and exchange end-to-end encrypted messages, files and media between agents with Beam Network (Bittensor SN105).

name: belive-aihub
description: BeLive AI Hub inference provider with live tool-capable chat model discovery.

name: belive-aihub-media
description: BeLive AI Hub backends for Thor' image_generate, video_generate, text_to_speech and speech-to-text (backend `belive-aihub` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider, tts.provider and stt.provider), with models from the live AI Hub catalogues. Disclosure: registers four backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool runs, the prompt, source images, text to speak or recording go to https://tokenhub-api.belive.sg/api/v1 (or the official staging base set in BELIVE_TOKENHUB_BASE_URL) with BELIVE_TOKENHUB_API_KEY, read through Thor' secret scope, and each call is billed to that AI Hub workspace with no Thor approval prompt; it reads the model catalogues, polls video jobs (up to 15 minutes), stores a video job id and idempotency key under the profile's plugin-data, and reads a local image or recording only when the agent names one. Requests that can charge are sent once and never retried or redirected.

name: bench-rewind
description: An undo history for a physical teardown: record removal steps on your own photos, keep a parts ledger by bag, answer "where does this go?" and reassemble in a valid reverse order. Human-confirmed records only, with native agent tools, a live Desktop page and a printable reassembly packet. Disclosure — no network, model, shell or subprocess use and no telemetry; it reads only an image or kit file the user names (or picks in Desktop) and refuses symlinks; it strips photo metadata (GPS, camera, XMP, text, content credentials) before storing a copy, and keeps projects and photo copies under the profile's plugin-data/bench-rewind/ folder (0700/0600); exported reassembly packets embed the user's photos unless the text-only variant is chosen.

name: benchforge
description: The flight simulator for AI-written Arduino firmware. Describe what the board should do and approve the checks in plain English; BenchForge compiles the sketch with arduino-cli, runs it instruction by instruction on a simulated ATmega328P with simulated sensors, buttons, relays, servos and buzzers, crash-tests it (noisy sensors, button bounce, millis() rollover, a cut sensor wire) and has Thor fix it until every check passes, with a reproducible proof receipt, an animated board GIF and a live browser board. A pre_tool_call flash gate stops the agent flashing any firmware without a passing receipt against checks a person approved. Disclosure — thor bench setup downloads the official arduino-cli 1.4.1 (SHA-256 pinned) from downloads.arduino.cc or GitHub, then the arduino:avr@1.8.6 core and Servo@1.2.2 library through arduino-cli's own package index, and Node.js through Thor's package manager only if it isn't installed; at run time it compiles the model-written sketch on the host with arduino-cli (compile only, in a sealed temp folder with a fixed environment) and runs the firmware in an emulated chip under node (Node's permission model), and makes no network calls; /bench sends the request, bench, sketch and failure details to the user's own model provider through ctx.llm; the "watch it run" link opens the author's GitHub Pages site (ohjay-official.github.io) with the firmware and checks in the URL fragment; writes only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/benchforge (receipts, firmware, drafts kept 7 days, approvals stored as platform plus a hashed user id); the flash gate reads the .hex file an upload command names.

name: benchline
description: Read-only preflight for a selected numeric-result CSV: checks structure, duplicate keys, numeric formatting, and exact analyte/unit-map matches. No clinical interpretation; the selected path, unit-map inputs, profile-source label, and bounded QC report are exposed to the configured model/provider.

name: bento
description: Bento (bentonow.com) email marketing: subscribers, tags, fields, events incl. $purchase, stats, draft/scheduled broadcasts and transactional email, with dry-run + human-approval gates on every send. Native Python plugin, no dependencies. Disclosure — sends real email (bento_email_send, bento_broadcast_schedule), and events, purchases and consent changes can trigger Bento Flows that email people; calls only app.bentonow.com (an operator base_url override is limited to https *.bentonow.com or loopback) with the BENTO_* keys from the profile .env; no telemetry, no self-update; T2/T3 calls go to the Thor approval prompt, which asks no human under YOLO, approvals.mode off, or cron/single-query/unattended mode set to approve. T3 sends then still need a dry-run confirm token and hard guards, but T2 writes (events, purchases, consent, bulk upserts) need no token unless safety.tier2 is token_only; T1 writes (tags, tag/field definitions, drafts, upserts up to bulk_threshold) are never gated and still run under environment=disabled; environment=staging does not block sends, only environment=disabled blocks T2/T3.

name: berrys
description: Turn one product photo into on-brand listing images, campaign visuals and short product videos through Berrys AI's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.berrys.io/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). The agent plans the work on Berrys' visual canvas — hero, lifestyle and detail shots for a storefront, coordinated image sets and copy variants for a campaign, or a storyboarded multi-shot clip that keeps the product identical across cuts by seeding each shot from the previous frame — and the results stay on a shared canvas the user can edit, undo or restore.
