Uses Berrys' curated multi-model image and video stack, so there is no provider key to configure. Bundles the Berrys workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Berrys' hosted server (app.berrys.io) and acts on the user's own Berrys account and credits; the tool set and the playbooks it loads are served by that server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha. Generation spends Berrys credits: the server quotes a price first and every paid generation requires explicit approval in the conversation before it runs. Nothing is published to a marketplace or storefront on the user's behalf — assets are produced on the canvas for the user to download or use. The server signs in with OAuth (Berrys account). The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: better-analyst
description: Convert PDFs such as bank statements, invoices, receipts and reports into Excel workbooks through Better Analyst's hosted MCP server (https://app.betteranalyst.com/api/mcp/connector, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles a pdf-to-excel workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to app.betteranalyst.com and acts on the user's Better Analyst account; PDFs the user uploads or links are sent there for processing. Conversions use the user's AI credits, 10 per page. The tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The server records account, tool name, outcome, latency and client user agent per call, not file contents or arguments. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores the OAuth token under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: better-capabilities
description: Delete and package skills, browse their markdown files, and save per-profile on/off presets from one Settings page. Disclosure — deleting a skill from its page moves the skill folder out of `<THOR_HOME>/skills` (on Windows to the Recycle Bin by running `powershell.exe`, elsewhere to `<THOR_HOME>/better-capabilities-trash/`); applying a preset switches skills, toolsets and agent plugins on or off, including for other profiles the preset names.

name: better-session-appearance
description: Set a color for each session and show an idle glyph to make rows easier to scan.

name: better-tg-cli
description: Telegram on your own account (not a bot) through a local MCP server and a skill: read and search chats, threads, comments and forum topics, press bot buttons, and send, edit, react or forward only after you approve each action. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Runs the `better-tg-cli@0.39.6` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+; no runtime dependencies, downloaded from npm on first start), in the plugin's data folder. Network: Telegram's own servers over MTProto; the project's login service (better-tg-cli.com, API at tg-cli-broker.login-c2d.workers.dev) only while you log in with a login key; a once-a-day version check to registry.npmjs.org only when the CLI runs in your own terminal (never under Thor; off with TG_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1). No telemetry. Login happens once in your own terminal (`npx -y better-tg-cli onboard`), and the skill may install the CLI globally from npm, brew or scoop after asking you; the session and the app's API hash are the CLI's own, stored in its own items in the macOS Keychain, the Linux Secret Service, Windows DPAPI, 1Password (when configured) or a 0600 file in ~/.config/tg, and anyone holding that session controls the Telegram account. It never reads Thor' secrets or another tool's login. mcp.json forwards only DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and the CLI's own TG_PROFILE, TG_READ_ONLY, TG_LOG_LEVEL, TG_FLOOD_WAIT_MAX, TG_TRANSPORT, TG_NO_UPDATE_CHECK; no credential. Tools that change state (send, edit, delete for everyone, react, forward, pin, leave a chat, and saving media or exports to a folder the agent names) go through MCP elicitation, one Allow Once / Deny per action; unattended runs time out and nothing is sent. Writing without asking can only be switched on in a terminal or OS dialog, never over MCP; on Linux without a secret store that setting is a plain 0600 file the agent's terminal could edit. Login, logout and account transfer are not exposed. Every write is logged locally. The server runs its bundled CLI as a child process per tool call. The tool set comes from the pinned npm version.

name: betterdb
description: BetterDB long-term memory provider — semantic recall on Valkey / valkey-search via the betterdb-agent-memory SDK. Completed turns are embedded and stored in a vector index; the next turn recalls the most relevant memories with a composite similarity/recency/importance score. Explicit betterdb_remember / betterdb_recall / betterdb_forget tools. Disclosure — turn text and tool-stored facts are embedded through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint you configure (embeddings_base_url, default api.openai.com) and written to the Valkey instance you point it at; plaintext http:// to a remote host is refused. Opt-in, off by default: a discovery marker (set discovery=true to let BetterDB Monitor enumerate the tier) and SDK usage analytics (set telemetry=true).

name: bharatcode-provider
description: BharatCode (bharatcode.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider — free student tier, native /model integration. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and BHARATCODE_API_KEY go to bharatcode.ai (BharatCode, India), which processes prompts through third-party inference partners, some outside India; outside paid Pro (complimentary or referral Pro included) BharatCode may retain private prompt/response logs for debugging, abuse review and product quality, and even on paid Pro a flagged account can have a time-limited sample of up to 100 prompts and responses captured for security review.

name: bhived
description: Shared lessons for AI agents over MCP: before a task, the agent can look up fixes, known mistakes and API changes that other agents already verified, and write back what it verifies itself. Lessons rise or sink as other agents corroborate or contradict them. Bundles a skill that tells the agent when to query and when to write. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — Disclosure: the server runs locally as `npx -y bhived-mcp@1.4.2` (Apache-2.0), fetched from npm on first run, so the npm package is not covered by the pinned sha. Queries and written lessons go to the bhived API at mcp.bhived.ai, authenticated with BHIVED_API_KEY or the key `npx bhived setup` saves in ~/.bhived/config.json after a browser sign-in. With a personal key a written lesson is public; with a team key it stays private to that team. The optional `npx bhived setup` also adds the bhived MCP server and a bhived instructions block to other agents' user-global config and instruction files it detects (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Continue and others; never Thor or the open project), and later bhived commands refresh that block. Activating a skill or MCP server found on the network starts that capability locally (npx or uvx, plus skill scripts, which get only system variables and the variables the skill declares). The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every write-capable tool (writes, outcome reports, activation, script runs, proxied tool calls) and refuses them in unattended runs; query, inspect and list tools are read-only.

name: bilinc
description: Hosted memory for Thor with a full history: see what your agent remembered, when it changed and why. Recalls relevant memories before each turn, adds bilinc_recall, bilinc_remember, bilinc_revise and bilinc_forget tools, and mirrors Thor built-in memory writes. Maintained by ReARC Labs; free plan available. Disclosure — recall queries (the text of each message, when auto_recall is on), tool arguments, mirrored built-in memory writes, the Thor session id and, only if memory.bilinc.capture_turns is turned on, each turn's user and assistant text are sent over HTTPS to bilinc.space under your BILINC_API_KEY; requests carry User-Agent bilinc-thor/<version> and X-Bilinc-Client: thor-plugin headers. Secret-looking strings are redacted before sending. Recall and writes run on background threads inside Thor; no separate process, local database or telemetry.

name: billing
description: Nous Portal usage widget for the Thor desktop statusbar — remaining credits plus plan-usage percentage, with portal detail on hover.

name: biomimetic-brain
description: Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read THOR_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

name: birdie
description: Lets each Thor conversation message the other AI agents on this machine, such as Claude Code, Codex and Grok, through birdie, a local open-source message bus, and, if you allow it, be woken by their messages. Each conversation gets its own address, so an answer comes back to the conversation that asked. Five tools: list agents, send, check the inbox, wait for a reply, read a thread. Disclosure: talks only to the local birdie service (http://127.0.0.1:7777 by default), with no telemetry or third-party calls of its own, though agents connected to birdie may be online services that receive what is sent to them; a background thread per active conversation reports it to birdie every 30 seconds, including its working folder's name and full path, which agents connected to birdie can see, and with waking on another waits for new messages; waking is off by default and, when turned on with `birdie setup thor --wake`, lets any agent connected to birdie start a turn, which spends model credits and can use tools under the usual approval rules, and sets allow_gateway_injection for this plugin; Thor stores this agent's birdie token as the BIRDIE_THOR_TOKEN secret, which the user gives it; `birdie setup thor`, run by the user, writes birdie.json in the plugin folder, changes Thor settings only through Thor's own commands (enables the plugin, removes any old birdie MCP server, sets the waking permission when asked) and backs up config.yaml first; it never writes Thor's .env.

name: birkin-mnemosyne
description: Local Markdown memory provider with multilingual lexical recall and profile-local durable notes. Writes are limited to primary agent contexts: create-only notes plus preview-by-default archive and restore, which never delete files. Uses published birkin-mnemosyne 0.9.0 with compatible updates below 1.0; no API key, network service or telemetry. Session handoff capture is opt-in. Native Thor memory files remain separate.

name: birta
description: Artifacts for Thor. Birta is a shared workspace where people and agents turn drafts into finished work: Thor publishes a website, HTML page, landing page, portfolio, report, docs or slide deck at a link you can share, and people leave feedback right on the page. With mention events on, @mention Thor in a comment and it picks the request up on its own: makes the change, replies in the thread and publishes the next version. Disclosure — hosted-only: every tool call goes to birta.dev and acts on your Birta projects; publishing makes a version visible at the project address; optional mention events (off unless you set `events: true` and run the webhook gateway, and approved per subscription) let anyone who @mentions Thor in your Birta review threads start an unattended agent run.

name: blackbox
description: Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `thor blackbox setup` (also started by the Set up button on Blackbox's Thor Desktop page) installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), joins the DKG peer-to-peer network, and asks the threat graph's owner to admit the node (its node address; admission to sync only, not sharing); package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Thor homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `thor blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700, and the Thor Desktop page reaches it through Blackbox's own Desktop routes, which also hold the audit/block switch; in block mode Blackbox refuses an agent's attempts to change its settings or disable it.

name: blastradius
description: Reads a destructive shell command before it runs and reports what it would actually delete: how many files, how many git can restore, how many it cannot, the total size, and which of them look valuable, then lets policy decide whether to show the report, block the call, or demand a one-shot blast_allow. Covers rm and rm -rf, git clean, git reset --hard, truncate -s 0, `> file` and `: >` truncating redirects, and mv overwrite, including nested bash -c, subshells, and chained commands with cd tracking; anything it cannot resolve is reported as unmeasured instead of guessed. Snapshots and verified restore exist as a separate step (blast_snapshot, blast_restore); restore skips files edited after the snapshot unless overwrite_conflicts is set. Disclosure - no network; reads file metadata, directory listings, and the output of read-only git calls (git ls-files, git check-ignore, git rev-parse); writes snapshot copies under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/; strict policy blocks the tool call while balanced and relaxed report and continue; local terminal backend only; no telemetry. Disclosure — no network and no telemetry; on every terminal call it reads file metadata, directory listings and the output of read-only git calls (git ls-files, git check-ignore, git rev-parse); it writes snapshot copies under the Thor plugin data dir (or BLASTRADIUS_SNAPSHOT_DIR), and blast_restore with confirm writes snapshotted files back to their original paths, skipping files edited since unless overwrite_conflicts is set; its blocks add to Thor approval and never replace it, and the agent can relax them through blast_policy or a one-shot blast_allow (BLASTRADIUS_ALLOW=1 turns them off); local terminal backend only.

name: blazephoenix
description: Swap quotes from BlazePhoenix, the on-chain DEX aggregator, measured on the user's own RPC and verified locally: net output, Phoenix Check verdict and unsigned Router calldata checked field by field before anything is signed. Base, Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum, Robinhood Chain. Disclosure: HTTPS calls to blazephoenix.xyz (prepare/decode, pure, no RPC; receives token addresses, amount, recipient and minimum, never the RPC URL) and eth_chainId/eth_call to the RPC URL the user sets. Never signs, never sends, never handles keys; no shell, no files, no background processes, no telemetry. Standard library only.

name: blender
description: Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Needs Git and uv; Blender 5.1+ is not needed at install. The skill opens Blender itself when a task needs it and, after you agree, installs Blender and Blender Lab's MCP add-on. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; the skill starts Blender with online access for that session only (your saved preference is unchanged), and the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password, so any program on this computer can use it while Blender is open; only after you agree does the skill download Blender from download.blender.org (about 400 MB, about 1.5 GB unpacked), check it against blender.org's sha256 list and install it in your own folder without administrator rights (Linux ~/.local/opt, macOS ~/Applications, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation; never over an existing Blender), and download the v1.0.3 add-on, check its hash and install or enable it; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.

name: blind-accessibility-reader
description: Describes the images and videos on any website for blind and low vision people, through their screen reader or an AI voice. A bundled Chrome extension outlines the image or video you're on, and Thor sends it to a vision model through OpenRouter. Auto mode describes as you scroll and narrates videos as they play; manual mode waits for a shortcut. A daily limit and a per-video limit keep the cost in check. Disclosure — runs a local server on 127.0.0.1:47823 that answers only the bundled extension; the bundled Chrome extension has access to all sites and fetches page images without cookies; sends downscaled images and video frames to the vision model configured for its auxiliary task (OpenRouter by default) using the key held by Thor; fetches OpenRouter's public price list with no key.

name: blindcouncil
description: Private human decisions in Thor with authenticated responses, deterministic rules and durable recovery. Disclosure — runs inside the Thor Telegram gateway: adds its own button and /bcprobe handlers to the bot, and a background delivery task that sends decision invitations and results through your bot to the two configured participant Telegram IDs (both must be in TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS); each participant's vote is stored in a local SQLite file in the plugin data folder, which the host operator can read.

name: blindoracle
description: Ask whether an AI agent is safe to pay before you pay it: free trust badge and reputation lookup (5 a day, no wallet, no account), the live price list for BlindOracle research, security-audit and due-diligence services, key-free receipt verification and a proof-of-delegation skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — crypto payments: the MCP server is remote (https://api.craigmbrown.com/v1/mcp, operated by the author) and receives each tool name and its arguments; its paid tools charge when called with an x402 USDC payment on Base or a BlindOracle starter-credit note, and the package marks the server trust: untrusted so Thor asks before each call; the package itself signs or sends no payment; the receipt skill runs a stdlib python3 script on a file you provide and calls the public Base RPC (mainnet.base.org) only when given a tx hash; the delegation skill can register a BlindOracle agent account, which returns an API key, only after you explicitly agree to its terms. No background processes or telemetry.

name: blinkenbar
description: Dense, animated supercomputer light banks driven by system telemetry and live agent activity in Thor Desktop.

name: bluff
description: Does your model make things up? Bluff asks about things that sound real but don't exist (Python functions, built-in exceptions, chemical elements), mixed with real ones and phrased as if they all exist, and checks whether the model admits the made-up ones aren't real. The result is a bluff rate, with real items as a control. Every item is checkable by machine, so no model judges another. Runs on your active model through ctx.llm, no setup.

name: board-insights
description: Read-only analytics page for the Thor Kanban boards, in Desktop. Two views over every board: List shows what is in flight, what is waiting on a person and every unfinished card in one filterable list; Dashboard shows summary counters, completed over time with a moving average, workload by status, net flow, tasks by department, cycle and run medians, stale runs and a per-assignee table, driven by one date range (today, 7, 30 or a custom window up to 90 days). Spaces are named board sets saved locally so the page can read one project or all of them. Disclosure — opens every kanban.db under the Kanban home with SQLite mode=ro and has no write path; writes only its own stored Spaces and date range in the plugin's storage; no tools, no hooks, no model calls, no network calls, no credentials, no background processes.

name: boardloop
description: Thor writes ESP32 and Arduino code, compiles it with arduino-cli, tests it in the Wokwi simulator (sets sensor values, presses buttons, checks pins, serial output and OLED screenshots), fixes it within bounded attempts, and flashes real boards with approval. Disclosure — runs the user-installed arduino-cli and wokwi-cli as subprocesses (no shell, with timeouts); wokwi-cli sends compiled firmware and the circuit diagram to Wokwi's cloud using the user's Wokwi CI token (stored as a Thor secret) and uses their Wokwi simulation minutes; arduino-cli may download cores and libraries on request; flashing a board and writing to a serial port always go through Thor's approval prompt; projects, run folders, screenshots and history are stored in the plugin data directory; no telemetry.

name: boardroomlist
description: Read-only MCP server and skill: search open senior roles (Manager to CEO) at the 500 largest US companies by seniority, function, work mode, place and pay. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to the public read-only MCP server at boardroomlist.com (https://boardroomlist.com/api/mcp), which only reads published role listings; results are summaries without the company name, full description or apply link, which the site shows to members on the role page. No sign-in, no key, nothing written, no local commands. The package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: boardstate
description: From one ask, your agent builds a live board of KPIs, tables, charts and live Thor data, then keeps it current as your plans change. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Thor Desktop; the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included, and binds sessions, usage and cron widgets to live Thor data. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/THOR_NODE_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under THOR_HOME/boardstate-state/. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from Thor internals (web_server._SESSION_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. boardstate_workspace_get also returns the text users type into Notes cards (read-only). No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

name: bonsai-garden
description: A live isometric bonsai garden for Thor Desktop: every profile on the roster is one bonsai on a drawn shelf, the focused busy agent's tree steps down onto a stand and returns to its exact shelf slot when it goes idle, and clicking any drawn tree opens that agent's conversation, exactly like its roster row; a monk walks its stretch of garden from elapsed time — drifting slowly at rest, faster while its agent is busy — and a cat spawns at random and can be dragged. Four opaque black plaques carry local time, local date, recurring agent routines and reported session cost, and can be dragged anywhere over the drawing, while each agent row opens that agent's conversation or stops its live session. Season and month come from the local clock in English, with one care line per month shipped inside the artwork, and every pot is signed with the agent's name and shipped avatar; the interface is English throughout. Disclosure — the page talks to the host only through the plugin SDK: it subscribes to the host's focused-session atoms (busy state, profile, session id, reported usage cost and tokens), asks each profile's own gateway cron store for its recurring jobs on demand (cron.manage list, scoped per profile), reads the focused session's own title metadata through session.info, and calls session.interrupt only when the user presses Stop. Reported cost is shown as reported; when only tokens are available a cost line marked with a tilde is estimated at one documented blended rate and the README says so, and unreported cost stays Unavailable rather than a fabricated zero. It reads no message content and no transcript, makes no outbound network requests of its own (every read goes through the host's own SDK socket), needs no credentials and no environment variables, installs nothing and patches no Thor core file. Derived from office-3d (listed): same isometric-room idea and the same MIT lineage, but a materially different implementation and behaviour — one bonsai per agent on a shelf grid measured on the artwork instead of desks and a cost leaderboard, no Python backend, no agent tool, no CLI-wide monitoring and no login backend.

name: booking-bridge
description: Find free time, then book, list, reschedule and cancel real Google Calendar consults (for example a Strategy consult) from Thor. Signs in with the user's own Google OAuth client through thor auth add booking-bridge:google; all calls go through credentialed_provider_request to www.googleapis.com only. Disclosure: network calls to Google Calendar API v3 only (scopes calendar.events and calendar.freebusy); write tools (book, reschedule, cancel) change the user's calendar, can email invitations to listed attendees, and are sent to Thor' own approval gate by a pre_tool_call hook (action approve), so Thor asks the user first and by default denies the call in cron, single-query and one-shot runs, webhook-style platforms and CLI sub-agents; they also require confirm=true and refuse, changing nothing, outside an allowlist of platforms and sources (interactive CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP and the chat platforms Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WhatsApp Cloud, Signal, Mattermost, Matrix, BlueBubbles), so cron, single-query, kanban, webhook-style, email, SMS and any unrecognized platform or source are refused; booked events carry a private hash property to prevent duplicates; revoke with thor auth logout booking-bridge:google; no shell commands, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

name: borealwork
description: Give Thor verified human hands: hire a verified person on boreal.work for a step no agent can do online (confirm a supplier is real, check a shelf price, photograph a site), with the money held until the result passes review against your criteria and a public rulebook. Twelve native tools for the task loop; a spend guard (pre_tool_call) that sends every money-moving call (funding at any amount, accepting a pass, judging a result yourself) to Thor's approval prompt, enforces per-task and daily caps on funding, and blocks terminal payments that aren't paying a boreal.work task; a verdict digest (pre_llm_call) that tells Thor what finished since it last looked; and /borealwork. With --yolo or approvals.mode: off Thor approves these calls without asking, and only the caps apply. Disclosure — HTTPS to the configured boreal.work site only (https://boreal.work by default, live PayPal money; testnet.boreal.work for the sandbox), from tool calls, from the spend guard (a task read before funding, accepting or judging, and the account's last-24-hour spend before funding) and from the digest (one task list on a session's first turn); every funding, acceptance and self-judged verdict asks through Thor approval, and funding is also capped at max_task_usd (default $10) per task and max_daily_usd (default $50) per day; with --yolo or approvals.mode: off Thor approves these calls without asking and only the caps apply; the guard also blocks terminal NEAR/USDC transfer commands that do not carry a boreal:<taskId> memo; stores the boreal.work agent key it collects in plaintext in its own plugin state, or reads BOREAL_API_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no self-updates, no compiled code; standard library only.

name: borrowed-hands
description: Lend your Mac's Xcode to a cloud Thor. Thor finds your paired Mac, compiles the Xcode project you granted (macOS arm64 or generic iOS Simulator, compile only) at an exact commit on a bh/* branch, and gets structured compiler diagnostics back: ask "Build my demo project on my Mac", or have Thor edit a repository with its own git tools, build its bh/* branch, fix what the compiler reports and check with `hands_job` `check_pr_ready` before it opens a pull request (the plugin never pushes, opens pull requests or holds GitHub credentials). Needs the separate Borrowed Hands Mac helper (Python source in the same repository) on an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode; the Mac connects out to Thor and decides what may build. Disclosure — when `listen.enabled` is set (off by default) the plugin runs an HTTP/WebSocket listener inside `thor gateway run` (default bind `0.0.0.0:8790`, routes `/bh/v1/ws` and an unauthenticated `/bh/v1/healthz`) that paired Macs dial into; connections are authenticated by a single-use pairing code and per-device Ed25519 keys. It keeps a server signing key and a SQLite database (paired device keys, signed job contracts, build diagnostics, audit log) in its plugin data dir; anything the agent can reach on the gateway host can read that key, and a holder of it can sign build requests to paired Macs within their grants. For a build with no commit it makes one anonymous HTTPS read of the granted public repository's branch list (public addresses only, no credentials, no redirects). With `check_pr_ready` it makes one more such read, for that build's repository. It registers one read-only skill, `borrowed-hands:xcode-build-pr` (text only: the order to use the tools in), and its system prompt section tells the agent to run the bundled standard-library script `templates/new_swiftui_app.py` with its own shell tool to write a new Xcode project into its working directory (no process, no network, nothing overwritten). `/hands whoami`, in a DM, tells any sender their own platform:user_id and nothing else. Builds ask for Thor approval; an "always" answer covers the same Mac, workspace, scheme, configuration and destination but not the commit or branch, so later commits build without a new prompt. The separate Mac helper is installed by the user from the repository, is not covered by this catalog pin, and installs a LaunchAgent, a hidden build user, a root-owned dispatcher and a sudo rule limited to six exact dispatcher commands. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: bot-activity
description: Live per-Bot activity timeline for Thor Desktop: turns, tool calls (arguments, result, duration), approvals and Group Chat streams, grouped by Bot or by Group Chat, with one-click tracking for new Bots. Disclosure — local only, no network or telemetry; records every Bot profile's turns, assistant replies, tool arguments and results, approval commands and Group Chat streams (redacted with agent.redact, capped per field, 3-day / 20k-row retention) into one SQLite file shared by all profiles under plugin-data/bot-activity; reads each Bot profile's state.db, profile.yaml and config.yaml read-only; Track now / Update runs `thor -p <bot> plugins install <same source> --ref <same sha> --enable --yes-deps` (or copies the plugin and runs `plugins enable`) in the Bot profiles you track, never re-enabling one you disabled.

name: bot-cabinet-v2
description: Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a Thor profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that Thor's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates Thor profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.thor/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private Thor modules (thor_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a Thor update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

name: bot-chat-agent
description: Thor Bots: a calmer Thor Bot Chat that still does the work: short agentic replies, a block-only safety guard, a Desktop status card, mid-turn asks that are no longer dropped, background results delivered back to the same chat, a local short-term / long-term memory (decisions, project state, lessons; /memoria) with no API keys, and an opt-in panteón: Thor may offer in one line to create a specialist bot and creates it only after your yes. Other sessions untouched. Disclosure — in sessions titled "Bot Chat" (and their subagent children) it injects a reply-style instruction, a bounded context / memory block, pending-ask reminders and (Desktop half enabled) a one-line specialist offer; blocks tool calls matching its rules (secrets, deletes, destructive git, protected-branch pushes, outbound messages, expensive models, kanban-lock bypasses, obfuscated exec, memory-injection) and, when team.assignees is configured, rewrites kanban_create arguments to add serialization parents and the teammate assignment; wraps tool output that looks like a prompt injection in an "untrusted data" label; it never approves anything. It opens <THOR_HOME>/state.db, <THOR_HOME>/kanban.db and <THOR_HOME>/cron/executions.db (plus cron output files) read-only; writes plugin-local files under <THOR_HOME>/bot-chat-agent/ (memory.db, deliveries.db, status.json, panteon-auto.json, dm-delegations.json, optional project-card.md) and its own team.assignees plugin setting; registers /memoria, /botmemory, /panteon and /pantheon; serves a small dashboard API at /api/plugins/bot-chat-agent; the Desktop half (opt-in in Capabilities → Plugins) calls the app's own profiles.create / profiles.configure for ONE preset profile, only after the user's explicit yes; changes the Desktop reasoning.collapsedByDefault setting while a Bot Chat is focused and restores it on leave/disable; makes no third-party network calls, no telemetry and no credential reads. Background work uses Thor kanban / the gateway dispatcher when team.assignees is configured; on Thor 0.23, results are offered into the next turn. A ContextEngine named bot-chat is registered but off until context.engine: bot-chat is set.

name: bot-dashboard
description: Two desktop panes in one plugin. Bot shows the focused bot's dashboard - profile and model, scheduled jobs, notes, the custom widgets that bot pinned for you, and optional tasks and projects from a markdown notes vault you point it at in the plugin settings; Group shows a group chat's members, activity, shared tasks and projects, and follows a group chat you open. Ships two agent tools in its own bot_dashboard toolset - bot_panel edits the bot's own panel, group_dashboard lets any member bot read or shape a group's dashboard - plus a pre_llm_call hook that adds a short panel snapshot on the first turn only (and an optional per-turn instruction, empty unless the user writes one). Disclosure - reads the local Thor home (bot profiles, config.yaml, group room records) and, only if the user sets vault_path, markdown notes in that folder; writes only each bot's own panel files (widgets, notes, layout) under its profile and, when the user creates or ticks a task, that task's note in the configured vault folder. Widgets render in a sandboxed opaque-origin frame with a no-network Content-Security-Policy. The panes talk to the Thor API on 127.0.0.1, with no third-party network calls, no shell commands and no stored credentials. Disclosure — reads the local Thor home (every bot profile's profile.yaml, config.yaml, SOUL.md, skills list and avatar, plus the gateway's group-room tables in state.db/shared-state.db, read-only) and, only if the user sets vault_path, markdown notes in that folder; the bot_panel/group_dashboard tools can copy any .html file the model names into a widget, and any bot can edit any local group's dashboard; writes only panel files (widgets, notes, layout) under each bot's profile and under plugin-data/bot-dashboard/groups, plus, when the user creates or ticks a task, that task's note in the configured vault folder; widgets render in a sandboxed opaque-origin frame with a no-network Content-Security-Policy; an optional panel_rule setting (empty by default) adds the user's own instruction to every turn; no third-party network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials.

name: bot-drops
description: Share a Thor bot as a link and a card, and adopt bots other people share as new profiles. A preview shows the bot's card, what it needs, the full text of each scheduled task and what was left out before anything is installed; adopting runs Thor' own profile install on the exact reviewed commit and never changes existing profiles. Sharing packages the personality, the author's own text skills and any scheduled tasks (name, task text, schedule and skills only, arriving paused), renders a link card and a story image locally, and publishes them as a new public GitHub repository with a GitHub Pages bot page. Disclosure — a preview clones a public GitHub or GitLab repository over HTTPS with size, time and file limits and never installs anything; adopting creates a new profile through Thor' own profile install with the shared bot's scheduled tasks paused. Publishing runs git and the user's own gh login to create a new PUBLIC GitHub repository and GitHub Pages page, only after an explicit confirmation in the plugin screen; the shared package holds the personality, the author's own text skills, the model provider/name and scheduled tasks (name, task text, schedule and skill names only). Keys, settings, memory, chats, plugins, MCP servers, Skills Hub skills and the delivery targets, scripts, folders and endpoints of scheduled tasks are never shared. Shared pages and cards carry a "by BrainArts" credit link to the author's X profile that the sharer can turn off. No telemetry, self-updater or background process.

name: bot-forge
description: Say "make me a <role>" and your agent spawns a complete Bot Mode Bot — name, face, SOUL.md, memory, tools, skills, routines, gateway — tested, with rollback. Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. Disclosure — spawns the thor CLI to create and run Bot profiles under THOR_HOME/profiles/, and installs its own small companion hook plugin (bot-forge-marks, two hooks, no tools) into each Bot profile it manages, enabling it in that profile's config.yaml; never the root profile. Disclosure — when a Bot journals a blocked/failed entry, the plugin emails its title and summary to your own address via the SMTP account in Thor' EMAIL_* settings (TLS verified; off with notify_blocked or notify_email false); adopt_bots (off by default) installs the companion hook into every profile on load.

name: bot-shelf
description: Search Bot Shelf (botshelf.dev), a directory of 9,000+ community Grok Bots, by the job in plain words, with each creator credited, through Bot Shelf's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.botshelf.dev/mcp, no account or key). Bundles the bot-shelf skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Bot Shelf's hosted server (mcp.botshelf.dev, on Cloudflare); the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. find_bots, get_bot, latest and list_categories only read the public directory; suggest_bot sends the link, note and name the user gives to a review queue kept up to 30 days. Searches are not stored.

name: botsee
description: AI-visibility research through BotSee's hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (https://botsee.io/mcp), with a bounded workflow skill for reviewing existing analyses, competitor recommendations and cited sources, and planning audits. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package; no local server, OAuth bridge, hooks or self-updater. Disclosure — every tool call goes to BotSee's hosted MCP server at botsee.io with the user's own BotSee API key (MCP_BOTSEE_API_KEY, sent as a bearer header), and the tool set is served by that remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; some BotSee tools spend account credits, generate billable content or top up the balance (including USDC payments), and the package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses those tools in cron and headless runs, which relies on BotSee's own read-only annotations; no spending cap is enforced.

name: bounded-results
description: Bounded tool outputs with hash-addressed full-result retrieval. Disclosure — rewrites what the model sees for six tools (`evidence_history`, `evidence_compare`, `evidence_as_of`, `evidence_verify_support`, `evaluation_report`, `memory_search`): results over 4 KB are replaced by a preview and a hash, and the full text is kept in a local SQLite file under the profile's plugin-data directory with no automatic deletion. It only has an effect when a plugin providing those tools is installed. Nothing leaves the machine.

name: boxcompute
description: Give Thor its own cloud Linux VMs through the hosted BoxCompute MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR): create and start VMs, run commands and background processes, read and edit files under /workspace, and open one-hour public preview links, with the sandboxes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.boxcompute.ai, and commands and files run in the user's BoxCompute VMs, not on their machine. A running VM spends the user's BoxCompute credit per minute until it stops (it stops itself 30 minutes after its last command, file or preview call); preview_create makes a URL anyone can open for one hour; sandbox_delete permanently removes a VM and its files; email_send emails only the account owner's own address. Thor itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the boxcompute MCP server. No telemetry. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `thor mcp add boxcompute --url https://mcp.boxcompute.ai/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

name: brain-graph
description: Local Markdown vault for Thor Desktop — notes, wikilinks, search, recycle bin, and an interactive graph.

name: brainvault
description: Memory you own for Thor, by Wave OS. Thor remembers on this computer right away, and a pasted page becomes memory cards. You mint the ones worth keeping to your own wallet's vault on the Theta blockchain with one approval in Wave Web (private by default, encrypted to you and this Thor), and any Thor you pair reads them back, fingerprint-checked. Ask Wavey answers Wave questions from chain-verified public cards. Disclosure — never signs, mints or holds wallet keys: minting happens on web.oswave.io, approved in the Wave Wallet Mint browser extension, and costs a one-time TFUEL network fee. Network calls go only to web.oswave.io (your vault's card index, sending your public wallet address; one-time end-to-end encrypted drops for pairing and Send to Wave, with the key kept in the link fragment; Wavey's public cards) and Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only card reads and gas price). Stores a decrypt-only, wallet-revocable agent key in the OS keyring if installed, else a 0600 file in $THOR_HOME/brainvault; reads Thor's config.yaml only for its setup check, and Thor's plugin list (names and versions, never sent anywhere) to show which Wave plugins you have. A background thread syncs every 10 minutes. Opens Wave Web in the browser for pairing and minting. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating. Recall runs locally; recalled memories reach the user's model provider like any context.

name: branchpoint
description: Explore the same task with 2-8 independent agent plans (default 4), optionally on different models. Build selected routes in isolated Git worktrees (default top 2), compare them with three blind reviewers and an evidence-linked decision record, then adopt or converge their ideas into another candidate. Includes a loopback live view, decision log, rewind anchors and reversible adoption. Disclosure — Branchpoint spawns git and up to 8 headless Thor agents (file tools only, your configured model and credentials) in git worktrees it creates in your repository, writes branches, snapshots and refs/branchpoint/ there (a snapshot on every prompt unless anchor_on_turn is off), and changes your working tree only when you run /branchpoint adopt. It runs your project's test, lint and type commands, including code the agents wrote, inside a bubblewrap or sandbox-exec sandbox (no network, home masked, allowlisted env), and refuses real builds without a sandbox unless you pass --unsafe-checks. Goal, source excerpts and route ledgers go to your configured model with best-effort secret scrubbing. A live view is served on 127.0.0.1 behind a token.

name: brave-search
description: Brave Search API tools for live web search inside Thor

name: breadcrumbs
description: Memory and a context engine in which every line has an address. Each turn, tool step and tool result is a crumb in a content-addressed, append-only store (CRC32C ids, Merkle commits). One tool, crumb(id, level), shows any memory from a one-line handle (0) to its exact bytes (1). crumb_find searches with BM25: no vectors, no model. Each recall, find, open and fold writes a record of what the model saw. With context.engine breadcrumbs, a long chat folds into a layer of crumbs with no model call, and the model opens any folded turn by its id. /island gives each codebase its own profile. A read-only explorer shows the sessions, the zoom and the context of each turn. Disclosure — Every turn, tool step and tool result is stored word for word, append-only, in $THOR_HOME/breadcrumbs/, with a usage.log of ids, model names and token counts for every model request (BREADCRUMBS_USAGE_LOG=0 turns it off). When config.json lists hive peers, crumb_find queries go to those peers and crumb fetches blobs from them. An optional background thread runs your local llama-completion binary on a local GGUF model after a span or session closes, with a minimal environment (BREADCRUMBS_SUMMARIZE=0 turns it off). Per-model request options you set in config.json are merged into chat-completions requests. The dashboard and log views read config.yaml and state.db of your profiles read-only, the memory slot setup writes non-secret values to config.yaml, and the `slot` command sets memory.provider through `thor config set`. When a chat starts in a terminal, the plugin opens its read-only, token-protected explorer once per process (a split in cmux, tmux, WezTerm or Kitty, else your default browser, on 127.0.0.1; BREADCRUMBS_VIZ=0 turns it off), and /viz opens it on demand.

name: breeze-tts
description: Breeze Blue text-to-speech as a Thor voice provider (tts.provider: breeze-blue), driven by the Breeze Blue Developer API. Voices come from the Breeze console — stock, cloned or designed — and the provider speaks whole replies through text_to_speech and read-aloud, with mp3 (default), wav, flac, opus, aac or pcm output, so Opus voice notes work on messaging platforms. No new Python dependencies: the plugin posts directly to the ElevenLabs-shaped endpoint. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice id and model, and your BREEZE_API_KEY (header xi-api-key) to api.breeze.blue, or to BREEZE_BASE_URL when you set it; synthesis is billed to your Breeze Blue account; generated audio is written to Thor's audio cache; the text is not logged; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry. Not implemented: realtime/WebSocket streaming (voice-mode replies are spoken sentence by sentence instead) and voice listing.

name: brethof-brain
description: brethof-brain long-term memory provider — the memory's briefing in the system prompt at session start, ambient recall on every turn, every turn archived; one memory shared with the user's other agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more). Sends each turn to the user's own brethof-brain memory (on their machine at 127.0.0.1:8610, or hosted at memory.brethof.cloud). Needs a brethof-brain account. Disclosure — sends every user prompt and each turn's user and assistant text, with your API key, to the brethof-brain server you configure (default a local box at 127.0.0.1:8610; hosted at memory.brethof.cloud), and puts the server's returned briefing and recall text into the system prompt and each turn; reads BRETHOF_BRAIN_* from $THOR_HOME/.env and ~/.brethof-brain/config.json.

name: brickfact
description: Find LEGO sets, compare regional retailer offers and inspect recorded retail price history with Brickfact. Supports nine delivery markets. Portable Agent Plugin with a public Streamable HTTP MCP server and shopping workflow skill. Disclosure — tool calls send shopping inputs (search text, market, set IDs, budgets) to mcp.brickfact.com; an optional Python standard-library helper makes the same calls when run explicitly; the hosted service records aggregate operational counts (see its privacy policy); results link to Brickfact comparison pages containing disclosed affiliate links. No account access, purchases, background processes or locally stored credentials.

name: bridge-adapter
description: Generic JSON-file-based bridge adapter. Bridges self-register via a registry/ manifest (presence = registered, rm = unregistered). Polls inbox/ for incoming messages, writes outgoing to outbox/. External services (imsg, Matrix, Telegram, ...) write/read JSON files in a shared directory.

name: briq
description: Run Thor' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a briq sandbox, a microVM with its own disk, instead of on this machine. Select it with terminal.backend: briq. Disclosure — every command and file operation is sent over HTTPS to the briq API (https://api.briq.cloud, or the URL in BRIQ_API_URL) and runs inside the sandbox; Thor' file sync uploads the credential, skill and cache files it syncs for every remote backend to that sandbox; the sandbox has outbound network access; a sandbox the plugin creates is billed to the briq account of the key and sleeps when idle (terminal.briq_sleep); at cleanup it is stopped and kept with its disk when container_persistent is true (the default), its id recorded in a small JSON file under the Thor sandbox directory so the next session reuses it, or destroyed when it is false. The API key is read only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret (BRIQ_API_KEY), is stripped from the environment of every command, and is never written to disk or logged. The plugin sends no environment variables into the sandbox and makes no network calls other than to the briq API. It imports private Thor modules for its environment base classes (tools.environments.base, base_output and file_sync), as the built-in remote backends do.

name: brownout
description: Power-cut guard for the machine Thor runs on. When mains power drops it messages you (Telegram or any thor send target) with the battery level, measures the real drain and sends a runway, and on /brownout park (or by itself at critical battery if you don't answer) pauses active cron jobs and blocks new tool calls with a pre_tool_call hook. When power is back it resumes only the jobs it paused and tells you. Nothing is killed or deleted; it stops the next tool call, not one already running. Undelivered alerts are retried in order. Disclosure — one daemon thread per Thor home polls power every poll_seconds (default 15) by running `pmset -g batt` (macOS), reading /sys/class/power_supply (Linux) or running `upsc` (NUT UPS, opt-in); alerts go out by running the documented `thor send --to <notify_target> --file -` CLI with a 30 s timeout, using the gateway's own credentials. No network calls of its own, no credentials read, no telemetry. Writes only to <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/brownout/ (events log, state, command queue, watcher lock).

name: browser-toggle
description: One titlebar button, next to HUD mode, that opens and hides the built-in browser: the same action as Ctrl+Shift+L. Label follows the active UI language. Front-end only: no agent calls, no network, no API keys. Disclosure — works by pressing the browser shortcut (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+L); breaks if the user rebinds it.

name: browser-viewer
description: Live view and human takeover of the browser Thor drives: stream its tabs to a web page on another device and click, type and scroll yourself to log in, pass 2FA or a CAPTCHA. Disclosure — starts a detached aiohttp server that listens on explicit IPv4 addresses (loopback plus the Tailscale address if tailscale is installed; never 0.0.0.0), over plain HTTP by default or HTTPS when the user opts in with thor browser-viewer tls (tailscale cert contacts the Tailscale control plane and Let's Encrypt, and the machine name appears in public Certificate Transparency logs); login links are single-use (10 minutes) and are exchanged for an HttpOnly session cookie (7 days by default, Secure over HTTPS), and the start and link actions return such links to the session transcript; launches Chromium with a persistent profile (cookies and logins) and CDP on 127.0.0.1, which makes its usual background connections; the server and Chromium get a minimal environment, not the Thor one (proxy settings and desktop-session variables are passed on); runs chromium --version, tailscale ip -4, tailscale status and tailscale cert (HTTPS mode only) and thor config set|unset browser.cdp_url (the use action changes browser.cdp_url for every session of the profile, and browser_exec then acts with that browser's logins); status and list return each tab's origin and a truncated title to the session transcript; reads /proc and /proc/net/tcp on Linux (the same process facts through psutil on macOS) and Chromium builds under the Thor tools directory; no telemetry from the plugin. Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon).

name: browserless
description: Run Thor' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Thor' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-thor-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.

name: browserpaw
description: Drive your own Chrome from Thor through a BrowserPaw MCP server you configure: 16 browserpaw_* tools for navigation, indexed DOM reading, click/fill, batch actions, screenshots and tabs. Disclosure — a thin wrapper over a BrowserPaw MCP server you add yourself (mcp_servers.browserpaw, plus plugins.entries.browserpaw.mcp_allowlist: [browserpaw]); it drives your real Chrome profile (logged-in sessions, cookies) through the separately installed BrowserPaw extension and native host on 127.0.0.1:12306, whose credential lives in ~/.chrome-mcp/bridge-token; the agent can click, fill, submit and read pages without a Thor approval prompt unless you set trust: untrusted on that server (the README sample enables the full 50-tool profile, including in-page JavaScript, HttpOnly cookie reads and raw CDP, as native Thor MCP tools); the optional Jev remote mode sends structured page state to TypeSafe AI or a base URL you set, and its local model download contacts hf-mirror.com/aifasthub.com/huggingface.co (probing baidu.com/bilibili.com first).

name: browsersolver
description: Fetch web pages behind Cloudflare, DataDome and similar protections for the built-in web_extract tool, through the BrowserSolver web unlocker API. Extract only; pair it with a search backend for web_search. Disclosure — sends each URL to api.browsersolver.com with your BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY so BrowserSolver fetches the page past Cloudflare, DataDome and similar bot protection; the default engine is webunlocker, the most expensive tier, and calls use BrowserSolver credits (set engine to crawler or rendering for cheaper fetches). Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers no tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: bsc-mint-guard
description: Safety-check a BSC ERC-721 free mint before you mint. Read-only on-chain reads, no keys, no signing, no spending. Disclosure — read-only on-chain lookups: the contract and wallet addresses you check are sent to third-party public BSC RPC providers (bsc.meowrpc.com, bsc-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, rpc-bsc.48.club, bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org); no keys, signing or transactions.

name: btw-studio
description: Side-channel /btw workspace, $0 read-only SQLite session radar, and Δτ steer playbook for Thor Desktop, CLI, Gateway, and Dashboard. Intercepts /btw mid-turn in the composer (with attachments, opt-in voice STT/TTS, and @session context) to render Markdown answers in a strip, popover, floating pane, or dialog without mutating the transcript or L0 prompt cache. Reads state.db?mode=ro at $0 for token/cache metrics, AST syntax checks, 10 loop-guard detectors, and cross-session file write conflicts, steers conversation_id-stable turns or child subagents mid-flight, formats output via a 6-axis reading lens ([0,1]^6), and retains only rules verified by 3-call Δτ behavioral contrast in BTW.md. Disclosure — registers 12 observer-only hooks returning None, a btw-studio.verified-playbook system-prompt section (lite/full modes), the BTW_CONVERSATION_ID session env, auxiliary tasks btw_studio_fast and btw_studio_title calling the user's own model via ctx.llm (redacted <=32 KB session digest; optional fast_base_url restricted to https:// or loopback, no redirects), 57 dashboard routes under /api/plugins/btw-studio/, 14 CLI subcommands, 12 gateway RPCs and 8 Desktop host RPCs. Reads $THOR_HOME/state.db read-only (sibling profiles' state.db only when scan_sibling_profiles is on), curator logs, .git/HEAD, config.yaml, MEMORY.md, up to 8 cwd-confined edited .py/.json files (parsed, never run) and denylisted workspace attachments. Off by default: allow_web_search (web_search/web_extract/browser_exec), allow_media_tools, wake_word_enabled, live_voice_enabled, tts_auto_speak, memory_md_sync_mode, scan_sibling_profiles, gamify_enabled. Opt-in voice sends audio/text to the host's STT/TTS providers, the Nous audio gateway, Groq or OpenAI (keys via agent.secret_scope: TOOL_GATEWAY_USER_TOKEN, TOOL_GATEWAY_DOMAIN, GROQ_API_KEY, VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY), or Microsoft Edge TTS when the edge provider is chosen. Writes stay in the plugin data dir unless memory_md_sync_mode is on (rewrites a marked block in $THOR_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md) or companion pet adoption installs a pet into $THOR_HOME/pets; no shell commands, subprocesses, servers or self-updater.

name: bubblewrap
description: Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), the dot entries of the home directory (credential stores always) and the Thor home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`thor config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) run inside the sandbox too, and because the working directory is a real host directory Thor keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.

name: budget-leash
description: Hard budget enforcement for Thor sessions. Tracks estimated model spend (token usage x per-model prices, cache read/write tokens included) and tool-call counts against a per-session cap and a persistent per-day cap; blocks tool calls via pre_tool_call once a cap is exhausted and cuts off the model calls themselves via the llm_execution middleware, answering with a synthetic budget-exhausted reply so the provider is never invoked (fail-closed), so unattended agents cannot run up unbounded cost; warns at 80% of a cap via context injection, keeps a flock-guarded day-ledger on disk that survives restarts and is shared safely across processes, and writes a per-session JSONL spend report. Disclosure — local code only; meters estimated model spend from token-usage metadata and tool-call counts, and with the defaults ($2 per session, $10 per day, 200 tool calls per session, 1000 per day) refuses tool calls and answers model calls with a synthetic budget-exhausted reply once a cap is reached; spend figures are estimates from a user-editable price table (default $1/$3 per million input/output tokens), not provider bills; reads its settings from budget-leash.json in the Thor home and writes ledger.json, its lock file and reports.jsonl under plugin-data/budget-leash/ there; no network calls, no subprocesses.

name: buildpilot
description: Project tracking and progress recovery for Thor Agent. Create projects, manage tasks, save progress checkpoints, and retrieve project context across sessions using local SQLite storage.

name: bulk
description: Apply one instruction to hundreds of independent files, CSV rows or JSON records from a /bulk slash command, with job state in SQLite, background processing, bounded concurrency, automatic retries, shared rate-limit waits, pause and resume, Bulk-enforced token limits, restart recovery and a combined Markdown or CSV export. Disclosure — sends each item to the configured model provider through ctx.llm, billed to the user; reads the paths given to --over, including outside the plugin data directory; runs background threads inside the Thor process while a job is active; token limits are approximate and are not a billing limit; interrupted items can be sent to the model again.

name: bulkpublish
description: BulkPublish (https://www.bulkpublish.com) social media scheduling through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.bulkpublish.com/mcp/full, 80 tools): draft, schedule, publish and retry posts on Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Discord, Telegram, Tumblr and Snapchat, with media uploads, bulk actions, team approvals, labels, templates, recurring schedules, RSS autopost, Inbox replies and analytics. Bundles 33 BulkPublish skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.bulkpublish.com and needs a BulkPublish account with its API key in BULKPUBLISH_API_KEY, sent as a Bearer header. Publishing tools post to the user's connected social accounts and Inbox tools reply to real people; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Recurring schedules and RSS autopost, once approved, keep publishing from BulkPublish's servers without further prompts, and the media skill has the agent upload local files to a BulkPublish-issued URL with curl. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: bumblebee-guard
description: Supply-chain guard: runs the local Bumblebee scanner bridge (read-only, no sudo), exact-matches every installed package, MCP server and editor/browser extension against curated catalogs of known-compromised packages, and adds OSV.dev advisory counts via the bridge's OSV layer. Tools: bumblebee_guard_scan / _status / _diff (baseline diff of findings). A rate-limited pre_llm_call hook injects a one-line supply-chain alert only when curated findings exist (never when clean, at most once per hour). /bumblebee slash command plus a bundled triage skill covering confidence classes, OSV alias deduplication and a documented false-positive pattern (scanner fixtures containing threat-intel strings). Disclosure — the plugin itself makes no network calls and holds no credentials; the wrapped bridge's scan queries OSV.dev and an opt-in, off-by-default catalog refresh fetches threat-intel JSON from the upstream perplexityai/bumblebee repository; scans run daily_scan.sh as the current user and read package metadata in $HOME (never .env or token files, never executes package managers); a full scan takes up to ~3 minutes and honors a configurable timeout; the hook fails open and never blocks turns, so cron and unattended runs are unaffected.

name: bundlebees
description: bundlebees: dispatch sandboxed coding workers (bees) from Thor, watch their attempts, and keep the apply, test and push step in your own hands. Four tools with 571 o200k tokens of schema between them. bundlebees_status reports launcher health, capacity, live attempts, events, containers and authorized projects. bundlebees_dispatch validates a file-leased brief and starts a worker in a disposable Cua sandbox (default model deepseek-v4.1-flash), optionally linked to a Thor kanban card. bundlebees_attempt gets, follows, cancels or reviews one attempt (cancel and review need confirm=true and a Thor approval). bundlebees_host_prompt writes a paste-ready setup prompt for a worker host and never takes a host, token or URL. When an attempt finishes, you run thor bundlebees verify <attempt_id>: it applies the patch on a clean feature-branch worktree, enforces the file lease, runs the named tests and a secret scan, and on green commits and pushes that feature branch (main and master are refused; --dry-run applies and tests without pushing). The plugin never merges, tags or force-pushes. Thor Desktop 0.23 or newer shows a dark pane with Health, Containers, Models, Concurrency, Projects, Live attempts, Verify results and Remote host tabs; the four tools still run without it. Skill id bundlebees:bundlebees-operator. It is for developers who split repo work into small parallel briefs and want cheap workers on a machine they control, with a human gate before anything lands. To start, you need Thor 0.23.0 or newer and a worker launcher (by default the Orbit local-workers adapter on the same machine). Run thor plugins install bundlebees and thor plugins enable bundlebees, store the launcher token as the Thor secret BUNDLEBEES_LAUNCHER_TOKEN (never in chat), load bundlebees:bundlebees-operator, and begin with bundlebees_status op=health. thor bundlebees doctor checks the token, the adapter and the schema size without printing values. Disclosure — network and cost: talks to a local or user-configured worker launcher (loopback by default; a private or LAN launcher URL requires allow_private=true in plugin settings and is never a tool argument); dispatching a bee can spend model budget on that worker machine. Worker events and logs are treated as untrusted text. Cancelling or reviewing an attempt asks for Thor approval first. Disclosure — credentials and CLI: secrets are read only through Thor get_secret. The user-run thor bundlebees verify applies a worker's patch to your feature-branch worktree and runs that code's named tests on this machine outside any sandbox before it commits and pushes the branch; verify and deploy run their child processes with a minimal environment and deploy, when you invoke it, reaches a remote host over ssh. A Cua sandbox is not a sandbox for the Thor process. The Desktop pane uses ctx.rest and never shows tokens or host addresses.

name: bunny_space-platform
description: Bunny Space gateway adapter for Thor Agent. Connects a Thor profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to Thor under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

name: burnclock
description: Status-bar chip and left-nav dashboard for the MIT burnclock CLI. The chip reads burnclock's local badge cache; the dashboard adds cached balance, runway, budget, the DeepSeek Flash off-peak clock, and an API-keys card. A key entered in the card is sent to the plugin's own local backend, written only to burnclock's keys file (mode 0600), and used only for the explicit `burnclock badge --refresh`; the desktop renderer stores no key and Thor credentials are never read or forwarded. Requires the separately installed burnclock CLI (pip install burnclock). Disclosure — the status-bar chip runs a read-only shell command (cat of burnclock's badge cache) in your active local session every 60 seconds, and the dashboard page runs `burnclock offpeak --json` every 60 seconds; a provider key you paste into the API-keys card is written to burnclock's own `~/.config/burnclock/env` (mode 0600), and Save or Refresh runs `burnclock badge --refresh`, which calls the chosen providers' APIs (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Moonshot, MiniMax, fal) with those keys, only when you click.

name: business-agent-os
description: Set up a file-based business operating system for an AI agent, for business owners who are not developers: one business folder of plain Markdown memory in two layers (a folder per client and project with state, dated changelog with a monthly archive, to-do and inbox; and a Karpathy-style wiki the agent maintains from saved sources: topic, entity and source pages with an index and a log), a daily log, a voice guide, session commands (/pickup with client, topic and daily modes, /wrap, /biz-status, /biz-review, /trace, /new-client, /ingest, /lint), optional local git save points and an optional tmux session menu. One skill plus a hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.danielbilsborough.com/mcp, no key, no sign-in) with four read-only tools: scaffold_business_os, house_rules, daily_routine and voice_guide_template. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: the MCP server is a stateless Cloudflare Worker whose source is in the repo; every tool call goes to mcp.danielbilsborough.com, which receives only the tool arguments (an optional business name and client or project names), returns static text, keeps no sessions, stores nothing and does not log inputs; every tool is annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted. The skill has the agent create and edit Markdown files only inside a business folder the user chooses, asking before each step; it installs nothing, uses no sudo, edits no shell or agent config outside that folder (the user adds one optional source line to ~/.zshrc themselves) and runs only local git commands inside that folder if the user opts in. No telemetry, no credentials stored or sent. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: butler
description: Turns the Thor desktop pet into an on-screen operator: WALK draws a guide on the real controls and verifies each step from the macOS Accessibility tree, DESCRIBE reads the control under your pointer (role, label, enabled state, value) without letting the click reach your app, and WATCH announces one condition from an app in the background and keeps it until you acknowledge it. Accessibility only: no screenshots, no OCR, no Screen Recording, no Input Monitoring. Disclosure — macOS only; needs the Accessibility permission, which lets its helper read the controls and text of other apps on screen. On first use it downloads its native screen helper from the author's GitHub release and refuses it unless it matches the checksum pinned in the plugin source (otherwise it compiles the bundled Swift source with swiftc), and LOOK mode intercepts clicks across the screen until you pick or cancel. Sending from the pet into a chat requires `allow_gateway_injection: true` for this plugin.

name: butler-assistant
description: Turns Thor into a proactive personal assistant. You set your daily non-negotiables and Butler checks in until they are done or deferred; you tell it about a commitment and it follows up before it slips, with the model choosing whether and when to follow up inside owner-set limits (max unanswered nudges, minimum gap between messages). If you opt in, it can also ring your phone for urgent follow-ups or place calls you approve, through your own LiveKit SIP trunk. You choose its tone (Gentle to Strict), how persistent it is, quiet hours, time zone and a daily cap on check-ins, and can pause it in one click. A concierge-style Thor Desktop page shows today's non-negotiables, upcoming commitments, recent activity and preferences, with a 4-step Quick Setup; the same controls are available to the agent as tools in chat. Disclosure — a background runner thread in the gateway process schedules check-ins, which run as normal turns in your admitted DM or local chat on your configured model, billed like any message; with background wakes enabled it sets allow_gateway_injection for this plugin; with system controls on it writes notification, display and nudge settings into your Thor config.yaml (keys listed in the README, including agent.gateway_notify_interval, skills.creation_nudge_interval, gateway.message_timestamps.enabled, platforms.*.gateway_restart_notification and the top-level timezone once confirmed), replacing existing per-platform values for those keys; the agent can change Butler's own settings through butler_controls when asked, while DM capture, notification arming and every phone setting stay user-only; the optional prompt review writes to SOUL.md and a butler-capabilities skill only after you select and apply each change, keeping backups; the optional 'verify time zone via IP' action calls ipapi.co or worldtimeapi.org only when you ask; phone calling is off by default; once you enable it in Desktop and add your LiveKit credentials (read through Thor secret_scope), Butler sends HTTPS requests to your LIVEKIT_URL to ring you within hourly/cooldown/quiet-hours limits, or to place third-party calls only after you approve the exact script (Desktop or CLI, never the agent; emergency and premium numbers blocked; calls open with an AI disclosure); if you also enable inbound screening, an AI answers inbound calls on your trunk and takes messages; an optional, user-started voice worker (pip extra 'voice') connects to LiveKit and OpenAI for live call audio and may run a local `thor chat` subprocess to answer your questions on a call; call transcripts and summaries, including what the other party said, are stored locally and shown to your agent after the call; iMessage voice and image helpers run local ffmpeg/ffprobe and hand files to Thor as MEDIA: reply attachments (Butler never reads Thor runtime secrets or calls the Photon sidecar);
