watches read the local file path you ask it to watch; inbound DM event capture is off by default and needs two separate opt-ins; all state is stored in plaintext SQLite in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.

name: buzzmark
description: Write, plan and schedule social media posts in a business's own voice through Buzzmark's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://buzzmark.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): post ideas from this week's news, posts for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Threads and TikTok with a version per platform, a score for how much a post sounds like the brand, pictures, a week of posts planned around the best posting times, and what worked. Bundles the buzzmark workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Buzzmark's hosted server (buzzmark.ai) and acts on the user's Buzzmark account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Nothing posts right away: tools save, schedule, move and unschedule posts on the user's Buzzmark calendar and delete drafts, and write_posts, rewrite_post and create_image use the plan's monthly allowance. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: by2kb
description: Discover learning videos by topic, select numbered recommendations, and turn Bilibili and YouTube videos into transcripts, abstracts, and study notes using the Thor host model. Disclosure — intercepts gateway messages with a Bilibili/YouTube URL, a "by2kb <topic>" prefix, or (for 1 h after a recommendation list, same user/chat) a bare number reply, and runs the separately installed by2kb CLI (BY2KB_COMMAND or PATH), which searches Bilibili/YouTube, downloads media and runs ASR; enrichment prompts go to your active Thor model.

name: cacheguard
description: Warns or blocks a large chat message sent after a pause, when the provider's prompt cache may have expired. Afterwards it shows how many tokens were reused or rebilled, and /cacheguard shows how often your cache was lost after pauses of each length. Modes (off, warn, block) are set per surface (terminal, desktop, gateway), and a model can have its own pause, size and mode. In block mode the message is not sent: the reply says so, and you send it with /retry or by sending the same text again. If the plugin fails, the message is sent. Disclosure — no network call, no LLM call, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry. Middleware llm_request reads every message of the request to hash the start of the chat (sha256, only the hash is kept) and removes cacheguard's own "message not sent" replies from what the model receives. Middleware llm_execution reads the token usage of each response; the provider call is Thor's own next_call(), never repeated. Hook pre_llm_call returns a block for a large message after a pause. Hook transform_llm_output posts a result line with ctx.post_message and never changes the reply. Reads config.yaml (its own settings through ctx.get_config) and the environment variables THOR_SINGLE_QUERY_SESSION, THOR_KANBAN_TASK, THOR_PLATFORM, THOR_INTERACTIVE. Writes its settings with ctx.set_config (/cacheguard set and setup) and, under <THOR_HOME>/cacheguard/, observations.jsonl (token counts, times and model name of calls after a pause; no message text, no session id) and one small json file per chat (times, token counts, hash). /cacheguard reset deletes them. Unattended runs (cron, kanban, subagents, curator, API server, webhooks) pass through untouched; one-shot runs (-Q, -z, --oneshot) are never blocked and show no line (a -Q run may be counted in the stats); with chat -q, block acts as warn. Private Thor names: tools.approval_context._is_single_query_approval_context (a run with no screen only warns) and agent.usage_pricing.normalize_usage (read the cache token counts). If one is missing, the plugin says so in /cacheguard and degrades: it only warns, or result lines are missing.

name: cadence
description: Local usage page: year heatmap, streaks from days a chat was used, model and place breakdowns, and this week against last week. Disclosure — reads the selected profile state.db read-only, or every profile's when the scope is all, and runs the local cadence command through Thor cli.exec. No network calls, secrets, telemetry, or provider logins. Not a fork of thor-activity.

name: caduceus
description: Answers about your own health that cite your DNA, Apple Health trends, medical records and new research, from a vault on your machine. Caduceus imports 23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage or FamilyTreeDNA raw data, a Promethease report, an Apple Health export, Health Auto Export data (a JSON export or a live sync) and US health records (FHIR) into local SQLite, then gives your agent gene–drug checks (CPIC guidelines plus GLP-1 research), trends before and after a medication start, a rebuilt variant report, a one-page brief for your doctor and a research watch that puts studies on your own gene–drug pairs first. No DNA file yet? /caduceus demo loads an invented person to try it. /caduceus erase deletes everything it stored; your settings and any schedules you created stay. Privacy levels are yours to choose: open by default, or standard, which hides Alzheimer's risk, hereditary cancer risk, carrier status, mental health and reproductive results until you unlock them. Information with limits, not medical advice. Disclosure — imports, search and reports run locally, and the vault is never uploaded as a whole; tool results (slices of your data) enter the conversation, so the model provider you chose sees them; a hook adds one fixed note, holding none of your data, to the first health, medication or DNA question of each chat when the vault has data (off with the `vault_hint` setting); the research watch (on by default, runs when you or the agent ask for it or on a schedule you create, off with the `research_watch` setting) sends gene and topic terms, the names of medications you recorded, and public marker and article IDs, never genotypes, to Europe PMC and NCBI; the Health Auto Export sync (off until you allow that app's MCP server for Caduceus in Thor config, and run only when you or the agent ask for it or on a schedule you create) reads Apple Health data from that server through Thor's own MCP client and sends none of your data out; scheduled checks run model turns billed like any message; no telemetry. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report, asks you to check it holds no health data, and files it to this repository with `gh` only after you approve the draft.

name: caduceus-governance
description: Deterministic, model-free admission control for what Thor writes into its own skills: content lanes, operator-owned executable checks, a provenance lane for writes made after untrusted web/browser/MCP content, a tamper-evident ledger, and operator release/rollback. Observe by default. Disclosure — Records a digest of every skill_manage call in $THOR_HOME/caduceus (observe mode, default); in opt-in boundary or enforce mode it blocks unadmitted skill_manage calls or deletes and restores files under $THOR_HOME/skills (and, if enabled, MEMORY.md/USER.md and config.yaml, of which it keeps owner-only copies in its state directory) to the last admitted state, including changes made by `thor update` skill syncs or hub installs. Operator-registered check commands run sandboxed (macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock/seccomp) or are held. The dashboard's POST /approve acts only on a signature from an operator-enrolled device. No network, no model calls.

name: calendar-agenda
description: Agent tools plus dashboard API routes for today's Google Calendar agenda — records what actually happened to each planned event (done / interrupted / cancelled / skipped, slot kept or released) in private extended properties, never touching titles or Google event status. Disclosure — reads today's events from your primary Google Calendar and writes private extended properties to them through your own Google OAuth client (signed in with `thor auth add calendar-agenda:google`); when you release a slot it shortens the end time of events you own that have no guests, keeping the original end so it can be restored; its dashboard routes can change event state.

name: call-me
description: /call-me gateway: text your Thor agent from the /call-me iPhone app, and the callme_call tool rings your phone, speaks the agent's text and returns your spoken answer as a transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the /call-me service at https://callmemcp.com/aiphone (run by the plugin author): creates one agent session, sends texts and call requests, and long-polls for replies while the gateway runs (at most one request every 3 seconds); sends message text, the text to be spoken and the destination numbers, and call audio is transcribed by the service so only the transcript comes back; the agent session token and event cursor are stored at $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/call-me/session.json (mode 600); only numbers in CALLME_ALLOWED_USERS can message the agent or be called, and inbound messages must come from that number's verified /call-me device; callme_call blocks until the call ends (300 seconds at most) and returns missed if nobody answers; no shell commands, telemetry or self-update. The /call-me iPhone app that receives the messages and calls needs a paid subscription; the plugin itself is free and MIT-licensed.

name: calling-mom
description: Lets a cheap model run your Kanban board and calls a stronger model only where the board or the tool results show it is needed. Mom (a good, affordable model) answers stuck signals, risky commands and completion checks; olymp (the expensive heavyweight) is asked only when mom escalates a rare high-stakes case, with hard limits per card and per day. Disclosure — once enabled, the plugin observes every kanban worker tool result (hashes and counts only, logged to logs/calling-mom.jsonl). With the advisor enabled AND a board or card opted in, redacted run excerpts go through Thor's ctx.llm to the mom and olymp models you choose; the answer is appended to the tool result and written to the card with the public kanban_comment tool. A card line verify: <command> runs an allowlisted command (no shell, scrubbed environment) for cards created by trusted creators. thor calling-mom setup writes the plugin's own config (calling_mom.* and its plugins.entries allowlist) with the values you pick, reads delegation.backends.model_map (read-only, to offer your Advanced Delegation routes) and creates one cron job, 'calling-mom: sweep', unless you pass --no-cron; the sweep reads the kanban databases and may push metrics to Pushgateway URLs you configure (off by default). No telemetry, no credentials stored. Since 1.4: a Desktop page (Needs you, Active cards, recent activity, status-bar chip) served by the plugin's dashboard route; it reads the log and the opted-in boards, writes only when you press a button (an answer card comment, a card move including complete, archive and unblock, written straight to the kanban database through Thor' internal kanban module), and shows each running card's last assistant message read through Thor' SessionDB (read-only, local, never sent to a model). web_verify (off by default) sends a one-line redacted claim to Thor' own web_search tool. The sweep and the optional chat-wait count read board events and the human-input hooks (kinds and seconds only, never prompt or answer text). The plugin sends nothing to a server of its own; details in SECURITY.md of the repo. Since 1.7.0: what waits under Needs you is also sent once to your phone by running Thor' own thor send CLI (setting calling_mom.notify.target, default off), and a reply in the chat the notice went to answers the card via the tool calling_mom_answer, whose 'allow' answer releases a held command once without a further prompt from the plugin; a held critical command can be fail-closed (opt-in calling_mom.preflight.fail_closed) so it stays blocked when Mom cannot check it; a new card can be started from the Dashboard page (POST /card through Thor' public kanban_create); a card can be parked with Decide later and resumed from the Later section. Since 1.7.1: that New card form can also pin the card's model (a model of one of your authenticated providers, sent to kanban_create as model/provider; GET /new-card lists them).

name: calm-mode
description: When you get frustrated, your agent slows down. Calm Mode scores the tone of each message ("still broken", "I already told you", capitals, "!!", the same message twice); frustration builds and fades. Past a threshold the agent works in small checked steps, at most two file edits per turn, and risky commands (rm -rf, git push, deploys, DROP TABLE) wait until the user says yes. /calm shows the level and forces it on or off. No model calls, nothing stored.

name: camel-guard
description: Gate sensitive tools on trusted user capabilities after untrusted tool output.

name: camofox
description: Camofox browser backend: browse with a self-hosted anti-detection Firefox (Camoufox, C++ fingerprint spoofing) through the camofox-browser REST server. Registers the browser_* tools (navigate, snapshot with clickable refs, click, type, scroll, back, press, get_images, vision, JavaScript console, plus cookie import when CAMOFOX_API_KEY is set) in the `camofox` toolset, with `thor camofox setup|status`; existing CAMOFOX_* variables and browser.camofox settings carry over. Formerly built into Thor core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure: one Python dependency (requests). It talks only to the Camofox server at CAMOFOX_URL (e.g. http://localhost:9377, which you run yourself: Docker or `npm start`), sending CAMOFOX_API_KEY as a bearer token when set. Page text reaches only your model as tool output; browser_vision sends the screenshot to your configured auxiliary vision model. Snapshots mask values that look like secrets (API keys, tokens), but text typed into form fields, passwords included, shows up in snapshots. Oversized snapshots and screenshots are written under the Thor home (cache/web, browser_screenshots). Cookie import reads Netscape cookies.txt files only from browser.camofox.cookies_dir (default ~/.camofox/cookies). browser_vault fills saved passwords on the Camofox tab (sent only to a loopback or HTTPS CAMOFOX_URL). Inert on Thor cores that still bundle Camofox.

name: camofox-human-auth
description: Universal human-controlled authentication for Camofox Browser, powered by the Camoufox engine. Supports login, registration, SSO, MFA, OTP, CAPTCHA, and device confirmation. Requires the Camofox backend; never changes an existing Thor browser provider automatically.

name: canadian-primary-care
description: Twenty-six offline Canadian-unit clinician decision-support calculators (preview). Disclosure — clinician decision-support calculators, not a regulator-reviewed medical device; runs fully offline with no network calls, stores only your favourites list in Desktop plugin storage, Copy puts the result on the system clipboard, and source citations open in your browser when clicked.

name: canary-trap
description: Catch prompt injection by the secret it tries to steal. Every turn the agent is shown a decoy credential (THOR_DEPLOY_KEY=hdk_live_…) with the instruction never to send it; no real task needs it, so if it shows up in a tool call — plain, URL-encoded, base64, hex, reversed, spaced out or as a 16+ character fragment, in any nested argument — the call is blocked (pre_tool_call), every later tool call in that session goes to your approval until /canary reset, and the reply opens with an alert (transform_llm_output). /canary shows status and incidents, rotates the decoy, or tests text. Disclosure — adds a ~60-token paragraph with the decoy to each turn's user message (pre_llm_call; Thor may persist the API-bound message for cache replay; the decoy grants nothing). Stores in its own plugin state: the decoy, up to 200 incidents (time, tool name, how the decoy was hidden, platform, session id — never tool arguments or conversation content) and locked session ids. Lockdown only adds approval prompts through Thor' approval gate (auto-approved under YOLO, so advisory there; the leaking call is always blocked). No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials, telemetry or background work.

name: canonry
description: Open-source, agent-first Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) platform. Measure brand mentions and source citations across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Meta; research competitors and SEO opportunities; audit AI readiness; analyze AI crawler and referral traffic; create and publish content; manage ChatGPT Ads; and get pages indexed. Connect Search Console, GA4, WordPress, and more, then measure what changed across brands, locations, and markets. Includes Canonry operator and Aero analyst skills with MCP tools. Requires a configured Canonry runtime.

name: capalis
description: Describe a job in one sentence, and Capalis sets it up, runs it and checks it really happened. It finds your channels and repository by name, picks the right tool for each step and does a practice run that sends nothing. It runs only after you approve that exact version, from your phone on Telegram if you like. For example, a bug posted in Discord or Slack becomes one GitHub issue, a Slack notice and a reply to the reporter, who hears back again when the issue is closed. Every write is read back, nothing is done twice, and the job stops itself when a token, permission or tool changes. Disclosure — Capalis runs a background worker in the Thor process that executes owner-approved Recipes (schedules, waits, alerts) and sends to api.github.com, slack.com, hooks.slack.com, discord.com and api.telegram.org with the tokens you configure. Its http.get step fetches HTTPS pages at public addresses that you approve. Its pre_gateway_dispatch hook takes every new message in a channel a Recipe listens to away from the agent. Once you approve a contract, Recipes can call Thor's web_search and web_extract tools outside an agent turn. The model can start an approved manual Recipe without a per-run prompt unless the Recipe requires per-run confirmation.

name: caprover-operator
description: Read-only setup diagnostics and human-approved, state-bound immutable-image deployment for one owner-configured CapRover app, with durable uncertainty, replay refusal and dated operation cards for self-hosted projects. Disclosure: contacts the configured CapRover HTTPS origin and optional fixed health endpoint; CapRover returns all app definitions in memory, while only the configured app's keyed fingerprint and sanitized evidence enter a private local ledger. Image startup may run migrations. HTTP alone does not prove the serving image; runtime task evidence is optional. No shell, telemetry, self-updater or automatic rollback. Apply requires fresh native human approval in in_process mode. Safeguards apply only to this plugin's caprover_apply workflow and ledger; independent terminal or execute_code actions, other plugins, direct API calls and external operators require their own access controls and approvals.

name: capturekit
description: Web pages for Thor through the CaptureKit API: page content as Markdown with metadata and links, screenshots and PDFs (full page, one element or a mobile view), and an AI profile of a page. Also a backend for the built-in web_extract tool. Disclosure — sends each URL and the tool arguments to api.capturekit.dev with your CAPTUREKIT_API_KEY, and calls use CaptureKit credits (1 per call; usage is free). capturekit_analyze has CaptureKit read the page with an AI model on its side. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 4 tools and a web_extract backend, no hooks or middleware, writes one image or PDF per capturekit_screenshot call under $THOR_HOME/cache/screenshots/ and no other files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: carbonvoice-platform
description: Carbon Voice gateway adapter for Thor Agent. Connects via Socket.IO (primary) with REST polling fallback — no public webhook or tunnel required. Persists a cursor to disk so messages received while Thor is offline are processed on the next startup. Replies via POST /v3/messages/start, so the Her

name: cardlake
description: Cardlake keeps what you mean to get back to (reminders, articles and videos to learn from, links, work) in one daily feed. This plugin puts that feed in your Telegram chat with Thor: /cardlake feed and today show your cards with Done, Tomorrow, Next week and Undo buttons and a pinned Today checklist, a morning message sends what's due, and you can send Thor a link to save it. Free account at cardlake.app, or host your own. Disclosure — talks to Cardlake only through Thor' "cardlake" MCP connection (cardlake.app or a self-hosted copy); sends and pins card messages in your private Telegram chat, and adds /cardlake to the bot's command menu unless you set that menu up yourself, through the bot Thor already runs; /cardlake save sends your text (with passwords, keys and tokens removed in code) to your own Thor model; stores only the id of the pinned Today message in plugin state. No shell commands, credentials, background processes or telemetry; the morning job exists only if you create it from the blueprint, and it cannot change cards.

name: cardworthscanner
description: PSA/BGS/CGC trading card grading ROI calculator, centering inspector and TCG market valuation (Pokemon, Yu-Gi-Oh!) via the hosted CardWorthScanner MCP server. Disclosure — card queries and values you ask about are sent to the CardWorthScanner hosted MCP server at cardworthscanner.com (operated by the plugin author).

name: carnet
description: A memory that stays bounded: core rules always in mind, facts recalled only when relevant, long sheets read on demand, and a memory graph inside the app. Disclosure — Carnet sends every saved fact and each turn's message to the embedding endpoint you configure (LM Studio on 127.0.0.1:1234 by default); the optional rephrase and scan features send fact text to the chat model you configure; the "local" backend downloads a ~310 MB model from Hugging Face only when you ask and runs it in a background Python process.

name: cartograph
description: Map local repositories and retrieve task-focused source excerpts with line references. Disclosure — runs the separately installed Cartograph Node CLI (no shell, bounded time/output, credential-free env) against any local directory the model names unless `allowed_roots` is set, returns source excerpts into the conversation, and caches excerpts in the plugin data directory.

name: cartridge
description: A handheld ROM emulator pane that plays the user's own .gb/.gbc files while the agent works, holds the frame the instant an approval arrives, and resumes on the same frame once it is answered. Desktop-only: no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, and the pane makes no network calls. Disclosure — the pane can answer Thor approval prompts: it shows the pending request with the same choices the chat offers (once / session / always / deny) and sends your click to Thor through the Desktop SDK; ROMs, save states and settings stay in the plugin's own Desktop storage and nothing is sent over the network.

name: case-trail
description: Trace case-history and treatment research to actual opinion passages; analyze supplied sources without a required repository. Disclosure — Sends case search queries and Justia page URLs through the web search/extract provider you configured in Thor, and can fetch one public OpenJurist case page you select after a robots.txt check (OpenJurist sees the URL and your IP). Reads local opinion files at paths given in chat, refusing kernel and device files, the Thor home and key stores; the plugin setting opinion_folders can limit it to folders you list. Stores fetched text, review receipts and rendered pages privately in its plugin data folder. Novelty research tool, not legal advice; unaffiliated with Justia or OpenJurist.

name: cash-desk
description: Chase overdue invoices from your CSV exports (generic, Xero, QuickBooks, Stripe, bank statements): apply payments only on an exact reference and amount, draft reminders at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days, and send one only after a person approves its exact text and Thor asks once more. Figure Lock holds every amount, invoice number, date, IBAN and reference to the ledger; a rewording that changes one is rejected with a diff. Disclosure — imports only CSV files inside its own data folder, its bundled demo folder and the folders you list in import_dirs, and keeps its ledger in SQLite under its plugin data folder; a reminder leaves only after a person approves its exact text (/cashdesk approve or the Desktop page) and Thor's approval prompt passes, never from cron, a subagent, yolo mode or approvals set to auto-approve; in the default eml mode it writes .eml files to its outbox folder, and in smtp mode it sends through the SMTP server you configure, with the password stored as a Thor secret (CASHDESK_SMTP_PASSWORD) and TLS always verified; with guard_outgoing_messages on (off by default) it replaces any agent reply that states an amount, IBAN or invoice number the ledger does not hold for that customer with a withheld notice, and replies stop streaming; no other network calls, no telemetry.

name: cashew
description: Cashew — persistent thought-graph memory with local embeddings, organic decay, and autonomous think cycles.

name: catalogo-it
description: The official Thor plugin catalog in a native page (sidebar entry, route /catalogo, plus a command-palette entry) with an Italian interface and on-the-fly Italian descriptions: Google Translate first, MyMemory as a second public source, and a final fallback to the user's own local llama.cpp model. Disclosure — it fetches the public catalog feed (thor-agent.thor-agent.local) and, when you open a plugin entry, sends that entry's English description to translate.googleapis.com (Google Translate's keyless public endpoint) and, if that fails, to api.mymemory.translated.net; nothing else leaves the machine. It reads no credentials or Thor files, and its backend route is empty. Translation runs when a plugin entry is opened, not for the whole catalog. No telemetry. UI is Italian-first with an English bundle.

name: cdp-manager
description: Local Chrome CDP debug ports in the status bar (probe, launch, stop, recheck) plus a managed port Thor keeps alive and the `cdp` agent tool, which also detects and repairs a Chrome profile-picker launch (wedged/unwedge). Disclosure: launches local Chrome on 127.0.0.1 only, with per-port profiles under the local app-data directory, and closes it with a clean Browser.close; state lives in the plugin's own config file. Windows only.

name: cellium-wallet
description: Connect Thor to a Cellium agent for wallet operations, swaps, bridges, and managed orders. Disclosure — Crypto wallet plugin: sends the Cellium agent credential, wallet addresses, transaction details and order parameters to the hosted Cellium MCP at app.cellium.xyz, which supplies its tool list at runtime and, with signing access granted on the Cellium account, can sign transactions, move funds, swap, bridge, trade on Aave/Morpho/Hyperliquid and schedule future orders; keys are held by Cellium, and the server is marked untrusted so Thor asks for approval before each write-capable call.

name: ceo-pack
description: CEO Pack — a CEO orchestration layer for Thor. Brief, route, plan, assign, call, verify, log, with Thor as COO. One owner and one due date per task, Type 1 / Type 2 decision gating, credential-safe tool calls, and owner approval for external actions. v0.4.0 adds seat aliases, head-CEO config, capability checks, opt-in business-data reading, and generalized closeout (Q1-Q4 + monthly). Free model default is Nemotron 3 Ultra free, with GLM Flash free fallback and paid Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 overrides the user chooses. The plugin returns model choices; it does not call a model itself (stdlib-only, catalog-safe).

name: certarc
description: Practise free scenario questions for the CISM, CISSP, CISA, AAISM and AAIA exams in Thor, with an explanation for every option. No account or keys. Also covers exam outlines and CertArc study guides, and can link to CertArc's free assessment when you finish a set. Bundles the certarc-practice skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to certarc.com through its free no-sign-in endpoint (https://certarc.com/mcp/grok), whose tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill's assessment links carry a utm source tag, and the user opens them and signs in themselves.

name: chalk
description: Thor teaches on a chalkboard. Ask it to explain something and Thor Desktop draws the lesson inline in the chat, stroke by stroke in chalk, while the narration plays; replay it or save it as an MP4. The agent's chalk_teach tool sends only structure (flow, list, compare, equation, graph, cycle, tree, note, labelled sketch, circle/underline, clear) and the board lays itself out, so small models produce clean boards; full boards are wiped by an eraser and continue on a fresh one. Other surfaces receive the narration as one audio file. Disclosure: narration text goes to the user's configured TTS provider through Thor' own text_to_speech tool (ctx.dispatch_tool); lessons and audio are stored under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/chalk; Save video uploads the recording to the plugin over plugin RPC and writes it to ~/Videos/Chalk (or ~/Downloads/Chalk when the OS blocks Videos), converting with ffmpeg when it is on PATH (fixed argument lists). A transform_llm_output hook appends the lesson's MEDIA line once if the reply left it out. Graph expressions are parsed by a small parser, never evaluated as code. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no background processes.

name: chalkline
description: A Thor back office for solo tradespeople: capture enquiries, prepare quote and invoice PDFs, retain receipts and agreed extras, review follow-ups and export an accountant ZIP. Customer sends require payload-bound owner approval, except three template kinds approved once by hash. Disclosure — Takes over WhatsApp on its dedicated profile: every non-owner WhatsApp message skips the agent and is stored (text, plus up to 30 attachments per sender per day at up to 32 MiB each) in the profile's plugin data folder, and Thor's unofficial Baileys bridge can get the number restricted or banned, so use a dedicated business number. Customer messages go out by running `thor send` only after the owner approves each payload, except three standing templates (enquiry acknowledgement, appointment reminder, review request) that are approved once by hash and then sent automatically. `/office setup` changes the profile's config.yaml to restrict WhatsApp, Telegram, CLI and cron to Chalkline tools (backup kept as config.yaml.bak) and creates a 15-minute no-agent cron script that sends approved and scheduled messages. Receipt photos are sent to the configured vision model.

name: channel3
description: Shop 100M+ products across thousands of US retailers: search, compare every store's live price, and switch variants (color, size) on inline product cards in Thor Desktop. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted Channel3 MCP server at mcp.trychannel3.com (no account or key; free tier rate-limited per IP); search queries (and any image URL for visual search), product ids and variant selections go to it, and the Desktop cards call it directly from the app; a server-issued thread_id links searches within a conversation; product images load from cdn.trychannel3.com; Buy buttons open buy.trychannel3.com redirect links in the browser; nothing is purchased in-app and no credentials are stored.

name: chartquery
description: Tools to render charts, QR codes and barcodes as shareable images, through the ChartQuery API. Disclosure — sends the tool arguments (chart configs and data, plain-English chart prompts, QR and barcode contents) to api.chartquery.com with your CHARTQUERY_API_KEY, and calls can use ChartQuery credits. Every image is created with sharing on, so anyone with the returned link can view it; do not chart private data. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 4 tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: chat-length
description: Tells the user when a chat is getting too long and hands them a short opener for a fresh chat; the new chat pulls the earlier context itself via session_search, no handover document. Fill level from real provider token counts, measured against Thor' compaction point by default; notices at 70 % and 90 % (configurable), once each per chat, re-armed after compaction, never in cron, subagent, kanban, batch or webhook runs. Notice in the conversation language, English or German. Disclosure — on the turn that crosses a threshold, pre_llm_call adds a one-turn instruction to that turn's user message (never the system prompt; replayed byte-identical, so prompt caching stays intact); post_api_request stores per-session token counts, model and provider name and which notice fired (no message content) under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/chat-length/, pruned after 30 days; reads the session title read-only from state.db and the compression settings read-only from config.yaml; no network calls, no tools, no dependencies.

name: chat-studio
description: Offline conversation customization with one-click presets and plugin-owned settings. Disclosure — enabled by default; injects a stylesheet that restyles the Desktop chat transcript (width, fonts, spacing, optional colours) keyed on app data-slot selectors, so a Desktop update can break the styling; settings stay in plugin storage, no network.

name: chat-tree
description: One window for branching chats in Thor Desktop. A side pane draws the open chat and its branches as a git graph, one node for each exchange. Branch from a node, ask on a model you pick, and merge back into any ancestor chat with Merge as-is or Digest. The model writes each digest through ctx.llm (auxiliary task chat_tree_digest, which follows the title generation model unless you set auxiliary.chat_tree_digest). Disclosure — Desktop pane reads up to 500 persisted session summaries and the transcripts, usage and subagent lists of the chats in the open lineage; it branches, resumes a chat, submits a prompt or sets a branch's model only when you click; Digest sends up to 24,000 characters of one chat (secrets redacted) to your configured auxiliary model (chat_tree_digest, defaults to the title-generation model) and only drafts the result in the composer; the Python history RPC opens the profile's state.db read-only for at most 30 chats of the open lineage; branch ids are shared with the side-chat plugin through the localStorage key __thorSideChatBranchIds.

name: chat-view
description: Struggling to find the right session in Thor? Struggle no longer with Chat View, a simple, reliable way to stop squinting at titles or guessing which chat you’re looking for. See your sessions in a spacious main view, with big, bold titles and message summaries that show what each chat is about at a glance. Disclosure — reads chat titles, recent messages and pull-request links of the active profile's chats through the raw window.thorDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no stored-transcript read); delete and folder-delete permanently remove chats after a confirmation, which the user can switch off for single-chat delete and archive.

name: chatgpt-style
description: Unofficial ChatGPT / Codex-inspired theme for Thor Desktop: light and dark palettes, a centred reading column, compact blue user bubbles, a rounded composer card with a blue send button, Codex-style model and effort pickers, a floating Files/Review card and a quieter sidebar and footer. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenAI. Disclosure — registered through THEMES_AREA; its customCSS restyles native Desktop surfaces (sidebar rows, composer, user bubbles, menus, model picker, file panel, status bar) by selecting the app's data-slot / data-sidebar / data-tree-group hooks; no script DOM access, no network calls, no storage; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: chatto-platform
description: Chatto gateway adapter for Thor Agent. Connects to a Chatto server (self-hosted team chat) and relays messages between rooms/DMs and the Thor agent.  Uses the Chatto ConnectRPC API (JSON over HTTP) for outbound messages and the Chatto realtime WebSocket protocol (binary protobuf) for inbound eve

name: cheatsheet
description: Title-bar cheatsheet. Describe what you want to do and it points to a real command or a cited passage; live slash commands and plugins, plus cited passages from this install's docs. No runtime network. No self-update. Disclosure — reads the Markdown docs shipped with your Thor install (website/docs next to thor_cli) through a local dashboard route and lists your commands, plugins and MCP servers via read-only gateway calls; no network at runtime (doc and GitHub links open in your browser only when clicked).

name: check-please
description: Pairs each "done" in an agent's reply (tests pass, sent, deployed, pushed, saved, scheduled) with the tool call that proves it, and adds one line when a claim is stale, failed, or proven only by something the agent edited. Disclosure — reads the tool calls and replies Thor passes to its hooks; runs no shell commands and makes no network or model calls; stores claim sentences, command first lines and a 14-day claim log in its own plugin state file; appends one "Check:" line under a flagged reply and, on cron runs, puts one line at the top of the delivered reply; on coding turns its pre_verify hook may send the agent back once to recheck a contradicted claim, and its pre_llm_call hook may add a one-line note about the previous reply's flagged claim (all on by default, each has a setting); `/check today` and `/check jobs` show profile-wide tallies, including short claim snippets from other chats on a shared gateway; the owner-run `thor check-please audit` command reads the profile's saved sessions (state.db) read-only and prints a summary locally; the Desktop pane polls the plugin's own dashboard route every 4 seconds while a session is focused; no telemetry.

name: chess-coach
description: Practice mate in one to four or play Thor with piece odds on an interactive Desktop chessboard.

name: chinamedvisit
description: China Top Tier-3A International Medical Center (IMC) procedure cost estimator, medical travel itinerary planner, and bilingual chief physician triage through ChinaMedVisit's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://chinamedvisit.com/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Benchmarks 50+ self-pay procedures (PET-CT, 3T MRI, painless endoscopy) with 70%-90% savings vs US cash rates. Bundles the chinamedvisit workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local runtime code: every tool call goes over HTTPS to chinamedvisit.com/api/mcp with the clinical query you give it (procedures, symptoms, travel dates), and the remote tool list is served by ChinaMedVisit at runtime, not covered by the reviewed pin; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses those in unattended runs. Cost and triage output is the vendor's estimate, not medical advice.

name: chineseworksheet
description: Printable Chinese handwriting worksheet grid geometry calculator (Tian Zi Ge, Mi Zi Ge, Jiu Gong Ge, Hui Zi Ge on A4/Letter), official Ministry of Education Hanzi stroke order rules, HSK 3.0 vocabulary difficulty analyzer (HSK 1 to 7-9 / CEFR), Mandarin Pinyin tone mark converter, and Kangxi 214 radicals decomposition through ChineseWorkSheet's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://chineseworksheet.com/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the chineseworksheet workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local runtime code, binaries, hooks, telemetry or self-updater; every tool call goes over HTTPS to chineseworksheet.com/api/mcp with only the Chinese worksheet or linguistic query arguments. All 6 tools are public, free, and annotated read-only (readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false). The package marks the server untrusted (trust: untrusted), so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. The remote tool inventory is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: chiron
description: An advisor who is also a friend. Chiron reads how much you know about the topic in front of you (setup, AI, code, business, general) from your own words, with no model call, and adds one short note per turn telling the agent how to talk to you: beginner (plain words, one step at a time, better options offered), medium, pro or maximum (terse, tradeoffs first). Levels are per topic and move one step at a time; a strong first message is read directly; your own word ("I'm a developer", "just do it", /chiron level code pro) pins a topic. At every level the note keeps a floor: before spending, sending, publishing, deleting or touching credentials, the agent says exactly what will happen and waits for a clear yes. Off in each session until /chiron on (or always_on). The system prompt never changes, so prompt caching keeps working. Live evals in the repo: with a real 40-row client file in reach, Chiron-on sessions asked before deleting it in 6 of 6 runs; plugin-off sessions wiped it on request in 3 of 3. Disclosure — pre_llm_call reads only the current user message and returns a short context note; it stores per-session topic levels and the on/off flag in one JSON file under its plugin data directory (last 200 sessions), with a sidecar lock file and short-lived temp files in the same directory; no network calls, no model calls, no shell or subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry."

name: chmod-ref
description: @chmod: context references that explain a file permission mode for the model: @chmod:<mode> takes an octal mode (755, 0755, 4755), ls -l text (-rwsr-xr-x, with the file type letter and a trailing + . or @) or an st_mode as stat and git write it (100644), and attaches both forms, each class's rights in words (directory rights named as such), what setuid, setgid and the sticky bit do and where they are ignored, and notes such as a mode everyone can change, one private to the owner, or a class holding rights the class before it lacks; @chmod:"644 u+x,go-w" applies a symbolic change step by step the way GNU chmod does (u g o a, + - =, r w x X s t, copies like u=g), @chmod:"100644 100755" shows what changes between two modes, and @chmod:"umask 027" shows what new files and directories get; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a mode as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's re; it never looks at a file on disk; no network, no files read or written, no permission changed, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what you write, but the @chmod: reference and the explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @chmod: reference provider.

name: chorepilot
description: Your house and family chore board as Thor tools, through ChorePilot's own MCP server on this machine, the LAN or Tailscale. Runs appliances (lights, climate, dishwasher/washer/dryer, sprinklers, vacuum and more via Home Assistant, Home Connect, MQTT or a simulator) and keeps a rotating chore board that devices verify. ChorePilot's policy decides every call: water/heat actions wait for the person's own yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent's approval queue, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available to an agent. Bundles the chorepilot:household skill. Disclosure — each tool call sends HTTP requests with the bearer token in CHOREPILOT_TOKEN to the user's own ChorePilot server at CHOREPILOT_URL, and the plugin also lists that server's tools once at every Thor start (plain http only to loopback, private, Tailscale or .local/.lan/.ts.net addresses); chorepilot_call runs any device or chore tool the token's person may use (lights, climate, vacuum, locking and more) without a Thor approval prompt, with ChorePilot's own policy deciding, so water/heat actions wait up to two minutes for that person's yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available; no other network calls, no files read outside the plugin, no background processes, no telemetry, stdlib only.

name: chrome-tab-watchdog
description: Conservative Chrome tab cleanup with in-process observation and browser-call leases. Disclosure — runs a background thread inside Thor that proxies your local Chrome DevTools port (127.0.0.1:9222 → 127.0.0.1:9223, loopback only, you must point browser.cdp_url at it), injects a focus/activity listener into every Chrome page, rewrites browser_exec session names to a per-profile namespace, and a cron script you schedule auto-closes idle, duplicate and blank tabs (including tabs with unsaved text).

name: chronicle
description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Thor — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.thor/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

name: chronomancer
description: A shared plan for the Kanban cards of every profile on a gateway. Give a card a slot (a planned start and an estimate): the plugin parks the card and releases it at the start, with no cron job. Thor Desktop shows one timeline with a lane per profile; drag a card to plan or move it. Slots that overlap and share a one-at-a-time label show as clashes, with the reason and the next free start. An orchestrator agent plans through five tools. The plan advises: it never blocks a card or a tool call. Disclosure — reads and writes the Kanban board through Thor's kanban tools only; its Desktop backend imports the private core module tools.kanban_tools to register those tools in the dashboard process (validate warns about it); runs one daemon timer thread in every process that loads it (except Kanban workers), which releases parked cards to the Kanban dispatcher when their planned start arrives, so agent work starts unattended for any slot the owner or an agent set; stores card titles, profile names and labels in its own plan.db change log for 30 days; no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials.

name: chronos
description: Speculative branching: try several candidate fixes in isolated git worktrees, verify each against the project's tests through Thor' terminal tool, and merge only a verified winner through Thor' file tools. Disclosure — runs the project's test suite (the operator's `verifier_command`, or an auto-detected `pytest`, `unittest`, `npm test`, `cargo test` or `go test`) through Thor' terminal tool inside git worktrees under `THOR_HOME/plugin-data/chronos/`, so repository test code and model-written candidate files execute on the configured terminal backend; by default `chronos_branch` writes the best passing candidate's files into the working tree through Thor' `write_file` tool (subject to its denylist and approvals), and `chronos_rewind` checks out an earlier recorded commit (refused on a dirty tree).

name: chutes-provider
description: Chutes model provider for Thor Agent via API key. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CHUTES_API_KEY go to llm.chutes.ai (or CHUTES_BASE_URL), plus a GET /models catalog probe with the same key

name: ci-red-to-green
description: When a watched GitHub Actions run goes red, Thor tells you which tests failed and which commits came in since the last green run; reply fix and the agent fixes a clone, and a PR is offered only after the plugin's own reading of Thor's terminal output shows each failing test PASSED at the last green commit (when there was one), FAILED twice before the change (a pass before it marks the test flaky and blocks the PR), PASSED three runs in a row after it, and no new full-suite failures. pytest and go test. The PR commit holds source files only (no tests, test config, CI files or gitignored files), and the plugin reports the PR's own CI result. Desktop pane, page, palette commands and notifications. Try /ci demo with no token: a real humanize bug on a bundled copy. Disclosure: polls the GitHub API for the watched repos every 30 s while a watch is on (one background thread, stops on /ci stop or restart), downloads failed job logs without forwarding the token to the log host, compares commits, and creates a branch, commit and pull request only when you pick Open PR, all with CI_RED_TO_GREEN_GITHUB_TOKEN read through Thor's secret scope; the plugin runs no shell commands itself, while the agent clones the repo into plugin-data/ci-red-to-green/worktrees/ and runs its tests through Thor's terminal tool, with the first command that runs repo code escalated to Thor's approval prompt and git push from that folder blocked; stores watches, incidents and recorded test results in plugin-data/ci-red-to-green/; no telemetry.

name: ciphervault
description: Zero-knowledge secret backup for AI coding agents — masked sprawl scan, RAM-only run with exact-value output scrubbing, encrypted snapshots, pre_tool_call leak guard, and a secret source for Thor itself. Disclosure — `ciphervault_run` runs a model-chosen command with vault secrets in its environment after Thor's approval prompt, and an "always" grant covers every later command for that program (e.g. all `bash` or `python` invocations); in a workspace with a vault, or when a tool call names a path inside one, every other tool result is passed through the CipherVault CLI for scrubbing (withheld if that scrub or its audit receipt fails) and logged by hash to that vault's audit chain, each `ciphervault_run` approval request and replicated push sends a signed audit checkpoint (entry count + head hash) to your configured operator fleet (default `op1`–`op3.cipherv.online`), recovery drills query that fleet, and `thor ciphervault bootstrap` downloads a checksum-pinned CLI binary from the author's GitHub releases into the plugin's folder.

name: circuit
description: Design real PCBs by talking to your agent — a two-layer board compiler with a part library, deterministic placement, autorouting, an independent DRC, and a fabrication package (RS-274X Gerbers, Excellon drills, KiCad 8 project, STEP AP214), rendered in 2D and 3D in the desktop UI. Disclosure — circuit_samples downloads KiCad demo boards from gitlab.com and circuit_import url=… downloads a .kicad_pcb from any public web URL the agent is given (private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses are refused); the generated shopping list links to Digi-Key, Mouser, LCSC and Octopart searches.

name: circuit-bench
description: ESP32 workbench for Thor and Thor Desktop, from pin choice to running firmware: checks GPIO choices for ESP32, S2, S3, C3 and C6 against Espressif data, sizes parts with 16 calculators, draws schematics, plans the solder order, builds and flashes with your PlatformIO and esptool, and decodes panics to function and line so Thor can fix them. 180 modules carry datasheet-cited values. Every verdict and value comes from code with its source, never from the model. A marked simulation runs the whole flow without hardware. Disclosure — runs your own pio, esptool and addr2line as subprocesses (no shell, minimal environment); a build runs the firmware project's PlatformIO scripts with your user rights and asks first; opens serial ports only on request, which can reset the board; writes firmware only with 'Allow flashing real boards' on (off by default) and after confirmation; a schematic can also be saved as a new SVG into a folder you or the agent name (out_dir); background threads only while a port is open or the Bench is in use; no network calls from the plugin (PlatformIO may download packages on a first build), no telemetry, no credentials; data under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/circuit-bench/.

name: citation-guard
description: Catches fabricated, mismatched and retracted references. Checks each DOI / PMID / arXiv id and each full reference entry against doi.org, Crossref, PubMed and arXiv: ids that do not exist, ids that point to a different paper, wrong year or first author, works found in no registry, and retractions (Crossref notices incl. Retraction Watch). A transform_llm_output reply guard appends a warning footer when the agent's own answer cites something that does not check out (the reply text is never rewritten); a verify_citations tool and a /citecheck command (.md .txt .bib .docx) give full reports. Deterministic, Python standard library only, no LLM calls, no API keys. Disclosure — network calls to api.crossref.org, doi.org, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and export.arxiv.org carrying only the reference itself (id, title, first author, year), never the rest of the conversation; when references appear in a reply, the reply guard checks them on every such reply (up to 15 s by default); the optional contact_email setting is sent to Crossref and NCBI and the optional ncbi_api_key only to NCBI; a 7-day cache of registry answers in the plugin data directory; /citecheck reads the file the user names.

name: cjk_sanitizer
description: Strip unwanted Chinese (CJK) and Cyrillic characters from LLM output. Korean Hangul and Japanese Kana are preserved.

name: clack
description: Encrypted agent-to-agent messaging with durable receipts and no plaintext fallback. Disclosure — sends your agent's signed identity, relay service token and end-to-end-encrypted messages the model writes to the configured Clack relay (default relay.tryclack.com); messages received from peers are untrusted input handed to the model, and their decrypted text is kept indefinitely in plugin-data/clack; Linux/macOS only.

name: claim-check
description: Receipts for agent claims: checks the success claims in each final reply ("all tests pass", "I created src/app.py", "committed and pushed", "installed requests", "ran make build successfully", "server is running on port 8000") against the session's actual tool results and appends a ✅ verified / ⚠️ unsupported / ❌ contradicted footer citing the tool call. Optional nudge feeds contradictions back into the next turn; `/receipts` and the `claimcheck_report` tool show the evidence ledger. Deterministic, pure stdlib, works with any model. Disclosure — the post_tool_call hook sees every tool's name, args and result and writes a per-session JSONL ledger (tool, file path or first 500 chars of the command, exit status, last 300 chars of output; max 500 entries) under its plugin-data directory only; transform_llm_output appends a footer without holding the stream; pre_llm_call injects context only when `nudge` is enabled; no network calls, LLM calls, subprocesses, credentials, telemetry, background processes or self-updater.

name: claim-gate
description: Deterministic evidence-readiness firewall for insurance claim submissions. Resolves model-supplied evidence and incident-fact IDs against an operator-controlled SQLite registry, evaluates a versioned policy, and returns a deterministic PASS, BLOCK, or HUMAN_REVIEW. The model never gets to verify its own evidence.

name: claim-receipts
description: Records the file changes and commands a session's hooks observe, then gives each prose claim in the session one of four verdicts against that record: backed, unbacked, unverifiable, contradicted. Compares a claim with a capture; does not prove it true. Disclosure — reads Thor's own session database (state.db in the active profile) read-only at session end; writes an append-only ledger and per-session receipts under the plugin data dir, including file paths, terminal command strings (credential values redacted before storage since 0.1.1, with a SHA-256 digest of the exact command kept for identity; ledgers written by earlier versions are not rewritten, and an unlisted secret shape is still stored as typed) and excerpts of the assistant's claims; runs no shell commands; no network.

name: claude-code-theme
description: Unofficial Claude Code-inspired theme for Thor Desktop, with light and dark palettes, rounded composer and side-panel cards, softer sidebar and menus, and a context-window meter beside the model switcher. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic or Claude Code. Disclosure — unofficial Claude Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles native Desktop surfaces (user bubbles, composer, file panel, sidebar rows, dropdown menus) and hides the chat backdrop image; the context meter reads session.usage through the SDK; an opt-in accent setting uses setAccentOverride; no network calls of its own.

name: claude-pacer
description: For power users running heavy automation in Thor on a Claude Pro/Max subscription: claude-pacer paces agents and cron jobs so the weekly limit lasts to the reset, keeps a reserve (20% by default), and spends the leftovers on spare jobs before it. Modes skip / light / normal / heavy via the claude_pace tool, /pace, `thor pace` and a `thor pace gate --priority vital|normal|optional|spare` cron gate: an over-budget run is skipped before the model is called; a vital job always runs (lightly in skip mode). Disclosure — each check (cached 60 s in memory) runs Thor' own Anthropic usage fetch, one GET to Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint made by Thor; if the sign-in is a borrowed Claude Code login whose access token has expired, Thor refreshes it first (a POST to Anthropic's OAuth token endpoint and a rewrite of the Claude Code credentials file), as /usage would. The plugin's own code never reads, holds or writes a credential, writes no files, runs no subprocesses and sends no telemetry.

name: claude-subscription-directsdk
description: Experimental model provider that runs Thor turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. Requires the claude CLI installed and logged in; the plugin checks for it at load, in thor model, in the pickers and before every request, and refuses cleanly with the install hint when it is missing. Disclosure — every turn is billed against your Claude subscription's Agent SDK allowance, and the provider inherits whatever account claude is logged into.

name: claw-messenger
description: iMessage, RCS and SMS for Thor through Claw Messenger. Your agent texts real phones and gets replies, with no Mac or SIM; send, receive, group chats and attachments. Disclosure — all inbound and outbound message text, phone numbers and attachment links pass through the Claw Messenger hosted relay (wss://claw-messenger.onrender.com by default, a paid third-party service); your Claw Messenger API key is sent in the WebSocket URL together with a fixed client tag (thor-imessage/<version>); inbound attachments are downloaded (https only, up to 20 MB) from links the relay supplies into Thor's media cache; with the thor-claw-messenger toolset enabled the agent can start a group text with any phone numbers it is given.

name: clean-exit
description: Review the new files one Thor run wrote to a local project folder. Keep the deliverable, move selected working files into a project archive, and restore any archived file to its original path from the same workspace. Clean Exit observes successful native write_file calls after the user starts tracking and stores paths, sizes, file identities, and hashes in a local profile ledger.

name: clearance
description: Per-user tool permissions for Thor on messaging platforms and webhooks (#527, #3897): give each sender a tier (owner, admin, user, guest, blocked or your own) and every tool call is checked in code against the sender's tier before it runs, so a prompt cannot talk its way to terminal access. Deny-by-default for tools a tier does not name (new MCP servers included), per-tier hourly rate limits, a /clearance command to inspect and assign tiers from chat, and a local audit log of refused actions. Disclosure — pre_tool_call may block a tool call (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system) and pre_llm_call may block a turn for the blocked tier or a rate limit and appends one line of context naming the sender's current tier (gateway senders only); with the default settings every messaging and webhook sender is the `guest` tier (chat only, no tools) until assigned a tier in the plugin settings or with /clearance set, except senders Thor already lists in allow_admin_from (DM chats) or group_allow_admin_from (group chats), who get the `owner` tier in that scope (gateway_admin_tier changes or disables this; an explicit users entry wins); registers /clearance; reads only its own settings, the per-message session identity and the allow_admin_from / group_allow_admin_from lists from Thor's gateway config loader; writes its own settings on /clearance set|unset (owner only) and an audit log (tool and argument names, never values) in its plugin data directory; no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update. Not a sandbox: an allowed tool keeps its normal reach.

name: clearing
description: The Clearing is a writing editor inside Thor with 159 editing methods you can run by name: 11 editor passes, 9 composition checks drawn from Strunk's rules, 33 editorial methods, 56 craft techniques and 44 figures of speech it can find in your draft or suggest where one would help. Press Read my piece and it marks your own words with what to change, most important first. Nothing changes until you press Use this. Three reviewers, a newcomer, a skeptic and a line editor, can each read the piece and then argue it out. When a suggestion adds a fact you never wrote, it says so before you keep it, and the page shows how much of the piece is still your own words. A built-in quick check and dictionary work without a model. An independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Thor Labs. Disclosure: no network calls of its own. Editor passes go to the model you set in Thor, only when you start one, with secrets removed by Thor first; Bring in a link hands a public address to Thor's web_extract after refusing non-public hosts; dictation goes to Thor speech-to-text and, for a cloud service, waits until you press Send. Reads only files you pick, plus Thor's speech-to-text setting and the Hugging Face model cache, both read-only. No shell commands, background processes, stored credentials or telemetry; one observe-only post_auxiliary_call hook reads the finish reason, model name and token counts of its own calls. When it falls back to a local faster-whisper model it sets KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE in the Thor process. Your writing, its versions and a quote-stripped debug.log stay in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/clearing/; Delete forever in the Trash erases a piece.

name: clearvoice
description: Local push-to-talk speech bridge — your words on screen and spoken clearly in 17 languages, with no account, no cloud and no audio on disk. Disclosure — downloads Whisper and Piper voice models from Hugging Face on first use (Piper pinned to a fixed revision and checksum-verified); the transcribe and say-back tools read any absolute audio file path the agent names (up to 25 MB) and transcribe it on-device; with "Allow cloud speech" and a Gradium key set, audio and text are sent to api.gradium.ai; a tool can only queue a sentence, which is spoken aloud only after you press Speak it in the ClearVoice pane.

name: clef-music-tools
description: Transpose chord symbols, spell piano chords, map guitar tab to piano notes and find music guides through Clef's hosted MCP server, with a practice skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: tool calls send the chords, tab or search text the user provides to https://clefdrills.com/mcp; no account is involved and no tool changes data. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. The skill includes an offline Python transposition helper that makes no network calls.

name: cli-session-tabs
description: Directory-scoped native TUI tabs when the public core capability contract is advertised, with isolated tmux fallback. Disclosure — the tmux backend requires OS-installed tmux; explicit `thor tabs` commands probe the Thor CLI (`--help`, `--tui-capabilities`) and start private, long-running TUI or tmux/Thor clients only when invoked, passing the selected profile and the current terminal's pane identity through a credential/bypass-filtered environment; the tmux backend stores non-secret workspace metadata in profile plugin-data and confirms closes; native-tab persistence stays in core. Does not patch Thor or read conversations/credentials.

name: clinepass
description: ClinePass model provider with live model discovery and a curated fallback catalog.

name: cliproxyapi-provider
description: CLIProxyAPI as native Thor model providers: discovers each CPA provider group (Claude, Codex, xAI, Gemini, Kiro and others) and registers one profile per group on the wire its CPA executor accepts (Anthropic Messages, Responses or Chat Completions), with context windows and reasoning levels from CPA. Disclosure — sends model-list and inference requests, authenticated with the API key env var you name, to the CPA base_url you configure; with an optional management key it also makes bounded read-only GETs to CPA's management API; with an optional billing route it sends inference, and a model-list GET, to the gateway URL you configure, authenticated with the gateway key env var you name. Known limit: Thor strips from agent subprocesses only the key env vars a registered provider declares, so the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, stay readable by agent shells; the cpa-status companion hides them from a chat session's terminal commands on Thor 0.23.1 or later (environment variables only). Writes its model cache under $THOR_HOME/cache/cliproxyapi/, plus lock files and a rejected-key marker (salted HMAC, never a key) under $THOR_HOME/cache/cliproxyapi/locks/.

name: cloro
description: cloro web search backend: live Google Search results for the built-in web_search tool (search only; pair it with an extract backend for web_extract). Disclosure — sends each search query and the configured country to api.cloro.dev with your CLORO_API_KEY, and each search uses cloro credits. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers no tools, hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: cloudflare-sandbox
description: Run Thor terminal, file and execute_code tools in Cloudflare Containers, with the workspace saved to a snapshot when idle. Disclosure — you deploy the bundled Cloudflare Worker to your own account first; running containers is billed by Cloudflare; commands and file contents run in the container at THOR_CF_ENDPOINT using THOR_CF_TOKEN; the container has outbound internet by default (ENABLE_INTERNET); host env vars, skills and credentials are not copied into the container; dangerous-command approval stays on.

name: cloudflare-web-search
description: Cloudflare Web Search backend for Thor' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. Disclosure — sends queries, result limits, gateway IDs, and optional BYOK aliases to api.cloudflare.com, which forwards searches to the selected provider and records them in AI Gateway logs. Requests can consume gateway credits or provider quota. Reads its own settings and CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN through Thor' profile-scoped APIs. Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin.

name: cloudflare-workers-ai-provider
description: Cloudflare Workers AI as a Thor model provider (`--provider workers-ai`, or Cloudflare Workers AI in `thor model`, which asks for the token and the account's base URL): the 16 Workers AI models with function calling and 64K+ context, Cloudflare's context windows (a custom endpoint lists no models and assumes 256K for the 128K gpt-oss), reasoning effort in the form each model accepts, and a clear message when a free-plan account picks a paid-plan model. Not affiliated with Cloudflare. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); the model list and details are built in, so nothing is fetched to show them; chat requests go to the URL in CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL through Thor' own client with CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN, both read by Thor per profile; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: cloudgpu-provider
description: cloudgpu.app models (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax) via the OpenAI-compatible API at cloudgpu.app/v1: live model list from the public /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CLOUDGPU_API_KEY go to cloudgpu.app (or to CLOUDGPU_BASE_URL when the user sets it).

name: cmi
description: Deterministic, zero-LLM context engine (context.engine: cmi): fewer tokens resent on every request, so sessions last longer on the same plan. Old tool results and stale screenshots become short digests and old write payloads are removed from past calls, while tool pairs and a byte-stable cache prefix are kept; every original is stored first and comes back byte-exact with cmi_recall. When enabled, a pre_tool_call hook blocks a write whose payload is a CMI stub; a stub write that went through is flagged at the next request with the file's last known content. Replay of 26 real sessions with the provider cache modelled: 30% fewer tokens on average (modelled API cost -25%); live 195-request sessions: 49% fewer tokens. Disclosure: originals and a full-text index (SQLite FTS5) are written under $THOR_HOME (0700/0600, 30-day retention, 512 MiB cap); regex credential detection skips recognized secrets but can miss some; no network calls, no LLM calls, no dependencies. Project memory (experimental) is on for sessions opened in a Thor Desktop project folder and stores only claims a model publishes with the user's exact words as proof; turn it off with context.cmi.auto_project_binding false.

name: coach
description: Four modes: Consult on demand, Active per-turn review, Review before claiming done, and Decide for forks with Jev. Disclosure — once you configure a coach model, Coach sends turn transcripts, tool-call summaries, short records of memory/skill/cron/connection/kanban actions, and up to 160,000 characters by default (up to 400,000 if you raise it) of `git` diff and changed-file contents to that model through Thor' model routing, covering every file the agent edited in the session, including files outside your working repo; the optional Decide mode (off by default) sends the agent's question, options and state to `openrouter.ai` (Typesafe's Jev model, your `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) or `api.typesafe.ai` (your `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`); it runs read-only `git` in your session directory, keeps a background review thread, can hold a "done" reply once for review, and `/coach grant` writes its own model-override permission into `config.yaml`.

name: code-assurance-engine
description: Change-assurance engine: evaluates an immutable repository candidate against an explicit, reviewer-approved check contract and returns machine-readable evidence, findings and unverified gaps, so a green result has a defined scope. Disclosure — 6 tools plus a `thor assure` CLI and an `/assure` slash command; `assure_inspect` reads the candidate repository read-only with git (minimal git environment, option-like base/head refs refused, repositories whose own git config defines filter drivers refused); the candidate is frozen and identified by content before the contract is agreed; `assure_run` is the only operation that executes repository code, and it refuses unless the assessment is APPROVED and its venue gates pass; state stays inside the plugin's data directory, including an explicit `--state-dir` given from `/assure` or `thor assure`; the `--owner-keys` file is a path the caller supplies, so owner approval is only as strong as control of that path and of `/assure`; reports are private, local and render without external assets; no third-party network calls, no stored credentials, no telemetry and no self-updater.

name: codecoach
description: Teach yourself to code in C, C++, Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby or Bash: build a real program one small step at a time, practice by predicting what code prints, and take no-hints tests. Every example really ran in a sandbox, every pass is a real test, and it warns you when your model is weak in a language. Disclosure — Code runs inside a bubblewrap sandbox (no network; system folders and a language's own toolchain folder are mounted read-only, the rest of your home folder is not mounted); if you turn on `allow_unsandboxed_code` on a machine without bwrap, learner and model-written code runs directly on your host as your user with no Thor approval prompt. Imported .txt/.md/.pdf files (any non-hidden path you or the agent names) are sent to your configured model. It makes background model calls you did not press a button for (the next step, a spare drill, and five short warm-ups per language; the setting `auto_fit_check` turns the warm-ups off).

name: codemode
description: Code-as-Orchestration: the model writes one JavaScript snippet that calls your MCP tools (plus web_search/web_extract) in a QuickJS sandbox, loops and filters there, and returns only the answer. Tool schemas are found on demand with BM25 searchTools(). Disclosure — every run starts a short-lived local Python child process hosting QuickJS (minimal env, no API keys, no fs/network access, killed on finish or timeout); scripts can call every connected MCP tool plus web_search/web_extract (more via the `extra_tools` setting) through ctx.dispatch_tool, which keeps per-tool approvals such as MCP trust prompts and spend limits but does not run other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks or tool middleware on those inner calls and does not apply per-platform toolset limits to them; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: coder
description: Run Thor terminal commands in an existing remote Coder workspace. Disclosure — runs terminal commands inside your Coder workspace at CODER_URL using CODER_API_KEY; starts a stopped workspace automatically; forwards only the env vars you list in TERMINAL_CODER_FORWARD_ENV.

name: codex-chat-look
description: Independent Catppuccin Latte/Mocha desktop theme with peach accents, SDK-native gateway/profile switching and host-owned session density. Legacy plugin identity: codex-chat-look. No self-updater or native layout overrides. Disclosure — Desktop theme derived from FPSUnleashed's MIT-licensed desktop skin; switches gateway/profile via host.ensureAgent only on user selection and a palette command rewrites the native sessionListDensity setting; no network calls of its own.

name: codex-theme
description: Codex × ChatGPT inspired theme for the Thor Desktop chat: dual light/dark palettes that follow the system appearance, graphite-on-paper typography with a 1.625 root line height (measured from ZCode's chat body) and content-spacing presets (1.5/1.625/1.75), the OpenAI radius scale (inline 4px / rows 8px / controls 10px / cards 12px / composer 20px), hairline borders instead of shadows, and an 880px reading column with 768/880/992px presets. Settings → Plugins → Codex Theme offers appearance mode, reading width, content spacing, text & code font presets, user/assistant chat bubble colors and a bilingual (EN/中文) UI as native controls; the theme paints theme-level tokens only and never writes user-configurable settings such as --chat-text-scale. v1.2.0 is a compliance release — the composer-drag and input-focus-guard features of the v1.1 line were removed because they patched prototypes and captured global events, which catalog rule 8 forbids. Disclosure — no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials; registers only through the Desktop plugin SDK (THEMES_AREA, PALETTE_AREA, ctx.registerSettingsPage, ctx.i18n), switches the active theme to Codex once on first install, and keeps its preferences in plugin-scoped ctx.storage.

name: codex-truly
description: Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Thor only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Thor's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through Thor's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote.
