No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Thor's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.

name: coffee-vram
description: VRAM fit-check, call queue, keep-warm and idle eviction for local Ollama models, with a desktop status chip showing the active Thor model (cloud or local), context, and tok/s, plus /vram. The panel includes a Performance pet and host stats (GPU, RAM, CPU, network). Disclosure — when a local Ollama model won't fit, Coffee holds that call for up to the queue timeout (default 600 s) and, by default, unloads idle Ollama models (including ones other apps loaded, unless pinned) to make room; it also refreshes keep-alive on loaded models and polls the configured Ollama URL and NVIDIA telemetry in the background.

name: cognee
description: Knowledge-graph memory for Thor, shared with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins: automatic recall, remember, forget, recaps and code search, on Cognee Cloud or a local cognee server. Disclosure — in local mode it installs cognee==1.6.5 and its dependencies (about 1 GB from PyPI) into a private environment, ~/.cognee-plugin/thor/runtime, when you choose local mode (`thor memory setup cognee` or `thor cognee install-runtime`; never at session start), and runs a local cognee server from it (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011); a session-close watcher runs in the background; each turn plus its tool calls and results (redacted, capped) go to that server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default), or to Cognee Cloud / COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode; turns the server could not take are queued in ~/.cognee-plugin; the store lives in ~/.cognee, outside THOR_HOME and shared across profiles and with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins; cognee sends anonymous telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; the system prompt tells the agent to prefer Cognee memory over MEMORY.md/USER.md (COGNEE_MEMORY_STEER=false turns it off), and an answer that used recalled memory may end with a one-line Cognee credit, drawn with the Cognee logo by a transform_llm_output hook (COGNEE_PLUGIN_CITE_MEMORY=off turns it off).

name: cognition
description: Cognition session-end memory — facts regex-extracted from your messages at session end, stored in a local SQLite queue and JSON log under one repo label, with fetch-first merge, per-entry provenance, and budgeted prefetch (tools: cognition_search, cognition_status, read-only cognition_dream). Disclosure — saves verbatim excerpts (up to 400 chars) of your own messages that match preference/decision phrases in plain local files under THOR_HOME/cognition/ (SQLite queue, JSON commit log) and re-injects them into later prompts sent to your model provider; the author name is read from ~/.gitconfig; the plugin makes no network calls of its own.

name: coldstart
description: Evidence-gated answering with a provenance hierarchy, for any local AI deployment. Material you feed it (internal: transcripts, contracts, code, spreadsheets, PDFs, emails) is retrieved first and cited first; public reference material is used only when internal material does not cover the question, and every answer that leans on it is labelled as public; when nothing covers the question the reply is refused instead of invented. Every reply is then checked mechanically against the passages that turn actually retrieved -- quoted spans must be verbatim, and figures, dates, URLs and identifiers must appear in a retrieved passage (line and passage references are masked so citations are not mistaken for claims); prose paraphrase is reported but never blocked. No model is asked to grade its own answer. The clearance rule covers every path that touches private material: the model is taken from the turn the host actually runs (`pre_llm_call` reports it, recorded per session), so a session switched with `/model` or a turn that lands on a cloud fallback counts as remote; when it is not local, internal passages are withheld, `corpus_ask` requires both its endpoint and the turn to be local and otherwise answers from public material only, and `corpus_audit` / `/trust` refuse rather than sample internal passages into it. `/trust` runs a battery against the configured deployment and scores it: invented quote and invented figure must be caught, verbatim quote and paraphrase must pass, and the pipeline must abstain on questions the corpus cannot answer. Ships an agent half (2 hooks, 3 tools, 1 command, 1 skill) and a Desktop half (evidence pane, status-bar chip, mode switch, audit button) over the plugin's own `/api/plugins/` backend. Stdlib only -- no embeddings, no third-party dependency, no model call for retrieval. Disclosure -- reads only the directories configured in `corpus_roots` / `public_roots` plus its own index under `$THOR_HOME/plugin-data/coldstart/`; makes model calls through Thor's configured model or the OpenAI-compatible `endpoint` the user sets; shells out to `pdftotext` and `tesseract` only when present and only for the user's own files; optional `COA_API_KEY` is read through Thor's secret scope, never from a file; no telemetry, no self-update. Enabling the plugin holds the reply until the gate has run, so token-by-token streaming is off while it is enabled. Disclosure — reads only the directories configured in `corpus_roots` / `public_roots` plus its own index under `$THOR_HOME/plugin-data/coldstart/`, which stores copies of the indexed passages; makes model calls through Thor's configured model or the OpenAI-compatible `endpoint` the user sets; judges a model local from its URL host (loopback, RFC1918, Tailscale `100.64.0.0/10`, `.local`/`.lan`/`.internal`/`.home` names), any configured fallback, and the model name the turn reports compared by its last path segment, so a local proxy that forwards to a cloud API, or a `/model` switch to a cloud model with the same name, counts as local; shells out to `pdftotext` and `tesseract` only when present and only for the user's own files, with a minimal environment; optional `COA_API_KEY` is read through Thor's secret scope, never from a file; the Desktop pane's mode switch writes `plugins.entries.coldstart.settings.strictness`; no telemetry, no self-update. Enabling the plugin holds the reply until the gate has run, so token-by-token streaming is off while it is enabled, even with the gate set to `off`.

name: colorado-traffic
description: Live Colorado highway events from CDOT COtrip. No API key. Default corridor is I-70 Golden to east Denver. Separates incidents happening now from scheduled work and unverified Waze reports.

name: comemo
description: Composite memory meta-provider for Thor Agent. Comemo multiplexes Honcho, Mem0, and Supermemory simultaneously. Write fan-out goes to all configured providers in parallel, reads merge and deduplicate results across them. Failed writes are queued in a local SQLite retry store and replayed at the next session start. Maintained by Anda Usman. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries are sent to every enabled backend (Honcho at api.honcho.dev or your configured base_url, Mem0 at api.mem0.ai or MEM0_BASE_URL, Supermemory at api.supermemory.ai) under that backend's own API key, and writes that fail are kept in a local SQLite retry queue under THOR_HOME/comemo/ and replayed at the next session start.

name: comfy-recipe
description: Visible ComfyUI sessions, consent-based setup, workflow tools and media preparation inside Thor. Disclosure — on first use it can install its own ComfyUI in a folder you choose: it downloads uv 0.13.7 (checksum-verified) from GitHub, Python 3.13, the latest ComfyUI release, PyTorch and ComfyUI-Manager (unpinned upstream versions), then starts ComfyUI on 127.0.0.1 with ComfyUI-Manager enabled, plus background installer, download and watchdog processes that can outlive the chat. Model downloads fetch public https URLs that workflows declare or that the agent supplies (bundled ones use Hugging Face; private and internal addresses are refused, and localhost mirrors need the allow_local_mirrors setting), and node packs install third-party code through ComfyUI-Manager with your permissions. Discovery reads process command lines and ComfyUI Desktop / StabilityMatrix settings. Prompts, workflows and uploaded files go to the selected ComfyUI. Media tools run ffmpeg. Session titles are written through the public SessionDB. Cloud Recipe workflows spend Comfy account credits when run in your signed-in ComfyUI window; the plugin's instructions tell the agent to ask first, but Thor itself does not prompt before a paid run. No self-updater.

name: comfyrizz
description: Chat-as-frontend for the Comfyrizz film pipeline: brief, plan, revise, explicit accept, generate, CPU assemble, export, and retake. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, stdio mcp.json, comfyrizz-film skill) with the MCP server in-tree. Disclosure — the stdio server launches local Node that talks only to a loopback Comfyrizz engine URL (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL); optional Streamable HTTP binds 127.0.0.1 only when deliberately enabled and has no authentication, so any local process or web page in your browser can call its tools while it runs. Paid generation (Google Colab, Comfy API, or ComfyUI) is dispatched by the agent with an approval id it reads from the engine's spend card; the bundled skill tells the model to get your explicit yes first, but Thor itself does not prompt before paid generation or retakes. Env vars are forwarded as ${VAR} from the user environment (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL, COMFYRIZZ_MCP_HTTP, COMFYRIZZ_TOKEN, and optional provider keys); no credentials are stored in the package. No self-updater.

name: command-ledger
description: Local ledger of the slash commands you run in Thor (built-in commands in the CLI, built-in and plugin commands on messaging platforms): /command-log shows how often each command was used, its share, in how many sessions and when last, per command, platform, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /command-log recent lists the newest commands (ten, or up to 100 with /command-log recent 50) with the alias typed. Disclosure — writes command metadata (command name, alias typed, surface, platform, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no arguments, session key or user id) to plugin-data/command-ledger/commands.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot block or change a command; no network

name: command-reviewer
description: Reviews every `terminal` and `execute_code` call before execution: deterministic hard rules block credential reads and destructive patterns, script contents are ingested and judged (not just filenames), an LLM reviewer with an injection-resistant prompt issues SAFE/SUSPICIOUS/MALICIOUS verdicts, and operator approve/deny decisions are recorded content-hash-bound so an unchanged script is never re-asked. Disclosure - the reviewer reads the contents of script files the command names (inside the Docker sandbox via `docker exec` when available, otherwise from the host path), with the command text, and sends both to your configured auxiliary LLM; keeps an audit log, a precedent database of your approval decisions, and verdict caches keyed by script content hash and by command+content combination — the reviewer's own SAFE and MALICIOUS verdicts are reused for identical commands and scripts with no LLM call, while SUSPICIOUS is never cached and always reaches the approval prompt — all under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/command-reviewer/; reads config.yaml (read-only) to see whether you answered \"Always\" to one of its prompts, and — for terminal commands only — whether your own approvals.deny globs will refuse it before spending LLM tokens on it; can only block or escalate to the approval prompt, never auto-approves; ships in shadow mode (log only) until you set `mode: enforce`.

name: command-tray
description: Session command tray — shell commands the Thor agent ran via the terminal tool (success and failure). Desktop pane and /commands. No API keys. Disclosure — records terminal commands with exit code, workdir and a 160-char redacted output preview to $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/command-tray/state.json; the Desktop pane inserts text through Thor Desktop's internal thor:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API) with clipboard fallback; no network.

name: commandcode-oauth
description: Command Code CLI-key model provider with a live OAuth catalog property bridge, plan limits and failover classification. Disclosure — uses the CLI-internal api.commandcode.ai/alpha/generate endpoint and CLI client headers, sends the full conversation, tool schemas, cwd path and OS/Python version, and imports a static key from the read-only CLI credential file or a browser hand-off; no OAuth exchange takes place. Thor also bundles commandcode for the documented Provider API.

name: comment-scraper
description: Ask about the Reddit and Hacker News threads you exported with the Comment Scraper browser extension: list, read, search and quote them by comment number. Disclosure — starts a local stdio MCP server with npx -y comment-scraper-mcp@0.1.0, which npx downloads from npm on first run; the server only reads JSON exports in ~/Downloads and the folders directly inside it, never writes files, makes no network requests, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry.

name: common-ground
description: Durable collaboration records, mutual contributions and evidence-backed commitments.

name: commonly-thor-plugin
description: Gives Thor tools to read a Commonly pod and post to it, through the @commonlyai/mcp server (stdio), plus a skill for working in a pod. The tools work while Thor is running. Nothing wakes Thor when someone @mentions it in the pod. Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — On first use, npx downloads @commonlyai/mcp from npm and runs it locally; that package is published from Team-Commonly/commonly but is not covered by the pinned sha. Every tool call goes to https://api.commonly.me with the Commonly agent token kept in the profile .env as COMMONLY_AGENT_TOKEN. The server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before any tool that posts or comments, deletes the agent's own messages, uploads a local file, changes tasks or memory, messages other agents, joins or creates a pod, or runs commonly_catch_up (which marks an unread backlog as skipped on the server); read-only tools run without a prompt. File uploads are limited to the folder the server starts in or folders listed in COMMONLY_ATTACH_ROOTS, and hidden and key files are refused.

name: commonplace
description: Commonplace — local-first curated memory in plain Markdown files on your own machine. Standing rules kept verbatim, a curated store with lexical recall, a handover card for fresh sessions, and a fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint (API v2) that archives the transcript before Thor may compress it — and blocks compression when the archive cannot be written. No cloud, no API keys, no third-party dependencies. Maintained by Chris Newton. Disclosure — stores everything as plain, unencrypted Markdown under the active Thor home's `commonplace/` directory, including a verbatim journal of every user/assistant turn and full-transcript archives written before each compression; none of it is pruned automatically. No network calls, credentials or third-party dependencies.

name: compartment
description: Encrypted, fully offline memory provider. AEAD-encrypted local vault (vectors included), bundled embedding model, exact hybrid search, no API key and no network at runtime. One vault shared with Claude, Cursor and any other MCP client on the machine. Disclosure — installs the full compartment engine (about 27 Python packages including onnxruntime, tokenizers, mcp and system-tray dependencies) into the Thor venv; the provider's system prompt instructs the model to store passwords and API keys in the encrypted vault.

name: completion-proof
description: Revision-bound receipts for operator-configured checks; changed source, tests or artifacts make earlier passes stale. Disclosure — proof_verify, `/proof verify` and `thor completion-proof verify` run the check commands the user configures (argv, no shell) in the configured workspace with the user's OS privileges, unsandboxed, with a minimal environment (no credentials); the model can start these runs by check id without an approval prompt but cannot add or change commands; `thor completion-proof init` writes a starter test command (pytest, npm test or unittest) into the plugin's settings for review; receipts, redacted output excerpts and hashes of tool commands/results are stored in the plugin's own database; once per coding turn the pre_verify hook may ask the model to run the checks; no network or telemetry.

name: completion-sound
description: Pick the sound Thor Desktop plays when a turn finishes: one of the 14 built-in presets or your own audio file (mp3, wav, ogg), with an optional different sound during night hours. Files stay in the plugin's local storage. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: composer-modes
description: Cursor-style composer modes (ask / agent / plan / debug) for the Thor desktop — the mode's operating note reaches the model inside the turn's model-facing bytes, never the bubble, transcript or session titles, and ask mode is enforced read-only on the tool side.

name: composio-connections
description: Connect and disconnect Composio accounts from Thor Desktop and the web dashboard. Lists every row the Composio CLI returns, including expired, duplicate, and unaliased accounts, opens OAuth in the user's browser, and disconnects one exact account after confirmation. No agent tools or hooks. Catalog metadata uses COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY through agent.secret_scope.get_secret and requests only https://backend.composio.dev. Disclosure — inventory, connect, and disconnect run the composio CLI already logged in on the gateway; the API key never reaches the browser. Removing a Composio connection does not revoke every permission at the provider. The bundled service logos include an Ngrok mark; the plugin does not open a tunnel.

name: compound-security
description: Security audit, dependency inspection, remediation, and verification skills. Disclosure — skills only (no code runs at load); when invoked, the workflows have the agent read the repository you point it at, write audit reports and checkpoints under `~/.compound-security/audits/` by default, and in patch / fix / run / lfg modes edit that repository (code, tests, lockfiles) through Thor' normal file and terminal tools; bundled Node.js scripts only validate and render its own JSON records; online `npm audit` / `outdated` runs only when you collect them.

name: computer-view
description: Private Telegram desktop viewing and user takeover with cooperative tool fencing. Disclosure — Exposes a dedicated Linux virtual desktop to the owner's phone through a user-run HTTPS proxy/tunnel: it uses the profile's `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` to send a single-use 5-minute bearer link (30-minute session) to the configured owner's private Telegram chat via api.telegram.org, and anyone holding a live link can watch and, after "Take control", type and click on that desktop; while enabled its tool_execution middleware refuses browser_exec, computer_use and browser_vault in every session of the profile whenever the user holds control, before `thor computer-view setup` has run, when `plugins.isolation` is not `in_process`, and after any failed browser action until the owner runs `thor computer-view recover --local-owner`; `thor computer-view assets` downloads a SHA-256-pinned noVNC archive from codeload.github.com.

name: concord-for-thor
description: Coordinates allowlisted GitHub existing-file writes with revision checks, verified receipts and exact-operation replay. Disclosure — writes file contents directly to the GitHub repositories you allowlist, via your own `gh` CLI and its authentication (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are forwarded to `gh` only, never logged or stored); keeps a local coordination/receipt database under the Thor plugin-data directory, which `thor plugins remove` does not delete.

name: conductor
description: Thor leads coding agents on your machines: any terminal coding agent, T3 Code threads, and Orca terminals. It starts a run, waits with no model, and puts one message into the chat that asked when the run finishes, errors, stalls, or needs an approval; T3 and Orca runs can be steered and stopped. It can run 10+ agents at once, one ping each. Two skills: brief researches, asks one round of questions and writes the brief; lead runs the work and checks each report. Disclosure — every start and steer of a coding agent goes through Thor's approval prompt; it runs only the built-in agents on this machine unless the owner lists extra commands and SSH hosts in plugins.entries.conductor.settings (both empty by default); runs the agent, git status, and ssh and tmux on listed hosts (argv only, no shell strings from user text, never an approval-bypass flag); the agents edit files and run commands with your user rights under their own approval settings; children get a minimal environment plus only the keys that agent needs; keeps one wait thread per run plus a detached agent process or tmux window; writes run records to its plugin data folder and event files, exit codes and logs under ~/.conductor on the machine running the agent; reads and stores no credentials; no telemetry. Finish messages on a messaging gateway need plugins.entries.conductor.allow_gateway_injection: true. In drive mode, which only the user can turn on, it asks Thor to send up to 5 follow-ups per run on its own.

name: confidential-mode
description: Thor Confidential Mode locks a Thor profile to one tier: attested (a Tinfoil enclave, or NEAR AI Cloud's gateway and models, verified and pinned to a build you approve) or on-host-only (loopback and hosts you list). While locked, the plugin refuses off-tier main model calls before they are sent; refuses to lock while a side call, fallback, memory, MCP URL or delegation route would leave the tier; on the attested tier encrypts request bodies to the verified enclave or model key and pins every inference connection to the TLS key of the attestation the plugin accepted (the attestation fetch itself is not pinned, by design), with headers, sizes and NEAR images still visible to the vendor; and asks you the first time each tool it does not class as on-host (by where the tool's data goes) runs in each conversation during a lock, blocking the call when nobody can answer. The plugin logs each model call's host and size, never its text, and renders a receipt whose attached enclave evidence replays offline; the rest of the receipt is the plugin's own record. The attested tier needs TINFOIL_API_KEY or NEAR_AI_API_KEY. Shell and code execution are not inspected for network access, and a side call that strays mid-turn is recorded, not stopped. Disclosure — the plugin contacts the vendor (atc.tinfoil.sh, the Tinfoil router and the *.tinfoil.sh collateral proxies, or cloud-api.near.ai), Intel Trust Authority (portal and portal.eu), Sigstore's TUF CDN, and GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com, api.github.com) for NEAR compose files, also in the background after a verification stages a NEAR entry; the plugin sends no telemetry. The plugin writes under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/ (including the ledger, evidence blobs, pins.yaml, allowlist.yaml, state and SDK caches), Thor' tool-discovery cache on a terminal lock, and, on a revoke only, config.yaml, removing its own plugin_rule:confidential-mode:tool entries from command_allowlist and no other entry, through Thor' save_config, which also normalises legacy model and max_turns keys as any Thor config save does; the plugin reads config.yaml and script files a locked tool call runs. The plugin reads TINFOIL_API_KEY and NEAR_AI_API_KEY through Thor' secret scope, checks only whether OPENROUTER_API_KEY and NOUS_API_KEY are set (to report Thor' side-call fall-through), reads TERMINAL_ENV, TERMINAL_CWD, THOR_HOME, CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_PROGRESS and CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_NO_FETCH, sets XDG_CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_TOOL_PROCESS, stores no credential and runs no shell command or subprocess. The plugin starts daemon threads of five kinds: an attestation, a pins.yaml match record, a NEAR compose-file fetch, the own-host-name DNS lookup, and, while locked, one long-running re-verification thread per attested provider. During each Tinfoil attestation and each thor confidential replay, the plugin wraps the Tinfoil SDK's fetch functions and requests.Session.request process-wide, inert for every other thread, and puts the original functions back afterwards; before its first verification it also re-points the Tinfoil SDK's cache-directory constants and sigstore-python's TUF directory function at its plugin-data directory for the rest of the process. The plugin adds a locked-mode note to each locked turn's context and may append one notice line to a reply. thor plugins validate counts 31 private core import sites, all reads (docs/DISCLOSURE.md).

name: constraint-vault
description: Pins the user exact constraints (numbers, addresses, hard rules) as structured local data and re-injects them verbatim into the model context on every turn and immediately after every context compaction, with a SHA-256 hash-logged injection record, because memory providers and compression silently paraphrase or drop exact values. Not a memory provider and not a compressor: a guard layer above both. Disclosure — local code only, no network or processes; stores constraints in constraint-vault.json in the Thor home and appends a hash record to constraint-vault-injections.jsonl on every turn; the model can pin or drop constraints through its own tools without asking, and pinned text is injected into the model context on every turn of every session until dropped.

name: construct
description: Persistent, editable objects for Thor, not one-off images or meshes. Thor researches a thing; Construct keeps its parts, sizes and sources, checks it, and lets you change, combine and reuse the same object across worlds, film and print. Disclosure — runs Construct's bundled Python (source, no binaries) in local subprocesses with a minimal allowlisted environment (no provider keys); optionally runs local programs the user already has (a Chromium-family browser headless over a local debugging port for review stills, ffmpeg, FreeCAD, Blender, and NetLogo/Java), each found via the plugin's settings, `CONSTRUCT_*` variables or PATH, never from tool arguments and never downloaded; NetLogo runs with agent-written setup/go code or a model outside the installed Models Library always go through Thor' approval prompt and are refused in scheduled runs; other program runs ask first, once for each program, while the "Ask before running programs" setting is on (on by default since 1.3.2; scheduled runs are then refused); reads model and scene files at paths the agent or user gives it, and writes only in its data folder and the user-chosen projects folder; long work runs as local background jobs; in Desktop, the Construct pages run the plugin's own `/construct` commands in a "Construct page" session it creates per profile; one network call only, downloading a gallery construct (its scene JSON, at most 8 MiB a file) from Construct's own GitHub repository at this version's tag, after the user approves it in Thor' prompt and never in scheduled runs (curl, with a minimal environment and no keys, only when Python has no certificates); no credentials, no telemetry.

name: contagion
description: Taint-aware execution. Once a session reads untrusted content, its commands lose network, secrets and out-of-project writes at the OS layer. Disclosure — Contagion replaces the local terminal backend (`terminal.backend: contagion`): until a session is marked tainted its commands and file tools run on the host like the local backend, and core's local-only locked-skill terminal guard does not run for it. Taint detection is pattern-based on tool names and terminal/code text and is kept in memory only, so a restart or `/contagion clear` lifts it for every session; while tainted, jailed commands can still read files outside your home directory and write inside the project folder, and egress tools are gated only by an approval prompt. The URL, query or first 120 characters of each command that caused taint are logged to the plugin's data folder.

name: content-engine
description: One long video in, a week of content out. Paste a YouTube URL, get scored 45 to 60 second clips and per-platform social copy. Live in 90 seconds, no editing software.

name: contract-hunter
description: Scout-powered EVM contract vulnerability hunter. Radar → surface → prove → report pipeline for bounty programs. Disclosure — wraps the separately installed scout CLI (github.com/NathanOyewole/scout, installed at commit e2889e0), which contacts Immunefi, Sourcify, DexScreener and block explorers, and whose prove step runs forge tests on a local fork of a public RPC (SCOUT_RPC overrides; never broadcasts); /hunt serve starts a detached scout dashboard on 127.0.0.1 behind a random token that keeps running until the user stops it; an optional session-start Immunefi pull is off by default (auto_pull_immunefi); scout runs with only PATH, HOME, USER and SCOUT_RPC from the environment.

name: contract-necromancer
description: Thor's done doesn't count until your tests pass. Type /necro freeze in your project: it finds your tests and the command that runs them, writes necro.toml, locks the test files and the settings that choose what runs by hash, and runs them once to say where they stand. When Thor says it is finished, the plugin runs them itself at the verify step and sends Thor back with the failing test named; the final reply says when Thor was sent back and ends with a receipt anyone can re-check, also in a fresh clone (/necro verify: CONFIRMED, MISMATCH or SUPERSEDED). Edits to locked tests are blocked, and any change that gets through fails the check. Only a person can freeze: /necro is a slash command the agent cannot type, and from its shell freezing refuses. A prompt or skill can only ask the model to test its work; these hooks run whether it asks or not. Disclosure — runs the test commands in the project's frozen necro.toml (split into words, no shell; a command the person types after /necro freeze that uses shell syntax such as && or | is stored and run as sh -c) in the project folder with the user's permissions, unsandboxed, with a small environment (no API keys unless a contract names them), at /necro freeze, from pre_verify, from the final-reply hook when project files changed or the reply claims done, from the necro_check tool (the model can call it but cannot change the commands) and from /necro check; verify re-runs them only for a lock the person approved for that folder, or with --run; with no necro.toml, /necro freeze reads file names and test settings (package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, Cargo.toml) to pick the command, and may run that command's Python with -c "import pytest" in an empty folder (a project interpreter such as .venv/bin/python only when the person typed it); contracts run with the PATH of the Thor process that runs the agent, minus Thor's own runtime; reads project files to hash them but never opens credential files such as .env (their pins hold only presence, size and file times); never opens or follows a link (its pin is the link's own text); runs git ls-files with fsmonitor and hooks off and the same small environment; writes .necro/ and necro.toml in the project, and approval records plus the key that seals them (HMAC) under the plugin's data directory; adds NECRO_AGENT_SESSION to the environment of commands the agent runs; runs ps when someone runs freeze, approve or unfreeze from a shell; no network, no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes.

name: contractguard
description: Thor-native API contract assurance: validates proposed requests before they are sent, verifies live responses even when the status code is 200, compares candidate contracts against a human-approved baseline, and keeps redacted evidence receipts. Disclosure — makes HTTP requests only to a loopback address (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) the user registered explicitly, and only with GET or HEAD; write methods are validated offline and never dispatched. Reads the OpenAPI document at the exact path named in a tool call, and writes only to the Thor plugin database (service registrations, immutable contract baselines, redacted evidence receipts). No telemetry, no third-party calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials; secret-bearing headers are rejected from tool arguments. Baseline promotion requires human approval and fails closed when approval is unavailable.

name: conxt
description: Conxt governed memory provider — recall before each turn (personal, plus a team's approved memories), conversation capture in batches, and tools to search, remember, and propose team memories that a person approves in Conxt before anyone recalls them. Disclosure — Each turn's message (first 500 characters) and the conversation's user and assistant messages are sent to the Conxt API at mcp.conxt.dev (or an https CONXT_BASE_URL you set) with your CONXT_API_KEY; tool results are not sent, but text the assistant repeats is. Every entry Thor's built-in memory tool adds is also copied to your Conxt memory, and conxt_remember / conxt_propose send the memory text they are given. No telemetry, no shell commands, and nothing is written automatically from cron or subagent runs. Requires a Conxt plan that includes API keys.

name: cooldown
description: Checks every package Thor is about to install with pip, uv, poetry, pipx, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun or npx. Blocks versions OSV lists as malicious, and holds the install in Thor's own approval prompt when a release is younger than 3 days (the rule Thor uses for its own dependencies), the package is brand new, or the name is not on the registry. Disclosure — for each package named in an install command the agent runs in the terminal, it sends the package name and version (never your code, files or prompts) to api.deps.dev, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and api.osv.dev (keyless, no account, no telemetry); it keeps the last 50 checked install commands (first 300 characters each, as typed) and their verdicts in its own plugin state; a lookup can add up to about 20 seconds before an install command runs; it never runs the install itself and only ever blocks or asks through Thor' approval prompt.

name: coolifybruecke
description: See what needs you across your Coolify instance, deploy with your approval, and let Thor explain failed deploys. Disclosure — Talks only to your Coolify instance with the tokens you give it, Coolify's public release feed (cdn.coollabs.io) and, for "branch ahead", your apps' git hosts (an optional git token is sent only to the host you name, or GitHub). Agent actions (deploy, restart, stop, rollback) each ask for approval and are refused in cron, webhook and one-shot runs. `thor coolifybruecke alerts on` writes a script to Thor' scripts folder and adds a no-agent cron job by running `thor cron`; `alerts off` removes both. No telemetry.

name: coreweave
description: Run Thor on CoreWeave Serverless Inference with live model discovery, streaming responses, and an OpenAI-compatible API. Disclosure — Thor sends model discovery and chat requests, including prompts and tool results, to https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1 (CoreWeave / W&B Inference) using COREWEAVE_API_KEY; the installed provider registers a profile only and reads no credential files, starts no processes and adds no telemetry.

name: corkboard
description: One shared board, across every profile, of things only you can do. Agents pin a task, a yes/no question, a choice of up to four (their recommendation starred) or a text question instead of burying it in chat; you answer from a Desktop side pane, the full Corkboard page, `thor corkboard` or `/corkboard`. Blocked kanban cards are pinned automatically and your answer goes back to the card as an "Owner decision" comment, which resumes the worker. Pins can clear themselves when a check passes (nameservers changed, a kanban card unblocked). Text pins never ask for secrets; credential needs are always tasks. Disclosure — keeps one SQLite board shared by all profiles at ~/.thor/plugin-data/corkboard/data.db, so every profile with the plugin enabled (and any authorized gateway user via `/corkboard`) can read, answer, complete or dismiss every profile's pins and answers; runs `dig +short NS` for DNS checks and `thor kanban show/list/comment` to read cards and post owner answers (an agent chooses which card a pin's answer is posted to); owner-added `--check-command` checks run a shell command (5s timeout) on `thor corkboard check` without an approval prompt (the agent tool cannot create them); no network calls of its own beyond DNS lookups, no background process, no cron, no telemetry.

name: corpus
description: Hosted Corpus MCP (Streamable HTTP at corpuslaw.us/api/mcp) plus two bundled skills: US law search/get_node/list_coverage over 571k+ provisions, and LLC/nonprofit formation intake (requirements, compare, NAICS lookup, handoff, USDC checkout, payment_status), with account.status for quota. Filing always stays human-gated and USDC pay is email-confirmed. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); no API key needed for anonymous research. The formation skill requires fixed vendor-authored marketing copy in the first reply and before payment, and sends founder PII (name, email, phone, address) to Corpus through links and MCP tools. Intake instructions are vendored; checkout requires exact-amount confirmation from the user in the current turn.

name: corpus-open
description: For pro se and self-represented litigants: people handling their own lawsuit or court case without a lawyer. Legal citation checking for AI drafts. Under every reply, a citation guard lists each case, statute and code cite with what CourtListener (case law), Corpus (statutes from all 50 states) and the person's own case file hold at it, and flags a fake (hallucinated) citation before it reaches a court filing; a cite that cannot exist is caught with no lookup at all. A quote guard refuses a write that misquotes a filed document or cites the wrong page. Each session opens with the case's court deadlines, and an intake skill interviews the person one plain question at a time. Twelve tools keep a local litigation case folder (labeled facts with sources, evidence, deadlines, brief check, a packet for an attorney deciding whether to take the case, court rules, hash verification), /matter shows it, and Thor Desktop gets a Case pane. Disclosure — cite checks are on by default for every case and send bare citations (never case text) to CourtListener (only once a key is set) and corpuslaw.us; each request is logged in the case folder, and checks can be turned off per case or everywhere (citation_guard local). Case files stay on the computer. The CourtListener key is read through Thor's secret settings, falling back to the key the kit's own matter.py saves in ~/.config/matter-kit. On a session's first turn it adds the case's deadlines to the agent's context, and it asks for Thor approval before shell or file commands that look like they change a registered case document. /matter watch on writes a deadline-check script into Thor's scripts folder and prints a cron command for you to run; it schedules nothing itself. PDFs are read with the local pdftotext program when installed. Not a lawyer and not legal advice.

name: cortexlayer
description: CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into Thor' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence Thor' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.

name: cortiq-thor-router
description: AllaiGate model routing for Thor — inexpensive models for simple tasks, stronger models for complex work. Classifies every call of a turn (POST /v1/route), picks a model from your globalTiers/taskRules and rewrites the outgoing request via llm_request middleware; tier entries with their own endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, cortiq, cloud) run through llm_execution with fail-open. Config: ~/.config/cortiq-thor-router/config.json, key: CORTIQ_ROUTER_KEY. Built-in statistics: /cortiq-router stats. Disclosure — sends the text of every model call (the user's message, and on each tool-loop step the tool outputs, up to 12,000 characters by default) to the AllaiGate classifier (router.allaigate.com by default) with your CORTIQ_ROUTER_KEY; set `toolSteps: "low"` to send only the first message of each turn; tier entries with their own endpoint send the whole conversation to that endpoint; its config file (~/.config/cortiq-thor-router/config.json) is shared by all profiles.

name: cortive
description: Adds Cortive, a private knowledge base for your Mac, to the agent's memory, alongside Thor's built-in memory: automatic recall of the pages, PDFs, screenshots, documents and notes you saved, plus cortive_search, cortive_get and cortive_collections tools. Finds by meaning while the Cortive app is running, by words otherwise. Read-only and local. Disclosure — reads the local Cortive library file (~/Library/Application Support/cortive-ai/cortive.db, SQLite opened read-only), which is outside the plugin's own data; connects to the Cortive app's owner-only Unix socket on the same Mac (~/Library/Application Support/Cortive/agent/search.sock) to send search text and receive capture ids and scores; writes exported screenshots and an optional config file inside its Thor plugin-data folder. No network calls, no credentials, no background services, no telemetry. Recalled excerpts reach the model Thor uses, like any context; passwords and keys are hidden first, and the plugin is off in group chats by default. Two tool hooks enforce that: pre_tool_call refuses other tools' calls that point at Cortive's data folder, and transform_tool_result hides passwords saved in Cortive from other tools' output.

name: cospark
description: Workflow skill for ad research, image and video generation, voiceovers, and media inspection with Cospark. Disclosure: skill-only portable package; the user separately connects api.cospark.so/mcp through Thor native OAuth. Hosted tools process supplied prompts and media and can spend Cospark credits or change project files. No executable plugin code, credential access, bridge, background process, self-updater or package telemetry.

name: cost-forecast
description: Quotes a task's cost before it runs and stops for your OK when it would go over budget. Before a task starts it estimates the number of model calls and tokens (P50 and P90), prices them at your model's rates, and shows a quote when the task is large or could exceed your per-task cap. While the task runs it costs every call (subagents included), re-forecasts after each call, and pauses or stops at the soft cap, hard limit or daily cap. Estimates learn from your own finished tasks. API-key users only. Disclosure — fetches public prices from https://models.dev/api.json on a short background thread, at most once a day when the fetch succeeds (it retries on later lookups after a failure); if the optional cheap-model estimate (l3_mode, off by default, needs the llm.model_override grant) is on, one extra short call per quote sends up to 1,500 characters of your message through Thor to your own provider; stores spend, task history (message text removed, only hashed word counts kept), learned coefficients and, for up to 30 minutes, the text of a request held for your OK in a SQLite database under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/cost-forecast/; reads model.provider and agent.reasoning_effort from your config and whether the working directory is inside a git repo (a .git check, no commands); no credentials, no shell commands, no telemetry.

name: cost-sentinel
description: Live cost ledger and daily budget guarddog for Thor Agent, per profile or fleet-wide — every LLM call is priced with Thor' own pricing engine into a per-profile SQLite ledger plus a shared fleet ledger (all profiles of the install roll into one daily number); /cost rules the budget (set, block, warn, off, scope fleet or profile, resume, reset), the cost_report tool lets the agent read it, and the hard pre_llm_call gate stops an over-budget turn with an escape-hatch message. Desktop pane shows the gate number (fleet or profile) with a spend ring, per-model and per-day breakdowns and a status-bar budget chip. Disclosure — writes a per-profile SQLite ledger and a ledger shared by every profile of the install at <default thor root>/plugin-data/cost-sentinel/fleet.db, which also holds the daily budget settings, so /cost set, block, resume or reset in any profile changes the budget for all profiles; rows store tokens, cost, model/provider, session/turn/request ids, platform and error type plus the first 400 characters of provider error messages, never prompt, response or tool-argument text; the hard gate is off by default, is checked once before each turn (a turn already running can overshoot), and counts calls Thor cannot price as $0; no network of its own (pricing goes through the host pricing engine), no MCP, shell, credentials or telemetry.

name: costguard
description: A brake pedal for model spend. Meters every API call per session and per day from the provider's own usage block; dollar figures are estimates computed only for models in its price table and are never invented for unknown models. When a provider reports no usage (common with streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints), it falls back to request-size estimates and flags those calls as estimated in every total, never pricing them. Warns the agent at a configurable ratio of any configured budget and blocks tool calls once a session or daily token/cost budget is exceeded, stopping the tool loops where runaway spend happens; with no budget configured it only meters and reports. Disclosure: observes API request/response metadata (token usage, model, session id) and tool call names in profiles where it is enabled; stores only aggregate counters locally under $THOR_HOME/costguard/; makes no network calls; the brake cannot cancel the reply already being generated when a budget trips, it stops the tool work that reply tries next.

name: costory
description: FinOps harness MCP for platform teams. Bills normalized in BigQuery and allocated to teams. Build on it, or try it next to your tool. Read-only on cloud. Starter from $300/month, 30-day free trial. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) connecting Thor to Costory's hosted MCP at https://app-api.costory.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Bundles seven FinOps skills: query, cost-change-investigation, virtual-dimensions, dashboards, reports, recipes and bigquery. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code beyond the pin; every tool call goes to app-api.costory.io after browser OAuth (enterprise SSO on Costory Team and above). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Costory has write-capable tools that create or change Costory objects only (alerts, reports, dashboards, events, allocation rules, archives), never cloud resources; plugin.json sets extensions.com.thorlabs.thor.servers.costory.trust: untrusted so Thor asks before writes and refuses them in unattended runs. No mcp-remote, no local credentials, no self-updater.

name: counterparty
description: Screens the companies your agent is about to pay, email, sign with or buy from. Before any outward action (email, payment, order, transfer, signature, form submit) a pre_tool_call hook reads the vendor, email domain or URL from the call and checks it against the DoD Section 1260H list, the FCC Covered List, Section 889, the UFLPA Entity List, the BIOSECURE list and OFAC sanctions, with the ownership chain from public records, then escalates hits through Thor's own approval prompt with the finding and its legal citation (never auto-approves; fails closed under cron). Search and page results that mention a listed vendor get a one-time note. Tools cp_screen, cp_lookup, cp_credit, cp_who_owns_address and cp_brief answer on demand; /whoowns gives a cited one-page brief. Works offline from a bundled list snapshot and says so. Disclosure — Sends the counterparty name, email/URL domain label, and (for cp_screen/cp_brief) the description and amount, or a street address and ZIP for address lookups, over HTTPS to shop.tensorust.com (Tensorust LLC, the plugin author's company) whenever a matching outward tool call (email, payment, order, signature, submit), one of its tools or /whoowns runs, plus a daily list-membership refresh; message bodies are matched locally only; optional TENSORUST_API_KEY through Thor's secret scope; no telemetry, no shell, no file reads outside its bundled data.

name: courier-by-autolane
description: Restaurant pickup delivery in Austin, Texas: the user places a pickup order, and an Autolane vehicle collects it and drives it to them for a flat fee, through Autolane's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE; the user links a mobile number with a texted code), with one ordering skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Autolane's MCP server at mcp.goautolane.com with store and drop-off addresses, the customer's name and order details, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. reserve_delivery, confirm_delivery, update_delivery and cancel_delivery book, change or cancel a real delivery and take payment; the package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Autolane's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Invite-only for now. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add courier-by-autolane --url https://mcp.goautolane.com/courier-mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: courierpr
description: Read-only press release wire MCP server and skill: browse newsroom desks, list and search published company press releases, and read the opening of one with a link to the full release. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to the public read-only MCP server at courierpr.com (https://courierpr.com/api/mcp), which only reads published press releases (company-written announcements, not independent reporting); no sign-in, no key, nothing written, no local commands. The package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: coursebook
description: A native Thor Desktop learning workspace where a lesson is governed state rather than chat: one objective at a time, typed checks, bounded grading, transactional transitions, inspectable evidence, and sourced visuals and audio, plus parent-prepared lesson packs. Disclosure — schoolwork, progress and evidence stay on this machine in profile-scoped SQLite under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/coursebook/; pack import reads a local archive the user picks and pack export writes a local file. The Workshop "Share to store" button publishes a course you wrote: after a confirmation step it uses your local git and gh CLI login to push a branch (forking DeseretSaint/thor-classroom under your GitHub account if needed) and open a public pull request with the course content. No telemetry, no credential store, no self-update. Provider calls go through Thor: lesson chat uses the selected chat provider, plan/lesson/Parent Studio generation uses the host plugin LLM route (optionally a configured validator model/provider) with the goal or parent brief and research excerpts, generated illustrations are sent to the host vision tool for review, and research uses the host web_search/web_extract tools. Its own direct requests are limited to downloading generated images from fal.media/fal.run and a first-use download of faster-whisper model weights from Hugging Face; pronunciation practice runs the local ffmpeg binary. It starts background job threads at load that run Desktop-queued generation jobs, injects lesson context into bound lesson chats through pre_llm_call and can block a turn when its lesson state cannot be read, and imports undocumented Thor modules (thor_cli.sqlite_util, tools.web_tools) that may break on a Thor update.

name: coursewright
description: `/course <topic>` turns a subject into one self-contained HTML course at three depths, novice, intermediate and advanced, switched in place without a reload. It researches before it writes: it searches through whatever web backend the host has configured, reads the pages it finds, collects videos that carry captions, and lists every source, dead end and filtered result in a footer. The model never writes HTML; it fills a validated spec and a renderer draws the page. Figures are drawn from the course's own outline — layered diagrams, sequence diagrams, small charts — and every section ends with an exercise that answers back. Disclosure — needs network access: the course is written by the host model through ctx.llm, pages are read over the web with the host's own extractor, an opt-in scraper URL you configure, or the plugin's own guarded direct fetch (public addresses only), and video lookups run yt-dlp and youtube-transcript-api. /course starts the build by sending a turn to the agent, and a background build reports back into the chat when it finishes. It writes only its own plugin data directory plus an optional copy under ~/Courses, and owns no credentials of its own.

name: covision
description: Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

name: cpa-status
description: /cpa in chat for CLIProxyAPI (CPA) pools: account health per provider (active, limited, cooling, error, disabled), the CPA version with an update hint, and on request each account's live quota (Claude, Codex, xAI, Antigravity, Devin, Kimi, Kiro), the same usage reads as CPA's own web UI. Companion to cliproxyapi-provider and reads the same cliproxyapi config. Disclosure — only when you type /cpa, and with the management key env var you name per instance: GETs the credentials list from your configured CPA and CPA's own update check (at most once per 6 hours); for /cpa quota, POSTs CPA's api-call so CPA sends each built-in vendor's private usage request (Anthropic, ChatGPT/Codex, xAI, Google Antigravity, Codeium/Devin, Kimi) with that account's token, using the vendor clients' own User-Agent and client headers as CPA's web UI does (Antigravity and Devin are vendor POSTs, the rest GETs), then one plan request per Claude account (GET api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile) and per Antigravity account (POST loadCodeAssist on daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com), from which only the plan fields are read, and GETs CPA plugin quota for Kiro; at most 20 accounts and 4 requests per account per run, 4 requests in flight. Stops at the first rejected key: one failed try, or up to 4 if the key is revoked mid-run; CPA bans an IP after five failed management logins. Writes only lock files and a rejected-key marker (salted HMAC, never a key) under $THOR_HOME/cache/cliproxyapi/locks/. On Thor 0.23.1 or later it also removes the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, from the environment of the terminal commands a chat session runs (setting hide_keys_from_shells, on by default). Known limit: that hides environment variables only, and only for commands run inside a chat session on the local terminal backend: shell hooks, cron job scripts, processes Thor starts with the profile's credentials, processes started with no session, remote terminal backends (docker, ssh) and any command that can read the file Thor loads keys from still see them; a variable whose name starts with THOR_, or that another plugin already manages, stays visible; on older Thor nothing is hidden.

name: crash-lab
description: Fault-injection and recovery testing for AI agents. Crash Lab manufactures the failure modes that break real agent workflows — a write that succeeds while the API reports a timeout, a malformed response, transient 503s — behind four registered tools (crash_start, crash_book, crash_inspect, crash_report), wrapping a deterministic, fictional booking service. An independent state oracle reads the persisted service state — verified by deterministic replay, so damaged or edited state is never certified — and returns PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED. PASS means the booking-state safety condition holds (exactly one booking, no duplicates); it does not prove the agent reasoned correctly or followed an optimal recovery procedure. Retry diagnostics (call_count, allowed_calls, reconciled, excessive_retries) are reported separately and never affect the verdict. Fully offline: the booking service is fictional — no network calls, no real bookings, payments or customer accounts; no telemetry, background services or stored credentials. Zero Python dependencies; writes JSON run files only in its own plugin-data directory. Concurrency: per-run exclusive write lock (kernel flock on POSIX; owner-release lock file elsewhere, no automatic stale-break). Integrity checking is replay-based consistency verification, not authenticated tamper-proof storage. Tested on Linux (WSL2); Windows/macOS unverified. Scenarios are fixed code constants, not a general fuzzer. Disclosure — verdicts certify simulated service state only, not the agent's reasoning; integrity checking is replay-based consistency, not tamper-proof storage; scenarios are fixed code constants, not a general fuzzer.

name: crash-recovery
description: Durable, hash-chained tool-call journal that blocks protected actions while a previous outcome is unknown, including after a crash or a new session. Operator reconciliation releases the recovery gate; actions are never automatically replayed. Disclosure — after any non-read-only tool call fails, errors or is interrupted, blocks every tool except the configured read-only list (default read_file, search_files) until the operator reconciles the action with the plugin's operator_cli.py; stores tool/session metadata, argument and result hashes, a local integrity checkpoint and operator evidence under the active profile's plugin-data directory and never auto-prunes; serializes protected calls per profile; no network, shell execution, credential reads or background tasks in the plugin itself; optional demos spawn and force-kill owned local workers, and the native demo opens a temporary loopback provider and starts/stops an isolated Thor CLI/gateway.

name: crash-test
description: A safety rating for AI agents. For one armed turn it breaks tools the way real systems break (timeouts, outages, empty or cut-off results), then rates what the agent did: retried, worked around it, told the truth, or claimed success anyway. 1-5 stars and an HTML report, comparable across models by seed. Blocked calls never run, silent faults only touch reads, and the agent gets no tools from it, so it cannot tell it is being tested. Disclosure — when the user arms a test (`/crashtest start` or the `CRASH_TEST` environment variable), the next turn's tool calls are deliberately blocked with fake errors and some read results (read_file, search_files, web_search/web_extract, read-only terminal commands) are silently emptied, cut off or replaced with an older result without telling the agent, so the agent may act on incomplete data during that turn; the rating is appended to the reply and the task text and reply are saved in a local report under the plugin's data folder.

name: crashlab
description: Test recovery before delivery, after commit and across restart; inspect saved records, verify the repair and keep a reusable regression. Disclosure — After a Thor approval prompt, runs the `app.start` command declared by a case file or a model-prepared experiment as a local process outside the Thor sandbox, and drives it with a Node/Playwright runner and a local Chromium launched with `--no-sandbox`; stores runs, experiments, exports and watch files under `~/.local/share/crashlab` (or `CRASHLAB_DATA_DIR`), shared across Thor profiles; the opt-in `crashlab_experiment_watch` adds a `pre_verify` reminder that asks Thor to continue after edits in a watched project; the dashboard tab can start an approved run after its own confirmation.

name: crawl4ai
description: Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

name: creator-studio
description: Make media with Thor from one request: researched lesson videos, two-host podcast episodes, captions for any recording, narrated step-by-step tutorials, and clips cut from a YouTube video or stream by reading its transcript. Bundles five plugins (YouTube Studio, Podcast Studio, Caption Studio, Tutorial Creator, Clip Studio) into one entry. Disclosure — Research pages are fetched through the Camoufox browser you set in the plugin settings, in a fresh anonymous profile (public addresses only). On first use it lists the voices and speech recognizers this computer has and asks you which to use; it never picks one for you. If you choose Gemini narration, each spoken line is sent to Google, either to Vertex AI (aiplatform.googleapis.com) with a Google sign-in that Thor holds for your own OAuth client (thor auth add creator-studio:google; the plugin never sees the token), or to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the Gemini API key in this plugin's settings (GEMINI_API_KEY, the same variable Thor' own Gemini provider uses), behind a spend guard (default 0.50 USD). To find speech servers it sends read-only GET requests (/v1/models, /openapi.json) to 127.0.0.1 only, on ports 2022, 5000, 5002, 7860, 8000, 8001, 8020, 8080, 8880 and 9000, plus any loopback address you set. Caption Studio runs the recognizer command you set in the plugin settings, or uploads audio to the HTTPS speech service you set (public addresses only) or to Groq (api.groq.com) with your key, only when you allow uploads; the model cannot set commands, endpoints, keys or upload consent. Programs it starts get a minimal environment (paths, locale, display/audio session and proxy settings), never your provider keys. Clip Studio runs the yt-dlp you installed (or set in the plugin settings) and makes requests to YouTube only when you give it a link: the video page and one caption track, then the audio track if you ask for speech recognition, the sections you choose to cut, and, if you ask what chat reacted to, the public chat replay of a finished stream (other people's messages and display names; kept in private plugin storage, the raw download deleted once counted, names kept only for paid messages). It never uses browser cookies or a YouTube sign-in. Recognizing a whole recording continues in a background thread inside Thor until its pieces are done. Clips, joined videos, titles, descriptions and thumbnails are written to plugin storage. Runs FFmpeg and ffprobe, an installed speech program if you choose one (espeak-ng, flite, piper), and for screen tutorials xwininfo, xprop, xdotool, pactl and xclip; the recorder starts one detached FFmpeg worker per take, and tutorial steps click and type through Thor computer_use, so its approvals apply. Stores projects privately in plugin storage. Nothing is published.

name: creature-workshop
description:
Manage your project's development lifecycle all in one place: your project.

The development lifecycle's grown more and more complex over the years. It's getting tougher and tougher to get truly polished features over the line into production. And with agentic development, the complexity is ramping more than ever.

Creature Workshop offers a one-stop shop right in your project to manage your project's entire development lifecycle, one piece at a time as it becomes relevant to you. From initial tooling setup, environment handling, and issue intake, to review, merge, testing, build, deployment, documentation, and monitoring, your project's devops should let you focus on your features instead of on the headache of pipelines or on ticking all the boxes for project readiness and change reporting. Disclosure — in a project the user lists in the approved_projects setting (empty by default; added from Settings → Plugins or the pane's Approve button, never by the agent), the workshop_* tools and the terminal pre-check run that repository's own .envrc and shell/ops scripts on the host outside the terminal sandbox, with no per-call approval and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, locale, terminal, XDG dirs plus any names in ops_env_passthrough); workshop_install can install the project's declared tools, which may use the system package manager via sudo; the pane's Explain and set-up buttons send the repository's README opening, top-level file names and matching source lines (secrets redacted) to a Thor auxiliary model that defaults to free Nous Portal models with free OpenRouter models as fallback.

name: crew
description: One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. A coordinator owns every card until its proof command exits 0 - one writer per card, an independent verifier, a hard token budget per card, and a live local dashboard of every card, run and tool call. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; it never approves shell hooks itself, but on a terminal offers (y/N) to open each profile's Thor so Thor asks for hook consent, first revoking approvals whose hook script changed; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the Thor dashboard and a native Crew page in Thor Desktop build that board inside the Thor backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge, Unstuck, Retry, Proof and Stop actions, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports (with longer proof-command and summary excerpts) and questions are sent to the originating chat via thor send, each linking its ticket id to the card on the dashboard (<dashboard>/crew?card=<id>); agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

name: cron-budget
description: Counts provider requests, not dollars, across every profile and holds cron jobs before they spend the requests kept for chat; chat is never blocked. Observe mode by default. Disclosure — one llm_execution middleware and one pre_auxiliary_call hook; stores request counts, timestamps, profile, job ids and names, provider and model names (never message text) in a local SQLite ledger under plugin-data/cron-budget/ in the root Thor home; no network calls, credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry; does not write the cron store.

name: cron-bulletin
description: Central Thor Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

name: cron-consolidator
description: A read-only plan for tidying a crowded cron list: groups jobs whose prompts are near-duplicates or that share skills and destination or run the same script (candidates to become one job), lists clock-time jobs that fire in the same minute, jobs on a failure streak and deliveries never confirmed, and estimates the prompt tokens a merge could save from usage_audit.jsonl. Deterministic (difflib, no model call); nothing is applied. Disclosure — no network; reads cron/jobs.json (including prompts, compared but never printed), cron/usage_audit.jsonl and cron/executions.db (opened read-only) of the chosen profile, and with --profile another profile's cron folder under the same Thor root or with --home the cron folder of any path given; the report (job names, schedules, delivery targets, up to 160 characters of a failing job's last error) is shown wherever the command runs, including messaging-gateway chats; writes nothing; runs no shell command and no background process; registers no hook, tool or middleware, only a slash command and a CLI command; no telemetry.

name: crontab-ref
description: @crontab: context references that explain a cron expression for the model: @crontab:"0 9 * * 1-5" (or a shortcut such as @crontab:@daily) attaches a plain-words reading ("At 09:00 on Monday through Friday."), each field on its own row, whether Thor's /cron takes it as a cron expression (shortcuts, ? and 5#3 are not), its next five runs in Thor's timezone setting worked out the way cron/jobs.py computes next runs, and notes on day of month OR day of week, * in the minute field, steps that do not divide the hour or day, days 29-31 and 7 as Sunday; the TUI and Desktop composer suggest examples and preview an expression as you type it. The reading comes from croniter, the library Thor's scheduler uses. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, the system clock and Thor's timezone setting (THOR_TIMEZONE, else timezone from the loaded config through thor_cli.config), using croniter (already installed with Thor) and Python's standard library; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read, no cron job created, changed or run; the @crontab: reference and its explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @crontab: reference provider.

name: crosodo
description: Cottage food and home bakery law lookups for US states and counties through Crosodo's remote MCP (https://crosodo.com/api/mcp): state rules, county permits, label requirements, Crosodo Certified credentials, and optional label-packet checkout. Portable Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tool call goes to crosodo.com. Lookups are open; checkout may require a signed-in Crosodo account. The package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable tools and refuses them in unattended runs. The live tool set is served by the remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: crowbot-provider
description: crowbot.sh as a model provider: frontier models plus the uncensored open models with their refusals removed. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks or commands); requests go to https://api.crowbot.sh/v1 through Thor' own client with CROWBOT_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: crowdcode
description: Cloud agents with their own wallets. Create CrowdCode agents owned by this install's Base wallet (no sign-up or API key), fund them with USDC, give them tasks that buy x402/MPP services or deploy paid services of their own, list and download the files they produce, and withdraw the earnings. A pre_tool_call guard sends every money-moving call (create, fund, task budget, withdraw, transfer) to Thor's approval prompt by default and blocks spending above a daily cap; unattended runs are denied. Disclosure — Network calls go to crowdcode.app (agent creation is paid by x402 on Base; owner requests are signed) and to a Base RPC to read the wallet's USDC balance. The wallet's private key is a declared secret kept in Thor's credential store. Agent creation, funding, task budgets, withdrawals and transfers spend real USDC; each goes to Thor's approval prompt by default, spending above a daily cap is blocked, and unattended runs are denied. crowdcode_download writes files only when asked, into ./crowdcode-files/<agent>/ or another folder inside the session's working directory, never overwriting; a folder outside it needs approval first, and paths refused by Thor's file-safety policy, THOR_HOME and autostart/service folders are never written.

name: crown
description: One leased speaker and a durable question/answer record for cooperating Thor instances on one Linux host. A replacement reads the same record. An old token cannot publish after a successor takes the lease. Crown writes only its own local SQLite outlet. It does not silence Thor chat or Telegram, and it does not follow you to a phone. Disclosure — after explicit /crown here, runs a local heartbeat thread; reads and writes an operator-configured shared SQLite database outside profile storage, and injects recent shared questions/answers written by other participating profiles into each turn's context as quoted data; no network calls, no credentials, no model calls.

name: crucible
description: Adversarial research and code audits. Proposer agents commit quoted claims, attackers try to break them, a blind referee checks every quote against its source and re-runs every proof of concept in a sandbox, and you get a map of what survived and what was held back. Disclosure — Crucible runs spend tokens on your configured model through parallel subagents (each run has a USD cap). Research mode fetches the web pages its agents cite directly from your machine (public addresses only), plus NCBI PubMed and OpenAlex for papers. Code mode copies the repository you name into the plugin's data folder and gives its subagents the file and terminal tools on your terminal backend. Proofs of concept are re-run only in a network-less, read-only Docker container (image python:3.12-slim by default, pulled if missing). The optional guard mode (`/crucible guard on|strict`, off by default) rewrites the agent's answers to flag unsupported claims. Run records stay local under the plugin data folder. No telemetry.

name: crypto-prices
description: Live crypto price ticker for the desktop status bar — Top 10 by market cap, seamless marquee, custom coins & 60+ display currencies, adjustable width (CoinGecko, no API key).

name: crystallize
description: Spend less on repeated work in Thor chats and cron jobs, without making your model think less: trims repeated context and tool output in chats, and lets a cron job skip its AI run when its input has not changed, with local receipts showing what each change saved. Disclosure — reads Thor session costs, user-message counts and final cron answers (state.db, read-only), cron outcomes and job definitions (cron/executions.db, cron/jobs.json) and your config and rate cards; looks up public model prices from the active route's /models endpoint and models.dev once a day with no credentials or chat data (off with thor crystal prices --lookup off); the optional helper, compare and check features make paid model calls through your own Thor route; cron tuning, promote and undo run thor cron CLI commands that edit the chosen job, choosing a helper model or deferring tools runs thor config set (auxiliary.crystallize_chat, tools.tool_search.defer), and generated pre-run wrappers, drafted snapshot scripts (which replay the job's recorded shell commands and URL reads) and approved snapshot scripts are written under scripts/crystallize/, scripts/crystallize-drafts/ and scripts/crystallize-native/ and run as ordinary cron scripts once attached; in CLI and TUI chats posts one short status line after each turn with ctx.post_message (never on Desktop or messaging platforms; off with /crystallize line off); stores captured tool results, cache entries and receipts in its plugin-data folder; no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update.

name: csharp-game-editor
description: Give it one feature for the Unity project open in your editor, and it builds the scripts, objects and scene in one plan, stops that plan when the compile reports an error CS line, and plays the scene when the compile is clean. Disclosure — Needs MCP for Unity pinned to v10.3.0, plus git and uv. Thor starts mcpforunityserver==10.3.0 through uvx with telemetry and the update check off. Disk reads run at once. apply_plan asks once and puts back a file the plan did not name. A plan that deletes, runs editor code, can lose unsaved work or writes outside the project asks again, and that summary is sent only when every line fits the approval card; otherwise nothing is sent and confirm_risky_plan asks. unity_docs sends the query to docs.unity3d.com after Thor asks. unity_generate can call paid providers you configured in MCP for Unity; that call was not part of the check. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway. Only users the gateway admits can reach the tools, and this plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron and a session with nobody to answer decline. Logs stay in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-csharp-game-editor-<hash>/logs. Stop with thor plugins disable csharp-game-editor, or thor tools for one surface. macOS only.

name: ctx_checkpoint
description: Memory provider that archives the direct user/assistant transcript into a ctx knowledge store before every compaction, deterministically and with no LLM in the path, and hands the resulting block IDs to the compaction summary so the exact wording stays recoverable. Set up from the Desktop/Dashboard memory form or `thor memory setup ctx_checkpoint` (ctx URL and API key, no YAML editing); compaction thresholds stay Thor' defaults, which suit 1M-token windows. Best-effort on any supported Thor; with compression.checkpoint_required on Thor 0.21.1+ it uses the fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint contract (#94639) and blocks compaction until the checkpoint is durable. Optional memory layer (`memory: true`, off by default): recall before each turn, ctx_query/ctx_store/ctx_search/ctx_get tools, a mirror of MEMORY.md/USER.md, fact extraction from compacted turns, session digests and a bundled `ctx-memory` skill, over the same ctx server.
