Disclosure — the turns about to be compacted (tool results and system prompts excluded, secrets redacted twice) and, with the memory layer on, the mirrored memory entries, extracted facts and digests (all redacted the same way) are written through Thor' MCP dispatch to the ctx server you configure in mcp_servers; setup, when you run it, writes memory.ctx_checkpoint and that mcp_servers entry to config.yaml and the API key to .env as CTX_API_KEY; the plugin never writes compaction settings, holds no credentials of its own unless you opt into transport: rest (CTX_KEY in .env; that client redacts the key from every error text it produces and follows no HTTP redirect), makes no other network calls and has no telemetry; with the memory layer on it keeps small dedupe state files under THOR_HOME/ctx_state and reads state.db read-only; it imports the core modules agent.redact, agent.secret_scope, tools.registry, tools.interrupt, thor_constants and thor_cli.config.

name: ctx_handover
description: Close the lid, the session goes on: ctx_handover moves a running Thor session, with the conversation and the project folder it works in, from one machine you own to another and back. `/handover to server` sends it after work, `/handover take` brings it to the laptop, and `--continue "task"` lets the agent keep working on the server if you allow it there; without a connection, `/handover export` writes one file you carry over. The conversation is copied message by message and checked with hashes on both sides, git projects keep branches, stash and uncommitted work, nothing at the destination is overwritten, and the session on the machine you left is retired only after the other one confirms. Works without ctx. Not the core /handoff. Disclosure — talks only to the gateways you pair (HTTPS; plain HTTP only on loopback or with --allow-insecure); no third-party services, telemetry or update checks. Transcript, tool outputs and working files travel unredacted and handover files are unencrypted; workspace .env files, keys and credential folders stay unless released per path with --include-secret, and Thor' own credentials always stay. A paired device can take this profile's sessions (pull right) or write sessions and project copies under allow_roots (push right) through Ed25519-signed routes behind the dashboard sign-in. Stores the peer's dashboard token or Basic login, which opens that peer's whole dashboard, and an identity key in the profile .env through Thor' secret routes. Runs git without a shell and with an allowlisted environment, --version probes of developer tools, and with --continue plus allow_remote_continue one `thor chat --resume` turn that never starts while approvals are off. One model call per handover (refine: off disables it). The complete list is in the README and docs/security.md at the pinned commit.

name: cua-spaces
description: Cua's own plugin: runs Thor's terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live, as a terminal backend (`thor config set terminal.backend cua`). On Thor 0.22.3 and later, Bot Desktop, computer_use and the browser follow the terminal into the Space too (needs the `cua` command). Disclosure — installs the `cua` Python SDK (>=0.5.0,<0.8); every command the agent runs, every file it touches, and (on 0.22.3+) every screen, click and page the agent drives go to the Space: on this machine for a local Space, or on Cua's cloud (cua.ai) or a machine you name, using the sign-in `cua auth login` saved (the plugin never reads or stores a token, and keeps CUA_API_KEY/CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN out of the Space). Windows Spaces run Thor's tools in Git Bash, like Thor on a Windows PC: if the Space lacks Git for Windows or Python, the plugin installs them inside the Space (pinned official installers checked against SHA-256, `winget` fallback) and adds `C:\c`-style drive aliases there. The optional `desktop` setting installs a desktop stack (VNC, Chromium, agent-browser, cua-driver) inside a Linux Space with sudo there. Nothing is installed on this machine. With the default `space: create` it makes a fresh Space per session and deletes it when Thor finishes (`delete_on_exit`); because that Space is a disposable sandbox, Thor skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends. A Space you name is never deleted and keeps the prompts.

name: culprit
description: git bisect for your agent. Records a snapshot after every tool call that changes a file, then binary-searches those snapshots with your test command to name the exact step that broke it, with its diff, and can undo only that step while keeping every later change. Works as /culprit, as `thor culprit`, and as tools the agent can call. Disclosure: no network and no telemetry; runs git against a private object store under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/culprit/ (the project's own .git is never read or written) and stores unencrypted copies of the working folder's files there, honouring .gitignore and always skipping .env files, keys, credential folders and dependency folders; keeps each step's tool name and the first 100 characters of its path or command with token-like values masked on a best-effort basis; during a search it runs the given test command through the system shell in temporary copies and deletes them; git and the test command get an explicit minimal environment (PATH, home, temp and locale variables, plus the names the user lists in pass_env), never the Thor environment; revert writes only the files in the reverted step's diff and refuses when later edits conflict; model-initiated culprit_bisect and culprit_revert go to Thor's approval prompt, which shows the exact command (masked) or the step, with a rule key derived from it, and fail closed in unattended runs; /culprit typed in the CLI or Desktop runs directly, and on messaging platforms it is read-only (steps, show, help) unless the owner sets allow_remote_commands; no background processes; nothing is pruned automatically (/culprit clear deletes a project's data).

name: cursor-acp
description: Use your Cursor subscription models (Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Composer 2.5, GPT-5.6, Grok) inside Thor Agent via the Cursor CLI's ACP server (`agent acp`). Install with one command (`npx thor-cursor-acp`) or `thor plugins install cursor-acp`. The plugin rewrites `.cursor/cli.json` in an empty private workspace every run with a deny-all list (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `WebFetch`, `Mcp`) to prevent Cursor's native CLI tools from accessing host files. It includes a custom extractor that recovers both flat `{"name", "arguments"}` and inline `<tool_call>` blocks that standard regex bridges drop, retries on concurrent `set_model` calls, and reports `usage=None` so Thor proactive context compression functions correctly. Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Thor tool schemas and tool results to Cursor through your locally installed, signed-in Cursor CLI (`agent acp`); Cursor's own tools are fenced by a deny-all `.cursor/cli.json` that the plugin rewrites in a private workspace under `$THOR_HOME/cache/cursor-acp-workspace` on every start (a differing existing file is backed up to `cli.json.bak`), and Thor executes every tool call under its own approvals.

name: cursor-provider
description: Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under THOR_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk. Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and Thor keeps tool execution and approvals; native custom tools are opt-in (default off) with an inert executor. Plan-only exhaustion and rejected model parameters are terminal and fail closed without fallback. The SDK passes a loopback tool-callback token on the bridge argv (not the API key) and copies the gateway environment into the bridge process.

name: cursor-sdk
description: Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Thor's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Thor support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.

name: cursor-subscription-directsdk
description: Experimental model provider that runs Thor turns on your Cursor plan through Cursor's official Python SDK (cursor-sdk), with Cursor Auto offered as `cursor-auto`, and Thor tools registered as native Cursor custom tools: each tool callback parks until Thor has executed the call under its own approvals, then the same Cursor run continues, so parallel calls arrive as one batch and tool rounds keep the model's native context and prompt cache. `thor auth add cursor-subscription-directsdk` runs Cursor's official browser sign-in with Cursor-side persistence off and stores the minted, revocable 90-day user API key in Thor' credential pool (CURSOR_API_KEY also works). Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Thor' system prompt, tool schemas, tool results and user images to Cursor with your key; installs cursor-sdk 1.3.1 from PyPI (hash-pinned, about 200 MB, includes Cursor's bundled node bridge) into the plugin's own .venv and runs it as a long-lived sidecar (one per Thor profile) that starts that bridge on loopback, with an environment rebuilt from an allowlist (PATH, HOME, locale, TLS/proxy, display variables for sign-in, its own CURSOR_SUBSCRIPTION_*), so no other Thor keys or tokens reach Cursor's code; Cursor's built-in tools are disabled (tools=["mcp"]) and agents get no MCP servers or Cursor settings sources, and local Cursor agent state lives under $THOR_HOME/cache/cursor-subscription-directsdk and is deleted when each conversation closes.

name: custodian
description: Autonomous operations monitor for a Thor install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under THOR_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

name: custom-dangerous-patterns
description: Add custom dangerous command patterns to Thor's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; a pre_tool_call hook sends block patterns to Thor's human approval gate and blocks deny patterns immediately. Modifies no Thor internals.

name: custom-song-gift
description: Explore 12 gift occasions, compare 16 studio-quality musical genres, and get personalized lyric storytelling advice for custom songs directly from Thor Agent via Custom Song Gift hosted MCP server. Compliant with Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Tool calls go to Custom Song Gift streamable HTTP MCP server at https://customsonggift.org/api/mcp.

name: customs
description: Plants fake credential files on your machine and blocks a hijacked agent the moment a tool call reaches for one, before the tool runs. It also redacts its own fake values from tool results and from the request to the model provider, reads local scripts before they run, and asks for approval when an upload follows a credential search and packaging. Disclosure — plants fake credential files (mode 600, never over an existing file, inside a Git repository only at paths Git ignores) under the home folder, including ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, when the user runs /customs plant, blend or add, and keeps its own state in its plugin data folder; it only recognizes its own bait files and fake values and does not find or protect real credentials. Its hooks read every tool call's arguments and results and every outgoing model request, block or send to Thor approval the calls that touch bait or carry a fake value, redact fake values from tool results and model requests, and after a block require approval for network actions in that session until /customs unlock (on by default). It reads the local scripts a command is about to run (up to 8 files, 512 KB each) and, during /customs blend, folder names under the home folder, and runs git check-ignore when planting inside a Git repository. No network calls by default; with alert_target set, alerts go out through thor send on the user's own Thor messaging route and carry the rule, the bait file's path, the likely source and a masked preview of the call (first 200 characters).

name: cut-sprite-sheet
description: pixel art sprite sheet cutter. png to tileset splitter. cut pixel art into game tiles. sprite sheet from pixel png. 2d walk cycle sprite sheet. tileset cutter for pixel art. split png into sprite sheet. shore tiles tileset tool. pixel art walk cycle sheet. png sprite and shore tiles. Cuts a pixel-art png into frames. Tools: inspect_grid, slice_grid, place_kit for a 2D game. Disclosure — The png stays on this computer. Nothing is sent. No API key. No daily cap. A gateway room can call the tools. Stop them with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. One approval on one line via pre_tool_call. Choosing always covers only the same call when a person is present and the plan does not delete a file. That choice adds one plugin_rule:<tool>:<16 hex> line to command_allowlist in config.yaml. That line stays after the plugin is removed. The plugin itself refuses cron, thor -q, webhook, msgraph_webhook, the API server, and the plugin host, even after always, so the same call still writes nothing there. A turn with no person and no gateway writes nothing, even after always. A plan that deletes a file asks on every call. An oversized line writes one list file, <stem>.paths.txt beside the png. A failed check writes nothing. Thor yolo and approvals off skip that prompt when a person is present. cron, -q, and unattended sessions default to deny. A sprite writes <stem>.spriteframes.tres, <stem>.png.meta, <stem>.png.import, and <stem>.slice.json beside the png, and, unless emit_scene is false, <stem>_stage.gd and <stem>_stage.tscn. A tileset writes <stem>.tileset.tres, <stem>.png.meta, <stem>.png.import, <stem>.slice.json, and <stem>.<name>.asset plus <stem>.<name>.asset.meta for each tile. A tight tileset also writes <stem>.extruded.png and <stem>.extruded.png.import, and writes <stem>.extruded.png.meta in place of <stem>.png.meta. place_kit writes the sheet png, <stem>_tiles.png, those sidecars, the stage, and project.godot only when that file is missing. Those project files stay after uninstall. The always line stays in config.yaml. The skill index line stays only while the plugin is enabled. Empty, unknown, or a restrictive license is not written. Unknown text is copied and next warns. CC-BY-SA is copied and next names share-alike. No license chunk still writes and next says no rights are attached. Import once or play fails: godot --headless --editor --quit --path <project>. No solid-color box and no sound effect. Does not launch Godot or Unity. Play may write app-userdata. That folder stays. Uninstall leaves no cron job. Linux is untested. Unity editor 6000.6.6f1 on macOS kept the walk-sheet fileIDs after a reopen.

name: cutroom
description: Local-first video editing studio: word-timed transcript cuts and filler review, silence removal, face/gaze/mouth review, person segmentation for graphics behind the subject, three source-quoted hook options with a storyboard, preview renders, human-approved final export, cover and automated quality checks. Ships a Thor Desktop Studio page, agent tools for projects and background jobs (no approval tool: only a person can approve a final export) and a CLI. Requires FFmpeg/ffprobe on PATH; speech, vision and segmentation need optional Python packages and local model files. Disclosure — reads only the local media paths it is given and launches local FFmpeg/ffprobe and a Python worker subprocess with a minimal allowlisted environment (provider API keys and tokens are not forwarded); the worker interpreter comes only from CUTROOM_PYTHON, the plugin's bundled .venv or Thor' own interpreter, never from project data or tool arguments; agent tools write projects, renders and reports only under its own workspace in the Thor home and never overwrite source or existing outputs; models are never downloaded automatically, and `cutroom setup-models --confirm-downloads` fetches pinned files from storage.googleapis.com (MediaPipe) and huggingface.co (faster-whisper-tiny) with SHA-256 verification; optional download/OBS/rclone/calendar adapters run only with explicit confirmation and are not used by the Studio pipeline; no telemetry, no API keys, no self-update. Final-export approval records a person's decision in the Desktop Studio page; it is a workflow record, not a security boundary against other code running as the same user.

name: cybopal-one-devkit
description: Unofficial, not made or endorsed by CyboPal. Drive a CyboPal ONE (a 27-inch 4K screen on a 6-DOF robotic arm with the Pauli companion display) from Thor: follow, posture presets, exact poses, gestures, both screens (markdown, pictures and videos), both cameras and an emergency stop; design new actions on the simulator and save them to run unchanged on the hardware. Works today against the open source CyboPal ONE DevKit live simulator. Disclosure — sends HTTP commands, screen text and any picture or video file the agent is given (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/MP4/WebM, up to 64 MB, checked by content) only to the device_url setting (default http://127.0.0.1:5000), never following redirects or environment proxies; saves camera pictures (newest 30) and saved routines in the profile's plugin-data/cybopal-one-devkit; moves physical hardware when device_url points at a real CyboPal ONE (allow_motion off refuses all motion, and only the person's /cybopal resume command can release an emergency stop).

name: daak-duffy
description: Autonomous background task queue (DAAK Duffy / Duet Do-For-You worker) with Human-in-the-Loop approval gates (duet_queue tool, /duffy and /duet commands), Ruflo multi-agent swarm orchestration (ruflo_swarm tool), and multi-model Antigravity CLI quota fallback worker (gemini-3.8-flash-high -> claude-sonnet-5-5-high -> gemini-3.1-pro-high -> claude-opus-5-5-high -> gpt-oss-120b-medium). name: daily-edition
description: A personal newspaper inside Thor Desktop: name interests, not subscriptions, and it compiles one dated front page — each story once, cross-posted stories merged with every publisher credited, consensus winning the lead, reprints withheld — with seven back issues, in-place reading, unread and saved state, and an optional editorial voice for headlines (off until you name a model endpoint; there is no vendor default). The same edition prints as a one-page broadsheet through a local CUPS queue, and the daily_edition tool or /edition can print it from chat or cron. Disclosure — compiling an edition sends your interest phrases to the news provider (Google News RSS by default) and opening a story fetches that article from its publisher, exposing your IP to them; pressing “Style as …” sends that edition's headlines and summaries to the endpoint you set in DAILY_EDITION_BASE_URL with the key in DAILY_EDITION_API_KEY, and nothing is sent while merely browsing; printing renders locally with the browser's background networking disabled and submits only to a local print queue; no telemetry is collected.

name: darkmoon
description: Triage the findings file of a Darkmoon autonomous pentest scan (JSON or SARIF): filter by severity and proof status, get a severity-sorted summary and a pass/fail gate for a release. Read-only and offline: no network, no subprocess, no credentials, standard library only. Darkmoon is open source (GPL-3.0); its web dashboard and remediation agent are Pro and are not used here. name: dashboard-auth-feishu
description: Feishu / Lark OAuth sign-in for the web dashboard, admitted by tenant + open_id allow-list. Registers the `feishu` dashboard auth provider once plugins.entries.dashboard-auth-feishu.settings (app_id, tenant_key, owner_open_ids) and an app secret are configured. name: dashboard-auth-ldap
description: LDAP / Active Directory password login for the web dashboard. Verifies credentials with an LDAP bind (direct or search-then-bind), never stores passwords, requires ldaps:// or StartTLS, and supports group restriction. Registers the `ldap` dashboard auth provider once dashboard.ldap_auth is configured. Disclosure — dashboard logins are verified by binding to your configured LDAP/AD server with the user's password (TLS with certificate validation required unless allow_insecure is set); sessions are stateless HMAC tokens (12h access / 30d refresh by default) signed with THOR_DASHBOARD_LDAP_SECRET or a random per-process key, and logout cannot revoke them; group removal and disabled accounts are not re-checked until the refresh token expires; failed logins count toward the directory's account-lockout policy.

name: dashboard-button
description: One-click access to the Thor Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

name: dashscope-image
description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.

name: dashscope-video
description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

name: data
description: An agentic report page. Open an Excel workbook, a CSV or a JSON file and Thor finds the story: it suggests a headline and a handful of charts, and you accept the ones you want onto the page. Every number on a chart is computed from your rows; the model picks columns and wording, never figures. Ask about the table or about one chart and an agent answers with a chart and its sources. Split a chart by a second column, point at any mark and list the rows behind it, export the report as a web page, Markdown or SVG. Once you allow it, any chat can read your reports and propose charts. Disclosure — Find the story starts a hidden Thor session told to use no tools (your Thor tools stay available to it, stopped after 2.5 minutes or 6 tool calls), which sees column summaries, grouped totals and the first eight rows, never the whole table; Ask starts a hidden session that uses your Thor tools and reads third-party web pages, stopped after 4 minutes or 24 tool calls; approval prompts inside these sessions are denied; open and export go through the system dialog and the plugin's own backend, which reads workbooks with the Python standard library and refuses paths inside the Thor home folder; a CSV or JSON file dragged onto the page is read in the page; reports live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy of the columns, charts and first 400 rows under plugin-data/data/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Thor profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; with the Sheets or Whiteboard plugin installed, a click hands a table or chart remarks to that page through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; no telemetry, no credentials, no shell commands or background processes of its own. Independent community project, not affiliated with Thor Labs.

name: data-lens
description: Automatic full-scan structural maps for eligible local CSV, JSON-array and JSONL reads, followed by bounded structured queries with exact Decimal sums. Opt-in host roots; no SQL, network, credentials or persistent runtime state. Disclosure — replaces the default (no offset/limit) `read_file` result for large CSV/JSON/JSONL files inside the folders you list in `roots` with a derived structural map of the whole file, and its two tools read files under those roots directly on the host using the plugin's own path and credential-name guards rather than core's read guards. Nothing is readable until you set `roots` and `host_local: true`; no network calls.

name: data-saver
description: A mobile-data budget for Thor. A pre_tool_call hook forecasts how many megabytes a terminal command will download before it runs (pip/uv with dependencies, git clone, docker pull, Hugging Face, ollama, curl/wget) and sends anything over the daily or monthly budget to Thor's own approval prompt, or blocks it in enforce mode. Execution middleware meters the real bytes each tool call and model request used from the OS network counters into a local ledger; a lean mode trims web results when the budget runs low. Tools: data_usage, data_forecast. Command: /datasaver. Thor Agent Plugin Hackathon entry. Disclosure — forecasts send read-only metadata requests (package, repo, image or model name only; no credentials) to pypi.org, api.github.com, auth.docker.io, registry-1.docker.io, huggingface.co and registry.ollama.ai, and one header-only request to a URL named in a curl/wget command, before the command reaches the approval prompt; that URL and every redirect hop are probed only when Thor' is_safe_url accepts them and every address they resolve to is public. The ledger (<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/data-saver/data.db) stores time, tool name, bytes and the first 300 characters of the command or URL (including any token written into it), locally. In lean mode it shortens web_extract and web_search results. Network counters are system-wide, so other apps' traffic during a tool call is counted. No telemetry, no shell commands, no background process.

name: data-wrangler
description: Deterministic tools for local tabular data — the counting a model should never guess at. table_profile computes an exact profile of a CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL file (row and column counts, inferred types, null counts and percentages, distinct counts, min/max/mean/median, top text values, duplicate-row and empty-row counts). table_query runs one read-only SQL query over the file in SQLite (table `data`): writes are refused up front and again by a connection authorizer, results are row-capped with the total matched count always reported, and a 10-second query budget applies. table_clean writes a cleaned copy — snake_case headers, trimmed cells, fully-empty rows dropped, exact duplicates removed (optionally on a subset of columns) — and returns a full change report; the input file is never modified. A bundled data-tables skill teaches the profile → query → clean → verify workflow. Python standard library only (csv/json/sqlite3): no dependencies, no configuration, no credentials. Disclosure — Reads local CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL files named in a tool call (Thor' read blocklist applies), and `table_clean` writes one cleaned copy to a model-chosen path (Thor' write denylist applies, and approval-gated paths are refused); no network calls, no shell, no state kept.

name: datacircle
description: Find the best GTM APIs. Four tools on Datacircle's open API, with no key and no account: every API on Datacircle's sheet, who is best for each by score out of 100, every plan and its price, and one provider's ranks. Disclosure — each tool call makes one HTTPS GET to api.datacircle.dev with the tool's own arguments and nothing else; no key, no stored data, no shell commands, no background process, no telemetry; tool results reach your model provider.

name: dataprobe
description: Exact, local structure and quality checks over large CSV/TSV and JSONL data files that don't fit in a model's context. data_profile reports per-column inferred type, null rate, distinct count, numeric statistics and top values (for JSONL, the inferred union schema with per-field presence); data_validate reports only the actionable problems — mixed-type columns with the offending line numbers, ragged rows, duplicate rows, non-unique key candidates, constant or all-empty columns and malformed JSONL lines; data_head returns a clean parsed preview that handles quoted CSV and JSON correctly. Streamed, standard library only: no network, no credentials, no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local data path you pass it (read-only) and honours Thor' core read denylist.

name: davinci-resolve
description: Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

name: day-panel
description: A Today page in Thor Desktop, plus thor day show and check, built from sections you list in a YAML file: any program that prints JSON (your tracker, a script of yours), your open GitHub pull requests and review requests through gh, one read-only tool of an MCP server you already configured, and your AI providers' limit windows from thor usage. Items can carry a colour, a progress bar and a relative time; the page follows the Desktop theme. Ships a demo page that needs no login or network. Read-only and no model calls; merging a pull request from the page is off by default and needs a preview and a confirmation pinned to the head commit. Disclosure — runs the programs your sources file names (no shell), plus gh and thor usage, as your user with your existing logins; calls a configured MCP server's tool only when the server marks it readOnlyHint, in a child process that imports three undocumented Thor MCP modules (there is no public seam for this yet); reads only the sources file; writes nothing to disk; logs carry section names and exit statuses, not source output. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

name: de-law
description: German federal law, EU law and German federal court decisions for Thor Agent: read one section or article (§ 203 StGB, Art. 6 DSGVO, Art. 50 AI Act) in the source wording with version status (Stand), gazette reference and a ready source line, search the index of federal laws, list a law's sections, and find and read published decisions of BVerfG, BGH, BVerwG, BFH, BAG, BSG and BPatG. Legal texts, not legal advice. Disclosure: sends HTTPS GET requests only to www.gesetze-im-internet.de (law folder names, the daily index, weekly abbreviation lists), www.rechtsprechung-im-internet.de (the daily index, document ids of decisions you read) and publications.europa.eu (CELEX numbers, text language, one SPARQL query per act listing its consolidated versions); section numbers and search words are not sent, because whole laws are downloaded and searched locally. Public sources, no key. Writes public legal texts and indexes (JSON with ETag, Last-Modified and fetch time; no questions, no session data) under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/de-law/cache, capped by the cache_max_mb setting (default 200 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 25 s timeout, 40 MB response cap. rechtsprechung-im-internet.de sends a tdm-reservation header; the plugin fetches its index and single decisions on request only, and case_law: false turns that source off. No hooks, no cron jobs, no background processes. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; thor tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

name: dead-drop
description: Autonomous agent-to-agent messaging across teams through a shared private mailbox. Disclosure — when you enable it (`active: true`), the model can send messages of up to 4000 chars, without a per-call Thor approval, to the peer agents you list. Each message is committed, with your configured scope, to the private GitHub repository you name, readable by everyone with access to that repo, using the `DEAD_DROP_GITHUB_TOKEN` you store in Thor. Sends are capped by `max_messages` and the deadline. Peer messages are fed back to the model as untrusted text. An optional cron job (`wake_enabled` plus the exact `wake_job_id`) can read and answer peer questions unattended. Requires Node.js 22+, which runs only the bundled engine, with a minimal environment.

name: deadbolt
description: Review and approve exact text-artifact writes through a local DeadBolt sidecar. Protects this plugin's commit tool only.

name: deadline-guard
description: Deadline governance for Thor. Reads a local Markdown deadlines table and exposes check_deadlines, next_founder_steps, propose_status_update, and deadline_guard_cron: commitments are bucketed overdue / 24h / 72h / 7d, founder-gated next steps are surfaced before they go critical, and a status can never be recorded as 'submitted' without an http(s) receipt URL - the proposal comes back unapplied for a human to confirm. Ships a daily-check automation blueprint (08:00 cron) and a bundled deadline-guard skill. Validated on Thor 0.23.0: thor plugins validate --install-deps exit 0, all 15 checks pass; 47 tests pass. Disclosure - stdlib only, no network calls, no model calls, no telemetry; reads only the configured local deadlines file (config deadlines_path, default examples/hackathon-deadlines.md); writes nothing itself. Disclosure — stdlib only, no network calls, no model calls, no telemetry; reads the configured local deadlines file (config deadlines_path, default examples/hackathon-deadlines.md) or a path the agent passes to a tool; the deadline_guard_cron install action writes an executable daily-check script to THOR_HOME/scripts/deadline_guard_daily.py, which you attach yourself with thor cron add; status updates are only proposed, never written.

name: debug-desk
description: Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the Thor agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.

name: decision-brief
description: Decision Brief MVP - a human decision layer for consequential agent and creative decisions.

name: decision-ledger
description: Exact decision receipts with a read-only web dashboard; models draft, a human confirms in a separate terminal. Not an execution gate.

name: decisions
description: Predicate Decisions API tools with background jobs and session-owned structured JSON results. Disclosure — each submission sends the model-supplied text and questions with your OpenAI API key to the configured Decisions endpoint (OpenAI by default; billable); jobs run on a background thread and results stay in memory only, lost on restart.

name: deepgram-voice
description: Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for Thor Agent.

name: deepinfra-sandbox
description: Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your Thor skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.thor; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

name: deepseek-search-fetch
description: DeepSeek Search & Fetch as a backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and web_extract URLs to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DeepSeek fetches the pages server-side; billed to your DeepSeek balance per successful request; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access.

name: deepseek-web-tools
description: DeepSeek's server-side web tools as one Thor tool: the model searches, opens pages and checks facts inside a single call, then answers with structured citations. thinking is opt-in (the server default is on and bills up to ~20 searches), and page text is never returned - use web_extract when you need the content. Disclosure — each web_research call sends the query, any URLs and image URL the model passes to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; DeepSeek's servers search and open those pages and bill each search to your account (up to ~20 per call when thinking is on); no other network host, no shell commands, no files written.

name: deepseek-whale
description: Live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing whale for the Thor desktop titlebar. Blue x0.5 off-peak, grey PEAK at full price, countdown on click, 30s repaint, no backend or API key.

name: deferred-questions
description: Durable non-blocking questions with exact answer binding and gateway continuation. Disclosure — pre_gateway_dispatch sees gateway messages, accepts answers only from the stored recipient and route, and may consume recognized stale/completed inputs; with enable_tool on, the model can send questions to any chat the gateway already authorizes, and continue_agent resumes the target chat with the answer; questions and answers are stored unencrypted in $THOR_HOME/deferred-questions/questions.sqlite3; profile-local Unix-socket notices wake event-driven workers; pre_llm_call/on_session_end observe current input, turn IDs and terminal status to correlate technical completion for payload retirement, not business success or delivery; automatic header-only repair preserves originals in quarantine, and text-free receipts retain caller-supplied idempotency keys and request hashes; private gateway and adapter APIs can break after a Thor update.

name: defuzz-componentize
description: Optional Defuzz companion for turning Python scripts into reusable components checked against saved baseline output, with 14 declarative project kits, CLI and slash commands, bundled guidance, and a Desktop settings page. Requires Python 3.13 or newer. Disclosure — Runs the baseline and test commands named in a componentize spec (`golden.argv`, `tests.argv`), and imports and calls `register()` on any plugin trees the spec lists, with your user's permissions, without a sandbox and without a Thor approval prompt, including when started from the `/componentize` slash command in chat; nested or detached commands can outlive a cancel. It reads the chosen projects, library, specs, inputs and job evidence; creates project folders, updates kit-owned AGENTS.md blocks and .gitignore/LFS rules; saves its two settings through Thor; and writes job evidence and locks under `<library>/.componentize/<name>/` (or `--state-root`). Libc lookup may run system utilities (ldconfig, gcc, objdump). The plugin itself makes no network calls, but the commands and plugins it runs can reach your files and the internet. Linux only; needs Python 3.13 or newer.

name: degeneracy-guard
description: Asks the user to confirm a tool call whose arguments look like a repetition loop rather than data, through Thor' approval gate (denied or unanswered means refused); replaces flagged degenerate output with a short notice; warns when a session grows long. Disclosure — no network, shell, subprocesses, own threads, telemetry or credentials; writes incident records and a session counter to its plugin data directory; a stream-side record keeps the last 800 characters of flagged output.

name: deja-fix
description: Stops the agent from putting back code that already failed. Every version of every file it writes in a session is fingerprinted and judged by the next test or build run, or by the user saying "still broken". An edit that would recreate a failed version is stopped once, naming when it failed and why; a second try goes through. Catches the same code reached by different edits, which Thor' identical-call guard can't. /deja shows what is tracked. No model calls.

name: deja-memory
description: Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Thor and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Thor and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, receives the turns Thor compresses so it can hand them back after compaction, and recalled text from those agents is injected into Thor turns, with lines deja marks "User said (this project)" requiring user confirmation before changing a command, file, rule, or config; nothing leaves the machine.

name: delegation-receipts
description: Verify what a subagent says it did before the parent reports the work as done. A "receipts" delegation backend asks every child to end its reply with a receipt (status, the files it changed, and the one command that proves the work); when a child stops, the plugin resolves and hashes each claimed path, matches every claim against the write targets that child's own tool history records so it cannot take credit for a file someone else wrote, and checks the cited command against a closed set of fixed check forms (pytest, uv run --no-sync pytest, cargo/go/npm/pnpm/yarn test), refusing a path rather than a bare name, a launcher, or inline evaluation. Host re-run is opt-in and off by default, because a hook-driven re-run bypasses Thor' dangerous-command approval and the child's terminal backend; when an operator enables it, the command is re-run argv-style with no shell, in its own process group, with output and time bounded. Either way a verdict reaches the parent: a rejection is appended to the delegate_task result, with the failing output attached when there is one; a background child's verdict arrives on the parent's next turn instead. Every check stays in a local JSONL ledger shown by `thor receipts`. One command per receipt, one receipt per child. Disclosure — the receipt's `verified:` command is written by the subagent being checked; host re-run is off by default, and when you enable `plugins.entries.delegation-receipts.settings.host_rerun` that command (one of pytest, uv run --no-sync pytest, cargo/go/npm/pnpm/yarn test) runs on this host with your privileges in the child's inferred workspace, outside Thor' command approval and the configured terminal backend, and executes the project's test code and scripts, including files the subagent wrote (no shell, argv-split, filtered environment, 120 s default timeout); receipts and claimed paths are checked locally, the ledger is local at <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/delegation-receipts/ledger.jsonl, and the plugin makes no network calls and holds no credentials.

name: delegation-scout
description: Delegation backend that routes each subagent by task shape and learns from recorded per-route outcomes — a delegation backend `scout` with auto/quick/deep task params, a post_tool_call outcome observer, and a scout_stats tool.

name: delivery-gate
description: Pre-delivery verification for Thor Agent: runs the deterministic checks a task spec declares (test commands, lint, repro scripts) and releases the deliverable only when every required check passes, writing a replayable, hash-chained evidence record per run. The verdict comes from the deterministic checker, never from the model. Disclosure — runs the shell commands a task spec declares (passed by the model or read from a `.json` spec file, possibly from a cloned repo) through Thor' terminal tool, so dangerous-command approval and the configured terminal backend apply to each check; writes evidence records under `<workspace>/.delivery-gate/evidence/` (or the configured `evidence_dir`).

name: delivery-shelf
description: Save delivered files together, preserve versions, and find finished work again in Thor. Disclosure — Stores copies of the files you save (with version history) under this profile's plugin-data, reads this profile's Thor session database (state.db) read-only to find files the agent delivered and a bounded slice of recent conversation, and sends that slice plus the chosen file's content to your configured auxiliary model to draft titles, tags and descriptions; renders PDF previews with the local `pdftoppm`; Telegram panels work only for user IDs you list in `plugin-data/delivery-shelf/telegram-owners.json`, and an "always" answer lets later versions of that one entry be saved without asking until you revoke it.

name: delx-recovery
description: Free recovery and continuity for agents through the hosted Delx Protocol MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no API key, no OAuth, no payment), with the delx-recovery-first-hour workflow skill bundled: triage an error loop or lost context, resume a prior session, capture state and context memory, seal a Continuity Capsule (goal/done/next/blockers/refuted) before compaction so the next session resumes warm, and turn failures into a recovery plan. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); Thor runs no code from it. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call, including the free-text problem description sent by public triage, goes to the remote server at api.delx.ai. Public triage needs no credential; private continuity uses a free agent credential returned at registration and passed as a tool argument. What the agent chooses to store (state, memory, capsules) is retained by Delx under its privacy policy, so do not send secrets. Requests carry ?src=plugin for channel attribution. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The hooks/ shell scripts in the directory are opt-in Claude Code hooks that Thor does not load.

name: demand-radar
description: Prove someone wants it before you build it. Searches Stack Exchange, Hacker News and GitHub issues for people asking for an idea, keeps only on-topic requests (a noise gate, not a model's opinion), and returns a GO / NARROW / KILL / NO SIGNAL verdict with the rule that fired, quotes with links, who already builds it, and how demand moved since the last check. Tools demand_radar_check and demand_radar_history, the /radar slash command and the validate-idea skill. No API key needed. Disclosure — each check sends the idea text and its phrasings as search queries to api.stackexchange.com, hn.algolia.com and api.github.com; check history and HTML reports stay in the plugin's own data folder; an optional read-only GitHub token is read through Thor's secret route; no shell commands, background processes, telemetry or Python dependencies.

name: desensitize
description: Chinese-context desensitization for Thor chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

name: design-discovery
description: Turns a vague product idea into a DESIGN.md a coding agent can build from: a few plain questions, three visual directions, changes in your own words. Loads fonts from Google Fonts. Disclosure — the Desktop pane and the exported DESIGN.md load fonts from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com), so the user's IP reaches Google when the pane renders; while a design session is active the plugin blocks non-design tools in that session until DESIGN.md is exported or the session is ended (ask the agent to stop designing).

name: deskrpg
description: Thor gateway integration for DeskRPG virtual offices, with profiles, kanban, cron, artifacts and NPC skill management. Install it through the DeskRPG setup wizard. Optional (off by default): when enabled by the operator, links the plugin into every profile so kanban workers and cron runs can save artifacts. Disclosure — NPC skill management runs thor skills/curator commands as background subprocesses per profile and edits that profile's skills, config.yaml and memory files; creating new review-policy kanban cards needs a review-policy API that upstream Thor does not ship (the README points at the author's thor-agent fork for it), and that feature stays inert on upstream.

name: desktop-inbox
description: An Inbox pane for Thor Desktop. Cron jobs, scripts and webhooks file items (Read, Answer, Decide, Do, or your own types) as Thor-started Desktop conversations, each with one clear ask. The pane is a keyboard-driven triage queue (snooze, undo, OS notifications) that also lists what waits on you elsewhere: chats with a pending question, blocked or triage kanban cards, and failing cron jobs (one click files a Fix item). Items close themselves when the kanban card they started is done. Disclosure: reads state.db, cron/jobs.json, cron/output and every kanban.db read-only; changes sessions only through public SessionDB methods (title, folder, archive state, hiding an item's opening message, its first Thor message); writes its own files in the inbox folder; runs `thor chat` once per new item (one model turn), `thor kanban archive` when you archive a card from the pane, and `gh api user` once when the webhook needs your GitHub login; the optional webhook listener (off by default) binds 127.0.0.1 only, refuses posts until its token or GitHub secret is set, and refuses browser (Origin) requests; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: details
description: Find curated website design references, inspect motion and implementation evidence, and retrieve reusable Vault components. Includes the details-design skill. Every tool call sends its arguments to https://api.details.so/mcp using the connected member's account. Available tools depend on that account's plan. The hosted tool set can change independently of the pinned plugin. Searches and inspections record usage and can consume Details credits. The package runs mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm) for browser OAuth, opens a local callback on first use, and stores tokens locally under ~/.mcp-auth. The server is marked untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable calls. Disclosure — every tool call sends its arguments to Details' hosted server (api.details.so) and acts on the user's Details account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha, and searches and inspections record usage and can consume Details credits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required; its own npm dependencies resolve at first run), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: detonator
description: Security testing sandbox for Thor plugins: detonate a plugin you did not write before you install it, and see whether it steals keys, phones home, runs shell commands or plants persistence. After you approve the run, /detonate fetches the plugin at an exact commit and loads it inside a disposable Docker container (no network, read-only, non-root, all capabilities dropped) with a throwaway Thor home full of decoy keys, drives its hooks and tools, jumps the clock to wake time bombs, and reports what it actually did: credential theft (even disguised or split up), network attempts, shell commands, persistence, prompt injection, tool poisoning, monkeypatching. A full test also watches from outside the plugin's container (a system-call tracer and a fake internet), so a plugin that hides from the inside monitor or fakes a clean result is still caught; a quicker inside-only test is offered, and every report says which test ran. A malware and supply-chain safety check you can run in seconds, with deterministic rules, a plain-language reason and MITRE ATT&CK / ATLAS IDs per finding; advisory only, a clean run is evidence, not proof. Disclosure — requires Docker; runs git (fetches the target repo over the network) and docker on your machine, only after you approve each run. One-time image builds pull a digest-pinned python:3.11-slim and install strace from Debian's signed package archive. A full test starts two extra short-lived monitor containers next to the sandbox: the tracer gets the SYS_PTRACE capability, the fake internet NET_ADMIN and NET_BIND_SERVICE; the plugin's own container keeps all capabilities dropped and reaches only the fake internet, never the real one. It refuses to run unattended; writes reports under its own plugin-data folder; never reads your real keys or Thor credentials.

name: developh
description: Free website audits through Developh's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.developh.co/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): Google PageSpeed Insights on mobile for any public website, with the four Lighthouse scores, real-visitor Core Web Vitals when Google has them, the failing audits that weigh most, missing security headers and page weight. Bundles the website-audit skill, which turns the report into a ranked fix list for the site's stack. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to www.developh.co, and run_website_audit passes the address it is given to Google PageSpeed Insights. Audits are not stored. Three tools are annotated read-only (run_website_audit, studio_info, list_case_studies). request_contact writes: it sends a project inquiry with the name, email and message the person gives, which Developh stores and records in its analytics, and emails them a confirmation. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before request_contact runs and refuses it in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: devin
description: Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Thor Desktop. Every launch goes through Thor approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Thor does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Thor approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Thor prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Thor provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.

name: devkit
description: One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.

name: devsentry
description: Read-only project inventory, traceback leads, and tracked Git diffs.

name: devtune
description: DevTune through its official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://devtune.ai/api/mcp): what AI answer engines say about a product and who they cite instead, AI crawler and referral traffic, the ranked queue of fixes with briefs and drafts, before/after results for shipped fixes, and Agent Picks (which tools coding agents pick when asked to add a capability). Bundles two skills, devtune and agent-picks, that pick the right tool for each question and report rates in the units DevTune measures them. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code, hooks or background processes; every tool call goes to devtune.ai with the user's own project API key (DEVTUNE_API_KEY, sent as a bearer header), and the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Some tools change project data or spend DevTune credits (briefs, drafts, agent runs, Agent Picks tests); the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every MCP tool not annotated read-only and refuses those tools in unattended runs, and paid Agent Picks tests also need a quote the user approves. When the MCP tools are unavailable, the bundled skills tell the agent to call DevTune's REST API (devtune.ai/api/v2) from the shell with DEVTUNE_API_KEY, where writes and credit spends are gated only by the skill's ask-first instructions, not by Thor approval; with no DevTune account, they tell the agent to follow devtune.ai/auth.md to register one with the user's email and use the claimed access token.

name: dexio
description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use; and a Thor Desktop pane showing which pages the agent recalled and wrote and what your other agents changed. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. The provider uses the standard library only, the pane's backend uses the FastAPI that Thor ships, and neither starts threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step; while the Desktop pane is open, its backend (loaded only with dexio in plugins.enabled) asks the same server for the wiki's recent changes, name, page count and page titles, cached 8 to 60 seconds; the last 200 recalls and tool calls (search text cut to 160 characters, page paths and titles, notes and errors) are kept in $THOR_HOME/dexio/activity.jsonl and pushed to Desktop windows connected to the same Thor, never uploaded.

name: diaktoros
description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Thor agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Thor agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, a `diaktoros/review` check run or commit status at each open loop PR's head, a repository ruleset requiring that check when you run `protect`, a GitHub App's webhook URL and secret when you run `app-webhook --set`, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts or, opt-in, when a loop PR falls behind, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; an opt-in approval by the adjudicator's account when it rules for the fixer, dismissing the change request it overruled; an opt-in one-time rerun of the failed CI jobs at the default branch's head when a failure looks like a flake, as a maintainer login whose token you provide, never a seat's; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files or GitHub App private keys you provide (for an App, the host signs a JWT, with Python's cryptography package or else the openssl command, and mints a short-lived installation token for that one repository); its create-apps command opens your browser and runs a one-shot server on 127.0.0.1 for GitHub's App-manifest flow, then writes each new App's private key (mode 0600) to a directory you choose (by default under the Thor home); edits Thor's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one thor cron job (its migrate command replaces the old thor-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose and prunes its own older default-named archives (10 kept unless set), and restore first backs up the live install, then writes an archive back into the Thor home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Thor home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices and an optional weekly report to the chat you name; opt-in shadow reviews spend a second profile's model tokens on reviews that are recorded but never posted; an opt-in change proof runs the tests a PR adds or changes inside the same bubblewrap sandbox, on the merge base and at the head, before each review; its optional Desktop page and local dashboard API read loop state and can re-arm a failed run as `thor dk retry` would, and, after an explicit confirmation, pause or resume a loop's hooks, escalate a PR, cancel a queued or running run, or declare or waive an issue dependency (a local record), and doctor compares the installed commit with the plugin's latest GitHub release (read-only); deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Thor token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.

name: dial-a-thor
description: Talk to Thor from any phone with no data: a USSD gateway platform (Africa's Talking-compatible callback) with 182-char paged replies, a 'thinking, press 1 to check' flow for long turns, keypad exec approvals (1 Approve / 2 Deny, full command shown first, Thor's own approval flow), clarify answers, optional SMS of the full reply, English/Nigerian Pidgin menus and a local feature-phone simulator. Owner-only phone allowlist, fails closed. Disclosure — opens a local HTTP listener (default 127.0.0.1:8095) for POST /ussd/<secret-token> and GET /health, plus a loopback-only simulator page when USSD_SIMULATOR=true; Africa's Talking does not sign callbacks, so the secret token in the URL is the boundary; outbound calls only when USSD_SMS_MODE=africastalking, to api.africastalking.com / api.sandbox.africastalking.com (reply text and the owner's number); stores per-phone language choice in the plugin data folder; no telemetry.

name: diff-review
description: Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs, in a diff you pass, the working tree (untracked files included) or a branch against its merge base.

name: digital-marketing-pro
description: Open-source marketing toolkit for agencies and in-house teams, one listing with three skill groups and 207 skills registered as Thor skills: Digital Marketing Pro (strategy, SEO/AEO/GEO, paid media, CRM, analytics; 164 skills), ContentForge (fact-checked long-form content with a run auditor; 22 skills) and SocialForge (a content calendar to images, carousels, video and copy; 21 skills). Skills only: no tools, hooks or background processes. Disclosure — Skills only (no tools, hooks or MCP servers). The optional scripts the skills run call third-party APIs (ad, CRM, e-mail, Slack, LLM and image/video providers) only when run, using the user's own keys from environment variables. Live writes need the user's typed yes. For writes the plugin sends itself, the script creates a single-use approval record when it prepares the write, and the agent approves that record after the yes, so Thor does not prompt before those script runs. Writes through MCP tools rely on the typed yes alone. Paid image and video generation is quoted first. refresh_models.py reads your Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and (strategy group) Evolink keys. Keys and data live outside the Thor profile: SocialForge stores API keys in plain text, plus a copy of any Google service-account file, in ~/socialforge-workspace; brand data goes to ~/.claude-marketing; deliverables are copied to ~/Documents/DigitalMarketingPro and ~/Documents/ContentForge. Nothing installs unless the user says yes; installs are exact-pinned pip packages into the Python that runs the script, plus Playwright's Chromium download. See the README and each group's PRIVACY.md.

name: dike
description: Diké: checks the article citations of Chilean law in a legal brief against a sealed, hash-identified local copy of 25 statutes (Ley Chile), and refuses to certify what it cannot prove. Each citation comes back verified, with its identifier, source URL and text SHA-256, or unverified with the engine's reason (AMBIGUOUS, UNRESOLVABLE). Three tools (dike_verificar_citas on text or a .md/.txt/.docx path; dike_leer_articulo and dike_buscar_corpus, read-only on the corpus), two commands (/dike-verificar, /dike-estado) and two skills. Text in English, Spanish optional; statute text and engine codes stay in Spanish. Not legal advice: it never certifies that a provision supports an argument, nor that a dated copy is today's text. The opt-in Desktop page adds a Case Writer (a brief editor where only the engine can mark a citation verified, a pseudonymization step you control before any text leaves, and a chat about the brief in your own Thor gateway), a read-only 3D map of the sealed corpus and a versioned case board; a Dashboard tab and a backend at /api/plugins/dike serve them. Disclosure — the vendored Diké engine runs in a child process (same interpreter, no shell, minimal environment without agent credentials), inside bubblewrap without network when it is available and in a declared degraded mode when it is not. One such sandboxed engine process stays up per session so the corpus is verified once (about 170 MB; it exits after 10 idle minutes or with Thor). Two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call) act only on Case Writer chat sessions, which carry a <dike-escritor v=\"1\"> envelope: they add fixed instructions and block every tool except skills, tool discovery and this plugin's three tools with text arguments; other sessions are untouched. Model calls happen only when you use that chat, case-board suggestions or opt-in prediction, through your own gateway, after pseudonymization unless you switch it off and confirm sending the real data. Reads only the text passed or the named regular .md/.txt/.docx file (no symlinks). Writes only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/dike: the corpus (about 300 MB, unpacked once after a SHA-256 check, checked by file stat on every call and fully re-hashed once per process), temporary files, engine caches, Case Writer briefs, pseudonym maps (they hold the real values; files 0600) and send and hook logs without content. The Desktop page adds one scoped <style> element and removes it on unload. No network of its own after dependency install, no telemetry, never signs.

name: dioramic
description: A Blender scene director. The agent describes a scene as a structured JSON spec (toy-style shapes and 3D text, finishes, colours, three lighting rigs, camera moves, keyframed spin, bounce, float, pop-in, move and wobble) and dioramic renders it in headless Blender (EEVEE) as a vertical 9:16 MP4 plus a still preview, returned as MEDIA tags so the gateway delivers the clip. dioramic_tweak merges only the changes into an earlier scene and renders a new version. Disclosure: runs the Blender binary you configure as a subprocess with a scrubbed environment (no API keys), a fixed build script that reads the spec as data (no model-written code), capped duration, samples and resolution, and a kill timeout; writes only to its profile-scoped plugin-data folder; no network calls.

name: disciplined-vibe-coding
description: Define/Plan/Build/Verify pipeline with five folded-in practices, for non-engineer builders

name: discord-tps
description: Show live tokens-per-second and the active model on your Discord bot's presence. Disclosure — Replaces the Discord bot's public presence with the live tok/s figure and the model name of the most recent API call in this gateway (any platform or chat), visible to anyone who can see the bot; updates at most every interval seconds (minimum 10) over the gateway's existing Discord connection. Reads no credentials and makes no network calls of its own.

name: disko
description: Run and steer a disko AI DJ set on your Mac from any Thor chat. disko's model picks each next track and beat-matches the mix; this plugin launches it on a music folder or a Spotify playlist, starts the set, steers the energy, asks for a different next track, pauses and stops, through ten tools, a /disko slash command and a thor disko CLI that need no model turn, and a pre_llm_call hook that tells the agent what is playing while a set runs. Standard library only. Disclosure — talks only to disko's local control socket (~/.disko/control.sock), which disko restricts to the same macOS user, so no token is used; reads ~/.disko/install.json (disko's folder and Python path, written by disko; not a credential) to find disko, and reads no token or credential file. No third-party network calls (an optional control_url, set by the user, is contacted over plain HTTP with a token from Thor's secret store). disko_launch starts disko as a background process with a fixed command (no shell) and a minimal environment (none of Thor's API keys) that keeps running after Thor exits and logs to the plugin's data folder (a Spotify playlist is passed only as `liked` or a playlist id; disko, not the plugin, then uses the user's own Spotify sign-in, and only if the user turned Spotify audio on in disko themselves); disko_start plays music out loud on the Mac. While a set runs, one line of track names is added to each message and reaches the model provider. Requires disko (github.com/emirkaan5/disko) on macOS. No telemetry.

name: distro-reader
description: Read independent news and content from Distro publications in Thor through the public Distro Reader MCP server: search, feeds, full stories, archive research, visual article and book rendering, podcasts, payment information, and user-approved tips. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with three workflow skills; public reading needs no account or API key. Disclosure — connects to Distro's hosted Reader MCP server (reader.distro.media); its distro_tip tool and bundled premium-access skill start x402 crypto payments (tips and premium story/book purchases) with the user's wallet, which the skill only does after the user approves the exact amount, asset and network; the server is declared untrusted so its write tools go through Thor approval.

name: dj-thor
description: The DJ that grows with you — Thor plugin for uzu-language beat making. Disclosure — The skills have the agent run Rscript (the author's maelstrom R package, installed separately from GitHub), llama-cli on an optional Rhythmancer 3B GGUF the user downloads from Hugging Face (Nanite-Labs/nanites-rhythmancer-3b-generator-gguf; not revision- or hash-pinned), and a local audio player (ffplay/aplay/paplay/afplay) through the terminal tool, writing rendered WAVs to the working directory; Strudel exports are strudel.cc share links built locally. No tools, hooks, commands or middleware are registered.

name: doc-markdown
description: doc_convert makes Markdown from one local PDF, .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, HTML, CSV, JSON, Markdown, or plain text on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown; CSV, JSON, Markdown, and plain text must be UTF-8. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — fetches no pages; after realpath, any allowlisted path it can open is readable, and it is not a sandbox; the child gets no Thor keys; unpublished Thor code locates the Thor home, and a failed check refuses the path; on every surface, including a gateway, for anyone you allow, and for unattended calls Thor makes; thor tools stops it; no cron; about 500 MB; removal leaves that install.

name: docket
description: Quotes for trades businesses (plumbers, electricians, HVAC): describe a job in words or a voice note and Docket prices every line from the owner's own price book with a deterministic engine (the model only picks item codes; it never writes a number). The owner approves with one tap on Telegram, Slack, Discord or Desktop, the customer accepts on a quote page, and the owner books the day and closes out with an invoice. Includes a plain-words price book editor with preview before save, PDF quotes and invoices, follow-ups, a run sheet and a Desktop Jobs board. Disclosure — Docket stores customers, quotes and invoices in a local SQLite file under plugin-data/docket and starts a local HTTP server for the customer accept page (127.0.0.1:8787 by default, in a background thread of the gateway, one server for all profiles the gateway serves); it reads a price list file only when the owner names one; job descriptions and unreadable price lists go to the model configured in Thor; the pre_transcription hook adds price book item names to the speech-to-text prompt; sending a quote and saving price changes ask the owner first, and both, plus closing a job, are blocked in scheduled runs; with Obol installed, close-out returns a prepared draft that the agent creates through obol_create_invoice, so Obol's own approval applies (Docket never calls Obol itself). No outbound network calls of its own, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry, no email sending.

name: docs-drift
description: Checks that the README and Markdown docs still match the code after the agent edits files. When a write_file or patch call leaves the docs naming a command-line flag, environment variable, default value, npm script, make target or file that the code no longer has, the tool result gets a docs_drift block with file:line on both sides, in the same turn. When an edit adds a flag or environment variable that no doc mentions while the docs document its siblings, the result says so and says where the siblings are documented. Fixing the doc reports the finding as resolved, and the agent is reminded once before it finishes if drift from this session is still open. Also adds a docs_drift_scan tool (whole repository or changed files only), docs_drift_explain (the evidence behind one finding), a /drift command and a python -m docsdrift command line for CI. Deterministic and offline: Python standard library only, no model call, no network, no API key. Markdown and MDX docs only. Disclosure — to do its job the plugin runs git (ls-files, status, cat-file blob, diff --cached --name-only, check-ignore, config --get-regexp; none of them writes) in the repository being edited, with options that keep that repository's git config from starting a program and with an environment that carries no API key, and reads that repository's text files and .git/config. It does not follow a link out of the repository, does not open .env or key files (templates such as .env.example are read), writes nothing to disk, makes no network request and sends no telemetry.

name: doctorpack
description: Local-first diagnostics, safety audit, and incident postmortems for Thor Agent.

name: document-reader
description: Profile-scoped document OCR for Thor Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

name: dome-relay
description: Escalate a task to another established agent through an always-on callback relay and read the result back in the conversation that sent it. Registers jobs with tools dome_relay_escalate, dome_relay_status, and dome_relay_cancel; a worker polls the relay; the relay (not this plugin) wakes a Grok Bot executive.
