Disclosure — sends each escalated job (task text, target name, optional https reference links) to the HTTPS relay you configure in `relay_url` (no default host; you deploy the relay from this repo's `relay/` folder), which forwards it to your Grok Bot webhook and spends Grok Bot usage on each successful wake; the model can queue a job without an approval prompt, and jobs leave the machine only while you run `thor dome-relay worker` (a long-running poller you start yourself); stores job metadata and results in the active profile's plugin-data database; its only secret is DOME_RELAY_KEY, read through Thor secret scope and sent only to that relay; optional settings (off by default) add finished results from the relay to the next turn's context.

name: done-bell
description: Ring when a Thor turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

name: doom
description: Play Doom in a dashboard tab. The GPL engine runs as plain JavaScript on Freedoom or your own WAD. Disclosure — The Doom engine is Emscripten-compiled JavaScript (doomgeneric, GPL) committed as a generated file and built by hand from the repo's engine/build.sh; clicking "Download Freedoom" fetches the 23 MB Freedoom 0.13.0 release zip from github.com/freedoom, checksum-verified, into THOR_HOME/plugin-data/doom. No tools, hooks or other network calls.

name: doorman
description: Wake-on-LAN doorman for sleeping inference backends. When an API request targets a host from a config-driven host map that is asleep, Doorman broadcasts a UDP magic packet, waits a bounded time for the inference port to accept a connection, then holds a per-request keep-alive (one packet per interval) for the life of the request, released on completion or on a terminal error; hosts that answer are left alone and no packet is sent. If the turn is cancelled (/stop), a lifecycle hook releases every live hold so the host is not woken for a request nobody is waiting on. Pure Python, no dependencies, config re-read per hook fire. Disclosure — sends UDP magic packets and TCP connect probes to the local hosts listed in its own `doorman:` block in config.yaml only, never to third parties; the keep-alive runs on one background daemon thread per plugin instance, with holds bounded by a leak cap (default 7200s) and torn down on completion or turn cancellation; no telemetry, no shell commands, no credentials or secrets, no self-updating code.

name: dosbox-full-auto
description: All-in-one solution for controlling DOSBox apps with your agent. Self-contained DOSBox-automation with built-in MCP server, registers in Thor and exposes 55 tools via the dosbox-full-auto skill such as vision based mouse movement, live process memory reading and more. Disclosure — Downloads the author's prebuilt DOSBox-automation emulator and MCP server binaries (GitHub release, sha256-pinned per tag) into plugin-data and registers them as an MCP server; the emulator exposes an unauthenticated HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8387 that any local process can use to type into DOS and read/write emulator memory; host folders can be mounted only under the plugin's drives folder and the roots you list as mount_allowed_bases in the emulator's own config; the optional visual check sends screenshots to decision.vllm-sr.ai with a key minted after the user accepts that service's terms.

name: dosbox-mcp
description: Drive a DOS machine from the agent through dosbox-automation's own MCP bridge: type and press keys, read the screen, take screenshots, record video and audio, run Lua scripts inside the emulator, read and write its memory. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only: it starts the bridge with uvx dosbox-mcp==0.2.4 from PyPI and bundles one usage skill. Disclosure — runs `uvx dosbox-mcp==0.2.4` (dosbox-automation's own bridge from PyPI) as a local stdio MCP server that talks only to the separately installed dosbox-automation emulator on 127.0.0.1, using the API token the emulator writes to its own config folder (read-only); its tools type keys, read the screen, take screenshots and recordings into the emulator's capture folder, run Lua scripts inside the emulator and read/write the emulated machine's memory, CPU registers and I/O ports; a Lua script or a direct REST call (session_info hands the agent a curl example and the token file location) can write an audio recording to any non-system path and use API routes beyond the bridge's capability mode; `bridge_start` launches the emulator binary named in the bridge's human-edited config and `bridge_setup` changes only the headless and protocol settings; host folders reach DOS only through MOUNT below the emulator's `mount_allowed_bases`; no telemetry, no accounts.

name: dossier
description: Sourced, dated, refreshable dossiers on organisations and people in a professional capacity, framed for the meeting you actually have: interview, sales call, partnership, due diligence or supplier review. Every claim keeps a verbatim quote, a source URL, a publication date and a retrieval date; conflicting sources print as contested instead of being resolved, a figure the sources do not agree on is filed as unconfirmed rather than quoted, and a refresh reports only what changed since the last snapshot. Renders an A4 PDF, HTML, a chat card and a Desktop page, and ships an automation blueprint for scheduled refresh. Disclosure — makes outbound HTTP requests to the entity's own site and the pages it links to, to whatever hosts your configured Thor web search backend returns, to api.github.com / github.com, and to www.sec.gov / data.sec.gov (SEC EDGAR); ABN Lookup (abr.business.gov.au) and Companies House (api.company-information.service.gov.uk) are contacted only when their credentials are configured; non-public addresses are refused; dossiers on people and organisations are stored under the plugin's data directory until you delete them with /dossier forget or the Desktop button.

name: doubt
description: Word-by-word certainty heat maps from the model's own token probabilities, and a guard that sends commands built on a guess to the approval prompt. Disclosure — with the guard on (default for `terminal` calls), each guarded tool call sends one extra chat request carrying up to 8 KB of the recent conversation to the configured scorer endpoint (default: the agent's own endpoint) using DOUBT_SCORER_API_KEY or, on openrouter.ai, OPENROUTER_API_KEY; it also asks the provider for token logprobs on every chat-completions request and appends a one-line certainty summary under replies (`annotate: off` disables it).

name: draft-cards
description: Email and chat-message drafts as reviewable cards in the Thor Desktop chat. The agent's draft_card tool stores each draft and its revisions; the card shows recipients, subject and body, highlights the words each revision changed (removed text on demand), supports inline editing, and offers Copy and Open in Mail. The plugin never sends anything: pressing Send records approval of that exact version and posts it to the chat, then the agent sends it with the user's existing mail or messaging tools and reports the outcome with draft_card_status. Disclosure — stores draft text (recipients, subject, body, versions) in the profile's plugin-data/draft-cards/drafts.db (the 500 most recent drafts are kept); the desktop half appends one scoped stylesheet, removed on disable; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: draftroom
description: A Markdown draft beside Thor chat, with selected-text rewrites and explicit Accept/Reject review. Disclosure — stores drafts, pending suggestions and every prior revision as plain files in this profile's plugin-data folder (revisions are kept until the user deletes them); the agent tool can list and read every draft in the profile, not only the current conversation's; draft text reaches the model through the normal conversation; the Desktop pane polls its own local backend every 2-10 s while open; the Rewrite, /blog and "Commit to repo" buttons put a prompt into the focused chat's composer, and a commit request asks the agent to write the draft to a path the user typed and commit (push only when ticked) using the agent's own file/Git tools and approval prompts. The plugin itself runs no Git or shell commands, makes no network requests, reads no credentials and has no telemetry or self-update.

name: drag-to-pin-session
description: Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

name: dramatis
description: Spoiler-safe reading companion: open a local EPUB, remember how far you have read, and ask who someone is or what happened. Answers come only from text at or before that position, with a short quote. Native Python plugin (plugin.yaml + __init__.py). Disclosure — reads EPUB files from paths you supply; stores extracted chapter text, reading progress, and character cards in Thor plugin storage (plugin-data/dramatis/ and the dramatis plugin_db); no network calls, no extra API keys, no shell, no telemetry, and it does not read .env files or Thor credential stores. Ships an original fixture EPUB at fixtures/the-glass-archive.epub (reviewable XHTML inside a standard EPUB zip, not a compiled binary). Cannot stop the host model from using pretrained knowledge about well-known books.

name: dreamer
description: When Thor goes idle, it dreams. A native plugin that watches for idle windows (default: 15 min idle, at least 12 h between dreams) and replays the day's session residue - tool traffic, dead ends, unfinished threads - into a short narrative dream generated by the LLM, graded light or deep by sleep distance and stored in a local dream journal (title, symbols, mood, dream_type). Up to 1-3 actionable insights are distilled from each dream and injected into the next fresh session as a [DREAM RESIDUE] block, so recurring issues (stale tasks, stuck PIDs, untested regressions) surface where they can actually be handled instead of dying silently between sessions. Tools: dream_now (dream on demand), dream_journal (read past dreams), dream_status (enabled/last-dream/idle state). Hooks: one pre_llm_call hook that injects the pending dream residue - and only it - into a new session's context. Disclosure — a background thread started at load (on by default; `enabled: false` stops it, but the `dream_now` tool and the session-start injection still work until the plugin is disabled) reads this profile's `state.db` read-only every 15 minutes. After 15 idle minutes, and at most once per 12 hours, it sends recent user messages and tool-error fragments from every session on the profile (all platforms and chats) to your configured model through `ctx.llm`, unattended. It injects the resulting dream digest (up to 2000 chars) into the first turn of the next new session, whichever chat starts it. Dreams are stored under `<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/dreamer`. No network calls of its own.

name: dreaming
description: Local memory provider (memory.provider: dreaming) after Anthropic's "The components of agent memory": every turn is kept as a transcript and the agent writes quick notes; an offline dream pass checks notes against the transcripts, resolves changes stated by reference ("she handed everything over", nicknames, "what I said last time"), and rewrites a linked wiki plus a short index loaded into every session. Tools via the memory provider: mem_search, mem_read, mem_write; CLI: thor dreaming status|dream|search|show. Disclosure — memory stays in <thor_home>/dreaming/ as markdown, JSONL and a SQLite FTS5 cache; the plugin makes no network calls of its own, and the dream pass sends transcript excerpts and memory files to the user's configured model through ctx.llm; with auto_dream on (default) a pass runs in a background thread at session start. No credentials, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-updating.

name: dress-rehearsal
description: Rehearse a task before it touches anything: /rehearse on, then give Thor the job. Reads run for real; every side effect (file writes and edits, modifying shell commands, messages, schedules, any tool not on a read-only list) is recorded into a numbered script instead of running. /rehearse shows the script with diffs and risk flags, /rehearse drop strikes steps, /rehearse go replays the kept calls exactly as recorded with no model in the loop, in the folder they were rehearsed in, stops at the first failure (resumable) and refuses any file that changed since the rehearsal. Disclosure — hooks pre_tool_call (blocks and records side-effecting calls only while armed) and pre_llm_call (a short rehearsal note only while armed); one slash command; stores one script per profile, including tool arguments, in its plugin state; on /rehearse go dispatches the approved calls, plus read_file on files it is about to overwrite, through Thor's tool registry, where Thor's own approval and write guards still apply but other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks do not run; read-only git commands still honour the repository's own diff.external/textconv config while armed; no network calls, no subprocesses, no dependencies.

name: dropstation
description: Turn private local folders into Thor inboxes with standing tasks. Drop a document or image to get a Markdown reply and a durable processing receipt. The adapter polls the configured owner-private spool and uses its filesystem permissions as the inbound authorization boundary. Its events skip messaging allowlists and pairing. Snapshots, reports and receipts are stored locally. The configured Thor provider processes the source contents. Disclosure — every supported file written into a configured inbox folder starts an unattended Thor turn with that lane's task; the platform is trusted_inbound, so these events skip messaging allowlists and pairing and the folders' owner-only 0700 permissions are the only gate. The file's contents go to the configured model provider, and unless platform_toolsets.dropstation is set (the example config sets it to []) the turn gets the default core toolset, terminal and file tools included; commands that need approval cannot be approved from the inbox and are not run. Snapshots, receipts and reports are stored under the configured root.

name: dsers
description: DSers multi-platform dropshipping plugin for dropshippers, combining eight bundled workflow skills with a remote MCP connection for supplier discovery, product sourcing, listing editing, product publishing, profit and pricing, store management, supplier mapping, order fulfillment, and shipment tracking. The DSers ecosystem includes AliExpress, Alibaba.com, 1688, DVAN, Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, eBay, TikTok Shop, Amazon, Walmart, BigCommerce, Squarespace, Square, Ecwid, Magento, SHOPLINE, Jumpseller, Big Cartel, Cartpanda, Genstore, and LPQV; available operations depend on account and channel access. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugin with eight bundled skills and remote MCP configuration, with no native registered tools. Thor v0.22.5 requires manual native OAuth connection setup. A DSers Advanced, Pro, or Enterprise subscription is required. Tool arguments and results are exchanged with ai.dsers.com; Thor manages OAuth credentials. Remote tools include write operations, among them supplier-order placement that spends money through the user's DSers account, pricing changes and listing publication; the package and the documented native entry mark the server untrusted, so non-read-only calls are subject to Thor's tool approval settings. The remote tool set can change independently of the pinned package. Removing the plugin alone leaves the native MCP connection.

name: dsh-pet
description: Desktop pet for Thor: runs the upstream dsh-pet standalone pet (Node + Electron window), maps session/tool activity onto its work status, and adds start/stop/uninstall commands. This entry points at a fork of PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet (MIT, copyright PC2005-cloud): upstream owns the pet runtime, the animation assets and the DSH plugin; the fork adds only the thor/ adapter, and the pinned dsh-pet@0.4.7 runtime is the unmodified upstream npm package. Catalog installs fetch that runtime on first start (~80 MB, one time) with npm ci from a bundled lockfile (98 packages at exact versions with sha512 integrities), and dsh-pet downloads Electron (~350 MB) unless a local copy is reused. The child process runs with a minimal environment (PATH/temp/user dirs plus DSH_HOME); no inherited Thor environment or provider keys. The pet listens on 127.0.0.1:3080-3089 and keeps its data in the plugin data directory. Disclosure — on first start this plugin runs `npm ci` with its bundled lockfile (dsh-pet@0.4.7 and 98 exact, integrity-checked packages from registry.npmjs.org, install scripts off) into its plugin data directory, and the pet downloads Electron 43.3.0 (~350 MB) from npmmirror.com (override: DSH_PET_ELECTRON_MIRROR); when the gateway runs it starts a Node/Electron pet process automatically (turn off with `autostart: false`) under a minimal environment without Thor's provider keys, which listens on 127.0.0.1:3080-3089 with a per-run token and receives only the current tool name; the pet's optional chat feature sends your chat messages to the AI endpoint and API key you configure in the pet's settings; Electron userData is shared at %APPDATA%\dsh-pet-electron-helper.

name: duty-board
description: Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and thor duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens THOR_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only THOR_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process Thor 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

name: dyscalculia
description: Cited dyscalculia statistics from dyscalculia.io through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.dyscalculia.io/mcp, no sign-in, no keys): prevalence figures by study and age, 93 references with DOI and PMID, chart datasets on persistence, math anxiety, interventions and comorbidity, and a description of the site's five-game screening test. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.dyscalculia.io; no account or personal data is needed. All six tools are read-only and none scores a person. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: dyslexiasteps
description: Phonics and sight word lists by grade from dyslexiasteps.com through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.dyslexiasteps.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys): CVC words, word families, Dolch sight words, digraphs and vowel patterns for pre-K to grade 3, word lists in German, Spanish, French, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese, pattern search and the source of every grade placement. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.dyslexiasteps.com; no account or personal data is needed. All six tools are read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: earnfi
description: Work, Money & Execution Layer for Thor — hire humans and agents, fund real-world work via x402, escrow, and receipts across Solana, Base, NEAR, and OKX X Layer. Disclosure — Crypto payments: connects to EarnFi's hosted MCP server at app.earnfi.fun, whose tools create paid jobs, fund escrow, settle x402 payments and withdraw USDC on Solana, Base, NEAR and OKX X Layer. The server is declared untrusted, so every write or payment tool asks for Thor approval, with no spend cap by default. `earnfi_sign_x402` signs an x402 payment locally with the user's dedicated wallet key only after a Thor approval prompt showing network, amount, asset and payee. Optional Node setup scripts install exact-pinned npm packages (with install scripts disabled) and create dedicated wallet keys that the user stores in the plugin's secret settings.

name: eatwise
description: Eatwise (外卖营养教练) — local-first Chinese dietary coach: deterministic meal nutrition reviews, personal daily energy/nutrient targets, and consented on-device profile and meal history through 9 MCP tools over a bundled open food database (TFND + USDA FNDDS). No network, no accounts, no payments; profile schema rejects name/phone/ID/medical fields by design. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (cbc08f6) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 22.5+ on PATH. Disclosure — the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first.

name: echarts-in-chat
description: Render a chart inline in the Thor Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.

name: edit-ledger
description: Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network

name: effortless-thor
description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Thor' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.

name: egress-guard
description: Automated output vetting for AI agents. Policy-driven guard for what leaves the agent. A pre_tool_call hook redacts credentials in tool arguments and sends shell commands that upload data to non-allowlisted destinations (curl/wget uploads, scp/rsync, cloud copies, gist create, git push to a URL, python/node upload one-liners) to Thor's approval prompt, showing a masked preview of the command (fail-closed when nobody can approve). transform_tool_result and transform_llm_output suppress small counts in tables, including complementary cells and percentages so hidden values cannot be recovered (statistical disclosure control). Presets, an optional strict network mode, and a /guard command (status, report, dry-run check). Disclosure: no network access, subprocesses or tools; reads its policy from EGRESS_GUARD_POLICY, ~/.thor/egress-guard.yaml or the bundled default, and its own audit log for /guard report; appends masked audit lines (never raw values) to ~/.thor/egress-guard/audit.jsonl; never auto-approves.

name: elcaro
description: Runtime prompt-injection defense and tamper-evident flight recorder. Every tool result is scanned before it reaches the model by a deterministic detector taxonomy (sub-10 ms, fully local, vendored — no network by default); quarantined content is replaced in place with a signed [CONTENT QUARANTINED] notice via transform_tool_result, and tool-call arguments (write_file, terminal, memory) are scanned for smuggled payloads via pre_tool_call. Beyond content, a kernel gate: a quarantine taints the session, and while tainted credential-path reads/writes and instruction-file writes are refused, network egress and outside-workspace writes escalate to the approval gate — tool_call, execute_code and process_manage are evaluated as the action they really make, and taint propagates into subagents via subagent_start. A canary-baited decoy credentials file (ELCARO-DECOY-* marker) forces a deterministic 1.0 quarantine on exfiltration; canary provenance edges record an injection propagating between scans; every verdict lands in a hash-chained, Ed25519-signed threat log with a Desktop pane (chain-verified badge, honeypot status, propagation rows, signed-receipts drawer), a /elcaro slash command (status / calibrate / verify / explain), and a `thor elcaro` CLI. Two on-demand tools close the loop input scanning can't: elcaro_lint_response flags concealed-compromise artifacts in agent output (canary echoes, text-channel tool calls, tracking pixels, secrets — caught 148/152 compromised transcripts in the public 24-task IPI benchmark), and elcaro_harden_prompt returns a hardened system prompt plus a gullibility score. Engine validated on that benchmark: 22/22 attack tasks flagged (regression coverage, not held-out proof). Disclosure — scanning is fully local by default: the vendored engine's env-driven LLM second passes (api.openai.com, inference-api.openserv.ai and others) and its Postgres canary registry are built disabled; scanned tool-result text leaves the machine only when the user sets the optional `api_url` hosted lane, which POSTs it there with the optional `ELCARO_API_KEY`; the optional `ELCARO_SIGNING_KEY` is read from the profile secret store; it writes only to its plugin data dir (threat-log.jsonl, decoy-marker.txt, and a bait service-credentials.env decoy it never reads); a quarantine taints the session so credential-path and instruction-file writes are refused and network/outside-workspace actions escalate to Thor approval (nothing auto-approves); Python deps pydantic, cryptography, httpx; no core overrides.

name: elevenlabs-music
description: ElevenLabs Music for Thor: describe a song or paste your lyrics and Thor writes, generates and sends the track, 3 seconds to 10 minutes, vocals or instrumental. It can redo one section, extend or loop a song, split it into stems (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other) and score a video. Long songs finish in the background and arrive in the chat. Bundles a music skill (prompting, composition plans, edit recipes) and, in Thor Desktop, an inline music card with synced lyrics, format downloads and a music library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Thor's ElevenLabs voice; needs a paid ElevenLabs plan, and a restricted key needs the Music permission); compose, plan, upload, stems and video calls are paid generations billed to your ElevenLabs account by length (drafting a plan and listing finetunes are free). Only the prompt or plan, its parameters and any file you name are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set); with store_for_editing on, ElevenLabs keeps generated songs so they can be edited later. Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Thor home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Thor).

name: elevenlabs-sound-effects
description: ElevenLabs sound effects for Thor: one tool, elevenlabs_sound_effect, that turns a text description ("glass shattering on a tile floor", "90s hip-hop drum loop, 90 BPM") into an audio file, 0.5 to 30 seconds, optionally a seamless loop, and sends it to you in chat. Bundles a sound-design skill with a local ffmpeg script (trim, loudness, mono, loop fixing, game variation packs) and, in Thor Desktop, an inline sound card and a sound library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Thor's ElevenLabs voice; a restricted key needs the Sound Effects permission); every call is a paid generation billed to your ElevenLabs account. Only the sound description and its parameters are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set). Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Thor home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Thor).

name: emailfig
description: Work in your EmailFig email marketing account through EmailFig's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://emailfig.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check campaign and automation results, look up and update contacts, lists and tags, add images, and draft campaigns that you review and send in EmailFig. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to EmailFig's hosted server (emailfig.com) and acts on the EmailFig account the user approved at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The server cannot send, schedule or delete a campaign; the only email it sends is a test of a draft to the user's own address, though adding someone to a double opt-in list emails them a confirmation and adding or tagging a contact can start the account's automations. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores the OAuth token under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: embargo
description: Embargoed news stays embargoed. When your agent reads 'EMBARGOED UNTIL <time>', tool calls that carry that text are blocked until the clock passes; a live countdown stamp shows what is held, and the hold lifts by itself. Disclosure: hooks pre_tool_call (blocks matching calls; fails closed while an embargo exists), post_tool_call and pre_llm_call (detect embargo headers in files read and messages), transform_llm_output (adds the card); stores label, lift time, file paths and hashed 6-word fingerprints plus hashed headline names and figures, never the raw release text (the one-line label, up to 80 characters, is plain text), in its data folder. Your model provider still sees the text you share; this is a send guard, not a privacy filter. Catches copies, quotes and reworded posts that repeat the headline names and figures; not a full paraphrase detector. Standard library only; it makes no network or model calls and reports nothing anywhere.

name: emotion-chip
description: Your Thor agent decides how to say it: the sighs, whispers and pauses it writes, voiced by ElevenLabs or Fish Audio. It writes its own delivery into the text it speaks, a small score in square brackets (a sigh, a whispered line, a pause, a warm and amused tone), and Emotion Chip renders exactly that for ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio (s2.1-pro, Drama 3), each in its own dialect, adding nothing the agent did not write. With voice replies on in a chat (/voice on), the chip tells the agent when Thor will read its reply aloud, so the agent can say it itself, score included, instead of Thor reading the plain text (not on Discord). Registers the emotion-chip speech provider, a delivery guide in the system prompt, the emotion-chip-voice skill, the emotion-chip-report-problem skill (guides the agent through a bug report and posts nothing without the user's yes), the /chip command (status says whether the chip can speak and what to fix; why, quiet, register) the thor chip command, which shows offline what each engine receives for any score, and two agent tools: chip_status (read-only) and chip_preview (offline). CC0 emotion data and pre-registered evaluations ship in the repository. Disclosure — with backend: eleven it sends your ElevenLabs API key, the rendered text, the model id, voice id, voice settings, an optional seed and, on v4 models, up to three earlier request ids from the same session (kept in memory for two hours) to api.elevenlabs.io over HTTPS; these are paid requests billed to your ElevenLabs account. The key is read at each call through the profile's secret scope and never stored. With the default backend: fish it sends nothing itself: it hands the rendered text to the Fish Audio plugin in the same process (which must be installed, enabled and signed in), and that plugin sends it to Fish Audio under its own disclosure and bills your Fish account; the chip reaches it through Thor's speech-provider registry and imports its tag adapter. In every guide mode it registers the emotion-chip-report-problem skill, which is text only: the plugin sends and writes nothing for it, and the skill has the agent publish a report only after the user approves the exact text. With guide_mode: generate (the default) it registers the emotion-chip-voice skill, and while it is the speech provider it adds a delivery guide of up to 4,000 characters to the system prompt and registers pre_gateway_dispatch (described next). With guide_mode: generate it also registers two agent tools. chip_status reads the plugin's settings, Thor's tts configuration and this session's last authored register and reports them; it sends nothing and changes nothing. chip_preview renders a score offline and returns the text each engine would receive and the cues it would drop; no synthesis, no network, nothing written. While the chip is the speech provider, each successful text_to_speech result gains an emotion_chip entry of at most 600 characters (the dialect, the agent's cue words, drops and notes); it stays in the conversation and is sent nowhere. The pre_gateway_dispatch hook: for each incoming message it asks the gateway whether it will read the reply aloud and keeps that answer in memory under the chat and message id (at most 256, never used after 15 minutes), used once to add one line to that message's turn; it never skips or changes a message, and registering the hook routes webhook and relay deliveries through Thor's hooked ingress path. When another speech provider is selected, its tool_request middleware rewrites text_to_speech text containing a bracket for that provider (the Fish dialect on Fish S2 and Drama 3 models, or the ElevenLabs dialect on a v3/v4 model; for any other provider or model, including Thor's default Edge, Fish S1 and ElevenLabs on older models, standalone bracketed words are removed as cues, a bracketed Step 2 too, while the words inside spans, numeric references such as [1] and code such as an array index stay), leaves command providers alone and records nothing. With signals on (off by default) it adds a dated situation line of up to 200 characters to the turn and, when a tool call fails, to that call's result. It reads Thor's tts configuration (read-only) to pick the dialect, model and voice. It writes under the profile's plugin-data/emotion-chip/ only the generated skill and, unless delivery_log is off, delivery.jsonl (time, session id, sender id, platform, model, dialect, rendering group, cue words, parameters, kinds of drops and character count, never the spoken text), moved to delivery.1.jsonl at 5 MB so at most about 10 MB is kept; Thor keeps its per-session state (task counters and timestamps, the ids of the last 16 tool calls counted, session keys, the messaging sender id and platform, the last situation and register lines, the quiet switch; the 50 most recent sessions) in the plugin's own namespaced folder under plugin-data/. Audio goes to the path Thor supplies. No background processes, no shell commands, no telemetry.

name: empiriolabs
description: EmpirioLabs AI as a Thor model provider (provider id `empiriolabs`): chat models with tool calling from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog, each with its context window, image input and reasoning support declared to Thor, a low-cost auxiliary model picked from the same catalog, and `reasoning_effort` sent only when you choose a level and the model accepts it. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests (prompts, tool definitions and tool results) go through Thor' own client to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, which Thor reads, and are billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account; the plugin itself only reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models, kept in memory for an hour), writes no files and starts no processes.

name: empiriolabs-media
description: EmpirioLabs AI backends for Thor' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through Thor' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no Thor approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into Thor' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.

name: emporia
description: An open network for AI agents: Thor agents meet other agents on relays — a signed feed, rooms, sealed DMs the relay cannot read, games, labs tied to code repos, and a season of quests. Testnet only; the relay holds no money. Disclosure — Crypto: agents can hold EVM/Solana wallets and pay in USDC over x402/Tempo (testnet by default; mainnet only after the person runs `emporia wallet mainnet`), with per-payment and daily caps; on testnet a Thor approval is asked above a set threshold, and on mainnet every payment asks for Thor approval and is refused in turns another agent or the rounds job started. The agent's posts, sealed DMs, game moves and declared model name go to the relay you choose; setup has no default relay. `thor emporia setup` fetches Emporia's runtime from github.com/wujitsana/emporia at a pinned commit, installs its locked Python packages from PyPI, creates an agent profile, writes `mcp_servers.emporia` and settings into that profile's config.yaml and .env, and adds a Thor cron job that runs unattended agent turns (every 4 hours unless you pick another interval in setup). The gateway runs a long-lived bridge process to the relay, and the dashboard starts a local console process on a Unix socket. Optional password-manager key sources run that vendor's CLI with a token kept in the profile's settings.

name: emporium
description: Thor opens a shop: sell this agent's skills to anyone (people, scripts, other agents) for USDC per job over x402, paid only on delivery. A new gateway platform takes paid HTTP jobs, verifies the payment before work starts and settles it on-chain only when the result is ready, so a failed, timed-out or abandoned job costs the buyer nothing. Each job runs in its own session that loads only the toolsets its service sells, behind a tool lock and a per-job tool cap. Every job is metered (model calls, tokens, and its inference cost from Thor's own session pricing), so /shop and the dashboard show sales, AI cost, profit and margin. Services can subcontract part of a job to owner-pinned shops, paid out of the job's own price. Thor can also hire other shops, after checking their receipts on-chain, within a per-job ceiling, a daily budget and its approval gate. Adds a storefront page, /shop, `thor emporium`, a dashboard tab, and stress and robbery benches. Disclosure — while the gateway runs the shop listens on host:port (default 127.0.0.1:9402) and calls the configured x402 facilitator (default x402.org) to verify and settle payments, and a JSON-RPC endpoint (default the network's public one) to check payments on-chain; the hire tools call the shop URLs the agent is given (public addresses only, unless the owner lists a private shop in buyer_allow_hosts; link-local and metadata addresses never) and the network's RPC; the optional EMPORIUM_BUYER_KEY (read via the secret scope) signs USDC transfer authorizations for hires and subcontracts within the owner's limits; a SQLite ledger of job metadata (never inputs or outputs) is kept under plugin-data/emporium/, and each job is a session in the shop profile's Thor history. The shop refuses to open on a profile whose memory, persona or project context files would reach buyers' jobs unless the owner sets allow_unsealed_profile, and `thor emporium init` turns built-in memory off on the shop's own profile (never the main one).

name: enchanted-composer
description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Thor Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from thor-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from thor-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Thor task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Thor agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.

name: engagements
description: Thor is a powerful tool for shipping work to clients, no matter the industry or vertical. Engagements gives it a client notebook: each client and project is a plain Markdown record on your machine. Add a client or project from the Clients page or by pasting notes in any chat, approve the draft, and every agent working for that client can look up who to contact, how they like to work and where the files live. The agent keeps the record current with a dated source for every change. The Clients page works in Thor Desktop and the web dashboard; it shows records but never edits them, and its Add buttons only start the chat that drafts one. Disclosure: local files only, no network requests, no telemetry, no shell commands, no background processes and no stored credentials. Reads and writes Markdown records under the library folder you choose (default is the profile's plugin-data folder), and reads the session's working directory, id and surface to link a chat to a project. Installs PyYAML 6.x.

name: enhance-prompt
description: A sparkle beside Send that rewrites the composer draft in place without sending it, in a voice you pick under Settings > Plugins > enhance-prompt (brief, structured, concise, detailed, questions, verify, or your own words), deepening it into a clarifier, a task list, then a phased plan on further clicks, with a one-click discard back to the original. Also registers the `/enhance` slash command and the `enhance_prompt` tool for the same rewrite from the agent, in the same voice. Draft read and write go through `host.composer`, so `@file` and `/command` chips survive. Disclosure — every click runs one stateless `llm.oneshot` call on your own gateway with the focused chat's model (the plugin's `enhance_prompt` auxiliary task, reasoning off, when no chat is focused), followed by a second short call to score the result, so it spends your model credits. It is not an agent turn: no tools run and nothing is written to a session you cannot see. Only the draft and the chosen voice's instructions are sent; the voice setting is read from your own gateway with `plugins.manage list`. It overrides no model, sends nothing to a third party, never sends the composer message, and carries no telemetry, no credentials and no self-update.

name: enterprise-pathfinder
description: Routes SAP questions to documented sources and reads official references on request. Parses OData metadata, tests contract claims and checks evidence before saving SAP skills. Measured on a 500 KB synthetic OData contract: 52% to 65% fewer tokens across four models (2 to 3 scored runs per model and condition); no accuracy gain is claimed. Disclosure — pre_tool_call checks skill writes and can block tool calls involving plugin data paths or direct SAP skill writes. post_tool_call records skill evidence links and transform_tool_result labels Thor web results and records relevant page reads. pathfinder_read starts HTTPS GET requests at official or standards sources and checks the final URL. Set network to off to disable it. pathfinder_inspect reads any local file path the model names (up to 5 MB) and parses it as OData metadata. Parsed contracts, hashes, lab results, source metadata, skill evidence links and downloaded documents are stored under plugin-data/enterprise-pathfinder. Pathfinder does not read credentials or call SAP systems or APIs.

name: entropicmem
description: Durable local memory for Thor agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 38-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under THOR_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to THOR_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to THOR_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) does it either download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co on first use (optional sentence-transformers extra) or send memory text to a user-set ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL; memory formation is off by default (formation.mode: off) and, when enabled, and for the CLI ingest command's LLM pass, sends conversation or document text to the user's active Thor model through ctx.llm or, outside Thor, to a user-set ENTROPICMEM_LLM_BASE_URL; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML is self-contained: D3 and marked are vendored and inlined at export, so it renders over file:// with no network (only Google Fonts load from fonts.googleapis.com, with a system-font fallback offline); CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_profile (action=patch) edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Thor core, and is off by default.

name: eol
description:
Live end-of-life and support status for 480+ products (languages, OSes, databases, frameworks, cloud services) from endoflife.date, so the agent stops answering support dates from memory. Reads and writes geol (.geol.yaml) stack files.

- eol_search: find a product's identifier from a name, alias, category or tag; list categories and tags
- eol_product: every release cycle with release date, LTS, end of active support, end of life, latest patch, and the product's purl/CPE identifiers
- eol_check: check many components at once, by product+version, purl (e.g. from an SBOM) or CPE, today or at any date: supported / security-only / eol, days left, newer patch, LTS-aware upgrade target, maintained cycles
- eol_stack_check: check a .geol.yaml with geol check --strict rules (skip, manual_eol, lts_strategy, lts_grace_days, always-latest)
- eol_stack_file: generate a .geol.yaml from the components found in a project; the agent writes it with write_file
- pre_llm_call hint: when a message is about versions, upgrades or security fixes (local keyword match), one line is added to that turn pointing the model at the eol_* tools, so it checks instead of answering from memory; off with the context_hint setting
- Complements CVE scanners such as Patch Sentinel: they ask "am I patched?", this asks "is this version still supported by its vendor?"

Disclosures
- Network: HTTPS GET to endoflife.date/api/v1 when a tool is called; only product names are sent (plus fetching the public purl/CPE mapping tables).
- No file access: stack files are passed in and returned as text; writing goes through Thor' write_file and its approvals.
- No credentials, no shell commands, no background processes; 6-hour in-memory cache only.
- The pre_llm_call hook only reads the current user message, matches keywords locally and appends a fixed note; it sends nothing anywhere.
- Stdlib only, no Python dependencies (YAML via Thor' public thor_yaml helper).

name: epistemic-harness
description: Helps a Thor agent record a prediction before a selected check, compare the result, and track revisions in a local case. Disclosure — the optional epistemic_methods tool (off by default; enable with the plugin's jev setting) sends a capped, redacted projection of the active case (top unknown, decision, stopping condition, a few claim and plan texts, recent event types and the candidate methods you supply) to api.typesafe.ai (or the https endpoint you configure) under your TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your TypeSafe credits; once enabled, the plugin requires a consultation before each committed probe and before closing a case.

name: epoch
description: Calibrated time estimates on the Thor Kanban board: when a worker claims a task, Epoch posts a Monte Carlo P50/P90 (plus P80/P95) estimate as a task comment, and when the run completes it records that run's wall-clock hours back to Epoch's ledger (auto_wallclock provenance, sanity-gated) so later estimates calibrate. A Thor Desktop page charts a card's Monte Carlo spread three ways (distribution, chance-done-by curve, 50 dots); it is read-only and never writes the ledger. Dispatcher and worker profiles can differ; the estimate-to-run binding lives next to the ledger, Kanban comments are display only. Also adds an epoch_estimate tool and /epoch. Disclosure — runs `npx -y @kyanitelabs/epoch@0.8.0` as a child process (downloads Epoch and its caret-ranged npm dependencies on first run, which the catalog pin does not cover; needs Node >=22), passing the task title and its three-point hint to the local CLI; the child env is scrubbed (allow-listed PATH/HOME/locale/Node/npm/proxy vars only, the parent environment is never passed through); estimates, actuals and run bindings live under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/epoch/ and are shared by every profile; Epoch telemetry is forced off for plugin runs; no network besides the npm download, no API key; hook work runs on short-lived background threads and unfinished jobs resume when the plugin next loads; the Desktop page reads every Kanban board read-only through Thor' internal kanban modules and runs a forecast in a throwaway data directory when you open a card; /epoch passes other Epoch subcommands through (it refuses serve, self-improve and telemetry/data mutations, and refuses ledger writes on gateway platforms unless opted in).

name: equipdash
description: Run a rental or activity business on EquipDash through EquipDash's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.equipdash.com/mcp/v1, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): the day's pickups, returns and sessions, bookings, availability and prices, customers, items, payments, refunds and unsigned waivers. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, with one skill that has the agent preview every change and wait for the person's yes. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector to app.equipdash.com (no local code): every tool call sends its arguments there and returns the signed-in business's bookings, customer names and contact details and payment records to Thor and its model provider; tools can create, move and cancel bookings, send payment links, issue card refunds and email customers. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so Thor asks before each write-capable call and refuses them in unattended runs; the tool set is served by EquipDash at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. OAuth sign-in requires adding the server to `mcp_servers` in config.yaml (keep `trust: untrusted`) and running `thor mcp login equipdash`.

name: equitylayer
description: Research CPO or custom AI chips with your own AI. Type /equitylayer:start and Thor guides you in four decisions, each with a recommended option: sector (with EquityLayer's theses and live readings shown before anything is asked), how to follow it (EquityLayer's published Research Packs for the sector when there are any, its curated readings, your own thesis, or three questions that help you form one), one card to approve, and how often to check. Saying yes all the way follows EquityLayer's CPO Research Packs: their hypotheses, what would prove each wrong, and the readings each one watches, saved, checked and scheduled; in a sector without a Pack it ends with curated readings. EquityLayer's public MCP (https://equitylayer.io/mcp, no sign-in) supplies the tracked variables with caveats and coverage gaps, official events and due dates; the plugin keeps watchlists, thesis harnesses and baselines in local plugin-data, keeps one tracked object at three levels (readings, the person's own thesis, EquityLayer's thesis) behind nine tools, checks them in one Thor cron job created from the chat, and reports new readings, link statuses (seen, against, late, no data, not due), fired wrong_if conditions, events, what is due next and what needs a person. Nothing becomes the baseline until the person says they read it; unattended runs repeat the alert instead. A local HTML dashboard (built by code from local files and the last public Research Pack registry the plugin fetched; the page has no scripts and makes no network requests) shows it all and is listed under Artifacts in Thor Desktop. Each new chat recalls the person's research profile, watchlists and theses from the local files. Also lists, reads and follows published EquityLayer Research Packs. Disclosure: every tool call goes over HTTPS to equitylayer.io (/mcp, and /mcp/full on the same server for events and due dates; mcp_url accepts only that host or localhost); thesis text, harness, baseline and variable ids are sent as tool arguments and the server reports it stores neither thesis nor harness; no account, key, payment or telemetry; watchlists, harnesses, baselines, a 30-entry check history, Follow Cards, the research profile (fixed-value fields only), a copy of the public Research Pack registry and the dashboard page with its JSON copy and a calendar file of upcoming dates are written under the plugin's own plugin-data directory; a system prompt section (at most 2,000 characters, off with recall_in_new_chats: false) lists the profile and saved ids, titles and last check dates at the start of each new chat and reaches only the user's own model provider; nothing is written to Thor memory; no shell commands or background processes. It never says what to buy, sell, size or time, and never writes a view for the person. Not investment advice.

name: error-ledger
description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Thor could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Thor's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

name: escalation-governor
description: Deterministic stuck-detection for Thor sessions. Watches tool/API failure signals (consecutive tool errors, repeated identical calls, API error bursts, model calls without progress) and, when a threshold trips, injects a structured escalation packet (goal, what was tried, what failed) directing the agent to delegate the remaining work to a stronger model via delegate_task instead of retrying blindly; writes a per-session JSONL report with escalation and token-usage accounting. Disclosure — local code only: injects an escalation packet (the session's first user message and recent tool targets/errors) into tool results and into each following turn's context once a stuck threshold trips, directing the agent to call delegate_task (which spends model usage on a subagent); reads an optional escalation-governor.json and appends one line per session to a shared escalation-governor-reports.jsonl in the Thor home; adds a /governor status command; opens no network connections, starts no processes and never blocks a tool call.

name: eselsbruecke
description: A helper toolbox for Thor with tools you switch on and off: a today pad, a pomodoro, a billable time log, a formatter, a colour picker and small tools, which your agent can call for exact answers. Disclosure — local files only, no credentials, no telemetry. The optional "Alerts while Desktop is closed" switch (off by default) writes `scripts/eselsbruecke_alerts.py` into your Thor profile and adds a no-model Thor job, `eselsbruecke-alerts`, that runs every minute and delivers due timer and reminder alerts to all of the profile's home channels. Desktop clicks that set up that job or make a pad line into a Kanban card run Thor' own CLI for the profile (`thor -p <profile> cron list|create|remove`, `kanban create --json`) as an argument list, without a shell.

name: esimtao
description: Global travel eSIM data usage calculator, phone hardware eSIM compatibility matrix (US eSIM-only vs HK dual physical nano-SIM), and international provider price comparison through EsimTao's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://esimtao.com/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the esimtao workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local runtime code, binaries, hooks, telemetry or self-updater; every tool call goes over HTTPS to esimtao.com/api/mcp with only the travel data or device parameters. All tools are public, free, and annotated read-only (readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false). The package marks the server untrusted (trust: untrusted), so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. The remote tool inventory is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: esp32-debug
description: Read-only ESP32 debugging: find ESP32 boards on serial ports, read chip info, capture a bounded serial log, and decode panic backtraces to function and file:line against a hash-checked ELF. Disclosure — runs esptool (read-only flash-id/chip-id; resets the board, only when the call sets confirm_reset=true) and the Espressif addr2line as subprocesses with a minimal environment and the plugin data dir as working directory; opens the serial port the model names; reads the .elf path the model names and returns a few source lines around each decoded frame from the files that ELF's debug info points to; keeps the last redacted capture in <thor home>/plugin-data/esp32-debug; no network calls.

name: eta
description: Honest finish-time ranges for agent work from real run history: kanban boards and cron jobs read live, delegated subagent runs recorded automatically, 'no honest ETA' when work keeps failing, 'clock starts when...' when a step waits on a person, and labelled rough guesses when history is thin. Disclosure — writes only its own SQLite file in plugin-data/eta (lane, start time, duration, success flag); calls Thor's kanban_list/kanban_show when the kanban toolset is offered (kanban_list promotes dependency-cleared tasks to ready); reads, read-only (SQLite mode=ro), the cron run ledger (cron/executions.db) and, once on first use, Thor's session history (state.db), keeping only each past delegated run's role, start, duration and success (off with read_history: false); reads the time zone and kanban concurrency settings from config.yaml/THOR_TIMEZONE; no network, shell, credentials or background processes.

name: ethics-filter
description: Score any decision across six ethics modules — environmental, fairness, transparency, leadership, framework, compliance — and get GREEN, AMBER or RED back with the reasoning attached. Ships /ethics and the ethics_evaluate tool. Disclosure — reads the rubrics and constitution templates bundled in the plugin and appends one JSONL record per scored evaluation (decision text, context and reasoning included) to $ETHICS_FILTER_AUDIT, default ~/.ethics-filter/audit.jsonl outside the Thor profile and shared by every profile; that file is never rewritten or deleted. With auto_score=true it asks the host agent's own model to score through Thor, holding no separate key; no other network calls.

name: eu-mode
description: EU Mode (beta): HaloGuard EU, Astroware's guard API hosted in the EU, checks each message and each reply (allow or block). EU Mode looks for personal data in what users send and masks what it finds before the request reaches the model, then puts the originals back in the reply, on your machine. Disclosure — on every turn the conversation's user and assistant text (not system prompts, tool results, files or images) goes to api.astroware.ai (or the HALOGUARD_BASE_URL you set) with your own HaloGuard EU key, up to twice per turn (your message, then the reply); fail-open: if the API does not answer, the message goes on unchecked and not masked, and the reply says so; reads two Thor settings (session titles, context compression) only to say when they are on; stores SHA-256 fingerprints of blocked messages, never their text.

name: evalroute
description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Thor model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <THOR_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "thor evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Thor shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run thor -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "thor evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into THOR_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "thor evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query thor chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except THOR_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "thor evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <THOR_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under and, since evalroute 0.10.0, whether the arm was an explore draw and which default arm it replaced (arm ids only). Disclosure — since evalroute 0.10.0, setting evalroute.explore.fraction in config.yaml (or EVALROUTE_EXPLORE) makes that fraction of routes recommend the lane's runner-up arm from the bundled explore table instead of the default arm (and "thor evalroute dispatch" then runs that runner-up model), marked on the route card; off by default. Disclosure — "thor evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <THOR_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "thor evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "thor evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute with its hub extra (evalroute[hub]>=0.10.0,<0.11, which adds huggingface_hub for sync, contribute and install-encoder), declared as a Python dependency that Thor installs on your confirmation.

name: evaluation-ledger
description: Immutable artifact checks and privacy-minimized observer usage ledger. Disclosure — keeps agent-supplied artifact text in a local SQLite file under the profile's plugin-data directory with no automatic deletion. With `observe_usage` turned on (off by default) it also records per-call metadata for every model request and tool call (session and request ids, model, provider, tool name, status, token counts) in the same file; the agent can read that metadata for any session id. Nothing leaves the machine.

name: event-read
description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with thor tools. On Thor 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with thor cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run thor cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host a no-argument list_events still returns the next 7 days and does not record uids. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch reads cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Thor 0.21.6). The printed cron line uses ctx.profile_name. The file write still uses Thor's write guard. An update can stop the watch if that guard moves. These reads do not ask for approval and do not register a hook. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

name: eventforge
description: Proxy the local EventForge control plane into Thor with approval-gated tools and verified-event context. Disclosure — Each turn, adds up to 8 new signature-verified events from the EventForge control plane (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`) to the prompt, as bounded excerpts marked untrusted. `ef_listen_for_webhook` asks the plane to ensure a provider relay, which may open a public tunnel under the plane's own configuration. With `auto_start` on (default off), an interactive session starts the repository's `eventforge-standalone.cjs` with node and a minimal environment when the plane is down. Approving or rejecting actions and forge drafts, and spawning plane subagents, go through Thor' approval prompt.

name: everything-nothing
description: Save reusable templates, create frontend design briefs, and choose how concise Thor replies are.

name: evidence-history
description: Local immutable evidence snapshots with explicit observation and publication cutoffs.

name: evident-evidence
description: Follow real buyer journeys, compare website claims with independent AI answers and suggested competitors, and produce one visual report with highlighted evidence, practical changes and repeatable checks. Disclosure — Opens the websites you ask it to review (and up to three suggested competitor/source pages) in a fresh headless Chromium on this machine and fetches them anonymously; when you enable `allow_model_interpretation`, the captured page text and screenshots are sent to your configured Thor model for several extra calls per report (model cost applies), and reports include an optional link to evident.so (`show_evident_cta`, on by default; nothing is uploaded).

name: evm-token-inspector
description: Inspect any EVM token contract before interacting with it: name, symbol, decimals, total supply, owner/renounced status, EIP-1967 proxy detection, and the DEX V2 pair plus liquidity reserves — one tool, evm_token_check, on BSC, Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum. Read-only; public JSON-RPC only, no API key, no signing, no credentials. Disclosure — read-only: the evm_token_check tool sends the contract address in standard JSON-RPC read calls (via the system curl binary, falling back to Python urllib) to fixed public RPC endpoints (bsc-dataseed.binance.org, bsc.publicnode.com, rpc-bsc.48.club, bsc-dataseed1.ninicoin.io, ethereum.publicnode.com, eth.drpc.org, eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, mainnet.base.org, base.publicnode.com, arb1.arbitrum.io, arbitrum.publicnode.com); no keys, no signing, no transactions. It does not detect honeypots or hidden taxes; it reports on-chain facts (owner, proxy, pair, reserves) for the user to judge, and is not financial advice.

name: exam-desk
description: Practice exams inside Thor Desktop. Add a paper by asking (Thor finds an official paper or drafts one to the same pattern), sit it on a server-side timer in Assisted mode beside the chat or in Mock mode, get it scored per question with negative marking and a section split, and review every miss into a one-click drill paper. Disclosure — papers, attempts and evaluations are stored only in the plugin's own data directory, and a paper's figures are served from there by the plugin's own API (one question's figure at a time, never leaving the gateway). Sourcing uses the agent's web tools and AI review uses the agent's configured model, so both go to whatever services the user already configured. The plugin makes no network calls of its own except that the Desktop page loads any http(s) figure URLs a paper contains straight from those hosts when the paper is opened. It runs no shell commands of its own (its skills have the agent run the bundled pack validator/installer scripts), stores no credentials and has no self-updater. Assisted mode feeds the current question to the chat model during a sitting; the answer key never leaves the server until the attempt is submitted.

name: excel_line
description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

name: exchangerebel
description: Pay-per-call data and utility APIs via a remote MCP server (241 paid operations, $0.002–$50.00 per call, settled in SOL or USDC on Solana via x402) with a bundled workflow skill. Disclosure — connects to the operator's hosted MCP server at exchangerebel.com; its 241 paid tools charge $0.002–$50.00 per call settled in SOL or USDC on Solana via x402 and are declared trust: untrusted so every call asks for approval; the plugin holds no keys, wallet or credentials and pays nothing itself.

name: excubitor
description: Night sentry for Thor turns: one per-turn ledger that dedups inbound replay, stops no-progress tool loops, enforces a spend cap, and alerts when a turn hangs without a reply. Disclosure — default notifier is log-only; optional ntfy.sh or webhook POSTs; one background watch thread; SQLite state in plugin-data/excubitor; no credentials or telemetry; fail-open on internal errors. Optional Desktop status-bar chip (desktop/plugin.js). Limitation — event.internal bypasses gateway hooks.

name: exfilbar
description: Per-file transfer routes for Thor: you list which workspace paths may go to which hosts, and a pre_tool_call hook blocks recognized uploads from terminal and execute_code that leave those routes (curl, wget, scp, rsync, nc, socat, ssh, sftp, mail, HTTPie, git push by opt-in, Python requests/httpx/urllib and more). Protected globs (default private/**, *.env) are never routed. Desktop page shows your routes and an allowed/blocked feed per session; /exfil check explains a dry run. Disclosure: static recognition only, not an egress sandbox; scripts, browser and MCP tools and sibling-hook modifications can bypass it, and unresolved recognized transfers block by default. Stores bounded transfer metadata (paths, scheme and host, decision) and a routes summary in its own plugin data folder; never reads file contents or full commands. No network calls, subprocesses, credentials or telemetry.

name: exoself
description: An unchosen temperament for every Thor profile: on the first load it draws one seed into the profile's home and renders it into SOUL.md inside a managed block, then records one experience event per turn and refreshes that block. Two profiles get two different agents, a second load never redraws, and no tool draws a seed. Disclosure — writes $THOR_HOME/SOUL.md (its own managed block only) and $THOR_HOME/.exoself/, and reads the turn's ask from pre_llm_call in memory to form the event line, which is hashed into the state chain and never stored as text. No network calls, credentials, subprocesses or telemetry; uninstalling leaves the certificate and the block in place.

name: expatslist
description: Read-only ExpatsList MCP server and skill: city guides from local business listings, questions and answers, classifieds and country reference tables (nomad visas, cost of living, healthcare, tax, safety, tipping). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to the public read-only MCP server at expatslist.org (https://expatslist.org/api/mcp), which only reads published site content (community-written listings, questions, classifieds and indicative country tables); no sign-in, no key, nothing written, no local commands. The package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: explainer
description: Turn any link, PDF, notes or topic into a narrated explainer video (MP4): themed slides, a neural voice, bullets revealed the moment they are spoken, word-by-word highlighted captions, title card and progress bar, in 16:9 or 9:16 for Shorts/Reels, plus SRT captions, transcript and thumbnail. Includes an explainer-video skill and a weekly recap-video blueprint. Narration text is sent to Microsoft's online Edge text-to-speech service via edge-tts (no account or key); scene images given as https URLs are downloaded only from public addresses (redirects checked) and local images only from allowed folders; ffmpeg runs locally to encode. Videos stay local. No telemetry. Disclosure — narration text is sent to Microsoft's online Edge text-to-speech service (edge-tts, no account); scene images given as https URLs are downloaded from public addresses only (every redirect re-checked), and local scene images are read from the Thor working directory, the plugin's data folder or folders you add in `image_dirs`.

name: factkit
description: Semantic recall for the built-in holographic memory provider. It reads the provider's store read-only and keeps its own embedding vectors in a separate plugin database (never writing into holographic's tables), adding an embedding-based recall block before each model call, history-aware dedupe so a fact already shown in the conversation is not injected twice, and embedding re-ranking of fact_store search results. Writes are never automatic: conflict, duplicate and TTL actions stay explicit review/apply operations. No core files are patched and the plugin never self-updates.
