Disclosure - the current user message and the stored fact text are sent to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint configured in the plugin's config (default http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1); point it at a remote host only if you accept that. The endpoint key is read through Thor' secret scope, never written to the process environment. Disclosure — the current user message and stored fact text are sent to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint set in the plugin's config (default http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1); point it at a remote host only if you accept that. The endpoint key is read through Thor' secret scope and is never written to the process environment.

name: factledger
description: A typed-facts ledger with structural truth — the agent records durable facts (prices, statuses, limits, decisions, capabilities) once and search/show them whenever they matter. For every (scope, subject, predicate) exactly one row is active; a new value closes the previous one (valid_to + superseded_by) instead of overwriting it, so contradictory versions never coexist and history is the audit trail. The full ledger stays queryable on demand, separate from the character-budgeted memory view that is injected every turn. Tools: add, show, search, history, compile, stale, export, check, stats. Local-first TSV store, stdlib only, no network, no credentials. Disclosure — none: no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no credential access; every tool reads or writes only the local ledger file.

name: fail-shrink
description: When a pytest, jest, vitest, cargo test, go test, tsc, ruff, or eslint summary line shows, the result is a short block with that place and the same exit code. No summary line, or a poll with only output_preview, stays as Thor returned it. Disclosure — rewrites long failing pytest/jest/vitest/cargo/go test/tsc/ruff/eslint terminal output into a short block and saves the full (ANSI-stripped, redacted) log under plugin-data/fail-shrink, keeping the newest 40 logs (32 MB) until the plugin data is deleted; the fail_full tool reads those saved logs only, makes no network calls and runs nothing, and is enabled on every platform, so anyone who can message the agent can ask it to read them.

name: fashio
description: E-commerce fashion photos from Fashio through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.fashiolabs.com/mcp): garment on an AI model, virtual try-on, catalog photoshoot packs, jewelry on model, flat lays, background removal, upscaling, reframing and short product videos, plus reusable style presets. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call, with its arguments and image URLs, goes to mcp.fashiolabs.com, which calls api.fashiolabs.com and needs a Fashio account with its API key in FASHIO_API_KEY. create_generation and create_catalog_job spend the account's credits (no test mode; failed jobs are refunded) and delete_template_set deletes a saved preset; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: fashion-design
description: Fashion design toolkit for drafting ideas, tech packs, size sheets, and manufacturing prep

name: fast-chat
description: One-command Fast startup for Thor CLI/TUI until built-in startup gets easier. Disclosure — `thor fast-chat` runs the Thor executable (or the one given with --thor-bin) without a shell to bootstrap the gateway and may start a long-running gateway that keeps running after it exits; on Thor releases without `gateway attach` it obtains a single-use session ticket over the local same-user gateway control socket; it reads the active profile's model, fallback-route and display settings from config.yaml (never inline keys) and, when no --model is given, tries the configured fallback routes until one accepts Fast, so the session can open on a different provider/model; sessions it creates (including empty ones left by refused routes) use the Fast/ultrafast service tier, which can cost more with the provider; no telemetry, no credential reads.

name: fatetell
description: BaZi (Four Pillars) charts, the Chinese almanac and the charts saved in a FateTell account, computed by FateTell's hosted MCP server, plus a skill on reading the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — hosted MCP server at https://mcp.fatetell.com/mcp (remote tool list not covered by the pin); the server calls no language model; cast_bazi_chart and get_almanac work without an account and send a birth date and time, IANA time zone, gender, hemisphere and optional longitude (no place name); the other seven tools need a FateTell account (four of them an active membership) and Thor native MCP OAuth (`mcp_servers.fatetell` on https://mcp.fatetell.com/login/mcp with `auth: oauth`, then `thor mcp login fatetell`; through the bundled mcp.json alone those tools answer 401), authorization server https://auth.fatetell.com, Thor stores the OAuth tokens; create_saved_chart is the only write tool: it adds a chart to the user's account from a display name, gender, birth date and time and a birthplace name, and cannot edit or delete charts; the package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before that call; birth data, saved charts and account details returned by the tools reach the model provider.

name: faultline
description: Local API flight recorder for debugging HTTP services with Thor. The agent starts a loopback reverse proxy in front of your service, captures every request and response (auth headers and secret JSON fields redacted before storage), learns an OpenAPI 3.1 contract from healthy traffic and flags drift (type changes, missing fields, 5xx, latency regressions), injects chaos faults (429/5xx, latency, truncated JSON), and after a fix replays the exact failing request to prove 500 -> 200. Ships six tools, a tool_execution middleware, /faultline and `thor faultline` commands, a bundled skill, a Faultline tab in the web dashboard, and a Thor Desktop studio page, waterfall pane, status chip and inline ::faultline-trace card. Disclosure — the proxy listens on 127.0.0.1 only and forwards to the target_url you give it (normally local; any http(s) host is accepted except literal link-local, cloud-metadata and reserved addresses and the cloud-metadata hostnames, and the URL may not carry a query, fragment or credentials); replay re-sends captured requests to the upstream they were recorded from only (the agent cannot choose another host), resolves it first and refuses link-local and cloud-metadata addresses, reaches loopback/private targets only when the owner enables the allow_local_replay setting (off by default), and replaying a POST repeats its side effects; captured traffic, contracts and chaos rules are stored in SQLite under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/faultline/; each running proxy is a daemon thread in the Thor process; no telemetry, no other network calls, no credentials read, no shell commands, no Python dependencies.

name: faxforagents
description: Fax preparation, quotes, approved sending, delivery status, cancellation, and inbox reading. The portable package starts faxforagents-mcp 0.4.1 through npx and sends data to api.faxforagents.com. MCP also exposes guidance, capabilities, balance, document previews, review requests, and billed extraction. Write-capable calls use the Thor untrusted gate. Live sends require quote-bound approval or an allowing delegated policy and spend wallet funds. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned faxforagents-mcp 0.4.1 from npm through npx and runs it as a local child process with only FAXFORAGENTS_API_KEY from your profile; it sends the documents, destination numbers and fax requests you or the agent give it to Fax for Agents' API (api.faxforagents.com) and reads received faxes and their extracted text from it. The server is marked untrusted, so every write-capable call asks first; live sends and paid extraction spend your prepaid wallet, and a delegated policy you set in the Fax for Agents dashboard lets a live send go out without its quote-bound human approval. The tool list comes from the npm package, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. The README's optional workaround for a Thor OAuth login stall edits a core file (tools/mcp_oauth.py) by hand.

name: feishu-new-topic
description: Feishu/Lark only: a message starting with `#new ` (or the spoken phrase 开启一个新话题) opens a new Feishu topic on that message, which Thor turns into a new session — a second lane, while the session that was already running keeps running with its turn untouched. That is the difference from `/new`, which interrupts the running turn and clears the conversation. Inside a topic the trigger is stripped, because Feishu topics do not nest; if topic creation fails the message is dispatched normally with a note. Disclosure — Feishu/Lark only. Hooks `pre_gateway_dispatch` (runs before gateway auth) and checks the sender itself with the gateway's authorization probe; unauthorised senders, in-topic messages and cached duplicates cause no calls. For an authorised `#new` message it makes two Feishu OpenAPI calls through the receiving bot's own client (messages/{id}/reply with reply_in_thread, retried up to three times, then messages/{id}/delete of the one-character placeholder), sets the message's thread id so Thor routes it to a new session, and strips the trigger from the text. Reaches gateway/adapter internals (`_is_user_authorized_for_source`, `_delivery_adapter_for`, the Feishu adapter's `_client` and `_run_blocking`), so a core refactor can stop topic creation (the message is then dispatched normally with a note). Keeps a 40-entry message-id → thread-id dedupe map in plugin state. Appended notes are Chinese-only. Requires plugins.isolation: in_process.

name: field-academy
description: The School of Thor. Thor will sometimes tell you it saved something when it didn't, and Field Academy teaches you to catch that. In Foundations you work through 11 missions in a throwaway copy of Thor with one thing quietly broken: you do a real job, say how you think it went, then look at what Thor actually wrote to its files. After that come 34 missions on five trails in your own Thor, each trail ending with a Field Record of your work. New in 0.9: Foundations and the trail map. Independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Thor Labs. Disclosure — no network calls of its own and no telemetry; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill. It creates and deletes practice profiles (named academy-practice) through Thor, which copies your provider sign-in into each; Field Academy never reads .env, auth.json or other sign-in files. Before a practice profile's first chat it writes allowlisted settings, memory, a sample skill and sample files into that profile only, and may turn on its memory or skill write-approval setting; it never changes approvals.* or the command allowlist, and never writes your own profiles. Some missions add a filesystem connector (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, pinned) that Thor downloads with npx, and scheduled practice jobs that, once repaired, run hourly on your model provider until you pause them. AI help (on by default) sends mission text, your answers and key-scrubbed practice excerpts to your own model; the in-chat practice offer (pre_llm_call, interactive sessions only) is off until you turn it on. It reads a file you name (UTF-8, max 5 MiB); on the Guide path it reads Thor's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files; progress, practice labs and Field Records stay in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/.

name: field-from-above
description: Free Sentinel-2 NDRE and terrain context for a Polish parcel or any point via GUGiK ULDK/NMT and Earth Search STAC. Disclosure — requested parcel IDs or coordinates (as bounding boxes) are sent to uldk.gugik.gov.pl, earth-search.aws.element84.com and services.gugik.gov.pl, and Sentinel-2 band files (up to 400 MB each, several per new scene) are downloaded from sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com into a raster cache capped at 2 GB under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/field-from-above, where the PNG maps are also written; no credentials, shell commands or background processes are used.

name: fieldkit
description: Offline observation forms for Thor. Describe your work in a Thor chat and Thor drafts the forms, then publishes them as a workspace after you approve. Fill them in on a phone with no signal (installable PWA served by the Thor dashboard: answers, photos, voice notes, GPS and signatures), and sync entries and files back to Thor when online, with duplicate protection and conflict review. Thor reads the synced entries and files through 12 tools and analyses them with its own tools when asked. FieldKit never calls a model. name: file-tray

name: finder

Desktop only; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: fine-print
description: Shows where Thor silently shrinks, cuts, swaps or hides what the model sees. When a turn ends in which a limit bit and no follow-up by the model was seen, the user gets one card with before/after numbers and the fix (a `thor config set` command, a workaround, or "hardcoded in v0.23.0"): a web page cut to head and tail, an image downscaled 4x or more, a search page that stopped at 50 with no "more" flag, a failed search backend swapped for the keyless tier, a file read whose lines were all cut at 2,000 chars, terminal output of which under half was kept, a tool result replaced by a 1,500-char preview, a context compaction, loaded images that the request no longer carries, an attached image that reached the model as a helper model's description, a pinned context window that is not in force, a sixth URL that web_extract never requested, a workbook read up to row 5,000 with its hidden sheet skipped. The model gets one short note inside the tool result only where Thor itself tells nobody. `/limits` shows the session's hits, explains 81 catalogued limits of v0.23.0 (`/limits explain <id>`), replays the same detectors and card policy over your own history (`/limits report`, or `/limits report html` for one self-contained page) and lists every detector with its status (`/limits self-test`): 16 are verified (on real history, or in a live session for limits that leave no stored row) and may raise cards, 19 are fixture-only and only log. Disclosure — no LLM calls, no network, no Python dependencies, no tools, no middleware. Reads tool results in memory through hooks (failed calls included) and, by structure and size only, each request's message lists and the user message of a turn (image parts, Thor's own placeholder and image notes); keeps a metadata-only ledger (sizes, counts, a URL host or file basename, hashes) in its plugin-data directory. Adds one `_fine_print` key or first line to a tool result for limits where core tells nobody (never on failed calls, images, write_file, patch or skill_manage; `/limits notes off`), and a section of under 1,000 chars to the system prompt of new sessions (`/limits sheet off`). Reads outside its own data, read-only: the profile's session database for `/limits report` (aggregates only; the FINE_PRINT_STATE_DB variable can name another copy), the .xlsx/.docx file that read_file just extracted (to count rows, sheets and tables), and the Thor config. Writes one file only when asked (`/limits report html`, into the profile's cache folder). Posts one notice per turn into the chat in the CLI and the TUI (in Desktop 0.23.0 the notice call was refused in my check; there the hits are listed by `/limits`); off on messaging platforms by default.

name: firecrawl-plugin
description: Search, scrape, crawl, map, interact, monitor and research through Firecrawl's hosted MCP server at /v2/mcp-oauth, with Firecrawl skills (get-started, routing, deep research and 16 workflow skills). The packaged connection uses FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, the same key as the bundled backend; Thor-managed OAuth on the same endpoint works through a native MCP entry. Disclosure — Connects to Firecrawl's hosted MCP server at `mcp.firecrawl.dev` and sends it the queries, URLs, prompts and files the agent asks Firecrawl to process, authenticated with `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` or a Thor-managed Firecrawl OAuth sign-in; calls use Firecrawl account credits.

name: fiscalisto

Bundles an English overview skill and thirteen Spanish workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure: every tool call goes to fiscalisto.com and acts on the companies the user approved, with their own role; stamping registers a CFDI with the SAT through Fiscalisto's PAC and uses a stamp from the user's plan, and the server refuses a stamp or cancellation without a confirmation token from a preview. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in opens a local callback port and stores OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. No telemetry. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: fish-audio
description: Your agent speaks and listens with Fish Audio: expressive voices in 80+ languages, voices you design from a sentence, and live word-by-word dictation. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Thor Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Thor speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop and word-by-word live dictation captions (stt.streaming: true); streaming and live dictation need Thor 0.21.6 or newer, and on 0.21.5 replies use whole-file speech and dictation is transcribed as a file. Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices, fish_transcribe, fish_settings, fish_account and fish_pronunciations tools, /fish and thor fish commands (including /fish setup, a checklist that ends by offering a spoken sample with /fish preview), and six skills. Also: voice auditions (up to four voices reading your passage), replies as a voice note or an audio file, long-form chapter narration with a resumable manifest, translate-and-voice for clips with several speakers, saved voice names in any script, editing your own voices on Desktop, and thor fish speak, transcribe, voices and balance with --json for scripts. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to Fish's native realtime speech-to-text at api.fish.audio (transcribe-stream-1, Preview) while you speak, billed $0.36 per hour of open session, per second, including silence; a session opens with the first audio and closes once Fish confirms the last words (the plugin stops waiting after 15 seconds), or 30 seconds after the last audio of a cancelled recording; if a live session fails or returns no text, Thor transcribes the recording as a file instead, a separate billed request; the live_transcription: compat setting uses Fish's older realtime endpoint instead, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models; when no model is set and your Fish wallet shows no API credit, free credit or past top-up, the plugin uses that free model (allow_free_model: false turns this off). The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Thor stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Thor's audio cache; clone samples, cover images and recordings it uploads must be regular audio or image files, and Thor config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Thor's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Thor dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Thor's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page, the /fish and thor fish commands and the fish_settings tool can set or reset the profile's Fish model, voice and reading speed and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config, so the agent can choose its own voice under the same rules; fish_pronunciations sends the pronunciation dictionary names, descriptions and rules you ask for to api.fish.audio (dictionary management is free; speech that uses a dictionary is billed as usual), can store up to three dictionary references as the profile's default in its config, and deleting a dictionary or a version goes through Thor's approval gate; /fish setup lists what the profile still needs without a Fish call and reads the key only through the secret scope; auditions are one billed clip per voice; the Desktop editor sends the title and description you type for your own voice to api.fish.audio; thor fish speak --out copies the audio and subtitles to the path you give and refuses to overwrite a file unless you pass --force; fish_speak output_path copies them to a path the agent gives, never overwrites a file, and refuses paths Thor's write guard protects; on operator-managed agents a cloned or saved voice gets a saved name in the profile config automatically; the long-form skill saves chapter files and a manifest in the folder you choose, with the agent's own file tools; /fish preview with no voice plays a short billed sample in the profile's voice; fish_account reads the Fish wallet like /fish balance and estimates costs from a dated price table without a network call; /fish use and thor fish use also make Fish the speech provider when none is set, and given a voice title they search your own Fish voices for it, and thor fish login sets the speech and transcription providers when they are unset or you confirm. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. When you ask for a voice that fits the agent, the voice-studio skill reads the agent's SOUL.md or persona and sends Fish a one- or two-sentence voice description, never the whole persona. Includes a report-a-problem skill: when you report a problem with Fish Audio, the agent runs thor fish doctor --no-synth, /fish status, thor --version and thor plugins list --json, reads recent Thor log lines that mention Fish, searches this plugin's GitHub issues for a few key words, drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and voice ids not confirmed as public library voices, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.

name: fitbit-mcp
description: Read the user's Fitbit activity, heart rate, sleep and body data through the local fitbit MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Fitbit. Runs the `fitbit-mcp-unofficial@0.7.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official Fitbit Web API. The user creates their own Fitbit developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.fitbit-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to Fitbit's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Thor credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.thor/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.thor/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: fitbit_profile_update (local profile only); fitbit_exchange_code (stores OAuth tokens locally); fitbit_revoke_access (revokes the Fitbit grant and deletes local tokens). The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

name: fivedive
description: 5dive app chat for Thor: talk to your Thor agent from the 5dive web and mobile app (text, voice notes, files). Disclosure — local spool folder only (0700, the agent's own user); reads the upload files the 5dive bridge names in a message; no network calls, no listener, no shell commands, no stored credentials.

name: fixmyscan
description: Turn scanned books (PDF or DjVu, up to 1,000 pages) into clean, searchable PDFs for Kindle, Kobo, reMarkable and tablets through FixMyScan's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.fixmyscan.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE, no keys in config): crop pages to the text, straighten them, make them sharp black and white or greyscale, split two-page spreads and add a searchable text layer, then return a download link. Write-capable tools: fix_scan and create_upload_link (start a book), cancel_scan and delete_scan (stop or delete one of the user's books). Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. The package marks the server untrusted. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add fixmyscan --url https://mcp.fixmyscan.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401 on tool calls.

name: flashdata-plugin
description: Web search with Google Search; Google News, Google Images, Google Shopping, Google Video Search and Google Places for research. Use YouTube Search or YouTube Extended Search; retrieve YouTube metadata, YouTube transcripts, YouTube captions and YouTube channel data; get YouTube autocomplete; inspect YouTube trainability as license-label metadata, not training permission. YouTube downloads deliver media to your own storage. One hosted MCP connection and 15 task Skills; bring your own API key and paid FlashData Credits. Disclosure — Connects to FlashData's hosted MCP service (data.flashdata.dev) with your own FLASHDATA_API_KEY; every search, YouTube read or download spends your paid FlashData Credits, and Thor asks before running only the tools the server does not mark read-only, so most paid searches run without a prompt. The YouTube download tool sends the storage bucket and storage access credentials you supply to FlashData, and those values stay visible in the chat history.

name: fledge
description: Skills have to earn their wings. Before Thor saves or rewrites a skill, Fledge checks what actually happened in the run it learned from (tools still failing when the turn ended, a failed or interrupted turn, the user correcting the agent in the next message, /undo or a /rollback restore right after, denied approvals), using only facts Thor reports through hooks: no model grades the model. A save learned from a bad run is held in Thor' own skills pending queue with the reasons (review from any chat with /fledge pending|diff|approve|reject, or /skills pending in the CLI); a foreground save after errors goes through Thor' approval prompt, and unattended runs queue instead of waiting. New and rewritten skills start on probation: clean real runs graduate them, repeated bad runs ground them, and a save from a run the user corrected right after is grounded at once; a grounded skill Thor created on its own is archived (thor curator restore brings it back), skills the user asked for are only reported. Skills the user edited by hand are fingerprinted, and autonomous rewrites or deletes of them become proposals in the same queue (optionally Thor' content lock). Modes: enforce, watch (records only), off. Disclosure — nine hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_session_end, on_session_finalize, on_session_reset, on_skill_lifecycle, pre_command, post_approval_response); pre_tool_call blocks or asks for approval on skill_manage only and lets the write through on its own errors (a write already queued for review stays held); reads hook payloads (tool statuses and error text, the first 280 characters of the next user message) and skill folders to fingerprint them; writes its own SQLite under each profile's plugin-data/fledge (skill names, fingerprints, verdict reasons, session/turn ids; reasons quote the matched correction phrase and up to 80 characters of a tool error, hold summaries the skill's one-line description; no other message text, no skill bodies), held writes into pending/skills/, and archives grounded agent-created skills into skills/.archive/; calls tools.skill_provenance, tools.write_approval and tools.skill_usage (the functions behind /skills pending and thor curator archive/lock) because no public seam exists yet, each guarded; no network, no model calls, no credentials, no shell commands, never approves anything. Needs plugins.isolation in_process to tell background-review writes from foreground ones. Measured on 2026-11-10: 153 tests passed on Python 3.14 and 3.11; `thor plugins validate` passes on Thor 0.23.1, 0.23.0 and 0.22.7 with only the private-import warnings above; live sessions with a real model in isolated THOR_HOMEs (bad-run hold, approve onto probation, grounding after a correction, hand-edit proposal and approval prompt, watch mode, 13 clean writes with 0 holds, fail-open under a locked database) in VALIDATION.md, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt and tests/profiles-2026-11-10.txt.

name: fledly
description: iOS App Store market data in Thor: young apps that already earn, app ideas scored from market data, top charts, App Store keyword research, keyword field checks, and daily rank and competitor tracking through Fledly's hosted MCP server (https://fledly.app/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the fledly workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Fledly's hosted server (fledly.app) and acts on the user's own Fledly account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. track_app, track_keywords, untrack_keyword, track_competitor, untrack_competitor and save_idea change the user's tracked apps, searches, competitors and saved ideas; every other tool only reads, and nothing spends money. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. No telemetry.

name: fleet-policy
description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`thor fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks). Disclosure — records only model, reasoning effort and service tier per role (no message content, headers or keys) via the pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call hooks and a pass-through llm_execution middleware, stored in $THOR_HOME/fleet-policy/observed.json; crons --cost opens cron/executions.db and state.db read-only and checks each cron run's final reply locally for silence; watch is an operator CLI command that calls one MCP tool at the config's server_url (or the admin-pinned watch_server_url) with config headers in which ${VAR} env values are expanded, follows redirects, and writes seen ids to a state file at the config-chosen path; the recurring-tasks skill has the agent write watch configs under $THOR_HOME/watches, a script under $THOR_HOME/scripts and a cron job; no other network access, no telemetry.

name: fleetkeep-agent-plugin
description: Review a supplied vehicle CSV for missing and ambiguous Fleetkeep import values. Agent Plugins v1 package with one local skill; it does not connect to Fleetkeep or change an account. Disclosure: the skill reads only material the user supplies to Thor; no plugin code, install scripts, network calls, credentials, background processes or telemetry. Material supplied to Thor remains subject to the user's Thor and model-service settings.

name: flightdeck
description: Live air-traffic control for your agents and model servers — which agent holds which local GPU slot, who's queued, plan usage on cloud lanes, and opt-in capacity-aware subagent placement. Disclosure — records LLM request metadata (ids, profile, session, model, provider, base_url, timings, token counts, finish/error status, a clipped error message and a subagent's goal text; no prompts, message text, tool arguments or credentials) from every profile into one machine-wide SQLite file at <thor root>/plugin-data/flightdeck/requests.db; reads every profile's config.yaml (provider base URLs, model names and its own settings only; the files can contain api_key values, which it never extracts, stores or sends) and every profile's state.db (session titles, read-only); sends GET-only metrics probes to declared model servers or to auto-discovered private/loopback provider URLs on each poll; the Desktop page reads plan usage through Thor's model.options RPC; opt-in capacity routing (off by default) changes which local server delegate_task subagents run on.

name: flightlog
description: Flight recorder for Thor. Records every tool call, model call, subagent and approval to local SQLite and flags runs that finish green but went wrong: tool errors the answer hides, loops, token spikes and effort collapse against each cron job's own baseline, failed subagents behind a "done", and "tests pass" claims with no passing check after the last edit. Flagged runs get a short incident report, a footer on the reply, per-step timelines in the CLI, dashboard tab and desktop page, and an opt-in loop tripwire that hands the 5th repeat to Thor's own approval prompt. Disclosure — local only: no network calls, subprocesses or background services beyond one in-process SQLite writer thread; stores short redacted previews of every tool call's arguments and result in $THOR_HOME/flightlog/flightlog.db (pruned after 30 days); flagged runs' redacted evidence goes to your configured model via ctx.llm for the incident report; appends a footer to agent replies when a run is flagged, and by default (break_silence) makes a flagged [SILENT] cron job post that note instead of staying silent; the opt-in loop tripwire registers a pre_tool_call hook that sends the 5th identical call to Thor's approval prompt.

name: flipletters
description: Split-flap and flip-dot board design through FlipLetters' remote MCP (https://app.flipletters.com/mcp/v1): FlipCode reference, validate boards, render videos, share. Portable Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to app.flipletters.com and needs a FlipLetters account (flk_ API key in FLIPLETTERS_API_KEY, sent as a Bearer header). Render tools spend the account's export quota, and share tools post into team libraries or schedule and publish to the user's connected social channels through Postiz; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before write-capable tools and refuses them in unattended runs. The live tool set is served by the remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: flota
description: Run delegate_task subagents on your own machines over SSH (delegation.backend: flota). Flota wakes the chosen machine (Wake-on-LAN, a relay host on its LAN, any command, or the machine's own wake timer), falls back to another machine if it does not come up, and suspends it after its last subagent, never a busy one (the model cannot force it). The agent tool checks and wakes machines; asking it to suspend or power one off is opt-in and every such call goes through Thor' approval prompt. `thor flota setup user@host` detects OS, MAC, broadcast and how the machine can sleep; `doctor` prints fixes; `uninstall` undoes it; fleet pairing with two codes (public keys only); a fleet map page for Thor Desktop and the web dashboard. Python standard library only. Disclosure — runs ssh to the machines you configure and your own wake/sleep commands, sends Wake-on-LAN packets on your LAN, can run `sudo -n` for one fixed wake-alarm command only if you allow it, creates an SSH key pair without a passphrase (`~/.ssh/flota_ed25519`) when you have none and adds that public key to a ship's `authorized_keys` at pairing as an ordinary login line with no `command=` or `restrict` options, creates `flota-<machine>` Thor profiles with `terminal.ssh_sync_files: false`, lets the agent suspend or power off a machine only if you turn on `agent_power_actions` and approve each call, and keeps auto-sleep timers in the gateway process; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.

name: flowcanvas
description: Visual workflow canvas for Thor Desktop: wire Thor tools, MCP tools and LLM calls into typed graphs with conditions, bounded loops, JSON/list transforms, per-step caching and media previews (image, audio, video and an in-place 3D model viewer). Build with Thor edits a graph from a description; seven agent tools and /flow list, build, run and inspect the same saved flows; twelve starter templates and user-saved templates. Disclosure — tool nodes execute through ctx.dispatch_tool on a background thread with Thor' own tools, credentials and approvals (commands held for manual approval are denied or time out on the canvas and under cron), and other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks do not see these calls; shell, file-writing, browser, session-mutating and known code-running MCP tools are blocked by name by default, an explicit allow_tools setting can unblock them, and other MCP tools are not blocked; provider, LLM and media-generation calls can cost money, and Build with Thor sends the prompt, node catalog and current flow to the active model before any run; a File node reads only files the user dropped (copied into the plugin's uploads folder) or picked with Browse… for that node, any agent edit or flow_run input drops the pick, and those files and media under Thor' folders can be passed to the tools they are wired to, possibly to remote providers as data URLs; Thor credential stores and .env files are never read; media URLs in tool output are downloaded with Thor' SSRF-safe client (every redirect hop checked, 200 MB cap); user regexes in If/Switch run in an isolated Python subprocess killed after 0.5 s; the Send message node uses Thor' official messaging bridge only after a per-recipient consent bound to flow, node and target plus a separate file consent, never caches or retries, and reports timeouts as unconfirmed; a local HMAC key (messaging-secret) signs that consent and the file picks; flows, runs, uploads and cache live under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/flowcanvas/; the Desktop UI uses only @thor/plugin-sdk; no stored provider credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: flower-shop
description: An AI business operating workspace inside Thor Desktop for a small flower shop: a business manager plus sales, inventory, production, finance, and logistics agents work from one SQLite record of orders, stock, production, deliveries, and money. Agents propose, the owner approves - order confirmation, stock receipts, adjustments, wastage, payments, and expenses create a pending approval decided by the owner from an inline chat card or the Approvals inbox (an opt-in chat relay, off by default, still confirmed through Thor' approval prompt). Includes Overview, Orders, Inventory and recipes, Production board, a read-only low-poly 3D Shop Floor fed by live production state, Delivery, Finance estimates labelled as estimates, an AI Team page, and a guided setup with removable demo data. The repo also ships an optional matching Thor skin (a light and a dark variant) that the setup offers but never applies on its own. Not flower-specific: the same shape - one record of what was ordered, stocked, made, shipped and paid, agents that propose, an owner who approves - fits any small physical business. Disclosure - all business data stays in one local SQLite database under the Thor plugin-data directory; the plugin makes no network calls, stores no credentials, runs no shell commands, and sends no telemetry. Not an accounting ledger: finance figures are operational estimates plus recorded payments and expenses. Single shop, single user; no WhatsApp parsing, no bouquet canvas, no multi-branch support. Disclosure — all business data stays in one local SQLite database under the Thor plugin-data directory; the plugin makes no network calls, stores no credentials, runs no shell commands and sends no telemetry; choosing its theme copies two bundled skin files into the Thor skins directory and reads the active skin setting, and the skin switches only when the owner clicks; assistant profiles are created only when the owner clicks Create on the Desktop team step; design references must be image files in the plugin's uploads folder, which the local dashboard serves; approving from chat is off by default and, when turned on, every decision still goes through Thor' approval prompt. Finance figures are operational estimates plus recorded payments and expenses, not an accounting ledger; single shop, single user.

name: flowlight
description: Watch public wallets and draw live on-chain money flows as glowing arcs. Read-only. Uses public NEAR, Blockscout, and RPC endpoints. When Intents Pay is installed, reads its invoice ledger and may GET 1-Click /v0/status. Never signs or sends transactions and never handles keys. Disclosure — sends the wallet addresses you watch to public third-party APIs (Blockscout, nearblocks.io, public EVM and Solana RPC nodes, CoinGecko) and, when Intents Pay is installed, reads its invoice ledger and queries 1-Click status for its deposit addresses; `thor flowlight serve` opens an unauthenticated loopback page on 127.0.0.1.

name: flowsery
description: Privacy-first web analytics through Flowsery's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.flowsery.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): visitors, sessions, bounce rate, time series, real-time visitors, breakdowns by page, referrer, channel, campaign, country and device, goals and revenue attribution, single visitor journeys, and the bugs and UX problems Flowsery found in session recordings. Bundles the flowsery workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Flowsery's hosted server (mcp.flowsery.com) and acts on the user's Flowsery account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Most tools are read-only; track_goal and track_payment record goal and payment events in the user's analytics (no money moves), delete_goals and delete_payments permanently remove those events, and update_issue_status changes an issue. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: fluent
description: Your agent becomes fluent in any program: checks the agent's terminal commands against the real --help and man pages of the programs you adopt, before they run. A long option the installed version doesn't have is stopped with the closest real one (--crf → -crf, --ammend → --amend), and subcommands it classifies as destructive (gh repo delete, docker image prune, rsync --delete) go to Thor's own approval prompt. Adds /fluent (adopt, show, forget, undo, mode), an @cli:<program> context reference and a dashboard tab that draws the agent's tree (a branch per program, a fruit per error caught). Tested on 333 real valid commands (0 blocked) and 22 typical mistakes (22 caught), including the tar macOS ships. Disclosure — /fluent adopt <program> runs that program on the host (not the terminal backend) with --version/-version/version/-V and --help/-h/help, plus <command> --help per subcommand only when the help carries a git, Go/cobra, argparse or click marker (git: --list-cmds and <command> -h; ffmpeg: -h full; curl: --help all; git filter-branch is never run): no shell, closed stdin, empty temp cwd, own process group, filtered environment (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, TMPDIR, XDG dirs; no keys or tokens), 5 s per call, about 25 s per program; a program that ignores those arguments runs normally. It reads man pages and terminal.backend from config.yaml; in block mode (default) pre_tool_call vetoes commands with options the installed program lacks and escalates destructive ones to Thor's approval prompt with a per-subcommand rule key, never approving anything (unattended runs follow Thor policy, default deny); posts one-line notices; writes only under its plugin data directory; makes no network, model or telemetry calls.

name: fluxer-platform
description: Fluxer messaging with reliable replies, attachments, rich cards, read-only guild tools, and opt-in threads and experimental voice. Connects to Fluxer and configured speech services; optional voice runs background Python processes and reads configured local context and session data. Disclosure — Reads Thor's own session store (state.db, read-only) to name Fluxer threads after session titles; its four model tools read Fluxer channel messages, search results, guild members and the guild audit log through the configured Fluxer API (api.fluxer.app or FLUXER_BASE_URL), limited to the home guild unless FLUXER_TOOL_SCOPE=global. Optional voice (off by default) runs background Python processes, reads a configured context file and session database, runs a user-configured local speech-to-text command through the shell, and sends voice audio and reply text to the speech services you configure: api.x.ai, api.groq.com, api.elevenlabs.io, or a Kokoro endpoint you set (FLUXER_VOICE_KOKORO_URL).

name: fmsg-platform
description: fmsg platform adapter for Thor Agent. Real-time inbound over the fmsg-webapi WebSocket (/fmsg/ws), outbound via its JSON REST routes. Authenticates with an fmsg API key (fmsgk_...) exchanged for a short-lived JWT — run the agent as a derived sub-account such as @alice_thor@example.com. Only http

name: followthrough
description: Capture and track user-selected commitments with owners, due dates, and source references.

name: followup-chips
description: Clickable follow-up question chips under assistant replies. One click sends the question as the next turn; Thor arc-border hover; the choice persists per block across reload. Single-file desktop plugin, no native components.

name: foreman
description: A green check the agent did not rig. A deterministic gate (no model, standard library and git) blocks git commit, git push and gh pr create when the change skips, deletes or moves tests, weakens what the check runs, bypasses hooks or carries a secret, and always blocks an agent-run gh pr merge; an optional second model reviews what rules cannot see, such as a loosened assertion. /foreman shows each pull request with a verdict and merges only on your command; a Desktop panel shows where each change is. Disclosure — runs read-only git in your repository; runs the GitHub CLI only on /foreman commands (merge and reject write to GitHub after your confirmation) and model calls only on /foreman commands or, with auto_review: finish, inside the agent's turn; notifications are off until you turn them on; no telemetry, no credentials, no network calls of its own. Full disclosure in the README.

name: foresee
description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

name: forgebox
description: Try-then-commit Git worktree workflow for Thor Agent. Snapshots dirty repositories and journals tool calls. Best-effort hooks redirect known file paths and command working directories; shell command text is unchanged. This is not an OS sandbox and does not contain shell writes or external side effects. Review and apply changes explicitly with forgebox apply or the dashboard/Desktop panel, or discard the worktree. Requires Git on PATH. Disclosure — redirects the agent's file-tool paths and terminal working directories into a git worktree under `<repo>/.forgebox/` while a session is active and blocks file-tool paths outside that repo (shell command text is not rewritten, so this is not a sandbox); applying copies the reviewed worktree changes into your real checkout and can create a git commit, which runs your repository's own git hooks.

name: forgebruecke
description: A bridge between Thor and your self-hosted Forgejo: Thor works as its own account, writes follow Thor' approval setting, and a desk in Thor Desktop shows the pull requests that wait for you. Disclosure — Talks only to the Forgejo address you set, as a separate Thor account whose token you provide; the optional personal write token is used only for the desk's Merge and Comment buttons on your click, and is available to Thor. Per-repo flows run a background loop in the gateway that reviews new pull requests by starting `thor -p <reviewer profile> chat` processes, which send each pull request's title, description and diff to that profile's model provider and post the verdict as a comment. The "Create a reviewer profile" button clones your profile (config.yaml, SOUL.md and every key in .env) into `forgebruecke-reviewer`, then removes its memories and the two Forgebrücke tokens through `thor` commands. The optional mention channel, once enabled in the profile, answers Forgejo mentions from any commenter on repos where mentions are on. The git credential helper setup prints `git config --global` lines for you to run.

name: formwork
description: Complete a packet of fillable PDFs inside Thor Desktop. See each suggested answer on the original form, open its exact source page and quote, and review it before export. Enter a missing fact once and choose which matching fields should reuse it. Save editable PDFs and a review record in one ZIP. Disclosure — Formwork sends the full text of your supporting PDFs, form field details and rendered images of each form page to the model in its "Formwork extraction" auxiliary slot (it uses your Thor Vision model until you set one), and it keeps imported PDFs, previews, exports and archived packets under plugin-data/formwork after the plugin is removed.

name: fortograph
description: Reversible image redaction through the Fortograph selective-encryption API: fortograph_redact encrypts chosen regions into the saved image (not just a black box) and fortograph_unredact restores the original with the password, so Thor can share redacted photos and recover them later. Disclosures — uploads the image to the configured Fortograph server (default https://fortograph.selectiveencryption.com) and stores the redaction password in the Thor secret FORTOGRAPH_PASSWORD; pure stdlib, no subprocesses. Disclosure — uploads each image you redact or restore, the redaction password and the chosen regions to the configured Fortograph server (default https://fortograph.selectiveencryption.com, run by the plugin author); results are written next to the input image or into the optional configured output directory.

name: fortytwo-provider
description: Fortytwo — Qwen3.8 27B inference; adds Fortytwo to the Thor model provider list. Disclosure — model provider: Thor sends prompts, images and tool results to Fortytwo's hosted API (api.fortytwo.network) with your FORTYTWO_API_KEY; requests carry attribution headers naming this plugin.

name: found
description: FOUND, the AI SDR for LinkedIn and email, through FOUND's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.foundtofind.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): warm leads found from buying signals with the reason for each, pipeline and campaign numbers, account research, new companies and the right contact at a company, work emails, drafted messages, lists, and paused campaigns with their sequences. Bundles the found-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to FOUND's hosted server (app.foundtofind.com) and acts on the user's FOUND account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools spend FOUND credits (FOUND states they quote the price first and spend only on a confirming second call), and FOUND states campaigns created from Thor start paused; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: foundry
description: Foundry — five creator bots sharing one memory ledger: research, draft, score, and price your work. Say 'foundry start' — a short interview sets up your brand. Approval is disabled — no trusted human review channel yet; nothing auto-posts.

name: fractal-memory-engine
description: Hierarchical vectorless episodic memory, procedural attractor clustering, and O(1) complex coordinate anchoring for Thor Agent. Eliminates external vector database and embedding model overhead via 3-ring orbital resonance decay and local JSON state persistence under THOR_HOME/plugin-data.

name: freebusy
description: Books meetings over email or chat from free or busy time only, with any CalDAV calendar and any IMAP/SMTP mailbox; every slot is held before it is offered. Disclosure — Fixture mode is the default: no network calls, demo data only. Connectors mode, switched on by /freebusy connect once its test passes, talks only to the CalDAV, IMAP and SMTP servers the owner sets up (https/TLS only, private and loopback addresses refused), plus one unauthenticated check of the owner's email domain for /.well-known/caldav during setup; app passwords are typed in a terminal and kept in the system keychain, never in config or chat. In that mode it reads only busy times, writes holds and bookings to the one calendar the owner picks (or a local feed file), reads only mail addressed to its agent address, and sends scheduling replies, invites and owner notes by SMTP without a per-message prompt, within the owner's groups, tiers and its own policy gate. Holds, settings and a redacted audit log stay in its data folder; a short scheduling context is added each turn. pre_tool_call gates its own actions, and other plugins' mail and calendar tools only with vet_other_tools. post_gateway_admission answers only admitted chat senders the owner lists in chat_contacts; everyone else reaches the agent as usual. Reminders are owner-only cronjob_manage jobs. Google adapter inert until 0.4.

name: freeze
description: Let Thor do a task once, then replay it without the model: /freeze turns the last turn's tool calls into a checked workflow (bindings, loops over lists, and model-worked values compiled into Python that must reproduce the recording exactly), and thor freeze run repeats it with 0 model calls, stops on drift, never overwrites a file you edited, and thor freeze schedule makes it a no-agent cron job. Disclosure — hooks record each turn's task, tool arguments, tool results (truncated at 256 KB), final answer and token counts in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/freeze/data.db, pruned after 14 days (at load and at most hourly while recording); /freeze makes model calls through your active model (one per compiled step, at most 3 attempts) and sends the task, shortened tool results and the recorded value; replays repeat every recorded tool call except clarify, todo, memory, delegate_task, session_search, skill tools, vision/image/speech tools, mixture_of_agents, cronjob_manage, send_message and tool search (so terminal, file, execute_code, browser, MCP and plugin tool calls are re-run) through Thor' own tools and Thor' approvals (unattended runs follow approvals.cron_mode, default deny), and run model-compiled code with no Thor approval in a separate python -I process with static and runtime module allowlists, no environment variables beyond PATH, and a 10 s timeout; /freeze run starts thor freeze run as a child process, --fallback agent starts thor chat; schedule writes <THOR_HOME>/scripts/freeze-<name>.sh and creates a cron job with thor cron create --no-agent that reports drift and stops (only with --fallback agent does it start thor chat on drift, which costs model calls); no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.

name: freight-reconciliation
description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

name: freshdesk
description: Generic Freshdesk API v2 tools for Thor Agent. Unaffiliated community connector, not a Freshworks product. Disclosure — calls the account's native Freshdesk HTTPS origin with profile-scoped secrets FRESHDESK_DOMAIN and FRESHDESK_API_KEY; downloads an attachment into the Thor cache only from that ticket's own attachment hosts; the five write tools (private note, create ticket, public reply that Freshdesk emails to the ticket's requester, time entry, status/priority update) escalate to Thor human approval and fail closed when no person is present. No third-party dependencies, shell commands, telemetry, or self-updater.

name: freshness-sidecar
description: Notes bound to a source file: before every turn each note's file is re-hashed, so the agent is told a fact is STALE (or MISSING) the moment its file changes, instead of confidently repeating an outdated value. /fresh add|list|check|forget works from the CLI and messaging gateways without the model; a freshness_note tool exposes the same actions to the model. Runs alongside any memory provider (does not take the memory.provider slot). Disclosure — reads explicitly registered local files within the session's workspace to compute bounded SHA-256 checks (1 MiB cap; symlinks, files outside the workspace and credential-looking files are refused). Stores note text, paths and hashes in profile-scoped plugin data. Selected notes and status snapshots are added to the user turn sent to the configured model and persist in Thor history; forgetting a note stops future recall but does not erase copies already in history. FRESH means matching bytes, not verified truth. No network calls, subprocesses, background services, credential access or self-update.

name: frihet
description: Official Thor Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical Frihet MCP surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Thor's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; /frihet brief uses get_business_context, list_invoices, list_quotes, list_expenses, list_clients, and list_client_activities through the same MCP client to display business data in the current session, without writes; reads ~/.thor/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

name: fusen
description: Fusen (付箋, Japanese for sticky note) are notes pinned to conversations: one editable body shared by every chat it is pinned to, handed to the model only when its view is stale, and rewriteable only when you allow it — by default Thor can merely propose a rewrite, and you apply or dismiss it.

name: fusion
description: Multi-model fusion router for Thor: detects the model fleet your harnesses (Thor, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `thor fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

name: fxmacrodata
description: FXMacroData macro and FX research with official-source releases, indicator history, release calendars, curves, FX, commodities, positioning and sourced research tasks. 100 native tools: 41 REST, 57 MCP, a USD brief and a version-pinned history snapshot. Disclosure — tool calls send their arguments, including user-entered research or positions, over HTTPS only to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com; optional FXMACRODATA_API_KEY is read through the Thor profile-scoped secret API and sent in request headers. Public USD catalogue, history and calendar require no key, account or card; other scope depends on data entitlement. No files written, shell commands, background processes or telemetry. Adds research guidance to the system prompt. Finite SSE capture; interactive MCP Apps preserved as data, not rendered. Remote MCP behaviour is not covered by the pinned source SHA. Host/model charges are separate.

name: gadget
description: Talk to your Thor from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Thor pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny), within Thor's approval timeout. The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Session hooks feed a dashboard on paired devices with each agent session's platform, a short id and its state (idle, busy, waiting for approval); a device that can switch profiles also sees the offered profiles' sessions. Optional profile switching (off unless `profiles` is set in the default profile's gadget config) lets a device paired on the default profile talk to the listed profiles; each profile approves the device through its own pairing flow (the device shows the `thor -p <profile> pairing approve` command), the plugin writes nothing into other profiles, and revoking the device in the default profile sends it back there. A paired gadget that draws faces gets the answering profile's face: its `gadget-face.bin`, or its Thor avatar (`assets/avatar.*`) converted with Pillow when installed; the plugin only reads these files, and `profile_faces: false` turns this off. `platforms.gadget.extra.stt_language` sets the transcription language of gadget recordings through the `pre_transcription` hook; other platforms' audio is untouched. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg; Opus reply audio uses the host's libopus when installed (loaded with ctypes, not bundled). `thor gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. A device that advertises `camera.capture` returns stills that are saved as PNGs under `~/.thor/gadgetpix/` and kept until removed by hand. A Thor Desktop page (`desktop/plugin.js`, plugin SDK only) runs a gadget in the window that connects to the local gateway as a device of its own: its device key, and the gateway access token when one is required, are kept in the page's plugin storage, it pairs like any device, and it uses the microphone only while its talk button or Space is held. The plugin's dashboard routes, behind the dashboard's login, can approve the pairing code a device is showing and send a card or run an advertised action on a connected, paired device; the requests pass through files under plugin-data/gadget/desk/. Otherwise writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Thor's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Thor Labs.

name: gambit
description: Play chess in a Thor terminal or Desktop pane, understand mistakes, and replay or practice public Chess.com and Lichess matches. Disclosure — runs a locally installed Stockfish executable (the path you set in plugin settings, or one found on PATH) as a subprocess that inherits Thor' environment; fetches public games for a username you enter from api.chess.com and lichess.org; uses your configured Thor model for each opponent move; and in Coach mode the Desktop pane automatically sends coaching requests into the bound chat when it is idle, each starting a model turn.

name: game-dev
description: Read-only project inspection and asset audits with playable-slice, asset-production, and verification skills. Disclosure — lists file names and sizes under any absolute project path the agent supplies (skipping hidden, symlinked and credential-named entries), reads that project's project.godot/export_presets.cfg and, on request, hashes asset files; no writes, no shell commands, no network calls.

name: game-editor
description: In the Godot 4 project open in your editor, it places assets into the scene, plays the game, and the next plan fixes each error from its file and line. Disclosure — Needs Godot 4.7 or later, the Godot AI 4.x add-on, and uv. The first start downloads godot-ai==4.3.0 from pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org. There is no API key. The editor is reached only on 127.0.0.1. A server this plugin starts sends no telemetry. The add-on follows godot_ai/telemetry_enabled (on by default) and can send usage to godot-ai-telemetry-v2-pudmurzsnq-uw.a.run.app. plan_change sends only the session list. apply_plan asks once. A plan that deletes, overwrites, drops unsaved work, writes outside the project or runs code it wrote is not made when what is lost exceeds 1,700 characters, and otherwise runs only after confirm_risky_plan. Play and tests ask once and run the project's code. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway, so anyone who can message Thor there can ask and approve. This plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron, thor chat -q and unattended runs decline. Data stays in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-game-editor-<id> after removal. Stop with thor plugins disable game-editor, or thor tools for one surface. macOS only. The studio plan step writes res://studio/ files and, with no editor open, a project under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor/studio-project, and runs headless Godot on code it wrote; each test, web export and recording needs confirm_risky_plan. studio import_asset copies a .glb, .wav, .ogg or .mp3 file of up to 64 MB from any absolute path the plan names into res://studio/imports/. studio web downloads the 1.3 GB Godot 4.7.2 export template from github.com once, only after its sha256 and sha512 match, keeps it in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor/export-templates, and serves the Web build on 127.0.0.1 only; it never uploads. Headless studio steps delete files that appear in the project outside studio/ and build/ while Godot runs. The pass ledger stays in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor after removal.

name: game-lab
description: Game Lab combines ModLab, Game Localization Studio, Sprites and experimental Playtest Pilot. ModLab works on a private game copy and invokes separately installed tools; localization drafts and exports RPG Maker text; Sprites inspects and previews character sheets. Playtest Pilot uses approved X11 input, captures screen pixels within the selected window, stores private evidence frames and returns reduced previews and optional local OCR hints; for a failed check it can build a short captioned MP4 from those frames with your FFmpeg, or cut one from a recording file you point to (that asks for approval). On first use ModLab reads Steam's library list and app manifests to find installed games, lists the files in the chosen game folder, runs read-only hardware checks, and asks which modding route to use. It never fills a disk: a free-space reserve, a total cap, pruning of old revisions and a confirm-first cleanup tool. The Universal Modder and REA programs are the ones you set in the plugin settings or find on PATH (the model cannot name a program), and each toolkit call and each playtest check asks for your approval. Every program it starts gets a minimal environment, never your provider keys. The plugin makes no network calls of its own. Disclosure — Playtest Pilot sends synthetic key presses and clicks to the X11 window you select (via xdotool and Thor computer_use, each check or batch approved), captures that window's pixels and stores evidence frames in the plugin's data folder; ModLab reads your Steam library and app-manifest files to list installed games, copies the game folder you choose into plugin data (with a disk cap), and, after your approval of each call, runs the Universal Modder / REA programs set in the plugin settings or found on PATH.

name: gameforge
description: Game development toolkit: sound effects, music loops with MIDI, NPC voices, pixel-art sprite sheets and autotiling tilesets, low-poly and AI 3D models (.glb); 4 playable web genres (topdown, platformer, arena, roguelike), Godot 4 and Unity builds; headless Blender and Unreal pipelines; an automated playtester that plays each genre and reports crashes, stuck spots and boring stretches; one-click PWA, itch.io, single-HTML and Capacitor export. Offline by default. Disclosure — runs local Chrome/Chromium for playtests, and Godot, Unity, Blender, UnrealEditor-Cmd, ffmpeg, xvfb-run or butler only when a call asks for them; blender action=script runs a bpy file the caller names. Network only when asked: fal.ai, Tripo or Meshy (FAL_KEY / TRIPO_API_KEY / MESHY_API_KEY, prompt and image sent), ElevenLabs (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, SFX prompt), Edge TTS when edge-tts is installed (dialogue text), Godot export templates from GitHub (~1 GB, target=godot_templates), itch.io via butler (target=itch with an explicit itch_target). Writes only inside the game project directory, plus a temporary browser profile. No telemetry.

name: garmin-connect
description: Unofficial community plugin for Garmin Connect data through Garmin's official Personal API: sleep, HRV, Body Battery, stress, steps, heart rate, activities, weight, heart-rate training load and fitness age, with deterministic baselines and trend flags (garmin_trends), a /garmin command, an optional one-line daily context, a morning readiness brief automation and a Thor Desktop readiness panel. Fourteen read-only tools. The key is entered in Thor Desktop under Settings > Plugins > garmin-connect (or with thor config set), stored in the profile's .env as GARMIN_PERSONAL_API_KEY and read through Thor's secret route. Disclosure — Unofficial, not affiliated with Garmin. Contacts only personal.connectapi.garmin.com (personal.connectapi.garmin.cn for region china): GET requests plus one POST that exchanges the user's GARMIN_PERSONAL_API_KEY for a short-lived token, which is kept in memory only. Health data in tool results goes to your model provider. With `inject_daily_context` on (off by default), a one-line health summary is added to new chats. A background thread reads the Garmin profile time zone when timezone is auto. `garmin_activity_fit` saves activity ZIPs under the profile's plugin-data folder. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: gateway-guardian
description: Telegram/gateway reliability guard for Thor — detects 409 polling conflicts, duplicate pollers, freezes, stale locks and missed deliveries, shows one health state (OK/DEGRADED/BLOCKED) and an approved recovery plan. Disclosure — read-only status: it reads the last 256 KiB of the gateway.log of this Thor home and of every profile under it, plus process command lines from /proc, and returns only pattern counts and file paths; recovery only prints a fixed checklist and appends the chosen action to a local intent log, and never restarts, kills or rebinds anything itself; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: gbrain-plugin
description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Thor as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

name: gbrain-pointer
description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex
description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `thor plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

name: gemini-live
description: Full-duplex Gemini Live voice calls in Thor Desktop and the web dashboard. The voice takes the profile's name and hands real work to your Thor agent while you keep talking. It can steer running jobs, threads, bot chats and subagents, use the profile's MCP tools, recall memory and past conversations, set and read iPhone alarms, timers and reminders through thor-mobile-device-access when a phone is paired, and report back when work finishes. Read-only local commands need three layers to agree: hard rules, a safety review and a contained run; files are read only from the workspace folder, /var/log and a few plain system files. When a job needs approval, the voice says so and Approve and Deny buttons appear; the voice model can never answer one, and spoken approval is opt-in. With the AirPods Approvals plugin, a nod or shake answers it too. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it from the client to generativelanguage.googleapis.com on a single-use ephemeral token; the Gemini key stays on the Thor backend, read through Thor' secret scope. Gemini also receives the voice's instructions, tool results, and, unless share_chat_context is off, the open chat's title and recent messages. On Gemini's free tier, Google may use this content to improve its products. Delegated work runs as a normal Thor turn with that profile's tools and approvals. The iPhone tools call that plugin directly, within the access granted in the Thor Agent app, and send alarm and reminder details to Gemini; turn them off with phone_tools.
