The opt-in readonly_shell and system_checks settings, both off by default, run bounded commands on the Thor host. No telemetry and no background processes.

name: gemini-media
description: Google Gemini image (Nano Banana) and video (Gemini Omni) generation backends for image_generate and video_generate, in one plugin built on the google-genai SDK. Image: text-to-image and reference-guided editing (up to 14 images). Video: text-, image- and reference-to-video with native audio. Model picker comes from the key's live models.list. Disclosure — prompts, reference images and the Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY, falling back to GOOGLE_API_KEY, the key Thor's own Gemini chat provider uses) are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; reference-image URLs are downloaded by the plugin (public hosts only, redirects re-checked) and a local reference path can be any image file the user can read (accepted only after a magic-byte check); generation is billed to the API key's Google project; writes generated media under $THOR_HOME/cache/generated/ and a model-list cache (key hash only) under $THOR_HOME/cache/gemini_media/; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates. Installs google-genai.

name: genealogy-research-recipes
description: Fact-checked genealogy instructions for DNA evidence, record searches and proof judgment. Native read-only skill bundle with recipe sources and an offline given-name lookup helper. Disclosure — optional third-party services and commands described by recipes require separately authorized tools and credentials; the adapter itself makes no service calls and registers no tools, hooks or MCP server.

name: genesispay-catalog
description: Search products, services and shops listed on GenesisPay and read their verified-purchase reviews through the hosted, read-only GenesisPay Catalog MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://catalog.genesispay.finance/mcp/catalog, no sign-in, no key), with a catalog skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — network calls to catalog.genesispay.finance, operated by GenesisPay (Genesis Technologies): search terms, filters and ids reach that server; no credentials are stored; all four tools are read-only and none pays, orders or changes anything; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: genflick
description: Connect Thor to Genflick creative and business workspaces for films, series, music videos, ads and marketing, with email-link sign-in and host-owned OAuth. Disclosure — tool calls send your prompts, project inputs and media requests to Genflick's hosted MCP server at genflick.com (which may pass work to its own downstream providers), its tools can spend from your Genflick account and publish ads, social posts and outreach; the package sets `trust: full`, so Thor does not prompt per tool and Genflick enforces its own approvals (credit confirmation above the account's threshold, exact-post approval before publishing, Stop), sign-in needs a hand-added `mcp_servers.genflick` OAuth entry in config.yaml, and the bundled skill may read the Genflick sign-in email through your connected mailbox tools and open its link.

name: genui
description: Live cards for Thor Desktop: the agent shows a long task as a pre-designed card (a pull request, a release, a slow machine, files to clean up, a study session), updates it in place after every tool result, and asks for a decision with a button only when one is needed; the click (and what you ticked or answered in the card) goes back to the agent as one turn. Disclosure — no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials; writes one small JSON file per shown card in the plugin's data directory, removed after 30 days untouched; adds a short turn hint to Thor Desktop turns only; cards run in a sandboxed frame, a click on a decision posts one visible message from the user, and a click on an http(s) link in a card (link targets come from the agent) opens it in the user's browser.

name: getyoutubetranscript
description: YouTube transcripts (optionally with timestamps), video search, and channel and playlist browsing through the GetYouTubeTranscript remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://getyoutubetranscript.com/api/mcp). Bundles four skills: fetch a transcript, search YouTube, summarize a video, and research a channel or playlist. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to getyoutubetranscript.com, which receives the video URL or search text and the user's API key (YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY, sent as a bearer header from the user's environment). The bundled skills can also call the same host's REST API with that key via curl, and can create an account for the user by sending the email address they give to getyoutubetranscript.com's signup endpoint. All tools are annotated read-only. Transcript fetches use account credits (100 free on sign-up, no card). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: gh-ref
description: @gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

name: ghl-command
description: GoHighLevel lives inside Thor. Create contacts, move deals, send email and SMS, trigger workflows from chat. Live in 90 seconds, no browser clicks. Disclosure — sends CRM reads and writes, contact deletes, workflow enrollments and outbound SMS/email (to recipients the agent names, each delete/send/enroll after a Thor approval prompt) through the user's own GoHighLevel account at services.leadconnectorhq.com using the GHL_API_KEY Private Integration Token; no other hosts, no telemetry.

name: ghost-run
description: Dry-run mode for Thor Agent. With /ghost on, file writes, patches, deletes and terminal commands are redirected into a throwaway copy of the working folder, and network-touching tools and commands are blocked. Review the diff in the system browser (thor ghost ui; the Desktop pane only opens that page), then optionally run one configured Verify command in the ghost (Pass/Fail banner; Apply stays human), then apply selected paths or discard. Commands: /ghost on|off|status|verify; thor ghost diff|apply|discard|ui|verify. Disclosure — copies the working folder into a temp sandbox (reflink, then copy; never a hard link) and runs the agent's terminal commands on the host with the working directory set to that copy; only literal absolute paths under the real folder are rewritten, so a command naming ~, $HOME or another absolute path still acts on the real disk, and MCP or other plugin tools are not redirected; Ghost Mode is process-wide, so in a gateway it covers every chat in that process; writes session state under the Thor home from thor_constants.get_thor_home() (then THOR_HOME, then ~/.thor), in ghost-run/; "apply" writes the chosen changes back to the real folder only after a person presses Apply or runs /ghost apply, and that copy does not pass through Thor' file-write denylist; /ghost apply and thor ghost apply with no paths apply every current change and can copy a named path that is in the ghost tree even if it is not in the diff; the review page never auto-ticks HIGH-risk files and asks to confirm any it names; thor ghost ui binds 127.0.0.1 only, checks Host, requires a per-session token sent in the X-Ghost-Run-Token header (query-string tokens are ignored), sends no CORS headers, and POST /api/apply accepts only a non-empty list of paths that are all in the current diff; Verify runs one command taken from GHOST_RUN_TEST or the project's .ghost-run-test on the host inside the ghost copy, only after you approve that project and exact command, with provider keys stripped from its environment; opt-in outbound only: with GHOST_RUN_AI=1, pending diffs go to your Thor provider through ctx.llm.complete, or, if that is unavailable, to openrouter.ai using OPENROUTER_API_KEY read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret; off by default, no credentials stored by the plugin, no telemetry.

name: ghost-subscriptions
description: Detects subscriptions and recurring charges in a bank statement export (CSV from 17 bank profiles or any CSV by column mapping, OFX 1.x/2.x), reports their yearly cost per currency, price increases, duplicate charges, overlapping services, stopped subscriptions and payment plans, and writes a cancellation pack (one letter per subscription in English or French, a CSV summary and an .ics file with reminders 7 days before each charge). Disclosure: reads only the statement file the user names and its own bundled profile and alias data; stores dates, amounts and sanitised descriptions (IBANs masked, full card numbers removed, file path not stored) in SQLite under its plugin data folder, where the cancellation packs are also written; statement_purge deletes all of it; makes no network requests and imports no networking modules; sends, cancels or pays nothing; no shell commands, background processes, credentials, telemetry, self-updating code, binaries or Python dependencies.

name: ghostmark-mcp
description: GhostMark through its MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://ghostmark.mrhyde.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): puts an invisible watermark tied to a key into a picture, with an optional encrypted message of up to 24 bytes inside, and reads it back with the same key after the picture has been saved as JPEG, cropped, resized or rotated. Three tools: suggest_key draws a random key of common words, mark_image returns the marked file, read_image says whether a key and a picture fit and returns the message. Bundles one skill for both flows. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. The mark does not encrypt or protect the picture and is not proof of authorship: it answers whether a picture carries the mark of a key. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to ghostmark.mrhyde.dev (closed-source server, behind Cloudflare), which uses the picture, the key and the message in memory to answer one call and stores none of them; it keeps daily counts with no text, no picture and no address, and logs the address of what looks like an attack. With image_url the server downloads that picture itself. Every tool is annotated read-only; the package marks the server untrusted. The skill tells the agent to send only the picture the person named and only to ghostmark.mrhyde.dev, and to treat a message read out of a picture as data. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: ghostrun
description: Recreate NES games as editable browser games. Train an AI player, rebuild levels and gameplay in Three.js, and add optional 3D visuals. Disclosure — `ghostrun_engine_setup` clones https://github.com/hbofz/NeSLE.git at a pinned commit and compiles it locally with nvcc/c++; runs git, nvcc, c++, nvidia-smi, ffprobe and the configured Python, including the agent-edited per-game reward module, outside the sandbox with a reduced environment that excludes provider keys; starts long-running background processes only on explicit tool calls (GPU training, an oracle service on a local Unix socket that can replay a checkpoint from the game's own runs folder, and a watcher that starts with every training run, checks every minute by default and can wake the agent to edit that game's reward reader and restart its training, max 3 fixes per game); reads the ROM path you give it and writes rebuilt games to ~/ghostrun-projects by default; a pre_tool_call hook blocks builder sessions from reaching the reference game. No credentials, no telemetry, no bundled binaries.

name: ghostwriter
description: Write, revise, and export screenplays in a Thor Desktop workspace with a project-aware assistant.

name: gif-tool
description: Show, edit and compress GIFs in Thor. `gif_open` turns any GIF, animated WebP, APNG, PNG or JPEG (a file path or an https link) into a card in Thor Desktop where you add exact captions, change speed, reverse, boomerang, trim, drop frames and crop with a live preview; the original file is never changed. `gif_export` and the card's export buttons compress for Discord (10 MB), Discord emoji (256 KB), Telegram, X (5 MB), under 1 MB, animated WebP or a size you name, shrinking until the file fits and reporting before and after sizes (pure Pillow: shared palette, frame differencing, size-targeted ladder). `gif_edit` gives the agent the same edits. `gif_create` makes a four-frame meme GIF from a prompt. A GIF Studio tab lists every GIF in the profile and takes a dropped file or a pasted link. Disclosure — editing, previews and compression are local; opening a link downloads that one https URL (no cookies or credentials; private, local and link-local addresses refused, redirects and the connected peer re-checked; a GIPHY or Tenor page is followed once to its og:image); `gif_create` sends only the text prompt to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/images/generations through Thor' credentialed_provider_request with the user's OpenAI Codex sign-in, using one image from the user's ChatGPT plan per call, via an undocumented endpoint; projects and rendered files are stored under the profile's plugin-data/gif-tool and cache/generated/images.

name: gigamail
description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Thor.

name: git-autosave
description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/thor-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `thor autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs each backup in a short-lived child process killed at the hook deadline, which runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs and short-lived private index files into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `thor autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background or long-lived processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.

name: git-hook
description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Thor touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.

name: git-review
description: Git review pane for Thor Desktop: every changed file of the agent's last turn, uncommitted, staged or unstaged work, the branch since it left the default branch, or any selection of commits, in one scroll, unified or split, with syntax colours; cites changed lines into the composer as @line: references; and stages, unstages, discards, commits, pushes and opens pull requests from the pane. Disclosure — reads run git subprocesses (rev-parse, status, diff, log, show, cat-file, ls-files, for-each-ref, branch, remote, rev-list, merge-base, symbolic-ref, hash-object) with timeouts and output caps, external diff and textconv drivers disabled. Writes run only when the user clicks: git add, restore, reset, rm, commit and push, on paths validated inside the repository; discard asks first in Desktop's confirmation dialog and deletes only the untracked files it names. By default hooks are skipped and any write that would run a program named by the repository's own config (filter drivers, signing, SSH or credential commands) is refused; the run_repo_programs setting allows them, and the read_only setting hides and refuses every write. Network use: push to the branch's own name on its remote, and the user's own gh or glab CLI for the PR/MR badge and for Create pull request; the plugin itself makes no network requests. Generate commit message sends what the commit will contain and recent commit subjects to the focused chat's model through Thor's commit_message one-shot template, only when clicked. It reads files and history inside authorized repositories only (the focused workspace, configured repos/roots and the latest agent selection), this profile's config.yaml, and the cwd column of the sessions table in state.db (read-only); it writes $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/select.sqlite3 (agent selection requests), $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/turn-snapshots/ (Last agent turn snapshots: the working tree's tracked and non-ignored untracked files as git objects, written with git add -A and write-tree against a throwaway index and an object store in that directory, never the repository's; newest 16 kept, three days max), Desktop plugin storage (display settings, turn baselines) and, through the actions above, the user's repository. While the pane is open it polls the local backend every 3 s (agent selections) and 5 s (live diffs); the status-bar count and the commit box's branch state refresh every 15 s; no background processes, credentials or telemetry.

name: git-tasks
description: Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for Thor Desktop. Disclosure — uses your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through Thor Desktop's shell bridge, or a GitHub token you paste in the panel (stored unencrypted in Desktop plugin storage, sent only to api.github.com); scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos and reads skill names under ~/.thor; polls the active-session list of every Thor profile every 10 seconds for status chips; approve, close, reopen, comment and merge act on GitHub from the panel; creates git worktrees and opens Thor sessions seeded with the issue/PR title and body as fenced untrusted text, and without a shell bridge asks the agent to run the worktree git commands.

name: github-copilot
description: GitHub Copilot model providers for Thor: `copilot` (the Copilot API with your Copilot subscription: GPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok models, sign in with `thor auth add copilot` or COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN) and `copilot-acp` (drives your installed GitHub Copilot CLI over ACP). Moved out of Thor core; profiles that used Copilot get it installed automatically. A Thor Labs plugin: built by Thor Labs, not supported. Disclosure — signs in with GitHub's device-code flow using the Copilot editor OAuth app, exchanges your GitHub token for a short-lived Copilot token at api.github.com and sends your prompts to api.githubcopilot.com (or models.github.ai); it calls GitHub only for profiles that chose Copilot, never runs `gh` or reads other tools' token files, and caches the exchanged token in <THOR_HOME>/.copilot_jwt.json. copilot-acp runs your local `copilot` CLI.

name: github_app
description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or THOR_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result. Talks only to https://api.github.com or the operator-configured GITHUB_API_URL / settings.api_url (HTTPS, no redirects; no tool argument can change the host). Issue/comment/review/merge writes stay disabled until settings.allow_write_actions is true and each one additionally goes through Thor's human-approval prompt via its pre_tool_call hook (an 'always' answer does not persist).

name: gitthor
description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in Thor Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `thor plugins update gitthor` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.

name: glance
description: Thor can't call a UI change done until it has looked. Glance screenshots the running iOS Simulator (or Android emulator) right before the agent's first UI edit, diffs it against the screen after the edit, and the pre_verify hook sends the agent back when the edit changed nothing, crashed to an error screen, or left the screen blank. On PASS the agent sees the before/after image, so it can catch a button that vanished. Desktop draws the result as a before/after slider. Disclosure — runs xcrun simctl (list, io screenshot) and adb (devices, exec-out screencap) as subprocesses; adb devices starts adb's own server if it is not running; on PASS calls Thor' vision_analyze on the compare image through ctx.dispatch_tool, which is one auxiliary vision model call when the main model is text-only; appends the compare image to the agent's final reply as a MEDIA attachment, so on messaging platforms the screenshot is sent into that chat; writes screenshots and check records under plugin-data/glance and does not prune them; no network calls of its own, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: glass-theme
description: Translucent glass surfaces for Thor Desktop in light and dark, teal accent, with terminal colors that match. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers one theme through the Desktop plugin SDK and injects no CSS, no DOM access and no stylesheet of its own; the palette ships light and dark sets and the desktop terminal pane takes its colours from them. The package also ships two optional CLI/TUI skins (glass-light, glass-dark) as plain YAML files the user copies into ~/.thor/skins, plus an inert __init__.py whose register() does nothing so the Agent loader imports the package cleanly instead of reporting a missing module. No network requests, no agent tools, no hooks, no background processes, no settings page.

name: glassbox
description: A contained, auditable terminal backend for macOS. Select it with `thor config set terminal.backend glassbox` and every terminal, execute_code, read_file, write_file, patch and search_files call runs under a generated Seatbelt profile: the system stays readable, the workspace is writable, the rest of the user's home is hidden, the home directory itself is never used as the workspace, and network access is off by default. The kernel-refused reads, writes and network attempts are recorded in a local audit log, so "what did the agent try to touch?" is answerable: `thor glassbox report` (text or a self-contained dark HTML timeline), `/glassbox status|verify|report|profile`, the glassbox_report / glassbox_policy / glassbox_verify tools, a containment self-test (`thor glassbox verify`: workspace read/write, home read/write denial, child-process confinement, parent traversal, network denial, secret-env filtering) and a one-command demo (`thor glassbox demo`). A pre_tool_call preflight turns file-tool denials into an actionable error with the exact `thor config set` line to allow a path, instead of the masked empty read a `2>/dev/null` shell probe would otherwise produce. Settings: network, allow_home, workspace_writable, read_paths, write_paths, deny_paths, audit — apply to the next command, editable from the Desktop Plugins tab. Disclosure — macOS only; runs the agent's shell and file-tool commands on this Mac as the same UNIX user under /usr/bin/sandbox-exec (an OS kernel sandbox, not a VM or a separate UID; it does not defend against a kernel exploit, and system mach services other than Apple Events and LaunchServices stay reachable); osascript, open, security and launchctl are blocked by path, and Apple Events plus LaunchServices mach services are denied; the home directory is never used as the workspace and shell startup files and ~/Library/LaunchAgents are always write-denied; the generated profile, a private scratch home/tmp area and the audit log live under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/glassbox/ (the audit stores command text truncated to 2000 chars, cwd, exit code, duration, blocked paths and a short output excerpt only when something was blocked — local only, capped at 4 MB with one rotation, never uploaded, `thor glassbox clear` deletes it); reads the workspace and any extra read_paths/write_paths the user configures; runs two `git config --global --get` calls to copy the Git author name/email into the sandbox environment because ~/.gitconfig is hidden; provider keys, tokens, passwords and SSH agent sockets are filtered from every sandboxed child environment; the containment self-test writes and removes canary files in the home directory; no network calls of its own, no background processes, no telemetry; Seatbelt is marked deprecated by Apple but shipped and functional on current macOS — if a future macOS drops sandbox-exec the backend reports unavailable instead of running unconfined.

name: glasser
description: Glasser's hosted MCP: search, inspect and run 1,000+ paid data endpoints (people and company enrichment, SEO, web, social media, US property, stock quotes) with one key, pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: a stdio bridge through mcp-remote (browser sign-in, no key in the package) plus a bundled skill for setup and the spending rules. Requires Node.js 18+. Disclosure — paid data broker: each run tool call charges your Glasser balance per the endpoint's published price with no in-Thor confirm step; runs npx mcp-remote@0.14.3 as a local stdio bridge to https://api.glasser.ai/mcp; the sign-in token is cached by mcp-remote under ~/.mcp-auth/.

name: glasses-platform
description: Your own Thor agent on your smart glasses and other devices: it sees what you see, answers by voice, and taps you on the lens when something is due. A gateway platform that adds glasses as a channel, with short spoken-style replies to the device that asked, camera photos (requested when you ask what you are looking at, or taken by the agent with its glasses_capture_photo tool), voice in and out through Thor's own speech settings, streamed replies for heads-up displays, approval and clarify prompts on every device (approval cards with buttons, or a spoken yes or no), and cron and heartbeat pushes to all of a user's devices, kept for offline devices across gateway restarts. Also connects Even Realities G2 glasses (an Even Hub app you pack yourself), ESP32 voice boxes running the open-source xiaozhi firmware, the Omi pendant (real-time transcript webhook) and Pebble watches (the open-source Bobby app); devices that cannot keep a socket open (an Apple Watch through a Siri Shortcut, scripts) use an HTTP route. Pair a device with `thor glasses pair` (QR code) or try it from the terminal with `thor glasses try`. Speaks the bridge protocol of the community thor-glasses iOS app (v0) and a richer v1; a simulator, JavaScript and Python clients and a conformance kit are included. Disclosure — opens an unencrypted listener on all interfaces (port 8765: WebSocket /voice, /xiaozhi and /bobby/<token>/query; HTTP /turn, /pending, /approval, /xiaozhi/ota/<token>, /omi/<token>/transcript and /bobby/<token>/quota) that refuses to start without a device token (use Tailscale or a TLS proxy off your home network; Omi's servers must reach the webhook over the internet); each device token, sent in a header, query or URL path, gets full agent chat as its user, bypassing the gateway allowlist, including answering approval prompts and clarify questions; `thor glasses pair` writes device tokens to the profile .env, and the xiaozhi OTA reply gives the box its WebSocket address with its own token; with Omi, transcripts come from Omi's servers and answers go back through them; the agent can take a glasses camera photo at any time during a glasses conversation and photos are also captured automatically on visual keywords (auto_capture: off disables that), saved in Thor's image cache; recordings and spoken replies use Thor's own stt/tts settings, so a cloud speech provider receives the audio or text; pushes for offline devices are kept in $THOR_HOME/glasses/outbox.json (owner-only); Omi transcript segments are held in memory until the session has been idle for ten minutes (the newest 256 per session); the device's new-session button answers Thor's /new confirmation for that user; it runs a local ffmpeg (no shell) only to convert audio; no outbound network calls of its own and no telemetry.

name: gleif
description: lei_lookup, lei_parents, lei_children, lei_search, and lei_isin return LEI records, ISINs, or name candidates. A parent is an official record, a reporting exception, or an explicit miss. Disclosure — sends the LEI, legal name, or ISIN you type to api.gleif.org (GLEIF) over HTTPS with no key, and does not follow redirects or use an HTTP proxy; tools stay on for every surface, including an empty gateway allowlist; the opt-in 08:00 job spends 0 tokens and does not fire until a scheduler serves this profile; local delivery keeps a line under cron/output and empty stdout sends nothing; removal leaves the cron job, scripts/gleif-watch.py, and plugin-data/gleif/watch.json; no GLEIF logo.

name: global-business-culture
description: Cross-cultural business intelligence: country culture briefs and home-vs-host gap analysis computed from bundled Meyer, Hofstede, GLOBE and Lewis data. Three deterministic tools (culture_brief, culture_gap_analysis, culture_countries), a /culture command and a bundled practitioner-playbook skill. 57 economies offline, no dependencies, no network, no env vars — the gap analysis ranks the exact scale distances between two cultures, names the misread each gap produces and prescribes adaptation moves. Deep ASEAN/frontier coverage (Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar flagged as extrapolated from GLOBE-cluster neighbours).

name: glorya
description: Ask Thor for an ad and get the finished file back in your chat. Glorya makes on-brand image ads, video ads, landing pages and websites, and launches ad campaigns on Meta, Google Ads and TikTok. The plugin follows each job in the background: one progress message that updates, Glorya's questions asked in the chat (answer in words or with /glorya answer buttons), and the finished videos and images sent back as attachments. Also /glorya commands that run without the model, weekly image and video ad blueprints, and a Glorya Studio tab in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — needs a Glorya account with an active plan and uses its credits; campaigns spend real money from your ad account, so a pre_tool_call hook sends every create_campaign and publish_site call through Thor' approval prompt (rule keys glorya:campaign and glorya:publish), and /glorya campaign and /glorya publish ask before they act. Tool calls go to platform.glorya.ai through Thor' own MCP client (mcp_servers.glorya, auth: oauth; Thor holds the token and signing in runs Thor' manage_connections flow), and the plugin calls that server with ctx.call_mcp (mcp_allowlist). Finished files are downloaded over https from the links Glorya returns into plugin-data/glorya, which also stores job ids, titles and chat session keys (pruned after 30 days). With allow_gateway_injection it starts one agent turn per finished job to attach the files. One background thread per followed job, at most 8. thor glorya setup runs only thor plugins enable and thor config set, each after a yes. Reads gateway.session_context.get_session_env and tools.mcp_tool_discovery.mcp_servers_not_connected. No telemetry.

name: gmail
description: Thor Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's Thor Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (one setting can skip every review dialog, and then the prepare ticket, account/profile binding, exact snapshot validation and readback verification still run); remote email images load only after the user allows them. Attachment metadata listing and bounded read-only attachment download (25 MB cap) are profile/account-scoped.

name: gmi-image
description: GMI Cloud image generation and URL-based image editing as an image_gen provider (image_gen.provider: gmi-image). Maps Thor aspect ratios onto each model's own schema, so seedream, gemini-image, gpt-image and luma models share one backend. Disclosure — sends prompts, the optional image URLs and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Thor secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every generation spends GMI credits with no Thor approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model). The result is downloaded from the URL GMI returns into the Thor image cache; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies.

name: gmi-nexus
description: Adaptive intelligence layer for Thor Agent over the live GMI Cloud model catalogue. A goal is understood, planned into steps, and each step is routed to the model that suits it from the catalogue read live at runtime, so a retired model stops being routable and a new one becomes routable without a code change. Results are evaluated against each step's own criteria, a failure is recovered on a different model with bounded retries, the verified outcome feeds the routing statistics, and the report says what ran, what it cost and what failed. Ships a vision module for screenshots and before/after comparison, a benchmarking arena whose results feed the router, a Dev Agent that writes and tests code through Thor' own tools, and a creative engine for image, video and audio generation and editing. Also ships a web dashboard tab. No third-party dependencies; the key is read through Thor' secret scope; a per-run ceiling, a rolling daily ceiling and an approval threshold are enforced before any request is submitted. Disclosure — Sends goals, prompts, files and images you or the model name, plus screenshots captured through Thor' computer_use tool, to GMI Cloud (api.gmi-serving.com, console.gmicloud.ai) for paid inference and generation billed to your GMI account. Spend at or above approval_threshold_usd, or with no published price, asks for approval in Thor' own prompt, under per-run and daily caps. Vision downloads model-supplied public image URLs on your machine before sending them. The Dev Agent writes files and runs test commands through Thor' write_file and terminal tools.

name: gmi-sandbox
description: GMI Cloud Sandbox terminal backend: Thor's terminal, file and code tools run inside an ephemeral cloud sandbox created from a ready template you provide (`thor config set terminal.backend gmi_sandbox`). Commands are polled to completion and cancelled on interrupt; truncated output is reported as a failure. Disclosure — community plugin, not a GMI product. With `terminal.backend: gmi_sandbox`, every terminal command, file path and file content the agent handles goes to console.gmicloud.ai and the GMI sandbox data plane with your GMI_SANDBOX_API_KEY (read per sandbox through Thor secret scope), tagged with the plugin name and the Thor task id. The first terminal call creates a billed sandbox with no Thor approval prompt, and a crash can leave it running until its lifetime (default 900 s, renewed per command) expires; the plugin creates and deletes only its own sandboxes. Not yet verified against the live GMI service (offline tests only).

name: gmi-speech
description: GMI Cloud text-to-speech as a tts provider (tts.provider: gmi-speech). Picks the voice, speed and output format parameters from the chosen model's schema and writes a file whose extension matches the real format; music models are excluded. Disclosure — sends the text to speak and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Thor secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every synthesis spends GMI credits with no Thor approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model). The audio is downloaded over HTTPS from the URL GMI returns and written to the output path Thor supplies; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies.

name: gmi-video
description: GMI Cloud text-to-video and image-to-video as a video_gen provider (video_gen.provider: gmi-video). Reads each model's live schema, so duration, resolution, aspect ratio and audio options use the values that model accepts. Anything it lacks is dropped and reported. Disclosure — sends prompts, the optional image URLs and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Thor secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every generation spends GMI credits with no Thor approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model, and most video models bill per second). The result is downloaded from the URL GMI returns into the Thor video cache; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies.

name: gnothi
description: Quantitative claim verification, statistical comparison, and evidence-qualified conclusions. Disclosure — with the optional `automatic_check` and `jev_remote` settings both turned on, sends the checked claim and aggregate evidence counts to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai) with your OpenRouter key for an advisory score, which may incur charges; `automatic_check` alone holds response streaming and may append a note to the agent's final reply.

name: go-whatsapp
description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.9.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64; credentials are read from the active Thor profile. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. An opt-in, direct-text watch injects one selected account/chat into its existing Thor session, with WAIT/REPLY/REPORT guidance and a best-effort five-minute inactivity follow-up. Requires a signed route, separate injection permission, and in-process execution. Listening does not authorize replies. No webhook configuration.

name: goalpost
description: Stops an AI agent from making tests pass by weakening the tests. Before a test-file edit or a test command that hides failures runs, Goalpost reads the change and blocks it: adding a skip or xfail marker, deleting a test, removing an assertion, or appending "|| true", "--exit-zero" or "--no-verify". The agent is told why and steered to fix the code. Text-based and model-free, with a local ledger of every decision; mode is block, warn or off.

name: godot-studio
description: Headless Godot 4 workflows for the agent game studio — godot_headless_check (script/resource validation via godot --headless, no editor needed), godot_export (CI builds from named export presets, e.g. a Web build a playtester agent can load), godot_builds (export presets + artifact state: exists/size/modified — gallery data for re-export decisions and attaching fresh builds in chat), godot_setup (read-only install-state report for Godot/godot-ai/uv with the exact registration path). Complements the hi-godot/godot-ai MCP editor bridge by covering the verification and export leg of the loop; bundles the godot-studio skill teaching edit → verify → export → playtest. Ships an optional desktop half (unified package): a Godot version statusbar chip and a builds gallery pane backed by its own read-only dashboard API; opt-in, degrades gracefully when the backend is off. Tools register only when a Godot 4 binary is present (check_fn). Disclosure — runs shell commands (godot --headless against the caller-targeted project; read-only godot --version in the desktop backend; read-only thor mcp list in godot_setup); godot_headless_check and godot_export execute the target project's own GDScript (autoloads, main scene, export plugins) with no approval prompt — point them only at projects you trust; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no background processes; exports write only inside the target project (the output path is resolved and confined to the project directory, existing files that aren't known export artifacts are never overwritten, and the default is the preset's own export_path from export_presets.cfg); the desktop backend reads export_presets.cfg and artifact metadata inside the project path the user configures in the pane.

name: godseye
description: Eye Of Thor (EOH) puts a live 3D globe beside your Thor chat that the agent can fly, read, annotate and watch. It is built on God's Eye View (bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view, MIT). Eleven composable tools (godseye_view, godseye_query, godseye_layers, godseye_feeds, godseye_annotate, godseye_nav, godseye_track, godseye_scene, godseye_watch, godseye_capture, godseye_admin) work on public data (aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, fires, weather, infrastructure and public SDR receivers) and drive the pane in Thor Desktop and the Webapp. The agent can fly to a place and switch the visual style (night vision, thermal, noir and others); answer "what am I looking at" from the camera, the open pin or your last click; search for places and pin them with research drawers and an attached YouTube or X clip; measure distances and areas and draw walk, bike and drive routes and reach isochrones; compare imagery before and after with Esri Wayback and replay earthquakes and fires on a time slider; walk a route in Street View; follow a public aircraft, ship or satellite by its identifier; play Director camera scenes; leave area watches that report new items on the next chat turn; and save an investigation as an HTML or Markdown report, GeoJSON or KML. The Overlays sidebar lists pins, routes, areas, watches and scenes and imports or exports eoh.overlays.v1 JSON. HUD summaries use your Thor model (ctx.llm), not OpenAI. Use it for situation briefs on a region, place and travel research, checking a fire or an earthquake, and any answer that is clearer on a map. To start, you need Thor 0.23.0 or newer, Node 24 or newer (God's Eye View documents 24.14 or later, or 26.x) and a running God's Eye View checkout; the public SDR layer needs gods-eye-view main at or after b361a25. Run thor plugins install godseye, thor plugins enable godseye and thor plugins doctor godseye, open the Eye Of Thor pane, and start a new chat. Try "Fly to Tokyo and switch to night vision" or "Any earthquakes above magnitude 5 in the last day?" (data questions work with the pane closed). The bundled skill is godseye:godseye-analyst. Photorealistic 3D tiles need CESIUM_ION_TOKEN, live ships need AISSTREAM_API_KEY and fires need FIRMS_MAP_KEY; the Google Maps, Mapillary and TomTom keys are optional. Set them as Thor secrets. Named-person search, face recognition and tracking of individuals are refused. Disclosure — processes: starts one node MCP child from your God's Eye View checkout, plus git rev-parse, node and systemctl --user children, all with a minimal environment. godseye_admin app_start, app_stop, app_restart and rebuild require confirm=true, are refused inside batch, may run systemctl --user on gods-eye-view.service, start Node on the checkout's vite.js, or run npm run build:panel in the checkout, and refuse a foreign listener. Disclosure — background work and prompt: runs loopback-only HUD bridge (127.0.0.1:18791) and live relay (127.0.0.1:18792) threads gated by a random token stored 0600 in plugin-data; registers a godseye.live-globe system-prompt section and ships the godseye-analyst skill; a pre_llm_call hook may add a short map line and queued watch alerts, whose feed titles are passed as quoted third-party text; an active area watch polls USGS, NASA FIRMS, OpenSky (falling back to api.adsb.lol when OpenSky fails), the local app, or Overpass/Nominatim from a daemon thread. Disclosure — network: place search, routes, isochrones, Wayback metadata and pin research call public services (Nominatim, Overpass and public Overpass mirrors, OSRM, Valhalla, Esri, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wikimedia and venue sites), and private-LAN service URLs are refused. Feed tools, including fire_check, and godseye_query op=sdr_receivers talk to your God's Eye View app, which itself fetches public third-party data feeds and the public SDR receiver directory. Disclosure — credentials: all provider credentials are declared in plugin.yaml requires_env and read only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret; no plugin dotenv reads, key-file installation or process-wide credential mutation. Browser-facing credentials are written only to gitignored mode-0600 runtime config, and server-only secrets never enter the pane. Disclosure — files and pane: overlay import and export stay under plugin-data/godseye/overlays and are not uploaded, and credential-named files are refused for import. Opening a pin drawer that has a clip loads a www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed or platform.twitter.com/embed iframe inside the sandboxed frame. Pane link opens and Ask Thor run only after a click on the pane's confirm bar. The pane backend adds a base tag, an opt-in UI flag, a Cesium worker shim, the overlay sidebar and Director bridge scripts, and the live agent script inside the sandboxed frame only.

name: gogogoogle
description: Hand bulk work to Google Antigravity's agy CLI as a worker agent on your Antigravity quota while Thor keeps its own model, then have a fresh agy conversation verify the result against the real files and git diff. Roles do, research and review; background jobs; resume after timeout; a verifier chain that skips models out of quota until their reset; a git check that fails read-only runs that changed files; per-run stats. Disclosure — Each `antigravity_delegate` call asks for Thor approval. `do` runs start agy with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so agy can run shell commands and change files outside the workdir. Research, review and verification runs deny writes, shell and non-Playwright MCP through agy session rules, which are not an OS sandbox: agy can still read files outside the workdir, and its headless browser (isolated profile) can reach your local network. Task text, files agy reads and a diff excerpt go to Google on your Antigravity account. Writes run logs and job records under the plugin data directory. Experimental, off unless configured: `antigravity_remote_review` sends one review-only task over the system `ssh` client (using your SSH agent and config; the plugin reads no key) to a second Windows machine you set up, where agy runs on that machine's Antigravity account. Tested on one Windows-to-Windows pair only.

name: gondola-provider
description: Gondola, a USDC-settled marketplace API for Venice AI inference

name: goneby
description: Retroactive project memory for LLM agents. Captures every turn into an encrypted per-project write-ahead log (zero tokens during work), then at project close walks the log backward from the shipped product — the oracle — keeping only entries that verifiably contributed; survivors are embedded (MRL-truncated) and stored in Valkey or Qdrant for semantic search in later sessions. General plugin: coexists with any memory provider instead of replacing it. Disclosure — On by default, GoneBy records every chat turn of each project (your messages, the assistant's replies and tool output text) into an encrypted log under your Thor profile's plugin-data folder. When you close a project, it sends the log to your configured model to choose which entries to keep, sends the kept text to the embedding endpoint you configure (default localhost), and stores it unencrypted in your Valkey or Qdrant database (default localhost). Turn capture off with the `auto_capture` setting or `/goneby gate off`.

name: gonogo
description: Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim. Disclosure — gonogo_report writes report JSON/HTML to the path the model supplies.

name: good-student
description: Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

name: google-workspace
description: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Contacts in one Thor workspace, with cross-app briefs and approval on every write. Disclosure — signs in with the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client through Thor (`thor auth add google-workspace:google`) and requests broad scopes (gmail.modify/send/compose, full Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar events, Contacts); tools and the Desktop page read and change mail, calendar, files, documents, sheets and contacts on that account, and sending, sharing, inviting, trashing and other writes ask for Thor approval first; a Changes tab keeps a local list (title and link) of the writes Thor made, pushed to every connected Desktop window.

name: googlehome
description: Google Home / Nest speaker as the mouth of a Thor profile: replies are cast over the Cast v2 protocol with zero third-party dependencies, voice arrives from the host microphone through Thor STT, and one speaker keeps one conversation. Adds googlehome_speak, googlehome_notify, googlehome_status, googlehome_volume and googlehome_devices, a Desktop page with push-to-talk and speaker controls, and thor googlehome CLI commands. Disclosure — talks to the Google Home / Nest speaker over the local network (Cast TLS port 8009 and mDNS) and serves each spoken reply as an MP3 from an unauthenticated media server on all interfaces, so devices on the same LAN can fetch recent reply clips; runs a token-gated loopback control API (proxied for Desktop through the dashboard) that can start agent turns without gateway pairing; and spawns PowerShell SAPI or edge-tts to synthesize speech.

name: govee
description: Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

name: graft
description: Persistent in-app features for Kanboard, with live data and reviewed task actions. Disclosure — Graft's Desktop half injects its own fixed renderer script into the Kanboard page open in Thor' Browser pane (after you allow it for that origin), and the graft_data tool sends a sample of your Kanboard task titles, projects and owners to the conversation's model; task changes are applied to Kanboard only after you confirm each one in the Graft pane.

name: greenlight
description: Greenlight is a Thor Agent plugin that puts you in control of xStocks trading. Thor can prepare a trade, but nothing is sent until you approve it. Ask for a trade and Greenlight shows what you pay, what you get, the fees, a simple risk check and your daily limit in a Thor Desktop window. Only after you approve do you get a link, or a QR code for your phone's wallet, to confirm the trade in your own wallet, so Greenlight never holds your keys or funds. Approve in the Thor Desktop window or with /greenlight in the terminal and chat apps. Optional daily and per-trade limits, a stock allowlist and a price-change tolerance. Every decision is kept in a tamper-evident history. Includes a no-wallet practice trade. Disclosure — crypto (Solana xStocks trading): talks to api.xstocker.com and xstocker.com, sending the wallet address, stock, amount, side and pay token for each quote and transaction signatures for status checks, through the official xStocker SDK (bundled unmodified in vendor/agent-sdk and used when Node.js 18+ is installed) or, without Node.js, directly over the same public HTTPS endpoints with Python's standard library; nothing is installed or downloaded at runtime and the plugin never updates itself; with Node.js, a short-lived node process per price request with a fixed command (node sdk-bridge.js), no shell and never an AI-chosen command; trades are released only after the user approves in the Desktop pane or with /greenlight approve (any user allowed to use that chat can run it) and are signed in the user's own wallet; writes only to <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/greenlight/ (or GREENLIGHT_DATA_DIR if set); reads no credentials; no telemetry; no Python dependencies; Node.js is optional.

name: greyridge-token-safety
description: Skill that runs a pre-trade safety check on Base ERC-20 tokens (honeypot/sellability, measured transfer tax, owner/mint/pause flags, liquidity, SAFE/CAUTION/AVOID verdict) by curling the Grey Ridge x402 API's free preview endpoint. Skill-only: no tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — the skill has the agent run `curl` against Grey Ridge Signals Group LLC's API (x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev, the same service as api.greyridgesignals.ai) with the token address and, for the swap gate, trade side and USD size; each response carries a paid URL that the skill tells the agent it can call with an x402 client (suggesting `npm i x402-fetch viem`), paying $0.01 USDC per call on Base from whatever wallet that client is given, and it mentions an unpinned `pip install git+https://github.com/rezearcher/greyridge-x402-tools` helper that the user installs themselves. Its verdict is a heuristic, not financial advice.

name: grimoire
description: Ask about your CSV, JSON, Parquet and SQLite files in plain words: DuckDB answers with one SQL query, Grimoire flags any number in the reply that no query produced, and a Data page gives charts, pivots, drill-down, data health and learning cards with no model tokens. Disclosure — reads only the data files you or the model name (CSV, JSON, Parquet, SQLite; files a message mentions are attached automatically), read-only, refusing files under ~/.thor, ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, ~/.aws, ~/.config, ~/.kube, ~/.docker and ~/Library unless allow_private_folders is set, with DuckDB's network, extension and other file access locked; copies SQLite files to a system temp folder as CSV; a pre_tool_call hook blocks raw reads of large data files by other tools; no network calls, shell commands, background processes, credentials or telemetry; stores saved queries, settings and HTML reports in its plugin data; installs the duckdb Python package.

name: grok-acp
description: xAI Grok subscription as a Thor model provider, driven over ACP stdio. Disclosure — spawns the vendor grok CLI found on PATH (grok agent over ACP stdio, plus grok models / grok login during setup) and drives your existing Grok subscription login; no API key is stored and Thor provider secrets are stripped from the child environment.

name: grok-bot-twin
description: Try Thor without leaving Grok. Gives each Grok desktop-app bot a Thor twin profile and a Desktop Twins page (conflicts, restore points); `thor twin demo` needs no Grok account. Name and description changes reach the twin in seconds; instructions are pasted by you or imported from the setup export the bot writes about itself (routines arrive paused, connectors as names only, its memories are dropped); skills travel through optional guided skill sync (a sync bot in your own Grok account); a bot's Grok memory and model setting are not copied. Several new twins are finished in one sheet: one model for all of them (model servers already set up in Thor listed first) and each twin's instructions from its own setup export, picked up from Downloads, a dropped file or skill sync's shared folder; optionally Thor does the Grok part with computer use, asking before every step. Optional and off by default: the same twins on your other Thor computers (macOS, Linux, Windows), linked once with a short code, with settings that follow by a fixed allowlist, skills, routines and end-to-end-encrypted memory each behind its own switch, and requests from one of your computers to a twin on another. Unofficial; not affiliated with xAI. Disclosure — Runs the user-installed external botport CLI (never bundled or downloaded; before it is ever run it is checked against the release SHA-256 digests shipped with the plugin or with `gh attestation verify` against hudsonwa/botport's release workflow, and its digest is pinned; `thor twin setup --allow-unattested` is a recorded opt-out), plus `gh` (for that check only) and `thor cron` (resume and pause on "Move routines to Thor", create --paused when importing a setup export), each with a minimal environment; while the new-twins sheet watches for setup exports (at most 15 minutes, every 4 s) the plugin lists your Downloads folder (that folder only: names, dates, sizes) and reads new .json, .txt or .md files of at most 2 MB there and, with skill sync set up, in the shared folder's exports/ (nothing moved or deleted; only digests are kept); it writes the model you choose into each twin profile's config.yaml; via botport it reads the Grok desktop app's bot list and the selected bots' local transcript files (capped, parsed for routine changes only) and writes the twin Thor profiles it manages; the plugin writes plugin-data/grok-bot-twin/, its own marked blocks in twin profiles' SOUL.md, plugins.enabled, a copy of itself and the allowlisted settings in each twin profile, a note per removed twin in profiles/.deleted/, and, only with their switches on, twins' skill files, memory files and cron jobs; botport keeps one owner-only key file per twin; it runs one background metadata-check/sync thread (default every 60 s) and one Grok-folder watch once a session starts, plus threads for the sharing features only while they are on; it sends no telemetry; it calls Thor' internal skill scanner (tools.skills_guard, fail-open) for the demo's skill preview. An optional pre_tool_call hook is active only for 30 minutes after you start "Let Thor do the Grok part" and tick that you approve each step: it makes Thor ask before every computer_use step and refuses other apps, other chats and other typed text; pictures of the Grok window then go to that chat's model provider. Network: none unless you switch on sharing; then the computer with the Grok app listens on ONE private address (its Tailscale address, else its home-network address; never all interfaces or a public one; TCP 18777) and your linked computers connect only to that address; linking proves a one-time 12-character link code (SPEKE; the code never travels) and every later call and answer is signed with a per-computer key; plain HTTP, encrypted by Tailscale on Tailscale, readable but not forgeable on a plain home network, except a twin's memory, which the plugin encrypts end to end. Besides that, the plugin connects only to the model servers already set up in your default Thor config.yaml, with one `GET <base_url>/models` each (at most 6, no key sent) when the new-twins sheet lists models; it never downloads a model (only `gh` reaches GitHub, for the attestation check). A request from another of your computers (off on each computer until switched on there) runs as one ordinary Thor chat turn of that twin, under that computer's own approval rules; a step that needs approval waits on that computer unless you chose there to let your own linked computers approve. An optional background helper (a launchd agent, systemd user unit or scheduled task of your own account, set up with launchctl, systemctl or schtasks; never root or SYSTEM) keeps a linked computer following while Thor is closed.

name: grokbot-staff
description: G.I.M.F. (Grok is my friend): a chief-of-staff and specialist team inside Thor (chief, research, design, writing, product, engineering — or a team you configure), plus an optional fail-closed bridge that hands long-running work to your own Grok Bot. Local staff answers with your current Thor model via ctx.llm. Slash commands /staff and /grokbot, a staff delegation backend for delegate_task, a bundled skill, and a Desktop pane for the roster, pending handoffs and recent jobs. The bridge does not call any Grok Bot API (there is none); it POSTs a JSON handoff to a webhook URL you set and/or writes handoffs/<id>.json in a folder you set, then collects results/<id>.json|.md|.txt or a pasted answer. Not an importer and not Grok Bot calling Thor — Thor delegating to Grok Bot. Disclosure — Answers staff tasks with your current Thor model through ctx.llm whenever a staff tool or slash command runs. When grokbot_delegate runs, POSTs the task as JSON only to the webhook URL you configure (stored as the GROKBOT_STAFF_WEBHOOK_URL secret; https only, http allowed for localhost; redirects refused) and/or writes handoffs/<id>.json in the inbox folder you set, then reads results/<id>.json|.md|.txt from that folder (symlinks and files over 2 MB ignored) and returns that text to the agent. A specialist you map to a Thor profile makes the `staff` delegation backend run delegated tasks as that profile, with its credentials. Job tasks, answers and collected results are stored in the plugin's own data folder. The Desktop pane polls a read-only /overview dashboard route every 10 seconds. No shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: groq-provider
description: Groq as a Thor model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `thor model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, Thor 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that Thor cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Thor' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: groundcontrol
description: Inspect deployment health, investigate deployment evidence and guide approved GroundControl operations from Thor.

name: grounded-recall
description: Before every model turn, searches your existing markdown notes (plain folders or an Obsidian vault), this profile's recent sessions and, opt-in, secret-manager item titles (never values), then injects a capped evidence block where each hit is labelled CURRENT, UNVERIFIED or HISTORICAL by freshness, plus a rule to search before answering "it doesn't exist / I have no access / I don't know". Every injection is logged per profile. No new memory store, works alongside any memory provider. Disclosure — on every turn reads the configured markdown folders, key-facts file and this profile's session store (state.db, read-only) and injects matching excerpts into the prompt; writes an audit log under the active Thor home; when secret-title search is configured it runs the user-configured secret-manager CLI in the background with a minimal environment (plus the variable names listed in `secret_titles_env`) and keeps only item titles; when the optional semantic re-rank is enabled it sends the user message and candidate note excerpts to the user-configured embeddings URL.

name: grounder
description: Grounder as the web_search and web_extract backend: each search is one call to one search provider, plus the live-data APIs (scores, prices, odds, flights and more) as you set each one, and returns one list of licensed results, each uncut. Free searches need no account. Connect a Grounder search key or `thor auth add grounder:grounder` for more. While Grounder is the web search backend, `/search` (the plugin's only command; on Slack, `/thor search`) opens a menu that chooses how Grounder searches, in three modes: Grounder optimized (the default), a Grounder preset (Fast, Cheap, Live, Deep, Code or Balanced) or Grounder direct (one provider you pick, and what it finds is what you get, even nothing), and sets each live-data API to Every call, Never or Grounder decides (the default), in every mode. A web_extract returns each page's text, read for the question of the search that found it, or the user's latest message when no search did. Adds grounder_search, for Grounder's own search options, and grounder_list_providers. Disclosure — each web_search query and web_extract page address is sent to api.grounder.net, passed on to the search provider and live-data APIs that answer it and to the service providers that help run a search, and kept under your Grounder account indefinitely (a free search has no account); when the model reads a page no Grounder search returned, your latest chat message (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as the ranking query; usage context is off by default, and only after `thor config set web.grounder.share_usage_context true` and a restart does a search also carry two random session and prompt tokens and the name of the model that asked; the first load in a profile makes Grounder the web_search and/or web_extract backend only where none is chosen yet, and writes Grounder's public OAuth client id to the profile's .env when no search key is set; answers that used Grounder get a Sources list and a "Searched with Grounder" line appended.

name: gsc-magic
description: Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Google Analytics 4, IndexNow and Core Web Vitals through GSC Magic's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.gscmagic.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): search analytics, URL inspection, sitemaps, GA4 reports, CrUX and PageSpeed, plus finished SEO reports (quick wins, traffic drops, content decay, cannibalization, CTR outliers, brand split, index health, Google vs Bing) with optional PNG charts. Bundles the gsc-magic workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to GSC Magic's hosted server (mcp.gscmagic.com) and reads the user's own connected Google, Bing and GA4 accounts; calls count toward the user's GSC Magic plan and are logged (tool, site, status, time) for 30 days in the user's dashboard; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Write tools (sitemaps, site management, Bing URL submission, IndexNow) work only on paid plans with write mode turned on, and the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Thor's connect timeout instead of hanging. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with thor mcp add gsc-magic --url https://mcp.gscmagic.com/mcp --auth oauth (or a token header) and keep the skill.

name: gsc-wizard
description: Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster, Google Analytics 4, Merchant Center and Yandex Webmaster through GSC Wizard's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.gscwizard.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): 130+ tools for search analytics, ranking changes, anomaly and change-point detection, content decay, cannibalization, CTR curves, URL inspection and indexing tracking, sitemaps, IndexNow, Core Web Vitals, migrations, forecasts, GA4 reports and Merchant Center listings. Bundles 34 workflow skills (site audit, traffic drop, weekly report, quick wins, content decay, indexing health and more). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to GSC Wizard's hosted MCP server (mcp.gscwizard.com), which reads the Google Search Console, GA4, Merchant Center, Bing Webmaster and Yandex Webmaster accounts you connected to GSC Wizard and logs each call (tool, property, status, duration; arguments of write calls only) for 7 days; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned commit. Write tools (site/tag management, IndexNow and sitemap submission, URL inspection batches, shared reports and client access, redirect mappings, deletes) exist; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+), which opens a browser and a localhost callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Requires a GSC Wizard paid plan or trial.

name: guild
description: Shared skill library for a team's Thor agents, or for one person's machines and profiles, kept in a git repository the team controls. A skill an agent saved is scrubbed of API keys, home folder paths, e-mail addresses and private IPs, pushed as a proposal branch, and merged only after a teammate approves it from the CLI, TUI or Desktop. Each member's agent then loads approved skills read-only. If an agent tries to edit a team skill, a pre_tool_call hook refuses the edit and tells it to use guild_propose. Thor Desktop gets a Guild page to review diffs and approve or decline. Commands: `thor guild init|join|propose|review|show|approve|reject|revert|log` and `/guild`. Disclosure — runs local `git` subprocesses (repository hooks disabled, no terminal prompts, only the environment variables git and ssh need) that fetch from and push to the remote you configure, using your existing git credentials; contacts nothing else and stores no credentials. Only the files of a skill you propose, or that your agent proposes after the approval prompt, leave the machine, with your member name in the commit. Optional background sync at session start (auto_sync_minutes, default 15, 0 turns it off); a sync moves a local skill identical to the team copy, or your own accepted proposal, into the plugin's backups folder. In a solo guild proposals are committed straight to main with no review. `init` and `join` add the library folder to the profile's skills.external_dirs and `leave` removes it. The write check reads tool arguments and does not inspect execute_code. The reviewer list is enforced by the plugin only; use branch protection on the git host for a server-side guarantee.

name: gurusup-brain
description: Your company's memory in Thor: search decisions, people, customers and projects across every source your team connected to Gurusup (Slack, HubSpot, Notion, uploaded documents and more), with the sources behind each answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1, no local code and no API keys. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Gurusup's server at mcp.brain.gurusup.com under the signed-in Gurusup account (OAuth via `thor mcp add gurusup-brain --url https://mcp.brain.gurusup.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401), and answers are limited to what that account can see; write tools save knowledge to the company's Gurusup workspace (add_company_knowledge, skills_publish) and send issue reports or feedback to Gurusup (report_issue, send_feedback), and request_human_info can message a teammate on Slack or phone them when its dispatch flag is set.

name: ha-sidebar-navigator
description: Full-power sidebar navigator & uncapped project/session explorer for Thor Desktop. Bypasses the 3-session overview cap with searchable, scrollable project trees and timeline view. Disclosure — browses and acts on sessions of every Thor profile and connection you pick (rename, archive, delete with confirmation, branch, move to a project, create, including bulk archive/delete/move of selected sessions; renaming or exporting a session that is not open briefly resumes it on that backend and closes it again), exports a session's full transcript as a downloaded JSON file on request, and keeps its own pins, colours, unread marks, tags and saved views in its plugin storage, mirroring pin and colour changes to the Desktop sidebar for the profile the window is showing.

name: habit
description: Learns which commands you already approve, proposes an allowlist entry after a few matching approvals (the exact command, or any-container docker stop|restart), tells you once in the chat where you approved, and only writes it to Thor's command_allowlist after you run /habit accept. Wipes, download-and-execute pipes, git push and secret paths are never proposed, and /habit undo or /habit uninstall take every entry back. Disclosure — learns from your approval answers to dangerous shell commands in a local plugin database (plugin approval rules and other non-command prompts are never learned, and only the owner's approvals count); in enforce mode (off by default) it proposes command_allowlist entries (the exact approved command, or `docker stop|restart *` / `docker compose stop|restart *` for any container or service) and writes them to this profile's config.yaml through Thor's config load/save only when you run /habit accept (owner_ids-locked on messaging gateways); when it creates a proposal it posts one message into the conversation where you approved through ctx.post_message (once per proposal, from a short-lived thread, never retried; turn off with notify: false; in-process only); an accepted entry waves through every command it matches, including ones Thor flags as dangerous; /habit undo and /habit uninstall remove only the entries Habit added; no network calls, no credentials, no background process.

name: habits
description: Habits gives Thor reflexes: the tool calls and small decisions it repeats, grouped into one file of steps that runs with no model turn between the steps (the advanced llm step is the one exception); decisions go to a small typed model (Jev). "Is Thor OK?": 41 s when Thor works it out, 2.7 s when the reflex answers with its six checks (medians of real chats, 10 November; the fast path needs your yes and a Jev key). A reflex has four kinds of step (do, check, ask, use) and ends done, or handed back with what is left. The dream re-reads the history Thor already keeps, with no model call, and proposes reflexes for what comes back. A reflex acts on its own only after your yes, with two exceptions named below. Try without a key: thor habits run thor-health. Disclosure — hooks read each user message, reply and tool call; the dream reads Thor's local session history (read only, 60 days) at most once a day (dream: manual stops it) and calls no model. Learning defaults to suggest: nothing is practised or run for you until you say try; learning: auto lets learned reflexes act with no question. A list of your reflexes (2,400 characters at most) is added to the system prompt, and Thor may run any shipped example by name without a yes, for real (six only read; tidy-downloads moves files inside ~/Downloads). An automatic request habit can answer a message itself, without a model call, and a habit that starts on its skill runs when Thor loads that skill. A read-only request habit you explicitly asked for starts automatic at once. Reflex commands run through Thor's own terminal and tools under Thor's approval rules. thor-health sends one HEAD request to github.com and reads ~/.thor gateway state, logs and disk use; other examples reach api.github.com, hn.algolia.com and the pages you or Thor name. With TYPESAFE_API_KEY set, decision questions go to TypeSafe Jev (api.typesafe.ai), else to your own Thor model. Once a message habit exists, each non-slash message of 2,000 characters or less goes there with your habit names and descriptions, and a reflex's ask steps send the text the reflex read (file names, page text). Saving a scheduled habit (every 5 minutes at most often) writes $THOR_HOME/scripts/habits-<name>.sh and a Thor cron job at once, before any yes, and is refused inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true; thor habits cleanup removes every habits-* job and script. Runs and traces are stored unencrypted in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/habits/. No telemetry. Private Thor imports are read-only, each with a fallback (docs/SAFETY.md §10).

name: habitude
description: Read-only journal reflection skill with opt-in local Vault MCP setup. Disclosure — after you run the bundled setup and add its local stdio MCP server yourself, the plugin reads Markdown notes from the one Vault directory you name (read-only), keeps its settings in ~/.config/habitude-agent/config.json and a search index in ~/.cache/habitude-agent/ (outside the Thor profile), and returned journal excerpts are sent to your configured model provider; it makes no network calls of its own.

name: hackathon-judge
description: Source-linked Thor hackathon and catalog preflight with explicit human review gates Disclosure — the optional `validate` action runs `thor plugins validate` on the plugin directory the agent names, through Thor's terminal tool, which imports and executes that candidate plugin's code; it is gated only by a `trusted_code` flag the agent sets, and no approval prompt appears for that command.
