The default audit is static and read-only, with no network calls.

name: hackertube
description: Source-backed media discovery with existing Thor providers and a profile-local library. Disclosure — each explicit Search sends your question and candidate metadata to the Thor auxiliary model you pick and your Thor web-search backend (this may spend credits). It also queries hn.algolia.com, itunes.apple.com, openlibrary.org, librivox.org and, with your key, www.googleapis.com (YouTube) and api.podcastindex.org. Searches run in a Python worker subprocess that re-launches the `thor` CLI from PATH with Thor's environment (YOLO vars stripped). An hourly local thread purges expired records from plugin-data/hackertube/profile.db.

name: hades-coding-workflows
description: Coding workflow skills — dual-model harness, subagent-driven development, and implementation planning patterns for Thor Agent

name: half-life
description: Freshness labels for supported read-only tool results.

name: hallway-test
description: Five simulated people with code-enforced limits (low vision, screen reader, colour blindness, tremor) usability-test your web page in real browsers and report who got stuck and why. Disclosure — the hallway_test tool opens the page you or the agent name in headless Chromium (Playwright) and five simulated testers browse it, sending page text and screenshots to the model set for 'Hallway Test people' (your main model if unset); only http/https pages are opened, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused and private-network hosts only when allow_private_hosts is on (loopback always allowed), with each navigation redirect checked (subresource redirects are logged, not blocked); the bundled demo is served on 127.0.0.1; reports, screenshots and replays are saved under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/hallway-test/; no telemetry.

name: handflow
description: Manus-style planning flow — the agent plans in steps and marks them as it works, with a live desktop pane.

name: handydandy
description: Session-size notices and structured handoffs for long Thor sessions. Disclosure — writes state.json, state.lock, events.log and short-lived atomic-save temp files under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/handydandy/ (profile and session ids, paths, thresholds and error details; no conversation text); asks the agent to write handoff files to handoff_dir (default <THOR_HOME>/handoffs/), which may hold work details from the conversation; optionally appends one row per completed handoff to a session_log_csv the owner sets (off by default). Reads its own state, the first byte and modification time of recorded handoff files, plugin settings via ctx.get_config, and THOR_HOME plus deprecated HANDYDANDY_<KEY> fallback environment variables. No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry; it does not auto-approve tools or change safety settings.

name: hardlight-ui
description: Frontend design guidance with sixteen original style grammars, twelve craft references, dated modern-web capability recipes, explicit direction context, and stateless tools for bounded source inspection, color contrast, and navigation task paths. Disclosure — the hardlight_inspect tool reads frontend source files (.html, .css, .js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx, .vue, .svelte and similar; at most 500 files and 8 MiB) under any local directory the model names, skipping hidden, symlinked, vendor/build and secret-named paths, and returns their design tokens and findings to the model; the plugin adds a short system-prompt section naming its tools to every session; the tools make no network calls, run no subprocesses and write no files; the optional hardlight browser command, run by hand from a shell, launches a locally installed Chromium against loopback or file:// pages only and writes its report to the output folder you give it.

name: harness-story
description: Plain-English session storyteller and Desktop workspace pane: reconstructs what you asked, the hidden Thor startup context load (skills, connectors, plugins, tools, memory), why the model chose each tool or pivoted after errors, and a 5-bucket context window bar synchronized with an auto-scrolling Chronicle. Disclosure — records 12 observer hooks (including short previews of your prompts, tool arguments and tool results) as JSONL under the plugin's data directory, writes a story JSON/HTML for every session by default, reads `state.db` read-only and the names of MCP servers, plugins and toolsets from `config.yaml`; optional narrative synthesis posts a session digest to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure (none by default). No third-party cloud calls, no shell execution, no stored credentials, no self-updater.

name: harnmem
description: Cross-harness long-term memory for Thor: injects a byte-stable memory snapshot each turn, exposes harnmem_write/search/read/forget/status tools, and can extract new memories when a session ends. Memories are plain Markdown under ~/.harnmem, shared with the pi, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, DSH, Grok, Cursor and omp adapters; the engine itself never opens a network connection. Disclosure — with auto-extract enabled the plugin sends the session transcript to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure, runs a local Node.js child process for every memory operation, and spawns a short-lived detached extractor at session end. The extraction key is read through Thor' secret scope; the plugin collects no telemetry.

name: hashference-provider
description: Hashference as a Thor model provider (`--provider hashference`, or Hashference in `thor model`): open and frontier models on one balance, funded by mining, QUAI, Qi or staking. Each model's real limits come from Hashference's catalog: the hosted models accept 98,304 input tokens inside a 163,840-token window and cap output at 8,192, so Thor compresses before an oversized-input refusal; models that cannot call tools are left out of the model list. Disclosure — model provider; chat requests (full prompts) go to https://hashference.com/v1 (or your configured base_url) using HASHFERENCE_API_KEY read by Thor; the plugin itself only sends an unauthenticated GET of the public model catalog (/v1/models), cached ten minutes.

name: hashtree-git
description: Git publishing and independent cloning using local Nostr keys and Hashtree. Instruction-only skill; requires separately installed htree and git-remote-htree, invokes shell commands, and can publish repository history. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs git, htree and git-remote-htree in the terminal (installed separately by the user, or by the agent from the project's release binaries or an unpinned `cargo install hashtree-cli git-remote-htree`); a push publishes the repository's history and author metadata to Hashtree storage servers and Nostr relays, publicly unless a link-visible or private URL is used; the CLI creates and stores a local signing key, and an optional htree daemon keeps running until stopped.

name: hathor-catchup
description: Check a child's vaccination card against a sourced national schedule (Egypt, Sudan, Syria, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Eritrea, South Sudan, WHO) and get the missing doses and a dated catch-up plan. Deterministic engine with no model or network calls; a schedule guard (pre_llm_call, post_tool_call, transform_llm_output) keeps vaccine answers tied to the tool and its source. Disclosure — no network calls, model calls, shell commands, credentials or stored data; a guard hook adds a short instruction to vaccine-related turns and appends a footer to those replies (the schedule source when the tool ran, a warning when it did not). The "checked" footer means the tool ran in that turn, not that the reply's wording was verified. Schedules are bundled snapshots (last updated 2025-12 to 2026-04) and some rule tables are marked pending physician sign-off in the tool output. Decision support, not medical advice.

name: headroom
description: Keeps Thor alive on small machines (1-4 GB VPS, Raspberry Pi). Heavy terminal jobs (package installs, builds, test suites, compilers, browsers, nested agents) wait for a machine-wide slot and enough free RAM, run inside their own memory-capped systemd --user scope with a raised OOM score, get single-worker flags where a stable one exists (jest --runInBand, pytest -n 0, make -jN, cargo -j N, Node heap cap), and are stopped by a watchdog if the host nears OOM or Thor' own cgroup starts stalling. Thor stays outside the scope, and the tool result tells the model the cap, the peak and whether the kernel killed the job, so it retries lighter. Adds headroom_status, /headroom and thor headroom status|events|explain|selftest. Disclosure — Linux only for enforcement; runs busctl --user (StartTransientUnit, AttachProcessesToUnit) and systemctl --user kill/reset-failed for its own headroom-*.scope units with a reduced environment (PATH, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS), plus one sleep placeholder process per isolated job; reads /proc meminfo, PSI and stat/status/cmdline/cgroup of the user's own processes and cgroup files of its scopes and Thor' cgroup; raises oom_score_adj of job processes; kills only processes inside its own scopes (or a tracked job's process group without systemd) when the watchdog fires; rewrites heavy commands before approval so the approved command is what runs; writes events to <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/headroom/events.jsonl and slot locks to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/thor-headroom (or an owner-checked thor-headroom-<uid> directory in the system temp dir); no network, no telemetry, no credentials; reads tools.interrupt.is_interrupted (guarded) so /stop cancels a queued command.

name: health-data
description: Local health and daily-context data store for Thor.

name: health-insights
description: Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills that drive the separately installed health-insights command line tool (installed from the plugin's own pinned copy); the plugin itself contains no executable. Works on a self-hosted HealthRelay or Health Bridge receiver database. Disclosure - it handles sensitive health data, so use a local model or one you trust; personal integrations (medication counts, model wording) are off by default. Disclosure — the skills run a separately installed health-insights CLI that reads your HealthRelay or Health Bridge SQLite database read-only and keeps imported lab and ECG results under ~/.local/share/health-insights; the health values it prints are sent to whichever model provider your Thor session uses.

name: healthcare
description: Local-first personal health records: encrypted on-device Vault (AES-GCM) for vitals, medications, activities, emotions, sleep, encounters, diagnosis mentions, medication plans and reminders, served through a Keychain-paired local daemon with 24 scoped MCP tools. Zero-config first run: the plugin bootstraps Vault + daemon + agent pairing automatically under PLUGIN_DATA. Engine pinned to an immutable PyPI release (healthcare-mcp==0.2.1) over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), macOS only, Python 3.11+. Zero network by default; the optional LLM report-import endpoint stays off unless the user configures it. Approval-gated deletes, tamper-evident audit chain. Disclosure — personal health record-keeping, not medical advice (the skill forbids diagnoses and dosage changes); first run has uvx fetch healthcare-mcp==0.2.1 from PyPI; the optional report-import path posts report images to Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-max) unless HEALTHCARE_LLM_ENDPOINT points elsewhere, and only when HEALTHCARE_LLM_API_KEY is set.

name: healthrelay
description: Read-only access to your own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one stdio MCP server (ten read-only tools, including intake evidence; no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills for setup, review and troubleshooting. Requires your own HealthRelay receiver (health-bridge) and an iPhone app you sign yourself; the plugin ships neither. Disclosure — exposes your Apple Health data, read-only, from your own receiver database to whichever model you run, so use a local model or one you trust with health data; runs the separately installed health-bridge binary from PATH; the setup skill can install the receiver from the author's git tag with uv tool install.

name: heartbeat2
description: Give your agent a working life between your messages. Put it in charge of something and it keeps working on it on its own time. A role is a standing responsibility with a charter, a notebook the agent keeps between turns and a rhythm it sets itself, and it doesn't expire on a timer. Turn on own time and the agent gets regular turns of its own: it looks at its desk (its roles, what's due, what it noticed, the budget left) and decides what to do. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) can also arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Thor event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions) that cost no model call until something changes. Every wake is a turn in the same messaging conversation, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Quiet work counts: a silent turn that makes progress is real work, and only wakes that keep finding nothing to do slow down, then pause and ask once. The guardrails are budgets you set: turns per day, an optional daily cost limit, turns per role, messages per day, the unanswered mute and quiet hours. They hold back messages and spending, not initiative, and the agent can tighten its own limits but never widen yours. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire. It delivers to messaging-gateway DMs by default (group and topic chats too when dm_only is off) and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Ships the plugin skill `heartbeat2:heartbeat2-report-problem`, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — wakes, watchers, roles and own-time turns run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes, watchers and roles itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; roles have no expiry, and the agent's recurring wakes and roles keep running turns during quiet hours, while the unanswered mute is on and after the daily message cap (only their messages are held), up to the daily turn cap and the optional daily_cost_limit_usd (no cost limit by default); keep-warm (off unless you send /pulse warm on in a chat) runs a short silent turn on that chat's model just before its prompt cache expires, while you have written there within keep_warm_idle_hours (12 h by default), billed like any message but outside the daily turn cap and daily_cost_limit_usd; own-time turns (off by default, own_time_hours) run without an assigned task; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote <url>` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Thor blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.

name: heats
description: Your tests, not the model, decide when a fix is done. A pre_verify referee runs the repo's check when the agent edited code and is about to finish, and sends it back with the real test output if the check fails. When one attempt is not enough, heats_run races N attempts in separate git worktrees (subagents launched through the public lifecycle API, kept inside their worktree by a tool_request middleware); failing attempts are restarted with the measured output, attempts that edit tests cannot win, and the winner is applied with one call. Desktop pane with live lanes and an Apply winner button. Disclosure: the referee runs your check command in your checkout after code edits, only in repos you approved with /heats trust (none by default; it will not run a check whose defining files the agent edited in that turn); heats_run asks for your approval before running a model-supplied or untrusted check; checks get a minimal environment (no provider keys); races create and remove git worktrees and branches under <repo>/.heats/, run the check in each worktree (never for an attempt that edited what the check runs) and launch N subagents on your delegation model (cost scales with N); saves reports and patches under plugin-data/heats; Desktop routes under /api/plugins/heats/; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.

name: hebe-longevity
description: Personal Longevity Intelligence for Thor, built on Insilico Medicine's open PLSI toolbelt (MIT). Reads nine routine blood markers from a confirmed CSV or typed panel, calculates Blood PhenoAge, shows trends and formula drivers across blood draws, and drafts safety-screened research plans challenged by a separate model call before only the user can start a plan. Includes a Hebe page and optional theme in Thor Desktop plus a chat result card. Disclosure — PhenoAge, trend and local HTML reports make no network or model calls. The Desktop page loads Cormorant Garamond and Montserrat from Google Fonts (falls back to system fonts offline). Planning tools run a pinned subset of the PLSI CLI as a child process of Thor' Python with fixed argument lists (no shell) and a minimal environment, and query PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA, RxNav (NIH), doi.org or Evipedia with topic queries and plan action names only. The challenger runs through Thor' own auxiliary LLM task (auxiliary.hebe_challenger); Thor itself sends chat and tool outputs to the user's configured model. Data is stored under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/hebe-longevity. No telemetry, self-updater or background daemon. Research prototype, not medical advice.

name: heirpros
description: Estimate the research hours for a US probate heir search (locating missing and unknown heirs for an estate) through HeirPros' free MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://heirpros.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): hours from the number of known and estimated unknown heirs (1.5 base hours + 1 per heir, the same formula as the heirpros.com calculator), plus general information about HeirPros' heir search service. Hours only, no pricing. Bundles the heir-search-estimate skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to heirpros.com, run by HeirPros, which does not store or email what is sent. Both tools are annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor would ask before any tool that is not. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: helm
description: A redesigned Thor Desktop. A Desk home page (greeting and crew status, a prompt that hands work to any bot, Continue, Needs you, Today's scheduled jobs); pending tool approvals and questions from every bot's live chats answered in one place, on the Desk and in a sidebar pane, only on your click; a Session pane with the focused chat's live task plan; a themeable redesign layer across the app (three bases, seven accents, type, corners, density) on a Customize look page; status everywhere (titlebar, session rows, status bar); and a Bots board of rendered robots (191 Blender-rendered PNG layers) that become each bot's Thor avatar. Disclosure — desktop half uses only Desktop SDK areas and public gateway calls the app itself makes: host.profiles.list and host.listPersistedSessions (held in memory), session.active_list, approval.pending, session.history (the focused chat's plan), cron.manage action list only (never adds, pauses or removes a job), host.onEvent for approval/clarify/todo events; approval.respond and clarify.respond only when you click Approve, Allow session, Deny or Send; profiles.create only from New bot; host.restartGateway only from the restart button on the flat-robots notice; with "Robots as Thor avatars" on (the default) it checks each bot's avatar once a minute (profiles.get_asset) and sets a robot with profiles.set_asset on any bot with no avatar or with Bot Mode's 160 px face, replacing Bot Mode's face each time it returns, and leaves other images alone (an uploaded image exactly 160 or 256 px wide is mistaken for a generated one); sends a chat message only from the Desk prompt on Enter or Send. The theme layer is the SDK theme customCSS and selects the app's data-slot names in CSS only (validate warns on these selectors); JS never queries, observes or edits app markup. Writes its own ctx.storage and, when changed in its settings, the app's sessionListDensity and chatTextScale. The dashboard half is a read-only FastAPI router serving the bundled PNGs (fixed-pattern names, no writes, no Thor internals imported). The agent half registers nothing. No third-party network calls, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-updater. tools/render/ holds the Blender source that produced the PNGs (not run by Thor).

name: helper
description: Desktop page for people who are new to Thor: a Dashboard with nine set-up cards (what each thing is, the steps from the Thor docs, a button to its place in Thor) and Helper, a small character with its own conversation window that answers questions about Thor in plain words, from lines checked against the Thor docs. Disclosure — reads, through Thor's read-only Desktop calls, whether a model is ready and its name, the list of profiles and each profile's skills, the connected chat apps, and the main profile's chat list (with previews, only to tell whether a first chat exists); in Helper's set-up conversation it also reads the main profile's SOUL.md text and the list of scheduled jobs; never reads .env, auth.json or config files. When its fixed rules are not sure of an answer it sends the typed message, the last few lines of the Helper conversation and chunks of the Thor docs to the person's own configured model (llm.oneshot), and once per set-up conversation it sends a fixed "Reply with exactly: OK" check when a model is set; both spend their model credit; no tools run and nothing is saved to their chats. Keeps a name, a few answers, the Done marks and the last 50 lines of the Helper conversation as plain text in Desktop plugin storage, shared by all profiles on the computer and not removed on uninstall. Only when the person presses its buttons, 'Do it for me' runs Thor's own importer (thor import-agent <agent> --dry-run, then thor import-agent <agent> --yes, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenClaw only) and, if the importer is missing and the person agrees, thor plugins install agent-importers --enable; no other command can run and the model cannot write one. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no self-update. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js, no __init__.py): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: hephaestus
description: Ask for a plugin and your own agent writes it, checked by the official validator and doctor; you approve each check, because it runs the draft's code. It installs disabled; only you enable it. Disclosure — forge_check imports each draft's Python and calls its register() on this machine, outside the sandbox, after you approve that exact draft (no prompt if approvals are off or YOLO is on); runs the thor CLI (fixed argument list, no shell, minimal environment) to validate, doctor, enable, disable and remove plugins; writes forged plugins under THOR_HOME/plugins and drafts and snapshots in its data folder; a pre_tool_call guard blocks the agent from enabling plugins. No network, no telemetry, no LLM calls.

name: herd
description: Keep one Thor across every machine. Settings, skills, memory and SOUL.md follow the user between devices, while each machine keeps what belongs to it — Docker paths, ports, bot tokens. `config.yaml` is merged per key against a stored base, with machine-bound paths resolved locally before any comparison, so a pull cannot delete the section the machine is running on. API keys never sync: herd does not open `.env`. The store is encrypted with a key stretched from a recovery code before anything leaves the device; every pull leaves a restorable backup and `thor sync undo` puts it back, removing files the pull added. Ships a per-device manifest store over any folder or git remote, three agent tools (`sync_status`, `sync_diff`, `sync_now`), session hooks that pull at start and push at end in interactive sessions, and a `thor sync` CLI. Pairing is one command that prints a 20-character code, valid once for 15 minutes, written as a sealed `pairing.json` in the store folder. A machine that can see that folder reads and deletes it. The file is not pushed to a git remote, because it wraps the recovery code and would remain in history after deletion; a machine that only has the git remote joins with `thor sync join <git-url> --code HERD-…`. Disclosure — reads the profile's config, memory, SOUL.md and skills and writes the ones that changed; credential-named keys in config.yaml and `mcp_servers.*.env`/`headers` stay on each machine; never reads `.env`, `auth.json` or `state.db`; in interactive sessions the session hooks pull and apply other machines' settings, skills, memory and SOUL.md at session start and push at session end without a prompt (turn off with `auto_pull`/`auto_push`); `sync_now` asks for approval and is blocked under cron and other non-interactive sessions, where the hooks also skip; cron jobs sync only on machines paired with `--cron`; the store is any folder or git remote the user names, and nothing is sent anywhere else.

name: hermagotchi
description: Co-op virtual pets for Thor: raise a pet, fight deterministic async battles, earn Bits, unlock cosmetics up to mythic tier, climb a seasonal leaderboard, and chat, DM, challenge and taunt other players in a native pane in the Thor web app and Desktop (Habitat, Battle, Shop, Leaderboard and Social tabs plus a persistent lobby rail). Thor gets 8 composable tools (hermagotchi_status, hermagotchi_pet, hermagotchi_goals, hermagotchi_challenge, hermagotchi_battle, hermagotchi_shop, hermagotchi_social, hermagotchi_meta). Disclosure — by default the tools run an offline practice simulation (in-memory, no network, reset on Thor restart). Only when the owner sets the network_enabled plugin setting do they act on the real game server, using the device session the pane paired; that state persists server-side. hermagotchi_status health/me report the active backend. Agent autonomy (autonomy-gated game actions such as practice battles) and agent chat need their own settings and are off by default; the agent can never buy items, and pet care/adopt are not gated by the autonomy setting. The network, autonomy and chat settings can also be switched on by the HERMAGOTCHI_NETWORK_ENABLED, HERMAGOTCHI_AGENT_AUTONOMY_ENABLED and HERMAGOTCHI_AGENT_CHAT_ENABLED environment variables. Network traffic goes over HTTPS only (plain HTTP is refused except loopback) to the game API base URL the user configures (the optional hosted API at api.hermagotchi.rizz.click run by the maintainer, or a self-hosted server from docs/deploy). It sends pet, battle, shop and social actions and, if agent chat is enabled, lobby messages, DMs and taunts, which that server stores; other players' messages come back to the agent marked as third-party text. The pairing session token lives in a 0600 file under Thor plugin data and is never returned by tools or logged. Online, hermagotchi_status op=pair refuses user_code/revoke_device_id (unsupported_online); approve and revoke stay human pane actions so lobby/DM prompt injection cannot attach a stranger's device. The dashboard tab renders with the dashboard SDK's React and authedFetch, used only for same-origin plugin asset and API routes; the Desktop pane uses ctx.rest only (no remote code, no host-token access). No hooks, no middleware, no subprocesses, no inbound ports, and no secrets are requested (requires_env is empty). The dashboard plugin API only proxies an allowlisted set of game routes for the pane.

name: hermeneus
description: Live translation for Thor. Hermeneus captures the audio playing on your Mac, so it works with any app that plays sound. Examples are YouTube, Twitch and X Spaces in the browser, Discord, meeting apps and podcast apps. Verified on real audio: YouTube live in Google Chrome. Captures the audio playing on your Mac (one app, or all system audio except Hermeneus) through a Core Audio process tap on macOS 14.2+, transcribes it with ElevenLabs Scribe v3 Live, translates each line with your own Thor model and shows live subtitles in a Desktop pane, a floating overlay above other apps, the terminal (thor hermeneus run), /translate, or an opt-in 127.0.0.1 page for OBS; spoken translation with ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 is opt-in, and language, mode, voice, output and source change while a session runs. Listening covers 100 languages and speaking covers 32. Disclosure: streams the captured audio to ElevenLabs (wss://api.elevenlabs.io) with your ELEVENLABS_API_KEY while a session runs (it stops sending after about 10 s of digital silence and resumes with the first sound), and sends the translated text there too when spoken translation is on; lists your account's voices with GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v2/voices (voices command and the pane's voice picker); sends each committed line plus up to 3 earlier lines (context_segments, 0 to 10) to your configured model through ctx.llm under its own auxiliary task, live_translate (doctor --test-model sends one tiny extra request); /translate start and /translate set --source are refused from chat platforms unless allow_remote_start is on (default off); needs the macOS System Audio Recording permission for the app that runs Thor (Microphone for the fallback); the setup's Allow system audio and Check again, the doctor, and the pane's Doctor tab every time it opens, play a 440 Hz test tone for about half a second through a short-lived player subprocess, on BlackHole or VB-Cable when installed, otherwise quietly on the default output while the tap mutes it (--no-audio-check skips it); the process tap runs one capture worker subprocess per session with a minimal environment, stopped with the session, on unload and at exit; the floating overlay is a separate Python process while it is open, with the same minimal environment, and keeps six files under plugin-data/hermeneus/overlay/: lock, settings.json, theme.json, positions.json, positions.json.lock (empty, locked while positions.json is written) and overlay.log; positions.json is written through a short-lived .positions-*.tmp file in the same folder, by the overlay and by the process that serves the pane's overlay routes; the pane's first-run setup writes plugin-data/hermeneus/setup.json (the last audio check result, no audio, no key) and audio-check.running while that check captures (removed when it ends); settings.json, theme.json and setup.json are each written to a short-lived .tmp file beside them and renamed over the file at once; settings you change (in the pane, in Settings or with thor hermeneus overlay-page) are saved by Thor in its config.yaml; one session at a time on its own thread, reached through a Unix domain socket (mode 0600) under its plugin-data; no TCP port unless you turn on the overlay page, which listens on 127.0.0.1:47821 (overlay_page_port) only, behind a per-session token and a Host check; runs /usr/sbin/system_profiler SPAudioDataType and /bin/ps (read only, absolute paths, argument lists, minimal environment) to check audio routes and name the app in the permission message, and /usr/bin/open with the System Settings privacy address (x-apple.systempreferences:...Privacy_ScreenCapture) when you press Open System Settings in the setup, which changes nothing; the fallback reads a virtual device (BlackHole 2ch or VB-Cable) that you install yourself, never bundled or downloaded; subtitles stay in memory (last 200 lines) and no audio or transcript is written to disk; no telemetry. Platform status: macOS is tested on real audio; Windows support is implemented and reviewed against documentation, not yet run on a Windows machine, so this entry lists macOS only (Windows preview: docs/windows.md).

name: hermetic
description: Status-bar popover for Thor Desktop with three views: Costs (spend, cache, pricing drift, OpenRouter provider routing), AAI (skill changes, ratings, tests and replays) and HDR (a guard for risky tool calls, hooks, destinations, sensitive paths, what runs on its own). Disclosure — reads this profile's sessions (and other profiles' when you pick them) to audit tool calls, paths and hosts; can edit and save config.yaml and rewrite skill files when you ship or revert a version, and once you give background tasks your routing rules, rewrites those tasks' entries in config.yaml by itself (from a background thread, at most once a minute) when the main provider changes; adds your data_collection and zdr routing rules to requests sent to Nous Portal; AAI replays and judge runs resend conversation context and tool definitions to OpenRouter with your OpenRouter key and incur cost (Nous Portal profiles are refused); HDR lists listening TCP ports via ps/lsof; HDR's guard (off by default) checks each tool call through a pre_tool_call hook and, when you turn it on, holds calls Thor does not check itself (reading keys and logins, writing startup items or key places Thor does not list) and asks you in its own card, blocking without an answer in time (6 seconds inside Thor' plugin hook limit: 24 seconds by default, 120 seconds when that limit is off) or at once when hermetic is not open, or blocks them outright; the guard is a best-effort match on the paths a call names, not a sandbox; questions from every profile wait in the default profile's hermetic folder; HDR also lists shell and gateway hooks and flags hook scripts edited after approval, keeping a copy of each script to compare; Costs reads public model price lists (OpenRouter, and hopscotchlabs.ai model pages for models a profile is billed for through Hopscotch) and, at most once a minute, asks Thor for the profile provider's account report (OpenRouter usage and limits, Anthropic and OpenAI Codex plan windows, Nous credits and spend cap), with Thor looking up the credential, and reads OpenRouter workspace and guardrail budgets itself with the profile's OpenRouter key, sent only to OpenRouter.

name: hermis
description: Disclosure — Windows only, not crypto. Runs a background WebSocket server on 127.0.0.1 (ephemeral port + session token) in a daemon thread. On the first autopilot or surface draw it launches a bundled transparent always-on-top Electron overlay as a detached process via npm (first run executes `npm ci` from the committed lockfile, downloading pinned npm packages and the Electron binary; disable with HERMIS_OVERLAY_AUTOSTART=0). The overlay obtains a short-lived interactive session ticket from the local Thor gateway control socket and listens only to voice.status and wake.detected. It renders HTML/SVG blocks from replies in a sandboxed iframe that may load scripts from cdnjs/jsdelivr/unpkg, and loads https images. While Autopilot is on, the titles of up to 15 open windows are sent to your model provider on every turn. launch_app opens desktop apps by name only (shells, interpreters and paths are refused); with arguments or outside a small allowlist Thor asks you first, except an allowlisted browser opening exactly one http/https URL, which opens without asking. layout_windows moves, resizes and focuses real windows via Win32 (user32); Store apps are found with a read-only powershell Get-StartApps lookup. Every child process gets an allowlisted minimal environment without provider keys. Optional camera gestures (off by default, Autopilot only) process frames locally with MediaPipe, and the model is downloaded once from storage.googleapis.com (SHA-256 verified). Reads config.yaml read-only and writes state.json, overlay.json, overlay.log and the gesture model to the plugin data dir.

name: hevy
description: Unofficial community plugin for Hevy strength training through Hevy's official public API: workouts, exercise progress with estimated 1RM, personal records, weekly sets per muscle group against your own baseline (hevy_training_load), consistency, routines and body measurements. Thor can also log workouts, build routines and record measurements, each one approved by you first (Thor' approval gate; the ask-before-writing setting can turn it off). Needs Hevy Pro. Fifteen tools: nine read-only, six that write. The key is entered in Thor Desktop under Settings > Plugins > hevy (or with thor config set), stored in the profile's .env as HEVY_API_KEY and read through Thor's secret route. Disclosure: unofficial, not affiliated with Hevy. Contacts only api.hevyapp.com, over HTTPS, with the key in the api-key header. Workouts and exercise templates are cached under the profile's plugin-data folder (the cache includes workout notes). No background threads, telemetry or self-update.

name: hey-pcb
description: Agent-driven PCB engineering through HeyPCB's first-party MCP server: design real KiCad boards from a text brief, instant fabrication estimates, and production tracking, with a workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. The server is declared untrusted with per-tool costs and a per-chat spend limit, so Thor names the cost and asks before any call that can spend (design reads stay free). The HEYPCB_API_KEY is forwarded from the user's environment and never stored in plugin files. Disclosure — the MCP server talks to api.heypcb.ai; npx fetches the pinned @heypcb/mcp@0.1.8 from npm on first launch; open_kicad_project and upload_kicad_project upload a local KiCad project folder to HeyPCB, and save_export/restore_local write files on your computer (each after Thor approval); engine runs and design-agent turns are billed to the user's HeyPCB account at its plan rate; ordering on heypcb.ai is still a human decision. Not affiliated with HeyPCB.

name: heycai-clinic-skills
description: For people who work with health clinics of any specialty: estimate what a clinic's front desk loses each month to missed calls, unanswered WhatsApp messages and no-shows, from the numbers the clinic gives, and audit a clinic website for Google and AI search (crawling and indexing, AI crawlers, llms.txt, schema.org JSON-LD, local SEO), with a fix for each finding. Two skills by HeyCAi, the AI receptionist for health clinics. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/), skills only: no plugin code, no MCP server, no hooks. Disclosure — instruction-only skills by HeyCAi (an AI-receptionist vendor) that name HeyCAi among the listed vendors; the website audit has the agent fetch the clinic's public pages with curl from your machine; no plugin code, no network calls of its own, no credentials.

name: hicortex
description: Shared fleet memory for Thor agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

name: hindsight
description: Hindsight long-term memory provider — knowledge graph, entity resolution and multi-strategy retrieval (recall/reflect/retain tools plus automatic per-turn capture). Maintained by Vectorize; cloud, local external and local embedded modes are available. `thor memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main). Disclosure — in cloud mode (and local external) every turn's conversation, and every entry the agent adds or replaces in Thor's built-in MEMORY/USER stores, is sent to api.hindsight.vectorize.io or the URL you configure, into every bank it writes to; local embedded mode starts a background Hindsight daemon (fetched with uvx, version-pinned, on first run when hindsight-api is not installed) and keeps its LLM settings in ~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env; setup writes the keys you enter to the profile .env; repositories under folders you list in trusted_project_dirs may choose their bank with .hindsight/config.toml; `thor memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main).

name: hindsight-curator
description: Bulk-curate stale Hindsight memories from chat via /memory-curate or tools, or from the Desktop Memory curation page: keyword/regex scan, the agent reads each match and plans only verified-stale ids (coincidental hits recorded as skipped / left untouched), waits for the owner's explicit OK, invalidates, writes one checkpoint fact in the owner's words, and restores via a local SQLite journal. Bundles the memory-curate skill (hindsight-curator:memory-curate). Separate from the official hindsight memory-provider plugin — talks only to the public HTTP API. Disclosure — network calls only to the configured Hindsight base URL (list, GET, PATCH invalidate/restore, retain checkpoint); optional Bearer auth via HINDSIGHT_API_KEY through Thor secrets; writes invalidations, restores, and one checkpoint fact to that server; stores plans/apply events/whitelist/history/skipped reasons in the profile plugin-data directory; Desktop half uses ctx.rest to the plugin dashboard API; no shell, no background daemons, does not read other plugins' config or credential files.

name: hireko
description: Hireko Recruiter MCP gateway: Cognito authentication, candidate screening interview link creation, and candidate search scoring. Hosted connector: tool arguments are sent to Hireko; an authenticated account is required. Disclosure — sends tool arguments and the user's Hireko bearer token to Hireko's hosted MCP endpoint (an AWS Lambda URL) and recruiter-<tenant>.hireko.ai, POSTs the password (env only) to AWS Cognito, opens a local 127.0.0.1 callback server during browser login, and stores Hireko access/refresh tokens under ~/.HirekoOpenPlugin/credentials.

name: hive
description: Thor remembers how its errors were fixed, and Thor installs can share those fixes: when a terminal command fails with an error that was fixed before, Hive adds the fix that worked (with how often it worked) under the output. Fixes are learned from exit codes, not guessed: a failed command, the steps after it, and the same command succeeding. Opt-in, Hive trades fixes with other installs over Nostr, signed by a random per-install key, with proof of work, cross-checks and a safety screen; it never runs anything. Disclosure — reads terminal command text, exit codes and output through the transform_terminal_output hook and (on `thor hive learn`) state.db read-only; stores learned fixes under plugin-data/hive; with `thor hive network read` it sends error fingerprints (hashes) to the configured Nostr relays (default nos.lol, relay.primal.net, relay.damus.io) to look up fixes; with `network share` it also publishes the normalized error line and the fix commands (home paths, private paths, hosts, IPs, e-mails and secret-looking text removed or withheld; preview with `thor hive outbox`). Network is off by default.

name: hive-intelligence
description: Crypto data for AI agents through Hive's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.hiveintelligence.xyz/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): find a token, get its price, check token safety, research a token, analyze a wallet, read market positioning and the market overview, and look up DeFi yields and prediction markets. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + the hive and hive-setup skills), no Python or executables. Needs a free Hive account (Free plan: 10,000 credits a month). Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything. Disclosure — every tool call sends the tool name and its inputs (a token, wallet address or query) to mcp.hiveintelligence.xyz and spends the account's Hive credits; the tool list comes from Hive's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it; when no Hive tools are connected, the bundled skills have the agent run the npm package `hive-intelligence@1.20.2` via `npx` on your machine, and `/hive-setup`'s one-command path (`hive init --all`, only after you say yes) edits every detected AI client's config and installs the `hive` CLI globally.

name: holdings
description: Holdings is a Thor Desktop plugin that shows your crypto wallet and exchange balances in one place. You can review activity against the original records and export records with a note on what each source covers. Ask Holdings answers questions with your Thor model and checks every cited number against your records. It is read-only and never signs transactions or moves funds. The demo uses fictional records and needs no keys. Disclosure — crypto portfolio viewer, read-only (no signing, transfers or trades). Sends the wallet addresses you add and your read-only exchange API keys (stored through Thor secrets) to their own vendors: Kraken, Binance, Bybit, Etherscan, Zerion, GoPlus, public RPCs (PublicNode, dRPC, MEV Blocker, Solana mainnet), DefiLlama and GeckoTerminal. Saved wallet and exchange records go to your active model only after you enable `share_private_chat_tools` (off by default). Weekly briefing and alert watch cron jobs are opt-in templates.

name: holographic
description: Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless an optional online feature is switched on: search by meaning (embeddings: on) or rescoring by a cross-encoder (rerank: on), both off by default. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.thor-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `thor update` moves existing users onto it; a file without merges keeps history schema 1; the first merge raises it to schema 2, after which writers of 0.15-0.18 refuse it until 0.19.0 or a pre-merge backup is restored. Taken over from Thor Labs's handoff copy (thor726/thor-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, thor_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Since 0.18.0 an optional, experimental second stage reorders the recall candidates with a cross-encoder at a /v1/rerank endpoint that answers in Cohere's shape without a key, such as llama-server (rerank: on, off by default). It does not raise hits: on the maintainer's held-out set (126 questions) it cut non-target facts in the top five by about 40 % and lines per turn by about a third, and lost about one target per hundred questions. Disclosure — local only unless an optional online feature (search by meaning or rescoring) is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($THOR_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact_store rebuild_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry (at the debug log level the recall stages log fact ids and scores, never text), and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on or rerank: on (both off by default). With embeddings: on, the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; with rerank: on, before a turn the user's message and up to rerank_top_k (40) candidate fact texts, and for a fact_store search its query and results, go to the rerank endpoint the user configures (rerank_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name), with no credentials and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject or that look like they hold a secret, and queries that hold one, are not sent; a failure or a slow answer gives the recall of rerank: off and pauses the endpoint (60 s, doubling to 900 s); nothing the endpoint returns is stored; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored. Since 0.19.0, fact_store merge combines duplicate facts in one transaction while keeping each copy's history, sources and confirmations under its original id. The retained fact keeps its own text, trust and origin; copies leave current search and recall. Optional expect pins the exact shown versions and refuses changed participants without a write. Scheduled jobs can merge only copies created in their own session. Forgetting the retained fact also erases its merged copies. Merge is local and makes no new network or model calls. Version 0.19.1 adds strict tooling for comparing recorded margins; the normal RECALL_MARGIN remains 1.0. Version 0.19.2 closes a timed-out rerank or embeddings request socket so a server dripping response headers does not keep its worker alive. During TLS wrapping, cancellation is retained but the handshake can continue until its own socket timeout; DNS resolution is outside socket cancellation. Version 0.20.0 adds an opt-in local task-outcome journal and the memory-provider tool fact_experience: emitted and candidate fact/version identifiers, an optional short task and correction, outcome/reason and optional corrected-source references. It is separate from trust, origin and ranking. Agent reports are not authenticated human confirmations. Collection and detailed tracing are off by default; retention is bounded to 30 days and 1000 attempts per store, with up to 10 revisions per attempt. Forgetting any referenced fact removes the dependent attempt and outcome from the store. No new model, network or credential use; synchronous local writes add latency. PR #45 also loads NumPy on first use outside the plugin-loader lock; concurrent first callers wait for import completion. Version 0.20.1 limits SQLite busy waits for the optional journal and retries transient contention once. Failed receipts are reported and are not queued; the SQLite timeout is not a full search deadline. Version 0.20.2 writes no receipt for a prefetch that emits nothing, applies journal retention whenever a writer opens the store (also with the journal off) and scrubs removed outcome text from the file like a forgotten fact. Version 0.20.3 adds one system-prompt line, only with the journal on, asking the agent to record an outcome when the person corrects an answer that used recalled facts (an agent report, not human confirmation). Version 0.21.0 adds an opt-in prefetch_max_tokens budget for the recalled block: facts that do not fit are left out whole, never cut; off by default. Version 0.22.0 keeps entity links honest on a text change: a new entities list replaces the declared names, and a declared name the new text no longer says is dropped; revert restores a version's declared names from an additive version_names table (names with keyed hashes, removed with the version and by delete_entity in every spelling a tombstone covers, including by older releases through triggers). Version 0.22.1 makes the secret/instruction screen about 30× faster on long texts with the same decisions (patterns unchanged; a prefilter chooses where they are tried). Version 0.22.2 sends a slow reranker only as many of the first candidates as its measured speed answers in half rerank_timeout (at least two), so a large pool no longer times out and pauses the endpoint; the candidates not sent keep their order behind the scored ones. Version 0.23.0 stops feedback (helpful/unhelpful) from refreshing a fact's age: optional temporal decay counts from when the current version was recorded, and updated_at changes only when the fact itself does; a correction with a new text (correct / update content) starts at its origin's trust without the old text's helpful marks, recalls and confirmations, like change, while a date-only correction keeps them and revert restores the old trust. Version 0.23.1 takes a correction that journal retention removed off the disk on the open connection (the file rewrite runs after the receipt write, with busy timeout 0 at every step) and clears only the rewrite mark it served. Version 0.24.0 adds two experimental features, both off by default and with no new network, model or credential use: memory_map.py, a command-line exporter nothing in the provider calls, which prints one store as a read-only JSON snapshot for a person to read (opened mode=ro in one read transaction; a forgotten fact is its id and date only; corrected versions and texts the safety screen hides carry no text; with --config it reads config.yaml's search settings, with --thor-home the thor-dreaming files about the profile store), whose output holds the facts' texts and so is personal data; and prefetch_clause_coverage: on, which gives each of two separate Russian or English questions in one message a second look at the facts the coverage gate left out. Version 0.25.0 limits the memory map export to 1000 facts and 300 names by default (--max-facts / --max-entities, 0 for none) and says what it cut in SNAP.limits; nothing else changes. Version 0.25.1 fixes recall by meaning dropping a fact that names a short Russian name in another grammatical case than the message (Eva as «Ева» / «Еву»): the name now also meets a capitalized word of the fact that may be a case form of it. Version 0.25.2 reads that word by its case ending rather than a short stem: names whose stem changes meet their forms («Лев» / «Льва»), and different names that only shared a short stem («Аня» / «Анна») no longer meet; nothing else changes. Version 0.25.3 no longer imports NumPy when the provider starts (the first search that needs it does, as does opening a store whose vectors need re-encoding) and treats a NumPy that is installed but fails to import as missing, so recall goes on by words; finds a Latin word written into Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Thai text by itself; refuses at write, and leaves out of recall, a prompt addressed to an assistant and the agent's report of its own steps; and auto_extract (off by default) no longer stores a reply such as "I like that" as a preference; no change to defaults, schema or network behaviour. Version 0.26.0 adds an experimental presence gate, prefetch_presence_gate (off by default): with it on, a fact this provider injected is held back past the six-turn repeat window only while the model can verifiably still see it (its exact recall line inside a <memory-context> block the core fenced, or its fact id and text in a fact_store result), reading only the messages the core already passes to sync_turn, with no new storage, network, model or credential use; tool results now carry raw Unicode instead of Unicode escape sequences (a payload that cannot be encoded keeps the escaped form); change names the keywords it drops and correct writes the keywords it is given; with the gate off, recall is unchanged. Version 0.26.1 fixes that gate after an independent review: a sync the core queued before a compaction no longer counts as the current view, a fact the compaction removed is recalled again once a fresh view no longer shows it, a compaction that fails no longer switches the gate off for the session, a late sync keeps its own turn, and a fact_store history result counts as the fact being visible; with the gate off nothing changes. Version 0.26.2: with the task-outcome journal on (off by default), a prefetch that only refreshes facts the session already holds records no new attempt and carries no Memory attempt line, so a repeated block adds nothing new to the context. Version 0.26.3: with the journal and the presence gate on, a delivery whose attempt could not be written after a compaction no longer stops that fact from recording attempts later. Version 0.26.4 fixes the presence gate after a second independent review: two late syncs in a row each keep their own turn, a quiet session that compacted leaves no lasting state, and a refresh no longer keeps token-budget room for an attempt line it does not carry. Version 0.26.5 fixes four edge cases found in a third review of the presence gate and the journal (both off by default): a long pasted message keeps its turn, a session the provider forgot drops its turns' messages, a failed attempt write drops only receipts older than the last compaction, and the token budget no longer keeps room for an attempt line in a block that became a refresh. Version 0.26.6 loads numpy's OpenBLAS on one thread on Windows when the plugin is what imports numpy, which saves about 225 MB of commit charge per Thor process on an 8-thread machine. Version 0.27.0 adds French auto-extraction of stated preferences and shared decisions, and an optional one-hop memory graph over the entity index that reaches facts next to the ones a query names (bounded reads, off by default). Version 0.28.0 links a wiki pointer line (Wiki page: namespace/.../slug.md) to its namespace and page slug as entities, and recall before a turn searches only what the person wrote: a reply's quoted message, attachment notes, the author's name prefix in shared chats and the cron hint are left out, and a notice of finished background work recalls nothing.

name: home-3d-workshop
description: Ask. It's in the box. A 3D printer as a member of the group chat (the persona is Mıstık by default; the name and the en/tr message language are settings, English by default). People in a family or team chat ask in plain words, often by voice note; the agent finds MakerWorld models through Bambuddy, scales one, or designs a part in OpenSCAD (it writes the code, renders it, looks at the preview pictures and keeps every version), slices, and queues with manual start. A print starts only with the owner's typed approval (never from a voice note); when someone else asks, the watcher passes the request to the owner with the exact command. A zero-token cron watcher follows the print; the person who asked gets a one-line start notice and, at the end, a line with a photo in the chat the request came from (groups setting: family or team tone, per-group language), and the owner gets a technical note. Notices go through a saved outbox with retries. Finished parts are tracked in a done box. The owner gets one Workshop screen in Thor Desktop (approval card with the part in 3D, Start, Pause and Stop, queue, done box, messages, filament, setup check, design versions). Each moment a person had to step in is logged, and repeats become upgrade proposals (for example a printed tilted base for auto-eject). Works with a Bambu Lab printer managed by Bambuddy, or with a built-in simulated printer (thor home3d demo). Disclosure — Network: only the one Bambuddy URL you set, over HTTP on your LAN. When HOME3D_BAMBUDDY_API_KEY is set, it is sent as X-API-Key, unencrypted over plain http. MakerWorld lookups and downloads go through Bambuddy; the plugin makes no other network calls. The setup check (thor home3d doctor, the status tool's capabilities, the Workshop screen) makes read-only requests, including GET /api/v1/updates/version, /api/v1/makerworld/status and /api/v1/printers/<id>/camera/status, and never takes a photo. Writes: import, scale, design upload, slice and queue add write to the Bambuddy library and queue without a prompt, for the owner and the people in the household list (unknown senders only with allow_guests); queued items are always manual start. Queue remove only removes the asking person's own waiting items: never a job queued outside the workshop or another household member's job, not even for the owner (who can remove anything by hand in Bambuddy). Bambuddy settings are read (GET /settings/) and never changed. With Bambuddy's require_plate_clear off, Bambuddy may start its own auto-start items on a finished printer before the camera check; thor home3d doctor warns about this. Chamber light: a tool photo or plate check switches it on for about 12 s and restores its earlier state. The cron watcher also switches it by itself for its plate checks and photos: at most once per pass (twice when a camera request fails), one photo near the end of each workshop print (other prints: one photo and plate check in one light cycle when they end), a check when a print ends, and re-checks that back off 15, 30, 60 and 120 min (at most 6) while a plate or a job waits. Approvals: start, resume and plate-clear confirm follow one rule for the agent path, /home3d and the Workshop screen. They are blocked in cron and in runs with nobody present (kanban workers, chat -q, -z, --source tool; both checks fail closed), when a safety gate fails (printer busy or offline, active HMS error, plate not judged empty, another person's job ahead, plate not confirmed after a failed print, bed hot or of unknown temperature for a plate clear), for unknown or non-owner senders, who are told that the owner approves with /home3d approve, and when the ask came in as a voice note (a typed confirmation is asked for). Voice is detected by the pre_gateway_dispatch hook, which reads only the message type and sender id of each inbound gateway message (never the text), keeps the newest few per sender in memory for 10 minutes and always returns None, and by the transcript shape of the turn text; it does not see local CLI, TUI or Desktop turns. A household member's blocked request is stored, and the watcher tells the owner once (when owner_target is set; otherwise the block tells the person to ask the owner directly). Only an owner session gets the Thor approve prompt. The owner is any id in owner_ids, plus, while local_is_owner is true (the default), any local CLI, TUI or Desktop session and any slash command typed in the TUI, Desktop or web dashboard or run by the Workshop screen; turn local_is_owner off when others can reach the dashboard. On IRC and ntfy, where people choose their own ids, only an entry written with the platform (irc:<nick>) matches a sender. The tool handler also needs a single-use pass from that hook or from /home3d approve, so a call that skips the hook is refused, and it checks the plate with the camera right before the action. /home3d approve runs the gate and the action at once and stores nothing for later. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt in an owner session (the unattended, identity and voice rules are blocks and are not skipped). Each rule_key is unique, so always does not carry over, and each always answer adds one unused command_allowlist line to config.yaml. Stop and pause need no approval and pass no gate; who may use them is stop_policy (known: the owner and the household list, the default; anyone; owner), and the person who did it is recorded. Hook time: pre_tool_call reads only printer status and queue (at most 5 s per request, 12 s in all, never the camera), so it stays inside Thor' 30 s hook limit; with a lower plugins.hook_callback_timeout it allows itself 0.4 of it. Workshop screen: three GET routes under /api/plugins/home-3d-workshop/ (health, overview, file), mounted only while the plugin is enabled and callable by anyone who can use that Thor's dashboard or API; overview returns printer state, queue, requesters' names and words, groups, the done box, filament, moments, upgrades, design versions and the setup check (notice texts and setup details only while local_is_owner is on, chat targets never), reads printer status and queue on each call and runs the setup check (read-only Bambuddy requests, thor cron list) in the background at most once every 5 minutes; file returns only design STLs, design previews and stored camera photos from the plugin's data folder; no route writes anything. The Desktop half (desktop/plugin.js, built with esbuild, three.js bundled) is off until turned on in Capabilities, calls only its own routes, the gateway's session.create (one hidden session titled Workshop actions (home-3d-workshop)) and slash.exec with /home3d commands only, polls overview every 15 s for its status-bar chip and every 5 s while the page is open, and runs printer actions as the local user through /home3d, so the owner check applies. Thor internals: besides ctx.current_cron_execution(), the cron, unattended and origin-chat checks read non-public Thor internals from sys.modules (gateway.session_context.get_session_env, also for THOR_SESSION_CHAT_ID; cron.execution_identity._CURRENT; gateway.session_finite; and thor_cli.plugins._resolve_hook_callback_timeout for the hook deadline); they are never imported or patched. A check that raises counts as cron or unattended (fail closed); a renamed one is skipped. Subprocesses: thor send for notices (with -p send_profile when set, each stopped after send_timeout_s, default 20 s, and all sends of one pass within send_budget_s, default 45 s); thor cron create, list and remove from thor home3d setup and teardown, and thor cron list for the setup check; openscad for the name-tag and label-box templates and for the agent's designs (and openscad --version for the setup check), and xvfb-run for the design preview pictures, when they are installed (one render at a time, a 180 s default time limit, a CPU-time limit, a memory cap and an STL size cap; a design may read files only from its own folder and OpenSCAD's own libraries, checked in the source and in OpenSCAD's list of the files it read). thor home3d setup writes THOR_HOME/scripts/home3d_watch.py and creates one thor cron create --no-agent --script job, every 2 minutes by default (720 runs a day, no daily cap); it runs while the Thor scheduler (thor gateway) runs; setup --print-only writes nothing. The job calls no model, and empty output sends nothing. A failed notice is retried on later passes (backoff from 1 min to 4 h, at most 10 attempts within 24 h), then the owner is told once. The script reads THOR_HOME/config.yaml (the plugin settings) and stays silent while the plugin is disabled or removed. The job and the script stay until thor home3d teardown (after an uninstall: thor cron remove and delete the script). Data stays local under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/home-3d-workshop: a SQLite database (requests with the platform and chat id they came from, jobs, household and group sender ids and names, approval requests, who stopped or paused a print, the outbox with every notice and its delivery state, done-box records with who a part is for and who picked it up, open human-needed moments, audit events), outbox.jsonl with every send attempt, camera photos, model files, designs (OpenSCAD source, STL, preview pictures and facts for every version), a watcher log and a settings snapshot without secrets (the watcher's fallback). pre_llm_call adds up to 900 characters of context (persona, speaker, printer state): for household members and the local owner on the first turn, on printing turns and on printer state changes, else one speaker line; for other senders only on printing turns; inject_context: never turns it off. The tools are on for every surface, and while the plugin is enabled its two skills add one line each to the skills index of every session. Tested on Linux with Thor 0.22.5; the Workshop screen was run in Thor 0.23.1 (Webapp) on the simulated printer, not yet in the Desktop app. Verified on a real Bambuddy 1.3.0 with an A1: printer status, queue, Bambuddy settings, lit photo with plate check, MakerWorld import, slice, scale, queue add and remove, and the watcher in dry run on a real print (finish and plate check). The templates, a sample design and the file-access probes are tested with OpenSCAD 2021.01 in CI; a part designed with home3d_design was uploaded and sliced on the real Bambuddy. Planned on the real printer: start, stop, pause and resume, watcher notices and auto-eject with this plugin; nothing new in 0.2.0 was run on it.

name: home-dashboard
description: Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Thor Web and Desktop.

name: homeassistant
description: Home Assistant gateway platform (state-change events in, persistent notifications and cron notify delivery out) plus the homeassistant toolset (ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service). Formerly built into Thor core; existing users are migrated automatically.

name: homeassistant-statistics
description: Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access.

name: homelab-watch
description: Your homelab, your agents and your agent's bill in one Desktop status chip: read-only checks of your router, servers, websites, a Bitaxe miner and your cron jobs with root-cause rollup (a router outage is one alert, not ten); token-free alerts through a no_agent cron job; per-day LLM token counts and API-equivalent savings (subscription, cheaper and free models; unpriced models never estimated); a Scan my network button on the Homelab page that finds devices on your own network (VPN tunnels skipped) and adds the ones you tick, six bundled skills (add-targets, diagnose with an approved-only fix handoff, watch-my-agents, weekly-report, tune-thresholds, bitaxe-advice), a first-run welcome note (a pre_llm_call hook, shown once per install), and the jev_route delegation backend, shadow by default, that sends simple subagent tasks to a cheaper model when a judge clears them. Disclosure — probes only the hosts and URLs in targets.yaml, except that the Desktop "Scan my network" button, when pressed and confirmed, pings and connects to ten common ports on every address of one private /24 the machine is on (VPN tunnels skipped) and appends only the devices you tick to targets.yaml; records token counts and model names from post_api_request, never prompt text; with alerts on, writes one script under scripts/ and creates one cron job via cronjob_manage; sends nothing off the machine by default, but with the optional TypeSafe key and delegation.backend jev_route each subagent task's goal and context (up to 4,000 characters) go to api.typesafe.ai for one judgment; no telemetry.

name: homework-coach
description: Homework photos and teacher updates become checked daily math practice PDFs and a separate parent key. Parent I/S/N feedback guides difficulty. Includes a class plan, read-back corrections, progress/history, a scheduling blueprint and a Desktop workspace. Data stays on the selected Thor backend; photos and teacher content use the configured model provider. JSON uploads and direct downloads support remote clients. Disclosure — when you turn on Daily sheets (off by default), a once-a-minute background check inside the Thor process builds each child's practice sheet on practice days without anyone opening the app; with "Who writes the sheet" set to your model, each sheet sends the child's grade, class unit, latest homework reading, your ratings and notes to your configured provider (or the homework_writer auxiliary model), names and file paths removed.

name: honcho
description: Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (Thor version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers, and requests after a turn starts also carry X-Honcho-Agent-Model (that turn's model id as configured in Thor, or the mixture-of-agents preset name); Honcho records these headers for usage attribution. Links the plugin opens or prints to app.honcho.dev and docs.honcho.dev carry static utm_source=thor, utm_medium=plugin and utm_content=<placement> parameters; nothing user-, machine- or session-identifying is added.

name: honeytrap
description: Catch a hijacked agent by the fake credentials it goes looking for. Honeytrap hides a realistic ops note (prod-access.md) in the agent's workspace with six decoys (deploy ref, signing key, AWS id, database URL, admin portal, license key) in shapes Thor's redactor leaves visible, and never mentions them to the model. If one shows up in any tool call, plain or disguised (base64, hex, URL-encoded, reversed, split, zero-width or Unicode-tag smuggled, lookalike letters, or leaked in fragments across calls), or the decoy file is sent out by path (curl -F @file, cat | nc), the call is blocked (pre_tool_call), the session's outbound tools are quarantined until /honeytrap release, the chat gets an alert with the attack chain (untrusted source, decoy read, blocked egress) and an OCSF-style Detection Finding is written for your SIEM. /honeytrap plants, tests, lists incidents and switches mode; thor honeytrap generates, rotates and removes decoys. Disclosure - writes one decoy file into the agent workspace when you run /honeytrap plant (through the agent's write_file) or thor honeytrap init --dir/plant; stores the decoys, their placements and incidents (tool name, decoy kind, encoding, destination host, chain of tool names; never arguments or conversation text) in its own plugin data.
