No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials or telemetry. Disclosure — adds pre_tool_call/post_tool_call hooks that scan every tool call's arguments and results (up to 256 KB each) for its own decoys; in the default enforce mode it blocks a call carrying a decoy, blocks the session's outbound tools after a critical hit until /honeytrap release (in-memory, cleared on restart, and release lifts every session), and blocks every tool call if the guard itself errors (switch to monitor mode to recover); /honeytrap plant (through the agent's write_file) or thor honeytrap init --dir/plant writes a decoy file prod-access.md into the chosen workspace; stores decoy values, placements and incidents (tool name, decoy kind, encoding, destination host, tool-name chain; never arguments or conversation text) under its plugin data dir; no network, subprocesses, tools, credential reads or telemetry.

name: hook-desk
description: Skills-only plugin. Studies the opening lines of posts you paste, names the pattern, keeps a sourced formula file and drafts opening lines in your voice for your approval. Never posts or browses. Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls of its own, no shell, no stored credentials; reads only text the user provides.

name: hopper
description: Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in Thor without modifying the core catalog.

name: hornlib
description: French Horn F/Bb double horn valve fingering charts (C1 to F6), multi-key pitch transposition (F, Bb, Eb, D, C, G, A, E), natural overtone harmonic series partials with cent deviations, mechanical vs lip trill fingerings, orchestral audition excerpt performance guides, stopped-horn intonation diagnostics, beginner horn and mouthpiece comparisons, and personalized daily brass warmup routines through HornLib's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://hornlib.com/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the hornlib and french-horn-fingering-chart workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local runtime code, binaries, hooks, telemetry or self-updater; every tool call goes over HTTPS to hornlib.com/api/mcp with only the musical query arguments (note name, horn key, or excerpt). All 8 tools are public, free, and annotated read-only (readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false). The package marks the server untrusted (trust: untrusted), so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. The remote tool inventory is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: hostbook
description: A dashboard for the machines and services on your home network, inside Thor, plus tools so Thor can check and fix them from chat under a rule per machine (read only, asks before changes, open). Disclosure — Connects over SSH (your existing keys or ssh-agent, accepting a new machine's host key on first connect) only to machines you add, and runs scripts there when asked in chat, after hostbook's per-machine rules and Thor's approvals; can create a no-agent Thor cron job (hostbook-scan) for scheduled read-only scans when you turn scheduling on; its pre_tool_call hook can block or require approval for other tools that use ssh or touch hostbook's files; keeps the last 20 chat sender ids locally for the setup page; one model call only when you click "Get AI help". No telemetry.

name: hostd-client
description: Request command execution from a separately managed thor-hostd daemon over HTTP or VSOCK, with host-side approval. Disclosure — run_on_host sends commands to a separately installed thor-hostd daemon (VSOCK, or HTTP to a URL you configure) that runs them on the host with the daemon account's privileges; each call asks for Thor approval first and then the daemon's own approval, whose optional ntfy channel does not authenticate the approver, and HTTP traffic is unencrypted unless you put it behind a tunnel or TLS proxy.

name: hostyourai
description: HostYourAI provider profile (hyai/auto, EU-only inference option) and the /hyai task/policy routing command. Disclosure — bundles an off-by-default hyai-decide skill for typed classify/score/route judgments against HostYourAI's decision API; disabled until explicitly enabled via config.

name: hot-thor
description: Compact profile service-state monitoring, resource planning and explicit Desktop connection retention. Detects shared gateways; no model keepalive prompts or unverified speed claims. Reads OS memory/CPU and sampler process metadata.

name: hotwire
description: Analog circuit design bench: Thor writes a SPICE netlist from plain English, proves it against measurable specs (gain, corner frequencies, distortion, bias, current draw, part stress) with Hotwire's own circuit simulator, plays your guitar riff or WAV through the simulated circuit so you can hear it, runs Monte Carlo yield over real part tolerances, explains what each part does, matches knob settings to a recording of a real pedal, tunes values to standard E-series parts, and lays the result out on a stripboard with a parts list and KiCad export. Ships a verified reference library (filters, transistor, JFET and MOSFET stages, overdrive, fuzz, tone stacks, wah), an analog-design skill, a /hotwire command and a Desktop Bench pane with live knobs. Disclosure — runs entirely locally with numpy (installed with consent); no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands; writes designs, plots and audio under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/hotwire/ and reads only the .cir/.wav files you or the agent name; the Desktop half plays audio in the browser (microphone only after you press Live and grant access).

name: house-rules
description: House rules your agent can't forget. Refuses tool calls that match your rules (a command with flags such as git push --force or rm -r, or a regex on a tool argument such as a .env path) or that leave the folders you allow. The refusal tells the agent why and to ask you; you lift a rule for the current session with /rules unlock <n>. /rule turns plain words into a rule draft as YAML and replays it on past tool calls; you paste it into the profile config.yaml yourself, the plugin never writes it. Rules apply from the next session. For an agent that forgets or ignores instructions; it is not a security boundary (scripts, aliases and indirect effects are not seen). Disclosure — no network call of its own, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry, no background task. Hook pre_tool_call reads each tool call's name and arguments and refuses matches; a refusal notice (tool name and reason, never the arguments) is posted to the conversation with ctx.post_message. /rule makes one LLM call through ctx.llm.complete_structured with the user's words, and reads the profile's state.db read-only to replay the draft (other profiles' state.db only if the user picks them). Reads its settings with ctx.get_config and the profile config.yaml read-only. Writes nothing to disk.

name: household-tiers
description: Per-person tool tiers for one shared Thor bot, with a family preset for curfew, a parent alert, and a homework note: built-in owner memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) withheld from non-owner prompts; an external provider block joined after those boxes is removed; a provider block with no built-in box, and compaction's auxiliary summary, are not filtered. Disclosure — gateway access policy: blocks tool calls per sender tier through pre_tool_call (fail-closed: an unreadable household-tiers.json blocks every tool call and withholds memory from every request, owner included), rewrites non-owner model requests through llm_request middleware to remove the owner's MEMORY.md/USER.md and filter tools (external memory-provider blocks with no built-in box and compaction's auxiliary summary are not filtered), resolves non-owner URL hostnames with the system resolver to refuse local targets, sends a curfew alert through the gateway's own adapter to the chat you set in `notify`, and writes household-tiers.json and a per-person audit log under the active Thor home; /family tier and /family forget change those files and are owner-only.

name: housemate
description: Hands-free Thor in every room: old phones, tablets and laptops become room speakers through their browser. Say the wake word, ask, and hear the answer in the same room. One household conversation across rooms, the nearest device answers when several hear you, timers and alarms that ring where they were set, intercom, cards on room screens, spoken approvals, and a Rooms page in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — the gateway runs an HTTPS + WebSocket hub on 0.0.0.0:8742 (self-signed certificate made on first start; its fingerprint is shown on the Rooms page and by thor housemate cert) and a loopback control API on 127.0.0.1:8743 with a token that changes on every start; only devices paired with a six-digit code approved on the PC are heard. Each started satellite streams its microphone to the hub continuously; the hub keeps the stream in memory and hands only the question after the wake word (or a held talk button or an open answer window) to Thor's audio cache and the STT provider configured in Thor; replies use the configured TTS. On first start it downloads openWakeWord v0.5.1 models (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial) from the official openWakeWord GitHub release and Silero VAD v6.2.3 from the official silero-vad repository, each pinned by SHA-256, into plugin-data/housemate/models/. It registers an optional streamed Piper voice (tts.provider: housemate-piper); when chosen, a missing voice is fetched with Piper's own downloader into Thor's cache/piper-voices. Runs ffmpeg from PATH to decode non-WAV speech. A start-up warm-up sends one quiet tone through Thor's STT in a side chat that the plugin's pre_llm_call hook vetoes (prewarm: false turns it off); the same hook applies spoken approve, deny, clarify and stop answers to Thor's own cards by request id through resolve_gateway_approval_card and resolve_gateway_clarify, never auto-approves, leaves an unanswered approval to Thor's timeout (deny), and takes only a tap for commands flagged by smart approval. The agent can speak in other rooms with housemate_announce, and /announce does the same from any chat. Writes only under plugin-data/housemate/ (SQLite with rooms, devices and SHA-256 hashes of their keys, timers; the certificate and private key; the control token), except that the Rooms page's Household / Per room switch writes platforms.housemate.conversation to config.yaml; paired device ids are set as the platform's allow_from in memory. The gateway log records the first 80 characters of spoken answers to prompts. thor housemate bench is opt-in: it downloads about 266 MB of public-domain LibriVox audio from archive.org (SHA-1 pinned), may generate test clips with Microsoft's Edge TTS service when edge-tts is installed, and pairs a device named Bench satellite. No telemetry.

name: htmi
description: Review the HTML pages your agent writes, on the page itself: comment on the exact element, chart, table row or passage; Thor is told about new comments, reads each one with its context, makes checked edits and replies. Pages can also be published as a GitHub issue or pull request description, and comments posted there are pulled back. Adds 11 tools, a pre_llm_call notice, a pre_tool_call approval gate, a skill, the /htmi command and a Review tab in the dashboard. Disclosure — runs its bundled engine (bundle/htmi.mjs, built from the repo's src/) with Node and runs git and gh with a minimal environment that carries no provider keys; reads and edits documents only inside the current repository (comments go to .htmi/); opening a review page starts a local review server on 127.0.0.1 (token-protected writes) that keeps running in the background until /htmi stop or a restart; GitHub work uses your own gh CLI login and only this repository's origin plus repositories you list in github_repos: creating an issue or replacing or editing a description waits for your approval, and replies to comments that came from GitHub are posted there; no telemetry, no stored credentials, no other third-party services.

name: hud-teach
description: Step-by-step lessons on any live Mac window — numbered click-through marks plus an on-screen step card for chess, games, Photoshop, Settings.

name: huddo
description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, answer or close polls and forms, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.10.2, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, and when a message contains a link it fetches that page once from this machine (public hosts only, skipped for links carrying a token or signature) and uploads a small preview image with the message; huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; Thor does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_answer/huddo_close_choices/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar/huddo_rename run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, and, if Thor can schedule recurring tasks, to schedule one that does the same between turns, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; the server also tells the agent to read the remote guide at https://huddo.ai/SKILL.md before starting (vendor-hosted, not pinned), and the skills point to npx -y huddoai@latest (unpinned) for identity export and app publishing; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) and a local copy of your rooms' messages (used by huddo_search/huddo_show/huddo_files; huddo_sync fetches older history from api.huddo.ai) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry; requests to api.huddo.ai carry an x-huddo-client header (cli/mcp/<version>) that the server counts for usage statistics, with no identity or content in it. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skills tell the agent to get confirmation in your own Thor chat before anything sensitive.

name: huntapi
description: Tools to read the metadata of public videos and download their video or audio, through the HuntAPI media API. Disclosure — sends the tool arguments to api.huntapi.com with your HUNTAPI_API_KEY, and calls can use HuntAPI credits. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 4 tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: hwiki
description: Markdown wiki as Thor long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside THOR_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Thor's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at THOR_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in THOR_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to thor backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

name: hyatlas
description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `thor hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `thor memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Thor's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through Thor's get_secret and reads no Thor credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as Thor auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `thor memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Nous Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `thor hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `thor hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with Thor's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Thor starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `thor hyatlas start` keeps running after Thor exits until `thor hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `thor hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads Thor auth.json). No telemetry.

name: hydradb
description: Long-term memory for Thor, backed by HydraDB. Relevant context is recalled before each turn, and completed turns are saved in the background. Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

name: hypd-ai-ads
description: Read-only paid-media analysis for Google Ads, Meta (Facebook) Ads, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics (GA4), Search Console and Merchant Center through the hosted HYPD MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with four skills (setup, tool rules, overview, ready-made analyses). OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Read-only: never changes campaigns, budgets or ads. Disclosure — runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (downloaded from npm on first run) as a local bridge to HYPD's hosted MCP server at mcp.hypd.ai; tool arguments and the ad, analytics, Search Console and Merchant Center data HYPD returns pass through HYPD's servers; sign-in is a browser OAuth flow whose tokens mcp-remote stores in ~/.mcp-auth; read-only is HYPD's server-side guarantee, and the analysis templates the skills follow are fetched from HYPD's server at run time.

name: hyperactive
description: Thor, but it texts you first. Keeps your goals (life > year > quarter > week), promises both ways and decisions with review dates, and speaks first on Thor's own cron: a daily brief, check-ins, decision reviews, nudges on stalled goals, and tap cards with a recommended answer. An unanswered card is re-asked after an hour and, only if low stakes, applied an hour later as a typed action the plugin performs itself (move or schedule its own reminder, set a goal's status); money, public and irreversible calls always wait for the person. Every message names the goal it serves and /ha why explains it. Disclosure — stores data in THOR_HOME/plugin-data/hyperactive/; on first use or `thor hyperactive setup` writes two 4-line shims to THOR_HOME/scripts/ and creates two recurring cron jobs: hyperactive-pulse (no-agent, no model call) and hyperactive-brief (agent mode, one model call a day through Thor's configured model, skipped when there is nothing to brief; brief_at empty turns it off); once set up, re-creates a missing job or shim on session start; the `thor hyperactive` CLI runs `thor cron` subprocesses; pre_llm_call appends a few lines of due items to turns and records a card answer when the message is exactly an option; reads Telegram reactions via gateway_platform_event. No network calls or telemetry of its own; no secrets; `thor hyperactive uninstall` removes both jobs and shims.

name: hyperliquid-desk
description: Live Hyperliquid dashboard tab, Flow Deck alerts, wallets and market tools with a commentary skill on Hyperliquid's public data, plus node panels from the plugin author's hosted relay (on by default, can be turned off) or your own engine feed. Read-only; no orders, no trading keys. Independent; not affiliated with Hyperliquid. Disclosure — Node panels default to the plugin author's hosted relay (wss://relay.perpdepth.com, node_feed "hosted"): while the collector runs and a node panel is open or a node tool is answering, it receives your IP address, the markets you follow and the one on screen; set node_feed to "off" or to your own socket/relay to stop it. Market data otherwise comes from Hyperliquid's public API (api.hyperliquid.xyz); no orders, signing or wallet keys.

name: hyperrizz
description: Hyperrizz: tell Thor the story and watch your HyperFrames film take shape in a live review pane, then get a verified MP4. Thor researches, art-directs, writes the scenes, builds, checks and iterates on a HyperFrames project while the pane plays the actual composition with sound, a scrubber and frame stepping. Pause on a moment, write a note and press Iterate with Thor: the note carries the project, revision and exact frame back into the chat. Full editor opens HyperFrames Studio inside the pane (timeline, assets, code, layers, inspector), and the agent reconciles your manual edits before it rebuilds. Renders are separate, cancellable jobs; a failed build keeps the last working revision and a failed export keeps the last verified MP4. Three tools: hyperrizz_project (create, inspect, edit, restore and reconcile projects), hyperrizz_review (open the pane, exchange frame notes, hand off to Studio) and hyperrizz_produce (build, check, render, inspect jobs, cancel), plus the hyperrizz:production skill with its guides, a broadcast kit and starter templates. Use it for product promos, release announcements, music-led cuts, and restyling or rescuing an existing film. To start, you need Thor 0.23.0 or newer, Node 22 or newer, Python 3.11 or newer and FFmpeg; Linux is the tested platform. Run thor plugins install hyperrizz and thor plugins enable hyperrizz, enable Hyperrizz under Capabilities → Plugins to show the pane, then ask: "Use Hyperrizz to make a 30-second film about this release. Show the live project as you work, then deliver the MP4." The first build installs the pinned npm dependencies. No API keys or hosted generation. Disclosure — processes: spawns local Node, Chromium and FFmpeg child processes with a minimal non-secret environment; runs background build, check and render workers and an optional loopback Studio sidecar (token-gated, 512 KiB capture budget, no redirects); the embedded HyperFrames Studio server listens on loopback without a token. Disclosure — code execution: project write can edit the project's scripts/*.mjs and package.json, and build, check and render run them with Node at your full privileges (no filesystem or network sandbox), the same power as file writes plus the terminal. npm downloads pinned dependencies on first build, and npm ci runs package lifecycle scripts. Disclosure — data: projects are stored in profile-scoped plugin data; the Desktop pane uses ctx.rest only; a post_tool_call hook binds projects to the host session. No credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: hypnos
description: Thor learns in its sleep. Consolidates your corrections and denials into a small LoRA brain overnight, then routes mastered turns to it with the learned habits pruned from its prompt. Disclosure — captures your messages, tool calls with their arguments and results, approvals and replies (secret-scrubbed) into its own plugin-data database for 90 days by default and reads MEMORY.md/USER.md read-only; nights run only when you start them (/sleep now, thor hypnos sleep, Desktop, or a cron job you create) and download the chosen base model from Hugging Face, call your own model through Thor for dream variants (budget-capped; teacher: scripted avoids it), and run the teacher's and brain's proposed shell commands only inside a networkless, mount-free Docker container you pull yourself; after a promoted night it starts an unauthenticated brain server on 127.0.0.1:8765, and with routing: auto (default) a learned habit family switches, after 5 agreeing shadow turns, to being answered by the small local brain (including terminal tool calls, which still go through Thor approval) instead of your configured model; a brain_endpoint you set receives the brain's prompts; Desktop replies carry a ~20-token ::hypnos marker kept in the transcript.

name: hypotize
description: Run growth experiments with Hypotize, the agent-native Growth OS, through its hosted MCP server (https://api.hypotize.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): read what the team already tested, write hypothesis-first ideas, score them with ICE, PIE, RICE or a custom framework, move experiments through an enforced lifecycle and record measured outcomes and learnings. Bundles three skills: the experiment method, a read-only weekly pipeline review and a backlog import from a spreadsheet or Notion export. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Hypotize's hosted server (api.hypotize.ai) and acts on the user's Hypotize account with their role in each project; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: hyprland
description: Hyprland-native computer use for Thor: grim capture, wlr-virtual-pointer clicks/drags/scroll, wtype text, and window-scoped target enforcement. No XWayland, accessibility tree, root, or /dev/uinput. Disclosure — the pointer helper is C source you build locally (`make -C <plugin>/pointer`) and the plugin runs it, or the binary named in `computer_use.hyprland.pointer_bin` / `HYPRLAND_CU_POINTER_BIN`, to inject pointer events; screenshots of the screen or the targeted window go to your model like any computer-use backend; capturing a named app focuses its window; and text that starts with `-` (or that wtype refuses) is typed by pasting through the Wayland clipboard, which overwrites your clipboard and leaves that text in it.

name: hypruse
description: Hyprland computer use through the hypruse CLI: controls from the accessibility tree clicked by number, typing and keys sent to one window, and a background mode where the agent works in apps on its own workspaces (99 down to 90) while your cursor, focus and workspace stay put. Select it with `thor config set computer_use.backend hypruse`. Disclosure: the provider is pure Python with no third-party dependencies. Each action runs the separately installed `hypruse` command (0.13 or newer), or the one named in `computer_use.hypruse.command` or THOR_HYPRUSE_CMD, as a subprocess with no shell, and that child gets only the desktop session variables and HYPRUSE_* settings, never Thor' API keys; `thor computer-use doctor` also runs `hypruse doctor`. hypruse clicks, types and presses keys in your live session, and a foreground pointer action moves your cursor. With the optional `computer_use.hypruse.delivery: auto`, an action on the window you are in runs on your screen. Screenshots of the targeted window, or of the focused monitor for `app='screen'`, go to your model like any computer-use backend's, and each capture file is deleted once read. It reads hypruse's state file `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypruse/cli-state.json` and never writes it. No network calls, telemetry, stored data or credentials.

name: icarus
description: Self-memory and replacement models for Thor agents. Remember your work. Train your replacement.

name: ichor
description: Catches the moments you correct Thor (a correction, /retry or /undo), pairs the rejected answer with the accepted one, scrubs secrets and personal data locally, and asks you once to keep, share or discard it with a one-letter reply. Kept pairs export as TRL preference JSONL and an Atropos environment, ready to fine-tune or run RL on your own model. Disclosure — captures your corrections (rejected and accepted answers, your feedback) into a local SQLite store in its plugin data directory after local secret/PII scrubbing, posts and edits its own card messages in the chat, and claims the bare replies k, s, d, keep, share or discard in a direct chat within 120 seconds of an open card; asks the session model for a one-word mistake label per captured pair via the optional llm.side_question capability (spends main-model tokens); makes network calls only on /ichor share, uploading scrubbed pairs to a Hugging Face dataset under the HF_TOKEN owner's account (private unless /ichor set public); the store is shared per profile, so on a multi-user gateway every allowlisted user can review, share or publish pairs captured from other users' chats.

name: icon-index
description: 40 free CC0 3D icons in one matching style for websites, apps, slides and videos. Browse them spinning in a Thor Desktop pane, recolour them (8 presets or any colour) and download the result, and let the agent find an icon by meaning, return embed code (iframe, model-viewer, React, three.js) and download links, show it as a draggable 3D card in chat (::icon-index directive), or save its files into a project folder. Disclosure — the pane, chat card and icon_save fetch icon files (GLB, PNG, MP4) from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/minutechreview/3d-icons at a pinned commit; the 3D viewer is https://motion.minutechbuilds.com/icons/viewer.html shown in a SandboxedFrame (opaque origin, allow-scripts, plus allow-downloads in the pane so its Download GLB button can save a recoloured model) and it loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; icon_save writes only into the folder the agent names and never overwrites a file; search, metadata and embed code come from the bundled data/icons.json. No shell, credentials, telemetry or background work.

name: idea-board
description: A nightly board of things your agent can take off your plate, each tied to your own words. Code finds signals in your last 14 days of chats (things asked on several days, remind-me loops, upcoming dates, corrections, failing tools, things the agent said it couldn't reach); a model drafts ideas, a second pass critiques them, and code checks every idea (evidence ids must exist, named capabilities must be installed, links and @file/@url references you never typed are rejected). Click an idea and a new chat opens with the prompt in the composer; you press send, nothing is sent for you. Dismiss with a reason and it becomes a rule applied on every later run. Also ranks which Portal connector to add next by how many ideas it would unlock that match your chats (no model call). Desktop board and setup page plus a Python half. Disclosure — no network calls of its own and no telemetry; all model calls go through Thor (two per run, ideation and critique, on the auxiliary task idea_board; unset it follows your main model; about 70–80k tokens for two weeks of heavy use). Reads outside its own data: state.db chats from the last 7/14/30 days you pick (scheduled-job runs, subagents, hidden and group chats skipped; only text you typed is quoted, other content is wrapped as untrusted), this profile's toolsets, MCP servers, connectors, skills, messaging platforms and scheduled jobs, Thor's suggested cron jobs, and memories/USER.md; some of that goes to your configured model inside the ideation prompt. Three imports of undocumented Thor internals (thor_cli.tools_config._get_platform_tools, toolsets.resolve_toolset, cron.suggestions.load_suggestions) trigger the catalog's rule 9 warning; each has a tested fallback (tests/test_compat.py) and a public-API request is open at thor726/thor-agent#149576. Stores ideas, dismissals, rules and run history in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/idea-board/data.db. A pre_llm_call hook only links a chat started from a card back to its card (no injection). Nothing is scheduled until you press Schedule it in setup, which creates one cron job (nightly, time you pick) through Thor's cron API; that job wakes the agent for one short turn (about 30k prompt tokens, mostly cached) to call idea_board_run. No shell commands, no stored credentials, no background process of its own.

name: ideacut
description: Turns a chat brief into an editable, art-directed video: seven agent tools capture and record a public page, write typed scenes, revise them and export H.264 MP4 locally with Chromium and FFmpeg. Capture goes through a loopback validating proxy that refuses private/loopback/metadata targets. Optional narration is sent to the user's configured TTS provider; the live preview is silent. Disclosure — ideacut_capture and ideacut_record open model-chosen public web pages in your installed Chrome/Edge (headless) and can scroll, click and type into them (forms included); every connection goes through a loopback-only proxy that refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses. Scene images, clips and music may be any local file path the agent names and are copied into the plugin's data folder. Rendering runs your system FFmpeg/ffprobe. Voice-over (off by default) sends each scene's narration text to your configured Thor TTS provider (directly via edge-tts when that provider is Edge).

name: idealphase-elevenlabs-audio-tags
description: Thor plugin that adds a few honest ElevenLabs delivery tags so speech sounds more human. It does not replace the built-in ElevenLabs voice provider, and it does not change the chat transcript. Disclosure — sends the prepared speech, voice ID, model ID, and any pronunciation-dictionary locator to api.elevenlabs.io with your ELEVENLABS_API_KEY; synthesis is billed to your ElevenLabs account. When automatic tags are on, the untagged transcript is also sent to the model configured for auxiliary.idealphase_elevenlabs_audio_tags, or your normal chat model if you did not pin one. Audio is written only to the path Thor requests. No tools, hooks, or middleware. Does not store the key, phone home, or log the transcript.

name: identity
description: View and edit the identity files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, AGENT.md/THOR.md) from chat, switch the active profile, and see per-line usage with colour-coded staleness timestamps. Adds six tools, /identity, /identity-switch and /identity-dashboard commands, and a utilization dashboard pane. Disclosure — reads and writes the identity files and a line-utilization record inside the selected profile directory under THOR_HOME, and can change which profile is active; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — the model-callable identity_edit tool rewrites SOUL.md/MEMORY.md/USER.md/AGENT.md and identity_switch_profile writes THOR_HOME/active_profile.

name: idm-radio
description: Generative ambient in the Thor Desktop status bar with the session's work written into it: reads drip, edits blip, commands ring, a failed call sends the radio dial through static, and a finished task lands a drop and becomes a track you can save as WAV. Three pictures (tunnel, sky, mosaic) read from the score. Synthesized live, no samples, no network. Adds the idm_radio tool, the /idm command and two hooks that report tool outcomes to the Desktop.

name: ikigai
description: Getting-to-know-you interview and periodic check-ins that build a detailed, sourced picture of the person using Thor. 76 questions in 11 modules with a 12-question express path (English and French). The interview runs itself: a pre_llm_call hook consumes each answer and returns the next question, so no model call is spent on it and a reply cannot drift into another topic. Every answer is stored locally with the user's exact words and a source tag (declared, inferred, corrected); guesses are held back until confirmed. /ikigai compile proposes a merge into USER.md that fits the 1,375-character limit and touches only the lines Ikigai owns (applied by the agent through the built-in memory tool, so write approval still applies), a SOUL.md draft that is never applied automatically, and detailed sheets kept outside the prompt. /ikigai show reads the profile back in the chat. Weekly 3-question check-ins and an offer to turn a thrice-repeated correction into a lasting rule. Disclosure: no network calls, no telemetry, no dependencies; reads USER.md (to show a diff) and the current turn's user message (local keyword matching to count corrections); writes only under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/ikigai/ (0600 files, 0700 directory); answers tagged local-only never reach USER.md, SOUL.md or the sheets.

name: image-utils
description: Inspect, resize, crop, rotate, convert and re-encode image files in-process with Pillow - no shell, no ImageMagick, no network.

name: imagegen
description: Image studio for Thor Desktop: generate, compose from references, edit and upscale across FAL, Nous Portal, Magnific, Vertex AI, the Thor image providers and a local image server of your own, with a guided prompt builder, campaign grids, a gallery and a local monthly budget. It can also serve the agent's image_generate calls when picked under Tools → Image Generation. Disclosure — Each generation is billed by the provider you pick (FAL, Magnific, Nous Portal, Vertex AI or a Thor image provider). On its screen each one starts from a button you click; the agent spends only if you pick ImageGen under Tools → Image Generation or add the optional MCP server; prompts and reference images go to that provider (queue.fal.run, fal.run, api.magnific.com, aiplatform.googleapis.com, or a Thor image provider, including Nous Portal and a linked ChatGPT subscription through Thor's own providers). With the optional local server address set, prompts for its models go only to that address, at no cost. Prompt writing and image reading use your Thor model through ctx.llm. Images, history and the spending ledger are stored in plugin-data/imagegen. Optional FAL_KEY, MAGNIFIC_API_KEY, VERTEX_API_KEY, VERTEX_PROJECT and IMAGEGEN_LOCAL_SERVER_KEY are plugin secrets. An optional command line runs single or batch generations only when someone starts it, as the `thor imagegen` subcommand. It imports some non-public Thor modules to read the image provider registry and the FAL catalog.

name: imagination-studio
description: Make pictures, video clips with sound, voice lines, songs and sound effects on your own machine with Imagination Studio (by keys + Wasserman): FLUX 3 Klein / Qwen-Image, MiniMax H3 / FastH3, Fish Audio Drama 3, MiniMax Music 3 and Stable Audio Open, rendered in the Studio's own queue and delivered to the chat as attachments. Disclosure: HTTP calls only to the Imagination Studio at the studio_url setting (default http://127.0.0.1:7870), no other service and no telemetry; copies finished files into THOR_HOME/plugin-data/imagination-studio/outputs (up to max_download_mb each, never pruned automatically); reads the optional Studio access key with get_secret (IMAGINATION_STUDIO_KEY) and stores none; no shell commands, subprocesses or background threads; a tool call blocks for at most wait_seconds (default 120, max 600). Rendering itself happens in the Studio, which uses the GPU under its own memory and thermal gates.

name: imprint
description: Compile a week of Thor activity into a cited, typeset book with an executive summary. Disclosure — records redacted one-line summaries (max 280 chars) of every tool call, model API call (model, tokens, cost), approval prompt and decision, and subagent goal/result into its own SQLite ledger under the profile's plugin-data; imprint_import reads up to 90 days of message content from the active profile's state.db read-only and stores redacted summaries; compiling sends ledger summaries to the user's configured model via ctx.llm and runs the user's own `typst` binary when it is on PATH; `/imprint burn`, `thor imprint burn` and the dashboard Burn button permanently delete a week's ledger and compiled books.

name: inbox
description: thor inbox: one read-only view of everything in flight for the active profile: failed or paused cron jobs, stalled or dropped delegations, orphaned background processes, blocked kanban tasks, running work, undelivered delegation results, upcoming cron runs and open chat sessions, with --json for scripts. A Thor Labs plugin: built by Thor Labs, not supported. Disclosure — reads processes.json, cron/jobs.json, runtime/active_sessions.json and state.db (SQLite read-only) in the profile's home, plus the shared kanban board's kanban.db (read-only); it never writes, repairs or prunes them, adds no model tools or hooks, and sends nothing anywhere.

name: inbox-sentinel
description: Watches a Gmail inbox (history polling over a read-only OAuth grant) or an IMAP mailbox over TLS, filters routine mail locally, asks your configured model whether the rest needs attention, and sends a notification through a configured `thor send` target, with an optional reply draft for review. Never sends, labels, archives or deletes mail. Gate and drafts run in two plugin-owned auxiliary model slots that follow the main model until pinned; daily attempt caps bound model calls. Sends one "not watching your inbox" alert a day if the mailbox can't be reached. Disclosure — runs a long-lived background poll after a session event; calls gmail.googleapis.com through a Thor-managed gmail.readonly grant from the user's own Google Cloud Desktop client, or the user's IMAP server with a profile-scoped password; message text goes to the configured model provider; alerts run `thor send` as a child process with the text on argv and may be stored by the destination; sender rules and counters are kept in profile plugin state; no telemetry.

name: inboxapp
description: Inboxapp, the shared inbox and CRM for X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp DMs, through Inboxapp's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.inboxapp.com/mcp): list, search and read threads; send, edit, unsend and react to messages from the user's connected accounts; update contacts (status, tags, notes, valuation, assignee); archive, assign and delete threads; manage the team's tags and statuses. Bundles four skills: inboxapp (connect and pick the right skill), triage, reply and pipeline. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Inboxapp's server at mcp.inboxapp.com, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, so it is not covered by the pinned sha. It sends, edits and unsends real messages from the user's linked X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp accounts and can delete threads, tags and statuses; the agent gets the same access as the user in the chosen team. Sign-in is by OAuth on inboxapp.com (token kept by Thor) or an Inboxapp API token. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool not annotated read-only and refuses those tools in unattended runs; the skills may also read docs.inboxapp.com.

name: incognito
description: Ephemeral clean-room chats and fail-closed RAM PII masking across CLI, TUI, Gateway, and Desktop: hides active sessions, blocks memory and skill writes, strips profile and personal memory in RAM in strict mode, masks outbound personal details before sending, zero-fills transcript and hook spill files before unlinking on close or sweep, and supports confirmed Save with reversible Undo. Disclosure — deletes the database rows, transcript files and hook-output files of chats marked incognito when you burn them, when they close, or on a sweep after their idle TTL expires (file contents are zero-filled first); the model cannot trigger a burn; Save moves an incognito chat into normal history and Undo (within the undo window) returns it to incognito; while any incognito chat is active it blocks terminal, file-read, search and code tools from touching Thor session storage in every session on the host; with Mask personal details on (off by default) it replaces detected personal details with placeholders in messages and tool results before they reach the model and blocks sends it cannot check; adds no-retention flags (`store: false`, OpenRouter `data_collection: deny`) to outbound model requests from incognito chats; stores content-free leases, save-undo metadata and receipt hashes under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/incognito/; makes no third-party network calls.

name: index-network
description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `thor index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Thor env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Thor model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $THOR_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Thor env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Thor sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.

name: index-search
description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. It searches a Meilisearch server you run, so notes or local files can be found only after you index them there; it does not search files on disk itself. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can search with your key. Turn a surface off with thor tools. On Thor 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. index_watch save stores one query and prints a thor cron create line for every 15 minutes. You run that line. A run is a model turn, and a tool call is another model request, with no daily cap. The watch covers only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run thor cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. This plugin does not create or remove the cron job and it does not ask. Writes use the guard in agent.file_safety. An update can stop the watch.

name: inference-exchange
description: Serve local Inference Exchange models while Thor CLI is idle. Disclosure — when `sell_enabled` is turned on (off by default), runs the Python interpreter and Inference Exchange checkout you configure as a background process that registers this machine as an open-trust inference provider with your configured coordinator (for example the author-operated `alpha.inferenceex.com`), passes it your `IE_PROVIDER_TOKEN`, and serves third-party prompts on your local llama-server while Thor is idle; it can block a turn if it cannot stop that process.

name: infisical
description: Secret source plugin that resolves environment variables from an Infisical secret store (cloud or self-hosted) at Thor startup. Registers a mapped source ("infisical", inf:// references) and a bulk source ("infisical_bulk").

name: infra-atlas
description: Registry-backed infrastructure graph with drift detection, a read-before-touch guardrail, and autonomous downtime response. Disclosure — on downtime of a registered service it can restart it on this host with one of a fixed set of commands (systemctl/service restart or start, docker compose restart/start/up in the registry's project directory, pct/qm start) taken from your registry, always through Thor' command approval and only when `auto_heal_mode` is changed from the default `notify_only`; it can install a recurring cron watchdog and a script under the Thor scripts directory, probes registered hosts over HTTP/TCP with TLS verification off, reads the Thor config (read-only) and cron job list, writes Markdown into the registry directory, and keeps a local credential vault whose values the agent can read (plaintext if `cryptography` is not installed).

name: injection-guard
description: Prompt-injection firewall for tool output. A tool_execution middleware scans results from web, browser, file-reading and mail tools for instructions addressed to the model, redacts the matched spans, strips zero-width and bidi characters, HTML comments carrying instructions, CSS-hidden text and oversized base64 blobs, then wraps what remains in a labelled untrusted- data envelope. Fully local and deterministic: seven weighted signal families with a default threshold of six, so one strong signal or two medium signals trip it; no network calls, no API calls, and no model in the decision path. Ships a read-only injection_guard_stats tool and a /guard command, and appends one audit line per block carrying signal names and scores only — never the offending text. Embedded envelope markers are defused before wrapping, so a payload cannot close the untrusted block early. For tools listed in file_reader_tools the destructive family is exempt, because redacting a local migration or deploy script would corrupt it if the model rewrote the file; instruction-override and concealment still fire on reads. Disclosure — it rewrites tool results before the model reads them, which is the purpose of the plugin and does change the content the model receives; detection is pattern-based, so a novel phrasing that avoids every rule will pass, and the guard covers the tool path only, not text a user pastes into chat.

name: injection-range
description: A prompt-injection fire drill for your own agent. /drill run plants eight documents, one at a time, each carrying a test injection (plain override, hidden HTML comment, forged system message, memory poisoning, base64, reply hijack, and two delegated-task cases where you tell the agent to follow a document), gives the agent an ordinary task with each, blocks any tool call that carries a drill canary before it runs (pre_tool_call), and scores each scenario as held, neutralized by a guard, or compromised from the tool calls and model requests it observed, never from the model's own account. Use it to test a model, or a guard plugin, before you trust the agent with real documents. Disclosure — hooks see every session's tool calls and turns and return at once when no drill is running; during a drill it reads outgoing request messages to check the payload arrived (not stored), blocks canary-carrying tool calls with a neutral message, and queues one user-role task per scenario into the session that ran /drill (terminal UI only, and only with plugins.entries.injection-range.allow_gateway_injection: true; otherwise it shows the task for you to send). Ships its test injections as plain text in scenarios.py; every payload points at a per-run random token or the reserved host range.invalid, and none asks for a secret or a real file. Writes planted documents to per-scenario temp folders (deleted when the scenario ends) and the last 20 results to its plugin data folder (verdicts, the first 240 characters of each blocked call's arguments, the first 400 characters of each drill reply). No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials, telemetry, background threads or dependencies.

name: injection-shield
description: Injection-Shield — defends Thor agents against prompt-injection attacks via tool outputs and untrusted content. Validates LLM responses, audits risky tool calls. Modes: audit / enforcement. Disclosure — privacy-shield sees every user message, outgoing LLM request and assistant reply. Its llm_request middleware rewrites the user messages in each cloud request (current prompt, earlier turns and injected context; Ollama is exempt) to replace detected personal data with tokens, and its transform_llm_output hook puts the real values back into replies on whitelisted channels (telegram, desktop, cli, kanban by default; cron only when you opt in). The token-to-value mapping is kept AES-256-GCM-encrypted in `~/.thor/privacy/mapping.db` (restored attachments go under `~/.thor/privacy/restore/`), and the audit trail is written to `~/.thor/profiles/default/workspace/privacy-shield-audit.jsonl` plus a rotating log, whichever profile is running. The plugin reads its key `PRIVACY_SHIELD_KEY` through the Thor secret scope, and the restore chat id from `PRIVACY_SHIELD_RESTORE_CHAT_ID` or your `pass` entry `thor/telegram/chat_id`. The dashboard/Desktop Controls pane and `privacy-shield set-mode` write its settings into `config.yaml` under `plugins.entries.privacy-shield`. The optional doctor/cleanup shell wrappers under `scripts/cron/` are never installed by the plugin: if you schedule them yourself, they read the key from your `pass` store and call a `telegram-alert.sh` under `$THOR_HOME/profiles/sysadmin/scripts/` if one exists. The plugin itself makes no network calls. Disclosure — injection-shield sees every tool call and tool result, MCP tool descriptions, each user prompt with its conversation history, and every model reply. It adds a firewall instruction block to each prompt as hook context. In enforcement mode it can block tool calls and replace suspicious tool results or model output (the default is audit mode, which only logs). It writes an audit log of detected attempts to `~/.thor/profiles/<profile>/workspace/05-Logs-Snapshots/prompt-injection-attempts.log`, and keeps MCP trust/integrity hash stores under `~/.thor/profiles/default/workspace/05-Logs-Snapshots/`. When you set `INJECTION_SHIELD_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` and `INJECTION_SHIELD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, it sends alert summaries (violation types, counts and time, no matched text) to `api.telegram.org` with your own bot token. Its dashboard/Desktop controls pane saves settings into `config.yaml` under `plugins.entries.injection-shield`. It installs no cron or launchd jobs.

name: inkbox
description: Inkbox email, SMS/MMS, iMessage, voice, and A2A platform plugin for Thor Agent.

name: inkly
description: Run your eSignature and document signing workflows directly from Thor. Inkly lets you send, track, and manage documents for eSignature. Send a contract from your saved templates, turn a PDF into a signable document, see which agreements are still waiting to be signed and send a reminder, or get the signed PDF of any completed document. Built for anyone who needs fast, simple document signing, whether it's contracts, forms, or approvals. Connects to Inkly's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.inkly.so/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the inkly workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Inkly's hosted server (www.inkly.so) and acts on the user's Inkly account at the workspace and access level they approve at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. send_template emails a real, legally binding document, send_reminder emails signers, and void_document voids a sent document and emails its signers; at the default Prepare level nothing is emailed until the user presses Send in Inkly. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: inline-platform
description: Use Thor Agent from Inline work-chat DMs, chats, and reply threads. Disclosure — the setup wizard can, on explicit opt-in, download https://inline.chat/cli/install.sh and pipe it to sh without a checksum, then run the vendor inline CLI login; on connect the adapter publishes your Thor slash-command list and the names and descriptions of installed skills to the Inline server (INLINE_SYNC_COMMANDS=false disables); by default (the bot's Detailed output mode) each turn posts a live progress message into the Inline chat showing the agent's terminal commands with up to 2,000 characters of their output, file paths read or searched, file-edit diffs, web URLs and searches, plans and sub-agent goals, with only best-effort secret masking, visible to everyone in that chat (switch the bot to Friendly output to hide tool details); the inline tool lets the agent add participants to, rename, and permanently delete Inline chats the bot can manage, on the model's decision with no confirmation; error telemetry is off unless a Sentry DSN is set.

name: innernet
description: One memory for every AI tool: load a project's context, answer from what was decided before, save new decisions back, and pick up where the last session left off, in the same memory Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Grok read and write. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at innernet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with CIMD and DCR); the two bundled skills load as innernet:innernet and innernet:innernet-handoff. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code, hooks, background process, telemetry or self-update. Every tool call goes to innernet.live, signed in as the user through innernet's own browser sign-in (a first sign-in creates a free innernet account); what a call carries (a project name, a question, text the user asks to save) is sent there, and what the memory holds comes back into the session context, so it reaches the user's model provider. Some tools write to the user's innernet account (save context, capture a note, write a handoff, update a task, forget on request); every write is versioned and can be read, edited or deleted on the user's dashboard. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with an `mcp_servers.innernet` entry in config.yaml (url https://innernet.live/api/mcp, `auth: oauth`) and `thor mcp login innernet`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: innerscape
description: Gentle check-ins, journaling and an Unstuck Coach with your own Innerscape server: save a mood check-in in your words, save a journal entry or park an inbox item only after you say yes to the exact text, and look back on today. When you're frozen or overloaded, the bundled unstuck skill names what's in the way, gives one next move and holds the rest. The skills never score, label or diagnose a mood. Adds four tools, /innerscape, two skills, a Desktop page and a dashboard tab. Disclosure — calls your Innerscape REST API (default http://127.0.0.1:3001) with INNERSCAPE_TOKEN, read through Thor secret scope, which can read and write your whole account; plain http only to this machine (https to any server you configure), no proxies or redirects; tool results go to your model provider and stay in session history, and mood and journal text is sensitive, so your provider sees it like any other chat; consent is model-mediated: save tools refuse unless the assistant has asked you and set user_confirmed, and Thor has no separate approval step (see README); the Desktop page reads today and saves a check-in or journal entry with that same token through the plugin's dashboard routes (/api/plugins/innerscape/), so anyone signed in to your Thor dashboard can read and write your Innerscape account; reads and saves are off on chat platforms by default and saves are off in scheduled runs; no telemetry, no background jobs.

name: inset
description: Opens your site in headless Chromium at phone, tablet and desktop widths, inspects every page section separately (the Section Atlas) and measures overflow, clipped text, covered controls, section spill-over and failed media with DOM selectors and pixel boxes. Thor fixes the source with its normal tools and approvals; INSET then rechecks the same URL and viewport and reports resolved, reproduced, needs review or not verified, never a pass it could not observe. Disclosure — INSET launches a headless Chromium (installed separately with Playwright) that opens any localhost/loopback port the agent asks for without an approval prompt and returns screenshots and page text to the model; other origins open only when you add them to INSET's allowed_origins setting, and private-network addresses are refused. It also runs read-only git commands in the session workspace.

name: inspeximus
description: Memory provider with keyed corrections you can undo. A correction retires the old value by key, so it stops being recalled, and inspeximus_revert puts the previous value back from the key alone, without anyone retyping what the record used to say. Recall before each turn returns retrieval minus what a later correction retired, so a value corrected three sessions ago cannot come back as context. Adds inspeximus_remember, inspeximus_correct, inspeximus_revert, inspeximus_forget and inspeximus_forget_me. Disclosure — installs the inspeximus package from PyPI (inspeximus>=3.23.1,<4, including its `inspeximus` command-line tools) into the Thor environment; the provider makes no network calls and carries no telemetry: memories live in a local JSON file under the profile's Thor home (or a path you set), recalled memories are added to each turn's context and to the compression summary prompt, and writes made with the built-in memory tool are mirrored into the store.

name: intelligent-tool-break
description: Abort a stalled in-flight tool call with /break, send a note with /break {message}, or retry it with /again without cancelling the rest of the task.

name: intelligent_memory
description: Local-first Arabic/English intelligent memory with canonical facts, conflict lifecycle, bounded recall, and selective Thor cloud enrichment.

name: intentrivet
description: Your existing Thor prepares posts for your own Telegram channels; a post is published only after you allow that exact version for that channel with Allow once in Telegram. Needs the separately installed IntentRivet executor, which holds the publisher bot's token and your decisions. Disclosure — sends the post text and channel key you prepare to the IntentRivet executor at INTENTRIVET_URL with your agent key; the executor (installed separately, holding the publisher bot token) publishes a version to Telegram only after you allow that exact version with Allow once in the bot.

name: intents-pay
description: Crypto invoices and cross-chain payment quotes for a NEAR account via the NEAR Intents 1-Click API. Dry quotes by default. A quote or invoice requires an explicit recipient — there is no default payee. Payable tool calls (invoices and non-dry quotes) wait for Thor's approval prompt via a pre_tool_call hook. Never moves funds and never handles signing keys. Disclosure — payments plugin: sends quote and invoice details (amounts, recipient NEAR account, refund address, and an optional partner API key as X-API-Key) to the NEAR Intents 1-Click API (1click.chaindefuser.com by default); creating an invoice or a live quote produces a real deposit address that anyone can pay, gated by Thor's approval prompt, a one-time confirmation token and a refusal under cron; never signs or sends funds; stores invoices in its plugin-data folder.

name: interim-ledger
description: Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). Counted even where display.interim_assistant_messages hides them. Disclosure — writes message metadata (model, provider, surface, step of the turn, length in characters, 12-digit hashes of the session and turn ids; never the message text) to plugin-data/interim-ledger/interim.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay, change or hide a message; no network

name: internet-outage-checker
description: Check whether a UK broadband provider is down right now, where, what the provider has said and how the last 30 days have gone, through FindBroadband's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.findbroadbanddeals.com/api/mcp/outages, no sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles one skill, uk-broadband-outage-check. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to findbroadbanddeals.com, which logs each call (the tool, the provider matched and the client) for usage statistics, with no IP address or cookies stored. All three tools are read-only and the package marks the server untrusted. Personal, non-commercial use only (findbroadbanddeals.com/terms, section 8). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: internship-scout
description: Find internships on public Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby job boards, pre-screen each application form for blockers (cover letter, essays, how-did-you-hear, transcript, sponsorship, graduation window, pay), and track applications in a local tracker with requisition-level duplicate detection. Disclosure — read-only HTTPS GETs to boards-api.greenhouse.io, api.lever.co, jobs.lever.co and api.ashbyhq.com when a tool is called; stores the tracker (companies, roles, statuses, notes) in a plaintext SQLite database under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/internship-scout/; never signs in, submits applications or contacts employers; no credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: interview-prep-coach
description: Prepares the user for their own interview: researches only the people they will meet, from public professional sources; predicts and tiers likely questions; builds STAR answers only from real experience; runs scored mock interviews; writes questions to ask; assembles a cheat sheet; lists post-interview signals with evidence (no grade or prediction); drafts application materials and thank-you notes the user sends. Disclosure: no tools, hooks, MCP servers, scripts or stored credentials; uses the agent's own web search, never with the user's name, resume or notes; never sends, applies or contacts anyone; never signs in; candidate-side only, its profiles are not consumer reports; never records or infers race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran, marital, family, citizenship or immigration status, health, politics, home address, personal accounts, graduation years, photos or other protected traits.

name: inventory-reminder
description: Live, evidence-backed inventory of the host an agent is running on: repos (cloned vs online-only), skills, MCP servers, CLIs, local models and services, regenerated from ground truth by read-only scanners. Registers two tools — inventory_where(term) answers "do I already have X?" across every section with a ready detail line, and inventory_summary() returns a one-line digest for session bootstrap. Both read a cached digest file ($INVENTORY_JSON, else ~/.thor/inventory.json); no live rescan per turn, no network, no writes. Disclosure — the digest describes the host (repo names, skill names, CLI paths, model names, service names) and that text is returned to the model.

name: invezgo
description: Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX/BEI) market data from the Invezgo API: company profiles, price and indicator charts, intraday and order book, running trade, broker summary and inventory, broker and sector stalker, sector rotation, shareholder composition (KSEI, >1%, >5%, insiders), financial statements, key stats, corporate calendar, news, disclosures and a formula screener, plus read access to the user's own Invezgo portfolio, watchlists, journal and trades. Tools are generated from the bundled OpenAPI spec (spec.json) at load time. Disclosure: every tool call is an HTTPS request to api.invezgo.com with the user's Invezgo API key and counts against their plan quota; results, including personal portfolio data, enter the session context and reach the user's model provider. Read-only by default; 18 write tools (watchlists, journals, trades, alerts, saved screeners) are registered only when INVEZGO_ALLOW_WRITE=1. No background processes, shell commands, stored files or telemetry.

name: invinoveritas-receipts
description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for Thor approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Thor passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

name: iolite
description: Pick an LLM that is smart enough, then cheapest, in one tool call. Set an intelligence floor or name an anchor model, and Iolite returns the few models on the cost x intelligence front, ranked toward cheaper, smarter or balanced. It answers from a catalog of 621 models bundled in the plugin, so a fresh install works offline with no setup. Adds three tools (iolite_shortlist, iolite_model, iolite_show), /iolite, a skill and a Thor Desktop pane that plots the catalog in 3D and 2D and follows the agent's picks. Data and credits: Epoch AI ECI (CC BY), LMArena ratings (CC BY 4.0), LiteLLM prices (MIT); every answer names its sources, and catalog rows whose source names Artificial Analysis are refused. Disclosure — no network unless you set catalog_url (one https GET, no credentials added; plain http only with allow_http); a post_api_request hook records tokens per second and per-task tokens and model seconds (task ids hashed) on your machine only, never uploaded, off with measure_speed and measure_usage false; your last shortlist, your own prices and temporary .pane-*.receipt markers are kept in the plugin data directory; three local Desktop routes (/landscape, /my-prices, /pane-receipt) add no auth of their own and rely on the dashboard's loopback bind, so keep the dashboard on 127.0.0.1; no prompt text is sent to the pane; no secrets read; tool results stay in session history like any tool output.

name: iowap
description: Fleet control for Thor Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). The task watcher posts stage/final task updates into the app's chat composer with user-typed authority (fail-closed, never a broadcast; switchable + persisted, a one-time long-run hint for tasks actually claimed beyond 5 minutes) and warns about fleet anomalies (node up/down, relay reachability) under the same toggle. Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the node-cli, and the plugin makes no raw HTTP calls of its own. Node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files, and tracked task ids are stored in your Thor home under plugin-data/iowap/. The task and fleet watcher is off by default. When you turn it on, it drafts task-event lines (task name, id and stage status, never node output) into the chat composer, or, in direct mode, which you must choose, sends them with your typing authority into the session that submitted the task or the session you configured. No third-party endpoints.

name: iris-chat
description: Private messaging through the separately installed Iris CLI. Instruction-only skill; uses a selected local identity and message history, connects to Nostr relays, and may run a persistent sync service.
