Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs the separately installed iris CLI in the terminal, which creates a local messaging identity (secret keys and message history stored on disk), connects to Nostr relays and peers, can run a persistent sync service until stopped, and sends messages on the user's behalf; messages received from other people are read into the agent's context.

name: iris-chat-channel
description: Chat with Thor through Iris Chat: Signal-like messaging using Nostr Double Ratchet end-to-end encryption, without phone numbers or signup. Iris also supports nearby messaging over local networks and Bluetooth. The native channel supports one approved contact, text replies, seen receipts and typing. Disclosure — invokes the separately installed Iris CLI and runs its background service when needed; Iris stores its own dedicated identity and message history and connects to configured message servers/transports. Plaintext requests pass through Thor and its selected model. No telemetry, automatic software downloads, imported personal keys, or added tools. Not filesystem isolation.

name: iteration-budget-meter
description: Status-bar chip for the focused session per-turn iteration usage (N/60), with a hover tooltip and a click popover of per-request stats.

name: its-in-your-head
description: It's in Your Head — observes how you work (tools, turns, friction) with local-only telemetry, a six-dimension perception engine, deterministic directional adaptation (opt-in, one bounded instruction per turn) and a 96px desktop signal strip with portrait/drift surfaces. Disclosure — network: zero by default (Tier-0 sketch embeddings, stdlib-only). The optional local ONNX Tier-1, enabled only by `/mirror engine enable`, downloads an Apache-2.0 embedding model (onnx-community/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2-ONNX) from Hugging Face, pinned by revision and per-file sha256, into the profile's plugin-data directory; it runs in a Thor-PM isolated environment (onnxruntime >=1.31.1,<1.32, CPU) as a persistent local worker subprocess with a minimal environment, one auto-restart and transparent fallback to Tier-0, plus a small detached watchdog process that kills that worker if Thor exits uncleanly. No other network calls. No credentials are stored, no external telemetry is sent, and raw prompts / reasoning are never stored (transient buffer, derived features only).

name: iwork-studio
description: Create, edit, design and export Apple Numbers, Keynote and Pages files: designed Keynote decks from data and the user's brand kit, spreadsheet cells, formulas and formatting, Pages text and tables, exports to PDF, Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Every write is backed up, made on a copy, re-read and checked, then swapped in; any change can be undone in one call. Arabic and right-to-left text round-trip exactly. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/): a local stdio MCP server (65 tools) and a workflow skill. macOS. Disclosure — first start downloads iwork-studio==2.6.1 and its Python dependencies from PyPI with uvx (about 60 MB; built from the v2.6.1 tag by the repo's release workflow through PyPI trusted publishing; the server code is that release, not the pinned tree); Pages, exports, render checks and Keynote slide operations drive Numbers, Keynote and Pages through osascript, and macOS asks once for Automation access; it reads and writes the iWork files and export targets the agent names, anywhere on disk unless IWORK_STUDIO_ROOTS is set to fence it, and Thor does not prompt before its write tools; it keeps backups in ~/.iwork-studio/backups (last 10 per file) and saved design kits in ~/.iwork-studio/kits; no network calls after the download, no telemetry, no self-updates.

name: ja-writing-guard
description: ja_writing_check returns line, column and fix hint. Default is report; enforce rewrites a flagged answer only when numbers, names, URLs, code, and negation survive and the score drops under threshold. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; the ja_writing_check tool has no user list of its own and is on by default on every platform for anyone who can use the agent there (`thor tools disable ja_writing --platform <platform>` turns it off); reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only Thor helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.

name: jackal-verified
description: Typed adapter for the reproducible JACKAL v1.7.3 release: 41 catalog-derived verification tools (exact, numerical, Lean-checked bounded lanes, claim replay).

name: jalancost
description: Offline Malaysian road-trip fuel and toll estimates with per-person splits, calculated only from user-supplied values.

name: jekyll-hyde
description: Context optimization and execution alignment for agent sessions.

name: jet-browser
description: Verify Jet Browser startup, native input, DOM agreement, and PNG capture inside a network-isolated WPE WebKit container. Disclosure — runs `docker run` (Docker access is root-equivalent on the host) on the digest-pinned image ghcr.io/masakaai/jet-browser@sha256:540a1fec…, pulled from GHCR on first use; the container has no network and only SETUID/SETGID capabilities, but runs with AppArmor and systempaths unconfined and a seccomp profile that allows user-namespace and mount syscalls for WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox; the tool takes no arguments and loads only a built-in local test page.

name: jev
description: Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

name: jev-agent-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (agent_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Thor tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-approvals
description: TypeSafe's Jev decision model as Thor' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.

name: jev-cron-gate
description: Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.

name: jev-curator
description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Thor' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Thor retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

name: jev-effort-router
description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing chat_completions provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. The six measured criteria are capability slots; a built-in Ollama:Cloud profile ships, and provider_profiles maps the slots to another active provider's models. Most catalog routers decide one half — a model or an effort level; this one decides both per turn, with a measured grid, a confidence guard, per-surface policy and an audit trail that reports what was applied. Ollama:Cloud is the shipped profile; another chat_completions provider is routed only when the operator declares a profile, and the router never switches providers. Every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to the Decisions surface selected by the key present (Requesty /v1/systemone with typesafe/jev-1.14.0, or OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13), billed to that account; credentials are read through Thor' profile secret scope; the local audit file keeps decisions and turn identifiers, message text only when explicitly enabled; no telemetry.

name: jev-judge
description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

name: jev-mcp-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (mcp_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Thor tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-memory-selector
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (memory_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Thor tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-model-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (model_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Thor tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-skill-router
description: Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads Thor' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

name: jev-skill-router-mcp
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (skill_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Suggests at most one skill per request via the TypeSafe (Jev) cookbook pattern; roster is read live from the profile skills dir. Note: the portable loader does not interpolate env in mcp.json — JEV_TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be present in the server's inherited environment (native mcp_servers declaration works too).

name: jev-typesafe
description: TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

name: jg-provider-usage
description: Provider usage in a Desktop status-bar chip, popover and full page: subscription windows, API balances, reset times and profile-scoped account state. Includes data-only JSON connectors with explicit destination approval, setup cards for Claude, Gemini and Z.ai, a running-agents footer with honest unknowns, and an active-account Codex banked-reset preview/confirmation. Stock Thor 0.23.1 needs no core patch; xAI subscription credits and exact worker-account usage need optional host metadata and otherwise remain unavailable. Usage reads use Thor account helpers or scoped API-key access and provider HTTPS endpoints; subscription tokens stay with Thor. Custom definitions are HTTPS GET only, approved-host restricted, with no redirects or executable code. Confirming a Codex reset spends one banked reset; refresh and preview do not. No purchase, automatic redemption, telemetry or self-update. Screenshots and demo use real plugin components with clearly labeled synthetic data, not live accounts. Disclosure — reads your own usage/credit data with vendor client-identity headers (`User-Agent: codex-cli` to chatgpt.com for Codex reset credits; `x-xai-token-auth: xai-grok-cli` to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com for Grok billing); the usage page can read every local Thor profile's provider usage through Thor' profile scope; confirming a Codex reset in the page spends one banked reset; it reads state.db read-only for token totals and fetches DeepSeek's public pricing page every 12 hours.

name: jira-browser
description: Jira workspace for Thor Desktop, linking tickets to Thor Projects, worktrees, and conversations. Disclosure — reads a Jira API token from JIRA_* env vars or ~/jira-config/config.json (owner-only, read-only) and sends it only to your configured https Jira origin; agent tools are read-only but return Jira text (untrusted) to the model; Start work / Draft update create chats seeded with ticket descriptions (Draft update auto-runs a turn); PR/CI status is read through your local gh CLI login.

name: job-hunt-tracker
description: Log job applications, check for duplicates before applying, and track follow-ups. A job-hunt tracker for Thor.

name: job-search
description: A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

name: jobby
description: Source-backed international job discovery and PDF/DOCX application drafts inside Thor; no autonomous submission. Disclosure — confirmed searches send your approved resume-derived search terms, country and location to Indeed and LinkedIn through the JobSpy scraper library; importing reads the absolute PDF path you (or the agent) give it on the backend machine and stores your resume facts, postings and generated documents in this profile's plugin data folder; the plugin never fills or submits applications.

name: jot
description: Notes, checklists and documents beside Thor that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.

name: joust
description: Races 2 to 4 coding subagents on one task, each in its own Git worktree, judges them with your tests and merges only the best patch after you approve. joust_launch provisions one detached worktree per contender under the profile's plugin-data folder (uncommitted tracked edits are mirrored and committed as the baseline) and, inside an agent turn, launches one Thor subagent per contender through ctx.subagent_lifecycle, optionally each on its own model. A tool_request middleware rewrites each child session's file paths, V4A patch headers, search roots and terminal workdir into its worktree, and a pre_tool_call hook vetoes escapes. joust_evaluate runs the bout's test command in every worktree through the Thor terminal tool, 1 to 7 times (Flake Shield: every run must pass, median speed, flaky contenders cannot win), scoring Correctness 60, Speed 25 and Diff minimalism 15. joust_crossfire fires each contender's new tests at every rival worktree, and survival is the first tiebreak. joust_merge applies the winner with git apply behind Thor's approval gate, after saving a rollback patch and keeping every contender as a joust/<bout>/<contender> branch; joust_report writes a markdown bout report. Also adds /joust, the thor joust CLI, the joust-arena skill and a Desktop half (/joust page, right pane, status-bar chip, palette command, ::joust-bout inline card). Disclosure — runs local git in the repository you name (rev-parse, worktree add/remove/prune, add -N, diff, apply, apply -R, reset, branch, write-tree and commit-tree; init/add/commit for its demo repo and the copy fallback, which copies the repository into the profile's plugin-data folder), registers worktrees in that repository's .git/worktrees until joust_merge action=cleanup, creates joust/<bout>/<contender> branches (config keep_loser_branches, default on), and writes the approved patch into your working tree. Contender subagents' file paths and terminal workdir are redirected into their worktrees, but their shell commands are not sandboxed beyond Thor's normal approvals. Test commands (yours or the model's) run only through the Thor terminal tool, also on a background thread when a contender subagent finishes (auto_evaluate_on_stop, default on); the CLI and dashboard refuse to judge, and only the self-contained demo uses a bounded subprocess with plugin-authored commands. Captured output is secret-scrubbed with a stdlib regex and stored, with diffs, goals and repository paths, in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/joust/joust.db (SQLite); bout snapshots are broadcast to connected Thor Desktop windows and the Desktop half polls the dashboard API while visible. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no Python dependencies. Linux and macOS.

name: jp-address
description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Give it a Japanese postal address as written, such as 東京都千代田区霞が関2-1-2, and it returns the prefecture, city and town as separate fields. Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL is read for the active profile on each call, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Called from Thor with five models in a small sample of 18 sessions (see CHANGELOG.md). The skill tells the model to pass a registered address from a company record into address_split only when a tool result already returned that address. If none was returned, it says the address was not split. When level is below 3, absent lists the missing parts, and those parts are not 0. pre_llm_call adds the address paragraph only on an address question, and adds nothing on other turns. An address question is 所在地, 住所, 都道府県, 丁目, 番地, a prefecture name, or address_split called in the previous turn. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says to call address_split only with an address copied from a tool result, names the absent parts by level, and says a missing part is not written as 0. When a previous turn returned a prefecture, it says to copy that prefecture. transform_llm_output returns no string unless address_split was called and jp-charts would leave the reply unchanged. It does not match success wording. When address_split returned no prefecture, a named prefecture is removed and the reply says the address was not split. level 0, bad_args, and upstream are not described as a completed split.

name: jp-charts
description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Following Japanese chart conventions, it turns a table typed in chat or read from a CSV or JSON file into a bar or line graph ready to post. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure — no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Thor home); writes PNGs to the Thor image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default). The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with thor tools. Installing the plugin also installs the Python packages matplotlib and matplotlib-fontja from PyPI. The PNGs are written to <THOR_HOME>/cache/images. Removing the plugin deletes its folder only; the PNGs and those two packages stay. A transform_tool_result hook remembers value and unit pairs in the process for that session and does not change the tool result. A pre_tool_call hook blocks chart_render when a plotted number was already returned in the same session with a different unit string, including a comma-grouped number such as 1,234, and no PNG is written. pre_llm_call adds one paragraph only on a chart question, and adds nothing on other turns. A chart question is 図, グラフ, チャート, or the word chart, or chart_render, chart_validate, or chart_types called in the previous turn. Company, filing, and unrelated questions do not add it. The paragraph says to call chart_render only with numbers and the unit copied from a tool result, that 1,234 is the same integer as 1234, that a different unit blocks the chart, and not to say a chart was drawn or write 取得しました when no number was returned. transform_llm_output does not replace or delete the model's sentences. It appends one line when this turn's tool record has no figure and an area tool was called, or some tool was called on a company or filing question. The line is: Tool record: this turn returned no company, filing, address, subsidy, statute, or chart figure, so a number or a fetch claim in this reply is not from a tool result. chart_types and chart_validate are not a figure. A turn whose only area tool is address_split is left unchanged by this hook.

name: jp-chatwork
description: Talk to Thor from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Thor in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Thor commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Thor commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

name: jp-corporate
description: Look up a Japanese company by name or 13-digit corporate number and read its gBizINFO record, from registration to subsidies, contracts, and financials. Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up only to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN, read on each call; no proxy, nothing written to disk; the tools are on for every surface, so anyone you allow on a gateway spends your token; the bundled japan-company skill adds one line to every skills index; on turns that look like company talk (a 13-digit number, 法人番号, 株式会社 and other legal forms, a few listed company names, or a jp_corp call last turn) a pre_llm_call hook adds a fixed paragraph, even where the tools are off, telling the model to find jp_corp_search via tool_search before web_search, copy next_step on token_missing, and not state data or write 取得しました/確認できます that the tool did not return.

name: jp-edinet
description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. It finds a Japanese company's annual securities report (yuho) and other financial reports filed on EDINET, and reads headline figures such as revenue and total assets from a filing. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. Each call reads EDINET_API_KEY for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Thor. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false means that line is absent from that period in periods or in filing_company (CurrentYear or Prior1Year to Prior4Year), not proof the filing has no figure, and not 0. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Thor internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup. Since version 0.1.6 it returns those five consolidated periods in periods and the filing-company six lines in filing_company. A missing line is not copied from the other series. pre_llm_call adds one of three paragraphs only on a filing question (有報, 有価証券, 連結, 提出会社, the word EDINET, securities, or consolidated) or when edinet_search_filings, edinet_financials, or edinet_save_document was called in the previous turn, and adds nothing on other turns. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. When the secret helper cannot be read, the paragraph says the helper could not be read and does not say the key is unset. When EDINET_API_KEY is unset, the paragraph says to call edinet_search_filings once with the company name only, not to invent a file date, and to copy the free-key next_step (WEEK0060, the unit, and the filing URL once a document id is known). When the key is set, the paragraph says to call edinet_financials once a doc_id is known, and otherwise edinet_search_filings with only the file dates the user wrote. Each paragraph says not to write successfully retrieved, verified, or obtained using. That ban is the same as 取得しました.

name: jp-egov-law
description: Japanese laws for Thor Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Ask for one Japanese law article, such as Article 32 of the Labor Standards Act, and it returns the official law text with the law number and the date that version took effect. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Thor tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until thor cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; thor tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint. pre_llm_call adds its paragraph only on a statute question, and adds nothing on other turns. A statute question matches 法令, 法律, 条文, e-Gov, 第N条, or 条 outside 条件, or egov_law_search, egov_law_article, or egov_law_revisions called in the previous turn. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says not to call egov_law_search with an empty query or a company name, that pre_tool_call blocks that search, that no article URL is written and a URL is not guessed, and to call egov_law_article when a law and an article are named and copy source.url; the same paragraph also tells the model not to call tool_describe and not to write 取得しました or 確認できます on that turn. pre_tool_call blocks egov_law_search when the query is empty or, in title mode, does not name a statute. 条 inside 条件 is not a statute name. The block says no article URL was written and a URL was not guessed. A text-mode search and egov_law_article are not blocked.

name: jp-estat
description: Japanese government statistics from the e-Stat API: search tables and fetch figures such as population, households, wages, and prices, with estat_search_tables, estat_table_info, and estat_get_data. Disclosure — It needs a free e-Stat application ID, set as ESTAT_APP_ID in the .env of each profile. Each call sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp and puts ESTAT_APP_ID in the request URL. The ID is read for the active profile on each call. An HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used, and no other host is called. Nothing is written to disk, and this plugin creates no cron job. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call them with your ID. Turn a surface off with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

name: jp-kokkai
description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Posts new Diet meeting hits as metadata and the official meeting URL, with kokkai_search, kokkai_speech, and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key. kokkai_speech requests speech text and returns a short excerpt. Speech text is not stored. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, read a speech excerpt, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with thor tools. kokkai_watch add writes THOR_HOME/scripts/jp-kokkai-watch.py and creates one cron job that does not call a model, once a day, at the hour you pick in Thor's own timezone. Each run costs 0 tokens and has no daily cap. Empty script output sends nothing. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run thor cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch returns one pre_tool_call approve line, as does a repeat add that switches the saved job. Thor shows it. An unchanged repeat add returns none. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt when a person is present. A cron job, thor -q, and a separate plugin process cannot add or remove a watch even after always. A webhook or API-server turn inside the gateway is refused by Thor unless "always" was already given for that exact add plan. plugins.isolation: host still blocks add and remove. Answering "always" on add covers only the same add plan. That choice adds one plugin_rule:kokkai_watch: line to config.yaml, and the line stays after the plugin is removed. A different add plan asks again. Remove builds a new rule key on every call, so answering always on remove does not cover the next remove, including the call that deletes the cron job. While the read-meetings skill is enabled, Thor adds one line to the skill index of every session, including a session whose tools are turned off. The scheduled script does not run inside plugins.isolation: host, so that setting does not stop the watch. kokkai_watch run still cannot save seen speech IDs under plugins.isolation: host and says so on every run of the tool. The cron mark is cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Thor 0.21.6). The daily job is created with the public thor cron command using --no-agent and --script. thor cron create on 0.21.6 cannot pin a toolset, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Running add again asks, then switches a model job onto the script and clears its prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next add. An update can stop the watch if the cron mark or that command moves. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data. The script timeout is 3600 seconds unless it was changed. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Thor 0.22.2, not in a live chat.

name: jp-reinfolib
description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Use it for Japanese real estate and property prices in one city: it returns the number of recorded sales, the median trade price and the first 20 rows for a quarter. These are transaction prices, not the official land prices published as 地価公示. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. thor tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until thor cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」

name: jp-subsidies
description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with thor tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. The /subsidies command is outside thor tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run thor cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows. subsidies_detail compares a corporation's published industry, capital, employee count, and address with the call text as characters, returns a cap only when the call states one, and does not estimate an award. pre_tool_call blocks subsidies_search unless keyword is contained in industry text copied from a tool result, including a list of industry strings. A company name does not pass, including when the industry text is contained in the company name. When industry text was returned and the keyword is not that text, the block does not say the industry was missing. The block says the search was not run, eligibility is not_claimed, and no award was estimated. A company name contained in business_summary does not pass as an industry keyword. That holds when the name field is absent and the summary is トヨタ自動車は自動車を製造する。: トヨタ自動車 does not pass and 自動車 does. transform_tool_result remembers industry text and returns nothing, so the tool result is unchanged. pre_llm_call adds its paragraph only on a subsidy question (補助金, 助成金, jGrants, or 募集) or when subsidies_search, subsidies_detail, or subsidies_watch_setup was called in the previous turn, and adds nothing on other turns. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says to call subsidies_search only with industry text copied from a tool result, that eligibility is not_claimed, and not to estimate an award or write 対象です.

name: junie-acp
description: JetBrains Junie coding agent as a Thor model provider over ACP.

name: jw3
description: JW3.ai non-custodial trading inside Thor: 12 market/risk/Diary reads, Diary propose cards, and 4 human-approved execution tools — all thin wrappers over the local jw3 CLI, which owns the PAT and enforces server-side scope, kill-switch, fee, and idempotency gates. Bundles the jw3-ops skill and /jw3-status. Disclosure — every tool call runs the local `jw3` CLI (installed separately from github.com/agnostic4321-ops/jw3-mcp-cli, not covered by the pinned sha) with a minimal env (PATH, HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, TMPDIR, JW3_*); the CLI holds the JW3 PAT and reaches JW3.ai's Supabase edge functions and the user's exchange accounts; jw3_execute, jw3_close, jw3_exits and jw3_cancel dry-run unless confirm=true, and every confirm=true call goes through a Thor approval prompt showing the exact command before it places, closes or cancels real orders with real funds (unattended runs follow the user's approval mode; an "always" answer pre-approves only that identical command); the plugin itself holds no secrets and stores nothing.

name: jwt-ref
description: @jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.

name: k6pane
description: Local load testing with Grafana k6 from chat. Three tools: k6pane_doctor (checks the k6 install and limits), k6pane_run (writes and runs a k6 test from a URL or a multi-step request flow with smoke, load, stress, spike, soak, constant or fixed-arrival-rate profiles, or runs your own k6 script) and k6pane_report (lists, reads and compares stored runs and flags latency, throughput and error regressions). Each run returns pass, fail, invalid (the requested load was never actually applied: dropped iterations, achieved rate short of target, or timeout) or error, with RPS, error rate, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and a per-endpoint breakdown. Bundles the k6pane:load-testing skill. Targets are limited to localhost and private networks unless the user lists a host in the allowed_hosts setting; link-local and cloud metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, fd00:ec2::254) are refused unless the exact host is allowlisted, and k6 is fenced with --blacklist-ip to exactly the validated IPs, so redirects, DNS rebinding and runtime-built URLs cannot reach anything else. VU, duration and request-rate caps reject oversized tests. One run at a time. Disclosure — runs the user's local k6 binary as a subprocess (never through a shell); sends load-test traffic only to the validated targets; resolves target hostnames via DNS; k6's anonymous usage report is disabled; no other network calls, no telemetry, no update checks. Writes each run (generated script, k6 summary, k6 log, parsed result, all redacted) under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/k6pane/runs plus a run.lock file. Reads only k6 scripts the user points it at. Custom script/script_path tests are JavaScript that k6 runs directly on the host, outside the Thor terminal sandbox and approval prompt, and k6's open() can read local files. Credentials: optional K6PANE_SECRET_<NAME> values, resolved per profile through agent.secret_scope.get_secret only when a test references ${secret.NAME}, passed to k6 through an inherited pipe (never disk or argv) and redacted from every stored file and tool result; k6 runs with a scrubbed environment. Standard library only, no Python dependencies; requires the k6 binary (not bundled).

name: kaggle-competitions
description: Track Kaggle competitions from your agent: live submission status, score history, personal-best watch, leaderboards, and new-score watch. Four agent tools over the Kaggle CLI (submissions, score history, watch for new results, leaderboards), a desktop pane, a full web page with sidebar nav, and a dashboard API route. Multi-competition - track any number of slugs via config. Auth resolves KAGGLE_API_TOKEN through Thor's secret scope (declared secret in the manifest) or lets the CLI read ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json; child processes get a minimal explicit environment; the token is never logged or echoed. No telemetry, no third-party services. Disclosure — the tools and the dashboard page run your locally installed `kaggle` CLI (a third-party binary not covered by this pin) with a minimal environment that includes KAGGLE_API_TOKEN from Thor's secret scope when set (otherwise the CLI reads ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json itself); submission data is cached under the Thor plugin-data directory.

name: kairos
description: The god of the opportune moment, now working for Thor. It waits for a clean stopping point to offer a short break or a wind-down at the bedtime you chose, saves your place so stopping costs nothing, and reports only what your data supports. Disclosure — reads Thor's own session store (state.db, read-only: message timestamps, roles and tool names, no message text) to chart when you work; `sleep_import` reads the sleep export file you or the agent name (CSV, Gadgetbridge SQLite, Xiaomi folder), and `kairos_wearable` calls only MCP servers you list in `plugins.entries.kairos.mcp_allowlist`; adds short blocks to the conversation through `pre_llm_call` (wind-down nudge, break suggestion, the opt-in pomodoro offer, and once per new session the handoff note the agent saved when you last stopped, kept in the plugin's data folder), never into cron or subagent turns; `on_session_end` records, with the pomodoro on, when each turn ended, whether it completed, and its tool-call count (timestamps and counts only, in the plugin's own database); the optional quiet-hours guard can require approval for or block destructive terminal/file/code tool calls during hours you set.

name: kanban-empowered
description: A redesign for the Thor kanban: per-board project status, a dashboard that explains what is really happening across your boards, a live summary of what each agent is doing right now, a chain view that shows where a block starts, and a fast way to answer what the kanban needs from you, by Telegram or Desktop. Cards waiting on a person get a structured ask, reminders and an escalation; cards held by guards or parked by host failures are reported or undone within a budget. No card stays silently stuck. Disclosure — a coordinator runs inside the gateway's kanban dispatch tick (coordinator profile only, leader lock, no extra process); it reads every board's kanban database and metadata through Thor' kanban functions and writes only through them (comments, unblocking a waiting card when its owner answers, undoing an infrastructure park, reassigning a card on the release command); its SQLite state lives under the coordinator profile's plugin-data/kanban-empowered and is read by the plugin in every other profile, and its doctor command reads every profile's config.yaml read-only; it consumes Telegram replies from the configured owners to its own messages before they reach the agent, except that an owner's answer to a card a worker cannot run is rewritten into an instruction (card title, assignee and the owner's answer) and passed on as a normal turn to the Thor session of that same chat, reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (the gateway's bot) only through Thor' secret scope, and, apart from the auxiliary model below, calls only the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage, editMessageText, pinChatMessage to the configured owner chats, one pinned panel; never getUpdates) plus Thor' own IPv4 fallback path (DNS-over-HTTPS lookups of api.telegram.org at dns.google and cloudflare-dns.com); to show what a running card is doing, the Desktop backend reads that worker's recent session from its profile's state.db read-only (what the agent wrote, including reasoning, and tool names; never commands or tool output), redacts secrets and sends it to the Thor auxiliary model the user configured, only when the session changed and at most once a minute per card; when the user asks to explain a project's blocks, it also sends that project's waiting cards (titles, block reasons, options and counts, already redacted; no sessions, comments or command output) to the same auxiliary model; no shell commands and no telemetry; imports private Thor kanban, i18n, profile, plugin and Telegram-network modules (listed in its README); ships an optional core patch adding kanban veto hooks that the user applies by hand to the Thor checkout (the plugin never applies it, and `thor update` drops it), and registers kanban_pre_claim only on a Thor build that exposes it.

name: kanban-gantt
description: One board, three views, and each answers a different question: List says what the work is, Timeline says when it happened, Graph says what hangs off what. The Graph view draws a card per task and an arrow per dependency, laid out top-down by longest path (or left to right, by status, or as a compact grid), with a transitive reduction that counts the arrows it implies instead of hiding them, links you draw, move and delete where they are drawn, and a click that lights the whole upstream and downstream lineage of a task. The Timeline renders any board as real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a period selector from 6 hours to 7 days. The List view trades the bars for a dense table — task, assignee, status, last activity. Quick scopes (Running, Blocked, Open, All) narrow the board in all three views alike, and a lineage switch widens any of them to what leads to the selection and what follows it. Tasks are created from the page (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parented by drag & drop or from the drawer, and moved between boards with their children; any task with files carries a paperclip, its files listed on demand — the board payload carries only a count — and previewed by type (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or downloaded. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download; read a task's worker log from the kanban worker-log folder); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.

name: kanban-graph
description: Live, read-only dependency graph of the Thor kanban boards in Thor Desktop: every board as a band, tasks as cards, dependencies as arrows with implied ones folded away. Click a task to light up its whole lineage with runs, last failure and the running worker's latest tool calls; deep links open a task directly, and a stdlib CLI renders the same graph as a standalone HTML file. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — reads every kanban board database and, for running tasks, the assignee profile's state.db (the kanban worker session's latest assistant messages and tool-call arguments), read-only, and shows them in Desktop through its own local dashboard routes.

name: kanban-live-gantt
description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the Thor kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.

name: kanban-stream
description: Live-stream Thor kanban worker activity to a Telegram ops channel: one edit-in-place message per task with rolling tool-call history, elapsed timer, tokens/sec, thinking indicator, and a pinned final state (done/blocked). Mid-task steering via task comments — /steer from Telegram through the bundled companion daemon, or straight from the board. Ships disabled by default; needs a dedicated ops bot (KANBAN_STREAM_BOT_TOKEN + KANBAN_STREAM_ALLOWED_USERS). Outbound calls go only to api.telegram.org; reads the kanban DB read-only; no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — sends kanban task titles, summaries and tool names with command/path snippets to the Telegram chat you configure via your own bot; the optional steer daemon posts allowlisted Telegram users' /steer text as task comments that reach the running worker.

name: kanban-task-threads
description: Give every Thor kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

name: kanban-tenant-labels
description: Shows each Kanban card's tenant as a colored label on the card in Thor Desktop, with automatic colors and pinned colors in Settings. Disclosure — the labels go through the Desktop SDK's Kanban card badge slot (KANBAN_CARD_AREAS.badges) and Desktop paints them; the plugin reads only what Desktop passes to its badge decorator (each card's tenant and the board's tenant list) and stores pinned colors in ctx.storage; no DOM writes, no query-cache reads, no network requests, no backend, no telemetry; no background timers, observers or listeners, only one 0 ms ctx.setTimeout that refreshes the settings page when a board's tenant list changes.

name: kareverse
description: Elder care at home in Bangalore, India, from Thor through Kareverse's public MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.kareverse.com/mcp, no sign-in): search services and prices, read a service's details, the monthly Care Plan, service areas and care guides, and send a callback request to the Kareverse team. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to www.kareverse.com, operated by Kareverse; submit_enquiry sends the name, phone number and details the user provides to Kareverse so the team can call back, requires consent: true, and the package marks the server trust: untrusted so Thor asks before it runs. The other six tools are read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: kata
description: Learns the multi-step tool routines your agent keeps repeating across conversations and, only after you review and approve each one, compiles it into a single deterministic tool that runs its steps without model round-trips in between. Proposals show the steps, data flow between them, permissions, input and output schemas, per-step side effects and a twelve-check offline validation (exact replay of recorded runs, held-out fit, injected failures and timeouts, secret scan, tool schema fingerprints). Approve, reject, disable, roll back and inspect run traces from /kata, `thor kata` or a dashboard tab. Disclosure — records tool names, arguments and results (first 64 KB, secret-named keys and common credential formats redacted) plus model request timing and token counts to a local SQLite file under its plugin data directory, kept for 30 days by default; registers tools only after explicit approval and executes their steps through ctx.dispatch_tool; katas whose steps have external or unclassified effects escalate every call to Thor's own approval prompt with a fresh rule key, so remembered approvals never repeat them and unattended runs follow Thor's approval policy; side-effecting steps are never retried; makes no network, model or subprocess calls of its own.

name: keenable-plugin
description: Web search and page fetching through Keenable's hosted MCP server, with search and research skills: single-site and publish-date filters, result and snippet limits, and page fetches that return only what a prompt asks for. Works without an API key; an optional KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limits. Adds direct MCP tools beside Thor's built-in Keenable web backend and leaves web_search / web_extract provider selection unchanged. Disclosure: connects to Keenable's hosted MCP server at `api.keenable.ai` and sends it the search queries, URLs and fetch prompts the agent issues, labelled with the header `X-Keenable-Title: thor-plugin`; sends `X-API-Key` only when the user adds the optional config.yaml entry with their key.

name: keepmd-mcp-eob-decoder
description: Explain the codes, insurance terms and patient-responsibility math on a medical Explanation of Benefits (EOB), Medicare Summary Notice or itemized bill through KeepMD's hosted, read-only MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.keepmd.org/eob, no sign-in, no keys): official ICD-10-CM and HCPCS Level II descriptors, code search from everyday wording, an insurance glossary, EOB arithmetic checks and a reading and appeal guide. Bundles the reading-an-eob workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to KeepMD's hosted server (mcp.keepmd.org), which receives only codes, search words, insurance terms and dollar amounts and stores nothing; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. All five tools are annotated read-only. General billing and coding reference, not medical, legal or financial advice.

name: keepvoice-thor
description: Start a KeepVoice voice-cleanup job from an authorized upload, track creator review and approval, and release the final video only for the approved revision. Requires a KeepVoice agent token; media processing and human review stay in KeepVoice. Disclosure — sends your KeepVoice agent token, the upload ID, a rights confirmation and the clip-provenance text you give to https://keepvoice.yablokolabs.com (the author's hosted service; media processing and human review happen there, no media leaves through the plugin). The rights confirmation is passed by the model, so confirm it yourself before asking the agent to submit. On CLI, TUI, Desktop and ACP the time-limited signed download link is returned into the session and stays in its history; on messaging platforms it is withheld. No telemetry, no background processes.

name: keln-provider
description: Keln as a Thor model provider (`--provider keln`): open models through an OpenAI-compatible API, with the live catalog and a tool-calling fallback list. Sends requests to api.keln.ai using your KELN_API_KEY.

name: keryx
description: Outbound phone calls from your own phone. Thor writes a brief and calls place_call; after you approve (every call, single use), your phone dials over Bluetooth hands-free through PipeWire's telephony API, the plugin plays an AI-disclosure line, and a realtime voice model (OpenAI Realtime or GPT-Live) holds the conversation, asking you mid-call when it needs a decision. The outcome, details and transcript go back to Thor; /calls lists recent calls. Guardrails in code: emergency, short-code and premium numbers blocked, quiet hours, hourly rate limit, hard 5-minute cap. Linux only (PipeWire >= 1.4, a paired phone). Disclosure — places real calls on the user's SIM; call audio streams to OpenAI (wss://api.openai.com realtime or live sessions) plus OpenAI TTS for the disclosure line and, for GPT-Live, one Responses request per call; runs busctl, pw-dump, pw-record, pw-play, pw-link, pw-cli and espeak-ng; audio processes and two temporary virtual PipeWire nodes exist only during an approved call; stores a call log (and recordings only if `record: true`) under plugin-data/keryx; reads OPENAI_API_KEY through Thor secrets only.

name: kestra-oncall
description: Puts Thor on call for Kestra. When an execution in an allowed namespace fails, Thor reads the failed task, its error logs and what changed since the last good run, proposes the smallest fix to the flow and asks you in chat. After one approval it saves the fix as a new flow revision, replays the failed execution from the task that failed (tasks that already succeeded are not rerun), follows the replay and checks the result. A failed replay restores the previous revision if the flow is still at the fixed one. Kestra Pause tasks become chat questions you can answer from any Thor surface. A Kestra on-call dashboard tab and Desktop pane list incidents, proposals and pauses (read-only). Disclosure: network: only the Kestra URL you configure (kestra_url, HTTPS required except for loopback and explicitly allowed private hosts), with the Kestra credentials you give Thor (KESTRA_USERNAME and KESTRA_PASSWORD or KESTRA_API_TOKEN, read through Thor secret scope). No other host, no telemetry. Writes to Kestra: a flow update, a replay, a rollback to the previous revision and resume or kill of a paused execution. Each needs a person: the typed command /kestra apply <id> <hash> (the hash must match the stored proposal) or Thor's approval card for the two write tools with the whole stored diff, bound to the proposal hash. Diffs too long to read in full are refused. The write tools refuse in webhook, cron, single-query and unknown surfaces and the model-driven path refuses while Thor approvals are bypassed. Fails closed: an empty namespaces setting allows nothing and protected_flows are diagnosis-only. Stored data: incidents, flow sources, error logs, task outputs, diffs, proposals and decision records in the plugin's profile-scoped SQLite database. Data sent elsewhere: the tools return flow sources, error logs, task outputs and execution inputs to the model, so they go to the profile's LLM provider. The dashboard routes under /api/plugins/kestra-oncall only read and show diffs and logs to anyone who can open the Thor dashboard. thor kestra-oncall setup --apply adds one named webhook route to config.yaml and never deploys a Kestra flow. Anyone holding WEBHOOK_SECRET can start a read-only model run against your Kestra. AI-assisted implementation.

name: keychain
description: Keep Thor provider credentials in the macOS login keychain instead of plaintext .env. Registers a SecretSource (secrets.keychain), so startup resolution runs through Thor's own orchestrator, after ~/.thor/.env loads and before credentials are read — the same path the bundled Bitwarden and 1Password sources use. Bindings are explicit (secrets.keychain.env: ENV_VAR: keychain-account) or discovered from an index the plugin keeps inside the keychain, so `thor keychain put NAME` is the whole setup. Adds keychain_status (vault-backed vs still-plaintext inventory; names, lengths and outcomes only), keychain_migration_plan (report-only: lists candidates and returns the exact `thor keychain migrate ...` command; writes nothing) and keychain_audit (fetch/migrate trail), plus a `thor keychain put|ls|rm|test|migrate|status|audit` CLI. Migration is operator-only in that CLI: it stores each value, verifies it by readback, backs up .env (0600), then removes the variable through thor_cli.config.remove_env_value() — the `thor config unset` path, so core's .env lock and its refusals for package-managed installs and admin-managed keys still apply. Disclosure — reads and writes generic-password items in the user's login keychain through /usr/bin/security called by absolute path (service `thor` by default); no network calls and no third-party service, nothing leaves the machine; the index of stored names lives in a keychain item (`thor!index`) and the audit log in <thor home>/plugin-data/keychain/audit.jsonl; the only .env write is the operator-run `thor keychain migrate` described above; the agent-facing tools write nothing; a locked keychain or denied ACL is a warning, never a startup block; a stored value is passed on argv for the single `security add-generic-password` call (visible to same-user processes for that moment) while reads, the once-per-process hot path, never put a value on argv. macOS-only, no Python dependencies, no env vars.

name: kfchow-llm-value-router
description: Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.thor/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.thor/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.

name: kimchi-acp-provider
description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Thor model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Thor's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Thor cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Thor.

name: kimchi-provider
description: Kimchi (kimchi.dev) models via the OpenAI-compatible API — live catalog from the metadata endpoint, API-key auth, gateway unknown-model 400s classified as model_not_found, and an identifying User-Agent (thor-agent/<version>) on every gateway request.

name: kimi-code-delegate
description: Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for Thor Agent

name: kin
description: Gives Thor Desktop a face. Pick one of thirteen original characters, six 3D busts and seven 2D cartoons, each with its own voice. It watches your sessions, frowns when a step fails, and grins when a turn finishes. An optional overlay adds a plain-English task drawer, voice input, and one-click screen diagnosis. Disclosure — the optional overlay is a separate Electron app you install with npm and run yourself. It reads Thor's state.db (read-only), processes.json and the latest terminal output to draw its task drawer. When you click it, it captures the active window or terminal with the OS screenshot tool, OCRs it with tesseract, and submits that text to Thor as a prompt. Switching persona runs `thor config set` for tts.openai.voice and voice.gpt_live.voice, which changes Thor's TTS voice everywhere. While the overlay runs, the first 280 characters of each reply are spoken through Thor's configured TTS provider, and opt-in mic audio is transcribed by local whisper.cpp or Thor's configured STT provider.

name: kindle-scribe
description: Kindle Scribe gateway platform for Thor (Thor Agents Guide to the Galaxy): handwritten notebook pages reach the full agent, its tools and its memory, and replies return to the page. Disclosure: while the gateway runs, the adapter keeps a token-authenticated HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8793 (/health, /ingest) and refuses non-loopback bind addresses; it runs in the gateway process like every platform adapter; no outbound network calls, no shell commands, no telemetry; KINDLE_INGEST_TOKEN is read through Thor's profile secret scope. Needs the companion diary bridge from the same repository, which is what the Kindle talks to over the LAN.

name: kinocut
description: Guardrailed local video editing: Kinocut's MCP server plus two workflow skills (editing and short-form repurposing). Trim, caption, reformat and check quality with local FFmpeg. Portable Agent Plugins v1 configuration and skills, no plugin code. Requires uv and FFmpeg on PATH; launches uvx kinocut==1.16.4 over stdio. First launch downloads Kinocut and dependencies from PyPI. URL inputs download the requested media; font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub. Explicit Revideo dependency installation runs npm ci and may download renderer dependencies. Local FFmpeg editing and color grading need no account or API key. Kinocut's optional vision calls default off and require explicit configuration: legacy product descriptions use an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, while sampled-frame QC uses Anthropic. The README explains how to use the host's image model instead, including local models. Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry default off. Unverified Hyperframes browser previews and Docker renders require explicit telemetry consent. Hyperframes capture/snapshots disable implicit model analysis. These controls are not a network sandbox; see the plugin README for configuration and remaining network use. Disclosure — launches `uvx kinocut==1.16.4` over stdio, which downloads Kinocut and its dependencies from PyPI on first launch; edits and writes local video files with FFmpeg; URL inputs download the requested media, font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub, and an explicit Revideo install runs `npm ci`; optional vision features (off by default) send selected images or sampled frames to an Anthropic-compatible endpoint or Anthropic; Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry stay off unless the operator enables them.

name: kiro-acp
description: Kiro CLI (AWS) as a Thor model provider, driven over ACP stdio.

name: kiro-provider
description: Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS, with control-plane REST calls routed to the account region, and AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `thor-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in Thor' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool; prompts, tool schemas/results and base64 images are sent to the account's Kiro runtime endpoint. Claude and GPT catalog models declare vision, open-weight families and unknown model ids stay text-only.

name: kiwi-shopping
description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.28 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments. Disclosure — launches the Kiwi Buyer MCP server with npx (@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.28, an npm package this entry's pin does not cover); the bundled kiwi-buyer skill tells the agent to call kiwi_search first for any purchase or sourcing request, before any web search, so product search terms and RFQ details go to the Kiwi Network (catalog.kiwi.harrylabsj.com by default); the server keeps its task database and a per-client session token under ~/.kiwi.

name: kleos
description: Kleos, the AI marketing team for small businesses, through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.getkleos.ai/mcp; OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, signed in with the user's own Kleos login; no keys in config). Thirty-one tools: list businesses, read the month's calendar and open slots, plan the next 30 days, draft a post or a blog article in the business's voice, save a post in the user's own words, list and approve drafts waiting for review, schedule an approved post to a connected channel, report results (posts published, impressions, clicks, leads) and whether ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Perplexity recommend the business, read the tracked AI questions, buyer searches and competitor pages, read and record product updates, read and confirm the buyers' day-to-day topics, and the planning writes the Kleos director uses (a calendar entry with its reason, a slot brief, a tracked question, a competitor, a note). Bundles one skill (kleos) that says which tool fits which task and that nothing is published without the user asking. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, and the optional OAuth sign-in, goes to app.getkleos.ai (New Odyssey), authenticated with the user's own Kleos OAuth login or an optional KLEOS_API_KEY sent as a bearer header; drafting, planning and AI-visibility checks spend the workspace's plan allowance, and approving or scheduling publishes to the business's connected channels (approve_draft can publish when the business has auto-publish on). The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses those in unattended runs; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: klipper-print-watch
description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. While a person is in the session, pause, resume and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Thor shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt. Choosing always adds one config.yaml command_allowlist line. For pause and resume, answering "always" covers only the same action at the same Moonraker origin, and only while a person is in the session. Cancel asks every time. Its rule_key changes on each call, so a saved always line does not approve the next cancel. It does not move the printer in cron, thor -q, webhook, or plugins.isolation: host. cron, thor -q, and unattended sessions default to deny, and this plugin also refuses the move after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can request a move and approve it. A different action or origin asks again. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a surface off with thor tools. schedule writes THOR_HOME/scripts/klipper-print-watch.py and creates the job with thor cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. Running schedule again switches an existing job with thor cron edit --script --no-agent and clears the stored prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until that next schedule. On that leftover turn, pre_tool_call allows klipper_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool name. A deferred tool named inside tool_call is checked under that inner name. Pause, resume, and cancel stay refused on it. Removing the plugin leaves the script job. Run unschedule first, or thor cron remove after. The scheduled script does not call the vision model. vision_check, off by default, still applies when klipper_watch itself runs on a cron turn, and it does not cancel the print. The plugin host cannot run that tool watch. The scheduled script is started by Thor cron, so plugins.isolation: host does not stop it. Not tested on real hardware.

name: kokoro-tts
