description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon (MLX) and Linux (PyTorch on CPU): adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Brazilian Portuguese and English (tested by the author) and Italian (not yet tested by the author), and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus thor kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — thor kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB on macOS or 1.3 GB on Linux from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release and, on Linux, the CPU-only torch wheel from download.pytorch.org, both pinned by SHA-256), downloads the model at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 on macOS, hexgrad/Kokoro-82M on Linux, about 340 MB), and installs a background service that keeps a local server running (a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux, both named dev.thor.kokoro-tts). The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. Writes the environment, model cache and log under ~/Library/Application Support/thor-kokoro-tts (macOS) or ~/.local/share/thor-kokoro-tts (Linux), the requested audio files, and the profile's config.yaml only when you run thor kokoro words add or remove. No API keys, no telemetry.

name: kokpit
description: A personal cockpit for Thor Agent. When a session produces something, Kokpit leaves a short card and receipt in plain Markdown that Thor, Claude Code and Codex all read, so the next session picks up where the last one stopped. It also captures notes and todos from any Thor chat, gives a morning brief, and runs a night pass whose proposals quote their exact source lines. Local, stdlib only. Disclosure — Adds notes from your Kokpit Markdown vault (threads, last session card, latest receipt, related notes) to each turn's context; by default writes a session card and receipt into the vault when a session captured notes or wrote files (listing the paths written); its tools let the agent append notes, tasks, journal lines and accepted idea files to the vault without a prompt and read the Kokpit app's SQLite database read-only; optional settings, all off by default, run the night pass in a background thread at session start (`night_auto`), send up to 10 vault files to your configured model (`night_model`), and run `systemctl --user is-active` for units you list (`server`).

name: kubernetes
description: Write one namespace in cluster.json to approve the scope, then use four reads: list pods, get one pod, list events, and read logs. Kubernetes is a registered trademark of The Linux Foundation. kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 is the GitHub release binary. The plugin downloads kubernetes-mcp-server-<os>-<arch> from https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.0.68/ into the plugin data directory, checks the sha256 against constants taken from that release's GitHub asset digest, and starts that file. MCP initialize and tools/list are answered before that download. A partial download is kept and continued with HTTP Range. A mismatch, including a file that was already there, is refused. read_only is true, toolsets stay core, and only pods_list_in_namespace, pods_get, events_list, and pods_log are enabled. Helm is not offered. Secret, ConfigMap, and ServiceAccount are denied. configuration_view is not listed. prod, production, live, and prd names are refused unless allow_production is true. Public and link-local hosts are always refused. The host must be local, and DNS is not resolved. readOnlyHint is true, so no approval card is shown. Before the call, name the namespace, the object, and that it only reads, because status, events, and logs reach the model. This plugin does not create a cron job. Disclosure — reads the kubeconfig you name in cluster.json (read-only) and sends its token only to that kubeconfig's API host (plain http sends it unencrypted); on the first tool call downloads the kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 GitHub release binary (~90 MB) into the plugin data directory, refuses it unless its sha256 matches the pinned release digest, and runs it as a subprocess (a file swap between the check and the start is not fully excluded); pod status, events and logs reach the model, with password-like env values and last-applied-configuration redacted; no HTTP proxy is used; gateway users can call these read tools with that kubeconfig; stop with thor plugins disable kubernetes or thor tools disable mcp-kubernetes.

name: kujo-thor
description: Native discovery and execution of Kujo engineering, context, verification and orchestration tools with explicit human approvals and local execution receipts. Requires separately installed canonical Kujo runtime and source tooling. Disclosure — runs the separately installed `kujo` binary (PATH or `kujo_bin`) and Kujo source checkouts that `thor kujo setup` clones from github.com/kujolang at commits pinned in `catalog/sources.lock.json` (default `~/.local/share/kujo/thor-sources`); read-only Abilities run in operator-trusted workspaces without a prompt, and every write/external or extension Ability needs a fresh human Thor approval.

name: kuma
description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

name: kumi
description: Kumi puts Thor inside Ableton Live, REAPER and Renoise: it hears your mix, makes changes you can undo, and turns your samples into new sounds. Disclosure — after you approve setup, downloads the Kumi release this pin names for your platform (27–35 MB, SHA-256 checked) from github.com/user1303836/kumi/releases into THOR_HOME/plugin-data/kumi/ and installs Kumi's part in your DAW (Live's Remote Script with its Kumi Ears device, a REAPER extension or a Renoise tool) at paths you approve; a newer release comes only with a new catalog pin. Runs Kumi's runtime and DAW bridge as local child processes on loopback that stop with the chat or after idling. Reads the open DAW project, the sample folders you list, THOR_HOME/cache/generated/audio, VST3 metadata in the standard plug-in folders and, after you approve, an existing Kumi's DAW connection files. Writes the Max for Live devices, presets and wavetables you ask for as new files in Live's User Library, copies your saved project beside it before some changes, and, using an existing Kumi's installation, keeps a write lease and listening renders in its folder. Runs a DAW script you ask for with the DAW's access to your computer (asked first, with its code). Plays the project only for a listen or play you ask for. Sends FOCUS notes and measurements to your Thor model, and with listen_interpretation on, a small band-energy image to the auxiliary model. Mirelo (paid, off by default): only with your key and a credit cap above 0, approved prompts and audio go to api.mirelo.ai and the transfer hosts it names. No telemetry.

name: kumiho-memory
description: Recall and save decisions, preferences and facts in your Kumiho Cloud workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with hosted OAuth MCP and six skills. Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by Thor); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so Thor asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring Thor cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.

name: lahja
description: Arabic dialect speech-to-text (provider lahja), fully local: a dialect fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo on whisper.cpp keeps Levantine, Gulf, Egyptian, Iraqi and Maghrebi speech as spoken instead of rewriting it as formal Arabic (WER 29% vs 41% for stock turbo with the same VAD, across 13 dialects), Silero VAD always on plus a filter for subtitle-credit hallucinations («ترجمة نانسي قنقر»), per-note language routing that never forces a non-Arabic language (English, including accented English the dialect model writes in Arabic letters, goes to a stock Whisper model you choose), and corrections taught once with /stt-fix. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally in a temp dir deleted after each call; nothing is uploaded. Network only in `thor lahja setup`, which downloads commit-pinned, SHA-256- and size-checked model files from huggingface.co (redirected to its *.cdn.hf.co CDN); the dialect model is a community ggml mirror (JoaoZaokk) that bench/convert.sh reproduces byte for byte from oddadmix's official weights. Runs ffmpeg (local files only) and whisper-cli with a fixed argv, no shell, one deadline per note, at most max_parallel at once, and a minimal environment (PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, TMPDIR, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) without Thor' variables. Reads the audio Thor passes, its own model files, and an optional other_languages_model .bin you configure. Writes model files and the two phrases of each /stt-fix correction to its plugin data dir; corrections apply profile-wide and any user the gateway admits can add one (control/invisible characters refused, max 500). No audio or transcripts stored; no tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or credentials.

name: lancedb
description: LanceDB hybrid memory — embedded vector + FTS recall, workspace facts, transparent forget.

name: lancedb-suite
description: Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Ships its memory-writing skill. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

name: lane-keeper
description: Keeps your agent on a few active lanes (current commitments): new ideas the user mentions are saved as dormant markdown lanes instead of quietly becoming work, only the user can promote one (/lanes promote, cap-aware, forces choosing what to park), and stale or over-cap lanes are called out once. Status lives in a registry in the plugin's own data, so editing a lane file can't promote it; the thor lanes CLI is read-only. Disclosure — no network calls, no subprocesses, no LLM calls of its own, no telemetry, no background work; one declared Python dependency (pyyaml>=6,<7); never reads credential stores; reads/writes *.md files in lanes_dir (default <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/lane-keeper/lanes, or a top-level folder the user configures) and <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/lane-keeper/registry-<hash>.json (statuses, stale notices given, ≤300 session fingerprints); sends to the model provider a rules section plus active lane titles/next actions and up to 15 dormant titles once per session in the system prompt, and a one-line note in the user turn only when lanes change; its pre_tool_call hook reads tool names/arguments to block agent writes to lane data, status-changing CLI calls, Lane Keeper settings changes and disabling the plugin, and stores nothing.

name: langfuse
description: Langfuse observability for Thor: one trace per turn, one generation per LLM call (usage and cost from Thor' own pricing, cache and reasoning tokens included), one observation per tool call and subagent. Content capture is sanitized by default (metadata-only and full are opt-in); sends traces only to the Langfuse project whose keys you set. Formerly built into Thor core as observability/langfuse; existing users are migrated automatically.

name: language-lock
description: Your agent answers in your language, and stays there (thor-agent#130117). Learns your language from your recent messages or a setting, detects each reply's language without a model (20 languages, by script and common words, ignoring code and links), and after a reply drifts tells the agent to switch back on the next turn. Asking for a translation on purpose is respected. /lang shows drifts caught and corrected. No model calls, nothing stored.

name: laso-finance
description: Spend USDC in the real world from Thor: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Thor approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 19 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for Thor approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in Thor (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order); all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

name: last-price
description: Lets Thor haggle with buyers in chat while the plugin, not the model, owns every price that leaves. You set an item's floor from your terminal; it stays in plugin state and never reaches a model, tool result, prompt or log. Every deal reply is held and checked, and one offering less is rewritten before anyone sees it; a buyer who offers or accepts a price the plugin would take is closed at their own number; deal sessions can use only Last Price's three tools (plus Thor's tool-search bridge, whose calls are checked the same way). Includes thor lastprice duel --vs-prompt, a side-by-side against a seller with the floor in its prompt (inside Thor, in the 48-duel bench of version 0.1.1: that seller sold below the floor in 10 of 48 duels; Last Price in 0), and thor lastprice challenge, a public 'buy it below my floor' Telegram challenge. Disclosure — buyer messages and Thor's draft replies go to your model provider, as in any Thor chat; a rewrite of a too-low draft goes to the same model (it sees the buyer's message, the draft and the current counter, never the floor). In a duel or bench, the buyer model (your own model, or the one you name with --buyer) receives the buyer's instruction and the whole conversation so far, the seller's replies included. duel and bench start thor chat child processes in your terminal (no --yolo; with --ignore-rules and --source tool, so your own rules and memory stay out and the duel sessions stay out of your session list): the Last Price seller gets Last Price's three tools only; the stock seller gets Thor's todo toolset plus every plugin toolset your profile turns on by default, and its system prompt carries the duel item's floor, which by default is a demo item's throwaway floor, never one of yours unless you pass --item <id> --real-item. Thor saves that prompt with the stock session in state.db; each duel deletes its stock session when it ends (thor sessions delete), and the stock seller's replies stay in Thor's 7-day deletion tombstones and in Last Price's duel records (and the deleted bytes in state.db's free pages until thor sessions optimize). thor chat starts Thor's background gateway when none is running; a duel or bench that started it stops it when it ends. challenge start and shop on run only in a profile with memory off (memory.memory_enabled and memory.user_profile_enabled false, no memory.provider; read with thor config get, and refused if unreadable), so strangers never chat with an agent that knows you: run them from a dedicated profile (thor -p shop ...) with a neutral SOUL.md. challenge start changes six Thor settings through thor config set (Telegram open access, a Last-Price-only Telegram toolset, owner-only slash commands) after reading their earlier values one by one with thor config get (it reads no .env and parses no config.yaml), and challenge end restores all six. Floors are stored as plain JSON in plugin state: hidden from the model in deal sessions, readable on your machine by you and by any agent you give file tools to. No payment provider is called in 0.1.x, no telemetry.

name: lastgood
description: LastGood records which of your preset checks passed on which tested state, and what restoring files will not undo. Checks you choose (file opens, words present, files exist, page loads) run after write_file or patch in an opted-in project, and on demand via /lastgood and /blame. Results are PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN, with a content fingerprint so changed files mark old results stale. Blame shows the first failing step and bounded configured-string presence deltas, not the cause. A ledger lists recognised tool calls a file rollback will not undo, without storing their arguments. Disclosure — the optional url_loads check fetches the http(s) address set in the project's lastgood-config.json (loopback and public hosts; link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused, including after redirects; private ranges only when you turn on allow_private_urls). The lastgood_setup tool refuses page checks, but the agent's own file tools can still edit lastgood-config.json, so leave allow_private_urls off unless you trust what the session writes.

name: lastscanned
description: Track parcels and ocean containers across 549 carriers and compare USPS, UPS and FedEx rate quotes between US ZIP codes, through the hosted lastscanned Streamable HTTP MCP server plus one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Works without sign-in within a small free daily allowance; for more, add the server with auth: oauth or an API key in your own Thor profile. No credentials are stored in the plugin. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; tracking numbers, container numbers, carrier ids and quote fields go to mcp.lastscanned.com; tracked numbers and quotes count toward your lastscanned plan or credits; all four tools set readOnlyHint, so Thor does not prompt for them, and the plugin sets no spend limit.

name: launch-desk
description: Built something? Ask Thor to prepare the launch, based on what posts.design learned from launches that worked: ideas from three real launch posts like yours, a post in your own words checked in code for slop, a share card from your own screenshots, colours and logo, and with /launch film a 14-second launch film in your brand plus a checklist so you don't post a sloppy video. You approve a preview first, then get the text, the card and a link that opens X with the post filled in. Disclosure: one posts.design search per run through your own posts MCP server, a fetch of your product site, brand kit and packs stored locally, two check-ins scheduled only if you say Yes, an optional Thor Desktop page (off until you turn it on) whose read-only backend, served while the plugin is enabled, reads your packs and the times of the check-ins it scheduled, a launch film made only when you ask with /launch film, rendered on your machine by the renderer you set up (a configured command or HyperFrames on PATH) with HyperFrames telemetry off (Launch Desk downloads nothing itself; HyperFrames may download its own headless Chrome on its first render), plus posts.design's free playbook list and, on Pro, one playbook read (1 credit) the first time and again only when posts.design updates it, and nothing is ever posted; see the README for the full list.

name: launchspy
description: Spy on the ads and funnels of the top coaches and course creators through LaunchSpy's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://launchspy.io/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): search creators by niche and country, see who is scaling and how they run ads, read their Meta ads with run dates and EU reach, pull the longest-running ads of a niche, find and take apart their funnels (steps, builder, pixels, payment stack, pricing), size a market by niche and country, and check what is known about any domain. Bundles six workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to LaunchSpy's hosted server (launchspy.io) and acts on the user's LaunchSpy account; each tools/call uses one credit (a free account gets 50 trial credits, once; paid plans include monthly credits); the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. All ten tools are annotated read-only and the server is marked untrusted. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth.

name: lazy-plugin
description: A dashboard page in Thor Desktop where you describe a plugin and watch it get built. Say what you want — or start from a skill the agent wrote, or a job that runs on a schedule — and your own agent drafts the plan in a chat turn you can read, the code comes from four fixed templates, and the page shows a receipt: plan, files, validator result, and a real try-out of every tool (purrs, needs a key, blocked upstream, held back, half-built, broken — with the exact failing line). The build never runs what it wrote: the try-out is your click, a key only travels to a public https host, and a file tool stays inside its own data dir. Nothing installs itself, and publishing is a SHA-pinned catalog PR you send. Also callable as lazyplugin_create from any conversation. Disclosure — the Desktop "try it" button runs every generated tool for real on your machine (generated `command` tools execute the drafted argv; declared keys are only sent to public https hosts named in the code, never Thor' own keys), and "publish" uses your `gh` login to create a public GitHub repo for the generated plugin and open a pull request to thor726/thor-agent in one click; builds from `lazyplugin_create` never run generated code.

name: ld-workbench
description: A new tool for high school debate students. Build a Lincoln-Douglas case with a coach, run a full timed round against an AI opponent, answer Extemp questions out loud, and study great speeches. You speak on a real clock that starts when you do. A practice judge writes a full ballot after every round and quotes your own lines back to you, and you can play each one back from your own recording. Try an answer twice and see what got better. Ballots are kept, and the habits that keep costing you are counted across them. Rhetoric lessons mark the figures in famous speeches. The coach asks questions first and writes nothing into your case until you press Add. In any Thor chat, /debate gives you today's question. New in 0.2: Extemp answers spoken on a real clock, a Rhetoric room, a Ballots page that counts your habits across rounds and shows which way each is heading, and a Start here guide to the four rooms. Disclosure — an independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Thor Labs, the National Speech & Debate Association, AllSides or any news outlet. Registers a Desktop page, a dashboard API, the /debate command, two read-only agent tools (debate_record, debate_today; both refuse in scheduled jobs), three model rows and a debate-coach skill; no hooks, middleware or env vars. The microphone opens only while you press Start speaking. Recordings, transcripts, cases, ballots and your extemp file stay in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/ld-workbench/, with delete buttons in Settings. Takes go to Thor's speech-to-text (a cloud provider gets a take only when you press Transcribe now on it) or to the plugin's own speech model, downloaded from huggingface.co (about 145 MB) only on a press. Pressing Hear it sends the AI opponent's or coach's speech text to the text-to-speech voice set up in Thor. Its own network calls start on a button (Pull headlines: Google News RSS and outlet feeds, https only; Get up to speed: up to 4 public pages from your Thor web search; a link you save, http or https), public addresses only, with time and size caps. Model calls go to your own Thor model; with coach examples on, one runs in the background after each 60-second answer. Uses one private Thor import (tools.voice_mode.transcribe_recording), guarded with a local fallback. No credentials, telemetry, background jobs or self-updates.

name: leadpoet
description: Send your website and get customers. Thor finds verified contacts at companies showing a buying signal, writes emails where every personal line shows its source, lets you approve from your phone, and brings replies back to chat. The first look at who buys from you needs no account. Disclosure — calls the Leadpoet API (leadpoet.com) with your LEADPOET_API_KEY: it can spend Leadpoet credits on contact searches, create and launch email campaigns to third parties from your connected inbox, and send replies, each only after you type the approval code shown under the exact content; it reads public pages of your site and your prospects' sites and sends that text and prospects' replies to your configured Thor model; the optional `thor leadpoet watch` cron check runs with no model, launches campaigns you already approved and approves matching drafts unattended; contact details and drafts are stored in the plugin's data folder.

name: lean-mode
description: Cheap-model subagent (quick_run) with a dollar cap, auto-escalation when the cheap model fails, and an honest cost receipt. Each child call starts with 4-10k prompt tokens vs the parent's 100-300k. Per-run budget cap (soft, stops within one call), watchdog timeout, escalation to the parent model, a restricted toolset (no delegation/memory/skills/clarify/cronjob), and a JSON audit logged to plugin-data/lean-mode/runs.jsonl. Requires the operator to configure lean: in config.yaml with a cheap model, parent model, prices and presets. Tested on Thor v0.23.0. MIT licensed. Disclosure — the model can start cheap-model subagents with quick_run and may set the model id, budget and timeout per call; the dollar cap is soft, works only for models priced under lean.prices, and is off by default. When the parent's toolsets cannot be narrowed, and on every escalation, the child runs with all of the parent's toolsets (skills included) on the parent model. Run metadata (tokens, cost estimate, model, child session id, result hash; no message content) is logged to plugin-data/lean-mode/runs.jsonl. No network calls, shell commands or credentials of its own.

name: learning-workbench
description: Study with Thor in a Desktop pane: a short diagnosis, a route of 2–7 steps you can rename or skip, then one lesson and exercise at a time, answered in your own words. The plugin keeps the record honest: answer keys, rubrics and hints are frozen before you answer, only you can submit an attempt (the agent's six tools propose and read), every check must quote your words and the quote is verified, and each attempt is labelled unaided, after feedback, after hints, after help in chat or after a revealed solution. Drafts and attempts survive restarts and compaction, a contest keeps the earlier verdict, and a study exports as a Markdown record. /study covers the CLI and messaging. Disclosure: studies are stored locally in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/learning-workbench/ (SQLite) until you delete them, including after uninstall; while an exercise is open in a chat, the pre_llm_call hook adds a short reminder with that exercise's question to the turn's user message and records that the turn happened (not its text); chats without an open exercise are untouched. No network calls of its own, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. Verdicts use the user's configured model.

name: learnloop
description: Structured lessons and practice inside Thor, after LearnHarness: /learnloop:study probes what you know, plans a path and teaches it one graded check at a time; /learnloop:practice drills it with a hint ladder. What you learn becomes a knowledge graph you can explore and practise from. Disclosure — Stores lessons, answers and your knowledge graph locally in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/learnloop/learnloop.db; makes no network calls. During an active lesson it blocks the memory and skill_manage tools and loading other skills in that chat; with `/learnloop recall on` (off by default) it adds up to 6 facts from your graph to other chats. Teaching method adapted from LearnHarness (AGPL-3.0).

name: leash
description: Lean OWASP Top 10 pentest toolkit run by the agent against your own dev app: scope-gated recon (TCP scan, same-origin crawl), multi-identity access-control testing with canary-based leak detection, parameter fuzzing, security-header audit and an evidence ledger that turns findings into a plain-language report grouped by OWASP category. Disclosure — sends TCP connects and HTTP requests (including model-chosen methods, headers, bodies and test payloads) only to hosts and CIDRs listed in the user's scope file, and refuses everything when no scope file is set; in the default audit mode its pre_tool_call hook only logs out-of-scope targets seen in terminal, web_extract and browser tool arguments (enforce mode blocks them); stores test-identity session cookies and tokens in plain JSON under plugin-data/leash, outside model context.

name: ledger-guard
description: Deterministic double-count and arithmetic checker for stacked sales/event goal ledgers.

name: leitmotif
description: Hear what your agent is doing. Every tool call becomes a short musical motif from a pure-Python synth, so reads, writes, shell commands, loops (the motif repeats and climbs), error streaks (dissonant, sinking), pending approvals (a heartbeat, then a distinct still-waiting cue until you answer) and finished turns (a V-I cadence) are audible without watching the screen; also a non-visual status channel for blind and low-vision developers. Modes full / ambient / alerts-only, themes studio / arcade / zen, and /leitmotif export saves a session as WAV, MIDI and a piano-roll SVG. Disclosure — observer-only hooks, never blocks or approves anything; starts the OS audio player (afplay, pw-play, paplay or aplay) as a short-lived subprocess per sound, or uses winsound on Windows; keeps tool names and argument hashes in memory only; caches rendered notes and writes exports in its plugin data directory; no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials.

name: lemma
description: An AI-scientist plugin that audits what your agent reads. Paste or mention a paper link and the ambient pre-LLM hook offers an audit unprompted; six tools (quick_audit, audit, doctor, status, judge, improve) extract testable claims, generate and run honest audit scripts behind a mandatory positive control, and render verdicts — supported, falsified, inconclusive — over an append-only evidence trail. The Desktop Audit Room pane shows live runs (stage, attempts, trace tail) and self-distrust flags (verify_gain) when a post-feedback flip to supported needs eyeballing. Everything stays local under plugin_data_dir. Disclosure — paper text and audit prompts go to your configured LLM provider (Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set via OPENAI_BASE_URL); papers are fetched from arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org and openreview.net; LLM-written audit scripts run inside a sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS: no network, workdir-only writes, minimal env) and are refused where no sandbox exists unless you turn on the plugin's `host_exec` setting, which runs them on the host without isolation; `lemma_audit` and `lemma_improve` run as detached background processes; a pre-LLM hook adds an "offer an audit" hint when a paper link appears in the conversation; all artifacts stay under the plugin data directory.

name: leonardo
description: Leonardo.AI video generation backend for video_generate: Motion 2.0 text-to-video and image-to-video through the Leonardo REST API, using only the Python standard library. Disclosure — the prompt and any reference image URL are sent to cloud.leonardo.ai and the finished clip is fetched from cdn.leonardo.ai, authenticated with your LEONARDO_API_KEY, which the plugin reads through Thor's secret scope and never from a file or the ambient environment; generation is billed to your Leonardo API token balance (about 200 tokens per 5-second clip, purchased separately from a Leonardo web subscription); the job is polled in-process with a bounded wall-clock deadline, and the token cost is reported back but no budget is enforced, so an unattended run can spend your balance; no telemetry, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials and no self-updates. Zero Python dependencies.

name: lethe
description:
Take one chat off the record with /lethe: nothing reaches memory, your profile or skills, the transcript is deleted, and a river shows every write it kept out.

Use an external memory provider? Copy this into a Thor chat and replace <PROVIDER> with yours:

Extend my local Lethe plugin (~/.thor/plugins/lethe) so off-the-record chats also skip my <PROVIDER> memory provider's per-turn sync, session-end extraction and save tools when store.is_on(session_id) is true. Show me the diff, add a test, then run thor gateway restart. Disclosure — Deletes the off-the-record chat's transcript (and its compression chain) from Thor's session database via SessionDB.delete_session when the chat ends, on /lethe-end or /lethe-forget, or from the Desktop panel's Delete transcript now (unless keep_transcript is on); while on, it blocks memory, user-profile and skill writes plus provider tools whose names look like saves, and adds a fixed off-the-record note to each turn's context; external memory providers' per-turn sync is not blocked.

name: letsfg
description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Thor itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `thor mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

name: letterpress
description: Drop in your PDFs, Word files and text, and Letterpress turns them into a finished deck, one-pager, graphic or audio brief in your own brand. Pick from three deck designs (Editorial, Data board, Statement), mix slides between them, and revise any slide by asking in plain words. Ask questions of your sources and get answers that cite the paragraph. Numbers and quotes are checked against your sources before export, and a Source notes PDF sets each one beside the sentence it came from. The check covers numbers and quotes, not claims or framing, so read the headlines yourself. Five built-in brands, or make your own. Independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Thor Labs. Disclosure — Sends source text (secrets redacted by Thor), questions, briefs and pictures of draft slides to the user's own Thor model (auxiliary task "Letterpress writing") and audio scripts to the user's Thor text-to-speech provider; fetches only web addresses the user enters, through Thor's SSRF-safe client or the user's web_extract tool; starts a headless Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave child process (path from LETTERPRESS_BROWSER or IMPRINT_BROWSER, install folders or PATH) with only a minimal environment to render exports with network blocked and, on macOS/Linux, to view up to four pages of a user-named website through a public-address-only proxy on 127.0.0.1; runs sips on macOS; on first start copies its own earlier data from $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/imprint/ when that folder holds this plugin's database, without changing it; writes only under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/letterpress/ (or LETTERPRESS_DATA_DIR / IMPRINT_DATA_DIR) and to paths picked in the save dialog.

name: levea-video-editor
description: AI video editor and agentic video editing agent by Levea — an autonomous online video editor and FFmpeg alternative driven by natural-language prompts. Turn podcasts, interviews, webinars, streams and long-form video into viral clips, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok videos: video trimming and cutting, silence removal, filler-word removal, jump cuts, 9:16 vertical reframe with active-speaker face tracking, automatic animated captions, subtitles, karaoke captions and transcription, B-roll and stock footage, multicam podcast editing, audio cleanup and noise reduction, music and sound design, AI voiceover, dubbing and video translation, color grading and film looks, motion graphics, lower thirds, motion tracking, green screen, crop and resize, verified MP4 export. A clip maker, shorts maker and reels maker for creators, podcasters, YouTubers and marketing teams — podcast-to-clips, webinar-to-clips and VOD-to-clips content repurposing, text-based video editing, an alternative to Opus Clip, vidyo, Descript and CapCut. Disclosure — Prompts, source video URLs/assets and project ids go to api.livecore.ai with your LEVEA_API_KEY; edits and exports consume your Levea account quota with no Thor approval prompt; levea_video_edit and levea_job_status (wait) can block up to 10 minutes. No telemetry, no shell, no background processes.

name: lfg-alarm
description: Put a real alarm on your phone from Thor, and on your friends', family's or community's phones, ringing together: for a time, an event, a post, a stream going live, a token price, or anything that can call a link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), with one workflow skill bundled. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to LFG Alarm's MCP server at mcp.lfg.gm, signed in as the user through LFG Alarm's sign-in. Alarm titles, times, notes, links and the people added are sent there, and what the tools return, such as the user's alarms and friends, enters the session and reaches the user's model provider. Tools make, change and delete alarms and can ring every phone on an alarm the user made. The tool list comes from LFG Alarm's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add lfg-alarm --url https://mcp.lfg.gm --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. That command replaces the package's server entry and its trust setting, so the README's next step sets it again: `thor config set mcp_servers.lfg-alarm.trust untrusted`.

name: lib-docs
description: Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through Thor Desktop's internal thor:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

name: life-manager
description: Records commitments a person states, keeps habit streaks, and injects the board before each turn. A daily Automation Blueprint runs an unattended check-in. Disclosure: no network, no credentials, no shell. Stores commitment text, due dates, streaks, nudged session ids, and the last check-in id in the active Thor profile plugin state only.

name: lifeboat
description: Rescue what a sweeper bot left behind in a drained EVM wallet: claims, unstakes and transfers in one EIP-7702 transaction paid by a fresh operator, sent only after you approve the exact text. Disclosure — moves funds on-chain: signs EIP-7702 delegations with the private key of the already-drained wallet (LIFEBOAT_VICTIM_KEY, read through the Thor secret scope) and sends transactions from fresh operator wallets whose keys it generates and stores sealed under its plugin data directory; sending is off until LIFEBOAT_ENABLE_EXECUTE=1, every send needs a per-transaction Thor approval prompt, and it refuses to send in yolo mode, with approvals off or in unattended runs (cron, -q, webhook, API); assets go only to LIFEBOAT_SAFE_ADDRESS; sends the wallet address to the public RPC of each supported chain (scan with no chain list queries all of them; override per chain with the `rpc` plugin setting) and to each chain's public Blockscout API for the balance scan and sweep history; reads Thor' private approval-mode functions to detect unattended runs (fails closed); no telemetry, no background threads.

name: lightkeeper
description: An Obsidian-compatible map of how your codebase works (modules, flows, integrations, platform traps, decisions), kept outside the repo and kept honest by hooks: a primer on the first turn, pointers to the notes that own what you are asking about or editing, and a reminder through the verify gate when code moved but the map did not. Eight lightkeeper:* skills carry the procedures (init, seed, tidy, trace, release, knowledge-vault, vault-sync, vault-tidy); the vault CLI (find, check, sync, status, log, export) works from any shell. Not a memory provider. Disclosure — each hook runs python3 on the plugin's own scripts as a synchronous subprocess with a 10 s timeout (on every user message, after every write_file and patch, at the verify step and at session end), and those scripts run read-only git commands (rev-parse, remote get-url, worktree list, ls-tree, status, log) in the session's checkout and in the vault folder; the session primer and prompt hints put text from the vault's notes into the model's context; the hooks read the vault registry ~/.claude/vaults and the vault folders it lists, and write only inside the vault (_meta/index.json), a small per-session state file in the system temporary directory ($TMPDIR), and the plugin's own data directory; the init, seed, sync, tidy, trace and release procedures run the vault CLI through the terminal and commit to the vault's own git repository, and vault init appends the vault to ~/.claude/vaults and, only when you pass its opt-in flags, copies a vault launcher to ~/.local/bin (--install-cli), installs report-only post-merge and pre-push hooks in your code checkouts (--git-hook), or adds a post-commit hook that pushes every vault commit to the remote you name (--backup-remote); vault export writes an HTML map that loads d3 7.9.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com when opened; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no dependencies beyond Python 3.9 and git. Silent until a vault covers the session's working directory.

name: lightningai
description: Lightning AI as a Thor model provider (--provider lightning, lightning-ai, lightningai): OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://lightning.ai/api/v1, models fetched live from /models. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to lightning.ai through Thor' own client with LIGHTNING_API_KEY (or LIGHTNING_AI_API_KEY), optional LIGHTNING_BASE_URL overrides the endpoint; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads/writes no files and starts no processes.

name: lightningai-rate-limit
description: Per-process throttle for Lightning AI (https://lightning.ai/api/v1) keeping LLM requests within the ~15 requests/min limit, using an in-memory token bucket. Gates only calls whose provider or base_url points at Lightning AI; no-op otherwise. Disclosure — registers one llm_execution middleware and nothing else; no network calls, files, or processes of its own.

name: lights-out
description: Nothing billable starts without your yes and its price: every AWS CLI create Thor runs (EC2, EBS, Elastic IP, NAT gateway, ELBv2, RDS, S3) goes to Thor's own approval gate from pre_tool_call with a dated us-east-1 price, a local ledger records what was created and how to delete it, and a receipt after the turn shows what is still running and its $/month; /lights out turns off everything not kept (asks first), /lights keep <id> <date> keeps one on purpose until a date, /lights check compares the ledger with the cloud; tools lights_status (read-only) and lights_keep (a proposal the user must approve). Disclosure: runs only through Thor's terminal tool and your own aws CLI and credentials: read-only describe/list calls for /lights check and once after a create whose output has no ID, and the shown delete commands for /lights out after you say yes; stores a JSON-lines ledger (resource IDs, sizes, prices, times, the creating command lines) in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/lights-out/; one optional ctx.llm call per end-of-session receipt through your own provider (off with summary_sentence: false); never answers or bypasses approvals (YOLO / approvals off auto-approve as configured; cron and non-interactive runs block); no network of its own, no credentials read, no telemetry, no self-updater.

name: ligis
description: Verify that a payee holds a live, third-party-issued, revocable on-chain capability credential before your agent pays them. Thor agents pay other agents, and the destination address comes from the HTTP answer asking for the money — nothing in the x402 flow ties that address to anything the payee has proven about itself, which is the gap ERC-8478 states in spec form. ligis reads the credential registry directly over read-only JSON-RPC and answers the question the payment flow leaves open: is this counterparty entitled to this? Five tools (ligis_check_capability, ligis_capability_hash, ligis_verify_payee, ligis_verify_payment, ligis_chains) plus two surfaces: a pre_tool_call gate that intercepts payment-shaped tool calls and escalates to Thor's approval prompt when the payee cannot be credentialed, and a transform_tool_result hook that annotates an x402 402 challenge with the payee's credential verdict before the agent signs. The registry lets anyone issue a credential for any subject, so a live credential only counts when a trusted issuer signed it: the operator's trusted_issuers setting is the sole root of trust — tool arguments can narrow it, never widen it — verified on-chain with isCapableFromIssuer. Before its first read the plugin probes eth_chainId and eth_getCode on the registry address, so an endpoint serving the wrong chain or an address with no contract reads as unknown rather than an answer. A capability is indexed by the keccak-256 hash of its name, so the same capability resolves to the same bytes on every chain. No key, no hosted service, no secret scope. Disclosure — makes read-only HTTPS JSON-RPC calls to fixed public testnet RPC endpoints (https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz for monad-testnet, https://atlantic.dplabs-internal.com for pharos-atlantic); the RPC operator sees the caller's IP address and the queried registry, subject and issuer addresses; it holds no keys, signs nothing, sends no transactions, reads and writes no files, runs no background processes, and has no telemetry. A credential counts only when its issuer is in the trusted_issuers setting; with none configured every credentialed payee is escalated. The pre_tool_call hook escalates to Thor's approval prompt, and --yolo and approvals.mode: off auto-approve those escalations while cron follows approvals.cron_mode; set mode: enforce to block outright. If the registry cannot be read, or a payee does not fit the hook's time budget, the call is not gated.

name: limbic
description:
Local long-term memory for Thor agents: facts and preferences stay on your machine in one SQLite file with bundled embedding and natural language inference (NLI) models, decaying and reconsolidating organically with use and abstaining rather than guessing. No LLM calls.

Disclosures
- Network: ~1.0GB of pinned, sha256-verified ONNX models download from huggingface.co on first session start (Arctic 2.0 L int8 ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI ~430MB). Optional spaCy models pip-install ~14.5MB from spaCy's GitHub releases — version not hash-pinned.
- Local files: everything lives under THOR_HOME (limbic.db, backup VACUUM snapshots) except the model cache ~/.cache/limbic, which is pruned at every model load — files not in the pinned manifest are deleted, so never point cache_dir at a shared folder. Memories at trust zero are deleted.
- forget: user-scoped two-step (list candidates, pick one) that appends a hash-only receipt (sha256, length, user id, fact id) to limbic.db.deletions.jsonl beside the database.
- Agent surface is exactly remember, recall, forget — no shell commands, no background services, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: limits-monitor
description: Read-only Thor Desktop quota pane showing provider allowance windows exposed by Thor across reachable profiles. It uses the public Thor RPC surface and deliberately avoids direct vendor usage endpoints and credential-file access.

name: lineage
description: Provenance for everything the agent produces: every file Thor writes gets a receipt (what it was made from — files read, pages fetched, searches run — by which tool call, model and agent, with SHA-256 hashes) and a Desktop page draws the graph back to the sources, with observed / evidenced / inferred links labelled, never blended. Verify a file and its sources against recorded hashes; export Mermaid/DOT. Disclosure — hooks only (post_tool_call, pre/post_llm_call, post_api_request, api_request_error, post_auxiliary_call, subagent_start/stop, on_session_start/end); no tools, middleware, LLM calls or credentials; runs no commands. Hashes files the agent read or wrote and files named in terminal commands (credential files such as ~/.ssh and .env are never opened), scans files the agent wrote (bounded text scan) and stats the working tree once after terminal/execute_code calls; receipts only for files the agent produced. Writes under plugin-data/lineage/ (SQLite, install.key) and, on request or with sidecar: true, <file>.receipt.json beside artifacts. Stores redacted, bounded previews of prompts, tool arguments and results (store_previews: false keeps ids and hashes only). Network only on an explicit `verify --refetch` (GET to the recorded source URLs, public hosts only; redirects are followed only to public hosts). No telemetry.

name: linear-digest
description: Schedule a model-free morning list of open Linear issues assigned to you, with linear_digest. Disclosure — LINEAR_API_KEY is read from this profile on each request and sent as the Authorization value with no Bearer prefix, as up to ten HTTPS POSTs to host api.linear.app path /graphql; redirects are not followed and proxies are not used; nothing is downloaded at run time and the schema file shipped here is about 1.3 MB; the tool and the script are read-only; archived issues are left out; tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call linear_digest with your key, and thor tools turns a surface off; schedule writes a no-agent cron at 08:00 delivered to local, empty stdout sends nothing, and there is no daily cap; unschedule removes the saved job, while the script stays only when another job is also named linear-digest; a leftover job is removed with thor cron remove, and that command leaves the script file; settings stay in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/linear-digest; the skill linear-issues is registered with the tool; bot-chat puts the list into another model turn and that turn is not model-free; an http loopback LINEAR_DIGEST_REHEARSAL URL receives the key in clear text, and any other value fetches nothing.

name: lingua
description: A language learning trainer for Thor Agent: plenty of plugins give the agent a memory, Lingua gives the user one. Build vocabulary decks (one per language) and Thor quizzes you in chat, grades your recall honestly (again, hard, good, easy), and schedules each card with SM-2 spaced repetition, the algorithm behind Anki, so words return right before you forget them: a good card comes back in 1 day, then 6, then stretches by its ease factor, and a failed card returns in about 10 minutes. A pre_llm_call hook nudges you at the start of a session, or when you mention practice, whenever reviews are due. Six tools (lingua_add, lingua_due, lingua_grade, lingua_list, lingua_remove, lingua_stats), a /lingua slash command (including one-command French and Spanish starter decks of 20 essentials each), and a bundled lingua-learning skill that teaches the agent to quiz one card at a time and never reveal an answer early. Decks live in a local SQLite database in the active profile's plugin data directory. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only files touched are the plugin's own SQLite database and its bundled starter deck.

name: linkedcamp
description: Plan, build and run LinkedIn and email outreach in LinkedCamp through LinkedCamp's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.linkedcamp.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the account's API key, no keys in config): campaigns, audience search URLs, multi-step sequences, leads, unified inbox and AI-drafted replies, sending-account health, analytics, reply agents, and agency sub-accounts. Bundles the linkedcamp-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to LinkedCamp's hosted server (mcp.linkedcamp.com) and acts on the user's LinkedCamp account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools reach real people (campaign_launch starts outreach, message_send delivers at once); the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and blocks them in unattended runs.

name: linkjolt
description: Run a LinkJolt affiliate program from Thor through LinkJolt's hosted MCP server (https://www.linkjolt.io/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the user's LinkJolt account, no keys in config): add affiliate tracking to a SaaS or web app's code for Stripe, Paddle, Polar, Creem, Lemon Squeezy or Gumroad, check that tracking works, review sales, commissions, clicks and top affiliates, go through pending commissions, see who is owed what, find out why a sale did not track, and manage affiliate coupon codes. Bundles six workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to LinkJolt's hosted server (www.linkjolt.io) and acts on the user's LinkJolt account for the brand picked at sign-in; LinkJolt logs each tool call by tool name (not its arguments) and each change the connector makes; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required) with a header that asks LinkJolt to sign in while connecting; it opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The write tools save business details, create or change campaigns, email an invitation to an affiliate, approve or reject an affiliate, record or change a sale, and add an affiliate coupon code (created in the merchant's own Stripe, Polar or Creem account when asked); none sends money. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: linkup
description: Linkup web search: live cited search (fast/standard/deep), URL-to-Markdown fetch with JS rendering, async deep research, and a Linkup backend for the built-in web_search / web_extract tools. Disclosure — sends search queries, fetch URLs and research briefs to api.linkup.so with your LINKUP_API_KEY (Linkup fetches pages server-side); when selected with thor linkup use-as-web-backend it also handles the built-in web_search and web_extract calls; large fetched pages are cached under $THOR_HOME/cache/linkup for 24 hours.

name: liquid-inference-provider
description: Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a Thor model provider (provider id `liquid`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model `liquid.auto`) and the model list go through Thor's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID_BASE_URL) with LIQUID_API_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. Each request is billed up to its `x-liquid-cap-usd` cap (1 USD by default, set with `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd`) and carries `X-Title: Thor Agent`. A top-level `reasoning_effort` is sent only when you select a level.

name: listeningkit-log
description: Your agent, working your DMs the way you would. Ask Thor who is waiting on a reply across X, Discord, Slack, Instagram and Reddit, read the whole thread, and get a draft in your own voice that sends only after you approve it. A log tab in the dashboard shows who is waiting, every account's session and today's sends against its daily limit. LinkedIn support is currently limited to a session-status check. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) plus a dashboard tab. Disclosure — starts the separately installed logMcp executable as a long-running stdio process; log makes network calls directly to the social platforms the user signed into and reads account sessions, cookies and message history from its own ~/.logCli data directory. Write tools can send replies, DMs and posts, and can like or follow as the user's account; the server is marked untrusted so Thor asks for approval. The dashboard tab's backend reads, read-only, log's session.json, governor_state.json and synced X inbox (inboxSync.json, including message previews) under ~/.logCli; it makes no network call, runs no command, writes nothing and never reads cookies. The MCP tool set comes from the user's installed log version at runtime and is not covered by this plugin's pinned commit.

name: listing-automater
description: Skill only plugin for real estate agents: explains Listing AutomatEr, a desktop app that posts listings an agent has permission to market to Facebook Marketplace with "Marketed by" and "Listing courtesy of" attribution, and gives guidance for writing clear, compliant listing posts. Registers one read only skill; no agent tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or env vars.

name: litthor
description: Adds lit to Thor Agent so a request is planned, built with tests and recorded checks, reviewed, and closed with a handoff note. 40 skills. MIT. Disclosure — adds per-turn workflow context and output marks through Thor hooks (including a ⛔ LIT: not done line when a reply claims completion while a goal's gate is closed or a lit session never opened one, and a pre_verify hook that asks the agent to keep going while the gate is closed) and writes its plans, goals, test baseline, handoff cards and run state under the workspace's .thor/litthor/ (default-on knowledge capture, opt-out: LITTHOR_WIKIFY_CAPTURE=0); after every terminal command it appends a signed note there with a redacted 100-character preview of the command and its exit code, and when a goal is open it reads the workspace's git state (rev-parse, ls-tree, ls-files) and scans its test files; keeps a per-install signing key at ~/.thor/litthor/litgoal.key; a new session reads other sessions' goal files in the same workspace to offer a resume (LITTHOR_GOAL_RESUME=0 turns it off); a read-only dashboard route, limited to folders inside the home directory and sending no CORS headers, feeds a Thor Desktop goal pane; /lit-adhd reads recent Thor session titles, asks and tool names from ~/.thor/state.db read-only with the sqlite3 CLI; /lit-hijack downloads the URLs and files you name (web pages, PDFs, X posts via api.fxtwitter.com, git clones of github.com repos and gists) into the workspace; bundled skill runtimes install from their own lockfiles when a skill asks; the processes the plugin starts (git, node, a prose detector, pdftotext) get an allowlist environment without provider keys; reads Thor internals read-only (context compressor, config defaults, model metadata, command registry, working-folder helpers), which can break on a Thor release.

name: little-canary
description: Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.
maintainer: roli-lpci (Thor Labs; independent of Thor Labs)

name: liv
description: The first real stateful memory for AI agents: a knowledge graph above the raw transcript, every word kept as plain text tables, local and yours.

name: live-artifacts
description: Create and use interactive artifacts - pages, designs and dashboards - in your sessions. Disclosure — runs a local web listener (default 127.0.0.1:47318) serving agent-written pages; anyone holding a page link can open it and write to its data store with no sign-in, so keep it on loopback or a private tailnet; pages may load scripts from public CDNs (cdnjs, jsdelivr, unpkg, Tailwind, jQuery, Plotly) inside a sandboxed frame; page-side MCP tool calls run only for servers you add to `plugins.entries.live-artifacts.mcp_allowlist`.

name: live-time
description: Thor Agent plugin: injects the current date, time and timezone into every turn as ephemeral context, so long or cross-day sessions stop using a stale wall clock. Zero dependencies, prompt-cache safe.

name: live-translate
description: Real-time speech-to-speech translation on your own computer: anyone speaks in any language and you hear them in yours, in their own voice, about 2-3 seconds behind. Hears ~100 languages (Qwen3-ASR + Whisper), translates between 201 (Qwen3.5-4B, a local server, a subscription, or the model Thor already uses through ctx.llm), and speaks with the speaker's cloned voice in 23 languages and natural voices in 600+. One-way, two-way conversations and meetings/streams through a virtual audio device (Zoom, Meet, Teams, Discord, OBS, with OBS closed captions viewers can switch on); echo cancellation, background voices ignored, several speakers each with their own language and voice. Tools translate_start/stop/status/languages, /translate, thor translate setup|start|file|serve|languages|devices, and an agent skill; optional desktop tray app (separate download). Disclosure — while translating it listens to the microphone or audio input you choose and plays to the output you choose; it never starts from a chat app or a scheduled job unless you enable allow_remote_start. Voice cloning uses a 5-second sample of each speaker on this computer, except with ElevenLabs voices, which upload each speaker's sample to ElevenLabs to create a cloned voice in your account that is deleted when the speaker changes or translation stops; temporary local copies are deleted when the session stops. Each session's captions are saved to plugin-data/live-translate/sessions/*.jsonl. thor translate setup builds a separate Python environment with uv (plus three voice-model environments on Windows/Linux) under plugin-data/live-translate, installs packages from PyPI, PyTorch's index (Windows/Linux) and llama.cpp's prebuilt-wheel index (abetlen.github.io), installs uv from PyPI into the plugin's data folder if it is missing, and downloads 6-9 GB of model weights pinned to exact commits from their official Hugging Face repos into the standard Hugging Face cache. While translating it runs the engine and voice-worker processes (stopped on Stop or when the session that started them ends) and a local server on 127.0.0.1:7865 only, protected by a token kept in an owner-only file under plugin-data/live-translate, a Host check and an Origin check. No network while translating with built-in or local models; a cloud model or voice you choose receives the session's text or audio with your key, read only through Thor's secret store. No telemetry. Licences: Apache-2.0/MIT models by default; OmniVoice (best preset) is CC-BY-NC-4.0; on CPU-only machines Kokoro uses espeak-ng (GPL-3.0).

name: live-video
description: Give Thor eyes in a live voice conversation. Open a page on your phone, talk, and the agent answers in duplex voice while seeing the camera; ask to be told when something comes into view and the relay watches the frames for 90 seconds, verifies a sighting against the image before claiming it, and says it once. The six-action tool starts the relay, hands you the URL to open, and replays what a session saw. Disclosure — audio and camera frames stream from your browser to a relay this plugin starts on port 8098 (loopback by default; a LAN bind is opt-in and protected by a token minted per start), and from there to generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Gemini Live, which also answers watch checks) using GEMINI_API_KEY read from Thor' secret scope; `start` spawns `node server.js` from the plugin's own directory as a background process, which spawns a Python frame-change tracker (numpy, Pillow, torch); the tool reads the relay's transcript.log and server.log back to the agent; watch verification spends the key's quota. No telemetry, and the key is never written to disk.

name: live2d-rigger
description: Create a provisional Live2D character from a brief with complete image parts, local cutout, placement, an experimental Umamo/JDK rig and Core motion review; also inspect and adjust a copy of an existing model. XY head turns, independent limbs and polished eyes are not provided. Disclosure — runs the Java (JDK) and Kotlin/Umamo classpath, the Python with Playwright and the Cubism SDK viewer folder that you set in the plugin settings (the model cannot name a program, classpath or command), plus FFmpeg and a local headless browser against a viewer served only on a temporary loopback port, each with a minimal environment; on first use it scans PATH and the hardware (read-only) and asks which routes to use; opening an existing model copies its folder into the plugin's data directory; on request it downloads official Live2D sample archives from cubism.live2d.com after you agree to Live2D's licence; the host image tool may use its configured provider; no Cubism SDK, Core, viewer, sample model, layers or textures are bundled, and the catalog thumbnail contains character artwork.

name: livetalk
description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Thor agent — a composer mini-bar for the Thor desktop app. The voice model answers small talk itself and delegates real work through a declared `talk` tool to a dedicated Thor agent session (acknowledge-first, context-first routing); the answer is spoken back in one of the 30 documented HD prebuilt voices. Native config_schema settings (provider, live model, voice, transcription languages, spoken-answer detail, transcript/log visibility). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost. No Thor agent tools registered; dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory. Formerly gemini-live-bridge — renamed for a provider-neutral roadmap; the old repository URL redirects.

name: living-field
description: Thor Desktop pane of the ABUZ8 living spatial field. Four domains and a seeded neural field. Synapses speed up only while the focused session is actually working, and the field dims when the gateway socket is not open. No network, no shell, no fabricated metrics.

name: living-spaces
description: An open canvas for your bots in Thor Desktop. Ask in chat and your bot builds dashboards, trackers, mini-apps and visual pieces in a Spaces tab. Each Space keeps its data, and you change it by asking. Disclosure — Spaces can fetch public HTTPS URLs through the plugin's mediated network path (Internet access is on by default per Space and can be turned off), forwarding the Space's own saved Cookie/Authorization headers; agent upkeep creates Thor cron jobs that run model calls on their schedule; data saved in a Space, including any API keys you put there, is stored in its revisions and can enter model context.

name: llm-antidote
description: Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for Thor Agent: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Thor's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `thor antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose.

name: llmapi
description: LLM API (llmapi.ai) as a Thor model provider (`--provider llmapi`, alias `llm-api`, or LLM API in `thor model`): Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen and more on one key, each on the API it works best on. Claude runs over the Anthropic Messages API (so Thor' prompt caching applies), GPT-5 and later over the Responses API, everything else over Chat Completions. The picker lists LLM API's tool-capable chat models with 64K+ context from its public catalog, which also supplies context windows, image input, per-model reasoning levels and list prices; catalog aliases resolve in /model. Gateway errors (out of credits, spend caps, model not allowed for the key) map onto Thor' fallback instead of a key rotation; /usage shows the credit balance and monthly cap; per-request cost is the billed amount when the gateway reports it, else a list-price estimate. Maintained by LLM API. Disclosure — none

name: llmslim
description: Context engine that compresses older tool output and turns locally with LLMSlim instead of asking a model for a summary: no LLM call, deterministic output, and the start of the prompt is sent unchanged, so prompt caching keeps working. Select it with context.engine: llmslim. Disclosure: installs llmslim==0.12.0 from PyPI (with numpy, scikit-learn and jsonschema); registers no tools, hooks or middleware; makes no network calls, runs no shell commands, needs no credentials, writes no files and sends no telemetry; reads its settings from config.yaml through Thor's config loader. Token counts use a character estimate unless tiktoken is already installed in Thor's environment, in which case tiktoken may download its encoding file once.

name: llmux
description: Compare Surplus Intelligence, Antseed and Solid offers in the Thor composer, then route through one local provider by price, speed or balanced policy. Includes seller trust signals, explicit mid-chat switching, cached market data and a local usage ledger. Disclosure — Loading the plugin starts a detached local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8378 (LLMUX_PORT) that keeps running after Thor exits and holds this profile's Surplus/Solid API keys (set LLMUX_AUTOSTART=0 to run it yourself); every chat sent through the llmux provider is forwarded in full to the seller it picks on Surplus Intelligence (api.surplusintelligence.ai), Solid (accounts.solid.xyz) or your local Antseed buyer (127.0.0.1:8377), where third-party marketplace sellers may serve it and bill your account with no spending cap; it also polls those marketplaces for prices in the background and keeps a market cache and proxy log under your Thor home.

name: load-lock
description: A machine-wide load broker for coding agents: Thor, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor and any MCP client share one heavy-work budget, so builds and test suites take turns instead of thrashing the machine. 19 load_lock_* tools (acquire, queue, offers, honest waits, background jobs that release their permit on exit, machine inspection), a policy brief at session start, a Load Lock dashboard tab, and a Desktop pane, status-bar chip and palette command. Disclosure — every tool shells out to the local load-lock CLI (Node >= 20, installed separately with npm), which auto-starts a per-user background daemon on a Unix socket with state in ~/.local/state/load-lock; load_lock_run_with_permit runs the command the agent passes on this host in its own process group, only when Thor's terminal backend is local (it refuses under docker, ssh, modal and other sandboxes, resolving the backend via tools.terminal_scope and config), and a pre_tool_call hook sends any command Thor's dangerous-command detector flags (imported from tools.approval_detection) to the same approval gate as the terminal tool; every child process (CLI, daemon, jobs) gets an allowlisted environment without provider API keys, plus any names the user lists in env_passthrough; machine inspection reads CPU, memory, load and cgroup limits; the optional auto_install setting (off by default) fetches the pinned npm package with npx, a network call to the npm registry; background work: the daemon, a heartbeat thread and job registry in the plugin process, and one idle `load-lock events --follow` tail in the process serving the dashboard; no telemetry, no credentials, no other network calls.

name: loaded-skills-indicator
description: Status-bar chip, popover and dockable pane showing which skills are read into the active Thor Desktop conversation's context: full bodies bold with an accent dot, compression-pruned ones ghosted, never-loaded ones not listed. A second pane view lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions and a loaded marker, and clicking a skill drops /<skill> into the composer for you to send (it never submits). A small local backend reads the profile's state.db read-only to tell a live skill body from a [SKILL_PRUNED] marker, and reads SKILL.md frontmatter for the descriptions. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no writes. Disclosure — the local backend opens state.db read-only for the requested session in this profile, the default root and, as a fallback, every other profile's state.db, and returns only skill names and load state; it reads SKILL.md frontmatter under the Thor skill directories and makes no network calls or writes.

name: local-business-leads
description: Build local business lead lists from chat: any niche and city from Google Maps (12 countries), plus Yellow Pages US and Canada, BBB profiles, and dentist, contractor and restaurant lists with phone, website, address, hours, rating and business email. Four workflow skills (find leads, list cleanup with email validation and CSV export, BBB trust check, cost estimate) drive eight Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of an Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.0015 to 0.05 per row plus up to USD 0.019 per run). Search terms and places, and any email addresses the user asks to validate, are sent to Apify; the Actors read public business listings and the businesses' own websites, and the results are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Results are business contact data, and outreach with them must follow the marketing laws that apply to the user. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Thor runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `thor mcp add business-leads --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Thor asking before each paid run. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with Google, Yellow Pages or BBB.

name: local-first-routing
description: Pinned local delegation with explicit manual escalation and no fallback.

name: local-fleet
description: Your local inference fleet, operated from Thor Desktop: routing across your own boxes (DGX Spark / GB10, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, clusters behind one endpoint). Probes each box, makes the least busy healthy one the primary model, falls back to smaller models on smaller boxes, then to your cloud model, and switches back when a box recovers. Why-this-box inspector, flight recorder, outage rehearsal, drift detection, readiness, savings with its working, doctor. Optional: subagents across boxes (delegation backend fleet), side tasks on the fleet (auxiliary.<task>), keep the routed model loaded, private inference (primary, fallback chain, side tasks and subagents held to your boxes, failing rather than using cloud; not air-gapping).
