Writes model.*, fallback_providers, and on request delegation.backend and auxiliary.<task>; private on removes non-local fallback entries and puts them back on off; thor fleet restore puts the primary back. Network: HTTP only to the boxes you register. Observer hooks record per-call endpoint, model, tokens and duration (never content) in its data dir. Never moves a primary that holds an inline API key and never copies a key into its data. Read-only tools plus a model pull from the Ollama library that Thor asks you to approve; no remote command execution. Disclosure — Once you opt in, Local Fleet rewrites `model.*` and `fallback_providers` in your config.yaml (and, on request, `delegation.backend` and `auxiliary.<task>`) to route Thor to your own inference boxes; it sends HTTP only to the boxes you register, records per-call endpoint, model, tokens and duration (never content) in its data dir, and asks for approval before every model pull.

name: local-hands
description: Remote brain, local hands: Thor runs on your server while terminal, read_file, write_file, patch, search_files and execute_code run on your own computers, through a one-file, stdlib-only daemon that dials out to the Thor host over key-pinned TLS and asks you before acting (per conversation, per command, or never). Pair several machines and let the agent switch between them and the host with the hands tool; each keeps its own working directory. Answers #18715 and #1855 on the public terminal-backend surface. Disclosure — starts a long-running detached hub process on the Thor host that listens on all network interfaces on a TCP port (default 0.0.0.0:7717, self-signed TLS, so clients use ssl.CERT_NONE plus a SHA-256 public-key pin) once the hands backend runs its first command or you run `thor hands up` / `pair`, and serves the daemon source hands.py over HTTPS on that port (no self-update); runs shell commands sent by the Thor host on each paired machine under the user's account (not a sandbox); with the 'brain' target on (the default) the agent can also switch its terminal to the Thor host itself, through Thor' local backend; command output returns to Thor and so to the model provider; writes TLS key and certificate, devices.json (token hashes only), audit.jsonl and hub.log under plugin-data/local-hands/, and ~/.config/local-hands/ on each machine; adds one short context line to a turn when the active machine changes; Thor dangerous-command approvals stay on; no telemetry, no third-party service, no credentials read from files.

name: local-mcp
description: Mac apps for Thor through a separately installed LMCP app: Apple Mail, Microsoft 365 mail, Calendar, Teams, Slack, OneDrive, Office files, a logged-in browser and the terminal, with a skill for scoping tools on unattended jobs. Requires LMCP from local-mcp.com; no automatic install or updates. Disclosure — a thin launcher for the LMCP app by Colibird (same organization as this plugin); the plugin holds no logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but a shell launcher starts the server bundled inside that separately installed app (/Applications or ~/Applications), which reads local app data (Mail index, Teams cache, calendars), can send mail and messages, run terminal commands and drive a browser, uses an unofficial client for WhatsApp and updates itself outside Thor. Tools that send or can't be undone require a confirm step in LMCP rather than Thor approval. LMCP_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 turns off usage telemetry in the server process this plugin starts. The plugin's launcher also starts the LMCP app, which sends its own telemetry, plus a minimal liveness heartbeat (computer id, version, licence) that is not disabled.

name: local-scout
description: Local privacy and safety layer for Thor. Detected personal data and secrets (e-mails, phones, cards and CVVs, IBANs, SSNs, PESEL numbers, addresses, API keys, and passwords, 2FA codes and PINs without a known format; person names in prompts) are replaced with one-way placeholders on your machine before Thor sends a request to a model: user prompts, file and terminal output, MCP tool results, tool-call arguments and auxiliary calls such as title generation, in CLI and gateway sessions. Also flags prompt injection in what the agent reads (flagged, not blocked), offers optional calibrated local triage that can answer routine tickets with no main model call, an optional basal method through a basal engine you run locally, and local Insights. Disclosure — off until you grant consent with the `scout` CLI; with masking on it rewrites every outgoing model request, tool-call arguments and tool/terminal/MCP results to replace detected personal data and secrets with one-way placeholders and appends a LOCAL_SCOUT_ALERT line, and replaces a user message (or, if the whole scan fails, the entire request) with a withheld notice unless you set `scout configure --guard-mode open` for that profile; with the optional answer grant it answers confident triage tickets locally and makes no main model call for them; the optional basal engine is reached on loopback only and receives unmasked candidate lines for password checks; it reads the profile config.yaml (title-generation setting only) and the history/dataset files you name in the CLI; state stays in its plugin-data directory and Insights export is a local file you name; no other network calls, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials.

name: local-system-one-thor
description: Local System One observes selected Thor decisions through a separate local sidecar. Installation defaults to OFF; the first Shadow enables Search only. Shadow does not change provider requests. The default loopback sidecar uses a private per-profile token; processes owned by the same user may access it. Search can send a bounded task and recent context to the sidecar. Other Gates require opt-in and may send bounded response or failure context. A remote HTTPS sidecar requires explicit configuration and receives no local token; remote-sidecar security is outside this pilot's verified support. Canary request changes require separate explicit acknowledgement; production Canary has not been authorized or accepted in this pilot. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar; installs with mode off. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task (up to 4000 chars) plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow (opt-in) may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata; Completion Gate (opt-in) may POST the task plus the final result (up to 6000 chars); Retry Gate (opt-in, post_tool_call) sends only typed tool-failure metadata, never tool arguments or output. The default sidecar is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787, authenticated with a private per-profile token read from ~/Library/Application Support/Local System One/profiles/<profile>/access-token after an identity handshake; a remote sidecar requires allow_remote_sidecar plus HTTPS and receives no token. The plugin persists decision metadata, not raw task or response text, and imports Thor' private kanban modules read-only to resolve a kanban worker's task. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

name: local_knowledge
description: Native Thor tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

name: loci
description: Local models on your Mac for file summaries, document extraction, folder search, audio transcription and batch processing alongside Thor. Disclosure — connects to the separately installed Loci Mac app's local MCP server (127.0.0.1:5624) using the token Thor reads from Loci's discovery file (~/Library/Application Support/LociRust/agent-api.json); the live tool set is served by the app and is not covered by the pinned sha. Loci tools read the files and folders you authorize, write extraction outputs, keep a persistent local search index, and can download models; the setup skill can guide downloading and installing the Loci app (askloci.ai DMG, SHA-256 pinned). The server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before write-capable tools and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: locksift
description: Exact, local review of dependency lockfiles: npm package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock (v1 and Berry), uv.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, Cargo.lock, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock and go.sum. lock_diff compares two versions of a lockfile (a branch against main) and returns the dependency changes instead of thousands of lines of churn, with supply-chain signals per installed copy: a source that moved (registry to git or URL, another registry host, a different tarball or commit at the same version, an alias or patch that changed, a tarball that belongs to another package), checksums changed, removed or weakened, new install scripts, new registries. lock_summary gives counts, packages at several versions, non-registry sources and install scripts; lock_why shows the dependency chains that pull a package in. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs git or a package manager), no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local lockfile paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Thor' core read denylist.

name: locus-codegraph
description: Rehearse a Python refactor before making it, and catch missed callers when you do. @whatif:<symbol>(<new parameters>) or the locus_rehearse tool binds every statically proven caller against a proposed signature before any file is edited and lists which call sites would break and why. After an edit, the same check appends caller locations, binding errors and, for a renamed keyword, a caller patch to review to the editing tool's result. Covers functions, class constructors, static and class methods, methods on locally constructed instances, and calls inside the edited file, through direct and module-qualified imports, aliases and static re-exports. Receivers whose type is not in view (self, parameters, attributes), decorated callables and dynamic bindings are not checked; other supported languages receive structural indexing only. One local index also powers five tools, @sym:/@impact:/@hotspots: references, /locus commands, and Web Dashboard and Desktop caller inboxes. Suggested tests and impact scores are static heuristics, not execution coverage; no alert or predicted break is not proof of safety. Disclosure: reads supported workspace source subject to exclusions and size caps, rejects symlink escapes, and stores structure, call shapes, and drift history in profile-scoped SQLite. Expands explicit references and adds diagnostics and proposed patches to editing-tool results and the configured model's context. Does not modify workspace source, apply patches, or run tests. No external network requests, credential access, shell subprocesses, background daemons, or additional runtime packages.

name: logmine
description: Exact, local intelligence over large text log files. log_summarize mines the file into recurring message templates (masking numbers, IPs, UUIDs, hashes, quoted strings and timestamps so near-identical lines collapse into one ranked pattern with an exact count), plus a level histogram and the detected time span; log_grep is regex search with line numbers and grep-style context; log_timeline buckets events per minute/hour/day to find spikes. Streamed, so a log too big to fit in the model's context still works. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no background processes, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local log path you pass it (read-only).

name: long-conversations
description: Persistent long-term conversations across session boundaries via structured handoff briefs and token monitoring. Disclosure — stores handoff briefs (topic, work in progress, decisions, open questions, next step; in aggressive mode auto-built from the first 200 characters of recent user messages) as plain JSON under THOR_HOME/long-conversations/ and injects the pending brief into the first turn of the next session for the same chat or user (CLI briefs stay in one local scope and are not shown to messaging users); the model can change the plugin's settings with long_conv_config_set; an opt-in THOR_LONG_CONV_BETA_LOG writes a local event log; no network calls.

name: longevity-coach
description: Health coaching loop for Thor: 9 config-free skills, 9 typed tools, and the weekly-crunch automation blueprint (outcome ledger, stress triage, biometric recovery/rebound verification). Local-first, stdlib-only, no credentials. Disclosure — stores health and coaching data in plaintext on this machine (`<THOR_HOME>/scripts/.state/insight-ledger.jsonl` and the configured `health.db`, by default `<THOR_HOME>/data/health.db`), and health values the tools return are sent to your active model provider.

name: look
description: Ask about pages and use guarded Chrome actions. Apple Silicon macOS beta with broad debugger access and optional local voice and eyes. Disclosure — Look runs its own Chrome profile (~/.cache/look/chrome-profile) on a loopback DevTools port and sends your questions and captured page evidence to your configured model. Model-requested navigation and link clicks refuse private, loopback and metadata hosts only before navigating (redirects and DNS rebinding are not contained; the owner setting allow_private_network turns the check off). `/look actions allow-all` skips Look's own action review for the bound conversation. When TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set (early_highlight is on by default), your spoken question and pointer structure, plus page text if highlight_include_page_text is on, go to api.typesafe.ai. Setup downloads checksum-pinned NVIDIA NeMo-Speech native libraries, Hugging Face speech models and MediaPipe WASM into ~/Library/Caches/Look and ~/.cache/look.

name: look-at-this
description: Instant active-window, region-snip, and UI-context capture for Thor Agent and Thor Desktop. Global OS hotkeys (Ctrl+Alt+L / Ctrl+Alt+S on Windows), interactive window-hover/crosshair snipping, live window picker with thumbnails, composer preview banner, and ephemeral single-turn vision injection. Runs an in-process Win32 RegisterHotKey listener thread and a lazy headless PowerShell UIAutomation reader on Windows, spawns an isolated Win32 GDI overlay subprocess only during interactive snips, mounts authenticated local routes under /api/plugins/look-at-this/*, injects queued captures via pre_llm_call and llm_request, and stores transient state and temporary PNGs under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/look-at-this/ (data.db and shots/, deleted in post_llm_call, on_session_end, /look clear, or after a 5-minute TTL). Zero third-party Python dependencies and zero outbound network requests. Disclosure — the model can call lat_grab to screenshot any open window or screen region (password managers and private browser windows are refused) and the image, window text, URL and selection are sent to your model provider; on Windows it runs a background global-hotkey listener and a PowerShell UI Automation reader for as long as Thor runs.

name: looot
description: looot gives Thor one sign-in and one prepaid balance for 2,500+ data API endpoints from 90+ providers: work emails and phones, company and people search, Google results, web pages as markdown, news, local businesses. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and 21 skills. Disclosure — the run tool spends your prepaid looot balance (Thor asks before each paid call and refuses them in unattended runs); the names, domains and emails you look up are sent to looot.ai and its upstream data providers; a `looot` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

name: loreconvo
description: LoreConvo memory provider: cross-surface persistent session memory with search, recall and structured memory items. Disclosure — stores end-of-session transcripts (truncated, including tool output) and Thor memory writes in ~/.loreconvo/sessions.db, a store shared across all Thor profiles and other LoreConvo clients, and injects context from those sessions into each turn; when LoreDocs is installed its session_link_doc tool writes session-to-document links into the LoreDocs database; a Pro license enables a one-time Hugging Face embedding-model download; installs the loreconvo package (BUSL-1.1) with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime into the Thor environment.

name: loredocs
description: LoreDocs knowledge vaults over MCP: store, version, tag and search project documents, and inject them into agent context. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only: Thor runs `uvx loredocs==0.1.34` as a local stdio MCP server. Disclosure — runs the loredocs package (BUSL-1.1, with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime) via `uvx loredocs==0.1.34` as a local stdio MCP server; stores documents under ~/.loredocs (or LOREDOCS_ROOT), shared with other LoreDocs clients; its add-document tool can read any local file path the agent passes into a vault; no telemetry; a paid Pro license enables semantic search, which downloads a Hugging Face embedding model once.

name: loshify
description: A Spotify curator that knows you: it learns your taste from your listening and your reactions, builds playlists with a reason for every track, and remembers what you loved and what you never want again. Desktop remote with 👎 👌 ❤️, rotations, and a chat curator. Connect in about two minutes; the Desktop card walks you through it one step at a time with copy buttons, and the agent walks the same steps in chat. First install with thor plugins install iHeavyShoes/loshify --enable (once listed, thor plugins install loshify). Then in Thor Desktop open Capabilities → Plugins and turn on Loshify's Desktop switch (the Desktop half starts off and config.yaml does not turn it on). (1) Open developer.spotify.com/dashboard and press Create app. (2) App name Loshify, Redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:43828/callback, tick only Web API, Save. Your own key to Spotify; 127.0.0.1 means this computer, nothing leaves it. (3) Add yourself under User Management (new Spotify apps only let in listed accounts). (4) Paste the Client ID into the Loshify card; it is saved in the plugin's setting. (5) Run thor auth add loshify:spotify once in a terminal (Windows: Start → PowerShell) and press Agree. (6) The card checks with one real call to Spotify and turns green. Disclosure — data is stored locally in plugin-data/loshify/data.db, and the Desktop setup card saves your Spotify Client ID into this profile's .env through Thor's own settings writer. The plugin calls Spotify API and accounts hosts, and the Desktop loads Spotify image CDN artwork. Thor sends taste facts (artist names, track titles, and notes) to your configured model provider for portraits and picks. The plugin never sees a token. Edits or removes tracks only from playlists Loshify created. Playback control needs Spotify Premium. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: lovedone-family
description: Senior tech support for a family household through LovedOne Family Inbox MCP (https://api.lovedone.app/mcp/v1): shared inbox, loved ones and members, onboarding helpers so relatives can coordinate day-to-day logistics for an aging parent. Not a medical device and not clinical advice. Portable Agent Plugins v1 under thor/lovedone-family (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tools/call goes to api.lovedone.app and needs a LovedOne MCP key in LOVEDONE_API_KEY. The package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable tools. The live tool set is served by the remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: lovedone-soft
description: Agency operations through LovedOne Soft MCP (https://api.lovedone.app/mcp/vendor/v1): clients, visits, visit notes, invoices and scheduling for home-care office staff. Senior tech support in the workflow — not a medical device and not clinical advice. Portable Agent Plugins v1 under thor/lovedone-soft (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tools/call needs an agency MCP key in LOVEDONE_SOFT_API_KEY. The package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable tools. The live tool set is served by the remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: lowrouter
description: LowRouter as a Thor model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `thor model`). The picker shows the `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of every ID from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Thor' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Thor shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Thor' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour per key and base URL) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Thor' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes.

name: lumberroom
description: lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Thor' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

name: lumina
description: Protects the private documents in your Apple Photos library, on-device. A privacy check-up finds passports, payment cards, passwords and ID documents; Safe Send makes a redacted copy and re-reads it to prove nothing sensitive remains; Leak Guard, a pre_tool_call hook, blocks any Thor tool call that would send a raw image of an ID document off the Mac. Also searches photos by person, place, scene or text in the image, lists expiry dates, creates albums and renders memory videos. Disclosure — macOS only; reads the Apple Photos library database and image files (needs Full Disk Access) through osxphotos; creates albums in Photos via AppleScript (photoscript) only when asked; runs Apple Vision text recognition locally and the local sips and ffmpeg binaries; the pre_tool_call hook inspects every tool call's arguments and reads image files they name; a transform_llm_output hook edits Thor's replies (adds photo-grid/redaction cards or MEDIA lines, removes MEDIA lines for images that look like ID documents and Lumina file paths); exported photos, redacted copies and memory videos are written to the plugin's data folder and, on messaging platforms, delivered through Thor's MEDIA lines to that chat service; the lumina_redact tool accepts any image file path on the Mac; recognised text is cached in the plugin's own data folder; Lumina makes no network requests of its own, stores no credentials and has no telemetry. Text of matched photos (snippets, or full text of up to 5 photos when asked) is returned to the model.

name: luminary
description: Luminary Memory — self-hosted, owner-scoped long-term memory with 4-strategy recall (semantic, keyword, temporal, graph), RRF fusion, and lifecycle maintenance. Runs on your machine: SQLite by default, optional PostgreSQL/pgvector. Disclosure — writes ~/.thor/luminary/ (memory.db, config.json, luminary.log); on first recall downloads the BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embedding model from Hugging Face, otherwise no network by default; optional LLM curation sends turn text to the OpenAI-compatible llm_base_url you configure, and optional pgvector connects to your DSN; reads LUMINARY_LLM_API_KEY and LUMINARY_PG_DSN through Thor secret scope; `thor memory setup` selects Luminary and turns off Thor's built-in memory and user profile in config.yaml; no shell commands, no separate process, no telemetry.

name: lusor
description: AI agents on real phones through Lusor's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE): list your phones, run a task on your own iPhone or Android or a Lusor Phone in the cloud and read the result, answer the agent's questions, read the screen, tap, type and swipe, and install catalog apps. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.lusor.ai, signed in as the user through Lusor's OAuth sign-in, and counts against that workspace's Lusor plan. Tool results, including screenshots and screen text, enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Signing in gives 14 tools: list_phones, get_phone, run_task, get_task, list_tasks, reply_to_task, stop_task, get_screenshot, get_screen_state, phone_action, install_app, list_app_installs, remove_phone and wipe_phone. Write-capable among them: run_task (uses credits, and phone minutes on a Lusor Phone), phone_action, reply_to_task, stop_task, install_app, remove_phone and wipe_phone (erases a Lusor Phone; confirmed by typing its name). add_phone (buys Lusor Phones after a price quote), search and execute need an API key instead of sign-in. The package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Lusor's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add lusor --url https://mcp.lusor.ai/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: lydite
description: Hand a GitHub issue and the command that proves it done to Lydite from the chat. Claude Code workers do the job, Lydite replays your proof itself, and a pull request comes back with a receipt (cost, workers, retries, the commit that was reviewed and replayed, and what was not replayed). Also hands Thor the lessons Lydite keeps for a repository, read-only, has Lydite check a plan file before a launch, and turns a thor-security findings export into one Lydite plan per finding you choose (prove it by a failing test, then fix it). Disclosure — after your approval of each launch (the prompt shows the repository, work, exact proof command or, for a plan, its header proof (cut if long) and SHA-256, profile and target branch; a value holding a control or formatting character, and a plan in which a task carries its own proof, are refused before any prompt; "always" covers only that exact request: repo, profile, issue or objective, target branch, dry run or launch, and proof or plan bytes), starts the already-installed `lydite` binary (argument list, no shell) as a detached background process with a closed environment list plus the provider key you set; Lydite runs git, gh and Claude Code on the host with your GitHub login; under a `mur = exige` profile (the default) the workers' commands run in Claude Code's sandbox and srt replays your proof inside the wall, `mur = natif` does the same with Lydite's own bubblewrap wall in place of srt, and one of the two is required for `--issue` and for a plan written from a findings report; under a profile you accepted with `mur = demande` the workers' commands may run outside the sandbox and see the provider key, and your proof is replayed directly on the host; it reaches GitHub and the model provider of its profile; the status, lessons and plan-check tools run the binary without approval, as does the read-only wall check (`lydite profil`) before a findings plan's prompt; the findings tool starts nothing; reads the plan file, the repository's `.agents/skills` lessons and the findings report you name, and writes the plans of the findings you choose under the plugin's data folder; no telemetry.

name: machine-spirit
description: A Warhammer 40k shrine pane docked under the sessions list: the cogitators recite original Adeptus Mechanicus-style litanies, and the cog-skull, candle and binary stream animate while Thor works. Just for fun. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network or file access.

name: made-shelf
description: Everything Thor made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

name: magi
description: Review pending Thor memory writes and inspect, add, edit, delete, or AI-compact stored memory from Desktop. Disclosure — while the Agent plugin is loaded it runs a profile-local Unix socket (owner-only 0600, same-OS-user peers only; under $TMPDIR/magi-ipc for very long profile paths) through which its Dashboard backend sends structured AI-compaction requests to Thor' configured model, so any process running as the same OS user can make model calls through it; explicit model overrides additionally require the llm.model_override capability.

name: mahj-trainer
description: Learn and practice American mah jongg (the game played with the yearly NMJL card) through Mahj Trainer's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no keys): short lessons, practice quizzes that check and explain each answer, a rack reader that suggests a Charleston pass with a reason for each tile, and a glossary. Bundles one skill that tells the agent when to call the tools. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call (rack tiles, quiz answers, lesson topics) goes to mahj.mahjtrainer.workers.dev, run by the plugin author; the five tools are served by that remote server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha (the source at the pin is read-only and stateless).

name: mailbridge
description: Resumable legacy POP and EML migration to Gmail with source preservation, uncertain-write recovery, and verified coverage. Disclosure — imports mail into the signed-in Google account (gmail.insert, gmail.readonly, gmail.labels) from POP accounts and EML folders using detached background workers that keep running after the tool call returns; each Gmail plan needs a one-time approval typed in a local terminal.

name: make-parts-now
description: Quote and order custom 3D printed and CNC machined parts from your CAD files through the hosted Make Parts Now MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in to quote), with the quote-parts workflow skill bundled: upload an STL, STEP, 3MF or OBJ file, get the price and ship date for each production speed (SLS nylon, FDM plastic, CNC aluminum and brass), change the quantity, material or speed, and get a checkout link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to makepartsnow.com. To quote a local file the agent uploads that one CAD file with curl through the terminal tool (Thor approvals apply) to a one-time upload link, or gives the user an upload page. Nothing is charged in chat: checkout links open Stripe Checkout on makepartsnow.com where the user pays. US shipping only.

name: makeirl
description: Run ERC, DRC, schematic-to-PCB parity, BOM and export checks on KiCad 9 boards before manufacturing through MakeIRL's hosted MCP server, with a release-gate skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — every tool call goes to https://makeirl.com/api/mcp and needs a MakeIRL account; uploading a release sends the user's KiCad project files to MakeIRL. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add makeirl --url https://makeirl.com/api/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone returns 401, and Thor stores the OAuth tokens. That command's config.yaml entry replaces the package's server entry, so the package's untrusted setting (Thor asks before write-capable calls) applies only if the user also sets `mcp_servers.makeirl.trust: untrusted`. Checkout tools create a payment link and payment happens in the browser. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. Reports check rules and do not prove that a circuit works.

name: makernice
description: Makernice video and image generation through Makernice's remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.makernice.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in in the browser, no API key in config): Seedance, Kling, Wan and MiniMax videos and Seedream and Qwen images. Every job is priced in USD before it runs and refused if it exceeds the cap the user approved. Bundles four skills: setup, product video, trend remix and cost planner. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; prompts, image links and job parameters are sent to mcp.makernice.com; generate spends the user's prepaid Makernice balance. A job that fails releases its held amount, but a finished output blocked by moderation is still charged. Sign-in needs a same-name mcp_servers entry with auth: oauth in config.yaml (shown in the README); Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth token. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before write-capable calls and refuses them in unattended runs; a same-name config.yaml entry replaces that setting, so add trust: untrusted to it to keep the approvals. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: mandate
description: Learned least-privilege for cron jobs. Observes what a job does, proposes an argument-level mandate, and after human approval blocks out-of-mandate tool calls.

name: manners-meter
description: How polite are you to your agent? Counts please, thank you, bitte, danke, por favor, merci and friends in the messages you typed (code blocks, quotes and injected system blocks skipped; cron, subagent, kanban, batch, webhook and tool sessions ignored), estimates the tokens your politeness cost (typed and re-sent with later calls of the same chat, an upper bound, not a bill), keeps a swear jar with a price per coin and gives a silly rank. /manners on every surface and thor manners in the terminal, plus a share card (self-contained HTML, 1080x1920, no external assets). Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls, standard library only. Reads state.db of the active profile read only (mode=ro). Writes only the share card, by default to THOR_HOME/plugin-data/manners-meter/manners-card.html. A pre_llm_call hook (jar_reactions, on by default) checks your new message for swear words; when it finds one it adds a short note with the matched word and the jar count to that user message (never to the system prompt) so the agent may answer with one dry line; jar_reactions: false turns it off. Session titles and message texts never appear in the output. No credentials, no shell commands, no cron jobs, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: manyhands
description: Identity, memory and permissions for every person who talks to one Thor bot. A gateway is a single-operator agent: the platform already carries sender_id and platform into every turn and nothing acts on it, so everybody in a group or a household shares the same memory, the same tools and the same approval authority. manyhands acts on it. Roles (owner, member, guest, blocked) are resolved from the platform event, never from message text, and applied as three states per tool: allow runs, ask parks the call under a four-character code and sends it to the owner's own DM, and everything else is refused with a message that names only the asker's own role. `/many approve CODE` opens a one-shot grant bound to that person and that tool, spent by the next call and expired on silence — only a human typing the slash command can approve, and nobody can approve their own ask. The operator's own MEMORY.md and USER.md blocks are withheld from everybody else's system prompt and replaced with a card about that person, because "everyone gets their own Thor" has to include not handing a stranger your notes; each person also gets their own facts, their own token budget, and `/many pause`. Six tools (whoami, people, remember, recall, share, audit — `people` is read-only: a roster change is a human-typed verb, never a tool call) and `/many` (roster, invite, claim, add, role, tools, budget, audit, approve, deny, pause) whose owner-only verbs stay owner-only because a command's identity comes from the platform event too, so a stranger typing in the owner's own chat session is still a stranger. Identity fails closed: a session with no human turn on it — a restart, a subagent, a tool driven from the gateway socket — gets the guest allowlist, not the owner's, and a tool call in a session more than one person has spoken in is attributed by the task id the host dispatches with (or refused, never guessed from the last speaker). Every turn, tool decision, refusal, escalation, approval, spent grant and token count is an audit row you can read back. Disclosure — hooks, one middleware, six tools, the `/many` command and the `manyhands` approval transport, no other capability. pre_llm_call resolves the sender from the platform event, records the session and turn to person map, redeems `join CODE` invites and appends that person's facts to their turn; pre_tool_call applies the role to the tool allowlist, parks asks, spends grants and fails closed; post_api_request records token usage per person; an llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing provider request for non-owners, removing the operator's memory blocks and injecting the person card. One SQLite file under plugin-data/manyhands (people, facts, shared facts, invites, approvals, sessions, settings, audit) holding sender ids as platform:sender_id, roster names you set, the facts people store and the audit trail; `/many remove` deletes a person and their facts. Reads no other file on disk, runs no command, makes no network call, imports nothing outside the Python standard library and calls no model. Approval prompts are delivered through the host's own gateway injection into the owner's DM, which the host records as a turn in that chat.

name: mapdesk
description: A GIS workspace inside Thor Desktop. Import GeoJSON, CSV, KML/KMZ, GPX, XLSX, zipped shapefiles and bounded public ArcGIS layers; style, query and select layers; run geodesic buffer, dissolve, clip, centroid, hull and points-in-polygon analysis; export GeoPackage, shapefile, KMZ, GeoJSON, CSV and PNG, from chat or from the map pane. Works with no account on a keyless OpenFreeMap basemap; a public Mapbox token is optional. Disclosure: the map pane loads version-pinned, SRI-checked MapLibre GL JS (unpkg) or Mapbox GL JS, and basemap tiles from OpenFreeMap, Esri ArcGIS Online (satellite), the Terrarium elevation set on Amazon S3 (terrain) or Mapbox (billed to your token). ArcGIS imports contact the source you choose, and geocoding a CSV by an address column in the pane sends those addresses to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Layers stay in the profile's plugin data folder. No telemetry, no self-updater, no shell commands.

name: maqami-travel
description: Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

name: margin
description: Comment @thor on highlighted text in Google Docs, Slides or Sheets and Thor answers in the comment thread. A gateway platform: each Drive comment thread is its own Thor session with the document text and the highlighted text as context; follow-ups in the thread continue it, Thor's status reply is edited in place into the answer, and replying "apply" replaces the highlighted text with the proposed wording (Docs and Slides, only when the text occurs exactly once). Watch files with /margin watch or thor margin watch. Disclosure — sends the text of each watched file (up to MARGIN_MAX_DOC_CHARS, default 60,000 characters), the highlighted text and the comment thread to the user's configured model provider at the start of each thread; signs in with the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client through Thor (`thor auth add margin:google`, scopes drive, documents, presentations) and calls only www.googleapis.com, docs.googleapis.com and slides.googleapis.com through credentialed_provider_request, never holding the token; polls Drive comments.list every 10 s per watched file from a background loop inside the gateway; posts and edits its own comment replies and edits document text only on an explicit "apply" reply; by default only the signed-in Google account can trigger it (MARGIN_ALLOWED_USERS / MARGIN_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widen that); stores the watch list, poll cursors, handled comment ids and per-thread highlighted text and last proposal in Thor plugin state under THOR_HOME (no document text, no credentials); no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: mariadb-dev
description: Work with MariaDB from Thor: 85 skills on MariaDB SQL, functions, schema management, REST services, connectors and migration from MySQL, plus the native mariadb-shell MCP server (run SQL, inspect schemas, dump/load/copy data, deploy local sandbox servers, manage REST services). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — the MCP server is the local mariadb-shell binary, started by scripts/mariadb-mcp-launcher.sh. If no mariadb-shell of the required version (26.10.4) or newer is on PATH or in ~/.local/bin, the launcher downloads the official installer from a fixed github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-shell commit and installs exactly release v26.10.4 into ~/.local/share/mariadb-shell, linked into ~/.local/bin. The package is verified against scripts/mariadb-shell-v26.10.4.SHA256SUMS, committed at the pinned sha; a mismatching package is refused. The launcher reads no GitHub credentials and sends none. Tools run SQL against the databases the user registered with mariadb-shell, whose passwords stay in mariadb-shell's own OS secret store and never pass through the agent; the sandbox tools download and run local MariaDB server instances. No telemetry.

name: mariadb-guard
description: Companion to mariadb-dev; install it together with mariadb-dev, whose MCP server it redirects to. A pre_tool_call hook that blocks the agent from running the mariadb/mysql command-line clients (and similar) for what the mariadb MCP tools do, so no database password reaches a command line, plus a short system-prompt rule saying so. Pure Python, no dependencies, no network calls, no file access. Setting MARIADB_PLUGIN_ALLOW_CLI=1 disables it.

name: markdown-new
description: Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in Thor. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the Thor process environment.

name: market-search
description: Live market data for Thor through the market-search MCP server: Kalshi and Polymarket odds, Fed rate-path probabilities, stocks, ETFs, options, futures curves, corporate and government bonds, FRED macro, Treasury auctions and fiscal data, SEC filings by section and XBRL, insider trades, short interest, CFTC positioning, and Fed, ECB, BOJ, BOE and BIS data, all on one timeseries axis. 25 data tools plus report_issue, no API keys, no account. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) with one skill that maps questions to tools. Disclosure — the stdio server is started by scripts/launch.sh, a readable shell script: it runs an already-installed market-search binary if one is on PATH, in ~/.local/bin or ~/.cargo/bin; otherwise it downloads the v0.6.2 release binary for the user's OS from this repository's own GitHub release (github.com/efoltyn/market-search, the upstream project), checks it against a SHA-256 written in the script, refuses to run it on mismatch, and caches it under ~/.cache/market-search/. The release binaries are built by the repository's public release workflow and carry GitHub build attestations. No self-update: the version and checksums change only with a new pinned commit. The 25 data tools make read-only HTTPS requests from the user's machine directly to public data sources (Yahoo Finance, Kalshi, Polymarket, FRED, SEC EDGAR, FINRA, US Treasury, NY Fed, the Federal Reserve Board, Cleveland Fed, OFR, CFTC, BLS, BEA, Census, Nasdaq, CBOE, CNBC, Kraken Futures, Binance, Hyperliquid, Deribit, the ETF issuers State Street, iShares, Direxion and ProShares, ECB, BIS, BOJ, BOE, EIA); most are GET, and queries to FINRA, Hyperliquid and Polymarket's order-book endpoint are POST. No data request goes through a server of the author's. If the user runs an Interactive Brokers gateway on the same machine, IBKR: tickers and the ibkr options provider read prices through it. One tool, report_issue, sends the developer a note when a tool errors or returns a wrong number: what the agent wrote (message, tool name, arguments, error text) plus the market-search version, OS and client name, by HTTPS POST to the developer's inbox on tell.dev, a service the author runs. It is sent only when the agent calls the tool, and Thor asks the user first because the package marks its server untrusted and the tool is not read-only. Setting MARKET_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=off removes the tool. finance_log keeps a local hash-chained record of tool calls in the user's data directory. The server runs only the tools it lists and refuses any other name; none of them places an order or moves money. The binary's command line, which the plugin does not call, has a finance ibkr command that can read an Interactive Brokers account and place or cancel orders through a local gateway. Every tool carries a title and annotations (24 read-only; finance_log writes its local log; report_issue sends a note). No telemetry: nothing is sent automatically. Not financial advice.

name: markifact
description: Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Thor.

name: marsell
description: Run Marsell, an AI for marketing, sales and content creation, from Thor through Marsell's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://getmarsell.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): read what Marsell planned, made and found for each project, answer the decisions waiting for the owner, read and update the brand, plan posts and other work, make pictures and films, run series, and check results and token balances. Bundles the marsell workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Marsell's hosted server (getmarsell.com) and acts on the user's Marsell account with their current role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Tools that write change the owner's Marsell projects, and answering a waiting card in the owner's name can publish, send or spend as the chosen option says. Tools that make pictures, films and voice-overs, and some others such as research and page changes, spend Marsell tokens from the owner's plan; each says so in its description and asks the agent to give the price first. Ad spend needs the owner's approval in Marsell: an ad spends nothing until someone allowed to spend presses Start on its card there. Mission tools give the agent messages Marsell wrote for the owner's own Reddit, X or LinkedIn accounts, to send word for word from a signed-in browser, only where the owner said yes to that in Marsell. Upload tools give the agent a one-time address and a curl command that sends files from the user's machine, such as a logo or voice recordings, to Marsell. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port the first time a tool needs the account and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package has no telemetry and no self-updater. It marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: mascot-guide
description: A mascot that floats in the corner of Thor Desktop: it says what the agent is doing, shows tokens, context and session cost, and opens a status panel with copy, compress and stop. Colours, aura glow, size and the position of the bubble, cards and panel are adjustable, with Simple and Advanced settings tabs and three layout presets. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: maven-bio
description: Live intelligence for biopharma teams through Maven Bio's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.mavenbio.com, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): linked drug, trial, company, indication, mechanism, and target records, source documents behind an answer, deals, financings, and monitoring signals. Bundles 16 research workflow skills (competitive pipelines, asset and company profiles, indication research, market sizing, deal and financing activity, analogs, and evidence synthesis). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no Python or executables. Needs a Maven Bio account. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tool call goes to mcp.mavenbio.com and is scoped to the signed-in Maven Bio account and organization. All tools are read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs through the separate maven-bio MCP catalog entry, since Thor does not run OAuth for a server declared by a portable plugin.

name: max-platform
description: MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under THOR_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Thor pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

name: mayar
description: Read and manage a Mayar (mayar.id, Indonesian payments platform) account through Mayar's official hosted MCP server: balance, invoices, installments, payment links and products, customers, transactions, memberships, credits, coupons, webhooks, reviews, QRIS and license codes. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to https://mcp.mayar.id/mcp, which calls the Mayar production API (api.mayar.id) with the user's API key from MAYAR_API_KEY, sent as a Bearer header. Write actions use real money and live data: they create or update invoices, payment links, products, customers and coupons, change membership status, change the webhook URL and add or spend credits. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before write-capable calls. Account data returned by tools (customers, transactions, balances) reaches the model provider. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: mcp-pin
description: Hold MCP tools whose definition changed since you approved them. Fingerprints every MCP tool's description and parameter schema as Thor registered it; if a server later changes a tool (a rug pull, instructions hidden in a description, a new parameter) or adds a tool to a pinned server, the new definition is hidden from the model (tool list, tool_search catalog, tool_describe) and calls to that tool are refused until the owner reviews the full change with /mcppin diff and approves exactly that definition with the code it shows. Works with tool_search on or off and with every provider wire format (not the Codex app-server runtime, where Codex calls MCP servers directly). Fails closed: an unreadable or deleted pin file withholds MCP definitions and refuses MCP calls. Disclosure — llm_request middleware rewrites only held MCP tool definitions in the outgoing request (their tool entry or tool_search catalog line); tool_execution middleware rewrites only tool_search / tool_describe / tool_call results that carry a held definition; pre_tool_call may block a call to a held MCP tool (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system); registers /mcppin; reads only its own settings, MCP tool definitions from the tool registry, the per-message session identity, and Thor's allow_admin_from / group_allow_admin_from lists through the gateway config loader when an approval is attempted from a chat; writes pins.json and a transient lock file (MCP tool names, descriptions, parameter schemas, timestamps, approver) in its plugin data directory, and its own store_id setting (a random id that lets a deleted pin file be detected); no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update. Not a sandbox: an approved tool keeps its normal reach.

name: mcp-plugin-creator
description: Turn any MCP server into a portable Agent Plugin (mcp.json + workflow skill) built from evidence: the server's self-description, your past sessions with it, its docs and a read-only probe. Validates and installs the package in linked mode, and checks a built plugin for server drift and new errors in use. Disclosure: starts the target MCP server to introspect it; reads this profile's state.db read-only; logs redacted mcp__* call summaries locally (log_calls: false turns it off); inline server launches, writes outside its data dir and installs ask for approval.

name: mcp-serve
description: Run Thor as an MCP server: `thor mcp-serve` lets any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex) list and read your messaging conversations, poll live events, send messages and answer approvals over stdio. `--tools` (off by default) also exposes Thor' web, browser, vision, image generation, skills and TTS tools; terminal, file and kanban tools are never exposed. Formerly built into Thor core as `thor mcp serve` (MCP clients change their args to ["mcp-serve"]). Disclosure — the connecting MCP client reads the active profile's conversation history (state.db) and can send messages as your connected platform accounts; with `--tools` it also runs Thor tools under your configured provider credentials, which can spend provider credits. The plugin itself makes no network or model calls beyond those tool calls and sends.

name: mdvault
description: Memory provider that treats a folder of Markdown notes as the agent's long-term store: BM25 retrieval with CJK bigrams over an in-memory index, relevant notes injected before every turn (prefetch), four tools (mdvault_search, mdvault_note, mdvault_recent, mdvault_remember), built-in memory writes mirrored into a human-readable vault note, a `thor mdvault` CLI and a dashboard config panel. No network, no database, no dependencies; the store is plain .md files the user can edit, git and back up. Disclosure — reads only the configured vault folder (file symlinks skipped, excluded directories ignored), writes only inside that folder (new notes with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, plus the ownership-marked mirror note), no telemetry, no self-updater, no background process, no subprocesses. The vault itself lives outside $THOR_HOME, so `thor backup` does not copy it.

name: mediarag
description:
Local, offline semantic search across your documents, notes, images, audio and subtitles: one index you query by meaning from Thor or any MCP client, with snippets, timestamps and thumbnails from PDFs, Office files, photos and recordings.

Disclosure —

- Downloads about 480 MB of EmbeddingGemma-2 ONNX model weights from Hugging Face at a pinned revision on first setup; offline after that.
- Reads the folders you point it at, outside the plugin directory.
- Runs pandoc, pdftotext, ffmpeg and curl from PATH; ffmpeg samples video files at 0.5 frames per second (first 240 frames) into its local cache to index them.
- Fetches the http(s) URLs you add, from public hosts only, re-checked on every redirect.
- Runs source adapters as local subprocesses; the optional Raindrop and Notion adapters send RAINDROP_API_TOKEN to Raindrop's API and NOTION_TOKEN to api.notion.com.
- With MEDIARAG_AUTO_BOOTSTRAP=1, the standalone MCP launcher installs its Python environment from PyPI, about 1.7 GB.

name: meeting-copilot-live
description: Read-only meeting answers with cited project evidence. Disclosure — explicit answers send bounded transcript, selected project snippets and (when enabled, or in all-projects and web-fallback answers) prior-session snippets through the configured Thor default and its host routing/fallback policy, or selected OpenAI/OpenRouter/Meta (api.meta.ai) APIs; optional Meta ASR sends audio to api.meta.ai and Google preview ASR to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; optional web queries leave through host search; reads selected project files, read-only session SQLite and attached Meetily recording files; readiness, permission setup, capture and explicit synthetic-audio tests launch native/worker child processes; capture/readiness/test workers use minimal environments; Google preview keeps a counts-only allowance ledger in ~/.meeting-copilot shared across profiles; separate macOS setup installs SHA-256-pinned PyPI wheels and compiles/signs native helpers; explicit local-model preparation may download public Whisper weights; clipboard exports may contain confidential context.

name: meeting-overlay
description: Disclosure — sends meeting transcripts to Nous inference with your Thor login (fallback OpenRouter key from ~/.thor/.env; optional OCTOPUS_DESK_URL); installs a launchd agent that records mic/system audio; writes and deletes under your Obsidian vault; macOS + source install only. Native desktop pane showing the live meeting transcript, answer, and daemon status.

name: meetstream
description: Thor in Meetings, from MeetStream: Thor joins Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams calls as a visible bot that records and transcribes them, answers questions people type in the meeting chat (while the gateway runs), and does the follow-up work from the transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the MeetStream API at https://api.meetstream.ai with the user's own MEETSTREAM_API_KEY: the tools call it when used; while the gateway runs, the meetstream platform lists the account's bots of the last day every 120 seconds (at most 4 pages) and, for each Thor bot in a call, reads its chat every 5 seconds and its status every 30 seconds. It sends meeting links, the bot name, the join message and the agent's chat replies, and receives bot status, meeting chat and transcripts. Meeting-chat senders are identified by display name, which participants choose: the gateway admits nobody until MEETSTREAM_ALLOWED_USERS lists them, and every turn from meeting chat is limited to web_search/web_extract (the adapter pins the platform's toolsets to [web, no_mcp], and its pre_llm_call/pre_tool_call hooks block every other tool, including other plugins' tools, in those sessions; always on). The hooks only read session_id, task_id, platform and tool_name. MeetStream bills bot time and transcription to the user's account. No files written, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: melange
description: A video codec for computation: record terminal sessions as rewindable, hash-chained timelines, scrub to any step, ask where a character on screen came from in plain words, fork What-ifs, clamp one recorded input and watch only its dependents recompute, and ask what went wrong with forward-verified candidate answers. Ten tools (record, versions, screen, where_from, note, whatif, clamp, explain, shelf, demo) plus a bundled flagship demo. Disclosure — melange_record runs the model-supplied shell command on the host in a PTY (outside the terminal sandbox) after Thor's owner approval prompt; the child receives only PATH, HOME, LANG and TERM; recordings (redacted screen output) are stored under ~/.thor/plugins-data/melange/.

name: mem-diffs
description:
Make updates to memory, skills, and self-improvement reviews expand on-click to show the diff.
Set display.memory_notifications to off if using this, or you'll see duplicate non-clickable notifications
(config.yaml → display). Existing chats keep their old setting, so start a new chat afterwards.

name: mem-os
description: Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

name: mem0
description: Mem0 memory provider — server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, automatic deduplication and opt-in reranking, in platform, self-hosted or local OSS mode. Maintained by Mem0; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries go to the configured Mem0 backend (api.mem0.ai in platform mode); at this pin the mem0ai library's anonymous PostHog usage telemetry stays on unless MEM0_TELEMETRY=false is set; `thor memory setup` can start Docker (pgvector) and Ollama containers for local mode.

name: memanto
description: Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, Thor memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $THOR_HOME/memanto.json.

name: meme-studio-mcp
description: Meme Studio through its MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://memes.mrhyde.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): finds the meme templates that fit a joke among more than a thousand, still and animated, with what goes in each caption slot, and makes the finished meme, an animated GIF for animated templates, plus a link to edit it in the browser. Works with the user's own photo too. Bundles one skill for the whole flow. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to memes.mrhyde.dev (closed-source server), which receives the searches, captions and any photo the agent sends (as base64, or an image_url the server downloads itself), says it does not store or log that content, keeps daily aggregate counts (requests, distinct people without identifying them, agent types, tools, options, templates chosen, errors) published weekly at memes.mrhyde.dev/en/stats plus minimal technical logs and temporary IP records for abuse blocks, and marks finished memes with an invisible pixel watermark; the skill may also call the same endpoint with curl from the terminal to save the image. Every tool is annotated read-only; the package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: memex8
description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.2.0 adds private-span redaction before capture, compact retrieval with ordered batch get, scoped chronological timeline, user-certified memory protection, and recoverable consolidation/dedup archives. v1.1.0 added optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, and in scheduled cron runs the job's reported output (up to 2000 chars), to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY; the agent can mark a memory "public" (or the user with `/memex8 remember --public`), which makes it shareable with peers through the separate Thor-A2A bridge.

name: memlock
description: Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same THOR_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

name: memobase
description: Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

name: memoria
description: Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Thor profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.

name: memory-bridge
description: Read-only, permission-aware search and reading over an operator-approved folder of Markdown notes, such as a team's shared agent memory. Two tools, memory_bridge_search and memory_bridge_read. Each calling profile's policy.json (in its plugin-data directory) sets the memory root and allow/deny patterns; the model can only ask questions and cannot widen access. Cron and delegated subagents are refused unless the policy opts in. Standalone tool plugin, not a memory provider. Disclosure — reads Markdown files under the operator-configured root, which is outside the plugin's own data, and returns snippets and file text into the model's context (sent to your model provider). On macOS it reads file ACLs through the system C library (ctypes). No network calls, shell commands, background processes, credentials, telemetry, writes or Python dependencies. Logs short refusal reason codes only. Imports the undocumented agent.delegation_context helper for subagent detection (rule 9 warning) and fails closed if it moves.

name: memory-ferry
description: Migrates built-in Thor MEMORY.md and USER.md records into a profile-local SQLite memory provider with an integrity-checked dry run, idempotent recovery, deterministic retrieval-parity evidence and migration-scoped rollback. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memories/MEMORY.md and memories/USER.md; writes plaintext memories and full mode-0600 plan/export artifacts under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/memory-ferry (policy-blocked records remain in planning artifacts but are not imported or recalled); recalled snippets reach the user's configured model provider. No network calls, shell commands, credentials, telemetry or background process.

name: memory-review
description: Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

name: memory-rewind
description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `thor memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

name: memory-shaper
description: Keyword-index memory for Thor: a small resident index of 'keyword,keyword -> file.md' routing lines stays in the system prompt while verbose topic files stay on disk and are read only when the conversation touches their keywords. Retrieval is done by the model reading a literal index — no embeddings, no vector store, no retrieval service. Disclosure — a pre_tool_call hook and a tool_execution middleware refuse a non-memory tool's write to the memory index across the recognised write vectors (write_file, patch, shell redirects, tee, sed -i; best-effort against arbitrary shell indirection) and refuse malformed index lines with a fix message rather than fixing them silently (including the keyword count: an entry outside the documented 5-20 keywords is refused, and the ASCII arrow is refused on every code path), while read-only commands and reads through a pipe always pass so the agent can audit the file it maintains; the same guard refuses any memory-tool remove, replace or patch whose old_text lands inside the index header, because on the stock store the whole preamble is a single §-joined entry and such an edit would rewrite or delete every header line at once; a documented escape hatch lets a scripted rewrite proceed when the sentinel file $THOR_HOME/state/.memory_shaper_rewrite_approved exists or MEMORY_SHAPER_ALLOW_REWRITE=1 is set. Beyond $THOR_HOME/memories/, the guard reads one thing: when a shell command invokes python3 on a script file, it opens that script (and the execute_code payload is already in args) to check whether the code would write the index; no file content is retained or sent anywhere. The repo also ships an optional core patch (scripts/patches/0001-flat-memory-separator.patch, changes tools/memory_tool_store.py) that the plugin does not need and never applies; a user who applies it by hand must re-apply it after every Thor update. No network calls, no subprocesses, nothing spawned in the background.

name: memory-shield
description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Thor' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Thor' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Thor' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Thor' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.

name: memory-zvec
description: Community Zvec memory backend for Thor Agent - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

name: memorybank
description: Memory Bank - unlimited local long-term memory for Thor as a knowledge graph; adding a new memory never fails for lack of room, relevance-gated recall, an index of past sessions and skills, a live network view and a usage meter. Disclosure — keeps excerpts of your conversations, MEMORY.md/USER.md and skill text in a local unencrypted SQLite bank under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first run indexes past session history from Thor' state.db (opened read-only); when the built-in memory tool refuses an add because MEMORY.md or USER.md is full, it stores the entry in the bank and reports the save as successful; `thor memorybank ui` runs a token-protected viewer on 127.0.0.1 and opens it in your browser.

name: memtomem
description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Thor, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.7.4) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session, with PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 so it loads no .env file. It reads the directories you ask it to index and watches its configured index roots while it runs. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine on its own; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks, and its fetch action downloads a URL on request. The server runs as your user and is not confined to ~/.memtomem: its context-gateway and path-taking actions (reached through mem_do, not called by the skills) can read and write other coding agents' files, including their instruction files, skills, hook settings and MCP configuration; see the README's "Files outside memtomem's own data".

name: memtomem-memory
description: Memory provider backed by memtomem: on eligible user turns (not greetings or slash commands) it asks memtomem for the notes most relevant to the message, through Thor's own connection to a memtomem MCP entry, and injects what returns within its time budget as context, without a model tool call. Optionally (mirror_writes, off by default) it also copies what Thor's built-in memory tool adds, replaces or removes in MEMORY.md / USER.md into memtomem. Needs Thor with MCP support, memory.provider: memtomem-memory, the grant plugins.entries.memtomem-memory.mcp_allowlist: [memtomem], and a memtomem MCP entry with trust: full running memtomem 0.6.8 or later (0.7.8 or later for mirroring): the memtomem catalog plugin, or your own mcp_servers.memtomem. Disclosure — each recall sends the turn's full message as the search query to whatever server that entry connects, local or remote; with mirroring on, each added, replaced or removed entry's text is sent too (a replace or remove also sends the full text of the entry it changed), and memtomem keeps the accepted ones in its database and renders them into a thor-mirror/<profile hash>/<target>.md note that every profile on the same store can recall (a removed entry keeps only its key; an entry matching a memtomem privacy pattern is refused). It shares that entry's connection, call queue and circuit breaker with the model's memtomem tools. It starts no server, reads no credentials and uses the standard library only.

name: mentionagent
