description: Run link building outreach through MentionAgent's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mentionagent.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): review the outreach drafts MentionAgent wrote, send the batch, answer publisher replies, close placements, and change campaigns in plain English, across every site in the user's account. Bundles the link-building-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to MentionAgent's hosted server (mentionagent.ai) and acts on the user's MentionAgent account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. approve_batch and send_reply send real email from the user's sending inbox, and trigger_run and draft_reply spend MentionAgent credits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: meridian
description: Finds and verifies the implicit state machines hiding in a codebase; enforces the accepted ones in CI. Meridian discovers status/state fields, anchors every state and transition to file:line (Python AST; TS/JS lexical, unguarded), flags unreachable and dead states, and gates on a human-reviewable .meridian.yaml spec (check exits 1 on violation, 2 when nothing is enforced). Every check event is appended to a SHA-256 hash-chained log for audit. No model calls, no network, no dependencies beyond stdlib. Disclosure - post_tool_call observes tools whose names contain write/edit/patch/replace/create/editor and re-runs the local analyzer only when a .meridian.yaml governs the repo (advisory; never blocks or approves); the ledger under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/meridian/ stores event names, machine ids, aggregate counts and repository/spec/report paths (never verdicts, never file:line anchors, never file contents); its chain is unkeyed SHA-256, so it detects edits but can be recomputed by anyone with write access; no telemetry; no background processes. Disclosure — post_tool_call observes tools whose names contain write/edit/patch/replace/create/editor and re-runs the local analyzer only when a .meridian.yaml governs the repo (advisory; never blocks or approves); meridian_spec accept and meridian_report out_file write only inside the agent's working directory (refused at /, $HOME or its parents, or the Thor home) and never through symlinks; the ledger under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/meridian/ stores event names, machine ids, aggregate counts and repository, spec, report and edited-file paths (never verdicts, never file:line anchors, never file contents) in an unkeyed SHA-256 chain that detects edits but can be recomputed by anyone with write access; no telemetry, no network, no background processes.

name: mermail
description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `thor mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in Thor.

name: mesh-check
description: Mesh Check reads one local STL, OBJ, PLY, GLB, or glTF file and returns whether it is closed, its volume, its bounds, and mesh, animation, and material counts. Use it before a 3D print or a game export. Disclosure — reads any local file path the agent passes (following symlinks) that ends in .stl, .obj, .ply, .glb or .gltf, up to 32 MiB including glTF buffer files in the same directory, and returns only measurements and mesh names; no network, file writes, rendering or repair; enabling it installs trimesh, pygltflib and numpy.

name: meshy
description: Meshy AI's own MCP server (pinned @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server@0.6.5) for text, image and multi-image to 3D, texturing, remeshing, rigging, animation, concept images and 3D-print prep, with a bundled meshy-3d workflow skill. In Thor Desktop: inline 3D cards with a download and convert menu, a gallery of recent generations and saved models (with a "Made from" history), image sets, and a credit chip in the status bar. Every credit-spending call goes through Thor's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a 200-credit limit per chat makes it ask again. Needs MESHY_API_KEY and Node.js 18+. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned server from npm through npx; it sends prompts and the images or models you or the agent name to Meshy's API (api.meshy.ai) under your key, gets only MESHY_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics (its User-Agent names Thor and its version). Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or the folder the agent names (never over an existing file); the Desktop backend fetches only from Meshy's asset hosts. The skill's helper scripts (model stats, preview render, optional Blender hand-off) run locally through the terminal tool.

name: metamask-wallet
description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for Thor — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

name: metronix
description: Metronix memory provider for Thor with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

name: mflow
description: Manage mFlow (m-flow.io) from Thor: boards and tasks, Knowledge Base/ADRs, and coding-agent delegation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with no Python and nothing runs locally — it points Thor at the hosted mFlow MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.m-flow.io/mcp) and ships a skill that teaches Thor how to use it (list_standalone_projects/tasks, create/update, create_comments, knowledge docs incl. ADRs, assign_to_coding_agent). Disclosure — network calls go to mcp.m-flow.io (mFlow's hosted MCP server); the plugin sends whatever board/task/KB data the user asks the agent to read or write, and coding-agent requests send the user's task text and, optionally, a public repo URL to mFlow's sandboxes. One auth path is OAuth (Google sign-in, access tokens last 90 days, re-auth every 90 days); the other is a future mFlow PAT via MFLOW_TOKEN (not yet shipped server-side — OAuth is the working path today). No telemetry, no shell commands, nothing stored or run on the host.

name: microbiz-desk
description: Customers, sales, debts and weekly reports for small businesses. Works offline, no API key needed.

name: microsoft365
description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

name: mindgraph
description: MindGraph typed knowledge-graph memory: bounded per-message recall, durable transcript/delegation capture and built-in memory mirroring, and the mindgraph-mcp general tool surface. Disclosure — tool calls, recall, capture and mirrored memory go to the MindGraph API (api.mindgraph.cloud, or MINDGRAPH_BASE_URL) under MINDGRAPH_API_KEY; automatic capture (default on; MINDGRAPH_AUTO_CAPTURE=off disables it) sends completed-turn user/assistant text and available participant ID/name/bot metadata, plus parent delegation task/result/child session ID, for extraction; other tool calls and outputs are not captured. Undelivered text and native memory operations rest in the profile directory (mindgraph/capture.db, mode 0600), are deleted on delivery, and transcript receipts are kept 30 days; background threads retry delivery. Native memory add/replace/remove changes are mirrored even with transcript capture off; replacements save new before forgetting old. Recall (MINDGRAPH_RECALL=off disables it) sends current-message content words and previous-message terms for subjectless follow-ups. Tool calls first send name, action and target node UIDs to the server governance check (MINDGRAPH_GOVERNANCE=off skips it). Automatic writes run only in the primary agent, except required compression checkpoints capture snapshots in any context. Ordinary turn/delegation capture requires plugins.isolation: in_process; isolated host mode reports that capture limitation while keeping recall, tools, native mirroring and required checkpoint snapshots. Queue overflow rejects new capture without evicting accepted evidence; v1 upgrades may replay previously delivered rows at the first required checkpoint. No telemetry, plugin-spawned separate processes or credentials stored outside Thor.

name: mindhall
description: One shared mind for every AI you use. Work, dates and a signed change log that Thor, ChatGPT, Claude and your other AIs all read and write. Disclosure — stores its data in ~/.mindhall/mindhall.db (outside the Thor home, shared by every profile unless MINDHALL_DB is set per profile) and injects a summary of it into every turn, telling the model Mindhall overrides its own memory; the optional, separately run mcp_server.py lets other AI apps read and write the same data and serves an edit page, protected only by a secret in the URL path, and the README suggests publishing it through a cloudflared tunnel, so anyone holding that URL can change what Thor is told each turn. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: minecraft-platform
description: Minecraft gateway adapter for Thor Agent. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the Thor agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

name: minicpm-ocr
description: Read images and PDFs with MiniCPM-OCR, score every region with MiniCPM-OCR Jev, and keep failed regions in a durable human review queue. Four tools: ocr_read, ocr_job, ocr_queue and ocr_verify. Works with the hosted ModelBest document-parse API or a local document service / OpenAI-compatible server. Disclosure — hosted mode sends the document and any scored region text to api.modelbest.ai; local mode uploads nothing. Reads only the path or public https URL passed to a tool, and stores review-queue state and CSV exports under Thor' plugin data directory. No telemetry, analytics, self-updater, shell commands or background processes. The optional MODELBEST_API_KEY is read through agent.secret_scope.get_secret; the plugin never reads .env, auth.json or another tool's credential store.

name: minimalist-themes
description: Eighteen warm, readable palettes for Thor Desktop, assigned natively per profile, with one embedded type system (Figtree + Geist Mono), matching terminal colors and a CLI banner painted per palette. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and its stylesheet adjusts a few Desktop surfaces (profile-rail glyph contrast, Capabilities metadata, the MCP JSON editor and the Manage Profiles overlay) only while a Minimalist theme is active. It also ships optional CLI/TUI skins as plain YAML files the user copies; the Desktop side never reads them. Fonts are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks, no background processes. The package also ships an inert Agent entrypoint whose register() does nothing, so Thor Agent imports it cleanly instead of reporting a missing module.

name: minimax-image
description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

name: minimax-search
description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

name: minimax-video
description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

name: mission-control
description: Live mission-control dashboard for Thor Desktop — tool waterfall, parallel subagent cards, token and estimated-cost meters with a prompt-cache badge, plus budget and possible-loop alerts, streamed in real time. Read-only; nothing leaves the machine.

name: mistral-vibe
description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models and mistral-large-4 (low/medium/high). Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "thor auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Thor credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

name: mixar
description: Mixar's own desktop MCP server over stdio, with a Mixar workflow skill: build and edit 3D scenes, generate models, textures, rigs and animation with AI, render, and export game-ready assets for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as Thor. Disclosure — runs the launcher the installed Mixar app writes at ~/.mixar/connector/mixar-mcp (%USERPROFILE%\.mixar\connector\mixar-mcp.cmd on Windows), which reads Mixar's own files under ~/.mixar/; tools execute arbitrary Python inside Mixar with your privileges; a tool call can start the installed Mixar app, which stays open after Thor exits; calls go over loopback to Mixar, which forwards them to api.mixar.app under the signed-in account; generation prompts and reference images go to the AI provider running the chosen model; Mixar's backend keeps diagnostic records of MCP tool calls (inputs and results) and deletes them within 30 days; AI generation and create_layered_material spend Mixar credits, declared to Thor as cost ranges with a 500-credit spend limit per chat; the plugin stores no credentials, ships no binaries, sends no telemetry and never updates itself; the optional MIXAR_MCP_LAUNCHER variable makes it run the program it names; at install Thor looks for Mixar (macOS: Mixar.app in /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows: the installed-apps entry or %ProgramFiles%\Mixar; Linux: a mixar command on PATH or Mixar's launcher) and refuses the install when it is missing or, on macOS and Windows, older than 4.2.1.

name: mnemos
description: A memory of the agent's own. It keeps what it decides to keep, in its own words, wakes with it at the start of every session, and with each message the few memories that bear on it come back to it; nothing is written from a conversation on its own. Memories fade unless used, and before one is gone the agent is asked what it taught. What you ask it to always remember never fades. Thor's MEMORY.md and USER.md stay on, and what the agent writes there is kept too. Each profile is its own agent with its own memory, one SQLite file on this machine that stays when the plugin is removed. No key or account needed. Disclosure — no network and no telemetry unless you choose it: deep_maintenance with a provider chosen for Mnemos (MNEMOS_LLM_PROVIDER, openrouter or openai) sends memory text to that provider during upkeep, and MNEMOS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=gemini sends the words of memories and questions to Google; keys are read only through agent.secret_scope, never from a file; the memory lives outside THOR_HOME, in ~/.mnemos/thor.db or ~/.mnemos/thor-<profile>.db, with settings in $THOR_HOME/mnemos.json, and Mnemos reads ~/.mnemos/config.json and Thor's config.yaml; what the agent marks shared goes to ~/.mnemos/shared-memory.db, readable by every Mnemos agent on the machine; upkeep, when due, runs in a short-lived child Python process that exits when done, and nothing is scheduled; mnemos_page serves a page on 127.0.0.1 (a port the system picks, a fresh path, this machine only) until Thor stops; it also shows the other agents whose memory Mnemos keeps in ~/.mnemos, and there the person can correct or let go of a memory, or leave a note, for any of them; the system prompt carries Mnemos's rules for keeping a memory and the agent's wake; on first start it raises the process's open-file limit to 4096 if lower.

name: mnemostack
description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (thor-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the Thor venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

name: mnemosyne
description: Local-first memory layer for Thor Agent — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

name: mnemosyne-dashboard
description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

name: mnemoverse
description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Thor runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by Thor, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

name: mock-review
description: Review boards for UI mockups and plans. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Plan boards add question cards and one footer button, Build, which stays locked until nothing is open and then wakes the agent with the approved plan; mocks carry working controls by default (`interactive_elements`). A design profile bound to a project is enforced: a round with off-profile colours or fonts is refused unless `--off-brand` gives a reason. Five mock_review tools, the `thor mockreview` CLI and slash command, a bundled usage skill, and a stdio MCP server (`bin/mockreview mcp`) that serves the same five tools to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode without Thor; that server starts only when you add it to such a client, and its boards do not wake an agent unless you pass `--wake`. Boards are served from your computer (loopback by default, or your tailnet) or published on here.now, behind a random per-review password by default (`herenow_password` setting, `--no-password` per review, `thor mockreview password <id> on|off` on a live board). Plain http(s) links in mocks stay clickable and open in a new tab; every other link scheme is stripped. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `thor mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes every review to your network with no login. Outbound calls: a signed POST to the local Thor webhook (localhost:8644, or the receiver you name in MOCKREVIEW_WEBHOOK_URL for the MCP server) on Send or Build, and, only for reviews hosted on here.now, https://here.now/api/v1 with your HERENOW_API_KEY (publish, Site Data reads, a metadata PATCH that sets or removes the board password, delete on close). Secrets are read through Thor's secret scope, or from the process environment when the stdio MCP server runs without Thor; no credential file is read. Runs `bash publish.sh` from the official here-now skill (key in the child environment), and for a password-protected here.now prototype launches your installed Chrome, Chromium or Edge headless (throwaway profile, credential-named variables removed from its environment, `--no-sandbox` only when run as root) to load the board behind its password before the link is shared; runs `git -C <project> rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` (read only) to match a project to its bound design profile; runs `tailscale status --json` and `tailscale serve status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes) for tailnet hosting, and from `setup` the thor subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. The opt-in `wake_toolsets` setting lets the session woken by Send use the toolsets you list (for example terminal and file), so board feedback reaches those tools; setup refuses it while any waking board is ungated and only prints the `toolsets` line for you to add to the wake route by hand (re-add it after every setup run). Reviews are stored under $THOR_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies.

name: modal
description: Modal Endpoints for OpenAI-compatible APIs

name: model-drift-watch
description: Catches silent quality drift in your model: 34 questions graded exactly against its baseline. Messages only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model, or a failed measurement. Disclosure — calls your model via ctx.llm on your bill (cap 120,000 tokens and $0.50); model_drift can start one; may fetch OpenRouter or models.dev prices; 10 code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child, not a sandbox, in unattended cron; job and script stay after removal until unschedule; no extra agent turn; questions still count on the cap; history stays in plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry; gateway users can run it at your cost; thor tools turns it off per surface; disable stops /model-drift-watch.

name: model-explainer
description: A Models page for Thor Desktop, plus a button beside the chat model pill that opens it as a pop-up, built around your own model picker: choose a model to see its Thor Index score, cost per task, context and output limits, price, abilities and your own measured speed and spend, with a score-against-cost frontier chart, and compare up to four side by side. Every value cites a source and date. Disclosure — one GET of a public JSON data file from the author's GitHub repo (raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/thor-model-explainer, main branch, so its contents can change after this pin), at most daily and only when the page or pop-up opens (can be turned off; the bundled copy works offline; the file is validated data, never code); reads model.options and the focused session's model and usage figures; writes plugin storage, and switches the chat model only when the user presses Use this model (the same config.set request as the built-in picker, scoped to the open chat). Desktop only: no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: model-fallback-heuristic
description: Multi-provider heuristic model fallback and automatic failover routing across all configured providers (parameter count, context window, release recency, flash tier, tool support, provider preference, and reasoning effort) — works seamlessly with or without an LLM call. Disclosure — session-start and API-error hooks rewrite fallback_providers and plugin settings in ~/.thor/config.yaml (primary model replacement is opt-in via auto_switch_primary_when_unavailable); queries public model catalog endpoints (models.dev/api.json, openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, and inference-api.thor-agent.local/v1/portal/models) to rank candidate models and check free-tier availability; optional interactive CLI setup saves user-entered provider API keys via thor_cli.config.save_env_value when explicitly requested.

name: model-forge
description: Local models for every modality — chat, vision, OCR, image generation and editing, video, 3D meshes, music, SFX and voice. Model Forge finds your hardware (local probes; remote compute targets use the budgets you declare), shows which models fit, maps each model to the right inference engine (llama.cpp, Strata, Ollama, vLLM, ComfyUI, a user-configured OpenAI-compatible media gateway and more), pulls the model, and wires it into Thor as a provider — so chat, image_generate, video_generate, vision and TTS run on hardware you control with no account and no API key. Six tools: model_forge_status (targets, VRAM/RAM, engines, loaded models), model_forge_browse (per-modality model catalog with hardware-fit verdicts), model_forge_target_add (register compute targets), model_forge_install (pull models through engine-native paths), model_forge_activate (wire a running chat model into Thor), model_forge_generate_media (3D, music and SFX jobs through a user-configured OpenAI-compatible media gateway). Disclosure — model pulls download weights from huggingface.co or modelscope.cn on user request, and model_forge_browse queries the public huggingface.co model API for fresh listings unless fresh=false (optional HF_TOKEN / MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN pull credentials live in plugin settings, are read only through Thor' secret route and are sent only to their own host family); shell commands are limited to read-only hardware probes (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi); hardware probes read local system state (GPU queries, sysfs, the Windows memory API) while remote compute targets use user-declared budgets; adding a compute target and model_forge_activate with apply=true (which rewrites model.default, model.provider and base_url in config.yaml) each ask for Thor approval first; media jobs and Maya pulls POST prompts and image bytes to user-configured endpoints; the bundled TTS helper POSTs text and base64 voice-clone reference audio to a user-configured /v1/audio/speech endpoint; the only background process is a download daemon thread; no telemetry.

name: model-forge-desktop
description: Model Forge cockpit pane for Thor Desktop — compute targets, live engines, loaded models and hardware at a glance. Companion UI for the Model Forge plugin. Disclosure — the pane polls each compute target you register in Model Forge (plus http://127.0.0.1:8080 by default) with read-only GET requests to /v1/models, /api/tags and /system_stats to show which local engines are running; no generation calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: model-forge-image
description: Model Forge local image-generation backend — routes Thor image_generate to any OpenAI-compatible images API (media gateway, vLLM-Omni, SGLang Diffusion, ComfyUI). Companion package for the Model Forge plugin. Disclosure — sends prompts, and any local PNG/JPEG/WebP image file named as an edit or reference input, to the image endpoint the user configures; no third-party network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: model-forge-providers
description: Local engine model-provider profiles for Model Forge (Strata, Project Maya) — run Thor chat on local MoE engines and make their models selectable in /model. Companion package for the Model Forge plugin. Disclosure — sends prompts and requests to user-configured endpoints; no third-party network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: model-forge-video
description: Model Forge local video-generation backend — routes Thor video_generate to any OpenAI-compatible video job API (media gateway, engines with /v1/videos). Companion package for the Model Forge plugin. Disclosure — submits video jobs to user-configured endpoints; no third-party network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: model-kombat
description: Head-to-head model evaluation: scout a task or kanban card into lanes, build a deterministic fight card (Warm-up 1pt, Main Event 2pt, Championship 3pt, sudden death) at standard, hard or gauntlet intensity, fight two models on identical prompts, and score mechanically — executed code, exact counts, numeric tolerances, phrase groups, JSON leaf equality, SQLite rows — with a per-lane Elo ladder, live arcade pane, kanban badges, and a measured best-value call when strong models tie ('equal quality — X is 18x cheaper'); a local task_stats.json remembers which tasks split the two models and demotes saturated ones. Disclosure — model calls: all fights go through Thor' own LLM facade with a per-call model override you must enable (`plugins.entries.model-kombat.llm.allow_model_override`); pure fights make two model calls per task, capped by `max_fight_cost_usd` / `max_fight_tokens` and `max_fight_seconds`, which tool arguments can lower but never raise; agentic fights create kanban tasks assigned to your active profile with a per-task model override, which start worker agent sessions with that profile's tools and are not spend-capped; code execution: off by default and switchable only in plugin settings, and when enabled, model-written Python runs as your user in a resource-limited subprocess that is not a security sandbox; local files: reads optional project tasks from `.kombat/tasks.json` in the working directory and writes reports, history, ladder, exports and stats only under its plugin data dir; kanban: posts display cards on a dedicated `model-kombat` board and auto-closes its own stale cards there; no third-party network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads.

name: model-leaderboard
description: Model leaderboard for Thor Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen Thor profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed Thor profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; keeps its state in <thor home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; no API keys of its own, no writes outside its data directory.

name: model-picker
description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $THOR_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

name: model-presets
description: Named model, provider and reasoning presets for gateway /model commands. Uses only the pre_gateway_dispatch hook; no network calls, credential access, shell commands, background processes or self-updating.

name: model-router
description: Execution visibility distinguishes requested from runtime-reported Heavy/Light/native-profile identity. Separately opt-in Gateway-owned profile_task jobs use an existing owner and the target tool-surface account/tools/memory/fallback policy, not a private executor or automatic parent wake. Full-profile grants remain OFF/empty until explicit host-operator CLI review/save; installation, ordinary allowlists and plugin activation grant none. Generic RPC cannot configure these grants or relay approval/denial/clarification, including forged human/operator fields; decisions stay in the exact native target conversation. Operator commands write only the origin plugins.entries.model-router.settings.profile_jobs record through the native settings writer with snapshot/CAS/readback; current raw/effective disagreement refuses. Target work and configured external memory capture/synchronization may transmit task material and use account quota even without a memory-tool call. Job journals store bounded pending/private visible-result prose and identifiers; unknown submissions are not automatically replayed and unresolved workspace claims remain held. Dependencies are PyYAML>=6,<7 and websockets>=15,<17 under native core constraints. Native introductions automatically supply bounded role hints for allowed profiles; existing delegation overrides remain unchanged. Optional AI role drafts first preview the exact bounded introduction, explicit SOUL Role section and enabled local skill identifiers, then require explicit Generate under the connected owner's saved main model and existing native recovery/fallback policy. Review and local draft acceptance are separate from normal settings Save. No target profile conversation/account use, global-introduction rewrite, history/private-memory source, skill-body or external-directory traversal. No automatic generation or plugin retry. Credential values remain host-owned; final account/billing identity and single network attempt are not guaranteed. Profile model settings and native purpose-bound Heavy/Light or allowlisted profile delegation. Explicit first-use preparation defaults only raw-unset backends to model-or-profile choice; installation, enablement, refresh and registration do not select a backend or grant profile/cost access. Existing modes, OFF/null selections, models, budgets and permissions are preserved. Each delegate_task task selects either origin-profile Heavy/Light models or an explicitly permitted profile using that target's own model/reasoning; these routes are not combined. The Desktop UI provides per-profile readiness, guided manual preparation when admission is unavailable, and a target-profile allowlist with account/tool-use consent. v0.9.0 currently requires normal native CLI installation for missing profiles; catalog merge does not activate its older automatic-preparation guard. Explicit settings saves change only the previewed profiles through the native config API/CLI; native package preparation is separate and bounded to 32 selected local profiles, requires dependency/activation consent, and never installs on refresh or into future profiles. Native subagents use the user's configured providers, tools and approval policy and may consume API or subscription quota. Ordinary and spare model continuation have separate backend-bound cost approval; other-profile access is never automatic. Background processes, wake/stop, ownership, tool ceilings and session records are managed by Thor, not a private worker supervisor or credential store. The coding_route tool is read/config/join only for new work; old private worker starts are retired. Routing guidance defaults ON after trust/activation when its own saved choice is absent, but that is separate from backend selection and never launches work at installation. Existing routing OFF and skill opt-outs remain OFF. Configured zero timeouts can remove wall-clock caps. Fast inheritance on covered first-party routes can raise cost. No telemetry, self-updater, core monkeypatch or approval bypass. Disclosure — after you trust and enable the plugin, routing defaults ON for every installed profile without a saved choice, including profiles that installed an earlier version and never saved one (the update turns it on); existing saved OFF and explicit skill opt-outs remain OFF. Once a profile's `delegation.backend` is set to `model-router`, `model-router-profiles` or `model-router-auto`, native `delegate_task` subagents are routed to that profile's Heavy/Light models or, for profiles you allowlist with explicit consent, run as another local profile with that profile's own model, credentials and tools. The model chooses the route and can set a task's total time limit to none, and continuation fallback chains you approve can add cost. The `coding_route` tool now only reads settings and inspects or joins earlier jobs, whose prompts and results stay in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation (including `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*`), auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first). The Desktop "prepare profiles" and first-use preparation actions, after you select profiles and confirm, install and enable this same catalog pin in up to 32 other local profiles through Thor's plugin manager and set an unset `delegation.backend` to `model-router-auto` there, where routing then defaults ON. The optional AI role draft, only after you press Generate, sends the target profile's `profile.yaml` description, up to 1536 characters of its SOUL.md "Role" section and up to 32 enabled skill names to the current profile's main model provider. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs. With the separate opt-in profile jobs grant, which only the host `thor` CLI can save, the `profile_task` tool runs a task as another local profile through that profile's already-running Gateway with that profile's own model, credentials, memory and tools; task prompts and results are kept in the plugin's job journal.

name: model-usage
description: Minimal triple-ring status-bar gauges for Claude and Codex — outer thin ring = context of the current chat, middle = 5-hour session, inner = weekly window, colored by remaining share — with a click-through detail popover and one-shot 30%/10% limit alerts (in-app toast + OS notification while Thor is unfocused). Duplicate pool rows of the same login are merged. EN/KO/JA. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (reads the gateway's model.options usage cache and the focused chat's usage stats), never reads or stores credentials, no subprocesses, no telemetry; stores only the list of alerts already shown in plugin storage.

name: model-usage-status
description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the Thor Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through Thor core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

name: modelscout
description: Per-task model choice from the models you actually have, so light work stops spending frontier-model tokens and subscription usage limits last longer. A pre_llm_call hook shows a short card for each new task (tier, best-fit model from your keys, subscriptions and live models.dev pricing, and why), then routes the work to a right-sized delegate_task child, up or down tier, asks, or stays, per your defaults. Bundles the modelscout skill and a /modelscout command for settings and a measured savings report. Disclosure — reads and writes ~/.claude/modelscout-profile.json (settings shared with ModelScout on other agents), appends routed-child outcomes (tier, model, status; no goal text) to ~/.claude/modelscout-outcomes.jsonl, and reads the model inventory and catalog JSON beside it plus Thor's own models_dev_cache.json; it opens Thor state.db read-only to look up a routed child's model and for the savings report, which also reads Claude Code transcripts read-only. A pre_llm_call hook adds routing instructions to each new task's prompt and can steer work into delegated subagents. In Thor the plugin code makes no network calls and reads no credentials. On Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build (not Thor), hooks/session_start.py runs scripts/catalog.py in a detached process to fetch the public models.dev catalog weekly, sending no keys or user data (`modelscout: catalog off` disables it). The bundled skill's optional discover-models.sh, run through the terminal tool, reads provider API-key env vars (and only checks whether Azure, Bedrock or Vertex credentials are present, without reading or using them), sends each only to its own provider's list-models endpoint and fetches the public models.dev catalog. Typing `modelscout: grok setup` (in any host, Thor included) writes Grok Build's rules file ~/.grok/rules/modelscout.md (or under GROK_HOME) and reads ~/.grok/config.toml for custom model names; later ModelScout settings commands rewrite that file only if ModelScout wrote it, and `modelscout: grok remove` deletes it. No telemetry or self-updating, and no background processes in Thor.

name: modernisation-engine
description: Controlled migration engine: maps an existing codebase, turns the behaviour that must survive into reviewable contracts, prepares a separate candidate and records old/new evidence before any production change. Disclosure — 27 tools plus a `thor modernise` CLI and `/modernise` slash command; `assess`, `plan`, `record` and `recipe` read source trees and files at absolute paths the agent supplies (refusing symlinks, `.env`, `auth.json`, `credentials.json` and SSH keys) and never import or run repository code; `recipe` creates a new directory at an agent-chosen absolute path holding a copy of the source with fixed metadata edits; job records live under the plugin's data directory; only after you set `operator_config` and sign a one-use Ed25519 owner grant do `run`, `cancel` and `recover` invoke the local `docker` CLI, outside Thor's command-approval prompt, to run, inspect and remove rootless, network-disabled, read-only, resource-limited containers from digest-pinned images you allow-list (never pulled); no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater.

name: modular
description: Modular Cloud model provider: open models (MiniMax, DeepSeek, Gemma) on an OpenAI-compatible API, with per-model reasoning controls.

name: moment
description: Keeps a Thor agent honest about its own memory. Thor injects SOUL.md, memories/MEMORY.md and memories/USER.md into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start; anything that changes those files while the session lives stays invisible to it, and the agent keeps answering from stale memory. Moment fingerprints the three house files at a session's first turn and re-checks them on every later turn (pre_llm_call); when one changed, it injects a short drift receipt — which file, its absolute path, baseline and detection timestamps, the changed lines, and the full current content for small files — so the agent answers from the present and says plainly that its memory drifted. It also provides a moment_check tool for on-demand freshness reports against the session's starting state. Disclosure — reads only the active profile's SOUL.md, memories/MEMORY.md and memories/USER.md (the agent's own house files; never credential stores); writes only its own baseline and receipt-journal state in its plugin data directory (plugin-data/moment); the hook only adds context and never blocks or modifies a turn; no network, no shell, no subprocess, no telemetry; Python standard library only, zero dependencies.

name: momentic
description: Write, run and repair Momentic end-to-end tests for web (Chrome) and iOS/Android (simulators and emulators), and run Mo bug bashes that file each bug with a Momentic regression test. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/), no plugin code. The skills drive the Momentic CLI and its local MCP servers (npx momentic mcp, npx momentic-mobile mcp), which users add to their own mcp_servers config; a Momentic API key is read by the Momentic CLI, never by the plugin. Disclosure — the skills tell the agent to run Momentic CLI commands in the shell (unpinned npx, and the documented curl https://cli.momentic.ai/qa | sh installer for Mo); test runs and Mo sessions call Momentic's hosted service with the user's Momentic account (Mo sessions are billed by effort), Mo can be given a reviewed git patch or source snapshot uploaded to Momentic's sandbox, and `qa tunnel` exposes local or private targets to that hosted service.

name: money-magnet
description: Finance tracker and money magnet for Thor Agent: record income and expenses, set a monthly budget and watch it fill, value a crypto portfolio against live prices, and scan for price gaps between exchanges. Transactions and budget live in local JSON under $THOR_HOME/money-magnet/. Disclosure: the portfolio and arbitrage tools query the public CoinGecko and Binance price APIs (no account or API key; only coin symbols are sent). The tracker tools work fully offline.

name: money-rules
description: Money rules for Thor: pay, split, sweep and alert on USDC from your own Solana wallet, under rules you set in chat. You sign one capped USDC allowance (SPL approve) to a local helper key; USDC stays in your wallet until a rule pays, and every new rule waits for /money approve. Every payment started from chat goes through the Thor approval prompt, and the relay fee is capped on the client (max_fee_usd, default 0.05). Rules fire on a schedule, when USDC comes in, or when a balance crosses a line. Gasless: a relay pays the Solana fee for a small USDC fee in the same transaction and only co-signs connect, revoke and pay. Disclosure — Crypto: moves USDC from your own Solana wallet through a local helper keypair (stored in plain JSON, mode 600, under the profile's plugin-data/money-rules) that you allow, with one SPL approve you sign on thor-money-rules.vercel.app, to spend up to a cap you choose; every payment the agent starts asks in the Thor approval prompt, and new rules and held payments wait for your /money approve, but approved rules (scheduled pay, incoming splits, sweeps of everything over a kept amount) then run unattended from a background thread that polls every 30 seconds while Thor runs, up to a local daily limit (default $100/day, relay fees included); every payment is co-signed by the author's relay at thor-money-rules.vercel.app, which takes a USDC fee in the same transaction, capped by your max_fee_usd setting (default $0.05, plus up to $0.60 for each recipient that has no USDC account yet); wallet reads go through that relay's RPC proxy unless you set rpc_url; /money revoke zeroes the allowance on-chain; no telemetry.

name: monid
description: Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a Thor approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

name: mood
description: A tiny evolving mood for Thor, built for slow local models. Tracks mood, rapport and three slow-moving traits (warmth, playfulness, directness) that change with keyword rules on what the user writes and drift back to neutral over hours, then appends one ~30-token line to each user message through pre_llm_call, so the system prompt and its cache are never touched. Adds a /mood command (show, reset, on, off). Disclosure — makes no model calls, no network I/O, runs no shell commands and holds no credentials; reads the text of each user message and reads/writes only its own plugin-data state file (state.json, per profile).

name: mood-engine
description: Dynamic 4-axis mood engine (energy, warmth, patience, focus) with async post-turn evaluation, passive decay, and zero-token neutral baseline. Disclosure — in auto/llm mode each user turn runs one background ctx.llm.complete_structured() call on your active provider (or configured auxiliary.mood_eval model); set evaluator_mode to heuristic for zero extra tokens; stores mood state locally in profile-scoped ctx.state.

name: morning-briefing
description: Personal daily newspaper for Thor: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

name: morph
description: One adaptive workspace across the applications you use, with human-approved, verified actions: an approval gate between the agent and the APIs it can write to. Connect a GitHub repository (`thor morph connect github owner/name`) or any service that publishes an OpenAPI document, and MORPH learns from the schema what can be read and what can be safely changed. The agent gets tools to read and to propose; it has no tool that approves and is never given the token an approval needs. A human approves each change in the dashboard, seeing the exact before and after; MORPH writes it, then re-reads the record from the API and reports it verified only if it matches what was promised. Only operations with a checkable effect are offered — for GitHub issues: close, close as not planned, reopen, set labels, set title, assign, unassign. The dashboard has five views (Workspace, Connections, Approvals, Activity, Context) and composes tables, boards and charts over the connected data from a goal stated in plain language. Every proposal, approval and result is kept in a hash-chained audit log. Disclosure — MORPH makes outbound HTTPS calls to the services the operator connects, including api.github.com when a repository is connected (loopback only with an explicit opt-in; private, link-local, reserved and cloud-metadata targets are refused, redirects are never followed, and the address actually dialled is validated at connect time); it stores its connection list, workspaces, pending proposals, read cursors and the audit log in its own plugin-data directory; it reads bearer tokens through agent.secret_scope by environment-variable name and never logs, stores or returns them; it calls the host model through ctx.llm for interface planning with a deterministic offline fallback, and sends the model schema only, never a record value. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating code. Ships three workflow skills and an optional offline sandbox of three loopback services (`thor morph connect sandbox`, started only by `thor morph up`) so the whole loop can be tried with no account and no key.

name: morphllm
description: Morph's OpenAI-compatible API for open models (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek)

name: motion-index
description: Browse 49 motion-graphics styles as live previews in a Thor Desktop pane, and let the agent find a style, turn it into a ready-to-build brief for your topic (length and 9:16/16:9 filled in), or suggest a new style to the Motion Index library. Disclosure — the motion_suggest tool posts a style title, link and an optional note (up to 1000 characters) to https://motion.minutechbuilds.com/api/submit when the agent calls it; the tool asks the model to confirm with the user first but Thor does not enforce that; the Desktop pane loads preview videos and poster images from https://motion.minutechbuilds.com/demos/; search, styles and briefs come from the bundled data/catalog.json. No file writes, shell, credentials, telemetry or background work.

name: motion-studio
description: Creation-first media studio for Thor Desktop. Quick Create turns a chat request into sound effects, images, voice or video takes you can play, compare, keep and download; Production collects chosen takes and imported files into a project and exports them. Image, voice and video come from Thor' own image_gen, tts and video_gen tools; sound effects generation is unavailable outside the author's pinned Stable Audio setup; imported sound effects remain supported for review and export. Disclosure — downloads finished media only from the provider URLs Thor' image_gen/tts/video_gen tools return (x.ai, openai.com, oaiusercontent.com, fal.media, fal.run, deepinfra.com, krea.ai; no proxies, cookies or credentials, same-host redirects only); runs ffmpeg/ffprobe to check imported and generated media, nvidia-smi to report GPU use, and the author's pinned local audio engine, each with a minimal fixed environment (no inherited credentials or provider keys); reads Thor' generator output cache read-only (secret and hidden files refused), checks only whether provider API keys are set through Thor' scoped secret API, and reads installed Thor provider source files to list available methods; stores projects and takes under the profile's plugin data directory; saved takes are kept, not deleted. No telemetry.

name: mqtt
description: MQTT as a Thor platform: one authenticated broker connection, per-topic routing (deliver, agent, job, drop) and JSON replies published outside the consumed namespace; ships its own standard-library MQTT 3.1.1/5.0 client over TCP or TLS (verified by default, optional private CA/mTLS) with keepalive, reconnect and opt-in burst coalescing, and drops unmatched topics. Disclosure — holds one outbound broker connection and its reconnect loop, reads the MQTT username/password through Thor's scoped secret route and optional TLS files at operator-provided paths, and enables trusted_inbound (the broker's authentication is the trust boundary): any publisher the broker's ACL admits can start agent turns, and on topics you map to deliver or job it can post text to the chat you name on another connected platform or run the cron job you name, while payload text can never issue gateway commands; job and cross-platform delivery go through Thor internals (tools.cronjob_tools, the gateway runner), so a Thor update can disable them; no telemetry, no shell, no writes.

name: mrscraper
description: MrScraper GET page retrieval, unified Web Search, and account usage via direct HTTP APIs. Disclosure — page and search requests can consume paid account tokens; target URLs, search queries, and request options are sent to MrScraper.

name: ms-decision-provider
description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Thor's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

name: mtg-deck-studio
description: A Magic: The Gathering Commander deck table beside the chat. The AI reads the deck before it speaks, searches Scryfall inside the colour identity, explains the card-to-card synergy graph from Oracle text with the clauses behind every pair, writes a strategy guide from computed evidence, keeps a sideboard of candidates it can promote or swap in, and runs 49 table operations the player can also do by hand. Seven agent tools plus a bundled skill and a Desktop pane with a sandboxed viewer. Disclosure — card data and images come from the public Scryfall API and cards.scryfall.io (no key, no account, card names and filters only); the plugin reads only the deck/CSV file or folder that the player or the agent names at import (network shares and device paths are refused) and writes only inside its profile-scoped data directory (decks, sideboards, exports, the name-index cache, scan photos), which is never uploaded; two bundled MIT Python helpers run as subprocesses with the host interpreter (strategy evidence pack, Moxfield text export — no shell, no network of their own); the webcam opens only when the player presses Scan. No telemetry, no update checker, no stored credentials.

name: mulligan
description: Counterfactual replay for Thor: record a run, rewind to any step, edit one tool decision, replay forward in a fresh child session, and diff the branch against the original. Replay-to-point reproduces the recorded steps with zero provider calls and zero tool side effects; the branch runs live with normal approvals. Uses llm_execution, tool_execution and tool_request middleware, pre/post_tool_call hooks and ctx.subagent_lifecycle.launch; stdlib only, no dependencies. Stores append-only JSONL traces (prompts, tool arguments and tool results) under $THOR_HOME/replay-traces/. Disclosure — while enabled it records every session automatically (full model responses, tool arguments and tool results, and the last user message) as append-only JSONL under $THOR_HOME/replay-traces/, which are sensitive, not rotated and persist until you delete them; mg_play launches a child session whose live tail spends provider tokens and runs tools with normal approvals; no network calls, no credential access, no shell execution, no self-update, and no approvals are bypassed or auto-answered.

name: multi-telegram
description: Run an arbitrary number of Telegram bot identities through one Thor profile and agent. Each bot has its own token reference, display identity, allowlists, role prompt, welcome message and session policy; replies always leave through the bot that received the triggering message. Optional shared-session groups continue one stored Thor transcript for the same external chat/user/topic. Disclosure - long polling to the Telegram Bot API uses one bot token per bot, read from the active profile's secret scope via a per-bot token_env; no telemetry, subprocess, self-update or core overrides; authorized inbound attachments are cached through Thor; non-secret status and proactive routes are stored under THOR_HOME/plugin-data. Transcript isolation is not memory isolation: MEMORY.md, USER.md, session_search and tools are profile-wide; use separate profiles or restrict toolsets for hard isolation. Webhooks, inline clarify/approval keyboards and out-of-process cron delivery are not implemented. Disclosure — runs one Telegram Bot API long-poll connection per configured bot, using a per-bot token read from the active profile's secret scope by its `token_env` name (optional operator-set proxy / custom Bot API base URL); inbound messages from allowlisted senders (deny-all by default; `allow_all_users` makes a bot public) reach this profile's one agent, whose memory, USER.md, session_search and tools are shared by every bot unless per-bot `toolsets` restrict them; attachments are cached through Thor and status/route files are kept under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/multi-telegram; may lazily install Thor's own `telegram` extra through Thor's package manager; adds a token-redacting filter to the process's root log handlers.

name: multiverse
description: Best-of-N for coding agents, with real checks. multiverse_race makes one git worktree per attempt (2 to 6) from the same base (HEAD, or the uncommitted working tree through git stash create), starts one delegate_task subagent per worktree with its own approach, pins each subagent to its worktree (pre_tool_call rewrites terminal workdir, file paths and V4A patch paths, and blocks access to the other worktrees and nested delegation), runs the same check commands in every worktree, ranks them by checks passed and then by the smallest real diff, and multiverse_adopt applies the winner with git apply. With delegation.backend: multiverse, each attempt can use its own model and provider. Thor Desktop: a live race board pane (each attempt's status and tool-call count, then checks passed, diff and the winner), a status-bar chip while racing, and a toast when judging ends. Disclosure — no network calls of its own, no credentials, no telemetry, no background threads. Runs git (rev-parse, stash create, worktree add/remove/prune, add -A inside the worktrees, diff, apply), mkdir, rm -f of its own .patch files and rmdir, plus your check commands, through the Thor terminal tool, so approvals and the configured terminal backend apply. Creates worktrees next to the repository in .<repo>.multiverse/<run id>/. Starts subagents through delegate_task, which uses your configured model(s) and costs tokens per attempt. Stores run metadata (goal, checks, worktree paths, scores, the last 1500 characters of each subagent summary) in its plugin state under THOR_HOME/plugin-data. Sends plugin.multiverse.run snapshots (goal, checks, per-attempt label, model, approach, status, tool-call count, scores and diff stats; no subagent text) to Desktop windows attached to the same Thor process, at most once a second while attempts run; the desktop half keeps the last 10 runs in Desktop plugin storage.

name: munin
description: Munin meeting notes for Thor Agent: ask what was decided in your last meeting, get a follow-up with every action item checked against the transcript and cited by meeting id, line id and clock time, and search who said what across meetings, through the hosted Munin MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and DCR) with two workflow skills bundled (munin-followup, munin-recall). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at app.muninlabs.ai; meeting notes, transcript lines, titles and people's names from the user's Munin account are pulled into the session context. On Munin's consent page the user picks a read-only or an editable connection; an editable one lists the server's two write tools (set_speaker renames a speaker in one meeting, import_meeting saves a meeting from another app). The package declares the server untrusted so Thor asks before any write-capable call, but the `thor mcp add munin --url https://app.muninlabs.ai/mcp --auth oauth` config entry that OAuth requires replaces that setting unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it (the README shows how); then `thor mcp login munin`, since the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. No local code, no hooks, no env vars, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: munito-provider
description: Munito AI model providers: open models (GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, Kolibri 1) on a global host and an EU-only host, with the context window, image input and price of each model bundled. Disclosure: registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1 or https://api.eu.munito.ai/inference/v1 through Thor' own client with MUNITO_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files, starts no processes and sends no telemetry.

name: muse-harness
description: Drive local Muse Code over MSP so Wonder Full can call MCP tools. Disclosure — runs your locally installed `muse` (Muse Code) binary as a child process with an allowlisted environment and sends the prompt to Meta through it; if the Muse Code subscription allowance is exhausted, the same prompt is retried once on pay-as-you-go billing with the Meta API key stored in Thor secrets (MODEL_API_KEY, META_API_KEY or META_MODEL_API_KEY) when one is set; with `approval_mode: allowAll` Muse runs its own shell and file tools in the session directory without asking; MCP servers the model passes are limited to loopback HTTP.

name: muster
description: See what your AI helpers are actually doing. Every worker thor starts shows up live in one pane: working, stuck (silent too long), failing on repeat, or gone (thor crashed). Stop a stuck one or send it a message with one click. Start your own helpers with muster_fanout. /muster-digest reports status, spend and the decisions you need; scheduled Fleet watch + Morning report blueprints speak up only when something needs you. No network, no setup.

name: my-github
description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

name: mybot-farm
description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall Thor packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party Thor profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

name: myeline
description: Myeline is a remote MCP memory server: every memory is a single fact with its source attached, AI proposals land in a human review queue, and removing a fact takes a written reason kept in an audit log. One retraction stops a stale fact in every connected assistant at once. Maintained by Sandbox Group, the Myeline vendor. Disclosure — registers the vendor-hosted remote MCP server cortex.myeline.si/mcp, signed in through Thor's remote MCP OAuth with your own Myeline account; the queries and facts the model sends in Myeline tool calls are stored and processed on Myeline's servers, and the server defines its own tool list, which can change without a new catalog pin.

name: myfolks
description: Persistent, exact memory about the people in your life. myfolks, /myfolks or /contacts saves and returns details word for word, with when and where each was saved; saving and recall never call a model. Plain words (remember, fix, forget, undo), a Desktop page to search, add, edit, delete and undo, vCard and CSV import, and optional Google Contacts sync. Encrypted SQLite store (AES-256-GCM) in the Thor folder. Owner only by default, group chats refused, optional per-person sharing (read or add). Disclosure — no network calls until the owner runs myfolks sync; after that Thor calls the Google People API (people.googleapis.com, contacts.readonly) for the plugin through its declared oauth client (signed in with thor auth add myfolks:google, token stored and refreshed by Thor, never given to the plugin), on each sync and automatically at most every 10 minutes when a save or lookup names someone not yet stored, until myfolks sync off. Replies sent over a messaging platform pass through that platform. AI access is off by default; when turned on, the details it needs are sent to the configured model provider. Hooks: pre_gateway_dispatch answers the owner's (and listed shared people's) MyFolks messages in chat apps before the session sees them; pre_llm_call stops a MyFolks command from reaching the AI; pre_tool_call blocks AI tools that directly name its files. Other messages get an in-memory text check only. Stores its own device key in a file only the user can read, or in the OS keychain when Python's keyring package is available.

name: myradio
description: Thor DJs your own myradio station. /radio shows a now-playing card, plays a song by title and sends song requests to the station's music maker, all without a model turn. The agent gets 12 tools to read the station, search the library, plan the queue, write the DJ's lines and ask for new songs, plus the myradio:dj skill and the myradio:dj-shift blueprint for unattended DJ shifts. Going live and deleting audio are not agent tools. Disclosure: each tool call starts myradio's own MCP adapter as a short-lived child process (no shell, small environment without API keys); that adapter reads the station's control.token from its data folder (~/.myradio by default) and talks only to the station on 127.0.0.1. /radio request makes one completion with the user's configured Thor model (Thor 0.23+). No other network calls, no files written, no background process, no telemetry. Needs a running myradio station.

name: myswarm
description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Thor default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Thor loads into every session's system prompt) after a Thor approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

name: nachalo
description: Pair Thor agents end-to-end from six spoken words (CPace + X25519 + ML-KEM-768) and catch a man in the middle with four safety words; the agent only drafts, a person sends. Disclosure — talks to a relay (ntfy.sh by default or your relay_url, plus whichever relay each paired peer chose) that sees topics, IP addresses, timing and fixed-size encrypted frames, never contents; while a peer is active a background thread in the gateway holds an HTTPS subscription to it; peers, inbox, drafts and an audit log (no words, no keys) live in the profile's plugin-data/nachalo, and channel state is sealed with NACHALO_STORE_KEY, which the plugin creates once in the profile's .env with save_env_value and reads through the secret scope; pairing is human-only, peer messages are held and never start turns or tool calls (each turn the agent is told only how many are waiting and from which peer names, and reads them as untrusted content with nachalo_inbox), sending needs a person who sees the exact text and does not rely on approval modes, and cron or -q runs never pair or send; a pre_tool_call hook blocks agent terminal calls that drive the nachalo CLI or its data; the native code ships in the nachalo wheel on PyPI with provenance attestations; the protocol and channel are unaudited drafts.

name: nachos
description: Durable memory and context compression for Thor Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under $THOR_HOME/nachos/.

name: needs-you
description: Thor is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

name: nerdit
description: Thor puts what it builds online on its own machine and keeps it alive. nerdit_ship deploys a folder to the local Nerdit engine (open source, Docker), waits until it is healthy and returns its URL, with the engine's diagnosis on failure. nerdit_share gives an app a hosted https URL, private by default and public only after the user confirms. A pre_llm_call hook tells the agent when one of its apps is failed, degraded or restarting, once per outage and with no model polling; /apps answers with the status of every app without a model call; the nerdit:watch automation blueprint checks the apps on a schedule, restarts what a restart fixes and reports. Two bundled skills (ship, rescue). Disclosure — requires the Nerdit engine and Docker on the same machine. Each call starts the engine's own `nerdit mcp` process over stdio (fixed argv, no shell; the outage check at most once a minute) with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONTEXT, NERDIT_*; none of Thor's provider keys) and acts with the rights of the user's nerdit CLI token, an admin token unless the user scopes it; the plugin never reads or stores that token. The engine zips and builds the folder the agent names. nerdit_call reaches every engine tool by name; only read tools and restart_service run directly, and every other engine tool, plus public sharing, goes to the human approval prompt. A pre_llm_call hook adds app status and a pointer to nerdit_ship to the agent's context. The plugin makes no network call and has no telemetry; sharing an app outside the machine goes through the optional Nerdit Cloud account.

name: nerve
description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Thor Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and Liquid D1 Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and D1 can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The Operator/Lean/Marie Kondo/Fat Cat presets (Operator is what `nerve setup` / the control panel picks for new homes) rewrite each outgoing model request to trim deferred tool schemas and skill descriptions to the current task, which can change the prompt-cache prefix between turns. The operator-only `nerve ui` control panel (127.0.0.1, per-run token) can replace the installed Nerve plugin with a local source checkout and run `thor plugins validate/enable`, and, after an explicit confirmation, can create a Python venv under THOR_HOME, pip-install Laya or PyTorch/transformers from PyPI, download model weights, and start a long-running localhost model server (D1 runs Hugging Face `trust_remote_code` model code). The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local ThorContextBus checkout into THOR_HOME/plugins/thor-context-bus and runs thor plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger any of this.

name: netease-cloud
description: NetEase Cloud Music (网易云音乐) mini player in the Thor Desktop status bar, in the spirit of the built-in Radio plugin: a compact themed popover with Now Playing (cover + scrolling synced lyrics with the current line highlighted), search for songs and playlists, daily picks / recommended playlists / Personal FM, favorites (heart / Liked Music), browsing and in-panel playback of your own playlists, play/pause/skip/progress/volume with outline-style controls, loop modes (list loop, single loop, shuffle), plus a mini control cluster on the status bar itself with a like/unlike heart, prev/next transport, a live audio-spectrum dot visualiser driven by the Web Audio analyser, and a vinyl-record Now-Playing visual whose articulated tonearm drops on the record while playing and parks off it when paused (v0.5.0). Also offers phone-number + SMS verification-code sign-in as a second login method. Desktop-only UI (desktop/plugin.js on the plugin SDK surface) plus a local FastAPI backend (dashboard/plugin_api.py) that implements NetEase's weapi/eapi request signing (AES-CBC/ECB + RSA) with the Python standard library only — no build step, no extra Python dependencies. Disclosure — unofficial NetEase Cloud Music client: the backend calls only NetEase hosts (music.163.com, interface3.music.163.com, and the p*.music.163.com CDNs for covers and audio) using NetEase's own web/PC client identity (Chrome User-Agent, music.163.com Referer/Origin, eapi os=pc/appver headers, x-os/x-login-chain-id QR-login headers with a locally generated anonymous browser-style cookie set; SMS verification-code login calls NetEase web endpoints /api/sms/captcha/sent and /api/w/login/cellphone with the phone number you type); after you log in, your NetEase session cookie (MUSIC_U) is stored in the plugin's own data/cookie.json and sent only to NetEase hosts, and 'Log out' deletes it; while logged in it reports each played track to NetEase (feedback/webenergy play history) and the heart button likes/unlikes songs on your account; no other third-party services and no telemetry; QR and SMS sign-in may be blocked by NetEase risk control (the panel then surfaces a one-click button to NetEase's official account-verification page); pasting the MUSIC_U cookie remains the documented fallback; VIP songs stream through your own VIP session.

name: netmind-provider
description: NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog.
