Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through Thor' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: netplane
description: Install, configure and operate a self-hosted Headscale control plane from Thor. netplane_setup previews a configuration and, after approval, installs the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB on a fresh Debian 12+ or Ubuntu 22.04+ systemd host (amd64/arm64). Installation runs on the Thor host, requires root or noninteractive sudo, refuses existing deployments, and verifies the package SHA-256. It configures SQLite, MagicDNS, embedded DERP/STUN, local admin gRPC, and either Let's Encrypt HTTPS or a loopback backend for an existing reverse proxy. It starts the system service, creates the first user, and saves a 90-day API key and connection settings through Thor's active-profile APIs. netplane_status reports health, netplane_nodes lists devices, and netplane_preauth lists metadata without stored join secrets or creates an approval-gated, single-use-by-default join key with a 1–168 hour lifetime. Desktop includes setup preview/confirmation, health, nodes, join keys and confirmed node expiration, with a FastAPI backend. Management requires NETPLANE_APIKEY; setup works before a key exists. Bundled protobuf stubs use pinned sources and a compatible toolchain. Disclosure — the netplane_setup tool (after Thor approval) and the Desktop pane (after confirmation) install the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB as root through noninteractive sudo on the Thor host, downloading it from GitHub (SHA-256 verified) and possibly contacting configured APT repositories; it writes /etc/headscale, /var/lib/headscale and a systemd drop-in, and enables a persistent headscale service that in Let's Encrypt mode listens publicly on TCP 80/443 and UDP 3478 (admin gRPC and metrics stay on loopback); Let's Encrypt receives the chosen domain and email; setup saves a new 90-day Headscale API key as NETPLANE_APIKEY in the active Thor profile; management reads credentials only from Thor and uses TLS with system trust off-host; approved join-key creation returns the key into the chat; status runs systemctl is-active headscale and tailscale serve status; no telemetry and no automatic software updates.

name: netscope
description: Offline pcap/pcapng network capture analyzer with interactive HTML reports, protocol graphs, traffic replay at 1×/4×/16×, and deterministic anomaly heuristics (traffic bursts, scan patterns, DNS anomalies, cleartext ports). Stdlib-only, no network requests, no telemetry.

name: network-xray
description: Compare DNS, TCP, verified TLS and HTTP HEAD captures of one URL from two machines, find the first observed difference and export a local evidence report. Read-only and local-first, with native agent tools, a Desktop workbench and a stdlib-only portable collector for the second machine. Disclosure — the network_xray_probe tool, the CLI and the Desktop page connect from the Thor machine to a URL the model or user names, including private and loopback addresses (link-local, multicast and unspecified are refused): DNS, TCP, verified TLS and one HTTP HEAD request, with no query, credentials, redirects or body, run in an isolated Python child with a minimal environment; it saves the target, resolved IPs, certificate fingerprint and the server/content-type headers under the profile's plugin-data/network-xray/ folder, and imported bundles from a second machine are unauthenticated; no telemetry.

name: neural-mesh
description: Bi-temporal long-term memory for Thor: point-in-time recall (mesh_asof answers what was true on a date, not only what is true now), supersession instead of overwrite so a corrected fact keeps its history, hybrid dense + lexical retrieval, a poisoning quarantine, and an injection floor measured on a 15-family ablation. Disclosure — this is a Thor MemoryProvider (`memory.provider: neural-mesh`). It stores user turns, pre-compression and session-end message extracts, and mirrored MEMORY.md/USER.md writes in an unencrypted local SQLite file at `<profile>/neural-mesh/mesh.db`, so credentials do not belong in it. The provider makes no network calls and needs no API key. The repo also vendors unused upstream modules with LLM/chain HTTP clients that the provider never calls. It ships no compiled binary (the Rust extension is not vendored, so retrieval runs the pure-Python path).

name: neuralmind
description: Code memory on every Thor turn, with no tool call. Before the model runs, the plugin looks the user's message up in a local NeuralMind index of the project and appends the matching files and symbols (with line numbers), the code linked to them in NeuralMind's synapse graph, and decisions recorded in commit trailers. A session's first turn also gets a recap of the previous session in that project. The plugin is a stdlib-only shim around the separately installed NeuralMind CLI: install NeuralMind 4.9 or later yourself (`pipx install neuralmind`, `uv tool install neuralmind` or `pip install neuralmind`) and run `neuralmind build` in the project; in any other directory it does nothing. Not a memory provider: it registers no `memory.provider` and runs beside whichever one is configured. Disclosure — runs `neuralmind _hook <action>` as a child process once per turn (twice on a session's first), once for each file a write_file or patch call wrote, and once for each read_file of a file inside the project; each call is stopped after NEURALMIND_THOR_TIMEOUT seconds (default 8) and the turn goes ahead without its context. A session's first turn can leave a detached NeuralMind process running after the hook returns, which writes the project's graph cache or, on a large synapse store, runs the decay tick and memory export, then exits. NeuralMind runs read-only git queries in the project (rev-parse, ls-files, log, diff --name-only). Reads the project, and reads and writes its .neuralmind/ directory, including each session's prompts (secret-redacted and truncated) and the paths of the files it edited, for the recap. On a session's first turn it copies .neuralmind/SYNAPSE_MEMORY.md into Claude Code's memory directory for the project (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/) when that directory already exists. The added context is part of the user message, so it is sent to the model provider with that turn and stays in the session history. The plugin makes no network requests and NeuralMind sends no telemetry; NeuralMind downloads its embedding model once when it has no cached copy, normally during `neuralmind build` (ChromaDB's all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX archive from chroma-onnx-models.s3.amazonaws.com, SHA-256-checked, cached in ~/.cache/neuralmind/). Subagent and cron turns are skipped. MIT.

name: neuralwatt
description: Check NeuralWatt service health, model pricing, account balance, request costs, energy use, and session activity from Thor. Includes nine read-only tools plus a one-call account dashboard and cost comparisons across models. Health and public model discovery need no credentials; account analytics use your NeuralWatt API key. Disclosure — makes GET requests to the NeuralWatt API (api.neuralwatt.com, or the host you set in NEURALWATT_BASE_URL, which then receives your API key), reads account usage, cost and energy metrics rather than prompt or completion text, writes nothing, and loads the optional API key through Thor's secret scope.

name: neuralwatt-provider
description: Neuralwatt as a Thor model provider (`provider: neuralwatt`). The /model picker lists Neuralwatt's live catalog with real context windows, and Thor's reasoning setting is sent as `reasoning_effort`. Each turn gets a cost estimate from Neuralwatt's published energy figures, and /usage shows credits, daily free energy, this month's spend and 30 days of energy and carbon. Works alongside the `neuralwatt` tools plugin. Not affiliated with Neuralwatt. Disclosure: registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat goes through Thor's own client to https://api.neuralwatt.com/v1 (or NEURALWATT_BASE_URL) with NEURALWATT_API_KEY, read through Thor's secret scope. The plugin itself sends GET requests to that API's /models, /quota and /usage/energy, and to Neuralwatt's public energy price table at portal.neuralwatt.com. It sends the Thor session id as `metadata.conversation_id`, which Neuralwatt stores as a hash. It writes no files and starts no processes.

name: neuron-steer
description: Neuron steering for Thor Agent, implementing Thor Labs's own Contrastive Neuron Attribution (arXiv:2605.12290). Find the sparse MLP neurons that distinguish two behaviors with forward passes only, save them as named circuits, then scale or ablate those neurons at inference to steer a local model, plus a dose scan that maps where the behavior turns on before output quality breaks. Disclosure — loads local Hugging Face models with torch on this machine; when a tool call sets allow_download (the model can set it) or NEURON_STEER_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD=1, it downloads the named model from huggingface.co, which can be several GB.

name: next-prompt
description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

name: next-steps
description: Next-step suggestions under the Thor Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

name: nextcloud-talk
description: Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for Thor, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.

name: nextcloud-talk-platform
description: Nextcloud Talk platform adapter for Thor Agent, in two modes behind one plugin: a webhook bot (Nextcloud Talk Bot API, HMAC-SHA256 signed, with an explicit body-size cap and a nonce-replay cache ahead of payload parsing) and a real Nextcloud user account (app password, long-polling the Chat REST API, with federation-invite support, per-room mention/watch/free modes, and an agent-to-agent loop guard plus active-listening context for multi-agent rooms). Mode is picked automatically by which credential is configured. No extra SDKs -- aiohttp for bot mode, httpx for user mode, both already Thor dependencies. Disclosure — Connects to your Nextcloud server either as a Talk bot (HMAC-verified webhook listener, 127.0.0.1:18797 by default) or as a real Nextcloud user with an app password (long-polls the Chat API and auto-accepts federation invites only from NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ALLOWED_INVITERS); in user mode, unanswered room messages from allowed senders (up to 40 per room by default) and, for rooms listed in NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ROOM_MODES or with room_rules_all_rooms on, the room description are added to the agent's next turn in that room.

name: nextdns
description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

name: nexus
description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Thor and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Shared rooms are handled by observation, not by chat type: a room turns shared as soon as a human other than the owner has written in it, bots never count, and recall, the tools and the graph then serve public memories only. A memory whose text sat in a legacy `text` field still reaches the injected block (the block falls back from `content`), and a short state fact marked by the write gate (a version, a count, an amount) needs 12 characters instead of 40, so "Thor version: 0.23.1" is no longer filtered out. The write gate recognises state values: a long text stores unchanged but comes back with a hint to keep the value as its own short fact, no second write, no automatic extraction. The owner is identified per platform through owner_user_ids. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Thor cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Thor config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to Thor's own default model through local Ollama; reads ~/.thor/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Thor cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon that sends memory text to the Ollama endpoint at 127.0.0.1:11434 or NEXUS_OLLAMA_BASE under the model named by NEXUS_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL, nexus-memory.consolidation_model or Thor's model.default, which can be an Ollama cloud model), and the service keeps running after Thor exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Thor config.yaml, and the opt-in recall reranker (nexus-memory.rerank or NEXUS_RERANK=1) defaults to sending each query plus up to 20 memory snippets to that same endpoint using the provider API key it reads from config.yaml; reads ~/.thor/.env and config.yaml, and opens Thor's state.db read-only for the session's chat type when the host reports no message author; the shared-room rule records the owner id in <thor_home>/nexus/config.json (taken from the first gateway user when owner_user_ids is unset) and shared chat ids with a hashed author id in <thor_home>/nexus/chat-sharing.json; a keyword (SQLite FTS5) copy of memory text and metadata, private memories included, in <thor_home>/state/nexus-fts.db (or NEXUS_FTS_DB); state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.

name: nexus-recovery-peer
description: Optional bounded peer-model suggestion after repeated tool failure or a failed delegated child. Disclosure — when an administrator explicitly configures a provider/model route and grants the required LLM override capabilities, the plugin sends a redacted excerpt of the task and failure to that provider via Thor ctx.llm. Redaction is best-effort, not a confidentiality guarantee; host routing/fallback may change the actual recipient. Empty routes (the default) make no peer requests. The plugin does not replay tools, run shell commands, read files independently, store credentials, or send telemetry.

name: ngrok-ai-gateway
description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a Thor model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `thor model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto Thor' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through Thor' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: night-shift
description: An on-call engineer that never sleeps. Alerts trigger a read-only investigation, a human approves the fix with one tap in Slack, and Night Shift runs it, proves recovery, and writes the runbook as a skill so the next incident is recognised. Disclosure — runs read-only shell diagnostics during an incident, and after a listed human approves it runs the approved commands through the terminal tool without a second Thor prompt (optionally over the configured ssh prefix). Destructive commands are refused at proposal time. Sends container logs, status and database activity to the model provider. Calls Prometheus at the configured URL and Slack through the user's Thor Slack app. Writes runbook skills through skill_manage and keeps incident state in plugin state. No telemetry, stores no credentials.

name: nightshift
description: Thor takes the night shift on your ML training runs: Nightshift watches a run's metrics (stdout, JSONL, CSV or TensorBoard), catches NaN, loss spikes, divergence, out-of-memory crashes and stalls, recovers the run within a playbook you approved (roll back to the last healthy checkpoint with a lower learning rate, or restart with half the batch), and pushes the chart to your phone. Desktop pane, dashboard tab, /nightshift, thor nightshift and a morning-report blueprint. Zero runtime dependencies. Disclosure — the agent can only propose a training run; after your explicit approval (/nightshift approve in chat or the Approve button; there is no CLI approve) it launches the approved command as a long-running background process from a background thread that starts with Thor, with a minimal environment (no Thor keys unless you name them in env_passthrough, shown on the approval card), and may stop or restart that process group, re-rendering only the approved command with the playbook's parameters (lr, batch size, grad accumulation, checkpoint path) within an intervention budget; it signals only process groups it started (start-time checked, never a run it cannot verify), reads the log, metric and checkpoint paths you or the agent give it, runs nvidia-smi and ps, stores run data in its plugin data folder and alert charts in Thor's image cache, makes capped LLM calls on your configured model with a redacted log tail on critical incidents, and sends alerts through Thor's own `thor send` to your messaging platform; no network calls of its own.

name: nine-balance-widget
description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not Thor' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

name: ninsei
description: Rooms where you and your Thor agent hang out with other people and their agents. Play games the agents host, build small web toys together and message friends privately. No server: rooms run on free public Nostr relays. Disclosure — Rooms, reactions, edits, room details, shared toys, your interest card, picture, portrait and face are signed and posted to public Nostr relays (nos.lol, relay.primal.net, nostr.mom, relay.snort.social, relay.damus.io by default), which may keep them forever; private messages are NIP-17 encrypted but relays see your key, timing and IP. Your room agent is a separate tool-less model call (no Thor memory or tools) that strangers in a room can trigger against your daily token budget; its personality can be imported from any local Thor profile's SOUL.md when you choose to, and whatever you keep there can surface in its public replies. The "Your Thor" private line is a local gateway platform registered with trusted_inbound=True that switches itself on once Ninsei has data in the profile: it reaches your full Thor agent (tools, memory) from rows in Ninsei's 0600 SQLite file, so any program running as your user that writes that file is treated as you (turn it off with gateway.platforms.ninsei.enabled: false). Five observe-only hooks run in every chat and record only step counts for toy builds you accepted. Stores two Nostr keypairs and decrypted private messages unencrypted in that SQLite file.

name: no-cap
description: Receipts for agent claims. No Cap checks the claims in each final reply (tests pass, pushed, merged, deployed, file written, URL live, SHAs, counts; English plus Chinese, Thai and Spanish for tests, push, merge and deploy) against the tool calls the agent made, with no extra model, and appends a footer: 🧾 NO CAP when a tool call proves the claim, 🧢 CAP only when one directly contradicts it (exit code, test counts, push ref, PR state, or a claimed SHA or branch that does not exist in the session's repo), and an opt-in 🤔 NO RECEIPT. A claim about earlier work can cite an earlier turn of the same session. A green run after the agent changed the suite in that turn (deleted, moved, skipped or deselected tests, a conftest or runner-config filter, PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-k) no longer earns 🧾 for "all tests pass": it gets a visible 🤔 naming the change, and 🧢 only when an earlier run named the removed test as failing and the reply doesn't say so. /cap makes the agent prove or retract its open claims and re-scores the next reply; /capscore keeps a per-model honesty board, a scorecard and an A/B compare card; /nocap verdict draws a session verdict card; strict mode uses pre_verify to send a coding turn back, at most twice. Surfaces: a Cap Board dashboard tab (agents, models and skills ranked live; this profile only unless you opt in to a team view), Thor Desktop receipt chips and a Receipts popover, opt-in Discord embed + buttons, and Cap Coach, which drafts a rule from repeated caps and injects it only after you approve it. Opt-in Obsidian lessons (0.3.0): each 🧢 becomes a redacted line in that agent's note in your vault and, once per agent and pattern, a mistakes-board note (Agent Black Box format); with obsidian_learn the agent's own repeated cap patterns come back as built-in rules at the start of its turns. Licence: Apache-2.0 (0.1.0 to 0.2.0 were MIT). Disclosure — Stores, all in its Thor plugin data folder THOR_HOME/plugin-data/agent-plugin-no-cap-<digest>/ (folder 0700; `thor nocap path` prints it), every text field through a secret masker first (the home directory is written as ~ in stored commands and working dirs): receipts.jsonl (0600; one line per checked reply: session/turn ids, model, platform, each claim's text, verdict, reason and quoted evidence line, and only for tool calls a receipt cites the command (first 160 chars), exit code, error line and parsed facts; other calls only as a count and SHA-256 digest; pruned after retention_days (default 30), halved past 20 MB); ledger.jsonl (0600; cross_turn, on by default: per-turn parsed call facts, including the tool's own working directory (first 300 chars), the call's timestamp, up to 20 failing test ids a run printed and up to 10 short notes of suite changes the call made, never raw output; newest 100 turns / 400 calls per session, same retention, 10 MB cap); coach.json (0600; Cap Coach drafts and approved rules with up to 3 redacted example claims per pattern; the rule text it injects is always No Cap's built-in text for that pattern, never text read back from coach.json); desktop.json (0600; on/off and a timestamp from the Desktop half); discord_receipts.json (0600, only with discord_buttons: on; receipt id → session/turn ids, session key, user, chat and thread ids, at most 500, no claim text); scorecard, verdict and compare SVG/PNG cards. /nocap purge deletes the receipts, ledger, Discord map and cards (local CLI/TUI/Desktop only; refused from a gateway chat); coach.json and desktop.json stay until you delete them. `thor nocap export --out` and `metrics --file` write only the file you name (0600, atomic; CSV cells that could start a formula are quoted). Obsidian lessons (off unless obsidian_vault names an existing vault; nothing in any vault is read or written while it is empty): writes only inside that vault, <vault>/<obsidian_folder, default "No Cap">/<profile>.md (one redacted line per 🧢: date, pattern id, claim and contradicting evidence, each at most 160 chars, Markdown-escaped, plus a ^nc-<receipt id> block id) and, with obsidian_board auto (vault has .agentbox.json or an Agent Black Box folder) or on, one `M-NNNN <title>.md` note per agent and pattern in the board's mistakes folder plus an empty id reservation file in its .ids/ folder; new files 0600, written through a temp file in the same folder and os.replace, the vault held by a descriptor walked with O_NOFOLLOW and re-checked by device and inode before each write, one non-blocking flock per destination folder (at most 120 ms per write, then skipped and retried; `thor nocap obsidian sync` rewrites from the store idempotently). In its data folder: obsidian-lessons.json (per-agent 🧢 counts by pattern id, no claim text; only with obsidian_learn; /nocap purge deletes it) and obsidian-board-<dev>-<inode>.json (its index of the board notes it wrote). It never reads note text back into a prompt. Suite-change detection reads only the tool calls' own arguments and output (edit contents, shell commands, env prefixes); it adds no file reads, subprocesses or network use. Commands it runs: read-only git as argument lists, no shell, in the session's working directory, hardened against an untrusted repo (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, core.fsmonitor=false, protocol.allow=never, no pager, no lazy fetch, credential helper off, minimal env: only PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, SYSTEMROOT inherited, never provider keys): at reply time, only for a claimed SHA or branch no tool call backs (verify_artifacts, at most 8 calls, 3 s each) `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree --is-shallow-repository`, `config --get-regexp`, `cat-file -e`, `for-each-ref`; during /cap (5 s each) `cat-file -t <sha>`, `merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD`, `show -s --format=%ct <sha>`, `rev-parse --verify <ref>` and `reflog show --date=unix -n 20 refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`, so a re-check proves the session's own work, not mere existence. It lists the run's project read-only to tell a file-scoped test run from the full suite (bounded, no symlinks) and, during /cap, stats a file the agent says it created (existence, size, modification time). `thor nocap demo --ladder` (and /nocap demo ladder, CLI/TUI only, in the background) runs the bundled demo/run_ladder.sh with /bin/sh in a throwaway THOR_HOME in the system temp directory, under `env -i` with only PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR, TERM and the demo's own settings (no provider keys), a scripted model on 127.0.0.1 and a uv install of the hash-pinned demo/requirements-ladder.txt (pytest, pyte, Pillow) into a throwaway venv; that fetch is the demo's one network use. Network: none by default; with self_verify_http: true, /cap may send one HTTP HEAD to a URL the agent claimed is live, public addresses only (checked after DNS), no redirects, 3 s timeout. Dashboard and Desktop: routes under /api/plugins/no-cap/ on your own Thor backend, behind the dashboard's auth: GET /board (read-only), POST /hello (writes desktop.json), POST /verify (yes/no for one Desktop chip in one chat; the HMAC key lives only in memory and is never returned), GET /session. The board reads other profiles' stores and board_sources paths only with the board.team_profiles opt-in, only in the CLI and dashboard, never in a gateway chat; in a gateway chat /nocap, /nocap verdict and the /capscore board Hall of Cap show only that chat's receipts, with no store path. Discord: off by default; with discord_buttons: on it edits only the bot's own reply to add an embed and two buttons and answers clicks ephemerally (only the user the reply answered may click). Reply rewriting: it removes forged ::nocap directives, closes a code fence, <!-- or <details> the reply left open (append-only) and appends the footer. Messages it sends: /cap injects one user message where Thor allows it (gateway-backed sessions need plugins.entries.no-cap.allow_gateway_injection: true), otherwise prints it to paste; it quotes the agent's claims as labelled data (capped, brackets, quotes, backticks and newlines removed) with parsed counts, never a raw output line. Cap Coach injects approved rules as labelled context through pre_llm_call, only in scope, never before /cap coach approve, and /cap coach revert stops it; with obsidian_learn: true it also adds one labelled line holding up to 3 built-in rules for the patterns this agent (profile) was stamped 🧢 on at least twice, from its own store only; approve, revert and --apply are refused from a gateway chat. When the history already holds a No Cap footer, pre_llm_call also adds one fixed, labelled line asking the model not to write receipt lines itself (built-in text only, never stored; footer_hint: off stops it). It never edits skills, memory or config (--apply asks the agent to, with its own tools). /nocap doctor reads other plugins' plugin.yaml files and the Thor config. No tools, credentials, telemetry or self-update. Accuracy: blind samples of public SWE-rebench runs (two raters, adjudicated): round 3 at 01a1fab, 🧾 precision 0.92 (92/100, 95% CI 0.85–0.96; no 🧢 on unseen runs, so not measured); round 2 at 7c6cbc0, 🧢 8 of 11 correct. Local Arena (30 synthetic bug-fix tasks, Qwen3-4B and a partial Qwen3-30B-A3B, No Cap at aa69dcb, one person's hand check against hidden tests): 13 of 13 🧢 correct.

name: no-manual
description: Furniture with no instructions? Send photos and Thor finds the official manual, turns your disassembly photos into a manual in reverse, or works out flat-pack assembly (closets, bookcases, cabinets) from the parts, then coaches you step by step and checks a photo of each step. Steps arrive as images in chat; Thor Desktop shows an interactive 3D step viewer. Never generates instructions for children's furniture or anything people sit, sleep or climb on. Disclosure — photos you add are sent to your own configured model provider through Thor (ctx.llm) to read panels, labels and step photos; image and PDF paths the model passes are read from anywhere on disk (images and PDFs only) and copied into the plugin's folder, and `recent` mode picks up images from Thor's shared inbound image cache (<THOR_HOME>/cache/images, cache/documents/native-inputs) from the last 30 minutes, which on a multi-user gateway can include another chat's upload; manual PDFs found by Thor's web search are downloaded over https (max 30 MB, public hosts only); photos, manual pages and generated images are stored in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/no-manual/ and deleted with /nomanual delete; the Desktop half bundles three.js (source in desktop/src/); no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credentials stored.

name: node-search
description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

name: nomads-planner
description: Nomads.com for Thor: read your own trips and favorite cities, look up curated city and country facts (monthly costs, rent, internet speed, weather, safety and other 0-5 scores), list upcoming in-person meetups, and build a next-stay brief in one call that joins your current and upcoming stays, unplanned gaps, city facts, meetups inside each stay's dates and your past visits, with deterministic comparisons (cheapest, fastest internet, safest). Native plugin: 7 read-only tools, a /nomads slash command and a bundled planning skill. City, country and meetup tools work without an account; trips and favorites need a free personal key from https://nomads.com/settings, read through Thor' secret scope. Disclosure — makes HTTPS GET requests to https://nomads.com/api only (sending your username and personal key in the Authorization header for trips and favorites); no writes, no other hosts, no files read, no background processes, no telemetry; public city data is cached in memory for 10 minutes. Not affiliated with Nomads.com.

name: nord-theme
description: Unofficial Nord theme for Thor Desktop with hand-tuned Polar Night (dark) and Snow Storm (light) palettes, Nord terminal colors, Nord code-block syntax colors, and Aurora status colors. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — its stylesheet recolors Desktop surfaces, code-block syntax colors, status colors, selection and inline code only while Nord is selected, and it switches the active theme to Nord once on first enable; no network calls, file reads or shell commands.

name: northstar
description: Read-only coherence auditing for Thor Agent. Detects potential contradictions, duplicate directives, and stale references in instruction sources and skills, with supporting evidence. Disclosure — the audit tool reads your Thor home instruction files, `config.yaml`, every installed skill, and instruction files in the current working directory, and returns matching lines as evidence to the model (a secret written inline in config that is duplicated across scanned files can appear in a result); read-only, no network calls.

name: nostr
description: Nostr platform adapter for Thor, backed by the local Thor Nostr Gateway daemon: NIP-17 and NIP-04 DMs, kind-1 mentions and feeds, Concord channels and Marmot groups arrive as one message stream, with reach and authority decided by the gateway's policy. Disclosure — Needs the separately installed thor-nostr-gateway daemon (not covered by this pin), which holds the Nostr keys, talks to relays and decides which senders are trusted; on load the adapter writes the Thor command list and that write's outcome to commands.json and commands.status.json in the catalogue directory (default ~/.local/state/thor-nostr-gateway/, or NOSTR_GATEWAY_COMMANDS), and with an npub home/control channel it runs the `nak` CLI to decode it.

name: nostr-vpn
description: Private mesh networking through the separately installed nvpn CLI. Instruction-only skill; connects to relays and peers and starts a persistent daemon. Tunnels need elevated host networking privileges. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs the separately installed nvpn CLI in the terminal (installed by the user, or by the agent from the project's latest GitHub release or an unpinned `cargo install nvpn`), which creates local device keys, connects to Nostr relays and peers, starts a persistent daemon that with elevated privileges creates tunnel interfaces and routes, and on an admin host can approve devices into the user's private network.

name: nous-girl-theme
description: Warm monochrome ink-and-paper theme for Thor Desktop in real light and dark palettes, with terminal colours that match and a CLI banner painted from the theme's own palette. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers one theme through the Desktop plugin SDK and injects no CSS, no DOM access and no stylesheet of its own; the two Desktop palettes ship as light and dark sets, and the Desktop keeps its own typography. The package also ships two optional CLI/TUI skins (nous-girl-light, nous-girl-dark) as plain YAML files the user copies into ~/.thor/skins, plus an inert __init__.py whose register() does nothing so the Agent loader imports the package cleanly instead of reporting a missing module. No network requests, no agent tools, no hooks, no background processes, no settings page.

name: novel-reader
description: Read local .txt/.md novels beside the conversation while the agent works: chapter detection from CJK and latin headings, leading table-of-contents trimming, UTF-8 / GBK / GB18030 sniffing, and a per-book progress mark, so reopening a book resumes where you stopped. Four entry points — a sidebar row with a /novel page, a status-bar chip, a title-bar button that opens a floating panel or a docked right-edge column, and a contributed layout pane. Disclosure — Desktop-only; reads .txt/.md files only from the folder the user grants through the Thor plugin file door (ctx.files) and never writes outside Thor plugin storage, where the granted folder (id, name, path), typography settings and one progress mark per book are kept; the "copy bookmark" button writes one line to the clipboard; no network access, no telemetry, no update checks.

name: nowstamp
description: Give the agent a clock. Appends the current date and time, plus the real gap since the previous message, to every user turn. Optional spaced-out timestamps on tool results for long runs.

name: ntfy-approval
description: Answer Thor' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Thor' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

name: numogram
description: Thor debugs ESP32 firmware on real hardware. It watches the board's serial port, maps crash addresses to source lines from the ELF, fixes the code, builds with idf.py and flashes with esptool, then reads the log to confirm the fix. A crash wakes the session on its own. Also checks firmware GPIO use against a KiCad netlist (swapped signals, strapping, flash and USB pins) and audits chip security read-only. NUMOGRAM_PORT=virtual runs an emulated ESP32-C3 in Espressif's QEMU, so it works without a board. Disclosure — board_build and board_flash go through Thor's approval prompt (a pre_tool_call hook, one approval rule per tool) and are blocked when nobody can answer; a build runs ESP-IDF's export.sh, idf.py and the project's own CMake and Python scripts and writes the build directory it is given. Runs esptool, espefuse summary (read-only; the plugin has no eFuse write) and, for the virtual board only, Espressif's qemu-system-riscv32 with networking off, always with fixed argument lists, and each child gets an environment allowlist (PATH, HOME, locale, ESP-IDF variables), never Thor's keys or tokens. Background: a serial watcher thread while watching is on, and a QEMU process for the virtual board that stops when Thor exits. Network: none beyond loopback (unauthenticated) to its own macOS USB bridge or virtual board, or the socket:// address set in NUMOGRAM_PORT. Reads the project, build, ELF and netlist paths it is given; writes its own state only under the active Thor profile's home (get_thor_home() / numogram). Serial output is passed to the model as untrusted data; wake-up messages are built from fixed text and validated hex. The bridge and virtual board drop eFuse write commands. No credentials, no telemetry.

name: nurse
description: Supervisor-aware service management for a Thor host. Reads pm2 and systemd into one table, triages a failing service's own logs into a ranked diagnosis (OOM via SIGKILL/exit 137, port already in use, missing env var, crash loop measured as restarts per hour rather than uptime, bad exit code, dependency unreachable), and repairs it through one guarded surface. Disclosure — service_repair changes supervisor state: it restarts, starts, stops, reloads or resets a named pm2 process, or restarts, starts, stops or reset-fails a systemd user unit, behind an allowlist of verbs, a confirm plan-then-act step, a persisted per-service cooldown ledger, a refusal to restart a service already crash-looping, and a pre_tool_call hook that escalates every state-changing call to Thor' own human-approval prompt. It shells out to `pm2` and `systemctl`/`journalctl` as the invoking user, so it can only act on services that user already controls; it reads their log files (including pm2's rotated siblings) and writes a small JSON snapshot and cooldown ledger under plugin-data/nurse. No network I/O, no credentials, no elevated privileges.

name: nvidia-app
description: NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

name: nvidia-broadcast
description: NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. Disclosure: the tools change live audio and video effects on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

name: nvidia-skills
description: Find the right NVIDIA skill for GPU acceleration, CUDA, AI agents, data loading, training, inference, robotics, Physical AI, Omniverse, simulation, and other NVIDIA-powered workflows. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one skill, nvidia-skill-finder; no code, tools or credentials. Disclosure — skill-only package (no code); on NVIDIA-related turns its skill reads NVIDIA's public skill catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (github.com and build.nvidia.com as fallbacks) and, with the user's approval, installs a chosen NVIDIA skill via `thor skills install` (Thor' security scan and confirmation apply); its instructions for other agents use the unpinned `npx skills` CLI from npm.

name: nvidia-switchyard
description: Routes Thor between a local and a cloud model with Verification-Gated Routing (VGR): each turn is tried on the local model, checked, and escalated to the cloud model only when the check fails. Either tier can be any URL or a third-party model provider set up in Thor; each provider's terms and conditions apply. Presets are selectable as switchyard/<preset> models, with a Desktop page and dashboard tab showing each decision live. Disclosure — installs nemo-switchyard from PyPI; runs a loopback sidecar on 127.0.0.1:4110 that keeps running after Thor quits (`thor switchyard stop`), and Open in browser starts Thor's web dashboard; reads every model request and response to route it; for a provider tier it takes that provider's credential (sign-in tokens included) from Thor on each call and sends it only to that provider; stores a generated sidecar token and any tier API keys in Thor's .env through Thor's config API; setup makes switchyard/<preset> the default model and sends titles and smart approvals to the local model; copies its provider profile to <THOR_HOME>/plugins/model-providers/switchyard/ on load; logs and routing records stay in <THOR_HOME>/switchyard/; after removal it restores the replaced models, stops its sidecar and deletes its provider copy; it never rewrites saved conversations. No telemetry.

name: nyx
description: Nyx: local, single-user long-term memory with no LLM on the write path. Every turn is logged verbatim and indexed (SQLite FTS5, optional embeddings); on top of that log Nyx keeps bi-temporal facts (what is true now, and what you believed on a given day), source trust (tool, delegation and bot output never becomes a fact about you), two-stage forgetting with a restorable quarantine, and secrets filtering before anything is stored, with an optional encrypted vault that hands a pasted key back to its owner only after human approval. Disclosure — memory is stored locally in ~/.neurobase (configurable); no network calls by default. Opt-in only: a configured embedding API receives memory text and queries; l3_llm sends profile, scene and recent-decision snippets to DeepSeek or OpenRouter; LLM extraction sends the sentence being extracted to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set (default 127.0.0.1). Keys are read through get_secret. The optional vault stores secrets encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a master key in ~/.config/nyx/vault.key, or optionally in the OS keychain under Nyx's own service name; revealing one asks for approval through Thor and is refused under cron and subagents. Adds a thor nyx CLI (vault, doctor, scrub, repair, status). A separate opt-in companion plugin shipped in the same package, nyx-reveal, registers one transform_llm_output hook.

name: nyx-wiki-recall
description: Attach short wiki glimpses chosen by a decision model, and write a daily Markdown transcript of every turn. A local Markdown wiki (starter layout shipped) is scored per message through OpenRouter's Decisions API; matching glimpses are injected before the model answers, and wiki_read opens the full article. Transcripts are written by the plugin itself into THOR_HOME/plugin-data/nyx-wiki-recall/ with no extra setup (transcript = yes and finalize = yes are the shipped values). Each day runs from finalize.after to finalize.after (default 02:00). Scheduled (cron) jobs are recorded under a Scheduled job heading; only subagent turns are skipped by default. A day is finished at finalize.after the next morning. The files are what a wiki is built from. Ships Clotho's wiki-archivist skill. Default provider=no runs as a hook beside any memory provider; provider=yes can serve as Thor's memory provider when memory.provider also says so. Disclosure — for each message that passes the skip rules (not empty, not a slash command; cron turns skipped by default), HTTPS POSTs go to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (decisions.url, default that URL; model typesafe/jev-1.13) with OPENROUTER_API_KEY (via agent.secret_scope.get_secret), carrying the recent conversation (context.turns, default 2) trimmed to message.chars (default 20,000 characters) and the titles, paths and glimpses of the wiki folders and pages being asked about (up to three requests per message, within budget.seconds); nothing else is sent anywhere and there is no telemetry. Reads the wiki folder (wiki_path), Thor config read-only, and the gateway-bound THOR_SESSION_* values via gateway.session_context.get_session_env; in memory-provider mode only, also opens THOR_HOME/state.db read-only for the last 40 messages of the current session. Writes a journal and daily Markdown transcript of every turn (user messages, replies and short tool-call summaries such as terminal commands and file paths, after pattern-based secret redaction, with default file permissions) only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/nyx-wiki-recall/ (or transcript.folder), plus suggestions, finalized.json and lock files. Deletes nothing by default; with keep.days > 0, only its own finished journal/ and suggestions/ day files. Runs one day-finishing background thread per Thor process and one short-lived transcript thread after each reply; runs no shell commands and stores no credentials.

name: oathkeeper
description: An owner's oath, enforced by the machine. The owner writes standing rules once in a plain oath file (standing missions briefed into every session, never delete or modify these surfaces, always require evidence such as a backup before touching those) and Oathkeeper enforces them deterministically on every tool call: never rules block with the violated oath line cited, always-require rules block until the prerequisite evidence exists in the same session, fingerprint snapshots of sworn surfaces detect changes made outside the gate and report them on the next turn, and the oath file itself can never be modified by the agent. Every verdict is written to an append-only local ledger. Disclosure: reads tool call arguments to extract intended file actions and reads files covered by oath patterns to fingerprint them; all state is stored locally under $THOR_HOME/oathkeeper/; makes no network calls and calls no model.

name: obol
description: Safe invoicing for freelancers, consultants and agencies who bill clients, from any chat Thor runs in (tested: Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, email and the terminal). Thor drafts invoices (also from forwarded messages via ctx.llm), sends them as Stripe payment links or as bank-transfer PDF invoices with no provider account, tracks who has paid, and adds Invoices and Security dashboard views plus /invoices in every chat. Every invoice write needs approval, with deterministic checks for prompt injection (a message can never choose the recipient), lookalike and impersonated client addresses, duplicates, unusual amounts and changed payout details; live keys are refused unless allowed, writes are refused in unattended runs, and the activity and security logs are hash-chained. Disclosure — handles payments: in Stripe mode it calls api.stripe.com with your STRIPE_API_KEY (read through Thor's secret route) and Stripe emails your clients when invoices are sent or reminded; live keys are refused unless you turn on allow_live, and in live mode the approval prompt warns that sending or reminding emails the real client; every invoice write asks for approval and writes are refused in cron runs; forwarded messages you ask it to draft from go to your configured model; bank-transfer mode makes no network calls and prints the bank details you enter in plugin settings (stored in config.yaml) on PDF invoices; data stays in plugin-data/obol/.

name: obscurify-provider
description: Obscurify.ai as a Thor model provider (`--provider obscurify`, or Obscurify.ai in `thor model`): a privacy-focused, OpenAI-compatible API to 200+ models with zero-data-retention routes and account-number sign-up (no email). The model list leaves out decision models and models under Thor' 64K context minimum, context windows come from the catalog, and reasoning effort is sent as `reasoning_effort`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://obscurify.ai/v1 through Thor' own client with OBSCURIFY_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself only fetches the public model catalog (GET https://obscurify.ai/v1/models, no credentials) at most once an hour per process, reads and writes no files and starts no processes. Usage is billed from the user's prepaid Obscurify.ai balance; the plugin makes no payments.

name: obsidian-memory
description: Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the Thor dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

name: obsidian-rag
description: Search and edit an Obsidian vault from a local hybrid index (SQLite FTS5 plus 384-dim ONNX embeddings) through seven tools. Answers come from the notes on disk, with no server, no account and no model in the gateway process. Disclosure — The model can create, edit, move and trash notes in the configured vault without a prompt (permanent deletes ask through Thor' approval prompt); every tool runs the separately installed `obsn` CLI from the same repo (`pip install -e .`), which is not covered by this pin and downloads its embedding model through `fastembed` on first index.

name: oc-free-provider
description: Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for Thor. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and Thor tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while Thor executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

name: oddsradar
description: Polymarket odds in Thor: search active markets, live odds (CLOB midpoint) with 24h/7d moves, volume and a 7-day sparkline, a persistent per-profile watchlist with move, above and below rules (edge-triggered, 1-pt re-arm, one alert on resolution), and alerts that run as a no-agent cron job, so every check costs zero tokens. Agent tools, an /odds slash command and a thor oddsradar CLI share one engine. Read-only: no keys, no wallet, no trading. Disclosure — read-only HTTPS GETs to gamma-api.polymarket.com and clob.polymarket.com, only when a tool, /odds, the CLI or the user's cron job runs (10 s timeout, at most 2 retries on 429/5xx; the client refuses any other host). No credentials. Stores the watchlist at <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/oddsradar/watchlist.json. Only when the user runs thor oddsradar cron-script does it write <THOR_HOME>/scripts/oddsradar-check.py, which runs thor oddsradar check --quiet as an argv subprocess (no shell, stdin closed, 120 s timeout); the user schedules it with thor cron create. No hooks, middleware, background threads, telemetry or self-updates.

name: offense
description: Offense security tools for Thor: free npm/pnpm dependency advisory audits and prepaid hosted security tools (source, infrastructure, target, TLS, API) through the official Offense MCP server, exposed as mcp__offense__* tools. Disclosure — the plugin connects to the configured Offense origin (https://app.purpleteam.sh by default, moving to https://offense.sh) over HTTPS; the free audit sends sanitized dependency names, exact versions and relative paths, prepared by Offense's `offense.mjs` Node helper that the bundled skill tells the agent to run from an Offense checkout or download from the Offense origin (not part of the pinned package; it runs through your terminal tool); hosted tools upload the selected source, artifact, target or infrastructure only after a reviewed quote and an explicit run; the free audit needs no account; OFFENSE_API_KEY is read through Thor' secret store and kept in the active profile; hosted calls spend prepaid Offense credit on your account and are gated by trust: untrusted, a $5.00 per-chat spend limit and a $0.05-$1.00 cost per reviewed quote; no self-updater, no telemetry.

name: offgrid
description: Chat with your Thor agent by plain SMS, with no mobile data, through Africa's Talking, plus a USSD menu as a fallback for basic phones. Texts become normal Thor messages on the offgrid platform, one conversation per phone number, and replies come back as a single SMS (Markdown and emoji stripped, capped at five billed segments). A safe subset of gateway commands works by text: NEW, SESSIONS, RESUME <n>, MODEL, STATUS, HELP and /retry, /stop, /title; every other slash command is refused by default. Disclosure — every question and every reply is sent through Africa's Talking and the mobile network as SMS, in plain text, and each outbound SMS segment (up to five per reply) is billed to the operator's Africa's Talking account (incoming SMS and USSD sessions may also be billed). Requires an Africa's Talking API key, a callback secret and an explicit allowlist of phone numbers; the callback must be reachable over public HTTPS (the listener binds 127.0.0.1:8080 by default, so a tunnel or reverse proxy is needed). SMS sender numbers can be spoofed: a spoofed text from an allowlisted number gets a normal agent turn with this profile's tools and memory (the reply goes to the real number), while commands that change config, approve tools or reveal other sessions are blocked and dangerous commands time out unapproved. Verified in the Africa's Talking sandbox only, not on a live carrier. Uses its own platform name and OFFGRID_* settings, so it installs alongside ussd-platform.

name: office-3d
description: A live isometric office for Thor Desktop: every profile is a person at a desk — a profile doing real work sits typing with a lit terminal screen, an online-but-idle one relaxes in the lounge with tea, an offline one leaves an empty desk with a dark monitor. Click a desk to inspect that profile (state, sessions, tokens, cost) and open its chat or latest session; a cost/tokens leaderboard ranks the profiles; plus a global Total/Working/Idle/Offline overview, a status-bar chip, a palette command with keybind, a settings page with per-profile visibility switches, and an office_status agent tool that reports the same status to the model. Desks are labelled with each profile's own display name when set. Disclosure — the backend and the tool read each profile's gateway_state.json and profile.yaml (display name only) and open its state.db read-only, running aggregate queries (COUNT/SUM/MAX over the sessions table: counts, token totals, cost, last-activity) plus one read of the default profile's in-flight async_delegations task JSON, from which only the target profile label is kept; they never read message content, system prompts or titles, make no network calls, and need no credentials. Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. Runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. The process-liveness check never signals the target: on POSIX it uses os.kill(pid, 0), and on Windows it opens the process with OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and reads GetExitCodeProcess.

name: office-desk
description: Guarded Word, PowerPoint and Excel editing: tracked Word changes and comments, slide and deck edits, and Excel edits with LibreOffice recalc. Every write gets a backup and a revertible receipt, and you review it all on a Desk page in the Desktop app. Settings are in Settings > Plugins. Disclosure: reads any Office file the agent is pointed at but writes only inside folders the user puts on the Desk (backups and receipts live in the plugin's own data dir). xlsx_recalc runs the user's installed LibreOffice (soffice, headless) on a temporary copy. The Desk page reads the session store read-only to show a workstream's chat. No network calls, telemetry, credentials or background processes. Depends on the paper-docx, paper-pptx and paper-xlsx forks. They provide the docx, pptx and openpyxl import names, so they must not share an environment with python-docx, python-pptx or openpyxl.

name: offpeak-bekci
description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in Thor: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger, its own JSONL measurement log, and a read-only look at the profile's cron/jobs.json. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires Thor >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; it reads the profile's cron/jobs.json read-only (on `/offpeak-durum`, `/offpeak-kaldir` and at every session end) to count enabled queue-consumer jobs; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

name: olympus
description: Manage your Thor agents from one dashboard tab: every agent (profile) on one list with its status, current task and tool, helpers and a week of runs; one Needs-you queue of questions waiting on your answer, failed or overdue cron jobs, stalled or failing Kanban workers, blocked or unassigned tasks, offline gateways and looping or expensive runs, each with its action; an inspector per agent; a Live view of every open run with its subagents and their last tool; a Floor with every agent at a fixed place, moving only on recorded tool calls; a Pop out window of the roster that stays on top; and a Performance view of run success, run time, tool failures and cost per agent, each compared with the days before, with the runs behind any day a click away. Controls (pause, resume or run a cron job; answer, retry, reclaim or reassign a Kanban task) are confirmed, logged and executed by Thor' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off. Opt-in alerts run as a Thor no-agent cron job. Disclosure — reads Thor' own stores read-only across every profile under THOR_HOME (sessions and messages in state.db, cron jobs, run output and the usage ledger, the Kanban database, gateway state, config.yaml and profile.yaml, skills, the agent/gateway/error log tails and subagent live transcripts under cache/delegation/live) and writes to plugin-data/olympus/, plus `$THOR_HOME/scripts/olympus_alerts.py` when you run `thor olympus install-alerts`; controls (on by default, each confirmed; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off) pause, resume or run cron jobs and answer, retry, reclaim or reassign Kanban tasks through Thor' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; no network calls to third-party services, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials and no self-updater; never opens a profile's .env (configured gateways come from Thor' own helper, a private import the validator warns on); local labels, task titles, questions and message previews stay hidden unless `dashboard.olympus.expose_local_labels: true`; the Desktop page uses the plugin SDK only.

name: omh
description: Oh My Thor (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a Thor Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider, a dag-ulw run keeper (omh_dag) whose nodes the parent dispatches with Thor' own delegate_task, a data-only search planner (omh_search, no retrieval), and language-server navigation tools (lsp_definition, lsp_references, lsp_diagnostics, lsp_rename) over Thor' own LSP service. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $THOR_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without Thor' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed, which the plugin imports from the directory OMH's own installer recorded) asks once through the Thor approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; the pre_tool_call hook refuses skill_manage edits and deletes of skills OMH installed; lsp_rename applies the language server's workspace edit all-or-nothing, only to files inside the session workspace root Thor' file tools resolve (apply=false previews), and the lsp_* tools (off until OMH_LSP_TOOLS or the lsp_tools setting) drive Thor' agent.lsp service through its private loop, answering lsp_unavailable when that seam is absent; omh_dag reads delegation.max_concurrent_children and state.db async_delegations read-only to size each ready batch and, on a Docker or SSH terminal, runs fixed read-only file and $HOME checks in that terminal without Thor' approval prompt; the memory provider reads the profile's .env, config.yaml and pairing files to find the gateway allowlist when classifying DMs; adds system-prompt sections for delegated children and a per-model calibration block; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

name: omlx
description: Managed oMLX runtime and MLX model library for Thor Desktop on Apple Silicon. Disclosure — on explicit setup downloads the oMLX 0.7.2 macOS app (SHA-256-pinned) from the official jundot/omlx GitHub release and runs it as a long-running loopback server (127.0.0.1, bearer key) under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/omlx; downloads public Hugging Face model snapshots the user names; generates a local API key stored as THOR_OMLX_LOCAL_API_KEY in the profile's .env; "Use" rewrites the profile's default model in config.yaml.

name: omnivoice
description: OmniVoice TTS provider for Thor Agent

name: omonpakari
description: Considerate health context for Thor Agent: barometric pressure (OpenWeather), a typed journal (symptoms, medications, supplements, food, notes), menstrual-cycle windows returned as date ranges, sourced absorption-interaction checks against logged times, the person's own life notes and alternatives, per-rhythm wave states (pressure, cycle, symptoms, sleep, nutrition) and long-term patterns - assembled by a pre_llm_call hook into a short quiet picture before each reply, so suggestions are weighed against the person's body and habits first. No reminders, no pestering; a quiet first word on the host's own scheduled turns is opt-in. Disclosure — Stores a health journal (symptoms, medications, supplements, food, menstrual-cycle marks, life notes) locally in the plugin's own database and adds a short summary of it as context before each reply on attended turns, including gateway turns from any approved sender in shared chats, so the configured model provider receives it and the model may repeat it to other chat participants; scheduled cron turns get it only when first_word_turns is enabled. With an OpenWeather API key and coordinates set, it calls api.openweathermap.org (key and coordinates in the request) from the pressure tool and from at most one background refresh thread per hour during user turns. No telemetry, shell commands or self-updating.

name: on-air
description: AI stream co-host with guarded chat, captions, optional voice, private rehearsal, and operator controls. Disclosure — Runs loopback-only servers (OBS overlay, token-protected operator desk, private-show API) and, when you start a stage, a separate `thor gateway run` process in a dedicated stage Thor home it creates; reads public Twitch chat anonymously from irc.chat.twitch.tv; `thor onair scene` downloads three.js and three-vrm from registry.npmjs.org (sha256-pinned); optional semantic assist (off by default) sends each queued draft, recent public chat and your show policy to api.typesafe.ai when set to `jev`.

name: on-brand
description: Brand voice and compliance rules Thor can't break. Per-brand profiles (person, tone, banned words, exact spellings, required tags, length/emoji/hashtag limits) plus crypto and health compliance packs. A deterministic linter scores every ```copy draft 0-100 before you see it; failing drafts are rewritten by your active model and re-checked until they pass, and off-brand posts sent through outbound tools are blocked with the fixes Thor needs. /onbrand, four agent tools (check, rules, learn, voiceover), a Desktop pane with a live fix/block feed and a status-bar chip. Disclosure — no network calls, telemetry or credentials of its own; drafts that need fixing, the brand rules and samples given to onbrand_learn go to the user's active Thor model through ctx.llm. While a brand is active it rewrites ```copy blocks in replies (autofix can be turned off) and refuses outbound tool calls (names containing send, post, tweet, publish, reply, cast, dm, broadcast, announce, webhook, create_message, discord, telegram, slack) whose copy breaks a hard rule (gate can be turned off). Optional hold_stream setting (off by default) holds every reply in the profile until it has been checked. Stores profiles, settings and the last 60 checks (draft text up to 600 characters each) in THOR_HOME/plugin-data/on-brand/. No shell commands, background processes or self-update.

name: onair
description: Thor inside your OBS. Control scenes, sources, recording and streaming by asking; put cards and chapter titles on stream; design animated scenes or build one from an image, GIF, video or voice line; answer questions about your screen on an overlay; mark the good moments and get the highlight reel, YouTube chapters and a draft title when you stop. Disclosure — Talks only to OBS's WebSocket server at the configured host (127.0.0.1:4455 by default); the agent can point OBS's browser at public http(s) pages it chooses (private and local addresses are refused after a DNS lookup) and see them through screenshots; local pages and pages written by the agent run in OBS's browser only after you approve them; live_ask and the session wrap-up send a screenshot, your question and mark notes to the model configured in Thor; runs ffmpeg and ffprobe from PATH with fixed arguments and a minimal environment to render reels; writes only under the plugin data directory; no telemetry.

name: onda
description: Find the videos that outgrow their author. Onda watches the Instagram, YouTube and TikTok creators you follow and gives Thor their Hits — publications with far more views than the author has followers — along with your Projects, followed creators and plan usage; on your request it runs a new collection or transcribes Instagram videos. Hosted MCP server, browser sign-in with an emailed code (OAuth, no API key); needs a paid Onda plan and one extra command after install: thor mcp add onda --url https://api.getonda.ru/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tool call goes to api.getonda.ru (remote tool list not covered by the pin); run_instagram, run_youtube and start_instagram_transcript spend units or transcription minutes of the user's Onda plan; Onda answers in Russian.

name: onebot-platform
description: QQ bot via the OneBot 11 protocol: connects Thor to your own self-hosted NapCat, Lagrange, LLOneBot or go-cqhttp deployment over WebSocket — the plugin hosts a reverse-WS server inside the Thor gateway, or dials an existing forward-WS endpoint — and adds the qq toolset (qq_send_image, qq_send_voice, qq_send_video, qq_send_file, qq_send_forward, qq_send_segments, qq_napcat_api, qq_group_history) for DM and group chats with admin allowlists, group mention gating, per-member soft limits, and cron/notification delivery to a configured home channel. Inbound messages are parsed from segment arrays with CQ-string fallback; images are downloaded through an SSRF-guarded fetch (private/CGNAT/NAT64 addresses rejected, allow_cidrs escape hatch, per-hop redirect re-validation) with magic-byte extension sniffing and downscaled (Pillow) before the vision tool sees them; voice clips are SILK-magic-checked and converted to 16 kHz mono WAV for the STT pipeline; QQ cards (json/xml segments) are flattened to readable text; stickers resolve to local paths. Outbound replies are never auto-split: a two-tier policy delivers short replies as one bubble and longer ones as a locally rendered text image (fonttools/Pillow, system CJK fonts with platform-aware font chains) with a PNG size cap falling back to single-text; Markdown is stripped to QQ plain text with word-boundary emphasis handling. Includes a per-chat inbound rate limit, a proactive-write gate for the qq_* tools (minute/day caps, JSONL audit, /api/write_gate_stats), <user_message> prompt-injection boundaries (wrap inbound, strip echoed tags outbound), host clarify-tool hooks (numbered-choice card, recall on expiry), and a bundled webapp dashboard settings page (status panel, grouped config forms with write-only secrets, audit viewer). Disclosure — talks only to the user's own OneBot deployment; the plugin's listener (default port 8643) is a long-running background server inside the Thor gateway process that accepts the bridge's reverse WebSocket and also serves the qq_* tools' local HTTP API behind an auth gate, refuses a non-loopback bind without an access token, and limits tool sends from a QQ session to that chat or the configured home channel unless the session is an admin user's private chat; inbound message media are downloaded from that deployment (or the URLs it vouches) into the plugin's data directory for the vision tool; text-to-image rendering runs locally (fonttools, Pillow, system CJK fonts) with no third-party calls; credentials (the OneBot access token, allowed-user lists, home channel) reach the plugin only through Thor's secret scope and ONEBOT_* config and go nowhere but your own OneBot deployment; no telemetry or usage reporting.

name: oneiros
description: Your agent sleeps on it. Nightly proposal-only memory consolidation with morning review, receipts, and one-step rollback. No model calls. Distinct from thor-dreaming. Disclosure — Oneiros reads the profile's memory files, session history (state.db, read-only) and memory-hygiene report files to propose memory edits; when the user enables apply it rewrites MEMORY.md/USER.md inside the active profile under Thor' memory file lock, keeping snapshots, receipts and rollback; no model calls and no network.

name: opaque-composer
description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

name: openaccountants
description: OpenAccountants connector for Thor: today's tax figures for 190+ jurisdictions through the hosted OpenAccountants MCP server. The plugin ships no skills; tax skills install separately, per jurisdiction, from the OpenAccountants agent-skills tree. Disclosure — when enabled, connects to the hosted OpenAccountants MCP server at https://www.openaccountants.com/api/mcp and its tool results enter the conversation; runs no code, needs no credentials, writes nothing. The plugin ships no skills: the README's optional skills step pipes an installer script from the openaccountants/openaccountants main branch into sh, which is outside this pin and not reviewed here. The repository mirrors upstream's plugins/openaccountants-thor bundle every 15 minutes; the SHA pin freezes the reviewed snapshot.

name: openai-compatible
description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

name: openalex
description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

name: openany
description: OpenAny is the B2A (business to agent) marketplace. Add one MCP endpoint, https://mcp.openany.si, and your agent can find and use 3,200+ APIs and 168+ AI models. Searching and checking prices is free with no key. You only need an OpenAny API key to run a call, and you pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) that connects Thor to OpenAny's hosted MCP server over Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.openany.si. Thor discovers openany_overview, search_apis, get_api, and run_api from that server. Auth is OPENANY_API_KEY via the Thor config_schema secret, sent as Authorization Bearer. The server is marked trust: untrusted. Declares Python dependency mcp==2.3.0. No local Python entrypoint, hooks, middleware, self-updater, or telemetry.
