Disclosure — connects to OpenAny's hosted MCP server (mcp.openany.si, Alephant AI LLC) with your OPENANY_API_KEY; every tool call and its inputs go there, and run_api forwards them to the third-party API you pick and can incur a pay-per-call charge. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so calls that are not read-only ask first and are refused in unattended runs. The tool list is served by the remote server and can change without a new pin.

name: openbao
description: Resolve mapped bao:// references from OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault KV v1/v2 into Thor environment variables at startup. Disclosure — makes outbound HTTP(S) calls to the configured Vault/OpenBao address and sends THOR_OPENBAO_TOKEN as X-Vault-Token; never reads .env/auth stores directly, never caches secrets, never prompts, and starts no background process.

name: openchi
description: Guided desk stretches and breathing breaks for Thor Desktop. When your agent takes on a long task, a card below the input box offers a few minutes of stretches; nothing starts until you click. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface). No network calls, agent tools, hooks or env vars.

name: opencode-free-acp
description: Real OpenCode CLI over ACP as a Thor model provider, with curated free-model selection and Thor-owned tool execution and approvals. Independent stdlib transport using only the documented provider API, not an HTTP compatibility client or a handoff to OpenCode's autonomous tools. Disclosure — starts the separately installed opencode acp executable for discovery/inference in the included restricted workspace; forwards the conversation, tool schemas and results to OpenCode and its selected upstream model. The CLI uses its normal HOME/configuration/login and may load user-configured vendor plugins/hooks; its normal network calls, local records and vendor terms apply. Windows batch launchers use the OS cmd.exe with fixed quoted arguments, AutoRun and delayed expansion disabled; processes join a private cleanup Job Object before running. Linux/macOS use an owned process group. These are not OS sandboxes. Child environment is allowlisted; Thor/provider keys and YOLO settings are not inherited. Plugin code reads no credential stores, writes no runtime state, makes no direct network calls, installs no binaries and sends no telemetry. Native ACP permission/file/terminal requests are refused, native tool events abort the request, and selection must be confirmed before inference. This is not authorization to use OpenCode; broader vendor policies can override workspace restrictions, and free availability/pricing/privacy can change.

name: opencode-shepherd
description: Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.

name: opendockit
description: Read local documents as Markdown: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV, HWP/HWPX, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, HTML and email, whole or by page, slide or sheet, with a skill for reading long documents in parts. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs a local stdio MCP server through uvx (opendockit[mcp]==0.3.8 with dependencies resolved as of 2026-11-16, downloaded from PyPI on first start); read-only; reads any file the user can read unless OPENDOCKIT_MCP_ROOTS names the allowed folders; no network when converting, no telemetry, no credentials; no OCR.

name: openinvest
description: Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so Thor asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.

name: openloft-memory
description: OpenLoft Memory — persistent graph-backed long-term memory for any Thor agent. Recall before every turn, ingest after every turn, loft_* memory tools. Works with the hosted OpenLoft service or a self-hosted backend. Zero Python dependencies. Disclosure — while openloft-memory is the active memory provider, each turn's user message, assistant reply and the core-redacted transcript slice (tool outputs included) are sent to the OpenLoft memory service (default https://api.openloft.xyz/api/memory, or the base_url you set) for storage and server-side LLM extraction, and each user message is sent there as a recall query; transcript archiving before compression, MEMORY.md/USER.md mirroring and backfill are off by default; loft_forget stops retrieval but the service retains the data (not erasure).

name: openltm
description: Long-term memory for Thor agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in THOR_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

name: openmail
description: Gives a Thor agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

name: openpaths
description: OpenPaths model provider for Thor: OpenAI-compatible inference at openpaths.io with auto, auto-easy-task, auto-medium-task, auto-hard-task and auto-think task-tier routes plus GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models, live /models listing, and Thor reasoning effort mapped to OpenPaths reasoning_effort. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results and conversation context are sent to openpaths.io with your OPENPATHS_API_KEY and forwarded to the upstream model vendors it routes to; the plugin makes no other network calls and registers no tools or hooks.

name: openrouter-balance
description: Live OpenRouter credit balance in the Thor desktop status bar — "OR $12.34 left", with total/used/remaining on hover, amber below 15% remaining, click to refetch. Polls every 5 minutes idle and refetches ~8 s after each chat turn. The plugin's Python half resolves the profile's OPENROUTER_API_KEY through agent.secret_scope (profile-scope aware, safe under multiplexing; the key never leaves the backend) and proxies the free openrouter.ai /api/v1/credits endpoint, mounted at /api/plugins/openrouter-balance/* behind the dashboard auth gate. The desktop half registers a statusBar.right chip via @thor/plugin-sdk. The Python register() is a no-op — no tools, hooks or middleware. Disclosure — the only network egress is the openrouter.ai credits call authenticated with the user's own key; no telemetry; no file reads outside Thor's own env resolution; no shell commands or background processes. Honest error chips (no key / bad key / offline / error) instead of silent failures; offline retries every 2 minutes.

name: openrouter-everything
description: One OpenRouter key for Thor web search and fetch, image and video generation, voice, decisions, extraction, reranking and embeddings, with per-task model selection and compatibility checks. Disclosure — sends prompts, documents, search queries, web-fetch URLs, audio and media to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai, or the OPENROUTER_BASE_URL relay the user configures) with the user's key, tagged with fixed HTTP-Referer: https://github.com/thor726/Thor-agent and X-Title: Thor Agent (OpenRouter Everything) attribution headers; requests can incur charges. Reads local media the user or agent names (credential files and non-image content refused), writes generated media under Thor' cache, and media URLs returned by the service may be downloaded from other hosts. `thor openrouter-everything setup` saves OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the profile's .env through Thor' own writer, and the setup command, the slash command and the agent-callable openrouter_everything_config tool (activate_all / set_model / reset_defaults) rewrite config.yaml to make OpenRouter Everything the web, image, video, TTS and STT provider (enabling STT and turning off gateway routing for those tools).

name: openrouter-picker
description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Thor secret store or THOR_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

name: openrouter-provider-picker
description: Pick which upstream providers serve each OpenRouter model, per model, from a desktop UI (Settings › Plugins › Provider Routing) or an agent tool. Writes provider_routing and provider_routing.models.<id> into the active profile's config.yaml — the keys Thor already sends as OpenRouter's `provider` request field, and which `thor config set` cannot address because model ids contain dots. The UI lists each model's real upstream providers with their context window and input price per million tokens, and supports a whitelist, a blacklist, and a per-model sort override. The agent tool exposes the same thing as list / providers / set / clear. OpenRouter only: Nous Portal decides routing centrally and ignores caller-supplied preferences. Disclosure — network calls to the public, unauthenticated openrouter.ai API (/api/v1/models, /api/v1/providers and /api/v1/models/<id>/endpoints) to build the model and provider lists, cached in-process; reads and rewrites the provider_routing block of config.yaml in the active profile via the comment-preserving atomic replace, from the Desktop settings page or from the agent tool, which the model can call without an approval prompt to change per-model or default routing (including data_collection and allow/deny lists); no telemetry, no credentials, no self-update, no other third party.

name: openrouter-spend
description: OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the Thor root.

name: openrouter-voice
description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for Thor Agent (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

name: openspec
description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

name: openviking
description: Long-term memory for Thor. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.5.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active Thor static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after Thor exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `thor openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus Thor bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

name: openwall-mcp
description: OpenWall through its MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://openwall.mrhyde.dev/mcp): a giant shared wall, 40,000 px across, where AI agents paint live while people watch. The agent finds free space, plans an artwork at wall scale, paints it with shapes, pixel art or a photo the server converts to pixel art, checks it with a picture of the wall, titles it and returns its link. Bundles one skill for the whole flow and an after-install note. Tested end to end with Thor 0.23 on a local copy of the wall: seven artworks painted from seven requests, plus a seagull added to one of them after a preview with look. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Each agent uses its own key (ow_...), created with Connect on the site and read from OPENWALL_API_KEY, declared as a secret in config_schema and sent as an Authorization header that Thor fills in. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to openwall.mrhyde.dev (closed-source server), and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. What the agent paints, its titles and its name are public on the wall; the server keeps a hash of the key and keyed hashes of IP addresses for rate limits; uploaded photos are converted and the original is not stored; moderation reviews artworks after they appear. The server is marked untrusted, so painting and erasing tools ask for approval (Once / Session / Always per tool).

name: operate-thor-plugin
description: Turn Thor Agent into an autonomous earner and buyer on the Operate.Center marketplace (https://operate.center): publish autonomous, manual, or hybrid service gigs with 3-tier pricing packages and JSON schemas, browse live marketplace operators, poll funded orders and revision requests held in Stripe Connect escrow, lock exclusive execution leases, upload files from the profile's confined outbox_dir and deliver structured output for an 80% creator payout share, check live earnings and human owner Stripe Connect KYC status, outsource tasks by hiring marketplace gigs as a buyer agent, manage order approvals/revisions/messages, and automatically organize downloaded deliveries into a profile-scoped vault (<plugin_data_dir>/deliveries). Registers 11 native tools (operate_create_gig, operate_update_gig, operate_list_gigs, operate_check_queue, operate_accept_job, operate_submit_fulfillment, operate_get_earnings, operate_hire_gig, operate_manage_order, operate_sync_deliveries, operate_heartbeat), a pre_tool_call human-approval and outbox-confinement hook covering money-moving/state/upload tools, the /operate slash command (status, demo, queue, gigs, orders, deliveries, heartbeat) with durable ctx.state earnings telemetry, the operate-center workflow skill, and the safe queue/KYC/delivery monitor blueprint (autonomous-worker). Disclosure — this plugin can spend and release the owner's money on Operate.Center: `operate_hire_gig` buys gigs and `operate_manage_order` approves deliveries (releasing escrow), requests revisions and messages sellers, while `operate_create_gig`, `operate_update_gig`, `operate_accept_job` and `operate_submit_fulfillment` publish listings and claim and deliver paid orders; each of these calls asks for Thor approval first (denied in cron by default) and uploads only files from the profile's outbox directory. Tool calls, `/operate` subcommands and the optional 15-minute `autonomous-worker` blueprint send HTTPS requests to https://operate.center (or the user's configured OPERATE_API_URL) with OPERATE_API_KEY, and `operate_sync_deliveries` / `/operate deliveries` download delivery files from seller-supplied public HTTPS URLs into `<plugin data dir>/deliveries`; when an `operate-mcp` MCP server is configured, tool calls go to it first.

name: operations
description: A Thor Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads thor-metrics-dash's <thor root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <thor root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through thor send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. From the setup checklist's Connect GitLab step it can also adopt this profile's own login - its environment read through Thor' secret scope, or the host the gitlab-mr plugin names - or take a host and token typed on the page; the host goes through the plugin-settings writer and the token through Thor' .env credential route as OPERATIONS_GITLAB_TOKEN, and the token is never sent back to the page. No other credential store is read: a login that exists only in another profile's .env or in the glab CLI's config is typed in instead. Since 0.3.5 the plugin keeps its own metrics store: it tails <thor root>/metrics/requests.jsonl and moa-refs.jsonl, guardrail lines in logs/agent.log, logs/model-router-requests.jsonl and clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl (all read-only, offset-tracked) plus its own host probes (CPU and memory via sysctl/vm_stat or PowerShell, LM Studio's lms ps, and every five minutes the local conformance.yaml's install-stamp, launchd/scheduled-task, loopback-port and key-name checks), and reads session titles and costs from <thor root>/state.db and every profile's gateway_state.json (read-only), into <thor root>/metrics/operations.db, which this plugin alone writes and prunes to the metrics_retention_days setting (30/60/90 days or forever, chosen on the page and written through Thor' plugin-settings writer); thor-metrics-dash's metrics.db is then only a read-only fallback until the own store holds data. It probes the local metrics dashboard's /api/about (METRICS_DASH_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8899, cached five minutes) to link to it rather than duplicate it, and every Thor process that loads the plugin starts a daemon timer: when no kanban dispatcher tick has arrived for two minutes it runs the same sweep itself every 30 seconds (collection, alerts and, with drift_action: automatic, the fix cards), and the page says so; OPERATIONS_HEARTBEAT_TIMER=0 turns that timer off. Since 0.3.4 a failed model call is classified with the host app's own error classifier and shown with its cause and remedy commands; no new outbound call is made for that.

name: opportunity-check
description: Read-only discovery and evidence checks for agent-work listings.

name: optchat
description: OptChat-style endless memory for Thor: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Thor's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $THOR_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

name: optmem-thor
description: Independent Thor integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under THOR_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Thor' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

name: orbit-desktop
description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Thor. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Thor provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Thor tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Thor conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Thor session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Thor Labs logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Thor Labs.

name: orcaslicer
description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Thor Labs. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/THOR_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.thor-orca (THOR_ORCA_HOME), outside THOR_HOME.

name: orphic-eyes
description: Pixel-only screenshot review for Thor: capture URL pairs, inspect changed zones, prepare coding-agent requests and run bounded follow-up review rounds. Disclosure — launches an installed headless Edge/Chrome/Chromium with a minimal environment; captured pages can load network resources and follow redirects (private and loopback destinations only when you set allow_local in the plugin config; link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused); renders http://localhost pages and file:// pages inside your configured file_root (default: the working directory), which can embed other local files; stores screenshots, reports and prompts under THOR_HOME/orphic-eyes and can serve them read-only on 127.0.0.1 with a random token until stopped. No telemetry or credential-store access; prompts are returned, never sent or executed by the plugin.

name: orquehelx
description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider Thor already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with Thor' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.

name: osv-ref
description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

name: otari
description: Use Otari, the open-source LLM gateway by Mozilla.ai, as a model provider, with one key for every model your gateway serves.

name: othigai
description: A fire drill for your Thor agent. /drill starts test agents on your machine with your model and your own SOUL.md, hands them an ordinary errand, and plants a trap in the email they read. Everything they can reach is fake: a fresh fake key, a throwaway folder in the system temp folder, and a listener on 127.0.0.1 standing in for the attacker. A default-no pre_tool_call gate checks every tool call a test agent makes, and you get a safety score with a 95% range, a step by step replay and fixes that the next drill measures. Nothing runs until you read a notice and type /drill yes. Disclosure — test agents make model calls on the model you name or your default, which costs money on a paid model (capped per agent and per drill, with a daily limit); before a drill it runs a harmless `rm -r` of its own temp folder plus curl and /dev/tcp probes to its listener through your session's terminal to check that the approval prompt works, so an approval prompt may appear and the right answer is no; test agents run a short list of commands inside a throwaway folder in the system temp folder; a local listener runs on a random 127.0.0.1 port for the length of a drill; it reads your SOUL.md and passes it to the test agents, and reads which memory provider is configured; test agent sessions stay in Thor's normal history, where memory or telemetry plugins may see the trap text. No third-party network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: oura-mcp
description: Read the user's Oura Ring readiness, sleep, HRV and activity through the local oura MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Oura. Runs the `oura-mcp-unofficial@0.8.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official Oura Cloud API v2. The user creates their own Oura developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.oura-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to Oura's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Thor credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.thor/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.thor/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: oura_profile_update (local profile only); oura_exchange_code (stores OAuth tokens locally); oura_revoke_access (revokes the Oura grant and deletes local tokens). The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

name: overhead
description: What changed at this place between these dates? Measures vegetation loss and gain, burned area by severity (dNBR) and water change in hectares anywhere on Earth from free Sentinel-2 L2A imagery, and delivers a before | after | change panel or a timelapse GIF to every surface, with an interactive before/after swipe and timelapse card in Thor Desktop. Provides the overhead_locate, overhead_scenes, overhead_compare and overhead_timelapse tools, the overhead:earth-watch skill, and post_tool_call / transform_llm_output hooks that append the image's MEDIA line when a reply lacks it. Disclosure — Makes unauthenticated HTTPS requests to the Earth Search STAC API by Element 84 (earth-search.aws.element84.com: scene searches by the area's bounding box, never its exact outline, and dates) and to the AWS Open Data sentinel-cogs bucket in us-west-2 (range reads of Sentinel-2 bands, with ~/.netrc never read), and, only to look up a place name, to Nominatim / OpenStreetMap (nominatim.openstreetmap.org, at most 1 request per second). STAC and Nominatim requests carry the User-Agent `overhead-thor-plugin/0.1.0 (+https://github.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead)`. Place lookups, the pixels read and searches over past date ranges are cached under the plugin's data folder (plugin-data/overhead: cache/ and runs/), which is not pruned automatically. The Desktop card's Open map button opens openstreetmap.org in the browser, only when clicked. Reads a system font to draw panel labels. The plugin itself needs no API keys or accounts, stores no credentials and adds no telemetry; rasterio installs only after Thor dependency consent. For optional visual interpretation, it offers local image paths and questions for Thor's public vision_analyze tool. If the agent calls that tool, Thor may send the selected images and prompt to its configured native or auxiliary model provider; images may include location and date labels, and credentials, costs and privacy terms depend on the user's Thor configuration.

name: own-compute
description: Bring your own compute. For researchers and scientists with a workstation, a lab server or a cluster account. Runs sandboxed container environments, Slurm batch jobs and cloud agents (a Thor agent in a sandbox on the user's own machine, not a hosted service, that hands its work back as a git branch) on SSH hosts, Slurm login nodes, and the Docker or Podman on this computer. Independent of Thor Labs. A Compute page in Thor Desktop shows every machine and what runs on it, and the same actions are chat tools with approval cards before anything starts, changes or is deleted. Disclosure — runs ssh, git and the container runtime (podman or docker), and on Slurm hosts sbatch, squeue, sacct, scancel and srun, on the hosts you add; opens ssh -L tunnels bound to 127.0.0.1 and terminal windows when you click; adds a host's key to your SSH known-hosts file on first contact (accept-new); remote hosts pull container images from public registries; cloud agents send the model key you store as a Thor secret (CC_AGENT_API_KEY or a profile model's key) into the agent's sandbox, where commands the agent runs can read it, and call the model endpoint you choose from inside that sandbox only; one background thread starts on the first tool call or chat turn (reachability checks, Slurm and agent polling, time and idle limits); stores hosts, templates, run records and saved file copies in the plugin's data folder; reads secrets only through the Thor secret scope; no telemetry, no update check, no call to any service run by the author.

name: ownmachine
description: A persistent private macOS or ARM64 Omarchy VM workspace for Thor with SSH/MCP and human-controlled browser access. Disclosure — Runs OpenSSH, using your own SSH config, agent and keys, to an operator-configured Mac host and streams VM screenshots, accessibility text and computer_use input to a guest macOS or ARM64 Omarchy Linux VM through a fixed-command MCP relay; `/ownmachine setup --run` executes remote provisioning stages on the Mac over a separate setup SSH alias; the opt-in `remind later --mode tomorrow` writes a helper script into the Thor `scripts/` directory and creates a one-shot no-agent cron job through the profile's local gateway; it keeps a shared control database in an operator-chosen directory. Licensed PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

name: pagecast-director
description: Editable cast narration with locked voices, source passage IDs, resumable synthesis and selective regeneration. Disclosure — Stores books and generated audio privately in its plugin data. On first use it lists the speech options on this computer and asks which to use; it never picks one for you, and online engines are blocked if you say no online services. To find local speech servers it sends GET /v1/models only to this computer's loopback address (ports 8000, 8880, 5002, 8020 and 8080, plus any local address you set; no redirects, 1 second timeout). Every program it starts gets a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG), never your provider keys. Voices are local (an installed speech program such as espeak-ng, Flite, Piper or say, or a speech server already running on this computer) unless you choose hosted Inworld, ElevenLabs or Google Gemini, which send passage text and voice choices to that provider with your own key and use your credits; the optional Gemini Vertex route uses a Google sign-in that Thor holds for your own OAuth client (thor auth add pagecast-director:google; the plugin never sees the token), sent only to aiplatform.googleapis.com. Can render a short captioned video clip (audiogram) of a finished chapter span into plugin data, with a cover image you point to. Runs local FFmpeg/ffprobe and adb; mpv only plays a preview aloud when you approve it. The optional Android tools check the author's GitHub releases (flabanabba8/PageCast) for the PageCast app and can download the latest APK (checked against that release's own SHA256SUMS); installing it on a phone with adb, replacing a locked voice and playing a preview aloud each ask for your approval (one pre_tool_call hook). No background processes beyond a render or preview you start.

name: pandy-tickets
description: Find events in Guatemala and draft new events through Pandy Tickets' official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://tickets.pandy.cloud/mcp, no sign-in, no keys). Public event search, checkout links, and event creation tools. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to tickets.pandy.cloud and the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. The public tools (search-events, get-event, get-checkout-link) need no sign-in; draft-event creates a draft the organizer must claim and publish. The bundled skill also documents Pandy's organizer REST API: with an organizer API key that has write permission, the agent can publish events, issue tickets, record refunds, cancel orders and message attendees.

name: pantheon
description: Let Thor exchange messages and agree on outcomes with other agents in a shared Pantheon chat. Disclosure — Sends chat messages, files you upload (from the session's working directory, up to 1 MB each) and static site bundles (up to 20 MB) to pantheon.talk, where other chat members can read them; saves files received from other members under the profile's plugin-data/pantheon/downloads; when you enable incoming replies (plugins.entries.pantheon.allow_gateway_injection), a background thread polls pantheon.talk and wakes the conversation with a prompt to read new messages, and the plugin resets that setting to its prior value after your last connection ends.

name: parallax
description: Multi-perspective fact-vs-frame lens, blind code security taste-test, and rubric-gated DPO/SFT dataset forge

name: parallel-search
description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside Thor's native web providers.

name: paranoy
description: Read and write a Paranoy evidence ledger from Thor: search, file and link claims, evidence and contradictions in shared collections, with roles (Scout, Claim Miner, Linker, Gap Finder, Fool, Ponder, Ledger) and optional capture of chat messages as evidence. The agent's Nostr key stays in Thor as a declared secret; writes are signed in-process and the model never holds the key. Disclosure — calls go over HTTPS to {server_url}/mcp (default https://paranoy.org/mcp); paranoy_fetch_url asks that server to fetch a public http(s) URL; writes ask a person first by default and are refused in cron unless allow_unattended_writes is on; capture (off by default) auto-publishes admitted human messages and claims extracted from the agent's answers when enabled, and by default also rewrites the agent's final answer with a second model call against claims retrieved from the shared collection; rejects, journal, role checkpoints and overview.md are written under the plugin data directory. No telemetry, shell commands, self-update or core overrides.

name: parcel-deliveries
description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

name: pareto
description: Pareto Inference as a Thor model provider (`--provider pareto`): GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and MiMo V2.6 Flash over OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, pay per token, with /reasoning mapped to Pareto's reasoning_effort levels and context windows from models.dev. Disclosure — model provider; registers one provider profile at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Thor sends prompts, tool results and a GET /v1/models catalog request to api.paretoinference.com with PARETO_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads or writes no files and adds no telemetry.

name: parlor
description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

name: parrotnotes
description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: pass-secrets
description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Disclosure — When enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; registers a pre_gateway_dispatch hook that consumes `!secret`/`/secret` messages before gateway auth and, only for senders listed in the plugin's `chat_allowed_users` setting (empty = off), writes the value into the pass store with `pass insert -f` (a `shared/` entry becomes an env var in every agent at next start); no network.

name: passkey-gate
description: Approve your agents' risky actions with your phone's passkey, even when you're not at the agent's keyboard. An agent asks for approval of an exact action (and optionally the exact command); you get a link in any chat, read it on your phone and sign with Face ID, a fingerprint or your screen lock; the agent then verifies your signature locally against your pinned key before acting. A relayed 'the human said yes' proves nothing; only your signature counts. Optional enforcement blocks matching tool calls until you approve them, and each approval runs once. Includes a guided `setup` wizard, a background service, a hash-chained audit log, and approvals between agents owned by different people. It is an honest approval record, and becomes a hard boundary only when agents can't modify the gate (see the README's Security model). Lanes choose which conversations need a passkey: you at the keyboard, your own chat accounts, other people, bots or other agents. Disclosure — runs a small web server on 127.0.0.1 that your phone reaches over HTTPS (by default published to your own tailnet with `tailscale serve`); can install a background service (systemd user unit or LaunchAgent) that runs as you; runs `tailscale`, `systemctl --user`/`launchctl` and a short Python process to time new patterns, never with elevated privileges; contacts only its own address and any peer gates you allowlist, follows no redirects, no telemetry; stores passkey public keys, requests, the pinned key, an audit log and a remote-minting token in its plugin data folder (no private keys); its hooks note each turn's platform, sender id and bot flag in memory only; with enforcement on, any failure blocks the call; only your pinned passkey can approve, and anyone with an approval link can read and deny that request; patterns are a best-effort list, not a sandbox.

name: pastdotdev
description: past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-thor/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

name: patch-sentinel
description: Measures the host, not the source tree: code review asks "can an attacker exploit this code?" and this asks "is this machine running what the vendor shipped?" — the two are complements, never substitutes. Answers "are we patched?" with evidence, for whatever the host runs — an adapter chosen from the host's own /etc/os-release (apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, apk), the running kernel against the newest installed and installable, whatever advisory names the fixed version per release (Ubuntu notices, OSV per release, Bodhi, Arch's tracker, SUSE's OVAL), container image digests, nine language ecosystems through OSV plus lockfile pins, package checksums and listening sockets against a recorded baseline, and a CycloneDX SBOM. Every check has three outcomes — clean, finding, could-not-look — so an unreachable host, an unimplemented distro or a rate-limited registry reads as unknown rather than clean. The pane reads one device at a time and hands over the exact commands per device; a gated cve_apply tool stages, applies, re-measures and writes a receipt for an agent explicitly asked to patch. Linux only: any other OS answers "unsupported" with its name. Disclosure — scans run fixed read-only commands on this machine and, over your own ssh agent, on hosts you list; package names and versions go to api.osv.dev, api.first.org and the distro advisory sites (ubuntu.com, bodhi.fedoraproject.org, security.archlinux.org, ftp.suse.com, cisa.gov); cve_apply, after Thor's approval prompt, runs the distro's full upgrade with sudo -n on the chosen host; scans, receipts and SBOMs stay under $THOR_HOME/patch-sentinel (mode 700).

name: patchreview
description: Routes recognized file-writing tool calls through Thor' native human-approval gate with a proposed diff. PatchReview never exposes model-callable accept tools and never writes target files: on approval, Thor executes the original tool through its normal write path and protections. Full-content and exact string-replacement previews support replace_all; unsupported or unparseable recognized calls are blocked. Coverage is limited to recognized tool names and does not intercept shell commands, scripts, or unrelated processes. The plugin makes no network calls, sends no telemetry, invokes no shell commands, stores no credentials, and starts no background processes.

name: patchsmith
description: Adds `implement_task` and `apply_patch`. The first hands a single well-specified coding task to a local model served through Ollama (the measured backend) and returns the resulting diff. Propose mode runs in an isolated temporary checkout, preserves the source checkout, and saves a full patch for review. The second tool applies an approved saved patch only after hash, base, affected-file and path checks. The local model works inside a fixed toolset with no shell (read, grep, glob, git status/diff, write/edit, run the configured test command, finish) under hard turn and total token budgets shared across up to three fresh-context attempts. An optional local model is used only on the final allowed attempt; failures return a factual handback. Includes a path jail, read-only test files, an auto-finish when tests go green, a repeat-call guard, and revert of partial edits when a run is blocked. Your main model spends tokens only on the instruction and the returned diff. Disclosure — runs git and the owner-configured test command (PS_TEST_COMMAND, never chosen by the model; it executes project code on the host) as subprocesses in the working directory with a minimal child environment plus an owner passthrough list (PS_ENV_PASSTHROUGH); in direct mode a local model writes implementation files inside the given workdir (never .git, node_modules, test files, .env* or .ssh/; the Thor home, the user home and filesystem roots are refused as workdirs) and a run transcript with file excerpts under <workdir>/.patchsmith/; propose mode copies the checkout to a temporary Git worktree and keeps the patch, provenance record and transcript under <thor home>/plugin-data/patchsmith/proposals/, with run summaries under <thor home>/plugin-data/patchsmith/runs/. Task text and file contents go only to the local model endpoint set in PS_ENDPOINT (loopback or private-network address; public and link-local hosts refused). inspect_hardware runs fixed OS probes (nvidia-smi, sysctl, system_profiler, PowerShell CIM) and reads the endpoint's model list. No telemetry, no self-update, no stored credentials.

name: patsnap
description: Patent and scientific-literature search through Patsnap's own hosted MCP server: prior-art and landscape searches across WIPO/EPO/USPTO/CNIPA/JPO/KIPO and more, paper search (PubMed, Nature, arXiv and others), assignee resolution, corporate trees and a patent's legal lifecycle, with a bundled patsnap-search workflow skill. Needs PATSNAP_API_KEY from the Patsnap Open Platform. A Thor Labs plugin: built by Thor Labs, not supported. Disclosure — connects to connect.patsnap.com over HTTPS and sends your queries and record ids there under your key (every call spends Patsnap credits); gets only PATSNAP_API_KEY from your profile and sends it in a request header, never in the URL; no local processes, files or telemetry.

name: pay
description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`thor mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a Thor profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: pay-cli
description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: Thor starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

name: payops
description: Read-only Paystack transaction inspection and reconciliation for Thor agents. Disclosure — read-only payments integration: sends the user's PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY (read through Thor's secret route) to api.paystack.co only, issuing GET requests for transactions and settlements; it cannot create charges, refunds or transfers. No other hosts, no files written, no telemetry.

name: pcs-security-tls-posture
description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

name: pdf-shrink
description: Shrink a PDF to a size limit (2 MB, 500 KB, whatever the upload form says) with everything running locally — no upload, no API key, no third-party service. Two tools and a bundled skill. pdf_inspect reports what makes a file heavy: image share of the bytes, the resolution each image is actually displayed at, fonts, embedded attachments and duplicates, with a verdict (images dominate / images not reclaimable / vector-heavy / already small) so a shrink that cannot work is caught before it runs. pdf_shrink downsamples images it can re-encode safely to the resolution they are displayed at, recovered by replaying each page's content stream (q/Q/cm/Do, including nested Form XObjects), then walks a measured ladder of DPI/JPEG-quality rungs from the mildest down and keeps the first that fits — each rung rebuilt from the pristine original, so the copy is one generation of compression rather than six. Text, fonts and vector art are never rasterised; images that cannot be re-encoded safely (JBIG2, CCITT, 1-bit or non-8-bit samples, soft/stencil masks, /Mask, /Matte or /Decode arrays, CMYK and other print colour spaces, tiny logos) are left byte-for-byte alone. When the limit cannot be reached without making the document unreadable it stops at the safe floor, reports the smallest safe size, saves that copy when it is meaningfully smaller, and names the levers that can actually help (a reachable higher target, or aggressive=true when it can do better) instead of handing back mush. Every copy is re-opened and verified (page count, blank pages, structural syntax) before delivery; a copy that fails is reported as failed, not as a success. The source is re-hashed before and after every completed run, and a change is reported rather than claimed untouched. A before/after render of page 1 comes back when PDFium is available and a verified copy was written. Writes only new files; an existing output path is refused, never overwritten. Ladder rungs are built in a private system-temp directory, never beside the PDF; a read-only source folder still works, and the default output falls back to the current directory when the source folder cannot be written. An explicit output_path must end in .pdf, and a location that Thor's own write denylist refuses is rejected before anything is written. The only destructive option is drop_attachments=true, off by default.

name: pdf-surgeon
description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Thor installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.

name: peakflo-spaces
description: Hand off repetitive finance and operations work to cloud agents or people through Spaces by Peakflo's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.peakflo.ai/mcp, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with PKCE, no keys in config): create one-off or recurring (cron) tasks and get a link to follow them, list workflows and their runs, query workspace data tables with read-only SQL, pull aggregated reports on bills, invoices, payables and receivables, search policy documents, and review pending approvals. Bundles the spaces workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Peakflo's hosted server (api.peakflo.ai) and acts on the user's Spaces workspace with their own role and permissions; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Spaces does not move money, make payments or trade. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only (creating tasks, running workflows, completing approvals, writing data) and refuses them in unattended runs. No telemetry.

name: pending-queue-monitor
description: Desktop-only, read-only monitor for pending memory and skill write approvals. Disclosure — the pane's API reads pending/memory/*.json and pending/skills/*.json under the default Thor root and every named profile directory beneath it (all profiles, not only the active one), and returns only counts, age buckets, oldest age, and per-item profile/subsystem/id/action/origin/created_at/age_seconds. It never returns or displays summaries, payloads, or record content; it exposes no approve, reject, or delete actions; it registers no tools, hooks, or middleware, performs no network I/O, and holds no credentials.

name: penguin
description: A penguin in Antarctica keeping an eye on everyone's time: deterministic IANA conversions, whole-meeting overlap windows, profile-local teams, and an optional Desktop planner with side-by-side clocks, Commander dispatch and proposal-only completion. Reads bundled artwork, non-executable IANA 2026f data and its own plugin state. Optional user-started AI-generated music and a halftone sky use bundled audio and offline analysis; no microphone access. No external runtime requests, shell commands, credentials, telemetry or calendar writes.

name: penny
description: Penny core memory and private notes for Thor. Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a Thor approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <THOR_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.

name: penthera
description: Offline, rule-based security checks run through the terminal: a repo scan, dependency capabilities, a passive scan of a URL you own, and an audit of your AI agent config (skills, MCP servers, hooks, permissions). A skill only: no tools, hooks, middleware or MCP server. It runs the pinned penthera npm package with npx, which downloads that package on first use (Node.js 22 or later). Rules decide every finding; a model never does. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no background process, no self-updater. Disclosure — the skill runs the third-party `penthera` npm CLI pinned at 2.4.0 through `npx -y`, which downloads it from the npm registry on first use and runs it on the host outside Thor' sandbox; it reads repo files and local agent configs (`~/.claude`, `~/.cursor`, `.mcp.json`), makes passive requests to URLs the user names, and, when the user approves, edits code on a local branch or installs a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` hook.

name: pep-ref
description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

name: pepper
description: Say “parlay this” to find a ParlayTix ticket or preview two outcome rights for one you own. Resume the same split across chats, review a listing for the other side in your wallet, or set a budget watch and ask for updates. Disclosure — crypto-adjacent ticketing: talks only to the ParlayTix hosted MCP server (mcp.parlaytix.xyz, OAuth via Thor) and can preview/create ticket splits that mint outcome-right NFTs on Base, prepare checkout and listing reviews, and create/activate/answer Scout watches; payment, purchase and listing signing happen in the user's ParlayTix wallet, and write calls are gated by Thor approval only when the server is configured `trust: untrusted` as the README instructs.

name: perf-hud
description: Live performance HUD for Thor Desktop: a status-bar chip with core-compatible TPS (sum of output tokens over sum of API durations for the last 10 completed calls, the same window and arithmetic as Thor' own status bar) in `tps`, `tps_ttft` or `calls` form, and a statistics popover with TPS, a separately labelled Session Avg TPS (the same ratio over every call in the session), median TTFT from `first_chunk_at`, LLM calls, an `Agent steps*` compatibility alias (equal to LLM calls, footnoted inside the snapshot by `agent_steps_note`), turns, errors, input, output and cache-read tokens, cache hit rate on Thor' `cache_read / (cache_read + input)` buckets, tool calls and tool time, tool time share, wall-clock session duration, and the model and provider. Two controls — Reset current statistics (clears the plugin's own in-memory counters, never Thor session state) and Clear history — plus local performance history for the last 50 sessions. Observes only: nine observer hooks, no tool or message is ever blocked, rewritten or reordered, no Thor core file is touched, the aggregation layer is pure with no I/O and no host imports, all handlers are fail-open so a telemetry bug cannot break a turn, and a corrupt history file is quarantined instead of raised. Disclosure — reads only from the observer payloads: token usage buckets (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning), API and tool timings, first-chunk timestamps, model and provider names, session ids, and tool names plus error status for the counts; prompts, model responses, conversation contents, tool arguments and tool results are never read and have no field in its snapshot, its desktop event or its history record. Writes exactly one JSON file per profile at `<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-perf-hud-*/history.json` containing only session_id, model, provider, started_at, updated_at, duration_ms, ttft_ms, tps_core, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_hit_pct, tool_time_ms and llm_calls, allow-list enforced, atomic, capped at 50 sessions; no other disk writes, and no config change beyond the documented `plugins.entries.perf-hud.settings.*` keys (chip_enabled, chip_metric, history_enabled, history_max_sessions, poll_ms, broadcast_min_interval_ms). Desktop updates travel over Thor' in-process plugin event bridge (`broadcast_plugin_event`, topic `plugin.perf-hud.stats.update`, throttled to 400 ms) and its REST routes are served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/perf-hud/ (snapshot, sessions, history, config, reset, clear-history, status), which requires the dashboard's auth ticket. Executes no subprocess, no shell command, no systemd unit, no Task Scheduler task; makes no network request; has no credentials, no OAuth and no telemetry. Standard library only, no third-party dependencies.

name: permission-canvas
description: Per-control permissions for the computer_use tool. In a native panel you preview the target window privately, click any control and set it to Allow, Read only, Ask first or Hide. The backend enforces the choice before every input and before a screenshot or accessibility tree reaches the model: read-only controls refuse clicks, typing and value changes; ask-first operations wait for a one-time human approval of the exact action and arguments; hidden controls are removed from the tree and their pixels masked, and a capture that cannot be masked reliably is refused. New profiles start paused with unknown controls set to Ask first. Select it with computer_use.backend: permission-canvas; adds the /pc-canvas and /pc-approve commands. Validated on Windows with cua-driver 0.21 and 0.39. Disclosure — launches cua-driver (telemetry disabled) and a bounded Windows accessibility helper as local subprocesses while the backend runs, reads the selected window's pixels and accessibility data, stores policy, approval records, an audit log and the latest redacted capture in its own data directory, and opens a local Tkinter panel on /pc-canvas; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry. Protects only actions routed through this backend; it is not an OS sandbox.

name: permission-tiers
description: Host-enforced tiered tool permissions: assign allow/ask/block tiers to tool-name patterns (fnmatch globs), and the plugin's pre_tool_call hook vetoes or escalates matching calls before they execute, while post_tool_call keeps a local SQLite audit ledger. Two tools manage it: permission_tiers_report (rules + ledger) and permission_tiers_set (add/update/ remove). Implements the per-tool permission-levels feature requested in issue #527 without touching Thor core — public hooks only. Safe defaults: shell and MCP tools ask, everything else keeps Thor' existing behaviour; hook errors fail open; unattended runs fail closed on ask escalations (the plugin never auto-approves). Disclosure — no network calls, no third-party services, no stored credentials; reads/writes only its own tiers.json and ledger under the Thor plugin-data directory; bundled permission-tiers skill documents usage.

name: personae
description: A messenger-style roster for Thor Desktop: one row per profile with its live sessions, per-profile colour, status lights, search, groups, multi-select and an Apropos beta that starts a new session already knowing the ones you picked. Disclosure — a Desktop pane over all your local profiles: it reads each profile's sessions, cron jobs and settings through the app's own requests and, only when you click, deletes or archives sessions (deletes ask first), changes cron jobs or edits profile settings; Apropos starts a new session with a hidden pointer message naming the sessions you picked; no network calls or telemetry.

name: personal-assistant
description: A remote personal assistant for your agent: it does the errands up to the final page and stops at your yes. It interviews you once ("grill me": eight short sittings on your business, people, decision rights, preferences and calendar rules), remembers corrections, people, SOPs and trust levels in a local ledger, and never asks the same thing twice. Travel and errands on real sites in English, Japanese and Korean: restaurant tables (TableCheck, Tabelog, OpenTable, Catch Table), hotels and flights on Trip.com, taxis, food and konbini delivery, with sourced prices, an approval packet for each action and an honest handoff at a sign-in, OTP or app-only wall. Optional Chief of Staff mode adds a daily plan, a weekly closeout and a radar. Adds the pa and pa_call tools, the /pa command and 42 skills (the Chief of Staff ones load only in that mode). Disclosure — Keeps its records in a SQLite ledger in your profile (state/travel-ledger/travel.sqlite): trips, prepared actions, setup answers and the chat setup runs in, preferences, people, SOPs, trust levels, call cards and transcripts, task evidence and receipts; its shell ledger helper, which skills run for payment-readiness and connectivity records, also stores browser checkpoints (page URLs, session ids), budgets and which providers hold a card. Optional features add a delivery packet queue (full packets, including priority-mail excerpts, never pruned), Daily Ops config and state, and a client index (names, emails, domains). Owner-memory and evidence records refuse recognised card numbers and credentials, records written through pa pass a lighter pattern filter, helper and approval records are kept as given, and nothing is deleted automatically. After you approve a setup review or a Chief of Staff closeout it writes USER.md, a marked PA section of SOUL.md, an operating-manual skill (or an edit of your existing one) and any context file you name, holding your approved business, people, spending-limit and approver answers as plain text, and pins the manual with thor curator pin; a trip export writes Trip.ics and Trip-Reference.md to a folder you choose; /pa mode writes the plugin's mode setting. A pre_tool_call hook sees every tool call and blocks only tools covered by a PA exact-action approval or its deny list, plus most tools while the ledger is unreadable; a pre_llm_call hook adds short notes to your own turns (setup offer and routing, and on a session's first turn, including another person's first turn in a shared chat, your preferences and people not yet in your files) and records which chat setup runs in. With your consent during /pa setup the agent reads USER.md, SOUL.md, its memory, the calendar, past itineraries, a context file you name and up to 20 recent sent emails (PA stores no raw mail); mail work you ask for reads messages and attachments; accepted Daily Ops routines sort unread mail twice a day and send you a digest of five lines or fewer; drafts are written only if you opted in during setup (gog's gmail.compose scope, which can also send), and every send, archive, delete or label change needs your yes for that item; during a provider sign-in it may read your connected email or SMS for a link or code; accepted Chief of Staff jobs run scheduled turns that read PA's ledger and your USER.md or manual, may read your calendar and inbox, and search the web for your radar topics. Calendar writes need your yes for each item and go only to calendars you opted in to (gog's calendar.events scope), with one standing exception: during trip work the agent may add minimal private trip events (flight and hotel times, check-in and leave-for-airport reminders, no details or guests) without asking each time. The agent creates Kanban tasks for open commitments, and with your approval may adapt an existing brief cron job. Errands drive Thor's browser tools on provider sites (Trip.com by default for flights and hotels, then airline or hotel sites or local sellers; reservation platforms, maps and guides for restaurants; another regional domain if blocked), in the local browser, agent-browser on Browserbase or another attended browser you configured, and provider sign-ins you give in chat are saved in the agent's credential lane and browser profile. What the agent reads and writes goes to your configured model provider as part of the conversation. Other network calls happen only when you ask or opt in: Browserbase (api.browserbase.com) with your BROWSERBASE_API_KEY and BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID, recording off for sessions PA creates, sessions kept alive up to 20 minutes, connect and live-view links visible to the model; PA holds no Google token and makes no Google API calls: the agent reads and writes calendars with the profile's own calendar tools, and Daily Ops reads them through the gog CLI (gog auth add stores gog's own credentials); parallel research subagents for SIM comparisons; Open-Meteo for an accepted trip watch; ElevenLabs read-only from the manual phone_poll command, with the declared ELEVENLABS_API_KEY read through Thor's secret accessor; and opt-in Daily Ops (gog mail and calendar reads, with selected mail and calendar items sent to your model provider and email addresses aliased by pattern; Nominatim and OSRM through curl after geo consent; Stripe and Supabase CLIs after consent). Background work only after a yes: an accepted trip watch arms a HeartBeat 2.0 watcher that, once you allowlist it, runs a local PA script every 15 minutes for at most 14 days, and its notices wake an agent turn (a flight change may look up rebooking options, never book), plus optional check-in and arrival wakes; opt-in conversation delivery injects packets into one verified Telegram session as agent turns, with priority-mail excerpts not aliased; opt-in Daily Ops routines and an optional watchdog on the schedule you accept (every 20 minutes or less when leave-by alerts are on); accepted routine suggestions run a local precheck every 5 minutes (scripts stay in the profile's scripts/ folder); approved follow-up wakes (Chief of Staff, and open-loop follow-through wakes created only for a date you approve in chat). An accepted daily brief also sends an end-of-day note after eod_time (default 18:00) unless the brief itself is set after it, and accepted due-action checks also wake the agent for open-loop chase steps (day 2, 5 and 10, then an escalation), which only remind you or hold a nudge draft for your yes. Updates go through thor plugins update; the version probe is read-only; developer eval scripts call model providers only when run by hand, with a token you pass in an environment variable (the optional lab judge runs the Codex CLI on its own sign-in), and PA code reads no saved login; the manual scripts/check_release.py reads this repo's GitHub releases through the gh CLI's own sign-in. PA's skills stop bookings, payments, reservations, orders and cancellations at the final page for your explicit yes, and its pre_tool_call gate enforces exact-action approval for actions a PA workflow has scoped; nothing dials a phone. No telemetry. Full list: the README's "What it touches".

name: pethost
description: Deploy and run Docker Compose projects on Pethost with its skill and Pethost's hosted MCP server: deploys, logs and requests, rollbacks, backups and restores, domains and commands in containers. Disclosure — connects Thor to Pethost's hosted MCP server (mcp.pethost.dev), signed in by OAuth through `thor mcp add pethost --url https://mcp.pethost.dev/mcp --auth oauth`, with no key or token in the package; the package marks its server untrusted, but that native entry replaces it and runs at trust: full unless mcp_servers.pethost.trust is set to untrusted, as the README's install does; tools act on the account's machine (deploys, restarts, restores, deletions, commands in containers); to move files the skill has Thor run tar and curl in commands the skill writes, only to https at the machine's own hostname (*.pethost.network) under /transfer/, never a command the server returns, and says before an upload that the project folder goes as it is, .env included; it also has Thor generate app secrets with openssl in the user's shell and fetches a deployed site to check it.

name: pfwa
