description: Provably fair randomness for Thor, plus prediction markets on Robinhood Chain. pfwa_random gives a number, coin flips, winner picks from a list or a shuffle from a drand evmnet (League of Entropy) round chosen before it existed, with the round, signature and derivation so anyone can recheck it: for giveaways, raffles, draws and tie-breaks an LLM would otherwise make up. Market tools list PFWA's open markets, read live prices onchain, show a wallet's positions and claimable winnings, list results, and build unsigned buy, sell or claim transactions for the user's own wallet to sign; two more read HoodRand requests and the live Sherwood game round. Native Python plugin, standard library only, no keys and no configuration. Disclosure — Crypto: reads PFWA prediction markets on Robinhood Chain and builds unsigned buy, sell and claim transactions that you sign in your own wallet; it never holds keys or sends transactions. Network calls go only to www.pfwa.fun (the PFWA agent API), rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com (read-only eth_call; wallet addresses you ask about are sent in balanceOf calls) and drand's public relays (api.drand.sh, api2.drand.sh, api3.drand.sh).

name: phoenix
description: Transactional SQLite WAL flight recorder, pre/post SHA-256 state fingerprinting, live idempotency guard, and deterministic fault-injection wind tunnel with Zeller ddmin for Thor agents. Guarantees exactly-once tool execution across crashes with zero duplicate writes and zero LLM calls in recovery. Disclosure — journals every tool call's arguments and result (common secret patterns redacted) to a local SQLite ledger under the plugin data dir, kept 7 days / 10,000 rows; the owner-typed /recover re-runs interrupted tool calls from earlier sessions through the tool registry, bypassing other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks, and the opt-in idempotency guard can return a stored result instead of re-running a repeated call in the same session.

name: phone-autopilot
description: Teach your phone a task once and replay it with no model in the loop: routines with checkpoints, repairs through the agent when an app changes, a daily automation blueprint and a live phone pane. Builds on phone-harness. Disclosure — runs model-written routines (Python you approve per version) on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package, which taps, types and runs adb shell commands on your real phone; its pre_tool_call hook puts every save and first run through Thor's approval prompt and prepends a foreground-app guard to phone_exec scripts, which stops at Android permission dialogs and, only if you turn on ask_before_apps, pauses to ask before any app you have not allowed; the guard runs inside the script as a guard rail, not a sandbox; run environments drop variables ending in _KEY, _TOKEN, _SECRET or _PASSWORD and keep the rest; stores routines, image refs, run records with screenshots and your app answers in its plugin data folder, reads the screenshot files the agent names when saving image refs, reads its settings from config.yaml and changes them only through Thor's plugin settings writers; the dashboard phone pane can tap, swipe and press keys on the phone when you use it; no network calls or telemetry of its own (phone-harness telemetry is switched off for routine runs); Pop out starts scrcpy if installed.

name: phone-harness
description: Drive a real phone from Thor with one phone_exec tool: an iPhone via iPhone Mirroring on a Mac, an Android over adb, or a cloud phone from Phone Harness Cloud. Disclosure — runs model-written Python on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package (installed from PyPI); every phone_exec call goes to Thor's approval prompt unless you opt in to classifier auto-run, a heuristic, bypassable check that decides which scripts ask first; taps and types into your real phone and its apps and accounts; screenshots go to the system temp folder and are attached to the tool result for vision models; a cloud phone streams its screen to Phone Harness Cloud and uses phone-harness's own cloud sign-in (~/.config/phone-harness/auth.json), and the push_file helper uploads a file from this computer to Phone Harness Cloud's file store to open it on the cloud phone; a cloud Android bills by the minute, and a cloud iPhone is a per-phone subscription; phone-harness's PostHog telemetry (script text, script output, helper arguments, errors, an install ID, and your cloud account and session IDs when signed in) is off under Thor unless you opt in.

name: phone-senses
description: Give Thor your own Android phone's senses through Termux:API: notification and SMS digests, sending SMS from your SIM, a bank and UPI money tracker with bill, subscription and delivery tracking, scam SMS warnings, a scam-in-progress tripwire (unsaved caller + screen-sharing app + OTP or debit, spoken warning on the phone), low-battery alerts and find my phone. Disclosure — needs the separately installed Termux and Termux:API apps (F-Droid) and runs the repo's own stdlib-only helper on the phone, which executes fixed termux-* commands (no shell) and serves an HMAC-signed HTTP API on the address you choose (plain HTTP: replies with SMS, contacts and location are unencrypted on that network, so use Tailscale or a trusted Wi-Fi); the plugin talks only to that helper; reads notifications, SMS, call log, contacts, clipboard, location and battery and returns them to the model; can ring the phone, speak, post notifications and set the clipboard without asking; sending SMS, calls, photos and OTP reveal always go to Thor's approval prompt (OTP reveal is also off until you enable it); OTPs are masked by default; parsed transactions (no message text), budgets, watch rules and approved photos are stored in the plugin's data directory; no telemetry.

name: photo-to-part
description: Photo to Part for Thor: turn photos, a few measurements, or a messy 3D scan into a parametric printable part, and check the mesh locally before you print. The agent writes the solid in code, checks that it is watertight and the right size, and renders views you can hold next to the original. Six tools: photo_part_template (watertight starting shapes such as plates with holes, an L-bracket, a print-in-place hinge, thread, knurl, hex standoff, bottle cap, spur gear and strap hinge), photo_part_build (runs one local build script after Thor approval), photo_part_validate (watertightness, shell count, size, bores, printability and spec.json dimension checks), photo_part_render (fitted views, a comparison sheet and a silhouette overlay scored against your photo), photo_part_heal (weld, fill holes and clean up a scan) and photo_part_measure (pixels per millimetre from a coin, a ruler or an ArUco/AprilTag marker). Output is STL or 3MF; a STEP solid needs CadQuery or build123d in the project environment. A millimetre value you state is never replaced by a photo measurement. Thor Desktop 0.23 or newer can show an optional Part studio pane with the stage, photo and overlay, renders, history and file paths while a run is in progress; the six tools still install and run when that pane is unavailable. It is for makers replacing a broken clip, bracket, knob, cap or gear, printing a fit test, or turning a scan into a clean solid. To start, run thor plugins install photo-to-part and enable it, then start a new session. Attach a photo with a coin or ruler in frame, give any dimensions you know, and ask for a printable replacement. The skill id is photo-to-part:photo-to-printable-part. Pass that exact string only to skill_view. Do not pass it to skills_list, and do not add a plugin: prefix or a slash. Disclosure — files and network: tools read and write only the paths you pass (STL, 3MF, PNG, JSON), plus progress notes in a .photopart folder inside those project folders and a pane index under the Thor plugin-data folder. Build scripts run with a minimal environment that carries no provider keys. No credentials and no printer connection. Enabling the plugin installs its Python packages from PyPI after Thor dependency consent. Installing CadQuery or build123d for a STEP solid downloads packages and can take several minutes. Chat photos still go to your model provider. In a session that uses the plugin, it adds short tool-call budget notes (a 40-call default) to other tools' results. Disclosure — build approval: photo_part_build asks for approval before it runs a local Python file with a timeout. Thor --yolo auto-approves a build prompt; this plugin does not block that flag.

name: photofresco
description: Edit images in a PhotoFresco window you approve: layers, masks, selections, adjustment layers, previews and PNG/PSD export. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with a local stdio MCP server and bundled skill; needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium 120+. Disclosure — opens https://photofresco.com/app/ (remote web editor, live code not covered by this pin) in a separate Chrome/Edge/Chromium profile under ~/.local/share/photofresco-connector (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/PhotoFresco Connector), with cookies/sign-in/autosave kept there; previews and document state the agent requests go to your model provider; with the Send/Spend permissions granted in the PhotoFresco window, AI ops spend PhotoFresco credits up to the budget you set and cloud/feedback ops send document data to PhotoFresco, and Thor does not prompt before those calls; with Export granted, quick-export ops save to the browser's download folder; no local folders are readable or writable unless you add --read/--write yourself.

name: physis
description: Offline evidence-backed execution memory: per-repo graph context, a deterministic verify hook, and verified tool recipes that replay with zero provider calls and refuse when their tools, registry or captured files changed. An opt-in pre-reasoning packet (pre_context) and an edit-following graph (auto_observe) are off by default; the packet reads an existing index only and is skipped when the graph is stale or retrieval is weak. Two bundled Linux engines and no API key or model download; approved host commands still run with host privileges and Python entry points need an interpreter, and untracked dependencies are not replay-checked. Operator-only approval and replay; the model cannot set executable paths or trigger raw commands. Disclosure — Ships two compiled Linux x86_64 engines (bin/physis-core, bin/replant) built and attested by the repo's own GitHub workflow; operator-approved replay commands and the operator's verify_cmd run as shell commands with the user's file and network access; physis_ingest can read shell history, ~/.claude/projects transcripts, every process's command line and the browser history database only when the operator enables those sources in plugins.entries.physis.settings.ingest_sources (off by default).

name: pickwise-photos
description: A correction tool, not an art critic: culls a folder of photos locally. Flags blurry and unrecoverable shots, labels what an edit could rescue, keeps the best frame of every burst and explains every decision. Follows a brief in your own words ("concert, dark is fine, best 30", "moody low-key shots") and learns gradually from your corrections. Treats RAW+JPEG pairs as one photo, handles folders of thousands of photos in resumable steps, and reads JPEG, HEIC and camera or iPhone RAW (DNG, ARW, CR3, NEF and more) through their embedded previews, using only Pillow and pillow-heif. On request it makes local previews so Thor can take a visual second look for closed eyes, a blurred subject or clear composition mistakes. Disclosure — reads image files in the folder you name (any folder the agent can reach; symlinks and hidden files skipped); writes only a Pickwise/ subfolder inside that folder (copy or reversible move) or .xmp rating sidecars that never replace existing ones; never deletes, overwrites or edits photos. The dry-run-then-confirm step is a tool argument the agent sets, not a Thor approval prompt. Stores per-photo measurements, reports, learned preferences and (only when asked) downsized previews in its plugin data folder; no network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry. A visual check sends the chosen previews to the model provider through Thor' own vision tool. Raises Pillow's image-size limit to 300 MP for the whole Thor process.

name: picky
description: Picks the best place to sleep (tonight or for your dates) and the best ride there, then sets up the reservation: real OpenStreetMap stays auto-ranked by OSRM drive time with a one-line why and backups, Uber/Bolt/Lyft options with rough fare and ETA estimates, and Booking.com/Airbnb/Expedia/Google Hotels links prefilled with dates and guests. Never books, never pays, never asks for a card: you make the final tap. Disclosure — sends the place names or coordinates you ask about to nominatim.openstreetmap.org (geocoding and a backup stay search, max 1 req/s), overpass-api.de and fallback overpass.kumi.systems (nearby OSM lodging), router.project-osrm.org (driving) and routing.openstreetmap.de (walking). When use_current_location / 'my location' is requested, also contacts ipinfo.io or ipapi.co once for a city-level approximate location (used once, never cached or stored). Returns (does not contact) www.booking.com, www.airbnb.com, www.expedia.com, www.google.com (Maps, Hotels), m.uber.com, lyft.com, bolt.eu, wa.me and www.openstreetmap.org links. No API keys, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-updater, no binaries. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

name: pilot
description: Give Thor a real interactive terminal. Pilot runs commands inside a private tmux server, so the agent can drive programs that need a TTY: ssh logins, vim/nano, htop/btop, fzf, less, package installers, ncurses menus and REPLs. It types literal text and named keys, reads the pane back as plain text, and keeps sessions alive across tool calls; a human can attach to the same pane and take over. The suite exposes 24 tools for session control, scripted expect flows, scrollback search, snapshots/diffs, logging, signals, resize, health and base64 file transfer. Disclosure — Pilot starts a private, profile-scoped tmux server as your user and runs model-requested commands and keystrokes in it (each one asks for your approval); terminal text, including output from remote hosts, enters the model's context; snapshots, pane logs and downloaded files can hold sensitive output and are kept under plugin-data/pilot; pilot_upload can type a local file into a remote session after approval.

name: piloterr
description: Web scraping for Thor through the Piloterr API. piloterr_fetch_page fetches any page with the crawler (plain HTTP), rendering (headless browser) or webunlocker (anti-bot) engine; 53 more tools return structured data from Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, LinkedIn, Instagram, X, GitHub, Pinterest, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, AliExpress, Target, Best Buy, Crunchbase, Trustpilot, G2, Similarweb, Indeed, Glassdoor, Yelp, Expedia and Zillow. Also a backend for the built-in web_extract tool. Disclosure — sends each URL and the tool arguments to api.piloterr.com with your PILOTERR_API_KEY, and calls use Piloterr credits (1 to 3 per call, stated in each tool description). Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 54 tools and a web_extract backend, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: pinned-folders
description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

name: pinocchio
description: Pinocchio is the honesty layer for Thor Agent: it keeps the receipts for everything the agent does and holds the agent's closing claims against them. A post_tool_call hook records work evidence for every session (commands and exit codes, test runs, builds, file writes, git operations, deploys); a transform_llm_output hook extracts the checkable claims in the agent's closing message (all tests pass, the build succeeds, a file was updated, changes are committed, it is deployed) and stamps the delivered message verified, unverified, or contradicted, citing the most recent matching receipt; a pre_verify hook bounces a contradicted claim back once on coding turns so the agent re-runs the failing step or corrects the record, and an all-time nose counter tallies the contradicted claims. Two tools (pinocchio_report, the session truth table, and pinocchio_receipts, the recorded evidence), a /pinocchio command (report, receipts, nose), and a bundled pinocchio-honesty skill that teaches the agent how to earn verified stamps. No second model grades the first: verdicts are deterministic comparisons between the agent's own words and its own tool receipts, in pure Python standard library. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands spawned by the plugin, no background processes, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only storage is a local SQLite database in the active profile's plugin data directory holding tool-call metadata (tool name, truncated command or target, status, exit code, timestamp) and the claim snippets it stamped.

name: pinpoint
description: Audit mode and Design mode for the live page in Thor Desktop's Browser pane. Measure it with in-page audits (contrast, tap targets, alt/labels, overflow, small text), pin findings on the real elements, point at any element to inspect its live box model, typography, layout and contrast, send a pin or an instruction to the agent, and re-audit to get a score delta, a pasteable receipt and a per-pin outcome: fixed (no longer reported and the same element signature is still present; not a re-measurement), gone (element signature missing, never counted as a fix) or not rechecked (unverifiable, stays open). Disclosure - Pinpoint's desktop half runs its own audit script inside the web page open in Thor Desktop's Browser pane, only after you allow it for that site (Desktop's per-origin consent dialog; revocable under Capabilities > Plugins). The script reads computed styles, layout, the page's visible text, and the values of the attributes id, name, href, src, alt and aria-label (plus title and placeholder when it works out an element's accessible name); it contains no cookie access and does not read form-field values, and it draws an overlay. Findings (CSS selectors, short element labels that can contain page text, measured values) are stored locally in a SQLite file under the plugin-data folder (`pinpoint/data.db`; at most 20 pages, 200 pins and 50 audits per page; entries older than 7 days are pruned). They are sent to the model only when the agent calls `pinpoint_audit`/`pinpoint_pins` or when you click Fix, Fix all high or Send in the Desktop pane (or its command-palette action); an event raised by the page itself never sends a chat turn. Pinpoint also adds a short hint to the system prompt that names its two tools. The desktop half polls the page every 0.5-1 s while pins are shown (via `executeJavaScript`) and re-audits automatically after page changes (switch off in the pane). `pinpoint_audit` blocks up to 90 s waiting for the Desktop (configurable) and returns `desktop_unavailable` when no Desktop window answers, including under cron. No network calls, no subprocesses, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no files written outside plugin-data; it never edits your source (the agent does, under normal approvals). Limits: verified on Windows 11 with Thor 0.22.7 only (macOS and Linux are untested). Results are a limited heuristic audit, not WCAG certification, and fixed / gone describe what this engine observed, not a guarantee about your page. Disclosure — Pinpoint's desktop half runs its own audit script inside the web page open in Thor Desktop's Browser pane, only after you allow it for that site (Desktop's per-origin consent dialog; revocable under Capabilities > Plugins); the script reads computed styles, layout, the page's visible text and the attributes id, name, href, src, alt, aria-label, title and placeholder, not form-field values or cookies, and draws an overlay. Findings (CSS selectors, short element labels that can contain page text, measured values) are stored in a local SQLite file under the plugin-data folder (pinpoint/data.db; at most 20 pages, 200 pins and 50 audits per page, pruned after 7 days) and reach the model only when the agent calls pinpoint_audit/pinpoint_pins (pinpoint_audit can also return the live box model of a model-chosen CSS selector) or when you click Fix, Fix all high or Send in the Pinpoint pane or its palette actions; an event raised by the page never sends a chat turn. The plugin adds a short hint to the system prompt naming its two tools. The desktop half polls the page every 0.5-1 s while pins are shown (via executeJavaScript) and re-audits automatically after page changes (switch off in the pane). pinpoint_audit blocks up to 90 s waiting for the Desktop (configurable) and returns desktop_unavailable when no Desktop window answers, including under cron. No network calls, subprocesses, shell, credentials or telemetry, and no files written outside plugin-data; it never edits your source (the agent does, under normal approvals). Verified on Windows 11 only; results are a heuristic audit, not WCAG certification.

name: pioneer
description: An inverted search for your own work. Pioneer reads your project folder, Thor memory and recent chats, then looks for what does not exist yet and should. Your own model writes the gaps. Code checks every citation, runs an absence check against existing tools, and scores need, originality, counterfactual value, value and durability. When an existing tool already does the job, the board says so and names it. Rounds expand into a trail, shown on a Desktop page and pane. Disclosure — reads your project folder (README, agent rules, manifests, recent commit subjects), Thor memory files and the title and first message of your last 14 days of chats (state.db, read-only) to build its seed for your own model; model-written search queries go to hn.algolia.com, api.github.com and api.openalex.org by default (api.firecrawl.dev and the api.typesafe.ai judge only when you turn them on).

name: pipefire
description: Pipefire (pipefire.ai) is cold email software for agencies that sets up and runs outreach for you. This plugin connects Thor to Pipefire's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://pipefire.ai/mcp) and adds two skills. 16 free email deliverability tools with no account or key: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI and MTA-STS checks, blacklist lookups, email header analysis, cold email and subject line scoring, sending domain ideas and DNS record generators. Pipefire customers can sign in with OAuth to read campaigns, replies, mailboxes and results. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to pipefire.ai. The free tools look up public DNS and blacklist data. Account tools see only the signed-in team's data; the plugin stores no credentials. Every tool is annotated read-only except pause_campaign, resume_campaign, create_campaign (draft only), redraft_reply and request_lead_list; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before any of them runs and refuses them in unattended runs. Sending and launching happen only in the Pipefire console. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: pit-crew
description: Proactive, safety-gated car agent: live state, a "will I be ready?" planner, a background watcher and approval-gated commands, with Home Assistant, Teslemetry/Tessie, TeslaMate or a built-in simulated car. Disclosure — once you switch it live with `/car live`, Pit Crew sends real commands to your vehicle (unlock, trunk, frunk, vent, Sentry-off, honk and flash go through Thor's approval prompt and follow your approval setting), and its background watcher polls your configured Home Assistant / Teslemetry / Tessie / TeslaMate endpoint and posts alerts to the chats you bind.

name: pixel-hq
description: Gamified headquarters for a Thor bot fleet: a pixel office of rooms and departments that you arrange in the page (Edit layout with drag and drop, live numbers per department: members, active, blocked, average HP, XP) and a class-based sprite per profile; each bot's character card shows its configuration (model pin, skills, toolsets, MCP servers) and edits its SOUL.md with a diff preview, a second confirming click and a restorable history; XP, levels and HP are scored automatically from Kanban outcomes (completed, changes requested, gave up, timed out, hallucinated references) plus optional pass/revise/fail reviews you give from the UI or that an orchestrator records with the `pixelhq_review` tool; a live board of what every bot is doing right now (current step, last tool call, tokens/cost, sub-agents, Kanban heartbeats) with Open session, Talk to this bot and Ask for status (prepares a draft, never submits it); a leaderboard; a blocked-card triage across all Kanban boards with Answer & unblock / Retry / Comment / Archive and a 'triage run' that opens a chat with your orchestrator profile; a GPU/LLM reactor panel; and an Update available notice for Pixel HQ itself. Works on a fresh installation: the roster is generated from your profiles, edited in the Roster tab, and settings live in the Desktop app. Disclosure — reads every profile's config.yaml (model name) and state.db read-only (session titles, current step, tokens/cost and the last tool call with its first argument, e.g. a terminal command or path, clipped to 160 characters), every Kanban board database read-only, and the reviews ledger (plugin-data/pixel-hq/reviews.jsonl, plus an optional legacy ledger path you configure); through Thor' own calls it reads a bot's profile (profiles.describe: SOUL, model pin, skill/toolset/MCP server names) when you open its Config section and the plugin list (plugins.manage list, at most every 6 h) for the update notice; no shell commands for reading; network only to the Prometheus / model endpoints you configure (none by default); bots on other hosts only through the Desktop app's own connections; writes only (a) the reviews JSONL under plugin-data when you rate a session or bot (or when an agent calls `pixelhq_review`), (b) plugin-data/pixel-hq/roster.json and its one-generation backup when you click Save or Reset in the roster or layout editor, (c) a bot's SOUL.md only through Thor' profiles.configure after a diff preview and a second click, with the previous version kept in plugin-data/pixel-hq/soul-history/ (newest 10 per bot), and (d) Kanban changes only from your clicks in its page and only through `thor kanban comment|unblock|archive` (unblock/retry/archive need a second confirming click; the workspace is backed up into the plugin's var/ before archive; audit log in var/actions.jsonl); the triage button opens a new chat with your orchestrator profile and submits a prompt with card ids and a host-built filter sentence only, and that agent then reads card text (untrusted) via the plugin's blockers.py; session actions never submit a prompt; no telemetry, no self-update, no credentials.

name: pixel-worlds
description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Thor Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

name: plagio
description: Gives the agent the real design of any public website through plagio's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://plagio.dev/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): capture one component or a whole page as a specification to rebuild from, read a site's brand tokens and animations, find references from a curated library, and read what the user saved with the plagio browser extension. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to plagio.dev under the user's account, which needs a paid plan after a 7-day free week and counts credits. All seven tools are read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: plan-mode
description: Plan mode for Thor Agent: it explores read-only and writes a plan, and its edit tools stay blocked until you approve. Approval comes as a Claude Code-style card; Thor' Codex app-server runtime and TUI /background and btw side agents are outside the block (see the Disclosure). It works on every interactive Thor surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Thor tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .thor/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Thor approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets Thor' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress; on Telegram, Discord, Slack, Desktop and the TUI a live progress card lists the plan's steps and updates as each one finishes. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use Thor' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions (say "grill me" for more, or set questions: thorough for an interview before every plan, one decision at a time), the reply names any tool call plan mode blocked (Thor itself shows none), and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, questions, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). When an approved plan finishes, the reply ends with one line of steps done and files changed (counts only on chat platforms); /planmode list shows the newest plans with their status, and the agent can read its own state with plan_mode(inspect) or list. Classic CLI enforced on every supported Thor; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Thor v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 or newer recommended, tested through 0.23.1. On the interactive classic CLI, Thor' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Thor' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Thor seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .thor/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .thor/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state, plus the status of up to 200 plans for /planmode list, in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. While an approved plan runs it posts one progress message through Thor' post_message and edits it in place (progress_card: false turns it off). When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Thor core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and thor serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file; if another plugin holds the stream to withhold commentary, that text can include the commentary it kept off screen (plan_profile: classic turns plan_once off, unless a custom levers list names plan_once or all). On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that Thor printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.

name: plan-usage
description: Plan usage across providers in the Thor Desktop status bar: a named chip per Claude and ChatGPT/Codex account in Thor's credential pool (5-hour and weekly windows from Thor's own usage cache via model.options, a default-account star and 90% / fallback warnings that name the next account), Nous Portal credits, and month-to-date (UTC) API spend from optional Anthropic / OpenAI Admin keys. Preferences are a Settings -> Plugins page. Disclosure — its own network calls go only to api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/cost_report and api.openai.com/v1/organization/costs, and only with the optional ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY / OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY config_schema secrets read through get_secret, with redirects refused; Nous credits come from Thor's build_credits_view (Thor makes the Portal request); never reads or sends a subscription token, never opens .env or auth.json; writes only its own settings in plugin-data, the shown-warning ids in Desktop plugin storage, and, on an explicit star click, the credential-pool order through CredentialPool.move_entry; no subprocesses, no telemetry.

name: planejamais
description: Review and update strategic plans (perspectives, objectives, initiatives, steps), Kanban boards, tasks and checklists, events, meetings, reports and support tickets in Planeja+ through its official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://planejamais.planejareconsultoria.com.br/api/mcp, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with DCR and PKCE, no keys), with the planejamais workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a Planeja+ account. Disclosure — the server exposes write and delete tools limited to the signed-in account's companies and role, invite_company_user e-mails an invitation and mentions notify members; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`thor mcp add planejamais`) replaces that entry with a native one at the default trust unless the user sets `mcp_servers.planejamais.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a Thor profile share the Planeja+ sign-in; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; no telemetry.

name: plansift
description: Exact, local review of OpenTofu and Terraform plans before apply, from the JSON of a saved plan (`tofu show -json` / `terraform show -json`). tf_plan_summary gives exact counts per action, every delete, replace and forget with the plan's reason and the attributes forcing the replacement, drift detected outside the tool, changed outputs, failing checks and the modules and resource types with the most changes; tf_plan_changes gives an attribute-level before/after diff (JSON policies stored in strings are diffed inside), filterable by action and address and paged; tf_plan_check gates the plan on denied actions for address patterns, a change budget, drift and failing checks. Sensitive values, text under secret-like attribute names, variable values and output values are never returned. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs tofu or terraform), no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local plan file you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Thor' core read denylist.

name: plastis3d
description: A local 3D scene editor for Thor Desktop, with agent tools to build and edit scenes. Disclosure — the assistant can import a 3D model file (.glb, .gltf, .obj, .stl, .ply, .splat) from any absolute path on the Thor machine into a scene; Plastis3D keeps scenes, copies of imported models and images, drafts, renders, screenshots and GLB exports in `<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/plastis3d/`, which stays after the plugin is removed; it makes no network calls.

name: playbox
description: Collaborate with other people's Thor agents in a private room: share a git repo, run sandboxed tasks, and keep a signed, tamper-evident history. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package wrapping the local 'playbox mcp' server, with a host/guest workflow skill. Requires the separately installed playbox binary. Disclosure — runs the separately installed `playbox mcp` binary (installed by the user from github.com/Epistetechnician/playbox releases; v0.1.0 is checksum-checked but not signed); hosting opens an iroh endpoint reachable through n0's public relays and discovery by default (`transport: local` keeps it on the LAN); a host started with a runtime (`docker`, `libkrun`, `openshell`) runs commands from invited remote members in a no-network, resource-limited sandbox on the host machine; git bundles, patches and chat are exchanged with invited members, and their text is untrusted input; keys, histories and room state are written under `~/.playbox`.

name: plugin-safehouse
description: Runs one local Thor plugin inside a disposable, canary-seeded macOS profile; invokes its registered handlers and reports observed file, environment, network, process, persistence, and model-context behavior as FLAGGED, REVIEW, INCONCLUSIVE, or NO_FLAGS_OBSERVED. Disclosure — the model-callable `safehouse_trial` tool (and `/safehouse`) executes the chosen local plugin's register() and handlers without a Thor approval prompt, inside a short-lived macOS sandbox-exec worker with a scratch HOME/THOR_HOME, fake canary credentials and a minimal environment; the sandbox profile is allow-default with network, fork/exec, signals to other processes, LaunchServices and writes outside a temporary trial root denied, so files outside the user's home and non-LaunchServices system services remain reachable; the trial root is removed afterwards. The report returned to the model includes short candidate-controlled text (handler return values up to 300 chars, worker stderr tail up to 1200 chars) with canary tokens redacted. It imports PluginManager and calls the private _scan_directory/_load_plugin loader inside the disposable worker so the candidate registers through Thor' real loader; this is a disclosed compatibility risk. The installed plugin makes no third-party network calls, stores no credentials, sends no telemetry, and starts no long-running background process. Optional repository-only launch scripts invoke local ffmpeg.

name: plugin-scout
description: A scout goes ahead, reports what's useful, and warns about trouble. Plugin Scout finds the plugins that fit how you use Thor (each pick with its evidence), and checks: it tells you what a plugin does with your data before you install it, warns when a plugin's fine print does not fit your settings, catches plugins that clash and explains what to do. Quiet weekly note, plain-English requests, and a dashboard tab. Recommends only; never installs or enables anything. Disclosure: one network call, a GET of the public catalog index from thor-agent.thor-agent.local (redirects to nousresearch.github.io/thor-agent; any other address or redirect is refused), cached 6 hours. Reads, read-only, the last 30 days of session history (up to 200 sessions) to count tools used and topic keywords locally, plus Thor memory files and the user's own (non-bundled) skill list for the same local topic matching, plus config.yaml (enabled plugins, memory provider, and settings named in plugins' known issues), other plugins' plugin.yaml and plugins/.install-metadata.json. Writes only its own plugin-data folder and plugin state. The dashboard tab adds routes under /api/plugins/plugin-scout on Thor's own local dashboard, behind its sign-in; the only changes they make are your onboarding choices and skipped picks. Optional ai modes send topic counts and public catalog descriptions to the user's configured model; message text is never sent. No shell commands, credentials or background processes.

name: plugin_foundry
description: Turn a narrow plugin request into a native Thor plugin: manifest, entry point, tool, SQLite state, tests, static scan and catalog draft. Two archetypes only: a SQLite folder watcher and a JSON API poller, each with one tool. The folder-watcher parser accepts one explicit supported file type or complete dotted suffix and refuses unsupported, composite, conflicting or ambiguous requests. A trailing period is removed only at request end or before validated supported follow-up instructions. Sentence boundaries are detected before a capitalised token or complete instruction verb, but that detection alone does not permit removal; other prose fails closed, and abbreviations without a sentence start stay inside the instruction. Writes stay under the Foundry data root, generated tests run in a minimal environment, and paths outside the root need a pre-tool approval. Provides pre_tool_call and post_approval_response hooks plus the public tool_execution middleware for trusted call IDs. Foundry itself makes no network requests. Installing or cataloguing generated code is a separate human step; nothing is auto-merged.

name: plur1bus
description: Profile-scoped long-term memory and Langzeitgedächtnis for Thor: Memory Engine, semantic search and recall, automatic capture, embeddings, reranking, Semantic Lens, Layer 1.5 (Schicht 1.5), Continuity Engine, Emotion and memory dynamics, Persona Voice, consolidation, Dream Echo, Obsidian and Skill Workshop. Includes a Desktop memory browser, model and storage settings, and diagnostics. Disclosure — records and indexes live in the active profile by default; configured remote embedding, reranker and model routes (OpenAI-compatible hosts, api.cohere.com, a local oMLX server by default) receive the text needed for their task; opt-in Jev automatic chunking sends capture text (up to 60,000 characters per message) to api.typesafe.ai; model setup downloads weights from huggingface.co; approved Skill Workshop proposals are written as skills into the profile's skills folder; the separate OpenClaw migration commands can rewrite the profile's SOUL.md and install per-user launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler jobs; an optional, user-run script builds a separately patched copy of Thor Desktop (the plugin works without it).

name: pmp-handoff-bridge
description: Verify selected PMP handoff files, detect workspace drift, and persist reception receipts. Reads/writes the explicitly authorized workspace; no network or credentials.

name: pocket-platform
description: A native Thor platform for an owner-enrolled low-bandwidth radio companion: bounded chat replies, notes and opt-in P2/R2 home-music controls. Requires a separately provisioned radio/USB bridge and a new dedicated, unrouted, in-process Pocket-only Thor home. Model tool execution is blocked in that dedicated process; installation alone does not block unrelated tool calls. Disclosure: the adapter listens on a private local Unix socket with peer-UID and HMAC authentication. POCKET_HMAC_KEY is read through Thor's scoped secret helper; the bridge is provisioned independently. Local request identities, notes and replay state are journaled. Optional location reads an operator-set SQLite snapshot; optional music reads approved local files through an existing loopback HTTP service. Normal chat uses the operator's Thor model/provider and may leave the host and incur provider charges. No arbitrary model tools, shell commands, self-updater, telemetry, bundled firmware or media. The source includes bridge libraries, not a turnkey standalone radio service or handheld firmware installer. The source qualification uses synthetic provider/HTTP fixtures and does not certify this published package's physical RF or audio.

name: pocket-watch
description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under THOR_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

name: pocketbook
description: Personal finance in Thor: a Finance tab, bank/account controls, spending, budgets, net worth, investments, goals, transaction categories, CSV imports and 15 money tools. Disclosure — contacts Plaid (sandbox.plaid.com or production.plaid.com) with your own keys when connecting, syncing or disconnecting banks; each bank's Plaid access token is written to the profile's .env through Thor' save_env_value and read back with the secret scope; reads user-selected CSV files up to 20 MB; stores financial data in the profile's plugin-data SQLite database; offers optional scheduled alert and digest blueprints, and on request has the agent read Amazon order history through Thor browser tools signed in to your accounts; disconnecting a bank or removing an import from chat asks for Thor approval. No telemetry, money movement or shell subprocesses.

name: podcast
description: Turn any article, PDF, paper, notes or the day's news into a mastered two-host podcast episode: neural voices per host, speaker-aware pauses, intro chime, -16 LUFS loudness, embedded chapters and a timestamped transcript in one MP3. Includes an audio-overview skill and a daily news-briefing blueprint. Script text is sent to Microsoft's online Edge text-to-speech service via edge-tts (no account or key); episodes stay local. No telemetry. Disclosure — episode script text (every spoken line), voice names and rate/pitch are sent to Microsoft's online Edge text-to-speech service via edge-tts (no account or key); the voice list is fetched from the same service and cached for 7 days; audio, transcripts and metadata stay in the plugin data directory; uses ffmpeg from PATH or the user's ffmpeg_path setting.

name: pokeit
description: Real-time Pokémon GO hunting inside Thor, with a live Radar, nearby catches and raids, approved scans, and desktop alerts. Disclosure — hosted-only connector to the author's PokeIt service: each tool call sends coordinates, place text and filters to https://mcp.pokeit.cc (tool list served at runtime, not covered by the pin; request_scan starts a scan and goes through Thor approval; the service keeps tool names, filters, timings and result counts about 14 days and scan coordinates 24 hours); on Desktop a gateway-side read proxy calls the same server's read tools and fetches species icons from https://pokeit.cc, the embedded map loads tiles from https://tile.openstreetmap.org (revealing the viewed area and IP), the last spot, radius and filter are saved locally per profile, and a user-started watch polls about once a minute for up to two hours while Thor runs; no credentials, shell commands or self-update.

name: policy-backtester
description: A test harness for Thor guardrails: what a rule would break, and what it would miss, on your agents' real work. thor backtest try replays the current profile's past tool calls through a policy, names the completed cron or Kanban jobs it would have broken and the sessions it would have caught, checks it against known calls it should stop, then starts it in shadow, which logs and changes nothing; log says when every scheduled job has run untouched, and enforce blocks or hands the call to Thor's approval gate. Enforce refuses a policy that hasn't run in shadow, would break a job, or hasn't seen every scheduled job run. Built-in guard rules keep an agent from switching its own guard off. run, diff, suggest (exemptions pinned to each broken job's exact command and folder, never applied) and check (one call, or a cases file for CI) are the tools under it. Disclosure — reads the state.db, cron/jobs.json, cron/executions.db and Kanban board databases of the profiles a command covers, read-only (SQLite mode=ro); writes its own index (<root>/backtest/index.db, 0600) and, in profiles where you promote a policy, the policy copy, promotions.jsonl, decisions.jsonl and three plugin settings; the index and log keep tool names, arguments (file bodies replaced by a length, commands unredacted) and result status, never result bodies; in shadow or enforce mode its pre_tool_call hook checks every tool call, and enforce blocks calls or sends them to Thor's approval prompt. No network calls, no shell commands, no telemetry.

name: polign-recall
description: Recall by Polign memory provider. A new statement replaces the old one, the old one stays in the history, and memory can be read as of any earlier time, so the agent sees the correction, not just the latest value. Memories in front of each turn, extraction after it, mirroring of MEMORY.md, and five memory tools. Local database under the profile by default, or a recall serve you run. Disclosure. Each turn is sent to the extraction model named in the profile (Anthropic or OpenAI key from .env, or a local Ollama model); with no model, text is kept as written and nothing leaves the machine. On first use the recall binary downloads polign-server from dl.polign.com and checks it against a SHA-256 built into the binary. Disclosure — each completed turn (up to 4,000 characters per message) and every built-in memory write is sent to the extraction model picked from the profile's Anthropic or OpenAI key (or a configured Ollama model; set extract_model to none to keep text local), or to the recall serve named by RECALL_URL; in the default local mode the polign-recall package's bundled recall binary downloads polign-server from dl.polign.com on first use (checked against a SHA-256 built into the binary) and starts it as a detached loopback server under $THOR_HOME/recall that keeps running after Thor exits.

name: pollinations
description:
Pollinations image generation and editing for image_generate.

The picker is read live from the Pollinations catalog, so it lists whatever Pollinations publishes and follows changes without a plugin update. No key is needed for the free route, which watermarks images and throttles per IP. A Pollinations key unlocks the rest of the catalog and image editing. Paid-only models stay hidden behind a toggle that ships off. Disclosure — sends prompts and any reference images to Pollinations (gen.pollinations.ai, image.pollinations.ai); with no key the free classic route is used (prompt in the request URL, watermarked, throttled per IP). A reference image given as a URL is downloaded from that host first (public addresses only, through Thor' SSRF guard) and a local reference path may be any image file the user can read (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, checked by magic bytes); both are then uploaded to Pollinations. With POLLINATIONS_API_KEY set, generation and editing spend the account's Pollen; the "Include paid models" toggle only hides paid-only models in the picker, a paid model set by id is still billed. Caches the model catalog and free-model list under $THOR_HOME/cache/ and writes images under $THOR_HOME/cache/generated/images/. No telemetry, no shell, no background processes, no self-update.

name: polydesk
description: Agent paper-trading desk for Polymarket: research a market, quote a trade against the live CLOB order book (fills sweep real book levels, so slippage is realistic), confirm with a single-use 5-minute ticket that is re-priced at execution, then track mark-to-market P&L with automatic settlement when markets resolve. Risk limits (max trade, max % of equity per outcome, max slippage, liquidity checks), a persistent ledger, a /desk command and a bundled workflow skill. The paper bankroll can be backed 1:1 by testnet USDC in a linked Base Sepolia wallet. Disclosure — HTTPS GETs only to gamma-api.polymarket.com and clob.polymarket.com (the client refuses other hosts); when polydesk_wallet is used, JSON-RPC eth_chainId/eth_getBalance/eth_call (USDC balanceOf) to sepolia.base.org or the configured rpc_url, which receives the linked public address; stores a SQLite ledger in the profile's plugin-data/polydesk/desk.db; no keys, signing, transactions or real orders. Paper trading only; not financial advice.

name: polyglot
description: Live interpreter for group chats on the Thor gateway (Telegram, Discord): an authorized user sends /polyglot on in a group, and every message from a sender Thor admits is then translated into each other member's reading language, returned as the reply. Languages are learned from each person's first message or set with /lang; "thor, ..." or an @mention still reaches Thor as a normal question. Translates with the user's own Thor model; a Sarvam AI key is optional for Indian languages. Disclosure — registers one hook (post_gateway_admission, so it runs only after Thor's authorization) and two commands (/polyglot, /lang), no tools; in chats where an authorized user ran /polyglot on, message text from admitted members goes to the configured model provider through Thor's ctx.llm, and, only if SARVAM_API_KEY is set, text for Indian languages goes to https://api.sarvam.ai; translations are posted back to the group as the bot's reply, and ordinary group messages in those chats no longer start an agent turn; stores each group's member languages and display names in Thor's plugin state; no file reads, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: popquiz
description: Pop Quiz, the room vs the models: any document becomes a live quiz for the whole room in about a minute. Thor writes the questions and the plugin refuses every question whose quote is not found verbatim in the document; people join from their phones with a QR code (no app, no account) while up to four Nous Portal models play the same questions on the same clock, with latency and cost on screen (a free preset plays models the Portal prices at $0); the report says what the room got wrong and which model understood the document best, for what cost. Disclosure — runs an aiohttp web server on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default while a quiz is up (it stops 10 minutes after the game ends); "Open to phones" (the /popquiz command, or the agent calling popquiz_control open_lan without an approval prompt) adds one listener on the machine's private LAN address (never all interfaces), plain HTTP, and from then on anyone on that network can watch the projector page (questions, source quotes, room code), join as a player and read the end-of-game report; the host page and host commands need the host token and a loopback client (with a public_url tunnel every visitor arrives as loopback, so only the token protects them); model players are ctx.llm calls on your Nous Portal account, started when the game starts (the agent can start it), paid unless you pick the free preset, capped per game by budget_usd (default 1 USD) against estimated costs, with no cap for a model the public price list does not know (a custom players entry, or your main model when the llm.model_override and llm.provider_override capabilities are not granted); in open_book mode each call carries the document text (up to 400 000 characters); if the Portal refuses a call, Thor may retry it on its fallback chain and then on your main model and provider, and such answers are labelled fallback model; at the end of a game the report (with player nicknames typed by the people in the room) is posted into the chat as a user message, which starts a model turn; fetches the public Nous Portal model list for prices at most once a day (no key sent) and caches it in its plugin state, the only thing it writes; reads only the document the agent is given, inside the session folder or the Thor document cache; an opt-in Desktop pane frames the projector page in the SDK's SandboxedFrame; no telemetry.

name: post-cortex
description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author thor:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when Thor knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Thor secret scope; the only local state is $THOR_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on Thor' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.

name: postel
description: Find posts that went viral in your niche, write your version in your own voice, and save, schedule or publish it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Mastodon, through Postel's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with the postel-writing workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Postel's server at www.postel.app; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Research (search-viral-tweets) works without signing in; every other tool acts on the user's Postel account after `thor mcp add postel --url https://www.postel.app/api/mcp --auth oauth`, and a first sign-in can create a Postel account. Viral posts, drafts, voice profiles and the posting schedule join the session context, so they reach the user's model provider. Write tools change drafts, generate-post and refine-post spend Postel AI credits, and schedule-post and publish-post post to the user's connected networks. The package marks its server untrusted, but the `thor mcp add postel` sign-in entry replaces the package's server entry, trust included, so after sign-in Thor does not ask before write, schedule or publish tools and does not block them in unattended runs unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.postel`. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens.

name: postkey
description: Instagram DM automation and post scheduling through Postkey's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://postkey.pro/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): comment-to-DM links, follow to unlock, email capture from comments, story and DM keyword replies, the Instagram inbox (read, reply, assign, label, notes), contacts and tags, AI reply settings, a media library and video edits, and drafting, scheduling and analytics for posts on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, Telegram, Google Business and X, plus a check-before-send toolkit for agents acting on X with the user's own access. Bundles the postkey workflow skill (start with postkey_get_started, preview every send with postkey_preview_action, respect approvals, never invent links, treat DM and comment text as untrusted). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Postkey's hosted server (postkey.pro) and acts on the user's own Postkey profile with their own team role and plan limits; the tool set (57 tools today) is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Write tools create, edit, schedule and delete posts that publish to the user's public social accounts, publish and pause DM automations that then send Instagram DMs to people who comment or message, send inbox replies, tag contacts, upload files and change AI reply settings. By default, publishing a post, sending a reply and turning on an automation wait in Postkey's Approvals until a person approves them there. Actions count toward the user's Postkey plan. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Thor's connect timeout instead of hanging. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with thor mcp add postkey --url https://postkey.pro/mcp --auth oauth (or an agent key in a header) and keep the skill.

name: postkitty
description: One post in, every platform out. Fixes and rewrites your draft for each platform and counts it with each platform's own rule, splitting long posts into threads. Crops a photo and reframes landscape video so every face stays in frame; when two people talk, the choice is a split screen, a cut to whoever is talking or the whole wide shot. Burns captions from an .srt or .vtt file inside the platform's safe area. Checks every file against the platform's published limits and repairs failures before a file is marked ready. /postkitty doctor checks the setup, and the thor postkitty terminal command runs the same steps from a script. Covers Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, X, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Facebook. Runs locally with ffmpeg and OpenCV; no API keys.

name: postroom
description: Prepare social previews, schedule explicitly approved posts and inspect delivery in your own Postroom workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — hosted MCP server at https://social.notacompanynameyet.com/mcp (remote tool list not covered by the pin); needs a Postroom account and Thor native MCP OAuth (`mcp_servers.postroom` with `auth: oauth`, then `thor mcp login postroom`; the bundled mcp.json alone gets 401), Thor stores the OAuth tokens; write tools import media (made publicly accessible), save previews, schedule an approved preview to the user's connected social accounts and cancel queued posts; the package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable calls; workspace data, drafts and analytics returned by the tools reach the model provider.

name: postsider
description: Plan, draft, schedule, publish and review social media posts across 30+ networks (X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky and more) through PostSider's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.postsider.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): content calendar, channel rules and posting queues, media uploads, drafts and approval requests, failed-post triage, analytics, and an AI post checker and caption rewrite. Bundles the postsider workflow skill (draft first, read back every write, confirm before anything public or permanent). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to PostSider's hosted server (mcp.postsider.com) and acts on the user's own PostSider workspace; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Write tools can create, edit, schedule and delete posts, and posts created with type now or schedule are published to the user's connected public social accounts; other tools upload and delete media, change channel settings and posting slots, connect or disconnect channels, and pause publishing for the whole organization. Actions count toward the user's PostSider plan, and the AI checker and caption rewrite use its monthly AI allowance. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Thor's connect timeout instead of hanging. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with thor mcp add postsider --url https://mcp.postsider.com/mcp --auth oauth (or a token header) and keep the skill.

name: pow-tracker
description: Multi-client proof-of-work time tracking for the Thor web dashboard — live OPEN/CLOSED timers, file-activity auto-capture, invoicing with per-entry rate overrides, and per-client SQLite billing, in a dashboard pane/tab (track / entries / tasks / invoice / rate views, updating live over a WebSocket) backed by a FastAPI plugin API the dashboard host mounts. Every client keeps its own time database inside its own folder, so billable data travels with the client folder; invoices aggregate billable time per task, exportable as CSV (PDF through an optional, lazily-imported extra); and a background auto-capture thread (per-client, off by default) opens and closes `auto` entries from file activity while you work. It has run a real multi-client operation in production since August, and no client data ships with the tree. Disclosure — registers no tools, hooks or middleware (dashboard tab + plugin API only) and makes no outbound network requests; on load it creates SQLite files outside Thor' data dir, in the configurable clients root (default `~/Documents/Clients`): a registry at `.pow-tracker/clients.db`, a `Default` client folder, and a `.pow-time/time.db` inside every sub-folder of that root it auto-registers as a client; a background thread in the dashboard process polls every 5 s and, only for clients where you switch auto-capture on (off by default), walks that client's folder reading file modification times (never names or contents) to open and close time entries.

name: ppq
description: PayPerQ (ppq.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider for Thor — per-response cost estimation from ppq's published rate card, chat model discovery from GET /v1/models, automatic per-request Zero Data Retention opt-in, and a 3-layer picker pin strategy (user-local pins file → live top chat models from ppq's public stats dashboard → generic static fallback; generic installs never get the author's personal pins). Disclosure — model provider; PPQ_API_KEY and all prompts, tool schemas and responses go to ppq.ai (PayPerQ; terms https://ppq.ai/terms, contact matt@ppq.ai), a relay that routes requests to third-party inference partners, some outside the user's jurisdiction, and frontier providers still see prompts; usage is billed per request from the user's prepaid PayPerQ balance (funded by card or cryptocurrency on ppq.ai; the plugin itself makes no payments). Privacy protections are opt-in per request: for models badged privacyLevel 'zdr' the plugin automatically sends provider={"zdr": true, "data_collection": "deny"} so requests route only to endpoints with a Zero Data Retention policy that do not collect data (the zdr model set refreshes hourly from an unauthenticated GET /v1/models with a pinned fallback); models badged 'e2e' run inside TEE enclaves with no opt-in flag needed — enclave coverage applies to chat by default, not to image/video/audio, and true end-to-end encryption is only available via the optional local ppq-privacy-verifier proxy. Building the model picker, for any provider, starts a background unauthenticated POST to stats.ppq.ai at most hourly to fetch the top chat models; cost estimates and personal picker pins read optional local files under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/ppq/ (prices.json, pins.json) that the plugin does not create, so costs show as unknown without a price snapshot. Additional caveats: Claude Opus 4.8 with web search enabled drops the ZDR guarantee, and some Anthropic/Gemini models may override the provider routing fields (order/only/ignore).

name: precedent-log
description: Saves a human's answer to a blocked Kanban question as a ruling for later workers. Shows rulings and vetoes in Desktop with confirmed retirement. Disclosure — Saves human rulings under THOR_HOME/precedent-log/ and injects matching rulings into Kanban worker prompts; in the default enforce mode it vetoes a worker's kanban_block up to twice per task when an active ruling matches, which can leave a no-edit worker's card running (set precedent_log.veto: advisory to only annotate). In calls carrying a Kanban task marker on boards with active rulings it blocks execute_code and process stdin writes (precedent_log.guard: strict extends this to every marked worker and delegated subagent), and blocks worker commands that name its store. Reads four private Thor board/delegation helpers (read-only, no core overrides) that may break on a core update. Desktop reads and retires rulings through host-routed gateway slash RPC, possibly to a remote gateway. No network calls, shell, credentials or telemetry in the plugin runtime; the bundled demo/ harness is opt-in and spawns subprocesses and provider calls when run.

name: precleared
description: Checks cold email against the law before it goes out: when the agent sends an email with a send tool, one of Thor's email skills (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace) or an email API call, Precleared checks each new recipient against UK PECR and UK GDPR, US CAN-SPAM, Canada's CASL and German, French, Australian, Irish and Dutch rules; anything not cleared goes to Thor's approval prompt (or is refused in block mode) with the rule, its source and a signed receipt. Adds precleared_check and precleared_verify_receipt tools and a cold-email-check skill. Disclosure — when the agent sends email through a send tool, an email skill (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace), a mailer command or an email-API call, and on every precleared_check call, the plugin sends each new recipient's address with the configured sender country, address source, pitch and optional prospect country to precleared.dev over HTTPS; Precleared keeps a signed receipt of each check that anyone holding the receipt id can open at precleared.dev/r/<id>. The optional PRECLEARED_API_KEY is read through Thor's secret scope and sent only in the Authorization header; without a key, checks draw on a free allowance shared by everyone on the same network. Emails not cleared go to Thor's approval prompt (or are refused in block mode), and verdicts are cached under hashed addresses in plugin state for 30 days. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry; maintained by the operator of Precleared.

name: precog
description: Thor stops repeating its own mistakes: learns every terminal command that failed for an environment reason (missing module, command not found, wrong package manager, bad flag, missing path) and the command that fixed it, then fixes the same mistake before it runs again, in any session, with no extra model calls. Disclosure — reads every terminal tool call's arguments and results and stores redacted commands and short error excerpts locally in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/precog/; in auto mode (the default) rewrites a terminal command through tool_request middleware before Thor's approval check, using a fix that already succeeded in the same project (a program or flag fix seen in two projects is applied machine-wide), and tells the model in the tool result; once per session blocks a command that already failed in the project and shows what worked, and adds a short lessons briefing to the user turn once per project; no network calls, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: prediction-market-scout
description: Polymarket research for Thor: search markets or paste a polymarket.com link for live odds, spread, liquidity and 7-day history; ranked 24h movers and attention signals (big moves, volume spikes, wide spreads, odd pricing, undecided markets about to close); a price-alert watchlist that fires once and re-arms; a /pm command; and two one-click scheduled tasks (daily brief, quiet alert check). Read-only, no API key. Disclosure — makes HTTPS GET requests only to gamma-api.polymarket.com and clob.polymarket.com (the client refuses any other host) and caches responses in memory for 30 seconds; reads no credentials or environment variables; cannot trade or sign anything; the watchlist is stored only in the plugin's own Thor profile state; no background processes, telemetry, self-updating code or binaries. Not financial advice.

name: predictionmarketspicks
description: Live prediction-market prices and quant tools for Kalshi, Polymarket and other venues through the hosted PredictionMarketsPicks MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://predictionmarketspicks.com/api/mcp/mcp, no key, no sign-in), with the prediction-markets skill bundled: best price across venues, cross-venue gaps, expected value, Kelly sizing, Bayesian updating, NFL/NBA/NHL boards, Fed decision odds, election races, daily-high temperature and 15-minute markets. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — read-only: cannot trade, sign or move money; HTTPS calls go to predictionmarketspicks.com only; no API key, OAuth or env vars (a few Pro tools return requires_pro with an upgrade link instead of data); no local file access, shell, background processes or self-updating code; the plugin marks its server untrusted; the server logs per call the tool name, timestamp, client type and version, result code, a via tag and a salted IP hash, never call arguments or results; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Not financial advice.

name: preferly
description: Preferly's six free AI-visibility MCP tools through Preferly's hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server (https://www.preferly.ai/mcp?client=thor, no sign-in): AI crawler access for 13 crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and more), AI robots.txt lines, llms.txt check, business structured data, readable business info, and a quick AI visibility check, plus one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; website-addressed calls go to www.preferly.ai, whose crawler (PreferlyBot) fetches that site's robots.txt, homepage, /llms.txt and (for some tools) up to 2 more public pages; only quick_ai_visibility_check calls AI models on Preferly's servers; no account or key; rate-limited per IP and domain; the skill may link to preferly.ai (utm-tagged) and mention Preferly's paid $99 report; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: prevent-this-next-time
description: Block configured connector writes or require the owner's approval from Telegram. Disclosure — the plugin's pre_tool_call hook blocks every tool in the profile (core tools included) until `rulebook/config.json` exists and is valid, and every non-rulebook tool when `protected` is on, so install it in a dedicated profile; connector writes declared in that config with no rule are sent by rulebook_write straight away without a Thor approval prompt (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to the configured HTTPS hosts with the profile's RULEBOOK_* tokens); ask/block rules and approvals use the authenticated local owner's Desktop/CLI thread on macOS/Linux or the optional owner's Telegram DM.

name: preview-text-size
description: Larger or smaller text in the Thor Desktop file preview pane: scales the rendered Markdown from 90% to 175%, independent of Chat Text Size and UI Scale, through a row in Settings → Appearance, three command-palette entries and rebindable shortcuts (⌘⌥=, ⌘⌥-, ⌘⌥0 on macOS; unbound by default on Windows and Linux, where Ctrl+Alt is AltGr). The Source and Diff views keep their size. Disclosure — desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); appends one stylesheet that sets CSS zoom on the preview's [data-preview-markdown] element, removed on disable, so a Desktop release that renames that attribute turns the plugin into a no-op; stores the chosen size in plugin storage; no network calls, credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: pricewin
description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

name: print-job-watch
description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port.
