Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Thor shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt while a person is present. cron, thor -q, webhook, and unattended sessions refuse the move, including after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running thor tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" on pause or resume adds a permanent allowlist line to config.yaml, so a later pause or resume of that same action at the same origin runs without asking while a person is present, until you remove that line. Each cancel asks again. Answering always on cancel does not cover the next cancel. cron, thor -q, and webhook do not use that line. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. thor print-job-watch schedule writes THOR_HOME/scripts/print-job-watch.py and creates one cron job with thor cron create --no-agent --script. This is the same when THOR_HOME is HOME/.thor and when THOR_HOME points somewhere else. unschedule removes that job and that script in both places. The job does not call a model. Empty script output sends nothing. The script binds the profile secret scope and then reads the URL and API key, and it does not print the key. The default schedule is every 5 minutes. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. Running schedule again switches an existing job in place with thor cron edit --script --no-agent. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. The create command cannot set a tool list, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Under plugins.isolation: host, the print_job_watch tool cannot watch the printer. Set plugins.isolation to in_process. The scheduled script is not that form, so that setting does not stop the watch. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run unschedule, which removes both. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam. A request that sent the API key is not followed on a redirect, including one that stays on the same origin.

name: print-tools
description: Printer-agnostic Linux CUPS printing for Thor: queue status, files, wrapped text, and styled one-page letters. Disclosure — every print tool call sends a real job to a CUPS queue installed on this machine (local or network printer, 1-5 copies, at most 20 pages) with no approval prompt; `print_file` reads a model-chosen JPEG/PNG/PDF/TXT/MD file under your home or temp directory (20 MB limit) and sends it to that printer; runs `lpstat`, `lp`, Ghostscript (`gs -dSAFER`), the CUPS `texttopdf` filter, `fc-match` and a Pillow letter renderer as child processes with a minimal environment (no Thor keys forwarded); no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.

name: print3d
description: Turn an idea, a photo of an object, or a shop listing into a sliced Bambu Studio project. The agent writes a Blender script, print3d checks the mesh (overhangs, thin walls, fits between parts, likeness to the photo), slices it and says what to fix, until it prints clean; each run also writes a 3D view the agent opens in the Desktop preview pane. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill and a stdio MCP server run through uvx, so Blender 4.2+, Bambu Studio and uv are required; at install Thor looks for Blender in the standard locations (/Applications and Steam on macOS; PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install without it. Disclosure — runs Blender and the Bambu Studio CLI as local child processes; Blender runs the agent-written Python with your user's permissions, outside Thor's terminal sandbox, and the server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool that runs a script or changes a job (the read-only tools still write preview images and the 3D view under ~/print3d/jobs without asking); installs Pillow and mcp from PyPI; the 3D view loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; the optional `print3d setup` command (not needed for a catalog install) edits Thor, Codex, Claude, Cursor and Gemini config files, with backups. Never contacts the printer; no telemetry, no credentials.

name: printsi
description: Get a PDF professionally printed and delivered. 19 MCP tools: a free preflight that reads the PDF from disk (bleed, trim size, safe areas, image resolution, fonts, colour) and returns each issue with its position and fix plus the page preview as an image; quotes for printing with tracked delivery; a payment link a person pays on Stripe; order tracking and support tickets. A Thor Desktop pane draws the page to scale with each issue marked, and shows the order's progress with a pay button. Flyers today, delivered in the contiguous US. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + one skill) with a desktop/plugin.js; no Python. The stdio MCP server ships in the package as one readable, unminified JavaScript file (server/printsi.mjs, run with node; Node.js 18+ required), so nothing is downloaded at run time; its TypeScript source and a locked build that reproduces it are in the repository under source/. Disclosure — calls the printsi API (printsi-api-live.magnus-ahmad.workers.dev) and nothing else; uploads the PDF being checked or printed and sends the delivery name, address, phone and email to printsi and its print supplier; saves check previews to a temp folder the server creates; orders cost real money, but the plugin cannot pay: order_purchase returns a link and a person pays on Stripe, with the card held until the printer accepts; the server is marked untrusted and only tools that send nothing of the user's are marked read-only, so Thor asks before every tool that uploads a file, sends an address or changes something; a tool argument can name no file except the PDF, and no folder to write to; no account is needed: on first use it mints a printsi guest key and keeps it, with order tokens, in the plugin's own data folder in the Thor profile, and reads no other credential store; the Desktop pane only reads this plugin's own tool results (no network, no files, no tool calls) and opens printsi's payment page in the browser when the user presses the button; the skill's optional helper scripts run Chrome and Ghostscript locally and fetch segno from PyPI through uvx; no telemetry (PRINTSI_TELEMETRY=0), no update checks, no self-updating code.

name: printwatch
description: Control 3D printers over the local network from your agent: fleet status (temps, progress, layers), file listing, print start/pause/resume/cancel, file upload with automatic dialect packaging (printer_upload), and camera snapshots delivered into chat. Dual protocol — Anycubic Kobra printers over their built-in stock LAN Mode (clean-room reverse-engineered handshake + MQTT; no cloud, no rooting, nothing flashed) and Klipper/Moonraker over HTTP, and Bambu Lab printers over their local MQTT/FTPS interface (user's LAN access code; X1/P1/A1 family). Includes a headless slice-to-print pipeline: any raw .gcode is repackaged into the exact Anycubic .gcode.3mf dialect the stock firmware requires (header blocks, M75, uppercase-MD5 sidecar, X-ACNext slice info) and started remotely. Disclosure — connects only to the printer hosts the user configures (PRINTWATCH_PRINTERS / PRINTWATCH_BAMBU / PRINTWATCH_MOONRAKER_URL via agent.secret_scope); printer_print, printer_upload, printer_pause_resume and printer_cancel move physical hardware and ask for Thor approval on every call (refused when no human is present); printer_upload sends a local .gcode/.3mf file the model names to the configured printer; printer_snapshot shells out to ffmpeg, and for Bambu printers the LAN access code is visible in ffmpeg's process arguments for the ~2s capture; Anycubic MQTT and Bambu FTPS/MQTT accept the printer's self-signed certificate (CERT_NONE) on the local network; no telemetry, no external services, no credentials persisted.

name: priors
description: Pay HTTP 402 (x402) APIs on credit: when the agent's wallet is short, it borrows the gap in USDG from its Priors credit line on Robinhood Chain, pays, and repays; before paying another ERC-8004 agent it reads that agent's repayment record. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for Priors: the priors-wallet server runs the local priors-mcp command (npm @priors/mcp, installed by the user, not bundled; the README pins 0.14.1) and signs payments, loans, repayments, savings, stock and market trades and Autopay allowances in USDG on Robinhood Chain mainnet with the key named by PRIORS_KEY_FILE (or PRIORS_KEY) in the profile's .env; both servers are marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every write-capable call, and where nobody can answer (chat -q, cron, the gateway without a prompt) the call is declined and nothing is paid; pay_url pays only https hosts listed in PRIORS_PAY_HOSTS when it is set (any public https host when it is not), at most max_price_usd a call, and borrows only when max_borrow_usd is given (a loan is at least the pool's minimum, 5 USDG today); a loan more than three days late can be marked defaulted, which ends the agent's record on Priors; the hosted read-only server (https://mcp.priors.trade/mcp) receives the tools' public arguments (agent ids, addresses) and counts connections by the client's runtime name only; the tool sets are served by @priors/mcp and the hosted server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha.

name: prism
description: Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

name: privacy-gateway
description: Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for Thor model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the Thor plugin DB under THOR_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

name: privacy-shield
description: Privacy-Shield — tokenizes personal data (PII) in LLM output before sending it to cloud providers, with encrypted AES-256-GCM mapping and whitelisted restore. Modes: off / audit / restore. Configurable via Desktop-Controls or YAML.

name: privacy-xray
description: Where does your data actually go? Records every outgoing model request, the main loop and side tasks such as title generation, compression and vision, as metadata only: destination host, vendor, vendor HQ country, the model vendor behind aggregators such as OpenRouter (read from the model id; the final processing vendor behind an aggregator is not visible), size and counts of detected personal data types (e-mail, IBAN, payment card, phone, IPv4, German Steuer-ID and USt-IdNr, own watch terms). /xray canary invents a fictitious person and /xray trace shows every request and local store that carried it. /xray check audits the config with a severity and the exact thor config set fix per path; /xray fix <id> --yes applies one; a session retention hint is advice only and is never applied. /xray fix --yes and /xray find run only on local surfaces (CLI, TUI, desktop, dashboard) unless allow_sensitive_on_gateways is turned on. /xray find searches the local stores for a person, /xray report writes a self-contained HTML leak map (no scripts, no external assets) with a before and after view of two canaries; a dashboard tab shows the same page in a sandboxed frame. Not legal advice and not a compliance certificate. Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls, standard library only. pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call are observers; they write one metadata line per request (time, session and turn id, task, provider, model, host, vendor, counts, canary id and message fields; never message text or matched values) to THOR_HOME/plugin-data/privacy-xray/ledger.jsonl (rotated once at ledger_max_mb, default 5 MB). The llm_request middleware is off by default (guard: false); when turned on it masks canary values and watch terms in main model requests before they are sent. Reads the merged Thor config through load_config_readonly. /xray trace, /xray find and /xray check read outside the plugin's own data, read-only and under a time budget (scan_seconds, default 30): state.db (messages, session titles, stored system prompts, delivery queue), session files including request dumps, memories, logs, cron output, other plugins' plugin-data, paste and pending folders; output shows counts and masked snippets only. Writes config only on /xray fix <id> --yes, through thor_cli.config.set_config_value (same code as thor config set); never deletes files. Stores fake canary persons, last check and trace results and requested HTML or Markdown/JSON reports under its plugin-data folder. Registers the tool privacy_xray (map, check, trace, find; read-only, never changes settings), the slash command /xray and a skill that adds one line to the skills index of every session while the plugin is enabled. No credentials, no shell commands, no cron jobs, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: prize-radar
description: Hackathon and bounty scout: finds open Devpost hackathons and Superteam Earn bounties ranked by prize per entrant, with exact deadlines in your time zone and eligibility for your country from the official pages; sizes the competition, including GitHub pull-request hackathons (entry counts and themes no entry covers); tracks your entries and reports each deadline change, closing and winner announcement once, at the start of a session or through a daily automation blueprint. Disclosure — read-only, unauthenticated requests to devpost.com, superteam.fun and api.github.com; one SQLite database under plugin-data; no credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry; never registers, submits or posts.

name: procgen-studio
description: Image and video backend that draws with code. Your configured model writes SVG/Python drawing programs, which are rendered locally to PNG (and MP4/GIF) with the editable source and a reproducible seed saved next to each image. No image API key, STYLE.md art contracts with six presets, a critic pass with bounded redraws, local seed re-rolls and restyles, /procgen and thor procgen commands, and a Desktop pane. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; every model call goes through ctx.llm on the user's configured provider (the procgen_draw / procgen_critic auxiliary slots when pinned); runs model-written Python drawing programs in a separate sandboxed Python process (AST import allowlist, audit hook refusing network, subprocess and file access outside the job directory, CPU/memory/file-size limits, wall-clock timeout; allow_python: false switches to SVG/pixel-only); invokes the system ffmpeg as a subprocess for video only; reads a STYLE.md from the session working directory when it has a preset:/palette: line; writes renders under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/procgen-studio/ and $THOR_HOME/cache/generated/, plus an optional user-configured output folder; no telemetry, credentials, background processes or self-updates. Installs cairosvg (needs the system cairo library), numpy and Pillow.

name: professional-finder
description: Skills-only plugin. Finds, shortlists, license-checks and vets licensed professionals in any US state from public license registries and regulator records, and drafts outreach the user sends. Not a background check and not intended to be a consumer report (FCRA); confirm findings with the issuing board. Disclosure: no tools, hooks, MCP servers, shell or stored credentials; uses the agent's own web tools to open public registries; sends nothing to KellerAI.

name: profile-models
description: Read-only Desktop model map for main, auxiliary, sub-agent and MoA routes. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's full config.yaml through the host's `config.get` (the response includes any credential fields it holds); only model-routing fields are kept and nothing is stored or sent off the machine.

name: profile-pane
description: Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

name: profile-picker
description: Pick the profile for a new chat right in the composer, next to the model pill, and see which profile a running chat belongs to.

name: profile-switcher
description: The Alt+Tab gesture for Thor profiles. Hold Ctrl+Alt and tap Tab to cycle through your profiles, release to land on the highlighted one — the same hold-tap-release rhythm as the OS app switcher. (Alt+Tab, Win+Tab and Cmd+Tab are owned by the window manager and cannot be bound by any application, so the gesture lives on ctrl+alt+tab, unclaimed by the OS and by Thor core.) Each row shows the profile's model and most recent conversation; a working profile shows a spinner. Also opens with a single contributed keybind (Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P, rebindable in the app's own keybind panel), a status-bar chip, and a palette command. The switch goes through the Desktop's own profile path, so the target profile's backend is activated and its chrome is scoped onto it. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls, or stored credentials.

name: progress-squash
description: Collapses carriage-return progress bars (tqdm, git clone --progress and similar) in terminal output to the frame a terminal would show, so the model reads one line instead of every redraw: a 300-step tqdm loop goes from 17,396 characters to about 120. Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.

name: progression
description: Right-side Thor Desktop panel showing, live, what the focused chat's agent and its subagents are doing: the task in progress (with the tool running now), subagents (queued, running, done, failed), the tasks up next and the done ones, color-coded, with a completion % and an ETA (finish clock time) recomputed every 30 s to 10 min, plus other active chats, and a flag when the agent or a subagent is parked on an approval, password, secret or question. Fed by the agent's own todo tool (todo.updated) and subagent.* events. /progression shows or hides it. English and French UI. Disclosure: Desktop half inside the plugin SDK surface; read-only gateway calls (subagent.list, session.active_list, and session.events.since for open_requests), polled every 5 s only while a chat is working or waiting; a native notification (ctx.os.notify) when a chat starts waiting for the user; the agent half only registers the /progression command; no tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network, shell or files; keeps its panel state in its own desktop plugin storage.

name: project-command-center
description: A board for every Thor Project: lane, live sessions, token spend, git branch and GitHub issues and pull requests in one place, with a detail page per project. Click an issue and a session opens inside that project's folder with the issue number, title and URL already in the composer, unsent. Branch rows open a session in a worktree or after a checkout, and each session carries its own lane, so a PR climbing to review is visible where the work happens. Includes a GitHub reader with full issue and PR modals, comments, status filters and a Zed-style commit graph. Disclosure — reads your git repositories and their history, switches branches and creates worktrees under `<repo>/.worktrees/` when you ask it to from the board (refusing on a dirty tree, an in-progress merge, a branch checked out elsewhere or an existing target; git's own repo hooks run as they would in your shell), and comments on or closes issues and PRs as your authenticated gh account. Board state lives in a local SQLite file under the Thor home. Two hooks read a terminal call's `gh pr create` output to link the PR and move the session to review, and inject one short line naming the session's own card into each turn; each has its own kill file (`auto_link.off`, `card_context.off`). Network calls go to api.github.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com, and a favicon of a homepage a project declares.

name: project-manager
description: Git workbench for the Thor Dashboard and Desktop: discovers the git repositories under the folders you watch, and inspects or changes them per file — stage, unstage, diff and discard — plus commit, push, pull, branches, commits and worktrees. Disclosure — reads the watch paths from its own SQLite table (under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/project-manager) and git metadata (branch, remote, ahead/behind, commit subjects, status and diff text) from the repositories under them, and lists folder names under any path you type when adding a watch folder; file contents are read only as diff text returned to the requesting UI; the five agent tools are read-only. Writes on request only from the Dashboard/Desktop UI: git add, commit, push, stash (including stash -u before a branch switch), fetch, merge --ff-only (also as "pull all" across every watched repository), restore, clean -f, git switch, and git worktree remove (including --force and remove-all). Discard on a tracked file restores it from HEAD and drops the uncommitted edits; on a file in no commit (untracked or staged-new) it leaves the bytes on disk but nothing here can restore a version of it, and both sit behind a confirmation naming which one you are doing. The Desktop Chat button starts a new Thor session whose working directory is that project's folder, and the project name and branch chip open the repository's remote URL in your system browser. The optional standalone server (project_manager_server.py, 127.0.0.1:9120) requires a per-run token printed to its log. No outbound network, no model call, no API keys; git fetch/push contact the remote named in the request (the UI sends the repository's own remote).

name: promise-keeper
description: Tell Thor a rule once ("never touch the prod folder", "ask me before you change migrations", "never force push"). It proposes an exact rule quoting your words; you turn it on with /promise or the Desktop panel. Every tool call is then checked twice (pre_tool_call, and tool_execution middleware on the final arguments) by deterministic code, and a block quotes you. Each rule shows what is enforced, best effort and not covered. Local only: rules in plugin data, no network, no telemetry; reads scripts, Makefiles, package.json and git config of calls it checks. Disclosure — every tool call is checked by a pre_tool_call hook and tool_execution middleware that can block it, or send it to Thor' approval prompt, under rules the user confirmed (via /promise or the Desktop Promises panel); to judge a call it reads the scripts, Makefiles, package.json, the repo's .git/config and ~/.gitconfig the call refers to and runs `git ls-files` in the target folder; rules and a block history are stored locally in plugin-data/promise-keeper/rules.db, with no network I/O.

name: promoat
description: Make realistic AI videos of yourself, with your own face and voice, from inside Thor. Powered by Promoat. Disclosure — sends your scripts, prompts and the public media URLs you supply to Promoat's hosted API (promoat-platform-plugins.vercel.app) with your PROMOAT_KEY; video, character, voice-clone and speech tools spend paid Promoat credits; clone_voice and create_character build a reusable voice or face from the samples you pass; delete_character and delete_voice permanently remove account assets.

name: prompt-enhance
description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

name: prompt-enhancer
description: A composer button for Thor Desktop that first repairs dictation typos in the draft, then rewrites it into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape); one click back restores the original typing, and ⌥-click repairs without enhancing. ⌘-click picks the model both steps use (written to auxiliary.prompt_* in config.yaml; the prompt_repair / prompt_enhancement task slots are registered by the plugin, as current Thor builds require). Ships three rebindable keybind actions in Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts (enhance / repair-only / enhance-with-previous-turn, unbound by default). Also ships a /enhance slash command (mobile app / Telegram / TUI: fix / raw / copy modes) and a POST /enhance HTTP door for iOS Shortcuts, running the same two templates host-side with the shared model config. Reads the session's own history (local, read-only) to build a proper-noun list for the repair step. Preserves @file and /command chips plus inline /skill references verbatim; per-session state. Multi-composer isolation: parallel sessions enhance independently and each result writes back to its own composer in real time; a result from a switched-away session applies automatically on return (never overwrites manual edits). UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

name: prompt-firewall
description: Community security-preview plugin that detects and quarantines selected prompt-injection patterns in tool results and evaluates risky tool actions; limited to hook/Core enforcement semantics. Disclosure — Rewrites tool results the agent sees: spans that match its injection heuristics are replaced with `[QUARANTINED:<category>]` markers, and output past its scan budget (or output it fails to scan) is withheld with a notice; may block or escalate to the Thor approval prompt writes to protected config/instruction/credential paths, endpoint changes and commands that disable prompt-firewall; adds a fixed trust-boundary notice to every turn; appends metadata-only audit records (tool name, target path, reason) to `<THOR_HOME>/logs/prompt-firewall.jsonl`. No network.

name: prompt-optimizer
description: Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.

name: prompt-pocket
description: Local prompt library for Thor Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

name: prompt-queue
description: Kanban-style prompt queue for the desktop: Play drains cards one at a time into per-card target modes — new session, existing session, project, or a profile's canonical Bot Chat — gated on the global model slot, background-review completion, and context compaction. Queue/Done/Skipped/ Failed tabs, two-row target picker, markdown ingest (Windows), and a trust-aware ::enqueue directive (ask-first by default). Disclosure — Desktop pane that runs queued prompts as full agent turns (all tools the session allows) in new or chosen existing sessions, projects it can create, or a hidden per-profile "Bot Chat" session while Play is on; reads recent agent.log lines to detect background reviews and context compaction; on Windows the markdown-ingest menu runs local shell commands (mkdir, dir, certutil, explorer, and python on a small bundled reader script it writes into the chosen folder) through Thor's shell.exec; an opt-in Auto-add setting lets ::enqueue directives in a live assistant reply queue prompts that run without a click.

name: prompt-snippets
description: Prompt snippet library for the Thor Desktop composer: a quick-pick overlay styled after the app's own slash menu (own shortcut), plus a management view with drag reordering, group tags and import/export. Inserts into the focused session, not the active one. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體. v1.8.0 is fully SDK-only: the quick-pick overlay renders as an official Popover anchored to the plugin's own contributed node and all draft writes go through the host composer draft API. No local network; v1.6.0+ adds local JSON import/export via the system clipboard.

name: prompt-studio
description: Step-by-step prompt builder for Thor Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (Thor Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns (plus any compaction summary) of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions; draft and form answers go to the same auxiliary model; no other network.

name: prompt-tray
description: Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the Thor composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through Thor Desktop's internal thor:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

name: proof-lens
description: Verify a DRAT refutation and profile its proof depth as a Desktop pane. Pick a CNF and a trace; every accepted line is re-derived by unit propagation (RUP only), and the pane reports the empty clause's certificate depth plus a histogram of derived clauses by depth. Deletions are ignored rather than replayed (sound, strictly more permissive than a deletion-aware checker). Disclosure — reads only the two files chosen in the browser file dialog; all work runs in the renderer; no network calls, no shell commands, no stored files.

name: proof-run
description: Capture demonstrated actions, check exact arguments and session-bound observations before reuse, and stop on unproven replay evidence. Local operator-controlled contracts and rebind; no model or network calls. Thor Agent Plugin Hackathon entry.

name: proofable-mcp
description: Context and control for any AI. Agent identity, scoped access, and proof across tools. Disclosure — skills-only package: its workflow skills steer the agent to Proofable's hosted MCP server at mcp.proofable.me (which you add yourself with `thor mcp add … --auth oauth`) to check identity proofs and agent permissions, create wallet-signed proofs, and store, list or revoke secrets in Proofable's hosted vault, so secrets you store and proof/agent data go to Proofable; Thor does not prompt before those MCP tools run unless you give the server a trust setting; the skills also suggest Proofable's own optional `proofable` CLI, which edits MCP/project config.

name: proofgate
description: No proof, no done. Verifies an agent's completion claims (file created, message sent, command ran, tests passed, figures quoted) against the tool evidence recorded in the same session, before the final reply is delivered. Unproven claims are flagged as unverified or withheld, fail closed, and every verdict is written to an append-only ledger stored locally in $THOR_HOME/proofgate/. Disclosure — observes every tool call and final reply in profiles where it is enabled and stores tool arguments (sensitive-named keys redacted) and the first 800 characters of every tool result, unredacted, in append-only files under $THOR_HOME/proofgate/ with no rotation; makes no network calls; in the default enforce mode it holds reply streaming and may append warnings to or entirely withhold a reply judged by keyword heuristics to contain unproven claims.

name: proofly
description: Checks an agent's claimed Base mainnet transfers against chain evidence: tx hash, receipt status, recipient, token and exact raw amount, over read-only JSON-RPC. It annotates results from the payment tools you list in its payment_tools setting and corrects unsupported "payment sent" claims in the final reply; adds the read-only proofly_verify_tx tool and the /proofly command. Disclosure — sends read-only JSON-RPC requests (tx hashes) only to the configured Base RPC endpoint (default https://mainnet.base.org), whose operator sees the hashes and your IP; replaces the results of the payment tools you list in payment_tools with its verdict and rewrites unsupported payment claims in the final reply; stores a verdict ledger (tx hash, verdict, expected and observed transfer fields, HMACs of session and turn ids, newest 300 rows) in plugin-data/proofly; registers transform_llm_output with hold_stream, so every reply in a profile that loads it is shown only after the check; no keys, signing, wallets, .env reads, shell, background processes, self-update or telemetry.

name: proofops
description: Verification for AI agent completion claims: turn "the agent said done" into a sealed receipt of what was checked, what was observed, and what passing does NOT prove. Thor runs a declared plan of read-only checks against a live service, a deliverable or a system of record, and gets a receipt: each check's actual result, what it proves, and - printed on every receipt - what passing does NOT prove. Fourteen check types: HTTP status/JSON/body/headers, command exit codes, file and directory inventory, checksums, CSV shape, image dimensions, PDF pages/size/text, and read-only SQLite queries. Receipts are sealed with a sha256 digest and can be HMAC-signed, so editing a verdict after the run is detectable; `verify` reports valid / tampered / unsealed / needs-key. A check that could not run is reported NOT RUN - never a green tick - and the receipt carries claimable: false. Refuses undeclared origins, undeclared commands, unknown check types, and paths outside the operator's allowed_paths. Disclosure - network: HTTP GET only, against origins the plan names, resolving each host once and connecting only to the addresses it classified (every redirect hop too), refusing loopback/private/link-local addresses unless the operator allows local targets, environment proxies ignored; shell: exactly the argv a plan lists, and only when the operator also lists that command verbatim in plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_commands - there is no approval prompt inside a tool call, because there is nobody to answer one; reads: no file or SQLite access at all until the operator sets plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_paths (an unset fence is a denial, not a default), then only inside the operator's roots and the plan's, SQLite opened read-only and single-statement; storage: receipts under the plugin's own data directory containing observed values, hostname, cwd and command output; credentials: none read or stored, signing is CLI-only; no telemetry by default and no network access at import or registration; telemetry exists only as an explicit opt-in: a one-time "Send anonymous diagnostics" checkbox after the first run, framed as the feedback that decides what gets fixed next, where Enter leaves it unchecked and the refusal is remembered and the exact bytes printable via `proofops share --dry-run` sending an anonymous six-field aggregate (random install id, version, platform, run and plan counts, pass/fail/not-run counts) that `proofops share --dry-run` prints in full beforehand, with version and platform allow-listed on both client and server so no name, path or hostname can be stored; the aggregate carries pass/fail/not-run totals plus the same totals per check type from a closed set of fourteen, so the report can say what kind of thing is verified (web service, file, PDF, database) without saying whose, and is published at https://rasrobo.github.io/proofops/metrics/ Disclosure — network: HTTP GET only, to origins the plan names, connecting only to addresses it resolved and classified (every redirect hop too, proxies ignored) and refusing loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT and other non-global addresses unless the operator sets allow_local_targets; shell: only a command the plan lists verbatim AND the operator lists in plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_commands, run without a shell and with PATH/HOME/LANG plus operator-listed env vars; reads: no file or SQLite access until the operator sets plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_paths, then only inside those roots, SQLite read-only; storage: receipts under the plugin's data directory, containing observed values, hostname, cwd and command output; credentials: none read, signing is CLI-only; telemetry: none from the Thor plugin, the standalone `proofops` CLI can send an opt-in anonymous aggregate to t.sqs.chat after a one-time prompt.

name: proofread-draft
description: Proofread Thor Desktop drafts with your configured model and review suggestions before applying. Disclosure — on each click the current Desktop draft (up to 6,000 characters) is sent to the model configured for the proofread_draft auxiliary task; the draft only changes when you select Apply.

name: protean-model-sync
description: Fleet-wide provider and model presets with CLI and Thor Desktop support. Disclosure — writes model/provider keys into the config.yaml of the profiles you select (backup taken first).

name: protean-ordaprompt
description: Jev-style comparative classifier for OrdaPilot. It compares all topic labels and session choices in one batch, including new-topic, ambiguous, and new-session options. It uses calibrated score and margin gates, weighs continuity against context cost and contamination, and abstains when uncertain. OpenRouter is optional for provisional new-label proposals and disabled by default.

name: protean-subagent-viewer
description: Read-only Thor Desktop pane for live and past delegated subagent workers.

name: protocol-chaos
description: Long-lived matters shared by all your assistants, kept on your own Protocol Chaos server (draft 0.2): Thor sees an overview of your open matters and the details of the ones a message names, records your words after it answers and folds them into that matter's goal, limits, plan, progress and state, and a bundled skill organizes what every assistant recorded once a day. Runs beside your memory provider, not instead of it. Disclosure — each new session's system prompt (not a scheduled job's; subagent sessions included) gets an overview of open matters, up to 3,900 characters. Before each turn the plugin fetches the server's directory (cached 30 seconds) and reads, by id, up to three matters whose titles share words with the message; the message itself is never sent to the server. After each answer, a background call to the auxiliary model Thor routes for protocol_chaos_capture (the compression model by default) receives the user's message, up to 600 characters of the previous reply, the matters' titles and states and today's date; when it decides to record, the user's words, copied verbatim, are sent to the server at PROTOCOL_CHAOS_URL with PROTOCOL_CHAOS_TOKEN, and a second call receives that matter's fields, up to six earlier words, the titles of its larger matters and parts, and the last few messages with the reply (about 6,000 characters), and the fields it returns are written to the server. Nothing else is contacted and there is no telemetry; logs hold ids, counts, times and token counts. Like any plugin's added context, the matters added to a turn are saved with it in Thor's session history and resent on later turns. Cron and subagent turns get no per-turn context and record nothing. The bundled organizer skill runs only as a scheduled job the user creates, uses the server's MCP tools, and keeps a checkpoint at ~/.thor/protocol-chaos/organizer-checkpoint.

name: protonpass
description: Proton Pass secret source: resolves pass://vault/item/field references (mapped source "protonpass") or every env-var-titled item of one vault (bulk source "protonpass_vault") into environment variables at startup through the user's own pass-cli, beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources, with a thor protonpass setup/status/token/set/remove/sync/disable CLI. Stdlib-only, no Python deps. Disclosure — when enabled, runs the user-installed pass-cli (argv only, allowlisted env, 30 s per call), which talks to Proton's API; a personal access token or AI-agent token is read from Thor' env and passed only to the pass-cli login child's environment (never argv); writes a 0700 session dir under cache/protonpass and a 0600 value cache (cache_ttl_seconds: 0 disables); no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry, no background process.

name: prove-it
description: Checks an agent's completion claims against local read-only probes before you read the reply: HEAD vs the remote-tracking ref for a push, git cat-file for a commit, a file stat for a write, observable output for tests pass. No model in the check. The footer says ✓ verified, ✗ contradicted, ⚠ could not verify, or ⏸ blocked on an approval; /proveit explain shows the claim, the probe and the raw output. Disclosure — runs local read-only git commands (rev-parse, merge-base, log, cat-file) in the repository the agent worked in this turn, with fsmonitor and ext protocols disabled and no stdin; never contacts a remote or authenticates; stats absolute file paths named in the agent's reply; makes no probe when the terminal backend is not local; stores a bounded ledger (arguments and output only for terminal, file-write, code-execution and delegation calls, truncated, secrets pattern-redacted, deleted after 7 days) plus checked claims and approval pattern/description (never command text) in plugin-data/prove-it/data.db; every probe has a 2 s timeout and the footer a 4 s budget; a plugin error never withholds the reply in footer mode; no telemetry

name: proveit-tests
description: Flags recognizable ways an agent weakens tests to reach green: removed or loosened asserts, skip/xfail/.only, deleted tests, expected literals rewritten to match failing output, assert True and tautologies, try/except pass wrappers, and test-runner escape hatches (pytest || true, -k "not ...", --deselect, --passWithNoTests, CI continue-on-error), and pytest config / conftest.py narrowing (addopts -k/-m/--deselect/--ignore, testpaths, collect_ignore, deselecting hooks). Net-new only: each edit is compared with the file as it was before, so pre-existing skips are not blamed on the edit. Deterministic AST + regex, no model calls. Modes: observe (default), escalate to the human-approval gate, or block on unattended/cron runs. SHA-256 receipts and a /proveit ledger. Python-strong; JS/TS coverage is heuristic and limited. Disclosure — no network calls and no model calls. Reads edited test, CI, pytest-config and conftest.py files and tool arguments to compare before/after; appends warnings into tool results; may escalate or block tool calls when configured. Ledger is written only under the Thor plugin data dir (in-memory if none); terminal findings keep a short, secret-redacted command excerpt locally. Not a sandbox and not unbypassable: an agent can still rewrite via shell, disable the plugin, or invent new weakenings. No findings is not proof that tests were preserved.

name: provenance-gate
description: Flags memory and skill_manage writes that state a user decision ("the user decided ...", "用户决定 ...") without the user's own words: each such sentence needs a quote that appears verbatim in text the user typed in this session, shares key words with the decision and does not drop a negation. A patch is checked by the text it produces. Observe mode (the default) records flagged writes and `thor provenance-gate report` lists them; block mode refuses them and tells the model how to fix the write. Measured on an independent blind set of 133 lines: precision 1.000, recall 0.694. Disclosure — two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call); keeps a local copy of the text the user types, with its sender_id and session link, and an evidence log of checked claims under plugin-data/provenance-gate (30-day default retention, `thor provenance-gate purge`); reads MEMORY.md, USER.md and skill files to reproduce what a patch produces; no network, no credentials, never asks for approval.

name: provider-copy
description: Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. Per-profile missing/present badges, fill-missing by default with an explicit overwrite opt-in. OAuth sign-ins and messaging bot tokens never travel; values never cross back in responses.

name: provider-endpoint-healer
description: Status and health listing for configured model endpoints. Probes them on session start and via /peh, and recommends the best candidate by health, latency, cost and capability. Reports only; it does not switch Thor providers. Disclosure — at session start and on `/peh` it sends an unauthenticated `GET <base_url>/models` to every endpoint listed in its settings (http/https only, no credentials sent, response body not read); it reports health and a recommendation only and does not change the provider Thor uses.

name: provider-status
description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Thor environment keys on exhaust, and an expired OAuth token asks for a new login. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent. Disclosure — Reads provider API keys from the Thor .env and its own config.json and calls each enabled provider's own usage or billing endpoint; Codex and Grok sign-ins use those CLIs' OAuth client identity and user-agent, keep the plugin's tokens in its install folder, and ask for a new login on expiry. When the Discord gateway runs, the bot's Discord presence (visible to everyone in servers the bot shares) is updated every 20 seconds by default with tokens/sec, context-window use and the active provider's name with its remaining quota or dollar credit balance (model and running tool are opt-in); turn it off with plugins.entries.provider-status.settings.discord_presence_enabled: false. /pulse and the agent_pulse tool report process-wide telemetry (model, provider, current tool, quota) to anyone allowed to call them on a gateway. Writes a secret-free quota-cache.json into its install folder and reads Thor config.yaml for the active model.

name: provider-usage
description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Thor desktop status bar. Pinned providers in the bar (or the current chat's provider when none are pinned), a popover sorted by risk with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, a per-window usage chart with burn rate and projected run-out, near-limit amber tint, and a desktop notification at a per-window alert level. Providers: OpenCode Go, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured, and GitHub Copilot on Thor 0.22.5 or older. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (Thor account-usage helpers and profile secrets, else the profile's .env and the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint (opencode.ai, chatgpt.com, openrouter.ai, api.anthropic.com, portal.thor-agent.local via Thor' Nous sign-in, api.deepseek.com, api.kimi.com, api.moonshot.ai/.cn, api.z.ai, api.minimaxi.com, www.minimax.cn, api.minimax.io, www.minimax.io, api.github.com); the Anthropic check sends the Claude Code `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header, and on Thor 0.22.5 or older the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity (`Editor-Version: vscode/1.96.2`, `Editor-Plugin-Version: copilot-chat/0.23.0`, `User-Agent: GitHubCopilotChat/0.23.0`). The plugin spawns no subprocesses itself (Thor helpers it calls may: the Claude Subscription DirectSDK plugin's usage hook runs the Claude Code CLI, and the old Copilot resolver can run `gh auth token`) and sends no telemetry.

name: proving-ground
description: A wiring test for your plugin stack: known, harmless test calls go through every installed plugin in a throwaway child Thor home with the model never called, and each cell shows which plugin blocked, rewrote, changed the result, gated for approval, or passed it through. Disclosure — Runs every enabled directory plugin's own code in child Thor processes under the system temp dir with your file permissions (approvals forced to deny, model never called, plugin settings with secret-shaped names withheld); the first warm-up copies your local Thor runtime or, if none exists, lets Thor's installer download about 650 MB.

name: proxy
description: Creative strategy and marketing engineering on live ad-library data through the hosted Proxy MCP: a brand's live ads from the Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, LinkedIn Ad Library and TikTok's EU ad library, keyword search on Meta, video ad transcripts, image analysis and competitor discovery, for creative briefs and scheduled competitor radars (Thor cron). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one research skill; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — read-only (no ad-account access, no spend); every tool call, with its brand names, keywords and ad URLs, goes to mcp.useproxy.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth, so sign in from an interactive chat before scheduling cron runs. Free tier 20 credits/day.

name: prsn-id
description: Gives a Thor agent its PRSN ID, read live from PRSN Connect, the desktop app that keeps the agent's signing key in the computer's secure hardware. The agent knows its own PRSN ID at each session and can seal email and files with its PRSN's key. Thor asks the human before each Seal with its own approval prompt. It also asks the human before a command or file action of Thor's own that names PRSN Connect or its files. /prsn shows the state, and Thor Desktop gets a status bar item. Disclosure. The plugin reads ~/.prsn-id/gateway.json, which PRSN Connect writes and which holds no token. It starts prsn-gateway-mcp, a program PRSN Connect installed, gives it a short fixed list of environment settings with none of Thor's API keys, and talks to it over standard input and output on this computer. PRSN Connect makes the calls to api.prsnid.ai, and a Seal's link opens verify.prsnid.ai. It writes its last state to status.json in its own data folder, and, only with the server_log setting on, PRSN Connect's server log. After a file Seal it opens the Seal's page at verify.prsnid.ai in the default browser, and no other address. It makes no network call of its own, stores no credential and sends no telemetry.

name: pstack
description: Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 17 playbooks, plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, unslop, and 46 other skills and principles. Disclosure — skills only, no tools or network calls of their own; when the user asks, the setup-pstack skill changes Thor `delegation` model/provider/reasoning settings via `thor config set`, the autopilot, shipping and babysit playbooks push and force-push the agent's own branches, squash-merge pull requests and arm hourly Thor cron jobs to watch them, and the reflect skill files backlog issues in your team's tracker without asking per item.

name: psychopomp
description: Every week, Thor helps you write a page of your life (your Book) from what it already knows of your week: proposed as a card in the chat, added only when you approve; once a year, a year in review. Seal letters for the people you love. If you ever go silent for good, Thor checks in, then asks your witness for a one-time code they can send on any channel, and only then carries your Book (one designed HTML file) and letters. Rehearse the whole passage in 20 seconds on a virtual clock, on the Desktop page or in any chat. Disclosure — sends weekly nudges, check-ins, a code request and (after the witness's code) the user's Book and letters to the chats the user sets, each through Thor' own `thor send` CLI with the text over stdin; reads every inbound gateway message before Thor' sender check to catch PSY- codes, and consumes those messages; stores the Book and letters in plain text under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/psychopomp; runs a 30-second background ticker; no telemetry.

name: public-holidays
description: Public holidays for 200+ countries and their regions, plus workday checks, workday counts and deadline math (N working days after a date), computed in code instead of by the model. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to date.nager.at (Nager.Date, free, no key) carrying only a country code and a year; no redirects, 10 s timeout, responses cached in memory only. No credentials, no files written, no shell commands, no hooks, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: publora
description: Draft, schedule and publish social media posts on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram through Publora's hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with nine skills; no local executable code.

name: pugin
description: A dancing companion for Thor Desktop that beams in while the chat you're viewing is working and beams out when its whole job is done: the reply, plus the subagents, background processes and Kanban cards that chat started. Work from other chats never counts. Click him for a list of what's running (with Stop for subagents and processes); NEED YOU!, STUCK? and DONE! callouts take you to the approval, the stalled card or the finished work. Seven characters, size, opacity, presence and reduced-motion settings. Disclosure — no network calls (all media is bundled inline), no telemetry, no shell, no credentials. While its window is visible the Desktop half polls Thor's subagent, background-process and pending-approval lists for the focused chat every 4 s, and its backend route opens the Kanban board databases under the Thor root (every non-archived board, shared across profiles) read-only with SQLite and returns only the cards linked to that chat. Its only actions are Stop (kills the chosen background process or interrupts the chosen subagent, after a click and a confirm click) and Open, which switches to the Kanban page and copies the card id to the clipboard. Settings are kept in Desktop plugin storage.

name: pulldown
description: Read public pages as bounded Markdown with source metadata and explicit Chromium rendering. Disclosure — fetches model-chosen public web pages (and, with render=true, their subresources in headless Chromium) through a separately installed Pulldown Python runtime; private addresses and redirects to them are refused, and fetched pages are cached in the plugin data directory.

name: pulse-rings
description: Live numbers beside your chat: a Pulses pane for Thor Desktop with rings, bars, numbers and trends from Discord servers, GitHub, feeds, public JSON APIs, read-only MCP tools, Windows notifications and Thor's own activity. The agent drafts a pulse; only a person can approve it, and the approval card lists every host and the hourly request budget. No model tokens to refresh. Network: GETs to discord.com, cdn.discordapp.com, api.github.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com and HTTPS hosts you approve; the builder's Find sends one query to geocoding-api.open-meteo.com or store.steampowered.com. Notification pulses read counts from the local Windows store; sender and text previews are a separate opt-in. No telemetry; background collection is opt-in. Disclosure — Approved pulses send HTTPS GETs to discord.com, cdn.discordapp.com, api.github.com (with your optional GitHub token), avatars.githubusercontent.com and any public HTTPS hosts you approve per pulse; the builder's Find sends a query to geocoding-api.open-meteo.com or store.steampowered.com. On Windows, notification pulses read the local Windows notification database (read-only), and a one-time import you start reads an old Discord Pulse plugin database read-only. Background collection is off by default.

name: puppetmaster-learn
description: Turns a Puppetmaster swarm into a Thor skill. Puppetmaster runs durable worker jobs (swarms and flow graphs) for an agent. When a Thor session ends, this plugin finds the swarm that finished during that session in the session's directory and, if it produced findings or a patch, writes its goal and findings (title, location, severity, failure scenario, evidence) as a skill candidate under $THOR_HOME/skills-candidates/. Promote it with `puppetmaster skills promote-candidate <slug>`. It never writes a live skill or starts an agent or job, and writes one candidate per job. Needs the Puppetmaster CLI (PyPI puppetmaster-ai). Disclosure — at session end it reads the ending session's cwd and started_at from the Thor session store (read-only, no messages), runs up to three read-only Puppetmaster CLI commands (last --json, status, artifacts) as child processes in that directory, 15 s timeout each, stdin closed, and reads the mcp_servers.puppetmaster entry of Thor config.yaml (no credentials); it writes only under $THOR_HOME/skills-candidates/; no network, no threads or background processes, no telemetry, no dependencies beyond the standard library.

name: pushary
description: Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native Thor approval transport, with optional per-tool gates and a Thor Desktop status-bar panel. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account, or to the approvers a Pushary Team route names (fails closed); the Thor Desktop panel answers an approval this Thor is carrying by withdrawing it on pushary.com and uses the answer only when Pushary confirms that withdrawal won; each approval is recorded owner-only in plugin-data/pushary/approvals (redacted command, choices, outcome; removed after a day); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/thor-commands; when the user has turned on Pushary's encrypted conversation history and installed Pushary's helper, a background thread reads the session through Thor's SessionDB, keeps owner-only snapshots in ~/.pushary/thor-history (removed after 48 hours unchanged) and runs that helper (pushary-native-transcripts or pushary-transcript-register) with the API key so Pushary's uploader can encrypt and send them; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when Thor marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Thor.

name: pushover-thor-plugin
description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Thor's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by Thor; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $THOR_HOME/logs and settings.json under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data, and $THOR_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.

name: pwn-board
description: Pwn boards for Thor: engagements and problems with a known origin, a testable goal and no known path (a foothold to reach, a privilege to escalate, a flag to capture; also flaky failures and regressions), and the workflow that takes a finished one to complete. The agent keeps a frontier of intents rooted at the board's origin, claims them (subagents too), and records findings that must cite real tool output: while a board is open every tool result carries an evidence id, and a finding citing an id no tool returned is refused. It never scores itself: the goal test is fixed at open, run through the terminal tool under normal approvals, and the plugin writes the verdict. A finished board is written up with the files as delivered, goes to the operator's review (notes the agent must answer before the next round), then to verification: an independent verifier subagent and the agent check it separately, the verifier's report held from the agent until it files its own, and the agent reconciles them for the operator to accept or send back. /pwnboard and a Desktop pane drive all of it. The board carries no offensive tooling of its own. Provenance — the fact-intent-hint board model originates in Cairn (https://github.com/oritera/Cairn, AGPL-3.0); this is an independent implementation for Thor and contains no Cairn source. Disclosure — while at least one board is open, records an excerpt of every tool result (first and last 2,000 characters, 1,000 of the arguments, length, SHA-256) in <thor home>/plugin-data/pwn-board/boards.db and tags the result with an evidence id (an added _evidence key in JSON objects, else a last line); uncited evidence is deleted after 14 days; pwn_board_test runs the board's goal-test command through the terminal tool (same backend and approval rules as any agent command); pwn_board_report reads the files the agent names through the read_file tool and keeps them in the database; each verification launches one leaf subagent through ctx.subagent_lifecycle with the terminal and file toolsets (Thor's child-agent rules, backend and approvals apply), whose goal and context carry the board, write-up, delivered files and cited tool output, on the user's configured model (a memory provider, if any, is told of the delegation); with allow_gateway_injection granted, the operator's workflow moves start a turn in the board's session through ctx.inject_message; pre_llm_call adds one line per board to the main agent's current turn; a daemon thread, started on first use, polls the plugin's own database every 3 s to deliver those turns (verifiers start only inside a main-agent turn); the plugin records its own version in its database, at load only if that database already exists so loading creates no files, for the pane's build check; the Desktop pane renders write-ups, checks, reports, notes and findings as Markdown with the chat's renderer in preview mode, loading no images and running nothing; no other network calls, no telemetry, credentials, shell commands of its own or self-updater.

name: qdrant
description: Dense semantic memory for Thor, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Six opt-in hardening knobs (gate, temporal, rerank, entities, cascade, ledger), metadata filter operators, decay_scan.py and semantic_dedup.py scripts, hybrid dense+sparse RRF search, and display.level (off|summary|verbose) — all default off, so existing users see no change unless they opt in. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Thor secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on, and the Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 cross-encoder or the configured rerank_model when the rerank knob is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding and reranking run on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <THOR_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials), last-operation status in <THOR_HOME>/qdrant-status.json, and, only when the ledger knob is on, per-memory history including the first 200 characters of each stored memory in <THOR_HOME>/qdrant-memory-ledger.db. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.thor/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/thor_default, ~/.thor/thor-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Thor home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate thor_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Thor process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Thor session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.

name: qdrant-memory
description: Durable native memory for Thor with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Thor-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; a restart-interrupted remote write stays retryable with the same request identifier, and a deterministic extraction failure is quarantined without stopping unrelated writers. Optional shared memory runs through one authenticated Owner over loopback or HTTPS MCP with provisioned device grants, fixed scopes and one writer per destination; the default stays private under a local ownership lock. scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — optional shared memory runs one authenticated Owner service (off by default, loopback or HTTPS MCP only, token-checked device grants with fixed scopes).

name: qeemah-zatca
description: Saudi Arabia ZATCA Phase 2 (FATOORA) e-invoicing compliance validation, KSA 15% VAT calculation, and Saudi business tax utilities for Thor Agent. Maintained by Qeemah Cloud.

name: qmd-workspaces
description: Convert uploaded document folders to Markdown, index them in QMD, and retrieve relevant passages for Thor Desktop with Ollama. Disclosure — reads documents you upload into Thor' workspaces folder and sends your prompt text and extracted document passages to the configured Ollama endpoint (loopback by default, optionally reached through the Tailscale CLI); writes the shared QMD index and collection config in your user cache and config directories (`~/.cache/qmd`, `~/.config/qmd`), loads QMD's sqlite-vec native extension, and may run `qmd status` and `pdftotext`.

name: qqq-ai-visibility
description: Free AI visibility and GEO check for any website through QQQ's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://qqq.ee/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): whether AI crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot may read a site, its technical readiness for AI search with the three most important fixes, and the latest public report of brand mentions and citations in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity answers. Three read-only tools and one workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to qqq.ee, and check_ai_visibility makes that server load a few public pages of the domain you name (limit five checks a day per IP address). The IP address is only the key of a daily counter, deleted after two days; usage statistics keep the step, language, domain, status, country and duration for 90 days. The server calls no AI model and stores no conversation. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: qrblox
description: QR codes, audio codes, menus and the Voice Agent Phone Book through Qrblox's remote MCP (https://api.qrblox.com/mcp/v1). Portable Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector; every tool call goes to api.qrblox.com. Ping and public voice-agent lookup work without a key; merchant/QR/menu tools need a sk-qrblox- API key in QRBLOX_API_KEY. The package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable tools. The live tool set is served by the remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: quegly
description: Schedule, publish and measure social media posts from Thor through Quegly's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.quegly.com/mcp, API key header): one post to any mix of Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, X, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest and Telegram accounts, scheduled up to 90 days ahead, published now or saved as a draft, with photos, videos, carousels, stories, Pins, video covers and per-platform or per-account captions, retries of failed platforms, and post analytics. Bundles the quegly workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Quegly's hosted MCP server (api.quegly.com) with the user's Quegly API key and acts on the user's Quegly account; write tools publish or schedule posts to the user's connected social accounts and delete scheduled posts, drafts and video covers; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before each non-read-only tool and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: quick-eval
description: Get a second opinion on any answer. /quick-eval sends your last question to other models, shows the answers side by side, and records which ones you mark good. Runs and picks go to an append-only JSONL file, and a review page (/quick-eval open: the Quick Eval page in Thor Desktop on Thor 0.22.3 or newer, or a browser page elsewhere; also a tab in thor dashboard) shows each comparison and a model leaderboard. Disclosure — sends your last question (only that message) to the models you name through Thor' configured providers; probes localhost ports 11434, 1234, 8000 and 8080 for local model servers and, the first time you name a model one of them serves, adds that server as a `providers:` entry in config.yaml; asks for the model/provider-override permission on Thor' consent screen (`/quick-eval allow` writes it into config.yaml on older Thor); writes ~/.thor/evals/evals.jsonl; reads ~/.thor/state.db read-only to show your sessions; `/quick-eval open` outside Thor Desktop serves the review page, which includes full session transcripts, on 127.0.0.1:8765 (or a free port) until Thor exits, locked to a random per-launch token in the opened URL.

name: quiroads-clinic-marketing
description: For people who market health clinics: audit who owns and controls a clinic's Meta Ads assets, review ads and landing pages against Meta and Google health ad policies and the health advertising rules of Spain, the UK, the US and Australia, set up lead follow-up over WhatsApp, SMS and calls, and turn first visits into care plans. Four skills by QuiroAds, a marketing agency for chiropractic clinics, in English and Spanish. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/), skills only: no plugin code, no MCP server, no hooks. Disclosure — instruction-only skills published by QuiroAds (a marketing agency); each skill opens with a short publisher note and two cite a published QuiroAds data report as a reference; the agent works only from text the user pastes, reads no URLs and runs no commands; no network calls of its own, no credentials, no patient data.

name: quota
description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the thor-quota-plugin User-Agent, caching Anthropic usage responses and rate-limit cooldowns in the Thor root directory keyed by a token hash so profiles sharing one Claude login share them; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Thor' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; when a Codex account is configured, each refresh also fetches public Codex reset announcements from the third-party site codex-resets.com (anonymous request, no credentials sent); the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Thor' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check first sends Thor' own xai-oauth access token (read via Thor or from auth.json, read-only) to grok.com's billing endpoint with a browser User-Agent, and on an authentication failure falls back to local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux, the macOS Keychain or Windows DPAPI for the browser's cookie key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or every saved commandcode credential in Thor' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.thor/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage, /api/balance and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Thor' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints. The opt-in (default off) Agent Monitor reads this profile's Thor session database and the local process list to show running sessions, spend estimates and model health, locally only.

name: quote-ask
description: Codex-style ask-about-selection for Thor Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill.
