Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: quotum
description: A quotum seat or prepaid PAYG project as a provider, with usage and dashboard records or balance and receipts. Seat 401/402 recovery hints, opt-in advisory preflight and shared meter caching. Disclosure — seat mode sends prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage, 402 guidance, optional QUOTUM_PREFLIGHT and the dashboard Seals tab send only a 16-hex sha256 handle of the seat key to quotum.org and read the seat's public record and model catalog there; QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 drops Thor web_search from seat requests for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); PAYG mode (QUOTUM_PAYG_KEY, takes precedence) sends prompts, replies and the project key to quotum.org/api/payg/v1, whose gateway processes them and bills a prepaid project balance, and the dashboard reads balance and receipt metadata from it; both modes replace Thor' HTTP client via create_client; seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token; keys are read only through Thor' profile secret scope; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials.

name: radar
description: Radar — real-time Multi-Agent Squad Mission Control for Thor across all profiles: live Bot Squad Roster with 1-click filtering, aggregate and per-session telemetry (tokens, tool calls, child subagents, git branch), safe 2-click session.interrupt RPC for runaway turns, always-on-top OS Picture-in-Picture, and English-first UI with EN/ES i18n. Strictly read-only SQLite (?mode=ro), zero external dependencies, Linux and Windows support. Disclosure — reads every local profile's state.db read-only (session titles, working directories, git branches, token and cost counts) to show them in one panel, and its stop button sends session.interrupt to a session in any profile through the Desktop's profile routes (two clicks, never automatic). No network, credentials or telemetry.

name: radio-dm-gateway
description: Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until thor tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until thor cron remove. Thor main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.

name: rails
description: Guardrails and decision plugin: a fast local System 1 model (d1-3B Decision Guard) decides on every turn whether the agent is only looking or changing things, flags work you did not ask for, makes code work load the matching skill and run a test before 'done', and shows every decision inline as a tag. Optional d3 vision checks the screen before a computer-use task is called done and adds decide, screen_find, screen_check and video_check tools. Disclosure — network calls only to local model servers on 127.0.0.1 (ports 8089, 8898, 8899), which receive your message, the agent's last reply, tool-call arguments, web/email tool results and screenshots; no third-party services, no telemetry, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no Python dependencies. Can hold tool calls: by default code edits and changing terminal commands are blocked until the suggested method skill is loaded, and "done" after code edits is refused until a test runs. computer_use_mode defaults to shadow (show only); set to on, it holds stand-in browsers, and clicks are not held when vision is down. computer_use_driver defaults to vision; text_first lets d1 pick a numbered element and d3 aim when it cannot, and cloud lets the model click on its own. Detected money and email actions ask d1 and are held unless d1 confidently authorizes that specific step, including when d1 is down. Detection includes cached screen targets and explicit curl SMTP requests; this is not a sandbox or exhaustive recognition of arbitrary scripts or unobserved controls. Appends a decision log to <THOR_HOME>/logs/rails.jsonl (long tokens masked); reads the newest computer-use screenshot and media passed to its tools to send them to the local vision model; checks a sibling superpowers plugin folder for skills; short-lived daemon threads for second-opinion and prompt-injection checks. Ideas (shadow mode, decision log) credited to kerpopule/thor-jev-skills; not a fork.

name: rainbowomma
description: One Mac, one human, many agents. Each Thor profile gets a Chrome of its own with a coloured, named window frame, its own ports, processes, clipboard and document leases in Word / Excel / Acrobat / Preview. A pre_tool_call guard refuses what would hit the human or another agent before it runs (pkill Chrome, quitting Word through AppleScript, a port or a process that isn't the agent's, the human's clipboard and Chrome profile, typing while the human types) and names the tool that does it safely; a Messages/Mail send goes to Thor's approval gate. Idle tabs, expired document leases, apps an agent launched and orphaned servers are cleaned up at session end and on a timer. With browser.cloud_provider: rainbowomma, Thor's own browser tools drive that Chrome. /rainbow shows who holds what; /rainbow pause stops every agent at once. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts Google Chrome for the agent (own profile folder, a DevTools port on 127.0.0.1, an unpacked theme extension) and runs osascript, ps, pgrep, lsof, ioreg, open and xcrun simctl with a minimal environment (no Thor provider keys); stops only processes that are provably the agent's, its own idle Chrome, and an Office app an agent launched and left empty. Keeps one guard helper process per profile and a housekeeping timer thread while Thor runs. Writes its state under ~/.rainbowomma (registry, leases, a receipts log, Chrome profiles, temp copies for Word conversions); conversion outputs go only into the source document's folder, and rainbow_save_document saves in place a document the agent itself opened. When one Thor process serves several profiles it prefixes the agent's shell commands with `export RAINBOW_AGENT=…` (modify directive; setting mark_commands). Its only request goes to 127.0.0.1 (the agent's own Chrome). No updater, no credential access.

name: raise
description: Fundraising desk for founders: imports your investor pipeline, ranks investors on cited evidence, checks every draft against code gates (one conversation per firm, a pass closes the firm, 3 touches per channel, working-day cool-downs) and lints it against your verified claims before it reaches your mailbox as a draft. Draft-only: Raise has no send tool, and a pre_tool_call hook refuses send, reply and forward calls to pipeline addresses on mail tools and terminal commands alike. Disclosure — Raise opens no network connections; web search, page fetches, mail, CRM and LinkedIn go through the user's own Thor tools via dispatch_tool, and LinkedIn tools get daily caps plus a 72-hour pause after a login or rate-limit error. Deck text, profile and investor facts are sent to the user's configured model through ctx.llm. Data stays in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/raise (SQLite, plus checked draft files for skill-based mail setups); CSV import reads only an existing .csv at the path the user gives, never inside the Thor folder or hidden folders. No credentials stored, no .env reads, no telemetry, no background processes; automation blueprints exist only if the user adds them. Export and delete via /raise export and /raise delete confirm. Bundles blader/humanizer v3.1.0 (MIT).

name: ram-first-context
description: Read-only RAM-first context memory — FTS5 keyword recall over the live Mnemosyne SQLite database, following the active profile's bank when Mnemosyne profile isolation is on; no embeddings, no network.

name: rariflat
description: Live character reactions and local reliability signals for Thor tool calls; explainable tool/skill recommendations use task fit, reliability, measured rarity, and repeated-call restraint. A local Thor/A2A registry ranks declared capabilities and caller-supplied completion observations; it only recommends and never executes, installs, or connects to agents. The opt-in failure-streak and repeated-call guard is disabled by default. Tool arguments are inspected in memory for non-secret task tokens and repeat fingerprints; credential-like fields are filtered before learning, and raw arguments/credentials are not intentionally persisted. No network requests, telemetry, or subprocesses are initiated. Disclosure — the Desktop pane shows "Review & install" and "Review A2A Agent Card" buttons for agents the model registers; those repos and URLs are unverified, and the install button opens Thor' plugin install dialog for that GitHub repo.

name: ratcatcher
description: Scam bouncer for Telegram groups: removes wallet drainers, fake airdrops, fake support and DM bait, doubling scams, look-alike phishing links and admin impersonators before members or Thor read them, mutes then bans repeat offenders, and DMs admins a report with Release and Ban buttons. Thor can check a pasted message, report catches, edit the blocklist and release false alarms. Disclosure — deletes group messages and mutes or bans members through your own Thor bot, in enforce mode with ban-on-sight and AI review on by default for every group the bot is in unless protected_chats is set; removed messages never reach Thor; sends borderline messages (only) from any group member to your current model via ctx.llm when ai_review is on; blocklist changes and releases by the agent ask for your approval through Thor, and a blocklist hit removes the message and adds a strike but never bans on sight; stores catches, strikes and member join times in its own plugin data; no third-party network calls.

name: rea
description: Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.7.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for Thor. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation. Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and Thor does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs.

name: rea-captcha
description: Inspect captured browser verification evidence locally when an agent task is interrupted by a CAPTCHA. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (pinned stateless mcp.json + skill); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ with npx on PATH. Disclosure — on first start Thor runs `npx rea-captcha@0.3.1`, which downloads that exact npm package and its dependencies (incl. Playwright) from the npm registry; the catalog config is stateless, so only the read-only, local captcha_analyze works and the browser-session tools fail closed until you configure a separate stateful server; no telemetry, hosted solver, browser-profile copying, or cookie/token transfer.

name: rea-video-thor
description: Reverse-engineer any video shot by shot: production-method classification per shot (live action / AI video / 3D / screen capture / code-template render), caption and sticker timelines, voice vs music stems, editing rhythm, and a concrete replication plan. Powered by JuneYaooo/rea-video (Apache-2.0, pinned commit d904b1e8). The six stdio-MCP tools expose the full pipeline (incl. mux_tracks for dual-track video downloads); for shots the pipeline flags as low-confidence, the agent reviews the tiled frames with its own vision and merges the verdict back via submit_review — no external VLM key required. Local runtime deps: ffmpeg and the pinned rea-video package (installed from the repo's venv). Disclosure — downloads video/audio from Douyin share and CDN URLs the agent passes in (https only, Douyin hosts only, curl with --noproxy), runs the third-party rea-video package (git-pinned) and ffmpeg on the host, writes all outputs under its own plugin-data folder (falling back to ~/rea-video-out), and the upstream pipeline downloads a ~67 MB audio-separation model on first run.

name: reachmap
description: Thor knows what it can reach before it says it can't. Scans signed-in browser sessions on DevTools ports, MCP servers, local services, CLIs and drives; freezes a compact map into each new session's prompt (cache-safe system prompt section); and catches replies that deny or hedge about access the map shows is live, with a footer for the user and a one-shot correction for the agent. Opt-in sign-in probes (off by default) tell an installed CLI apart from a signed-in one, and flag replies that plan to use a CLI whose login has lapsed. Keeps a SQLite ledger of when each capability, or a CLI login, appeared or vanished. Disclosure — loopback-only HTTP GETs to Chrome DevTools /json/version and /json/list (tab titles and URLs, never navigates or executes); runs ps, lsof (or ss) and shutil.which on a fixed CLI list (presence only); only for tools the user lists in auth_probes, runs that tool's one fixed read-only status command (e.g. gh auth status, xurl whoami, wrangler whoami; no shell, 6 s timeout, minimal child env: PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/LANG/LC_*/XDG_*/TMPDIR plus only that tool's own variables such as GH_* or AWS_*, so Thor provider keys never reach it), which contacts that tool's own service, keeping only the verdict and never the output; reads browser.cdp_url and MCP server names via load_config_readonly; the map text, including account emails visible in tab titles unless show_identities is off, is sent to the model provider as part of the prompt; writes plugin-data/reachmap/data.db (and auth.json when probes are on); never reads credential stores; no other network calls, no telemetry.

name: reaction-feedback
description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.

name: reaction-ledger
description: Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with Thor: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). Only reactions the gateway authorizes reach it. Disclosure — subscribes to gateway_platform_event as an observer only and ignores every event but a reaction change; writes the emoji a message has after the change, a count of custom emoji and 12-digit hashes of the chat and message ids (never a user id, user name or message text) to plugin-data/reaction-ledger/reactions.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

name: read-once
description: On a repeated identical local read_file, tells the model to answer from the earlier result when READ_ONCE_HITS=1, the file bytes are unchanged, and that exact result is still in the latest model request. Observe-only otherwise. /read-once stats shows hits. Disclosure — reads and SHA-256-hashes regular files under READ_ONCE_ROOT (1 MiB max), inspects the model request in memory for that result digest, and keeps ephemeral metadata only. No network, no telemetry, no disk cache, and no background watcher. It does not hash dotenv names, auth.json, or paths under vault, mcp-tokens, browser-profile, webapp, or pairing. Hits stay off unless READ_ONCE_HITS=1. A repeat of the same read can be Thor's unchanged-stub rather than the file bytes.

name: read-only-mode
description: Ask/read-only toggle beside the Desktop composer (Cursor Ask-mode equivalent): while it is on, each send is prefixed with a read-only instruction so the agent answers from reading only, and asks before changing anything. Per-chat state, palette command, no agent tools or hooks. It is a prompt-level constraint, not a sandbox: Thor has no session-level read-only policy, so the model can still disobey. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no tools, hooks, env vars.

name: reading
description: Newsletters out of the Gmail inbox, into a reader in Thor Desktop (a page in the sidebar) and on your phone (dashboard web app). Setup scans the inbox and suggests the newsletters; native Gmail filters then move the senders you pick into one label, even when Thor is off. Read with j/k, dark or original colors per sender, unsubscribe in one tap, add or remove senders by hand, and ask Thor about any issue (a new chat with the issue attached, or the @newsletter: reference in any chat). `thor reading export` feeds digest cron jobs. Disclosure: uses your own Google OAuth client, declared under oauth: and signed in with `thor auth add reading:google` (Thor stores and refreshes the token; the plugin never holds it); calls only the Gmail API through credentialed_provider_request, plus, when you press Unsubscribe, a one-click POST to the sender's List-Unsubscribe URL (public https hosts only) or an unsubscribe email from your account; changes Gmail only to create its label, write and delete its own filters, move routed senders' mail out of the inbox, mark opened emails read and trash emails you delete; `thor reading setup` runs `thor config set` and `thor auth add` in your terminal (without YOLO or auto-approve variables); writes only its own THOR_HOME/reading folder; @newsletter: and Ask Thor send the newsletter text to your model provider; no telemetry.

name: reading-buddy
description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.

name: readonly-guard
description: Three-mode, per-session tool guard for Thor: read-only (writes blocked; inspection tools plus single allowlisted read-only shell commands), plan (the same, plus the plan markdown), and writable. Switched from the status bar, /readonly, the dashboard API, or — in the Desktop app — three contributed keybinds (Ctrl+Alt+R read-only, Ctrl+Alt+P plan, writable left unbound), which appear in Settings -> Keybinds under Session and are rebindable there; keybinds are desktop-only, because the registry belongs to the desktop renderer. A session that is never switched follows a configurable default (read-only). Disclosure — registers a pre_tool_call hook that can block any tool call, and fails closed when the hook raises; writes <THOR_HOME>/readonly-guard.state (session -> mode) and plugins.entries.readonly-guard.settings.default_mode; a writable lease expires after writable_expiry_minutes (30 by default) minutes without a message from the user, the expiry is latched (a later message does not revive it), and a turn that is already running is never interrupted; in read-only and plan modes it runs single, allowlisted, read-only shell commands through terminal (a speed bump, not a sandbox; on Windows those run under Git Bash); no network calls, no environment variables, no Python dependencies.

name: realcryptocap
description: Live crypto prices, real market cap rankings and AI market briefs from RealCryptoCap, free with no API key. Real market cap ranks native crypto only: stablecoins, wrapped/staked receipts and tokenized assets are left out. Three tools (rcc_price, rcc_top, rcc_market_brief), a /crypto slash command for an instant price table with no model call, and a bundled skill that tells the agent to use live data instead of quoting prices from memory. Disclosure — HTTPS GET requests to realcryptocap.com only (/api/cg, /api/market-analysis, /api/news); an optional REALCRYPTOCAP_API_KEY, read through Thor's secret scope, is sent as a Bearer header to realcryptocap.com only; rcc_market_brief sends the fetched market data (prices, analysis, headlines, no conversation content) to the user's active model through ctx.llm. No shell, no file writes, no background processes, no telemetry, no stored credentials. Standard library only. Market data, not financial advice.

name: reapx
description: Turn the bookmarks you saved on X into ready-to-load, registered Thor skills — without the paid X API. The plugin is data-in: `reapx_import` runs the whole pipeline — map, categorize into a fixed set of domains, two-track assess (integrate-into-your-makeup and business-opportunity), generate, register (`reapx:<name>`) — from a bookmarks file you point it at, or from items passed inline (collected by you through the host's own browser tooling); `reapx_status` is read-only state; `reapx_review` surfaces everything LLM-shaped item by item for the human before anything is relied on. Incremental via a persistent seen-ledger (a bookmark is never processed twice). The map / categorize / assess stages optionally run through the host LLM (`ctx.llm`, one registered auxiliary task) with a deterministic rules engine as the bit-for-bit fallback (`enrich: rules` = zero LLM calls); generate is never the LLM. Registration: handler-time `register_skill`, live in the same session; `register_generated_skills` defaults to false — generated skills land in the review and on disk, and register only after you say so. Settings are read from plugin config only (tool args can never flip enrichment, lift a spend cap, or force registration). Disclosure — Derived from starlearner-nexus (same owner; different input and engine). The plugin reads no browser profile, cookie store or keychain; the repo also ships standalone browser-harvest scripts (scripts/fetch_x_bookmarks.py, scripts/cookie_store.py) that copy your browser's Cookies database and drive it over CDP, run by hand only and never imported by the plugin. `reapx_import` reads the bookmarks JSON file at the path you or the agent name (or the configured `import_dir`). LLM enrichment is on by default (`enrich: rules` turns it off) and sends bookmark text to your active provider through Thor (`ctx.llm`), capped by `llm_max_items`. Generated skills are written to the plugin's own data dir and registered only when `register_generated_skills` is turned on. No other network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: reasoning-switch
description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

name: recall
description: Local file recall: a private on-device index of the documents already on the user's machine, with a search tool over file content (SQLite FTS5, no network and no embedding service), a recall_open reader for PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, Markdown, CSV, email and source files, an @recall: context reference that expands matching passages into the turn, and a pre_llm_call hook that puts up to three candidate file paths in front of the model before it answers a document question. Five tools (recall_index, recall_search, recall_open, recall_stats, recall_forget), a bounded background refresh on session start, and the /recall slash command. Extraction is standard library only (FlateDecode-aware PDF stream extractor, OOXML text nodes). Disclosure — reads the contents of files under the folders the user points it at (default ~/Documents; any folder can be named, and a folder inside Thor' own home is refused), and recall_open / @recall: read any absolute file path the model or user names outside the refused set; extracted text is stored in a plaintext SQLite index under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/recall/, short excerpts are injected into the model prompt on turns whose message looks document-related (disable with the ambient setting, or drop paths with recall_forget), and indexed or opened text reaches the user's model provider in the normal course of a turn. Every read is checked on the RESOLVED path first: credential stores (.env, *.pem, id_rsa, .ssh, .aws, .config, auth.json, state.db and a wider built-in denylist), anything inside Thor' home (vault, session transcripts, mcp-tokens/, webhook_subscriptions.json, dashboard session token, this plugin's own index) and virtual filesystems such as /proc are refused. Files on disk are never modified, moved or deleted; no network calls and no credentials.

name: recall-vault
description: A policy vault and memory for agent money. The agent remembers its spending rules, per-transaction cap, daily cap, confirm threshold, and allowlist, and Recall Vault blocks over-cap payments, refuses unknown recipients, and escalates over-threshold payments to human approval before any tool runs. Dry-run only, no money moves. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook inspects every tool call and blocks, or sends to Thor' approval prompt, calls from other plugins whose tool name looks like a payment (pay, transfer, withdraw, payout, settle) and whose arguments carry an amount and a recipient; policy and ledger are stored in this profile's plugin data; the policy and remembered rules are added to the model input every turn; dry-run only, it moves no money itself.

name: recalllayer
description: Local-first layered agent memory (working / episodic / semantic) with FTS recall and retrieve-after-write tools. Disclosure — local-only memory provider with no network calls, credentials or telemetry; when selected as memory.provider it saves the first 500 characters of every user message and assistant reply, plus a copy of built-in memory writes, in plaintext SQLite at $THOR_HOME/recalllayer/memories.db and injects matching memories into later turns; the store is shared across all sessions and users of the profile (no per-chat or per-user separation); settings in $THOR_HOME/recalllayer.json; short background threads for capture and prefetch only.

name: receipt-printer
description: Your agent says it's done. Get the receipt. Receipts detects action and completion claims and checks observed tool history or explicit local task evidence. Each claim is supported, contradicted, unverified or not evaluable; missing evidence is never called a lie. Output: PNG, ASCII, Desktop pane or optional USB printer. Configure kits, fields, five styles, paper, branding and automatic triggers; verdicts cannot be hidden or recolored. Chat requests stay in the caller's session. Disclosure — Reads this profile's state.db conversation history and kanban.db read-only; an explicit local `thor receipt fleet --roots` scan can read other profiles' state.db files you choose. Stores a tool-name/argument-hash ledger and receipt PNGs (containing answer excerpts, private, review before sharing) under the profile's plugin data and receipt-printer directories until you delete them. The optional `runtime.jev` classifier, off by default, sends redacted conversation context to OpenRouter; the optional USB printer path uses separately installed python-escpos.

name: receipts
description: Verification receipts tied to Git content; gates terminal pushes and PR creation on a passing check. Disclosure — runs read-only local `git` commands (rev-parse, status, ls-files, hash-object without -w) in the agent's repository on terminal tool calls, and blocks `git push` / `gh pr create` there until the user's configured check has passed on that exact content; also refuses a push that selects its repository indirectly (`--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR`, a path it cannot read) whenever any repository has a check configured, and any publishing command it fails to evaluate; observes `pre_llm_call` to read only the session id and model name (never prompts or history; returns nothing) and records that model, the session id and a locally minted issuer id on each receipt; stores receipts in a local SQLite file under the plugin data dir; no network. While Thor multiplexed profiles are active the plugin cannot issue receipts and blocks every recognized `git push` / `gh pr create` with an explanation, including in repositories with no check configured; use a single-profile session for the gate.

name: recency-anchor
description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

name: recloc
description: Location reminders that never leave your phone: ask the agent to remind you at a place, and Apple Reminders alerts you when you arrive. The plugin posts a brrr notification whose subtitle is the validated address; an iOS Shortcuts automation turns it into a reminder with a When I Arrive alert, and iOS watches the geofence on-device. Nothing listens on your machine — outbound HTTPS only. Disclosure — each reminder's text and destination address are posted to brrr.now through the user's own BRRR_WEBHOOK_URL and delivered as a push notification; saved place names and addresses are stored in the plugin's data folder.

name: recued
description: Connect Thor to your own self-hosted Recued server on the same computer: your notes, tasks, mail, calendar and records, through the tools a Recued contract grants. Reads run at once, and every change waits for your approval in Recued. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json and one skill), no plugin code: Thor starts the installed `recued --mcp` as a local stdio MCP server. Disclosure — the tools reach the services you connected to Recued, such as your mail, only as the contract allows. The contract's key is saved in Recued with `recued mcp-key set`, never in Thor or the plugin. The plugin makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

name: redactgate
description: Reversible PII pseudonymization at the model boundary. Names, e-mails, phones, payment cards, IBANs and national IDs (CA, US, EU, UA) become [[TYPE_xxxxxx]] placeholders in every main-loop model request, across all roles, tool-call arguments, tool results and the system prompt (Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses shapes). Real values come back in the reply (transform_llm_output with hold_stream) and in the arguments of local tools only (terminal, file tools, execute_code, memory, clarify); web, browser, MCP, other plugins' tools and subagents keep placeholders. Checksum-validated detection (Luhn, mod-97), offset-preserving Unicode normalization, HMAC placeholders per session kept in memory, fail-closed on error, hash-chained audit journal, /redact command (status, what the model received, dry run, audit, verify, custom terms). Flags auxiliary calls that carried personal data, and /redact harden turns off model-made session titles. Disclosure — no network calls, no model downloads, no shell commands, subprocesses, background threads, credentials or telemetry; standard library only. Writes only in its plugin data folder: audit.jsonl (entity type counts, tool names, provider host, hashed session ids; never values) and its state.json (random HMAC secret, user-added terms). Reads the merged Thor config read-only; writes Thor config only when the user runs /redact harden (auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled = false). The transform_llm_output hook holds the reply stream until values are restored, so commentary between tool calls is not shown on streaming surfaces. Detection core vendored from RedactGate (same author, AGPL-3.0); see DISCLOSURE.md for what predates the hackathon.

name: redaction-pack
description: Teaches Thor's built-in secret redactor 71 more vendor credential formats (HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Amazon Bedrock, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Tailscale, Docker Hub, JFrog Artifactory, CircleCI, HubSpot, PostHog, Grafana, Sentry, Shopify and others) through register_redaction_patterns, so those tokens are masked in logs, tool output and model-bound text like the built-in ones. Disclosure — register() makes one call, ctx.register_redaction_patterns; no tools, hooks, network access, subprocesses, files or environment variables; the patterns can only add masks, and security.redact_secrets: false still turns redaction off.

name: redline
description: Guided Markdown and source-code review in Thor Desktop — annotate passages or line-numbered code in a docked pane and send comment/question/change-request batches back to the opening chat session; cards are offered automatically for qualifying delivered Markdown or source files. Disclosure — reads any user-selected local .md/.markdown or source-code path (.py .sh .js .ts .tsx .c .h .cpp .go .rs .rb .yaml .yml .json .toml .sql, so config files such as config.yaml or auth.json are shown if you open them) up to 1 MB (symlink-resolved), writes only a <file><ext>.redline.json sidecar beside it, and reviewed paths and sidecars are on the gateway host; in Thor Desktop chats the transform_llm_output hook appends a ::redline directive line to qualifying final agent responses; source selections carry L<n> anchors, annotations re-anchor by saved offsets or quote with a margin fallback, and code highlighting uses Pygments in the local gateway host with plain-text fallback; no network beyond the local gateway, no credentials, no telemetry, no subprocesses; the pane polls the local backend every 3 s while open.

name: redreplier
description: Find leads in public conversations through RedReplier's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.redreplier.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): keyword mentions on Reddit, Hacker News, X, Bluesky and Facebook, each scored 0-100 for relevance, with filters by score, keyword, source and date, the reason behind a score, approve and reject triage, monitored websites and keywords, and alert settings. Bundles the redreplier workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to RedReplier's hosted server (mcp.redreplier.com) and acts on the user's RedReplier account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Keywords count against the user's RedReplier plan. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: reduck
description: Run tested browser scripts on any website, in your own Chrome signed in as you or on a Reduck-hosted browser, through Reduck's MCP server (https://mcp.reduck.ai). Configuration only: plugin.json + mcp.json. Disclosure — every Reduck tool call and its arguments go to mcp.reduck.ai with your REDUCK_API_KEY; runs act on websites as you (in your paired Chrome or a Reduck-hosted browser) and can submit forms, post or buy when a script does that, and Thor does not ask before these remote tools run; runs, traces and scripts are stored on your Reduck account and hosted-browser runs use plan credits; the tool set comes from the server at runtime, not from the pinned sha.

name: reflexes
description: Senses for your computer: when a file lands in a folder, a USB stick or SD card is connected, or a log file gets a matching line, Thor starts a turn in the chat that armed the reflex and acts with its normal tools and approvals. Nobody types anything. Durable queue, loop protection (a reflex firing more than 30 times an hour pauses itself), missed firings are logged, never dropped silently. Includes /reflex commands, a bundled skill and a Thor Desktop page. Disclosure — starts agent turns nobody typed (via ctx.inject_message) in the chat that armed a reflex. Reflexes are armed only by you (/reflex or the Desktop page) or by the model after a Thor approval prompt. Gateway, TUI and Desktop delivery also needs plugins.entries.reflexes.allow_gateway_injection, but reflexes armed in the classic `thor chat` terminal run there without that grant and without being displayed. It lists the folders you name about once a second (names, sizes, times) and opens new files briefly only to check they are complete. For log reflexes it reads the bytes appended to the one file you name and sends matching lines (and any /regex/ you give is run on every new line) to your model. It enumerates connected drives and lists the top level of a newly connected one, runs a background thread while Thor runs, and stores a local SQLite database at <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/reflexes/reflexes.db. No network, telemetry, shell commands, subprocesses, credentials or dependencies beyond the Python standard library (uses ctypes on Windows to list drives).

name: reframe-proceed
description: Personal planning tools and an opt-in skill for vision, plans, check-ins, and reviews. Disclosure: stores user text in Thor profile-scoped storage that persists after updates/removal; same-period saves replace records. No third-party network calls, shell commands, credentials, or telemetry.

name: refusal
description: Detects when a model refuses a request or deflects to an educational alternative, and retries the turn on the next model in your fallback_providers chain; optionally appends your own text to the retry's system prompt after a refusal. Detection is local and rule-based (regex patterns over the response prose); tool-calling responses, code blocks and partial answers are treated as genuine answers. Disclosure — an llm_execution middleware inspects every model response before the agent loop uses it, and when it detects a refusal it sets finish_reason to content_filter (Anthropic: stop_reason to refusal) so Thor activates its fallback model; this is logged and counted identically to a real provider-signalled refusal (reason=content_policy_blocked), with no way for a plugin to register a distinct reason, so the detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id to let the two be told apart by hand; a triggered fallback resends the full conversation to the fallback provider and spends tokens there; with no fallback provider configured, Thor replaces the response with its standard safety-refusal notice, so a false positive discards a valid answer. Optional (off by default, empty preprompt/preprompt_escalated settings): an llm_request middleware appends your configured text to the system prompt of requests in an armed session, so a same-route retry of the same model carries it; armed state is memory-only unless persist_state is enabled, in which case session ids/levels/turn ids (never text or credentials) are kept in Thor's plugin state. No network calls, no files read or written outside the plugin package (and, if persist_state is on, its own plugin-data file), no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry sent anywhere.

name: rehearse
description: Practise any interview or talk out loud: job, technical, case, admission, visa, medical, media and podcast interviews, presentations, investor and sales pitches, product demos, thesis defences and speeches. Thor asks realistic questions aloud in a natural voice (Thor's own text-to-speech), you answer on camera on a Desktop page (or by microphone alone, or upload a recording), and you get a scored replay: filler words, pace, pauses, answer length and eye contact on a clickable timeline, plus content feedback with a stronger-answer outline built only from what you said; retries report the points gained. Full interview mode runs it live: the interviewer asks each question aloud, recording starts when it finishes, live nudges appear while you answer (facing, framing, distance, light), and the session ends with a hiring-panel debrief across every answer. /rehearse and three tools bring the same coaching to any chat, answering by text or voice note. Disclosure — uses the camera and microphone only while the practice screen is open (about once a second a small frame is checked locally for the live nudges); speech-to-text (faster-whisper) and eye-contact analysis (OpenCV YuNet face landmarks plus pupil position) run locally and no audio or video leaves the computer; each answer's transcript goes to the user's configured model through ctx.llm for questions and feedback; one-time downloads from official sources: the faster-whisper speech model from Hugging Face and the 230 KB YuNet model from opencv/opencv_zoo at a pinned commit, verified by SHA-256 before use; stores sessions, scores and recordings under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/rehearse (deletable from the page; keep_recordings: false deletes each take after scoring; unused uploads are removed after a day); adds /api/plugins/rehearse/ routes (upload, page calls) behind the dashboard's authentication; no shell commands, no background process beyond analysing a take just recorded, no network service or telemetry of its own; never coaches anyone to misrepresent facts.

name: reka-provider
description: Reka as a Thor model provider: Reka's agent-capable models on Reka's OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Reka's top-level reasoning_effort. Pick Reka in `thor model` or use `--provider reka`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access); chat requests (prompts, tool schemas and results, supported user images) and the model list go to https://api.reka.ai/v1 (or REKA_BASE_URL) through Thor's own client with REKA_API_KEY, which Thor reads; usage is billed to your Reka account; the plugin itself opens no connections.

name: rekindra
description: Recover forgotten local files and rebuild them as source-backed original animated worlds. Rekindra reads a folder you name, recovers images and text (including ZIP and PDF text), keeps recovered evidence separate from the agent's interpretation, builds a 3D scene, compares its preview with the source, and holds export until flagged differences are fixed or answered with a recorded reason. Disclosure: the plugin makes no network calls of its own. It reads only the folder you name, read-only, and writes only under its Thor plugin-data directory. Tool results, including recovered text, go to your active Thor model like any tool result, and rekindra_plan sends selected images to that model only with send_images=true. It starts short-lived, killable child processes without a shell: an isolated Python reader for images and PDFs, and a headless installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium for previews, with a 45 second limit. The browser is started with a minimal environment (PATH, the system and user profile paths, LANG, and temp and cache paths inside the project), so provider keys and other variables are not passed to it. It stores no credentials and leaves no background processes.

name: relay-telegram
description: RELAY incoming agent calls on your Thor Telegram bot with owner-only Accept and Reject buttons. Disclosure — reads the Telegram home-channel id (or an optional owner_chat_id setting) to identify the owner chat, listens on a local Unix socket (`~/.config/relay/telegram.sock`) for RELAY bridge notifications, sends call metadata to that owner chat through your Thor Telegram bot, and forwards owner-only Accept/Reject decisions to the bridge's local socket. The separate RELAY CLI and bridge (not installed by this plugin) connect outbound to the author's hosted relay `relay.thecheetah11.com` by default, manage local identity keys and phonebook data, run as a background user service when installed through the repository installer, and answer accepted calls from known contacts through the gateway's loopback A2A endpoint with full agent context.

name: reliability-desk
description: High-reliability practices on your real launches, changes and incidents: go/no-go polls with named veto owners, blameless incident reviews that fix conditions rather than people, FMEA with RPN and severity override, closed-loop readbacks, stop-the-line triggers, change-control recommendations and session checklists. Every finding cites its evidence, and every GO, NO-GO or change-control outcome is a recommendation for a named human. Disclosure: no tools, hooks, MCP servers, scripts, network calls or stored credentials; works from what the user pastes; never sends, posts or pages anything; merges, deploys, rollbacks or other changes happen only when the user confirms that exact action in their own message; never signs in.

name: relic-gumi
description: A companion that gets to know you and supports self-reflection, built on published psychometric instruments (TIPI for the Big Five, ECR-RS for attachment) as a self-report baseline plus consented check-ins, with an output safety critic and Telegram or Desktop onboarding. Not a diagnostic tool; based on the paper arXiv:2611.08504. Disclosure — state lives under $RELIC_HOME (default ~/.relic); the installer creates a dedicated relic-gumi profile, edits that profile's config.yaml (enables the plugin, sets cron.wrap_response false, copies the base model provider/model/base_url but never keys), creates an empty .env there that the plugin never reads or writes, moves a relic plugin copy found in the base Thor home to a backup and removes it from the base plugins.enabled list, and creates Thor cron jobs in that profile that stay silent until the user consents during onboarding; with the "learn from what you write" consent it reads the profile's own Thor state.db user messages to update a self-report profile; credentials (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS, TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL, GEMINI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_API_KEYS) are optional plugin secrets read only through Thor' secret scope; check-ins are delivered by detached subprocesses (job and scoped credentials over a private stdin pipe, minimal environment with proxy/CA settings) straight to the Telegram Bot API; network is the configured Thor provider, Telegram, local Ollama classifiers, Google Gemini/Lyria media only with RELIC_ENABLE_GOOGLE_MEDIA=1 and a key, Ollama Cloud (ollama.com) only if explicitly configured, and local ComfyUI or ACE-Step servers only if the user enables them; no telemetry, no self-updater.

name: reliquary
description: Local, inspectable long-term memory with source provenance, conversation capture, General/project REL routing, a read-only PHY identity layer, and an interactive relationship-driven 3D graph in Thor. Disclosure — launches a profile-scoped Rust background host (built by the user from the repo's source or taken from its attested CI build; nothing is downloaded by the plugin) on HMAC-authenticated loopback HTTP that can keep running after a session to finish recovery; reads/writes the selected REL files, reads the selected PHY and a nonsecret processing-routes JSON, and stores copied source text, queues, recovery state and graph caches under the Thor profile's reliquary directory; setup generates a local host token into the profile .env through Thor' secret writer and sets memory.provider and plugins.enabled in config.yaml. Optional processing and retrieval send bounded queries, source excerpts and Memories to the model endpoints the user configures and can incur provider charges. Automatic and manual conversation capture and the Desktop graph need Thor core patches the repo ships but does not apply (patches/thor-104a7c4-hu08-history-export.patch, patches/thor-45882968-plugin-rest-bytes.patch); on stock Thor capture stays paused and Desktop shows list and inspector only. No telemetry or self-updater.

name: remarkable
description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.thor/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

name: reme
description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.

name: remesher
description: Bounded image-to-GLB jobs using an isolated Remesher CLI, with existing ComfyUI/Comfy3D or native TRELLIS.2 and Pixal3D runtimes. Four Python SDK tools provide health, generation, persistent job status and hashed GLB assets, plus a setup/generation skill. Apache-2.0 for Remesher code; third-party terms remain separate. Disclosure — reads selected local images and configured files, uploads images to the configured ComfyUI server, launches local CLI subprocesses and detached supervisors, optionally owns a GPU runtime, and stores inputs, logs and assets in profile plugin data. Client/runtime installation and model downloads require separate explicit opt-ins; no model weights are bundled. No credentials or telemetry are required. No Desktop viewer or hosted service is included.

name: remoet
description: Tech job search: search the public board of open tech roles, find companies by the stack they hire for, star the ones that fit and pull new roles from your shortlist, through Remoet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Remoet's MCP server at api.remoet.dev with the search terms and the profile, job and application details the user asks for, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. search_jobs, search_listings and get_listing work without an account. Write tools change the user's Remoet account, and apply_to_job submits an application to an employer; profiles and saved work, project and education entries are public. The package marks the server untrusted, so write tools ask first, but the sign-in step (`thor mcp add remoet`) writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Remoet's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

name: render-platform
description: Deploy, debug and manage Render applications with 20 unchanged skills from render-oss/skills and Render's hosted MCP connection. Disclosure — connects Thor to Render's hosted MCP server (mcp.render.com) with your RENDER_API_KEY; the server is marked untrusted so tools without a read-only annotation need approval; account permissions apply and changes can incur Render charges; bundled skills guide shell commands, file edits and Render CLI installs (including the vendor's curl | sh installer).

name: renor
description: Renor memory provider: one durable memory shared by Thor, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor over MCP, so what you tell one agent the others already know. Recalls before each turn within a hard deadline (1.5 s by default; the turn goes on without it) and saves the durable statements you make (preferences, decisions, rules, "remember that ...") after it, through a bounded background queue with retries; also on compaction and at session end. Stored text never enters the prompt automatically: recall reports a count and the agent reads matches with renor_recall, labelled untrusted data. Hosted (mcp.renor.cloud, connection key) or the open-source engine, offline. Standard library only. Maintained by Renor. Disclosure — in hosted mode each non-trivial user message (as the recall query), the durable statements picked out of user messages, renor_remember saves and Thor built-in memory entries are sent over HTTPS to mcp.renor.cloud (or the configured RENOR_MCP_URL) under RENOR_API_KEY; RENOR_AUTO_SAVE=turns also sends each turn's user message and reply. The plugin has no telemetry. Renor's own learning setting is the hosted workspace owner's (anonymous usage numbers by default, never text; off under Settings > Learning); in self-hosted mode the plugin starts the user's RENOR_ENGINE_COMMAND as one long-lived child process with DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and RENOR_SHARING=off unless RENOR_ALLOW_SHARING=1, and makes no network calls of its own.

name: rentahuman
description: Find people and coordinate real-world work through the RentAHuman marketplace. Disclosure — runs the third-party `rentahuman-mcp` server via npx, which sends your requests and your RentAHuman API key to rentahuman.ai and stores agent identity keys in `~/.rentahuman-identities/`; its tools can post and fund tasks, accept workers, send messages and release real money to people — write-capable calls ask for approval because the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, but each approval moves money or commits you to work.

name: repager
description: Evidence-bound hero design lab with approved copy, local layout exploration, revision-bound browser checks and portable review handoffs. Disclosure — captures the public page you name with a locally installed Node.js + Playwright + Chromium (you install the npm dependencies and Chromium; nothing is downloaded at runtime) through a public-address-only local proxy; when you enable allow_model_calls it sends the captured page text, your brief and the approved copy to the host model configured under auxiliary.repager_layout; `thor repager` opens an optional token-protected workbench on 127.0.0.1; reviews, screenshots and ZIP exports are kept under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/repager.

name: replaid
description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

name: request-dump-viewer
description: Inspect local Thor request dumps, messages, tool calls, schemas, and diffs in a dashboard tab. Disclosure — reads matching request dumps and Thor state.db read-only; its capture switch writes only plugin-data/request-dump-viewer state and sets or clears THOR_DUMP_REQUESTS in the gateway process, which is process-wide, so in a multi-profile gateway capture also records requests handled for other profiles while it is on. No network, shell, telemetry, or credential-store access.

name: requesty
description: Requesty LLM gateway as a Thor model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `thor model`). The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the Thor session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through Thor' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.

name: research-notes
description: Research notes for Thor: fetch web pages as text, save notes with tags, search notes, list notes, and delete notes. All data stored locally in JSON.

name: reset-rescue
description: Redeems expiring OpenAI Codex rate-limit reset credits across every openai-codex account in the active Thor profile's credential pool, with two Thor one-shot cron attempts 10 and 4 minutes before expiry and success confirmed by backend readback. Includes opt-in early redemption at low weekly quota, per-account overrides, Thor channel notices, a Desktop status-bar chip and popup, and dashboard settings. Account labels and domains are masked by default. Disclosure — reads every openai-codex row of the profile's credential pool with Thor' read_credential_pool helper; in a named profile with no Codex rows of its own that helper falls back read-only to the root profile's accounts, so the plugin then redeems the root profile's credits. It holds each account's access token in memory only and sends it only to https://chatgpt.com (redirects refused) with Codex CLI client headers (User-Agent codex-cli, ChatGPT-Account-ID, x-openai-internal-codex-residency, the same headers Thor' own usage fetcher sends) to list reset credits (/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits), read usage (/backend-api/wham/usage) and consume credits (/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits/consume); the consume POST spends an owned credit through a private, undocumented endpoint. An empty pool falls back to the active sign-in through credentialed_provider_request. On HTTP 401 it runs thor auth refresh openai-codex <entry>, so Thor may rotate and save that account's tokens; the plugin itself never reads or writes credential files or stores or logs tokens. Running thor reset-rescue ensure, or turning on the Desktop status-bar chip (off by default; its first status check arms the jobs), writes five launcher scripts to <THOR_HOME>/scripts/ and creates no-agent Thor cron jobs (a recurring scan plus one-shot rescue, backup and reminder jobs per credit); these run the thor CLI with the inherited environment minus approval-bypass variables. It sends notices with thor send to notify_target or the home channel, keeps credential-free state under plugin-data/reset-rescue, and its dashboard settings write its own plugins.entries.reset-rescue.settings through Thor' settings writer. Automatic redemption is on by default and can be turned off globally or per account (dry_run pauses spending); early redemption is off by default and manual redemption requires confirmation. Run thor reset-rescue uninstall before removing the plugin to delete its jobs and scripts. It does not purchase credits or enable overage.

name: resortlife
description: Maldives travel research through Resortlife Travel's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://resortlife.travel/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): resorts and guesthouses, villas, dining, spas, dive sites, surf breaks, wildlife seasons by month, 360-degree tours, photo galleries, nearby places and the Velana airport board. Bundles one trip-planning skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to resortlife.travel, which keeps daily counts of calls by tool name and assistant family (no address, arguments or question text) and rate-limits by a hash of the caller's address. No credentials are needed or stored. Every tool is annotated read-only; the package still marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: restoreproof
description: Recovery drills for real application stacks: restores a declared database backup (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB or SQLite) and uploads archive into an isolated Docker network, boots the app, and proves whether customers' journeys come back (every database file reference, a real user flow, recovery time and RPO), then cleans up and writes a hashed evidence report. Deterministic engine; the model never decides a verdict. Disclosure — runs the local docker CLI (argument lists, minimal environment) to create and remove containers, networks and volumes labelled restoreproof.run, each drill gated by Thor approval bound to the contract's sha256 and the backup folder; reads the contract and backup folder you point it at (discover also reads the project folder and may write a new restoreproof.draft.yaml inside the session's working folder, never overwriting); writes evidence under its plugin data directory; only the user-typed /drill demo builds a demo app image and pulls database and probe images from Docker Hub; no network calls of its own and no telemetry.

name: retouch
description: Mark the parts of any image that need work in a Thor Desktop pane, leave a note on each, and Thor fixes only those areas. Each mark has its own thread; every edit is a new version, checked pixel by pixel and refused if anything outside its mark changed; only you can accept a mark. Tonal and privacy edits need no image provider, removals and replacements use the image_generate provider you configured. Saves new files, never the original. Disclosure — images you open are copied into this profile's plugin-data/retouch folder. Send starts hidden Thor sessions, one per group of overlapping marks and up to three at a time, with your usual tools, settings and approvals; they use model credits and stay in your session history. Your chat model's provider, or that of the model picked beside Send, receives a downscaled overview of the image, a close-up of each mark and before/after strips. The generate method sends a crop around the mark to your image_generate provider and downloads the result (https only, public addresses only, at most 40 MB). Text inside a picture is treated as picture content by instruction, which is not a barrier, so treat an untrusted picture of text like pasted text. Untouched pasted scratch projects are deleted about a day later. The plugin itself makes no other network calls, runs no shell commands, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry; exports strip GPS and embedded text metadata.

name: return-line
description: Carry the agent's own state and dated excerpts of its own record into every live turn — appended to the message being answered at API time, never the system prompt, so per-conversation prompt caching is untouched. One raw ledger line per turn goes the other way. Works stand-alone; pairs with the biomimetic-brain mind kit, which produces the state file it reads. Disclosure — it appends an agent-state block and retrieved record excerpts to the current user message on every turn, leaving the system prompt untouched; it indexes recent user and assistant messages from $THOR_HOME/state.db across all sessions and platforms into a local plaintext SQLite index under the configured agent directory, and may surface those excerpts in any later conversation (relevant on multi-user gateways); it appends every turn's inbound and outbound text to <agent_dir>/turn-ledger.jsonl; it loads <agent_dir>/scripts/wander.py from the companion mind kit in-process and may run that script and <agent_dir>/scripts/consolidate-mind.py as background subprocesses with the Thor environment; no network calls of its own, no credentials, no dependencies beyond the host interpreter (numpy and scikit-learn are optional, with a keyword-search fallback).

name: revamp
description: Winamp-style music, audiobook and radio player for Thor Desktop. Disclosure — starts a token-protected HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 for as long as Thor runs (Host-checked); scans `~/Music` (or the configured library folders) and stores its library index, playlists and a credential-masked agent-activity ticker in its own data dir, with automatic backups every 10 minutes under `~/.local/share/revamp/backups/`; contacts Radio Browser for station search, the radio stations (and their redirect/playlist/favicon hosts) you or the agent pick, `api.webamp.org` / `r2.webampskins.org` for the Skin Museum and `lrclib.net` for lyrics; may run `ffprobe` for audiobook chapters; the optional pop-out launches a local Chrome/Chromium with a private profile and, on Linux, writes desktop entries and icons under `~/.local/share`; its hooks observe tool calls and approvals without answering or changing them; no telemetry.

name: rex
description: Rex terminal integration: Thor sessions started in a Rex pane learn which session and pane they run in and get Rex's own agent skill (rex:rex), the same context `rex skill setup` gives Claude Code and Codex. Adds status marks on the window title, a macOS alert when Thor waits for you, /title and /resume label sync, and follower panes for subagents and kanban workers. Needs terminal.client_env_passthrough set to the REX_* variables (see README).

name: rfc-ref
description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

name: rh-preflight
description: rh-preflight by quotum with HEY Research Lab. Before Thor acts on Robinhood Chain (chain 4663), a pre_tool_call hook reads HEY Research Lab's builder record and ten Robinhood Chain projects for the addresses, agent ids, pools or repositories in the call, then applies your own rules: go, ask (a human approval prompt) or stop in detected cron by default; other asks use Thor approval, including its YOLO bypass. Unsigned transactions and wallet signing requests get a Toll simulation card with sender balance changes. The card lists each source's line with its link; builder_card and /rh-preflight read a card without acting. Desktop page shows recent checks and human answers. Disclosure — sends only the identifiers you act on to the source hosts listed in the README, plus read-only Robinhood Chain RPC, DexScreener and GeckoTerminal reads; when transaction simulation is on, the detected unsigned transaction or signing request goes to Toll (t0ll.xyz) and HookrRouter trades get a read-only Hookr pool check. Keyless and free (an optional TOLL_API_KEY, read from your Thor profile secrets, is sent only to Toll); no payments, signatures, subprocesses or writes. Stores a local SQLite ledger of checks in its own plugin data folder. Source records describe what each project published; rh-preflight does not call a token good or bad.

name: rhythm-reaper
description: A hip-hop producer desk — 41 lanes across seven families (foundational, trap, drill, melodic, alt, hard, conscious), each with the full production spec (tempo family, key centres, drum programme, low end, harmony and sample source, vocal delivery, metatag vocabulary, exclude list, generation notes) and, for any of them, a complete pasteable Suno deliverable: the style field written out with the dynamic ARC, the Exclude Styles line, a tagged lyric frame with bar targets, an energy map and a pronunciation lexicon. It validates a finished draft against the real platform limits (style <= 1000 chars, lyrics <= 3000, every section carrying a recognised structural tag, no contradictory dynamic tags in one section, a real chorus/hook, known-to-slur proper nouns left un-respelled) and enforces the two character limits in code rather than by eye. It deliberately does not generate lyrics — template bars are slop and the desk says so — it hands the writer a frame that is already correct. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials, no shell, no subprocesses and no files written outside the plugin: the 41-lane catalog is a Python module in the repo and every tool is pure local computation, so no tool is credential-gated (a missing secret can never hide one). 55 offline tests, including a sweep asserting all 41 lanes build a deliverable that passes its own gates.

name: riah-swipe
description: Swipe through what your agent made. Thor puts a batch of options (images, video, audio, names, taglines) into a swipe deck; you keep, cut, or send one back with a note, and Thor remakes the ones you sent back. On Telegram the deck appears in the chat with Keep, Cut, Redo and Undo buttons, and you type a note on any card to say why; elsewhere you get a sign-in board link for desktop or phone. Runs a small local HTTP server inside Thor and writes only to its plugin-data folder; no extra dependencies, telemetry or accounts. Full disclosure in the README. Disclosure — runs a local HTTP board server inside Thor (127.0.0.1 by default; every browser signs in once with a one-time link), and with `lan: true` it listens on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) over plain HTTP; the board page loads fonts from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com), and `https://` media links on cards are loaded by your browser and by Telegram; `swipe_publish` copies local media from the working folder, Thor' media caches, the temp folders and `media_dirs` into its plugin-data folder; while a Telegram deck is open, the swiper's own text and voice messages become card notes instead of reaching Thor, and voice notes go through your configured Thor speech-to-text.

name: rich-paste
description: Paste web pages, screenshots and Finder files into Thor Desktop with their structure, and send each image to the model where it sits in your text. Web HTML becomes Markdown (headings, links, lists, tables, code) with its images downloaded and attached; an llm_request middleware moves each image block next to its label instead of after all the text (kimi-k3, several images per paragraph: 18/30 today, 30/30 interleaved). Also: screenshot chips placed after what you typed, Finder files and folders as Desktop blocks, TIFF/HEIC/BMP/AVIF sent as PNG, pasted audio transcribed with Thor's own STT, Markdown preview. Disclosure — network calls only to download the images of pages you paste (http/https; loopback, private, link-local and reserved addresses refused on every redirect, except DNS answers in 198.18.0.0/15 for proxy fake-ip setups; the pasted page's URL is sent as Referer; at most 50 images per paste and 20 MB each); no telemetry. Runs /usr/bin/osascript once per file paste to read file URLs on the macOS clipboard. Reads image attachments you add (hashes them, converts TIFF/HEIC/BMP/AVIF to PNG) and Desktop's saved long-paste files. Writes only under its cache folder. Pasted audio is transcribed with Thor's own STT, which uploads it to your configured cloud STT provider when one is set (the plugin asks first). An llm_request middleware reorders the image blocks of every user message that carries its markers in the outgoing request.

name: rocketchat-platform
description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Thor Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Thor dependency) — no extra packages needed.

name: rocketchat-team-gateway
description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Thor Agent, built for shared team rooms. Per-person sessions with room context since the asker's previous mention, a default-deny guard for Thor commands, approval buttons, restart catch-up and duplicate suppression that survive a restart. Supports Rocket.Chat 8.7 - 9.x. Disclosure — By default each @mention sends up to 50 recent room messages from other room members to your model provider as context (`ROCKETCHAT_TEAM_HISTORY_LIMIT=0` turns this off), and the optional webhook transport opens an HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8645 that requires `ROCKETCHAT_TEAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

name: rom-studio
description: Make your own small game by talking with your agent, one scene at a time, from a decomp (the community-made source of an original handheld game) that you supply. A pane in the desktop app shows each change as a sentence with a picture from the running game, plus a play link, scenes, gallery, maps, music, dialogue, source search and the agent's questions. Ships a command-line kit the agent runs, a browser player with an always-on flash guard and the make-your-game skill; starts one local page on 127.0.0.1 once a game folder is set. kit agent-play, started by hand, can send game pictures to a model API you name. No agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Linux only. Disclosure — Starts a local page on 127.0.0.1 (port 8778) whenever a game folder is set, and `kit play` starts a local player on 127.0.0.1:4870 (with `--phone`, also an https listener on this computer's LAN addresses, opened by a key link). `kit setup` git-clones the decomp address you give, downloads the poryscript 3.6.1 compiler from GitHub (checked against a sha256) and installs the player's npm package, and the build runs your decomp's own Makefile and tools on your computer. Words typed into the game's agent menu are sent to `thor chat` in a session named rom-studio-game, which runs with your normal approval settings. `kit agent-play --provider`, run by hand, sends pictures of the game and its on-screen state to the model API you name, using the key from the environment variable you choose.

name: rookery
description: A step-sequencer DAW inside Thor Desktop: tell the agent the beat and watch the grid fill in, then add free Soundza loops (Openverse CC0 fallback), arrange a song, and render locally at an exact length, checked for clipping, loudness and the loop seam and reproducible byte for byte. Exports WAV, stems, MIDI and cues.json for video. Disclosure — writes projects, history, renders and exports under plugin_data_dir("rookery") and reads the configured user_kit_dir; loads only the VST3 effect you set as corvus_vst3_path, in-process through pedalboard (third-party native code running with your permissions), and none when it is unset; rookery_samples calls api.soundza.com and follows its signed Cloudflare R2 download links, or api.openverse.org and cdn.freesound.org with source="openverse" (search needs no key; downloads need the optional free SOUNDZA_API_KEY, which is sent only to api.soundza.com); no telemetry.

name: roomsmith
description: One 3D room that you and Thor both edit. It tells you whether things fit and what they cost. Drag furniture in a live editor inside Thor Desktop or the dashboard, or tell Thor what to change: one saved room with undo, and each sees what the other did. Give a budget and Thor furnishes the room with real products, read from their pages and checked against your room and your money. Start from a photo or measurements. No accounts or keys. Network: only GETs to product pages (public addresses only, rate-capped). Never buys anything. Disclosure — the agent's product tools make GET requests to product-page and product-image URLs that you or the agent give (http/https on public addresses only; private/LAN/loopback hosts and redirects to them are refused; rate-capped; results cached under the plugin's data folder); roomsmith_from_photo reads JPEG/PNG/WebP files at paths the agent names and sends them to your active Thor model to draft the room; a pre_llm_call hook adds a few lines about your editor changes and furnishing budget to turns in rooms sessions; all data stays in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/roomsmith; it never buys anything.

name: ros2-console
description: Read a live ROS 2 graph over SSH: topic health, measured rate, one message, camera frame, doc answers with commit provenance, and one gated publish that proves delivery. Disclosure — runs fixed ros2 CLI scripts on the robot over SSH using your own SSH config and agent (or locally with bash when no host is set); the agent may choose any SSH host per call, and new host keys are accepted on first connect (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new); publishing is off until you set publish_allow topic globs, and actuation-style topics are always refused.

name: rosegold
description: Get offers and rewards matched to what you buy on Amazon, including discount codes, promo codes and influencer codes. Thor shares the order details in your Amazon order confirmations with rosegold, then looks up the offers, creator codes and spending rosegold has for you. rosegold reads order confirmations from Amazon, limited to order number, email id, date, total, and each item's title, quantity and price; it does not read your address, payment details or any other emails. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json only); hosted MCP server with three tools, sign-in by emailed code over OAuth, no API key; one command after install (see known issues). Disclosure — every tool call goes to rosegold.app, and the remote tools are not covered by the pin; the tools ask the agent to search the user's Gmail, with Thor's own Gmail tool, for Amazon order confirmations, and to send rosegold each email's id and date and each order's number, items and prices; a look-up brings the user's offers and spending into the chat; under the default trust the tools run without an approval prompt; Thor keeps the OAuth token.

name: roster-compiler
description: Reads a hospital duty roster (CSV, plain text, Excel or a text-layer PDF), flags uncovered shifts, double bookings, runs longer than six days and night-then-day turns, and writes a clean schedule plus an HTML exception report. Deterministic: no model calls, no network, staff names only. Honours Thor's read and write denylists, never modifies its input, and treats a file it cannot read as an error rather than a clean bill of health.

name: rowverdict
