description: Review drafted CSV/XLSX/JSON contracts, fix quarantined rows through replay, and export source-bound receipts plus self-contained HTML audits locally.

name: rply-platform
description: rply gateway platform: talk to Thor from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Thor as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Thor' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `thor rply` setup command; credentials read through Thor' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: rss-lite
description: Lightweight RSS, Atom and YouTube reader page for Thor Desktop: folders, unread/saved, search, a sanitized reader view, and optional AI summaries on your configured model. Disclosure — the gateway fetches only the feeds you add (and a pasted web page or YouTube @handle page once, to find its feed) through the plugin's own SSRF-guarded backend route, sending YouTube's anonymous consent cookie SOCS=CAI to YouTube hosts only; Desktop loads thumbnails and article images directly from publishers (can be turned off) and a YouTube video only after you press Play, through Desktop's own embed; Summarise sends the article title and up to 12,000 characters of its text to your configured model; subscriptions are stored in THOR_HOME/rss-lite; no shell commands, background processes, credentials or telemetry. Independent implementation, not derived from thor-rss or rss-reader.

name: rss-reader
description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.

name: rtk-rewrite
description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Thor terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/thor/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

name: rtk-rewrite-docker
description: Community plugin that rewrites Thor terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local). Docker and remote backends stay unchanged unless opted in; install rtk inside each backend before opting in. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Thor host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

name: ruapi
description: RuAPI as Thor model providers on one key: `ruapi` serves Claude models over RuAPI's native Anthropic Messages API (so Thor' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `ruapi-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, leaving out image and video models, and context windows and image input are declared for the main models. Maintained by RuAPI. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and RUAPI_API_KEY go to https://www.ruapi.ai (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Thor' own clients, and RuAPI forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Thor' standard GET https://www.ruapi.ai/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

name: runa
description: Bring your Runa meetings into Thor: prep for what's next, recap decisions and who owes what, draft the follow-up, and find the exact words behind a claim, through Runa's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with four workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Runa's MCP server at mcp.joinruna.com, signed in as the user through Runa's sign-in (Google or Microsoft), and a first sign-in creates a Runa account. Meeting titles, summaries, transcripts, action items, people and company notes, and reads from apps the user connected to Runa are pulled into the session context, and so reach the user's model provider. No tool changes data in Runa or in those apps; Runa logs each call's metadata. The tool list comes from Runa's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add runa --url https://mcp.joinruna.com/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: runbox
description: Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In Thor Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without Thor' dangerous-command approval like Thor' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.

name: runcrate-provider
description: Runcrate (runcrate.ai) open models via the OpenAI-compatible API at api.runcrate.ai/v1: live model list from /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default, and Thor reasoning settings sent as reasoning_effort. Disclosure: model provider; prompts, tool schemas and RUNCRATE_API_KEY go to api.runcrate.ai, and free requests can be served by third-party model providers under their own terms (runcrate.ai/privacy).

name: rung
description: Stops an agent from marking its own work done until the tests you approved pass. Tests are approved before any code; when an agent reports claimed work done (rung_report, kanban_complete or a todo item), a deterministic pre_tool_call hook blocks the report until those tests pass on the current code and names the ones that fail. No model is asked. A Desktop pane and dock hold the ladder from need to test result; manual checks stay with a person, and milestones verify whole user journeys. Local SQLite, no network calls of its own. Disclosure — Runs the shell commands a person approved as tests, contract checks, milestone checks and environment probes/migrations on the host, outside the Thor sandbox, with the user's privileges, including when the agent calls rung_run_tests; those commands execute files in the project folder that the agent can edit, and receive only PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, the project's own virtual environment and the variables a person names in the project's settings. Pressing Send or Suggest in the Rung pane starts `thor -p <profile> chat` subprocesses that work in the project folder. On first open Rung reads every profile's config.yaml (platform_toolsets only) and runs `thor -p <profile> tools list` for each one. A profile without its own Rung store shares the root profile's ladder.

name: runproof
description: Verify a Thor cron report and release its exact bytes to a local outbox once per workflow slot.

name: s2docs
description: Source 2 documentation and mod tooling for CS2 and Deadlock from a local index of Valve's own game data: convars, Hammer entities with their inputs and outputs, schema classes and enums, game events, the cs_script and Pulse APIs and Source2Wiki pages, plus the mod pipeline — scaffold addons, validate scripts and .cfg files, start map builds on a registered Windows host over SSH, deploy and verify hashes, and record evidence, test runs and job state. Needs uv and an index built with s2docs sync; every write-capable call asks for approval. Disclosure — runs its MCP server with uvx from the pinned git commit, resolving its PyPI dependencies on first start as of a fixed 2026-10-10 snapshot; nothing is sent to a third party, but SSH/scp go to any host registered through register_host, build_start runs agent-written shell commands on that host and its builds keep running after the session ends, deploy_push and job_attach copy local files the agent names, and it writes its own index and addon workspace; write tools ask for approval through the package's untrusted server trust.

name: s3
description: Generic S3-compatible backup and restore operations for Thor

name: saascity
description: Plan a SaaS, AI or developer-tool launch through SaaSCity's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://saascity.io/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): audit a homepage the way directory scrapers see it, pick launch directories from 1,600+ with Ahrefs DR, link type and price, research products listed on SaaSCity, run SaaS metric calculators, and draft a SaaSCity listing for the user to review. Bundles one workflow skill, launch-plan. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to saascity.io, which runs SaaSCity. check_launch_readiness, check_badge and check_backlink make saascity.io fetch the URL the user gives. submit_project sends the approved product details to SaaSCity and stores them as an inert draft, with the caller's IP for rate limits, that expires after 7 days unless the user claims it; nothing is published or charged unless the user opens the claim link and pays on saascity.io. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_project; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before it runs and refuses it in unattended runs. saascity.io is not available in every region (HTTP 451 there). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: sabbath
description: Your agent never rests. Now it rests with you. Once a week (say Saturday 18:00, for 24 hours) Thor keeps a day of rest with you: it says goodnight on your phone, pauses its own scheduled jobs (except the ones you exempt), keeps you company in anything but work and offers to set aside what can wait, then sends one gentle digest when the rest ends while the jobs catch up. /sabbath ox lifts it for an hour when something truly can't wait. Desktop page with your week at a glance; /sabbath on every chat surface; try a two-minute Sabbath. Disclosure — pauses and resumes the user's Thor cron jobs through Thor' cronjob_manage tool (resuming only the jobs it paused); sends a goodnight and a digest to the chat the user sets by running Thor' own `thor send` CLI with the text over stdin; adds rest context to each turn while resting; stores its state in plain text under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/sabbath; no telemetry.

name: sabi-metadata
description: Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on Thor 0.21.3.

name: safe-swap
description: Rewrites destructive shell commands into safe twins before they run instead of snapshotting afterwards: git push --force becomes --force-with-lease --force-if-includes, rm -r becomes a move into a quarantine folder (with a file and byte count), and git reset --hard, git checkout -- / git restore, git clean and git stash drop take a private snapshot first, with /swaps and /unswap to undo and a visible note whenever a destructive command was left unswapped. Disclosure - rewrites the command of the terminal tool before it executes (modify only: never blocks, never prompts, any error or doubt leaves the command unchanged); writes quarantine files and receipts under the user's home on the machine where the command runs (~/.safe-swap/trash by default) plus one SQLite file in the plugin data directory; for git clean, git reset --hard and git stash drop it writes snapshot commits into the repository's own object store under private refs refs/safe-swap/<id> (a git clean snapshot copies the content of the untracked files, and of the ignored ones with -x, until a purge; sets above 20,000 files or 200 MB are skipped and reported); it prints one marker line to stderr for an rm swap and removes it again from the tool result; the only deletion it ever performs is an explicit /swaps purge (or thor safe-swap purge) by the user, which runs rm on its own quarantine directories and deletes its own private refs through the terminal tool and is subject to normal approval; no network calls, no telemetry, no background processes, no self-update; reads no credential files or .env, only the receipts it wrote and the sizes of the files an rm swap moves; approvals are respected: the rewritten command goes through Thor' normal approval gate, and because a swapped rm -r is a move it no longer matches the recursive-delete pattern and does not prompt (the git rewrites keep prompting as before). Targets such as /, ~, $HOME, system directories and anything in the system temp directory, privilege-elevated commands, and commands with heredocs, subshells, command substitution or eval/xargs/find -exec are deliberately left alone, and the agent is told so. Not covered, by design: mv, cp overwrite, sed -i, redirects, write_file/patch, find -delete, git rebase (pair it with undo-effects for those).

name: safeailabs-provider
description: Safe AI Labs as a Thor model provider (`--provider safeailabs`, or Safe AI Labs in `thor model`): an OpenAI-compatible API with one endpoint per region, the model list from its /v1/models and the context window of its fallback model declared. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://us.api.safeailabs.ai/v1 (or SAFE_AI_BASE_URL) through Thor' own client with SAFE_AI_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: salesforce-chatter
description: Talk to Thor from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. Disclosure — authenticates as a dedicated bot user with the OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer flow, reading the private key file at SF_CHATTER_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH; talks to the configured Salesforce login host and the org instance (attachment downloads follow Salesforce redirects); image URLs in the agent's replies are fetched from the gateway host over HTTPS (any public host; private, loopback and metadata addresses are refused) and uploaded to Chatter; polls the To Me feed every 60 s and, for allowlisted groups, runs a SOQL probe every 5 s by default (counts against the org API quota); writes Likes, comments, files in the bot user's Files and optional home-channel posts; keeps its ledger in plugin-data/salesforce-chatter/inbox.sqlite. dry_run defaults to true (no Salesforce writes, no outbound image fetch); with SF_CHATTER_ALLOWED_USERS unset nobody is answered. Optional, off by default: html_preview renders model-generated HTML to PNG with Chromium in a network-isolated Docker container (digest-pinned image, pulled if missing). No telemetry.

name: salesforce-guard
description: Salesforce release-impact and scoped-access review: explicit-scope snapshot comparison, source-reference maps, local access evidence and HTML reports. Bounded security heuristics and partial OWASP mappings produce review signals, not org-wide assurance. Dedicated review profile blocks unrelated tools while the plugin is enabled. Custom native inputs require separate operator folder approval with model-sharing acknowledgement. Disclosure — while enabled, its pre_tool_call hook blocks every tool except its nine sfg_* tools and tool/skill discovery in that profile (terminal, files, browser, memory, delegation included), so install it in a dedicated review profile; reads only Salesforce source folders the operator approves in the plugin's input-approvals.json and sends requested source excerpts to the active model; writes reports under the plugin's own data folder; no network, shell or credential access from the plugin; the separate operator CLI in the repo (not installed by the catalog) runs the user's Salesforce CLI, which keeps its own login.

name: salts-secrets
description: Let strangers talk to your Thor without reaching your private memory. Built on Thor' own gateway.profile_routes: only your own DM reaches your profile; everyone else (strangers' DMs, groups, channels, threads, the web) is answered by a separate public profile with its own sessions, an empty working directory, a fail-closed tool allowlist with no file, terminal, memory or session tools, and only the facts, documents and methods you approved, one click per item. Dashboard tab to review, rewrite, publish and revoke; revoking an item deletes every guest session (the store cannot tell which session saw it), and a reply being written at that moment is replaced with an ask-again notice. Disclosure — setup creates profiles/public, turns on gateway.multiplex_profiles, writes gateway.profile_routes named salts-secrets:* (your Telegram/Discord id to your profile, a platform catch-all to the public one) with TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS / DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS (and adds * to DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS when that list names users, because the Discord adapter checks it before any route), stores the public profile's API key as SALTS_PUBLIC_API_KEY through Thor secrets (and generates the owner profile's API_SERVER_KEY when it is shorter than 16 characters), and installs this plugin into the public profile with `thor -p public plugins install ... --enable --yes-deps` at the owner copy's revision (with --force for a non-catalog source or an existing copy); messages the routes leave in your profile that are not your DM (your Discord server messages, unrouted platforms) are answered after admission (post_gateway_admission) by the same gateway's /p/public/v1 API over loopback; deliveries on your own signed webhook routes are not chat and go to your agent, as without the plugin; each guest gets 20 messages an hour (guest_rate_per_hour); the Context tab reads the owner's memory, USER.md, skills, session history and configured workspace folders to list them (owner only); opening the Context tab applies local rules only; Classify and Draft send item text, and Rewrite with Thor sends the disclosure policy and the owner's one-line instruction, to the owner's own configured model, only when the owner clicks; revocation runs `thor sessions delete` on the public profile, and a guest session it could not delete is never resumed (the guest moves to a fresh session) and `sync` exits 1; writes approvals, the disclosure policy, the owner's own privacy rules (validated before saving), tool-call receipts, the last revocation time and a routing heartbeat under plugin-data/salts-secrets. No telemetry.

name: sampler
description: Set temperature and top_p for your Thor agent (thor-agent#17565): a default, first-match rules by platform, model or provider, and a per-session override with /sampler. Works through llm_request middleware on OpenAI- compatible, Anthropic and Bedrock Converse requests. Models Thor itself sends without a temperature, such as reasoning models, are never changed. No model calls, network, files or dependencies.

name: samskara
description: Relational memory provider backed by a knowledge graph (MillenniumDB or any SPARQL endpoint): multi-hop recall with provenance on every fact, an ontology that infers subsumption (Incidente ⊑ Evento) at reindex time, per-fact weights that are reinforced by use and decay with disuse, and explicit conflict reporting — when two values disagree, the agent says so instead of guessing. Zero-setup mode: SAMSKARA_ENDPOINT=embedded://seed/demo.ttl serves a built-in demo corpus from an in-process, read-only store (stdlib only, no network, no service to run) for the first minute; it answers the three query shapes the plugin issues and refuses arbitrary SPARQL rather than guessing. Onboarding backfills the graph from the sessions the agent already had (state.db, read-only) and reconciles new entities against existing ones. Disclosure — with session-end extraction enabled (default), the plugin sends the recent turns of a session to the user's own model through ctx.llm (host-owned credentials, no provider override) to extract facts. If the host does not expose ctx.llm — Thor' in-process memory-provider path does not today — extraction is skipped rather than redirected: the session records its entity mentions lexically and no model is called. The plugin reads no provider API key from the environment and has no default model host. The graph endpoint defaults to loopback and is the only other network call. The CLI tool tools/backfill.py (never imported by the plugin) reads past sessions from state.db and sends them only to the endpoint the user names, via SAMSKARA_LLM_BASE_URL and SAMSKARA_LLM_API_KEY. No telemetry. Credentials (SAMSKARA_PASSWORD) are read through agent.secret_scope.get_secret.

name: sapiens-sinteticos
description: Operate your Sapiens Sintéticos account from Thor: images, video, music, voice, characters, your repertoire and the members' forum, through the hosted Sapiens MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the 18 house skills bundled (prompting rules, engine choice, cost traps, publishing flows). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to the Sapiens server at https://www.sapiensinteticos.com/api/mcp/mcp, added with `thor mcp add sapiens --auth oauth` (the README then has you set `trust: untrusted` on mcp_servers.sapiens so Thor asks before each generation, publish or delete call); generation tools debit Sinapses, the prepaid credit of your Sapiens account, and publishing tools post to the members' forum and to social accounts you connected on Sapiens, only when asked; in companion mode the agent speaks in the persona your Sapiens account sends and, after telling you once per session, saves condensed notes of your conversation (your decisions, preferences, what you tell about yourself) to your Sapiens notebook, which you can view and delete on the site, and skips them if you say no; on request the skills write `.claude/skills/sapiens-voz/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/sapiens-soul/SKILL.md` into the current project; the skills are in Brazilian Portuguese.

name: sarvam
description: Sarvam AI for Thor: speech-to-text (voice notes and live transcription in voice mode) and text-to-speech (Bulbul voices) for 22 Indian languages, plus six tools: sarvam_translate, sarvam_transliterate, sarvam_detect_language, sarvam_read_document (PDF/image OCR), sarvam_translate_document and sarvam_transcribe_recording (long audio with speaker labels). Not affiliated with Sarvam AI. Disclosure — registers one transcription provider, one TTS provider and six tools (toolset "sarvam"), no hooks; requests go to https://api.sarvam.ai (and wss://api.sarvam.ai for live transcription) with SARVAM_API_KEY read through Thor's secret store; document translation and long recordings upload the file to, and download results from, the signed https storage URL Sarvam returns for that job; sends audio Thor asks to transcribe, text to speak, tool text, and files whose path the agent supplies; writes the requested audio file and translated document copies beside the original under a new name; one WebSocket only while live transcription runs; no stored state, shell commands, background processes or telemetry; every call is billed by Sarvam to the user's key.

name: sarvam-provider
description: Sarvam AI as a Thor model provider (`--provider sarvam`): Sarvam-105B and the open models Sarvam hosts in India, with tool calls, JSON output and reasoning levels. Not affiliated with Sarvam AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.sarvam.ai through Thor's own client with SARVAM_API_KEY, which Thor reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: say-do-gate
description: Checks agent claims against what actually ran this turn. Deterministic, zero tokens.

name: scalekit
description: Call any Scalekit connector from Thor: 500+ connectors and 20,000+ tools. Disclosure — HTTP calls go to the Scalekit environment URL you paste; the three Scalekit values are read with get_secret; one person id is stored at plugin-data/scalekit/identifier; the model can request an approval link, run a named tool, or proxy one HTTP request. Provider tokens stay in Scalekit; no shell, no background process, no telemetry.

name: scaleway-provider
description: Scaleway Generative APIs as a Thor model provider (`--provider scaleway`, alias `scw`): European, OpenAI-compatible, pay-per-use, with a curated tool-calling model list led by deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (the default) that stands in when the live catalog probe fails, the cheapest vision-capable aux model, and real context windows and pricing through models.dev. The credential is SCW_SECRET_KEY, the same secret key the Scaleway CLI and SDKs use; because it is ambient, the provider is never auto-detected and turns on only when explicitly selected. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and SCW_SECRET_KEY go to api.scaleway.ai (or SCALEWAY_BASE_URL), plus a GET /v1/models catalog probe with the same key

name: scamgate
description: Offline scam gate. Blocks known-bad links and payments before a tool runs, and asks a human when it cannot see the destination. Disclosure — blocks agent tool calls that would edit Thor config/profiles/plugins/hooks or Claude Code settings/hooks/plugins, turn approvals off, or disable a Claude Code plugin or its hooks, and asks before an agent installs or enables a plugin; with approvals off it turns its "ask" into a block (setting when_approvals_off: allow restores asks); keeps its signing key and ask log under ~/.local/state/scamgate and phishing feeds under ~/.cache/scamgate (not per-profile); downloads phishing feeds (openphish.com, Phishing-Database on GitHub, optional urlhaus) in the background every 6 hours while Thor runs (auto_update_feeds: false turns this off) and on /scamgate update, thor scamgate update-feeds or its no-argument scamgate_update_feeds tool; the downloads carry nothing about the links being checked; optional SCAMGATE_RDAP=live sends each checked link's domain to its RDAP registry.

name: scar
description: scar keeps the tool-call shape you denied on a Thor approval card and stops that shape before it runs. scar does not call a model. thor chat --cli stores only the choice id deny. The shape is the tool, the argument keys that held an rm command, and the danger tokens, including an rm inside a shell -c body and an rm after env flags, so rm -rf and rm -fr are one scar. Only a tool that has a scar is compared, and only under the argument keys that scar kept, so read_file, write_file, web_search, a sentence, and a touch of nine files are not stopped. A bare rm that dropped a token is not this scar. A path is not part of the match. The block line names the scar, the weekday, the numeric offset, and the words you pressed deny, and it tells the agent not to paraphrase the command and not to run it again. Disclosure — A deny is written only under this profile plugin-data/scar/ledger.json after secret-shaped text is removed by the plugin patterns and then by the Thor redactor. A secret shape that neither knows can stay in the preview. The ledger is read on every foreign tool call, up to 800KB and 200 scars. An unreadable file stops only a terminal command that carries an rm danger token, and it is left in place. On a tool that has a scar, a kept value over 200,000 characters, a shell nested past 8 levels, or more than 8 wrapper words is not compared and is not run. The block applies on every surface, including yolo, cron, the gateway, and approvals off, once a scar exists. A scar stays until scar_forget removes it or the plugin is disabled. scar_forget asks on the Thor approval card when it fits in 7 lines of 63 columns. A longer question is not sent, and the scar stays. Each forget asks again. Its rule key changes on every call, so always does not cover the next forget. Yolo and approvals off skip that card when it fits, so that scar can be forgotten with no second prompt. Cron, a single query, a webhook, msgraph_webhook, api_server, and a plugin host do not forget a scar: the hook blocks scar_forget before Thor's gate, including after always and including when yolo is on. Thor checks a permanent allowlist before its own cron deny. Those sessions do not store a new scar. scar_list returns each scar, including the redacted preview, on any platform that can call the tool. thor tools disable scar --platform <platform> hides the tools on that platform and does not stop the block. Disable the plugin to stop the block. A running gateway keeps the hook until it restarts. The plugin registers scar:keep-a-scar. A skills-tool session adds one system prompt skills index line. -t terminal,scar adds none. Nothing is sent off the computer. Yolo and approvals off skip the Thor prompt, and this plugin does not add a second prompt. Setting isolation to host blocks new scars. This plugin creates no cron job. The install scan is safe, with 15 medium findings, all in the test tree.

name: scope-recall
description: Local, source-backed long-term memory: recalls what you told an agent in your own words, with when you said it, keeps earlier versions as history when you change your mind, and shares one store with your other agents (other Thor profiles, Codex, Claude Code). Disclosure — captured messages, assistant replies and tool results are kept in a local SQLite store under ~/.scope-recall/shared, outside the Thor home and shared by every Thor profile and other agent (Codex, Claude Code) you attach to it; it makes no network calls by default; if you configure a model or embedding route, message excerpts go to that endpoint within the budget you set; keys are read only through Thor's secret routes; it starts short detached background worker processes that inherit Thor's environment; setup sets memory.provider in config.yaml and installs two skills (scope-recall-setup, scope-recall-memory) into your Thor skills folder.

name: scopeledger
description: Local-first billing-evidence reconciliation and owner-review reports for service agencies.

name: screen-overlay
description: Gives Thor the ability to draw on your screen. On your real Windows desktop it draws a gliding pointer, spotlights, boxes, arrows and numbered steps anchored to live UI Automation elements, a floating step guide with Next and Back, and handwritten glass notes, including ones that stay for you to drag and edit. Works over any app. Marks are click-through and nothing takes focus unless you choose to edit a note; DPI- and multi-monitor-aware, with an emergency clear hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12). Disclosure — Windows only. Starts one detached background process (the overlay, run by Thor's own Python) on first use; it exits on the hotkey, on stop, or after 10 idle minutes with nothing on screen (a note left open keeps it running). No network: the plugin and the overlay talk over a local named pipe with a random key. The overlay process is started with a minimal environment (Windows basics, PATH and PYTHONPATH), so it inherits no API keys. Reads monitor layout, visible window titles, process names and bounds, and UI Automation names, types and bounds of elements in the window you target; these appear in tool results and so reach the model Thor is using. Takes no screenshots, logs no keys, never moves the mouse or types, reads no credential or config files. Writes only to its plugin-data folder (pipe key, pid, logs, saved guides). Registers the global hotkey Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12 while the overlay runs. While a guide is open it looks up the current step's target about once a second. Installs PySide6-Essentials (about 215 MB) and comtypes. No telemetry, no self-update, no paid APIs.

name: screenpipe
description: Ambient retro-recall from the user's local Screenpipe screen+audio corpus — fail-silent pre-turn context injection, search/timeline/status tools, /recall. Disclosure — auto-recall is on by default: before a turn it searches your local Screenpipe server (http://localhost:3030 unless you change `api_url`) and adds up to 600 characters of matching OCR'd screen text and audio transcripts to the prompt, so captured screen and audio content is sent to your model provider; the search and timeline tools return more of it on request. Set `enabled: false` in the plugin config to keep only the tools and `/recall`.

name: screenrig
description: Free, agent-driven digital signage. Your agent pairs Players, uploads images and video, builds pages from docs, sheets and calendars, publishes playlists to TVs and kiosks, and checks each screen with a screenshot. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugin with two bundled skills, a bundled Node.js CLI (readable JavaScript, no binaries; Node.js 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+ or 26.12.1+) that the skill runs through the terminal tool, and one remote MCP server (screenrig-views, https://api.screenrig.ai/mcp, OAuth). The CLI calls api.screenrig.ai, uploads files and fetches URLs the user names, can launch a local headless Chrome/Chromium for card previews, and keeps its own screenRIG sign-in in its config directory; it never reads Thor's or other tools' credentials. Web-dashboard connections upload the password, authenticator (TOTP) key and cookies the user supplies to screenRIG, which stores them to sign in to that dashboard. Enrollment and sign-in report the install source ("thor/catalog"). Under Thor the bootstrap makes no update check and never replaces its own files. Write operations change what physical screens show and can spend screenRIG account credit on advertising.

name: screenscene
description: Narrated explainer video generator using screenshots, narration, and animation. Disclosure — sends each beat's narration text to api.elevenlabs.io with your ElevenLabs key; runs your installed manim, ffmpeg and ffprobe as subprocesses with a minimal environment (manim executes a scene script the plugin generates); reads the image file the agent names; writes the final MP4 to ~/screenscene_output, outside the Thor profile.

name: screentime
description: Measure how long a product is on screen in a video: every can, bottle or shoe is tracked, each one is checked against the product photo so look-alikes are not counted, plain-English contract terms are checked with the moment that proves each, and a proof reel comes back in the chat. Runs on the models your Thor already has (your vision model tracks and checks, Thor speech-to-text listens); an optional Meta Model API key switches to SAM 3.1, Muse Spark and Voice Transcribe. Compare measures a draft against a reference shot by shot with ffmpeg only. Disclosure: with your own models, sampled frames, crops and the product photo go to your vision provider and short audio clips to your speech-to-text provider; with a Meta key the video is uploaded to Meta (one-hour expiry, deleted after the run, spend caps enforced); Compare, /screentime demo and selftest make no network calls; runs ffmpeg and ffprobe on files you name; no background processes, no telemetry.

name: sealed
description: Secret source that keeps provider credentials in one AES-256-GCM encrypted file instead of plaintext .env: a 32-byte key file unlocks the store at startup and the Thor secret orchestrator applies the values, so precedence and provenance behave like any other source. Ships `thor sealed init/set/unset/list/status/rotate`; values are read from a prompt or stdin and are never printed or passed in argv. Disclosure — no network, no helper CLI, no subprocesses. Reads the configured store and key file only (default $THOR_HOME/secrets/sealed.{store,key}, both 0600); refuses to load when a file is group/world readable if secrets.sealed.strict_permissions is on. The CLI writes those two paths (plus .bak copies on init --force and rotate); values are entered by prompt or stdin. By default sealed values overwrite .env / shell values for the same variable (secrets.sealed.override_existing). No telemetry, no self-updater, no daemon. Requires the `cryptography` package, declared as a plugin dependency.

name: search-sources
description: Shows the pages a turn searched or fetched as a 'Searched N pages' capsule under the reply and a Sources side panel in Thor Desktop; cited pages first. Reads web search / fetch tools of Thor, the plugin catalog and common MCP servers, JSON or Markdown output. Disclosure — stores page URLs/titles/summaries under plugin-data/search-sources; appends one ::search-sources paragraph to Desktop replies; the Desktop half looks up site icons via Google and DuckDuckGo icon services and the site's /favicon.ico unless set to Off; no telemetry.

name: search1api
description: Live web search, news, Ask, page crawl, sitemap, and trending via Search1API

name: searchapi
description: SearchApi (searchapi.io) as a backend for the built-in web_search (provider name searchapi): Google by default, or Bing, YouTube, DuckDuckGo, Google News, Google Scholar and other engines via SEARCHAPI_ENGINE. Disclosure — sends web_search queries to www.searchapi.io/api/v1/search with your SEARCHAPI_API_KEY (Authorization header) read through Thor; SearchApi is a paid service billed per successful search; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with SearchApi.

name: searchscope-ai-visibility
description: Audit any public website for AI search visibility through Search Scope's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.searchscope.com.au/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Three read-only tools: audit_ai_visibility (ten-section audit with ranked fixes), extract_site_entities (entity and relationship map) and generate_geo_query_universe (AI search prompts by intent), plus the ai-visibility-audit skill that tells the agent when and how to use them. Search Scope is an SEO consultancy in Perth, Western Australia, providing AI search visibility, multi-location SEO and national SEO. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Search Scope's hosted server, which fetches up to 15 public pages of the named site and keeps no page content (sampled request logs may record the audited URL); /mcp is rate limited to 60 requests a minute per client, with tool calls further limited to 20 a minute per client and 10 a minute per audited site; tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider; the server is marked untrusted; the tool set is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the skill links to searchscope.com.au.

name: second-hands
description: Hands-on task coach: a live camera pane in Thor Desktop watches your hands step by step and says STOP (on screen, out loud, in chat) before a costly or dangerous mistake. Mistakes must repeat across frames and high-risk STOPs are double-checked by a second model. Demo mode needs no camera or model calls. Disclosure — camera frames (downscaled JPEGs, ~every 2 s while a session is live) and step text go to the user's configured model provider through ctx.llm on the plugin's own auxiliary slots; optional web research uses Thor's own web_search/web_extract tools; one background thread per live session (stops on finish or after 30 idle minutes); files only under plugin-data/second-hands; no network calls of its own, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: second-key
description: Team approvals for shared Thor bots. Dangerous commands need N votes from your roster by Telegram DM, sized to the risk. The requester never counts, and an agent that edits its own approval settings is stopped on its next tool call. No answer, an error or too few approvers always means deny. Disclosure — Disclosure: Network: `api.telegram.org` only, with the bot token from `SECONDKEY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. Redirects are refused; What approvers see: the command after Thor' own redaction, Thor' reason for asking, and the requester's display name, platform and platform user id. While a ballot is open the DMs are edited in place about every 15 seconds with the current votes and time left. The same ballot text, plus a note that their own vote does not count, is also posted to the Telegram chat the request came from (which may be a group) or to the requester's DM; Re-arming after a change that weakens the settings opens its own critical ballot to the previously armed roster; Background thread: one long-poll thread reads the bot's updates while a request is waiting for votes, and for five minutes after `/secondkey enroll`. It stops on its own once neither holds, and when the plugin unloads; Files: writes its ledger, the armed settings (`armed.json`) and a pane state file (`state.json`: open and last eight closed ballots with the redacted command, requester name and approver names) under `plugin-data/second-key/`. Reads Thor' `config.yaml` (read-only) before tool calls and in its Desktop Approvals pane, whose dashboard route is read-only; Credentials: reads the bot token through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`. It never reads `.env`, `auth.json` or any other credential store; No telemetry, no self-updater, no shell commands, no dependencies beyond the standard library.

name: secret-drop
description: Give Thor a secret without the value appearing in the chat. Disclosure — the value is stored in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600), and storing narrows the file to that mode itself instead of inheriting whatever mode it finds. The model references it as {{secret:NAME}}; a pre_tool_call hook substitutes the value in terminal and execute_code arguments in memory, immediately before the call runs, so the transcript, the prompt and the provider request carry the alias. The same hook guards the store as a whole: every string argument of every tool is inspected, including tools it does not know by name; write payloads are walked into nested edits; directory arguments such as workdir are resolved, and a persisted cwd into the profile home is refused; wildcard spellings are compared with the guarded file names; and a path is resolved before a name is matched, so a symlink alias does not slip through. A command that names the store, a bare environment dump, and a mutation aimed at the profile home are refused. Tool output is scrubbed of stored values, of credential-shaped environment entries and of credential values kept in the profile config file, in their common encodings. What it does not do: it is not a sandbox for the effects of a command the model writes, and the guards are denylists - a value that is short or word-like is stored but not searched for globally, and a program that reassembles a value is covered only by scrubbing of the values it knows. The desktop dialog and its nine locale bundles promise the chat, not model-inaccessibility. Adds a static system-prompt section, a /secret command and a desktop drop dialog. An optional username can be entered beside the value and is stored as NAME_USER; it is injectable through an alias but never used as a global output needle. Only a name this plugin wrote as a username is treated that way, tracked in an account index that belongs to the guarded store, so a secret the user stores directly under a NAME_USER name stays a credential whose value is scrubbed. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_thor_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK). On every session start it rewrites config.yaml to drop stored names from terminal.env_passthrough (migration from versions before 1.5.1), and it reads credential-shaped values from the profile config.yaml only to use them as output-scrub needles. A substituted value still leaves the host with whatever the command sends, and core's local tool-completion display receives the resolved arguments.

name: secret-guard
description: Enter API keys through a hidden dialog into the macOS keychain, never chat; block and scrub secrets before any model sees them. Disclosure — Secret Guard stores the keys you enter in your macOS login keychain as `thor-<ENV_VAR>` items created with `-T /usr/bin/security`, so any process running as your user can read them without a prompt; it runs `/usr/bin/security` and `/usr/bin/osascript` (hidden-input dialog), observes every tool call, tool result, terminal output and model reply to block or redact registered secrets, keeps a names-and-fingerprints-only registry under the Thor root, and makes no network calls.

name: secret-handoff
description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the reply is typed into the focused field of the page whose origin matches the requested service, over the endpoint from BROWSER_CDP_URL or SECRET_HANDOFF_CDP_URL; the answer is visible in the CLI scrollback or the chat history of the surface that asked, and the value is never written to disk, the tool result, or the session transcript.

name: secret-remediation
description: Fingerprint leaked credentials in the Thor workspace, logs, and session history. Redacts them, blocks the turn, and gives text-only rotation advice. Disclosure — Rewrites credential matches into fingerprint placeholders in tool results, terminal output and replies, blocks turns or tool calls that contain credential-shaped text, and keeps fingerprint-only incident records under its plugin-data directory; it reads state.db and spawn-ledger.json read-only to report affected session ids, and only `thor secret-remediation purge --shell-history` (operator CLI) rewrites your bash/zsh/fish history files after a safety copy; an operator-run `thor secret-remediation schedule` adds a no-agent Thor cron scan; no network calls.

name: secret-vault
description: Keeps API keys and other secrets out of the model's context on gateway chats (Telegram, Discord, …): detected values become {{SECRET:name}} placeholders, are resolved only at tool time, and are redacted from tool/model output. Per-profile vault at <thor_home>/secret-vault/vault.bin (Windows DPAPI CurrentUser; filekey-dev elsewhere for tests only). /secret set|list|rm|show-placeholder. Limits — CLI, TUI and Desktop input is not scrubbed (no rewrite hook in Thor v0.23); detection is heuristic and can miss or over-flag; original platform messages (e.g. Telegram) are not deleted and must be removed by you. Disclosure — swaps `{{SECRET:name}}` placeholders for real values in the arguments of any tool call (before Thor' approval prompt, so a prompt may show the value); stores values at <thor_home>/secret-vault/vault.bin, encrypted with Windows DPAPI on Windows but with a key file stored beside it on Linux and macOS; secrets typed in chat stay in the platform's own message history until you delete them.

name: secretshield
description: Credentials stop at the tool boundary. Scans every tool call's arguments before dispatch and every finished reply before delivery for credential material (vendor API keys, GitHub/AWS/Google/Slack/Stripe tokens, PEM private keys, JWTs, bearer credentials, passwords in assignments), blocks the call or redacts the value fail-closed, and appends every attempt to a local incident ledger that stores only metadata (kind, length, masked preview), never the secret. Disclosure — SecretShield observes all tool call arguments, tool results and final replies in profiles where it is enabled and scans them locally; in the default enforce mode a detection blocks the tool call and a reply containing a credential is redacted with a notice; reply streaming is held until the reply is complete while it is enabled; it stores only detection metadata under $THOR_HOME/secretshield/ and makes no network calls.

name: secure-env-ingress
description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing .env secrets and native encrypted Browser Vault login/TOTP/card storage; retained exact-parent login, saved TOTP, protected payment fields, transient codes and approved secret operations outside chat and model input. Browser destinations follow native Vault classification, origins and stamped-control selection, with bounded frame/Shadow extensions and asynchronous owner/profile/lease/cancellation checks. No CSS/history locks, sibling-tab fallback, core override or login backend registration. Disclosure — in-process internal Thor Vault, browser, gateway, redaction and config APIs can break on host updates; setup instructions require approval for privileged host/TLS changes; TLS listens on all interfaces by default; the gateway hook observes messages for sender binding. Native encrypted card storage includes CVC. Site input callbacks can authorize or auto-submit; unknown outcomes need external verification before retry. SHA-256-pinned administrator-allowlisted operation consumers run unsandboxed with gateway privileges, none enabled by default; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer. Links authorize their holder, not submitter identity. Explicit .env ingress adds approved missing keys; setup bootstrap reads selected-profile .env owner IDs.

name: seedguard
description: Secret firewall: private keys, seed phrases, API keys and 2FA codes become placeholders before they reach the model; armed tools can still use them. Disclosure — rewrites provider requests, tool arguments, tool results, final replies and inbound chat messages to replace detected secrets with placeholders; real values are kept only in process memory, scoped per chat, and are released to the allowed tools (`terminal`, `execute_code` by default) while you arm a secret or set `rehydrate: always`, so an armed agent can use or misuse that secret; writes `hmac.key` and a no-values `events.jsonl` under its plugin data directory; `/seedguard doctor` reads `config.yaml` read-only.

name: selaeron-paperclip-sel9
description: Posts one approved, comment-only writeback on a Paperclip issue, bound to the issue's current live run; never changes issue status. Fail-closed: nothing is approved until PAPERCLIP_APPROVED_ORIGIN and PAPERCLIP_APPROVED_ISSUES are set. Disclosure — adds a model-callable tool that posts a comment (fixed template plus up to 120 chars of model text) to a Paperclip issue, using your PAPERCLIP_API_KEY against PAPERCLIP_API_URL, after a read-only live-run lookup; posts only to the exact https origin in PAPERCLIP_APPROVED_ORIGIN and the issue IDs in PAPERCLIP_APPROVED_ISSUES (read from the process environment at load time), with no per-call Thor approval prompt; never changes issue status; no telemetry, shell commands, file writes or background processes.

name: selenite
description: Takes friction off the person, treated as accessibility: one test, "does this step, wait or check earn its cost to you?", applied to steps handed to a person, agents parking Kanban work on each other for reasons that aren't real, and checks that can't change the decision. Calm mode cues the agent toward no questions and one-line replies when your messages show overload. A read-only cleanse ranks what to clear across skills, plugins, hooks, approvals, runbooks and boards. Walls always stand: credentials, spend, publishing, destructive steps, legal, named freezes. Adds /frictionless, the selenite_ledger and selenite_show tools, two fake-gate tools, skills, a Desktop page and a dashboard tab. Disclosure — no network, no credentials and no shell from the plugin itself; /frictionless starts an agent turn through the gateway only when Thor's allow_gateway_injection is on, otherwise it prints the text for you to send; selenite_show and ledger, cleanse and evolve tool calls send local Desktop events (short keys only, no paths or private text) that the open Selenite page reacts to; hooks add a context note in Calm mode, and in fake_gate_mode "nudge" (default) or "ask" they add a note to, or hand back once with a question, a kanban_block that reads as agent bureaucracy (they never approve, unblock, close or edit a card, and any error fails open); when you approve a safe command once or for the session, its approval key is logged as an allowlist candidate (denials, timeouts and dangerous commands are never logged); writes a metadata-only ledger (no block reasons or prompt text, 0600, rotates at 4 MB), per-card question counts and a counts-only snapshot under plugin-data/antibeaurocracy/, and reports under the Selenite state directory (SELENITE_STATE, else XDG state, else THOR_HOME/plugin-data/selenite, else ~/.local/state/selenite); reads kanban.db read-only (the CLI audit's --all-homes flag adds every ~/.thor* home); the cleanse pass (the selenite_ledger tool, the Desktop page and the dashboard tab can run it) reads, read-only, the hook commands in ~/.claude/settings.json, the skill folders of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and ~/.agents, and Thor plugin manifests; the `thor antibeaurocracy audit` CLI also reads agent rule files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md) and the SOUL.md/AGENTS.md of every Thor home and profile; the bundled frictionless skill's miner script, when the agent runs it, reads your own messages from local agent transcripts (Claude Code, Codex and Thor state.db, all read-only) and keeps only counts plus a few redacted samples (emails, IPs, tokens, secrets and your home path stripped), 0600, in that state directory; the CLI's opt-in --judge runs a command you name, the plugin never does; all hooks turn off with hooks: false or SELENITE_HOOKS=0.

name: sem-weave
description: CLI-backed skills for local code discovery and entity-diff review with Sem, plus optional Weave branch-merge previews. Requires user-installed CLIs; does not apply edits or merges, install binaries, or change Git configuration.

name: send-lock
description: Default-deny pre_tool_call hook: it allows a short explicit list (read-only tools, ls/pwd/whoami, a plain `curl -q -s <URL>` GET, and two narrow write_file paths gated by an owner step 0-4) and blocks every other tool call with a plain-English reason. A friendly first layer, not a containment boundary. Disclosure — it reads the owner config file (<THOR_HOME>/axiom-owner.json or the path in AXIOM_OWNER_CONFIG) and the THOR_HOME and AXIOM_OWNER_CONFIG environment variables; it writes only one log line per refusal and one at load to <THOR_HOME>/logs/send-lock.log (tool name and block kind, never arguments); it blocks every tool call not on its allowlist; it makes no network calls, no subprocess calls and no model calls, and it stores no credentials and never updates itself.

name: sendblue
description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

name: sendsafe
description: Inspect hidden Word and Excel content before risky reads, and create verified visible-content sharing copies.

name: senler-io-user
description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — Thor installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Thor) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass Thor allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Thor approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<THOR_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native Thor messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.

name: sentinel
description: Local runtime policy, redacted execution history, supported-file recovery, agent preflight tools and a runaway breaker, with Telegram-ready /sentinel commands. Trusted hooks, not an OS sandbox; native approval modes apply and backups retain original bytes.

name: sentinel-governance
description: Audit-first Thor tool governance with profile settings, profile-local policy, exact tool rules and per-event native approval. Settings enforce cannot be loosened by the environment; once resolved, enforce stays on per profile/process until restart. Unknown allow/approval requires named tools excluding terminal/execute_code. Known read_file/search_files/write_file/patch calls receive pre-rule credential/governance path checks and require canonical absolute regular-file targets; directory/default-path searches and ambiguous aliases are refused. Ordinary allowed file alternatives proceed without asking. Other tools remain whole-tool operator trust decisions; arguments/capabilities are not inspected beyond the disclosed file checks. Disclosure — runtime inspects arguments and file metadata, reads configuration/policy and a local audit key, and writes argument-free decision records plus HMAC-signed mode-change/policy-failure records under the active Thor home (sentinel/). It starts no network calls/subprocesses and reads no external credential contents. Report shows sanitized counts/current policy health; another plugin can veto a Sentinel allow. User-invoked replay copies raw selected history DB/WAL/journal files into 0700 temporary directories with 0600 files, uses an isolated worker and returns counts only; it writes no Sentinel journal events. Current profile is default; --all-profiles is explicit. Copy/scan budget is two seconds with 2,000 calls/20,000 messages/200 sessions; full database copy cost and retained-history limits apply. macOS uses validated per-user system temp outside HOME/profiles, otherwise /tmp; Linux uses /tmp, ignoring TMPDIR/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Normal/timeout/signal shutdown cleans snapshots; killing both processes, power loss or filesystem errors may leave private files. Later replay sweeps eligible marked, unleased, owner-only leftovers older than 60 seconds; unmarked directories remain. Deletion is not secure erasure. Audit defaults to no veto, but host hook timeouts can block. Enforcement is restrictive; filename heuristics are partial and can overmatch benign names. Opaque tools, remote backends, filesystem races and same-privilege/key holders are outside these protections; local HMACs are not an append-only guarantee. Experimental, not a firewall or sandbox.

name: sentinel-security
description: Scans scripts before the agent runs them and blocks, asks for approval, or allows them; also hashes files. Disclosure — reads script files referenced in terminal/execute_code tool calls and any path given to its tools (hash and pattern scan only, never executed or returned); appends an audit line (path, SHA-256, verdict) to plugin-data/sentinel-security/sentinel-audit.jsonl in your Thor home; when a VT_API_KEY is configured, sends each scanned file's SHA-256 (never its contents) to www.virustotal.com, including from the pre-run guard before every flagged command.

name: sentinel-vision
description: Tell Thor what to watch on a camera, screen or video, and Sentinel detects events, stores snapshots and injects alerts into your chat. A local change detector and configurable call caps reduce vision-model usage; rules, event history and feedback make the watcher useful over time. Frames and rule text are sent to your configured model; see the README for setup, privacy and limitations. Disclosure — Captures from local cameras, the screen (mss), image folders, video files and stream/snapshot URLs you configure. A background watcher (capture threads, judge workers, scheduler) starts about 25 s after load when rules exist and sends camera/screen frames and rule text to your configured vision model. Snapshots, events, teaching images and chat routes are stored under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/sentinel-vision/. Fired rules inject alerts as user messages and can replay a rule's stored action prompt as unattended agent turns; outside the classic CLI this needs plugins.entries.sentinel-vision.allow_gateway_injection: true. The model can name local image/video paths to read and send to the vision model.

name: seomatic
description: SEO agent for your own website through SEOmatic's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.seomatic.ai/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): Google Search Console queries and pages, striking-distance keywords, traffic drops, site audits, keyword, backlink and SERP competitor research, AI visibility and AI citations (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews), daily local rankings and Google Business Profile, plus site fixes staged in SEOmatic for WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, Wix and other connected sites. Bundles twenty workflow skills (SEO audit, striking distance, traffic drop, CTR fix, cannibalization, content refresh, keyword research, competitor gap, local SEO and more). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/ in the repo's thor/ folder), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to SEOmatic's hosted server (app.seomatic.ai) and acts on the user's own SEOmatic workspace with their role in it; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Search Console, stored-data and site audit reads are free; live market data (keyword metrics and suggestions, backlinks, SERP competitors, local SERP visibility), fresh AI visibility scans and approved fixes spend SEOmatic AI credits, content generation quotes its estimate and runs only after the user confirms, and generate_article uses one prepaid article unit. Fixes proposed through the tools are staged in SEOmatic; approving, publishing, undoing and rolling back change the user's live site and require an explicit confirm from the user. SEOmatic's own background agents follow the workspace's autonomy mode set in SEOmatic: in Assisted, the default for new workspaces, reversible changes (titles, descriptions, internal links, schema, page text, articles) go live on their own with a one-click undo, while new pages, bulk changes, redirects and removals wait for the user; in Approval mode every change waits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which registers an OAuth client, opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Thor's connect timeout instead of hanging. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with thor mcp add seomatic --url https://app.seomatic.ai/api/mcp --auth oauth (or an API key header) and keep the skills.

name: sequenzy
description: Run Sequenzy email marketing through Sequenzy's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.sequenzy.com/v1/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): subscribers, lists, tags and segments, campaigns with A/B tests, automated sequences, templates, transactional email, inbox replies, webhooks, integrations, and delivery and engagement stats. Bundles the sequenzy-email-marketing workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Sequenzy's hosted server (api.sequenzy.com) and acts on the user's Sequenzy account with the permission level they approved at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Campaigns, sequences and transactional sends email real recipients and count toward the user's Sequenzy plan. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores the OAuth token under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: serpapi
description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, Travel Explore, and page extraction for Thor Agent. Scrape pages, map URLs, or crawl sites.

name: serpkite
description: SerpKite web search and extract provider for Thor Agent. Google web results through /v1/search and pages as Markdown through /v1/webpage. Requires SERPKITE_API_KEY (https://app.serpkite.com/keys). Disclosure — Sends the search queries and the URLs the agent issues to SerpKite's API at `api.serpkite.com`, authenticated with `SERPKITE_API_KEY`.

name: session-cassettes
description: Record one good session's read-only tool results as a cassette, pin the facts a good answer must contain, then replay the same request against another model, prompt or skill: tool_execution middleware answers every tool call of the replayed turn from the recording (exact hit, or a search/slice of a snapshot of the workspace files the session's results named; anything else gets a cassette-miss error) and never calls the real tool; the verdict is PASS, FAIL, DIVERGED or INVALID from the pins, with no judge model. Disclosure — cassettes are plain JSON in the plugin data folder and hold the request, the answer and the full results of recorded tools (file contents, search hits, web search results and extracts, skill text, session-search results, output of a fixed list of read-only terminal commands) plus the redacted text of workspace files those results named; at the end of a recorded turn the plugin reads those files from the session's working directory (hidden paths and secret-looking names such as key files, credentials, auth.json and token.json skipped by file name, Thor's redact_sensitive_text applied to the rest, which does nothing if the user has switched Thor's redaction off); `thor cassette run` starts two `thor chat -Q` children (argument list, no shell, no -z, no --yolo, THOR_YOLO_MODE removed from the child, run refused when the gateway's environment has THOR_YOLO_MODE set at ping time, which is not Thor's own startup yolo flag; the child's output is held in two temporary files in the system temp folder until the child exits) and the replay's model call goes to whatever model/provider the user names, so a cloud model is sent the request and the recorded results; if no session claims the replay its turn runs live with real tools under the user's own approval settings and is graded INVALID afterwards; the middleware sees every session's tool calls and passes unbound sessions through, keeping only an in-memory count of them so a late claim can be marked INVALID; the pre_llm_call and post_llm_call hooks are called for every turn of every session with the message and the answer, and keep nothing for a session the plugin has not bound; it registers the /cassette slash command and the `thor cassette` CLI command; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no self-update, no third-party dependencies.

name: session-dashboard
description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the Thor desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

name: session-find
description: A search window over your Thor session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. Finds a session by an exact word, identifier or phrase through the gateway's own full text index, and by meaning as well when a session-find service answers on loopback; typed filters (in:, -in:, after:, before:, me:, repo: and quoted phrases) are mirrored as chips under the box. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. The window half ships off by default and is switched on in the app's plugin inventory. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your Thor session database read-only.

name: session-flow
description: Session pane for Thor Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local Thor gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.close, session.delete); captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.

name: session-lens
description: Read-only observability for Thor Desktop: what each session cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron/gateway state, config.yaml and .env (key names, and the values of keys an adapter uses); with the credentials Thor' own resolvers return, calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README), sending Grok CLI client headers to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and a Claude Code user-agent to api.anthropic.com; Thor' resolvers may renew Thor' Codex, Nous and xAI logins and, when Thor holds no other Anthropic credential, Claude Code's login; runs the local monid CLI when installed; an Anthropic one-token Claude Haiku probe is off by default; writes no Thor state itself and sends no session content anywhere.

name: session-mirror
description: Mirrors Thor Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Thor's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $THOR_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $THOR_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `thor session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $THOR_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

name: session-receipts
description: Session Receipts turns a Thor session, a date range, or a kanban card's evidence chain into one self-contained offline HTML document: the original ask, every tool call as a timed node, failures and retries exactly as recorded (never collapsed into the success that followed), per-model token spend, and the cost Thor recorded, with a reconciliation delta. A client theme renders the same data as a paper document for sharing; `--redact` writes a share-safe copy with a redaction manifest (secrets, emails, user paths, IPs, phones, plus a user word list); and `receipts rollup --since 7d` aggregates a window into a deterministic weekly digest: failure taxonomy, cost by model and card, slowest tools by p50/p95, retry hotspots, week-over-week deltas. Standard library only; reads the local session store and kanban boards read-only; no network, no credentials, no new dependencies. Disclosure — a receipt contains the session's real text; secret masking is pattern-based (a safety net, not a guarantee), and shared copies should be reviewed before they leave the machine.

name: session-ref
description: Reference another Thor session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

name: session-relay
description: Hands a long-running conversation over to a fresh session before the context window fills up: a ⚡ chip in the status bar shows live context usage, and at the threshold (45% by default) the agent writes a hand-off note while the plugin opens a new chat, seeded with that note as its first message and named after the current one (+1). On Telegram and other messaging platforms the gateway half provides a session_relay_handoff tool; after /new it attaches that chat's note to the first message of the new session, so the fresh session opens with the hand-off. Disclosure: each relay runs one extra agent turn and therefore uses model tokens.

name: session-token-counter
description: Accumulated input/output token totals and context-window occupancy for the focused session, in the Thor Desktop status bar.

name: sessioncrew
description: Browse sessions and related projects across profiles in a Thor Desktop side panel, with observed activity, completion reminders, and project creation. Disclosure — the backend reads every profile under the Thor data root, not only profiles that enabled the plugin: profile.yaml display fields, gateway_state.json, processes.json and each state.db opened read-only (session, turn-lease, admission, worker and delegation metadata plus token/cost aggregates; only the profile label is kept from delegation task JSON; no conversation message bodies).
