Folder browsing, folder creation and non-overwriting IDEA.md writes run on the gateway filesystem from the user's own dialog and are not confined to the Thor root (the Thor root and common credential directories are refused). Creating sessions or generating a project idea runs on the selected profile and sends the project name to that profile's configured model provider. On POSIX systems a liveness fallback may run `ps -o state= -p <pid>` without a shell. No credential-store reads, telemetry, self-updater or separate listener.

name: sessionguard
description: Work survives the session. Keeps a local work-state checkpoint for every session, built from tool evidence: current task, files touched, recent tool calls and outcomes, failure count, and the agent's own progress notes saved through the session_checkpoint tool. A checkpoint closes only when the agent marks its task done; otherwise the next session from the same origin (same platform and sender) is briefed from the most recent open checkpoint, so work interrupted by a dead process, a dropped gateway, or a compaction resumes from evidence instead of a lossy transcript. Subagent and cron sessions neither record checkpoints nor receive briefings. Disclosure: observes user messages (only the latest task text is kept, truncated, with credential-shaped values redacted), tool call arguments (stored only as short summaries), and turn outcomes, in profiles where it is enabled; all state is stored locally under $THOR_HOME/sessionguard/; makes no network calls.

name: severian
description: Local-first long-term memory for Thor agents: a canonical append-only store (SQLite or PostgreSQL+pgvector) with five-dimensional tenant/profile/collection/agent/session scope, hybrid BM25+vector retrieval with a re-ranker, memories that cite the observations they came from, per-turn user facts, real dates next to relative times, truth resolution when a newer fact replaces an older one, and a conflict note when two returned memories disagree. Fully offline by default; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B semantic embeddings opt-in, locally or in a user-owned sidecar. On OmniMemEval's public long-term-memory leaderboard (its own models, prompts and full public sets) it scores 90.6 LongMemEval (1st), 87.3 LoCoMo (2nd) and 71.6 BEAM 100K (2nd, within noise of the lead); it re-ran LCM-X to check the board's records, and per-question results, a strict second marker and scripts are published in the repo. Disclosure — stores every conversation turn in one SQLite database under the Thor root (`<thor root>/severian`) shared by all profiles with rows scoped per profile, or in the PostgreSQL database named by `SEVERIAN_DSN`; the opt-in Qwen/Granite embeddings download a model from Hugging Face on first use, and the opt-in embedding sidecar sends memory text to the URL you configure.

name: sgme
description: SGME (拾光记忆) self-hosted long-term memory engine — tagged memories with provenance, per-turn recall, automatic session refinement, a skills library, wiki knowledge base, care signals, communication roles and a three-pool task system (ideas/demands/projects), all behind one HTTP service you own. The plugin is a thin bridge: no LLM, no database, everything heavy runs in your SGME server (local or remote). Disclosure — the plugin talks only to the SGME server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:9910, SGME_BASE_URL for a remote server), sending SGME_AGENT_KEY / SGME_ADMIN_KEY read through Thor's secret scope; each session's user, assistant and tool messages are appended to that server and refined into memories at session end by an LLM you configure on the SGME side; its sgme_* tools let the model read and change memories, skills, wiki pages and tasks on that server and write skill packages under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/sgme/skills/ on the SGME host; credential names in the SGME vault can be listed, and reading a credential value into the conversation is off by default (credential_get_enabled / SGME_ENABLE_CREDENTIAL_GET); no third-party services, no telemetry.

name: shaderbruecke
description: Make GLSL shaders with your Thor agent, see them render, tune them by hand, and take them into the tool you ship in, with a frame-by-frame proof on every export. Disclosure: each render starts a headless Chromium child on the Thor host with the network blocked; no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials.

name: shadow
description: Find out which model is better at your work, from your real prompts. After a plain chat turn, the same conversation goes in the background to a second model you choose, through ctx.llm. /shadow vote shows both answers blind in random order; models are revealed after you vote, and your leaderboard shows wins with a 95% range. Off until you set compare_model and allow the override; tool turns are skipped and answers are deleted after each vote. Disclosure — when enabled (compare_model set and llm.allow_model_override on), the last 12 plain-text messages of every eligible chat turn are also sent to the second model/provider you configured, costing one extra model call per compared turn; up to 100 unvoted prompt/answer pairs are kept in plugin-data/shadow until you vote, and each chat can only see the pairs it captured.

name: shadow-army
description: A different model family must PASS the exact code before the agent closes a Kanban card; it asks before a push of unreviewed code and flags deleted test assertions. Disclosure — Once armed, verifier subagents run on a second already-configured provider and read the card's repository and run the configured check command through Thor' terminal; the plugin reads Kanban databases read-only and keeps receipts in its own plugin data.

name: shapeless
description: Make and publish social media content from Thor: plan posts, edit video, generate images and clips, design carousels, and publish or schedule to LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky and more, through ShapelessAI's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE), with two skills bundled (get-started and shapelessai). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to shapelessai.com, signed in as the user, with the post text, media and brand notes the session hands it, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. Publishing tools post to the user's real social accounts, and the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks the user before each write tool. Media tools spend the account's credits at the cost each tool states; posting spends none. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from ShapelessAI's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add shapeless --url https://shapelessai.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: shared-memory-domains
description: One memory several Thor profiles share, split into domains with per-agent read/write grants: agents only propose facts, a human verifies them before they are recalled, revocation is immediate and sticky, and decisions are audited. Disclosure — no network, no subprocess, no credentials; reads and writes one local SQLite file (default THOR_HOME/plugin-data/shared-memory-domains/shared.db, or the shared db_path you configure, which is outside the plugin's data dir by design) and refuses any file it did not create; injects up to 6 verified facts per turn by default (`inject_limit`, 0–20; 0 disables recall) into the agent context (pre_llm_call); blocks the agent's own terminal/execute_code/file-tool calls that name the database (pre_tool_call trip-wire, trivially bypassed, not a sandbox); one /shared-memory admin command; admin commands and cross-domain views only from the cli surface by default. Cooperative access control inside the Thor process: an agent with shell tools can bypass it, and facts already shown stay in conversation history and in any conversation-recording memory provider.

name: sharelet
description: Share a Thor tool as a link anyone can use in a browser. Pick a tool on the local creator page, create the link and send it: guests need no Thor, account or API key, and the tool runs on your computer. Links have a run limit, expiry and off switch; guests can change only the inputs you leave open. Tools without a read-only hint need a separate confirmation for each share. Works with explicitly allowed native Thor plugin tools and MCP servers. Default links use a temporary tunnel address; stable links require your own relay or fixed public_origin. Disclosure — while enabled it serves a token-protected creator page and guest pages on 127.0.0.1; when a public link is active it downloads cloudflared 2026.10.7 from Cloudflare's official GitHub release (SHA-256 pinned in code, re-verified before each launch) and runs it as a background process that exposes only the guest port through a Cloudflare quick tunnel; anyone holding a link can run that shared tool on your computer through Thor with the inputs you leave open, up to its run limit and expiry (tools without a read-only hint need your confirmation per share); relay routing is off by default, and a relay_url you set yourself receives a random host ID, a relay secret and the current tunnel address and serves the guest landing page, so run it yourself; it writes links, run records, uploaded and generated files, its signing keys and any OpenAI key you type into its page (plaintext, owner-only file) to its own data folder; optional image recipes are off until enabled and call api.openai.com with that key or, if you enable it, your Thor profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, spending its credit. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: sharewise
description: See what your photos and videos reveal before you share them. Reports, as yes/no counts only, exact location, location detail, time, device, unique IDs, owner name, captions, hidden thumbnails, edit history, depth maps and (videos) per-frame face data; on macOS finds faces, people, street names, house numbers and plates with Apple Vision on this computer; a local review page lets the user switch areas off, draw, move, resize, rotate and reshape them; hidden areas are rebuilt from their surroundings (faces) or become a blank plate in the sign's colour, so nothing of what was there is kept; copies drop all metadata except copyright and are re-read and verified. Videos (MOV, MP4, M4V, 3GP) are cleaned without re-encoding: metadata boxes, timed-metadata tracks and unreferenced media bytes are zeroed in a copy and the whole file is scanned; faces inside videos are not hidden. Disclosure — reads JPEG, HEIC, PNG, WebP and the video types above only in a folder the user names inside the home folder or on an external drive; refuses the operating system, disk roots, the whole home folder, ~/Library, hidden and locked items, symlinks and app-managed libraries. Writes only new copies to a Sharewise/ folder inside that folder and never writes or overwrites originals. sharewise_share takes check ids, photo numbers, fixed keep choices, the user's selection codes and areas to add (never file paths), is validated by its own pre_tool_call hook, and keeping location is escalated to Thor' human-approval gate (fails closed with no human present). The agent can add areas but cannot switch them off; switching off comes from the review page's selection code (a design rule, not a cryptographic barrier). Stores the last 10 checks (paths, yes/no findings, area boxes), review pages with downsized photos and downsized finished copies in its plugin data folder; never stores metadata values or text read in photos. Sends to the model provider, as part of the conversation, the folder, file names and yes/no and area counts, and, only when the user asks for a visual check (sharewise_look), downsized finished copies that are already hidden and clean. Apple Vision runs on-device via pyobjc-framework-Vision (macOS only; elsewhere detection is off and areas can be drawn by hand). No network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry; no process-wide settings changed.

name: sheets
description: An agentic spreadsheet. Ask for a sheet and a Thor agent finds the rows on the web, each with its source, or bring your own. Thor suggests typed columns, fills only the ones you pick, explains what the answers add up to, and, once you allow it, lets any chat read your grids and propose cells, columns and rows that you approve and can undo. Formula columns, a totals row, cell formatting with highlight rules, and Excel import and export are built in. Disclosure — Build sheet, research columns and Ask start hidden Thor sessions that use your Thor tools and read third-party web pages; approval prompts inside build and research sessions are denied; import reads and export writes the one file you pick in the system dialog (text, CSV or an Excel workbook), through the plugin's own backend, and the folder source reads a folder you grant; grids live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy under plugin-data/sheets/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Thor profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; with the Data or Whiteboard plugin installed, a click hands a table or ticked rows to that page through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; no telemetry, no credentials, no shell commands or background processes of its own. Independent community project, not affiliated with Thor Labs.

name: shelldrop
description: Set up a Mac or Linux machine so AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, any CLI agent) can be run and checked from an iPhone or iPad over SSH: SSH on, tmux sessions that survive a dropped connection, Tailscale for the route in, the phone's SSH key, then the exact connection details. One skill plus Shell Drop's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.shelldrop.sh/mcp, no key, no sign-in) with four read-only tools: setup_guide, tmux_howto, generate_tmux_conf and troubleshoot_connection. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: the MCP server is a stateless Cloudflare Worker whose source is in the repo; every tool call goes to mcp.shelldrop.sh, which receives only the tool arguments (an OS name, a short task or symptom phrase, tmux.conf options), returns static text, keeps no sessions, stores nothing and does not log inputs; every tool is annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted. The skill has the agent run shell commands on the user's own machine under Thor's normal approvals: it edits ~/.tmux.conf, optionally ~/.zshrc, and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (public keys the user supplies only), and after asking runs sudo to enable SSH, install tmux or Tailscale (Tailscale's official curl | sh installer on Linux) and stop the machine sleeping. No telemetry, no credentials stored or sent. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: shelly-direct
description: Control Shelly Gen 1/2/3 devices directly on your LAN — discovery, relays, dimmers, covers, power meters. No Home Assistant, no MQTT, no cloud. Disclosure — the shelly tool switches relays, dimmers and covers on the user's LAN Shelly devices with no per-action confirmation; discovery sends UDP broadcasts and HTTP probes (with digest auth when a device password is set) to private LAN addresses only (RFC1918, 100.64/10, IPv6 ULA), and the agent can sweep a CIDR range only when the user sets allow_model_sweep: true; no cloud, no telemetry.

name: shiftrepair
description: Repair weekly staff schedules with minimum disruption, verified constraints and a shared Desktop board.

name: shinjuku
description: A private USDC wallet for Thor that the user holds. It pays paid web services and APIs (x402) privately: the seller and the blockchain do not see which wallet paid. From plain requests Thor checks a price, finds paid APIs, pays, and shows a wallet card (/shinjuku:wallet), receipts, add funds and a send back to the user's own wallet. New plugin. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/ + a small launch.mjs). The wallet itself is the npm package shinjuku at the exact version in mcp.json (0.3.218), which the user installs once (npm install -g; npm.cmd on Windows) and sets up in a terminal (shinjuku setup; shinjuku.cmd on Windows). Disclosure — Crypto payments: runs the user's own closed-source Shinjuku wallet (npm shinjuku@0.3.218 / shinjuku-shield@0.3.218, installed by the user, not covered by the pinned sha) as an untrusted MCP server; Thor asks before every price check, payment, send, deposit address, backup and stop, but searches, receipts and balance reads run without asking, and a balance read (and wallet start) moves USDC the user added into the user's own private balance. Payments go through Shinjuku's payment service (pay.shinjukustaition.com or its .onion), which takes a per-payment fee, and paid AI answers send the prompt to api.usepod.ai over Tor; with Tor on, traffic goes over Tor, and on Windows the wallet downloads Tor from torproject.org and runs it in the background. Keys stay in the wallet's folder in the user's account.

name: ship
description: Deploy static websites, landing pages, and prototypes instantly, through the hosted ShipStatic MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.shipstatic.com). Free, no account needed: publishing works with no sign-in, and the site comes back with a link to share and a claim link to keep it; the account tools (your sites, your domains) need a sign-in Thor does not start on this server and answer Unauthorized; to keep sites in an account, use the ShipStatic CLI with an API key. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only, no code. Disclosure — connects Thor to the hosted ShipStatic MCP server at https://mcp.shipstatic.com; the files the agent publishes are sent to ShipStatic and nowhere else; a site published with no account is public, stays up for 3 days and is kept through its claim link (anyone who opens that link and signs in owns the site); the plugin holds no key or token; it marks its server untrusted, so every write call (a publish, a delete, a domain change) goes through Thor's approval gate and is refused in unattended runs, and a user who wants unattended publishing sets their own `mcp_servers.ship` entry to `trust: full`; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: ship-reel
description: Turns a URL and a one-line brief into a finished product demo reel. The agent plans a shot list and dry-runs it against the live page, records it in headless Chromium, edits it with auto-zoom, a drawn cursor, captions, title and end cards, optional local voice-over and a music bed into 16:9 and 9:16 MP4s, verifies the result (duration, resolution, black or frozen frames, loudness, captions) and fixes what fails, then drafts the post text. It never posts. Disclosure — opens the user-supplied URL and the pages in its shot list in headless Chromium behind a local filtering proxy; runs ffmpeg/ffprobe and local render worker processes; writes only to its plugin data directory (or SHIP_REEL_HOME); with the optional kokoro-onnx extra installed, downloads the Kokoro TTS model (~120 MB) once from its official GitHub release, SHA-256 pinned. Public hosts only: loopback, private, link-local/metadata, CGNAT and reserved addresses are refused for every URL and browser request unless the user sets allow_private_hosts or SHIPREEL_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=1. Sign-in, payment, send, submit and delete clicks trigger a Thor approval prompt via a pre_tool_call hook; typing into password fields is refused. No telemetry, no API keys.

name: shipframe
description: AI coding workflows for teams that plan, prove, and ship — 44 read-only skills covering project context refresh, feature discovery, planning, implementation, TDD, two-phase code review, release evidence, PR/MR creation, project wiki knowledge, and accessibility/security auditing. Native plugin: a plugin.yaml manifest plus a dependency-free Python entrypoint that registers every skill through ctx.register_skill (no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars). Disclosure — the skills themselves instruct the agent to run shell commands (git, gh, project test suites, occasional installer commands) as part of the workflows they describe, and some skills write project context files such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the user's repositories; the plugin code makes no network calls, spawns no processes, reads no credentials or files outside its own tree, ships no telemetry, and contains no self-updater (updates arrive only through sha-bump PRs in this catalog).

name: shipwrit
description: Outcome-based release verification for Thor: detect false-green deployments with bounded user journeys and redacted evidence receipts. Disclosure — sends the HTTP requests in the project's release-witness.json (GET by default; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE steps when writes are allowed) to the hosts that file lists, which may include localhost or LAN addresses; writes receipts and release state under `.release-witness/` in the working directory, and its pre_verify hook can ask the agent to keep working when a detected deploy command has no passing receipt.

name: shodan
description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

name: shopmate
description: Personal shopper agent: finds products with live Google Shopping prices and photos (SerpAPI, or a labelled demo catalog without a key), quotes delivery to the customer's location with doorstep or pickup-stop options, and on an explicit yes takes payment by Paystack (NGN, GHS, KES, ZAR, USD, XOF, EGP, RWF) or crypto via NOWPayments, verifying amount+currency with the provider before marking the order paid. Supports conversation-scoped order lookup (cross-conversation email/phone lookup is an operator setting, off by default), saved-card charges via Paystack charge_authorization (cards are bound to the conversation that paid and identified by a local opaque card_id; a pre_tool_call hook sends saved-card checkout with confirm=true to a Thor approval), request_refund (Paystack Refund API + manual crypto payouts; optional NGN bank transfers only when the allow_transfers plugin setting is on, which moves the operator's Paystack balance and is off by default; confirm=true on all refund methods also goes through the same Thor approval, and bank_transfer requires account_name), webhook signature verification (HMAC x-paystack-signature helper for operators), and contact_support with optional SUPPORT_EMAIL/SUPPORT_WHATSAPP — no BVN/phone identity lookups. 17 tools plus the shopmate:shopping skill. Disclosure — payments plugin: on checkout it creates Paystack payment links / charge_authorization charges and NOWPayments crypto invoices on the operator's own merchant keys (no money moves until the customer pays, or a saved-card charge or refund confirm is approved in Thor); request_refund can call Paystack Refund / Transfers (transfers gated by the allow_transfers plugin setting) or leave a manual crypto payout pending; the reusable Paystack authorization code is stored in orders.sqlite and is never returned as card_id; network calls to serpapi.com, api.paystack.co, api.nowpayments.io, open.er-api.com, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, ipapi.co (auto-locate is on by default and sends the host's public IP when a conversation has no saved location) and maps.app.goo.gl (expanding shared Maps short links); carts, saved locations, saved card authorizations (last4/brand/bank and conversation binding only), support tickets and orders (customer name, email, phone and address) are stored in the plugin data directory; API keys are optional and read through Thor's secret scope.

name: shorguard
description: Post-quantum crypto guard. Stops the agent from writing quantum-vulnerable public-key crypto (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, EdDSA, X25519, DH, DSA) before it lands: pre_tool_call checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code and, in the default block mode, refuses calls that ADD classical crypto, returning the NIST replacement (ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA) with working cryptography>=48 code so the agent rewrites it (approve mode routes to Thor's approval gate instead; warn mode only annotates). Tools shorguard_scan / shorguard_explain, /shorguard (status, mode, scan, explain) and `thor shorguard scan` give a post-quantum readiness grade with text, JSON or SARIF output and CI exit codes. 52 rules across Python, JS/TS, Go, JVM, Rust, .NET, shell/CI, TLS config, PEM keys and JWT algorithms, mapped to NIST IR 8547 (deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035). Disclosure — reads the content of inspected tool calls, the file a write_file is about to overwrite (to flag only newly added crypto) and paths you ask it to scan; writes its own plugin state (counters and the last 50 events: time, action, tool, file name, rule ids — never code or arguments) and its own settings when changed via /shorguard; writes a report only with --output. No network, subprocesses, credentials, telemetry or background work.

name: shotlane
description: A real browser for your agent: screenshots, phone, tablet and desktop checks, pages as Markdown and HTML to PDF, from Shotlane's hosted MCP server (https://shotlane.dev). Disclosure — connects to Shotlane's hosted MCP server at https://shotlane.dev/mcp (declared trust: untrusted, so write-capable calls ask first); every tool call, with its URL or HTML, goes to shotlane.dev with the API key in SHOTLANE_API_KEY as a Bearer header, and successful calls spend the account's Shotlane credits; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill also teaches the agent to call Shotlane's REST API directly with its script (URLs or local HTML files sent to shotlane.dev, results written to files you name), to use keyless shotlane.dev/md/ and /shot/ fetches, and to sign you up for a key by sending the email address you give it to shotlane.dev.

name: show-your-work
description: An evidence board for a change's acceptance criteria: which requirements your agent actually tested, what the imported results say, whether they still match the code, and whether you signed off. Point it at the requirements you already have (a ticket, bug report or spec in Markdown) and it shows four separate statuses per requirement, never merged into one green check: coverage (is a test linked?), outcome (latest imported JUnit run), freshness (tracked files changed since?) and human review. For review, click a requirement and then a linked test to see that test's source and its own diff against the base branch (new, changed or unchanged), plus the change under review. The agent links tests and imports reports from wherever they ran (terminal, Docker, CI); it has no tool to accept or reject. Sign-off comes from the Desktop page, /syw or thor syw. Five tools (syw_board, syw_link, syw_import, syw_run_detail, syw_test_evidence), a /syw command, a thor syw CLI, a Desktop page and a workflow skill. Disclosure — runs no tests and makes no network or model calls; reads syw.toml, the criteria file, tracked files (to hash them) and JUnit XML inside the project folder (paths outside it and symlinks refused), runs read-only git (rev-parse, merge-base, diff, show, ls-files) in the project folder when you open a test's evidence or the change panel, stores links, results, hashes and reviews in SQLite under the profile's plugin-data, and writes show-your-work-review.md into the project only when you export.

name: showly
description: Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from Thor Agent, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to thor` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.thor/config.yaml.

name: showreel
description: Turn any Thor session into a demo video under 90 seconds. Six observer hooks record what the session actually did (the ask, terminal commands and output, file edits, screenshots, token usage), scrubbed twice for secrets; a deterministic storyboard keeps a failing test and its fix together and fits a hard 89 s budget; Pillow and your own ffmpeg render a 1080p MP4 (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) with burned-in captions, an .srt and a poster. Desktop half: a Showreel page with a moment editor (drop beats, edit captions) and inline player, a REC chip, and a player card for showreel_render results. Narration is off by default; optional free offline voice (espeak-ng or piper on PATH), Thor text_to_speech, or the user's own ElevenLabs key only when explicitly chosen, with `thor showreel plan` showing the exact text and character count first. Disclosure — records every session by default (capture on): the user's prompts, terminal commands and output, file edits, token usage and any image file whose path appears in tool output, scrubbed for secret patterns (best effort; screenshot and image pixels are not scrubbed) into its plugin-data SQLite DB; old recordings are pruned to the newest keep_sessions (30) only when a video is rendered; runs ffmpeg/ffprobe (and espeak-ng or piper with local narration) as subprocesses with fixed argument lists; writes renders to its plugin-data renders folder or the user's output_dir; no network unless narration is set to elevenlabs (HTTPS to api.elevenlabs.io with the caption text, using the user's ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) or thor (the TTS the user configured); no telemetry, no background processes, no self-updates.

name: shvl-agent-plugin
description: Read authorised SHVL workspace receivables and connected Xero financial reports through a hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server, with a skill for selecting a workspace and interpreting the results. Disclosure — enabling this package connects Thor to SHVL's hosted MCP server at https://shvl.app/mcp/v2, and the README's OAuth setup adds a native `shvl` server at https://shvl.app/mcp/v2/oauth signed in through Thor' MCP OAuth flow (that native entry replaces the package's server); tool calls send the selected workspace and requested parameters to SHVL and return business receivables and Xero financial data to Thor and its configured model service. Access needs an SHVL account with an active trial or subscription and the applicable workspace and Xero permissions. The server's runtime tool set is outside the pinned Git commit. The package has no local executable code, install scripts, bundled credentials, background processes or telemetry.

name: sidebar-cycle
description: Step through Thor Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

name: sidebar-manager
description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

name: sidecar
description: Remote brain, local hands: a paired execution backend that lets a remote Thor run terminal, file, patch, search and execute_code commands on the user's local machine. A local daemon applies a workspace boundary and a hard deny list (privilege escalation, recursive root deletes, download-to-shell, Apple Events, keychain access, outbound network shells), and by default asks the person at the keyboard before anything that is not a side-effect-free read-only command. The pairing token is 32 random bytes, stored mode 0600 and compared in constant time; the daemon binds to loopback by default and warns otherwise. Commands run as the local user with a sanitized environment (no provider keys or SSH agent socket), a timeout and a process-group kill; every decision is written to a local JSONL audit log with command text redacted for common secret shapes and no command output stored. The remote plugin makes no network calls of its own beyond the configured daemon URL, has no Python dependencies, no telemetry and no self-updater. Not a sandbox: an approved command runs with the user's privileges; pair with Glassbox for kernel enforcement. macOS and Linux only.

name: siemless
description: Agent security telemetry for SIEMs. Every tool call, file read, shell command, outbound request, approval, subagent, scheduled job and configuration change a Thor agent makes becomes an OCSF 1.9 security event; 14 deterministic rules correlate them into findings (secret access then egress, prompt-injection chains, credential discovery, persistence, governance tampering, …) with MITRE ATT&CK 20.1 mapping and evidence labelled observed or inferred. Exports as JSON Lines (Wazuh), RFC 5424 syslog, CEF, Splunk HEC and Elastic ECS, with a pack and 22 Sigma rules. Desktop page with evidence chains and exporter health; /siemless and thor siemless incl. replay of recorded sessions. Disclosure — observer hooks only (no pre_tool_call, no middleware, no tools; nothing is blocked or rewritten). Reads only the hook payloads Thor passes, bounded and redacted before storage; prompt text, model output, tool results, file bodies and message text are never stored (hashes and lengths only; record_prompts adds a 200-char redacted preview). Writes its own SQLite database, JSONL files and spool under plugin-data/siemless/ (0600). Network: none by default; with remote_export true and a destination set, sends the configured event scope to that syslog (UDP/TCP/TLS), Splunk HEC, Elastic or JSON receiver endpoint over verified TLS (plain HTTP to 127.0.0.1 only behind a lab switch); tokens via agent.secret_scope.get_secret, never read from .env. Three daemon threads per process (pipeline, dispatch, settings watch). The dashboard half reads plugin settings through thor_cli.config.load_config. `/siemless` works in any chat that can run plugin commands: it shows stored findings and events (tool names, targets, hosts, session ids across sessions), `ack` marks findings reviewed, and `replay <file>` reads a JSONL file the user names and runs it through the detections, labelled as a replay. No shell commands, no telemetry to the author, no self-updater. The install scanner reports caution because the detector lists the patterns it looks for (ssh paths, webhook hosts, curl|sh, cron, env dumps) in siemless_core/sensitive.py and in the tests.

name: sightline
description: Give your Thor agent a Solana wallet without giving it your wallet. Intent-level SOL and SPL tools, including Solana Pay payment links; every send is simulated, explained in plain English and checked by a firewall against human-issued, time-boxed, revocable grants (caps per day, week or month) before the plugin signs it. Cron jobs and bots can pay inside a grant unattended. Through its tools the model never sees the key, has no raw-transaction tool and cannot create or widen grants (on Thor' local terminal backend the agent's shell could read .env or edit the grant database; edited grants are refused, and a sandboxed terminal backend is recommended for real funds). ALLOW / APPROVE / BLOCK with a hash-chained audit log and a Desktop pane. Devnet by default. Disclosure — crypto wallet: stores a Solana secret key in the profile .env (never shown to the model or in tool output) and sends simulation and signed transaction requests to the configured Solana RPC (default api.devnet.solana.com); mainnet only with SIGHTLINE_ALLOW_MAINNET=1. Payments inside a human-issued grant are signed and sent without a prompt, including from cron jobs; everything else needs your approval. On the local terminal backend the agent's shell can read .env and the grant database, so use a sandboxed terminal backend for real funds. No telemetry.

name: signado
description: Find warm leads on LinkedIn through Signado's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.signado.io/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): list and read warm leads and hiring leads, export them, find work emails, draft first messages, and add, preview, schedule or run the LinkedIn sources that watch keywords, posts, creators and company pages. Bundles three skills: a warm-lead brief, a post engagement catcher and a competitor audience watch. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Signado's hosted server (mcp.signado.io) and acts on the Signado workspace the user chose at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. find_email, draft_message, preview_source, add_source, set_source_schedule and run_source_once spend Signado credits, and a Daily or Custom source keeps spending on each scheduled run. Lead results include LinkedIn posts and comments written by other people, which the skills treat as data, never as instructions. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 18+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: signal-atlas
description: Turn a public source into a visual investigation with source-linked claims, charts, and follow-ups.

name: signal-dog
description: Listens through the microphone for household sounds (a door knock, an appliance beeping, a smoke alarm or other steady tone) and sends a chat message through the agent's messaging platform. A signal dog is a dog trained to alert a deaf person to sounds; this does the same job with a microphone, and it is built by a deaf developer. Off until the user turns it on with /signaldog on. Not a certified smoke alarm: it can miss sounds and raise false alerts, with measured rates and limits in the README. Disclosure: microphone: while switched on it listens to the microphone continuously. Background process: it runs one long-running ffmpeg process (two for about 30 seconds every 10 minutes while one replaces the other), stopped when the user turns it off or the plugin unloads; ffmpeg must already be installed and the plugin never downloads anything. Audio from the microphone is never kept: it is analysed in memory and dropped, with no option to keep it. /signaldog demo writes one recording made by code (no real sound) to a private temporary folder and deletes it when the demo ends. Stored locally: a size-limited numbers log in $THOR_HOME/signal-dog/events.log (times, levels, what was detected, plus an optional note of up to 80 characters the user types after /signaldog wrong or right). The read-only tool signal_dog_recent_alerts returns alert times, kinds, pitches, the user's right and wrong marks and the listener state to the agent, so it reaches the user's model provider; it does not check who is asking, so do not use the plugin on an agent that strangers can message. Network: the plugin makes no network calls and has no telemetry; alerts are delivered by the agent through the messaging app the user already set up. No credentials are read or stored. The pre_llm_call hook only notices which chat session is live and reads no message content. While a beep keeps sounding, it edits its own first alert ("still beeping", then "no longer detected") where the messaging app allows edits, and otherwise sends periodic reminder messages (every three minutes by default, for as long as the beep continues); it never edits anyone else's messages.

name: signal-notify
description: Signal texts when a Thor turn pauses, fails or is interrupted, and when Thor waits on a clarify question, approval or sudo prompt. Sends through the user's own signal-cli HTTP daemon (the same SIGNAL_* settings as the core Signal gateway); skips Signal-origin, cron and subagent turns, and dedupes identical texts within 60s. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled turns POST to SIGNAL_HTTP_URL (plain HTTP unless that URL is https), which signal-cli delivers as a Signal message; by default each text includes up to 300 characters of the final reply (not secret-redacted) or of the redacted question/command (include_text: false or reply_chars: 0 sends none); each event has its own on/off setting; sudo passwords and clarify answers are never seen; nothing is stored on disk, at most 64 clipped reply previews are kept in memory, and each send runs on a short-lived daemon thread with a 20s timeout.

name: signaldesk
description: Draft-first lead desk for founders and marketers: scan public hiring and launch signals (HN Who is hiring, YC hiring, Show HN, Launch HN, new YC companies; optional Product Hunt with a token) and local businesses on an OpenStreetMap map (LocalLead Map: city + business type or a drawn area, shown on an OpenLayers map), score them against your ICP, draft outreach, and never send without user approval (board, Desktop, or /signaldesk approve; the model cannot approve a lead or move a lead to sent/replied/won). Cron and unattended runs fail closed. Disclosure — fetches public JSON from Algolia HN Search and the yc-oss static API, and (only when you run a map scan) geocodes with Nominatim and queries public Overpass API instances; the board loads OpenStreetMap tiles in the browser; Product Hunt GraphQL is used only when PRODUCTHUNT_TOKEN is set; optional DNS MX lookups; lead data stays in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/signaldesk/; it never sends email itself, and its pre_tool_call hook blocks other send tools unless the lead was approved by you and the run is not a cron job.

name: signet-drive
description: Your agent's own encrypted drive, with dated restore points of its memory, which only you and your agent can open unless you invite someone. Disclosure — Automatically uploads the agent's MEMORY.md and USER.md as encrypted restore points to your Signet Drive (drive.mysignet.ca by default) through the vendor's signed `signet` macOS app, about 30 minutes after a memory change and at each session start; the save tool uploads files from one save folder you choose (default: the plugin's own to-save folder), fetched files land in the plugin's own folder, and once per app version it downloads the published app archive from that server and hashes from raw.githubusercontent.com/prsnex to verify the installed app. Anyone you invite to write to the drive can place files the agent fetches, or restore points it can apply to memory only after you approve them in Thor.

name: sigrex
description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skills instruct the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data; connecting an exchange or prediction-market account gives Sigrex that account's API key or wallet private key, which the skills tell the agent to leave to the user in the Sigrex dashboard.

name: simular-box
description: Give Thor a computer of its own: box is a cloud Linux desktop with Chrome and a shell that the agent drives over MCP, around the clock, while your own machine stays free. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no code: one remote MCP server (https://mcp.box.simular.ai/mcp, streamable HTTP) and one skill. Needs a box personal key from box.simular.ai/keys, set in Settings > Plugins or as MCP_BOX_API_KEY in the profile .env. Disclosure — every tool call and the MCP_BOX_API_KEY go to mcp.box.simular.ai (Simular); the agent can run shell commands, read, write and delete files, browse sites, and hibernate, save, upgrade or delete the user's box on Simular's cloud computer; the package marks the box server trust: untrusted, so Thor asks before each tool that is not read-only until the user approves it; box use counts against the account's box plan; the user can watch and take over the box at box.simular.ai/box. Nothing runs or is stored on the local machine.

name: simular-sai
description: Give Thor a computer: hand tasks that need a screen (web apps behind a login, admin consoles, desktop software, forms with no import) to Sai, Simular's computer-use agent, which does them on a cloud computer Simular hosts and reports back in text. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only; the MCP server runs as npx @simular-ai/sai-mcp@0.4.0 over stdio, so Node.js 22.12+ and npm are required. Needs a Sai API key (from platform.simular.ai), set in Settings > Plugins or as SAI_API_KEY in the profile .env. Disclosure — Runs the npm package @simular-ai/sai-mcp@0.4.0 through npx; every task, its results and the SAI_API_KEY go to api.simular.ai and spend the account's Sai credit or free computer time; the agent can upload any local file it chooses (up to 25 MB) to Simular with sai_upload, run code on the Simular cloud computer (sai_control_exec), and approve Sai's own permission requests, without a Thor prompt; a local task view is served on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run token, and sai_live_link returns a link that lets whoever holds it control the cloud computer until it expires.

name: singularity
description: Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend: Thor's terminal, file and code tools run inside a hardened, rootless container on this machine (--containall --no-home), with CPU/memory limits and an optional per-session persistent overlay (`thor config set terminal.backend singularity`; image from `terminal.singularity_image`). Formerly built into Thor core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it drives the `apptainer` (or `singularity`) CLI you install, which pulls the configured image (default `docker://nousresearch/thor-sandbox:desktop`) and caches a SIF under your scratch directory. Your skills and registered credential files are bind-mounted read-only into the container, and because the container is a disposable sandbox Thor skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as for its other container backends.

name: siteform
description: Review planning PDFs, compare evidence-linked 3D options in Thor chat, and edit the same revision in Studio. Disclosure — The siteform_import_pdf tool reads any local .pdf file whose absolute path the agent supplies and stores a copy in this profile's SiteForm library (plugin-data/siteform); optional "use model" quantity extraction sends selected PDF text rows to your configured Thor model; OCR runs locally with bundled Tesseract tessdata_fast data, and the plugin makes no other network calls.

name: sketch-pad
description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next Thor chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

name: skill-court
description: Skill Court tests the skills your agent writes. With automatic trials turned on (opt-in: `thor court auto on` or the Desktop page's Turn on switch), after the agent writes or changes a skill, and the first time each agent-written skill's current version is used on a model, it replays that skill's real tasks with and without it in the background, in Docker sandboxes when Docker answers or answer-only (skills, todo and web tools only, judged on final answers) when it does not; `thor court trial` runs one on demand. Each pair is scored by the task's check or a blind pairwise judge; a skill that hurts is hidden from that model only (skill index, skills_list, skill_view), and the next turn shows the verdict, the cause and the SKILL.md line behind it. An appeal drafts a fix, proves it on the same tasks and writes it only when you apply it (undo restores the original). Usage evidence per skill and model from recent sessions, read-only. CLI (thor court trial/report/appeal/auto/tasks/quarantine/release/list) plus a Desktop page. Disclosure: automatic trials are off until the user turns them on (the first turn after install and after-install.md say how; `thor court auto off` stops them), within $1.00 a day of provider-reported replay spend plus 300,000 judge tokens (runs already under way finish). Trials run thor and docker/podman commands, create and delete two replay profiles cloned from yours (config, API keys, SOUL, memory, skills; never messaging channels; no MCP, other plugins, context engine, shell hooks or inline shell). Replays are single-query sessions with approvals denied, never -z. The judge (your provider, via ctx.llm) sees task text, both runs' answers and sandbox files, and for a cause a transcript excerpt and the skill. Verdicts are posted with ctx.post_message to the conversation that changed or used the skill, never into the model's context. A live SKILL.md is written only by `thor court appeal apply` or Apply fix.

name: skill-governance
description: Consolidated skill-governance plugin behind one composed hook surface: on_skill_lifecycle, on_session_start, pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call. The manifest engine enforces UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md — arrivals need a manifest row, content changes in manifested skills re-flag until re-acknowledged against a content fingerprint via the preserved /skill-manifest-ack command. The advisor engine observes behavioral skill edits (never blocking) and injects one bounded reminder to run the contrastive-refinement probe cycle (bundled as skill-governance:contrastive-refinement), recording every delivered advisory to ~/.thor/skill-probes/fire-ledger.jsonl. Both legacy state namespaces import by copy (destination-wins, sources never modified) and a conservative governance.records summary joins them (acknowledged never implies validated). A clearance Automation Blueprint (daily schedule, origin delivery) replaces both legacy schedulers and preserves both clearance procedures verbatim; the user adopts it from the blueprint gallery or /blueprint, and the plugin imports no private cron modules and writes no cron state. Stdlib only, no network calls, fail-soft everywhere (malformed state keeps hooks inert, never aborts the host turn). Disclosure — reads the profile's skills tree (SKILL.md files, fingerprinted read-only) and UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md, and copies the legacy skill-manifest / contrastive-advisor plugin state read-only on first run; writes its own plugin state, `<THOR_HOME>/skill-probes/fire-ledger.jsonl` when the opt-in advisor fires, and `plugin-data/skill-manifest/acks.json` on a manual `/skill-manifest-ack`; injects advisory reminders into turns; the optional daily clearance blueprint, once the user adopts it with `/blueprint`, runs an unattended agent that edits UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md and the plugin's dismissed list, reads past session tool calls from state.db, and writes probe notes; never deletes, never blocks tool calls, no network.

name: skill-hint
description: Local-first skill discovery: on each user turn it runs a BM25 query over the installed skill library and injects up to three candidate skill names, only when the match is confident — catches colloquial phrasing, shorthand and non-English wording that a description-written index misses. Pure standard library: no network, no model call, no API key, ~0.03 ms per query, and at most a few lines of injected context. Says nothing when nothing fits; never raises into the conversation. Disclosure — reads SKILL.md front matter and the first 1,000 characters of the body under the profile's skill roots (symlinked skill directories are followed) and keeps the index in memory; it writes nothing and sends nothing anywhere. Skill names and descriptions reach the model only when a hint is injected, exactly as they would if the model had opened the skill itself.

name: skill-layers
description: Preserve source skills, create writable derivatives, and review three-way source updates. Disclosure — publishing (only from the Desktop page, the dashboard or the `thor skill-layers` CLI; the three agent tools are read-only) writes a new `sl-*` skill folder into the active profile's skills directory and never replaces an existing one; three-way source updates run the local `git merge-file` with a scrubbed environment; history is kept under the profile's plugin data and is not removed on uninstall.

name: skill-lineage
description: Records where each skill version's content came from, so a skill that rewrites itself can be audited afterwards. For every skill write — a foreground skill_manage call, a background-review edit, or a curator consolidation — it stores the skill content fingerprint before and after, the sources present earlier in the same session (the text the user typed, tool results such as a fetched page or a file, and skills that were read), how each source is linked to the added lines — strong (at least three shared 8-word shingles), anchor (a shared operative token: a URL or host, a shell command with its first argument, a package install, a file path, an environment variable, an IP or e-mail address, that is not common across sources), or context (seen in the session, nothing measurable shared; recorded, not followed by default) — and a seq -> prev_hash -> hash chain over the entries. Text is never stored: hashes are keyed per install and the key stays in plugin-data/skill-lineage. `thor skill-lineage trace <skill>` shows where the newest version came from, `descendants <url|skill>` lists every skill a source produced, `report` lists versions carrying operative lines of no traceable origin, `verify` re-walks the chain, and `head` prints a value to record elsewhere so a later `verify --head` can tell truncation from an intact chain; a key reset is recorded in the chain and shown in `status` rather than happening silently. The plugin does not stop a write and does not judge a skill: it records and it verifies, and it does not claim a source caused an edit. Prior work on memory lineage (MemLineage, arXiv:2605.14421) is acknowledged in the README. Measured on 2026-10-22 against Thor 3166d61: Python 3.14 62 passed; Python 3.11 54 passed, 1 skipped; `thor plugins validate` reports no warning other than one known false positive (a test template that quotes a "curl | sh" instruction as data and never runs it). Evaluation (generated scenarios and 120 real-model runs) in the README; raw output in eval/. A manual end-to-end run in an isolated THOR_HOME (one real session creating a skill through skill_manage, then status/trace/descendants/report/verify/head) passed, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-10-21.txt. Disclosure — four read-only hooks (on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call); reads tool results, user messages and skill files (in this profile, every other profile's skills folder, the project's .thor/skills and the skills.external_dirs it reads from config.yaml) to compute keyed hashes; keeps hashes (no text) for 7 days per session and the lineage chain (hashes and skill names) under plugin-data/skill-lineage; no network, no credentials, never blocks or changes a tool call.

name: skill-retrieval
description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is declared via pip_dependencies in plugin.yaml, so the installer installs it. On CPython 3.14 the host's thor_yaml facade is used when PyYAML is unavailable. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (leading injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and the ids and descriptions of up to 12 shortlisted skills (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error); with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_PROVIDER=openrouter the same payload goes to openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone instead, keyed by OPENROUTER_API_KEY (each provider reads only its own key, from the environment only). A local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders, rerank scores) is appended under $THOR_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

name: skill-router
description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

name: skill-stats
description: Skill Stats shows which skills you actually use in Thor Agent, when, and how much. Type /skill-stats in any chat to see that session's skills ranked by loads with a % share, or run `thor skill-stats` in the terminal for all-time totals; switch the window from 1 day to 90, page through the rows, group them by category, and answer questions like "which skills did I lean on this week?" or "is this skill still worth keeping?" Point the command at another chat by title or short id (for example -s stageshow-bentora) to compare sessions, or add `global` from a chat to see everything combined. In `thor --tui` the same numbers open as an interactive modal: browse skills with the arrow keys, open a skill's chart, flip between bars and a cumulative line, and set the period with keys 1 to 6. The web Dashboard gains a Skill Stats tab where you pin the skills you monitor so they stay on top of the table, page 10 to 100 rows, and drill into per-skill charts. Nothing to configure: install it and the counting starts on the next session. Disclosure — no network calls, no telemetry, no shell commands and no credentials; the plugin writes only its own stats files under $THOR_HOME/skill-stats/ (plus one copy of its TUI widget file into $THOR_HOME/tui-widgets/ at startup so the modal works) and reads Thor' session registry read-only to resolve a session title or short id, never message content.

name: skill-workshop
description: Get new skills for Thor safely: mine them from your past chats (Skill Miner), build them from a description (First Principles Skill Builder), and guard against prompt injection in skills and content you bring in (Taint Shield). Scans skill writes before they land and holds back flagged external skills at first use (Skill Guard); Workshop installs need your approval. Disclosure: Skill Miner reads the Thor session database read-only through the public thor_state module (tool names and counts, plus the first request of each session in abstracted, redacted form; for one session you choose, also the ordered tool steps as argument shapes and your own messages as redacted quotes, to draft a skill from it); Skill Builder runs --version on a fixed list of common tools and nvidia-smi with a minimal environment and reads memory, disk space, skill names and model-cache folder names; Taint Shield watches tool calls in memory; Skill Guard reads the text of skills in your skills folders (and external skill folders named in config.yaml, read through Thor's config loader) when they are installed or loaded and keeps a hash and a decision for each in plugin storage. Drafts, revisions and the trusted list live in plugin storage; installing a skill writes one file into the skills folder after your approval. Two install approvals, the Shield's block-or-ask rules and Skill Guard's install scan use pre_tool_call; Skill Guard also uses transform_tool_result and pre_llm_call (hold back a flagged skill, once) and on_skill_lifecycle (scan a skill after Thor reports it installed). No network calls.

name: skillcheck
description: CI for agent skills: snapshots the pre-write state of skill writes arriving through Thor's in-band tool surface (skill_manage create/edit/patch/write_file/remove_file/delete and write_file/patch/edit_file into the skills dir; hooks observe landed writes, no pre-write blocking; creates have no prior state, out-of-band edits are detected at run time but carry no snapshot), LLM-generates regression cases as human-review drafts, re-runs them against the candidate revision in child sessions launched through the Thor subagent lifecycle API with allowed_toolsets=() (no file, shell, browser or network tools; timed-out children get a cancellation request whose accepted/refused outcome is reported), and reports GREEN / REGRESSION / FIRST-RUN. Promotion and revert are user-invoked only (slash command or CLI; not registered as model tools), and revert validates the skill name, stays strictly inside the skill folder, skips dotfiles and restores byte-exact snapshots. Disclosure — reads your skills directory and stores pre-edit snapshots of skill files plus its own state in its plugin data folder; `/skillcheck revert` (user-run only) deletes and rewrites files inside that one skill's folder to restore the snapshot, keeping the pre-revert state as another snapshot; case generation and the optional judge call the session's configured model.

name: skillens
description: Live skill-execution fidelity - watches whether the agent actually performs the steps a loaded skill requires, with a checklist pane, an in-session corrective nudge, and a status-bar fidelity score. Disclosure — records every tool call's arguments and the first 1,500 characters of its result (which can include secrets printed by tools) in a local SQLite file under `$THOR_HOME/plugin-data/skillens/` with no automatic pruning, and adds a one-time corrective context note to the model's next turn when a loaded skill's numbered steps show no matching tool calls; no network.

name: skilluminati
description: Your skills, judged blind: finds out whether each skill your Thor agent loads makes its answers better. /skilluminati <skill> takes the latest 12 times you used the skill, each with the chat as it stood at that moment, and your model answers each one twice, once with the skill and once without. The Owl, a blind judge, sees both answers and the skill's one-line description of its job, never which answer had the skill, and sees every pair twice with the answers swapped; if it picks differently the second time, the pair counts as Same. Verdicts: Enlightened (answers are clearly better with it), Dead weight (the model does this anyway, it only costs tokens), Hindrance (answers are worse with it) or Unproven (too few uses to tell yet), each marked Probable or Plausible. Built-in question sets for frontend-design, systematic-debugging and thor-agent let a fresh install run a test with no history, and /skilluminati selftest plants a helpful, a harmful and an empty skill to prove the Owl can tell them apart. Surfaces: the /skilluminati command, two read-only agent tools, a Desktop page with a sidebar entry (plugin SDK only) and a read-only dashboard backend. Disclosure — opens THOR_HOME/state.db read-only and reads installed skill files, skills/.usage.json and skills.disabled/model.default from config.yaml; for each test it sends up to 12 past tasks (the stored session system prompt, the chat up to the moment the skill loaded and any tool output in it, after best-effort regex blanking of emails, phone numbers, key-shaped strings, token-carrying URLs, money amounts and names in plugin-data/skilluminati/names.txt) plus the skill text to the active provider and model, or a per-role provider/model you configure, through ctx.llm, at up to 64 model calls per skill on your own allowance; runs start only from a local CLI/TUI/Desktop/ACP session (never cron or a messaging gateway) on a background thread; writes only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/skilluminati/; imports one private core helper (agent.skill_utils.get_all_skills_dirs) to list skill folders; no other network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials.

name: skysay
description: Configure Skysay AI agents and numbers, place calls, send SMS and inspect results. Review OAuth consent: optional write/content permissions may be preselected. Write-capable tools use Thor native approval (trust: untrusted); calls, SMS and numbers can incur charges. Disclosure — v2 connects to Skysay's full customer MCP endpoint (api.skysay.ai/mcp): with the OAuth scopes you grant, the agent can change voice agents, request paid phone numbers, place calls, send SMS, launch campaigns and create wallet checkouts that spend Skysay funds (Thor asks before each write-capable tool), and can read call recordings, transcripts and messages into your model's context.

name: slaide
description: AI presentation maker: build, edit and export PowerPoint slide decks, Word documents and Excel workbooks from chat through Slaide's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugin v1 package (plugin.json, Streamable HTTP mcp.json, one skill). Disclosure — connects to Slaide's hosted MCP server (app.slaide.de) and needs a Slaide account (free tier available); after sign-in its tools read, create, update and export the user's own Slaide documents, which uses the user's Slaide plan allowance; it cannot delete documents or change a plan. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted` so every non-read-only call asks first. Export files arrive as a private link that expires after 15 minutes. The remote tool list can change without a new pin of this package.

name: sluice
description: An airlock for agent changes. A terminal backend that runs the agent's commands and file tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) in a staged copy of the workspace, so the real files are untouched until you review the diff hunk by hunk and apply only what you approve (/sluice diff, /sluice apply, /sluice discard, also as `thor sluice`). Calls a copy cannot contain (git push, package installs, network writes, deploys, writes or deletes outside the workspace) are sent to Thor's own approval prompt labelled NOT CONTAINED. Select it with `thor config set terminal.backend sluice`. Disclosure — No network calls and no background processes. Runs the agent's shell commands and file tools on this host as the user, in a staged copy of the workspace kept under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/sluice (every non-gitignored workspace file plus a copy of .git; stages idle 14 days are deleted), and runs `git ls-files` to list files; it never reads Thor credential files. Only when the user runs `/sluice apply` does it write the approved changes (including new symlinks) into the workspace. One pre_tool_call hook sends calls the copy cannot contain (installs, network writes, git push, writes outside the workspace) to Thor's approval prompt and never approves anything itself. Not an operating-system sandbox: the hold list reads command text, so Python in execute_code or a command that builds its target path at run time can write outside the workspace without being held.

name: sluice-search
description: Tiered free-first web search and extraction router and backend manager for Thor Disclosure — routes web search and page extraction through third-party engines the user enables (keyless public endpoints such as DuckDuckGo via ddgs and the keyless modes of Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl, Tavily and Keenable; paid APIs with the user's own keys; an optional local SearXNG), so queries and fetched URLs go to those services; fetches pages itself with httpx and, when installed, a headless Playwright Chromium and a local Camofox server, refusing redirects and later navigations to private or metadata addresses on the httpx and Chromium paths (Camofox's own redirects are not checked); `thor sluice-search install` runs npm/podman/docker/playwright installs (Camofox pinned by digest/version) with a minimal environment.

name: smart-dictation
description: Native local dictation with opt-in proofreading and an advanced contextual review workflow.

name: smart-model-swap
description: Run a big and a small local LLM on one GPU rig and let the agent switch between them by task: the small one for quick or voice chat and to free VRAM for GPU jobs (ComfyUI), the big one for deep work. SmartModelProvider launches and stops llama.cpp's llama-server itself, swaps in the background without cutting replies, checks per-GPU VRAM before loading, restores the big model when idle, and ships a launch-parameter editor in the dashboard and Desktop, plus a bundled routing skill. Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio are detection-only. Disclosure — starts and stops llama-server as a long-running background process (in a transient systemd-run --user scope when available), autostarts the primary model when the gateway starts and swaps back to it if a smaller model was left serving (GPU memory), and keeps a detached runner per swap and a watcher that restores the primary after inactivity and, by default, loads another registered model if the serving one dies; sends SIGINT/SIGKILL only to the engine process it manages or an engine of the same kind holding its port; runs nvidia-smi, ss, systemctl --user show, systemd-run and llama-server --help/--version with a minimal environment (no provider keys); reads /proc of other processes to identify the engine and GPU users, and its guard reads shell scripts a terminal command is about to run; adds one-line hints to turns, can veto terminal/execute_code calls that manage the engine by hand, and can end a turn with an explanation while the LLM is unloaded on purpose; writes its own settings to config.yaml and, only on request, installs a model-provider plugin under plugins/model-providers/smart-model-provider; HTTP only to the configured engine and ComfyUI endpoints (localhost by default). No telemetry, credentials, self-updater or approval bypass.

name: smb-growth-agent
description: Local-first growth diagnosis, explainable opportunity ranking, 30-day plans and approval-gated simulated actions for small businesses. Includes two fictional demo businesses and nine tools. No outbound network calls, external execution, credentials, telemetry, or payments. Uses locally stored profile and action state only.

name: smolmachines
description: smol machines' own plugin: runs Thor's terminal, file and code tools in a smol machine, a microVM with its own Linux kernel on this computer (macOS on Apple Silicon, or Linux with KVM), as a terminal backend (`thor config set terminal.backend smolmachines`). It needs no Docker and no account. Disclosure: installs the `smolmachines` Python SDK (>=1.27.2,<2), which carries the VM engine. Everything runs on this computer: the plugin always asks the SDK for a local machine, so nothing is sent to smol machines' cloud, even with SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN set or the smol CLI signed in (Thor strips SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN from the commands it runs). Creating a machine pulls its image (default `python:3.12-slim`, from Docker Hub), and the engine pulls with this computer's Docker registry login when one is configured (`~/.docker/config.json`, including a credential helper such as the macOS keychain), read-only and sent only to the registry being pulled from. A machine has outbound network access and mounts nothing from this computer. With `terminal.container_persistent` (the Thor default) each Thor home and session keeps one machine, which keeps running after Thor exits until stopped or deleted with the smolvm CLI, otherwise the machine is deleted when the session ends. Because the machine is a disposable sandbox, Thor skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends.

name: smriti
description: Local personal memory with dated facts, scoped corrections, and source records you can retrieve from any compatible MCP client.

name: snag-shelf
description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

name: snare
description: Prompt injection tripwire with attack-chain forensics. Plants decoy credentials (PROD_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, PROD_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, PROD_DATABASE_URL) in the environment of every command the agent runs, never in the prompt. A tool call that tries to send one out (plain, URL-encoded, base64, hex, reversed, partial or nested) is blocked, and so is a command that reads a decoy variable or dumps the environment while using the network, including inside a local script the command runs. The alert names the page or file the injected instruction came from, quotes it, shows how the decoy was exposed and what the agent tried, then locks the session behind Thor approvals until /snare reset. Disclosure — adds three fake variables (PROD_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, PROD_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, PROD_DATABASE_URL) to commands on the local terminal backend (names already set are skipped); reads, never writes, up to four local script files a terminal command runs (64 KB each) to check them; prepends its alert to the agent's reply in the session that tripped it and redacts the decoy values from replies; after a trip, every further tool call in that session goes to Thor' approval prompt until /snare reset; on /snare selftest, and on /snare status with the local backend until one check is conclusive, runs one command through Thor' terminal tool that prints which decoy names are set, never their values; stores owner-only files in its plugin-data folder: the decoys, and per incident a JSON line plus an HTML report with the tool name, shortened arguments of the blocked call, destination URLs, the source URL or path, up to 280 characters of the injected text and the session id; no network calls, telemetry or Python dependencies.

name: snippet
description: Connect a Snippet account to manage creator brand deals, sponsorship rates, brand emails, decisions and contract reviews through Snippet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp, OAuth). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. The hosted server supplies its current tool list at runtime; tool availability can change independently of this catalog entry. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Snippet's hosted MCP server (https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp), which receives tool arguments and returns account data (deals, brand email threads, contract text); the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; some tools write (send_reply sends brand email, answer_decision and draft_reply change account state) and the package declares trust: untrusted so Thor asks before them and blocks them in unattended runs; a Snippet account is required and some actions need a paid plan; sign-in currently needs `thor mcp add snippet --url https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp --auth oauth`, and that same-name native entry replaces the package's server entry including its trust setting, so add `trust: untrusted` under mcp_servers.snippet afterwards; Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens; the package ships no credentials, executables, dependencies, self-updater or telemetry.

name: snooze
description: A reminder that repeats in your chat (Telegram, Discord) until you answer it exactly: Ok, your word, an emoji, a Telegram reaction, or one of several choices; reply later to postpone. A wrong answer gets the list of valid answers from the plugin's code, never from the LLM. Then it can hand a follow-up to the agent. Created with /snooze in plain words ("Stop the GPU at 19:00 every 10m then shut it down"), by the agent through the snooze_create tool, or with thor snooze add. Zero LLM calls per reminder. Disclosure — no network call of its own, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry. A timer task in the gateway checks every 15 s and sends due reminders, each showing its follow-up ("Then: ..."), through Thor's send path to the snooze's chat or home channel. The pre_gateway_dispatch hook sees every inbound gateway text message before Thor authorization, but acts only on messages from the snooze's owner in that snooze's chat: an answer, a reply to a reminder or the first message after one is consumed, and an answer with a follow-up becomes the follow-up prompt. The post_gateway_admission hook handles snoozes with no owner (created from the CLI for a channel or group), where any sender Thor has admitted in that chat may answer. The gateway_platform_event hook reads Telegram reactions on reminders in private chats. Follow-ups after a reaction, /snooze ok or an admitted answer are queued with ctx.inject_message, which needs allow_gateway_injection, and in a cron run snooze_create refuses a follow-up unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true. It stores snoozes.json and lock files in its plugin data dir, writes only its own notification_platform setting, and reads private Thor internals (tools.send_message_tool.send_message_tool, agent.estop.is_engaged, and the gateway runner reference and event loop in gateway.run), so a Thor release can break it.

name: snyk
description: Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

name: so101-arm
description: Give Thor a robot arm, safely: an SO-101 (a MuJoCo sim on your laptop, or a real arm through LeRobot) driven by named skills, never joint angles. A top-down camera grid corrects its aim, a missed pick is rehearsed on simulated copies before the retry, a plain-code watchdog parks the arm on faults, a pre_tool_call guard refuses motion until a repair is verified, and only a person can lift a freeze (/arm unfreeze). Disclosure — the tools move a robot arm with no Thor approval prompt: with the arm host started as `serve --real`, the agent drives a physical SO-101 over USB serial, limited to taught poses and motions, ±40 mm aim corrections and no more than the recorded speed (the default `serve` is a MuJoCo sim). The plugin talks only to a local Unix socket (mode 0600, default `<temp dir>/so101-arm.sock`) served by an arm host you start yourself (`python -m so101_host serve`). Any program running as you, Thor's terminal tool included, can send that socket any command, unfreeze included, and the motion guard lets calls through when the host is down. Its log hooks send tool names, results and token counts (never conversation text) to that socket for the viewer. The arm host is a separate program from the same repository: it writes run records and camera frames under `~/.so101-arm/`, `fetch-model` runs git to download MuJoCo Menagerie's SO-101 model at a pinned commit, and `serve --video` runs ffmpeg.

name: sochen
