description: Give Thor a phone with nothing to set up: Sochen (sochen.dev), a cloud agent for any open-source agent, phones a US business for you and brings back the answer, with no Twilio account, number or voice keys of your own. When the business asks something only you can answer, the question comes to your Thor chat while they hold the line, and your reply goes straight back into the call. It also runs long research in the cloud and handles email and calendar jobs that wait for your OK, and Thor is told when each job finishes. Every account gets 100 free Sochen API credits, spread over any number of jobs; after that, packs or a monthly API plan (sochen.dev/pricing#api). Free GST invoices, rent receipts for HRA and UPI bill splits with no account, and your Sochen desk as a page in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — network calls go to sochen.dev only: the Agent API with your SOCHEN_API_KEY (read through Thor's secret scope) for jobs, job status and the desk, and the public tools endpoint, with no key, for the free tools. Jobs run on your Sochen account and credits, and Thor asks before each handoff. On your next message the plugin checks up to two open jobs (4 s each; a job whose call is going on, every turn), sochen_job may wait up to 60 s for news while a call goes on, and sochen_answer sends only the answer the user gave. Thor Desktop reads the desk every 30 s while open. A short list of handed-off jobs (id, label, status) is kept in the plugin's own state. Requests carry a thor-sochen/<version> client name; there is no other telemetry.

name: softhalo-usage
description: Shows your Thor token usage in Soft Halo's always-on-top Windows overlay, which you can resize and make more or less transparent, next to Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw. Observer hooks only: after each model call it writes the token counts (uncached input, cache reads and writes, output), the provider, model and session id to a small file in Soft Halo's local folder on Windows, reached from WSL through /mnt/c. Disclosure — after every model call it writes a small file with token counts, provider, model and session id (never prompts, responses or tool output) into Soft Halo's local usage folder, which on WSL is the Windows user's AppData folder reached through /mnt/c; on a machine without Soft Halo those files are never cleaned up. No network requests and no tools or commands.

name: sogni
description: Sogni AI image generation backend for image_generate: text-to-image and image-to-image (identity edit) on Sogni's decentralised GPU network, driven through Sogni's own sogni-agent CLI. Registers as an image_gen provider, so the normal image_generate tool works unchanged — aspect ratio and reference images are threaded through. Disclosure — every generation submits a job to the Sogni network via the sogni-agent-thor CLI, which this plugin spawns as a subprocess, so unlike Thor's bundled providers it is not zero-install: it needs Node.js and npm install -g @sogni-ai/sogni-creative-agent-skill@3.56.1 (or SOGNI_AGENT_BIN pointing at an existing binary). The prompt and any reference image (including a local file path the model passes) are sent to api.sogni.ai on the way to the network and the finished image is downloaded from media.sogni.ai; the plugin reads SOGNI_API_KEY through Thor's secret scope and hands the CLI a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, SOGNI_API_KEY and, if set, NODE_OPTIONS, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, XDG_CACHE_HOME), so no other Thor provider keys reach it, and it presents an honest custom User-Agent because Cloudflare (Error 1010) rejects library-default ones. Generation is billed to your Sogni account per job with no Thor approval prompt, and the plugin reports the model used but enforces no budget cap, so an unattended run can spend your balance. Generated media is written under $THOR_HOME/cache/images/. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no background processes beyond the CLI call, no self-updates.

name: solana-token-facts
description: Verifiable on-chain facts about Solana tokens and their developers: mint/freeze authority, supply, Token-2022 risky extensions, whether name/symbol/image can still change, top holders and concentration, wallets that bought in the creation block, creation time, creator wallet and launchpad, who funded the dev wallet, a developer's past launches (graduated, dev sold out, minutes to sell out) and the newest pump.fun -> PumpSwap graduations. Adds 8 tools, a /token fact-sheet command, a due-diligence skill and an opt-in automation blueprint that saves dev reports for new graduations. Facts only: no verdicts, no trading advice, no transactions, no wallet keys. Disclosure: makes outbound HTTPS JSON-RPC calls only to the user's configured Solana RPC (default https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com; token_holders, dev_launches, launch_buyers, dev_funding and recent_graduations need a provider such as Helius); an optional private RPC URL is a type: secret read with get_secret; writes local Markdown files only when save_dev_report runs (folder set by reports_dir); no background processes of its own, no telemetry.

name: soldgraph
description: Check what items sold for on eBay, Poshmark and Mercari, and search live resale listings on Depop, Whatnot, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, Vinted and TCGplayer. Portable Agent Plugin with one skill and Soldgraph's hosted MCP server (19 read-only tools). Disclosure — tool calls go to api.soldgraph.com with the user's own Soldgraph API key (SOLDGRAPH_KEY, sent as a bearer header), and the tool set is served by that remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha; each completed search uses 1 request from the user's Soldgraph allowance; listing text comes from marketplace sellers and is untrusted.

name: soloknuckle
description: Deterministic local guardrails for Thor and dev workflows. Three invocable tools—git-diff secret scanning, a destructive-command firewall, and a project health score—plus native Thor surfaces: additive credential-redaction patterns, a soloknuckle:hygiene skill, thor hygiene CLI, /hygiene, and a weekly hygiene-report blueprint. One rule set, same verdicts across CLI/hooks/MCP/Thor. No hooks, no middleware, no prompt rewriting, no telemetry.

name: solverforge-planner
description: Plans your tasks into your week around your meetings, deadlines, task order and focus hours with a SolverForge constraint solver, and proves every hard rule holds before anything is written. The planner keeps its own local calendar (SQLite plus a planner.ics you can subscribe to); Thor pulls your cloud calendar and pushes the plan with the calendar tool you already use, and the planner only ever creates, moves or deletes its own events, each with a fixed ID so a repeated push adds nothing. Applying a plan and unscheduling a task ask for your approval. Desktop: a plan card in chat, a Planner page (week view and tasks) and a status-bar chip. Disclosure — `thor solverforge-planner install` (or /planner install, or the Desktop Install engine button) downloads one engine binary for your platform from this repository's own engine-v0.1.0 GitHub release, built by its release workflow with a GitHub build attestation, and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches the value pinned in engine_bin.py; the agent cannot start that download. Each solve runs that binary once as a subprocess (JSON on stdin and stdout, stopped at solve_timeout, no network). planner_busy_from_ics fetches an https/http/webcal iCalendar link (up to 10 MB) or reads a local .ics file, only the one you name. All data stays in <thor home>/plugin-data/solverforge-planner/; no credentials are read or stored, no cloud calendar is touched by the plugin itself, no telemetry, no background process; an optional Morning plan automation blueprint runs only if you schedule it, and never applies.

name: solverforge-routing
description: Personal multi-stop driving trips: tell Thor where you need to go, review the places it finds, and a SolverForge constraint solver orders the stops on OpenStreetMap roads. Change plans in the conversation (skip a stop, choose the first visit, add a place, finish elsewhere) and the trip is repaired, keeping visited stops, the next stop and before rules; an older solve never overwrites a newer edit, and results are labelled best-found, not proven optimal. Desktop: the road map beside the chat, a route card, a status-bar chip, Google Maps, Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap links, and one QR code at a time for the phone. Disclosure — `thor solverforge-routing install` (or /routing install) downloads one engine binary for your platform from this repository's own engine-v0.2.2 GitHub release, built by its release workflow with a GitHub build attestation, and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches the value pinned in engine_bin.py; the agent cannot start that download. Place searches the user asks for send the query and region to Nominatim (configurable with geocoder_url). The first solve in a new area sends a bounding box to Overpass to download OpenStreetMap roads; each solve then runs the engine once as a subprocess (JSON on stdin and stdout). The map pane loads OpenStreetMap tiles, which reveal the visible area and your IP to the tile servers. Opening a navigation link or scanning its QR code sends the stop coordinates to that provider. The route database, road cache and engine stay in <thor home>/plugin-data/solverforge-routing/; a geocoder pacing lock file (a timestamp only, shared by all profiles) is kept in ~/.cache/thor-solverforge-routing/. No credentials, no location tracking, no telemetry, no background process.

name: soul-finder
description: Build or fix your agent's SOUL.md — the personality file behind every reply. A few plain questions draft one from scratch; /soul audits a stale one and ships a diff. Disclosure — reads $THOR_HOME/SOUL.md and writes it only through the agent's own file tools after you approve the draft (the bundled skill can suggest copying the approved file into other profiles' SOUL.md, again only on approval); on a profile with no real SOUL.md it makes a one-time offer through a system-prompt section and an injected first-run message, and writes two booleans (nudge_sent, flow_complete) to its own plugin-data state so the offer happens once. No network I/O, no credentials.

name: source-tray
description: Session source tray — URLs the Thor agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

name: sourcebind
description: Bind one explicit business job to its current local JSON customer ID at one selected native tool's execution boundary. Default mode checks job and customer_id arguments; opt-in ID-only mode checks customer_id for registered customer-only tools while retaining the source-job and native-scope checks. Both modes reread the selected source for each protected call and retain the originating scope through public delegation and compaction events. Disclosure — reads the user-selected local JSON with the process's OS permissions; stores the binding, check mode, absolute source path, native scope aliases and fictional demo records in profile-scoped Thor plugin state. Source-file writers can change authoritative values. Plugin-initiated network requests, shell commands, background processes, telemetry and credentials: 0.

name: sovereign-finance
description: A self-custodial Smart Agentic Wallet for your agent on BNB Chain and Ethereum, with a Desktop pane. Your passkey is the admin, and the agent's session key is limited onchain to the contracts, functions and daily caps you approve. Powered by Altana. Disclosure — Crypto wallet plugin: the agent signs BNB Chain/Ethereum swaps and liquidity actions with a session key stored in plugin-data; every sovereign_execute call asks for Thor approval (an "always" answer covers one pool or swap direction for that session key), but YOLO mode, approvals.mode off or approvals.cron_mode approve skip the prompt, and anything that reads the session key file (including the agent's own shell) can sign within the onchain contract/function/daily-cap limits without asking, because those limits do not pin recipients. Signed batches go to the Altana relay; it also talks to publicnode RPCs, DexScreener and skills.altana.network, runs a bundled Node CLI, and serves a localhost-only passkey page during admin actions. Its pre_tool_call guard refuses other tools' calls that mention its files, admin routes or the Thor gateway socket.

name: sovereign-plus
description: UK Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) and right to work answers for construction contractors who pay subcontractors, through Sovereign Plus's read-only MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sovereignplus.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): yearly CIS exposure from the contractor's own numbers, late CIS300 penalties, deduction rates, verification, gross payment status, the April 2026 fraud rules, right to work checks for subcontractors from 1 October 2026, and how to book a free CIS check. Every figure comes with its GOV.UK or legislation.gov.uk source and is an estimate, not tax advice; the tools never ask for names, share codes or passport numbers. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.sovereignplus.com, run by Sovereign Plus (S+), a UK CIS bureau, and tool results end by offering S+'s free CIS check (the user contacts S+ themselves; the tools book and send nothing). All four tools are annotated read-only; the package marks the server untrusted. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: spacewise
description: Free up space without the fear of losing what matters. Scans one folder you name for exact duplicates (one copy always stays), leftover .dmg/.pkg installers, similar photos (the sharpest stays) and blurry or near-black photos, and reports large videos, screenshots and other large files without ever proposing them. A local preview page shows what would stay and what would go; only categories you approve move to the Trash of the same disk, and spacewise_undo puts them back. Disclosure — reads image, video and installer files (and the name, size and date of other files) only in a folder you name inside your home folder or on an external drive; refuses the operating system, disk roots, the whole home folder, other users' and shared folders, ~/Library and ~/Applications, hidden and locked items, unreadable folders, symlinks, and app-managed libraries (Photos, Lightroom, Final Cut, iMovie, Music, apps, Time Machine); skips cloud placeholders without opening them. spacewise_trash takes only a scan id and categories (never file paths) and is escalated by its own pre_tool_call hook to Thor' human-approval gate, so it follows the user's approval settings (YOLO, approvals off or approvals.cron_mode can let it through; with no human present it fails closed); each request gets a one-time rule key. Moves are same-disk renames into ~/.Trash or <drive>/.Trashes/<uid> (freedesktop Trash on Linux), never copies or deletions; files changed since the scan, hard-linked files and RAW+JPEG pairs are left alone. Stores per-file measurements and SHA-256 hashes, recent scans, Trash batches, reports and preview thumbnails in its plugin data folder. Sends to the model provider, as part of the conversation, the scanned folder, counts, sizes and names of listed photos, videos and installers; names of other large files stay in the local report. No network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry; no process-wide settings changed. Windows: scan and report only.

name: spanwall
description: One Kanban wall for every Thor session, across every profile: Needs you, Running, Idle, Done (24h) and Failed columns, one card per session. Approve requests, answer clarify, sudo and secret prompts, chat, steer and stop agents right from the card. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — acts on the sessions of every watched profile, not only the active one: approving or rejecting requests, sending prompts, steering, interrupting and creating sessions there, each only on an explicit click (nothing is approved automatically). Sudo passwords and secrets typed into a card go straight to the owning gateway and are not stored. Polls every watched profile's gateway every 3 s, which may start that profile's backend. Keeps UI preferences and a 24-hour archive of finished turns (title, profile, model, tools used, the error message if any, the first 600 characters of the reply) in the Desktop's plugin storage. No network calls outside the Thor gateways, no telemetry.

name: spawn-backrooms
description: Work SPAWN jobs with human-approved proposals, child commission drafts and verified file delivery. Disclosure — talks to spawnbackrooms.com (SPAWN's job marketplace, amounts in USDC) through Thor-managed OAuth with 14 scopes; accepting, proposing, submitting, abandoning, drafting child commissions and creating Backrooms always ask for your approval and are refused in cron, but uploading deliverables (text, any workspace file up to 5 MiB each, game zips) and posting progress run without a prompt and send the selected files' bytes to SPAWN; while a job is active a background thread renews its lease and each turn gets a short active-job context line; customer job inputs are cached under the plugin's data directory with no expiry.

name: speckle
description: Browse, query and diff 3D/BIM models (mainly for the AECO industry) from Speckle (Revit, Rhino, IFC, Archicad, Tekla, ETABS, Civil 3D, Blender), run saved checks on every new version, get a chat message when a watched model gets a new version, and see the model in a live 3D viewer in Thor Desktop. Requires a Speckle personal access token (SPECKLE_TOKEN). Disclosure — network connections go to the configured Speckle server (app.speckle.systems by default), the only host that receives the token, and to the file storage that server links to for model downloads, without the token; the 3D viewer library ships bundled in the repo and makes no network connections; while a model is watched a background thread checks it every poll_seconds (default 60, minimum 15); watches, checks, the viewer selection, caches and preview images stay in the plugin's data folder; speckle_create_issue is the only write to Speckle and the agent asks first; no shell commands, no telemetry.

name: specsentry
description: Evidence-backed API contract drift analysis using OpenAPI and HAR traffic, with deterministic verdicts, coverage intelligence, and reproducible regression tests.

name: specstream
description: SpecStream gives Thor finished lists from the live web: describe the list in plain words and get every matching row with the page it was read from, priced per match with a maximum you approve before anything runs. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and four skills (compile, review-work, approve-work, continue-work); no Python, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure — your request text and your answers to the price are sent to api.specstream.ai; approving a price spends your SpecStream balance (new accounts get $10 free) and the plugin marks its server `untrusted`, so Thor asks before every call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `specstream` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

name: spectator
description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

name: speechify
description: The official Speechify text-to-speech provider (tts.provider: speechify), maintained by Speechify. Simba 3.5 voices in 48 languages with low-latency streaming in voice mode, Opus voice notes for messaging platforms, and a thor speechify command to list voices and hear a test line. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice and model, the plugin's name and version (Speechify-Caller attribution headers), and your SPEECHIFY_API_KEY to api.speechify.ai (or the base_url / SPEECHIFY_BASE_URL you configure); synthesis is billed to your Speechify workspace; generated audio is written to Thor's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry.

name: spendwarden
description: A spend policy firewall and local ledger for Thor agents that can move money. A pre_tool_call hook checks payment-shaped tool calls against daily, monthly and per-call USD caps, recipient/asset/network allowlists and an approval threshold; in enforce mode it blocks hard violations and escalates uncertain ones to Thor's own approval gate. Four tools add spend_check, idempotent spend_record receipts, spend_report totals, and x402_inspect (decodes PAYMENT-REQUIRED / X-PAYMENT without signing). State is a local SQLite ledger under the plugin data directory; no network calls, no credentials, no key handling, no transaction signing. Observe mode logs only; enforce mode is opt-in. Terminal recognition covers cast send, solana transfer, bitcoin-cli sendtoaddress, near call --deposit and curl with X-PAYMENT. Disclosure — detection is best-effort: it recognises payment-shaped calls by tool-name patterns, common amount/recipient argument names and five terminal command shapes (cast send, solana transfer, bitcoin-cli sendtoaddress, near call --deposit, curl with X-PAYMENT), so payments made any other way pass unchecked; the default observe mode only logs, nothing is blocked or sent for approval until you set mode: enforce, and a policy-check error lets the call through unless fail_closed is on; it does not replace wallet-side spending limits.

name: spine
description: Does your model cave when you push back? Spine asks questions with one exact answer, then tells the model, confidently, that a plausible wrong answer is right, and checks whether it holds its ground. The result is a Spine score, the share of correct answers it kept, under polite, firm or authority pressure, with every exchange in a report. Graded by the answer line, so no model judges another. Runs on your active model through ctx.llm, no setup.

name: spoonmaster
description: Compare restaurants using local recommendations, venue facts, and optional private tastes. Disclosure — Spoonmaster runs restaurant research through your enabled Thor search/extract tools (search providers and venue sites see the queries), observes your own native `browser_exec` calls in its named `spoon-<request>` browser session to keep their printed page text as evidence, adds about 2 KB of dining guidance to every turn, and stores optional tastes and saved companion groups, including other people's dietary needs, in a local 0600 SQLite file in this profile's plugin data; viewing them puts them in your transcript and model provider.

name: spotify
description: Spotify for Thor: seven tools (playback, devices, queue, search, playlists, albums, library) over the Spotify Web API, plus `thor spotify login|status|logout` (loopback PKCE with your own Spotify developer app; Premium needed for playback control). Formerly built into Thor core; existing users are migrated automatically.

name: spotify-desktop
description: Spotify Connect remote for Thor Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the Thor Spotify login (Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

name: sql-dryrun
description: Shows how many rows a DELETE/UPDATE/DROP/TRUNCATE will touch before it runs, and sends it to Thor' approval prompt when it is too many. Built-in approval matches command shape only, so UPDATE with no WHERE, DELETE ... WHERE 1=1, a WHERE that matches every row, and DELETE FROM t; SELECT ... WHERE ... all run unprompted; sql-dryrun flags them with the real count ("228,789 of 250,000 rows"). Covers sqlite3, psql and mysql/mariadb (inline -c/-e, heredoc, piped), execute_code, and tools passing SQL in a sql/query/statement argument. Settings: row_threshold (default 100), mode approve|block, count timeout. Adds a sql_impact tool for dry-running a statement and a /sql-dryrun command. Tested on SQLite, Postgres and MariaDB. MIT licensed. Disclosure — reads the arguments of terminal, execute_code and tools with a sql/query/statement argument. For a destructive statement whose database it can reach, it runs read-only SELECT COUNT(*) queries: SQLite in-process (mode=ro, trusted_schema=OFF); Postgres/MySQL only via a bare psql/mysql/mariadb resolved with shutil.which() and never from inside the working tree, with a minimal env (PATH/HOME/LANG/LC_*/TZ plus PG* except PGOPTIONS, or MYSQL_PWD/HOST/TCP_PORT/UNIX_PORT) and allowlisted connection flags only (options= in a conninfo/URI, any other flag including --defaults-file, or a password prompt skips the count; mysql always runs with --no-defaults). A statement containing ';' or a backslash is never sent to a database and goes to approval uncounted. Because the WHERE runs before approval, it is only counted when it is a plain predicate (comparisons, AND/OR, IN/EXISTS subqueries, an allowlist of pure built-in functions); any other function call, INTO, FOR UPDATE, '$' or a comment marker skips the count. Postgres runs BEGIN READ ONLY and verifies SHOW transaction_read_only before counting; MySQL runs inside START TRANSACTION READ ONLY ... ROLLBACK; both with a timeout and no password prompt. Counts only run when terminal.backend is local; on docker/ssh/modal/daytona statements are flagged by shape only. No network calls of its own, no files written, no data changed, no credentials stored; the flagged SQL appears in the approval message.

name: squad-hub
description: One Desktop list for Thor Agent Squads: bot, project, folder, worktree and chat, several bots open at once without a profile switch; the squad's cron jobs; a bell for what waits on you; live Kanban cards in chat; squad managers ask with clarify buttons; the empty chat names the squad and project. Disclosure — reads and manages other profiles' chats (list, start, rename, archive), projects and cron jobs (pause, resume, remove) through Thor RPC on running backends, and reads Kanban boards through its own read-only dashboard route built on Thor' internal kanban_db module; adds a system-prompt section telling agents to ask with clarify buttons and appends Kanban card lines to Desktop replies; writes its own desktop_cards setting on manager profiles and applies its Squads theme on every bot by default (switchable in its settings); git worktree create/remove is only copied as a command unless the separate repo-only squad-hub-plus companion handles it; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, never reads .env or credentials.

name: stablelens
description: Read-only tools for Arc Network, the stablecoin-native L1 where USDC is the gas token: native USDC and Circle token balances (USDC, EURC, USYC, cirBTC, WETH, plus any ERC-20) read at one block, transaction status with the USDC fee and decoded ERC-20 transfers, the current cost of a transfer, and token, address and block lookups, on mainnet (chain 5042) and testnet (5042002). Standard library only; never signs, sends or holds keys. Disclosure — each tool call sends JSON-RPC requests carrying the addresses, transaction hashes, token addresses and block numbers asked about to Arc's public RPC endpoints (rpc.mainnet.arc.io / rpc.testnet.arc.io and the Blockdaemon, dRPC and QuickNode endpoints Arc publishes), or first to a private endpoint the user stores as a Thor secret (STABLELENS_MAINNET_RPC_URL / STABLELENS_TESTNET_RPC_URL, read through the secret scope); registration makes no network calls, and there are no other network calls, file writes, shell commands or background processes.

name: stack
description: Git-backed Markdown memory with background curation and model-based recall. Disclosure — runs a background curation agent with terminal, file-read and patch tools on your configured auxiliary model, fed raw conversation turns; it commits and pushes the memory store to whatever git remotes you configure, and pulls shared submodules at session start; the engine runs via uv run, which fetches pyyaml==6.0.2 from PyPI; an optional dataset file (memory.stack.dataset_enabled, off by default) stores full transcripts locally with no rotation.

name: stacktree
description: Publish what Thor builds (reports, dashboards, briefs, proposals) to a private link that opens in any browser with no account for the viewer, set a passcode or limit it to a company's email addresses, update it in place, and see who opened it and what they commented. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Stacktree's remote MCP server at api.stacktr.ee (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, token kept by Thor); the HTML the model passes to publish_html or update_site is stored in the user's Stacktree account and served at the returned link (unlisted by default, public when a public_slug is set); page titles, open counts and third-party reader comments from that account are read into the session; the remote tools that publish, update, gate, delete pages or email approval requests run without a Thor approval prompt; the required sign-in step `thor mcp add stacktree --url https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp --auth oauth` writes a config.yaml server entry that replaces the package's own.

name: stage
description: Stage Thor write_file and patch calls in a scratch copy. Original files stay unchanged until stage_apply. Disclosure — while enabled, write_file and patch land in a scratch copy under the Thor plugin-data directory and the real files change only when the model calls stage_apply (the model can apply without asking the user); writes outside the session workspace are refused, terminal commands that would modify workspace files (redirects, tee, sed -i, rm/mv/cp, git checkout/restore/reset --hard) are blocked, and any execute_code that uses subprocess, os.system or file-writing calls is blocked; stage_apply re-checks Thor' write denylist and approval-gated paths before writing.

name: stagehands
description: Typed backstage subagent delegation provider (scout, librarian, code_monkey, adversary, briefer) and deterministic 48k/120k context-sanitation janitor that keep bulky tool gravel out of the frontier parent session. Disclosure — Stagehands adds a system-prompt section and delegate_task guidance that push the model to send multi-step tool work to subagents, which by default run on fixed worker models (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, qwen/qwen3.7-flash, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5) through your own configured provider, so delegated task text and tool output go to those models; it reads the active profile's state.db read-only for `/stagehands stats` and `@stagehands:` telemetry, and only when you run `/stagehands on|off|janitor` does it change `delegation.backend` and `compression.*` in config.yaml through Thor's atomic config writer, with no separate backup.

name: stalkchain
description: Crypto research in plain English through the official StalkChain Data MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://data.stalkchain.com/mcp/directory, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check a coin before you buy, vet a trader before you copy them, see what smart money is buying, review a wallet and set price alerts, across Solana, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Monad, Hyperliquid and Robinhood Chain, plus the StonkFun launchpad. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + 18 skills), no Python or executables; needs a StalkChain account with credits. Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything; the only write is the user's own price alerts, after they confirm. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; each tool call sends the tool name and its inputs to data.stalkchain.com and spends the account's credits; price alerts are stored by StalkChain with their destination (account email or a user-given Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook URL, which can embed a bot token) until deleted or fired.

name: standing-orders
description: Plain-English camera triggers that wake your agent. Say "tell me if I leave my mug on the desk for 10 seconds"; the camera stays silent until it is true, then Thor starts a turn with a short clip as evidence. macOS only; not a safety or security system. Disclosure — Runs a gateway platform that opens the macOS webcam in a background thread only while at least one order is armed (1–2 frames per second), or whenever the gateway runs if you turn on `record_when_idle`; keeps a rolling local recording of those periods (60 min / 2 GB, deleted when the last order is disarmed) plus event clips (kept until `thor orders purge`) under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/standing-orders; frame crops and one reference frame per new order are sent to your configured Thor model through ctx.llm; armed orders start Thor turns unattended with camera-derived text, and those turns get all core tools unless `platform_toolsets.standing_orders` is set.

name: starlearner-nexus
description: Turn the repositories you star on GitHub into a living library of registered Thor skills. `starlearner_sync` runs the whole pipeline — fetch, map (the LLM curation pass), categorize into a fixed set of domains, two-track assess (integrate-into-your-makeup and business-opportunity), generate, register (`starlearner-nexus:<name>`) — incrementally via a persistent seen-ledger (a repo is never processed twice); `starlearner_status` is read-only state (including token set / not set); `starlearner_review` surfaces everything LLM-shaped item by item for the human. The map / categorize / assess stages optionally run through the host LLM (`ctx.llm`, one registered auxiliary task) with a deterministic rules engine as the bit-for-bit fallback (`enrich: rules` = zero LLM calls); generate is never the LLM. Registration is opt-in (`register_generated_skills`, off by default): generation writes the skills and lists them for `starlearner_review`; switching registration on registers them. When it is on, registration timing is handler-time `register_skill`, accepted and live in the same session (a skill view on a name the sync just returned resolves the same second); a plugin reload re-registers everything generated before it. Disclosure — contacts api.github.com only (GET /user/starred, HTTPS, paginated with a hard page cap), authenticated with your own read-only GitHub token read through Thor's secret scope and never written to the plugin's files, logs or results; LLM enrichment (on by default; `enrich: rules` turns it off) sends public repo metadata (name, description, topics, language, stars) to your active provider through Thor (`ctx.llm`, auxiliary task starlearner_enricher); every new starred repo becomes a generated skill whose description and body carry that repo's own third-party description text, so text written by the repo's author appears in your skills index and in skills the agent loads; writes only to its own plugin-data store; no shell commands, no subprocesses, no telemetry; the bundled "StarLearner-Nexus sync" automation blueprint runs only if you schedule it. Origin of the reapx lineage (same owner).

name: stash
description: A capture bin for the Desktop sidebar: paste links, YouTube urls, image urls, uploaded images or plain notes and they wait there, out of the chat. One item per line, so a block of links becomes several items; titles and thumbnails are filled in server-side, so capture costs no model calls. Each row carries a Chat button that opens a new session with that item as the opening message. Adds stash_add, stash_list and stash_update, so the agent reads and empties the same store the page writes. Disclosure — saving an item issues one GET to that url from the Thor host (4 s timeout, 400 KB cap) to read its <title> and og: metadata, refused for loopback, link-local, private and reserved targets and re-checked on every redirect hop; YouTube urls also use www.youtube.com/oembed and i.ytimg.com thumbnails, and the Desktop page loads each item's og:image thumbnail directly from whatever host the page names. No credentials, no telemetry, no shell commands, no Python dependencies beyond the FastAPI Thor already ships. Items are plain JSON at ~/.thor/stash/items.json (shared by every profile) and uploads (max 8 MB) in ~/.thor/stash/media/.

name: statejar
description: Verifiable memory for Thor Agent (memory.provider statejar): typed facts with one value per field, append-only content-addressed versions, recall of only what a message needs with the handle of the state it came from, and an audit trail of every disclosure. Disclosure — the user's current message (first 2,000 characters) is sent to api.statejar.com as a recall query on every turn, and the user's own messages (three words or more), every entry Thor's built-in memory tool saves, and the text or query the agent passes to the statejar_* tools are sent there with STATEJAR_API_KEY; assistant replies and tool output are not captured, and API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords and card numbers are removed locally first (best effort). StateJar's server sends each captured message to a cloud model provider it uses for extraction (today Google Gemini and OpenRouter). A capture queue is kept under the Thor home (created mode 600; a queue rewritten after a failed send uses default permissions). Only the primary agent writes; cron and subagent runs only recall.

name: stave
description: Describe a piece of music and Thor writes it as sheet music in Thor Desktop: it plans the form, writes every bar in ABC notation, checks bar lengths, instrument ranges, guitar chord shapes and syntax and repairs what fails, then engraves the score. Playback lights each note as it sounds, guitar parts get TAB, and you change any bars you select by asking in words, with undo. Exports PDF, SVG, MIDI, WAV and ABC. Two agent tools (stave_check, stave_open) and the stave:compose skill let any chat compose and open pieces on the page. Disclosure — the page makes one stateless llm.oneshot call per step through its own Stave composer auxiliary task (Settings › Models; reasoning off by default) and creates no sessions; playback downloads FluidR3 GM instrument samples from paulrosen.github.io/midi-js-soundfonts the first time each instrument plays; stave_open writes one JSON file per piece to plugin-data/stave/inbox, which the page reads through the plugin's dashboard route and deletes; pieces and undo history live in Desktop plugin storage; files are written only when the user exports; no shell commands, no processes of its own, no telemetry.

name: stepup
description: Authenticator-app 2FA for your agent: on messaging platforms the protected tools (terminal and execute_code by default) stay locked until the sender sends a one-time TOTP code from an authenticator app, so an unlocked phone is not a remote shell. One valid code unlocks that sender for 10 minutes, each code works once, five wrong codes lock the sender out for 15 minutes, and `lock` re-locks at once. Local CLI, Desktop and cron runs are never gated, and nothing waits for input. Disclosure — pre_tool_call may block a protected tool call (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system); post_gateway_admission reads the text of admitted gateway messages and consumes only a six-digit code sent while a lock is pending, `unlock <code>` and `lock`, so codes never reach the model; pre_llm_call only records which platform and sender a session belongs to and injects nothing; holds one secret, STEPUP_TOTP_SECRET, read through Thor's secret scope and never written to state or logs; stores unlock expiries, failure counts and the last used code counter in plugin state; no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no dependencies, no self-update. Not a sandbox: tools outside protected_tools keep their normal reach.

name: steward
description: Your chief of staff in the team chat. Collects every department's weekly update in its own group (voice note in any language, text, photo or file), nudges only late teams, and gives the founder one weekly pack in their language with promised-vs-done, a stuck radar and a voice brief. Founder says "send" and all staff get the update. Disclosure — Steward reads every message in the department groups you configure and sends their weekly updates (text, voice-note transcripts, photos, documents) to your model and TTS providers; it creates Thor cron jobs that post check-ins and nudges into those groups and deliver the founder pack, keeps reports and copies of attachments under THOR_HOME/steward, and posts the staff pack to the all-staff group when the founder says "send".

name: sticky-notes
description: In-window sticky notes for Thor Desktop.

name: stitchslop
description: Work on the embroidery design open in Stitch Slop, watch it in a pane, and digitize artwork into machine stitch files. Ships the bridge its tab dials into (loopback WebSocket, protocol 1 of stitchslop.com/agent), a viewer page that streams a dedicated Chrome window and forwards clicks and keys, four tools, an arc-typesetting and art-prep script, and a bundled skill covering the digitizing workflow. Disclosure — writes ~/.stitchslop (pairing, Chrome profile, exports, logs), shared by every Thor profile on the machine; starts a loopback WebSocket bridge, a token-gated viewer server and a dedicated Chrome (launched with --no-sandbox and Local Network Access checks off) on a private X display; the viewer binds to loopback only unless you set STITCHSLOP_PANE_BIND to a Tailscale address, which exposes the token-gated viewer (live view and click/key control of that Chrome, logged into your Stitch Slop account) to your tailnet; navigation is limited to https://stitchslop.com; first pairing needs you to paste the Agent-panel token by hand.

name: stmp
description: Use a phone as the trust boundary: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, contacts, notifications, a credential vault and SSH over STMP — every gated call waits for a human on the device, and no credential is ever stored on the host. Disclosure — needs the STMP Android app (public repository, Apache-2.0, APK on its releases page) reachable from the Thor host over LAN or tailnet, so it does nothing without a paired phone; acts on that phone's signed-in Google account (sends mail, writes calendar events, uploads and downloads Drive files — a download writes only inside the configured download_dir and an upload reads only inside upload_dir or outside the credential stores, since the model names those paths and the settings bound them) and runs SSH commands through private keys stored on the device, which never leave it; stores nothing at rest beyond the connected instance's capability snapshot (contract version, plugin and route counts, SSH connection names) in Thor's own plugin state, rewritten only on change; two routes are gate-exempt by design and say so in their tool descriptions — POST /tts and POST /audio/{cue} play sound only; every other route goes through the phone's approval gate, whose per-route mode (WHITELIST, PARANOID or DONT_DISTURB) is the device owner's policy, not the plugin's; declares and reads no credential (requires_env is empty, no oauth block), no telemetry, no self-updater, and talks to exactly one address: the configured base_url.

name: stoa
description: The CRM for Thor Agent, a lightweight one you talk to: map a market, find the leads, run the pipeline and see it through to cash. Thor runs it and you approve: what it finds waits for your yes or no, and every change can be taken back. Optional paid lookups and network calls happen only with your own keys; the README's Disclosure section lists everything it reads, writes and sends. Disclosure — optional network calls to api.peopledatalabs.com (paid per result, capped), api.exa.ai and public-api.granola.ai only when their keys are set; dictation on the page is the browser's own speech recognition (in Chrome, Google's service) and runs only while its button is on; reads the notes folder, .csv and .tsv files in its imports folder, a folder you name or the working directory, and a file you drop on the page; writes only inside its own data folder, including daily backup copies of each pipeline; scheduled jobs reach the desk only when you add cron to its channels setting, and then change only what its autonomy setting allows (by default they only log what they find and leave every other change waiting for your approval; "Run it" lets them make any change); the automations offered under /blueprint run only when you switch them on, and the Google Sheet ones use your own Google connection in Thor; invoices and payments are records kept on the desk, never sent or charged; a Slack button works only for the person a card was posted for or the people listed in slack_users; with allow_gateway_injection a button click queues one agent turn in the thread; the page's dock sends what you type to a visible conversation of its own. Thor Agent Plugin Hackathon entry.

name: stock-runway
description: See when each product will run out and when to reorder. Forecasts seasonal monthly demand, shows past demand, deliveries and stock on one chart, grades forecast accuracy, and lists what to order now (quantity and order-by date, with lead time, MOQ and pack size). Works from the bundled sample, a local CSV (reads SAP, NetSuite, Zoho, Odoo, Sage, QuickBooks and Dynamics export column names as is), or an optional read-only Odoo connection configured through Thor secrets. Adds a /stock command, a stock_runway tool and a Desktop page. Disclosure — with the Odoo source it makes read-only XML-RPC calls to the Odoo server you configure; the sample and CSV sources make no network calls.

name: stop-ledger
description: Local ledger of the turns you stopped while Thor was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, Thor's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network

name: storage-utility
description: Keep Thor fast, healthy and tidy from one Desktop panel. Clean up sorts the Thor home into Safe to clean, Take a quick look and Kept safe on purpose, with plain-language answers to what is it, is it safe and can I undo; it reviews exact items before anything happens and reports the measured space recovered. It runs the maintenance Thor ships but few people find (sessions prune with preview, pm gc, uv cache prune, checkpoints, worktree prune, session-database packing), finds folders Thor created elsewhere from its own session history, and moves reviewable items to a restorable 30-day Trash. Checkup explains down or crash-looping Thor services and stops leftover agent processes; Explore shows a size map with folder descriptions and duplicate finding; optional consented AI explanation via its own auxiliary task. Disclosure — Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd); no network except an optional, consented AI explanation (folder totals and counts only) through Thor's routing; reads home metadata, tool caches, session history, /proc process and open-file info, systemd unit settings, journal lines, crontab and git ls-files; on macOS instead the process table via psutil, Thor's own processes.json and spawn ledger, Thor LaunchAgent plists (label, program, KeepAlive, log path, THOR_HOME/HOME only), the settings of every LaunchAgent and LaunchDaemon plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchDaemons without their environment entries (to see whether a job starts something from a project folder, kept local), launchctl print/list/print-disabled (state, PID, run count, last exit code only) and the last lines of a service's error log inside <Thor home>/logs (never .env, auth.json, env files, start scripts, any other process's environment or other launchd environment entries); on user confirmation it permanently deletes chosen files in Thor-created project folders and ~/.cache, ~/.npm and ~/.pnpm-store tool caches, moves other items to a restorable 30-day Trash, runs allow-listed thor/uv/pnpm/git maintenance plus journalctl --vacuum-size and apt-get clean when root, starts/restarts/stops/disables Thor systemd services or (macOS) starts/restarts Thor LaunchAgents and boots out + disables a crash-looping one (plist kept), can write a Restart=always drop-in (Linux) and enable the disk-cleanup plugin, sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL if it does not exit) to selected leftover processes, and briefly stops Thor services to pack state.db (Linux; on macOS it shows the manual steps instead); non-Thor child processes get only PATH, HOME and locale.

name: storm-fusion-research
description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through Thor's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

name: strategic-arena
description: Understand the landscape before you invest: give it a link and get the room that reacts — who can block adoption, what each concession buys, and the claims you can score later. Research papers also get a replication clock. Disclosure — sends the documents you give it and the simulation prompts to your active Thor model via ctx.llm; fetches URLs you or the model supply (http/https, public addresses only, re-checked on every redirect); reads the public Nous model catalog (inference-api.thor-agent.local/v1/models, anonymous, cached 6h) to price runs; runs simulations in a background thread; writes run history and exported decision records only under plugin-data/strategic-arena; adds a Desktop page and dashboard API routes.

name: stream-speed
description: How fast each model starts answering and how fast it writes: /speed shows the median and p90 time to first text and the median characters per second per model, provider or day, or lists the newest streams (ten, or up to 100 with /speed recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded, from the streaming hooks. Disclosure — writes per-response stream timings (ids, model, timings, character count, no text) to plugin-data/stream-speed/streams.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; atexit waits up to 1 s; no network

name: strunk
description: Document review in Google Docs: publish a draft to Google Docs for review, pull reviewer comments back with the spans they anchor to, revise the doc in place, and reply to and resolve each thread. Existing comments and anchors survive a re-publish. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json) with Strunk's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE) and two skills, one for setup and one for the review round trip. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to strunk.io with the drafts you publish, and returns reviewers' comments and names, which also reach your model provider through the session. Google access uses the drive.file scope, limited to docs Strunk creates and files you pick. Write tools create and edit Google Docs and reply to and resolve comment threads under your Google account. The package marks the server untrusted so write tools ask first, but the sign-in step (`thor mcp add strunk`) writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to it. Thor stores and refreshes the Strunk OAuth token; WorkOS holds the Google refresh token on Strunk's side. The tool list comes from Strunk's server at run time, so the pinned commit does not cover it.

name: stt-vocab
description: Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt Thor sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters Thor keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; Thor uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.

name: study-tree
description: Study with the agent without losing the thread: a side question you ask becomes its own branched session, the side threads show as a tree in a Desktop pane, and each one hands one recall-checked takeaway back to the thread it came from. The agent can also draw interactive widgets and one-question quizzes inline, with follow-up buttons. Disclosure: stores its tree in SQLite and agent-written HTML widgets under the active profile's plugin-data/study-tree/ (a widget over 200 KB or with any network reference is refused; Desktop shows it in its sandboxed preview frame); opens Thor' state.db read-only to follow compression lineage; adds a short section to every session's system prompt, and through pre_llm_call injects a side-thread frame on each side-thread turn and each takeaway once into the parent's next turn; through transform_llm_output rewrites the final reply (study cards moved to the end as their own paragraphs, cards with unknown ids dropped, widget directives put on their own paragraphs, a widget button's prompt quoted at the top); creates a branched session (session.branch or session.branch_stored), renames it with session.title and sends the side question as its first prompt only when the user clicks Open; the Desktop half keeps the last text selected in the window in memory for 60 seconds to prefill the side-question dialog, and writes the glossary to the clipboard only when the user clicks Export glossary. No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: submission-desk
description: Readiness ledger for one application (a grant, a scholarship, a university or a job portal). Each requirement you confirm is tied to a verbatim quote from your saved instructions, the exact portal field label and the exact file revision (SHA-256). Local checks run on those bytes (real format, exact size, PDF pages, word counts) and say unknown instead of guessing; a changed file, rule or mapping makes earlier reviews stale. The agent proposes; only you confirm, review and attest, on a Desktop page or with /submission-desk. Exports a hand-back checklist and manifest. It never logs in, uploads, signs or submits. Disclosure: reads files only inside the application folder you choose (a folder the agent proposes is read only after you confirm it); never writes your files; parses PDFs with pypdf in a short-lived child process with CPU, memory and time limits; keeps its ledger and exports in the plugin's own data folder. No network calls, telemetry, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

name: subnano
description: Subnano's local MCP server for the pay-per-post marketplace. Search and read Posts, buy access in Nano (XNO) or USDC on Base, draft and publish Posts, answer comments and Requests, and receive payouts. Bundles seven workflow skills. Disclosure — spends real money. Native agent installations act within their own account without approval prompts, including paid publication, scheduling, unpublishing and deleting their own drafts; money stays off until the operator sets a rolling asset/network budget and standing immediate-delivery consent bound to current legal version, hash and exact text. Operators control payout addresses, folders, budgets and regime; adding or raising a budget or turning on standing consent requires typing ALLOW SPENDING in an interactive terminal; direct Nano transfers are unavailable to agent tools. Browser signature login is an exception to account actions without prompts: a selected, verified and fully onboarded native `setup new-agent` identity requires fresh human approval of the exact website, account and `nano-signin-v1` request, even in agent mode. Approve only a request started in your own browser. The client signs locally without a Nano transfer and returns no key, signature or session credential to the agent. Proof acceptance alone does not sign the browser in. Continue in the original browser completes login. External Nano identities and delegated connections are unsupported. If the host lacks a qualified approval form, only the human may run `subnano-mcp auth browser-signin --request-url` with the copied public request URL in their own trusted terminal. The agent must never run or answer it for them. A decline or cancellation ends the attempt without another approval route. Browser connections always use human mode with owner-selected Read, Drafts or Full server access. Human public actions follow five browser choices; paid publication/scheduling, draft deletion, payout changes and direct transfers always require exact confirmation. Native human mode has no standing choices or budget. A decline is final; unsupported hosts receive website guidance, not another approval path. Installations without a saved regime, including new-agent installations upgrading from 0.3.58 or earlier, stay in human mode until the operator runs `permissions regime --regime agent` in a terminal; a brand-new identity created with `setup new-agent` or `first-draft` starts in agent mode with no budget, and the low-level `setup new-agent` and `first-draft` commands create it without a human confirmation step. Legacy grants remain readable/revocable with separate explicit cumulative spending. Local controls are best effort and do not isolate agents with shell/credential access. Calls subnano.ai, the configured Nano RPC, BerryPay's public work endpoint by default (public root/difficulty only), and mainnet.base.org for balance reads. Keys and sessions are stored owner-only in ~/.local/state/subnano-mcp. Connecting an existing account opens the browser and uses a short-lived loopback listener for its approval callback; that account-connection flow is separate from native agent browser signature login. Updates are host-managed through `thor plugins update subnano`; the plugin never downloads or installs its own updates.

name: subscription-sheriff
description: Track subscriptions and free trials in plain English, get warned before they charge, and see what you really spend. Quiet renewal reminders (only when something is newly due, plus a trial-about-to-turn-paid warning), monthly and yearly totals per currency, biggest spenders, overlapping services, a /sheriff command and two one-click scheduled tasks (renewal reminders, monthly spend review). Fully offline. Disclosure — makes no network requests and imports no networking modules; reads no credentials, environment variables or files outside its own Thor profile state, where the subscription list and reminder markers are stored; cannot cancel or pay anything (cancelling only marks the entry); no background processes, telemetry, self-updating code or binaries.

name: sugar
description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine. Disclosure — Sugar stores memories in local SQLite at the nearest project `.sugar/memory.db` and `~/.sugar/memory.db`; before context compression it archives a transcript checkpoint (first 4,000 characters) there, mirrors built-in memory-tool add/replace writes into it, and (only when `sync_turns` is enabled) records a compact note per turn.

name: summon
description: Your own @grok on X that learns: tag your bot under any post and your Thor answers in the thread; say "learn this" under a how-to thread or video and it saves it as a skill that waits for your approval. A gateway platform for X that only reads posts from its owner, by user ID. Judges: thor gateway setup, choose X, "Borrow @taybotfyi" with invite code judge-thor; no bot account needed. Disclosure — polls the X API every 20 s while the gateway runs (the owner's posts that tag the bot, thread reads, replies); on the free trial and the borrow path those X calls, including the agent's reply text, go through the author's relay at summon.taylor.fyi (Cloudflare Worker, source in relay/), which holds the bot's X OAuth tokens and stores a hash of the trial key, both handles and user IDs, and reply and read counts (no post text, error logs only); with your own X app the four keys are saved to Thor's .env through Thor; with consent, setup sets platform_toolsets.summon to [safe, video, skills] and turns on skills.write_approval for all of Thor; videos in a thread go to Thor's configured video model through video_analyze; replies are public posts on X; on the borrow path the relay posts as the author's bot under the user's posts only, after Cloudflare Workers AI (Llama Guard) reads the reply.

name: sunshine-moonlight
description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run Thor. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a Thor approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

name: super-agent
description: Runs the Thor chat agent like a secretary with a team of workers: keeps chat turns responsive (60s reminder, 120s edit/execute pause, 30s terminal auto-detach), briefs every subagent before it starts, stops subagents that repeat identical results, brings open decisions back to the main agent, has it ask the user after repeated failed subagents, never takes a subagent that ended without its report as done, tracks background results until they reach the user, and records every delegated task in a SQLite ledger across gateway restarts (`thor super-agent status` shows it). Governance is a positive allowlist: only the platforms named in governed_platforms (default weixin) and the subagents they spawn are affected, and every other surface runs untouched. Disclosure — registers hooks for pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, subagent_start, subagent_stop, on_session_end, on_session_reset and on_session_finalize, a system-prompt section and a tool_execution middleware, so for governed sessions it can block or amend tool calls and results, LLM request context and subagent handoffs, and asks a governed foreground terminal command still running after 30 s to move to Thor's background process registry (through core's internal yield flag, which a Thor release may change); it copies your Thor USER.md and MEMORY.md memory files in full into every governed delegate_task brief, can start an internal agent turn via inject_message to re-report an unseen subagent result, writes a local ledger.db under the plugin's Thor data directory, and at startup reads the effective Thor config through Thor' own resolver to tell the main agent once about settings that weaken it (inline delegation, a high delegation.max_iterations); it also registers a read-only `thor super-agent status` CLI command that prints its settings and the ledger's recent tasks; no network calls, no agent tools, no credentials, no shell commands.

name: super-artifacts
description: Publish pages, forms, trackers and proofs as live URLs that open on a phone, and read back what visitors submit, through the hosted Super Artifacts MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the super-artifacts workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to superartifacts.app/mcp; published artifacts and what visitors submit to them are stored on Super Artifacts' servers. Artifacts are private by default, and the skill tells the model to publish private and never widen who can open one unless the person asked; Thor does not prompt before these tools run unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the server. No telemetry. OAuth must be enabled with `thor mcp add super-artifacts --url https://superartifacts.app/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: superlist
description: Tasks and lists in Superlist through Superlist's official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.superlist.com/mcp, OAuth 2.0 sign-in with the user's Superlist account, no keys in config): capture tasks with due dates, reminders, priorities, labels and repetition, plan projects as lists, read the Today and Inbox views, search, update, move, assign, complete, share lists, and read or reply to task messages. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Setup after install and enable: add an mcp_servers.superlist entry to ~/.thor/config.yaml with url https://app.superlist.com/mcp, auth: oauth and trust: untrusted (required; thor mcp login fails without auth: oauth, and this entry replaces the package's, trust included), then run thor mcp login superlist. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to app.superlist.com and acts with the signed-in user's own permissions. Tools can delete and restore tasks and lists and change list sharing; share_list sends the invited person an email and a push notification. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every write-capable call. OAuth tokens are stored by Thor, not by the plugin. The plugin sends no telemetry, but the Superlist server records each MCP call for product analytics, including the MCP client's name and version, and keeps per-tool usage metrics; this is part of the hosted service and not opt-in. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: superlocalmemory
description: Local-first long-term memory for Thor, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into Thor config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.

name: supermemory
description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

name: supranalytics
description: Five analytics workflow skills for SuprAnalytics: weekly performance reports, traffic source analysis, funnel drop-off analysis, revenue attribution, and Core Web Vitals / audit review. Connects to the SuprAnalytics remote MCP server via OAuth. All access is read-only. Network destination: https://supranalytics.app/mcp. No credentials are stored in the plugin. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + five skills), configuration only, no code; every tool call goes to the SuprAnalytics remote MCP server at https://supranalytics.app/mcp, which records usage per its privacy policy (https://supranalytics.app/privacy); the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The bundled mcp.json alone gets 401 under Thor: sign-in needs a native `mcp_servers.supranalytics` entry with `auth: oauth` and `thor mcp login supranalytics`, after which Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The skills only read analytics data.

name: surp-thor-x402-llm
description: Marketplace-aware LLM routing for Surp — live prices for all models, provider TPS and trusted flags, mid-chat seller switching, secret masking, and approval-gated paid chat. Disclosure — the messages passed to surp_chat and SURP_API_KEY go to the surp.ivc.lol gateway, run by the individual developer ivcained (operator page https://surp.ivc.lol/operator, terms https://surp.ivc.lol/terms; not affiliated with Surplus Intelligence), which forwards them to third-party sellers on the Surplus Intelligence marketplace, including sellers not flagged trusted unless trusted_only is set; paid surp_chat calls spend from the user's prepaid Surp balance (USDC on Base, 5 % gateway markup), each behind a per-model Thor approval prompt (denied in cron and other unattended runs by default) plus a per-request ceiling (max_spend_usd, default $0.05); the price, provider, quote, combo and cache tools call the same gateway without a key; routing preferences are stored under THOR_HOME/cache/surp-thor-x402-llm/.

name: surplus-intelligence-seller
description: Sell the full daily Venice DIEM allowance on Surplus Intelligence before 00:00 UTC. Seller-only and Venice-only: lists DIEM-funded Venice inference as Surplus offers, rebalances discount and caps through the epoch, and deepens price late in the day so leftover DIEM (which does not roll over) is avoided. Earnings settle in USDC on Base. Disclosure — Venice API key is sent to Surplus Intelligence (encrypted at rest) so Surplus can proxy buyer traffic; Surplus seller API and Venice billing/rate-limit endpoints are called to manage offers and read remaining DIEM; the tools create, reprice, pause and cancel offers without an approval prompt (price floor 0.10x), and if the Venice account also holds paid USD credit, buyer traffic past the DIEM can bill it unless the key's USD limit is 0; SIWE mint uses a throwaway wallet whose private key is discarded after signing, and the minted seller key is shown in the conversation.

name: survey-desk
description: Exact land-survey computation for Thor: closed traverses with misclosure and Bowditch/transit adjustment, area cross-checked by two independent methods, blunder-leg detection when a traverse fails tolerance, PROJ datum conversion (Minna, Nigeria belts, UTM, any EPSG) with the published datum-shift accuracy, and plan drawings exported as PNG, PDF, DXF, KML and GeoJSON, driven from a /survey field-book command or the agent. Disclosure: no network calls (PROJ network access stays off), no shell commands, no background processes, no credentials, no telemetry. Plans are written to <thor home>/plugin-data/survey-desk/plans/. Dependencies: pyproj, matplotlib, ezdxf.

name: svault
description: Field-level secrets protection: encrypt sensitive fields in a database at rest, redact them automatically when the agent reads the data, and reveal a single value only with human approval. Disclosure — encrypts files and JSON fields you point it at inside the session working directory (deleting a plaintext original only when you ask for it and approve), stores its agent private keys locally under the profile's plugin-data directory, and reveals values only through the human-approved `/svault` slash command on a local CLI/TUI/Desktop session, writing revealed values to a file under plugin-data instead of the chat; its key-directory guard is a best-effort string match on other tools' arguments, not a sandbox; no network calls.

name: swarm-for-hire
description: Post, inspect and pay AI-agent jobs on the Swarm-for-Hire NEAR escrow, with every payment behind Thor approval. Disclosure — crypto: signs NEAR transactions locally with SWARM_NEAR_PRIVATE_KEY (read only through Thor's secret scope; use a dedicated low-balance key) and sends them to the public NEAR RPC (or the user's rpc_url); swarm_post_job, swarm_approve_payout and swarm_cancel_job each go through Thor's approval prompt, and bounties above max_bounty_near are refused before approval; the default escrow contract yunganas.testnet is the author's testnet account and is unaudited; mainnet is off unless allow_mainnet is true and then needs your own contract_id.

name: switch402
description: switch402 web data tools: public page to markdown (full and lite), site map, page metadata, screenshots and web search, plus a free price and health quote. Disclosure — tool inputs (URLs and search queries) go to api.switch402.com, run by the switch402 team that maintains this plugin; the six paid tools spend USDC on Base ($0.001–$0.012 per call, charged only on success) from the wallet in SWITCH402_WALLET_KEY, which is used only locally to sign one x402 payment per call through Thor' secret scope and is never sent or logged; every paid call needs a fresh human answer to the Thor approval prompt (session/always answers do not carry over), stays under a per-request cap (max_spend_usd, default $0.02), and is refused in cron, yolo, approvals-off, smart-approval and other unattended runs; screenshots are saved under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/switch402/; no telemetry, no self-update.

name: switchbot-control
description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. The watch does not report Plug Mini on or off. A command can still turn a Plug Mini on or off. The published card sentence ("No Plug Mini on/off.") does not describe a command on this pin. Locks off unless enabled. When safety_devices is on, each lock or door command asks again. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. On this pin, yolo and approvals off skip the prompt only when a person can answer. A cron job, thor -q, and a webhook cannot send a command, even after always. Each watch run costs 0 tokens. The unmanned run holds no tools. schedule writes a script under THOR_HOME/scripts and creates the job with thor cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. A 0.1.x job stays a model turn until the next schedule. That turn allows switchbot_devices, switchbot_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool. The script drops every other profile .env key. If thor cron fails, unschedule still removes the script and says the job was not removed. thor cron create has no per-job tool list, which does not matter here because the unmanned run holds no tools. switchbot_command is a separate toolset. A cron turn hides it and refuses it, even after always. The published lines ("Every command asks for Thor approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions."), (Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time.), and ("The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule.") are not this pin. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. When they are enabled, each of those commands asks again, so always does not cover the next one. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Thor gateway can request a command and approve it. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a toolset off per surface with thor tools. On this pin, answering always in an interactive chat covers the same device id, command, and parameter, and it does not send from cron, thor -q, or a webhook. The optional watch is a no-agent cron script (every 5 minutes by default, 0 tokens a run) that stays after uninstall. While the plugin is installed, remove that job with thor switchbot-control unschedule. After uninstall that command is gone, so remove the job with thor cron remove. Not tested on real devices. Saved files are under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/switchbot-control for the active profile. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

name: synap
description: Synap — OpenAI-compatible hosted inference. Sends prompts and SYNAP_API_KEY to synap402.com; usage is billed against the user's Synap balance.

name: synento
description: Live video sessions that record themselves. The agent uses a restricted server key, then checks the recording before calling the integration working. Disclosure — connects to Synento's hosted MCP server (api.synento.com) and needs a Synento account; after sign-in its write tools can create projects and sessions, mint a short-lived connection token and a restricted server key (shown once in chat, then written to your app's env file), and run a synthetic media check, which use plan allowance and can fire your project's webhook. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted` so those calls ask first; sign-in needs a native `mcp_servers.synento` entry with `auth: oauth`, which replaces the package's server settings, so keep `trust: untrusted` in it. The remote tool list can change without a new pin.

name: syrinx
description: Your agent is fast; Syrinx makes it wait for the right moment.
