In a focus block (/flow 45) the agent's questions are parked with the default it took and it keeps working; when you return you get a catch-up, a list counted by code from the tool calls (files changed, commands run, anything that left your machine, and how much work rests on unconfirmed defaults), and every question in one card. During the block a fixed list of outward actions (git push, publish, send, deploy) is held before it runs and offered back on that card. Settle a question once with /always and it is never asked again. Late-night requests become a morning brief. Deep-work hours, a question budget, a time receipt, a Desktop pane and Argus, a pet whose pose shows the state. Disclosure: pre_tool_call can block the built-in clarify tool (during a focus block, over the question budget you set, or when a standing answer covers it) and tells the agent which default to use, and during a focus block only it blocks tool calls that match a fixed list of outward actions (push, publish, gh create, curl with a body, ssh, docker push, kubectl, terraform, send/post/deploy/upload/pay tools), storing a label, never the command (a guard, not a sandbox: scripts, execute_code and browser or MCP tools still run); hold_outward: false turns that off; parked questions, held actions and queued requests are handed back only to the session that created them; pre_llm_call appends short blocks to your message (standing answers, focus notes, the hand-back, the morning brief) and, after your cutoff and only on cli, tui and desktop (or platforms you add with night_platforms), ends the turn to queue the request; post_tool_call stores tool names, file basenames and program names, never arguments, plus your answers to clarify cards; with auto_focus on (macOS, off by default) it runs ioreg and lsappinfo read-only; /syrinx pet writes the bundled sprite sheet through Thor' pet store. No network calls of its own, approvals untouched; cron runs, subagents, the API server, kanban workers and messaging users are never refused at night.

name: t3-code-theme
description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Thor Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

name: tabella
description:
Read, create and convert documents — .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, .odt, .ods, .odp — from structured JSON or HTML/CSS, with OCR for scanned files.

Disclosures
- Shells out to pandoc for conversion, a TeX engine for PDF output, and tesseract for OCR.
- Re-execs into its own dependency venv, bootstrapped from PyPI on first run.
- Optional self-host HTTP server; a bearer token is generated into the plugin data directory on first run.
- Reads and writes only the filesystem paths you pass.
- Runs entirely locally: no network calls, no telemetry.

name: tablekeeper
description: Tabletop RPG campaigns for Thor group chats. Code rolls the dice and owns hit points, positions, initiative and turn order, each player controls only their own character, and the model narrates the results. SRD 5.1 monsters, characters and spells, including a young red dragon with a fire breath cone. With `/table dice phone`, each player throws their own d20 from a Telegram button; code still rolls the number. Disclosure — Disclosure: Storage. `<thor home>/plugin-data/tablekeeper/campaigns.sqlite3`, resolved per profile, WAL mode, file mode 0600. The Desktop pane and dashboard route open it read-only; Prompt. In a chat that has a campaign, and in a local CLI or Desktop session once it has used `/table` or a `tk_` tool, a compact state summary of at most about 600 tokens is added to each turn and the reply passes through the narration guard. The guard lets a reply quote any hit point or AC figure the state block listed or a tool returned, flags invented damage, rolls and hit points, and appends one compact correction line. A campaign with no table activity for 24 hours adds no prompt tokens until the next `tk_` call or `/table` command wakes it. Other sessions and chats without a campaign are untouched; Network and processes. The plugin opens no connection of its own, starts no subprocess and reads no credentials. With `/table dice phone` on a Telegram session it registers one callback handler scoped to `^tk:throw:<id>` and sends one button message per pending throw through the gateway's own bot; a tap is accepted only from the character's owner id; each throw result, including an automatic throw when the owner does not tap within the timeout (15-600 s, default 120), is queued into that chat as a message from the owner and starts an agent turn without anyone typing; Identity. Platform, chat id and sender id from the turn context, used as the campaign and owner keys.

name: tailgate
description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Thor hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

name: taint-sentry
description: Provenance and taint tracking for tool results. Every tool result is stamped with where it came from; content authored by a third party (web fetches, MCP servers, screenshots, images, and files written from untrusted content) is stripped of invisible characters, wrapped in an <untrusted> marker, and marks the session as tainted. While a session is tainted, side-effecting tool calls are checked against a policy: credential reads, and writes into files the agent reads as instructions (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hook handlers, Thor' own config), are refused; network egress and writes outside the workspace go to Thor's own approval gate, which is never auto-approved. A call is evaluated as the call it really makes: tool_call, execute_code and process_manage are unwrapped to what they actually run, taint is copied into subagents, and an encoded payload is decoded and judged by what it decodes to. What is reliable and what is not: the taint mark is provenance-based — it comes from which tool produced the content, not from guessing at it. The credential, egress and write detectors are best-effort pattern matching over tool arguments, so an obfuscated command, a payload assembled to avoid the patterns, and writes through the memory or cron tools can get past them. A seatbelt, not a sandbox; the README's Known limitations lists exactly what is out of scope. Ten rules, each tunable to allow/monitor/escalate/block; a receipts ledger; a `thor taint-sentry` CLI with a dry-run policy tester. Ships a Desktop half in the same package: a pane, a status-bar chip and ⌘K commands showing live taint state, the receipt feed and per-rule actions, backed by `/api/plugins/taint-sentry/`. The pane changes a rule on the user's click; a tool call that tries the same thing — the CLI, `config.yaml`, or that API over loopback — is refused. Disclosure — no network access, no credentials, no python dependencies and no core overrides: it reads tool arguments and results in-process, writes its decisions to a local SQLite ledger under the plugin's own data dir, and reads an optional policy file there. Nothing needs configuring; `mode: monitor` records without interfering and `mode: off` disables enforcement.

name: takeover
description: Human-in-the-loop screen takeover. When a step needs you (sign-in, approve/authorize, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment) the agent asks, you take over its browser/desktop from thor-webui, the dashboard or Desktop (even on a phone), then hand back. Installs TigerVNC + Xfce via Thor's Bot Desktop installer (root) and runs a local VNC/websocket service. Disclosure — on first deliberate use (the Screen page, the agent's first `request_takeover`, or `thor takeover setup`) it installs TigerVNC and Xfce as root through Thor's Bot Desktop installer and sets `browser.headed: true` in your config (turn off with `auto_install: false`); when the plugin loads it copies a Screen page into thor-webui's extensions folder and runs a loopback Takeover service there (turn off with `webui: false`); whoever holds the takeover controls the agent's browser and desktop, and the agent's screen tools are refused until they hand back.

name: tala
description: Read your Tala AI phone agents and their call results from Thor through Tala's official read-only connector (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.tala-assistant.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in on Tala's consent screen): list the agents you authorized, list their calls with date and status filters, and read a call's status, duration, context and summary. Bundles one skill for the connector. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Tala's hosted MCP server (mcp.tala-assistant.com) and acts only on the organization and agents the user selected at OAuth sign-in; results include callers' phone numbers and call summaries (third-party text), which reach the user's configured model. The connector is read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: talaria-bench
description: A physics test bench for DIY servo robots: build your robot from a template and a few measurements, see it in 3D next to its photo, run a one-click MuJoCo arena (flat, ramps, bars, pushes, slippery floor) across randomized worlds with a report card that says why it fails, compare design variants or watch a changed version side by side in the Arena, and gate robot_play / robot_pose with an exact-motion preflight in simulation before a move may play on the real robot (ESP32 + PCA9685 firmware included, or a virtual robot). CPU only, no GPU, no CAD. Disclosure — the automatic return to home (before a move and on robot_stop) is speed-limited (at least 3 s) but not simulated on its own; runs benchmark and comparison jobs as background Python subprocesses with worker pools (up to N-1 cores each, at most 2 jobs at once); starts local virtual-robot HTTP servers on 127.0.0.1 (random port, no token) on demand, and `thor talaria sim` listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 unless --host is given; sends plain HTTP only to the robot address you set (bypassing proxies; the robot token travels unencrypted on your LAN); reads a robot photo only from a path you give under your home or Thor folder; writes robots, photos, moves, approvals, jobs, reports and caches under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/talaria-bench (the trace cache is not pruned). The optional robot token is a Thor secret. No third-party services, shell commands, downloads or telemetry.

name: talaria-shortcuts
description: Write, compile, sign and audit iOS Shortcuts from Thor with no Mac: six tools turn plain-language intent into reviewable Cherri source, compile it to an unsigned .shortcut inside a bwrap sandbox, sign it through RoutineHub HubSign on explicit consent, and audit any .shortcut (signed AEA1 container or plain plist) for what it reads, writes and sends before it is installed. Bundles the shortcuts-authoring skill (file shape, verified action signatures, house patterns, and the traps that make a shortcut compile cleanly and still be broken). Disclosure — the Cherri compiler runs as a subprocess under bwrap with no network namespace, a read-only root, a throwaway HOME and only the job directory writable, and a build is refused rather than run on the host when bwrap is missing; talaria_setup, after Thor approval, downloads the third-party Cherri v2.4.0 compiler (electrikmilk/cherri) from GitHub and installs it only if both recorded sha256 checksums match. Network call sites: talaria_status opens one TCP connection to the signing host only when called with probe_signer=true; talaria_inspect on an iCloud link fetches that shortcut from Apple's iCloud hosts only; talaria_sign uploads the compiled shortcut as an XML plist plus its name to https://hubsign.routinehub.services/sign (RoutineHub, a third party) only after Thor approval per artifact, so unattended runs fail closed. Artifacts are written only under $THOR_HOME/talaria (or $TALARIA_HOME). No telemetry, no credentials.

name: talaria-webui
description: Extends Thor Agent API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the Thor API server (cross-session history search, rewind/compress of API sessions, branching any session into a new API session, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata and compaction sizes (no message bodies) in $THOR_HOME/talaria/observations.db, deleted with their session; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.

name: tallybuy
description: Price comparison for Germany and Austria through Tallybuy's public MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://tallybuy.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): product search, shop offers with delivery cost and delivered total, price history and side-by-side comparison. Bundles the tallybuy-shopping skill: unknown prices stay unknown, every price carries its shop and time, no basket totals, and the person is sent only to the offer's own link. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — connects to the hosted Tallybuy MCP server at tallybuy.com (no key); search words, market and destination country go to it and it sees the caller's IP (used for rate limits); shop links it returns are affiliate links and Tallybuy may earn a commission; the six tools are served by the remote server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha.

name: tallyhand
description: Twitch chat for Thor Agent that treats chat as untrusted input. Roles come from chat badges and are enforced in code before every tool call: viewers get no moderation tools, and bans, unbans and long timeouts wait for the streamer's approval. The streamer also gets Twitch and OBS tools, chat commands that need no model call, viewer notes kept only with consent, and replies in the stream's language. Disclosure — chat in the configured Twitch channels starts Thor turns for allowlisted viewers (or everyone, if TWITCH_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true), and those viewers' turns run in this profile with its persona and the questions go to your model provider; while this profile's memory, user profile or an external memory provider is on, only your own questions are answered unless you set allow_profile_memory_for_viewers: true, which puts your MEMORY.md, USER.md and memory-provider recall into viewers' turns; viewers and moderators get no Thor tools beyond the to-do list and, for moderators, capped Twitch moderation, while bans, unbans and long timeouts need your approval; the bot token is used only against Twitch's own endpoints and OBS is contacted on this computer unless TALLYHAND_OBS_ALLOW_REMOTE=true; viewer notes (!remember) are stored under the profile's plugin-data for 90 days by default, and !forgetme deletes the viewer's notes and their own per-viewer Thor sessions; the setup wizard writes the token to .env and, after a yes/no, Twitch toolset/context settings to config.yaml. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: tallyseal
description: Checks each group in a CSV report against a pinned source and seals the exact report bytes that pass. Disclosure: the check tool directly reads source.csv and report.csv in an operator-configured host folder and returns counts, record numbers and hashes. The local seal command writes a new file to an operator-selected path. No network, subprocesses, credentials or telemetry.

name: talos
description: Automatic, unskippable smart-contract security checks for code Thor writes and deploys (EVM, Solana/Anchor, Sui/Move): scans every .sol/.rs/.move file Thor writes, feeds open findings back so Thor fixes its own bugs, and gates deploy commands (anchor/solana/sui/forge/hardhat, including inside scripts) — mainnet blocked on high/critical findings, escalated to Thor's human approval on medium, allowed with a warning on devnet/testnet; plus a /talos report command and a talos_scan tool. Disclosure — its pre_tool_call hook can block terminal deploy commands (anchor/solana/sui/forge/hardhat, including inside scripts, package.json scripts and Makefiles it reads) or escalate them to Thor approval; every non-deploy call passes through. Never runs repository code: Slither analyses each .sol file with plain solc from an empty temp directory (no Hardhat/Foundry builds, no repo slither config), with import remappings read from static files. Runs local CLIs when present (slither, sui move build --lint, solana config get, sui client active-env, cast chain-id), each with a minimal environment that excludes Thor's API keys; cast chain-id contacts the RPC URL named in the deploy command and sui move build may fetch the package's git dependencies. Requests no capabilities. Stores findings and a file-hash scan cache in its plugin data directory. No telemetry, no third-party APIs, no credentials read or stored. Fails closed: unknown network counts as mainnet, and a missing, crashing or timed-out analyzer reports code as unchecked. Heuristic rule packs, not an audit.

name: tam
description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: Thor provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside THOR_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; thor memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

name: tamathor
description: Grow a local TamaThor pet from real Thor agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $THOR_HOME only; the optional python -m tamathor CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

name: tameru
description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_read_original tool brings back the exact original. You can also Restore or Keep a shortened output in full, pin lines of your own through every summary, and see it all in a Desktop panel and a /tameru command. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Replaces Thor's context engine and subclasses its built-in ContextCompressor through a private import, overriding its private prune/demote methods (it checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Thor's re-prune runway for the running session. Adds a model-callable tameru_read_original tool (tameru_expand is still answered but no longer listed) that returns pruned tool output from memory or this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process (python -I -S, with a timeout). Adds a short note to the system prompt and, only when something changed, a short note to your message for the model. An optional lazy_tool setting (off by default) registers an llm_request middleware that leaves the recovery tool out of requests until a result has been shortened. Optional learned_priors, net_estimate and stats_ledger settings (off by default) keep small files (numbers only) under the Thor home. Keeps per-chat records (lean mode, pinned lines, Keeps, policy choices) in the plugin's own durable state (ctx.state), under one key per chat, and clears a chat's record after 90 days unused. Registers the hooks pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, post_api_request, api_request_error and post_compaction. No network calls, no credential reads; the render log is off by default.

name: taofind
description: China reverse proxy shopping hub, 1688 link desensitizer, IATA volumetric shipping calculator (5000 vs 6000 divisor), and proxy agent fee comparator through TaoFind's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://taofind.com/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the taofind workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local runtime code: every tool call goes over HTTPS to taofind.com/api/mcp with the shopping links and parcel details you give it, and the remote tool list is served by TaoFind at runtime, not covered by the reviewed pin; the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses those in unattended runs.

name: tap-proof
description: Find the exact CSS viewport widths where a control on a local web page loses its center hit. Tap Proof reports the blocking element and saves boundary screenshots and a receipt. Replay the same check after a fix. Disclosure — launches a bounded Node subprocess and headless Edge, requests same-origin resources over loopback HTTP, and writes receipts and witness PNGs to the active profile's plugin data. The tool returns the saved paths.

name: task-navigator
description: Source-grounded 5W1H task cards and advisory prompt-preparation workflow for Thor. Disclosure — registers a `pre_llm_call` hook that adds a fixed reminder to most substantive turns telling the model to call `housekeeper_prepare` first, so most turns gain one extra tool call.

name: taskreel
description: Teach Thor a local task once, then replay it with no model call. Checkpoints stop the replay on the first failed step. Disclosure — taskreel stores the exact, unredacted arguments of every tool call (file contents, shell commands) in its own plugin database and replays saved routines with no model call; replayed steps still hit each tool's own approval but bypass other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks and tool middleware.

name: taskwatch
description: Background-task watchboard for the Thor Desktop status bar and a side pane: every process the focused chat dispatched through terminal(background=true) (claude, opencode, codex, a build, anything) with live output tail, runtime, a silence heartbeat, a two-click stop, and OS notifications when a task goes quiet past a configurable threshold or exits (success/failure by exit code). Agent-agnostic by construction — it renders the gateway's own process.list projection for the focused session. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network. Everything is local.

name: taster
description: Runs another Thor plugin once in a locked box (fake home, canary wallet files, network denied and logged) and reports what it did versus its manifest. Disclosure — /taster runs the plugin folder you point it at as real code on this machine, once, inside macOS sandbox-exec (network denied, writes only in a throwaway fake home, reads of your home folder denied); the box does not block reads elsewhere on disk or macOS system services such as the keychain, and the report shows what the tested plugin printed, so it is a tripwire, not a safety guarantee. Taster itself makes no network calls, stores no credentials and runs nothing in the background. macOS only.

name: tavily-plugin
description: Search, extract, map, crawl, and research through Tavily hosted MCP, with Tavily skills. The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports Thor-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a Thor-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.

name: teach-back
description: Make sure you understand the code your agent writes. Teach-Back records every file the agent writes or patches, and /teachback quizzes you on it: short questions about what the new code does (behaviour, edge cases, failures), written from the real change by your own model through ctx.llm and graded the same way, with the right answer explained when you miss. /teachback score shows how many agent-written lines you were quizzed on and understood.

name: teamorouter
description: TeamoRouter as Thor model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Thor' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Thor' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: thor-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.

name: tebar
description: Publish and schedule social media posts through Tebar's (tebar.app, Indonesian social media scheduler) official hosted MCP server: Instagram, Threads, Facebook Pages, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Pinterest, Telegram and Discord; edit, cancel and retry scheduled posts; read account and post statistics; reply to comments, answer Instagram DMs and run comment-to-DM automations; keep an ideas board. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to https://api.tebar.app/mcp, which calls the social platforms' APIs for the user's connected accounts, with the user's API key from TEBAR_API_KEY sent as a Bearer header. Write actions are public and cannot be taken back through Tebar: they publish posts, reply to comments, send DMs and turn on automations that reply to people on their own; posting to X is paid from the user's Tebar balance. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool not annotated read-only. To upload a file from the Thor machine, the bundled skill has the agent run a curl upload command returned by Tebar's server with that file's path. Account data returned by tools (posts, statistics, comments, DMs, commenter and customer names) reaches the model provider. API access needs a paid Tebar plan or the free trial. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: telegram-app
description: Phone control panel for Thor inside Telegram: live status and usage, sessions and their messages, agent cron jobs (create, edit, pause, run now, stop, catch-up per job), logs, skills and memory, a send-to-Telegram box and error alerts, opened from your bot's menu button. Login is Telegram initData (HMAC-SHA256 with Ed25519 fallback, freshness window) checked by a token-only dashboard-auth provider on one token route, against a plugin-owned admin list (TELEGRAM_OWNER_ID plus the plugin setting admins) that refuses everyone until set; being allowed to chat with the bot never grants login. Alerts and the send box reach admins only. Built by Muhammad Aiman (aimanmalib) at Sasa Teguh. Disclosure — a verified login returns the dashboard session token, which authorises the whole dashboard API; because Thor asks every token provider on every token route, valid initData also passes the token gate of /api/gateway/drain when THOR_DASHBOARD_DRAIN_SECRET is set (a route the session token cannot reach); the plugin's principals carry the scope telegram-app and its login route demands it once Thor has per-route scopes (#146551), which also closes drain to initData; loopback dashboard mode only, with the phone app (web/ in the repo) served by your own reverse proxy that forwards only /api/plugins/telegram-app/*. Calls api.telegram.org with TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (read through Thor's secret route) for the send box and alerts. Runs one background alert thread in the dashboard process (polls errors.log and cron state every 30 s; the plugin setting alerts_enabled: false turns it off) and stores its settings under $THOR_HOME/state/telegram-app. Reads Thor sessions, cron jobs, logs, skills and memories; writes only agent cron jobs (no script, no_agent or workdir). No telemetry, no self-update.

name: telegram-client
description: Telegram client pane for Thor Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's Thor secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in THOR_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).

name: telegram-notify
description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Thor agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under THOR_HOME/telegram-notify.

name: telegram-stickers
description: Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through Thor' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Thor answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Thor. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Thor' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Thor like any tool. Uses Thor functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.

name: telegram_dashboard_probe
description: One pinned Telegram message with your Thor' state on one phone screen, edited in place from inside the gateway. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — reads Thor' files read-only, the agent's context files wherever it works, and the free space of the disk THOR_HOME lies on. Disclosure — edits the message through the Telegram adapter, private members included. Disclosure — Thor' usage facade every 5 min, which may read the Claude Code or Codex CLI login and refresh its token. Disclosure — GitHub releases without a token, at most every 15 min, no off switch. Disclosure — opt-in: loopback limit sources, a drift command. Disclosure — its own code writes only its record; the full list is in the README.

name: telesec
description: Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat, with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export), correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend Thor is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the Thor model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; an optional message check on the same gateway and optional Cloudflare fact extraction are off by default); an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) into the Business chat for the contact to read; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; opt-in dossiers run a gateway background thread; modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under THOR_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; no telemetry.

name: telnyx-provider
description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

name: telos
description: Telos — workspace routers and canonical models through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint; browser sign-in (PKCE) or an existing Telos API key. Disclosure — sends your prompts, model discovery and your Telos key to app.telosplatforms.com (or TELOS_BASE_URL), which routes inference to the upstream providers your workspace policy allows; requests carry the Thor conversation ID as metadata.conversation_id.

name: tenderlead-agent-plugin
description: Review supplied UK tender documents against a supplier profile before a BID or SKIP decision. Agent Plugins v1 package with one local skill; it does not fetch live tenders or submit bids. Disclosure: the skill reads only material the user supplies to Thor; no plugin code, install scripts, network calls, credentials, background processes or telemetry. Material supplied to Thor remains subject to the user's Thor and model-service settings.

name: tensorfold
description: TensorFold's native server (github.com/ashhart/TensorFold) as a Thor model provider (`--provider tensorfold`, or TensorFold in `thor model`): the served models from its /v1/models and each model's context window from the same list, on `tensorfold serve`'s loopback default (http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, TENSORFOLD_BASE_URL for another), plus a TensorFold dashboard tab with the server's model, speed, streams, token totals, MTP acceptance and memory. Disclosure — registers one model provider and one dashboard tab and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); it connects only to the TensorFold server at TENSORFOLD_BASE_URL: chat requests go through Thor' own client with TENSORFOLD_API_KEY, the provider reads /v1/models, and the tab's backend route reads /health, /stats and /v1/models, so the key never reaches the browser; it reads and writes no files, starts no processes and reports nothing anywhere.

name: tenure
description: Revocable trust for Thor agents, per action type. By default every kind of action works as with Thor alone (files, memory, subagents, known dev tools: npm, pytest, cargo, git...), and every local change is saved first: file writes and plain rm, mv, cp, sed -i or `> file` on project files act, then tell you, with `/tenure undo` for 24 hours. The first mistake on a kind of action (an undo, a flag, a refusal of Thor's own prompt, a file it wrote that no longer parses) puts that kind, for every model of the profile, on probation: it asks first, earns back acting-then-notifying on a run of approvals, then acting alone with random spot checks, from a rule preregistered on OSF (Wald SPRT to the middle tier, Dodge's CSP-1 series to the top, a guarantee you choose). What leaves the machine (push, publish, deploy, registry logins, cloud writes, payments), unreadable shell, and anything after the agent read outside content keep asking; one "Allow for this session" covers a session. Signed, hash-chained, replayable autonomy passport (`thor tenure verify`), a per-model benchmark of your own work, a switch preview before you change model, a Desktop page and a dashboard tab at parity, five languages. Linux, macOS and Windows (on Windows, plain shell file commands keep asking instead of acting with an undo). A friction bench in the repo replays an ordinary 30-call coding session: 3 questions Thor would not ask, against 23 when every kind of action asks first. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_api_request, pre_tool_call, post_approval_response, post_tool_call, post_llm_call, subagent_start, subagent_stop), no tools; no network, no LLM call, runs no command. It can only add an approval prompt through Thor' own prompt, never answer one. Reads the profile's config.yaml and its own plugin settings, and writes settings back only through ctx.set_config when the owner saves them. Writes under plugin-data/tenure: a SQLite record and a hash-chained ledger (action types and outcomes, no paths, no commands, no free text), a signing key and an undo HMAC key, and undo snapshots of the project files an action is about to change (file bytes and paths, owner-only, deleted after 24 hours, 5 MB per action). The dashboard tab and Desktop page show the tenure records of every profile on the machine (read-only); revoke, flag, undo and settings act on the current profile only.

name: terraform-drift
description: Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every Thor surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with thor tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with thor plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires Thor >=0.21.4.

name: test-drive
description: Don't guess which plugin helps. Test-drive it. When Thor hits a capability wall (it says it can't, or a tool fails as unavailable) test-drive appends one line naming the best catalog match; /testdrive <need> and test_drive_find show the top 3 with trust cards (tier, pin, keys needed, declared tools/hooks, disclosure); after you approve, test_drive_run or /testdrive run installs the candidate into a throwaway THOR_HOME, runs your original request once with thor chat -q, attempts cleanup and reports a before/after with tool-call evidence when available; keep goes through Thor's own installer; /testdrive history keeps receipts. Disclosure — fetches the public catalog index from thor-agent.thor-agent.local (redirects only to https Nous hosts, cached 6 h); an approved drive installs the selected catalog repository and pin by URL through Thor, whose custom-source scanner may block caution verdicts, and installs its Python dependencies from PyPI into the sandbox's own runtime, runs child thor CLI processes (plugins install, chat -q, sessions export, gateway stop) with hard timeouts and process-group kill, sends your request to your configured model provider (twice with a baseline), and runs the candidate's code as your user inside the temporary profile (not an OS sandbox), including any network calls it makes; every test_drive_run is escalated to Thor's approval gate (fails closed unattended) and the slash command asks via ask_choice or an explicit --yes; the child runs single-query mode with dangerous commands denied; the child gets only system env vars plus your model route's key and the candidate's declared requires_env, read through agent.secret_scope (literal credential fields are stripped from the model and provider config written to the sandbox's 0600 config.yaml; a drive whose key exists only as a literal is refused); no memory, sessions, .env or auth.json are copied; temp dirs thor-testdrive-* are removed after drives when cleanup succeeds; cleanup failures are reported; stores the catalog cache, last gap per session and up to 50 drive receipts in its plugin-data folder; a transform_llm_output hook appends one nudge line to gap replies (off with nudges: false); optional llm_check calls your active model; no telemetry.

name: testsift
description: Exact, local analysis of JUnit XML test reports (pytest --junitxml, Maven Surefire, Gradle, Jest/Vitest junit reporters, go-junit-report/gotestsum, PHPUnit, .NET, CI artifacts), from one file or a directory of them. test_report_summary gives exact pass/fail/error/skip counts, failures grouped by cause (messages that differ only in numbers, ids or quoted values share a group), the slowest tests and flaky suspects; test_report_failures lists failing tests with type, message, file/line and the start and end of the trace; test_report_compare diffs two runs into newly failing, fixed, newly skipped, still failing, added, removed and much slower tests. Streamed, standard library only: no network, no credentials, no third-party dependencies, no self-update; DOCTYPE and entity declarations are refused. Disclosure: reads the local report paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Thor' core read denylist.

name: tether
description: One Thor agent, many machines: lends a remote Thor agent the terminal, files, screen and apps of your paired desktop machines (macOS and Windows). Say 'tether <machine>' and the agent's terminal, file and computer-use tools act on that machine under its own Thor rules and approvals; send 'untether' to bring them home. Each machine dials the host over a pinned, mutual TLS 1.3 link (256-bit suites only), and the person at the machine allows every session on its own screen before anything runs. Includes a Tether panel for Thor Desktop (paired machines, labels, idle limits, connection log). Disclosure — the host listens on the LAN or tailnet address you configure (default 127.0.0.1) and each paired device connects to it over pinned mutual TLS 1.3; no third-party services, no telemetry; while a machine is tethered, the host session's shell commands, file reads/writes and computer use run on that device after the person there allows the session, judged by the device's own Thor rules (its hardline/deny floors always; commands the host's approval gate already passed skip the device's own approval prompts); skills opened during a tethered session are copied read-only into a per-session workspace on the device and removed when it closes; background tasks: the link listener (host), the device's connection, an idle sweeper and a settings watcher; stores one Ed25519 key per machine, encrypted at rest, with its passphrase in Thor's secret store; adds a short per-turn note while a machine is tethered; reads private Thor approval internals (tools.approval) and fails closed if they change.

name: the-millionaire-matrix
description: Every model family you have a seat for generates a candidate; all of them blind-score each other on a peer validity matrix anchored by real tests (hard and measured gates outrank the matrix), the field steps down round by round to one answer behind a human gate, and verified lessons carry into your next session. Disclosure — after you approve each `critic_run` (Thor shows the repo and every test/sensor command), this plugin runs those commands on the host against model-generated changes, and can launch your installed coding CLIs (codex, claude, grok, qwen, kimi, agy) to edit files in git worktrees under the repo with your user's permissions. Merging a winner happens only through `/critic gate` or `thor critic gate`. Its usage panel runs those CLIs' own read-only quota commands and reads Claude statusline/Grok billing logs to show your plan usage.

name: thefaceanalysis
description: Face shape, facial proportion and face-type data from thefaceanalysis.com through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.thefaceanalysis.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys): the site's seven-rule face shape classifier on four distances, face/eye/lip/nose type definitions with their exact threshold rules, reference statistics from 102 research faces, methodology and an embeddable face shape finder. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.thefaceanalysis.com; no account or personal data is needed. All seven tools are read-only and the server accepts no photos. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: theme-catalog
description: 606 terminal color profiles (iTerm2-Color-Schemes) as Thor desktop themes and TUI skins, with in-app authoring. Browse and filter the catalog, apply a theme, then click the background or body-text chip to repaint it with the system color picker, hex, RGB, a page-wide hover lens or a screen eyedropper; repainting a catalog theme saves your version as a separate copy and leaves the catalog entry as shipped. Every derived token recomputes so the 4.5:1 readability floor still holds. Export/import JSON, star favorites, sort by minimum contrast. All 606 register through THEMES_AREA, so they also appear in Settings → Appearance, the ⌘K picker and /skin. Disclosure — on plugin load the Python half writes 606 skin files to ~/.thor/skins/catalog-*.yaml (overwriting same-named files) and copies a picker widget to ~/.thor/tui-widgets/ (outside the plugin's data directory, stamp-guarded); the TUI /themes picker applies a theme by running `thor skin use <theme>` as a child process; color edits, saved themes and favorites live in the plugin's own storage. No network calls, no credentials required.

name: thomas
description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Thor venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under THOR_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

name: thor-9router
description: Dashboard tab for a 9Router gateway configured as the `9router` custom provider: groups the router's models by route prefix, shows the last test result for each model, the `/models` response time and, with the optional admin password, connection health and cooldown counts. A Test group button retests one group at a time. Routing and load balancing stay in 9Router. Disclosure — calls only the 9Router URL from `providers.9router` in config.yaml; a group test sends real chat/completions requests (max_tokens 16, at most 25 models per press, never in the background), so it can spend credits or quota; the optional admin password logs in to 9Router's admin API and only connection name, provider, active state and test status reach the page; secrets are read through Thor get_secret and not stored; results are kept in $THOR_HOME/thor-9router.json. No telemetry.

name: thor-aac
description: Communication boards, explicit speech, switch scanning and reviewed AI proposals for Thor Desktop. Disclosure — Desktop-only page; Speak sends your message text through the Thor gateway to the TTS provider configured in Thor (cloud providers receive it) and the audio plays on the gateway host, which may be remote; the AI helpers open a separate Thor chat session per request and send your topic or message as a normal agent turn on your model provider; saved phrases and approved boards are kept in plaintext in the plugin's Desktop storage.

name: thor-action-bar
description: A selection bar for Thor Desktop with two kinds of action. Select text in a chat and a small bar appears: Reply, Ask, Explain, Summarize, Fact-check, Copy. Reply keeps the quote and one comment as a card above the composer; the cards go in front of your message as Markdown blockquotes when you send, so several passages each get their own comment in one message. Ask, Explain and Summarize open an answer card next to the highlight, with follow-up questions: the answer does not enter the chat and the agent does not see it, unless you click Send to chat, which puts it in the composer without sending. Fact-check is a template for the agent: it saves the quote as a reply card with a ready request to verify it, and calls no model. Actions are a label, a prompt and a place (answer card or agent), editable on a settings page, with an optional research set. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — reads the text you highlight (window.getSelection) in Thor Desktop; an answer card (Ask/Explain/Summarize, or any action you set to answer in a card) sends the selected text (up to 6000 characters), up to 4000 characters of surrounding text and the card's earlier turns to your configured model through Thor' stateless llm.oneshot request (the open chat's model, else the auxiliary model) and writes nothing to the session; Reply, Copy and an action for the agent (Fact-check by default) send nothing; a composer middleware prepends pending quoted replies to your next message; links in answers open in your browser only when clicked; no other network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: thor-activity
description: Thor Desktop session analytics and provider-reported usage: annual heatmaps, token mix, model breakdowns and source-period summaries. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's state.db read-only and, for the Providers tab, an Activity cache under plugin-data/thor-activity plus the optional Quota quota_cache.json. Fetch provider data runs a local Node.js (22.18+) collector and, only on that explicit click, calls chatgpt.com through Thor's signed-in Codex request route (requires_auth: openai-codex) and api.commandcode.ai, opencode.ai and ollama.com with the optional API keys you configure as plugin secrets; it stores usage aggregates and hashed key identifiers locally. No other credential reads, telemetry or sign-in flow; remote profiles go through the configured gateway.

name: thor-adaptive-effort
description: Choose a separate scorer to set the reasoning effort of each Thor request. Disclosure — off by default; when a mode is enabled (or on an explicit `/hae probe`), sends the latest user message (or the parent-written subagent goal), truncated to 4000 characters, plus any configured guidance to the scorer you select (TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenAI Decisions, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI, Nace at console.nace.ai, a local Ollama endpoint that needs no key, or a custom URL) using that service's key, or with no key at all for Ollama and for an unauthenticated custom endpoint; by default an enabled mode also sends up to 4 earlier user/assistant text messages (1200 characters each, up to 6 when configured; never on subagents or `/hae probe`) and a separate yes/no continuation question to the same scorer on each turn (set `dialogue_context_messages` or `continuation_downgrade_votes` to 0 to stop this), and an opt-in setting can also send the target model identity. The prompt stays on this machine only when the Ollama endpoint is local: this plugin cannot vouch for a remote address an operator types. In Thor Desktop it also sets the focused chat's session reasoning selector through the gateway `config.set` API after each applied change, and it keeps a prompt-free effort-change history (64 changes × 64 conversations), per-conversation mode overrides (at most 256 conversations) and per-route cache verdicts built from provider token counters (at most 128 routes) in its plugin data directory.

name: thor-agent-builder
description: Guided Desktop workspace in BOTS: tailored questions, reference files, editable instructions and capabilities, version comparisons, model-only trials, and native Bot Chat handoff. Saves specialists as separate Thor profiles and installs the Builder companion plugin into its own bot profile. Disclosure — "Talk to Builder" auto-creates a thor-builder profile cloned from the active profile with copied .env/auth.json and copies+enables this plugin there outside the catalog installer (uninstall does not remove that copy); "Save agent" creates new profiles the same way and rewrites their tool/skill selection.

name: thor-agent-mixer
description: A mixing desk for how much a coding agent may change: four enforced dials (edits, write-scope globs, per-turn line budget, new-dependency policy) with /mixer, live presets, a Desktop dial panel in the composer, a web-dashboard saved-defaults bar and a steering-console page. Also drives Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through the agent-mixer hook command. Disclosure — enforces edit/scope/line-budget/new-dependency dials in pre_tool_call (blocks, or escalates "ask" to Thor approval, which /yolo skips) and adds a one-line rules context via pre_llm_call when a dial is off its default; per-session dial state is stored under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-agent-mixer/sessions/, and the Desktop panel and dashboard bar write the plugin's own saved defaults into config.yaml (plugins.entries.thor-agent-mixer.settings); the separately installed agent-mixer CLI keeps its own state in ~/.config/agent-mixer and ~/.local/state/agent-mixer, writes hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/commands/mixer.md, ~/.codex/hooks.json or ~/.gemini/settings.json only when run as `agent-mixer install <harness> --yes`, and `agent-mixer ui` serves a token-guarded console on 127.0.0.1:8377.

name: thor-agent-radio
description: A 24/7 radio station about Thor Agent and open-source agents, written, fact-checked and voiced by agents, inside Thor. Desktop gets a player bar under the composer that lifts into a panel, a full player page, a status-bar dot and a detachable pop-out window. Your agent gets eight tools and a /radio command to see what is on, read the guide and sourced show notes, browse stations and songs, request songs, vote in the weekly chart and send the hosts a question, topic or roast; a human producer reads every one before anything airs. Disclosure — the tools make HTTPS calls only to the configured station (default thoragentradio.com, run by the plugin's author; plain http is refused except for localhost) and send what the agent submits (question/topic/roast/track text, song ids, votes) plus an optional sender name and an anonymous random listener id stored in the plugin's data folder. The Desktop half shows the station's own player page and audio stream, loaded live from thoragentradio.com (or a self-hosted station set under Settings, Plugins), in the Desktop SDK's sandboxed frame. No hooks, context injection, shell commands, background work, credentials, telemetry or self-updater; Python standard library only.

name: thor-android
description: Remote Android device control for Thor Agent: 58 android_* tools (read screen, tap/type/swipe, open apps, camera, screenshots & screen recording, files, notifications, microphone streaming, media, clipboard, SMS/calls, Health Connect) plus a companion Android bridge app (Kotlin/Compose). The phone dials out to a relay you host — works behind NAT, no port forwarding, no VPN. Chat and media are end-to-end encrypted with a Double Ratchet (the relay sees only ciphertext); device commands travel over your own TLS-authenticated relay. Disclosure — drives a paired Android phone (screen reading and input, camera, microphone, files, notifications, clipboard, SMS/calls, Health Connect) through a relay the plugin starts inside Thor (localhost by default; a non-localhost bind requires TLS or an explicit ANDROID_RELAY_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1); SMS, calls, file deletion, intents/broadcasts, APK install and relay setup go through Thor' approval prompt (cron follows approvals.cron_mode, other unattended runs refuse); chat and media are Double-Ratchet end-to-end encrypted, but device commands are protected only by the relay's TLS when configured.

name: thor-anilist
description: AniList tracker for Thor Desktop — airing countdowns, a season browser, a local or account-backed watchlist, episode alerts and a daily digest, plus agent tools that read your own list and answer about a single show. Disclosure — stores your pasted AniList token in the active profile .env (sent only to graphql.anilist.co); alerts and the daily digest are Thor cron jobs it creates on the host you pick, and the digest job asks that host's agent to query the public AniList API itself.

name: thor-arcade
description: A neon arcade cabinet inside the Thor dashboard: three playable canvas games (Snake, Breakout, Pong) with glow effects, particle bursts, chiptune synth SFX and an attract mode that plays itself. Persistent top-10 leaderboards with arcade-style initials entry are served by a FastAPI backend plugin and shared with the agent: LLM tools (arcade_games, arcade_top_scores, arcade_player_stats) let Thor answer questions about your scores. No env vars, no hooks, no middleware; scores are stored only under the plugin's own data dir. The dashboard CSS loads Google Fonts (Orbitron / Press Start 2P) from fonts.googleapis.com — the only third-party network call. Disclosure — the dashboard tab loads Google Fonts (Orbitron / Press Start 2P) from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, which sends your IP and user agent to Google each time the tab opens; scores are stored locally in <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/thor-arcade/scores.json.

name: thor-arcade-tui
description: Three terminal games inside the terminal Thor already runs in: chess against the model Thor is using, a side-view kart racer, and Chrome's dino wearing the Thor cap. Disclosure — `/race` runs Python written by the model on your machine (in a child process with a time cap and no API keys in its environment, not a sandbox); chess and `/race` make extra model calls on your configured provider; when the game opens in its own window it reaches your model through a loopback-only local server protected by a random token.

name: thor-arena
description: A pixel-art platform fighter that runs inside Thor Desktop. Four fighters, two stages, and three ways to play: against a CPU, with a second player on the same keyboard, or online through Find a match or a room code. Online play connects the two computers directly. Disclosure — online play connects to the public PeerJS signaling server (wss://0.peerjs.com) and Google's STUN server (stun.l.google.com), then opens a direct WebRTC connection that shows your IP address to the other player; the game page loads Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) into the Desktop window each time it opens. No chats, Thor data or credentials are sent.

name: thor-ark
description: Encrypted, versioned backups of your whole Thor — memory, SOUL, skills, config, cron, sessions and every profile — with item-level restore. Snapshots happen automatically before every memory/skill write and after sessions; a health guard tells the agent (and you) when memory or skills suddenly shrink, with the exact /ark restore command that undoes it. Off-site copies to any S3-compatible storage (AWS, R2, B2, MinIO) or a folder, new-machine recovery (thor ark pull), and thor ark verify to prove every snapshot restores. AES-256-GCM, deduplicated, retention pruning; a Thor Desktop page with timeline, diffs and one-click restore. Self-defense: a prompt-injected agent cannot prune, delete, reconfigure or switch off Ark. Commands: thor ark …, /ark …; tool: ark_checkpoint. Disclosure — reads the Thor home and its profiles; Thor credential files (.env, auth.json, vault, pairing, browser logins, Webapp session token) are never read, captured or restored; ARK_PASSPHRASE and the S3 keys come only through the secret scope and are never stored. Writes snapshots to the configured repository folder (default $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-ark/repo) and restores into the Thor home only on an explicit user command or Desktop confirmation (the agent has no restore tool). tool_execution middleware on every tool call: snapshots before memory/skill writes and adds a note when the guard fires; refuses tool calls that would delete, rewrite or reconfigure Ark's backups or settings or disable it (allow_agent_admin lifts this); raises a tamper alarm when Ark is changed anyway, and never writes back settings, enabled state, secrets or its own plugin files — the user's changes always stick. The only repair is Ark's own repository key file after an agent tool call deleted it. Background threads: periodic snapshot/auto-push after sessions, and a 10-second watchdog in the agent process that stops when the plugin is disabled or unloaded. Network only to the user-configured S3 endpoint (HTTPS; plain http only for localhost). No subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-updater.

name: thor-artifacts
description: Claude-style artifacts for Thor: docs, sheets, whiteboards, slide decks, dashboards, designs, 3D models, films and design systems that Thor makes and you edit in place, versioned, in a gallery and sandboxed viewer inside Thor Desktop. Sheets calculate, dashboards re-run stored MCP queries, and everything exports locally (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf, png, svg, mp4, glb). Disclosure — stores artifacts, versions, comments and a 30-day trash under the profile's plugin-data folder; reads and writes host files only inside the chat's working directory (never Thor' home or hidden folders); live dashboards call your MCP servers through Thor only for servers you add to plugins.entries.thor-artifacts.mcp_allowlist, re-running a query without asking only when the agent ran that exact call in the chat (otherwise Thor Desktop asks first; set require_approval to always ask); the agent may suggest the allowlist command, and on an unsandboxed terminal it could run it itself; runs your system node with a minimal environment to calculate sheets; the optional browser viewer listens on 127.0.0.1 only; no telemetry.

name: thor-asgard
description: Twelve Norse gods carved in runestone and wood: Odin, Thor, Freyja, Loki, Frigg, Baldur, Tyr, Heimdall, Hel, Skadi, Freyr and Bragi, as Thor Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named asgard-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Thor skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

name: thor-atoll
description: Native Thor Agent plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for Thor session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every Thor session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. thor notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Thor's npm ci prompt. Run thor notch stop before removing.

name: thor-attention
description: Repeating desktop alerts for pending approvals and questions, with sound signals, custom audio and optional cached speech. Disclosure — Optional speech generation sends the alert phrase you type (never conversation content) to your configured Thor TTS provider, or to Microsoft Edge TTS when you pick a specific language, and may incur provider charges.

name: thor-audio-api
description: OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions and /v1/audio/speech endpoints backed by Thor' configured STT and TTS providers. Disclosure — opens an HTTP listener (127.0.0.1:8643 by default) that starts with the gateway as soon as a key exists, protected by a bearer key (AUDIO_API_KEY, or the API server's API_SERVER_KEY when reuse is on, which is the default); uploaded audio and requested text go to whichever STT/TTS providers Thor is configured to use; runs ffmpeg when it must convert the output format; calls Thor' internal transcription and TTS helpers, which are not a stable plugin API.

name: thor-australian-legal
description: Experimental public prototype for synthetic evaluation. The behavioural benchmark and qualified legal review have not been completed. Prepare Australian deal questions for counsel using dated regulatory sources. Reads selected Commonwealth instruments from a separately cloned local Git corpus, retains compilation commits and caveats, refuses dates outside recorded coverage, checks review prerequisites, calculates explicit hypothetical earn-out scenarios, and checks literal quotations. Preparation for counsel, not legal or tax advice. Disclosure — bounded local Git subprocesses, no shell; reads committed objects and metadata in the operator-selected corpus. No plugin network calls, credentials, telemetry, automatic updates, persistent matter writes or background jobs. The host model can receive supplied clause text and returned source excerpts. Approval fields are user attestations, not authenticated counsel approval or a host-wide permission gate. Quote matching does not verify source authenticity or legal support. The inspected corpus records selected Commonwealth instruments only and ends on 2026-09-01; it does not establish current law, Acts, case law, State law, tax or transaction-specific applicability.

name: thor-auto-titler
description: Topic-aware session title tracking for Thor Agent. Thor generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your Thor title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.thor-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

name: thor-autonomous
description: Proactive follow-ups: reads the recent conversation, finds things worth returning to (care / utility / risk / curiosity) and comes back at the right moment — a check on the weather before a trip, the price of something bought yesterday, or just "did your throat get better?". Event-driven rather than a daily digest: a cheap no-LLM gate runs on the cron tick and only wakes the agent when something is actually due. Sending goes through followups.py send, which enforces the 90-minute cooldown, the 23:00–08:00 quiet window, muted categories, at most three items and six lines per message, and records the receipt immediately. Disclosure — it reads the Thor session database (~/.thor/state.db) read-only: only sessions owned by the configured owner, DMs by default, with group/thread/forum/channel sessions (including other members' messages) only after setup --include-groups; it reads the cron job store (~/.thor/cron/jobs.json) read-only when doctor or setup runs, and writes only its own plugin-data directory (mode 0600). The install step copies two helper scripts into ~/.thor/scripts/; doctor --fix edits only this plugin's own cron job via thor cron edit and never creates or deletes jobs. During a review the agent runs the plugin's helper through its terminal tool, and followups.py send delivers the DM with thor send; the optional offline scripts/decide.py calls thor -z. No credentials are read and there is no telemetry.

name: thor-axiom-agent
description: Adds the nine-article Axiom Doctrine as pre_llm_call context (compact form capped at 1800 characters, full at 4000, owner additions separately at 800) and a /doctrine command that reports, per article, whether a matching enforcer plugin (standing, thor-axioma, tripwire, handydandy, thor-gatekeeper) is loaded and enabled. Enforces nothing itself: no tools, middleware or approval hooks, and ENFORCED means an enforcer is loaded and enabled, not verified coverage. Reads an optional owner additions file and only the top-level name line of user-plugin manifests, without following symlinked files; makes no writes, network, subprocess or model calls. No Python dependencies.

name: thor-axioma
description: Inline signal color in the agent's normal reply. The agent marks the few phrases that deserve a second look (stop, caution, go, whisper) and the plugin renders them per surface with color, a style cue and a word, never color alone: Desktop through KaTeX color, CLI/TUI through truecolor ANSI, Telegram/Discord/Slack as bold plus the word, SMS and email as the word only. Green renders only when a tool call Thor reported as successful in this session backs it; a rarity budget caps marks per reply; in completed replies Axioma transforms, malformed tags in prose are removed when a recognized tag is present; malformed-only replies, preserved code and raw tags during streaming can still show brackets. A color-vision-safe palette and a style-and-words-only mode are one setting away. Secondary: an advisory card (intent, light, signal, question) staged before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls and shown through Thor's own approval prompt. Each card and notice carries a short card code (a keyed hash of the exact text shown, the tool, its arguments and the card id), logged when shown and again with the answer; /signals verify <code> reports in plain words whether what was staged, shown and answered line up (spec section 5.6, shown equals staged). New in 0.4.0, an optional Desktop half (Axioma Desktop): a living caduceus drawn in code shows the run (staff for the main agent, serpents for running workers, amber while Thor waits on you, wings green only when a standing_proof tool call reports passed), with a side pane to change course or stop the main turn and each worker, two themes, and a switch for each part. New in 0.5.0, Axioma Charter: the axioma_charter tool and /charter command ask ten plain-English questions about what the agent may do and compile the answers into a readable CHARTER.md and a matching settings block for the owner to review and paste; it applies nothing itself. New in 0.6.0, two optional Desktop additions: an inline advice card the model may write in a reply on the Desktop surface only (light, one-sentence signal, who is affected, a question, and Hold / Go ahead buttons that only send that short reply to the same chat), and a small Axioma light on kanban board cards showing the worst advice recorded for that card's work. Advisor, not a gate: it never blocks, approves or executes anything. Disclosure — before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls (by default send_message, email/post/publish tools, payment/checkout tools, cron and kanban creation, delegate_task, terminal deploy and git push/gh pr commands, and terminal rm/mv when no workspace is configured) it escalates the call to Thor's own approval prompt with an advisory card, using a fresh rule key each time so remembered Session/Always approvals never skip later prompts; under cron and other unattended runs Thor's approval policy (default deny) then refuses those calls; it never auto-approves or executes anything, makes no network, model or subprocess calls, reads credentials only as presence checks through agent.secret_scope, adds a short markup guide to the system context through pre_llm_call, rewrites the agent's reply text to render the marks, and writes metadata, salted span hashes and keyed card-code digests (no message bodies) to an owner-only SQLite file plus a separate owner-only key file under its own plugin data directory. Optional operator-configured preflights probe file-presence metadata for required SKILL.md paths under external skill roots and lstat metadata for external device-lock paths; the policy resolves configured workspace/output roots and candidate remove/move paths, including symlinks, for containment checks, without reading those files' contents. Pasted-card verification optionally imports undocumented gateway.platforms.base_exec_approval text helpers and agent.i18n.t behind one compatibility function to recognize localized host framing, falling back to built-in English text if they are absent or change; it neither inspects approval state nor overrides approval. The optional Desktop half registers a right-side pane, a status-bar item, two themes, three palette commands, a settings page and a full-window canvas drawn over the app at low opacity (7-24%) with pointer events off; it subscribes to all gateway events but uses only event types, worker id/goal/status/tool-count/tool-name fields and the passed boolean of a standing_proof result, never message text; on a button press it calls session.steer, session.interrupt, subagent.steer or subagent.interrupt with the text the user typed; it keeps its on/off switches in local plugin storage and makes no network or model calls. The axioma_charter tool and /charter command write two local files, CHARTER.md and charter-settings.yaml, in a charter folder inside the plugin's own data folder and read them back; they make no network or model call, never edit config.yaml or any profile, and apply nothing. The card-code key must be owner-only; if its permissions cannot be confirmed, durable verification is refused.

name: thor-band
description: Compose and render original music on your own machine — an arrangement is data (tempo, key, chords, parts) rendered to exact-length wav and mp3. No music API, no model download, no per-track cost. Disclosure — renders by running the host's fluidsynth and ffmpeg against a local General MIDI soundfont and writes the wav, mp3 and per-part midi/wav stems into ~/thor-band-out/<name>/ (configurable via output_dir). Long renders take tens of seconds and run in the foreground of the tool call. No network calls, no credentials.

name: thor-beads
description: Native Beads (bd) work-graph plugin: fixed-argv adapter, scoped ready frontier, claim with read-back, guarded writes. Six tools over an explicit store path + actor; honest exit-code map incl. stale-13; plain bd stays fully sufficient (escape hatch). No desktop pane ships yet.

name: thor-bim-studio
description: Inspect local IFC files: report wall/slab BaseQuantities and door/window counts, optionally price only these four categories using caller-supplied rates, and generate an interactive offline 3D viewer. Disclosure — reads any local IFC file path the model or user supplies (parsed in-process by the ifcopenshell native library) and writes its .xlsx/.html reports only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-bim-studio/; the generated files embed the IFC path, its SHA-256, quantities, element IDs and model geometry. No network calls.

name: thor-blogwatcher
description: A Blogwatcher inbox for Thor Desktop and web, with themes, read controls and on-demand AI summaries. Disclosure: runs the original Blogwatcher CLI against its database; scans contact subscribed sites; requested summaries fetch public pages and send text to the configured Thor model after consent, which may incur costs. Summaries are cached locally. No telemetry or self-update.

name: thor-blueprint
