description: Turn a raw idea into a plan you can build, with the quality rules enforced in code: every verified claim quotes a page the plugin fetched, a fresh-context verifier re-checks them, the critic commits its verdict from base rates before you can push back, and estimates split agent hours, your hours and outside waits. Then /idea handoff writes a project folder and kanban cards, and a weekly re-check scores the predictions.

name: thor-board
description: A Miro-like board the agent draws with its own tools and you edit in a desktop pane, both sides working on one JSON document. board_apply builds a whole diagram in one call from ordered ops (nodes, edges, free lines, groups, notes, captions, layered auto-layout, bus trunks); board_render writes a PNG for chat or the interactive HTML editor; board_watch reports your own pane edits back to the agent. The pane docks beside the conversation with the same editor, saves your edits, and takes agent updates live. Disclosure — board_render shells out to a headless Chrome/Chromium already on PATH (nothing is downloaded; private temp profile, sandbox kept unless running as root) for PNG and self-test rendering; boards live in ~/.thor/board/ shared across profiles (THOR_BOARD_DIR / THOR_BOARD_RENDER_DIR / THOR_BOARD_WATCH override); serves /api/plugins/thor-board/ on the plugin host; reads this profile's state.db read-only to find the session board_watch should wake; no external network calls and no stored credentials; board_watch's wake into a messaging chat additionally needs plugins.entries.thor-board.allow_gateway_injection: true.

name: thor-body
description: Thor Body turns a phone into a first-class Thor channel: a private camera-and-voice page streams frames and speech transcripts into the gateway, and the full agent answers out loud and can act with any tool. Disclosure — the plugin runs a local HTTP/WebSocket server (default 127.0.0.1:8788, token-gated) that serves the phone page and receives camera frames, speech transcripts and recorded voice clips; it stores the pairing token (0600) and the newest 50 received frames and voice clips in the plugin data directory; frames reach the configured model provider the same way any photo attachment does, and voice clips go through Thor' configured speech-to-text like any voice note; it opens no outbound connections of its own and sends no telemetry; the page must be served over HTTPS (Tailscale Serve or another proxy) for browser camera and microphone access.

name: thor-boot-screen
description: Six-act boot animation for the Thor desktop app — black-screen brand reveal, over-exposed whiteout bridge, a technical-dossier plate, an authorization handshake with identity confirmation, and a welcome finale — with audio cues, theme-aware light/dark plates and Esc/Enter/Space controls. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Fully English UI. Adapted from 6shenhonghong9/dsh-startup-screen (MIT). Disclosure — on every Desktop launch (default: once per session) it covers the whole window with a full-screen animation that plays audio and spoken narration and waits for Enter/Space/click on two steps (Esc skips); while it is up it captures Enter/Space/Esc at the document level. Turn it off or switch to daily in its Startup Animation settings page.

name: thor-borealis
description: A Thor Desktop theme with a live dithered landscape behind the window: aurora curtains over mountain ridges and a mirroring lake by night, a two-ink pink and teal dawn by day. Install once, then switch with /skin borealis. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers one theme through the plugin SDK, and its stylesheet restyles parts of Desktop's own UI (tabs, composer, sidebar edge, wordmark colour) and clears the window's field backgrounds only while the theme is active, and the scene fades back behind text. While active it also adds one canvas behind the app and draws the scene on it with WebGL, watches the root element's theme, mode and accent attributes to show, recolour or remove that canvas, and reads the pointer's horizontal position to slide the ridges. No images or fonts; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks. The repo also ships borealis-cli, a still terminal skin for the CLI and TUI, installed separately by copying one YAML file into ~/.thor/skins/.

name: thor-bot-hq
description: Desktop fleet page plus a per-bot Home (status, metrics, alerts, tasks, routines, buttons) published by the bot as JSON. Disclosure — reads each local profile's home files, can run a declared cron routine from the UI on that bot's profile and credentials, and opens chat, a path, or a URL the bot declared; send_prompt buttons send the shown prompt into the bot's Bot Chat. Bot-declared run_action buttons run a script from the bot's home/actions/ folder: a script runs only after the user approves that exact file (SHA-256), is re-approved if it changes, and is limited to 30s and to that folder, but it runs as your user with the Thor backend's full environment, including provider keys loaded for the profile Thor was launched with. Approvals are kept under the Thor root in bot-hq/approvals/. The `thor thor-bot-hq setup` command (asks first unless --yes) links the plugin into every profile's plugins folder and enables it there. No database, signup, or telemetry.

name: thor-browser-extension
description: Connects Thor to the separately installed Thor Browser Extension for user-shared page context, opt-in control of explicitly attached browser tabs, and opt-in background task tabs that a local gateway chat opens in its own Chrome tab group. Full browser control requires Chromium; Firefox supports chat, page context and restricted control. Serves authenticated routes on the Thor API server and stores bounded redacted receipts and screenshots in profile-scoped plugin data. Disclosure — when Background task tabs is turned on in the extension, any chat of that Thor profile, including messaging-platform chats, can open, read and act on pages in background tabs of your signed-in Chrome; leave it off unless you want that.

name: thor-call-ledger
description: Per-call cost ledger for Thor Desktop: every model call Thor makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Thor' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through Thor's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from thor-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

name: thor-call-me
description: Thor phones its owner through CALL-E before a risky action, when it is stuck, or when it finishes: call_for_approval, call_for_help and call_report each place one real phone call, the owner says a PIN the plugin compares (an approval also needs a one-time code read on the call and repeated back), and a wrong PIN, wrong code, no answer, busy, silence, an unclear reply or a timeout is never approval; an optional pre_tool_call guard blocks deploy/delete/payment-style tools until a single-use approval is on file. Disclosure — Each call_for_approval, call_for_help or call_report places a real phone call billed to your own CALL-E account, and the model decides when to call, within a one-at-a-time limit and a daily cap of 8 by default. The action summary, issue or report text the model writes, your phone number, a one-time code and the call task go to api.heycall-e.com, which handles the call audio and transcript. Call records and transcripts, with spoken digits redacted, are stored in the plugin's data folder. A tool call can block for up to 180 seconds by default (600 max) waiting for you to answer.

name: thor-canvas
description: Your agent's plan, wired to its real work. The agent draws its plan as hand-drawn boxes in a Desktop pane next to the chat. Each box is bound to files and a check command: hooks mark a box doing when the agent writes one of its files, and done or failed when its check command exits. The user steers the running build on the canvas: answer a question box, link boxes, leave a note (it reaches the subagent that builds the box), remove a box (its next write is blocked), add a drift write to the plan, replay every revision. Disclosure — hooks read tool arguments and results (file paths, terminal commands and their output); canvas documents, revisions and user edits are stored in this profile's plugin database; pre_tool_call blocks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls that would write files of a box the user removed, and nothing else; canvas edits and a short plan summary are added to the model input (pre_llm_call, transform_tool_result); pre_verify keeps the agent working while one of its boxes is failing, capped by agent.max_verify_nudges; the inspector diff runs read-only git (rev-parse, cat-file) in the canvas project folder and reads the files a box wrote there, up to 512 KB each; serves /api/plugins/thor-canvas/ on the plugin host; never writes project files; no network calls, no credentials, no background processes, no self-update.

name: thor-chan
description: A chibi desktop companion who walks around your screen, reacts to Thor, and does its computer-use clicks and typing. Disclosure — on first run builds its Rust overlay from source with cargo (downloads the crates pinned in Cargo.lock from crates.io, several minutes; needs a Rust toolchain) and then runs it as a long-lived always-on-top desktop window that Thor restarts on crash; the build and the overlay get a minimal environment without your API keys; with computer_use.backend: thor-chan it performs real mouse clicks and keyboard input through the core computer_use tool; its mischief setting (on by default) visually glitches and, after 20 s of user inactivity, moves or shakes the active app window; optional heartbeat/watch modes (off by default) send the active window title and a screenshot to your current model; its chat bubble injects your typed messages into the local chat only after you allow plugin injection; the desktop-tidy tools move files on your Desktop into a "Thor-chan Tidy" folder after you approve each run and each undo in Thor's approval prompt (journaled, undoable); no network calls besides the cargo build, no credentials read.

name: thor-chat-share
description: Share Thor Desktop conversations as long PNG screenshots, self-contained HTML, Markdown, JSON, or PDF — per-turn selection with gutter drag range-select, search, collapsing and share-scope control; light/dark theme override with syntax-highlighted code; remembered export preferences; session info (model, thinking level, cache hit, tok/s, Thor version) in every export header and footer. The Thor Desktop counterpart of dsh-share. Disclosure — makes no network calls; reads the conversation you share through the gateway's session.history / session.usage RPCs and the session.info gateway event, plus the session list for titles; writes to the clipboard or downloads a file only when you trigger an export. HTML exports keep the conversation's image and link URLs, which load when the file is opened.

name: thor-chronos
description: Time-travel filesystem checkpoints, approval-gated rollback, and a scrubbable Desktop timeline for Thor Agent. Disclosure — Snapshots the whole working directory, untracked files such as `.env` included, into a shadow git repo at `<workspace>/.thor/chronos/` before each file-editing or shell tool call. Rollback overwrites workspace files and by default deletes untracked files missing from the snapshot. The model's rollback asks for approval first, but `/chronos`, the dashboard API and the Desktop pane restore without a prompt.

name: thor-cloud-file-manager
description: Your agent's server files, as easy as local: drag in whole folders, preview, and review every edit before Save, in Thor Desktop. Browse, search and sort by date, see which files are new or updated since you opened a folder, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, preview its images, PDFs and code files, download a file, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you press Save in the review, which shows the line diff for files up to 20,000 lines), drag files into the chat or add them with Add to chat (also right after an upload), draft a rename, move or delete request to the agent in the chat box with Ask agent (you check it and send it yourself), import files from the agent's own Google Drive, hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading, and open, preview, download or add to chat a file the agent hands you as a card in its reply. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Ships one plugin skill, thor-cloud-file-manager:cloud-file-manager-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders: the configured roots, else terminal.cwd, TERMINAL_CWD or MESSAGING_CWD, else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists, sorts and searches those folders, reads the files you open or preview (Markdown and .txt files up to 1 MiB in the editor; the first 1 MiB of other code and text files; images and PDFs up to 10 MiB), creates folders, and writes uploads, Drive imports and editor saves (staged as hidden .cfm-* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It has no delete action: it removes only its own .cfm-* staging files and folders (aborted ones, and stale ones over a day old) and, when an upload or import fails to publish, the empty file it had reserved for it. It never follows links out of those folders, and its file API never exposes the agent's Thor home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Download, drag and Add to chat use Thor Desktop's own authenticated file download and @file/@folder references; the plugin adds no route for them. Ask agent only types a drafted request with @file/@folder references into the chat box; it never sends it, and the plugin itself still has no rename, move or delete action. Desktop listens for the agent's tool-completion events to refresh the open folder, and its Desktop windows pass each such event's type and agent to one another in the app (a BroadcastChannel; nothing leaves the machine). In Desktop chats only, it adds a short section to the agent's instructions that names the shown folders (at most ten, as configured) and explains the ::cloud-file{path=...} card; it carries no file names or contents. A card's path goes only to a read-only lookup route under the same folder and Thor-home guards as a listing; a path outside the shown folders is refused. Each write names the folder it started in, and the gateway refuses it if Settings have since changed which folder that is. Apart from Desktop's calls to the gateway and the report skill's GitHub requests, its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's Thor home, else the copy bundled with Thor) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys, buffering their output in the gateway's temp directory. The plugin never reads the Google token itself, but those scripts (setup.py --check for the sign-in check, google_api.py drive for listing and download) refresh the agent's saved Google token (google_token.json in its Thor home) when it has expired, as they do when the agent runs them. While Desktop is open it re-checks the plugin and Drive sign-in about once a minute. The report skill runs thor --version, thor plugins list and thor logs (filtered to this plugin), may save its search words, title and draft as local files, and searches electricsheephq/thor-cloud-file-manager issues with gh or a web tool before drafting; it posts a public issue or comment there only after the user approves the exact title and text.

name: thor-cobrowse
description: Real-time multi-window spatial co-browsing canvas and interactive human-in-the-loop web automation for Thor Agent via a localhost web studio with CDP screencasting, 8-way window resizing, Inspector telemetry, and 2FA handoff. Disclosure — launches headless Chromium with a minimal sanitized env and runs a token-authenticated localhost server on 127.0.0.1:9876+ with Host/Origin checks; blocks local files and private/link-local IPs by default across redirects, redacts password/OTP values in DOM state, executes agent-supplied JS via cobrowse_eval_js, reads no local credentials, and sends no external telemetry.

name: thor-codex-resets
description: Know the moment OpenAI resets your Codex usage limits. A status-bar chip counts the time since the last reset; when a new one lands, a small card rises out of it (chip-only while you type), with a history page of every reset. Disclosure — polls the public codex-resets.com API every 60 s and loads fonts from Google Fonts; sends nothing about you or your sessions.

name: thor-colab
description: Run Python scripts and Jupyter notebooks on Google Colab GPUs (T4 free tier, L4, A100, H100, TPU) from chat: Thor assigns the runtime, uploads the code, keeps it alive, streams progress and GPU use, syncs outputs and checkpoints home while the job runs, resumes on a fresh runtime from the last checkpoint when Colab reclaims one, and reports back to the chat that started it; a Desktop page shows live runs with cancel and resume. Disclosure — needs the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app, Colaboratory scope) signed in with thor auth add thor-colab:google; Thor attaches the token to colab.research.google.com only. Uploads the run's files (hidden files and folders, symlinks, hard links, virtualenvs and common credential files excluded; the home directory, THOR_HOME and credential folders are refused as code or output folders) to the user's Colab runtime and executes them there with a small stdlib runner that pip-installs the run's requirements; runtimes consume the account's Colab compute units and are released when a run ends; a daemon thread supervises active runs (one per profile, lease-protected; with no active run it only reads the run store every 30 s); run records live in the profile's plugin data directory; a pre_llm_call hook adds a finished run's one-line summary to the starting chat's next turn.

name: thor-committee
description: A committee of AI models for hard decisions. You set the seats (each with its own role and model) and a chairman; the seats answer independently, rank each other's answers blind, debate the points they disagree on, and the chairman writes a decision with confidence, dissent, role-fit notes and next actions with owners. Evidence files (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, text, photos) go to every model as cited [E1] passages; optional Research first searches the web once through Thor's own web tools and adds checked [W1] passages before the seats start. Time and budget limits with a mid-run ask to extend, follow-up runs, saved committees, a live Desktop page (Brief, Convene, Decision) and a Markdown + PDF report. Disclosure — one run makes several calls through ctx.llm to each seat's and the chairman's model on your existing Thor providers (typically 2-4 per seat plus 1-3 for the chairman; an estimate and a budget cap are shown before it starts; clerical steps ask for low reasoning, answers and the verdict for medium); with Research first on, the question (never file contents) goes to the web search provider set up in Thor and up to 6 pages are read through web_extract; evidence files the user picks or names in chat are read and their text is sent to every participating model (paths named in chat inside the Thor folder or matching known credential files are refused); runs, reports and evidence copies are kept under the plugin's data directory; the Desktop page's Convene button starts a new Thor chat in the background to run the committee; a run uses worker threads inside Thor and no background process outlives it; pricing reads Thor internal pricing tables; no credentials read or stored; no telemetry.

name: thor-consult
description: Website voice consultations with an embedded server and bilingual Desktop settings. Disclosure — starts a local Node consultation server on 127.0.0.1 that you publish through your own HTTPS reverse proxy, so website visitors can send questions that are answered by your active Thor model (one tool-less ctx.llm call per question, using your provider credits); stores business data, inquiries and usage in <THOR_HOME>/consult/; voice sends audio to OpenAI, and the optional subscription voice lane launches your installed Codex CLI (its own login) or the Thor Live module from the same profile; optional Turnstile contacts Cloudflare.

name: thor-context-overview
description: Context window usage at a glance: a Context button in the status bar shows tokens used vs. budget, percent full, free space and an estimated breakdown by category, plus context-file sources. Works during a running turn. Read-only token/usage monitor, no backend.

name: thor-continuity-capture
description: Records Thor lifecycle events (session, subagent, and kanban task) as Continuity schema-v2 events in a local SQLite spool under the plugin data directory, and can forward them to a NATS/JetStream server you run yourself. Disclosure - binds nine lifecycle hooks and writes SQLite (spool_path defaults to spool.db in the plugin data directory, 90-day retention, periodic sweep; the file grows with event volume); free-text fields (prompts, tool results, args, summary, reason, tool_call_history) are always dropped before the INSERT and only their length is kept (there is no setting that keeps them). The optional NATS password is read from the environment variable THOR_CONTINUITY_CAPTURE_NATS_PASSWORD, never from config.yaml. Delivery is opt-in: the default publish_mode is spool-only (nothing leaves the host); in core/jetstream mode a background thread publishes to your own NATS endpoint using the bundled standard-library client, and failed deliveries stay as error rows and are retried. Only the NATS server itself is external - it is not part of this plugin. Inactive until an operator enables it. Disclosure — binds nine lifecycle hooks and writes a SQLite spool (default spool.db in the plugin data directory, 90-day retention sweep) holding event type, profile/agent id, host FQDN, process id and start time, session/subagent/task ids and tool names; prompts, tool args/results, summaries, reasons and tool_call_history are always dropped before writing and only their lengths kept. Default publish_mode is spool-only (nothing leaves the host); in the opt-in core/jetstream modes a background thread sends those events to the NATS server you configure in nats_url (default 127.0.0.1) using the bundled standard-library client, and unless nats_tls is on or the URL uses tls:// (TLS is off by default) the NATS user and password travel in plaintext.

name: thor-continuum
description: An integrated nine-system plugin for Thor Agent that provides task continuity, review-first episodic memory, environment reality checks, evidence tracking, goal integrity, trust-aware tool policies, impact previews, retry-loop protection, and verified workflow distillation. Its systems share an append-only SQLite Event Spine and a Continuum Console for Thor Desktop. Includes 12 tools, 11 lifecycle hooks, checkpoint export, and a review-first approach to generated artifacts. Live verification and test coverage are documented in the repository; not every capability has been verified in a live host workflow. Disclosure — Records every tool call, approval prompt/response and session event (with redacted argument previews) in a local plugin database; its pre_tool_call policy can block tool calls or escalate them to Thor' approval prompt, labels web/browser results as untrusted, injects recalled memory facts (including unreviewed candidates) and an auto-built task charter into each turn, and its model-callable continuum_forge tool can register new plugin skills and automation blueprints distilled from session traces when called with confirm: true.

name: thor-council
description: LLM Council (karpathy/llm-council) as a Thor plugin. Four fixed advisor seats (First-Principles Analyst, Skeptic, Pragmatist, Researcher) answer in parallel, anonymously review and rank each other, and a Chairman model synthesizes the final answer. Members borrow your existing provider credentials - no API keys. Registers a Council group in every model menu, a council_deliberate tool, /council, thor council CLI, and a desktop panel. Disclosure — council_deliberate and the Council model fan each prompt (as a session model, the whole conversation) out to every seat, judge and chairman model you assign, up to 2N+1 billed calls per turn on your existing provider credentials; it also adds a non-secret "council" marker row to auth.json and keeps run history in $THOR_HOME/council/runs/.

name: thor-creator-forge
description: Four Thor skills for authoring and reviewing skills, workspace operations, and host-provided Python execution.

name: thor-crm
description: ThorCRM is a working CRM for Thor Desktop. Manage contacts, companies, deals, events and follow-ups in the same workspace your Thor agent uses. Build reports and dashboards with drill-down charts, and tailor the CRM with custom fields and deal stages. Ask Thor to schedule one-time task reminders, CRM analysis or public research you approve. Scheduled jobs run unattended and deliver results locally. They use CRM tools and, for public research, Thor web and search tools. They can’t schedule additional jobs. If you choose PostgreSQL, CRM records are stored in the database you configure. Disclosure — on your request the agent creates one-shot Thor cron jobs (task follow-ups, internal CRM analysis assignments, and scheduled research runs that use Thor' web/search tools on a public question you approve); jobs run unattended with CRM-only plus those tools, deliver locally, and cannot schedule further jobs. Optional PostgreSQL storage sends CRM records to the database URL you configure.

name: thor-cron
description: Operating skill for Thor cron: lifecycle rules (pause vs disable vs remove, `in 30m` vs `30m`), four ways to avoid needless LLM runs (no_agent, wakeAgent pre-check, monitor, [SILENT]), verify-after-change, a layered runbook and a read-only doctor that complements `thor cron doctor` and reports one error across several jobs as one scheduler fault and a cron store that cannot be written. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — skill only, no network; the bundled doctor reads ~/.thor/cron/jobs.json, ticker stamps and executions.db (or a named profile's store with --profile) read-only, checks the cron directory's permissions and free space without writing, and runs the local thor cron doctor (argument list, no shell), whose job loader may repair malformed jobs.json entries (--no-builtin skips it).

name: thor-crux
description: Explore explicit assumptions, exact affine decision thresholds, hard-constraint conflicts, and a live visual atlas.

name: thor-custodian
description: Local, read-only security-posture monitor for the machine a Thor agent runs on (Linux, macOS, native Windows): scoped file and permission baselines, evidence-backed findings and a change history, a first-run terminal setup, an optional background monitor and an on-demand authenticated loopback dashboard. Registers four read-only tools (warden_status, warden_findings, warden_changes, warden_scan). Disclosure — reads: regular files and metadata under paths the user approves in setup; Thor profile config metadata (model, provider, plugin and MCP-server names) only after explicit consent; credential files (.env, auth stores, keys), memory, chat history and SOUL are never opened (metadata only) and only .py/.md files are content-hashed; symlinks and reparse points are not followed. Runs: a foreground or per-user background monitor (systemd user service, LaunchAgent or Task Scheduler task) only when the user starts or installs it; fixed argument-array subprocesses with timeouts, explicit command-specific minimal environments and no shell (systemctl and apt list --upgradable; launchctl and softwareupdate -l; schtasks and a fixed PowerShell Windows Update query); update detection installs nothing; a Linux-only root security-update plan/apply is a separate terminal command with typed confirmation that the AI tools and dashboard cannot reach. Network: no telemetry and no model calls; the dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 only behind a username/password session (scrypt, signed cookie, exact Host and Origin checks); native OS update queries may contact the OS vendor's update service. Stores: paths, fingerprints, findings and the hashed dashboard login in a private per-user state directory; never credential contents. No self-updater, no approval or confirmation arguments for the AI, no root shell. Not an antivirus or EDR: same-user software can change its configuration. Native tests pass on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11-3.14 at the pinned commit.

name: thor-design-studio
description: Non-destructive shader image editing inside Thor Desktop, manually or with an agent. Human-approved shader tools, recipes, numerical previews and PNG export.

name: thor-desktop-camera
description: A camera button for the Thor Desktop composer. Open the preview, take a photo, and the frame lands in the composer as an image attachment, ready to send.

name: thor-detox
description: Tool output firewall. Saves redacted tool output locally (unencrypted; redaction is pattern-based and can miss secrets; no network), gives the model a compact report, and retrieves exact lines on demand.

name: thor-discord-rpc
description: Native Discord Rich Presence (RPC) integration for Thor Agent — real-time session, model, token, and tool tracking with local-only IPC. Disclosure — publishes your most recent session title (or, in full title mode, the workspace folder name), model name and token total to the local Discord client as Rich Presence every 3 s (visible to other Discord users); opt-in settings also publish the git branch and a "View Repository" button with the public github.com/gitlab.com remote URL (credentials, ports and other hosts stripped); reads ~/.thor/state.db read-only; reads the active workspace's .git/HEAD and .git/config read-only to resolve repository and branch; on Linux may scan running Discord processes' environment via psutil to find XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; writes a small presence-ownership file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or the system temp dir) and, under herdr, queries the local HERDR_SOCKET_PATH socket for pane focus.

name: thor-dpapi-secrets
description: Resolve Thor environment variables at startup from a single secret file encrypted with the Windows Data Protection API, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.dpapi.map, an ENV_VAR -> store-name mapping (bare names or dpapi:// names) plus an optional file path (default <THOR_HOME>/secrets.dpapi). The file is one DPAPI blob keyed by the current Windows user profile, so it is unreadable by another Windows account and worthless off the machine; it is written by the bundled CLI (python -m thor_dpapi_secrets set NAME, value read from a prompt or stdin, never from argv) and only read at runtime. Mapped names that are missing or empty are skipped with a warning; a file that is not ours, a blob this user cannot decrypt, or a payload that is not a flat string map is reported as an error with nothing injected. Disclosure - this source decrypts a file for every Thor process that enables it: resolved values become environment variables of the Thor process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. User-scope encryption only (the machine-wide flag is never used and is not exposed), and the at-rest protection is a bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles, not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no subprocesses, no network calls, no self-update. Windows only. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — decrypts a DPAPI-encrypted secret file (default <THOR_HOME>/secrets.dpapi) at startup for every Thor process that enables it, and the resolved values become environment variables of Thor and its child processes like `.env` entries; the encryption is per Windows user and protects backups, cloud sync and copied files, not against other code running as the same user. Local only: no network calls, no subprocesses.

name: thor-drawbridge
description: Give your remote Thor agent limited access to folders on your device. Disclosure — the Desktop component sends the contents and names of files in the folder you share (up to the configured read limit) to the Thor backend serving that chat, so they reach chat history and the model provider; with Create/Update enabled the agent can propose whole-file writes that Desktop applies after you approve the diff in the chat, and "Allow this session" lets later edits in that share apply without a further prompt until the share ends; no deletes, no network calls beyond your own Thor connection.

name: thor-dreaming
description: Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Secrets and instructions are screened by the dream's own rules plus a verbatim copy of the holographic plugin's screen (scripts/holo_screen.py, MIT, same maintainer), applied to stored facts and human messages before anything reaches memory, the report or the model. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — by default the scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro; with holographic >= 0.15.0 including its fact_versions/fact_confirmations tables, to say who stands behind a fact); they also read Thor config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror_memory_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote_from). An optional cloud judge (judge in dreaming.json, off by default; off, its code is not even loaded) may, once the owner enables it, send for each mention the rules counted the fact's text and that person's own words (no reply quote, link, id, sender or time; names inside the text may be included; screened for secrets and instructions first), only from the chats, sources and chat stores the owner lists, over HTTPS to the providers the owner lists, in the owner's order: OpenRouter's Decisions API (model typesafe/jev-1.14, Jev by TypeSafe; the data reaches OpenRouter and TypeSafe) and/or OpenAI's Decisions API (model gpt-6-luna); when the first gives no usable answer the same pair may reach the next. A verdict can only remove a counted mention — from promotion, confirmation, fact decay, "said again" after a rejection, the selection of new facts and conflicts, and evidence. Keys OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY are read from the environment or, since Thor withholds these provider keys from cron scripts, straight from their own line in $THOR_HOME/.env; the judge's calls are billed to those keys. It keeps a 90-day verdict cache and a 90-day local journal of the pairs sent in $THOR_HOME/cache (the journal is deleted on nights the judge is off); the nightly spending cap ($0.05 by default) is soft; data already sent cannot be recalled and falls under the providers' retention terms. The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $THOR_HOME/scripts, seeds $THOR_HOME/dreaming.json and, through Thor' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files, judge files and diary without them, deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text) and deletes the set-aside copies of its own broken state files; with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $THOR_HOME/cache and a diary to $THOR_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact_store (with holographic >= 0.15.0 marked said or inferred; with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact_store update. Since 3.4.0, with holographic >=0.19.0 and profile scope, it also reads fact_merges and current version ids to propose disjoint duplicate pairs. It saves immutable proposal numbers, both full texts, version ids, origins, keywords and the provider database path in cache/dream-proposals.json; open proposals expire after 180 days and closed ones are removed after 30 days. Full pair texts are included in the agent report and therefore reach the configured agent model. Old facts are merged by fact_store only after the adult memory owner approves the exact proposal; the response checks the database and uses expect to refuse changed versions. Scheduled extraction may merge only a newly added paraphrase from its own session into an existing fact, never old facts from other sessions. The scripts themselves still open the fact store read-only. The sweep also cleans the state of merged copies and archives their hashes so a later forget can remove older untagged diary copies; merging itself does not erase the diary. No new credentials, network providers or tools are introduced. Version 3.4.2 clarifies that forget cleans the store and the skill's own files; Git history, external database dumps, system backups and Thor session history require separate cleanup. Reports distinguish a successful store deletion from a retained external copy and do not promise that retrying removes a documented history boundary. Version 3.5.0 adds explicit cron maintenance: known stock prompts are synchronized while custom prompts are preserved; --update-existing applies only explicitly supplied settings and --job-id scopes the entire operation. cron.expected_roles controls desired creation without pausing existing jobs. --upgrade validates the request before copying gate scripts and updating cron through public APIs, then checks the result. Checks expose paused jobs, execution modes, missing roles and duplicates; no automatic activation or job deletion. --inherit-model explicitly clears both model and provider pins. The public cron update API has no CAS; avoid concurrent configuration edits during installation. Version 3.6.0 adds opt-in read-only task-outcome summaries and recorded memory-attempt explanations from holographic >=0.20.0 (experience_schema=1). It reads bounded attempt/version references and agent-reported outcomes; usefulness does not change truth, trust, ranking or MEMORY.md. It makes no new model or network calls and keeps no second correction-text cache. Explicit --memory-store must be in chat_stores.promote_from; stores are never joined. task_outcomes: true adds only summary counts to the ordinary nightly result and creates no extra wakeup. Missing capability is reported as unsupported, not as a successful empty journal. Human corrections reported by the agent are not authenticated human confirmation. Version 3.6.1 reuses parsed numbers within a bounded in-memory nightly cache, reducing repeated work without changing contradiction rules. Version 3.6.2 copies the cron gate scripts atomically (an interrupted install keeps the previous gate) and names any cron job the installer refuses to change with the fix. Version 3.7.0 keeps the whole-store duplicate search within its nightly budget on large stores (it also narrows candidates by the numbers and names the pair rule requires; the rule still decides every pair) and names the store in task-outcome summaries. Version 3.7.1 derives each message's data once per nightly pass, with memory bounded by corroboration.memory_mb (default 256 MB; above it data is rebuilt on demand, never changing decisions). Version 3.7.2 makes the quarantine screen about 40× faster on long messages with byte-identical decisions (re-vendored holographic screen 0.22.1). Version 3.7.3 fixes an install-time scanner false positive in that screen's start list (3.7.2 was refused by thor plugins install) and runs thor plugins validate in CI. Version 3.7.4 changes no behaviour: the vendored holographic screen is copied whole and checked before it is written. Version 3.8.0 no longer promotes an agent's conclusion nobody confirmed (holographic origin inferred) to MEMORY.md by any corroboration route; people repeating it offer it for confirmation instead, and stores without origins are promoted as before; --explain says why, and --memory-explain keeps the provider's count of candidates that changed before the record. Version 3.8.4 keeps, for each memory entry, hashed word stems and numbers plus a 60-character preview (none for an entry with a secret) in the loss-guard snapshot in $THOR_HOME/cache, so an entry the agent compressed, reworded or merged is no longer reported as lost; the alert names lost entries by that preview. Version 3.8.5 has the nightly agent change memory entries with the memory tool's patch (Thor 0.22 removed replace; replace remains only as the fallback for Thor 0.21), counts a patch staged in the pending/memory approval queue as waiting, and compares a lost entry only with entries the night wrote (also across a split, with numbers compared as numbers); for an entry of fewer than two word stems the snapshot also keeps hashed stems of its short words or, for one with no words and no secret, hashed character trigrams; state files with a UTF-8 BOM are read. Version 3.8.6: install.py --check counts a judge key only from its own line in $THOR_HOME/.env, the one a cron script can read, and names DREAM_* variables set only in the terminal it runs in, compared with their lines in that .env (a DREAM_* value may be printed, a key never is); it and a new read-only dream.py --nightly-status read the dreaming jobs' next_run_at in cron/jobs.json to say when Thor will not fire them (a gateway that is down, a job paused or with no next run). The nightly prompt never patches through another entry's whole text and keeps an absorbed entry when a merge fails; the loss-guard snapshot also keeps hashed full dates and each entry's hashed head key. No new credentials, network calls, tools or writes.

name: thor-droid
description: Turn physical Android devices into automated hardware testbeds and QA companion nodes for Thor Agent — wireless MQTT APK deployments, Logcat crash diagnostics, and screen captures. Disclosure — gives the agent control of a paired Android phone: it can run device shell commands, send SMS, place calls, reply to notifications, install APKs and toggle radios (each behind a Thor approval prompt and refused in cron runs), and without a prompt it can read SMS, contacts, notifications, recent photos, location, take camera/screen captures and pull device logs. Commands travel over the MQTT broker you configure (loopback by default; TLS and credentials required for remote brokers), and the companion app trusts any client that can publish to its command topic on that broker.

name: thor-egm
description: Fresh-context, tool-free design reviews with checked source evidence and EGM workflow skills.

name: thor-ego
description: Thor Ego reads and saves pages in the user's ego(lite) browser through a loopback MCP relay (Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8767/mcp). The Mac daemon and the relay are installed separately, the same split as local-mcp; this package does not start, embed, or update them. Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Derived from thor-tabs (relay code); talks only to a separately installed loopback MCP relay at http://127.0.0.1:8767/mcp with bearer EGO_RELAY_TOKEN from the Thor profile (a remote Thor host needs an SSH local forward); a long-running relay and a Mac daemon, installed separately, run the ego CLI against the user's logged-in ego(lite) browser, so pages that session can open are readable; ego_save_page_markdown writes markdown under the relay's configured save root (for example an Obsidian vault) and downloads third-party page images, some in a background pass after the tool returns; the server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every relay tool, reads included, and refuses them in unattended runs. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: thor-entity54
description: Role-based authorization for Thor Agent: OWNER, ADMIN, USER, GUEST roles, default-deny, per-tool and per-bot scoping, tamper-evident receipts, governed Linear issue creation, and versioned policy sync. Disclosure — a local Node MCP server whose principal is one static identity per profile (OWNER by default), so everyone who can talk to that profile acts as that principal; its roles govern only its own eight tools, not Thor tools. `entity54_linear_create_issue` creates issues on api.linear.app with your LINEAR_API_KEY without a Thor approval prompt; it needs a one-time `npm ci --omit=dev` in the installed `server/` directory and a manual `node scripts/setup.mjs` run that writes the signing keys to a local env file you copy into the profile `.env`.

name: thor-experientiallabs
description: Experiential Labs - OpenAI-compatible multi-model gateway provider (chat, /model picker, aux and curated fallback models, /usage wallet snapshot). All network calls go to api.experientiallabs.ai - /v1 chat + models via Thor' own transport, /api/v1/credits and /api/v1/key only when /usage runs; no telemetry; credentials resolve through Thor routes (thor auth / .env). Disclosure — When you pick Experiential Labs as your model, every prompt, tool result and attachment of that session goes to api.experientiallabs.ai, a third-party gateway that routes to upstream model vendors. /usage sends your key to its Cost API (GET /credits and /key) or to the cost_api_base you set. Independent integration, not affiliated with Experiential Labs.

name: thor-eye-memory
description: Local visual memory for Thor: index a photo library, search by meaning, build albums, cull duplicates, extract receipts, and recall what the camera saw.

name: thor-fal-video
description: Video edit, video extend and reference-to-video on FAL (MiniMax H3, FLUX 3, Kling 4.0, Wan 3.0, Seedance 2.5, Gemini Omni Flash and more), with a skill that chains them. Disclosure — sends prompts and media to FAL as paid jobs billed to FAL_KEY, with no per-call approval; a local path the model passes is uploaded to FAL storage (which returns a hosted URL) when the resolved file has a video or image extension and is under the size cap (200 MB by default), from anywhere the user can read; http(s) URLs are handed to FAL to fetch.

name: thor-federated-search
description: Federated web search backend (provider name `federated`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key `ranker`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (`type` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (`reasoning_effort=off`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.thor-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).

name: thor-field-notes
description: Field notes for a Thor install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each thor update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Thor core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.thor/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.thor/field-notes), ~/.thor/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.thor/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.thor/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py (it reads ~/.thor/installs/*/facts.json to find Thor' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.thor/.env), else local.

name: thor-finance
description: Personal-finance tools over your own local thor-finance database: spending, budgets, transactions, net worth, bills, loans, investments, cash flow, goals and categorization rules (read-only), a bank sync on request, and four writes (file a transaction, add a rule, set a budget cap, track a bill) that each wait for your approval and are blocked under cron and other unattended runs. Needs a separate trusted app checkout prepared with Python 3.12 and `uv sync`, set as THOR_FINANCE_APP_DIR. Disclosure — reads open the separate thor-finance app's SQLite database outside the plugin directory, and the plugin imports that app checkout's code into the Thor process, so it runs whatever that checkout contains, not the catalog pin. `finance_sync` runs the app's sync, which calls Plaid with your optional Plaid keys and fetches security logos from financialmodelingprep.com (ticker symbols leave the machine). `thor finance completion`, started by the app's Ask panel, sends that conversation and your finance results to your profile's own model. The opt-in report jobs (`thor finance crons plan/apply`) write profile-owned entry scripts and run the app on a schedule. They call Plaid and, with a live read-only key, Alpaca (GET-only); they look up car and home values through NHTSA, Wikimedia/OpenStreetMap and, only if you switch them on, Carfax (in the local Chrome at 127.0.0.1:9222) and Redfin. The daily job's agent applies transaction categorizations through the app's own CLI without a per-change approval card. The four approval-gated writes stay blocked in cron. Nothing moves money or places trades. The optional Plaid and Alpaca keys are read through Thor's secret scope only; the plugin opens no key file. Installing starts no server, sync or job. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies in Thor.

name: thor-fleet-connector
description: Owner-approved universal phone pairing and bundled read-only Live Operations reporting for selected Thor profiles. Disclosure — paired phones get broad fleet:operator access over the internet, including cron jobs (unattended runs), Kanban task dispatch and media reads, and see live session titles/previews and subagent goals from the profiles you select for reporting; any messaging account you make an owner (with a one-time claim code from `thor fleet claim`) can create pairing links and approve phones from a private chat, so that account's security is your host's security. Runs an explicitly activated background connector/reverse proxy behind your HTTPS origin and may launch a local Thor backend; legacy QR flow opens a private local browser. Keeps an owner-only control socket in the system temp directory, plus pairing/owner state and shared local snapshots; reads selected profiles' session registries through private read-only imports. `thor fleet reporting configure --apply` edits the selected profiles' config.yaml (with a backup). Local idle/retirement maintenance is explicit and not exposed to phones. Reporting adds no control power.

name: thor-flow
description: Reconstruct Thor agent sessions as local graphs and compare them with trusted paths. Disclosure — reads the profile's state.db read-only and writes reports only where you point it; the optional bundled customer_review example, when you run it yourself, installs and enables a demo plugin and demo skills in your active profile, raises delegation.max_spawn_depth to 2 if it is lower, and makes openai-codex model calls with that profile's existing sign-in.

name: thor-gatekeeper
description: Gatekeeper enforces rules the owner configures; not legal advice and not a compliance guarantee. A deterministic pre_tool_call gate for recognized outbound sends: literal `thor send` and `imsg send` terminal commands (including terminal calls made from execute_code), and a send_message call if one ever traverses the hook, are checked in full. Thor registers no model-callable send_message tool. Other tools whose names look like a send (connectors__*, mcp tools, plain names, and a cronjob_manage create/update/run with a delivery target) are not parsed: they only require owner approval, because consent, STOP and quiet hours cannot be checked for them. Browser and computer-use driving of an app and scripts that send through a subprocess are not inspected. Rules: absolute suppression, per-channel consent and recipient-local quiet hours (block), and native Thor approval requests for unanswered threads, minimum gaps and unapproved wording (the host auto-approves these under --yolo, approvals off and thor -z). Uses the public post_gateway_admission hook to record observed STOP keywords and DM replies (excludes control, approval, steering and slash-command traffic). Reads tool arguments, results and normalized inbound snapshots; writes only profile-local SQLite (owner-only permissions) with recipient/thread hashes, message SHA-256, decision metadata, consent source/date, timezone/region and owner template variables. No raw message-body log; hashes are not anonymity. No network, subprocess, model calls, telemetry, credential reads, external file scans or core patches. Invalid settings or storage errors block recognized sends. Disclosure — gates only the outbound sends it recognizes (literal `thor send` / `imsg send` terminal commands and send_message calls) and asks owner approval for other send-looking tools; a whole-message STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END or QUIT from any admitted gateway sender silently suppresses that sender and is consumed without reaching the agent or getting a reply; a storage or inbound-observation failure blocks every recognized send until the owner repairs records and reloads; writes only a profile-local SQLite ledger of hashes and decision metadata, with no network, subprocess or credential access.

name: thor-gauge
description: Context gauge — a live ring/dash showing how full your agent's context window is, per session and topic, with a desktop plugin and tools (gauge_check, gauge_report, gauge_set_window, gauge_render, gauge_action). Runs fully local: no API key, no telemetry. Disclosure — reads Thor' state.db (read-only) for session titles and scans the memories folders (including other profiles' when run from the default profile) for size metrics; `gauge_action` lets the agent queue `/compact` and `/new` in the current session when you answer a gauge alert; with `alerts.route` set to `home` or `custom:` it runs `thor send` to deliver alerts to that chat, and `/gauge audit` runs `thor doctor`.

name: thor-gemini-live
description: Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Thor. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — thor_task starts, thor_tasks reads the call's task board, and thor_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Thor needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the Thor home's .env; delegated work runs as a Thor run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.

name: thor-gensyn-delphi
description: Seven read-only tools. Disclosure — Seven read-only tools for Gensyn Delphi prediction markets; no funds move and nothing is signed or sent. Needs Node.js 20.18+ and a manual `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the plugin folder (installs the pinned @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk and its locked npm deps) before the tools work. Runs a local Node subprocess per call (25 s deadline, not a sandbox). Sends your DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY only to delphi-api.gensyn.ai (testnet) or api.delphi.fyi (mainnet); history and quotes read api.goldsky.com and gensyn-testnet/mainnet.g.alchemy.com without the key, and quotes use a throwaway in-memory key the SDK requires. Tools are on for every surface by default, including messaging gateways, where anyone admitted can run these reads on the owner's key (rate limit 30 requests per minute per process); disable per surface with `thor tools`.

name: thor-gensyn-ree
description: ree_validate_receipt, ree_verify_receipt, ree_infer. Validate does not re-execute and does not stand behind text_output, finish_reason, token_count, model.name, or ree_version. Verify re-executes on CPU. Infer runs one of three small models and writes one receipt. Disclosure — Starts containers from the local image gensynai/ree:v0.8.0 (pinned by digest) and never pulls it; running docker pull yourself is consent to the REE-Binary-License. ree_verify_receipt and ree_infer mount ~/.cache/gensyn and ~/.cache/huggingface read-write (a Hugging Face token file stored there is visible to the container; no token is passed in the environment), may download Hugging Face weights for any model a receipt names, and their container network is not limited to Hugging Face; they ask for Thor approval on every call and refuse under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended runs, host isolation, or when the approval API is missing. ree_validate_receipt runs with network none, does not ask, and returns no receipt text. Any person admitted to one of your gateways can call these tools and approve containers on your Docker daemon; disable per surface with thor tools. Choosing "always" adds one config.yaml allowlist line per call and never covers the next call. New receipts and temporary work files are written under ~/.cache/thor-ree; nothing is stored under THOR_HOME. The container is not a hostile-code sandbox. No cron is created.

name: thor-genui
description: Generative UI for Thor Desktop: the agent answers with interactive blocks drawn inside the chat reply (charts with hover cards, KPI cards, sortable tables, day-by-day plans, photo strips, calculators with sliders and live charts, forms, checklists that keep their ticks, and step-by-step explainers with flow diagrams, simulations and a 3D layer stack). The model sends data only (JSON blocks, never HTML, scripts or SVG); the plugin validates every block and draws it with its own components, in the app's theme. Telegram, the CLI and other chat apps get readable Markdown instead. Ships nine recipe skills (thor-genui:trip-planner, compare, explain and more). Disclosure — network calls only when the model uses a tool, carrying the model's search words or ticker: market prices from Yahoo Finance (query1.finance.yahoo.com); photos from the Wikimedia Commons and Openverse APIs, from Unsplash or Pexels only when the user adds that key, from Tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set (including one already set for Thor's own Tavily web search), from the user's configured web search, and from the head (at most 256 KB) of the top result pages; each photo host is contacted briefly to check the picture loads (https only, public addresses only, DNS pinned, redirects re-checked). Boards are saved as JSON under the profile's plugin-data/thor-genui/ folder; a recipe the user asks to save becomes a profile skill through Thor's own skill_manage (write approval applies); no telemetry and no account. Adds a short drawing rule to the system prompt and, in Desktop only, a one-line reminder next to messages that ask for something visual, steering answers to blocks instead of Thor's ::preview widgets.

name: thor-ghost-call
description: A real-time AI assistant on your own phone calls. You stay on the line; Thor listens and streams one-line hints to your page and chat (what they just offered, what to ask next), knows your private target without ever saying it, plays a hint in your earpiece on one tap, and posts a summary with what was agreed and a draft confirmation message when you hang up. Works with two browser links, a real phone line through your own Twilio account, or any call on speaker. Disclosure — streams live call audio of BOTH parties to OpenAI (realtime transcription at api.openai.com, plus hint, earpiece-TTS and summary models) and stores text transcripts (on by default; `store_transcripts: false` turns it off), hints and summaries in plugin data (SQLite); the other party is not told by the plugin that the call is transcribed, and call-recording consent law is the user's responsibility; runs a FastAPI bridge (`thor ghost serve`, 127.0.0.1:8766 by default) that you must expose publicly at PUBLIC_BASE_URL (e.g. a tunnel), protected by one-time link tokens and Twilio signature checks; Twilio mode places paid calls through your own Twilio account to numbers the model may choose, but only numbers on your THOR_GHOST_TEST_ALLOWLIST (empty = no dialing; THOR_GHOST_ALLOW_ALL=1 lifts it) and never emergency/premium numbers, without a Thor approval prompt; Thor speaks on the call only after you type `/ghost intervene allow`, and then first says it is an AI.

name: thor-github-mentions
description: Run approved GitHub mentions as Thor tasks and reply in the original thread. Polls GitHub's API in a gateway worker and sends signed local webhooks granting terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools. Optional Discord copies and read-only Thor session progress tracking. Disclosure — polls the GitHub notifications API every 60 s or more as the bot account, and when a GitHub user on your allowed_authors list @mentions the bot in any repository the bot can see, starts an unattended Thor agent turn with terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools on this computer through a signed local webhook route; the mention text and the repository content the agent reads are untrusted input, and the agent acts with the bot's classic `repo` token (the same GITHUB_TOKEN Thor' GitHub tools use). Thor' unattended approval mode (deny by default) still governs flagged commands. `thor github-mentions routes --apply` edits this profile's config.yaml (adds webhook routes, enables the webhook platform on 127.0.0.1). Optional progress notices read Thor' state.db read-only; optional Discord notices post through Thor' own Discord adapter.

name: thor-gruvbox
description: Six Gruvbox themes for the Thor Desktop app — dark and light, each in hard, medium and soft. Installing the pack writes its skins into <thor home>/skins/ and has desktop/plugin.js contribute the same six to the app's own theme picker, with their real labels and descriptions instead of the app's hard-coded "Thor skin". No commands, tools, hooks, middleware, credentials, network access or background work, nothing runs on a turn — it only writes its own skin files, never config.yaml, and it never overwrites a skin you edited or switches your active theme.

name: thor-guard
description: Defensive prompt-injection guard for Thor Agent: a pre_llm_call hook scans every inbound message locally (deterministic patterns, no model calls) for Unicode smuggling, hidden instructions, special tokens, and Base64-decoded payloads; a pre_tool_call hook blocks RCE/subshell patterns, sensitive credential paths, and call-ID races. High-confidence attacks are blocked; suspicious messages are quarantined for manual review via the guard_review tool (release is manual re-send by design). Includes a Predator pattern store (human-corrected signatures), a SHA-256 hash-chained ledger, secret redaction, a live Posture Score, a 28-vector simulation arena (21 message + 7 tool-arg), and a standalone Obsidian & Gold HUD. Python stdlib + SQLite only. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials read or stored, no data leaves the machine, no core overrides, no self-updater. Phase 3 verified live on Thor 0.21.5 (validate 13/13, doctor OK, plugins list enabled, live hook-fire test: attack blocked on both hooks, benign passed); v1.1.2 re-verified the same way (validate 13/13, live hook-fire test 19/19 through the real plugin dispatch, 168/168 tests).

name: thor-guardian
description: Deterministic allow/approve/block policies for Thor tool calls, with read-only Policy Lab regression simulation and operator-reviewed policy proposals. Exact tool-name rules, explicit protected local paths, a deliberately limited shell grammar, and payload-free persistent decision audits. Unknown tools default to block; ambiguous recognized-tool arguments, invalid policy, and audit failures block. Uses the public pre_tool_call hook and native Thor approval directives. Disclosure: reads its own settings through Thor and filesystem metadata and symlink targets for path comparisons; writes redacted JSONL under the active profile's plugin-data/thor-guardian directory. No protected file-content reads, enforcement-hook network calls, subprocesses, model calls, credential storage, telemetry, core overrides, or self-updater. The operator CLI optionally uses public ctx.llm structured generation, sending instructions and policy paths to the configured provider, which may charge; no separate key is required. Explicitly confirmed activation uses ctx.set_config for atomic settings updates and stores private policy backups. Offline generation is a limited exact-language template. Approval rules follow host YOLO/approvals-off and unattended-mode settings; hard block rules do not ask for approval. A policy hook, not a sandbox: intended for a trusted local POSIX backend and trusted plugins that do not rewrite arguments after inspection.

name: thor-guide
description: Read-only diagnostics for Thor configuration: /thor-doctor in-session and thor guide in a terminal. Twelve read-only health checks (config, mcp, skills, commands, hooks, plugins, memories, sessions, storage, dashboard, update, gateway) and points to 32 troubleshooting skills, installed separately as a skills tap, for what the built-in doctor doesn't cover. Complements — never replaces — thor doctor. Disclosure — reads config.yaml, SKILL.md frontmatter, skill bundles, plugin manifests, the shell-hooks allowlist and the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md stores read-only (the report quotes short memory snippets); the sessions and gateway scopes read the tail of logs/agent.log read-only for runaway-session and gateway websocket-disconnect signatures (session ids, model names, token counts, disconnect peers and reasons appear in the report); the dashboard scope reads the Thor package-manager toolchain facts, the checkout's Node lock pin and package.json engines, the web UI build record and security.allow_lazy_installs read-only, and never runs node or npm; the storage scope stats $THOR_HOME/state.db for its size only (never opens it); the update scope reads the update-lock record in the co-located thor-agent checkout under $THOR_HOME and probes it — owner-PID liveness, then a brief lock acquisition it releases immediately, opening the lock file writable, with a read-only fallback for a root-owned lock on POSIX (writes no content, never deletes the lock); registers one read-only plugin skill, thor-guide:start, listed in model sessions while the plugin is enabled; /thor-doctor and thor guide run thor config path as a subprocess (argument list, no shell); the default hooks check reads hook configuration, consent state and the exec bit in-process and executes nothing, while hooks --deep runs thor hooks doctor, which executes every approved shell hook once with a synthetic payload (--fast starts no subprocess and executes no hook); /thor-doctor and thor guide (except with --fast or --json) also run git ls-remote once per process against the plugin's GitHub repo to print a newer-release notice (no download, no local writes); with opt-in proactive: true it runs the checks (including the agent.log scan and the update-lock probe) in-process at each session start/end (no hooks executed, no subprocesses, no network). The 32 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover.

name: thor-handle-it
description: Handle It: your agent sits in the customer support chat so you don't have to. Thor holds a company's live customer-support chat for you in its own browser, negotiates toward your goal for as long as it takes, and asks you before it agrees to an offer, pays, cancels or shares a detail you did not allow. Ends with the outcome and a saved transcript. Disclosure — Opens the support pages you name in a local Chromium (Playwright) with its own profile under $THOR_HOME/thor-handle-it, or in Thor's own browser (with its signed-in sessions) when browser.cdp_url is set, public addresses only (every page, redirect hop and frame is checked; private, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses are refused), types messages into them on your behalf, and saves transcripts and screenshots there. Never reads passwords or Thor's vault: a sign-in is made by Thor itself. For phone calls it talks to bland.ai's API with your own key (BLAND_API_KEY, read through Thor's profile-scoped secrets), sends bland.ai your task and the details you allow to share, and places a call to a number you name only after you approve it; bland.ai's AI voice agent then speaks on the call and checks with you before agreeing to anything only when you expose its local approval bridge (127.0.0.1) through a public tunnel you set up as call_bridge_url, otherwise it agrees to nothing. bland.ai records the call when you ask, and call costs are yours, billed by bland.ai. No other network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

name: thor-handoff
description: Profile-bound semantic session handoffs for CLI and Desktop with independent destination and optional summary-writer models. Derived from yuzushi-dev/session-handoff. Disclosure — reads bounded persisted session evidence from the originating profile's state.db and project/Git metadata; runs local Git and foreground Thor subprocesses without a shell; stores private handoff/journal sidecars under that profile; optional writer and new chat turns use configured model providers and may incur inference costs. No telemetry or plugin-owned credential store. Four internal tool-policy imports remain version-coupled; no runtime overrides or self-updater.

name: thor-helm
description: One /helm menu in Discord or Telegram for the Thor you run 24/7: switch MCP servers, skills and toolsets on or off, ranked by the tokens each adds to every request; resend the turns a gateway restart or crash killed; set a daily spend limit that blocks new turns; and get Discord replies too long for 8 messages as a .txt file instead of truncated. Owner-only, and menus open only in a DM. Disclosure — writes mcp_servers.<name>.enabled, skills.disabled, agent.disabled_toolsets and its own plugins.entries.thor-helm.settings in config.yaml through one function that logs old and new values and refuses when the config is managed; stores the text of every top-level user turn, from any sender on any platform and from the CLI, for 7 days (to resend lost turns; subagent turns skipped), tokens and cost per model call, and the change log in plugin-data/thor-helm/helm.db; writes helm-reply-*.txt into Thor' document cache for long Discord replies; resends a lost turn with ctx.inject_message only when allow_gateway_injection is on, and Thor re-checks the allowlist; reads some private Thor internals (toolset resolution, pricing) behind try/except fallbacks. No network of its own, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: thor-herald
description: Cross-profile agent dispatch for Thor Agent — 12 tools for agents talking to agents: async dispatch with SSE completion, synchronous multi-turn chat, model-selectable in-process subagents, a durable SQLite run ledger, fail-closed per-target model-route discovery, and host-owned bare LLM inference. Disclosure — sends task text and bearer tokens to the Thor API servers you configure (plaintext HTTP permitted, warn-only); stores full dispatch text in a local SQLite ledger; delegate_subagent may use any provider credential you have configured.

name: thor-honcho-plugin
description: Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, add confirmed corrections or source files, and choose what Honcho learns from the chat's session. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Thor's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. Settings changes only the focused Honcho session's learning switches (conclusions, summaries, dreams, peer card updates) and its peers' observation settings, and only after you review the changes and press Save. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

name: thor-hyperframes
