description: Drive Hyperframes (Apache-2.0 HTML video compositions) from Thor: six hyperframes_* agent tools (lint, managed Studio preview lifecycle, timeline readback, frame snapshots for visual verification, Studio-selection context bridge, MP4 render) plus a dashboard tab with project switching, the live Studio preview embedded, an agent chat bound to a real Thor gateway session (async turns with polled status) — the same conversation a terminal sees via `thor chat --resume`. Wraps a pinned local Hyperframes CLI (no npx) and talks only to loopback services: the local CLI and the gateway's own api_server. Disclosure — Runs the Hyperframes CLI (Node) on the host for projects under the projects_roots you configure (default ~/projects/personal and ~/projects/clients, or <thor home>/projects when it exists), including a project's own node_modules/.bin/hyperframes, which executes that project's composition code; it starts and stops the Studio preview process and writes renders inside the project directory. The dashboard chat sends your messages to your own gateway api_server using API_SERVER_KEY, and every message costs a model call.

name: thor-impossibl
description: Impossibl, the AI gateway (100+ models from every major lab behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

name: thor-insight
description: Selection-definition lookup for Thor Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless thor insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `thor insight` CLI run; no background process remains. When web search is on it also queries your configured searxng instance and fetches result thumbnails from their image hosts, inlining them into the panel; nothing is fetched without a searxng URL.

name: thor-intercom
description: Discover and message existing Thor sessions within one profile using session_list and session_send. Delivery uses only the public ctx.inject_message API with attributed native notices, hop limits, per-sender duplicate detection, bounded retry identities and per-target rate limits. CLI and unknown sender surfaces are refused. Unverified routes and dormant targets that the public API cannot reach are refused; there is no private gateway transport or automatic mounting. A scheduled result confirms scheduling, not execution or durable delivery. Disclosure — lets the model list sessions in the active profile (titles, sources, working directories and routing metadata, read from `state.db` read-only) and inject attributed messages that start model/tool turns in other sessions, including other users' Discord/Telegram chats on a shared gateway, once `plugins.entries.thor-intercom.allow_gateway_injection: true` is set; bounded by `max_hops` and per-target rate limits; restrict the `intercom` toolset to owner-only platforms on shared gateways; writes a metadata-only audit log (no message text) to `$THOR_HOME/cache/thor-intercom/audit.jsonl`.

name: thor-ios
description: Build and visually iterate on native iOS apps in Thor Desktop through localhost. Runs Xcode commands and a pinned preview server; known dependency security limitations are disclosed in the README. Disclosure — on approval, setup downloads an exact-pinned serve-sim (0.1.49-beta.139.1) and its locked npm tree from registry.npmjs.org into the plugin's data dir. The plugin runs Xcode/simctl commands and keeps background serve-sim preview and watchdog processes on 127.0.0.1, whose simulator stream/input/start/shutdown routes are unauthenticated to local processes (shell execution stays disabled). It reads the local Thor config to pick its lifecycle mode. Never expose, forward or tunnel the preview port.

name: thor-iroh-interconnect
description: Authenticated Thor agent-to-agent tasks and optional file transfer over Iroh QUIC. Disclosure — tasks from a paired peer run in your live gateway agent with its full toolset; pairing is confirmed via the tool's confirm=true argument, not a UI prompt. Uses n0's public relays by default (THOR_IROH_RELAY=off or a self-hosted URL for LAN-only). iroh_send_file can share any readable path the model names (credential-name denylist only, overridable with allow_sensitive); remote-triggered auto-fetch is off by default and confined to THOR_IROH_AUTO_FETCH_DIR. The Rust sidecar is built locally with cargo, never downloaded.

name: thor-issue-orchestrator
description: GitHub issues as Thor's task queue - claim, post progress with token counts, and hand off. Disclosure — Posts public comments to the GitHub repository you configure using your token, including an automatic progress comment with token counts after each turn that holds a claimed issue (turn off with `progress_enabled: false`; the model's reply text is included only when `progress_include_reply` is on), and its tools can label, assign, close and reassign issues there without a Thor approval prompt.

name: thor-issue-sync
description: Two-way sync between Thor kanban cards and Linear or Jira issues. Open issues with a chosen label in the projects you pick become cards; card status moves the issue through its workflow; a finished card posts its summary on the issue; a worker that blocks with a question gets it posted on the issue, and the first human reply there unblocks the card with the answer. Several connections (Linear workspaces, Jira sites, several projects each) run side by side, and one failing never stops the others. Desktop adds an Issue Sync panel, a status-bar chip and kanban card badges; /issues status and /issues show work from any chat. Disclosure — calls api.linear.app and your Jira Cloud site with your own API key or token (read by name through the profile secret scope, never stored); moves issues and posts comments as you, each signed "— via Thor issue-sync", including each finished card's summary and each blocked card's question; turns the titles and descriptions of labelled issues into kanban cards, and the first reply on a blocked card's issue unblocks the card with that reply's text, so anyone who can label or comment on those issues supplies text your kanban workers act on (cards stay unassigned unless you set an assignee); runs a short background sync thread on kanban dispatcher ticks and runs `thor kanban` subcommands to read and update the board; writes only to its own plugin data folder; no telemetry. On multi-profile gateways it binds the profile's secret scope itself through the public agent.secret_scope API until thor726/thor-agent#151126 is fixed.

name: thor-jailbreak-kernel
description: Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Thor Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that, by default (`on`/`full` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); `slim` appends it instead, and `off` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); `/jailbreak dump off` or `THOR_JAILBREAK_DUMP=0` turns it off. No network, no exec.

name: thor-janus
description: Bi-directional temporal state engine & MVCC workspace for Thor Agent. Zero-copy Content-Addressable Storage (CAS), Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), Merkle-DAG branching, instant rollback, Mark-and-Sweep GC, and tournament consensus. Disclosure — Janus keeps full copies of workspace files (including `.env` and other secrets) and a log of every write/terminal call's arguments in a `.janus/` folder in the workspace, and adds `.janus/` to `.gitignore`; `janus_rewind`/`janus_branch`/`janus_merge` overwrite workspace files and delete files Janus has snapshotted that are absent from the target checkpoint (copies stay in `.janus/` until `janus_gc`); `janus_elect` with a test command runs that command on the host, outside your terminal backend, after your approval.

name: thor-jetstream
description: NATS JetStream event bus: agents publish events (nats_publish), pull one batch (nats_fetch), and wake on subject matches — live-session watches or wake routes (config-declared or runtime-registered via jetstream_wake) with durable consumers, manual ack, an idempotent wake ledger and rate rails; an opt-in lifecycle tap mirrors Thor events onto thor.> subjects. Disclosure — connects only to the NATS servers in your own config (no third-party calls, no telemetry); the platform adapter holds persistent subscriptions and reconnect loops for the gateway's lifetime; token/nkey/user-pass secrets come from ${VAR} references read via the profile-scoped secret scope and a configured creds file is read from its path, never written or rotated; wake routes render event payloads into prompts that start gateway turns or fire an existing cron job (optionally under another named profile), the agent itself can add up to 16 durable wake routes with jetstream_wake that persist in plugin data across restarts (subject still limited to subscribe_allowed, no cron-job or cross-profile targets), and jetstream_watch injects matching events into the live session when allow_gateway_injection is on, so keep subscribe_allowed scoped to trusted publishers.

name: thor-jev-routing
description: Per-turn model routing for the request that is about to go out. Jev reads the turn, picks the tier it deserves, and the plugin rewrites the provider request onto that model, including the reasoning level when the request carries one. Shadow by default, with notify, confirm and auto modes, a strip under the composer for the turn that was just routed, and a spend ledger. A pick on another provider is reported rather than sent, because a plugin cannot open a second provider client. Disclosure — once a routing JSON is configured, every turn (shadow mode included) sends the current message, up to 4,000 characters of recent user/assistant turns, the active model name, an estimated context size and the spend/budget snapshot to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai, endpoint overridable in that JSON), and the jev_route tool and /jev-routing route send their text the same way; in auto mode it rewrites the model and reasoning level on outgoing requests, and in Thor Desktop the auto mode and the approve row also switch the session's model, including onto another provider (core's expensive-model confirmation is shown to the user, never answered automatically).

name: thor-jina
description: Jina Reader web backend for web_extract (r.jina.ai, works without a key) and web_search (s.jina.ai, needs JINA_API_KEY). Unofficial; not affiliated with Jina AI.

name: thor-jobs
description: Google Calendar is the one supported backend today (scope calendar.events, one bound calendar). Bidirectional sync between Thor cron (system of record) and that job board. discover/status are read-only; sync plans both directions and is dry-run unless --confirm on the CLI. Read-only /jobs slash command shows the 7-day agenda and pending changes; each job's last run time and status (ok/error) is written to its event as a colour and one description line, never the title. Disclosure — syncs Thor cron job names, next-run times and last-run status (never prompts; only a prompt sha256) to one Google Calendar you bind, over Thor plugin OAuth (`thor auth add thor-jobs:google`, scope calendar.events, host www.googleapis.com). Reads `~/.thor/cron/jobs.json` read-only, and the first 8 KB of each no-agent cron job's script under `~/.thor/scripts/` only to recognise its own auto-sync job. Calendar edits change a cron job's schedule or name only when you run `thor thor-jobs sync --confirm`. The opt-in experimental skip writes `~/.thor/scripts/thor-jobs-skip-tick.py` and creates two one-shot no-agent cron jobs. The opt-in `mcp-serve` push mode polls Calendar every 60 s and POSTs signed event ids to your own gateway webhook URL.

name: thor-kame-api-rotation
description: Smart API key rotation: the healthiest key for every call, each 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota refusal sized from its own evidence. Install with its companion thor-kame-provider, which hands Thor this plugin's rotating client through ProviderProfile.create_client (and create_messages_client where Thor offers it); no core override. When Thor has a fallback list, a reply whose model is busy, resting or slow moves down a ladder: the model the reply started on, then the main model (model.default), then the rest of the list; a model of the same provider answers inside the plugin on the same keys and endpoint, a model of another provider is handed to Thor' own fallback (which walks the list), and a late reply can be raced by the next model of the same provider; nothing moves once part of the reply is on screen, and never_fall_back_to_another_model turns every switch off (the plugin reads the model and fallback_providers from config.yaml, read-only; no new network destination). Disclosure — /kame-keys add|import|split, and on start a key variable holding several comma-joined keys, write one auth.json pool row per key through Thor' pool API after an owner-only plaintext backup (last 5 kept; switch: resolver_disabled); settings changed from /kame or the Desktop panel are saved as KAME_* lines in Thor' .env; key-redacted, size-capped owner-only local logs (current file plus one previous), a status file, a small lifetime-counters file (replies answered and saved, requests sent per model in 24 hours, the provider's stated daily limit; no key, prompt or text) and a small model-health file (the time and the success or failure of each model's last judged outcomes, at most 7 days; no key, prompt or text) per profile; the Desktop panel reads that file and queues its settings requests through its own dashboard/plugin_api.py route (GET /state, POST /control, this plugin's plugin-data folder only); after Thor' own fallback answered a reply, the Desktop page sets that conversation's model back to the model the reply started on with config.set --session (never --global; config.yaml is not written); while every key is resting and no fallback model can take over, chats (CLI, Desktop, messaging gateway) keep waiting with no total limit (each key's rest capped by max_hold_seconds) and cron runs give up after 300 s with the provider's refusal unless max_total_wait_seconds is set. Optional speech: where Thor offers register_tts_provider, the plugin registers a text-to-speech provider named kame-gemini, unused until the owner sets tts.provider: kame-gemini; it sends each sentence to Gemini's own endpoint on the owner's Gemini keys, rotated like the chat's, rests a refused key as long as Google said and waits at most once, under 2 s, for a key about to come back. Optional listening: where Thor offers register_transcription_provider, the plugin registers a speech-to-text provider named kame-gemini, unused until the owner sets stt.provider: kame-gemini; it sends the recording to Gemini's own endpoint on the same keys, rotated the same way. Extra billed requests (chat replies only, plain API keys only - a credential Thor records as a subscription is never raced; hedge_mode off turns them all off): a late reply, or one whose model has just answered busy (a 5xx on a key: the next model of the list is then asked beside the retry at once), may also be sent to up to two more keys of the same model (about 10% of replies, 30% in "Faster", bursts of 3), to up to two next models of your fallback list on the same provider, keys and endpoint, and to one more model of the list when it stays silent; a best model that is busy, or remembered as failing (its latest judged outcome failed, with at least two failures in its last ten within seven days; the reply then starts on the next model of your list, and KAME_NO_REMEMBERED_TROUBLE=1 turns this off), may be asked again beside a reply every 20 s - less often the longer it keeps failing, at most every 5 min - and that ask is heard to its first word or 30 s; a model of the list left out for its record is a candidate again 10 min after its latest failure (doubling, at most 2 h); when keys keep coming back out of quota the next attempt asks 4, then 8, then up to 16 keys at once (probe_burst_max_legs); and a reply that showed a thought and then went quiet with nothing shown past its learned limit (8-20 s, at most 90 s; thought_quiet_s sets it, 0 turns it off) may be asked once more on another key of its model (the same key when it has only one) and once on the next model of your list (another key of the same model when no other model may be asked), its thoughts still shown live, the first to show text or a tool call being the answer; if those stay silent too, the reply is handed to the next entry of your list; and an answer that has begun and then sends nothing for answer_quiet_s (45 s; 0 turns it off; never while a tool the provider runs on its side is in flight) is continued with one more request. Titles and other background jobs are limited to a few requests and are stopped with a timeout so Thor moves them down your own list; a title on a model remembered as failing, or busy, goes once to the first healthy model of your list on the same provider.

name: thor-kame-provider
description: Companion to thor-kame-api-rotation (install both). A model-provider plugin that re-registers Thor' bundled API-key profiles unchanged except for create_client and create_messages_client, which return the rotation plugin's key-rotating client; otherwise None and Thor builds its own. Same endpoints as Thor, no third-party service, no core override.

name: thor-kemet
description: Twelve Egyptian gods in painted relief and gold leaf: Thoth, Ra, Isis, Osiris, Anubis, Horus, Bastet, Sekhmet, Set, Nut, Ptah and Hathor, as Thor Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named kemet-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Thor skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

name: thor-lang-ca
description: Catalan (Català) language pack for Thor Agent — UI translation for core (CLI, gateway, approval prompts and tips), TUI and Desktop. Covers all text-overridable catalog keys; preserves command syntax and non-text Desktop values. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-cs
description: Czech (Čeština) language pack for Thor Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,515/3,515 keys), the Ink TUI (1,390/1,390) and the Desktop app (5,404 of 5,523). Core and TUI keys match the English source of `main` at 40b566502a (2026-11-02) exactly: no key upstream has since removed and no placeholder divergence, checked by flattening both sides. The remaining 119 Desktop keys are 117 whose English value is a function with branching (plural counts such as `cron.count`, conditional labels such as `assistant.thread.errorSwitchToModel`) plus two array values, which the pack format cannot express as one template — they are omitted so they fall back to English instead of rendering a wrong Czech form. Ships the same text as upstream PR #105503, so if that PR lands the bundled locale and this pack agree. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no network, no dependencies. Disclosure — an `__init__.py` whose `register()` is a no-op is included so the Desktop "Install from Git" flow accepts the pack (#138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via `thor config set display.language cs`. Česká lokalizace rozhraní Thor Agent.

name: thor-lang-el
description: Greek (Ελληνικά) language pack for Thor Agent — Desktop UI (5,377 of 5,384 keys) plus the 102 most visible core CLI slash-command descriptions; missing keys fall back to English. TUI and the remaining core CLI strings are not covered yet. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-he
description: Hebrew (עברית) language pack for Thor — core CLI, gateway and tips (3,396 of 3,486 keys on main), TUI (1,331 of 1,356) and Desktop (5,153 of 5,245), with Desktop flipped right-to-left. Thor bundles no Hebrew, so the pack ships all three catalogs; values identical to English and entries whose English wording depends on an argument (on/off, show/hide) are omitted so they fall back to English. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-it
description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for Thor Agent — UI translation for core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI and Desktop. Coverage: core 3437/3437, TUI 1259/1259 and Desktop ~5,000 keys (missing ones fall back to English). Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Traduzione italiana dell'interfaccia Thor Agent. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-it-full
description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for Thor Desktop covering nearly every Desktop string (firstRun, themePicker, connector accounts and the update-channel picker included; the few array/object leaves the pack format rejects fall back to English). Core, CLI and TUI keep the Italian catalogs already bundled with Thor. Generated from the hand-reviewed typed catalog maintained in gradia64/thor-agent (gradia-desktop-it branch); function-backed keys ship as positional {0} templates. Independent community translation, unrelated to thor-lang-it. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-ko
description: Korean (한국어) language pack for Thor Desktop — Desktop UI (5,282 of 5,384 keys on v0.22.5 and main cb757fac59; 349 new translations); CLI, gateway and TUI keep the Korean catalogs already bundled with Thor. Independent translation from the English source; values identical to English are omitted so missing strings fall back to English. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-pt-br
description: Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) language pack for Thor Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,535/3,535 keys), the Ink TUI (1,445/1,445) and the Desktop app (5,588/5,592). Every translatable key exists and every value is translated against the English source of `main` at the revision this release was cut from: zero unknown keys and zero placeholder divergence on all three surfaces, and the four remaining Desktop keys are arrays/structured values a text pack cannot carry. Checked with `thor plugins validate` and with the pack's own `tools/verify_pack.py`, which also runs as public CI on every push. Core and TUI mirror the bundled `pt` locale, registered as a real `pt-br` variant so it wins over the `pt`/`pt-BR` alias; the Desktop catalog is the original contribution (first proposed upstream in PR #92590, 2026-08-23), since the Desktop app ships no Portuguese at all. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `thor config set display.language pt-br`. A weekly drift workflow reports when `main` adds or drops keys; nothing self-updates. Tradução pt-BR da interface do Thor Agent.

name: thor-lang-th
description: Thai (ภาษาไทย) language pack covering all three Thor UI surfaces — Desktop (5,023/5,030), core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,437/3,437), and the Ink TUI (1,259/1,259) — 9,719/9,725 keys total (99.9%). All three catalogs checked against the English reference with `thor plugins validate`. Manifest-only plugin: flat nested YAML overlays under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `thor config set display.language th`. Disclosure — text-only catalogs (no code, network or dependencies); untranslated keys fall back to English: the 7 array/conditional Desktop keys listed in the repo README, plus strings Thor added after the pack was built.

name: thor-lang-tr
description: Turkish (Türkçe) language pack for Thor — core (CLI approval prompts, gateway replies, tips), TUI and Desktop. Full coverage: 3,535 core keys, 1,440 TUI keys and 5,569 Desktop keys, every key matching the English catalogs, placeholders preserved. Independent community translation prepared with AI assistance. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack); no Python logic, no network access, no stored credentials; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lang-vi
description: Vietnamese (Tieng Viet) language pack for Thor Agent — full UI translation across every surface: core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI, and Desktop catalogs. Checked against the English catalogs with thor plugins validate. Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved; multi-line values use real newlines exactly like the English catalogs. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Ban dich tieng Viet day du cho toan bo giao dien Thor Agent. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

name: thor-lcm-x
description: Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 16 lcm_* tools for search, recall and expansion (lcm_memory only with LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1). Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from thor-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Thor, then in plugins.enabled replace thor-lcm with thor-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Thor is configured with. Disclosure — local semantic recall is on by default once its dependency companion is installed (thor plugins install electricsheephq/lcm-x/companions/thor-lcm-x-local-embeddings --ref <the LCM-X commit>; it carries fastembed): summaries and message chunks are embedded in-process with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 after a one-time model download, in the background, and stay on the machine. Without the companion, recall answers from full text and lcm_doctor prints the install command; on hosts with 2 or fewer effective CPUs the default answers from full text unless LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true; LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false turns semantic recall off. Cloud embedding providers (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama) send message text to that provider and run only with LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true and an explicit model. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in), including a delegated subagent's turns as it runs; on gateway platforms the sender's platform user ID is recorded with each user message by default (LCM_SENDER_CAPTURE=0 turns it off), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under THOR_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads Thor' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads the files Thor saves for oversized tool results so it can store their full content, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Thor builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use. An opt-in event recorder (LCM_RECORDER_ENABLED, off by default) writes local files under THOR_HOME/lcm-recorder (up to 20 GiB by default): what Thor sends to LCM-X and what it returns, including conversation content, copies of lcm.db and lcm-large-outputs, session rows from state.db, and the LCM-related parts of config.yaml with credential values replaced by set/unset markers.

name: thor-ledger
description: Tamper-evident flight recorder: every tool call (arguments redacted), a SHA-256 of every result, and every approval decision are appended to a local hash-chained, Ed25519-signed log. `thor ledger verify` walks the chain and names the first edited, deleted, reordered or truncated entry; `thor ledger show` prints a timeline; `thor ledger export --receipt` writes a signed receipt of one session that anyone can check with only the public key (records from other sessions appear as content-free stubs), with `thor ledger verify-receipt` or the bundled standalone verify_receipt.py. An approval record binds to the exact call it approved. Adds a /ledger slash command, a Ledger dashboard tab with a chain-intact badge, and the skill thor-ledger:ledger-audit. It proves the log was not changed after writing, not that the agent was honest when it wrote it (threat model in the README). Disclosure — five observer hooks (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, post_approval_response, on_session_start, on_session_end) see every tool call's name, arguments and result and every approval prompt; arguments are redacted by pattern (sensitive key names, bearer/sk- and other token shapes, PEM keys, NAME=value secrets) before writing, which is best effort; results are hashed, never stored; writes only under plugin-data/thor-ledger/ (ledger.jsonl, ledger.head, an Ed25519 private key at mode 0600 that is never printed, and its public key); the log is never pruned; observer only, never blocks, approves, denies or changes a call; no network, no credentials read, no background processes, no shell commands.

name: thor-ledgerline
description: Inspect session costs and usage in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — reads session lists, session detail, search, usage analytics and cron targets from the gateway's core REST API through the raw window.thorDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no route to those endpoints), and runs thor version, thor insights and thor send --list through the gateway's cli.exec. Only when you start them: explain and audit send the selected session's digest (tool arguments only if you tick that box) to your configured model, as a new Thor session or a background prompt on the focused one; alerts and test messages are sent with thor send to a messaging target you pick; scheduled reports create a Thor cron job (one agent turn per run on the default model, delivered to the target you pick) and are paused, resumed or removed through cron.manage. Budgets, dismissed tips, scans and saved answers are kept in Thor plugin storage on the desktop. Nothing is sent elsewhere and it exposes no tools to the model.

name: thor-lens
description: Talk to your own Thor agent through Ray-Ban Meta glasses. A platform channel for a companion iPhone app that holds a Gemini Live voice call; requests that need your data or an action become ordinary messages to your agent, and Thor approvals appear as an Approve / Decline card that only your tap resolves. Disclosure — opens an HTTP listener (default 127.0.0.1:8795, plaintext; expose it only through a TLS proxy such as tailscale serve) where any phone holding the shared THOR_LENS_TOKEN chats with the agent as its owner, bypassing the gateway allowlist, and resolves approval prompts with a tap; sends GEMINI_API_KEY only to generativelanguage.googleapis.com to mint single-use Gemini Live call tokens, after which the companion app speaks the agent's answers and any glasses photos you attach through Google's Gemini Live (with Google Search); `thor lens setup` writes THOR_LENS_TOKEN (and a Gemini key you type) to the profile .env; stores only daily call-time totals in its plugin data dir; no telemetry.

name: thor-line
description: A phone line for Thor: with your approval it calls a business from your Twilio account, works the phone menu, waits on hold, then bridges you in or finishes the task, and can answer callbacks. Disclosure — Places real phone calls and sends call audio through your own Twilio account (api.twilio.com), and through xAI (api.x.ai) when XAI_API_KEY is set; every call and every released SMS code needs your approval in chat. With `enabled: true` it runs a call service inside Thor on 127.0.0.1:8788 that you expose through your own HTTPS tunnel, plus a loopback-only tool server, and it starts one `thor acp` process per call on a separate neutral call profile with a minimal environment. With `sms_source: adb` it reads the attached Android phone's SMS inbox. The setup check (`/line check`, `thor thor-line check`) runs `thor --version` and makes read-only Twilio GET requests.

name: thor-live
description: Multi-provider live voice calls with Gemini, Grok, Qwen, and a Codex subscription in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — voice audio and recent chat go only to the live-voice provider the user picks (Gemini, Grok or Qwen); the Codex option drives the user's own Codex CLI on its own ChatGPT login; tasks the voice model submits run as normal Thor chat turns with the usual approvals.

name: thor-live-voice
description: Full-duplex Live Voice for Thor Desktop — GPT-Live-1 on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription via the local Codex app-server, with live transcript, voice tool calls and task delegation to the user chat. Disclosure — subscription voice uses your Thor openai-codex sign-in through Thor-signed requests (requires_auth; the plugin never holds or refreshes the token) to mint OpenAI Realtime client secrets, and the usage panel reads Thor's own account-usage fetcher; the gpt-live-1 lane runs the local codex app-server on the Codex CLI's own login, and the dashboard can run codex login --device-auth, copying ~/.codex/auth.json (or $CODEX_HOME) to a backup before that login, restoring the backup if the login is cancelled, and reading the file read-only for sign-in status; with TALK_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY set it uses that key instead; if thor-talk is installed it loads that plugin's modules from ~/.thor/plugins/thor-talk and substitutes its own talk_auth; voice audio goes to OpenAI over WebRTC, and spoken tasks are submitted as messages in your focused chat.

name: thor-loadout
description: Desktop pane to manage skills and MCP connections across agent apps: save named loadouts, review changes, apply them, and undo the latest managed operation. Agent half is inert (no tools or hooks). Disclosure — MCP sync copies your Thor mcp_servers env/header secrets into ~/.codex/config.toml and claude_desktop_config.json (with 0600 backups).

name: thor-local-voice
description: Voice memos become text on the machine that recorded them: no API key, no account, and no audio leaving the host. Capture from PipeWire or ffmpeg, run faster-whisper locally, and the transcript arrives as a note. Four tools (transcribe_audio, voice_record_start, voice_record_stop, transcribe_last) plus a speech-to-text provider registered through ctx.register_transcription_provider, so core transcribes only admitted messages when stt.provider is set to thor_local_voice. pre_llm_call attaches the pending transcript to the turn; the legacy pre_gateway_dispatch path is opt-in and off by default because it runs before sender authorization. Ships model management (list supported Whisper sizes with disk cost and cache status, download explicitly) and a live capture path with a silence gate so ambient room tone is never transcribed. Disclosure: all processing is local. Network access happens only when the user explicitly runs the model download command, which fetches weights from Hugging Face into the Thor model directory; no telemetry, no automatic updates, no reads outside the Thor home and the recording paths the plugin creates. Disclosure \u2014 transcription runs locally with faster-whisper; when the user configures a loopback job server URL, audio files are POSTed to it and its reply is used as the transcript; the transcribe tool and the pre_llm_call hook read any local audio path named in the chat, and with cleanup enabled the tool deletes only recordings the plugin created; the opt-in auto_transcribe_inbound setting transcribes gateway voice messages before sender authorization; models are read from the Thor model directory,  or , and are downloaded from Hugging Face only when the user runs the model download command; no telemetry, no automatic updates. Disclosure — transcription runs locally with faster-whisper; when the user configures a loopback job server URL, audio files are POSTed to it and its reply is used as the transcript; the transcribe tool and the pre_llm_call hook read any local audio path named in the chat, and with cleanup enabled the tool deletes only recordings the plugin created; the opt-in auto_transcribe_inbound setting transcribes gateway voice messages before sender authorization; models are read from the Thor model directory, `~/.cache/huggingface/hub` or `HF_HOME`, and are downloaded from Hugging Face only when the user runs the model download command; no telemetry, no automatic updates.

name: thor-lyrics
description: Time-synced lyrics for the song playing on Spotify: a Thor Desktop page that highlights and centres the current line as the song plays, click any line to seek, with a per-user sync offset. Lyrics from the public LRCLIB API; playback through the official spotify plugin.

name: thor-make-plain
description: One-click composer polish for the Thor Desktop chat: a wand button at the right of the input box rewrites the draft in place into a clear request an AI can act on, with nothing added and nothing dropped. The layout follows the draft: a symptom report with a request stays one paragraph, separate edits get one short line each, and a draft that is already a list keeps its line count and markers. An answer longer than four times the draft is rejected with a toast, so a runaway answer never replaces the draft. Pure filler and repeated restatements are dropped, and every concrete detail is kept exactly as written: names, numbers, versions, ports, paths, file names, URLs, @-references, /commands and code. It stays in the draft's language and never translates. The message is never sent; the button spins while the rewrite is in flight, rejects an empty box before any work starts, and never overwrites a draft edited while the call is running. Disclosure: one model call per click through the llm.oneshot auxiliary route to the auxiliary.title_generation model; no other network calls, no telemetry, no analytics; reads and writes only the composer draft through the official SDK and keeps no copy of the text (plugin storage is a one-field load heartbeat); no shell commands, no credentials.

name: thor-manas-aegis
description: [ALPHA] Experimental Thor guardrail (prototype, not standalone security): pattern-based pre-tool checks that can block or rewrite some risky tool arguments, with a canary honeypot, local telemetry and a loopback HUD, plus STIX 2.1 export. Opt-in, test environments only. Disclosure — alpha guardrail: its pre_tool_call / pre_llm_call / transform hooks can block tool calls or rewrite their arguments (honeypot redirect to a decoy file, safe-flag git rewrite) and scrub tool results; serves a token-protected loopback-only HUD on 127.0.0.1 (default port 18777, off with auto_launch_hud_server: false); fetches public CISA KEV and NVD CVE feeds over HTTPS (no key) for the threat-intel panel, refreshed every 6 hours while the HUD runs; the full scan reads files under the active Thor home (skipping .env, auth.json, config.yaml, webhook_subscriptions.json, mcp-tokens/, *.bak backups and other profiles); writes redacted telemetry and a STIX 2.1 feed under the plugin data folder; no credentials read, no telemetry sent out.

name: thor-maps
description: A live map you and Thor share, docked beside the chat. Thor plots places it finds on the web with real coordinates, flies the camera, drops pins with a note and source link, and draws routes. You click a pin or circle an area and Thor receives what you picked. Two looks: a clean flat map and a cinematic globe. No keys and no cost. Disclosure — viewing the map sends tile requests (your IP address and the area viewed) to tiles.openfreemap.org; a bundled world outline is the offline fallback. Plotting and place search send place names and search text (and the visible map bounds for a visible-area search) from this machine to photon.komoot.io, a free service with no uptime guarantee; results are kept in memory for an hour. Google Maps links and a pin's source link open in the browser only when clicked. Selections you send become chat messages and reach your model provider. Pins, routes, camera and selections are stored in Thor plugin storage on this machine. No background processes, no telemetry, no credentials, no self-update.

name: thor-market
description: Discover skill APIs across sellers, publish tested services, and buy results with human-approved x402 payments. Disclosure — calls only the service directory, seller and local wallet-approval gateway you configure (none are set by default and the default mode is local simulation); the directory you choose lists sellers, and in testnet mode a listed seller may be any HTTPS host and receives your quote input and your wallet session token for that seller; payments are simulation or Base Sepolia test USDC only and are approved by you outside the agent (terminal digest or browser wallet signature); service_draft sends a SKILL.md you name, and text references in its folder, to your configured LLM and saves drafts in draft_dir; keeps a purchase ledger and an encryption key file at paths you configure; the Desktop page's optional "Public demo" button opens the author-operated directory market.0xeddie.kim in your browser.

name: thor-memory-pane
description: A Thor Desktop pane for the built-in memory: see what the focused chat remembered, updated or forgot, and edit, delete or undo any entry without leaving the conversation. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — a tool_execution middleware reads MEMORY.md and USER.md around each memory call and logs the entry-level changes to $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-memory-pane/; the pane rewrites memory entries only when the user edits, deletes, adds or undoes one, through Thor's own memory store; no network, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

name: thor-memory-ui
description: Read-only Thor Dashboard and Desktop plugin for inspecting built-in, holographic, Mem0, Honcho, Mnemosyne, Hindsight, and ByteRover memory. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memory files, provider configs and provider API keys (keys are never returned to the UI), and on user action sends search/recall/reflect queries with configured bank/peer/user IDs to the configured Mem0, Honcho and Hindsight endpoints (Hindsight Cloud default api.hindsight.vectorize.io) using those keys; ByteRover queries run the local `brv` CLI; for a local embedded Hindsight setup a contents read may start the `hindsight-embed` daemon; no memory is written.

name: thor-memory-wiki
description: Memory Wiki dashboard tab and opt-in native Desktop page: browsable subject pages and daily logs derived from local session history, plus a read-only Persistent Memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) audit panel.

name: thor-microduck
description: Drive Microduck, the open-source bipedal duck robot from Pollen Robotics / Hugging Face, in a MuJoCo simulation running its real trained ONNX RL policies: look through the duck's head camera, walk, turn, sit, stand, move the head, and line up and kick a ball at a goal (10 tools), with every motion gated by a pre_tool_call safety interlock (speed and duration caps, an arena geofence, a latching e-stop only a human clears with /duck clear, every blocked call logged). Ships a /duck command, a bundled skill and a dependency-free mock duck, so it runs with no MuJoCo at all. Independent community integration, not affiliated with Pollen Robotics. Disclosure — network: in sim mode, plain HTTP to the sim server you configure (default 127.0.0.1:8765, sim/server.py, a long-running process you start yourself); mock mode (default) makes no network connections. Setup: sim/fetch_assets.py, run by you once, downloads Pollen's MJCF, meshes and ONNX policies (~7 MB, Apache-2.0) from the official pollen-robotics/microduck-simulator Hugging Face Space pinned to a commit; the plugin downloads nothing at runtime. Files: camera snapshots, a blocked-call audit log and the e-stop latch under the plugin data dir. No credentials. The interlock limits this plugin's tools only; it does not stop other tools (terminal, code execution) from calling the sim server or changing the limits in config.yaml.

name: thor-minimizer
description: YAGNI coding and code-review guidance for Thor: reduce over-engineering, reuse existing behavior, and preserve requirements. One static prompt section; no tools or hooks.

name: thor-mobile
description: WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE_CATALOG_AFTER_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE_DELIVER_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $THOR_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through Thor's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through Thor's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.

name: thor-model-switcher
description: Choose models across Thor profiles from a Dashboard tab: a per-profile picker built on host-supplied model data (SDK-authenticated GET /api/model/options), a preview of provider/model intent across every supported model-selection slot (main, delegation, auxiliary, judge, fallback, MoA, cron, plugin and specialist), and one-click apply or revert with presets. Main-slot preview shows intended provider/model, not the exact persisted diff; the exact diff is shown only after host readback. Disclosure — its apply route reads and edits the profiles' config.yaml (that is the plugin's function) through public seams only: POST /api/model/set for main and compatible auxiliary slots, and public thor_cli.config load/save under the target home for other slots; credential presence checks use public profile-scoped secret helpers (agent.secret_scope), and profile discovery uses public thor_constants. The plugin makes no direct third-party requests and opens no provider caches or pricing registries directly, but its browser tab does call the host's /api/model/* routes through the Dashboard SDK, and the host options route may itself initiate provider or pricing I/O even without an explicit refresh request, so reads are not guaranteed cache-only. It runs no shell commands or background processes and reports nothing. The private undo journal stores a full pre-change snapshot of each config it edits, which can contain sensitive fields including embedded credentials. Saved presets also persist reviewed change values, potentially including inline credentials or credential-bearing base URLs, in presets.json (0600) under get_thor_home()/state/thor-model-switcher/ (0700). The host write route has no expected-revision check: readback surfaces many foreign edits as recovery_required, but a concurrent same-key edit can be overwritten undetected and full-state deletions retain an unrelated-write race, so not every foreign edit is guaranteed to surface.

name: thor-monitor
description: Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens THOR_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every Thor profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls Thor' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, Thor core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress.
maintainer: Thor Monitor contributors (independent of Thor Labs)

name: thor-monitoring-dashboard
description: Prompt-customizable desktop dashboard with live host metrics, session activity, clocks, calendars, and text widgets. Disclosure — polls ~/monitoring-dashboard on the desktop device through the Desktop native file bridge, and its Reset command moves only the dashboard's own page/panel marker files in that folder to the OS trash (never dashboard.json or the folder); host metrics and session activity stay on the machine.

name: thor-mpp
description: Pay supported HTTP 402 MPP challenges on Tempo through mpp_fetch and in-process HTTPX clients. Uses a dedicated wallet. Disclosure — with MPP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset, any supported HTTP 402 MPP challenge returned to core HTTPX traffic (not only mpp_fetch) is auto-paid from the Tempo wallet with no per-payment cap or confirmation; the origin allowlist is the operator's control.

name: thor-multibot
description: Several Telegram bots in one Thor profile: each extra bot is its own private-DM transport with its own session, alias and numeric allowlist, while memory, skills and tools stay shared. Independent BasePlatformAdapter registered through register_platform; no core patches, no fork or wrapper of the bundled Telegram adapter. Disclosure — network: Telegram Bot API long polling, messages and file downloads; credentials: up to eight declared password secrets read only through Thor secret scope; files: own replay store and capped media cache under THOR_HOME; one poller per configured bot inside the gateway process. No telemetry or self-update.

name: thor-multiplayer
description: Multiplayer Thor. Channels, DMs, threads and a shared team room where you, up to four teammates, and each of your Thor agents work in one place. No server to host — or one small relay when teammates can't reach each other. Disclosure — Syncs channels, DMs, threads, reactions, edits and presence with up to four teammate gateways at addresses you configure (authenticated by a shared Thor Multiplayer secret; adds code-gated `/thor-multiplayer/v1/pair` plus secret-protected `/thor-multiplayer/v1/sync` and `/thor-multiplayer/v1/ping` routes, and the same routes under the legacy `/herd/v1/` prefix, to your Thor API server, which must be reachable by teammates), and, if you join or start a team room, sends everything it holds to the relay address you give it in plaintext where the relay operator can read it (there is no built-in relay); the `multiplayer_post` tool lets your agent post to teammates and the room without an approval prompt; with "Let my agent answer @mentions" (on by default), a chosen chat and `allow_gateway_injection: true`, a teammate's or a teammate agent's @mention starts a turn in that chat with your agent's memory and tools (at most 6 per minute, and at most 6 agent-only replies in a row per thread before a person must speak).

name: thor-muse
description: A proactive companion for Thor: follows accepted goals (active/done/cancelled), prepares sourced research and Feed articles, maintains memory, and assembles rolling 30-day or natural-month calendar views. Read-only local Dashboard/Desktop pages show Feed, Ideas and Goals; profile selection cannot install, enable or disable Muse in any profile. One Skill, one state tool and six fixed recurring jobs; selected notices and weekly/monthly reports go to the active profile's Bot Chat and run an assistant turn there. Sources, authorization, quiet hours and actual result/delivery receipts remain distinct; partial coverage is not global availability. Disclosure: first load creates profile-local files/SQLite state and owned Cron scripts/jobs. Private/local input inbox rows retain their first 8000 characters and source identities, with associated chat/user routing IDs when present. The newest 500 remain; older rows are cleaned on later input only after both hourly/nightly cursors cover them. Unprocessed backlog can exceed 500 and has no fixed retention time. Native conversations/tool results are read separately; research records can retain returned payloads. Idempotency journals and oversized tool results stay in the profile state database without automatic expiry and may contain written content or tool output. Bounded conversation previews support full revision-checked paging. Delegates are instructed to remain read-only under inherited permissions, not sandboxed. Workers always use public delegate_task dispatch and follow the user's delegation settings; leave delegation.provider/model empty to keep the parent model. New Cron watches require cron.allow_agent_scheduling; local goal registration creates no job. Watch prompt/stop fields each allow 4000 characters; new repeating watches (interval or cron) must be at least 30 minutes apart, one-off schedules are exempt. Windows is not supported (POSIX file locks) and CI does not cover it. Background work incurs normal model/tool costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory service, core/SOUL replacement or phone/read-receipt guarantee. Native remove retains data/tasks for the documented owned-only cleanup.

name: thor-muse-code
description: Muse Spark in Thor billed to the Muse Code monthly login (device-code login, no API key). Disclosure — Unofficial: uses a Muse Code subscription credential outside Meta's Muse Code client, which Meta's terms (Model API ToS §3.2) restrict; a local 127.0.0.1 proxy renames tool declarations so Meta's client check does not refuse the request; Meta may suspend the account or subscription. The key is cached in the Thor home (muse-code-sub.json) and sent only to auth.meta.com and api.meta.ai; `*-contributor` models in the picker let Meta use that traffic, including background calls on the picked model, as training data.

name: thor-newswire
description: Breaking-news ticker for Thor Desktop: a scrolling RSS/Atom/JSON-Feed strip above the statusbar with per-source favicons, feed search + discovery, grouping modes, offline cache, and in-app reading. Zero API keys, zero model tokens.

name: thor-notify
description: Phone notifications, questions, release progress and exact command approvals through Notify. Run `thor notify setup` to sign in, connect the phone app, send a test and route command approvals to the phone. Disclosure — when enabled, sends model-written notifications and questions, optional release workspace data, and (when security.approval.transport is notify) each Thor approval request's redacted command and description to the third-party Notify service (notify.belweave.ai); release Apps also go to a Cloudflare Worker you deploy yourself (uses THOR_NOTIFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN). `thor notify setup` signs in to notify.belweave.ai with a device code (sending a "Thor on <hostname> (<OS>)" device label), saves the resulting 90-day NOTIFY_API_TOKEN to the profile .env and, once a phone is registered and no other transport is chosen, runs `thor config set` to select security.approval.transport notify and transport_fallback builtin (terminal prompt when Notify is unreachable; skip with --no-approvals, undo with `thor notify approvals off`). Phone approvals are approve-once or deny only; a phone timeout denies. Phone replies are injected into the session only when you set allow_reply_injection. Optional `thor notify webhooks on` creates a Notify reply webhook, saves NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the profile .env, may run `boat host` to give the port a public HTTPS URL, sets allow_reply_injection and plugins.entries.thor-notify.allow_gateway_injection, and then listens on 127.0.0.1 (inbound_webhook_port) for signed answer events that it re-checks with Notify before injecting the answer into the asking session as untrusted input; `thor notify webhooks off` removes it. Runs one background delivery thread, plus a webhook listener thread when webhooks are on.

name: thor-nous-prices
description: Browse Nous Portal model prices and account balances in Thor Desktop.

name: thor-office
description: View and manage Bot Mode agents in a shared office in Thor Desktop.

name: thor-office-desktop
description: Workbench by Atlas Omnia — Open and edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Outlook for the web in Thor Desktop. Live-tested in the automated harness and real Thor Desktop sessions on macOS and Windows; see docs/live-evidence.md. Every edit requests Thor approval and returns a readback/undo receipt; undo has exceptions (large Word snapshots, Excel over 10,000 cells, some PowerPoint edits and OneNote page creation), and history is lost on pane reload. powerpoint_add_speaker_notes returns Unsupported. Requires Microsoft sign-in and Upload My Add-in. A loopback HTTPS bridge on 127.0.0.1:47615-47619 (https://localhost) serves the add-in from this pinned plugin (only files listed in addin/SHA256SUMS with a matching sha256, never addin/dev), accepts only Workbench's own loopback origins (or a self-hosted addin_base's exact origin) and a user-typed single-use code, then a per-pane token; idle listeners release after ten minutes. One manual step per Thor profile: trust the plugin's local certificate authority with the command it prints (the plugin never changes OS trust); /workbench manifest writes the add-in manifests. Earlier live runs used a private add-in site; the plugin-served default passed one live Excel run on macOS (2026-11-12) and is not live-tested yet in the other apps or on Windows. The pane loads Microsoft Office.js. Document data enters the local Thor conversation; OneNote pages and email indexed on request persist unencrypted in brain.db. Reads are capped at 20,000 characters for Word and Outlook bodies. No Graph, credentials, telemetry, shell commands or unattended runs. Outlook reads only the open item; mail and calendar drafts are never sent or saved and recipients/attendees never changed. Image URL fetches alone use outbound HTTPS (public addresses, checked redirects, PNG/JPEG, 4 MiB); local images are restricted to allowed folders. Full disclosures and known limits: README and docs/reference.md. Not affiliated with Microsoft or Thor Labs. Disclosure — Workbench serves its Office add-in from this plugin's pinned files over HTTPS on 127.0.0.1 ports 47615-47619 (https://localhost). To make that work you trust, by hand and once per Thor profile, a local certificate authority the plugin creates. That authority can vouch only for localhost and 127.0.0.1, and its private key is stored unencrypted in the profile's plugin-data/thor-office-desktop/tls folder, so keep that folder private and remove the trust when you stop using Workbench. The pane loads Microsoft's Office.js from appsforoffice.microsoft.com. Document and mail content you work on enters your Thor conversation, and OneNote pages and email you index stay unencrypted in the plugin's local brain.db. Every edit asks for Thor approval; deletes and other edits that cannot be undone have their own approval rule. Image URL fetches go out over HTTPS to public addresses only.

name: thor-openready
description: Prepare an open-source release candidate from a private repository and refuse to publish it: five tools (status, doctor, candidate, verify, gate) plus a pre_tool_call guard that inspects the terminal tool and blocks or escalates the publish commands it recognises - the gh, gh api and curl shapes that create a public repository or change visibility - until the owner has approved that exact candidate digest. It does not claim to catch every way to publish. No tool can push, change visibility or upload: candidate writes a local candidate directory and verify may write one packet under .openready-private/. The approval check runs the separately installed Open-Ready CLI with an allowlisted child environment carrying no Thor provider keys or GitHub tokens. Disclosure — the tools run the separately installed Open-Ready CLI (openready_bin / openready_python from your config) as child processes with an allowlisted environment (no Thor provider keys or GitHub tokens); openready_candidate writes a candidate directory at <repo>/.openready-candidate and openready_verify with write_packet writes one file at <repo>/.openready-private/packets/packet.json; the pre_tool_call guard inspects every terminal command and blocks, or sends to Thor' approval prompt, the recognised gh / gh api / curl commands that create a public repository or change visibility, which is not a complete barrier (other tools, scripts or shell forms can still publish).

name: thor-openwhispr
description: Local-first OpenWhispr dictation history and shared notes for Thor agents: find what the user said, search notes, transcribe local audio. Free local desktop bridge by default, paid cloud opt-in only. Skill-carrier plugin, no tools or hooks registered. Disclosure — skill only: the agent runs the external OpenWhispr CLI (installed with an unpinned `npm install -g @openwhispr/cli`) through the terminal tool to read your dictation history and notes over the OpenWhispr desktop app's authenticated loopback bridge, and, with your consent each time, to create, update or delete notes, transcriptions and dictionary entries and to transcribe local audio files; OpenWhispr Cloud (api.openwhispr.com, including an email-code sign-in that mints an API key kept in the CLI's own config) is used only when you opt in; the agent never opens credential files itself.

name: thor-opper
description: Opper, the EU-hosted AI gateway (700+ models behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

name: thor-osint-map
description: A live situational-awareness globe in Thor Desktop: earthquakes (USGS), disaster alerts (GDACS), natural events (NASA EONET), US severe weather (NWS), military and nearby aircraft (adsb.lol), satellites propagated live from CelesTrak elements, GDELT news incidents, about 5,000 official traffic cameras (Transport for London, with its short JamCam video clips, Caltrans, the Hong Kong Transport Department and Singapore LTA), shipping chokepoints and an opt-in live cyber-attack layer on a dithered 3D globe, with satellite orbits, aircraft tracks, a camera wall, a tour of what matters right now, day and night shading and night-vision, thermal and CRT looks, country dossiers (World Bank facts, events, headlines), NOAA space weather, markets, a feed of events, headlines and alerts, and a passive recon toolkit (DNS, RDAP, TLS, security headers, CT subdomains, CVE with CISA KEV, IP, GitHub, MAC). Seven agent tools (osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news, osint_watch, osint_show) answer from the same sources in any chat; osint_show lets Thor fly the Desktop globe, pin places and switch layers while it answers, and the page's Brief me, Ask Thor and dossier buttons open a chat that uses them. In Thor Desktop, answers about a place end with a live map card. Watches check an area on a schedule and alert only on new events. No keys needed; an optional TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (plugin setting, read through Thor's secret scope) adds equities and commodities. Unofficial; not affiliated with any data provider. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public data from fixed hosts (earthquake.usgs.gov, eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov, gdacs.org, api.weather.gov, data.gdeltproject.org, api.adsb.lol, celestrak.org, services.swpc.noaa.gov, api.tfl.gov.uk, api.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and static.data.gov.hk (camera lists), and camera stills and clips from TfL's JamCams bucket on s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, images.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and tdcctv.data.one.gov.hk, fetched only by camera id for cameras the user opens, api.worldbank.org, the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, Guardian and France 24 RSS feeds, api.gdeltproject.org (GDELT article search, only when a news query is given, which sends up to six words of the query), api.coingecko.com, and api.twelvedata.com with the key in a header when set), cached and only while the page is open or a tool is called, with a thor-osint-map User-Agent; the cyber-attack layer is off until the user turns it on and then reads threatmap-api.checkpoint.com, the undocumented feed behind Check Point's public threat map (unofficial; one stream, closed about 45 seconds after no page shows the layer); recon sends the domain, IP, CVE id, GitHub name or MAC prefix the user or agent enters to dns.google, rdap.org, crt.sh, cve.circl.lu, cisa.gov, ipwho.is, api.github.com and api.macvendors.com, and the TLS and headers lookups connect directly to the host named, refusing private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other internal addresses on every redirect, on ports 443/8443 (TLS) and 80/443/8080/8443 (headers) only; GDELT incidents are machine-coded from news coverage and labelled as such, incident titles are read from the article URL, and country-centroid locations are flagged as country-level; a watch is a normal Thor scheduled job the user creates and can remove (named “OSINT watch · <name>”, every 15 minutes at the fastest), each check is one short model call with the user's default model plus the same public-source requests, and alerts go only to the destination the user picked (Thor or a connected messaging channel); watch state (area, rules, the last 2,000 event ids seen, the last 20 alerts) and Thor's latest globe scene are kept in the plugin's own state file under plugin-data; the page keeps its layer choices in Desktop plugin storage; no shell commands, no processes of its own, no telemetry.

name: thor-output-enhancement
description: Display-only Markdown styling for Desktop assistant replies — theme-aware headings, emphasis, inline code and readable tables. Reply content is never modified.

name: thor-pantheon
description: Eighteen Thor Desktop themes in dithered classical marble, one god each: all twelve Olympians plus Hades, Nyx, Helios, Selene and Medusa. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while a Pantheon theme is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named pantheon-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Thor skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

name: thor-parallel
description: Run three isolated, verified file futures inside Thor, compare, then choose one to apply. Disclosure — `/parallel apply` replaces the chosen workspace folder under your configured `root` with the selected future (the original is kept as a hidden backup sibling for `/parallel rollback`); snapshots of that folder are stored in the profile's `parallel-data` directory; when you set `ai_enabled`, `parallel_explore` makes three model calls with your filenames, and with `context_enabled` also the contents of the files you name.

name: thor-pentest
description: Guided local Vite/Supabase source input discovery, fresh human approval, offline build and isolated testing with synthetic data. Populated/absent SQL controls and authenticated persisted-text XSS checks verify actual input/render paths. Reports distinguish rejected probes from failed controls and count planned versus completed same-user and cross-user stored workflows separately. Uses the provider already configured in Thor. Also supports explicit local web/API discovery, controlled SQL injection, browser-proven reflected/DOM/stored XSS, access contracts, owner-approved localhost servers, multi-service applications and native/CLI checks. Durable budgets, supervised execution, stop/recovery, immutable evidence, fixed-build regression and reports. Disclosure — trusted Python controllers use the local Docker socket to manage exact run-owned containers; Docker targets get no host mounts, published ports or external network. Existing localhost servers are unmanaged and are tested only at origins the owner lists in `allowed_localhost_origins` (empty by default), which receive state-changing requests with the configured test-session headers. macOS supervised-local mode runs only executables the owner lists in `allowed_native_executables` (empty by default), under Seatbelt plus an RSS watchdog, not Docker isolation. Guided preparation reads the selected source and dependency trees and may fetch lockfile-verified Linux build packages from registry.npmjs.org. Guided assessments need a fresh one-shot human approval. Evidence stays in the selected profile's plugin data; no telemetry or model calls.

name: thor-persona-stickers
description: Instant persona-aware emotion reaction stickers for Thor: stamps pre-baked chibi bases with comic captions in about 13 ms, and falls back to a pure Pillow vector path when the pool misses. Slash command /sticker and tool generate_persona_sticker return MEDIA:<path> PNG/WebP. Disclosure: writes sticker PNG/WebP files under the active profile at get_thor_home()/plugin-data/thor-persona-stickers; no third-party network, no telemetry, no self-update, no shell commands; ships pre-baked RGBA persona assets in-repo.

name: thor-pets-all
description: Browse every pet installed for this Thor profile in its own desktop pane (thumbnails, search, click-to-adopt), plus a read-only list_pets tool for the agent.

name: thor-phone
description: Let your Thor agent place real phone calls for you with explicit approval. It shows a brief card and dials only after you reply "call" (or tap Call), says it is an AI in the first sentence of every call, relays mid-call questions to you in chat with a suggested answer, and reports one clean result (what was agreed, confirmation number, duration, cost) plus the transcript. Disclosure — places outbound PSTN calls through your own Twilio account (costs money; a web-phone mode needs no telephony account), streams call audio to OpenAI Realtime, runs a small FastAPI bridge that must be reachable at your PUBLIC_BASE_URL (binds 0.0.0.0 when a hosting PORT is set), and stores call logs and text transcripts in plugin data (SQLite); calls dial only after a human approval, only to numbers on your allowlist, with emergency and premium numbers blocked; card, address, ID, bank, email and phone details are shared with the callee only with per-call consent, CVV, passwords and one-time codes never; no audio recording, no telemetry, no self-updater, no credential-file reads.

name: thor-phone-control
description: Preview of a phone-native Android companion with local MCP controls and optional voice. Disclosure — Once `control_enabled` is on, the phone tools tap, type and navigate on your paired Android phone without Thor' per-action approval prompt (payments, final message sends and calls still wait for a confirmation on the phone or a spoken "allow"). During voice turns the model can run short Python programs, after a spoken approval, in a seccomp-restricted child process (Linux/aarch64 only). The voice bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 behind a device token. Recognised speech goes to your configured model provider, and replies go to your configured Thor text-to-speech provider.

name: thor-phone-use
description: Operate your real iPhone or Android from any Thor (for example one on a Linux server) through Pinky on the Mac the phone is connected to. Approvals and hand-offs wait for the person and are announced in chat; screenshots come back as images. Disclosure — talks only to the Pinky URL you set (plain HTTP intended for a private network such as Tailscale), sending PINKY_TOKEN read through Thor's secret route; Pinky decides which apps the agent may use, gates risky steps behind the person's approval and never lets the agent type passwords or codes; screen text and screenshots reach your model provider like any tool output, and screenshots are saved under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-phone-use/screenshots/; while Pinky waits for an approval the tool posts one line to the chat and waits up to 10 minutes (cron runs return approval_pending at once); no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: thor-pickup
description: Pick up where you left off: up to 10 cards (5 by default) of unfinished work from your recent Thor chats, project folders and files, each with where you stopped and a one-click next step. Adapted from Herald OS by Luke (iamlukethedev), MIT. Disclosure — after explicit in-app consent (stored per profile), each Refresh reads recent chats from every profile's session store (read-only; profiles the user skips in Settings are never opened) and sends chat excerpts and metadata, project/file names and paths, git branch/changed-file names and recent commit subjects to the current profile's Thor LLM route (the auxiliary title-generation model, main provider unless configured); runs read-only git and, on macOS, Spotlight `mdfind`; never reads document contents; writes only $THOR_HOME/pickup/. The "Next step" button can submit a model-written prompt straight into the card's chat in one click. The optional install.sh, when asked, adds the plugin to every profile's plugins.enabled (undone exactly by uninstall.sh).

name: thor-pii
description: Uses local Presidio and spaCy to redact supported PII in outgoing user text. Disclosure — filters Chat Completions user messages and Responses user input locally; system prompts, tool outputs and tool-call arguments are preserved. Fail-open: detector errors, including a missing model, send original text. Install spaCy en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 separately from its GitHub release wheel in the Thor Python environment before enabling; Thor installs only the named PyPI dependencies. No runtime model downloads or remote detection.

name: thor-plant
description: A calm little garden for Thor Desktop that grows in real time. It sits above the app like the Thor pet, takes no layout space and can be dragged anywhere. Click a plant for a care wheel: water, prune (you choose which tip to cut, and the piece drops away), rotate, fertilize, repot, pick, sell, or ask Thor. Four species (leafy plant, fern, cactus, little tree) grow in their own ways, pruning shapes how each one branches, and neglect only pauses them. Care earns play coins, and a small shop sells more plants and fertilizer, up to six pots. Bugs land now and then and can be shooed away. Two agent tools let Thor check the garden and tend it when you ask. Original blue-ink artwork drawn in code. Reachable from the status bar, the command palette and the keyboard, and it speaks through the Thor pet when one is showing. Disclosure: no network requests, no background model calls and no background processes; Ask Thor submits one chat message only when you press it; coins are play money inside the plugin; the garden is kept in Desktop plugin storage and in plugin-data/thor-plant/data.db; the plugin adds its own floating element to the page (Thor has no SDK area for one) and removes it on unload, without reading or changing core markup.

name: thor-plex-music
description: Mini-Plexamp for Thor Desktop: statusbar player for your Plex music library — likes synced to Liked Songs, custom playlists with rename/delete, shuffle + repeat, sleep timer, queue editing, OS media keys. Needs only Plex Media Server. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — talks only to the Plex Media Server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:32400), sending your Plex token in the request URL as Plex requires; the token is stored in Desktop plugin storage, and the optional "Get token…" button reads the Plex `.LocalAdminToken` file you pick. Likes and playlist create/rename/delete write to your Plex server. No agent tools, no telemetry.

name: thor-plexus
description: Your local markdown vault as a note graph, file tree and tabbed editor in one Thor Desktop workspace tab, with Obsidian-style wikilinks, nested folder regions in the graph, link rewriting on rename, image and note embeds, and a ::vault chat link.
