Disclosure — reads and writes markdown files (and images for previews) only inside the one folder you grant, through Thor Desktop's folder-scoped file API (ctx.files); deletes go to the OS trash. No network calls unless you turn on loading of images that notes link from the web (off by default; the image's host then sees your IP address). No shell commands, background processes, telemetry, agent tools or stored credentials.

name: thor-plugin-chrome-profiles
description: Switch every Thor browser surface — browser_exec, the built-in browser_* tools, and browser_vault_* — to a named Chromium-family profile (Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Brave Origin, Edge), local or remote, over CDP. The endpoint is published as the active Thor profile's live CDP override, cleanup and the CDP supervisor are profile-scoped, and a browser the plugin launched is terminated on unload. Disclosure — a launched browser is user-visible and holds the user's live logged-in sessions; remote profiles connect to an endpoint the user already runs.

name: thor-plugin-dev
description: Thor Plugin Dev: build Thor plugins with Thor. A plugin-development skill plus two offline tools that scaffold a new plugin and lint it against the catalog rules before you submit. The thor-plugin-dev:thor-plugin-development skill covers manifest v2 and strict YAML, the ctx API, all 46 hooks, capabilities and isolation, dashboard and Desktop panes, testing, release and catalog submission, and lessons from catalog reviews, with a template plugin and catalog-entry and PR-body templates. hpd_scaffold(target_dir, name) copies the hello-thor template, which passes thor plugins validate and doctor --ci as-is, renames it, and adds a catalog entry and PR body stub; it refuses non-empty folders and never overwrites. hpd_check(path, catalog_entry?) is a read-only lint: strict YAML, manifest rules, provides_tools against the registered tools, a security preflight, static schema token cost, and catalog entry rules (sha, image hosts, category, subdir, at most 6 screenshots). Both tool schemas together cost 190 o200k tokens. It is for anyone writing a first Thor plugin or getting one ready for a catalog PR. To start, run thor plugins install thor-plugin-dev and thor plugins enable thor-plugin-dev, then ask: "Scaffold a Thor plugin called weather-now in ~/code/weather-now, then check it." Finish with thor plugins doctor <dir> --ci and thor plugins validate <dir> --install-deps. The same skill installs into other coding agents with npx skills add mojomast/thor-plugin-dev. Disclosure — `hpd_scaffold` creates files in any new or empty folder the model names (fixed template content only); `hpd_check` reads any folder or file the model names (read-only, never imports it); the user-run `thor hpd check <dir> --execute` imports and runs the target plugin's `register()` unsandboxed in the Thor process, so use it only on code you trust.

name: thor-plugin-gen
description: Generate, scaffold, and extend Thor Agent plugins from simple descriptions.

name: thor-plugin-guard
description: Static review of candidate Thor plugins; target code is never executed.

name: thor-plugin-netbox
description: NetBox change management: query DCIM/IPAM objects, build a reviewed field-level diff, apply with a journal and roll back.

name: thor-pokemon
description: A cozy pixel-art companion garden for Thor Desktop with three starters, nicknames, fetch, berries, XP, and optional evolution through all nine starter forms. The companion keeps you company on long turns, reacts quietly to failures, to what Thor is doing and to turns finishing in other chats, and lives through seasons with real day length and moon phases, offline showers, wild visitors it greets in character, old-friend cameos, keepsakes, milestones that leave a bench, a lantern and bunting in the garden, and a sapling that grows with the days. Reachable from the keyboard, the status bar and the command palette. Independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab community contributions; artwork is excluded from the source-code MIT license. Uses local plugin storage and read-only session activity, with no runtime network requests, credentials, backend, or model calls. Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

name: thor-portals
description: Stateful interactive tools with laptop-to-phone camera handoff and optional local Mac gesture control. Disclosure — `/portals start` launches a background local web companion (its own venv, built by a manual `scripts/setup.sh` that downloads hash-pinned Python/npm packages and a checksum-verified MediaPipe model from storage.googleapis.com); with a LAN IP it listens on all interfaces on port 8766 over unencrypted HTTP with token pairing; the optional source-built macOS app uses Camera and Accessibility permissions to move the cursor, click, scroll and switch apps from hand gestures.

name: thor-pr-studio
description: Review GitHub pull requests in Thor Desktop: inbox of your open PRs across repos, diffs with inline threads, line comments and reviews, private-repo images, watched PRs, one-click Send to Thor for any comment, and batch review: tick several PRs and Thor reviews them in parallel chats, handing its findings back to the panel as draft comments you accept or dismiss. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI (and `git remote get-url origin` in the open project), passing it Thor's process environment; GitHub writes only on explicit click, reviews confirmed, and Approve needs a separate explicit confirmation (UI and API); registers one agent tool, pr_studio_submit_findings, which only writes review findings to the plugin's own data directory (validated input, no network, no GitHub access); "Send to Thor", "Review in this chat" and "Review in new chats" submit prompts containing PR titles, branch names and comment text (written by other GitHub users, flagged to the agent as untrusted) to your chat immediately, and each new chat (up to 5 per batch) spends tokens on the model you pick; polls watched PRs every 60 s and Thor findings every 4-5 s while Desktop is open; no stored credentials, no telemetry. Independent codebase, not derived from gitthor.

name: thor-presenter
description: Present a selected JSON slide deck with the calling local Thor conversation as co-presenter. Disclosure — Requires a separately installed companion engine (Node, `npm ci` of `engine/` from this same repo commit) whose code runs outside the catalog-installed `plugin/` folder; uses undocumented Thor gateway client modules (`thor_cli.gateway_client`, `thor_cli.gateway_runtime`) to submit presentation prompts (deck text, speaker notes and, when `microphone: true`, transcribed speech from anyone near the mic) into your live conversation, which keeps its tools; serves the deck on 127.0.0.1 with no auth beyond same-origin cookies; sends reply text (and optional microphone audio) to ElevenLabs, billed to your key.

name: thor-proactive-radar
description: Proactive assistant: follows your mail, calendar, GitHub, scheduled jobs and your own chats with the agent as long-lived tasks (trips, purchases, work items, commitments), does the legwork itself and writes to you first, on the gateway platform you choose, only when something is yours to decide. Sending email always asks; paying, booking, deploying and merging never run on their own. Disclosure — runs a scheduler task inside the gateway and delegates bounded work to 'thor chat --oneshot' child processes (2 at a time, 100 a day by default) whose finished sessions it archives in the host session store; reaches mail and calendar only through the MCP servers or command-line tools you configure (gws, gog, the google-workspace skill's own script) and GitHub through gh, each started with a minimal environment; with Gmail push enabled, listens on 127.0.0.1:8666 (token + Google OIDC) and forwards to a host webhook route; reads the host session store (state.db), cron job outputs and the host memory provider; replies you send to its notices are passed to the chat agent with a task brief; `thor radar setup` writes its MCP allowlist into config.yaml only after you type yes; model fallback needs the llm.provider_override / llm.model_override capabilities Thor asks you to grant; stores tasks, bounded snippets, facts, a consent key and an audit log in THOR_HOME/radar/ with retention limits; two optional secrets read through the host secret scope; installed disabled and in shadow mode; no telemetry.

name: thor-profile-switcher
description: Composer profile picker with explicit context handoff into a new chat and verified single-folder project inheritance. Disclosure — reads focused session/project metadata; may read the live roster and transcript to verify empty sources, even for Start fresh. Copy context and Brief handoff store selected source text in a new target-profile session. No automatic submission or model call. Cross-gateway handoffs have no inherited project; source chat, composer drafts and profile configuration are not modified.

name: thor-project-stewardship
description: Durable project ownership and bounded initiative management for Thor fleets. Disclosure — a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a project's saved rules, decisions and facts to turns of bots assigned to that project; objective checks run allowlisted local programs only at autonomy level 3+ and GitHub objectives shell out to your own `gh api`; it creates and edits Thor Kanban tasks through Thor' internal kanban modules (title/body/tenant written directly to kanban.db), reads other Thor profiles' project registries (projects.db, read-only, profile names and project counts only) to hint where existing projects live during onboarding, keeps its own SQLite DB under `<Thor home>/plugin-data/thor-dockyard/`, and its optional HTTP API (`/stewardship/v1`, 127.0.0.1) stays closed until you set a bearer token.

name: thor-proof
description: Deterministically verify agent task outcomes and persist auditable evidence reports.

name: thor-proton
description: Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a Thor Agent, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `thor proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by Thor's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot Thor cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

name: thor-psfn-avatar
description: 3D VRM VTuber and companion avatar overlay for Thor Desktop and the Web Dashboard (Three.js + @pixiv/three-vrm, default Nous-Girl VRM with an on-demand catalog of DeepSeek-chan, Claude and Claude Suit, 42 baked ARDY humanoid motion clips, 28 GoEmotions mood performances, text-driven lip-sync that patches no host audio, eye/head gaze, touch reactions, and optional PSFN Lite continuous emotional-state bridge). Disclosure — stores avatar state and user-uploaded .vrm/.glb models under ~/.thor/plugin-data/thor-psfn-avatar/ and caches VRM models in browser IndexedDB; fetches models on demand from raw.githubusercontent.com at pinned commits (Desktop verifies each by SHA-256 before caching; the Web Dashboard loads the same commit-pinned URLs without a digest check): the default Nous-Girl from CGIC-AI/nous-girl-vrm at 70bfc01c3bbc105267612f94486e0e7ee1b5a7d6 (SHA-256 34c72ebaf068f3d692c29e5b1878b42e0039f63a2b0679aab18bb365b4abc275), and when selected DeepSeek-chan from tegnike/deepseek-chan-vrm at 3aceb037df7a8b8126efea89d3a75664d1af868d (SHA-256 9fa455e48ee2271dc7c2b62f2f2edcd47709406ca89067b6f544979589958f42) and claude.vrm / claude_suit.vrm from SkyeShark/eidoverse-video at 404a00e7db3068af51bd914d61e608e6b8dc9b82 (SHA-256 883eb1d6c63c7409e1cbebb335509af346e92d046c4c9916ebc7695da4c64073 and 7be6286215c0d7e4251633ec741d9f5bde943dc635f05a312ca7d1b45bceaa5d); when the local FastAPI plugin route is absent, fetches baked motion clips from raw.githubusercontent.com/CGIC-AI/thor-psfn-avatar at pinned commit 7b9a7f7f677b2fd25ed889b56e5ec83055202463; when psfn_lite_bridge is enabled and ~/.thor/psfn-lite.json configures a loopback garden endpoint, queries GET <garden.url>/api/lite/overview on localhost using the profile's secret scope; the transform_llm_output hook removes the plugin's own ::avatar{} directive lines from replies (strip_directives, on by default); no shell commands, background daemons, or telemetry.

name: thor-pubky
description: Setup helper for managed Pubky agents. The launcher syncs agent state, including conversation database snapshots and portable configuration, to your remote Pubky homeserver.

name: thor-quest
description: Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real Thor Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local Thor data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (THOR_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <thor_home>/thor-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local Thor backend.

name: thor-quote-to-chat
description: Codex-style quote cards for Thor Desktop: select text outside an input and press Add to chat; the excerpt becomes a removable card above the composer while your question stays a separate draft. On send the quotes are prepended once as Markdown blockquotes (composer.middleware). Quotes are scoped per chat, several can be collected and removed one by one, a busy-agent send goes through host.composer.submit with the quote attached, and a rejected send gives the quote back. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, Python middleware or env vars. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; adds its own button element to document.body; reads the live draft through host.composer.getDraft; keeps quotes in memory only. No network calls, no credentials, no files, no telemetry.

name: thor-r0b0t-vibecad
description: Profile-driven FDM CAD: executes trusted build123d workspace models or prepares a local single-shell STL, checks printer fit, renders depth-tested full and detail views, and writes geometry handoffs. Bambu adapters cover X2D and P2S; native process projects, live AMS binding and print dispatch are not produced. Meshy is an optional separate plugin; its paid service calls are not made by vibeCAD. CAD libraries require a separately bootstrapped Python 3.12/3.13 environment. Disclosure: reads/writes workspace files and runs trusted Python in a local subprocess. Agent execution requires approval of the final script path and bytes; direct runtime calls bypass the agent gate. The subprocess environment is minimized, not a sandbox: approved code can access files, credentials and the network. Approval binds only the top-level script. Internal Thor approval and interrupt APIs may change and produce catalog rule 9 warnings. The plugin itself makes no runtime network calls or telemetry.

name: thor-reading
description: Discover public feeds and GitHub projects; read articles, PDFs and YouTube transcripts. On request, source text is sent to the configured Thor model for summaries and Q&A. Disclosure — the reader fetches the feeds and pages you open directly from their sites (default feeds: hnrss.org, lobste.rs, rss.arxiv.org, simonwillison.net, openai.com), searches api.github.com without a token, reads YouTube captions through yt-dlp, and, if the optional faster-whisper extra is installed, downloads a Whisper model from Hugging Face to transcribe videos without captions; source text is sent to your configured Thor model only when you ask for a summary or answer.

name: thor-receipts
description: Deterministic evidence for explicit file, native test-result, and website checks. Preserves immutable as-of receipts with failed, verified, or unverified outcomes. Disclosure — reads selected workspace files (refusing paths Thor' read denylist blocks and workspaces inside the Thor home), GETs explicitly scoped URLs, observes and stores armed matching native terminal command/output evidence, and writes local profile-scoped state and exports; receipt handlers never execute commands or bypass approvals; imports agent.file_safety.get_read_block_error (fails closed if unavailable); no credentials, telemetry, model calls or paid service; standalone opt-in offline scripts use Thor dispatch internals and run synthetic test commands and are not imported by the plugin; not a sandbox or signed attestation.

name: thor-rehearsal
description: Rehearse SQLite customer merges, inspect exact changes and conflicting identities, then apply human-approved verified plans. Disclosure — reads only the SQLite databases you connect (via /rehearsal add or the Desktop/dashboard page) and sends their customer and order rows to the configured model when the agent inspects them; the agent can only rehearse on an in-memory copy, and the real database is changed only by /rehearsal apply in a local CLI/TUI/Desktop session or the Apply button on the plugin page, after you confirm the exact plan digest. Plans and receipts are stored in the plugin's data folder.

name: thor-reliability
description: Architecture-aware reliability testing for agent repositories: discover real usage datasets, generate scenarios, review them independently, execute configured targets and inspect evidence in Thor web and Desktop dashboards. Freeze audited benchmarks and compare regressions across code changes, with baseline references for native Thor memory. Disclosure — Sends source excerpts from the repository you point it at and sampled public dataset messages to your active Thor model, queries huggingface.co and zenodo.org (HF_TOKEN only to Hugging Face), clones the supplied HTTPS repositories into profile plugin data, and starts a detached background worker per campaign; execution is off by default, and when enabled and approved through Thor' prompt it runs generated evaluator tests, model-authored reference actions and the target agent (a cloned Thor) on this host outside any sandbox, sending the target API key to your configured target base_url, while OpenHands/DeerFlow targets run in a network-disabled Docker image you build.

name: thor-remote-hands
description: One Thor brain on a server, hands on your own Mac. Over plain OpenSSH (e.g. on a tailnet), with no agent, memory or model on the Mac, it adds six tools: mac_computer_use drives the Mac's screen with the same actions, element indices, hard blocks and verify ladder as the built-in computer_use (through cua-driver, in the background), while computer_use keeps driving the server's own screen in the same chat; mac_shell runs commands; mac_file, mac_patch and mac_search read, edit and search code; mac_process runs dev servers in a private tmux server. Disclosure — runs commands, reads and writes files, takes screenshots and sends input on the Mac named by the ssh_host setting, using the system ssh client and the key named in your SSH config (the plugin never reads, stores or copies keys). Every call goes through Thor's approval gate with its own mac_* keys: commands, typed text and set_value are approved per exact text by default; credential stores, startup files, LaunchAgents, writes into .git or outside the configured project folders, and sensitive commands prompt every time; a pre_tool_call hook sends other tools' calls that mention the Mac or this plugin's code to a single-use approval; unattended runs fail closed (all of this while Thor approvals are on, not in YOLO mode). No third-party network calls or telemetry. Background processes: an SSH ControlMaster for up to 30 s after the last call (socket under $THOR_HOME/cache/ssh), one `ssh … cua-driver mcp` session per chat while mac_computer_use is in use, and mac_process jobs in `tmux -L thor` on the Mac.

name: thor-replicate
description: Native Replicate backends for image generation, video, transcription and speech, with user-configured models and schema-validated mappings. Disclosure: paid predictions send prompts, text and uploaded audio to Replicate and its model providers; outputs are downloaded into the active profile cache. Requires a Replicate API token. Video defaults to Pruna P-Video's 5-second 720p draft preview, without audio. No streaming voice or native image editing.

name: thor-rescue
description: Keeps your agent from breaking Thor, and says what really went wrong. Refuses agent tool calls that would delete or hand-edit Thor's own data (sessions, state.db, memories, skills, settings, profiles, keys) and names the supported command instead; sends edits to settings, SOUL.md or memory files to Thor's approval prompt with a snapshot first (/rescue undo); and when a reply fails or quietly comes from a backup, adds one plain line per attempt with the real cause and the fix (thor726/thor-agent#144562, #147620). /rescue in every surface, plus a Desktop status chip and pane. Disclosure — reads tool-call arguments (command, path, code) to decide; writes plugin-data/thor-rescue/rescue.db (event kind, short description, up to 200 characters of the command, provider/model/status of failed model calls, Rescue's explanation; about 2,000 events kept); copies files a risky change would touch (config.yaml, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/, cron/, plugins/, state.db up to 300 MB) into plugin-data/thor-rescue/snapshots/ before the change (newest 30 kept, so up to 30 state.db copies on disk) and writes them back on /rescue undo (for state.db only missing conversations come back, through Thor's SessionDB export_session/import_sessions; folders are merged; only inside the Thor folders); never opens, copies, moves or overwrites .env, auth.json or the other credential stores Thor lists; after a failed model call that ends a turn, a short-lived background thread posts the note to the same conversation with ctx.post_message and edits it if a later attempt answers; never auto-approves (in YOLO mode Thor itself approves the ask-first edits).

name: thor-resetwatch
description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Thor Python interpreter located via THOR_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the Thor installer's managed venv (THOR_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the Thor .env (through Thor's get_secret helper, else read directly), the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; Thor's saved OAuth logins (the credential pool through Thor's read_credential_pool helper, else auth.json directly, and THOR_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through Thor get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. For Codex, a 401 or 403 is retried once with another saved login for the same account. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL (honored only for https grok.com / x.ai hosts), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under THOR_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.

name: thor-rich-ui
description: Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop

name: thor-roam
description: Encrypted, host-scoped sync of the Thor Agent home between your own machines: an AES-256-GCM sealed bundle of the shared home (config.yaml minus host-scoped keys, SOUL.md, memories, skills) is pushed to storage you own — an S3 or Cloudflare R2 bucket, a private git repository, or a local directory — and pulled back on another machine through a plan-first, journaled, backed-up, roll-back-able install. Secrets (.env, auth.json, API keys) never sync; pulls apply only on explicit user action (the agent cannot apply by default); conflicts are detected with a signed compare-and-swap head, never merged. Every pushed version stays recoverable (thor roam history / restore). Works across profiles and bots: one store carries every profile (each profile's identity, SOUL, memories, skills and shared config), from any profile context; a profile can be excluded per device. Opt-in, off by default: a read-only, encrypted archive of session transcripts (exported with thor sessions export --redact) that other devices can list and read, and cron job definitions (pulled jobs land paused until thor cron resume). Disclosure — network calls only to the user-configured store (boto3 for S3/R2, the git CLI for the git backend) and only when a roam command, tool, slash verb or session hook actually runs; the git backend also runs git as local subprocesses with an allowlisted environment, the opt-in session archive runs thor sessions export once per profile, and thor roam auto runs thor config set, all as bounded local subprocesses; the shared ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY and S3 credentials come only through Thor's secret scope, never from files; session hooks run bounded daemon threads; no telemetry, no self-update.

name: thor-room
description: Thor Room washes untrusted web, email, file and tool output before Thor reads it: deterministically, with model help for semantic attacks, and with receipts you can audit. Layer 1 (always, local, stdlib-only) strips zero-width/bidi/control characters, ANSI escapes and hidden-HTML payloads, and masks leaked secrets (AWS/GitHub/GitLab/Slack/OpenAI/Google keys, JWTs, private-key blocks, password=/secret= assignments). Layer 2 runs only when Layer 1 flags something: a host-model reviewer via ctx.llm.complete_structured, your active Thor model - no provider/model override, no extra API key - 20s timeout, 800 tokens, fail-open to Layer 1. Every change yields a local JSONL Trust Receipt (SHA-256, rule IDs, counts, reviewer verdict, never raw content): trust_receipt shows what changed, trust_report exports Markdown. Disclosure - reads only tool-output text; no network beyond the user's own provider call via ctx.llm; no shell, no background processes, no telemetry; no credentials required (requires_env is empty); writes solely to <THOR_HOME>/thor-room/receipts.jsonl (hashes/counts only, local); fails open, never blocks or breaks the tool loop. Disclosure — rewrites the result of every tool (web, email, MCP, read_file, terminal, skills) before the model sees it: it strips hidden HTML/control characters, deletes phrases that look like injected instructions, masks secret-looking values and adds an `[UNTRUSTED ...]` header, so files read through it may differ from what is on disk; when a rule fires it sends up to 8,000 characters of the unmasked output to your active Thor model for review (an extra model call, up to 20 s) and may replace the result with the reviewer's re-washed text; receipts in `<THOR_HOME>/thor-room/receipts.jsonl` hold hashes, rule IDs and counts plus the reviewer's verdict, quoted snippets and up to 2,000 characters of its reply; no other network, shell, background work or telemetry.

name: thor-ros
description: Drive and observe ROS / ROS 2 robots from Thor over rosbridge: list topics, services and nodes, read odometry, grab camera frames for the vision model, publish, call services, drive and e-stop, with every tool call gated by a pre_tool_call safety interlock (speed and duration limits, optional geofence, topic and service write allowlists, a latching e-stop, every blocked call logged). Ships a built-in mock robot (2D sim with a camera and a red cone) so it runs with no ROS at all, a bundled safety skill, and an optional read-only dashboard tab. Disclosure — network: in rosbridge mode it opens one unencrypted websocket to the rosbridge server you configure (default localhost:9090), lazily on first use; mock mode (default) makes no network connections. Files: camera snapshots, a blocked-call audit log, the e-stop latch and the last pose under the plugin data dir. No credentials. One dependency, websocket-client (already in Thor's lock). With a real robot attached the agent can physically move it; limits default to 0.5 m/s, 1.0 rad/s and 5 s per command and are enforced on this plugin's tools outside the model, but they do not stop other tools (terminal, code execution) from reaching the rosbridge server or changing the limits in config.yaml.

name: thor-routines
description: A minimal Routines page in Thor Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

name: thor-rss
description: Read RSS and Atom feeds and discuss articles in Thor Desktop. Disclosure — feeds and full articles are fetched with curl through the gateway's shell.exec on the connected Thor host (public-IPv4 SSRF guard); opt-in AI grading sends article excerpts to your configured model and creates THOR_HOME/skills/rss-importance-grading/SKILL.md if missing; opt-in image loading fetches publisher images directly from Desktop.

name: thor-rustpush-imessage
description: Local-only iMessage platform plugin backed by a launchd-supervised OpenBubbles RustPush sidecar over a same-user Unix socket.

name: thor-salespilot
description: An approval-gated sales desk inside Thor: collect companies from quoted page evidence, qualify them against your ICP, draft the first email, and send one email only after you pick "send" in the host approval prompt — then keep a customer timeline, hot prospects and follow-up dates. Sends nothing on its own, and a refusal, bounce, do-not-contact or archive stops a draft that was written before it. Eleven salespilot_* tools plus a Desktop workspace (Customers, Hot Prospects, Settings, CSV import). Disclosure — fetches the public web pages you or the agent point it at (http/https only, private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses refused); network mail traffic goes only to the SMTP and IMAP servers you configure, with mailbox credentials from Thor secrets (SALESPILOT_SMTP_USERNAME / SALESPILOT_SMTP_PASSWORD); each email is sent only after you choose "send" in the Thor prompt (daily cap 5); lead data lives in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/thor-salespilot/; no telemetry.

name: thor-sanctuary
description: Watch your Thor Agent work: five animated characters wake up when Thor uses their tools, in two illustrated worlds (Olympus by default, the Clearing), in Thor Desktop and the web dashboard, in English or French. The guard barks, with a bubble saying why, on tool and provider errors, silent fallbacks to a backup model, loops (same tool, same arguments, 4 times in a turn), heavy turns, a daily budget overrun and permissions waiting for an answer; a daily journal shows turns, tools, where the work came from, tokens and estimated cost per model hour by hour, with a shareable image of the day and a sped-up replay. Disclosure — observer hooks only (they never block, change or answer anything); records tool names, turn times, platform and scheduled-task names, counters, model names with token counts, the short description Thor gives for a pending approval (never the command) and one-letter event codes with their time for the replay (never messages, arguments, results, error texts, file paths or ids) under plugin-data/thor-sanctuary/, files older than 2 days removed; a hash of each tool call is kept in memory for the current turn only to spot loops; read-only dashboard routes serve that activity and the plugin's own theme and images; cost is estimated with Thor's own agent.usage_pricing module (a private import the validator may warn on); no network calls of its own, no shell commands, no background process, no secrets or .env access, no telemetry and no self-updater; the panorama runs in a sandboxed frame that receives everything by postMessage; Thor Desktop may show native notifications (at most one per kind every 2 minutes); the daily budget is stored by Thor Desktop or the browser.

name: thor-screen
description: Pick what to watch from your own Jellyfin library using real watch history, play movies and saved scenes on your Chromecast with receiver-verified status, send YouTube links to the TV, and play camera rock-paper-scissors against Thor. Network calls: your Jellyfin server, your Chromecast (Cast protocol, TCP 8009), YouTube on the TV, www.gstatic.com (receiver SDK), your own optional game service, and optional YouTube Data API. Listeners: a temporary expiring movie relay while something plays, and an opt-in two-container game service you deploy yourself. No telemetry. Secrets only via Thor; no .env reads. Camera frames never leave the phone. Disclosure — while something plays, tv_play opens a temporary listener on your configured cast_relay_bind that serves only the selected Jellyfin item at a random, expiring URL; anyone on your LAN who learns that URL can fetch that one item until it expires. The optional rock-paper-scissors service you deploy yourself runs behind a public Cloudflare quick tunnel.

name: thor-secret-gate
description: Stop agent-drafted secrets from leaving the machine — deterministic scan, fail-closed gate, receipts.

name: thor-security
description: Security review for a local repository. The agent builds a threat model, splits the code into chunks and reviews them with parallel subagents, checks each candidate against the code and traces whether an attacker can reach it. Reports keep evidence, rejected candidates and coverage gaps, export to Markdown, JSON, CSV and SARIF, and get a Security page in Thor Desktop. Standard, deep and diff modes; `/security` slash command and `thor security-review` CLI. Optional "Run tests to confirm findings" writes small reproductions and runs them in a temporary copy of the repository; testing a running app needs a per-scan grant (one origin, one hour, 200 requests) that agent tools cannot issue. Apache-2.0 (parts adapted from Apache-2.0 source, see NOTICE). Disclosure — the first scan downloads a pinned osv-scanner release from GitHub (about 55 MB, refused unless its SHA-256 matches) into the plugin data folder; package names and versions go to api.osv.dev and api.deps.dev, declared runtime versions to endoflife.date (`THOR_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CHECK=off` disables this). Test confirmation runs repository code as your user in a temporary copy with credential-looking environment variables removed; that is not a sandbox. The configured model provider receives the code under review; scan data stays in the profile's plugin data folder. With `plugins.entries.thor-security.allow_gateway_injection` turned on (off by default), the plugin queues one "Continue security scan" message into the chat when a scan stalls, at most 3 times without progress. No Python dependencies.

name: thor-security-audit
description: Approval-gated local security audit for Thor Agent using Gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, and Semgrep CE.

name: thor-security-plugin
description: Check the security headers of a public URL and look up sourced penetration testing provider data through two remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no keys): check_security_headers on penetrationtestservices.com, and list_providers and get_provider on pentestcompare.com. Bundles the check-security-headers workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; the URL you check is sent to penetrationtestservices.com, which fetches it with one GET per redirect. The pts server also has request_pentest, which sends a contact request to Excession Labs and needs an agent key the plugin does not hold. Both servers are marked untrusted, so Thor asks before any call that is not read-only. The tool set is served by the remote servers at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: thor-self-healing-context
description:
Intercepts runtime errors and dynamically patches the context window 
using local SQLite FTS5 memory for zero-downtime recovery.

name: thor-sentinel
description: Deterministic runtime circuit breaker and local execution auditor. Disclosure — blocks any turn whose new user message contains a credential-shaped string; refuses the third consecutive identical tool call (including legitimate repeated polls) until `/sentinel reset`; redacts credential-shaped text in every tool result and truncates each result to 4000 characters / 100 lines before the model sees it; stores audit events (redacted 200-char argument previews) in `<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/thor-sentinel/sentinel_audit.db`, falling back to memory-only or no auditing; no network calls, subprocesses or telemetry.

name: thor-seo
description: Native Thor port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped thor_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the thor_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the Thor host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `thor seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in Thor plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active Thor profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.

name: thor-session-diff
description: Persistent session file diffs, run comparisons, and individual edit history in Thor Desktop.

name: thor-session-reset-policy
description: Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

name: thor-session-signal
description: SDK-backed Working labels and titlebar navigation for visible Thor Desktop sessions. Native row layout stays under Thor control. Input/Done deferred pending SDK support. Desktop-only; no tools, hooks, middleware, direct network calls, or env vars.

name: thor-session-warmer
description: Opt-in bounded idle prompt warming for explicitly allowlisted OpenAI-compatible text-chat endpoints. Sends potentially billable requests; no tool execution or conversation writes. Does not support Codex/Responses or native Anthropic. Authenticated endpoints use optional THOR_SESSION_WARMER_API_KEY.

name: thor-sfx-forge
description: Offline seeded WAV sound-effects generation and QA. Writes WAV files, a manifest, and a retained lock file inside a configured workspace root. No network calls or subprocess execution. Runs in the Thor plugin host. The CLI, but not the registered tools, accepts an explicit --root.

name: thor-shaperotator
description: Parametric mechanical CAD and linear-static FEA for Thor, with a claims checker: stress, deflection, safety factor or mass the agent quotes is checked against the analyses it actually ran, and a verification footer is appended to the reply. One toolset drives FreeCAD (headless, cross-platform) or Autodesk Inventor (Windows, COM); every feature reports a volume/topology delta; FEA (FreeCAD FEM + Gmsh + CalculiX) reports equilibrium, mesh convergence and an AS/NZS-aware yield safety factor, and a design sweep finds the lightest part meeting a target SF; drawings on both backends to the standard the user picks once per chat (AS 1100, ISO, ASME, DIN, BS 8888, JIS, GB), with PDF export gated on a QA check. Desktop pane: live 3D view, click a face to reference it in chat, stress map, evidence log. On Inventor, cad_native exposes 100+ inventor-forge tools (sheet metal + flat-pattern DXF, assemblies, interference, BOM, materials, mass properties, stress/modal analysis in Inventor's own Stress Analysis feeding the same evidence log). Disclosure — starts FreeCAD's Python as a worker process (which runs Gmsh and CalculiX) and, on Windows, can drive Autodesk Inventor over COM; cad_python runs Python inside the CAD app only after the user approves each call; reads files the user names; writes models, renders, FEA folders and exports in the session's job folder, and any write outside it (or a save over a file opened from elsewhere) goes through a Thor approval prompt naming the path; child processes (FreeCAD worker, MCP servers, headless browser for the PDF report) get a minimal environment without provider keys; appends a verification footer to assistant replies that quote engineering figures; Inventor stress/modal analysis (no API exists) takes over the mouse and keyboard for about half a minute, only after the user approves each call; no network, telemetry or credentials. Inventor backend: inventor-forge (MIT, same author), vendored.

name: thor-shortcuts
description: Share to Thor from any iPhone or Android app, ask Thor with Siri and hear the answer, or photograph a receipt, whiteboard or document as a task. iOS Shortcuts and Android HTTP Shortcuts call one token-protected endpoint; replies return in the HTTP response and are forwarded to your Telegram home channel (a Siri question only when it says "save the answer" or times out). Setup is three steps: `thor shortcuts pair` prints a QR code, the iPhone "Thor Setup" shortcut scans it into iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/thor.json, and the shared shortcuts (which contain no token) read it. Disclosure: off until SHORTCUTS_TOKEN (32+ random chars; weak or placeholder tokens are refused) is set and the plugin is enabled; then the gateway runs an HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8645 (non-loopback bind needs SHORTCUTS_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND=true) that you expose through your own HTTPS tunnel or proxy. A single bearer token is the only authentication and every request acts as the owner. Requests run agent turns on shared, untrusted content; by default each action gets only the toolsets it needs (web, vision, plus memory for remember and cronjob for remind/ask; events get cronjob/todo only; no terminal, file, code execution, browser or MCP servers), enforced by toolsets_for_source and by a pre_tool_call hook that only acts in shortcuts sessions: it blocks any other tool, limits cronjob to create/list and makes created reminder jobs run once with no tools. `@file:`/`@url:`-style references in shared text are defanged (Thor core would otherwise inline local files before the agent runs). Forwarded replies show URLs as code (no Telegram link previews). SHORTCUTS_TOOL_PROFILE=full opts into the platform's full toolset (then shared content can reach the terminal, directly or through cron jobs). Approvals are not bypassed. Uploads are cached in Thor' media cache; sessions are stored in Thor' session database; replies are sent to the configured platform's home channel. Registers the CLI command `thor shortcuts pair`, which prints a QR code containing the server URL and SHORTCUTS_TOKEN (optional 0600 PNG; token text only with --show-token) and may query the local cloudflared metrics endpoint on 127.0.0.1:20241-20245 to find a quick-tunnel URL. On the phone the token is stored in plain text in iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/thor.json (synced to iCloud; end-to-end encrypted only with Advanced Data Protection) or, with manual setup, inside the shortcut.

name: thor-sidepulse
description: SidePulse lifecycle status backend; Desktop focus tracking requires the separate companion in the linked setup guide. Disclosure — forwards event names, a hashed agent id, the raw session_id and tool names to a local AF_UNIX socket and a 0600 jsonl log; no network egress.

name: thor-skill-router
description: Removes the always-on skill catalog from every Chat Completions request and injects a short fused shortlist instead. Ranks partly by the skills you loaded for similar prompts in past sessions. Disclosure — On Chat Completions requests this plugin removes Thor's skill catalog from the system prompt and appends a per-turn skill shortlist as a trailing system message. Your newest message, plus up to 10,000 characters of your earlier messages, is sent to the embeddings and rerank endpoints you configure (loopback by default; any non-loopback host must use https). The query text is written to the plugin log. Its index, skill path cache, display record and learned-association database live under ~/.cache/thor-skill-router, shared by every profile. The optional association backfill command reads ~/.thor/state.db read-only and stores normalised prompt terms. The optional bundled embeddings server and its systemd unit are started manually by you.

name: thor-slash-router
description: Jev-powered routing for misspelled, shortened, and meaning-based slash commands in the Thor Desktop composer. Preserves drafts when unsure. Requires a TypeSafe API key; every non-exact lookup uses paid TypeSafe API usage. Disclosure — every non-exact slash token is sent through the plugin's local backend to api.typesafe.ai (paid, your TYPESAFE_API_KEY) together with the Desktop command catalog (names and descriptions), any prior route, up to 8 saved correction explanations and any clarification you type into its panel; message arguments and conversation content are not sent; the backend reads THOR_HOME/.env only to check whether TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set.

name: thor-slots
description: A grimy little slot machine pet for Thor Desktop, drawn as low-resolution pixel art. It sits in the bottom right corner above the app, like the Thor pet, takes no layout space and can be dragged anywhere. Drag its lever down and let go, or click the machine, to spin a five by three screen for play coins. Three in a line pays across, down or diagonally on 20 lines, so about three pulls in four pay something, and a line of sevens pays 100 times the bet. Bet any whole number of coins. A piggy bank beside it keeps coins safe and pays 1% interest an hour, worked out from saved timestamps, and its panel also holds the pay table and the sound switch. Reachable from the status bar, the command palette and the keyboard. Disclosure: coins are play money inside the plugin and cannot be bought, sold or cashed out; no network requests, no model calls and no background processes; spins use the browser's random numbers and the published pay table; sound effects are CC0 clips by Kenney built into the bundle, played only after a click or key press; the game is kept in Desktop plugin storage on this machine; the plugin adds its own floating element to the page (Thor has no SDK area for one) and removes it on unload, without reading or changing core markup.

name: thor-snapcompact
description: Snapcompact context engine: archives conversation history as dense bitmap PNG frames that vision models read back at ~1/3 the token cost.

name: thor-snitchboard
description: A dashboard tab that turns OpenSnitch connection evidence into plain-language findings mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, with a hash chain that makes alteration of stored history detectable. Thor can tell you what it did and application-layer tooling can record which model requests it made; neither tells you what the machine actually connected to. The tab answers that from the firewall's own record of outbound connections and the process behind each one. It shows a summary of connections, denials, unique processes and destinations, AI traffic and unattributed traffic; an hourly coverage strip that renders a missing hour as a gap rather than as a quiet hour; findings carrying severity, confidence, the ATT&CK technique and tactic, the literal records behind the finding and one concrete next step; regular-interval destinations stated with both the benign and the malicious reading, with services on the configured expected list labelled rather than flagged; novel destinations ranked by rarity against prior runs; activity by AI process and by configured agent account; a per-run connection chart with a run that collected nothing drawn as a marked gap instead of a zero; byte volume where the firewall's connection tracking measured it; the daemon's reported state, the rules in force and open sockets; and an integrity panel that recomputes every link on request. Addresses, host names, hardware addresses, home directories and process arguments are masked by default, a deliberate control reveals them, and that control can be switched off entirely in settings. Until real runs exist the tab shows clearly labelled demonstration records built from addresses reserved for documentation (RFC 5737, RFC 3849, RFC 2606), so every panel is visible without installing OpenSnitch. Collection and viewing are kept apart on purpose: the half that runs inside Thor never opens the firewall database, and the optional reference collector is run by the machine owner's own account, never by Thor, which suits setups where Thor runs under a different account from the person who owns the machine. The integrity claim is scoped deliberately: the chain attests to the order of stored records and to the digest each full record held when it was sealed, so a record that has since been trimmed keeps a shortened summary the chain does not cover, and that summary is a derived analysis aid rather than evidence. The chain makes alteration detectable; it does not prove what the network did, and anyone able to rewrite every record could recompute it. Disclosure - registers no tools, no hooks and no middleware, and needs no environment variable. Its only surface is the dashboard tab and seven GET routes served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/thor-snitchboard/ (health, settings, runs, runs/latest, runs/{run_id}, series, verify), which require the dashboard's auth ticket. It writes nothing to disk at all. It makes no network request, opens no socket, loads no external font, script or image, executes no subprocess, no shell command and no systemd unit, starts no background process, holds no credential and no OAuth client, and sends no telemetry. It reads three things: the run records in the directory named by its runs_dir setting, which may sit outside the plugin's own data directory and which the operator chooses; a settings.json in its plugin data directory when Thor's own settings are unavailable; and the plugin's settings from Thor configuration through the read-only helper thor_cli.config.load_config_readonly, with plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir for the data path. Both of those imports are guarded and fall back rather than raise. Record files are opened with O_NOFOLLOW, symbolic links in the runs directory are skipped so nothing outside it can be reached through one, no value supplied by a client ever reaches the filesystem as a path, a file is never read past the schema's size cap, and every response is bounded in both row count and serialised bytes. Record data is rendered through React element construction with no innerHTML anywhere, because process and host names from the firewall flow through that code. Python standard library only; FastAPI comes from Thor and no third-party package is added.

name: thor-sonic-ui
description: Design procedural sounds, assign them to Thor Desktop interactions, compose layered loops, and export WAV, JSON or TypeScript. Local synthesis; optional configured-model drafts. Disclosure — the inject_sonic_hooks tool rewrites .jsx/.tsx files (with backups under <project>/.sonic-ui-backups) and synthesize_ui_soundscape writes a new TypeScript file at a model-chosen path, each only after Thor's approval prompt and never inside the Thor home or install; injection runs a bundled Node parser with a minimal environment; the optional "Generate sound" action sends your description and patch to the active profile's configured model.

name: thor-soniox
description: Native BYOK Soniox text-to-speech and asynchronous speech-to-text providers with configurable languages and voices, automatic STT language detection, and Thor voice-bubble support. Disclosure — TTS sends reply text and synthesis settings to tts-rt.soniox.com; STT uploads audio, optional language hints, and optional prompt context to api.soniox.com, then best-effort deletes the remote transcription and uploaded file. SONIOX_API_KEY is resolved through Thor' active-profile secret scope. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, or stored credentials.

name: thor-speech
description: Give your agent the voice it deserves. Guided TTS and STT setup for Thor, with voice search and previews, model switching, testing, and native spoken replies across supported providers. Access 80+ speech models through a single API key with the AllModels router.

name: thor-ssh
description: Manage SSH connections and remote workspaces in Thor Desktop.

name: thor-stage
description: A multi-profile terminal bot room for Thor with one shared transcript, profile lens tabs, and public @name routing (`@everyone` and `@all` are not room addresses). Profiles load lazily; due cron jobs wake them, and public profile speech and cron notifications are mirrored from non-default profiles' state.db files into the room. Disclosure — joins the profiles you choose into one room: every room message (including other profiles' replies) is sent to each addressed profile's agent session, and a bot reply containing `@name` may wake a cold profile and start a turn (up to 3 rounds / 10 messages per discussion); starts a local gateway session for each profile in the room, saves the room transcript in plaintext under the Thor state directory, and needs a one-time `npm install` of its Node dependencies (ink, react, string-width). The feed excludes tool calls, failed turns, private user prompts, assistant (pass) rows, and duplicate room rows.

name: thor-standing
description: Earned trust for Thor workers. Each profile has a level (L0 read, L1 draft, L2 act, L3 trusted) that decides which tool calls need the owner's approval, and a local record of checks that held up and checks that did not. A worker can always report on its own card (block, comment, request review, heartbeat), but it cannot mark the task done on its word: kanban_complete is blocked until the task has a passing standing_proof in the same session, and Standing runs that check itself (owner-scoped file, owner-allowlisted HTTP URL, or exact owner-allowlisted read-only command). Ten clean passes raise a level (capped at L1 automatically; L2 needs the owner's explicit opt-in); one failed check lowers it; a check that could not run is logged as unavailable and changes nothing. Seeds only create new actors, so restarts never undo a demotion. /standing shows the record, /standing log the last events, and /standing set (local owner only) changes a level. Optional same-machine shared ledger for a governor and its workers, and a short score line on the task card after a completion or demotion. Disclosure — pre_tool_call returns Thor' own approve directive for every tool call outside the profile's level (at the default L1 that includes every terminal/shell, send and unknown-tool call) and blocks kanban_complete until a Standing proof passes in the same session; a worker's block/comment/review/heartbeat calls on its own assigned card skip the Standing prompt; under cron and other unattended runs Thor' approval policy (default deny) decides; it adds a guidance note to the model context through pre_llm_call; it never auto-approves or calls a model, and makes network or subprocess calls only for owner-scoped proofs (HTTP GET with no redirects, proxies or credentials; exact allowlisted argv, shell=False, minimal environment); it stores actors and hashed proof events in SQLite under its plugin data directory (or an owner-set db_path) and, when card_line is on, posts task-card comments through the public kanban_comment tool.

name: thor-structured-aux-models
description: Routes selected Thor auxiliary tasks (approval, MCP sampling, compression) through bounded Jev decision calls on OpenRouter instead of free-form chat prompts, failing open to the operator's own auxiliary provider for anything it cannot express as a decision. Disclosure — sends redacted approval prompts, MCP tool names and compression transcript blocks to openrouter.ai using your OpenRouter key (read-only); on any error approvals escalate to you, never auto-approve; the default decision_model is a moving alias, pin it.

name: thor-strudel-studio
description: Local Strudel live-coding studio for Thor: write patterns, hit Play, and let the agent compose alongside you with one poptart_studio tool and a Desktop SandboxedFrame pane. Disclosure — lazily starts a Node sidecar on 127.0.0.1 with a random per-install token in private profile plugin-data (mode 0600 on POSIX; inherited user-private ACL on Windows; token never reaches guests or the browser); evaluated music runs only after user Play/apply in isolated frames (not an OS sandbox); Strudel patterns may fetch samples/CDN over the network; audio output to the host. AGPL-3.0-or-later with toaster GPL notices — review LICENSE and NOTICE before redistribute. Self-contained catalog install; Node 22+ is required at runtime, not npm or a local build. No self-updater.

name: thor-stt-enhance
description: Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally. Post-processing is on by default and sends the transcript text to the LLM Thor routes the stt_enhance auxiliary task to (your main, usually remote, provider unless you point it at a local endpoint or set post_processing.enabled: false). It reads the body of the SKILL.md you configure (never executed) and runs ffmpeg/ffprobe. The opt-in Parakeet backend reads a local model export and, on first use and only when your config.yaml explicitly sets security.allow_lazy_installs: true, installs pinned sherpa-onnx and numpy from PyPI into ~/.thor/plugin-runtimes/thor-stt-enhance/ (shared by all profiles). No tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

name: thor-studio
description: Local video tools for any Thor Agent: long video or link in, captioned shorts out, plus timeline edits, Canva-style designs and photo tools, as 14 chat tools and a /studio chat slash. Whisper + FFmpeg on your machine. Never posts. Disclosure — every tool runs the separately installed thor-studio engine CLI (v0.6.2+, installed by its own command, not covered by this pin) as a subprocess with a timeout and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR, PYTHONPATH, THOR_STUDIO_*); tool calls read only media/image files under your home folder, /mnt, /media, /srv or the Studio library and write only new files inside ~/.thor/clips (never overwrite); links must be public http(s), and yt-dlp runs with every connection and redirect hop checked against loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and reserved addresses; thor_studio_desk starts a detached local desk on 127.0.0.1 (loopback only); the plugin ships a local `thor-studio mcp` server entry; the `/studio` chat command queues a Studio job into the current chat as a user message; optional local Ollama for clip titles; caption cues and the desk log go under <thor home>/plugin-data/thor-studio; caption lines are written by the calling agent; no credentials, no telemetry and no social publishing.

name: thor-studiotwin
description: StudioTwin cloud images, environments, PBR materials, meshes, rigs, motion, sound effects and Concepts via remote MCP, with an optional Desktop media workspace. Disclosure — Sends prompts and any media you upload to StudioTwin (api.studiotwin.ai; uploads and downloads via StudioTwin's Amazon S3 and assets.studiotwin.ai) with your StudioTwin API key, and StudioTwin passes jobs to its own model providers. Generation spends StudioTwin wallet credits with no plugin spend cap; paid, upload, cancel and delete tools go through Thor approval. The optional Desktop backend can read media-type files anywhere in your home folder (except hidden folders) for its viewers and stores downloads in its plugin-data folder. The optional local helper scripts run Blender, ffmpeg and headless Chromium with its sandbox disabled, and on first preview download three.js 0.180.0 from npm (integrity-checked).

name: thor-superagent
description: A resident router that dispatches and never executes, isolated workers that report only to it, team-written trigger rules, and an external watchdog that checks real progress and goal drift, plus an item ledger that keeps every task, issue and Claude Code session your sources show until it's confirmed closed. Disclosure — spawns long-running worker processes from the argv you configure, runs the outbound send, heartbeat and connector commands you configure, which read sources into its ledger, including a read-only session probe sent through the host command you configure, and, only when relaunch is turned on, types one short nudge into a stopped Claude Code session's terminal, stops or restarts its own workers, and spends tokens on the profile's model during ticks and when it writes a worker brief; on a profile set to router it drops every chat message whose sender is not on its allow list, and a webhook event from an allow-listed author starts a worker directly; the send and heartbeat commands run with the full Thor environment. Writes its database and worker directories under the configured home, and its optional Claude Code hook logs session events to ~/.superagent/sessions. Its hooks stay inert until a profile sets a role.

name: thor-switchyard
description: Jev-powered Thor plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after Thor redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the Thor redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of the current user turn after Thor redact_for_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local_only); light turns (greetings, closed acknowledgements, and read-only listings) skip that hosted call by default. Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after Thor redact_for_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence_finder_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.

name: thor-sysadmin
description: Windows and Active Directory RMM for Thor Agent and Thor Desktop: users, groups and lockouts, Group Policy, RDP, Windows Server Backup, a desktop fleet and 231 vetted PowerShell scripts, all behind tiered approvals with a preview before every change, protected objects and a local audit log. Disclosure — runs PowerShell on the Thor machine (local transport on a domain-joined Windows host, optionally as a configured account via runas /netonly) or over WinRM to one configured jump host, and from there talks to your domain controllers and the computers you target (AD, SMB, RPC, WinRM). Reads the account password only through Thor secret scope. While the dashboard is open a background collector in the gateway refreshes read-only snapshots (setting background_collector turns it off); scheduled monitoring adds a Thor cron job (and two launcher scripts in the Thor scripts folder) only when you turn it on, and a cron run cannot create or remove it unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true. In permissive mode standard writes run without an approval prompt. Writes a local SQLite audit log with passwords redacted. Never reads .env or any other credential store; the opt-in monitoring cron script gets the password only if the user lists SYSADMIN_WINRM_PASSWORD in terminal.env_passthrough. No telemetry and no other network calls; the raw PowerShell tool is off by default.

name: thor-t3-control
description: Bounded tools to list, read, create, and control local T3 coding threads on Linux and WSL2.

name: thor-t3sidebar
description: T3 Code-style session sidebar for Thor Desktop: Input/Done/Woke badges, Pinned/Working/Snoozed/Archived shelves, unsent drafts synced across Desktops, project picker and filter, AutoTitler rename, a token/cost Usage page, and a Codex/Claude Limits page that pools accounts by plan, forecasts run-outs and wasted quota, and redeems banked Codex resets. Disclosure — The Limits page reads Thor's credential pool and, every 5 minutes, fetches rate limits for every openai-codex and anthropic pool account with that account's own token through Thor's read-only usage fetch (chatgpt.com, api.anthropic.com). At most hourly it lists the active Codex sign-in's banked reset credits through Thor's signed request, and a user-confirmed button redeems one banked Codex reset. When the anthropic pool is empty it reads Claude Code's login ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude/.credentials.json) and sends that token to api.anthropic.com (/api/oauth/usage, /api/oauth/profile). An expired login is refreshed by Thor's Claude Code resolver, which writes the new token pair back to that file. Unsent composer drafts (text and folder) are stored in the plugin's data on the Thor host and synced to every connected Desktop. A resumed turn un-archives its session's compression lineage in state.db. The backend reads private Thor internals (live session registry, session DB and pool-routing helpers) and can break on a Thor update.

name: thor-tabs
description: Settings page (in the language set in Thor, nine languages; incl. which browser Thor works in and its safety level; loosening must be confirmed in the browser) and guard rails for thor-tabs, which lets Thor work in individual tabs of your real, signed-in Chromium browser through an extension and an MCP relay. Disclosure — talks only to the thor-tabs relay you configure (THOR_TABS_RELAY, default 127.0.0.1:8766) with THOR_TABS_ADMIN_TOKEN (paths /admin/settings and /admin/select, the latter picks the browser when several are connected); caches the last seen settings in plugin-data/thor-tabs/settings.json and its own opt-in switch in plugin-data/thor-tabs/options.json; the pre_tool_call hook rejects the tabs tools while switched off and, only if the user turns that switch on, blocked sites in Thor' own browser tools and web_extract. No shell, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: thor-tabular
description: Tabular AI that grows with your tables — Thor skills for honest tabular ML, one entry point. Disclosure — Installing pulls numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow, joblib and pyyaml into Thor's environment. The skills have the agent run Python on your data files, may ask it to pip install catboost, tabicl/torch, mapie or matplotlib, and the TabICL skill downloads a pretrained checkpoint of a few hundred MB on first use. Saved checkpoints are pickles: load only ones you made.

name: thor-tag
description: Feishu platform override with per-chat Tier-0/Tier-1 context, standing work, and privacy lifecycle controls. Disclosure — replaces Thor' bundled Feishu, Slack and DingTalk platform registrations with wrapped adapters; in chats listed in enabled_chats it stores every received group message (text and attachments, including from members who never talk to the bot) plus each @-mention question and reply in a plaintext SQLite file under the plugin's data directory (Tier-0 kept up to 24 h / 500 rows, Tier-1 memories with no time limit), answers /tag commands itself before Thor' gateway admission (state-changing ones limited to the configured admins), and lets admins create Thor cron jobs that post to the chat.

name: thor-tailscale
description: Browse Tailscale devices and connect to remote Thor instances in Thor Desktop.

name: thor-talk
description: Realtime voice for Thor through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Disclosure — Realtime on the ChatGPT subscription uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Thor's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex); the plugin never reads, refreshes or holds a token. GPT-Live on the subscription (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) starts one local `codex app-server` child per call on the Codex CLI's own login (API-key variables removed from its environment); that call uses the undocumented chatgpt.com Codex realtime endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice. The app-server's Codex thread is ephemeral and fenced (no environment, read-only sandbox, approvals declined, apps, shell, web search, plugins, sub-agents and each configured MCP server disabled, replies only "skip"); Talk reads only the MCP server names to disable them, and each voice request costs one small Codex turn of subscription quota. Voice audio and conversation context go to the selected provider (OpenAI, xAI, Google, optionally ElevenLabs); on Desktop the voice model can list the profile's sessions, read their titles and recent messages, create sessions and queue or steer prompts into them without a per-action confirmation; spoken requests are handed to the user's Thor agent, whose tools run under Thor approvals. No telemetry.

name: thor-taskbar-badge
description: Colour-coded badge on the Thor taskbar button: a green disc for a turn finished in a session you have not opened, an amber ring while a session waits on an approval, a clarify or a password, a red triangle for a failure. Opening a session clears only that session; failure outranks waiting and waiting outranks finished. The settings page holds the three colours, a test button each, per-event overrides and a switch back to the plain grey count. Disclosure — Disclosure: the desktop half posts the current badge state to 127.0.0.1:8766 on the same machine once per event, and the Python half starts at plugin load in each Thor process, listens on that loopback port (no token, CORS open to any origin, so any local program or open web page can also set or read the badge colour) and, from a background thread, calls the Windows taskbar overlay API or, on Linux, runs `gdbus emit` for the Unity launcher badge once a second while a badge is up; it writes `badge_bridge.log` in its plugin folder; nothing leaves the computer and no other network call is made. Where colour cannot be drawn, Chromium's grey count and the status-bar dot remain.

name: thor-teammates
description: Give your agent a fixed team. You define each specialist's instructions, toolsets and model once, and the agent picks only a name: a reviewer limited to todo gets no built-in web, file or terminal tools, whatever the prompt says (built-in delegate_task children inherit the parent's toolsets). Teammates also works its own lane on Thor' Kanban board inside the chat, where each card it finishes waits in Review, and keeps a per-profile ledger of every run's goal, status and result. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock Thor; no patched core. Disclosure — adds eight tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_request_changes, teammate_chain, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Thor subagents using credentials selected by Thor from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); Thor can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where Thor provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, complete final results up to 256 KB of text per run, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. teammate_request_changes reopens a lane card that is in review (Thor reopen_review_task), adds the feedback as a card comment and starts a teammate on it again; it never completes a card either. teammate_chain creates up to eight linked cards in its lane through Thor' kanban_create (so Thor wakes the creating chat when a card reaches review), archives the cards it created if the chain cannot be finished, and never completes a card; a lane card's teammate receives the finished results of the cards it depends on in its launch context. The lane tools take an optional board that names an existing, non-archived Kanban board (validated before any write; the plugin never creates or recreates a board); the run records it and keeps its claim, heartbeats, review handoff and rework on that board. On Thor builds with plugin prompt sections it adds one short paragraph (under 600 characters) about the Kanban lane to new top-level session prompts. The paragraph is rendered from its settings, carries no conversation content, and is left out without a usable teammate, for delegated children and under host isolation. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion notices are off by default and never inject unless the operator turns on both notify_on_completion and trust_notice_routing, because Thor cannot confirm which conversation would receive them; teammate_wait is the default. With both on, a finished run sends one line (teammate name, run ID and status, never result text) as a user message to the chat it was assigned from through ctx.inject_message, which also needs Thor' own allow_gateway_injection consent; a run with no recorded chat gets none, and after /new, /reset or /resume the line reaches that chat's current conversation. Includes two skills: teammates-workflow, a playbook that explains the tools, the Kanban Review loop and how a teammate's model, route and reasoning effort are inherited (it adds no tools, settings or permissions); and a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.

name: thor-teamops
