Disclosure — reads your Thor session history (read-only) to build the video, runs a pinned `npx hyperframes@0.8.217` renderer that downloads a headless Chrome on first use, and `thor wrapped schedule` adds a weekly cron job that delivers the video to your chosen chat with `thor send`.

name: thor-wrm-pro
description: A guided Thor skill for working with an existing WRM Pro MCP server. Connect Thor to your WRM Pro deployment and safely inspect or operate authorized servers through the configured MCP connection.

name: thor-wsl-terminal
description: Run Thor' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and thor doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). THOR_WSL_DISTRO and THOR_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and Thor never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in Thor is patched or rebound at runtime.

name: thor-wslc-sandbox
description: Run Thor' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.

name: thor-x-bookmarks
description: Reads your own X bookmarks (long posts and X Articles in full) through the official X API with your own X app, sorts them with your Thor model (category, tags, kind, priority, summary) and exports them to a board on your Desktop, Obsidian notes, a Notion database or a Google Doc. A weekly digest (best bookmarks numbered, 3 post ideas) arrives in your chat; reply "task 3" or "skill 2" to turn an item into a task or a Thor skill. Disclosure — calls api.x.com (read-only, keys of your own X app from the Thor .env via secret scope, or Thor' X OAuth 2.0 sign-in, or `xurl token` when you pick the xurl sign-in, which runs that CLI); sends post text to your configured Thor model; only when you export there: Notion through Thor' Notion connector (ctx.call_mcp to the notion MCP server, only if you add it to this plugin's mcp_allowlist; creates the database, two boards and pages, updates those pages) or api.notion.com with an optional XBM_NOTION_TOKEN, and docs.googleapis.com through Thor' Google sign-in (your own Desktop client, scope drive.file only); writes an 'X Bookmarks' folder on your Desktop (or export_dir) and notes into your Obsidian vault's 'X Bookmarks' folder, and reads Obsidian's obsidian.json to find the open vault; bookmarks, labels, export ids, digests, tasks and skill drafts are stored in plugin data; only on your command it creates one Thor cron job (/xbm schedule, through cronjob_manage; it stays until /xbm unschedule) and Thor skills (/xbm skill N save, through skill_manage, subject to Thor' approval); a pre_llm_call hook adds a one-line note only to a message that is just "task N", "skill N" or "done N" after a recent digest; no credentials stored, no telemetry, no background process of its own.

name: thor-xai
description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to Thor as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal Thor turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

name: thor-zh
description: Simplified Chinese (简体中文) language pack. Declarative locales/zh.yaml overlay for part of approval.* and gateway.*; placeholders match en.yaml.

name: thor-zotero
description: Search and read the papers in your own Zotero library before going to the web: a local, read-only full-text index (SQLite FTS5, BM25) built from a copy of Zotero's database, so it works with Zotero open or closed. Four tools (zotero_search with a strong/thin/none coverage verdict, zotero_read for passages, your own highlights and notes and a citation line, zotero_status, zotero_sync), a bundled skill that sends literature questions to the library first, and a `thor zotero` command (doctor, snapshot, sync). Since 0.2.0, for users who supply their own Markdown conversions: tables are searched and read as tables (in_tables, mode=tables) and papers carry the flags ocr and text_damaged; the plugin contains no converter. Disclosure — reads outside its own data folder: the Zotero data directory (copies zotero.sqlite and its write-ahead log, reads the .zotero-ft-cache text files in storage/), Zotero's prefs.js to find that directory, and a Markdown folder only if the user sets one; writes only to its plugin-data folder (snapshot, index, lock file) and never to Zotero; the index holds the full text of the user's papers and stays on the machine; its only network request goes to Zotero's local API on 127.0.0.1:23119 for formatted citations, bypassing any proxy, and succeeds only when the user has switched that API on (off by default); no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Zotero.

name: thor64
description: Author and edit room-based N64-era-style 3D games with story checks, bot playtests and local exports. Disclosure — Builds and playtests run Godot, Blender, Python and ffmpeg as local child processes (macOS: sandboxed, no network, writes confined to the game project; Windows: only after the owner opts into the Job Object runner, which has no network or write confinement). `/thor64 setup --fetch --yes`, typed by the user, downloads SHA-512-pinned official Godot 4.6.2 files from github.com/godotengine (export templates about 1.25 GB) and clears macOS quarantine on the verified app. Hub downloads stay off until the owner sets `hub_url`. A `pre_llm_call` hook adds a hint steering game requests to Thor64 into the user's turn, and the Studio tab can start a local 127.0.0.1 server for a web export or launch exported macOS/Windows builds.

name: thor_otel
description: OpenTelemetry for Thor Agent: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list or an OTEL_* variable); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $THOR_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http and -exporter-otlp-proto-grpc (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

name: thorford
description: An HD-2D pixel-art village page for Thor Desktop: every chat is a villager who walks to the forge, library, woods or town hall depending on the tool its agent is running, waits at the town hall when the chat needs you, and goes home to sleep when the chat is not active. Click a villager to open its chat. Built on the Luminati engine (MIT). Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface, read-only session.list / session.active_list polling every 3 s); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network calls.

name: thormade
description: Community bot shelf for Thor. Add bots from thormade.lol in one click (thor://open/thormade?add=<id>), share your own with /sharebot, and move your Grok Bot bots into Thor, one Thor bot each. Added bots are treated as untrusted: a package holding anything a share never includes is refused, its config is rebuilt from an allowlist (no hooks, approvals, terminal, plugins or model settings), schedules arrive paused, MCP servers arrive off, and every skill is scanned first. Each becomes its own profile on your model and login. Sharing and adding from the agent tool go through Thor' approval prompt. Shares never include .env, auth.json, keys, tokens, memories or chats, and a single secret hit aborts the upload. Disclosure — network calls only to https://thormade.lol, when you browse, add, share or unshare (no telemetry, no install counting). Creates profiles under ~/.thor/profiles. Keeps listing manage tokens in ~/.thor/thormade/shared.json (0600). Reads profile secret values through agent.secret_scope only to block a leaking share (compared in memory, never stored or sent). Grok Bot migration reads grok-bot-export*.json from Downloads, makes no network calls, uses the official agent-importers plugin, and installs it with `thor plugins install agent-importers` only after the user confirms.

name: thorvault
description: Keep secrets out of plaintext .env files: a local encrypted vault (FloorVault, AES-256-SIV) whose items Thor loads as environment variables at startup (mapped source "thorvault", hv: references), with a thor hvault CLI to manage items. The vault key lives in your OS key store (Keychain, Secret Service, DPAPI), a key file, a systemd-creds credential, or THOR_VAULT_KEY. Disclosure — reads an encrypted store under <THOR_HOME>/agent-vault (or secrets.thorvault.dir) at startup; thor hvault commands write to it and thor hvault setup (or the first thor hvault bind) creates it; thor hvault bind also writes the secrets.thorvault env mapping (an hv: reference, never the value) and enabled: true into the profile's config.yaml through Thor' own config writer (--print-only prints it instead); thor hvault bind and allow also keep a sealed binding record of each item's bound command lines in the per-user state directory (FLOOR_VAULT_STATE_DIR, else the platform's non-roaming state directory), outside the store; reads its own master key only from the variable named by token_env (default THOR_VAULT_KEY) in the environment Thor scopes to the profile being fetched, else from the custody set in secrets.thorvault.custody: os (default; macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service or Windows DPAPI, service floor-vault, shared with other FloorVault apps on the same account), key_file (the file named by secrets.thorvault.key_file, which must not be writable by group or others), or systemd-creds (master.key.sdcred beside the store) — never from FLOOR_VAULT_KEY, VAULT_MASTER_KEY or FLOOR_VAULT_KEY_FILE, which it also protects from being overwritten; a configured custody that fails is reported, never replaced by another; a passphrase-protected store (floorvault 0.4) is not supported, because startup never prompts and never creates a key, a credential or a store (a locked or missing key is reported and Thor starts without those variables), and only thor hvault setup may unlock the key store or create the key; reads Thor' own command line (sys.argv and sys.orig_argv, no other process's) to compare with the command bindings stored on an item by floorvault secrets allow or thor hvault allow, and resolves a bound item only when Thor was started with one of them (thor hvault bind binds a new item to the command line Thor starts its local gateway with, built from this interpreter and the profile home; --no-bind skips it) (secrets.thorvault.require_binding, default off, also skips items with no binding); resolved values become environment variables of the Thor process and its children, like .env entries; installs floorvault>=0.2.8,<0.5 from PyPI (plus secretstorage on Linux, pyobjc-framework-Security on macOS); one subprocess, only with custody: systemd-creds: the system's own systemd-creds (decrypt --user at startup; encrypt and decrypt in thor hvault setup), found only in system directories, run as an argument list with no shell and a minimal environment, the key passed through a pipe; otherwise no subprocesses; no network calls, no self-update; protection is at rest, not against code already running as the same user.

name: thoth
description: Agents working as one team, each with its own harness: Claude Code, Codex and Thor today. Ask Thor for a website, an app, artwork or a doc: it plans the work on a shared board and hands each task to the real Claude Code or Codex CLI, on your own logins and plans, so every improvement their makers ship reaches your team. Each agent works in its own git worktree with a brief of what the team decided and made (goal, decisions, handoffs, what its dependencies produced), reviews the other's work, and Thor merges what passes once you say yes. In Thor Desktop, Thoth sits beside each project's chat: a side window with the live canvas and a Team & brain tab (who did what, decisions, reviews, versions), and every Thoth project is also a Thor project on the same folder. Claude Code or Codex can join the board through the bundled MCP server or take over as coordinator, and a task that needs the web gets a clean Chrome, or yours when it needs your logins. When a Claude or ChatGPT plan runs out, the other agent carries on from its work, and the side window and Team card show how much of each plan is used and when it resets. Approve a plan once and autopilot runs it to the end: it starts, cross-reviews and merges each task, and asks you in the chat only when something needs you; any change to the plan pauses it. Once work is merged, the side window offers it to open, download as a zip or find in Finder. Start a project from the project menu or the chat: a new one gets its own folder in ~/Thoth, and a folder you already have becomes a project that keeps every version. After an update, the Thoth page says what's new, once. Disclosure — after you approve each launch in Thor, or a plan card for autopilot, runs your installed claude and codex CLIs as background processes (stopped on cancel, timeout (30 min by default), unload or exit) under their own logins and plans, which Thoth never reads, with Claude Code's OS sandbox and Codex's workspace-write sandbox; gives them and project commands only PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, TERM, LANG, the LC_ locale settings, CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from its environment, plus names you list in env_passthrough; inside Codex runs it pre-approves only its own three worker tools (read the board, write a note); writes .thoth/ (SQLite brain, run logs, worktrees), thoth/T<n> branches, exact-path lines in .git/info/exclude and, only when you approve a merge, merge commits on your base branch; makes a new project's folder in ~/Thoth (the projects_dir setting) and, in a folder that is not in git yet, a git repository with its files as the first version (.env and other secrets, dependency folders and files over 50 MB stay in the folder but out of git, through .git/info/exclude), never in your home, Desktop, Documents or Downloads folder; links ignored node_modules/.venv folders into task worktrees, gives each worktree copy-on-write copies of the other files the project keeps out of git (read-only links where the disk can't copy) and moves the new files a merged task made outside git into the project folder without overwriting anything, and never reads or copies .env files or other secrets; a project board is used only if Thoth made it on this computer or you said yes to it on a Thor card (adopting one starts nothing), and its setup or run command runs as you outside the sandbox only if you approved that exact command for that board on Thor's card (hashes kept in approvals.json in its data folder, never in the project); starting a run preview asks you first (on a free localhost port from an export under .thoth/previews/); a project whose .thoth folder is committed to git, or a .thoth folder Thoth didn't make, is refused; Thoth's own git commands run without hooks or fsmonitor; static previews are served read-only on 127.0.0.1; the Desktop page's Connect buttons run claude mcp add thoth / codex mcp add thoth only when clicked; in Thor Desktop it adds two panes (the side window and Team & brain) and a Chat + Thoth layout template that changes your layout only when you pick it, opens one chat per project and pins it in the project's colour once, creates (or reuses) a Thor project on each Thoth project's folder and moves that project's chat into it through Thor's own project calls, and keeps which chat and folder belong to which project, and the last version whose notes you saw, in its data folder (chats.json, projects.json, whatsnew.json); reads plan usage from Claude Code's run output and asks `codex app-server` for Codex's limits (a read that uses no tokens), kept in plans.json; autopilot (only after you approve its plan card, never under an always-allow) starts, reviews and merges that plan's tasks without a card for each step, pauses when the plan changes, keeps the Mac from idle sleep with caffeinate -i while it runs and holds .thoth/autopilot.lock; the Download button writes a zip of the merged files (never .env files) to your Downloads folder; completion notices and autopilot's messages reach the chat only with allow_gateway_injection; a task you give a browser has its agent run npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.2.0 (pinned, fetched from npm on first use, usage statistics off): a temporary headless Chrome, or, if you choose your own Chrome, the Chrome you are running once you turn on remote debugging and allow the connection in Chrome, where the agent sees your tab titles, acts with your logins in a tab of its own and is told to only look. No network calls of its own, no telemetry.

name: thott-bot
description: Everything about World of Warcraft: Forever in your AI, from every change to live auction prices. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to thott.bot's server (mcp.thott.bot), which records the queries your agent sends it (not your conversation, and not used to train models); its tool set is served remotely and is not covered by the pinned sha; it requires a free thott.bot account, signed in by running `thor mcp add thott --url https://mcp.thott.bot/mcp --auth oauth`, whose config entry replaces the package's own server definition.

name: thought-we-wouldnt-notice
description: Insert a quarter, get a tiny original space-bug shooter, and a wry "thought we wouldn't notice" line. A whole-message quarter is swallowed by pre_llm_call so Thor skips the model and replies "Thought we wouldn't notice. But we did." Thor Desktop opens the Top Sails cabinet over the window; Esc dismisses it. The dashboard tab has the same cabinet and a Play button. Disclosure — no third-party network calls, no shell, no credentials, and no telemetry; the quarter ledger and high score are stored only under the plugin's own data directory; pre_llm_call blocks the model turn for matching messages only.

name: threejs-stage
description: Live three.js r187 scenes and GLB, GLTF, STL and OBJ models in Thor chat. Thor calls one tool, three_scene, with scene code or a model file. Thor Desktop draws the result as an interactive card with orbit, zoom, fullscreen, restart, screenshot and Ask Thor to change this, and other surfaces get a standalone HTML file. With Desktop open, each scene is dry-run in a hidden frame before the tool returns, so a crash or a blank render reaches Thor in the same turn. Disclosure — scene code written by the model runs in Desktop inside a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin, scripts only) whose content security policy blocks all network requests; three.js r187 is bundled (MIT). The exported HTML file loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened in a browser. Given a model path, the tool reads that file and the .bin, .mtl and image files it references in the same folder (50 MB limit) and copies them to plugin storage; scenes, screenshots and delivered files are stored under plugin-data/threejs-stage and cache/generated/threejs-stage on this machine. The dry run makes the tool wait up to 2.5 s for Desktop and up to 16 s for the result, and can be turned off (verify_scenes). Fix with Thor and Ask Thor to change this each send one ordinary chat message. No API keys, no telemetry, no background processes, no self-update.

name: thumbs-fix
description: React with a thumbs-down to a bad Thor reply on Telegram and it names the skill behind it, asks one question, shows a proposed edit as a diff, and changes the skill only after you approve. Disclosure - registers pre_gateway_dispatch (records private-chat messages as turns and takes your one answer; never drops other messages), pre_llm_call (adds a short note after a repair is applied), post_tool_call (watches skill_view to log which skills a reply used) and gateway_platform_event (Telegram reactions). Stores turns, repairs and message ids in ctx.state, and one backup copy of SKILL.md per applied repair under plugin-data/thumbs-fix/backups. Edits a skill only after you approve a diff with a thumbs-up or /feedback approve, through skill_manage, and /feedback undo restores the backup. Makes one call per repair to your own configured model with ctx.llm.complete_structured; the prompt contains the skill text and your answer. No network requests of its own, no tools, no environment variables, no secrets, no processes. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (records private Telegram chat messages as turns, including from senders not yet approved, and consumes your one answer to a pending repair; never drops other messages), pre_llm_call (adds a short note after a repair is applied), post_tool_call (watches skill_view to log which skills a reply used) and gateway_platform_event (Telegram reactions). It stores turns, repairs and message ids in ctx.state, and one backup copy of SKILL.md per applied repair under plugin-data/thumbs-fix/backups. It edits a skill only after you approve a diff with a thumbs-up or /feedback approve, through skill_manage. /feedback undo restores the backup, writing the original bytes directly to the skill's SKILL.md if skill_manage's restore differs. It makes one call per repair to your own configured model with ctx.llm.complete_structured; the prompt contains the skill text and your answer. It makes no network requests of its own and uses no tools, secrets or processes.

name: tibber
description: Read-only Tibber account, electricity prices, and consumption history via MCP, with a cached cost-summary skill. Disclosure — on first load with TIBBER_ACCESS_TOKEN set it adds an mcp_servers.tibber entry (npx -y tibber-mcp-server@0.2.2, token passed as an env reference) to the active profile's config.yaml, which stays after uninstall until the user removes it; the server sends authenticated requests to api.tibber.com and reads account details, home addresses, prices and consumption history; the skill caches home addresses, IDs, costs and consumption (no credentials) in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/tibber/tibber.json.

name: ticklist
description: A checklist the user ticks, in a Desktop pane — every tick, untick, add and removal is announced to the agent as it happens.

name: tickover
description: Ears for Thor. Thor can switch things on; Tickover lets it hear whether they started. tickover_verify listens before and after any action (a relay, a smart plug, a shell command, a robot move) and returns confirmed, no_change, other_change or unclear, with the level change in dB and a card. It needs no setup and no baseline. tickover_hear says what a sound is and whether the recording is usable. tickover_enroll and tickover_check remember a machine from three healthy recordings and report drift in robust sigmas with the frequency band that moved. tickover_watch puts a machine on a Thor cron schedule, with a person sending voice notes or unattended from a stream or a recorder folder. tickover_fleet shows every machine on one card. Name a repairer with tickover_watch(notify="telegram:<chat_id>") and a confirmed drift reaches them on Telegram, WhatsApp, email or any Thor channel, once per change, while the fix is still small. bridge/tickover_bridge.py, one standard-library file, turns an old Android phone, a Raspberry Pi or a spare laptop into a listening device that Thor reads over the local network. tickover_teach (experimental) learns named states from a few recordings. tickover_selftest proves the install with synthetic sound. Training-free: frozen CED-base and EfficientAT mn10 encoders in onnxruntime, about 0.6 s per check on CPU. Benchmarks with their limits are in the README. Disclosure — first use downloads the CED-base ONNX model (87 MB, Apache-2.0) from huggingface.co/mispeech/ced-base at a pinned commit and verifies its sha256; a 12 MB mn10 ONNX graph ships in the repo, checked by sha256 at load. Audio is processed locally and never uploaded. tickover_listen and a source-less tickover_verify record 3-120 seconds from this computer's microphone when the model calls them, with no approval prompt (needs the optional sounddevice package). The tools read any audio or video file, folder or glob the model names, and open a stream URL only for hosts the owner lists in the plugin's allowed_sources setting (empty by default), connecting only to the checked address and re-checking every redirect; private addresses pass only for listed local names or IPs, and link-local and cloud-metadata addresses only when listed literally. ffmpeg (the one on PATH, else the binary shipped by the imageio-ffmpeg wheel) runs as a subprocess with protocol and format whitelists and a minimal environment; http(s) streams are fetched by the plugin and piped in, rtsp goes through a local relay that refuses redirects. tickover_watch creates and replaces Thor cron jobs (no faster than every 15 minutes, never from inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true) that ask the owner for a recording or check a stream unattended. With a repairer set through tickover_watch(notify=...), which only the owner's chat or the local operator can change, a confirmed drift sends the repairer a message and a card through Thor delivery, via a one-shot cron job with no tools or, when agent scheduling is off, from the listening job itself; this happens without an approval prompt. Three hooks (pre_gateway_dispatch, post_gateway_admission, pre_llm_call) note audio files that arrive in chat and add one context line telling the agent where the file is; the note is stored only after the gateway admits the sender, and they never block a message. The optional bridge script runs on the user's own device, serves only audio it records on request, and requires a key on any non-local address unless started with --open. Baselines, cards and history live in plugin-data/tickover. No credentials, no telemetry.

name: tidal
description: TIDAL for Thor Agent: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (thor tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the Thor machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the Thor machine.

name: tightbeam
description: Beam shorts to every platform and keep your whole YouTube catalog optimized: 11 tools + 2 automation blueprints (nightly back-catalog sweep under a quota budget, post-publish optimizer for new uploads), plus multi-platform publishing through OpusClip with collision checks, platform caps and read-back verification built in. Disclosure — video metadata (titles/descriptions/tags/ids) goes to the Google YouTube Data API through YOUR OWN OAuth client declared in the plugin manifest (thor auth add tightbeam:google; Thor stores and refreshes the token, the plugin never sees it); video bytes and post copy go to OpusClip through YOUR Thor-managed opusclip MCP connection (thor mcp login opusclip); title and copy generation uses your Thor host LLM; the plugin stores no credentials; publishing is irreversible once the platform window passes.

name: time-gap
description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

name: time-machine
description: Visual timeline scrubber, split diff inspector, surgical per-file rollback, and failure diagnosis for Thor Agent and Desktop. Captures pre-mutation snapshots in an isolated store, diagnoses broken edits in dry-run mode, and restores files only after the user runs /tm restore or confirms in the Desktop/dashboard pane. Disclosure — snapshots the session working directory with git add -A into its own git store under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/time-machine/ before file-mutating and command tool calls, excluding .env, *.pem, *.key, node_modules, and virtualenvs (.env.example is kept); model-called restores are preview-only; workspace files are overwritten or deleted only when the user runs /tm restore or confirms a restore in the UI, and a full-workspace restore stays unchecked until the user opts in; /tm commit, /tm comment, /tm clone, /tm push, and /tm pull are user-typed commands that write only a private checkpoint, a ledger note, a new directory the user names, or a .bundle file, and they never run git commit, git clone, git push, or git pull on the project repository; no network, no telemetry, no state.db.

name: timecapsule
description: Sealed messages for later — seal a note so it cannot be read until its release condition is met (a date, N days of silence, or the sealer's explicit release), with a grace ladder and slow, announced deletion. Local-only, stdlib-only, no network. Disclosure — the seal is access control, not encryption: capsule text is stored in plaintext in store.json under the plugin data directory, so anything with file access (including the agent's own file tools) can read it, and manual release trusts the author name given by the caller.

name: timeline-replay
description: Animated replays of recorded Thor activity across the profiles you select: Social, Balanced and Linear paces with up to 16 profiles stacked on one screen, or nine canvas styles: Orbit (a turning ring where every event shoots out as a ray), Galaxy (a spiral with one arm per profile), Skyline (an isometric city of activity), Flow river (profiles to models to tools), Pulse (a heart-monitor trace per profile), Day clock (events at their time of day), Neural net (sessions firing into tools and models), Code rain and Ridgelines; tool calls, sessions, delegations, model/provider switches and token totals. Preview the private HTML player in Desktop or the Webapp (loop or play once), then export MP4 at 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K on the Thor host, with live progress and an ETA learned on that host. Settings → Plugins holds per-user defaults; `thor replay` adds the same options in the CLI plus a live terminal HUD. Disclosure — observer hooks only (on_session_start, on_session_end, pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, post_tool_call, post_api_request, subagent_start, subagent_stop); they record metadata, never block or change a turn and never return directives. Prompts, tool arguments, results, command lines and credentials are discarded; session IDs are hashed. Reads outside its own data: the active profile's profile.yaml (display name only) and the state.db of this profile and of profile homes the operator explicitly enrolls, read-only (SQLite mode=ro, query_only) and metadata columns only. Writes only under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/timeline-replay/. Exports show profile labels, timestamps, tool/model labels and totals, so choose neutral labels before sharing. Rendering starts only when the user asks: it runs the preinstalled HyperFrames CLI (Node.js, driving Chromium/chrome-headless-shell) and FFmpeg/ffprobe as argument-list subprocesses with a limited environment (no provider or bot credentials), as a background thread in the gateway process; HyperFrames telemetry and update checks are turned off. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no installs (video setup only drafts a chat request for the user to review and send), no credentials. When the Desktop page and the plugin on the Thor host differ, the page shows both versions, a button to Thor' Capabilities → Plugins tab, and copy buttons for the host command (thor plugins update timeline-replay && thor gateway restart) and Thor' catalog install link (thor://plugin/install?catalog=timeline-replay), both of which stay on the reviewed build; nothing installs unless the user acts in Thor, and the plugin never checks for updates online or downloads or replaces its own files. Readiness runs the configured HyperFrames CLI with --version (same limited environment) to report its version. Desktop uses the SDK surface only (routes, sidebar nav, settings page, SandboxedFrame, the MEDIA player, captureGatewayFileDownload).

name: timelinesai-whatsapp
description: WhatsApp CRM inbox automation for teams: ask what needs a reply, then send WhatsApp messages, label, assign and close chats from Thor. Regular WhatsApp numbers and WhatsApp API numbers, one browser OAuth sign-in to TimelinesAI, no keys in config. Hosted-only connector, no local code (details and disclosure in the README). Disclosure — Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, including the WhatsApp message text and chat history the agent reads, goes to mcp.services.timelines.ai (operated by TimelinesAI) and acts on the WhatsApp account you sign in with, including sending messages, notes and labels and assigning, opening and closing chats; OAuth tokens are stored by Thor, the server is marked untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable calls, and the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. A TimelinesAI account is required.

name: timestamp-ref
description: @ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

name: tinfoil-provider
description: Tinfoil confidential inference as a Thor model provider. Open-weight models from Tinfoil's live catalog (Kimi, GLM, gpt-oss and others) run in attested hardware enclaves that neither the cloud host nor Tinfoil can read. Thor reaches them only through Tinfoil's local tinfoil-proxy, which verifies the enclave's attestation and pins its TLS key before forwarding anything; there is no fallback to an unverified connection. The proxy starts on demand. Disclosure — Thor sends requests, including a /v1/models read for the model list, only to the local proxy (127.0.0.1:3301, or TINFOIL_BASE_URL); the proxy is what contacts Tinfoil. When nothing listens on the proxy's port, the plugin starts the user's installed tinfoil-proxy binary in its own session and leaves it running after Thor exits, logging to proxy.log in the plugin's data directory; it never downloads a binary, and TINFOIL_PROXY_AUTOSTART=0 turns this off. The proxy inherits only an allowlist of the environment (PATH, home, temp and user, locale and time zone, SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR, HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY, and Windows system directories); every other variable, including all TINFOIL_* variables, is withheld. TINFOIL_API_KEY is read through Thor' provider profile and sent to the proxy as the request's bearer token. The plugin writes catalog.json (the last model list it saw) and proxy.log under its plugin-data directory, registers no tools, hooks or middleware, and sends no telemetry.

name: tinfoil-sandbox
description: A tinfoil terminal backend: Thor' terminal, file and code tools run inside your own Tinfoil Container, an attested enclave, reached over the Tinfoil CLI's attested SSH tunnel. Select it with terminal.backend: tinfoil and terminal.tinfoil_container. Needs a Tinfoil organization with Containers enabled; the public template https://github.com/counterposition/thor-tinfoil-workspace sets up a suitable workspace. Dangerous-command approval stays on, and the plugin never creates, starts, stops or bills containers. Disclosure — every tool call runs the user's installed tinfoil CLI (tinfoil ssh) and OpenSSH client as subprocesses; the CLI contacts Tinfoil's control plane to look the container up, then the enclave. The plugin passes TINFOIL_API_KEY, read through Thor' secret scope, to the CLI as the tunnel key, and the admin key when set (TINFOIL_ADMIN_KEY, or an admin_ key in TINFOIL_API_KEY, which the CLI also accepts); beyond those the CLI and ssh get only an allowlist of Thor' environment (PATH, home, temp, user, locale, SSH agent socket, certificate and HTTP proxy settings, the CLI's TINFOIL_CONTROLPLANE_URL and TINFOIL_CONFIG, Windows system directories). It never reads the CLI's saved login, and strips TINFOIL_API_KEY, TINFOIL_TUNNEL_API_KEY and TINFOIL_ADMIN_KEY from the environment of commands the agent runs. An SSH control socket under the system temp directory (thor-tinfoil/) keeps the verified connection open for five idle minutes. A pre_tool_call hook rewrites a leading ~ in the path argument of read_file, write_file, patch and search_files to the container's home directory, only while terminal.backend is tinfoil, because Thor otherwise expands it to the host's home. No telemetry.

name: tinyfish
description: TinyFish: the web, built into Thor. Free Search and Fetch power Thor's own web_search and web_extract, and when a site needs clicks, forms or a login, a remote browser and the tinyfish_agent web agent handle it, signed in through saved TinyFish profiles when needed. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Thor's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `thor tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Thor .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking. Profile tools manage TinyFish Browser Context Profiles (saved website sign-ins) over the same API; you sign in to sites yourself at an agent.tinyfish.ai link and never give Thor a password; the agent can create, rename and re-default profiles without asking, and deleting a profile goes through Thor's approval prompt for each profile unless approvals are off (YOLO). Setup telemetry is off by default: only if you opt in (`thor tinyfish setup --share-usage`, `tinyfish.telemetry: true`, or answering yes to setup's y/N question) does each setup run send one event to agent.tinyfish.ai with its outcome, where the key came from, the plugin version and OS, plus a one-way hash of the key (never the key). TINYFISH_NO_TELEMETRY=1 turns it off regardless.

name: tirith
description: Check every terminal command with your installed tirith before it runs: lookalike and homograph URLs, pipe-to-shell, obfuscated execution, credential and .env exfiltration, malicious packages and terminal injection. tirith blocks and required policy approvals go to Thor's approval prompt, critical findings are refused, warnings run with the warning added to the result; unattended runs follow approvals.*_mode. Disclosure — runs the user-installed tirith binary (0.5.0 or later; never downloaded, installed or updated by the plugin) on every terminal command and completed shell command sent to a background terminal, in the command's working directory, with the command on stdin; tirith logs each check locally and, unless offline is set, may refresh its signed threat database, query OSV.dev, deps.dev and ecosyste.ms, download the CISA KEV feed, and query Google Safe Browsing (only with your key); fails closed (asks, or refuses when unattended) if tirith is missing, older than 0.5.0, times out or gives no verdict.

name: tironian
description: Trains a small local model on the requests you keep repeating in Thor, tests it on held-out steps from your own past sessions, and lets it answer those requests only after it passes, checking every answer and falling back to your usual model silently. Capture uses llm_execution middleware and observer hooks; secrets and personal details are masked before anything is stored. Disclosure: reads this profile's state.db read only on first use and on `thor tironian import`; stores masked contexts, grades, datasets and GGUF files under plugin-data/tironian; makes no network calls during normal use (the router talks only to student_endpoint, Thor's local model server on 127.0.0.1 by default); `thor tironian trainer setup`, run by the user, creates a venv in plugin data and installs the modal client from PyPI; training starts only on an explicit user action and then uploads that family's masked examples to a private Volume in the user's own Modal account (deleted after the run), or runs on the user's own GPU; the optional judge (off by default) sends held-out examples, and in shadow mode differing answers within a daily budget, to the model assigned to the "Tironian judge" auxiliary slot; `thor tironian verify`, run by the user, downloads only the proof and model URLs the user gives it, into plugin-data/tironian/verify. No telemetry.

name: titanos-mcp
description: Connect Thor to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.

name: tldr
description: One-click summaries of long agent replies in Thor Desktop. A card shows status first (Done, Blocked, Running, Waiting on you), what changed with each item marked Shown (backed by a tool step) or Stated only, risks, and the decisions the agent left you, with a recommended option and notes; Insert into chat drops your answers into the message box. Scope: last reply, since you last checked, or the whole session (with optional conflict warnings against earlier instructions); S/M/L length; per-reply history; reminders for skipped questions; optional automatic mode with a daily cap. Runs on its own auxiliary task (tldr_summary), so you can pick a cheap model in Models > Auxiliary without touching the chat model. Disclosure — Sends the selected chat text, tool names with short argument previews (up to 160 characters, e.g. commands, paths, URLs) and your preferences note to the model assigned to its `tldr_summary` auxiliary task (Thor' auxiliary routing, host-owned credentials), only on click or in the opt-in automatic mode (off by default, 30 per day cap); reads this profile's session database and config read-only; stores settings and answers in Desktop plugin storage; no shell, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: tmewai
description: Local, offline index for your own Facebook JSON export (Meta's your_activity_across_facebook.zip). Imports messages, comments (including comments_v2), reactions and posts into a seven-table SQLite database without ever extracting the archive to disk, then exposes six tools: archive_scan and archive_ingest validate every ZIP entry in memory (absolute paths, .., drive paths, NUL bytes, duplicate names and symlinks rejected) and give each entry exactly one source_files row so nothing is silently dropped; archive_search runs FTS5 over text folded for Arabic (harakat, alef variants, taa marbuta, alef maqsura, tatweel) while stored text keeps its original spelling; archive_person and archive_overview aggregate over people, conversations, events and attachments; archive_evidence builds a hard-capped bundle (20 events, 4000 characters) with a metadata-only consent row that cannot carry excerpt text. Imports are idempotent by content fingerprint. Python standard library only, no network access, no API key, no environment variable; the database lives under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/tmewai/ and TMEWAI_DB_PATH overrides it. Disclosure — the plugin reads a personal social export the user points it at and stores it unencrypted in that local SQLite file; it never sends archive content anywhere, and archive_evidence only returns its capped bundle to the agent that requested it.

name: tmux-live
description: Live tmux tab for the Thor web dashboard: pick a pane, watch it in ANSI colour, type into it when needed, and terminate the process, pane or session. Disclosure: calls the local tmux binary with argv lists (capture-pane, send-keys, kill-pane, kill-session), can signal the pane's foreground process group, and probes /proc/<pid>/root/tmp for the tmux socket when the dashboard runs under systemd PrivateTmp. No network access, credentials, telemetry or self-updater. English and Spanish UI.

name: together
description: Together AI model-provider plugin — OpenAI-compatible API, 270+ serverless open-weight models, live catalog discovery.

name: token-cost-meter
description: Live token usage, model-aware USD cost and prompt-cache savings in the Thor Desktop status bar, with a persistent per-day ledger that survives restarts. Disclosure — Desktop only; no network calls of its own (prices come from the gateway's model.options and a bundled models.dev rate table); stores per-day token totals, per-session counters and last-known rates in its own Desktop plugin storage; costs are list-price estimates, not billing data.

name: token-dashboard
description: Token cost and usage dashboard for Thor Desktop: a right pane with the focused session's live input and output tokens, session cost (backend-reported cost_usd when available, otherwise a labelled estimate from a built-in per-model price table), API calls and context usage bar, plus a recent-sessions overview with message counts and a status bar cost chip. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Disclosure: reads the focused session usage state and the session list through the Desktop host API and renders them locally; no network calls, no storage.

name: token-lens
description: Token consumption analytics for Thor: records exact per-call usage from pre/post_api_request hooks, decomposes every request into categories (system prompt, built-in and per-MCP-server tool schemas, skills, memory, history, tool results, output, reasoning) calibrated to billed totals, and adds a Token Lens dashboard tab plus a Sessions-page card with deterministic and AI-evaluated token-reduction suggestions; `thor token-lens refresh` runs a suggestion refresh from the CLI. Disclosure — records per-API-call token counts (no message text) from pre/post_api_request hooks into token_lens.db at the Thor home root (per-call rows kept 90 days, rollups kept), and reads Thor's state.db read-only for session token totals and, during the optional dashboard history import, message text for estimation only; after 10 recorded sessions it automatically calls your configured main model through Thor's plugin LLM facade every 5 sessions (up to two calls per refresh, capped at 50,000 tokens by meta_budget_tokens), sending aggregated token statistics plus the names of your enabled MCP servers and plugins, and auto-applies the model's proposed category regex rules and rubric changes (logged to token_lens.EVOLUTION.md; evolve_rules: false turns this off); the dashboard's refresh button spawns a detached `thor token-lens refresh` process that logs to logs/token-lens-refresh.log; its data paths follow the THOR_HOME environment variable rather than the active profile, so in a multi-profile gateway every profile records into the launch profile's database; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.

name: token-master
description: Token spend analytics for Thor Desktop: one stacked daily chart of token consumption across every Thor profile, provider and account on the machine (7D/30D/90D/1Y, stacked by token class, provider, profile or source), per-provider / per-profile / per-model / per-task breakdowns, and an Accounts and limits card that marks each credential as subscription (quota), pay-per-token API spend or free and shows the live allowance windows Thor can fetch. It reads the token accounting Thor already records — every profile's state.db opened read-only, plus DeepSeek Harness session files — and adds no collection of its own. Disclosure — reads every Thor profile's state.db token accounting read-only, DeepSeek Harness session files under ~/.dsh, and the labels, ids and status of Thor credential-pool entries (no token values); `Refresh limits` goes through Thor' read-only fetch_account_usage(provider, read_only=True) to the provider's usage endpoint (no token is refreshed, rotated or stored); the optional `Sync now` button runs ssh with your own SSH setup into a host you added and streams the bundled read-only collector into that host's python3, installing and writing nothing there, and the Remote machines card runs `tailscale status --json` to offer online peers (discovery only — adding a host is still a click); state lives in plugin-data/token-master/ on the root Thor home only; no telemetry, no background process.

name: token-rate
description: Live output/input tokens-per-second chip in the Thor Desktop status bar for a local llama.cpp server. Thor itself reads the server's log ($THOR_HOME/logs/llama-server.log, last 200 lines: `tg = X t/s` for output and `prompt eval time ... X tokens per second` for input) and serves it at /api/plugins/token-rate/; the chip polls that route once a second. The counter starts off — click the chip, or run the palette entry "Token Rate: start/stop the tok/s counter" (Ctrl/Cmd+K), to start it; the on/off flag is a file ($THOR_HOME/cache/token-rate-state.json). It also registers the get_token_rate agent tool, so the model can read its own speed. Disclosure — it reads one local file (the llama.cpp log) and nothing else: no network calls, no external process, no extra port, no API key, no credentials, no telemetry. UI is English by default, Italian when the app locale is Italian.

name: token-speed
description: Live token generation speed plus session up/down token totals in the Thor Desktop status bar, with a click-through dashboard: 60-second sparkline, this-turn output tokens, model, call count, average t/s, cache hit %, context usage % and estimated cost. Speed is estimated from a 2-second sliding window of streamed characters and continuously recalibrated against the session's authoritative UsageStats, so mixed English/CJK traffic tracks without a fixed heuristic. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls or file writes.

name: tokenjuice
description: Compact successful terminal output locally before model consumption. Disclosure — runs the separately installed `tokenjuice` CLI (from PATH or `TOKENJUICE_BIN`; installed outside the pinned commit with `npm install --global tokenjuice`) on every successful foreground terminal command's output and replaces what the model sees with its shorter summary; the plugin sends nothing over the network.

name: tokenwatch
description: Monitor Thor token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

name: tokstat
description: Live token usage in the Thor Desktop status bar: cumulative total, a real-time this-turn counter, last-turn delta, context occupancy, and prompt-cache hit rate. Event-driven (no polling, no RPC); English and Chinese, follows the app locale.

name: toll
description: Safety checks before an agent buys a coin, signs a transaction or pays another agent, through Toll's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://t0ll.xyz/mcp, no key, no sign-in): who is behind a coin (snipers, bundles, linked wallets, the dev's funding and record), whether the LP can be pulled, whether the product a coin claims exists, one word before a buy (BLOCK / WARN / ALLOW / WAIT), ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK before signing a transaction, EIP-712 message or x402 payment, a wallet's live approvals with the unsigned revoke, an ERC-8004 agent's registration and x402 terms, paid x402 APIs and who they pay, and a Uniswap v4 hook's powers, on Robinhood Chain (4663) only; plus Robinhood Stock Token market data (debt securities, not shares), SEC fundamentals, insider trades, 13F institutional holders, earnings guidance, the Stock Token event feed and US macro figures. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to t0ll.xyz, which receives the tool's arguments (token contracts, wallet addresses, agent ids, tickers, the unsigned transaction passed to check_tx); 24 of the 28 tools are lookups annotated read-only; 4 are not (watch_coin and watch_wallet store a watch that makes Toll POST signed events to an https url the caller gives, unwatch_coin and unwatch_wallet remove one) and all 4 refuse without a Toll key, which this keyless package does not send; the server never signs, sends transactions or moves money; the package marks the server untrusted; no key is stored or sent (free daily quota of 10 new coins and 50 market calls, more with a Toll key the user sets in their own config); past the quota answers end with a paid x402 URL the plugin cannot pay; no telemetry (the quota is counted per caller with a daily-rotated keyed hash of the IP, deleted after 3 days). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: tone-forge
description: AI guitar tone engineer for IK Multimedia AmpliTube 5 inside Thor Agent: plain-language tone recipes (ordered chain, amp/cab families, mic placement, pedals, 7-band EQ, noise gate, levels) with a per-decision rationale, a versioned JSON preset library, a reference-track analyser that sets the numbers from a measured recording, and a MIDI bridge that drives only the CCs the user assigned. Disclosure — the analysis tool runs ffmpeg on a local audio file the caller names and, only when an explicit url is passed, yt-dlp (http/https URLs resolving to public addresses only, fixed argv, no shell) into a temporary directory deleted after the call; the MIDI bridge sends only the CC numbers the user mapped to the MIDI port they selected; the plugin writes only under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/tone-forge (or TONEFORGE_DATA_DIR when set) and never modifies AmpliTube's own files; no telemetry.

name: tool-call-salvage
description: Removes tool-call markup that a model wrote into its final reply as text instead of calling the tool (Qwen <function=...>, <invoke>, DeepSeek DSML and tool tokens, Harmony, Kimi, Mistral and Llama formats). Only complete markup that ends the reply is touched; code blocks and markup followed by more text are left as they are. When text is left before the removed markup, a one-line notice names the tools that were not run. An optional salvage mode, off by default and limited to the models you list, turns the markup into a real call to a tool offered in that request. Disclosure: no network, files, shell, subprocesses, telemetry or stored state; logs name the format and tools, never arguments; in salvage mode text the model wrote can become a real tool call (tools offered in the request, or Thor's tool_call bridge when deferred_tools is on), run through Thor's normal approvals.

name: tool-slimmer
description: Reduce Thor tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Thor core on older Thor and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

name: toolaria
description: Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

name: toolfound
description: Search the Toolfound product directory, compare alternatives, plan a launch and use launch-preparation helpers through its hosted MCP server, with a launch workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: every tool call goes to https://toolfound.com/api/mcp; discovery tools need no account. toolfound_submit_product sends the product details and owner email the user confirms, and the owner completes verification separately. The package marks the server untrusted so Thor asks before write-capable calls. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: toolrecall-light
description: Deduplicates byte-identical repeated tool results inside Thor Agent: repeats of terminal, search_files, MCP, web and connector output are saved to a local SQLite table and replaced by a one-line stub before they enter model context, with a recall_result tool that restores the original bytes on demand. Fail-open, stdlib only, no core patches. Disclosure — stores the full text of every successful tool result of 2,000+ characters (terminal, search, MCP, web and connector output, which can include secrets the tool printed) in plaintext in Thor's plugin storage (<THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/toolrecall-light/data.db, SQLite WAL), pruned after about 24 hours; any session in the profile can recall a stored result by its id; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes.

name: topoi
description: Group your Thor Agent chats into topics, in Thor Desktop and in the Dashboard. A sidebar lists the topics active in the past week with a status dot per thread (working, waiting, unread, idle), a new chat files under your home topic, threads move between topics, and a topic's threads are searchable by message content. Cron job results arrive as topic threads you can reply to, and the reply continues that run's session. The gateway owns one topic registry and both clients read and write it over the plugin's REST API, so an edit in the Dashboard reaches the desktop app. Disclosure — registers a no-inbound `topoi` gateway platform adapter in the Thor process; serves an HTTP API at /api/plugins/topoi/ behind the Dashboard's own origin and auth; writes its topic registry and the `home_channel` projection into the `platforms.topoi` section of config.yaml; keeps session-to-topic bindings in a plugin-private SQLite database; reads the per-profile session databases and cron job store (partly through private core helpers that can change between releases) and marks threads read or deletes them through core's own session routes; bundles one skill; no third-party network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: totem
description: Connect a Totem agent for peer discovery, durable messages, shared tasks, Missions, persistent memory, and activity. Agent Plugins v1 configuration-only package with six workflow skills and Streamable HTTP MCP. Disclosure — the agent's Totem tool calls (message text, attachments, memory, task and Mission records) go to Totem's hosted MCP server at https://totemlayer.com/mcp under your Totem agent identity, authenticated with TOTEM_NETWORK_API_KEY from Thor's secret scope (or Totem OAuth); messages and files from other Totem agents enter the conversation as untrusted content; Thor does not prompt before Totem write tools (send/reply, attachment upload, task and Mission delegation); remote tool behaviour is not covered by the pinned SHA; the package licence is proprietary.

name: touchdesigner
description: Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

name: tracekit
description: Tracekit's signer decides every tool call before it runs (deny blocks, ask waits for a person) and signs each call and its outcome into a run you can verify offline. Disclosure — every tool call's name and arguments, plus its result (in full for tools Tracekit's policy marks untrusted, otherwise a SHA-256 digest), go to a Tracekit signer: by default a same-user dev signer (`python -m tracekit signer serve --dev`) that the plugin starts on first use as a detached background process, which keeps running after Thor exits until 15 minutes idle and stores signed runs plus each call's redacted arguments and results (encrypted, kept 7 days) under your user's data directory (~/.local/share/tracekit on Linux), or a remote signer when you set TRACEKIT_SIGNER to an https:// URL. The plugin fails closed: when tracekit-ai can't load or the signer refuses or can't be reached, tool calls are blocked (including every tool an execute_code script calls), and an `ask` decision holds the call until someone approves it in Tracekit or Thor's hook timeout runs out.

name: traceverse_thor_otel
description: Thor Agent OpenTelemetry traces and dashboard logs, with local-model cost estimates and optional in-process evaluation, GPU, energy, and CO2 metrics via genai-otel-instrument. Disclosure — Sends OpenTelemetry traces and log records for every turn, LLM call and tool call (session ids, models, token counts, costs, tool names, errors) to an OTLP endpoint, `http://localhost:4318` unless `THOR_OTEL_ENDPOINT` points elsewhere; prompt, response and tool argument/result text is included only when `THOR_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`; if `genai-otel-instrument` is installed it is activated in-process and instruments the LLM client libraries Thor uses.

name: track-record
description: How often is your agent right when it says it fixed something? Each reply that claims success ("this fixes it", "this should work") is logged with how sure it sounded, then checked against your next message and any test or build run in the next turn. /trackrecord shows hit rate per confidence level and model, the calibration gap and a Brier score. When certain claims hold up under 80% of the time, the agent is told its record. Pattern matching only, no model calls.

name: trackbuddy-parcel-tracker
description: Track parcels and ocean containers from chat: DHL, FedEx, UPS, Amazon Shipping, GOFO, SPX Express, USPS and 1,000+ postal and cross-border carriers through 17TRACK, plus Maersk containers and bills of lading. Five workflow skills (single lookup, container tracking, bulk report, delivery-exception triage, cost estimate) drive nine tracking Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of a tracking Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.005 to 0.04 per tracked shipment plus USD 0.005 per run). Tracking numbers are sent to Apify, looked up on the carriers' public tracking pages, and the results are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Thor runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `thor mcp add package-tracking --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Thor asking before each paid lookup. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with the carriers.

name: trade-preflight
description: Deterministic, fail-closed execution firewall for AI-initiated equity orders. A pre_tool_call hook normalizes broker-specific trade calls into one canonical order, evaluates it against an operator-owned policy (gross buy notional cap, max quantity, symbol / order-type / side allowlists) and blocks anything it cannot prove compliant; every decision and execution outcome is recorded in SQLite. Ships two paper-trading execution tools with deliberately different broker schemas (symbol/side/quantity/limit_price vs ticker/direction/qty/price), a read-only dry-run tool, a policy inspector and an audit reader. Disclosure - no network calls, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials; no requires_env; reads only its own shipped policies/default.json (copied once into the plugin data directory to seed the operator policy) and writes only inside plugin_data_dir('trade-preflight') (the policy file and the SQLite audit/ledger database); execution is simulated locally in SQLite and never reaches a broker or a real trading venue, so the plugin adds no real trading capability; the policy file is operator-owned and an agent with unrestricted shell access as the same OS user could modify it, which is a documented limitation rather than a guarantee.

name: tradeguard
description: Read-only stocks and ETF research for Thor: evidence-aware fundamentals, daily technical observations, ETF structure, comparable ranking, microstructure calculations and an explicitly experimental walk-forward ML baseline. It provides explainable heuristic research priority, not trade execution, personalized investment advice, calibrated win probabilities, price targets or position sizing. Optional ticker-only research fetches historical daily bars from Yahoo Finance's unofficial public chart endpoint only after explicit plugin configuration consent; it uses no API keys, credentials, broker access, background processes or live orders. Supplied snapshots and issuer metadata are read only from paths the user explicitly requests. Disclosure: public-data requests leave the local machine for the requested symbols, may fail or be stale, and are not entitled real-time quotes; technical-only scores are not combined valuations and all scores are unvalidated research heuristics.

name: tradytics
description: Tradytics market data in Thor through Tradytics' hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://tradytics.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with dynamic client registration and PKCE, no keys in config): live and historical options flow, dealer positioning and volatility, ranked dark pool prints, quotes and price history, fundamentals, SEC filings, insider, institutional and Congress trades, earnings and economic calendars, a full-market screener, Kalshi and Polymarket odds, Tradytics signals and the AI Fund. Bundles the tradytics skill, which teaches the agent every endpoint of the Tradytics REST API with its parameters and fields. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Tradytics' hosted server (tradytics.com), signed in as the user through Tradytics' OAuth page; the tool list is served by that server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Thor stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. Without the connector, the bundled skill calls the Tradytics REST API with an API key the user gives it, sent as a URL query parameter to tradytics.com only.

name: train-ultra
description: Ask your Train Ultra endurance coach about your training through Train Ultra's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://trainultra.app/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): today's workout, how a run went, the training plan, goals and race readiness, recovery and nutrition. Bundles the train-ultra skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Train Ultra's hosted server (trainultra.app) and acts on the user's own Train Ultra account, which needs Train Ultra Pro or the 14-day trial; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. ask_train_ultra_coach is annotated read-only. ask_train_ultra_coach_to_change can add, move, update or remove planned workouts and rest days, change goals, the training plan, zones and nutrition targets, and save coach memories; the server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before each such call. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth.

name: transcribo
description: Transcribe audio and video files to text with speaker labels through Transcribo's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.transcribo.es/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), in Spanish and 60 languages in total, up to 4 hours per file. Takes local files, public links, and Google Drive or Dropbox links. Bundles the transcribo workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Transcribo's hosted server (api.transcribo.es) and acts on the user's Transcribo account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Audio is uploaded to Transcribo, and the transcript and a compressed copy of the audio stay in the account until the user deletes them. start_transcription and start_uploaded_transcription spend the account's audio balance. To send a local file, the skill has the agent run curl to upload it to a presigned URL. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: transcription-dashscope
description: Speech-to-text for Thor via DashScope (Qwen) — voice messages and live dictation. Needs a Qwen AI Platform API key. Disclosure — voice messages and live dictation audio are uploaded to Alibaba's Qwen AI Platform (DashScope, maas.qianwenaiapi.com by default, or the base URL set in stt.dashscope.base_url / TRANSCRIPTION_DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL / DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL); the API key is TRANSCRIPTION_DASHSCOPE_API_KEY, falling back to the THOR_CUSTOM_DASHSCOPE_API_KEY custom-provider key or the built-in Alibaba provider's DASHSCOPE_API_KEY; clips are converted with the local ffmpeg into a temporary wav that is deleted afterwards.

name: treasury-cash-forecast
description: A 12-month monthly direct cash-flow forecast for corporate treasury. Fill one template (Excel or CSV) with your past cash-flow statement, the future cash flows you already know and your what-if percentages. Recurring lines are projected by a statistical model (ETS by default; SARIMA and four simple baselines selectable), known lines come from your schedule, and a known amount can replace the model for single months. The base case and every scenario run together and come back as one Excel workbook: a summary, a cash-flow statement per scenario (12 actual months, then 12 forecast months) and a sheet showing where every figure comes from, reconciled every month to the cent: opening cash + net cash flow = closing cash. A fourth tool runs the same data through several models to show how much the answer depends on the method. All figures come from a tested engine (95 tests); the language model picks the tool and explains the result. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no background process. Reads only the workbook or CSV folder you name and writes the template, the result workbook and audit files to the folder you name or next to your input. Installs two Python libraries, statsmodels and openpyxl, both with upper bounds. The optional Chronos-2 model is not installed by the plugin and is loaded from local files only, never downloaded. The bundled example company is synthetic.

name: triage
description: Keeps the list of every skill out of your context. Triage suggests skills in the composer as you type and as the chat goes on, ranked locally with no model call; a skill loads only when you pick it or clearly ask for it. Disclosure — rewrites outgoing model requests (removes Thor' skills index from system messages and adds the bodies of skills you or the model pick, which changes the cached prompt prefix on those turns) and blocks skill_view for skills not approved in the chat; with 'Hide Thor' own skills' (on by default) it adds the skills it serves to skills.disabled in your Thor config.yaml, undone with `thor triage restore`, which you must run before uninstalling; the model's skill_manage edits to skills it serves from other tools' skill folders you connect are written into those folders (edits to Thor' own skills go through Thor' skill_manage, and with skills.guard_agent_created on it makes no skill edits itself); it watches the skill folders you configure from a background thread, reads Thor' session database (state.db) read-only and the current project's AGENTS.md/README and `.thor/triage.yaml` to rank skills; `thor triage migrate --apply-config` / `--empty-roots --yes` rewrite your skills config and move your Thor skills folder aside (with backups) only when you run them; the optional `embedder` setting imports a Python class you name; it makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

name: tripo
description: Tripo's official plugin, made by VAST, the company behind Tripo. Tripo's own tripo-cli (pinned tripo-cli@0.11.1) runs locally as an MCP server with 26 tools for text, image and multiview to 3D, concept and multiview images, texturing, rigging and animation, retopology, segmentation, Gaussian splats, format conversion (GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, USDZ, 3MF) and downloads, plus the tripo-3d and tripo-game-asset workflow skills; Game Studio turns a rigged, animated model into a character you play in Thor Desktop, a three.js web prototype, Godot, Unity or Unreal. In Thor Desktop: inline 3D cards with Next and Download menus and a Play mode, a gallery of recent generations and a credit chip. Every call that is not read-only goes through Thor's approval prompt, local-file uploads included; no per-tool costs or spend limit are declared. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY from an international Tripo account. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned tripo-cli from npm through npx, which Thor runs on its managed Node.js as a local child process; it sends prompts and the local images (up to 20 MB) or models (up to 150 MB) you or the agent name to Tripo's API (openapi.tripo3d.ai) under your key, gets only TRIPO_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics. Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or a folder the agent names, replacing files of the same name there; tripo-cli keeps a task history (prompts included) and the Desktop half a record of which chat made each task, both in the plugin's data folder. The Desktop backend reads your balance and recent tasks from Tripo's API, serves models only from the plugin's data folder or your home folder, and downloads results only from Tripo's result storage; the Desktop renderer shows task previews from Tripo's short-lived result links. Through Thor's terminal tool the skills run `thor config path`, file-size checks and background sleep timers on chat apps, and, when asked, a preview-video renderer (headless Chromium and ffmpeg already on the machine; its first run downloads three.js 0.180.0 from npm, integrity-checked), Python's http.server on 127.0.0.1 for the web prototype (which loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net) and your own Blender for an optimized copy. No telemetry.

name: tripscout
description: Cheap city-break finder: prices flights AND lodging together across a date window, adds the ground cost of reaching each departure airport, and ranks whole trips by total cost, with lodging-type filters (hotel/hostel/apartment) and optional food and attraction estimates. Say where you leave from and it works out the airports serving you: any town on earth is geocoded on OpenStreetMap and its nearest airports with scheduled flights are found in a bundled OurAirports table (4,008 airports), with train/bus costs estimated from distance; 33 hand-checked departure presets and 49 destinations ship with it. Every result carries prefilled booking links (flight, stay, ground, airport transfer).
