Ships four agent tools plus a Thor Desktop pane (desktop/plugin.js) whose backend runs the same engine as the tools. Disclosure — no API key and no account: searches read the Google Flights results page and Google Hotels' public batchexecute RPC from your own IP address with a browser TLS fingerprint, so the cities, airports, dates, traveller count and currency you search are sent to Google; a departure place that is not one of the built-in presets is also sent as a search query to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim geocoder (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) to find nearby airports; nothing else about you is sent. Prices, hotel names, geocoding results and cache keys are stored locally in SQLite under Thor' plugin data directory. A consent cookie declaring essential-only cookies is sent, because from the EU Google otherwise answers with its "Before you continue" interstitial instead of results; no tracking-consent value is ever sent. Results include prefilled search links to Google Flights/Hotels/Maps, Booking.com, Hostelworld and Airbnb that open only when you click them. Python dependencies (fast-flights, primp, typing_extensions) are prepared in the shared plugin environment at install time with the user's consent. Nothing is booked, no card or passport data is taken, and no credentials are stored.

name: tripwire
description: Logs every refused agent action (a tool blocked by a guardrail or plugin, or a dangerous command denied, cancelled or timed out at approval) as one JSON line, so a no-agent cron script can send the owner one short alert. Observer only, fails open. Disclosure — appends one JSON line per refused action to ~/.thor/tripwire/events.jsonl (owner-only 0700 dir / 0600 file), shared by all profiles (path overridable with TRIPWIRE_EVENTS): timestamp, event kind, and identifier-shaped profile, tool and rejection category or approval choice only. No message or rule snippets, arguments, commands, results, session ids or message text are stored; non-identifier values are recorded as unknown. A pre_tool_call hook reads ~/.thor/tripwire/TEST_BLOCK and, only while that file exists, blocks the single tool it names for the single profile it names (a drill switch to prove the alarm). No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

name: trophy-room
description: Achievements for Thor Desktop: 120 illustrated trophies earned from real Thor work (tools, skills, profiles, cron, plugins, messaging, kanban, media), collectible cards across five tiers, unlock pop-ups with a synth sting, optional OS notifications, recent trophies and replayable away collections. Hooks only on the agent side (no tools, middleware or env vars); progress is stored in the plugin's own data directory. No telemetry or third-party services; artwork is bundled and the sound is synthesized locally. Optional read-only import from the bundled thor-achievements plugin. Derived in part from thor-achievements by PCinkusz (MIT): the 60 original achievement definitions.

name: true402-swap-guard
description: Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Free edition: it never pays, holds no wallet key and has no payment code. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Thor approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: trurl
description: Private taste memory for Thor with proactive hypotheses, sourced cross-theme discovery, compact context, Taste Atlas and Sunday editions. Disclosure — During new-profile setup the bundled skill proposes a weekly "Sunday edition" (20:00 local time) and, unless you say "one-off only", has the agent create a recurring Thor cron job that runs a curation turn on your model plan every Sunday. The plugin itself only reads the cron list to confirm it, and `trurl_schedule off` plus pausing that job stops delivery. Your taste profile, feedback and history are stored locally in the plugin's data directory (trurl.sqlite3, taste-atlas.html, editions/).

name: trust-ladder
description: Correct your agent once and it stays corrected. trust-ladder compiles each user correction to the highest rung it can prove: a pre_tool_call guard that blocks the repeat, a check on what a write puts into matching files, a rule injected every turn, or human review through Thor's own approval prompt. A model-proposed guard is installed only if it matches the mistaken call and spares the corrected one, regexes are profiled against ReDoS before install, verifier commands gate "done", and a ledger counts every catch (/teach, /trust, /verify). Disclosure — local only: stores rules, tasks and a catch ledger (matched snippets, redacted, no full arguments) under <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/trust-ladder/; no network, no telemetry, no credentials or env vars read; verifier commands run only through Thor's terminal tool (normal approvals apply); the model can add rules but only the user can disable or remove them; guards are best-effort pattern matches, not a sandbox.

name: truthgate
description: Deterministic final-turn verification for newly introduced Python stubs and common embedded-secret patterns, using pre-edit baselines and at most two corrective continuations. Standard-library-only, fail-open, and no network, subprocess, LLM, approval-bypass, or core-patching behavior. Disclosure -- reads only changed-file paths supplied by Thor (including an absolute changed path outside the session directory), persists sanitized finding metadata in Thor's profile-scoped plugin data without raw secrets or source text, and can produce false positives or false negatives. Disclosure — reads every file the agent edits (including paths outside the working directory) to compare it with a pre-edit snapshot, can make the agent continue up to two extra times per turn (extra model cost), and stores finding metadata (file path, line, kind; no source or secret values) in its plugin data directory.

name: tsubasa
description: Tsubasa OpenAI-compatible model provider (tool calling not supported yet). Disclosure — sends prompts and your TSUBASA_API_KEY to api.tsubasa.sh, operated by PalmAndWand; the API currently serves Canada only and answers HTTP 451 to requests from elsewhere.

name: ttsbuddy
description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Thor voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `thor ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

name: tubesaku-creator-insights
description: Read-only Japanese VTuber, stream, game trend and cover-song research via hosted TubeSaku MCP. Disclosure — requests and bounded tool arguments/client metadata are logged by tubesaku.com with hashed session IDs; hosted logging cannot be disabled by this package. Read terms before enabling (discovery may contact the service); the skill asks for explicit agreement before tool calls, but consent is not server-enforced. No credentials, local executable, local telemetry or self-updater. Hosted service changes independently of the pinned package.

name: tuneviva
description: Read-only sheet music discovery and practice links through TuneViva's Streamable HTTP MCP server, with browser-local recognition guidance.

name: tupliq-launchpad
description: RevenueCat revenue & subscription metrics for your apps, plus git changelog drafting for Play Store releases.

name: turn-bell
description: A bell in the Thor desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic Thor already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic Thor is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).

name: turn-completion-nudge
description: Nudges the agent to continue when a turn ends prematurely (planning or announcing next steps it has not done). Fail-open: never blocks a turn. Disclosure — when the user sets `send_turn_text: true`, clipped turn text (about 1,200 chars of the user request and 1,500 chars of the assistant reply) is sent to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai, billed to the user's OPENROUTER_API_KEY) after each turn to score whether to nudge; with `amos_fallback: true` the same text may go to the keyless Amos/Scira API (api.amos.scira.ai). Both are off by default.

name: turn-usage
description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

name: tusk
description: Thor long-term memory on Walrus mainnet (decentralized storage on Sui) through the official Walrus Memory SDK: encrypted inside the relayer's TEE, owned by your key, survives wiping or reinstalling Thor, and the same on every machine and for other agents on the same account. Recall before each turn, turn capture, built-in memory mirroring and pre-compression saves; a crash-safe, rate-paced SQLite write outbox with a receipt and public Walruscan proof per memory; a Tusk dashboard tab (semantic search across namespaces, live write queue, one-click verification that downloads the blob from a public Walrus aggregator and checks it is ciphertext); /tusk and thor tusk (status, recall, proofs, verify, namespaces, import, flush, export, restore). Secrets are redacted before anything is queued. Disclosure — each turn's user message (as the recall query), finished turns (for fact extraction), built-in memory entries and tusk_remember facts are sent over HTTPS to relayer.memory.walrus.xyz (or MEMWAL_SERVER_URL) signed with MEMWAL_PRIVATE_KEY / MEMWAL_ACCOUNT_ID; verify downloads blobs from aggregator.walrus-mainnet.walrus.space; queued writes (until sent) and receipts are kept in plugin-data/tusk/outbox.db (0600); one in-process background writer thread; dashboard routes sit behind the dashboard auth gate; no shell commands, no subprocesses, no telemetry.

name: twenty-crm
description: Twenty CRM for Thor Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

name: twitch-assist
description: Put your Thor in your Twitch chat as a co-host: viewers type !ask (or @mention the bot) and get a real agent answer in chat, and the broadcaster or a mod can run Backseat Mode, a chat vote whose winner becomes Thor's next task. Stdlib only (asyncio IRC over TLS). Disclosure — network calls go only to irc.chat.twitch.tv:6697 (TLS IRC) and https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/validate; the Twitch token is read through Thor's secret scope; private by default (broadcaster and TWITCH_ALLOWED_USERS ids only), and opening it to every viewer needs TWITCH_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true, after which non-broadcaster requests are dropped unless both memory flags are off and platform_toolsets.twitch is pinned; viewer turns are limited to web search by a pre_tool_call guard; Thor injects the owner's SOUL.md persona into every gateway session (skip_context_files does not remove it on 0.23.x) and MEMORY.md/USER.md unless the memory flags are off, and allowlisted viewers are served even then, so run the bot in a dedicated Thor profile with an empty SOUL.md and memory off.

name: twring
description: Call your Thor from your phone and let it call you back, through the Twring app (iPhone and Android): live two-way voice calls and typed chat in one Thor conversation, dangerous-command approvals answered by voice or tap through Thor's own approval card, and a phone ring when a scheduled job delivers. Twring does the speech; Thor keeps its model, memory and tools. Disclosure — while the gateway runs, one outbound WebSocket to the linked Twring server (api.twring.com by default, or the TWRING_SERVER you set) carries call and chat turn text in, and Thor's replies, approval questions (command preview and reason) and cron results out, plus the name and success or failure of each tool Thor runs while a call or chat turn is in progress (never its arguments or output; Thor's tool hooks are global, so a tool another chat runs at the same moment can be reported too; the pre_tool_call and post_tool_call hooks never block or change a tool); anyone signed in to the linked Twring account drives this Thor as its owner and can approve one dangerous command at a time by voice or tap through Thor's own approval card; HTTPS calls to the same server link the account (sending this computer's hostname as its name), post replies to the chat and ring the phone (cron results ring by default; TWRING_RING_ON_DELIVERY=false turns it off); one link token (TWRING_TOKEN), saved by `thor twring link` through Thor's .env route; no files of its own, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: typesafe-skill-router
description: TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

name: uk-companies
description: UK Companies returns one sheet. Disclosure — Names and numbers to api.company-information.service.gov.uk as HTTP Basic with COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY when set. Registered name to www.thegazette.co.uk, no key. A double quote is not sent. Charity names and numbers to api.charitycommission.gov.uk with CHARITY_COMMISSION_API_KEY when set. Postcode to landregistry.data.gov.uk, no key. Lookups stop after 60 seconds. Requests wait at most 20 seconds. Morning job sends watched numbers to Companies House only. Remove leaves plugin-data/uk-companies/watch.json, scripts/uk-companies-watch.py, and the morning job. Stop it with thor cron remove <job id>. About 680 KB with .git. Empty allowlist keeps tools enabled. thor tools disable uk_companies --platform telegram. Contains HM Land Registry data © Crown copyright and database right 2021. Licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

name: ultimate-dashboard
description: A customizable dashboard page for Thor Desktop and the Webapp, with 16 cards: approvals you can answer, running sessions, scheduled jobs with a 7-day timeline, job results, plan usage, spend, tool activity, health, services, machine stats, logs, agent memory, skills, files made, Workers and live tasks, plus Quick launch shortcuts. Arrange cards into views, save templates, and the layout syncs between Desktop and the Webapp. English and Arabic (RTL); follows the Thor theme. Disclosure — no telemetry and no third-party requests; the page talks only to your Thor gateway. Runs one command through cli.exec, `thor usage --provider <slug> --json`, which asks each signed-in provider for plan usage. Its backend opens state.db read-only (session titles, token and cost columns, tool names and outcomes, MEDIA file paths; no message text), and reads the size of memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (never the text), the dates in skills/.usage.json, the newest file in cron/output/<job id>/, Thor' Worker transcripts in cache/delegation/live/ (goals, tool names and one-line command previews; never result text), and machine stats via psutil including the hostname. Stores the layout in plugin-data/ultimate-dashboard/state.json. Answers an approval only when you click, with once or deny, never always. Anyone signed in to your dashboard can see what the cards show.

name: umami-digest
description: Each morning one letter arrives with yesterday's pageviews, visitors, day-over-day change, the top five pages by pageviews, and a surge flag from the Umami instance you already run, with no model. Umami 3.4.1 returns expanded paths 500 at a time in visitor order. The letter sends limit 500 and walks offset until a short page, or 20 pages, then ranks by pageviews. A day that hits the cap says the five are the top 5 among the first N paths. Disclosure — GET only to the origin in UMAMI_URL with Authorization Bearer UMAMI_API_KEY; plain http only to loopback, otherwise https; the plugin downloads nothing at runtime; umami_digest is read-only and asks for no approval; anyone you allow on a gateway can call it; turn a surface off with thor tools; thor umami-digest schedule writes a no-agent cron script that costs 0 tokens with no daily cap; empty stdout sends nothing; run unschedule before removal; a leftover job stops with thor cron remove <id>; after thor plugins remove, thor cron remove <id> leaves scripts/umami-digest.py and you delete that file yourself; state stays in plugin-data/umami-digest; schedule uses thor_constants.get_thor_home, so an update can stop it.

name: umt
description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

name: unbl0ck
description: One queue of everything blocked on you: live agent prompts, pairing requests, blocked Kanban cards and chats on any platform that ask you something. Answer Kanban cards in place; optional one-line summaries and Ask send item text to your configured model through ctx.llm (both can be turned off). Disclosure — reads every local profile's chat history (state.db, read-only), profile titles and pending pairing requests (through Thor's PairingStore, never the codes) to build one queue, records live clarify/approval prompt text in its plugin data, and can comment on and unblock Kanban cards when you answer one; by default sends each new queue item's text (other profiles' chats included) to the configured model for a one-line summary, and card data on Ask (turn off with `bluf_enabled: false` / `ask_enabled: false`); on messaging platforms `/unbl0ck` replies with a count only; uses Thor's internal Kanban modules, so a Thor update can break it; no network of its own, no shell, no credentials.

name: unblockbruecke
description: Cards to unblock yourself or your agent, drawn by you when you are stuck and by Thor when its tool calls keep failing. Disclosure — With auto-draw switched on (off by default), once 3 of the last 5 tool calls in a turn failed it adds one card's text to that failing result (one card per turn), so the model reads it, and adds one line naming the card after that turn's reply (not in scheduled jobs, webhooks, the API server or single-query runs); the agent's deck tool can import a deck from any file path and export a .yaml deck file to any folder you name (attended chats only, never overwriting a non-deck file); the page's settings switches save through a short `thor config set` child process.

name: unbrowse
description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

name: understudy
description: Audition cheaper models on your real Thor history before you switch. Understudy replays a sample of your past decisions (replies and tool calls) on candidate models through Thor's own credentials, has a blind judge compare each step with what your current model actually did, and reports how often each candidate could have taken over (with a 95% confidence interval), its critical misses, a per-category breakdown and projected monthly cost. Two tools, /understudy, thor understudy, and a Desktop page with an inline scorecard. Disclosure — reads this profile's session history read-only; sends redacted excerpts of past conversations (plus, by default, an excerpt of the agent's system prompt; `include_persona: false` stops it) to the candidate models and the judge model you pick, through ctx.llm on your existing provider credentials; each audition is capped by budget_usd only when Thor reports the call cost (unpriced models are bounded by the sample size, not the budget); the agent tool spends without its own confirmation prompt (the bundled skill tells the model to dry-run and ask first; /understudy asks unless --yes); reads Thor's local models.dev cache (active profile, then the default root) for list prices; writes run records and reports under plugin-data/understudy; runs a background worker thread only while an audition runs; requests the llm.model_override and llm.provider_override capabilities; no telemetry, no other network calls.

name: underwriting
description: Commercial real estate underwriting that shows its work: rebuilds net operating income from the rent roll and T-12 instead of trusting the broker's claim, runs buy-box tests against a DSCR-sized loan, returns the counter-price at which a rejected deal actually clears, sweeps price to find where a deal flips, models a hold period, and returns null rather than inventing a number the document never stated. Seven deterministic tools plus an /underwrite command and a skill. Extraction reads a document the user names (local path or URL) and is audited back against the document text: every figure is matched to the line it came from and marked verified, and a citation the document cannot support is reported. The arithmetic is pure Python standard library with no network calls and no third-party packages; only extraction calls the host model, and only a URL passthrough fetches anything over the network. Writes are confined to the plugin's own data directory: memos and extraction audit trails take a bare filename under <data_dir>/exports/, and the deal book is JSON under <data_dir>. Document input is treated as untrusted, because it is: local reads go through Thor' read block list with no $HOME fallback, and URL input is limited to public http(s) with every redirect hop re-checked. Not investment advice.

name: undo-effects
description: Puts back files an agent deleted or overwrote: before write_file, patch and destructive terminal commands (rm, mv, cp, redirects, tee, sed -i, find -delete) it saves the affected files to a local store and lets the tool run unchanged; /undo-effects lists the effects and restores them, refusing to overwrite later edits unless forced and keeping a safety copy so a restore can be undone. Disclosure — no network; reads the contents of the files and directories a covered tool call is about to change; writes unencrypted copies of them under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/undo-effects/ (files named like credentials, anything inside .ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .docker, .kube, .azure and .gcloud, files above 50 MB, node_modules, .venv and .git are skipped and reported); the same folder also keeps the paths and the first 100 characters of each terminal command, with secrets masked on a best-effort basis; runs no shell command and no background process; never blocks, rewrites or approves a tool call, and runs the tool even if a snapshot fails; covers the local terminal backend only; no telemetry.

name: undo-send
description: Undo Send for your agent: outward-facing actions (thor send / imsg send messages to Telegram, Slack, Signal, SMS and others, app connector and MCP writes, git push, gh pr/issue create, npm publish, curl POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) wait in a short grace window before they run, so you can cancel them from a Desktop status-bar countdown (Undo / Send now), by replying "undo" in Telegram or another gateway chat (owners listed in undo_senders), or with /unsend. On undo the agent is told the action never ran and not to retry it. Disclosure — delays matching outward-facing tool calls (messages, MCP/connector writes, git push, gh/npm/twine publishes, thor send, curl POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) by up to window_seconds (default 20), including unattended/cron runs, never indefinitely; makes no network calls of its own, reads no credentials and sends no telemetry; stores a one-line summary of each held action (URLs reduced to their host), its chat origin, timestamps and outcome in THOR_HOME/plugin-data/undo-send/pending.db; reads inbound gateway text before gateway auth only to match a bare "undo", acting only for owners listed in undo_senders (empty by default, so chat undo is off) and only on actions held from that same chat; /unsend from the CLI, Desktop or an admitted chat user cancels the newest held action in any session; runs no shell commands or background processes; a classifier error runs the tool unchanged.

name: unibaseio-membase
description: Long-term memory for you and your AI from Membase (membase.com, by Unibase): one memory every connected AI shares. Searches the user's Membase memory before each turn (8 s, fail-open) and adds membase_search, membase_save and membase_profile. Disclosure — user prompts are sent as search queries to the Membase API (api.app.membase.com); with the opt-in capture_turns setting the user's messages are saved there too; on a Thor build with memory.user_store: provider, what Thor' memory tool records about the user is saved to their Membase profile instead of USER.md. MEMBASE_API_KEY comes from the Thor secret scope; the only local file is $THOR_HOME/unibaseio-membase.json. No background processes, shell commands or telemetry.

name: unicode-ref
description: @unicode: context references that spell text out character by character for the model: @unicode:"text" attaches a table of every character of the quoted text (code point, Unicode name, category) with notes on what does not show on screen: invisible characters and their positions, text-direction controls, spaces other than the ordinary one, Unicode tag characters (decoded), words that mix Latin letters with lookalike Cyrillic, Greek or fullwidth ones, and private-use or unassigned code points; @unicode:U+200B describes up to 20 code points (name, category, UTF-8 bytes, decomposition); the TUI and Desktop composer suggest characters by name. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's unicodedata; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @unicode: reference provider

name: unified-inbox
description: One inbox for the user's WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn messages through their own Unipile account (API v2): a synced local copy, search in any language, triage with a reason for each chat, memory of people and open items, drafts in the user's own writing style, scam warnings, plans offered for the calendar, translation, a people radar and a spoken brief, plus an Inbox page in the web dashboard and Thor Desktop. Every send and reaction goes through Thor's own approval prompt (a pre_tool_call hook) and is refused when approval would be skipped (yolo mode, approvals off, cron), under hard pacing limits. Disclosure — calls the Unipile API (api.unipile.com) with the user's key; Unipile reaches WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn through unofficial access, which may break those platforms' terms. Every send and reaction goes through Thor's own approval prompt and is refused under yolo mode, approvals off or unattended runs; the model may attach any file the user can read (key and login files excepted), and each file is named in that prompt. Optional and off until configured: a cloud embedding provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere or Voyage AI) that receives message text, the user's own Supabase project for two-way sync (api.supabase.com once, to create tables), a private iCal address read for busy times, a webhook receiver on 127.0.0.1 that accepts only HMAC-signed Unipile deliveries, and alerts injected into a chat the user picks. Runs a background sync thread by default that summarises, drafts and translates new messages with Thor's model (capped per day); text sent to a model or provider has one-time codes, passwords and card, bank and ID numbers removed first. Stores chats, messages, memory and a send log in SQLite under the plugin's data folder; secrets come only from Thor's secret store. Calls Thor internals that are not a stable plugin API (tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio for voice notes, private tools.approval checks). No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-update.

name: unitares
description: Records each Thor session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

name: unraid
description: Read-only Unraid monitoring for Thor Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through Thor secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.

name: upstash
description: Long-term memory and searchable chat history for Thor on Upstash Redis Search, with hybrid recall (keywords and meaning) and no separate vector database. Recalls related memories into each turn, saves every session as a searchable transcript, mirrors the built-in memory tool (adds, corrections and removals), and gives the model upstash_memory_save / upstash_memory_search / upstash_memory_forget and upstash_chat_search. Memories use the same keys as @upstash/agentkit-sdk, so they are shared with AgentKit apps on the same database. Works on the Upstash Free plan (one search index). Disclosure — memories and full chat transcripts are written to the Upstash Redis database you configure (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN) and sent to it over HTTPS on every turn. Memory text and each recall query are embedded by Upstash Redis Search's managed embeddings in that database; chat transcripts are not embedded, and the plugin contacts nothing else. Telemetry is opt-in and off by default: UPSTASH_THOR_TELEMETRY=1 adds SDK, Python version and platform tags to request headers sent to that same database.

name: upstash-box
description: Terminal backend that runs Thor terminal, execute_code and file tools in an Upstash Box cloud container, paused and resumed by name per task or created per session and deleted when it ends. Disclosure — requires an Upstash Box API key (UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY); every command and the files the file tools touch are sent to Upstash Box; your Thor skills, cache and skill-registered credential files are uploaded to ~/.thor in the Box and skill and cache files changed in the Box are copied back to your machine; SDK telemetry is turned off; Boxes are created, paused and deleted in the key's account and billed to it; persistent mode keeps one paused Box per task (each Thor Desktop chat is its own task), and paused Boxes count toward the account's Box limit; if the Upstash account has GitHub connected, every Box holds those GitHub credentials in ~/.git-credentials, and every Box has an UPSTASH_BLOB_TOKEN environment variable, both readable by the commands the agent runs; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the Box.

name: us-air-rules
description: Does this EPA air rule apply to me? Screen a plant or a household against Title 40 and get applies / check with EHS / skip, with the citation. Compare two plant scenarios with the same bundled pack (changed inputs, changed verdicts, missing facts, unchanged count) without contacting the network. Read or search current eCFR Title 40 text, list recent EPA Federal Register documents for one part, and look up a state's EPA-approved SIP rules in 40 CFR part 52. Disclosure: HTTPS GET only to www.ecfr.gov (title currency, section or subpart XML, part structure, search words) and www.federalregister.gov (part, optional term, date window, document type). No API key. The citation and the search words are sent; a facility or household profile is not. usair_plant_compare makes no request and does not upload a profile. Writes public regulatory responses (JSON, with fetch time) under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/us-air-rules/cache, capped by cache_max_mb (default 100 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 20 s timeout, 10 MB response cap. No hooks, no cron, no background process, no telemetry, no self-update. Screening aid, not a compliance determination and not legal advice. eCFR is an editorial compilation, not the official edition.

name: us-census
description: ACS population, income, age, and housing for a US place, with vintage year, variable id, and margin of error. This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau. Disclosure — HTTPS only to api.census.gov, geocoding.geo.census.gov, and tigerweb.geo.census.gov (all US Census Bureau); your free CENSUS_API_KEY goes only as the data-call key; metadata, the geocoder, and TIGERweb are keyless; redirects are refused; on every surface, including gateways, no user list, so an admitted guest can estimate with this profile's key; schedule writes scripts/us-census-vintage.py and one local no-model morning job; the job, script, and vintage file remain after disable or removal.

name: us-filings
description: US Filings lists recent SEC EDGAR filings for a ticker or CIK and locates one by accession number. It sends one morning message when a watched company files. Disclosure — HTTPS only to data.sec.gov and www.sec.gov (US SEC), no API key, no proxy, no redirects; US_FILINGS_CONTACT is read with get_secret each call; add and remove use pre_tool_call, yolo and approvals off skip it if a person is present, and cron, thor -q, webhook, or a separate process cannot add or remove even after always; thor cron create --no-agent --script creates the job, empty stdout sends nothing, and the job, scripts/us-filings-watch.py, and plugin-data/us-filings/state.json stay after uninstall; tools are on every surface.

name: usage-flame
description: Pinned glowing chip + fire-themed panel with live subscription-quota windows (remaining %, reset countdown, burn-rate pace and run-out forecast with sparkline history) for every provider Thor reports usage for. 12 color themes and fonts, RU/EN, zero dependencies, works on Windows. Disclosure — runs thor usage --json through the Desktop gateway (cli.exec) every 1–15 minutes and sweeps up to 8 providers every 15 minutes; each run queries that provider's usage endpoint with the credential Thor already holds. Reads the composer's selected provider from Desktop localStorage. No network calls of its own.

name: usage-guard
description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage Thor already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent` (a lone Anthropic reading of exactly 100% with extra usage off is treated as possibly 1%, because Thor's Anthropic parser scales any utilization <= 1 by 100 until thor-agent#139916, and passes; a 100% that follows a higher reading in the same window, or any 100% while extra usage is on, refuses), and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through Thor's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; a `/usage-guard` slash command and a Thor Desktop status-bar chip (polling a read-only `GET /api/plugins/usage-guard/status` route every 60 s and after each turn) report the guard's decision from the same cache, never making a usage request; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated. Borrowing is off by default: when `hydrate_from_paths` names files, the guard may read those JSON snapshots instead of reading the endpoint, validating every window and never writing them into its own cache.

name: usage-hud
description: Compact Codex account limits and focused-session token usage for Thor Desktop. Disclosure — uses Thor gateway session.usage and model.options; Thor may refresh provider account usage; no direct credential access or author telemetry.

name: usage-ledger
description: Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows and macOS beta).

name: usage-stats
description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the Thor Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Nous.

name: usage-watch
description: Shows how much of your Claude or Codex usage window is left as one line in the chat, every few turns, with reset times. No LLM calls.

name: ussd-platform
description: Talk to Thor from any phone by dialling a USSD short code: no app, no data plan, no smartphone. A gateway platform for Africa's Talking-style USSD callbacks: replies are paged into 160-character keypad screens, exec approvals become numbered menus whose choices appear only after the last page of the command, answers that outlive the session wait in an inbox or arrive by SMS, and a dropped call resumes on the page it left. Ships a keypad-phone simulator served to localhost only. Disclosure — runs an HTTP callback server on 127.0.0.1:8788 while the gateway runs (the user exposes it through their own tunnel); callbacks are authenticated by a 16+ character secret in the URL path because USSD gateways do not sign requests; only when AFRICASTALKING_USERNAME and AFRICASTALKING_API_KEY are set, message text and the recipient's number go to api.africastalking.com (or its sandbox) to send SMS; USSD and SMS are readable by the mobile operator and aggregator; inboxes are in memory only; no telemetry, no shell commands, no self-update.

name: uuid-ref
description: @uuid: context references that decode a UUID or ULID for the model: @uuid:<id> takes a UUID in any common spelling (hyphens or not, braces, upper case, urn:uuid:) or a ULID, and attaches what its bits say, read the way RFC 9562 lays them out: version and variant in words, the creation time a v1, v6, v7 or ULID carries in UTC with how long ago, the clock sequence and node of a v1 or v6 and whether the node is random or looks like a network card (MAC) address, the local id and domain of a v2, a ULID's 128 bits written as a UUID, and the Nil, Max and RFC namespace UUIDs by name; up to 10 identifiers in one reference are compared by creation time; the TUI and Desktop composer preview an identifier as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's re, datetime and fractions; nothing is looked up; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the identifiers, but the @uuid: reference and the decoded text become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @uuid: reference provider.

name: ux3-product-design-harness
description: MIT-licensed product judgment across User, Evidence and Business flows, with one portable Agent Plugins v1 skill and all 91 original skill files. Disclosure: skill instructions run bundled local Python/jsonschema validators and read/write user-controlled local briefs, context packs and review outputs, which can contain personal data. Optional evidence gathering uses explicitly user/host-authorized tools, including external search and connectors; selected claims, queries or evidence go to the chosen services under their policies. There is no publisher-operated receiving endpoint, retention service, telemetry or background process. The bundled jev_gate.py runs offline; connecting a remote decision service needs separate configuration and consent. No MCP server, native plugin entrypoint, registered tools, hooks or middleware.

name: vail-agent-assurance
description: Find, test and fix risky behaviors in your AI agents with the VAIL Agent Assurance Engine: upload an agent's source to scan it for behavior risks and generate probes, then run those probes against the agent locally, graded as VAIL grades them, fix what fails and rerun to prove the fix. Works on LangGraph, Thor and OpenClaw agents, including your own Thor profiles. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the hosted VAIL MCP server plus the agent-assurance and agent-improvement skills. Needs a VAIL account and a personal access token, set as VAIL_TOKEN (the plugin's secret setting, kept in the profile's .env). Disclosure — every call goes to agents.projectvail.com with your VAIL token; scanning uploads the agent source you choose to VAIL, which stores it as that agent's source (replacing the previous upload); the agent-improvement skill downloads VAIL's grading package (a version VAIL's server chooses at run time, sha256-checked against that server's own value), installs it into a local virtual environment, runs it, and sends test messages to the agent you name. No telemetry.

name: vail-assurance-panel
description: A Thor Desktop page that assures every Thor profile (each bot) with the VAIL Agent Assurance Engine: scan a profile in one click, then see its behavior risks by severity, probe coverage, whether it changed since the last scan, and which risks were fixed locally with probes passing before and after. Pairs with the vail-agent-assurance plugin, which does the testing and fixing. Native package with a desktop/plugin.js page and a dashboard backend; needs a VAIL personal access token as VAIL_TOKEN (secret setting) and the Desktop half switched on in Capabilities → Plugins. Disclosure — the backend calls agents.projectvail.com (or the vail_url you set) with your token; Scan with VAIL uploads the chosen profile's SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, config.yaml, its own skills and plugins (text files only; never .env or hidden files, credential-named files, sessions, memories, logs or databases; token-shaped strings and config.yaml values under secret-looking keys are replaced with <redacted> by pattern matching, so review the file list) only after you confirm a dialog listing every file; it reads SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, config.yaml, skills, plugins and .vail/improvement records of every profile on this machine; while a scan runs, a thread in the Thor backend checks VAIL every 15 seconds and starts probe generation (at most 45 minutes); it writes only links.json in its own data directory. No telemetry, no shell commands.

name: valun
description: Let your Thor agent negotiate service-for-credit deals with other independently controlled agents, signing with its own key within limits you set; credit notes, debt transfers and set-offs recorded by a real Basis tracker anchored on Ergo testnet (amounts in nanoERG of Ergo testnet: test coins with no monetary value). Disclosure — Talks to the Valun server set in `server_url` (default https://valun.tech, run by the plugin author's Valun project), sending your participant id, locally signed offers/acceptances/credit notes/consents, deal terms and deliverables, and the goals/limits your agent records; whoever runs that server sees all of it. Your handle, display name, operator name, about text, offered services (`join --services`) and the work you pay others for (`join --wants`), with your deal counts and what you hold and owe, are public on that server (its directory and your agent page, `/agent/<handle>`). A guarantee (since 0.6.0: your agent backing another agent's IOU to one creditor, up to a cap) is seen in full by its backer, its issuer, its creditor and the server; the counts and amounts of the guarantees a participant gave, was backed by or holds, and of the calls honored, honored late or overdue, are public in its record. With public vouches (since 0.6.2: `thor valun profile --public-vouches on`, off unless chosen), the guarantees between your agent and agents that also chose them are public on both agent pages: who backed whom, the cap and how calls were honored, never the creditor. `thor valun profile` (you, at a terminal) also changes the public profile fields you give it (services, wants, about, display name). Stores VALUN_AGENT_TOKEN and VALUN_SIGNING_SECRET via `thor config set` (passed to it through the child process's environment, not its command line). Commitments go through Thor' approval prompt by default; `thor valun join --approvals none` (or `confirm_commitments: false`, `--yolo`, `approvals.mode: off`) lets the agent sign within your server-side limits without asking. With `process_consents` on (set by `thor valun join --sandbox`; off for invited joins) the client also signs, without a prompt, the net-neutral set-offs, transfers of your own debt and payments to you that your policy allows, each capped by `consents.max_PC` (50,000,000 nanoERG by default). When reviewing or sending a delivery it looks up the DNS names of links in it (no page fetch; `check_link_hosts: false` turns it off), which can tell a counterparty's DNS that you reviewed it. `join --direct-tools` sets `tools.tool_search.enabled off` in that profile. The owner's `thor valun ergo` commands, run at a terminal, read the boxes a reserve or a redemption spends from the Ergo testnet node the Valun server names (by default a public testnet node, which sees your IP address and those box ids), check them, sign the Ergo testnet transaction with the agent's own key, and submit it through the Valun server only with `--broadcast`. A note can be redeemed on Ergo testnet against its issuer's reserve, in tERG, test coins with no monetary value.

name: vape-coach
description: Local-first webcam vape tracker and taper coach. A MediaPipe watcher spots hand-to-mouth puffs plus the exhale, and the target gap between vaping sessions grows ~10%/day after a 1-day baseline. Hitting early climbs a nudge ladder: a roast, a sarcastic (never real) PR threat, a protein-shake order, then jumping jacks the same watcher counts on camera by itself. Nag-only: never blocks a request, never gates a tool, no tool that can touch code. Desktop pane with camera Start/Stop and a live rep counter, a status-bar countdown, pet/toast roasts, /vape and three agent tools. Disclosure — uses the webcam only while the watcher runs (after the user clicks Start camera, which starts `python -m vapecoach.cli watch` as a child process, or while `thor vape watch` runs in a terminal); frames stay in memory and are never written or sent; stores timestamps, scores and counts in the plugin data dir; downloads three SHA256-pinned MediaPipe models from storage.googleapis.com on first start; the Desktop half polls the plugin's own local API every 3 s. No LLM calls, credentials or telemetry.

name: vault-view
description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Thor Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host and records that folder in ~/.thor/vault-view-root.json; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in; the optional vault_view_present_note agent tool is on by default for anyone who can use the agent on any platform and copies any requested Markdown note from that vault into the Thor document cache (copies are not cleaned up) to deliver it as a file card.

name: vaultknox
description: Secret-leak protection for Thor chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional thor-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

name: vaultwarden
description: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

name: vector-platform
description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Thor becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `thor gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `thor gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/thor-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.thor/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.thor/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

name: veille
description: Fraud and validity checks for Thor through the Veille API: emails (with an SMTP inbox check), domains, IPs (VPN, proxy, Tor, data center), phone numbers, EU VAT numbers and IBANs, plus ECB exchange rates. Disclosure — sends the values you check to api.veille.io with your VEILLE_API_KEY, and calls use Veille credits (1 to 5 per call, stated in each tool description). veille_qualify_email has Veille contact the address's mail server. Reads the key only through Thor's secret scope. Registers 9 tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

name: vellum
description: Vellum: Thor draws inside the paper. Highlight a passage in an arXiv paper (HTML version) in Thor's browser and your own Thor session gives you the gist like a friend at a whiteboard, talking while it sketches a live, interactive figure right under the paragraph (built from the paper's own example and numbers); follow-ups, typed or spoken, change the same sketch. Adds tools (vellum_draw / vellum_look / vellum_clear / vellum_read), a skill, hooks on turns started from the paper, a Desktop plugin and dashboard routes under /api/plugins/vellum/. Disclosure — reads arXiv HTML pages (arxiv.org/html, ar5iv) with Desktop's per-site consent and saves the open paper's text when you switch it on; puts Visualize/Ask drafts into your chat box for you to send (never submits a turn itself); the highlighted passage and nearby paper text go to your configured model as part of that turn (the full paper when Thor calls vellum_read, and a picture of the figure when it calls vellum_look), marked as web text; runs model-written drawing code only in a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin, CSP default-src none with scripts pinned by hash plus 'unsafe-eval' for the drawing steps, WebRTC constructors removed; best effort, since CSP does not cover a frame navigating itself); tools reach the card through plugin events (plugin.vellum.*); speaks with Thor's own text_to_speech, one call per spoken sentence and at most 60 per turn (Edge TTS by default, an online service; a paid provider bills each sentence); stores the text of the 20 most recently opened papers, the ids of the 50 most recent figure cards opened, the current Ask passage and short-lived request/voice files under plugin-data/vellum; no telemetry, no credentials, no external CLIs, no downloads.

name: vercel-agent-desktop-support
description: Vercel Agent Desktop Support: operate Windows apps through the accessibility tree instead of the screen. Reads a window's real UI as roles, names, states and refs, then clicks, fills a field, selects an option, toggles a checkbox, scrolls, sends a key combo, and manages windows and the clipboard. Actions are semantic and headless by default, so they do not take focus, move the cursor or synthesize keystrokes, and they fail closed rather than guess. desktop_install downloads the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release for the running Windows target, verifies the archive against a sha256 pinned in the plugin, and proves the install by running version and status. Disclosure — the plugin runs the agent-desktop executable as a child process with arguments it builds, using the copy it installed or one already on PATH, in the npm global folder, AGENT_DESKTOP_BIN or the bin_path setting (those are not checksum-checked); starting or closing a program, installing the binary, and the first call that auto-installs a missing binary (auto_install, off by default) go through Thor's approval prompt (Thor Agent 0.18.1 or newer), while key presses, field values and clipboard writes into any window, a terminal included, run without a prompt; desktop_install is the only tool that uses the network, downloading the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release from GitHub, and a release without a digest pinned in the plugin is refused; it reads window titles, labels, field values and the clipboard on request, which can contain private content. Windows only.

name: verifiable-math-kernel
description: Deterministic symbolic computation, integer factorization with Baillie-PSW probable-prime testing, elliptic curve invariants, and formal Lean 4 proof auditing for Thor Agent. When Lean 4 is installed on PATH and enable_lean_cli is enabled, lean4_proof_audit can verify proofs via isolated execution. Disclosure — With `enable_lean_cli` on (default off), `lean4_proof_audit` runs the user's local `lean --stdin` on model-written Lean code after a Thor approval prompt. Lean can execute code while it elaborates, with the user's privileges, a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, LEAN_PATH) and a scratch working directory under the plugin's data dir. No network calls.

name: verifyum
description: Privacy-preserving file proofs on Solana Mainnet through Verifyum (no account, no key): the agent hashes a file on the user's machine, anchors only a domain-separated commitment, follows the proof until it is finalized, and verifies public proofs, with one skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: the package contains no code and declares two MCP servers. verifyum is Verifyum's hosted server at api.verifyum.com (Streamable HTTP). verifyum-local runs npx -y verifyum-mcp@0.1.1, which downloads that exact npm release (MIT, JavaScript source, published by aisenseapi) on first start and needs Node.js 20 or later. verifyum_anchor_commitment and verifyum_create_proof_from_file write a real, public and permanent Solana Mainnet transaction, so plugin.json marks both servers untrusted and Thor asks first. The file tool reads only regular files inside the directories listed in VERIFYUM_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS, which the package does not set, so it refuses every path until the user sets it. It writes a private draft the user must keep. Verifyum receives only the commitment, the idempotency key and proof IDs, never the file, filename, raw hash, nonce or private manifest. Tool arguments, local paths included, still reach the user's model provider through the session. Verification also reads from a public Solana RPC endpoint. At most ten new anchors per IP address per rolling hour. The tool lists come from the servers at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover them.

name: vet402
description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. ALLOW, and a WARN that only says vet402 has not bought there yet, let it run. Any other WARN, a URL with no record for the paying HTTP method, and a vet402 outage ask for approval, and the call is refused when nobody can answer (yolo, approvals off, cron). vet402 only knows endpoints in public x402 and MPP discovery, so an unlisted URL asks. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside Thor HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

name: veyrul-media
description: Saved media workflows, code and references for captions, editing, audio and production troubleshooting. One portable skill and five remote read tools. Disclosure: enabling the anonymous HTTPS MCP connection sends chosen queries or record IDs and request metadata to veyrul.com; keep private briefs and assets out of queries. No account, API key, executable, dependency installer, background worker, file upload, self-updater or separate analytics sender. Existing agent-provider usage and public-service rate limits apply.

name: vezz-me
description: Contextual AI reading assistant, webpage text extraction, and prompt preset engine for Thor Agent. Powered by Vezz me.

name: viajante
description: Flight and hotel search from your own machine through a local MCP server and one skill that tells the agent how to read the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). No API keys and no account. Disclosure — mcp.json runs `npx -y @viajante/mcp@1.5.2`, which downloads the pinned npm shim and then `uvx` installs the same-version `viajante` package from PyPI on first start, so it needs Node.js, uv and Python 3.10+. Searches read Google Flights and Google Hotels public pages from your IP address (Booking.com and Skiplagged are opt-in). Optional local state (price-history log, cooldown file) is written under the viajante state directory. Nothing is booked and no credentials are stored.

name: vibe-relay
description: Vibecoding without burning your best model. Sets Thor `delegation.backend` to a quota-aware strategy: when remaining usage is above a threshold (default 51%) the parent model keeps the work (`self`); otherwise each `delegate_task` is routed to a configured cheap executor (provider+model or profile). When the executor lane is selected, a `pre_tool_call` hook blocks the parent from `patch`/`write_file` and obvious terminal writes (`sed -i`, `>`/`>>`, `tee`) so coding work must go through `delegate_task` (children never blocked; `enforce_executor_lane` default true). At `stop_used_percent` (default 90% used) the same hook blocks parent `delegate_task` and writers, auto-parks once per reset window (handoff + one one-shot cron), and injects `parked until …; do not start new work` via `pre_llm_call`. Every task must carry `allowed` path globs and a `gate` command — exit 0 alone is not done; `post_tool_call` captures gate PASS bound to a working-tree hash, `pre_verify` continues the turn until a fresh PASS exists, `vibe_accept` checks changed paths ⊆ allowed. Night shift for large projects left overnight (`vibe_night_start|log|status|arm|report`, `/night`): plan, queue, decisions and timeline in a self-ignored `<repo>/.vibe-relay/night-<stamp>/`; `pre_tool_call` refuses new dispatch after the hard stop or at the quota reserve (running work is not killed); `post_tool_call` keeps a parent liveness stamp so continuation wakes exit instead of becoming a second orchestrator; wakes (early checkpoint, quota reset, report) are armed once from the live session via `cronjob_manage` after a quota preflight on the provider cron will use (the plugin never sets a job's model); the morning report is assembled from records. Ships an Agent Workshop of 15 portable skills, including `night-shift` and `lean-executor-orchestration` 2.0, registered as `vibe-relay:<name>`. Vendors DEV Framework tools (`df_init`, `df_check`, `df_nav`); `df_check` returns the gate command for the agent to run via `terminal` (approvals apply). Disclosure — only documented Thor surfaces; quota via `fetch_account_usage(..., read_only=True)` at most once per 180s (15s negative TTL) cached per provider in `$THOR_HOME/plugin-data/vibe-relay/`, which stores metadata only (no gate commands, gate output, task text or raw usage payloads); night shift writes its plan, queue, decisions, timeline and morning report into the working repo under a self-ignored `.vibe-relay/night-<stamp>/` (refused inside Thor home); `vibe_night_arm` creates up to three one-shot cron wakes through `cronjob_manage` with the repo as workdir after a quota check, never sets the job's model, provider or delivery, and refuses to run inside a cron job; the night hook blocks new `delegate_task` dispatch after the hard stop or at the quota reserve without stopping running work; park skips its resume cron inside cron runs unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling`; handoff slugs confined to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` under `docs/`; `df_init`/`df_nav` run the plugin's vendored scripts with `python -I` and a scrubbed child env, `df_nav` never executes the target's navigate.py, and `df_init` refuses Thor home, `$HOME`, `/` and protected dot folders; template scripts may call `git`/`gh` only when the user or agent runs them; no credential-file reads; no YOLO shells.

name: vibeleak-atlas
description: Owner-approved VibeLeak website assessments in a native Thor Desktop workbench. You approve each scan before it runs, private evidence and fix-plan drafts stay on your machine, and read-only local folder review is opt-in. Website assessments need an optional VibeLeak owner API key (Pro plan). Desktop-only, inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or required environment variables. Disclosure — website assessments you approve send the target hostname to VibeLeak (www.vibeleak.app) with your VibeLeak owner API key (Pro plan); the optional hosting map, after a separate approval, sends up to 12 assessed hostnames to Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS and maps them with a bundled DB-IP country database; local folder review reads only a folder you grant and makes no network calls; results are stored under the plugin's data directory.

name: vibeline
description: Show agent work as rails in the TUI, web and CLI. One lane per agent, tool calls and acceptance-criteria results as marks. Disclosure — `thor vibeline web` serves a local web UI (127.0.0.1 by default; a token is required for any non-loopback client) that shows every Thor session transcript on this machine and can open terminals running `thor --resume` and rewind sessions (soft-deleting later messages via core's `/rewind`); `--peer` URLs you add receive and forward these requests to other machines, and `--read-only` disables open/rewind.

name: video-xray
description: Drop a video file into the chat composer and get a structured report: segment-wise frame observation by whatever vision-capable chat model you already configured (local llama.cpp/Strata or cloud), timestamped dialogue from R2T2, Whisper, or any OpenAI-compatible cloud ASR, and a frame gallery of the key moments inside the job detail. Exports the report as Markdown or as a MiniMax-H3 integrated multimodal description prompt. Ships the R2T2 engine worker source (the same code the panel uses); the heavy R2T2 runtime binaries and any Whisper models are user-supplied, nothing else is downloaded. Spawns ffmpeg/ffprobe and local ASR worker subprocesses; network calls go only to the user's own configured inference and cloud-ASR endpoints, never to third-party services; background analysis jobs run as worker threads tracked in a local job ledger. The panel is pure @thor/plugin-sdk React and user-visible text goes through ctx.i18n. Disclosure — runs ffmpeg/ffprobe and local ASR worker processes on your computer, and by default starts an analysis job for every video you attach when you press send (turn off "Analyze attached videos on send" in the panel); video frames go to your configured Thor chat model and audio goes to the cloud ASR endpoint you set, if any; the faster-whisper engine downloads its model weights from Hugging Face on first use when they are not already cached; the cloud ASR key you save in the panel is stored in plain text in an owner-only (0600) file in Thor' data folder.

name: vidiq
description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with thor mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

name: visor
description: Live holographic canvas for AI agents: the visor_push tool pushes visual blocks — sections, markdown findings, clickable todos, tables, KPI stats, charts, code, images, audio and video — to an infinite-canvas webpage that updates in place over SSE (the page is never rewritten), so agents SHOW work instead of dumping it in chat. Turnkey: the plugin ships its own server, no separate install. Disclosure — on first use, if nothing is listening on localhost:8900, the plugin auto-starts its bundled server as a long-running background process (bare-python subprocess by default, state in ~/.local/share/visor or VISOR_DATA; `docker compose up -d` when VISOR_DOCKER=1), restarted if unreachable, and the child gets only a minimal environment (PATH/HOME/LANG/TZ, VISOR_* values, plus DOCKER_* and proxy vars for compose); it listens on 127.0.0.1:8900 by default, and VISOR_HOST opts in to a non-loopback bind that is refused unless VISOR_TOKEN is set; /api/* and /media/ are always gated by a per-install token (0600, <state>/visor-token), which the page receives automatically only on a loopback bind (otherwise open the page with ?token=...); the page refuses framing and foreign Host headers; the bundled live module polls user-pushed http(s) URLs every 2s (10s timeout, 1MB cap, no redirects) and refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses unless they are listed in VISOR_LIVE_LOCAL_HOSTS; the chat module forwards card sends to a configured Thor webhook (VISOR_CHAT_URL + VISOR_CHAT_SECRET) and does nothing until those are set; raw-html cards render in a sandboxed iframe whose postMessage bridge can only read board state and edit blocks on the current board; visor_push copies local image/audio/video files the model names (no dotfile paths) into its media dir; no credentials beyond its own VISOR_* settings, no telemetry.

name: visual-gate
description: Lets Thor check the web UI it just built. Drives a real headless Chrome, diffs the page against a stored baseline and audits WCAG 2.2 AA on the same render, then returns one PASS or FAIL with changed regions, computed contrast ratios and exact CSS selectors. A page that failed to load is an error, never a pass, and text it cannot measure is reported for a person to check.

name: visual-oracle
description: Makes a UI claim measurable before an agent reports success: captures a page as a baseline, then pixel-diffs later renders and answers PASS, FAIL or REVIEW with independent change regions (bbox, pixel count, area, density), a diff image, an overlay and per-region crops. Waits for document.fonts.ready, an optional selector and two identical frames so a capture is settled, records the Chrome version and viewport that produced it, and refuses to guess when rendering never stabilises. An optional visual change contract declares expected changes and protected regions so a declared change can pass while an undeclared one fails; selectors name locations, not meaning. Masks accept rectangles or CSS selectors and are applied before capture, a selector matching nothing is an error, and masks may not cover more than half the viewport. Only public http and https are rendered: file://, data:, private ranges and the cloud metadata address are refused on the URL and on every request the page makes, redirects included, with localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 allowed and VO_ALLOW_HOSTS for anything else. Disclosure - renders the URL you give it in a local Chrome over the DevTools protocol (no Selenium, Playwright or pip install), so the page's own network requests happen in that browser; reads the PNGs it produced and writes baselines, diffs, overlays, crops and report.json under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/; runs no shell command of its own and no background service; the baseline is never updated automatically; image input must be a real PNG and a header claiming more than 8192 px on a side is refused before decompression; no telemetry. Disclosure — renders the http(s) URL you give it in a local headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol (no Selenium, Playwright or pip install), so the page's own network requests happen from your machine; refuses non-http(s) schemes and private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses on the URL and on every request the page makes (localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 allowed, more via VO_ALLOW_HOSTS); launches Chrome with --no-sandbox only when running as root, without user namespaces, or with VO_NO_SANDBOX=1; reads the PNGs you point it at and writes baselines, diffs, overlays, crops and report.json under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/visual-oracle/; a failing or REVIEW check keeps the agent's turn open through the pre_verify hook; runs no shell command of its own and no background service; the baseline is never updated automatically; no telemetry.

name: visual-workflow
description: Visual drag-and-drop agent-workflow designer for Thor: Trigger, Agent, Condition, Approval, Output nodes on a canvas, executed by a plugin-owned sequential runner. Disclosure — Workflow Output nodes send text to messaging channels through Thor's send-message path; a model-started run of a design with a delivering Output node first asks for your approval, and scheduled runs that would send are blocked unless approvals.cron_mode allows them; scheduled workflows run as Thor cron jobs created from the dashboard; agent steps run Thor subagents or the plugin LLM facade on your configured models; designs and run records are stored under THOR_HOME/workflow-designs and THOR_HOME/workflow-runs.

name: vitam
description: Turn a modded PS Vita into a voice-powered Thor handheld: hold-to-talk mic with faster-whisper STT on your own machine, an agent turn through your Thor gateway, TTS reply spoken through the Vita speaker, and optional rear-camera vision frames. LAN-only; the bridge makes no outbound calls except to your configured gateway. Disclosure — runs a bridge daemon that listens on all network interfaces (port 8643 by default) so the PS Vita can reach it on your LAN; every request except a reachability ping needs the pairing token, and voice audio and camera frames are processed on your machine and sent only to your configured Thor gateway.

name: vitrail
description: Live GLSL shaders in the chat. Ask for a visual and the model writes a Shadertoy-style fragment shader that animates inside the reply in Thor Desktop, with the sliders, colour pickers and switches it declared as annotated uniforms. Before vitrail_render returns, the Desktop half compiles the shader with WebGL 2 on the user's GPU and reports the verdict, so a compile error goes back to the model with the driver log and the model fixes it in the same turn; a still frame comes back too, for models with a vision tool. The card is drawn through a tool media renderer where Desktop has one and through a ::vitrail transcript directive where it does not (Desktop 0.22.5). Other surfaces (Telegram, CLI, TUI) get a standalone HTML player of the same shader. Adds a gallery page with hover-to-play tiles, GLSL copy and 1920x1080 PNG export, the vitrail_render and vitrail_library tools, the vitrail:shader-studio skill, and post_tool_call / transform_llm_output hooks that append the shader's delivery line (MEDIA file or directive) when a reply lacks it. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry; GLSL written by the model runs on the user's GPU through WebGL 2 in the Desktop window; files are written only under plugin-data/vitrail (per shader: source, standalone HTML player, GPU report, a 640x360 JPEG still, exported PNGs); the still's path is given to the model, which may open it with its vision tool; while a Desktop window is open its half calls the plugin's own local route once a minute so the tool knows a GPU is listening and which transcript surface it has, and vitrail_render then waits up to 6 s for the verdict.

name: vivarium
description: A living artificial-life world inside Thor. Real tool calls drop nutrients into a 48x48 cellular-automaton dish; creatures carry genomes, forage, reproduce, mutate and go extinct on their own; every skill the agent learns births a new species. Deterministic, mathematically grounded, private. Disclosure — Vivarium starts a background thread in every Thor process that polls its own state about once per second to repaint the terminal, finds the controlling terminal by reading `/proc/<pid>/environ` and `/proc/<pid>/stat` of parent processes (terminal-type variables only, never stored), and `/vivarium serve` runs an unauthenticated read-only gallery on 127.0.0.1 that shows your installed skill names and the dish (`--keep` leaves it running until Thor exits).

name: vividsites
description: Cinematic website design sources for Thor. Free UI components without a key; website templates, build prompts and blueprints with an optional paid VividSites library account. Disclosure — calls VividSites (www.vividsites.app): free component lookups send only search words and component names without a key; library tools send the optional VIVIDSITES_API_KEY and the requested template or component names, and build-prompt and blueprint retrieval may use the paid account's daily allowance (Thor asks for approval before each).

name: vk-platform
description: VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.

name: voice-gate
description: Reviews changed prose with 75 mechanical rule families and optional contextual review against the complete humanizer skill and its references. Settings keep everyday controls visible and collapse Vale, bots, and individual rules. Slow inventory requests allow up to two minutes and offer retry; the page includes five-row exceptions and Vale installation guidance. Revision requests allow at most two opportunities and compare protected spans and quantities. Prose em dashes are flagged while bullet label separators and empty table values remain allowed. Reads the changed prose paths reported by Thor; manual tools can check supplied text. Model review is off by default and sends reviewed documents to the configured Thor provider when enabled. It provides editorial judgments, not authorship proof. Vale is optional; status, check, and install request approval before starting a program, turn-time findings use only a binary approved that way, and Vale runs with a short environment rather than the host's. No project-file writes or core overrides. Simple PDF text extraction has no OCR. Disclosure — reads the changed prose files Thor reports after each turn and any text or paths given to its tools; optional model review (off by default) sends reviewed documents to the configured Thor provider; optional Vale support downloads a sha256-pinned Vale release from GitHub into <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/voice-gate/ only after approval, and runs Vale (status, check, install, and turn-time advisory checks on changed files) only for a binary approved through Thor' approval prompt and recorded by digest, with a minimal environment.

name: voice-ledger
