description: Local ledger of the voice messages and recordings Thor transcribes (voice messages from messaging platforms, CLI voice mode): /voice-log shows how many recordings there were, how much audio in total and typically, and how long ago the last one was, per speech-to-text provider, model, source, language or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days or everything recorded; /voice-log recent lists the newest recordings (ten, or up to 100 with /voice-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes recording metadata (source, provider, model, language, file size read from the file system; no audio, file path, prompt or transcript) to plugin-data/voice-ledger/voice.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, always returns None so the transcription request is unchanged; no network

name: voice-unleashed
description: A hands-free voice interface to Thor, for any model, on your own VoiceManager server. The plugin serves a web page, so any device with a browser, a microphone and a speaker is the client, a phone, a tablet on a wall or a spare laptop: you talk, Thor answers out loud while the model writes, and you talk over a reply to stop it. The page shows the conversation, each tool call and the model's reasoning, speaks approval prompts and the model's questions and takes spoken answers, and picks up any session of the profile or starts a new one. Thor Desktop and Webapp chats get a voice toggle. Disclosure - adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN); the session list and history are read from the profile's own Thor state and nothing is stored. It registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Thor use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction (start the reply with a short spoken summary) only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on. The Desktop half ships switched off. No Python dependencies beyond Thor core (websockets, httpx); VoiceManager's client is vendored. Disclosure — adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token carried in the page URL; whoever holds the token is the platform's one gateway user (owner), is made its slash-command admin, can list, resume and read the history of every session of the profile, and answers approval prompts by voice or by tapping the page's allow-once/session/always/deny buttons, where a single spoken approval word (including "always") or a short approval phrase such as "go ahead", "sure", "yeah" or "allow" (approve once) is sent as the reply, so a misheard word can approve a command; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN), and nothing is stored; it registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Thor use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on; it reads a few undocumented core helpers and the gateway's session DB read-only, so a Thor release can break it; the Desktop half ships switched off.

name: voicestudio
description: Client for the local VoiceStudio text-to-speech app (debpalash/VoiceStudio): speak short text, design or clone voices, browse voices, render chaptered long-form audio, dub videos, and check server status. Six tools with mirrored slash commands plus a bundled skill. Disclosure — sends the text, script files, videos and voice samples you point it at to the VoiceStudio server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP) and saves the returned audio under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/voicestudio; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: voicestudio-tts
description: VoiceStudio TTS provider for Thor: registers a TTS provider so replies can be read aloud, or auto-spoken, in the user's own voices from the local VoiceStudio app, per profile. Settings are read through ctx.get_config, voices through GET /profiles, audio through POST /generate. /voicestudio refresh stores the voice list in the plugin's own state; it copies the list into the plugin's plugin.yaml only when the user turns on sync_dropdown, which is off by default and is what turns the voice setting into a dropdown. Disclosure - sends the reply text, the voice id and the engine name when one is configured to the local server (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP); no credentials, no telemetry, no other network calls, no declared dependency (the YAML write uses the module Thor ships), no self-update of code.

name: vornik-companion
description: Vornik as Thor's hardened broker and long-term memory: Thor holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN (and VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN for memory); broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon, and asks the daemon to stop recalling (not delete) a mirrored entry that Thor removes or replaces (/vornik-memory lists and /vornik-forget forgets what Vornik keeps); artifact tools expose only named outputs allowed by the approved workflow from completed runs and read bounded text or return short-lived binary download links from the daemon; task diagnosis tools (offered only when the daemon advertises companion-progress) return a broker task's execution events and closed error classes as the daemon serves them to a broker key; thor vornik approvals on writes security.approval.transport (and vornik_companion.approval_namespace) to Thor config, after which Thor's own dangerous-command prompts (the redacted command text) are sent through the local vornikctl agent host-approval to the daemon and answered on the paired phone, any failure or a Vornik outage denying the command unless transport_fallback: builtin is set, and the plugin never decides itself; thor vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to Thor config; the daemon's engineering guidance is added as a system prompt section (vornik.rules); with VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN, short hints are appended to the result of the tool call that caused them (after a commit, a design-document write, a failed test run), behind a marker naming Vornik, which hints fired and whether they were followed is reported to the daemon, and the vornik_companion_delegate tool reads the local files the model names (at most 20 files and 2 MB; symlinks, hard links, credential files such as .env, and anything under the Thor home refused) and sends them to the daemon for a review or a memory ingest.

name: vt-check
description: VirusTotal reputation for downloads and links. Files are hashed locally and looked up by SHA-256 — never uploaded. URLs are checked read-only, and archives are inspected in memory for path traversal, decompression bombs, double extensions and document-named executables. Disclosure — network calls to www.virustotal.com (SHA-256 hash, URL, domain and IP lookups with the user's VT_API_KEY); vt_check_url with submit=true, which the model sets, POSTs the URL to VirusTotal for a new scan and makes it public there; vt_check_file reads (hashes and inspects in memory) whatever local path it is given, and the file itself is never uploaded; no shell, no background processes, no telemetry; lookup cache in plugin state; credential read via get_secret.

name: waifu-sprites
description: Video waifu companion that reacts to agent activity in real time — 12 states, 12 emotions, draggable dashboard overlay. Disclosure — by default the dashboard overlay downloads its video clips from jsDelivr (cdn.jsdelivr.net, a pinned commit of waifuai/waifuai.github.io), so jsDelivr sees your IP when the dashboard is open; set Clip source to local to serve your own clips. No agent text leaves the host.

name: wait-ledger
description: Local ledger of the times Thor stopped to wait for you (approval prompts, clarify questions, password prompts): /waits shows how many waits there were, how many were answered or left unanswered, and how long Thor stood still in total, typically and at most, per kind of prompt, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /waits recent lists the newest waits (ten, or up to 100 with /waits recent 50). Disclosure — writes wait metadata (session id, platform, kind of prompt, how it ended, wait time; no prompt text, answer or session key) to plugin-data/wait-ledger/waits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer, delay or change a prompt; no network

name: waiting-on-you
description: One list of the questions your Thor bots are waiting on you to answer. /waiting and thor waiting scan profile session stores, keep only replies that end by asking you something (English and Indonesian), merge the same question asked by several bots, and drop an item once you reply in that chat or dismiss it. Disclosure — opens state.db (sessions, messages) with SQLite mode=ro and PRAGMA query_only and shows the text of matching bot replies: every profile on this machine for the terminal command and CLI/TUI/Desktop, but only the chat's own profile for /waiting in a messaging chat unless the owner turns on all_profiles_in_chat (off by default). Writes only plugin-data/waiting-on-you/dismissed.json in the active profile. No network calls, no model calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no background processes, no tools or hooks.

name: waiting-on-you-desktop
description: Desktop panel listing every question your agents are waiting on you to answer, across all chats and profiles, sorted by urgency and importance. Yes, No and Reply can be answered in place, with five seconds to undo, but only for a chat whose composer is visible in this Desktop window; other chats get Open instead. Later snoozes an ask from any chat. Disclosure: sends chat excerpts, task context, your priority note and recent priority corrections (as examples) to your configured Thor model, and to an optional decision provider you choose; see the README for full details. Reads every local profile's state.db and projects.db read-only, plus Thor config.yaml; saves its plugin settings through Thor; runs a background scan in the gateway. Optional SSH reads, chat archiving and local action-handler commands are all off by default. Handlers run with a minimal environment plus only the variable names you list, and can do whatever their command does. No telemetry.

name: wake
description: Lets your agent speak first. Scheduled notes and cron jobs arrive as a turn for your own agent in the chat you bind: Desktop Bot Chat, Discord, Telegram, Slack and other gateway chats. Disclosure — once you set plugins.entries.wake.allow_gateway_injection, scheduled wakes (including ones the agent schedules for itself) and cron output sent to the Wake Agent target start billed agent turns in the bound chat, plus one optional precheck call on your model per wake; stores its queue in plaintext under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/; no third-party network calls, telemetry or credentials.

name: wake-me-when
description: Wakes you the moment something happens in live audio or video that has no feed: a keynote reaching pricing, an earnings call giving guidance, a Twitch boss fight, a council agenda item, a launch at T-minus 1 or a scrub. /wakeme <url> when <condition> (or just ask the agent) watches YouTube Live, Twitch, HLS, RTSP or a bundled demo:// stream with local speech recognition (faster-whisper, Thor's own stt-whisper extra), on-screen OCR and an optional vision check, and posts an alert in the same chat with the quote, the stream time and a jump-in link; replying 'clip' hands you the moment as a video, 'not it' teaches the judge and keeps watching, 'every time …' alerts on each occurrence, /wakeme catchup summarises what you missed, and /wakeme <recording> <question> searches recordings for timestamps; one slash command in all. Cheap cue matching runs first; one LLM judge call (its own auxiliary task, wakeme_judge) confirms, citing transcript rows so times never come from the model; a per-watch hourly budget falls back to unconfirmed cue alerts instead of missing silently. Disclosure — runs one ffmpeg (plus streamlink for Twitch, HLS and web-media links) per active watch in its own process group, killed on stop, unload and exit, and one shared speech-recognition thread; contacts only the stream hosts you give it (via yt-dlp, streamlink, ffmpeg), Hugging Face once for the Whisper model, and Thor's package index when it installs the stt-whisper extra; sends transcript excerpts, on-screen text and (only for visual conditions) keyframes to your configured model through ctx.llm; external tools (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, streamlink, tesseract, a JS runtime for yt-dlp) are user-installed and detected, never bundled; subprocesses use argv lists, -- before user URLs, an explicit ffmpeg -protocol_whitelist per source and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale, XDG and proxy/CA settings; no API keys or tokens); refuses private network addresses, including the stream URLs yt-dlp and streamlink resolve a link to, unless allow_private_network is on; direct HLS and web-media links are fetched by streamlink through a loopback proxy on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-source random credentials) that checks every connection, playlist entries and redirects included, and dials the address it checked, unless you set your own proxy; and local files from messaging chats unless they are in allowed_media_dirs; keeps a 3-minute media buffer per watch, clips for 2 days and transcripts for 7 days under its plugin-data; while a chat has watches, its pre_llm_call hook adds a one-line note naming them to the user's turn; optional allow_gateway_injection (off by default) lets it ask the agent to attach the clip right after an alert (one agent turn on your main model) and hand an alert it could not post to the agent; DRM streams are not supported; no telemetry.

name: wakeshift
description: Wakes your Thor chats when Wakeshift-enabled MCP servers you've added have news for them: a price drop, a finished build or a reply starts a new turn in the chat that asked for it, even while it's idle, framed as outside information rather than as you. Works for API server (gateway) and CLI chats. Disclosure — contacts only the Wakeshift servers it trusts (https://app.wakeshift.ai unless you set plugins.entries.wakeshift.settings.issuers): fetches their signing keys, exchanges signed beacons from MCP tool results for each chat's stream link, holds those streams open in background threads while Thor runs, and acknowledges delivered messages; no telemetry. Starts runs on Thor's own API server at 127.0.0.1 with the API server's key (read through agent.secret_scope). Fills in the harness argument (thor), and the chat's own session_key when the model omits it, on calls to Wakeshift-enabled tools. It starts no turn in any chat (API server or CLI) until the user turns on plugins.entries.wakeshift.allow_gateway_injection: true; until then it tells the chat the command, and holds messages until it is on. Removes Wakeshift beacons from MCP tool results and adds a one-line note. Stores each connected chat's stream links and session keys, one per server (which include access tokens), cached signing keys and delivery state under $THOR_HOME/wakeshift (files 0600). Never answers approvals and runs no shell commands. Wakeshift's Connector Terms (https://wakeshift.ai/connector-terms) and Privacy Policy (https://wakeshift.ai/privacy) apply.

name: walkie-talkie
description: Let one session message another existing session (Telegram topic, group thread or DM), waking it like a user turn so the reply lands in that chat Disclosure — starts agent turns in other existing gateway sessions (any routed chat, including groups, and from cron jobs) via ctx.inject_message, only after plugins.entries.walkie-talkie.allow_gateway_injection: true; after an accepted handoff it posts a visible copy into the target chat through Thor's send_message helper using your existing gateway bot credentials; reads state.db, config.yaml and cron/jobs.json read-only; no network calls of its own, no shell, no telemetry.

name: wallaby-provider
description: Wallaby Token — curated open-weight inference (Kimi K3, K3.1 Pro); adds Wallaby to the thor model provider list.

name: wallpaper-theme
description: A Thor Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/thor-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @thor/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG_*_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: wally
description: Wally by RunAnywhere as a Thor model provider: open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax) on an OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Wally's top-level reasoning_effort, clamped to the levels each model accepts. Pick Wally in `thor model` or use `--provider wally`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access); chat requests (prompts, tool schemas and results, images for image-capable models) and the model list go to https://inference.runanywhere.ai/v1 (or WALLY_BASE_URL) through Thor's own client with WALLY_API_KEY, which Thor reads; usage is billed to your Wally account; the plugin itself opens no connections.

name: warden
description: Defensive security operations plugin for Thor Agent, built on one rule: model-facing tools read and request, they never configure. A deny-by-default scope engine decides what may be touched before anything runs; scopes are created only by the operator (the thor warden CLI), never by the model, and adapter directories are operator config, never tool input. Vulnerability assessment runs two engines (Grype and Trivy) over one canonical SBOM from Syft and records their disagreement as finding confidence instead of hiding it. Sigma rules evaluate over the event store through sec_campaign, osquery host telemetry feeds the same store, and a deterministic correlation engine groups actors into campaigns; the anchored membership view (measured precision 1.000, recall 1.000 on the validation corpus) is the only view allowed to justify defensive action. Investigations answer only with citations to stored evidence; uncitable claims are dropped and counted. Containment is a policy-enforced plan engine (approval classes, blast radius, TTL, rollback) whose execution is disabled in this build; apply mode is refused. The agent's own actions are written to a redacted ledger and a hash-chained audit log. Dry run by default. Disclosure — Warden runs operator-installed scanner binaries (nuclei, trivy, grype, syft, osquery; version-attested against their adapter manifests at run time, with an optional operator SHA-256 pin, never bundled) as local subprocesses with a scrubbed environment, only against targets in operator-created scopes; a hostname target is authorised by name and resolved by the scanner at run time. It connects only to those targets and, when configured, to threat-intelligence providers, stores no credentials, and executes no containment action in this build.

name: watch-with-me
description: Follows Plex playback and publishes sourced, spoiler-safe notes about the scene you are watching. Disclosure — once you link Plex (plex.tv PIN sign-in; the token is kept in plugin data), a background thread polls your Plex server for playback and, by default, auto-claims your own account's streams; notes and "what did I just see?" answers send subtitle/transcript text (and, with a vision model, a timeline frame) to your Thor auxiliary model, and fetch en.wikipedia.org; optional off-by-default features: `chat_notifications` (also requires `allow_gateway_injection: true` on the plugin entry) injects a "playback started" message with the companion link into your last-used chat session as a user turn, Jev entity selection sends entity names to api.typesafe.ai or openrouter.ai with your key, `download_subtitles` writes subtitle files into your Plex library, and `extract_command` runs the command you configure (for example ssh + ffmpeg) to extract subtitles; no telemetry.

name: watchline
description: Watchline delivery adapter for Thor Agent. Polls a Watchline pull channel and forwards matched events into the Thor gateway as inbound messages.

name: waterloo-jane-street-qr
description: Offline quant toolkit: option pricing, EV puzzles, game solver, market-making/execution/portfolio maths, plus a trading-desk answer persona. Disclosure — adds a "quant trading desk" persona to the system prompt and a reminder to every turn that tell the model to end EVERY answer, in every chat, with a [TAKE]/[PASS]/[HEDGE] trade verdict and sizing; with the default `enforcement: strict` it also appends a "Desk compliance … no position should be taken on it" footer to any reply without an explicit EV and verdict (set `plugins.entries.waterloo-jane-street-qr.settings.enforcement` to `reminder` or `off` to stop it). Tools are offline calculators: no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials; it gives no financial advice you should act on.

name: wavebots
description: Verified AI bots for Thor, by Wave OS. Browse the official Wave bots from the bots.theta store (Checker, Tally, Planner, Maker and more); each one is checked on the Theta blockchain on your computer (name record, listing, rules, mascot and every knowledge card, fingerprint by fingerprint) before it's marked Verified. Add one and it becomes its own Thor bot (a wave-<name> profile in your Bots list, with its mascot), answering from its checked cards on your own AI model with code, terminal, file and web tools turned off, re-checked daily. An optional Wave OS bot key lets you ask the real bot on Wave, with Thor approval for every question. Disclosure: never signs or sends transactions, and needs no account for browsing, checking or adding bots. Network calls go only to Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only name and card reads) and, only if you set a Wave OS bot key and ask the real bot, app.oswave.io (your question to the bot). The optional Wave OS bot key (limited and revocable, spending limit you pick, default 0 TFUEL) is a Thor secret: declared as config_schema secret WAVE_OS_TOKEN, entered in Thor's plugin settings, read with get_secret; the plugin never stores it (Disconnect keeps only the key's SHA-256 fingerprint in $THOR_HOME/wavebots so it stays off here). Creates and removes only its own wave-* Thor profiles; reads Thor's profile and plugin lists locally. A background thread re-checks added bots once a day. Opens app.oswave.io in the browser to get a key. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating. Disclosure — reads Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only) and, only if you set the optional Wave OS bot key (a Thor secret, WAVE_OS_TOKEN), sends your questions and a free key check every 10 minutes at most to app.oswave.io, where a paid bot answer can spend TFUEL from your Wave OS account up to the limit you set on the key, each paid ask after Thor approval and never from cron; creates and removes its own wave-* Thor profiles (tools off, SOUL.md built from on-chain card text), rewrites an added bot's SOUL.md from a background re-check once a day, keeps only key fingerprints (never the key) in $THOR_HOME/wavebots for Disconnect, opens app.oswave.io in your browser to get a key; never signs transactions, no telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating.

name: wavegrain
description: Curated TikTok slideshows and Instagram carousels for your brand on autopilot, through the hosted Wavegrain Streamable HTTP MCP server plus one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a Wavegrain account and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then thor mcp login wavegrain); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: your brand details, photos and slide texts go to wavegrain.com; generating tools spend Wavegrain credits within the limit set per connection, and posting publishes to your connected TikTok/Instagram accounts (needs Wavegrain's separate post permission and its own approval setting); the server is marked untrusted, so Thor asks before each of its tool calls.

name: waypoint
description: Session status for Thor Desktop: a thin bar next to every sidebar session with four states — Working (remembers your next step), Waiting on someone (who/what plus a follow-up reminder), Done (outcome plus a fresh-start handoff) and untracked. Suggests 3 next steps per session (instant quick ideas from the chat, opt-in AI ideas from the auxiliary model, priority colours) with one-click Ask, a Power up button that asks a strong model for sharper ideas on demand, and Mark complete to stop suggestions. Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Thor llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (Thor default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Thor log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <THOR_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Thor reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

name: wazoo
description: Wazoo world-model memory provider — typed memories (decision, preference, person, project, finding, correction) in an RDF graph with retraction provenance, background recall prefetch, hybrid search, and SPARQL for structural questions. Works against the hosted Wazoo cloud (provisions a world automatically from a platform token) or a self-hosted worlds endpoint with a locally minted key.

name: wearos
description: The whole Thor gateway on a Wear OS watch: the watch enrolls its own tailnet node, pairs with a gateway-minted 6-digit code, and talks to a private tailnet lane from then on — every agent, streaming answers, mid-session tool-call approvals, cron-run notifications, and replies spoken out loud in a voice cloned from ~3 seconds of reference audio, synthesized on your gateway's CPU. A desktop pane runs the checklist (APK, pair, enable) with per-agent voice dropdowns and readiness lights. Parakeet STT and the TTS engine arrive as checksum-pinned source builds at first use — nothing pre-bundled, no telemetry, no calls home after setup. Disclosure — pairing mints single-use Tailscale enrollment keys and `thor watch setup --fix serve` runs `tailscale funnel --bg --https=443` (mounting the claim door at the root of your node's :443); the plugin runs a loopback claim door (Funnel-fronted, answers only /pair/*) and a private HTTP lane on your tailnet IP for paired watches; checking an agent in the pane lets paired watches receive that profile's API_SERVER_KEY, and un-pairing rotates it (hot for named profiles; for the default profile a watch-initiated unpair restarts the gateway); the optional voice-in/voice-out installers build pinned source from github.com, install Python packages from pypi.org into private venvs, and download multi-GB model weights from huggingface.co (the gated neuphonic/neucodec codec needs a Hugging Face token and loads at its latest revision; the "set agent voice" pane button sets tts.provider to wearkit-gateway); once installed, one resident ~3.4 GB TTS worker stays loaded and the plugin kills any other idle `air_runner.py --serve` process on the machine; cloned-voice reference recordings are stored under the plugin's data dir.

name: weather
description: Weather data, radar/model imagery, and verified meteorological calculations. Built on metrust, rusbie, wrf-rust, rustdar, and ecape-rs.

name: web-crawler-spider
description: A small spider that lives on the Thor Desktop window: a web that grows with tool calls, helper spiders for subagents, an amber mood while Thor waits for approval, spider-sense for risky commands, flies, napping. By default it roams only its own overlay and reads nothing from the app; walking between the app's real buttons and links is an opt-in setting (off by default). Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — draws an animated overlay on the Desktop window and reads gateway events (tool runs, subagents, approval waits, risky-command flags) and the app's theme colours; the opt-in "Explore the app" setting (off by default) also scans the window's buttons, links and alert banners, including button labels, to walk to them.

name: web-deepseek
description: DeepSeek Search + Fetch — routes web_search and web_extract through DeepSeek's in-house AI search engine and server-side fetcher on api.deepseek.com (opened up in the vendor's 2026-10-17 changelog: AI-native engine indexing hundreds of billions of pages, multilingual, filters SEO spam / GEO manipulation / low-quality AIGC). Registers the provider id `deepseek-web`. Disclosure — each search/fetch is a separate billed DeepSeek call at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests per endpoint, and only HTTP 200 responses that produce a result are billable (5 QPS per account per endpoint, plus a per-domain QPS limit on fetch); the provider reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and sends it only to api.deepseek.com; extract returns Markdown only (no HTML variant, so web_extract(format="html") gets Markdown), and anti-bot or JS-rendered sites fail (zhihu.com, x.com, nytimes.com returned HTTP 404 in testing) while static pages work.

name: web-defuddle
description: Defuddle content extraction — local, free, no API key. Shells out to the defuddle CLI for clean article markdown. Extract-only; pair with SearXNG or another search provider.

name: web-local
description: Keyless local web extract: fetches pages from this machine with httpx and reduces them to readable text with trafilatura. No API key, no third-party service. Extract-only; pair with any search provider.

name: web-meta-ai
description: Meta web search — routes web_search through the server-side web_search tool on Meta's Responses API (Muse Spark); search-only. Disclosure — each search is a separate billed Meta Model API call (per-query web search fee plus tokens) on MODEL_API_KEY.

name: web-octen
description: Octen web search with query-focused highlights and page extraction.

name: web-ollama-cloud
description: Ollama Cloud web search + content extraction via Ollama's native REST API. Search returns web results; extract fetches page content. Reuses OLLAMA_API_KEY (https://ollama.com/settings/keys).

name: web-search-plus
description: Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's THOR_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, provider_order, searxng_url, donsetch_bin) and, in its status command, the web backend and keyless_rescue settings, and checks (without opening it) whether a pre-5.1 .env file exists in its plugin folder or THOR_HOME/plugins, to tell upgraders where their keys went; only when the operator opts in (serper.resolve_redirects, off by default) it sends one GET per Google /goto result link to google.com to resolve it; may spawn an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as a subprocess (argv, no shell).

name: web-serply
description: Serply web search provider for Thor Agent. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

name: web-specstream
description: SpecStream Search API and Extract API for web_search and web_extract. Search is $5 per 1,000 searches, extract is $0.80 per 1,000 pages (web pages, PDF, Word and Excel, up to 20 URLs a call, a page with no text is free). Needs a SpecStream API key. Disclosure — paid third-party backend: search queries and every URL passed to web_extract are sent to api.specstream.ai with your SPECSTREAM_API_KEY, which SpecStream fetches server-side and bills to that key's balance.

name: web-toon
description: Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

name: web-venice
description: Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

name: webgraft
description: Local web_extract backend (trafilatura for pages, Thor's own anydoc converter for PDF and Office documents, optional Crawl4AI browser view of pages the site served) that reports HTTP errors and bot walls as errors and never tries to get past them; lists the pages an answer really used, from tool results, as clickable links; nudges the model to open pages rather than answer from snippets; reads a page's Markdown version when the site's llms.txt lists one, and returns pages that opt out of AI use (noai, TDM reservation) as errors; keeps several pages within a small model's context (one URL per web_extract call: a multi-URL call reads the first URL and its result lists the others); long pages are left to Thor's own window, handed the whole text. Bundles a research skill, a setup wizard and an uninstall command. Disclosure — downloads the URLs web_extract is asked to read, from this machine with Thor's own User-Agent (ThorAgent; the browser sends the same), and each site's /llms.txt once per hour (on by default, setting llms_txt), through Thor's SSRF-safe client (private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses refused on every redirect hop; with an HTTP(S) proxy configured, where Thor's guard leaves hops to the proxy, webgraft checks each redirect target itself; results report the final URL so Thor re-checks it; a browser view that ends on a non-public address or on another site is dropped; requests made by the page's own scripts and assets in the browser are not checked); `setup` also checks the SearXNG URL it is given and reads two test pages on iana.org; `setup` optionally creates an isolated `thor pm` environment with Crawl4AI, which drives Thor's own Chromium (`thor pm install chromium` if missing; the plugin downloads no browser); each Crawl4AI read is a child process (at most 3 at once per Thor process, 60 s cap, stopped with its Chromium on timeout or when Thor cancels the call) that starts that Chromium headless with a DevTools port on 127.0.0.1 and a temporary profile, runs the page's scripts and loads its assets, keeps the browser profile and Crawl4AI's log and cache in a temporary folder that webgraft creates and removes (its own folders left by an earlier, interrupted run are removed after an hour); each document is converted by anydoc in a child process (60 s cap, stopped if Thor cancels the call); `setup` installs Thor's `doc-extract` extra if missing, and its `ddgs` extra when DuckDuckGo search is chosen; `setup` optionally creates an OCR environment (RapidOCR, onnxruntime, pypdfium2) whose first run downloads about 32 MB of OCR models from RapidOCR's official modelscope.cn repository, checked by SHA-256, and each scanned PDF is then read in a child process (100 s cap, stopped if Thor cancels the call); appends a short note (about 110 tokens) to each user message (setting `remind`); once a conversation has read web content (web_search, web_extract, x_search, browser tools, MCP tools, vision_analyze / video_analyze on a URL, a terminal command or execute_code script holding an http(s) URL, tools a script runs, a subagent that read the web), sends every tool that is not read-only (terminal, code, browser, file writes, memory, messages, subagents, session_search, unknown tools, read_file / search_files outside the folders where Thor keeps fetched pages, and vision_analyze / video_analyze on a local file) to Thor's own approval prompt through the pre_tool_call approve directive, refused where nobody can answer such as -Q or cron (setting `tool_guard`: ask by default, block, off), because a web page can hold instructions aimed at the assistant; keeps the ids (no content) of those conversations, at most 1000, in plugin-data/webgraft/web_sessions.json, so the guard holds after a restart and after Thor compresses the history; a continuation session or subagent inherits its parent's mark; `setup` writes web.search_backend, web.extract_backend, skills.auto_load and SEARXNG_URL, recording replaced values and the Chromium path under plugin-data/webgraft; page-reading child processes get a minimal environment, never Thor's API keys; `setup` optionally raises web.extract_char_limit (only on a yes; the replaced value is restored by `uninstall`); page text stays in memory only; no telemetry.

name: webly
description: Publish a website, or share files and folders, at a live *.webly.site URL from Thor Agent with no account, then sign in to claim it, edit it, and publish drafts the person approves through the hosted Webly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — MCP tool calls go to api.webly.ai/v1/mcp, sending WEBLY_API_KEY as a bearer header when it is set, and the webly server is marked untrusted so Thor asks before each Webly MCP tool that changes something. The bundled webly skill runs a local Node.js 20+ helper (scripts/webly.mjs) through the shell: it uploads only the files and folders the person asks to publish or share to api.webly.ai (sites are public unless password-protected), runs the project's npm/pnpm/yarn install and build first when the folder has a build script, opens the browser for sign-in and claim, and keeps its anonymous-site token and optional OAuth sign-in in ~/.webly (mode 0600). Its doctor command reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml only to see whether a webly MCP server is configured there. Publishing, deleting and replacing sites through that helper are gated by skill instructions, not by Thor approvals. The catalog copy has no update check.

name: webmint
description: Turn a website into a deterministic tool: a real browser captures the page once, the host's own model writes a declarative extraction spec, two runs must agree (same field set, >=50% fill per field) before it is saved, and every later call runs that spec with no model in the loop (~2.7s). Five tools: setup, mint, run, list, remove. Disclosure — needs Node >= 18 and Playwright; on first mint the plugin installs Playwright and Chromium into its own directory (~120 MB, opt out with WEBMINT_NO_AUTO_SETUP=1). Capture runs in a fresh signed-out browser: actions may fill, click and submit forms, and http specs replay the captured GET or POST (Cookie and Authorization headers are never replayed). Public http(s) URLs only — file:, loopback/private and link-local/metadata addresses are refused, with private/loopback behind WEBMINT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1 or the host's security.allow_private_urls. Headless Chromium is refused by some bot-protected sites.

name: webtwizz
description: Build, change and publish websites and web apps with WebTwizz through its hosted MCP server (https://app.webtwizz.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in in the browser, no keys in config): landing pages, online stores, booking sites, portfolios and web apps with sign-ins and a database, published to a webtwizz.app address or the user's own domain, with version history, site data and GitHub sync. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to WebTwizz's hosted server (app.webtwizz.com) and acts on the user's WebTwizz account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Builds and edits spend WebTwizz credits, and publish-site only returns a link: the site goes live when the user presses Publish in the WebTwizz editor. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

name: wechat-social-assistant
description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

name: weft
description: Catch conflicts between coding agents while they edit, before Git merge time. Disclosure — In a checkout linked with `/weft setup` (a `.weft/space.json` plus the saved agent token), every file edit the agent makes is sent to the Weft gateway that checkout names: file paths, symbol keys, full diffs, agent and change ids, the Thor model name and the Kanban task title. The gateway is local (127.0.0.1) by default, Weft's hosted `https://weft-hosted.elier.ai` when chosen or named by a checkout, or a gateway you add with `/weft trust`. Gateway diagnostics are appended to tool results, and `mode: enforce` blocks conflicting edits, `git commit` and task completion. `/weft setup` and `/weft feed` run `npx -y @celador/weft@0.3.0`, which installs `wrangler@4` from npm, starts a background local gateway that outlives the chat, creates a paired Git worktree and installs Git hooks in the repository. Activity snapshots and logs are kept in `~/.cache/weft-thor`, shared across profiles.

name: weightscope
description: Offline-by-default safetensors checkpoint inspector: per-tensor and per-layer weight diffs (L2, relative change, cosine, NaN/Inf) via tools ckpt_summary and ckpt_diff, plus `thor weightscope` and `/weightscope`. Optional remote GPU worker, and an opt-in `demo --fetch` of two pinned public SmolLM2-135M checkpoints. Disclosure — reads only the checkpoint paths you pass; writes recent diff headlines under the plugin data dir (optional) and, with `demo --fetch`, caches 513.2 MiB of pinned public Hugging Face weights plus an SVG heatmap; network is off unless you set remote_url (HTTPS to that worker only, bearer token from a named Thor secret, no checkpoint upload) or pass `demo --fetch` (HTTPS to huggingface.co / official HF CDNs, no token); no telemetry, no shell, no background processes, no model execution. Numeric differences are not a safety, quality, or alignment verdict.

name: weir
description: Public X (Twitter) and Reddit data through Weir's hosted MCP server: search posts with X's operators, and read profiles, timelines, replies, threads, Lists, subreddits and comments. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with a client ID metadata document or dynamic client registration, so no keys in config) and one skill; no code, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure: every tool call goes to api.weirapp.io and spends Weir credits (5,000 free a month, then prepaid packs); the search terms, handles and links you look up are sent to Weir. Data tools are annotated read-only; the optional monitor tools appear only with the monitors:write scope, and the package marks its server untrusted, so Thor asks before any call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `weir` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`. Weir is not affiliated with X or Reddit. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: werk
description: Plain-language equipment description in, engineering package out: werk triages the description into domains, breaks it into work items, runs them through review roles and domain-pack checks (a build123d STEP model for mechanical work; the elec pack ships SKiDL/KiCad tools but designs nothing in this release), and writes a COVER.md with the gaps it found written down. Proof of concept, NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION. Disclosure — `thor werk doctor --setup` (after consent in a terminal) creates two worker profiles (werk-builder, werk-reviewer) and a Kanban board `werk`, symlinks werk into those profiles' plugins dirs and their plugin-data/werk to your own werk data dir, and uses uv to download a CPython 3.12 build and hash-pinned pack packages from PyPI (mostly wheels, including build123d/OCP) into the plugin's data dir; the elec pack's sdist-only skidl, hierplace and kinet2pcb are built locally with setuptools fetched unpinned at build time, in a minimal environment with no provider keys; `thor werk run` is a long foreground run (default caps 60M tokens / 24 h) that spends model tokens through your configured providers and runs `thor kanban` CLI calls; pack tools run as subprocesses in their own venvs with the network cut via `unshare -rn` when available, the elec pack calls the system `kicad-cli` (GPL) if present, and signed overrides use `ssh-keygen`. Three optional supplier-key settings are declared but unused in this version. No telemetry, no self-update.

name: werracle-evm-guard
description: Autonomous EVM execution guardrail and DeFi liquidation risk radar for Thor Agent. Intercepts cast send transactions before broadcast to block unlimited token approvals, NFT operator takeovers, and high-value transfers. Performs Radar lookups to api.werracle.com by default on every werracle tool call and intercepted cast send. Disclosure — by default sends the target address and chain of every intercepted `cast send`, and the addresses, accounts and market pairs passed to its werracle_* tools, to api.werracle.com (or the user-configured api_url); WERRACLE_API_KEY is sent only to https://api.werracle.com. The guard is best-effort and fails open when the Radar lookup or key lookup errors.

name: wever-labs
description: Check agent readiness, review oversight evidence, look up records, and run treasury checks with 226 tools in the Wever Labs main catalog and 30 in the free catalog. Paid tools cost 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402. Thor sends tool requests and inputs to the two hosted Wever Labs MCP servers. Both connections use Thor approval for write-capable calls. Disclosure — sends every Wever Labs tool request and its inputs to the hosted MCP servers at weverlabs.com/mcp and weverlabs.com/mcp-free (tool definitions are served by the vendor at runtime and can change without a re-pin); paid tools on the main catalog cost 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402, which Thor does not pay itself; both servers are declared `trust: untrusted`, so write-capable calls ask first.

name: whatsapp-agent-platform
description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Thor Labs) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Thor through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under THOR_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Thor fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under THOR_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Thor; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Thor .env; the state file under THOR_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

name: wheelspin
description: Spin a real wheel: any list becomes a weighted, animated Desktop wheel that lands on an answer in chat, with hidden jackpots and a slot-machine reveal. Disclosure — by default each Desktop spin posts "The wheel says: <winner>" into the active chat as a user message, which starts a model turn (toggle in the pane); stores wheels and spin history in plugin-data/wheelspin/.

name: which-copy
description: Answers the question that silently decides everything else: which copy of a command is the Thor process actually going to run? On a Mac the same tool can exist five times over — a Homebrew formula, an npm global install, a pyenv shim, a standalone download, and Thor's own bundled copy — and the name resolves to whichever one PATH reaches first, with no warning when that is the wrong one. which_copy resolves one name against the PATH of the running Thor process and, separately, against the PATH your own login shell builds for a terminal (that shell is started from the system default PATH, not Thor's, so the entries it reports are its own), and says so when the two disagree. It also states, in every report, that Thor's terminal tool runs commands in a login shell whose PATH gains directories Thor adds — so it never claims the process PATH is the PATH a terminal command gets. It lists every copy it can find, on PATH and in the usual off-PATH install locations, with the evidence for where each came from (a Homebrew Cellar directory names the formula, a node_modules tree names the npm package including its scope, pyenv versions, uv tools, pipx venvs, nvm, Thor's own directories, a plain folder, the macOS system), the version it reports, and whether it can even execute here — an Intel-only binary on Apple silicon is named as needing Rosetta to run. Then it gives a verdict in plain language: an older copy shadowing a newer one, a dead symlink earlier in PATH that the shell silently skips, Thor preferring its own bundle to yours, several copies whose versions were measured (the same version, the winner being the newest, versions that cannot honestly be ordered, copies that reported no version, copies the sweep did not ask, or copies it did not run), or nothing wrong at all. which_copy_scan sweeps the usual AI tools — python, python3, node, npm, npx, bun, pnpm, uv, pip3, pipx, git, gh, brew, thor, claude, codex, opencode, gemini, grok, aider, cursor-agent, rustc, go, ruby, java — in about a second, one line per tool, worst first. It diagnoses and stops: no installs, no PATH edits, no relinking, no "fix" that hides the problem. Versions are asked with an argv-only probe (three-second deadline, own process group, 8 KB output cap, cwd at the filesystem root, and a stripped environment so a shadowing binary never sees Thor's API keys), and only for copies this machine put there: an absolute entry on Thor's PATH, an absolute entry on the login shell's PATH, or one of the fixed install directories. Nothing named in a tool call is ever executed — a file passed as a path, a copy found only in a PATH string the call supplies, and a copy behind a relative or empty PATH entry are described with their version left unchecked — so a prompt-injected repository cannot get its own script run. For a call that supplies `path`, every version probe still runs with Thor's own process PATH, never the raw supplied string. probe_versions false skips every probe, and the login-shell check is separate, so pair it with check_login_shell false for a call that starts no process at all. When two version strings were never meant to be compared, it says it cannot order them instead of guessing.

name: whiplash
description: Let Thor jam live on an Elektron Digitakt II over USB MIDI: genre/mood beats with MIDI clock, routed onto a session kit map of what each track holds (tracks 1-16), in any key with chord progressions, arranged into song sections (whiplash_arrange: intro, build, drop, outro on bar lines), written melodies and rhythms, bar-quantized pattern switches with DJ-style transitions (filter swap, drop swap, riser), track levels and pan with saved mixes (whiplash_mix), listening to the unit's real output over USB audio (whiplash_listen: loudness, clipping, band balance, timing and kick offsets as numbers, never audio) with a loudness guard that refuses level increases after clipping, a kit scan (whiplash_scan_kit: with the beat stopped, one note per track, heard and classified into proposed kit-map labels that are never applied without the user's yes), play along (whiplash_play_along / whiplash_follow: reads the unit's MIDI input to show the user's knob moves, stop a ramp on a knob they grab, and answer phrases they play in key on another track; whiplash_undo reverts the last part, mix or arrangement change), named sound parameters, clock-synced parameter ramps, live fills/drops/density/swing/humanize, switching a track among samples already in the project pool, mutes and tempo. Disclosure — controls MIDI hardware (MIDI Start also starts the unit's own sequencer; a clock-only mode is available), can change which already-loaded sample a track plays, runs a background sequencer thread while a pattern plays, and opens a virtual MIDI port named "Whiplash" when no Digitakt is connected. Optional visualiser (whiplash_open_view): an unauthenticated read-only local web page served on 127.0.0.1 from a background thread, opened in the default browser, showing the beat and the live Thor conversation including tool calls and results (taken from in-memory observer hooks; nothing is stored), readable by any local process while it is open. whiplash_listen opens an audio input (the Digitakt's USB audio by default, or WHIPLASH_AUDIO_INPUT or any input named in the tool call, which can be a microphone) only for the length of one call (at most 24 s), through the optional numpy/sounddevice extra, which needs microphone permission on macOS; the audio is analysed in memory and dropped. whiplash_scan_kit does the same for at most about 35 s and sends only note-on/off. whiplash_play_along and whiplash_follow open the Digitakt's MIDI input (never another device) on a background reader thread that only reads; what it hears is never sent back, and the session (notes and CCs sent and heard) is kept in memory only, at most 65,536 events, never written to disk. Never sends SysEx or program changes; no file transfer, project writes, shell or credentials, and no network beyond that localhost page.

name: whiteboard
description: An agentic whiteboard. Say what you're planning and Thor lays it out as a route, columns or a map, with hand-drawn stickers. Add rough notes and Thor proposes groups, owners and action items that you accept one by one and can take back. Hand an action item to Thor and an agent does it on the board and delivers the result next to the note with its sources, or run the whole route and get a brief at the end. Select anything and ask about it. Once you allow it, any chat can read your boards and propose changes. Link a board to the chat its work is in: the board shows what that chat is doing, and the chat hears what you change on the board. Send notes to Thor Kanban or lay a Kanban board out as a whiteboard. Disclosure — laying out a board, grouping notes, unpacking a result and the brief each start a hidden Thor session told to use no tools; Hand to Thor, Run the route and Ask start hidden sessions that use your Thor tools and read third-party web pages, at most three at once, each stopped after 4 minutes or 24 tool calls; approval prompts inside these sessions are denied; export writes the one Markdown or CSV file you name in the system dialog, through the plugin's own backend; boards live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy under plugin-data/whiteboard/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Thor profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; a Planning model and an Agent model in Settings name a model you are signed in to in Thor when a session is created, and a refused model stops the run; with the Sheets or Data plugin installed, a click on that page pins notes to the open board through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; Send to Kanban and New board from Kanban make the plugin's backend run the `thor kanban` command, with no shell and with note text passed after `--` and on standard input, to list boards, create cards and read a board; cards are created in Blocked with no assignee, and in Triage, which Thor works through on its own, only when you tick a box; while the page is open on a board that has Kanban cards it reads those Kanban boards about every 25 seconds, and it never changes a card after making it; a board can remember the id of the chat it is linked to, the page places a request in that chat's message box for you to send and never sends it, and after that it listens to that one chat for up to 30 minutes and reads its answer from the transcript; the plugin registers four hooks (pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, on_session_end, post_compaction) that run on every chat turn and return at once unless the chat is linked to a board; for a linked chat they keep the state of its latest turn and the first line of its answer under plugin-data/whiteboard/, and, only while chat access is on, add to the message you send in that chat a short notice that the board exists and the notes you added, edited or removed on it since the chat's last turn; the plugin never sends a message to a chat; the linked chat can put a doing, done or blocked mark on its own board's notes with no review, which changes nothing else and clears with a click; which chat each board is linked to is kept under plugin-data/whiteboard/ as ids only, whether or not chat access is on; no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes of its own, and no command other than `thor kanban`. Independent community project, not affiliated with Thor Labs.

name: whoami
description: Coloured pill in the composer showing which Thor profile a new session will use.

name: whoop-mcp
description: Read the user's WHOOP recovery, HRV, sleep and strain through the local whoop MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with WHOOP. Runs the `whoop-mcp-unofficial@0.7.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official WHOOP OAuth API (v2). The user creates their own WHOOP developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.whoop-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to WHOOP's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Thor credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.thor/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.thor/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: whoop_profile_update (local profile only); whoop_exchange_code (stores OAuth tokens locally); whoop_revoke_access (revokes the WHOOP grant and deletes local tokens). The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

name: whos-listening
description: Memory that knows who's listening. Each memory is Private or Shared. Private memories go into a request only when the machine running Thor (the gateway), the app you chat in (the platform) and the model provider are all trusted. By default, the gateway you install it on is trusted unless it's a hosted Thor such as Thor Cloud; the trusted platforms are the terminal and Thor Desktop, including its Webapp; and the trusted model routes are Venice's private models and models on your own machine or local network. Everything else gets Shared memories only. You can configure all of these options in the plugin's settings: trusting either more or fewer gateways, platforms or model providers. Disclosure — memories stay in $THOR_HOME/whos-listening/. Once a day it fetches Venice's public model list from api.venice.ai (nothing about you is sent). With a Venice key in Thor, a duplicate check (on by default) sends each new memory, each memory arriving by sync and each memory in a /memories review scan, together with up to 20 others, Private ones included, to Venice's private Clef model (duplicate_judge off keeps it local). Shared memories sync to your GitHub repository only if you set that up.

name: why
description: Ask why any line of agent-written code exists. Each time the agent writes or patches a file, Why records the lines it wrote and that turn's user request, locally. /why app.py:42 (or thor why, or the why_line tool) then names the request, date, model and session behind the line; /why app.py shows which requests wrote which share of a file. Lines are matched by text, not number, so they are found after they move. No model calls, network or dependencies.

name: wicked-memory
description: Persistent, wallet-scoped long-term memory for Thor: remember, semantic recall, versioned update, history and approved hard delete, backed by the hosted Wicked Memory service, plus skills for using it and for connecting the Wicked MCP server. Works with no setup (a wallet is generated on first use; search uses the service's shared free key). Disclosure — sends the memory text and search queries the agent chooses to memory.wickedapi.com (or your configured base_url), each request signed by the agent's wallet, plus one GET to /v1/status on first use to read the published community key; stores a generated private key unencrypted in the plugin data dir unless you supply WICKED_MEMORY_PRIVATE_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry; every wicked_memory_forget asks for human approval. The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.

name: widespread
description: Earn verified-work bounties on the widespread protocol — discover funded markets across every forge, claim one, ship a signed dg-ship-1 attestation, watch the adjudicator, collect the payout. The earning-side counterpart to payment plugins: wide_* tools let an agent get paid for work it can prove, and the payer side (post a bounty, accept a claim) is approval-gated by the human. Plain HTTPS to the live bridge — no browser, no runtime dependency. Disclosure — sends claims, signed work attestations (commit SHAs, optional proof items) and bounty posts to the widespread bridge (widespread-bridge.widespread.workers.dev) and forge (code.widespread.fyi), overridable with WIDE_BRIDGE / WIDE_FORGE; keeps an Ed25519 agent signing seed (mode 0600) and a claim ledger under the profile's plugin-data/widespread; wide_post (model-chosen amount) and wide_accept (releases a payout) wait for your approval, and an "always" answer for wide_post covers later posts in the same amount band (up to $10, up to $100, over $100) while one for wide_accept covers every later accept.

name: wiki-ref
description: @wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

name: wing
description: Extra features for the Wing Android app: GPT Live voice and email draft cards. GPT Live voice uses ChatGPT subscription access with the selected Thor profile's context. Email draft cards show recipients, cc/bcc, subject and body, then open the user's chosen email app for final edits and sending. Drafts work independently of voice and need no OpenAI credentials or mail account access. Draft cards adapt arsiktech's thor-draft-cards design (MIT); the voice integration builds on Synero's thor-live-voice work (MIT). Disclosure — voice calls send the WebRTC SDP, the selected profile's Thor-built system prompt (including memory) and client-supplied chat excerpts to chatgpt.com (Codex realtime endpoint) through the profile's openai-codex sign-in, with the headers OpenAI-Alpha: quicksilver=v2, originator: thor-agent and random session ids; building fresh voice context runs a short-lived Python child that initialises the profile's memory providers and reads context files from the profile's configured terminal.cwd only; email drafts persist in the profile's plugin-data/wing SQLite database; relies on undocumented Thor prompt-inspection and voice helpers that may break on update; draft cards and voice adapt arsiktech's thor-draft-cards and Synero's thor-live-voice (MIT). No telemetry, stored credentials or self-updater.

name: wings
description: A private WireGuard network between every Thor you own and your phone. Two devices are enough: run setup on a computer, scan one code on the phone. Bots and sessions from all your machines in Desktop, the terminal and the Thor app. Computers link directly when they can. No account, no coordination server, no third party. Disclosure — Wings asks for admin rights once per machine and installs a root helper (/usr/local/libexec/wings-root) with always-on systemd units (wings-sync, wings-watch, wings-relay, wings-address, wings-dns), a WireGuard interface wings0, an nftables table, firewalld/ufw rules, a wings-net system user, a marked /etc/hosts line and a private certificate authority trusted system-wide but limited to .wings names; it may install wireguard-tools and nftables from your package manager and downloads wstunnel 11.1.0 from its official GitHub release (checksum-pinned). It also adds a per-user wings-upkeep timer that runs every minute, installs and starts the Thor gateway service, and sets webapp.enabled and webapp.public_url in config.yaml. Every device you pair can sign in to Thor on every machine in your wing net without a password (full dashboard and terminal access), and every joined computer holds the shared wing-net key; turn this off per machine with `thor wings trust off`. The Wings page lists the bots and recent session titles of every Thor profile on each of your machines. A hub opens one UDP port (plus TCP 443 for the optional HTTPS relay), and `thor wings router open` asks your router over UPnP to forward it.

name: wireguard
description: Read-only status and peer list for a WireGuard server running on the same Windows machine as Thor. Two tools: vpn_status (service state, tunnel address and port, server public key, per-peer handshake and transfer) and vpn_peers (the peer list only). The plugin runs only wg.exe show, sc.exe query, and one PowerShell adapter lookup; it never changes the tunnel and never reads the tunnel configuration file or any private key material. Windows only (WireGuard for Windows). Disclosure — runs local wg.exe show, sc.exe query and one PowerShell Get-NetIPAddress lookup (read-only, never touches the tunnel config or private key); tool results put peer public keys, allowed IPs and peer endpoint IP addresses into the conversation sent to your model provider.

name: wiretap
description: Inspect the request Thor hands its provider client for each model call (system prompt, messages with whatever was added at send time, and tool declarations as far as Thor passes them to hooks) and the model's response, aligned to the stored transcript, in a dashboard tab and a Desktop page; also per-call latency, tokens, prefix-cache hits with miss forensics and cost, and a read-only CLI. Captures exclusively from pre_api_request, post_api_request, and api_request_error hooks without wrapping httpx or modifying requests. Disclosure — stores full prompts, tool results and model responses locally in an owner-only SQLite file (kept 72 hours by default; turn off `capture_payloads` to keep timing/token/cost rows only), reads Thor's state.db read-only, and reads two private Thor modules (pricing tables and write-provenance) that a Thor update may change; it makes no network calls of its own.

name: wiro
description: Wiro AI as a Thor model provider (`--provider wiro`, or Wiro AI in `thor model`): one OpenAI-compatible API and one key for GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Grok models, paid as you go from the Wiro wallet. The listed models declare their context window, tool calling and image input, `/reasoning` is sent as the gateway's `reasoning_effort` (models that cannot switch reasoning off get their lowest level), and openai/gpt-6-luna handles background tasks and image description. Disclosure: registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access). Prompts, tool schemas and results, attached images and the GET /v1/models catalog request go to https://llm.wiro.ai/v1 through Thor' own client with WIRO_API_KEY, which Thor reads; usage is paid from the user's Wiro wallet; the plugin itself opens no connections and sends no telemetry.

name: wiro-media
description: Wiro AI's image, video, speech, music, transcription and 3D models as thirteen wiro_* tools: generate and edit images (upscale, remove backgrounds, prompt edits), text or image to video, text to speech, music, transcription, image to 3D, catalog search with prices, any catalog model, task follow-up and Wiro AI workflows. It also registers Wiro AI as an opt-in backend for image_generate, video_generate, text_to_speech and speech-to-text, and ships the wiro-media:wiro skill. Every tool takes any catalog model; outputs are saved in cache/generated/ with MEDIA: tags, and every result reports its cost. Disclosure — prompts, settings and input files go to https://api.wiro.ai/v1 with WIRO_API_KEY, read per call through Thor secret scope; every generation spends the user's Wiro AI balance with no Thor approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options such as high resolution or long video. Local input files are read only from Thor' media cache, or from anywhere the user can read when the terminal backend is local (system and credential folders and the rest of the Thor home excluded), and only when their bytes are media or documents of the expected kind; they are uploaded to the user's Wiro AI storage. Output files are downloaded only from *.wiro.ai hosts. Ogg Opus voice notes and bmp, tiff or avif images are converted with the local ffmpeg when it is installed.

name: withhuman
description: Human approval for Thor tool calls, with human in the loop guardrails. Set rules for what runs automatically, and send the rest to your team to approve or deny from Slack, Discord or your phone. Keep an audit log of every call. Disclosure — every tool call's name and arguments are sent to your withHuman organization (app.withhuman.ai or the address you configure) and run only after approval. The plugin downloads a pinned, checksum-verified withHuman CLI from downloads.withhuman.ai and runs it once per tool call. Setup offers to set the profile-wide `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` to 0, which removes Thor's hook hang guard for every plugin. On hosted withHuman, setup adds the `withhuman-gateway` MCP server, which sends your agent key to your withHuman address, and offers to install the withHuman skills from withhuman.ai.

name: wolfmarkdown
description: Create, clean, and verify standalone Markdown with conservative semantic repair and deterministic artifact checks. Disclosure — skill-only plugin that has the agent run its bundled Node.js 22+ scripts through the terminal; on first use it runs `npm ci` in the plugin folder (lockfile-pinned packages from registry.npmjs.org), and the optional `/wolfmarkdown setup` also creates skill symlinks in ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills.

name: woof
description: Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run thor woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

name: word-miner
description: Turn any text you are consuming (lyrics, subtitles, articles, chat) into a personal vocabulary deck and run short daily spaced-repetition sessions inside Thor. Any language pair. Local only — SQLite event log, SM-2-like scheduler with response-time adjustment, 3+3+3+1 sessions, two-stage graduation. No Anki, no AnkiConnect, no network. The model extracts lemmas; four tools plus /deck and a bundled mining skill. Disclosure — stores decks and review history under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/word-miner; no outbound calls, no shell, no credentials.

name: word-peek
description: Explore HTML passages in a folder-granted reader, ask Thor in the passage's captured chat, and save notes or whole-document edits with verified backups and Undo. Web selections use the consent-based preview SDK and are read-only. Chat answers are matched to their submitted turn. Selected text, context, references and whole-edit documents go through the configured Thor agent and its tools. Reads and writes use the Desktop file SDK; edited documents and exclusive .word-peek-*.bak copies stay in the granted folder. Glossary and recovery metadata use plugin storage. No agent tools, hooks, middleware, credentials, telemetry or direct model API calls are added.

name: words-into-music
description: Create original songs from an idea or your own lyrics, check generation progress and browse your private song library through the hosted Words into Music Streamable HTTP MCP server, plus a skill that walks the agent through preparing a brief, confirming the one-credit cost and polling the job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, mcp.json, skills/), no plugin code. Requires a Words into Music account and browser OAuth consent (add the server with --auth oauth, then thor mcp login words-into-music); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: song briefs, lyrics and titles you send go to mcp.wordsintomusic.com under your Words into Music OAuth sign-in; start_song spends one existing song credit and is declared as a costed tool, and the server is declared untrusted so Thor asks before every write-capable call; the server also exposes create_checkout_link, which only creates a Stripe checkout link you open yourself to buy a plan or song pack and never charges a saved card.

name: workbench-link
