description: Route Thor native file, terminal and code tools to one explicitly selected Linux/Docker project worker. Disclosure — when `terminal.backend: workbench_link` is selected, terminal, file and code-execution commands and their output are sent over HMAC-authenticated HTTPS to a project worker you start and bind, which runs them in a network-less, read-only Docker container with your project directory mounted read-write; `thor workbench-link serve` opens a TCP listener (127.0.0.1:8765 by default, any address you pass with --listen) and keeps a ledger of commands' retained output under the plugin data folder.

name: workflow-record
description: thor record: demonstrate a browser workflow once (clicks, field values, navigations) and its bundled skill lets /learn turn the recording into a skill that replays it with the browser tools. A Thor Labs plugin: built by Thor Labs, not supported. Disclosure — attaches over CDP to a Chromium you point it at (--cdp, BROWSER_CDP_URL, browser.cdp_url or 127.0.0.1:9222) and records what you do in that tab until Ctrl-C; password, one-time-code and card fields are masked inside the page as {SECRET:name} and never written. Recordings stay local in <THOR_HOME>/recordings; nothing is sent anywhere until you run /learn on one, which hands it to your active model.

name: workout-tracker
description: Plan gym workouts through Workout Tracker's hosted MCP servers (Streamable HTTP at workout.lbyte.app): search a rated exercise catalog and check a draft plan's weekly sets per muscle and session length with no account, then, with a personal access token, save plans to the user's account and make one active. Bundles the workout-tracker skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: two servers. workout-tracker (/mcp/public) needs no credentials and never receives the token. workout-tracker-account (/mcp/account) acts on the user's account with a token they create in the app, sent as an Authorization header from WORKOUT_TRACKER_TOKEN in the profile environment; when it is unset, Thor skips that server and the catalog tools still work. The token covers plans, timing, gear, targets and read-only history; it cannot sync workouts or manage tokens. Both servers are marked untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The skill tells the agent to read https://workout.lbyte.app/llms.txt for the plan format. The tool set is served by the remote servers at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry.

name: workroom
description: Gives the agent a room to work on Word, PowerPoint and Excel files while you stay in charge. Figures are linked to their source cells and kept in step when a source changes; the agent can prepare a release but has no tool to approve one; figures in its text are marked supported, calculated or not verified from what it read; a reply that claims a file that does not exist gets one honest line. Desktop panels: Needs you, Made (list or gallery), Room, Rules. Disclosure: reads and writes only inside the folders the user registers and in the plugin data directory; no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater, no native binary. To be able to put protected files back, the safety net reads, in memory, the bytes of every managed or protected file of a registered project (including .env and key files) before a shell, code or editing tool runs; they are never shown to the agent and are kept in plugin data only if the agent changed the file (the agent's version). Hooks (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, transform_llm_output, pre_llm_call, pre_verify, subagent_start, subagent_stop) can block a tool call, append one line to a tool result or reply, and, after a shell, code or other editing tool runs, put back any Office or protected file of a registered project that changed (the agent's version is kept in plugin data); they never approve or auto-approve. To check the figures in the agent's text it stores, in a local SQLite file in the plugin data directory, the text of tool results the agent read this session (capped at 20 MB per session) and the owner's chat messages; nothing is sent anywhere. Subprocesses: a local Python child to build files; the Windows icacls tool once for the signing key file; PowerShell only on request on Windows with PowerPoint to draw slide pictures, or LibreOffice (soffice) for the same on other systems when it is installed. Starts no scheduled job itself (a user-created Thor cron job may run its watch script, which can prepare a release but never approves one).

name: worktable
description: Connect Thor to Worktable, a workspace for Docs, HTML Docs, Records, annotations and threads shared with people and other agents. Thor answers Worktable thread messages addressed to it, one Thor conversation per thread, and gets Worktable's tools and skills. Disclosure — connects only to the Worktable address you give `thor worktable connect` (Worktable Cloud or self-hosted) and sends it this computer's hostname and a random installation id when pairing; while the gateway runs, thread messages addressed to this Thor run as full Thor turns with this profile's terminal, file and MCP tools, for the person who connected it and (unless `trust_own_agents` is turned off) the agents that same person connected, and for other members or other people's agents only if the owner turns on `trust_all_members` or `trust_all_agents`; connecting writes mcp_servers.worktable, plugins.entries.worktable and platforms.worktable in config.yaml and stores a self-hosted pairing token as WORKTABLE_TOKEN in the profile's .env; no telemetry.

name: world-clock
description: One time zone in your Thor Desktop status bar, every other zone you work with a click away. Click the time for a drop-up of your enabled zones; Edit zones lists standard IANA zones with live UTC offsets. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no network, agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: world-window
description: World news your agent walks to: headlines grouped by story across named, rated outlets, each in the outlet's own words and link. Pull only.

name: worldmonitor
description: Source-aware global intelligence through WorldMonitor's hosted MCP: country risk, conflicts, markets, energy, shipping and natural hazards. Configuration-only Agent Plugins v1 package with one skill. Public source inventory works without credentials; other intelligence requires a signed-in account and some tools require a subscription. Disclosure — connects to the hosted WorldMonitor MCP server at worldmonitor.app and sends tool arguments there; the remote tool list is dynamic and not frozen by this SHA; authenticated calls use the user's WorldMonitor account allowance, and remote tools include `start_upgrade` (creates a personal checkout link) and `report_issue` (submits a report to WorldMonitor); the package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so Thor asks before any tool not annotated read-only. No local runtime code, hooks, telemetry or self-updater.

name: wow
description: Chat with a Thor agent from inside World of Warcraft: Forever. The plugin registers a kind: platform gateway adapter that serves a local HTTP endpoint (/v1/wow/message, /v1/wow/outbox, /v1/wow/health) authenticated with a bearer token; one character (Name-Realm) is one Thor DM session. A companion bridge runs on a Windows 11 PC next to the game client: it captures a 1600x400 pixel strip from the game window with the Windows Graphics Capture API (mss/GDI fallback), decodes chat, POSTs lines to the adapter and long-polls the outbox. It also writes reply/state files into the WoW AddOns tree and reads SavedVariables for reload mode, and plays silent doorbell WAVs. The adapter binds 127.0.0.1 by default and can be bound to a LAN address explicitly; the bridge then makes outbound HTTP requests to that configured Thor host. Adds five WoW-only tools (wow_addon_search, wow_addon_guide, wow_addon_install, wow_addon_uninstall, wow_quest_help), three per-character toolsets selected with /mode (standard, wow, full; full needs an in-game confirmation and expires after 60 minutes), and a bundled wow-player-guide skill. Disclosure - the plugin opens a local HTTP listener guarded by a shared bearer secret (WOW_BRIDGE_TOKEN, auto-generated in memory when unset, so the bridge cannot pair until it is set); it makes CurseForge API calls (api.curseforge.com) with the player's own CurseForge Core API key, stored as a profile-scoped Thor secret (WOW_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY in the selected profile) with no plugin-managed credential file; addon installs and uninstalls are queued to the bridge, which writes or moves files under the WoW AddOns directory only after the player confirms in game and keeps a removal backup instead of deleting permanently; a desktop setup page creates or updates a dedicated Thor profile (wow), writes its .env, config.yaml, SOUL.md and a profile skill, and can hot-serve that profile through a running gateway multiplexer. The bridge is a separate long-running background process (screen pixels plus files only); the plugin does not read the game process or its memory, does not inject input, and does not automate gameplay. Chat text and tool results are sent to the model provider configured for the WoW Thor profile (cloud or local), with that provider's data-handling terms and the usual token cost. Requires Thor >=0.22.7, Windows 11 for the bridge, WoW: Forever (Interface 16001), and uv/Python downloaded for the bridge; a CurseForge key is needed only for one-click addon installs (without one the addon tools return a guided CurseForge link). Disclosure — the plugin opens a local HTTP listener (127.0.0.1 by default, plain HTTP if bound to a LAN address) guarded only by a shared bearer token (WOW_BRIDGE_TOKEN); whoever holds that token can chat as any character and, after the in-game `/mode full confirm` step, use terminal, file and code tools on the Thor host for 60 minutes. It calls the CurseForge API (api.curseforge.com) with the player's own CurseForge key, stored as a Thor secret in the selected profile. The Desktop setup page creates or updates a dedicated Thor profile: it copies this plugin into that profile, writes the profile's .env, config.yaml (including turning off tool deferral for that profile), SOUL.md and a profile skill, and can hot-serve it through a running gateway. A separate long-running Windows bridge reads a strip of the game window's pixels, writes reply and state files and installs or backs up addons under the WoW AddOns folder only after an in-game confirmation, opens links the agent sends in the default browser, and downloads a checksum-pinned uv release and Python on setup; it never reads game memory, injects input or automates play. Chat text and tool results go to the model provider configured for the WoW profile.

name: wow-addon-forge
description: Builds World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.1, Interface 16001) addons that load and run, for players who are not programmers. Nine tools: wow_env (install/addon detection), wow_api (queryable index of the real client build's API, events and restrictions), wow_check (six-stage static + headless verification: TOC lint, Lua 5.1 syntax, global resolution, restricted/secret API rules, headless load in an embedded Lua 5.1 VM stub of the game, efficiency lints), wow_test (multi-client headless Lua test runner), wow_new (scaffolds an addon from tested building blocks: core, replicated record log, guild sync, trust, lazy Classic-theme window, Discord bridge), wow_install (installs after wow_check passes, with backup), wow_savedvars and wow_errors (read game data and in-game Lua errors back, via the bundled ForgeProbe companion addon), and wow_bridge (file-based Discord seam: pull an outbox, push an inbox, one /reload of latency each way). Ships Guildhall, a guild-management addon built entirely with these tools (board, calendar, a Marks currency earned automatically by playing, Discord mirror), the wow-addon-builder skill, /wow, thor wow, and an Addon Forge Desktop pane. Disclosure — runs addon and test Lua code you point it at inside an embedded Lua 5.1 VM (lupa, a native extension) on your machine; `wow_api sync` downloads public API documentation from raw.githubusercontent.com; reads your WoW install (Interface/AddOns, WTF SavedVariables, .build.info); `wow_install` replaces Interface/AddOns/<name> after backing the old folder up under the Thor cache, `wow_bridge push` rewrites that addon's Inbox.lua, and `wow_new` creates a new addon folder at the path given.

name: wp-manager
description: Look after a fleet of WordPress sites from Thor: scan every site for plugin, theme, core and translation updates, install them behind Thor's approval prompt with an automatic health check afterwards, and draft or edit posts and pages from chat (publishing asks first). Includes a WordPress page in Thor Desktop and pairs with the "Website Manager: WP Connector for Thor" WordPress plugin shipped in the repo. Takes no backups. Disclosure — talks only to the WordPress sites you add (REST API, WordPress Application Passwords; plain http refused unless opted in per site; no cross-host redirects with credentials). Passwords resolve through Thor secrets, or through the 1Password CLI you configure as op_binary, which wp-manager runs as a subprocess (argument list, no shell) to read op:// references, list vault names and, only when you choose it, create a new Login item (password passed on stdin). Stores site addresses, usernames and credential references (never passwords) plus an action log in its own folder under THOR_HOME. Never reads or writes the Thor .env. No telemetry.

name: wrenchboard
description: Turn Thor into a circuit board repair bench: a live boardview beside the chat, opened from 14 boardview formats, test plans with readings pinned on the pads, part cards drawn from the real copper, and your schematic and datasheets read on your computer. Disclosure — needs a WrenchBoard account (RepairMind LTD's hosted service at app.wrenchboard.cloud; free to read boards, Pro for repairs and test plans); boardview files you import, your repairs and readings go to WrenchBoard through Thor' MCP client; the board view is a page served by WrenchBoard, in a sandboxed frame, that can send chat messages as you and record readings/steps on your WrenchBoard repair without a model turn; pressing Connect (pane, `thor wrenchboard connect` or `/wb connect`) adds the `wrenchboard` MCP server and its `mcp_allowlist` grant to config.yaml; adds ~5,300 characters of system-prompt sections in Desktop/Webapp; schematics, documents and camera pictures stay on your computer.

name: write-gate
description: Deterministic pre-write content gate for Thor Agent. A pre_tool_call hook parses the exact bytes about to be written as JSON, TOML or Python (stdlib parsers), rejects NUL bytes, oversized content and user-declared regex contracts, and short-circuits invalid writes with a precise line/column error returned to the model as a tool-call error, so the agent fixes the content in the same tool-calling loop instead of leaving a broken file behind. Also adds a write_gate_check preflight tool, a /writegate slash command and Settings -> Plugins config. Patch/replacement fragments are never parsed as whole documents: NUL, size and regex contracts still run on the fragment, and the reconstructed post-edit file is parsed when it can be rebuilt. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no subprocesses, no background processes, no credentials, no telemetry; reads the in-memory arguments of the tool call it gates, one optional user-specified JSON rules file named in the rules_file setting, and (for fragment edits only) the size-capped target file named in that same tool call, read-only; persists three integer counters in profile-scoped plugin state; never auto-approves or bypasses Thor's approval gate; fails open on any internal error.

name: writing-guard
description: Style check for every Thor answer in German and English: finds em and en dashes outside code, links and quotes (optionally replaces them by rule: ranges and list bullets become hyphens, dashes between words a comma), reports stock AI phrases (German and English) and mixed or switched forms of address (du/Sie) in German. Reports by default with one line appended to the answer; rule based, no model calls. Disclosure — no network calls and no model calls. A transform_llm_output hook reads the final answer of each turn; in report mode it appends one report line when there is a finding, in fix mode it also replaces dashes, with footer: false it never changes the answer; the returned text is what Thor stores and shows. Stores per chat session id only the last form of address (du or sie) and a timestamp in THOR_HOME/plugin-data/writing-guard/sessions.json (30 days, at most 2000 sessions); the last report with matched phrases stays in process memory only. Reads only its own plugin settings. Off on cron, subagent, kanban, batch and webhook by default. Registers the tool writing_guard_check (checks a draft, returns JSON), the slash command /writing-guard (settings, last report, check a text) and a skill that adds one line to the skills index of every session while the plugin is enabled.

name: wyoming-voice-bridge
description: Wyoming speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a Wyoming server you run (stt/tts provider `wyoming`), plus a wyoming_voice_status tool that lists the server's models and voices. Disclosure — Audio and text to speak go to the WYOMING_* host:port you set over cleartext, unauthenticated TCP (public addresses accepted). Once selected, the providers send speech in every session, including cron and webhooks. This build imports the installed package only when its file tree is the official wyoming 1.5.4 wheel, and a different tree sends nothing. This build lists no ffmpeg digest, so audio that is not already 16 kHz, 16-bit, mono WAV is not converted. wyoming_voice_status asks with one public pre_tool_call line. Choosing always stores one command_allowlist line for that same which and the same host:port list. A later call skips the question only when a person is present. cron, thor -q, webhook, msgraph_webhook, and api_server do not send a describe, even after always. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt, and this plugin does not add a refusal for those modes. The plugin does not import Thor approval, config, or write-guard modules. Thor 0.21.4 does not list the skill. The v0.21.5 canary and Thor 0.22.2 add one skill line to every session that loads the plugin, including a surface where the tools are turned off. The status tool is on for every surface, including the gateway, and a guest there can call it and approve it when a person can answer. Turn the wyoming_voice toolset off per surface with thor tools.

name: x-dashboard
description: Zero-cost ($0.00) X analytics dashboard for Thor Web and Desktop with profile KPIs, verified-follower & impression goal tracking, post/mention feeds, SVG charts, and CSV/JSON export. Disclosure — Free Mode fetches public profile and post metadata from api.fxtwitter.com / api.vxtwitter.com and r.jina.ai and caches snapshots in <thor_home>/plugin-data/x-dashboard/; when the xurl CLI is on PATH it runs `xurl auth status` locally to detect your linked handle; optional xAI x_search discovery (enable_x_search=true, billed to your xAI account) and Live X API v2 mode (api.x.com with X_BEARER_TOKEN, or the xurl CLI) run only when explicitly opted in.

name: xchat
description: X Chat gateway platform: talk to Thor in X's end-to-end encrypted DMs. Thor runs as the X account you connect: chat with it in your own self-chat ("message yourself"), or give it a separate account and DM that. Messages are decrypted and encrypted locally with X's official Chat XDK, so X only routes ciphertext. Encrypted media, threaded replies, group mention gating and cron delivery.

name: xmemo
description: Native XMemo memory provider for Thor Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall and the search tools), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Thor memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); keeps a local SQLite cache of recalled results and a queue of unsent writes in $THOR_HOME/xmemo_cache.db, partitioned by a hashed account identity; reads the key from XMEMO_KEY (also MEMORY_OS_API_KEY / MEMORY_OS_MCP_TOKEN) and, if none is set, falls back to the xmemo login token in ~/.config/xmemo/credentials.json (a catalog rule 11 deviation kept for existing users); workflow and destructive tools and timeline capture are off by default and opt-in.

name: xray
description: Sets traps for plugins instead of watching them. thor xray detonate runs a plugin in a throwaway child process with a fake home full of honeytokens, fuzzes its tools, fires its hooks and replays it at +30 and +90 days to catch time-bombs, then gives a RED/AMBER/GREEN verdict with file:line proof, a per-version behaviour diff and a drafted disclosure line. Opt-in live bait flags any installed plugin that reads a decoy credential file and can route its next tool call to Thor' approval prompt. Disclosure — spawns child Python processes to detonate plugins; the child runs as you (fake HOME, real keys stripped) and is not an OS sandbox, so its egress and spawn blocking (Python audit hooks, incl. fork and fork_exec) is a tripwire native code can bypass; reads of your real credential stores are refused and make the verdict RED; runs git clone when you detonate a remote repo, including from the dashboard's detonate button; by default (bait_runtime) installs a Python audit hook in the Thor process that watches for plugins touching bait files or honeytokens; reads installed plugins' source dirs to attribute events; bait plant (opt-in) writes decoy files only into empty default credential paths of the AWS CLI/SDKs, git credential store, ssh and Solana CLI, so those tools use the fake values until bait remove, which deletes only unchanged files it wrote; enforce (off by default) uses pre_tool_call approve; no LLM calls, no telemetry; X-Ray itself never reads real credentials or patches Thor core.

name: xscapes
description: Living ASCII scenes under Thor in the terminal that show what the agent is doing while you wait: the wind, the sea or the rain rises with the work, a thought cloud means it is thinking, owlets, crablets or kittens arrive for subagents, the moon sinks as the context fills, and the companion knocks with a sound when Thor finishes or needs you (a question, a password prompt, an approval). Forwards fifteen lifecycle hooks to the xscapes CLI (`xscapes hook <event> thor`, stdin JSON, never waited on, never blocks); needs the xscapes binary. No tools, middleware or env vars; no network. Disclosure — forwards every tool call's name and full arguments, approval commands, and the first line (up to 120 characters) of each prompt and reply to the separately installed xscapes binary, which is not covered by this pin and keeps events under ~/.config/xscapes/.

name: yandex
description: Yandex Search API for Thor web search and generated answers with cited sources. Uses the paid Yandex Cloud service. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and yandex_generative_search questions to searchapi.api.cloud.yandex.net, or to the base URL in YANDEX_SEARCH_API_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_API_KEY and YANDEX_FOLDER_ID read through Thor; the Search API is a paid Yandex Cloud service billed to the folder that owns the key; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yandex-disk
description: Browse, search and manage files on Yandex Disk. Read and write files, transfer them locally, share links and restore items from the bin. Disclosure — sends every request to cloud-api.yandex.net, or to the https URL in YANDEX_DISK_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_DISK_OAUTH_TOKEN read through Thor; file bytes go to the upload and download hosts the API hands out, without the token; unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS leaves search out, loading the plugin sends one search request to learn whether the token may search, and yadisk_search is registered only if it may; every tool, permanent delete, emptying the bin and public share links included, is offered unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only Disk); yadisk_upload reads a local file and sends it unredacted, and yadisk_download writes one, after Thor' shared file-safety rules and the plugin's own: upload refuses .env files, Thor' credential stores, Thor' own directory and the home directories that hold keys and logins; download refuses credential files, Thor' own directory, .thor directories, agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, system locations and paths outside THOR_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other local files are within reach; YANDEX_DISK_ROOT confines Disk paths, not local ones; an upload from a URL makes Yandex fetch that URL; file names and contents written by other people reach the agent as tool output; no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yandex_calendar
description: Manage events, invitations and RSVPs across Yandex calendars through CalDAV. Choose which calendars and actions Thor can use. Disclosure — sends every request to caldav.yandex.ru, or to the HTTPS URL in YANDEX_CALENDAR_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_CALENDAR_LOGIN and YANDEX_CALENDAR_APP_PASSWORD read through Thor; all seven tools, delete included, are offered unless YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS narrows them; the tools act as your Yandex account, so adding attendees makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it; delete removes the event from the server and the plugin keeps no copy; event text written by other people, such as whoever invites you, reaches the agent as tool output; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yandex_mail
description: Search and read Yandex Mail, organize messages and reply through IMAP/SMTP. Choose which folders and actions Thor can use; saving attachments and sending require explicit opt-in. Disclosure — reads and changes your Yandex Mail over IMAP at imap.yandex.ru and sends over SMTP at smtp.yandex.ru (or the hosts in YANDEX_MAIL_IMAP_HOST / YANDEX_MAIL_SMTP_HOST if you set them, which are not restricted to Yandex), over verified TLS, with your YANDEX_MAIL_LOGIN and YANDEX_MAIL_APP_PASSWORD read through Thor; flagging, moving and deleting, including irreversible permanent deletion, are offered unless YANDEX_MAIL_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only mailbox); saving attachments and sending are off until YANDEX_MAIL_ACTIONS names save_attachment and send_message; once on, sending asks no per-message confirmation, also in cron and other unattended runs, and reaches any address unless YANDEX_MAIL_SEND_TO fences recipients; saved attachments go to Thor' shared document cache, where other tools can read them, and are pruned after 24 hours; mail written by other people reaches the agent as tool output; uses Thor' private tools.credential_files helper to map saved paths into sandboxes; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yantrikdb
description: Persistent memory for Thor. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

name: yantrikdb-thor-dashboard
description: Local-only YantrikDB dashboard for Thor Agent memory operations

name: year-wrapped
description: Your year with your agent as shareable story cards. thor year-wrapped (terminal) and /year-wrapped (every surface) read your own history and write 13 cards, 1080x1920, each in its own colour: persona (16 types from four axes: night or day, build or ask, terminal or chat, one model or many, with the real shares printed on the card), top tools, most used skill, manners and swear jar, night shift, longest chat, tokens processed, night crew (cron jobs and subagents), main model, projects started vs. archived, word of the year and a black and gold summary. Session titles are hidden unless --show-titles; client names can be excluded or shown under a code name (exclude_words, rename_words). No cost figures. English and German. Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls, standard library only. Reads state.db and, if present, projects.db of the active profile read only (mode=ro); never writes to them. Writes the cards as self-contained HTML (no scripts, no external assets) plus an index.html under THOR_HOME/plugin-data/year-wrapped/<period>/ or the folder given with --out. The terminal command thor year-wrapped renders PNG files by starting a locally installed headless Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave or Playwright headless shell (or the one set in browser_path) as a subprocess that opens only the local card files; --no-png skips it, and /year-wrapped in a chat never starts a browser. Nothing is downloaded. No credentials, no hooks, no tools, no cron jobs, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: yolo-auto
description: Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

name: you
description: You.com skills for live web search, URL content extraction, cited research, finance research, and integration discovery via the You.com MCP servers (api.you.com). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.

name: you-should-know
description: A side agent rereads the conversation while Thor works on longer turns and surfaces the one thing you might have missed — a silent tradeoff, an unverified result, an irreversible action — as a dismissible note above the prompt. Disclosure — on tool-using turns in Desktop, CLI and TUI (configurable via `platforms`), sends up to 12,000 characters of the recent conversation, including clipped tool calls and results, to Thor's configured auxiliary model up to five extra times per turn (45 s cooldown), which adds model cost; notes are stored in the plugin's own data folder.

name: youtube-dock
description: Open your signed-in YouTube Home recommendations and Shorts in the existing Thor Desktop Browser beside your conversation, without pasting video URLs or launching an external browser. Desktop-only SDK launcher; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or API keys. Disclosure — explicit user clicks load YouTube and its normal service/CDN requests in the native Browser; this plugin does not read credentials, cookies, recommendations or watch history. No telemetry, shell commands, backend service or self-updater. Uses the native preview toggle (Hide for an already-open destination), not a dedicated PIP player.

name: yuanbao
description: Tencent Yuanbao messaging platform (DMs and group chats over Yuanbao's bot WebSocket, native media and stickers, DM/group access policies, cron home-channel delivery) plus the yuanbao toolset (yb_query_group_info, yb_query_group_members, yb_send_dm, yb_search_sticker, yb_send_sticker). Formerly built into Thor core; existing users are migrated automatically. A Thor Labs plugin: built by Thor Labs, not supported, and likely not maintained going forward. Fixes from the community are welcome. Disclosure — messages, media and group member lists travel between Tencent's Yuanbao servers and your Thor gateway using your own Yuanbao bot App ID and App Secret. The plugin also downloads image URLs that appear in replies or inbound messages, and its sign-token requests carry the Thor version and an instance id.

name: z-midi-console
description: Universal MIDI control-surface builder — any USB/MIDI synth as live on-screen controls in Thor Desktop, MIDI-learn bindings, multi-synth deck, spectrum analyzers, software mod matrix, .mid export, seven agent tools. Zero Python dependencies. Disclosure — The MIDI Console chat box sends your typed request (masked for key- or token-shaped text), a summary of the active device preset (names, MIDI channel, control labels, CC numbers, modulation lanes) and the last few chat-box turns to your Thor model, or the model you pin under Settings → Models → Auxiliary → MIDI Console chat; device presets, recorded takes and a log of every MIDI message sent are stored under plugin-data/z-midi-console in your Thor home (a pre-0.2 store at %LOCALAPPDATA%/z-midi-console is copied in once and left in place); the audio analyzers read the companion audio-strip plugin's state file; the MIDI engine is Windows-only.

name: zalo-platform
description: Zalo Bot Platform gateway adapter for Thor Agent — relays messages between Zalo DMs/groups and the agent over the official Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com), long-polling or webhook mode. Adds slash commands and moderation. Zero extra dependencies (uses httpx, already a Thor dependency). Production-tested on multiple Vietnamese deployments. Disclosure — connects to the third-party Zalo Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com) with your bot token; long-polling by default, or opt-in webhook mode with a listener on 127.0.0.1 by default that checks the X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header; the setup wizard writes ZALO_* values to ~/.thor/.env; group chat history is stored locally under <THOR_HOME>/zalo-history.

name: zalodesk
description: Read, search and reply to Zalo chats, personal Zalo accounts and Zalo Official Accounts (OA), through the hosted ZaloDesk MCP: catch up on unread conversations, read and search messages, send replies, find customers by phone, labels and friend requests; and for the workspace owner, the team (Phân quyền): invite, change and remove staff, which Zalo accounts and chats each sees, their permissions, routing of new chats and calls, conversation assignment, which PC runs a company Zalo, and the AI credit each staff PC may spend. Everything runs within the user's ZaloDesk role (an employee sees only the chats assigned to them). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill); OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — send_message sends real Zalo messages from the user's account, the team tools add, change and remove people's access, and set_ai_credit lets a staff PC spend from the owner's AI wallet; the package marks the zalodesk server untrusted, so Thor asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Every tool call goes to app.zalodesk.com; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: zambo-receipts
description: Verifiable receipts for Thor Agent sessions. Lifecycle hooks journal every tool call in a session to Zambo (zambo.dev) as it happens, and when the session ends the plugin wraps it into an AER-1 verifiable receipt that anyone can open and check at a public zambo.dev/run link. Receipt pages are public: anyone with the link can read them, and the summary and goal text passed to zambo_wrap_session is published on the receipt page. Adds three tools (zambo_verify_receipt, zambo_wrap_session, zambo_session_status), a /receipt slash command, and a bundled skill. Disclosure — while enabled, the plugin makes network calls to zambo.dev (the configured MCP endpoint) carrying, per tool call, the tool name, duration, result size and a SHA-256 hash of the result; result text (truncated to 4,000 characters) is sent only when journal_results is set to full; at session finalize (/new, quit, gateway reset) it publishes a receipt as a public zambo.dev/run page, including the summary and goal text passed to zambo_wrap_session; failed entries buffer in a bounded outbox under $THOR_HOME/plugin-data/zambo-receipts/ with a stable per-install caller id; no credentials.

name: zaprite
description: Get paid from a Thor chat. One checkoutUrl for card, bank, Lightning, on-chain bitcoin, and stablecoins, then re-fetch until Paid. Disclosure — every call goes to api.zaprite.com (or the base_url you set in plugin config) with the key you put in the Thor secret store (ZAPRITE_API_KEY), read on each call and never logged; payment, order, invoice, quote, charge, ticket, webhook, contact-delete and dashboard-handoff writes happen only after you approve that exact call, while contact create/update run without a prompt; writes are refused in cron and while /zaprite kill is active; it registers no webhook of its own, and its only background option is an opt-in daily read-only digest automation that runs nothing unless you add it; payment truth comes from re-fetching the order, because a Zaprite webhook is id-only and unsigned. It cannot reach connections, payment-link creation, POS, events, recurring invoices, refunds, or branding, because those have no API.

name: zedmode
description: Every Thor Desktop conversation in one stack that recedes into the screen, ordered like an inbox: failed, needs you, working, unread, pinned, then the rest. Answer approvals and questions on the card, hold a thread beside the stack, start or branch a chat without leaving, switch a live chat's model, and tune the 3D live. Desktop plugin (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface) plus a read-only dashboard backend that reads the session list from state.db. No network, no credentials, no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — reads every session's titles, prompts and tool-call summaries from state.db read-only for its stack (cache in the profile's plugin-data folder); its Desktop page can send prompts, answer approval and clarify requests you click, rename/branch chats and switch a live chat's model; the backend calls Thor' private model resolver (`thor_cli.model_switch.switch_model`) to explain unusable models, which can query your configured provider's model list.

name: zerofactory
description: 24/7 AI multi-agent software engineering factory and durable SQLite Kanban board. Flexible triage with Grill Me clarification and EGM sequential spec audit, isolated Git worktrees, deterministic precommit pipeline, thematic continuous review, autonomous self-healing recovery, and Mem0 vector memory. Disclosure — once you turn on auto_start_dispatcher it runs background worker subprocesses using Thor agent profiles (zf-orchestrator, zf-goldfish, zf-builder, zf-reviewer) inside dedicated Git worktrees that push branches and open pull requests on boards' repos; workers use the profiles' normal approval policy unless you enable allow_unattended_approvals (which passes --yolo and --accept-hooks); mounts a web dashboard at /zerofactory with an embedded SQLite database; workers run each project's .zerofactory/precommit.sh checks; optional Mem0/Qdrant repository memory (off by default) sends memory text to the LLM endpoint you configure.

name: zeromem
description: Local memory that keeps every message word for word in one SQLite file. Storing and searching make no LLM calls and cost zero tokens. Rust core, with a one-command import of your existing Thor history. Disclosure — installs the author's compiled `zeromem` Rust extension from PyPI and, on first run, downloads a ~130 MB embedding model from Hugging Face into `<THOR_HOME>/memory/zeromem-models` (set `use_model: false` to stay offline); stores every user and assistant message as plain text in `<THOR_HOME>/memory/zeromem.db` and recalls them verbatim into later turns across all sessions of the profile (all chats and senders on a gateway); the agent can permanently delete a past session's stored turns.

name: zerosignal
description: ZeroSignal — private, pay-per-request inference through the local zs-proxy; no API key, your wallet is the credential.

name: ziztu
description: Plan, price and make AI micro dramas and anime episodes with the same characters in every shot through the hosted Ziztu MCP server (30 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://getziztu.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE through Thor' MCP OAuth flow), plus four skills: micro drama series writing, viral faceless reels, YouTube Shorts and TikToks, faceless YouTube videos, and cinematic depth for image and video prompts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted connector: every tool call sends prompts, scripts and project data to getziztu.com under the user's Ziztu account (OAuth sign-in through Thor' MCP OAuth flow). Tools that make frames, clips, music or scripts spend that account's credits (each takes max_credits, accepts dry_run, and the server asks for confirm above 5,000 credits); the package marks the server untrusted, so Thor asks before every call that is not read-only. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned commit. The skills ship four standard-library Python helper scripts the agent may run: three read local text files (episode scripts, season grids, prompts) and one (split_season.py) writes per-episode .fountain files into a folder the agent names; no network calls, install scripts, bundled credentials, background processes or telemetry.

name: zolva
description: Read Zolva's trading agents on Robinhood Chain (tokenized US stocks and ETFs, ETH and BTC, and Lighter perps) through Zolva's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no API key): published agents with their return against simply holding the same markets, every hourly buy, sell, short, cover or hold with the agent's own reason, market prices and recent trades. Two skills are bundled: zolva-agents for questions, and zolva-trade-watch, an hourly cron job that sends an agent's new trades to the user's chat and stays silent otherwise. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Zolva's MCP server at zolvaagent.app/mcp (60 requests a minute per IP). All five tools are read only and annotated readOnlyHint; none signs, sends, spends or reads a key, and the package marks the server untrusted. The data is paper trading (virtual money at real prices), not investment advice. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. The tool list comes from Zolva's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

name: zotero
description: Research with your own Zotero library: search it, read your PDF highlights and full text, cite with Zotero's citation engine (any CSL style, BibTeX/RIS export), add papers by DOI/arXiv with PDFs, and check a draft's citations against the library. Reads Zotero desktop's local API on loopback; zotero_add alone writes to the library and calls Crossref/arXiv. No telemetry, no credentials.

name: zoth
description: Zoth Studio tool catalog and ZOTHOS local-service tools (search/open Studio tools, probe Zoth services on 127.0.0.1, pull published tools)
